text: Uŋ wa kaalɛɛ la, u ga lau u saata la wir, ka kpa u luhanni laala la di laali.

ref: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
text: Juda ge bir la ka ga gil u dammu Adulam hinuu la lau a buuŋ di la ú ga tɛu, ka lɛɛ u kuna la uŋ ŋɔ nua di kpa tɛɛ a haaŋ la wa tɛu. Ka wɔɔ ga nawɛɛ.

ref: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
text: Denii u pɛɛzi baala baŋhina n du de, “Lee sɛnsɛnni la n faa du a bol naa ŋmɛnikɛrii la duɛi?” Ba bir ŋɔ u be, “Yaa waa sɛnsɛnni maa dɔɔwɛ bɔnnaa.”

ref: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
text: Hira jaa bir la ga ŋɔ Juda be lugɔ wɔɔ nawɛɛ. Haali de hina gba ŋɔ lugɔ ba waa sɛnsɛnni maa dɔɔwɛ de.

ref: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
text: Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Gil u kpogli a kuna. Yaa ɛɛ aniaa di lau a buuŋ ya vii ga tɛu, ka yaa wɔɔ nawɛɛ. Di yaa bittɔ la de, ba daŋ gaa mam yaa.”

ref: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ baaguzi ahoro, ba tili Juda be lugɔ u biibaal haaŋ Taama sɛmmɔɔ di kpogli hia. Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Aa! Ií lawuu ba di wa fuuuh.”

ref: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
text: Ka baŋ wa lawuu di ra la ba ga kpu la, u tili di ŋɔ Juda be, “Baal la maa kuŋ n ɛɛ hɔna jagrikuŋ ni u ŋmɛŋ ani daŋkpala naabuu duŋ a hia. I zum a hiŋaa?”

ref: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
text: Juda sɛɛ lugɔ u kunaa, ka ŋɔ, “U hor summɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, maa n nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ yuu Sɛla la hiŋŋɛ.” Ama, waa kaa sɛɛ u nuu chɔɔ maa.

ref: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
text: Unna lul la, bɛl nonii feli lii, haaŋ la n lawuu la kpa gessiaahmu di u nonii hiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Unniibuu felee lii.”

ref: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
text: Ka uŋ wa bittɛ di lau u nonii du, unla hiŋ bir feli di wa lii.

ref: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
text: Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ, “I fittɔɔ lii.” Ba faa dau u sɔŋ Pɛrɛz. Ba kaa dau unla ge gessi n vɔɔ u nonii la sɔŋ, Zɛra.

ref: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
text: Ismɛl kɔkɔɔza la kpogli Joosɛf kaali Ijip. Pɔtifa la n ɛɛ Ijip koori kooridia binna nabɔma yawuu.

ref: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
text: Denii u dɔɔri la n wa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du Joosɛf benii, u wia maa dɔɔ siwee la,

ref: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
text: u wia paruu werge maa, u jaa kpau birgi u himmaa huŋhunni. U kpa Joosɛf di birgi nɛr la n na binni u diahina wiimaa ni, di faa kpa u kundɔɔlaa maa du u nonee.

ref: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
text: Denii Pɔtifa faa jaa kpa kunla maa un dɔɔwɛ fɔŋŋa di du Joosɛf nonee. Joosɛf n du u be la, wiimaa faa waa kaa tiruu, di diwee la unna di bɛŋ wia lɛi. Joosɛf mai faa wesso nɛnnɛ, u kaa ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ,

ref: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
text: Denii Pɔtifa haaŋ faa bir di ra nyiŋŋuu, di ŋɔ ú nuu chɔɔ.

ref: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
text: Ka Joosɛf vɛɛ, di ŋɔ u be, “N dɔɔri yardimbuu, di gil n na binni kummaa n du dia naa biini. Awiarɛ waa kaa ra du a tau la.

ref: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
text: Nɛr maa waa a fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ di kaaliŋ. Kummaanii u kpa tɛŋ di i bɛŋ lɛi. U haannɛ hiŋ. Ɛrɛɛ ń wer ɛɛ keŋ widɔŋai? Guŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, Kɔraawiizi be.”

ref: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
text: Haali uŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ Joosɛf be guŋ hɔpizi bii maa gba, ka Joosɛf waa ɔɔ sɛɛ, u nuu chɔɔ gɛɛ u du u be gba.

ref: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
text: Denii a hɔl bɛl u zuu a dia ú hum u huma, di a dia balii bɛl maa waa hoo.

ref: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
text: A haaŋ la ga lau u tagtajaŋ di ŋɔ, “Gil n nii chɔɔ!” Joosɛf waa sɛɛwɛ, ka wir u tagtajaŋ hiŋ di du u nonee, ka chɔ lii bossee.

ref: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
text: u yir u diahina, di ŋɔ, “Ií na gunla Hibru hina yombaal naa n jaari n yauwɛ naa n ɔɔ hanna binni yaa pɛɛ, haali u wa zuu ŋɔ ú pumiŋ, ka n lɔ wile werge maa.

ref: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
text: Miŋ jaa lɔ a wile hiŋ, u wir u tagtajaŋ du n nonee, ka chɔ lii bossee.”

ref: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
text: U kpa a tagtajaŋ hiŋ di dau. U jaari n wa ballɛ,

ref: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
text: u kpa guŋ bagli tɛu, di ŋɔ, “Hibru hina yombaal naa hiŋ lauwɛ ba naa binnimbuu pɛɛ, haali di wa zuu n be,

ref: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
text: n lɔ wile u wir u tagtajaŋ du n nonee ka chɔ lii.”

ref: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
text: U lau Joosɛf di tɔ dia, bɔr la u dɔɔri Ijip koori la n na tɔ nɛra la. Joosɛf n du a nɛra tɔi dia hiŋ,

ref: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
text: Kɔraawiizi faa haa du u benii di ra hiinuu u wiɛɛlaa maa biini, u wia ra par nɛr la n na binni banla baŋ tɔ dia la ni.

ref: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, u gil Joosɛf ɛɛ u dɔŋahina la baŋ tɔ dia la maa nabɔma, di ra du wii la maa n na ɛɛ a dia biini tau.

ref: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
text: A nɛra tɔi dia binni la faa waa kaa ra fɔŋ wia la maa uŋ kpawɛɛ du Joosɛf nonee ŋɔ ú ra binni wia, Kɔraawiizi faa du u benii, di gil u wiimaa ra vol nɛnnɛ.

ref: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
text: u lau baa di tɔ dia, u dia binna nabɔma Pɔtifa dia, bɔr la baŋ tɔ Joosɛf la.

ref: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
text: Ban du a nɛra tɔi dia la, Pɔtifa gil Joosɛf ra du ba tau. Ban du de hiŋ,

ref: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
text: a hɔl bɛl hamuŋa ni, koori libikpogli ni u paanuɔɔzi chɔɔ deezi, bɛl maa deeza zɛɛ kur.

ref: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Joosɛf ba ba be, u na lugɔ ba biine chɔkkɔɔ.

ref: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
text: U pɛɛzi baa, “Beedee n kpogli ia zinaa, ii nyɛm gunnɛi?”

ref: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
text: Denii ba ŋɔ, “Yaa dɛɛ deezoore, ka nɛr maa waa hoo ú bagli a zɛɛzi tɛɛ yaa.” Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Deeza zɛɛzi baglaa lii Kɔraawiizi benii. Ií bagliŋ ii deeza hiŋ.”

ref: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
text: A koori libikpogli la ŋɔ, “N na grepu daa bɛllɛ n chigɛ n see,

ref: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
text: di dɔɔ kela ahoro. U ni waraa di u fiiwɔ, u ni u fii di u nɔnnɔ, u nɔna aah.

ref: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
text: N kaa na lugɔ miŋ kpogli Ijip koori libee. Denii n kpa nɔna la di hanzi a niiri di du a libee biini, di kpa tɛɛ Ijip koori.”

ref: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
text: Joosɛf ŋɔ, “N zum i deeza hiŋ zɛɛrɛ. Kela ahoro la ɛɛ hɔpizaa ahoroo.

ref: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
text: Hɔpizaa ahoro biini, a koori daŋ lizii lii nɛra tɔi dia naa biini, di gil i kaa ra kpogli u libee, ú ra nyɔɔ gunla hiŋ faa ɔɔ ra kpogluu di ra tɛu saŋa maa la.

ref: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
text: Awia, di i wa liwɔɔ, i wiimaa kuari nɛnnɛ, ɛɛ ra liizi n wia di ɛɛŋ nɛnnɛ, di gil Ijip koori zum n wia di liziŋ bɔnnaa.

ref: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
text: N kipar lɛi ba lii n ni Hibru hɛri di ba ɛŋ. Maa wii maa ɛɛwɛ di dɛg lugɔ bá tɔŋ dia gba.”

ref: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
text: Too, a paanuɔɔza nabɔma la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ lugli hiŋ la deeza zɛɛ wessoo la, u ge bagli u deeza tɛɛ Joosɛf, di ŋɔ, “N deezoore di na alugɔ miŋ chigɛ paanuuzi kɛɛgɔɔzi ahoro.

ref: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
text: Unla n hɔŋ chiŋ la su paanuɔɔzaa irizi miŋ chigɛ di ra la ń ga tɛɛ Ijip koori. Ka zumbizi ba di waa dia.”

ref: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
text: Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ, “N daŋ bagli a ge zɛɛ tɛi. Kɛɛgɔzi ahoro la ɛɛ hɔpizaa ahoroo.

ref: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
text: Hɔpizaa ahoro biini, Ijip koori daŋ teŋ i nyuu, ka kpa i bɔrahɔŋ tɔɔh daa ni, zumbizi ba di waa di.”

ref: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
text: Hɔpizaa ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Ijip koori lulaa hɔpizii hel, u daali diuzenaa di tɛɛ u huŋhunna ni ba nabɔnzi ani u diahina maa. Denii u hum dí ba ga lizi u libikpogli la ani paanuɔɔza nabɔma la, a nɛra tɔi dia biini di ba u ni u nabɔnzi la see.

ref: He put the personal servant back in his old job
text: Baŋ wa ballɛ, u kaa kpa libikpogli la waa nabɔmuu la tɛu,

ref: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
text: ka ŋɔ bá kpu unla waa, di kpau tɔɔh daa ni, gunla himmaa Joosɛf n baglɛɛ la.

ref: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
text: Binni anɛɛ n wa bɛrɛɛ, a hɔl bɛl Ijip koori chɔɔ di deezi uŋ chigɔ Muu Naal baŋgia.

ref: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
text: U deeza hiŋ biini, u na nauna aniidaanɛɛ n pɔllɛ di du wer werge maa, a lii a nii biini di ra di kooree u baŋgia.

ref: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
text: Denii akɔgni werge aniidaanɛɛ ge kaa lii a nii biini, di ga chi anla n pɔllɛ la be.

ref: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
text: U ŋɔ u binni, di akɔgni la lauri a pɔllaa la di ligli. Ijip koori n na gunla, u hassi izi.

ref: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
text: Denii u kaa foozi chɔɔ dɔɔ di kaa deezi di na midaakpaŋ n dɔɔ nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ, a du bee nɛnnɛ di du wer.

ref: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
text: Denii minyuuni aniidaanɛɛ kaa wa lii di jaa anla ni. Ka aawaa, peu lii wiifurii di wa ta a ni, a hil, a bee maa war di chogli.

ref: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
text: A minyuchɔga hiŋ kpa a minyunanaa aniidaanɛɛ la di ligli. Ijip koori kaa hassi izi, di deeza biinii.

ref: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Ijip koori haa ra liizaa, a tiruu werge maa. U chaali u ziŋgaabo hina ni nunzunna la maa n du Ijip hɛri, di bagli u deeza la tɛɛ baa. Ka bɛl maa waa wette u bagluu a zɛɛzi.

ref: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
text: Denii koori libikpogla nabɔma la ŋɔ u be, “Zinaa n liizi wii bɛl miŋ ɛɛwɛ di leu.

ref: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
text: Saŋa la i baaŋ n faa fuuh n ni i paanuɔɔza nabɔma ni, i kpa yaa tɛɛ i dia nɛbinna nabɔma u tɔ dia la,

ref: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
text: a hɔl bɛl hamuŋa ni yaa bɛl maa deezi, a deeza bɛl maa dɔɔ u zɛɛ.

ref: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
text: Denii yaa bagli yaa deeza la di tɛɛ Hibru hina biipɔllii la n ɛɛ i dia nɛbinna nabɔma Pɔtifa balii, di ge du a nɛra tɔi dia la, u bagli bɛl maa deeza zɛɛ tɛu.

ref: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
text: Gunla uŋ baglɛɛ la, guŋ himmaanii wa ɛɛwɛ. I bittɔɔ kpa n nabɔmuu tɛŋ, ka teŋ paanuɔɔza nabɔma la ge nyuu, gunla himmaa uŋ baglɛɛ la.”

ref: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
text: Denii Ijip koori hum dí ba ga lizi Joosɛf ba. Ba ɛɛ manaŋ di ga lizuu lii a nɛra tɔi dia, di gil u fuŋ u taŋhuna manaŋ, ka ba kpa laala tɛu u laali, ka kpogluu la Ijip koori be.

ref: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
text: Ijip koori ga ŋɔ, “Dɛɛla n deezoore ka n nɛra naa bɛl maa waa wette ú bagliŋ a zɛɛ. Ka n nuu lugɔ i wettoo di ra bagli deeza zɛɛzi.”

ref: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
text: Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Miŋwaa wàá wer bagli a zɛɛ. Kɔraawiizii niŋ baglii a zɛɛ i bɔra wer sɔɔnii nɛnnɛ.”

ref: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
text: Denii Ijip koori ŋɔ, “N deeza hiŋ biini, n na miŋ chigɛ Muu Naal baŋgiarɛ.

ref: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
text: N ŋɔ n binni di nauna aniidaanɛɛ n pɔllɛ, di du wer werge maa lii a nii biini, di ra hee kooree u baŋgia.

ref: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
text: N kaa ŋɔ n binni di aniidaanɛɛ aŋhina n kɔkkɛzi werge ge lii a nii biini. A kɔkkɔɔ werge maa, haali n haa waa a dɔŋa nawɛɛ Ijip hɛri naa maa.

ref: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
text: Haali an liglaa la, ka a faa haa du a duulaa. Denii n hassi izi.

ref: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
text: N kaa chɔɔ deezi na midaakpaŋ n lul nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ, a ge maa du bee nɛnnɛ di du wer.

ref: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
text: N kaa ŋɔ n binni di nyuuni aniidaanɛɛ aŋhina ge lii a midaakpaŋ la ni. Peu lii wiifurii di wa ta a ni, a maa war di chogli.

ref: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
text: A minyuchɔgaa hiŋ ge kpa a minyunanaa la di ligli. Too, n bagli a deeza naabuu tɛɛ n ziŋgaabo hina ani n nunzunna maa, ka ba waa wette bá bagliŋ a zɛɛzi.”

ref: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
text: Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ Ijip koori be, “A deeza anɛɛ hiŋ maa zɛɛzi ɛɛ kpannɛ. Kɔraawiizi a bagliibuu wia la un niŋ wa ɛɛ.

ref: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
text: A nauna aniidaanɛɛ la n pɔllɛ werge ani a minyunanaa aniidaanɛɛ la maa chigɔɔ tɛɛ binni aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
text: A nakɔgni werge aniidaanɛɛ la ani a minyuchɔgaa aniidaanɛɛ la peu n lii wiifurii di ta a ni a war la maa ge ra bagli binni aniidaanɛɛ lɔchɔgii n niŋ wa chol labuu.

ref: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
text: Kennaa miŋ baglɛɛ naa himmaanii niŋ ɛɛ. Kɔraawiizi teŋ bagliibuu gunla un niŋ ɛɛ.

ref: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
text: Diwee daŋ su Ijip hɛri maa binni aniidaanɛɛ n niŋ ba la.

ref: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
text: Ba wàá ka liizi diwee werge la wia, dikuu lɔchɔgii la n na ba ú wa chol ba ni wia.

ref: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
text: Hiŋ deezi wikpaŋ bunɛɛ la, gunna bagluu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lau gunla un niŋ ɛɛu nɛnnɛ, a wàá birgi ka ú ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
text: Denii Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ Ijip koori be, “Nyiŋŋi nɛr la n ɛɛ nunzunni, di dɔɔ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ, di kpa Ijip hɛri du u nonee u ra binni.

ref: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
text: I daŋ kaa lizi nabɔnzi di gil ba ra lɛɛ Ijip hɛri pattikuna. Di nɛr maa ɔɔ wa kpa u koo kuna, bá lɛɛ a bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ, guŋŋ a binni aniidaanɛɛ la diwee n niŋ du de werge maa la biini,

ref: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
text: di gil bá chaali a maa di du buugizenaa biine, di chiŋŋaa bolzenaa la maa biine, di ra gua,

ref: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
text: diwee wer du a bola maa biine, mɔɔ ka lɔzi wa chol Ijip hɛri, di lii a guŋ binni aniidaanɛɛ naa biini. Guŋ daŋ gil lɔzi wàá kpu nɛra, bá siuzi.”

ref: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
text: Ijip koori ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ wer na nɛr u hum a keŋ huma naa, di kaa kaali baal naa? Kɔraawiizi Duma du u benii.”

ref: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
text: Denii u jaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Kɔraawiizi n pilli a wia naa maa tɛi i zumaa kennaa, nɛr maa waa kaa dɔɔ nunzuma ni nfɛrɛ di kaalii.

ref: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
text: Awia, hinuu niŋ jaa ra binni n hɛri ni, n nɛra maa ra sɛɛ i dɔɔra. N bɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ nabɔma i ni.”

ref: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
text: Denii a koori lizi u nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, u kpa ra jag kuna ni la, di du Joosɛf nonibii. U kaa tɛu laalinanaa, di kpa saliŋ baŋaakuŋ di duu.

ref: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
text: Ijip koori kaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Minuu Ijip hɛri maa koori, ka nɛr maa wàá wer izi di ɛɛ wiimaa Ijip hɛri naa biini, di hɔɔ tɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ.”

ref: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
text: Ijip koori faa kaa bir dau u sɔŋ Zafɛnaf Pania, di kaa nyiŋŋi suŋguru bɛl banna yir Asɛnaf tɛu. A suŋguru mɛɛrɛ faa Pɔtifɛra. Waabuu faa Hɛliɔpɔlis vug Ɔɔn kizeehiŋ. Joosɛf faa jaa gaagi di ra binni Ijip hɛri maa.

ref: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
text: A binni biinii Joosɛf faa kpa pattikuna maa ni a dizi banna par Ijip hɛri yeŋa, di ra chiŋŋi ba bolzenaa biine. A bolzeŋ bɛl maa kooni diweere u faa kpa di ra chiŋŋi de.

ref: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
text: Ba buugazi maanii faa suugi diwee werge maa alugɔ muunua hɛɛhriichaa. A diwee faa kannɔɔ werge. Awia, Joosɛf faa gil a mɛgzaa.

ref: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
text: Mɔɔ ka lɔzi wa chol la, di Joosɛf ni u haaŋ Asɛnaf la lul biibaala banɛɛ.

ref: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
text: Joosɛf faa dau u biinabɔma sɔŋ Manasɛ. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi hiinimbuu n suuh tɔɔrɔɔzi ani n mɛɛ diahina maa wia.”

ref: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
text: Di dau nɛɛhiŋ la ge sɔŋ Ɛfram. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n lul biizi hɛri la miŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ la biini.”

ref: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
text: Denii a binni aniidaanɛɛ la diwee n du de werge la n wa tunnɛ,

ref: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
text: ka a binni aniidaanɛɛ a lɔchɔgii n niŋ chol la jaa faari, gunla himmaa Joosɛf n faa baglɛɛ la. Diwee faa waa hoo hɛssi la n dugli Ijip hɛri la. Ama, diwee faa su Ijip hɛriwaa maanii.

ref: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
text: Awia, lɔzi faa ra kpu nɛra werge maa Ijip hɛri. Denii ba ga suŋŋi Ijip koori dí u tɛɛ baa diwee. U ŋɔ ba be, “Ií la Joosɛf be, ú ga bagli ia gunla iin niŋ ɛɛ.”

ref: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
text: A lɔzi n faa chol a hɛri maa, di du kpeg wia, Joosɛf faa jaa pilli a buugazi hiŋ, di yoo a diwee ra tɛɛ a Ijip hina.

ref: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
text: Hɛssi la gba n dugli de la gba nɛra ɔɔ la Ijip hɛri di gaa yau diwee Joosɛf be, dikuubɛɛwiai, lɔzi faa chol durnya yemmaanii werge maa.

ref: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
text: Denii Jekɔb wa nuu lugɔ sɔgmia du Ijip hɛrii. U ŋɔ u biibaala be, “Ɛrɛɛ ii so di ra binni dɔŋa ninɛi?

ref: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
text: N nuuwɔ lugɔ sɔgmia du Ijip hɛrii ba ra yoo. Ií la ga yau aŋhina ba. Di guŋ lɛi, lɔzi daŋ kpu yaa maa ya siuzi.”

ref: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
text: Joosɛf kpɛɛnna fi la jaa la Ijip hɛri, bá ga yau a sɔgmia.

ref: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
text: Ama, Jekɔb faa waa sɛɛwɛ Joosɛf niwee Bɛnjamin lawaa la. U faa ra ɔmuu lugɔ wii bɛl daŋ ga ɛɛu.

ref: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
text: Denii Jekɔb biibaala la ani nɛkpila maa ga hel Ijip hɛri, bá yau a sɔgmia, dikuubɛɛwiai, Keenan hɛri maanii a lɔzi faa chol.

ref: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
text: Joosɛf n faa ɛɛ Ijip hɛri maa nabɔma, di kaa ra yoo a sɔgmia la wia, u benii u kpɛɛnna la faa la bá ga yau a sɔgmia. Baŋ ga hel u be, ba togni hɛri di jaamuu.

ref: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
text: Denii u jaa ra liizi deezazi un deezee la, ka ŋɔ ba be, “Nɛchɔgaarɛ ia, ii ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na, ka ba wa lɔ yaa laal.”

ref: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
text: U kpɛɛnna hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai, nabɔma, i balaa ballɔɔ bá wa yau sɔgmia.

ref: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
text: Nɛkpaŋ biizii yaa maa. Yaa ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinaa. Yaa waa wichɔgii maa fɛwɛɛ ka ba.”

ref: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
text: Joosɛf haa vɛɛ ka ra ŋɔ, “Ií kara de! Ií ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na yaa gɛrga.”

ref: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
text: Ba kaa ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa du biibaala fidibanɛɛrɛ yaa mɛɛ lul Keenan hɛri. Yaa kalugu du yaa mɛɛ be, ka yaa bɛlwaa siuwɔɔ.”

ref: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
text: Ka Joosɛf haa ŋɔ, “Ií kara de! Maa ŋɔ ii ballɔɔ ií wa daani yaa naa?

ref: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
text: Kenne ya ɛɛ di zum di gunla iinna ŋɔ naa ɛɛ wibiire. N hɛɛhzi Ijip koori lugɔ di ii kalugu la waa ɛŋ ballɛ, ii bɛl maa wàá lii Ijip hɛri naa biini.

ref: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
text: Ií bɛlhiŋ la ga kpogli ii niwee hiŋ ba. Ií banla n kawɛɛ daŋ du nɛra tɔi dia, ka ya ra kpaŋ baa. Gunnɛ ya ɛɛ di zum di ii wiŋɔzi naa ɛɛ wibiire gɛɛ di karaawɛi? Di karaa ii ra kanni, guŋwaa, n hɛɛhzi Ijip koori la n du de lugɔ ii ballɔɔ ii wa daani yaa di na.”

ref: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
text: Denii u lau baa tɔ dia hɔpizaa ahoro.

ref: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
text: A hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl la, Joosɛf ŋɔ ba be, “N na ɔm Kɔraawiizii. Awia, di ii daŋ ɛɛ wii naa min niŋ ŋɔ naa, ii daŋ na miibɔɔ.

ref: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
text: Di ii ɛɛ wibii hinaa, ii gil ii bɛl du nɛra tɔi dia naa, ka ii banla n kawɛɛ la kpa sɔgmia di la bol di ga tɛɛ ii nɛra, lɔzi n na kpu baa wia.

ref: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
text: Ama, di ii ga bittɔ di ra ba, ií kpogli ii niwee la ba. Di ii wa ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ zum lugɔ ii ɛɛ wibii hinaa, ɛnnɛ maa, màá ka kpu ia.” Denii ba sɛɛ, dí ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
text: Ba ra ŋɔ dɔŋa be, “Gunla yaa n ɛɛ Joosɛf la wiarɛ annii maa ra huuzi yaa la. U suŋŋi yaabuu siaahmu maa ni lugɔ ya ta u haahkɛ, ka yaa vɛɛ. Aabuu gillɛ a keŋ siaahmu naa huuzi yaa la.”

ref: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
text: Rubin pɛɛzi baa, “Maa ii be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ya gilɛɛ ɛɛ yaa niwee wichɔgaa, ka ii vɛɛa? Too, u kpui labuu ra pɛɛzi yaa nua zinaa la.”

ref: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
text: Ba waa wette zum lugɔ Joosɛf ra nuuabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɔɔ faa ŋɔ wiarɛ, nɛbɛl biraa di ra du ba mɔɔri biini di ra tɛɛ baa.

ref: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
text: Uŋ wa nuu gunla banna ŋɔ la, u lii bossee di ga nyiŋŋi bɔr la un niŋ wer suah di wii. Uŋ ga wiiwe tuŋ, u bir ba, di lizi Simɛɔn di lii ba biini, di gil ba vɔɔzuu ba maa sibɔɔ. Joosɛf kpɛɛnna n bittɛ kaali Keenan hɛri wia

ref: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
text: Denii u gil u balaa ɛɛ sɔgmia di du banla n kawɛɛ la bɔɔtizi biine. Di kaa ŋɔ u balaa hiŋ be lugɔ ba suahzi bir bɛl maa kebee di du u bɔɔti biini, di kaa tɛɛ baa sɔgmia ban ninna di ŋmɛnɛɛ. Baŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ,

ref: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
text: ba jaa kpa ba bunni di chug ba kauzi di ra kaali ba bol.

ref: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
text: Baŋ wa hel bɔr la ban niŋ chɔɔ hɔpizi la, bɛl pilli u bɔɔti ú ɛɛ mia tɛɛ u kawee. Uŋ pillɛɛ la u na kebee n du a bɔɔti nua di ŋɔ,

ref: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
text: “Ií na, ba bir n kebee labuu tɛŋ. Aabuu du n bɔɔti biini la.” Denii ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba ŋɔ, “Beedee Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ yaa kennei?”

ref: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
text: Baŋ ga hel ba mɛɛ Jekɔb be Keenan hɛri, ba bagli gunla maa n du de di tɛu, di ŋɔ,

ref: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
text: Ka yaa ŋɔ yaa ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinaa. Yaa waa wichɔgii maa fɛwɛɛ ka ba.

ref: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
text: Denii yaa kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ yaa du biizi fidibaanɛɛ yaa mɛɛ n lullɛ, bɛl siu, ka yaa kaluguwaa du yaa mɛɛ be, Keenan hɛri.

ref: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
text: Denii a hɛri nabɔma hiŋ ŋɔ dí mɔɔ ka ú zum yaa wibii, u daŋ lau yaa bɛl di tɔ dia, ka yaa banla n kawɛɛ la kpa sɔgmia di ba bol di wa tɛɛ yaa nɛra, lɔzi n na kpu baa wia.

ref: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
text: Ama, dí ya lau yaa niwee hiŋ di ra ba, ú jaa zum lugɔ yaa ɛɛ wibii hinaa ɛnɛ maa. Dí, di yaa ɛɛ guŋ, u daŋ lizi yaa kpɛɛma la tɛɛ yaa, ka ya ɔɔ ba u hɛri di waa yau sɔgmia u be.”

ref: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
text: Ka baŋ pilli ba bɔɔtizi la, bɛl maa na kebee la uŋ kpawɛɛ turgi a sɔgmia la. Ɔnsii lau ba ni ba mɛɛ werge maa.

ref: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
text: Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Ií gillɔɔ maa kaa dɔɔ bie maa! Joosɛf waa hoo, Simɛɔn waa hoo. Ii kaa ŋɔ ii lau Bɛnjamin ge di jaa, ka n haŋ so di ra di dɔgnyaa?”

ref: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
text: Denii Rubin ŋɔ u mɛɛ be, “Di maa bittɛ ba, kpu n biibaala banɛɛ la min dɔɔwɛ la. Kpau du n nonee biini. N daŋ bir kpogluu ba.”

ref: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
text: Ka Jekɔb bir ŋɔ u be, “N biibaal naawaa wàá ka hiŋ ia la de. Joosɛf n siuwɛ la, u bɛnnɛ jaa ka u maa biibaal. Di wiimaa kaa wa huuzi u ge, ii daŋ gil biinichɔg kpuŋ.”

ref: The famine in Canaan got worse,
text: Denii lɔzi la faa haa ra nyaŋŋi werge maa, a hɛri biini.

ref: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
text: Sɔgmia la baŋ yauwɛ Ijip hɛri ba la n wa tunnɛ, Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ u biibaala la be, “Ií kaa la Ijip hɛri di ga yau sɔgmia di wa tɛɛ yaa.”

ref: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
text: Di hàá gil yaa nuu lawaa, guŋwaa, yaa gba n haŋ so bolle bɔ. A baal ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ wàá sɛɛ ya kaa nau, di yaa waa ya niwee kpoglee ba.”

ref: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
text: Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Ka bɛɛ n baani ii ŋɔ lugɔ ii dɔɔ niwee bɛllɛ bol, di ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa tɔɔrɔɔ duŋ kennei?”

ref: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
text: Ba kaa ŋɔ, “A baallɛ faa ra pɛɛzi yaa nɛnnɛ yaa diahina wia, di ra nyiŋŋi u zum di yaa mɛɛ haa du de gɛɛ, di kaa pɛɛzi lugɔ yaa dɔɔ niwee bɛllɛ di jaa? Ɛrɛɛ ya faa ɛɛ zum lugɔ u daŋ ŋɔ ya wa lawuu banɛi?”

ref: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
text: Juda ŋɔ u mɛɛ be, “Kpa a bie du n nonee ya kaali manaŋ. Di guŋ lɛi, lɔzi daŋ kpu yaa dia naa hina maa.

ref: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
text: N kpa n miibɔɔrɛ di ra char u siu. N danna binnuu, wiimaa wàá wer ɛɛu. Di maa wa bittɛ ba u ni di wa tɛi, minuu u haahkɛ chug saŋa maa, di ra la.

ref: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
text: Di i vii sɛɛwɔɔ yaa nuu la, keŋ yaa vii jaa la ga yau a sɔgmia naa bunɛɛ maa di ba.”

ref: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
text: A tuna maa, Jekɔb wa ŋɔ, di gunnɛ amɔ, ba nyiŋŋi ba ge hɛri kunnaanaa di ra la ga sunzi a baal. Denii ba nyiŋŋi nuuri aŋhina dizi, huuhnuu, dɔzi tiuzaa kuna ni kunsɔɔhrisuma ani daanɔna n summɛ, di ɛɛ sirya.

ref: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
text: Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ, “Bɛl maa kpa kebee la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ la guŋ bunɛɛ, di bir kpa anla un nawɛɛ u bɔɔti biini la ga tɛu. Aŋhinabe, nɛbɛl faa suuhwɔ ka ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
text: Ií lau ii niwee la di ɛɛ manaŋ kaali.

ref: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la hiini ia, di ga gil a baal suŋ ii ni, di lizi Simɛɔn a nɛra tɔi dia, di kaa gil Bɛnjamin ge gba bir ba n be. Gunla maa an niŋ du, di ba daŋ siuwuu gɛɛ di ba waa siu, ka ɛrɛɛ n kaa ɛɛi?”

ref: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
text: Awia, ba jaa lau Bɛnjamin di kpa ba kunsunzaa la ge ani ba kebee bɔra anɛɛ, di yali siwee di lii di ra la Ijip hɛri. Baŋ ga hel de, ba la Joosɛf be.

ref: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
text: Uŋ wa na Bɛnjamin ni baa n na ba la, u ŋɔ u diahiŋ be, “N ni nɛra naabuu niŋ di diwee wibaŋa naa. Awia, lau baa di zuu dia, ka lau sel kpu di daali a diwee.”

ref: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
text: A baal jaa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di lau baa la Joosɛf dia.

ref: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
text: Baŋ wa hel de la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa. Ba ŋɔ, “Kebee la baŋ bittɛ kpa du yaa bɔɔtizi biine lugli la wiarɛ la. U ra nyiŋŋuu ú lauri yaa di birgi u yoma, ka foozi yaa kauzi.”

ref: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
text: Baŋ ga hel Joosɛf dia dominua, ba la a diibinni be,

ref: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
text: di ga ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa n felee ba ɛŋ di wa yau sɔgmia

ref: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
text: di ra la la, yaa ga hel yembɛl yaa n niŋ chɔɔ, di ŋɔ ya binni yaa bɔɔtizi biine, di kebee la yaa n kpawɛɛ ba di wa turgi a sɔgmia labuu du yaa bɔɔtizi biine. Aabuu keŋ yaa bir kpa ba ya wa tɛi.

ref: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
text: Ama, yaa dɔɔ kebee aŋhinaa yaa n niŋ kaa kpa yau sɔgmia. Yaa waa zum gunla maa a kebee n ɛɛwɛ zuu yaa bɔɔtizi biine.”

ref: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
text: A diibinni la ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ gil a tir ia. Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi la ii ni ii mɛɛ n na hum labuu kpaa di du ii bɔɔtizi biine. N faa lɛɛ ii kebee hinnɛ, wibii maa.” Denii u ga pilli Simɛɔn di kpogluu ba ba be.

ref: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
text: Ka u jaa kpogli baa di zuu dia, di ga ɛɛ nii tɛɛ baa ba sanzi ba naazi, di tɛɛ ba kauzi la diwee a di.

ref: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
text: Baŋ wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba daŋ di diwee de la, ba ɛɛ ba kunsunzaa la sirya di ra kpaŋ Joosɛf, ú ba ba di a wibandiwee.

ref: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
text: Joosɛf n wa ballɛ, ba kpa a kunsunzaa zuu dia, di ga togni u see di kpaa tɛu.

ref: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
text: U pɛɛzi baa gunla baŋ duwɛɛ, di kaa pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ ii bazɛŋa duɛi? U haa du de ni miibɔɔ, di dɔɔ alaanfiaa?”

ref: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
text: Ba ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh nabɔma, i balii, yaa mɛɛ dɔɔ alaanfiarɛ.” Ka kaa tognuu.

ref: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
text: Joosɛf binni di na u niwee Bɛnjamin la n ɛɛ u maabie himmaa la, ka ŋɔ, “Ii niwee la iiŋ ŋɔ u wia labuu keŋŋ? Kɔ́raawiizi hiinii, n biibaal.”

ref: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
text: Denii u hahzi di lii. U niwee la wia faa sɔɔni u bɔraa werge maa, haali u ra nyiŋŋi wiraa. Uŋ ga zuu u chɔɔribɔr, u jaa ra wii.

ref: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
text: Uŋ wiiwe la, u sam u siwee, ka kaa lii di ba ba be, di lau u hiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Ií kpa diwee la ba.”

ref: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
text: Baŋ wa ba a ni, Joosɛf so u bɛŋ, u kpɛɛnna la ge so ba bɛnaa, a Ijip hina la ge n du de la ge gba so ba bɛnaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina faa ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Hibru hinaa, ba waa ɔɔ sɛɛ ba ni baa ra so bɔkpaŋ di ra di.

ref: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
text: Denii Joosɛf gil u kpɛɛnna la so hiŋ nabɔmuu guŋŋ di ga chug bichalahiŋ, ba nuu chaŋ dɔŋa. A tir baa.

ref: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
text: Ka ba jaa ba bɛl maa diwee ni di wa tɛu, di lii bɔr la Joosɛf n soge la. Ka Bɛnjamin diwee kaali ba bɛl maa hora lugɔ naabunue. Denii ba nuu maa so di di, ka nyɔɔ.

ref: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
text: ka kpa u himmaa saliŋhuŋŋu libee la di du ba bichala hiŋ la bɔɔti biini di jaa kebee la ni. Denii a diibinni ɛɛ gunla maa Joosɛf n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
text: Bɔr n waa chaani kɔlɔkɔlɔ, u ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba ni ba kauzi hiŋ chi ba bunni di ra kaali.

ref: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
text: Ba faa haa waa yemmaa helle, ka Joosɛf ŋɔ u diibinni la be, “Duŋŋi baala la luge manaŋ. Di i ga huuzi baa, pɛɛzi baa, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ii kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgi winanaa kimɛi?

ref: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
text: Bɛɛ n baani ii ŋmɛɛ n dɔɔri saliŋhuŋŋu libee la uŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra nyɔɔ nii, di kaa kpau ra vug lai? Ií na gunla biinikpola huma iiŋ hummɛ!’ ”

ref: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
text: Joosɛf n bagluu gunla, u izi dau ba luge di ga huuzi baa, di kpa guŋ ŋɔ.

ref: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
text: Ba pɛɛzi a baal, “Beedee wiarɛ i ra ŋɔ gunnɛi? Kɔraawiizi la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ alugɔ ya ɛɛ a keŋ wichɔgaa naa dɔŋ.

ref: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
text: Kebee la yaa n nawɛɛ yaa bɔɔtizi biine la, yaa waa bittɛ kpaa di lii Keenan hɛri di bir baa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya ŋmɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu gɛɛ saliŋ himmaa i dɔɔri diai?

ref: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
text: Di i wa na a saliŋhuŋŋu libee yaa bɛl maa be, guŋwaa, kpu a hiŋ, ka yaa ge maa birgi i yoma di hanna la.”

ref: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
text: A baal ŋɔ, “N nuu gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛrɛ. Unla n ŋmɛɛu la bɛnnɛ niŋ birgi yom. Ka ii banla waa maa n kawɛɛ daŋ wer di ra la.”

ref: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
text: Denii ba chug ba bɔɔtizi ba kauzi hiŋ ni manaŋ, bɛl maa lau u hor pilli.

ref: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
text: Joosɛf diibinni hiŋ faari di chi ba nabɔma hiŋ la be di pigzaa di ra la. Denii u ga na a kuŋ ba bichala hiŋ Bɛnjamin bɔɔti biini.

ref: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
text: Uŋ wa nau Bɛnjamin be la, u kpɛɛnna la lauri ba laala di piili ni biinichɔg, ka bir vɔɔzi ba bunni di chug ba kauzi, di bir ra la a bolzeŋ.

ref: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
text: Joosɛf haa du dia biinii, ka Juda ni u niuna la bir ba di wa togni u see.

ref: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
text: Denii Juda ŋɔ, “Oo, n dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ ya kaa ŋɔi? Ɛrɛɛ ya suŋŋɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ, í zum lugɔ yaa waa u wia zummɛi? Kɔraawiizii ra tɔɔri yaa dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia. N dɔɔri, yaa maa bittɔɔ ba ya wa birgi i yoma. Yaa ni yaa niwee la baŋ na i libee la u bɔɔti biini la maa daŋ birgi i yoma.”

ref: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
text: Ka Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Akai, n ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ. Unla n ŋmɛɛ kunla bɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ n yom. Ií banla n kawɛɛ la, iawaa daŋ wer ra la bol ii mɛɛ be ani bɔsɔna.”

ref: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
text: Denii Juda tuzi hel u be, di ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, n dɔɔri, di kanyitti tɛŋ, ya ŋɔ wikpaŋ tɛi. Haali hiŋ du lugɔ Ijip koori gba, ka i gilɛɛ gil i baaŋ waa fuuh n ni.

ref: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
text: N dɔɔri, i faa pɛɛzi yaabuu, ‘Ii dɔɔ mɛɛ gɛɛ niweeaa?’

ref: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
text: Yaa ŋɔ yaa dɔɔ mɛɛrɛ u jaa zɛŋ ani yaa kalugu uŋ zɛŋŋɛ ka lul. U kpɛɛma siuwɔɔ ka kau, u bɛŋ jaa ɛɛ u maa bie. Dikuu guŋ wia, u mɛɛ nɔŋŋuubuu werge maa.

ref: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
text: Denii i ŋɔ ya la ga lawuu ba, í himmaa nau.

ref: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
text: N dɔɔri, yaa ŋɔ i be lugɔ a bie wàá wer gil u mɛɛ. Di u liwɔɔ ka kau, u daŋ siu.

ref: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
text: I ŋɔ lugɔ haa kaa ra nyiŋŋi i na yaa ni siwii, di yaa waa yaa niwee hiŋ ni ballɛ.

ref: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
text: Denii yaa n bittɛ la, yaa ga ŋɔ yaa mɛɛ be guŋ.

ref: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
text: U kaa ŋɔ ya bir ba wa yau diwee tama ba.

ref: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
text: Ka yaa ŋɔ yaa wàá wer ba, di yaa ni yaa niwee la waa haŋ ba, nabɔma la ŋɔ waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi u na yaa ni siwii.

ref: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
text: Yaa mɛɛ la ŋɔ, ‘Ií zummɔ lugɔ n haaŋ hiŋ biizi du banɛɛ bɛŋ.

ref: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
text: Di ii kaa lau u niwee naa ge lɛɛ, wii bɛl ga huuzi u ge, ii daŋ gil biinichɔg kpuŋ.’

ref: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
text: N nabɔma, filaŋkennaa, màá ka wer bir la n mɛɛ be, di n ni a bie lɛi. U miibɔɔrɛ a bie.

ref: that he will die if Benjamin doesn't come back with me.
text: Di yaa laŋŋɔ, di Bɛnjamin waa hoo yaa be, n mɛɛ daŋ siu. Yaabuu niŋ gil u siu ani biinichɔg la.

ref: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
text: Nabɔma, n kpa n miibɔɔrɛ di char u hor, di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ n mɛɛ lugɔ di maa haŋ wa bir ba a bie ni, minuu u haahkɛ chug saŋa maa di ra la.

ref: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
text: Awia, jaande, nabɔma, gil miŋwaa lɛɛ u bɔr di birgi i yom, ka ú ni n lulla naa waa bir kaali.

ref: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
text: Di guŋ lɛi, ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ di bir la n mɛɛ be, di Bɛnjamin waa n ni jaawɛi? Akai! Gilɛɛ gil n wàá na n mɛɛ biinichɔg.”

ref: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
text: A guŋ saŋa, Joosɛf faa waa kaa wer ú lau u hiŋ. Denii u ŋɔ u balaa be kpegzi ni, “Ií maa lii bossee!” Nɛr maa faa waa hoo saŋa la Joosɛf n kpa u hiŋ bagli u kpɛɛnna la.

ref: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
text: U jaa ra wii werge maa. Ijip hina ra nuu u wiraa, haali ba la ga ŋɔ Ijip koori be gunla n ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
text: Joosɛf ŋɔ, “Ií tuzi hel n be.” Ba tuzi di heluu, u kaa ŋɔ, “Minuu ii niwee Joosɛf la iiŋ yoowe tɛɛ Ijip hina la.

ref: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
text: Ama, ii gilɛɛ gil a tir ia, ii ra pag iihinaa ni, dikuu iiŋ ɛɛ guŋ wia. Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ guŋ. Waabuu gillɛ n tɔ ii see di ba bɔnnaa, ya wa wer lɛɛ nɛra, bá gilɛɛ siuzi.

ref: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
text: Lɔzi teŋ cholloo binni anɛɛ la, ka u daŋ haa du de di ra la binni anue biini. Nɛr maa wàá ka wer par, ba wàá ŋɔ kuna kumaa wia.

ref: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
text: Kɔraawiizii gillɛ n tɔ ii see di ba bɔnnaa, ń wer ɛɛ wizenaa naa, di lɛɛ ii ni ii naanna maa miibɔɔni.

ref: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
text: Wibii maa, ia lɛi ba n ni, Kɔraawiizii ba n ni bɔnnaa, haali di gil n birgi nɛr la n ɛɛ nabɔma, di ra hiŋ Ijip koori ni, di ra binni u dia kummaa ani Ijip hɛri maa ni.

ref: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
text: Ií la manaŋ di ga ŋɔ n mɛɛ be lugɔ kenne u biibaal Joosɛf ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n birgi Ijip hɛri maa nabɔma. Awia, ú ba manaŋ, u gilɛɛ waa birgi.

ref: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
text: U ni u biizi ni u naanna ni u kundɛɛzaa maa daŋ wa so Gɔsɛn di dugliŋ.

ref: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
text: N danna binni i ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, a lɔchɔgii daŋ haa di binni anue di jaa anɛɛ naa n bɛrɛɛ naa ni. Maa nyiŋŋi lɔzi ra kpu i diahina maa.’ ”

ref: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
text: Denii Joosɛf kaa ŋɔ, “Ii himmaa ani n niwee Bɛnjamin gba binniŋ na. Ií daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Joosɛf, wibii maa.

ref: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
text: Ií ga ŋɔ n mɛɛ be gunla miŋ ɛɛ nabɔma Ijip hɛri. Ií bagli wia la maa iin nawɛɛ tɛu, ka gil u ba n be manaŋ.”

ref: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
text: Denii u ga faami Bɛnjamin kpogli, di ra wii ni bɔsɔna, u ge gba faamuu ka ra wii.

ref: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
text: Gunnɛ u ra wii ka faami u kpɛɛnna la maa guŋŋ di wa kaali. Uŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u ni baa haa wer ra ŋɔ wia.

ref: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
text: Filaŋkeŋ maa, di a amaniye teŋ hel Ijip kooridia lugɔ Joosɛf kpɛɛnna ballɔɔ. Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzi bɔra faa sɔɔni guŋ wia werge maa.

ref: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
text: Denii Ijip koori ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Gil i kpɛɛnna kpa sɔgmia chug ba kauzi manaŋ, di bir la Keenan hɛri.

ref: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
text: Gil ba ga kpogli i mɛɛ ani u diahina maa, bá wa so Ijip hɛri bɔnnaa. Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Ijip koori daŋ tɛɛ baa Ijip hɛrnanii ba so, di ra di a hɛri suma.

ref: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
text: Kali i kpɛɛnna hiŋ, bá kpa zagra ni torkozi di lii Ijip hɛri bɔnnaa, di ga kpogli ba haana ni ba biizi ani i mɛɛ di ba.

ref: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
text: Ba daŋ wer gil ba kundɔɔlaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, apazi la maa n du Ijip hɛri la daŋ wa ɛɛ ba hora.”

ref: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
text: Denii Jekɔb biibaala la ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Joosɛf kpa a zagra torkozi di tɛɛ baa gunla Ijip koori n baglɛɛ la. Di kaa tɛɛ baa diwee la ban ninna di ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
text: Denii u kaa tɛɛ ba bɛl maa kunlaalifalaa. Di tɛɛ Bɛnjamin waa laala bɔra anue ani saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaahoro.

ref: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
text: U kaa vɔɔzi kunnanaa werge maa n du Ijip hɛri di chug kauzi fi. Kauzi fi ge kaa chi mia ni paanuu ani diuirizi maa, bá ga tɛɛ u mɛɛ, di ba wa lii ŋmɛnɛɛ di ra ba Ijip hɛri, ba kpa ra hiini ba hiŋ.

ref: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
text: Denii u jaa ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka karfi baa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra dazi ii waa naa ŋmɛnɛɛ!”

ref: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
text: Ba jaa lii Ijip hɛri di kaali ba mɛɛ be Keenan hɛri.

ref: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
text: Baŋ ga helle, ba ŋɔ Jekɔb be, “Joosɛf haa du denii ni miibɔɔ, haali di ɛɛ nɛzeŋ di ra binni Ijip hɛri maa.” Jekɔb n wa nuu guŋ, u nua kpu, waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ wibiire.

ref: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
text: Ka baŋ wa baglɛɛ gunla maa Joosɛf n ŋɔwɛɛ, u ge kaa na torkozi la uŋ gillɛ ba kpa ba, bá wa hiinuu la Ijip hɛri la, u siwee jaa ba hɛri.

ref: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
text: Denii Jekɔb ŋɔ, “N jaa zumuu lugɔ wibii maa, Joosɛf haa du denii ni miibɔɔ. Guŋwaa n daŋ la ga nau mɔɔ ka siu.”

ref: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
text: Jekɔb ɛɛ sirya manaŋ, di kpa kunla maa un dɔɔwɛ di ra la Ijip hɛri. Uŋ ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba, u kpu sela tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la u mɛɛ Aizik n faa ra hum la, di lizi mbusu.

ref: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
text: Kɔraawiizi ba u be lugɔ deeza biini hamuŋa ni, di wa yiruu, “Jekɔb! Jekɔb!” Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Minuu keŋ.”

ref: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu i mɛɛ Aizik faa ra hum la. Gilɛɛ ra ɔm Ijip hɛri laŋaa. N daŋ du i be, di ga hiinii de, í dee wazi di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.

ref: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
text: N daŋ tɔ i see í ga zuu Ijip hɛri, di kaa wa bir lizi i nɛra lii Ijip hɛri, di bir ba ba ni Keenan hɛri naa. Joosɛf daŋ na i tuna.”

ref: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
text: Biibaala la Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Lia n lullɛ Mɛsɔpɔtemia labuu faa la, di kpa ba niuhambie Daina jaa, ba ge faa du tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni bahoro.

ref: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
text: Awia, di Ijip koori haŋ wa yir ia, di pɛɛzi huma la iinna hum,

ref: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
text: Ba nɛra fidibanumbɛl naa genii faa ɛɛ Jekɔb ni u haaŋ Zilpa biibaala. Zilpa naa faa ɛɛ balii la Lia mɛɛ Laban n faa kpawɛɛ tɛu labuu.

ref: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
text: Jekɔb ani Bilha la Laban n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ u biihaaŋ la biibaalaa faa la. Ba ge faa du nɛra baniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
text: Jekɔb dee la n faa la Ijip hɛrii la. Ba faa du nɛra tokkoahoro ni banumbɛl. U biiziwaa haana faa waa jaawɛ.

ref: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
text: Denii Jekɔb hum Juda ú tɔ see di ga huuzi Joosɛf, ú bagluu Gɔsɛn bɔr. Baŋ wa hel de,

ref: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
text: Joosɛf zuu u zagra torko, di la ga chem u mɛɛ ni de. Baŋ wa chem dɔŋa ni, Joosɛf la ga faami u mɛɛ, ka jaa wii birgi.

ref: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
text: Denii Jekɔb ŋɔ u be, “N jaa ɛɛ siryaa ń siu filaŋkeŋ, dikuu n himmaa n nai ni siwii, di zum lugɔ i haa du denii ni miibɔɔ wia.”

ref: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
text: Joosɛf bir ŋɔ u kpɛɛnna ni ba nɛra la maa be, “N daŋ bir la ga kali Ijip koori be lugɔ ii jaa lii Keenan hɛrii di ba n be.

ref: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
text: N daŋ kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ii ɛɛ senɔɔnaa, di ra dɛɛzi sela. Awia, ii kpa ii peeza, buuna, nauna ani kunla maa iin dɔɔwɛɛ di ba.

ref: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
text: ií kaluu lugɔ ii ni ii naabaala maa humaa sela dɛɛzaa, ii de dui maa. Di ii wa ŋɔ u be guŋ, guŋwaa, u daŋ gil ii so Gɔsɛn hɛri naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina faa ra gbɛlli senɔɔnaa.”

ref: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
text: Ijip koori pɛɛzi baa, “Beedee humaa ii ra hummɛi?” Ba ŋɔ, “Jara, yaa ɛɛ senɔɔnaa.

ref: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
text: Yaa ballɔɔ ya wa du Ijip hɛri, di wer na diwee ra di. Lɔzi la nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ Keenan hɛri, yaa sela ge waa kaa na diwee di ra di. Awia, yaa ra suŋŋiibuu í gil ya so Gɔsɛn hɛri.”

ref: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
text: Ijip koori jaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Filaŋkeŋ, i mɛɛ ni i kpɛɛnna ba i benii bɔnnaa.

ref: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
text: Hinuu dɔɔ a Ijip hɛri naa maa. Nyiŋŋi u bɔnanii tɛɛ baa ba so. Gɔsɛn hɛrii wesse. Gil ba ga so de. I daŋ kaa wer binni ba biini, di lizi banla n zum huma nɛnnɛ, di gil ba waa nɔɔni n gba sela ra tɛŋ.”

ref: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
text: Denii Joosɛf faa gil u mɛɛ Jekɔb ge ga jaami Ijip koori. Jekɔb faa kissuu.

ref: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
text: Ijip koori pɛɛzuu, “I binni du aŋmɛnɛi?”

ref: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ ú lii Ijip koori be, u kaa kissuu mɔɔ ka haa kaali.

ref: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
text: Awia, Joosɛf faa jaa binni Ijip hɛri bɔnanii n dugli bol bɛl banna yir Ramɛsis, di faa kpa de di tɛɛ u mɛɛ ni u kpɛɛnna ba so, gunla Ijip koori n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Joseph also provided food for their families. A Famine in Egypt
text: Ka faa jaa kpa diwee werge maa tɛɛ baa, gunla maga n niŋ wer hel ba ni ba biizi maa nɛnnɛ.

ref: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
text: Annii n na ɛɛ naa, di lɔzi faa haa ra nyaŋŋi werge Ijip ani Keenan hɛssi maa. Diwee faa waa hoo, lɔzi ra kpu nɛra, ba ra huahgi bɔr maa.

ref: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
text: Joosɛf lɛɛ diwee la ban faa yoowe la kebee maa di lii Ijip ni Keenan hɛssi, di faa kpaa la Ijip kooridia.

ref: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
text: Ka Ijip ani Keenan hina n waa kaa wa dɔɔ kebee ba yau diwee, Ijip hina ba Joosɛf be, di wa wii ra duu, di ŋɔ, “Tɛɛ yaa diwee ya di! Di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ siuzi. Yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kebee ya yau diwee di.”

ref: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
text: Denii Joosɛf ŋɔ ba be, “Iiŋ waa kebee dɔɔwɛ ii yau naa, amɔ, ii lauri ii sela di waa char a diwee.”

ref: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
text: Ka bina bɛl n kaa wa hel, ba kaa ba Joosɛf be di wa ŋɔ, “Wiimaa waa hoo yaa n niŋ wer kpa suah i ni, yaa nabɔma. Yaa kebee maanii tunnɛ, yaa sela la maa gba kaa birgi i hora. Awia, yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa, di yaa bɔrahɔna ni yaa hɛssi naa bɛŋ lɛi.

ref: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í ra binni yaa ka ya siuzɛi? Awia, yau yaa ni yaa hɛri naa maa, yá ɛɛ Ijip koori yoma, ka í tɛɛ yaa diwee ya di. Tɛɛ yaa kundee ya kpa a yeŋ di, ka kpa a yeŋ ga duu yaa hɛssi, á gilɛɛ chɔɔ pɛɛ, ya ge gilɛɛ siuzi.”

ref: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
text: Hɛssi la bɛŋ uŋ faa waa yauwɛ Ijip hɛri biinii faa kizeehina hɛssi, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip koori faa ɔɔ ra tɛɛ baawaarɛ diwee. Gunnɛ baani ba waa ba hɛssi yoowe.

ref: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
text: Joosɛf ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Miŋ yau ii ni ii hɛri zinaa di tɛɛ Ijip koori filaŋkennaa, kundeere keŋ, ií kpa duu a hɛri.

ref: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
text: Di ii wa kpa ii diwee, ií lizi a bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ di tɛɛ Ijip koori, ka a bɔr la n kawɛɛ lawaa, a daŋ birgi ii kundee ni ii diwee.”

ref: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
text: Ba ŋɔ, “Ii lɛɛ yaa miibɔɔnii. Gil yaa wia parii, nabɔma. Yaa daŋ ɛɛ Ijip koori yoma.”

ref: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
text: Awia, Joosɛf dau guŋ, u ɛɛ gbɔg Ijip hɛri. Haali ni zinaa, pattikuna bɔra anue bɔkpaŋ haa ɛɛ Ijip koori hotte. Kizeehina hɛssi bɛnnɛ waa Ijip koori hor ɛɛwɛ.

ref: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina la so Ijip hɛri, Gɔsɛn paga. Ba na kuna de, di ra lul di wazi.

ref: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
text: U siu n waa dugli, u yir u biibaal Joosɛf, di ŋɔ u be, “Di n wia parii, kpa i nonii du n naapɔg zɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛŋ winanaa, di gil i wia dɔɔ wibii. Gilɛɛ waa hugiŋ Ijip hɛri,

ref: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
text: ka di n wa siuwɔ, kpaŋ lii Ijip hɛri, di ga hugiŋ n mɛɛwaa hugribɔr.” Joosɛf ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
text: U mɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hɛɛhzi tɛŋ.” Denii Joosɛf hɛɛhzi tɛu. Jekɔb jaa pi u daŋkpala ni di jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, a hɔl bɛl Joosɛf nuu lugɔ u mɛɛ waa alaanfia dɔɔwɛ. Denii u lau u biizi Manasɛ ani Ɛfram, ba la ga nau.

ref: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
text: Jekɔb n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Joosɛf ballɔɔ, u ɛɛ ania di izi so u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni.

ref: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
text: Denii u ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “Miŋ faa du Luuz Keenan hɛri la, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ba n benii di wa kissiŋ.

ref: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ n be, ‘N daŋ gil i naanna wazi werge maa, di birgi hɛrzenaa kpila maa nɛra. N daŋ kpa Keenan hɛri naa tɛɛ i ni i naanna maa, ú ɛɛ ii hor di hanna la.’

ref: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
text: N daŋ lɛɛ i biibaala Ɛfram ni Manasɛ naa hiŋ lullɛ Ijip hɛri naa ka n ba la, bá ɛɛ n himmaa biibaala gunla Rubin ni Simɛɔn n ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
text: Ama, di i kaa wa lul biizi baŋhina waa, ba daŋ jaa ɛɛ i hora. Ba kapɛttɛ la baŋ niŋ wa di, daŋ wa lii Manasɛ ni Ɛfram be.

ref: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
text: Miŋ kaa bir lii Mɛsɔpɔtemia di ra ba labuu Rachɛl siu Keenan hɛri, di dugli Ɛfraf. N biini faa chɔgi werge maa, ka n kpau hug a Ɛfraf ŋmɛnikɛrii.”

ref: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
text: A guŋ saŋa, di Jekɔb faa jaa ra nyiŋŋi nyuŋŋaa, dikuu uŋ binnɛ werge la wia. Waa kaa ra na nɛnnɛ. Denii Joosɛf kpogli a biizi di tuzi heluu, u kor baa ani bɔsɔna.

ref: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
text: Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “N faa waa kaa ɛɛ tamii lugɔ n daŋ ŋmɛnɛ kaa nai. Ka Kɔraawiizi gil n wa na i biibaala ge gba di kaa jaa.”

ref: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
text: A biibaala faa so ba naabaal naazii, ka u ra ŋɔ annii naa maa. Denii Joosɛf jaa lau baa lalli ba naabaal hiŋ naazi, ka togni u see.

ref: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
text: U lauri baa di chiŋŋi ba naabaal see, Ɛfram chi u nomɛɛl, Manasɛ ge chi u nodig.

ref: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
text: Ka Jekɔb n ŋɔ ú kissi baa la, u gil u nodig bir kaali u nomɛɛl barii, u nomɛɛl ge bir kaali u nodig barii. Awia, u nodig faa bir sag bichalahiŋ Ɛfram nyuu, ka u nomɛɛl ge sag nabɔmahiŋ Manasɛ ge nyuu.

ref: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
text: U jaa kissi Joosɛf di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi la n naabaal Abraham ani n mɛɛ Aizik n faa ra hum la, u kaa binniŋ guŋŋ saŋa naa wa hel,

ref: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
text: u mɛlika ge n lɛɛŋ di lii wichɔgii maa biini la, kissi biizi naa, di gil n sɔŋ ni n mɛɛ Aizik sɔŋ ani n naabaal Abraham ge sɔŋ ra hiŋ baa. Kɔ́raawiizi gil ba dee wazi werge maa.”

ref: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
text: Ama, Joosɛf bɔra faa waa sɔɔnɛɛ, dikuu u mɛɛ n kpa u nodig di sag Ɛfram ni la wia. Awia, u lau u nonii la lalli ú sag Manasɛ ni di ŋɔ,

ref: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
text: “Akai n mɛ, unnii n du ɛŋ naabuu nabɔma. Awia, kpa i nodig di sag u ni.”

ref: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
text: Ka u mɛɛ waa guŋ sɛɛwɛ, di ŋɔ, “N zum wii la minna ɛɛu, n biibaal. Manasɛ gba dee daŋ wa wazi werge maa, di birgi hɛrkpila maa nɛra. Ka u niwee daŋ wa ɛɛ nɛzeŋ di kaaluu, ú dee ge wa wazi di birgi hɛrkpila maa nɛra.”

ref: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
text: Denii Jekɔb faa kissi baa di ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina daŋ wa kpa ii sɔna di ra hiini dɔŋa. Ba daŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi hiinii gunla uŋ faa hiini Ɛfram ani Manasɛ la.’ ” Awia, u faa gillɔɔ Ɛfram tɔ Manasɛ see.

ref: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
text: Denii Jekɔb kaa ŋɔ Joosɛf be, “N siu helloo. Ama, Kɔraawiizi daŋ chi i harbɔɔ, di ŋmɛnɛ gil i kaa la i naabaala hɛri la.

ref: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
text: Denii Jekɔb yir u biibaala la maa, ba ba. U ŋɔ, “Ií chaali n be, ń bagli ia gunla n niŋ wa huuzi ia.

ref: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
text: Jekɔb biibaala, ií chaali ba n be, di wa nuu ii mɛɛ Izrɛl wiŋɔzi.

ref: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
text: Rubin, hinuu n biinabɔma, n kaa feli lulii saŋa la miŋ faa ɛɛ biipɔllii la. Hinuu dɔɔ girme ni fɔŋŋa werge.

ref: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
text: Ka i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nii n ɔɔ su di ra lɔ. Hàá ka ɛɛ n biibala sitɔɔri, dikuubɛɛwiai, i lau n hahjigaa di chɔɔ, di doŋ n kunchɔɔrikuna.

ref: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
text: Simɛɔn ge ni Levii ɛɛ lulla, ba kpa ba tokobizii di ra kpuuzi nɛra.

ref: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
text: N ni baa wàá kpau di ta jina. Màá zuu ba sɛttibɔr maa. Ba baana gillɔ ba kpuuzi nɛra, di ra chaahzi nabala zaŋŋuzi pɛɛpɛɛ.

ref: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
text: Nuuseei di baa, dikuu ba baana n chummɛ, ba kaa dɔɔ sikpegii werge wia. N daŋ gil ba yaari Izrɛl hɛri maa.

ref: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
text: Ka Juda, i niuna maa danna chɔlii, í kaa kpegli i dɔma ge, í niuna maa ra sɛɛ i dɔɔra.

ref: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
text: Juda ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyimbii, n lau ol ka bir ba u chɔɔl. U kaa ɛɛ lugɔ bunyiŋ n tɛrgɛɛ ka chɔɔ, alugɔ bunyinniina, anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛ koozuuwei?

ref: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
text: U daŋ wa kpa u kaupɔl di vɔɔ grepu daa ni, u kel la n wesse werge ni. U daŋ kpa siŋ di chag u laala.

ref: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
text: U siwee daŋ aah lugɔ siŋhuu, u nyina ge huuzi lugɔ ilanii.

ref: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
text: Zɛbulɔn ge daŋ so muuzeŋ nua, muugbessi ɔɔ ra chi de, u hɛri ge magbɔɔ ga hel Saidɔn.

ref: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
text: Isaka ɛɛ lugɔ kaukpeg n chɔɔ u bunni bambaaŋ.

ref: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
text: Ka u na lugɔ bɔr la uŋ chɔɔwɛ la wessoo, a hɛri ge paruu, awia, u gil ba kpa bunni chuguu, di firuu u hum huma alugɔ yom.

ref: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
text: Dan ge daŋ waa di u nɛra wibii, di du gunla Izrɛl hina dizi maa n duwɛɛ la.

ref: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
text: Dan ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hɛrikuŋ n chɔɔ ŋmɛnikɛrii, dumkpola n chɔɔ ŋmɛnikɛrii, u dum zagu naa ú kpa u dɔɔri ha.

ref: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
text: N yardɔɔrɛ lugɔ i daŋ lɛɛŋ, n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
text: Nɛchɔgaa daŋ ga pig Gad ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka ú lɔ baa yaari.

ref: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
