ref: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
text: Awia, u fɛ u biini, “Bɛɛ wiarɛ kennei? N daŋ hel de di na gunla wia a daapuza n waa fuuh.”

ref: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
text: Kɔraawiizi n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Moosis ra bau ú wa binni na la, u yiruu lii daapuza la biini, di ŋɔ, “Moosis! Moosis!” Moosis sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Minuu keŋ.”

ref: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ waa dugliŋ. Lau i gawa lizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, bɔnnaa hiŋ chigɛ naa ɛɛ bɔnaniinaniirɛ.

ref: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala, Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n faa ra hum labuu.” Awia, Moosis tɔ u siwee, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi binnaarɛ.

ref: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “N na gunla maa banna tɔɔri n nɛraa Ijip hɛri. N nuu ba wiraare banna nyiŋŋi lɛɛi banla n na fir baa la be. N zum gunla maa banna sunni baabuu.

ref: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
text: Awiarɛ n tuu ba ń wa lizi baa lii Ijip hina nonee, ba lii a Ijip hɛri biini la ga du hɛri la n wassɛ di du wer, di du sum, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge, Keenan, Hitti, Amɔri, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina n duwɛɛ filaŋkennaa la.

ref: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
text: N nuu Izrɛl hina wiraare wibii maa, di kaa na gunla maa Ijip hina n na sunni baa.

ref: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, n na humiibuu Ijip koori be, í ga lizi n nɛra Izrɛl hina hiŋ lii Ijip hina nonee.”

ref: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
text: Ka Moosis ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Anɛɛ minnɛi lugɔ ń wer la Ijip koori be di ga lizi Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛrɛi?”

ref: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ du i be. Di i wa lizi n nɛra hiŋ lii Ijip hɛri, i ni baa daŋ jaamiŋ bizeŋ naa nyuu. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, i daŋ zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii humii.”

ref: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
text: Ka Moosis haa vɛɛ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Di n haŋ wa la a Izrɛl hina be di ga ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n faa ra hum labuu humiŋ ba be, ba daŋ pɛɛziŋ, ‘U sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ?’ Di ba wa pɛɛziŋ guŋ, ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ ba benei?”

ref: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ, Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n faa ra hum labuu humiŋ ii be. N sɔnnɛ guŋ di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa, di tɛɛ jimini naa hina ani jiminizi n niŋ haa ba.

ref: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
text: La ga chaali Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la maa di ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n faa ra hum labuu ba i be di wa ŋɔ, ‘N faa binni iabuu di na gunla maa banna dau ia Ijip hɛri.

ref: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
text: N ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ n daŋ lizi ia lii ii dɔgnya la iinna di Ijip hɛri biini di ga du nɛra baŋhina banna yir Keenan, Hitti, Amɔri, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge maa la.’

ref: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
text: Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi daŋ nuu tɛi. Denii i ni baa jaa la a Ijip koori be di ga ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔraawiizi la Hibru hina n na hum la ni yaa na dɔŋaa. Awia, gil ya lii kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ di vol hɔpizaa ahoro zuu hɛribɔduma la ga lizi mbusuzi kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.’

ref: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
text: Ka n zummɔ lugɔ Ijip koori la wàá sɛɛ di tɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ ii lii, di maa haŋ bagluu lugɔ n fɔŋŋa kaali u hotte.

ref: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
text: Awia, n daŋ kpa n fɔŋŋazeŋ di ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia maa dee, di tɛr ba digna. A har, u daŋ sɛɛ ii lii kaali.

ref: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
text: N daŋ gil Ijip hina tɔgzi ia, ii wia par baa werge maa, di ii wa ŋɔ ii lii, ií gilɛɛ haŋ lii ra kaali ni ii nodumazi.

ref: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
text: Izrɛl hina haaŋ maa daŋ suŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ Ijip hinuu gɛɛ Ijip haaŋ maa u nuu n du dia saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ kuna ani laala di jaa. A kuna naabuu bá kpa laali ba biibaala ni biihaana. Gunnɛ bá ɛɛ di wer paagi Ijip hina daama kaali.”

ref: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Ka di Izrɛl hina waa wa sɛɛwɛ yardiŋ gɛɛ di ba waa sɛɛwɛ ba nuu n be, ka ŋɔ lugɔ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi waa n be ballɛ, ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛi?”

ref: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ i kpogli naanɛi?” Moosis ŋɔ, “Daŋkpalaa n kpogli.”

ref: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Kpau ha hɛri.” Moosis n haŋ waa hau, di u birgi hɛrikuŋ, u chɔ lii a hɛrikuŋ be.

ref: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Hel a hɛrikuŋ di lau u diŋ.” Awia, Moosis hel u be di lau u diŋ la, u kaa birgi daŋkpala la u nonii biini.

ref: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kenne í ga ɛɛ ba yardi di zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n faa ra hum labuu ba i be.”

ref: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa i nonii du tagtajaŋ la hiŋ laalɛɛ la biini.” U ɛɛ guŋ ka lau lizi, di u maa huuhzɔɔ paratatata lugɔ bɔchɔgaa.

ref: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ u be, “Kaa kpa i nonii hiŋ hau i tagtajaŋ biini.” Moosis kaa ɛɛ guŋ. Uŋ haŋ waa lizuu, di wiila la maa tunnɔ, u kaa bir du gunla u bɔrahɔŋ maa n duwɛɛ la.

ref: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
text: Haali di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ ba wàá sɛɛ tɛi a wizenaa anɛɛ naa wia, di vɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ ga ŋɔ ba be la, ɛɛ nii lii Muu Naal la biini, di kpa a nii wa fug waari hɛri, bá see. A nii maa daŋ birgi chal.”

ref: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
text: Ka Moosis haa vɛɛ di ra ŋɔ, “Eei, n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, gilɛɛ waa humiŋ. N nua waa zum birgaa. Saŋa la maa hiŋ faarɛɛ di ŋɔ wia ra tɛŋ di wa lii saŋa naa maa la, maa wette ra ŋɔ wia manamanaŋ.”

ref: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
text: Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Moosis, “Anɛɛ tɛɛ newee u nuai? Anɛɛ ɔɔ gil newee birgi dignitaŋa hiŋ gɛɛ di kaa ɛɛ gɛnii lai? Anɛɛ ɔɔ gil newee ra na di kaa gil u ɛɛ nyuŋŋɛi? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ra ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
text: Filaŋkeŋ, a la! N daŋ hiinii i wer ŋɔ wia, di kaa baglii gunla maa minna nyiŋŋi i ŋɔ tɛɛ baa.”

ref: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ jaa fuuh Moosis ni, u pɛɛzuu, “Ka i kpɛɛma Aarɔn la n lii Levi dee biini la geu? Waabuu nua zum birgaarɛ nɛnnɛ. U tenna bau ú wa nai. Di u haŋ wa nai, u bɔra daŋ sɔɔnuu werge maa.

ref: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
text: U daŋ lɛɛ i bɔr di ŋɔ wia di ra tɛɛ nɛra alugɔ hinuu Kɔraawiizi u be, i ŋɔ wia di ra tɛu, ú ge ŋɔ ra tɛɛ a nɛra.

ref: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
text: Awia, kpa daŋkpala naa di ra la, di ga kpau ra ɛɛ wizenaa.” Moosis n bittɛ la Ijip hɛri wia

ref: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
text: Denii Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi n wa ŋɔ wia tuŋ, u bir la u hilabaal Jɛtro be di ga ŋɔ u be, “Gil ń bir la n lulla be Ijip hɛri di ga na, di ba haa du de gɛɛ ba waa kaa hoonei?” Denii Jɛtro ŋɔ, “A la, Kɔ́raawiizi ga kissii.”

ref: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
text: Kɔraawiizi faa teŋ ŋɔ Moosis benii di u haa du Midian hɛri, dí, “Bir la Ijip hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra la maa n faa ra nyiŋŋi ba kpui la siuzɔɔrɛ.”

ref: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
text: Awia, Moosis gil u haaŋ ni u biizi tinni kawee, ba jaa ra la Ijip hɛri, ka u kpa Kɔraawiizi daŋkpala di kpogli.

ref: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Di i wa hel Ijip hɛri, ɛɛ ania maa ka ɛɛ wizenaa la maa miŋ baglii la Ijip koori see. Ka n daŋ gil u digna du kpeg werge, u vɛɛ, di ŋɔ wàá tɛɛ a nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ ba lii u hɛri.

ref: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
text: Denii i jaa ŋɔ a Ijip koori be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ n biibambilugli.

ref: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
text: N ŋɔ i benii lugɔ í tɛɛ n biibaal la ŋmɛnɛɛ ú la ga jaamiŋ, ka i vɛɛ. Awia, n daŋ kpu i biibambilugli.’ ”

ref: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
text: Baŋ faa ra la la, bɔr ga biri baa, ba jaa chɔɔ yembɛl. Denii Kɔraawiizi ba Moosis be di faa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpuu.

ref: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
text: Ka u haaŋ Zipɔra kpa bidiilii lau u biibaal hɛŋ di teŋ, di kpau wa gbɔgzi Moosis naapezi ka ŋɔ, “N fug chal naabuu, awia, i birgi n lullii yaa dɔŋa kpai biini.”

ref: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Izi di zuu hɛribɔduma naa biini di ga chem Moosis ni.” Denii u izi la ga chem u ni Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ di koruu ka jaamuu.

ref: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
text: Moosis jaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be wii la maa Kɔraawiizi n humuu di ŋɔ u ga ŋɔ ani wizenaa la ge maa uŋ ŋɔ ú ga ɛɛ de la.

ref: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn la Ijip hɛri di ga chaali Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa.

ref: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
text: Aarɔn bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis la, di tɛɛ baa. Moosis ge ɛɛ wizenaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la, a nɛra see.

ref: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
text: Uŋ wa bagli baa tuŋ, a nabɔnzi maa yardi gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Baŋ wa nuu gunla ba wia n tir Kɔraawiizi, u kaa na gunla banna di tɔɔrɔɔ la wia, ba giŋŋi hɛri jaamuu.

ref: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn jaa la Ijip koori be di ga ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Tɛɛ n nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ bá la hɛribɔduma di ga di hɔpizizeŋ di tɔgziŋ.’ ”

ref: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
text: Ijip koori bir pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ Kɔraawiizɛi? Bɛɛwiarɛ ń nuu u nua di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaalɛi? Mɔɔ zummɛ, màá sɛɛ ba kaali.”

ref: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
text: Awia, ba ŋɔ u be, “Kɔraawiizi la Hibru hina n na hum labuu ba yaa be. Awia, tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ya kpa hɔpizaa ahoro di zuu hɛribɔduma, di ga lizi mbusuzi kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum. Di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ kpa wiilchɔgaa ni laal ta yaa ni.”

ref: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
text: Denii Ijip koori kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina kpillɔɔ werge, ka ii ra lizi baa huma biini.”

ref: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
text: A hɔl himmaanii Ijip koori du gbɔg bɛl tɛɛ Ijip hina banla n ɔɔ ra fir baa, ba ra hum lugɔ yoma la, ni Hibru hina banla n na binni a huŋhunna ba ra hum nɛnnɛ la,

ref: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
text: di ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá tɛɛ baa kɔlaa bá ra mɔnni birkissizi, ií gil ba himmaa ɔɔ nyiŋŋaa.

ref: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
text: Ka ii gil ba ɔɔ haa mɔnni a birkissizi gunla maga baŋ ɔɔ faa mɔnnaa la, ka gilɛɛ waa mɔŋ a yeŋ di ra ha. Ba dɔɔ yaaraa, awiarɛ ba ra chɛɛhgi, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Ií tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ya kaali ga lizi mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum.’

ref: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
text: Ií gil ba huma du kpol werge di jaa, ba ra hum di gilɛɛ kaa dɔɔ saŋa di ra nuu kara la.”

ref: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
text: Denii nɛra la n ɔɔ ra fir a huŋhunna la, ni Hibru hina huma nabɔnzi la ga ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Kenne Ijip koori ŋɔ, ‘Màá ka gil ba tɛɛ ia kɔlaa la iiŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra hum la.

ref: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
text: Awia, ií la ga nyiŋŋi ii himmaa kɔlaa, bɔr la maa iin niŋ ga di naa. Ka màá mɔŋ ii huma yeŋ ha maa!’ ”

ref: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
text: A nɛra jaa yaari Ijip hɛri yemmaa di ra nyiŋŋi kɔlaa.

ref: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
text: Banla n na fir baa la jaa nyɛg ba ni, di ra ŋɔ, “Ií ɔɔ tuŋ ii hɔpizi biimaa huma gunla yaa n ɔɔ faa tɛɛ ia kɔlaa ii ra hum la.”

ref: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
text: Ijip hina nabɔnzi la n ɔɔ ra fir baa, ba ra hum lugɔ yoma la faa lɔɔzi Hibru hina la baŋ lizɛɛ ba ra binni a huŋhunna ni la, ka pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii waa wette mɔnni ii dɛɛla ni zinaa maa birkissizi, a su a magai?”

ref: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
text: Denii a Izrɛl hina huŋhunna binna la la ga suŋŋi Ijip koori di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra tɔɔri i huŋhunna gunnɛi?

ref: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
text: I nɛra waa i huŋhunna tɛɛwɛ kɔlaa maa, ka ɔɔ ŋɔ ya mɔnni birkissizi, di ɔɔ ra lɔɔzi yaa, ka a lii i nɛra benii.”

ref: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
text: Ijip koori ŋɔ ba be, “Yaara hina! Ií waa huma ra nyiŋŋi! A guŋ wiarɛ ii ɔɔ ra ŋɔ lugɔ ń gil ii kaali ga lizi mbusu di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
text: Ií bir kaali huma filaŋkeŋ maa. Ba wàá tɛɛ ia kɔlaa maa, ka ii daŋ ɔɔ haa mɔnni birkissizi gunla maa maga baŋ ŋɔ ii mɔnni.”

ref: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
text: Saŋa la baŋ faa ŋɔ ba be lugɔ ba wàá mɔŋ ba hɔpizi biimaa birkissizi mɔnnaa la maga yeŋ ta la, a huŋhunna binna jaa na lugɔ wiarɛ huuzi baa.

ref: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
text: Baŋ wa lii Ijip koori be, di Moosis ni Aarɔn sogo di ra kpaŋ baa.

ref: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
text: Ba ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔ́raawiizi binni gunla iiŋ ɛɛwɛ di di ia seriya, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii gillɔɔ Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzi hah yaa werge, di tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ bá ga, di kpu yaa.” Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua bá lɛɛi wia

ref: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
text: Moosis kaa bir di la Kɔraawiizi be di ga ŋɔ, “Hoi, Kɔraawiizi! Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i gil biinichɔg chol i nɛra naa ninɛi? Guŋ wiarɛ i humiŋŋ?

ref: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
text: Di haŋ lii saŋa la maa miŋ la Ijip koori be di ga kpa i sɔŋ ŋɔ wia la, u gillɔɔ biinichɔg chol nɛra naa ni. Ka haa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ, í lɛɛ baa!”

ref: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Filaŋkeŋwaa, i daŋ na gunla min niŋ ɛɛ Ijip koori. Dikuu n fɔŋŋazeŋ wia, ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛŋ lɛi ú tɛɛ n nɛra bá kaali, ka u daŋ duŋŋi baa, bá lii u hɛri.”

ref: My name is the Lord.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
text: Minuu faa ba i naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb be, di wa kpa n hiŋ bagli lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la. Ka n faa waa baa baglɛɛ n sɔnnaniinanii la.

ref: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
text: N ni baa faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa Keenan hɛri la baŋ faa duwɛɛ di ɛɛ hɔɔhra la, ú ɛɛ ba hor.

ref: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
text: N kaa nuu Izrɛl hina la Ijip hina n birgɛɛ yoma la himaa, di jaa liizi n ni baa nuukpaŋ la wia.

ref: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
text: Awia, ga ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ‘Minuu Kɔraawiizi. N daŋ lɛɛ ia lii tɔɔrɔɔ la iinna di Ijip hina nonee biini la. N daŋ lɛɛ ia, ii wàá ka ɛɛ yoma. N daŋ kpa n fɔŋŋazeŋ ni wizenaa di di baa seriya di lɛɛ ia ha.

ref: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
text: N daŋ kpa ia ɛɛ n himmaa nɛra, n ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum. Denii ii jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii tɔɔrɔɔ la iiŋ faa ra di Ijip biini la.

ref: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
text: Denii ń jaa kpogli ia ba hɛri la miŋ faa lɔ bampirii di hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ lugɔ, n daŋ wa tɛɛ ii naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la. N daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia ú birgi ii hor. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: Then the Lord told Moses
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
text: “La ga ŋɔ Ijip koori be lugɔ ú gil Izrɛl hina la lii u hɛri.”

ref: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
text: Ka Moosis bir ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Di Izrɛl hina wàá sɛɛ tɛŋ, ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Ijip kooriwaa sɛɛ tɛnnɛi, n nua n waa zum birgaa?”

ref: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, “Ií ŋɔ Izrɛl hina ni Ijip koori be lugɔ minuu ŋɔ ií tɔ Izrɛl hina see lii Ijip hɛri.” Moosis ni Aarɔn diini hina wia

ref: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
text: Banniibuu faa ɛɛ ba domeezi nabɔnzi, Jekɔb biibambilugli Rubin biibaalaa keŋ, Hanɔk, Palu, Hɛzrɔn ani Kaami. Bannii sɔnaa ba kpa dau Rubin domeezi.

ref: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
text: Simɛɔn ge biibaalaa, Jɛmuɛl, Jamin, Ɔhad, Jakin, Zɔha ani Sual. Sual naa faa ɛɛ Keenan hina biihambie biere. Bannii sɔnaa ba kpa dau Simɛɔn domeezi.

ref: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
text: Gɛsɔn biibaalaa Libni ni Simei. Ba domeezi ge sɔnaa guŋ.

ref: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
text: Mɛrari ge biibaalaa faa Mali ni Musi. Levi dizii guŋ baŋ sɛbɛɛ dau.

ref: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
text: Izhar ge biibaalaa faa, Kɔra, Nɛfɛg ani Zikri.

ref: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
text: Uziɛl ge biibaalaa, Misɛl, Ɛlzafan ani Sitri.

ref: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
text: Aarɔn ge kpa Aminadab biihaaŋ la n ɛɛ Nasɔn niuhambie banna yir Ɛlisɛba la, di lul Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza ani Itama.

ref: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
text: Kɔra ge biibaalaa, Asir, Ɛlkana ani Abiasaf. Kɔra domeezi ge sɔnaa guŋ.

ref: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
text: Aarɔn biibaal Ɛliaza ge kpa Putiɛl biihaaŋ bɛl di lul biibaal, ba ra yiruu Finɛhas. Banniibuu faa ɛɛ Levi diahina domeezi nabɔnzi.

ref: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
text: Aarɔn ni Moosis naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ lugɔ bá tɔ Izrɛl hina ni ba domeezi see, di kpogli baa lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
text: Baabuu faa laŋŋɛ ga ŋɔ Ijip koori be lugɔ ú tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii. Aarɔn n lɛɛ Moosis nua ra ŋɔ wia

ref: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
text: Saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Moosis Ijip hɛri la,

ref: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
text: u faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi. La ga ŋɔ Ijip koori be wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ i be la.”

ref: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
text: Ka Moosis bir ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “N nua n waa zum birgaa naa, ɛrɛɛ Ijip koori ɛɛ sɛɛ tɛnnɛi?”

ref: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “A nuu, n daŋ gil i ɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Ijip koori be, í kpɛɛma Aarɔn ge ɛɛ i dɔgtɛɛ.

ref: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
text: I daŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ wii la maa min niŋ ŋɔ tɛi la tɛɛ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn, u ge ŋɔ tɛɛ Ijip koori, ú tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii u hɛri.

ref: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
text: ka wàá sɛɛ tɛi. Denii ń jaa kpa n fɔŋŋazeŋ tɛr Ijip hina digna, ka jaa kpogli n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni ba domeezi lii ba hɛri.

ref: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
text: Denii Ijip hina jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi, di n wa lalli n nonii tɛr ba digna, ka lizi Izrɛl hina lii ba hɛri.”

ref: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
text: Moosis ni Aarɔn faa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n bagli baa la.

ref: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
text: “Di Ijip koori wa ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ii ɛɛ wizeŋ, ŋɔ Aarɔn be ú kpa u daŋkpala ha Ijip koori see, u daŋ birgi hɛrikuŋ.”

ref: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn maa kpa la Ijip koori be di ga ɛɛ wii la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ba ɛɛ la. Aarɔn faa kpa u daŋkpala la ha a koori ni u nabɔnzi la see, u birgi hɛrikuŋ.

ref: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
text: A koori ge yir u nunzunna, u ijɔzi ani u ziŋgaabo, ba ge ɛɛ guŋ himmaa.

ref: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
text: Bɛl maa kpa u daŋkpala ha hɛri, u birgi hɛrikuŋ. Ka Aarɔn hor la lauri ba hora la di ligli.

ref: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
text: Ka Ijip koori digna haa vɛɛ du kpeg, waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ba be la. Chal wia

ref: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ijip koori digna haa kpekkoo werge, awiarɛ u vɛɛ lugɔ ú tɛɛ n nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
text: Kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, kpa daŋkpala la n faa birgi hɛrikuŋ la kpogli, di gaa kpaŋuu Muu Naal nua.

ref: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
text: Denii í ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔraawiizi la Hibru hina n na hum labuu humiŋ, dí n wa ŋɔ i be lugɔ í tɛɛ u nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ bá kaali, di gaa jaamuu hɛribɔduma biini. Ka haali ni zinaa i haa waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu.

ref: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi ra ŋɔ i benii lugɔ i daŋ zum lugɔ waabuu Kɔraawiizi di lii u wiɛɛlaa biini. Na! N daŋ kpa daŋkpala naa miŋ kpoglee naa, di lɔ muu naa, ú nii birgi chal.

ref: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
text: Nyinni la maa n du Muu Naal biini daŋ siuzi, ka a nii ge maa ra sɔɔhri werge puihpuihpuih, Ijip hina wàá ka wer nyɔɔu.’ ”

ref: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Aarɔn kpa u daŋkpala la di tɛr guali Ijip hina niiri ni. Ba gɔŋa, ba polni maa ani anla maa baŋ kiwee la, daŋ birgi chal. Chal daŋ jaa su Ijip hɛri maa, haali ba daazi bokittizi ni ba bia golaa niiri maa.”

ref: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
text: Moosis ni Aarɔn faa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ba ɛɛ la. Denii Aarɔn lalli u daŋkpala la Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzi la maa see, di lɔ Muu Naal la, u nii maa birgi chal.

ref: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
text: Nyinni la maa n faa du a muu biini la siuzi. A nii maa ra sɔɔhri werge puihpuihpuih, Ijip hina waa kaa wer ba nyɔɔu. Chal su Ijip hɛri maa.

ref: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
text: Ka Ijip hila la ge ɛɛ guŋ himmaa ni ba hiri. Ijip koori digna nyaŋ kaa du kpeg u vɛɛ, waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Moosis ni Aarɔn, gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ba be la.

ref: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
text: Ka u bir kaali u dia, haali a wii gba wɔɔ titte.

ref: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
text: Ijip hina maa jaa ki bulli Muu Naal la kɛraa, bá wer na nii di ra nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa waa kaa weraa nyɔɔ a muu nii. Sampussi aŋhina wia

ref: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ bɛri di lii saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n chɔgi a muu nii la.

ref: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kaa la Ijip koori be, di ga ŋɔ u be, ‘Tɛɛ n nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaali gaa jaamiŋ.

ref: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
text: Sampussi daŋ su Muu Naal maa ga bɛri. Haali a daŋ ba i kooridia ni i chɔɔribɔr, di tɔ i kunchɔɔrikuŋ maa ni ani i nabɔnzi maa ge diini, i nɛra maa diini, haali di su i paanuu ɔɔzibɔra ni a hɛnni maa biine.

ref: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
text: A daŋ zaahzi ra togni i ni i nɛra ani i nabɔnzi maa ni.’ ”

ref: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Aarɔn be ú tɛr u daŋkpala la guali muuni, gɔŋa, polni ani anla baŋ kiwee la ni, di gil sampussi lii a biine di wa su Ijip hɛri maa.”

ref: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
text: Ijip hina hila la ge kpa ba hiri di ge gil sampussi lii yaari Ijip hɛri.

ref: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
text: Denii Ijip koori yir Moosis ni Aarɔn, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi lizi sampussi naa n ni n nɛra be, ka ń jaa tɛɛ ii nɛra la ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii n hɛri, di la gaa lizi mbusuzi di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
text: Moosis ŋɔ a koori be, “Hinuu dɛkkɛ lugɔ i tɛŋ saŋa la min niŋ suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ i ni i nabɔnzi ni i nɛra maa, á sampussi maa tuŋ. A wàá ka du ii ni ii diini biine, anla n du Muu Naal la bɛnnɛ niŋ ka.”

ref: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
text: Ijip koori ŋɔ u be, “Suŋŋi tɛɛ yaa kɛrɛ.” Moosis ge bir ŋɔ u be, “Kennaa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, guŋ himmaanii niŋ ɛɛ, í zum lugɔ kummaa waa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum.

ref: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
text: Moosis ni Aarɔn n wa lii koori be la, Moosis lɔ wile di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dikuu sampussi la uŋ kpawɛɛ wa du Ijip koori ni la wia.

ref: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi nuu tɛɛ Moosis, di ɛɛ gunla uŋ faa suŋŋɛɛ la. A sampussi maa faa siuzi ba diini, ba diŋŋizi ani ba kooni biine maa.

ref: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
text: Ba chaalaa dauri kululuzi bɔr maa di kaali, a hɛri maa jaa ra sɔɔhri puihpuihpuih.

ref: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
text: Ka Ijip koori n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ sampussi la maa siuzɔɔ la, u haa vɛɛ ka dɔɔ dignikpega, waa sɛɛwɛ ú nuu tɛɛ Moosis ni Aarɔn, gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ize aŋhina wia

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Aarɔn be ú lalli u daŋkpala la lɔ hɛri, Ijip hɛri maa hɛɛhraa daŋ birgi ize.”

ref: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
text: Ba ɛɛ guŋ. Aarɔn n wa lalli u daŋkpala la lɔ hɛri la, ize ba wa tɔ newea ani sela maa ni, Ijip hɛri hɛɛhraa maa faa birgi ize guŋ zugzugzug.

ref: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
text: Ka Ijip hina hila la ge ɛɛ ania bá ɛɛ guŋ himmaa ni ba hiri, ka ɛɛ huhzi. A ize faa tɔ nɛra ni sela maa ninɛɛ.

ref: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
text: Denii a hila faa ŋɔ tɛɛ a koori, “Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ guŋ.” Ka u haa kpogli dignikpega werge maa, waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa, gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. Nakɛɛhzi aŋhina wia

ref: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa kuari ŋɔ Moosis be, “Feli izi chɔɔzi ni di ga hau a koori ni, saŋa la unna la Muu Naal la, di ŋɔ u be, ‘Tɛɛ n nɛra ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaali gaa jaamiŋ.

ref: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
text: Di i haŋ wa vɛɛ, n daŋ gil nakɛɛhkpilakpila wa tɔ i ni i nabɔnzi ani i nɛra maa ni, di su ii diini biine maa. Ijip hina diini maanii niŋ su nakɛɛhzi, haali ba hɛri maa.

ref: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa ɛɛ guŋ, a nakɛɛhzi ba wa su Ijip kooridia ni u nabɔnzi maa diini. Nakɛɛhzi jaa su Ijip hɛri maa, di ra chɔguu.

ref: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
text: Ijip koori yir Moosis ni Aarɔn di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií la ga lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hɛri naa biini.”

ref: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
text: Ka Moosis ŋɔ, “Di yaa ɛɛ guŋ, a wàá du wer, dikuubɛɛwiai, mbusuzi la yaa n niŋ lizi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la daŋ ɛɛ kii tɛɛ Ijip hina. Di yaa ra lizi a mbusuzi la banna kii, ba wàá paagi bia lɔɔzi yaa kpuuzaa?

ref: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ya kpa hɔpizaa ahoro di vol zuu hɛribɔduma di jaa lizi mbusuzi de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”

ref: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”

text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii, “Ijip koori wàá nuu gunla hin niŋ ŋɔ u be la, guŋ gil ń wer ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia Ijip hɛri, di jaa.”

ref: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
text: Moosis ni Aarɔn faa ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la maa, Ijip koori see, ka Kɔraawiizi faa gil a koori digna du kpeg, waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii u hɛri kaali.

ref: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, Ijip hɛri,

ref: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
text: “Baagu naabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii bina maa lugli baagu.

ref: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
text: Kali Izrɛl hina maa be lugɔ baagu naa, u hɔpizaa fi hɔl, baal maa daŋ lau pepɔl gɛɛ bupɔl kpu tɛɛ u ni u diahina maa.

ref: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
text: Ií ra binni a ni nɛnnɛ di ra ba a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl la. A duaninsɔnnɛ Izrɛl hina maa kpua.

ref: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
text: A diini la biine ban niŋ hee a ola la, bá ɛɛ a challi di fɔg a bossee dominuuzi gbessi kɛraa ni a chine daazi.

ref: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
text: A hɔl hamuŋa hiŋ, bɛl maa daŋ ɔɔzi a ol, di kpa tagkpola ani paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ jaa a ni, di hee.

ref: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hee a olhuu gɛɛ u daalii. Ka ii ɔɔzi u maa, haali u nyuu, u gballi ani u biini kuna maa jaa.

ref: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gil a yemmaa wa ka hɔɔ wàá pizi, di a yeŋ wa kawɔɔ, ií fuuah.

ref: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
text: Kenne dɛkkɛ ii dia, ii kirsi ii tagtajaŋra, di du ii gawa, di kpa ii daŋkpalli kpogli alugɔ iinna la ŋmɛnɛɛ la, di ra dia manamanaŋ. Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali diweere.

ref: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
text: A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋaa ń wa gaagi Ijip hɛri biini, di kpuuzi ba biibambilugla ani ba sela ge biilugla. N daŋ tɛr Ijip hɛri vuga maa digna. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
text: Challi labuu niŋ bagli diini la biini iin duwɛɛ. Di n wa na a challi, n daŋ gilli ii ni kaali. Di n wàá tɛr Ijip hina digna, wichɔgii maa wàá huuzi ia.

ref: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ. A lugli hɔpizii la, bɛ́l maa lizi yiisi maa lii u dia, dikuubɛɛwiai, di nɛr maa haŋ wa di diwii la maa n dɔɔ yiisi, di lii a lugli hɔpizii di ra la a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, bá lizuu Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
text: Ií gil a lugli hɔpizii hiŋ ɛɛ hɔpizii la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali jaamiŋ. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la ge, ií kaa jaamiŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma a hɔpizaa naa bɛl maa biini. Ii wiɛɛlii maanii ií ɔɔ daali diwee tɛɛ nɛra maa, bá di.

ref: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔpizii naabuu n lizi ii dizi maa lii Ijip hɛri. Awia, ii ɔɔ ra diu saŋa maa, di gil ú ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii naanna di hanna la.

ref: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
text: A lugli baagu la biini, ii gilɛɛ waa hee paanuu la baŋ du yiisi, di lii a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ la duana ni, di ra la u hɔpizaa tokko ni kpaŋ la ge duana ni.

ref: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, bɛ́l maa gilɛɛ waa gil yiisi ra du u dia. Di nɛr maa haŋ wa di kummaa n dɔɔ yiisi a ni, di hɔɔhrii gɛɛ di bol biere, ba daŋ lizuu Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hee kummaa n dɔɔ yiisi. Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ.”

ref: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
text: Denii Moosis chaali Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií izi la manaŋ, di ga lizi ii sela la tɛɛ ii diini hina, bá kpu di di Gillikaali.

ref: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
text: Bɛ́l maa mɔŋ daa bɛl banna yir hisɔp, di kpa lii u sel chal n du tassazeŋ biini, di kpa fɔg u bossee dominua kɛraa ni u chiŋ daazi la maa. Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ kaa wàá lii u dia a hɔl hiŋ di hɔɔ waa pizɛɛ lɛi.

ref: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi wa gaagɔɔ di ra chɔgi Ijip hina la, u daŋ wa na challi la n fɔg ii dominuuzi chine ani kɛraa daazi la ni. Di u wa naa guŋ, u daŋ gilli ii ni kaali, wàá sɛɛ mɛlika la n na kpu la zuu a diini di kpu nɛr maa.

ref: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
text: Di ii wa zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ia la, ii haa ra liizi a widaulaa naa di ra ɛɛa.

ref: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
text: Di ii biizi wa pɛɛzi ia, ‘A Hɔpizizeŋ naa dii zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?’

ref: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
text: Ií ŋɔ ba be lugɔ u ɛɛ Gillikaali mbusuzi yaa ra lizi di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Dikuu uŋ faa gilli yaa Izrɛl hina n faa du Ijip hɛri diini ni di kaali, ka waa yaa ɛɛwɛ wiimaa, ka kpuuzi Ijip hina la waa wia.” Denii a nɛra jaa giŋŋi jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
text: Izrɛl hina la sɛɛ, di ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be la.

ref: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
text: A hɔl hɛhhɛɛhzi ni, Kɔraawiizi ba di wa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla maa, di lii Ijip koori biibambilugli la n niŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa di kora la ga hel banla baŋ tɔ dia la gba biibambilugla ani ba sela biilugla maa.

ref: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
text: Ijip koori ni u hɛri nabɔnzi la maa ani Ijip hina maa izi a hamuŋa ni, ba chɛɛhgaa werge maa tɔ Ijip hɛri maa, dia maa waa hoo di nɛr waa siuwɛ. Ijip hɛri lii wia

ref: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
text: A hɔl hamuŋa ni, Ijip koori yir Moosis ni Aarɔn, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ga kpogli Izrɛl hina maa lii n hɛri! Ií ra la gaa jaami Kɔraawiizi gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
text: Ií kpa ii sela maa gunla iiŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la di ra la. Ka ií suŋŋi wiizi ú kissiŋ.”

ref: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
text: Ijip hina la jaa ra fɔrgi a nɛra dí ba ɛɛ manaŋ di lii ba hɛri, di ŋɔ, “Di guŋ lɛi, yaa maa daŋ siuzi!”

ref: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
text: Awia, Izrɛl hina kpa ba saŋmittaa n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ di du hɛnni la banna ŋmiraa la biine, di kpa wɛjɛzi fɔɔzaa, di kpaa sagzi ba baŋaazi.

ref: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
text: Izrɛl hina la faa ɛɛ gunla Moosis n ŋɔ ba be la, di suŋŋi a Ijip hina kuna baŋ kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu kuari ani laala.

ref: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
text: Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina wia ra par Ijip hina, ba tɛɛ baa kuna la maa baŋ faa suŋŋɛɛ ba be la, a guŋ gil Izrɛl hina chi Ijip hina daama kaali.

ref: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
text: Nɛra la n faa waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ gba, faa jaa ba ni ba kundɛɛzaa ninɛɛ di ra la.

ref: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
text: Saŋmittaa la baŋ faa chigɛ di lii Ijip hɛri ba la, ba kpaa ɔɔzi paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi ra du a ni la. A saŋmittaa faa waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ a ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, Ijip hina la faa duŋŋi baabuu lii ba hɛri, ba waa kaa dɔɔ saŋa bá daali diwee.

ref: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
text: Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n faa du ba tau a hamuŋa maa guŋŋ di lizi baa lii Ijip hina nonee biini wia. Awia, bina maa biini, gunnɛ Izrɛl hina ge ɔɔ so di ra nyiŋ hamuŋa hiŋ ni guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Gunnɛ ba ni ba naanna ɔɔ ra ɛɛ, di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi saŋaa saŋa maa. Gillikaali widaulaa wia

ref: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, “Gillikaali widaulaarɛ keŋ, hɔɔhri maa gilɛɛ waa diu.

ref: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
text: Ka yom la maa iiŋ yauwɛ, di ii teŋ u hɛŋ daŋ wer diu.

ref: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
text: Hɔɔhri la maa ge n du ii be di ra di paah, gilɛɛ waa diu.

ref: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
text: Ií ɔɔ so diikpaŋ biini di ra diu, di gilɛɛ waa kpa a ol yemmaa di ra lii bossee. Ií gilɛɛ waa ku u hog bɛl maa.

ref: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
text: Ií Izrɛl hina maa daŋ ɔɔ ra di a hɔpizii naa.

ref: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
text: Hɔɔhri la maa n du ii be ka ra nyiŋŋi ú di Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali naa, a hiŋ gil ba teŋri baala la maa n du u dia hɛna. Denii ú jaa wer jaa Gillikaali diire ni alugɔ nɛr la baŋ lullɛ a hɛri. Baal la maa hɛŋ n waa teŋŋe, ú gilɛɛ waa diu.

ref: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
text: A widaulii naa du denii tɛɛ nɛra la baŋ lullɛ a hɛri ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ba be.”

ref: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
text: Izrɛl hina la maa sɛɛ di hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa bagli Moosis ni Aarɔn la.

ref: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
text: A hɔpizii himmaanii Kɔraawiizi lizi Izrɛl hina dizi la maa lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
text: “Kpa biibambilugla maa tɛŋ. Biibaal maa gɛɛ sebal maa baŋ luglɛɛ lul Izrɛl hina biini ɛɛ n hotte.”

ref: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa Keenan, Hitti, Amɔri, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina hɛssi la n summɛ di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la tɛɛ ia, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala la. Denii ii jaa gaa di a hɔpizizeŋ naa baagu naa biini, bina maa.

ref: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ la bɛŋ. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la, ií ɔɔ di a hɔpizizeŋ di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi.

ref: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, ií ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la yiisi n waa hoo a ni. Ií gilɛɛ gil yiisi wàá dugli gɛɛ di wàá du ii hɛri waa yemmaa.

ref: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
text: A hɔpizii hiŋ, bɛ́l maa ŋɔ u biibaal be, ‘N na ɛɛ kenne dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛŋ, saŋa la miŋ lii Ijip hɛri la.’

ref: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
text: Wia naa daŋ ɛɛ alugɔ kuŋ iiŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, di gil ii ra liizi lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg n du ii nuuzi. U kpa u fɔŋŋazenne lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi wa ba ii ni Keenan hɛri, di wa kpau tɛɛ ia gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala la,

ref: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
text: ii daŋ ɔɔ kpa ii biibambilugla tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Sel maa biibal un luglɛɛ lul ɛɛ u hotte.

ref: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
text: Kaweewaa hor, ií ɔɔ kpa pebii charuu, ka di ii wàá ɛɛ guŋ, ií ku u baŋaa. Ií ɔɔ bir yau ii biibambilugla waa, di lɛɛ baa.

ref: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
text: Di ii biibaala ŋmɛnɛ wa pɛɛzi ia lugɔ wii naa zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ? Ií ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kɔraawiizi kpa u fɔŋŋazenne lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri, yaa waa kaa ɛɛ yoma.

ref: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
text: Saŋa la Ijip koori n dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛ lugɔ ú tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ya kaali la, Kɔraawiizi faa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla maanii. Newea ni sela maa. Guŋ wiarɛ yaa ra lizi a biibambilugla di ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di bir turgi yaa biibambilugla maa kima di ra lɛɛ baa la.’

ref: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
text: Wia naa daŋ ɛɛ alugɔ kuŋ iiŋ kpawɛɛ vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, di gil ii ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ labuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri.” Muuzeŋaahmu gii wia

ref: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
text: Saŋa la Ijip koori n wa gillɛ a nɛra lii di ra la la, Kɔraawiizi tɔ ba see ba ra la, ka u faa waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpogli baa ga Filisti hɛri. Haali de ŋmɛnɛɛ n faa duglɛɛ gba. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di nɛra naa haŋ wa chem laal maa ni, aŋhinabe, ba daŋ bir ba nfɛssi, di bir kaali Ijip hɛri.”

ref: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
text: Dikuu guŋ wia Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ba bɛɛ kpa hɛribɔduma ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di ra la Muuzeŋaahmu la. Izrɛl hina faa ɛɛ sirya ni ba laal kuna di lii ra la.

ref: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
text: Moosis faa paa Joosɛf hoga di jaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Joosɛf faa gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina naabaala hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋmɛnɛ hiini ia ii lii bɔnnaa wibii maa. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ií paa n hoga di jaa ra la.”

ref: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
text: Baŋ wa izi bol la banna yir Sukɔf la, ba ga baŋzi ba tantizi yembɛl banna yir Ɛtam n du hɛribɔduma kɛrii la, di chɔɔ de.

ref: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
text: A baama la n du miriti la chiŋ labuu ɔɔ faa tɔ ba see bɔchaaŋ ni hamuŋa maa la, faa du ba benii saŋa maa.

ref: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba bir har di ga chɔɔ dugli bol la banna yir Pi Hahirɔf n du Migdɔl ni muuzeŋ la baambaaŋ, a muuzeŋ kɛrii, di chaŋ Baal Zɛfɔn.

ref: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
text: Ijip koori danna fɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina leuwoo a hɛribɔduma biini, di ra juuri, dikuu a hɛribɔduma n tɔ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ wia.

ref: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
text: N daŋ gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, ú duŋŋi ba luge, ń na girme tɛɛ n hiŋ di lii a koori ni u laallɔɔra maa be. Denii Ijip hina chi zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi himmaa la.” Awia, Izrɛl hina la faa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
text: Saŋa la a koori n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ a nɛra chɔwɔɔrɛ kaali la, u ni u nabɔnzi la kaa bir ba nfɛssi a Izrɛl hina wia, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ yaa ɛɛ gunnɛi? Yaa gillɔɔ ba maa kaali, ba wàá kaa du de di hum di ra tɛɛ yaa!”

ref: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
text: Denii u gil ba ɛɛ u laal torko sirya, di chaali u laallɔɔra jaa.

ref: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa gil Ijip koori digna du kpeg, a guŋ gil u ra dau Izrɛl hina la luge, di Izrɛl hina la ta chɔŋ di ra kaali banni ni, a saŋa.

ref: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
text: A koori ni u laallɔɔra n waa dugli, a Izrɛl hina kɛɛ binni, di na banna ba. Ɔnsii lau baa werge ba bɔra ra sa. Ba lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi lugɔ ú mɔgli baa.

ref: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
text: Ba ŋɔ Moosis be, “Amɔ, Ijip hɛri n waa ŋmama dɔɔwɛ, ba hug nɛra wiarɛ i ba yaa ni hɛribɔduma naa biini ya wa siuzaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ɛɛ yaa gunnɛi?

ref: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
text: Yaa faa waa felee ŋɔ i be Ijip hɛri lugɔ i gil yaa, ya hum di ra tɛɛ Ijip hina laa? Yaa n faa ɛɛ yoma, di hum ra tɛɛ baa la, a guŋ faa bɔ yaa n niŋ siuzi hɛribɔduma naa biini.”

ref: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Ií chi chigigi ka na gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lɛɛ ia zinaa. Ijip hina naa iin nawɛɛ zinaa naa, ii wàá ka na baa maa.

ref: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ yoo tɛɛ ia, ii wiimaanii ii chi bɔɔiih.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii wii ra duŋ gunnɛi? Ŋɔ a nɛra be dí ba izi ra vol.

ref: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
text: Lalli i daŋkpala, di tɛruu guali a muuzeŋ ni, ú chah bɔra anɛɛ, hɛrhilii chɔɔ, á Izrɛl hina wer ga de gi.

ref: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
text: N daŋ gil a Ijip hina digna du kpeg, ba duŋŋi ia zuu de. A koori ni u laallɔɔra ni ba laal torkozi ni baala la n tinni zagra la maanii niŋ duŋŋi ia zuu de. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ na girme.

ref: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
text: Di n wa kpegli Ijip hina, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi himmaa.”

ref: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la n faa tɔ Izrɛl hina laallɔɔra la see la, bir kaali ba harbɔɔ. Baama la n du miriti di la chiŋ la ge lii ba see di kaali ba harbɔɔ.

ref: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
text: A wa chi Ijip hina ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra la baambaaŋ. A hamuŋa maa baama la ɔɔ gil bɔr biri Ijip hina la keŋkere, ka gil bɔr chaani Izrɛl hina la waa keŋkere. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ ba waa dɔŋa duglɛɛ, a hamuŋa maa.

ref: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
text: Denii Moosis lalli u daŋkpala di guali muuzeŋ la ni, Kɔraawiizi gil pekpeg bɛl lii wiifurii a hamuŋa maa, di wa lau a muuzeŋ nii chah bɔra anɛɛ, hɛrhilii chɔɔ.

ref: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
text: Izrɛl hina la ga a muuzeŋ biini hɛrhilii la di kaali, ka a muuzeŋ nii maa faa chi ba nodig ni nomɛɛl alugɔ koŋlaa.

ref: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Kɔraawiizi faa du baama ni niŋ alugɔ dola la biini, ka liŋŋi na Ijip laallɔɔra, di gil ba bugmi.

ref: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
text: U gil ba laal torkozi la naazi nir, a jaa du kpol ban niŋ kaa wer la see. Denii a Ijip hina la ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya gil baa ka bir chɔ kpo! Kɔraawiizii yoowe di ra tɛɛ baa la.”

ref: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kaa lalli i nonii guali a muuzeŋ ni, á nii wa tɔ a Ijip hina maa ni ba zagra ni ba laal torkozi ani banla maa n tinni zagra la ni.”

ref: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
text: Moosis lalli u nonii guali a muuzeŋ ni. Hɔɔ n waa pizi, di u maa bittɔ su gunla uŋ faa suwee la. Ijip hina la faa ra chɔ bá lii, ka Kɔraawiizi bir taa baa di du a muuzeŋ biini.

ref: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
text: Nii la ba wa tɔ Ijip laallɔɔra la n faa ra duŋŋi Izrɛl hina la n zuu muuzeŋ la biini maa ni, ba maa mag de.

ref: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
text: Ka Izrɛl hina la waa faa ga hɛrhilii a muuzeŋ biini, a niiri n faa chigɛ alugɔ koŋlaa ba nodig ni ba nomɛɛl keŋkerezi la di kaali.

ref: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
text: A hɔllɛ Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ Izrɛl hina di lii Ijip hina nonee biini, ba jaa na a Ijip hina n siuzɛɛ di chɔɔgi a muuzeŋ kɛraa maa.

ref: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
text: A saŋa Izrɛl hina n wa na gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagli u fɔŋŋazeŋ Ijip hina ni la, ba jaa ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di yardi u ni u balii Moosis maa.

ref: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
text: Denii Moosis ni a Izrɛl hina yir yir naa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, “N daŋ yir yir tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu uŋ yoo laal lii, di dɔɔ sɔŋ werge wia. U vigzi zagra ni a tinna la maanii ha muuzeŋ la biini.

ref: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
text: Kɔraawiizii n fɔŋŋa, u wiarɛ n na yir yir naa, waabuu ɛɛ n Lɛɛri. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, awia, n daŋ chɔluu, Kɔraawiizi la n mɛɛ n na hum, awia, n danna tɔgzuu werge.

ref: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
text: Kɔraawiizii u sɔŋ, u ɛɛ lugɔ laallɔɔri.

ref: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
text: U vigzi Ijip koori laallɔɔra ni ba laal torkozii ha muuzeŋ la biini. U laal nabɔmkpega la maanii a Muuzeŋaahmu di.

ref: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
text: A niiluŋ la tɔ ba ni, ba maa tuu zɛɛ alugɔ bia.

ref: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i kpa i nodigre, di bagli i fɔŋŋazeŋ. I nodigre i kpa pinti, yaa dɔma maa.

ref: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
text: I fɔŋŋa ni i zennii, i kpa lɔ i dɔma ha. I gillɔɔ i baaŋ haahri baa, ba fuuh alugɔ zɔga.

ref: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
text: I heeza kpegzi wiarɛ a nii chah di izi chi. Di chi alugɔ koŋlii, a niiluŋ la zɛɛ maa jaa bir chɔɔ kpantalaŋ.

ref: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
text: Ba dɔm ta barabara di ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ duŋŋi ba luge di ga lau baa. N daŋ paagi ba daama di bɔnnaa, n daŋ di di piŋ nɛnnɛ. N daŋ pam n tokobi di chɔgi ba maa.’

ref: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
text: Ka hinuu heuzi baa, a muuzeŋ tɔ ba ni. Ba tuu kaali a muuzeŋ zɛɛ alugɔ kpana.

ref: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
text: Vug bɛliirɛ ge du de lugɔ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizɛi? Anɛɛ ba kpa di mɛgziinɛi? I zenni ni i nanni waa dɔŋ dɔɔwɛ. I zenni dɛg ɔmaarɛ, hinuu kaa ra ɛɛ wizenaa.

ref: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
text: Hinuu tɛr i nodig, a hɛri di yaa dɔma.

ref: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
text: Durnya hɛssi nɛra maa daŋ nuua ba bɔraa sa, biinichɔg daŋ lau Filisti hina werge maa.

ref: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
text: Ɔnsii daŋ lau Ɛdɔm hina koora werge maa, bɔsai chol Moab hina sitɔɔra ni, Keenan hɛri nɛra ge bɔra huah,

ref: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
text: ɔnsii werge ni banchullɔi daŋ lau baa. Kɔraawiizi, dikuu i banonii fɔŋŋa wia, ba daŋ chi siriti alugɔ bii guŋŋ, ka i nɛra la hiŋ lɛɛwɛ di lii ba dɔma be la wa kaali.

ref: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
text: Hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ di i kora di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
text: Ijip koori zagra ni laal torkozi ani zagtinna la n waa zuu muuzeŋ la biini la, Kɔraawiizi gil muuzeŋ la nii bir ba, di wa tɔ ba ni, ka Izrɛl hina la waa vol di ga a muuzeŋ biini hɛrhilii di kaali.

ref: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Miriam la n faa ɛɛ Aarɔn niuhambie la kpa kuŋyigzii bɛl, u dɔŋahina haana maa izi di ra hiŋuu, di ge kpogli ba kuŋyigzaa, di yigzi di ra sa.

ref: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
text: Denii Miriam yir yir tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ, “Ií yir yir di chɔli Kɔraawiizi, waabuu dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa. U vigzi zagu maa ni u tinnii ha muuzeŋ biini.” Mara ni Ɛlim niiri wia

ref: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
text: Moosis tɔ Izrɛl hina see, di kpogli baa lii Muuzeŋaahmu la, di kaali Suur Hɛribɔduma la. Ba faa volloo hɔpizaa ahoroo a hɛribɔduma biini, di ba waa nii nawɛɛ bá nyɔɔ.

ref: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
text: Baŋ wa hel yembɛl banna yir Mara, ba faa waa wette bá nyɔɔ de nii, dikuu a nii n faa kpolle wia, guŋ wiarɛ ba ra yir de Mara.

ref: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
text: Awia, a nɛra ra nuumi di ra du Moosis ni, di ra ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ ya nyɔɔi?”

ref: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
text: Denii Moosis lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, u faa bagluu daa bɛl. Moosis faa kpa a daa vigzi nii la biini, a nii bir du sum. Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ baa na de, di du Gbɔgni tɛɛ baa.

ref: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
text: U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di ii ɔɔ keŋŋi digna di ra nuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wiŋɔzi nɛnnɛ, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee n be, di ɔɔ sɛɛ ra nuu n widaulaa, di ra hiŋaa, màá gil wiila la miŋ faa kpawɛɛ ta Ijip hina ni la bɛl maa lau ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la n na chaa ia.”

ref: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
text: Izrɛl hina ni ba dee maa kaa izi Ɛlim di la Sin Hɛribɔduma la n du Ɛlim ni Sinaai baambaaŋ. Baŋ lii Ijip hɛri la, a baagu anɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ hɔllɛ guŋ.

ref: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
text: A hɛribɔduma hiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina maa kaa ra nuumi werge maa di ra du Moosis ni Aarɔn ni.

ref: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
text: Izrɛl hina la ŋɔ ba be, “Di Kɔraawiizi faa kpuuzi yaa Ijip hɛri la, a vii bɔ. Yaa ɔɔ faa sou di bar viini ni ola, di ra di diwii la maa yaa n faa ra nyiŋŋi. Ka ii gil yaa lii de wa du hɛribɔduma naa biini lɔzi ra kpu, ya ni yaa dee maa siuzi.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ ɔɔ gil diwii bɛl lii chiŋ chol lugɔ donii tɛɛ ia. A dɛkkɔɔ nɛr maa ɔɔ lii hɔpizi biimaa di paa gunla maga un niŋ ɔɔ wer di di piŋ, a hɔl hiŋ. Kenne ń ɛɛ baa di na, di ba daŋ sɛɛ di hiŋ n widaulaa gɛɛ ba wàá hiŋɛi.

ref: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
text: Hɔpizaa anumbɛl hɔl la, ba daŋ ɔɔ paa hɔpizaa anɛɛ diwee di daali.”

ref: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn ŋɔ a Izrɛl hina maa be, “Duana naa ni, ii daŋ zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizii lizi ia di lii Ijip hɛri,

ref: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
text: chɔɔzi ge ni, ii daŋ na Kɔraawiizi girme, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ii nuumaa labuu. Yaabuu babɛlaa ii nuumi ra du yaai?”

ref: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií daŋ zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du ii benii, saŋa la un niŋ tɛɛ ia ola ii ra hee duana ni, di kaa tɛɛ ia diwii bɛl iri la maga iinna nyiŋŋi chɔɔzi ni ii di, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ii nuumaazi la maa iiŋ faa nuumɛɛ di ra duu labuu. Yaabuu babɛlaai? Yaa lɛi ii nuumi ra du, Kɔraawiizii ii nuumi ra du.”

ref: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la maa be bá wa chi Kɔraawiizi see, dikuubɛɛwiai, u nuu ba nuumaa labuu.”

ref: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
text: Saŋa la Aarɔn n haa ra ŋɔ a wia Izrɛl hina maa be la, ba ŋɔ ba binni a hɛribɔduma hiŋ, di Kɔraawiizi girmee du baama biini di ra nyɛgzi.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
text: “N nuu Izrɛl hina nuumaarɛ. Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Di bɔr waa lauri siwee, ii daŋ hee ol, chɔɔzi ni ge ii na diwii bɛl di. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”

ref: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
text: A hɔl duana ni zaahra ba di wa su bɔr la baŋ baŋzi ba tantizi la biini maa, chɔɔzi ge ni, ŋmɛnii chol di tɔ de baŋgia bar.

ref: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
text: A ŋmɛnii n wa tunnɛ, ba na kumpɛglɛgzi aŋhina alugɔ nyiŋ hɛga n tɔ a hɛribɔduma hiŋ maa.

ref: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
text: Izrɛl hina n wa naa, ba bir di ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Bɛɛ kunaa gunnɛi?” Dikuu baŋ faa wàá zummɛ wia. Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “A kuna naa ɛɛ diwii bɛl irii Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ iabuu ŋɔ ií ra di.

ref: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ii ɛɛ, ‘Ií bɛl maa la ga paa gunla maga n niŋ heluu, ú dia. Nɛra la n du tanti dia maa biini, a dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa na kookoo tassa suul.’ ”

ref: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
text: Izrɛl hina la ɛɛ gunla maa baŋ bagli baa. Baŋhina paa werge, baŋhina ge paa tama.

ref: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
text: Ka baŋhina faa vɛɛ Moosis nua la, ka gil a yeŋ chi hɔpizi. Hɔɔ n wa pizɛɛ, di a pɔɔhwɔ, di dɔɔ sandule di ra sɔɔhri. A guŋ gil Moosis baaŋ fuu ba ni.

ref: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
text: Chɔɔzi maa, bɛl maa ɔɔ la ga paa gunla maga un niŋ wer di, ka di wiizi wa nyaazɔɔ, anla n kawɛɛ la ɔɔ ŋmɛɛri di zuu hɛri.

ref: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
text: Hɔpizaa anumbɛl hɔl la, bɛl maa ɔɔ paa kookoo tassa suul bunɛɛ. Denii ba nabɔnzi wa ŋɔ a wia tɛɛ Moosis.

ref: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
text: Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi widauliirɛ keŋ, ‘Kɛrɛ daŋ ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii, di ɛɛ hɔpizinanii tɛu. Awia, a dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa ɔɔzi gɛɛ daali kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi. Ka anla waa maa n kawɛɛ, ií gilaa chiŋŋi hɔpizi.’ ”

ref: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií dia zinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Awia, ii wàá naa paa zinaa.

ref: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
text: Hɔpizaa anumbɛl biini, ii daŋ ɔɔ naa di ra paa, ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la n ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii la waa, ii waa ɔɔ na kummaa.”

ref: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
text: Ani a maa, ka baŋhina faa liwɔɔrɛ bá ga paagaa a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la. Baŋ laŋŋɛ ge, ba wàá nawɛɛ.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Moosis, “Ɛrɛɛ ii vɛɛ n widaulaa ni n baglaazi di birgi magɛi?

ref: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
text: Ií ra liizi lugɔ minuu tɛɛ ia Heezaa Hɔpizii naa. Awiarɛ n ɔɔ ra tɛɛ ia hɔpizaa anɛɛ diwee hɔpizaa anumbɛlhiŋ hɔl la. Bɛ́l maa ɔɔ du u dia, di gilɛɛ kaa wàá lii ra nyiŋŋi diwee a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la.”

ref: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
text: Izrɛl hina la faa ra yir a diwiire ‘maana’. A faa huuhzɔɔrɛ alugɔ zule. Di i diu, u ɔɔ du kpir ninɛɛ lugɔ baŋ kpa huuhnuu ɔɔzi kɛrɛkɛssizi.

ref: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ yaa benii dí ya nyiŋŋi a maana naa kookoo tassa chiŋŋi nɛnnɛ. Di yaa naanna wa izoo, ba wer na di zum diwii la iri Kɔraawiizi n faa tɛɛ yaa saŋa la un lizi yaa di lii Ijip hɛri yaa ga du hɛribɔduma la.”

ref: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
text: Moosis jaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, dí u kpa vii jiga bɛl di mɛgzi maana kookoo tassa di du u biini. Di kpau chiŋŋi bɔr la yaa n na jaami Kɔraawiizi la biini, yaa naanna maa wer izi huuzaa.

ref: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
text: Moosis gil Aarɔn ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ u be la. U kpaa di chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, á wer du de di gilɛɛ waa leu.

ref: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
