text: Izrɛl hina la ni ba dee maa lii Sin Hɛribɔduma la, di vol di ra la bɔra gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ bá ra ɛɛ la. Ba faa wa baŋzi ba tantizi yembɛl banna yir Rɛfidim, ka nii faa waa hoo de bá nyɔɔ.

ref: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
text: Awia, ba ra naa Moosis wia, di ra ŋɔ, “Tɛɛ yaa nii yá nyɔɔ.” Denii Moosis bir ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra naannɛi? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra da Kɔraawiizi zɛɛi?”

ref: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
text: Ka niinyɔgzi n faa lau baa werge wia, ba haa vɛɛ ka nuumi ra du Moosis, di ra ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri, í wa kpa niinyɔgzi kpu yaa ni yaa biizi ni yaa sela maa, yá siuzɛi?”

ref: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
text: Denii Moosis lɔ wile werge maa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ n ɛɛ nɛra naa wiai? A ka tama ka ba paagi bia lɔɔziŋ kpu.”

ref: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
text: Kɔraawiizi n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tɔ nɛra la see di ra la. Lizi Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi baŋhina jaa i hiŋ ni, di kpa daŋkpala la hiŋ faa kpawɛɛ lɔ Muu Naal nii la, di ra la.

ref: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
text: N daŋ chi ii see bii bɛl nyuu n du Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ. Di ii wa hel de, kpa i daŋkpala lɔu. Nii daŋ lii nɛra la maa nyɔɔ.” Denii Moosis ɛɛ guŋ Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la maa see.

ref: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
text: U faa dau a bɔr sɔŋ Massa ni Mɛriba, dikuubɛɛwiai, denii Izrɛl hina nuumi di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi na, di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii naa, gɛɛ waa kaa hoo yaa benei?” Izrɛl hina n kpegli Amalɛk hina wia

ref: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
text: Nɛra baŋhina banna yir Amalɛk hina faa ba wa pig Izrɛl hina ni laal, Rɛfidim.

ref: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ baal bɛl banna yir Josua be, “Lizi yaa nɛra baŋhina ií la ga lɔ Amalɛk hina laal. Kɛrɛ, n daŋ tinni giŋgimii naa nyuu chi, di kpa Kɔraawiizi daŋkpala la kpogli.”

ref: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
text: Denii Josua ni Amalɛk hina faa ra lɔ a laal gunla Moosis n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la. Ka Moosis ni Aarɔn ani baal bɛl banna yir Hur faa la ga tinni a giŋgimii nyuu.

ref: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
text: Di Moosis haŋ wa lalli u nonee chiŋ, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ ra kpegli ba dɔma labuu, ka di u wa gillɔ u nonee tuu zɛɛ, Amalɛk hina la ge ɔɔ ra kpegli baa.

ref: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
text: Moosis nonee n wa kuuhwɛ, ba kpa bii dau u so u ni. Aarɔn ni Hur lau u nonee lalli, bɛl chi u nodig bɛl ge chi u nomɛɛl, ú nonee wer chi guŋŋ wiizi wa chol.

ref: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
text: Gunnɛ Josua ɛɛ di wer kpegli Amalɛk hina laallɔɔra la maa.

ref: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Sɛbi kennaa iiŋ wette kpegli ii dɔma naa di dau hɔŋ ni, ií wer di ra liizaa saŋa maa. Gil Josua nuu guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai n daŋ dim Amalɛk hina, nɛr maa wàá ka liizi ba wia maa.”

ref: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
text: Moosis kpa bia sagzi dɔŋa ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr di dau u sɔŋ, “Kɔraawiizii n kpegzi dii tuuta.”

ref: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
text: Moosis faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií lalli Kɔraawiizi kpegzi dii tuuta chiŋ! U daŋ ɔɔ ra yoo Amalɛk hinaa laal saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
text: Jɛtro faa tiloore ŋɔ Moosis be, “Mìŋ́ i hila Jetro ni i haaŋ ni u biibaala banɛɛ la ra bau.”

ref: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
text: Denii Moosis lii ga chem u hila baal hiŋ ni, di togni ka izi faamuu di suuzuu, gunla banna jaami dɔŋa la. Ba maa jaami dɔŋa ka zuu Moosis tanti dia biini.

ref: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
text: Moosis jaa bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n kuu Izrɛl hina wia di ɛɛ Ijip koori ni u nɛra. U kaa ŋɔ ba be tɔɔrɔɔ la maa baŋ faa diwee ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi faa lizi baa a biini.

ref: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
text: Jɛtro kaa ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ n zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii kaali vuga maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ gunnɛ tɔɔri banla n faa ra gbɛlli Izrɛl hina la.”

ref: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
text: Moosis hila Jɛtro n wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u faa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ani mbusuzi lizaa kuna aŋhina tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Aarɔn ni Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa lii ba Moosis ni u hila la be, ba maa kpau di a diwee Kɔraawiizi see. Izrɛl hina seriya diire lizaa wia

ref: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
text: Di i ra ɛɛ guŋ, i ni a nɛra maa daŋ wa gɛrgi. Huma la siili i ninɛɛ. I bɛŋ huŋhunnaa lɛi.

ref: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Moosis so ra kuari a nɛra dɔŋa ni, ba maa chi baruu guŋŋ bɔr wa duani.

ref: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
text: U hila n wa na wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ a nɛra la, u pɛɛzuu, “Beedee wiarɛ i ɛɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra naa, ba ra ba i be kennei? Ɛrɛɛ i bɛŋ ɔɔ so di ra kuari baa dɔŋa ni, ba chi barii lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ di wa hel duanai?”

ref: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
text: Moosis bir ŋɔ u be, “A nɛraa ɔɔ ba n be ŋɔ n bagli baa Kɔraawiizi kipar.

ref: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
text: Di banla maa wa naawɔ, n benii ba ɔɔ ba, n bagli unla hor n summɛ, di kaa bagli baa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni.”

ref: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
text: Moosis hilabaal hiŋ ŋɔ u be, “Gunla hinna ɛɛ la waa wer.

ref: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
text: A nuu n be n birii liize. Di i nuuwɔ tɛŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ du i be. A dɛkkɔɔ i chi a nɛra naa, di kpa ba wia ra ba Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
text: A bagli baa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni, ni ba de dui wia ani wia la ban ninna ɛɛ.

ref: You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of
text: Ka lizi baala baŋhina hiŋ zummɛ baŋ wer wiɛɛlaa, di kaa yardi Kɔraawiizi nɛnnɛ, ba wia dɔɔ wibii, ba waa wikara ra sɛɛ, di gil ba ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa, kalfazi, tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fifi ani fizi sitɔɔra.

ref: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
text: Gil ba ɛɛ a nɛra sitɔɔra saŋa maa, ka gil ba ɔɔ kpa wia la n kpolle werge, baŋ wàá wer kuari waa ba i be, ka anla n waa kpol la waa, ba ɔɔ kuaraa. Guŋ daŋ gil i huma yɔɔ, dikuu i ni baa n bɔnnaa wia.

ref: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
text: Di i ɛɛ kennaa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ i ɛɛ naa, a wàá kaa ra nuui, ka a nɛra maa ɔɔ bir kaali diini ni bɔsɔna.”

ref: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
text: Denii u lizi baala la n wer wiɛɛlaa lii Izrɛl hina maa biini, bá ɛɛ ba nabɔnzi di ra binni nɛra kagboŋa, kalfazi, tokkoanɛɛgaa ni fifi ani fizi ni.

ref: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
text: Denii Moosis jaa ta u hila Jɛtro ŋmɛnɛɛ, u bir kaali u hɛri.

ref: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
text: Moosis tinni a bizeŋ nyuu Kɔraawiizi be. Denii Kɔraawiizi yiruu di ŋɔ u be lugɔ u ŋɔ keŋ tɛɛ Jekɔb naanna Izrɛl hina,

ref: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
text: “Ií na gunla maa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tɔɔri Ijip hina ka kpa n fɔŋŋazeŋ kpa ia alugɔ chig n ɔɔ kpa u biizi zaah la, di wa tɛɛ n hiŋ.

ref: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
text: Di ii daŋ sɛɛ di ra hiŋ n nua nɛnnɛ, di lau n ni ia nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la nɛnnɛ, ii daŋ ɛɛ n nɛnɔŋŋaa. Durnya nɛra maa n ɛɛ n horaa, ka iabuu n lizi.

ref: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
text: Iawaa daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehina di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa. Wia naabuu í ŋɔ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.”

ref: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
text: Denii Moosis lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu la ga chaali a nɛra nabɔnzi maa, di ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la di tɛɛ baa.

ref: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
text: Ba maa kpau sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ.” Denii Moosis bir kpa ba loobii hiŋ di ga tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “N daŋ du baamatɔg biini ba i be, á nɛra ɔɔ nuu minna ŋɔ wia ra tɛi, bá yardii saŋaa saŋa maa.” Denii Moosis la ga ŋɔ a nɛra be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “La ga sɔ a nɛra di lizi ba doŋa ha, ka bá ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, zinaa ni kɛrɛ. Gil ba chag ba kuna,

ref: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
text: di ɛɛ sirya ra kpaŋ hɔbil, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔllɛ ń tuu Bizeŋ Sinaai la nyuu ba maa naŋ.

ref: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
text: Pii maga bar a bizeŋ tɛɛ a nɛra, ka ŋɔ ba be dí ba ra dazi di gilɛɛ waa tinnuu gɛɛ di waa gbɔgzuu. Di bɛl maa haŋ wa vɛɛ ka ɛɛ guŋ, bá kpuu.

ref: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
text: Biarɛ ii paa lɔɔzuu gɛɛ hobeere ii virguu kpu. Nɛr maa nonii gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi a hindee. Di nɛruu gɛɛ selle, ií gilɛɛ giluu u du de di ra nyiŋ. Ka di ba wa nuu nyigaa wiraa guŋŋ, a guŋ saŋaa ba jaa wer tinni a bizeŋ nyuu.”

ref: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
text: Moosis n wa lii a bizeŋ nyuu tuu la a nɛra be la, u gil ba sɔ ba doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. Ka ba jaa chag ba kuna.

ref: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
text: Denii u ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Bɛl maa ɛɛ sirya nɛnnɛ di ra kpaŋ a hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ la. Baal maa ni haaŋ gilɛɛ waa chɔɔ.”

ref: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
text: A hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ la chɔɔzi ni dooŋ ra pogzi di ra nyɛgzi werge maa. Denii baamatɔg wa guali a bizeŋ ni, ka ba nuu bensunoniina n wiiwe werge, ɔnsii lau baa, ba bɔra ra sa yogyogyog.

ref: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
text: Denii Moosis jaa tɔ ba see di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la, bá ga chem Kɔraawiizi ni, ba ga chi a bizeŋ zɛɛ.

ref: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
text: A bizeŋ nyuu maa faa tɔ nyɔɔzi guŋ kuull, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi du niŋ biinii di tuu u ni. A nyɔɔzi bir di ra tinni chiŋ kuull lugɔ ninzeŋ nyɔɔzi. A bizeŋ zigli werge maa guŋ gbigbigbi.

ref: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
text: Ba nuu a bensunoniina wiraa n kaa ra nyaŋŋi werge maa. Denii Moosis ŋɔ wia, Kɔraawiizi sɛɛ alugɔ dooŋ n pozee.

ref: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
text: Kɔraawiizi tuu ba a Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu di wa yir Moosis, dí u tinni ba, u tinni.

ref: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Tuu la ga karfi a nɛra dí ba ra dazi, di gilɛɛ waa fir ba naŋ. Di ba wa vɛɛwɔ ka ɛɛ guŋ, ba kpila maa daŋ siuzi.

ref: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
text: Kizeehina la gba n na ba n be la, dɛkkɔɔ bá sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ tɛr ba digna.”

ref: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
text: Moosis bir ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “Nɛr maa wàá wer tinni a bizeŋ nyuu, dikuu i himmaa n karfi yaa lugɔ ya pii maga bar a bizeŋ di gil u ɛɛ i bɛŋ hor, di ɛɛ naniinanii wia.”

ref: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ u be, “Bir tuu la ga kpogli Aarɔn, i nuu maa tinni ba. Ka a kizeehina ni a nɛra waa gilɛɛ waa fir, bá tinni ba n be, di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ tɛr ba digna.”

ref: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
text: Denii Moosis tuu la ga ŋɔ a nɛra be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: God said to the people of Israel:
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ,

ref: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
text: A nɛra faa haa chi a bɔɔnɛɛ, ka Moosis ga dugli bɔbiri limpiriŋ la biini Kɔraawiizi n faa duwɛɛ la.

ref: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
text: “Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lɛɛ ia lii Ijip hɛri, saŋa la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma de la.

ref: Do not worship any god except me.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá dɔɔ vuga maa di ra jaa n ni.

ref: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa ú li kuŋ n du chiŋ gɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ nii biini di ra tɛɛ iihinaa.

ref: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
text: ka nɔŋŋi jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la maa n nɔŋŋiŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni la.

ref: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kpogli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sɔŋ di ra dua. N daŋ tɛr nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ guŋ digni.

ref: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra di Heezaa Hɔpizii la, di gil ú ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinanii ii be.

ref: You have six days when you can do your work,
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di ra hum ii huma maa,

ref: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
text: ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lawaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ ii ni ii biizi, ii balaa, ii sela ani hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola ra hum huma a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
text: Mìŋ́ ii Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ta chiŋ, hɛri, muuzeŋ ani kuna la maa n du a biine, ka heezi hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, di kissuu, di gil u ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinanii.

ref: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
text: A kpa i mɛɛ ni i maa girme, gunnɛ í wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n na tɛɛ ia naa biini.

ref: Do not murder.
text: Gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛr.

ref: Be faithful in marriage.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm.

ref: Do not steal.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ.

ref: Do not tell lies about others.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá kanni kara di ra chug i dɔŋhiŋ.

ref: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
text: Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ dia ni. Gilɛɛ wàá kɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ gɛɛ u balii gɛɛ u sel gɛɛ u kuna maa ni.”

ref: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa di ra jaa n ni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa saliŋhuŋŋu ni saliŋ di kuari vuga tɛɛ iihinaa.

ref: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
text: A nɛra n wa nuu dooŋ la pogzaa, di na u nyɛgzaa, di nuu a bensunoniina la ge wiraa, di kaa na bizeŋ la maa n na lii nyɔɔzi la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa ba bɔra ra sa. Ba chi bɔɔnɛɛ,

ref: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
text: ka ŋɔ Moosis be, “Í himmaa ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ yaa, yá ra nuu. Gilɛɛ gil Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ yaa. Di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ siuzi.”

ref: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
text: Denii Moosis bir ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Kɔraawiizi ballɔɔ ú wa ɛɛ ia na, guŋ gil ii ra ɔmuu di ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ, ka gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa.”

ref: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ u ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Ii himmaa nuuwɔɔ miŋ ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia di lii chiŋ.

ref: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
text: Ií kpa hɛɛhraa di ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛŋ, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa la de. Ií ɔɔ kpa ii peeza ni buuna ani nauna di ra ɛɛ guŋ. Bɔr la maa min niŋ lizi di ŋɔ ii ra tɔgzi n sɔŋ, n daŋ ba ii be di wa kissi ia de.

ref: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
text: Di ii wa ŋɔ ii kpa bia di sagzi dɔŋa ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr tɛŋ, ií gilɛɛ waa sɛɛhzaa. Di ii vɛɛwɔ ka kpa kuŋ sɛɛhzaa, ii daŋ doŋuu.

ref: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá ga keeriilɔŋa ni di tinni ra la n mbusu lizibɔr. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ ba daŋ na ii chakpalli.”

ref: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
text: Di nɛr la maa wa lɔ u maa gɛɛ u mɛɛ, bá kpuu.

ref: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
text: Di nɛra banɛɛ ra naa, bɛl kpa bii gɛɛ noguruŋ di lɔ u dɔŋ di duu wiila ka waa siuwɛ, ka chɔɔ waa kaa wer ra lii baŋgia,

ref: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Kpa Gbɔgni naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.” Yoma Gbɔgni wia

ref: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
text: “Di i bɛl maa wa yau Hibru hinuu, u daŋ humii binni anumbɛl. Ka di aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la wa hello, gil u dɔɔ u hiŋ di lii, gilɛɛ gil u turgi kummaa tɛi.

ref: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
text: Di u bɛnnɛ ballɛ, u bɛnnɛ niŋ kaa kaali. Ka di u ni u haannɛ ballɛ, u nuubuu niŋ kaali.

ref: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
text: Di u dɔɔri tɛu haaŋ u lul biibaala gɛɛ biihaana, a baal bɛnnɛ niŋ kaali. U haaŋ ni u biizi la waa, ɛɛ u dɔɔri horaa.

ref: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
text: Ka di a yom wa ŋɔ lugɔ u nɔŋŋi u dɔɔri ni u haaŋ ni biizi hinnɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ú du ba be,

ref: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
text: a dɛkkɔɔ u dɔɔri hiŋ kpogluu la nabɔnzi see, di ga lau u digni pɛli gbera gɛɛ u daa ni di kpa hɛm furuu, ú jaa ɛɛ u yom di hanna la.

ref: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
text: Di baal yoo u biihaaŋ tɛɛ nɛr, waabuu wàá wer dɔɔ u hiŋ alugɔ yombaal.

ref: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
text: Ka di u wia waa u dɔɔri la n yawuu, ú kpa ɛɛ haaŋ la ra par, ú gil u mɛɛ bir yawuu. Ka ú gilɛɛ wa yoou di ra tɛɛ hɔɔhra, dikuu uŋ wɔɔ ɛɛwɛ nɛnnɛ wia.

ref: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
text: Di unla maa wa yau biihaaŋ di tɛɛ u biibaal u ɛɛ u haaŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ uŋ kpogluu lugɔ u himmaa biihaaŋ.

ref: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
text: Di u kaa wa kpa hahnɛɛhiŋ, u gilɛɛ waa kpolli u hahlugli la diwee ni laala gunla uŋ faa ra tɛu la, di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nuu chɔɔi.

ref: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
text: Di wɔɔ wàá tɛɛ kuna ahoro naa bɛl maa, amɔ, ú tau ŋmɛnɛɛ ú ra la, di gilɛɛ waa lɛɛu kummaa.” Nɛr pira dui ni kpui Gbɔgni wia

ref: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
text: Ka di waa kuttɛɛ lɛi ɛɛ guŋ, ú chɔ la ga zuu bɔr la min niŋ lizi ii ra lɛɛ iihinaa de la.

ref: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
text: Di nɛr kuttɔɔ kpu u dɔŋhiŋ, ií kpu u ge gba. Haali di u chɔwɔɔ ga lau Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la gba, ka ii lawuu lii de, di kpuu.

ref: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
text: Di nɛr la maa wa fittɔ lau nɛr yoo, gɛɛ di ba wa nau u be, bá kpu a hiŋ.

ref: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
text: Nɛr la maa n na see u mɛɛ gɛɛ u maa nua, bá kpuu.

ref: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
text: di unla baŋ lɔwɛɛ la wa wetto kpa daŋkpala di ra lii bossee, ba wàá ɛɛ unla n lɔu la wiimaa. Ka a dɛkkɔɔ u turgi u saŋa la uŋ chɔkkɛ la maa kim tɛu, ka ra du u tau u wa nyaagi nɛnnɛ.

ref: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
text: Di nɛr wa kpa daa di lɔɔzi u yombaal gɛɛ u yoŋhaaŋ, u siu a biini, a dɛkkɔɔ ba tɛr u digni.

ref: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
text: Ka di u wa izoo hɔpizi kpaŋ gɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ biini, ba gilɛɛ waa tɛr u digni, dikuubɛɛwiai, u kundɔɔliirɛ.

ref: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
text: Di baala waa naa, di ga magzi haaŋ n kpogli hia ú lul, di u lulaa haa waa helle, ka waa piree werge, gunla n par u jaari ani gunla nabɔnzi n sɛɛwɛ, gunnɛ unla n piruu la turgi.

ref: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
text: Ka di a haaŋ piroo werge waa, di wa siu, bá kpu a baal ge,

ref: burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
text: Di ninne u kpa baaruu u boŋŋi, gɛɛ u lɔubuu u yembɛl yigli chal, ba ɛɛ u ge gba guŋ.

ref: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
text: Di nɛr lɔ u yombaal gɛɛ u yoŋhaaŋ siwii chɔgi, a dɛkkɔɔ u gil u jaa dɔɔ u hiŋ, u siwii chɔgaa hiŋ turgi u kinnɛ.

ref: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
text: Di u nyiŋ genii u lɔ foŋ, u gil u jaa dɔɔ u hiŋ, a turgi u kim.

ref: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
text: Di nɛbɛl nabal wa gbuuri baal gɛɛ haaŋ u siu, a dɛkkɔɔ ba paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu, ka gilɛɛ waa hee a nau ol. Ka a waa dɛkkɛ baŋ tɛr a nau hiŋ digni.

ref: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
text: Ka di a nau hiŋ zummɔ lugɔ a nau ɛɛ nakpaaliirɛ, ba ŋɔ u be, ka wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ du lig, ka u kaa wa kpu baal gɛɛ haaŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ba paagi bia lɔɔzi a nau ni u dɔɔri hiŋ maa kpu.

ref: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
text: Ka di ba wa tɛu kim maa ŋɔ u turgi, u daŋ wer turgi a kim ka dɔɔ u miibɔɔ.

ref: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
text: Di a sel wa kpu biibaal gɛɛ biihaaŋ guŋ himmaanii ba ɛɛu.

ref: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
text: Di nɛr wa pilli bɔɔ gɛɛ di u ki bɔɔrɛ ka wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ, nabal gɛɛ kawee wa chol u biini di siu,

ref: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
text: u daŋ turgi a sel kim tɛɛ u hiŋ, ka kpa a sesiwii.

ref: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
text: Di nɛbɛl nabal boŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ hor ú siu, ba yoo u nyinii la di bɔnni u kebee a mɛgzi, di kaa bɔnni u siwii la ge ol, ba maa di mɛgzi.

ref: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
text: Ka di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ bɛl ɛɛ nagbuuriirɛ, nɛr maa zum, ka u dɔɔri wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ, ka guŋ wa ɛɛ, u daŋ nyiŋŋi u nyinii di turgi u siwii la kim tɛɛ u hiŋ, ka kpau.”

ref: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di nɛr la maa wa ŋmɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ nabal gɛɛ peezi di kpu gɛɛ di yoo, ú turgi nauna anue di du a nabal bɔɔ, di turgi peeza anaazu di du a peezi ge bɔɔ.

ref: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
text: Di nɛr maa wa nɔɔni u sela a gaa di u koo gɛɛ u grepu daazi koo, ka a sela leu di ga zuu nɛbɛl koo di di u kuna, a dɛkkɔɔ u kpa u koo kuna di turgi a kim.

ref: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
text: Di nɛr maa gaa fuuh u koo kɔlaa gɛɛ kooree, a niŋ loŋŋi ga fuuh u dɔŋhiŋ mia la uŋ kummɛ di chaalaa dau gɛɛ anla n haa chigɛ gɛɛ u koo maa, a dɛkkɔɔ unla n du a niŋ la turgi a kim.

ref: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
text: Di nɛr kpa kebee gɛɛ u kunnanaa tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ u dau, nɛbɛl wa ŋmɛɛa ba lawuu, u daŋ turgi a kuna guŋ dɔŋ bunɛɛ.

ref: But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
text: Ka di ba wɔɔ lauwɛ waa, ba lau unla n dawaa la di la nabɔnzi see. Ba ga na di waabuu ŋmɛɛa gɛɛ di waalɛiyɛi?

ref: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
text: Di nɛra waa gbirgi dɔŋa nuuzi dikuu kuna wia, di naballɛ gɛɛ kaweere gɛɛ peezii gɛɛ laalaa gɛɛ kunla maa n leuwene, ba maa kpa a wia la nabɔnzi see, bá ga ŋɔa. Di a wa chol unla maa ni, ú nyiŋŋi a kundee dɔŋ anɛɛ di turgi u dɔŋhiŋ la.

ref: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
text: Di nɛr wa kpa u kawee gɛɛ u nabal gɛɛ u peezi gɛɛ u sel maa di tɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ ŋɔ ú ra binni, u wa siu gɛɛ ba wa boŋŋuu gɛɛ ba wa ŋmɛɛu nɛra harbɔɔ,

ref: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
text: ba kpa a wia di ba Kɔraawiizi see. Unla n na binnaa la wa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi see alugɔ waa lɛi ŋmɛɛu. A dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ a kuŋ hiŋ sɛɛ lugɔ wibiire di gilɛɛ gil ú turgi kummaa.

ref: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
text: Ka di ba ŋmɛɛ a selle di lii u be, a dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ unla n na binni a sel la turgi u kim tɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
text: Di sechɔgii bɛllɛ lawuu di di ka ka, a dɛkkɔɔ u binni la paa u bɔr la n kawɛɛ la, di wa bagli lugɔ wibiire. Di u wetto ɛɛ guŋ, wàá kaa dɔɔ kim un niŋ turgi.

ref: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
text: Di nɛr kim u dɔŋhiŋ sel, ba wa boŋŋuu gɛɛ di u siuwɔɔ, di a sel hiŋ la himmaa waa hoo de, di na lugɔ wibiire, ú kinni la daŋ turgi u kim.

ref: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
text: Ka di a sel hiŋ du denii ka guŋ ɛɛ, nɛr la n kimuu la waa kim maa dɔɔwɛ un niŋ turgi. Di u faa dau kebeere ka lɛɛ a sel, aabuu u kpa turgi u kim.” Gbɔgni la n kaa jaa wia

ref: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
text: “Di baal maa wa lau biihaaŋ la n haa waa baal la un niŋ yuu dɔɔwɛ di nyiŋŋi, ú kuari u wia ka u jaa ɛɛ u haaŋ.

ref: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
text: Di a biihaaŋ mɛɛ waa ba yuuri hiŋ sɛɛwɛ, ka a baal daŋ haa turgi kuna la maa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú turgi dikuu uŋ chɔguu la wia.

ref: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
text: Haaŋ la maa n na vug, bá kpuu.

ref: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
text: Di nɛr maa wa lau sel nyiŋŋi, bá kpuu.

ref: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
text: Nɛr la maa n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ka ra kuari vuga, bá kpuu.

ref: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni hɔɔhra di ra ɛɛ baa wichɔgaa. Ií gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri.

ref: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni luhaaŋ gɛɛ lalbie maa.

ref: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
text: Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, ba wii duŋ, n daŋ nuu ba wiraa. Wibii maa n daŋ hiini baa.

ref: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
text: N baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ń kpuuzi ia laal biini, ka ii haana ni biizi birgi luhaana ni lalbiizi.

ref: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
text: Di n nɛra la bɛl maa wa nyaawɔ di kim kebii u dɔŋ be, u gilɛɛ ɛɛ lugɔ kebikinni di wàá saguu nii.

ref: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
text: Di i lɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ wɛjɛ dau talma, ɛɛ ania ka bir kpau ga tɛu ka wiizi chol,

ref: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, u bɛnnɛ u wɛjɛ. Bɛɛ u kaa dɔɔ ú kpa tɔ di chɔɔi. Di a waa nuu, u wii duŋ, n daŋ nuu u wiraa, dikuu minna suŋ nɛra ni wia.

ref: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
text: Gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi gɛɛ di ra see nɛr la n ɛɛ i hɛri nabɔma nua.

ref: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
text: Bɛl maa ɔɔ lizi mia, siŋ ani ɔlivi nuu di ra sunziŋ, di gilɛɛ waa kpolliŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa ɔɔ kpa u biibambilugli tɛŋ.

ref: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
text: Gunnɛ bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ɛɛ u nauna ni peeza biilugla. Ka u ɔɔ gil a du a maawaa be di wa hel hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ lawaa, ú kpau tɛŋ.

ref: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
text: Ii ɛɛ n nɛra la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hinnɛ. Awia, ii gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa u dɔŋa n diwee ka ka. Ií ɔɔ kpaa tɛɛ nuuzihina.”

ref: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá hiŋ nɛkpila di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Di i waa ŋɔ wia seriya diiribɔr, gilɛɛ waa jaa nɛkpila ni di lau wia birgi, a chɔgi wibii dii.

ref: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
text: Di nyaari wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, gilɛɛ wa lɛɛ ra jaa u ni seriya diiri bɔr.

ref: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
text: Di i wa na i dɔm navarga gɛɛ kawee n leuwe, ɛɛ ania ka lawuu ga tɛu.

ref: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
text: Di i na i haahri kawee n chigɛ buntɔga a nyaŋŋuu u chol, gilɛɛ giluu de, aah siwii di hiinuu.

ref: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
text: Di nyaara wa la wia ni nabɔnzi see, gilɛɛ waa kpolli baa wibii.

ref: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
text: Gilɛɛ waa jaa karkanna ni. Gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛnanii la n waa wichɔgaa biini jaawɛ gɛɛ wibii hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ kpa bilchɔg tɛɛ a guŋ hiŋ.

ref: Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
text: Gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ sunzaa la n niŋ gil i siwee tɔɔgi, i di wibii huhzi.

ref: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni hɔɔhri. Ií zum gunla hɔɔhrinaa n duwɛɛnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ge gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri.” Heezaa Hɔpizii Gbɔgni wia

ref: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
text: “Ií kpa binni anumbɛl di ra duu kuna ii kooni di ra kumaa bina maa.

ref: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
text: Ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, ii gilɛɛ waa par a hɛri gɛɛ di waa duu kummaa de. Di diutɛɛri wa lii a hɛri, a ɛɛ nyaara ge horaa. Di ba ge wa gil a yemmaa, pir sela genii dɔɔa a di. Guŋ himmaanii ií ɛɛ ii grepuzi ni ɔlivizi kooni.

ref: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di hum ii huma, ka aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la waa, ií ɔɔ heezi. Guŋ gil ii yoma baŋ lul ii diini ni hɔɔhra la n du ii be di ra hum ia, ni ii navargazi ni u kauzi maa gba wer heezi.

ref: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
text: Ií ra du tau di ra ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia la. Ií gilɛɛ waa yir vug maa sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzuu, di gilɛɛ gil ba ra nuu a sɔna ii nuuzi gba.” Hɔpizizenaa Ahoro Dii wia

ref: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kunla maa n dɔɔ yiisi di ra jaa sel maa ni, di lizi mbusu ra tɛŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil sel la iiŋ kpawɛɛ lizi mbusu tɛŋ la nuu wàá chi hɔɔ ra pizi.

ref: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
text: Ií haana hizi ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá lii gɛɛ bɛl maa ge wàá ɛɛ hahbara ii hɛri biini. N daŋ tɛɛ ia miibɔɔjaŋ ge jaa.

ref: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
text: Ií ɔɔ di Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ di ii waa faari a kumaa. Ií ɔɔ di Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ bina maa tuna, di ii wa chaali ii kooni kuna di ba bol.

ref: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
text: Bina maa diuzenaa dii buhoro naa biini, a dɛkkɔɔ baal maa ɔɔ ba di wa jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.

ref: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
text: “Ií ɔɔ di hɔpizizenaa buhoro bina maa biini di ra chɔliŋ.

ref: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
text: Ií ɔɔ di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛrɛ ií ɔɔ hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ gunla miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ií ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ baagu la banna yir Abib la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u biinii ii kpa di lii Ijip hɛri la. Nɛ́r maa gilɛɛ waa ba n be ni u nodumazi.

ref: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
text: Bina maa, ií ɔɔ lizi ii pattikuna lugli horpazi di ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia. Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ wa kpa buuŋ ilanii di ra daali u bie.” Kɔraawiizi mɛlika n niŋ ɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ sirya wia

ref: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
text: “Ií ra nuu, n na hum mɛlikaa ú tɔ ii see di kpogli ia, di ga hel bɔr la miŋ kuarɛɛ dau ia la.

ref: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
text: Ií keŋŋi digna di ra nuu u be, di ra hiŋ gunla maa un niŋ bagli ia. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nua. Di ii wa vɛɛwɔ, wàá gil tɛɛ ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, n tɛubuu fɔŋŋa.

ref: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
text: N mɛlika daŋ tɔ ii see di hiini ia ii ga zuu nɛra la banna yir Amɔri, Hitti, Pɛriz, Keenan, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina la hɛssi. N daŋ dim ba maa.

ref: Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ ba vuga dɔɔra gɛɛ di ra kuaraa gɛɛ di waa hiŋ ba wiɛɛlaa. Ií purgi ba vuga ni bia la baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛa la burburbur.

ref: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛŋ. Di ii ra ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ ɔɔ kissi ia, ii dɔɔ diwee ni nii, di lizi wiila maa ii ni.

ref: I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you.
text: N daŋ ɔɔ gil ɔnsii werge feli lau hɛri la maa hina ii ni baa n niŋ naa, ba bɔra ra sa, ba bugmi. N daŋ gil ii dɔma ɔɔ bir chɔ.

ref: I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach.
text: N daŋ gil chirinchaazi tɔ ii see di ga duŋŋi Hivi, Keenan ani Hitti hina ii ŋmɛnɛɛ chaani.

ref: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
text: Ka màá duŋŋi baa biŋkpaŋ biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɛri daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ, pir sela ge wazi werge tɛɛ ia.

ref: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
text: N danna duŋŋi baa tama tama guŋŋ, di ra la saŋa la iin niŋ wazi di wer dɔɔ a hɛri la.

ref: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
text: N daŋ gil ii hɛri magbɔɔni ga Muuzeŋaahmu la ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, di kaa lii hɛribɔduma di ga chug Muu Yufretis la. N daŋ kpa nɛra la n du a hɛri du ii nonee ií duŋŋi baa.

ref: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni baa ni ba vuga dɔɔ nuukpaŋ.

ref: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ba so ii hɛri, di guŋ lɛi ba daŋ gil ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu n ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba vuga kuaraa daŋ birgi lugɔ sidɛɛzi di lauri ia.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Í ni Aarɔn ni u biibaal Nada, Abihu ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi tinni ba n be bizeŋ la nyuu. Di ii waa ba, ii chi bɔɔnɛɛ, ka jaamiŋ.

ref: but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
text: Ka hìŋ́ Moosis bɛnnɛ niŋ hel n be. I dɔŋahina lawaa, gilɛɛ wàá dugliŋ. A nɛra waa gba gilɛɛ waa tinni a bizeŋ.”

ref: Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!”
text: Moosis n ga ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii ni u Gbɔgni la maa wia tɛɛ a nɛra, ba maa kpau sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.”

ref: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Moosis jaa sɛbi wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la di dau. Denii u izi chɔɔzimpikke ni di kuari mbusu lizibɔr a bizeŋ zɛɛ, di kpa bia fidaanɛɛ ge baŋzi, bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la.

ref: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
text: Denii u gil Izrɛl hina biipɔllaa la ga lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa, di kpu naballi di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
text: Moosis bargi a challi bɔra anɛɛ, di kpa bɔkpaŋ du tassazi biini, ka kpa anla n kawɛɛ di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la.

ref: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
text: Denii u kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Hɔŋ la di karmuu tɛɛ a nɛra. Ba sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua di ɛɛ wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.”

ref: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
text: Denii Moosis kpa a chal la n du a tassazi biini la di mizi baa ka ŋɔ, “Chal la n kuari ii ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ labuu keŋ, dikuu u wiŋɔɔlaa la wia.”

ref: Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the
text: Moosis, Aarɔn, Nadab, Abihu ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi la faa tinni a bizeŋ,

ref: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
text: di ga na Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la. Kumbɛl ɛɛ lugɔ binanii bɛl banna yir safaaya la du u naazi zɛɛ di chaani lugɔ chiŋ.

ref: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa a Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi hiŋ tɔɔrɛɛ. Ba faa na Kɔraawiizii ka piri. Awia, ba di ka nyɔɔ.

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Tinni ba n be a bizeŋ naa nyubaaŋ di wa du ɛŋ ń kpa n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa la miŋ sɛbɛɛ dau bipɛntɛnzi ni di tɛi, í gaa bagli a nɛra.”

ref: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
text: Denii Moosis ni u balii Josua ra la, Moosis waa ga tinni a Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ nyubaaŋ.

ref: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
text: Moosis faa ŋɔ a nabɔnzi be, “Ií du bɔnnaa di ra kpaŋ yaa, ya wa bir ba ii be. Aarɔn ni Hur du ii benii. Di bɛl maa wa dɔɔ wii, ú kpa ba ba be.”

ref: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
text: Moosis n wa tinni a bizeŋ la nyubaaŋ, baama wa tɔ de maa.

ref: and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud.
text: Kɔraawiizi girme ba di wa tɔ Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu di ra chaani guŋŋ hɔpizaa anumbɛl. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la, Kɔraawiizi yir Moosis di lii a baama biini.

ref: Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ ba lizi kuna di wa tɛŋ. I daŋ lɛɛ kunla bɛl maa bampirii n tɛu lugɔ ú kpa ba wa tɛŋ.

ref: Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze;
text: Kuna naabuu í lɛɛ di lii ba be. Saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ,

ref: tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood;
text: pebala hɔna la baŋ liiwe a aah, hɔŋbuglaa, akeesia daazi,

ref: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests;
text: fintina nuuri, kunsɔɔhrisuma ban niŋ kpa di kuari nuuwaarii, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la banna fuuh,

ref: and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece.
text: binanaa banna yir ɔnigs ani anla n kawɛɛ ba kpa margi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma tagtakpurii ni u bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni.

ref: I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people.
text: Gil ba kuari Tanti Diinanii tɛŋ ń wa du ba be de.

ref: The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand.
text: Kuari katooljigzi aniidaanɛɛ di hɔŋzi u ni, á ra chaani bɔr la uŋ chigɛ la see.

ref: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
text: Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ himmaa di tɔ u biini ni u har maa di kpa saliŋ bar u nua.

ref: Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
text: Luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu di kpa bɛl maa, dí du u naazi anaazu la bɛl maa ni, anɛɛ du keŋkere bɛl, anɛɛ ge du keŋkere bɛl.

ref: Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold
text: Kpa akeesia daa di kuari daajaŋra di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a maa ni.

ref: and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles.
text: Kpaa di suuzi gbittizi la bɔɔni, bá ɔɔ wer lawaa di ra kpa a dakka.

ref: Don't ever remove the poles from the rings.
text: Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa lizi a daazi.

ref: Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest.
text: Luu a chɛrub bɛl u chi a dakka tua kɛrii bɛl, di kaa luu bɛl ge ú chi u kɛrii bɛl ge. Kpa saliŋ luu a ni a tua la maa á ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: The creatures must face each other with their wings spread over the chest.
text: Gil a chɛrubzi siwee chaŋ dɔŋa di ra binni a tua, a keeri ge yaa di guali u ni.

ref: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
text: Kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la, min niŋ wa kpa tɛi la di du a Dakka biini, di kpa u nua tua di tɔ.

ref: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
text: N daŋ chem i ni bɔr la chɛrubzi la n chigɛ n ni n nɛra Nuukpaŋ Daansɛɛ Dakka ni la baambaaŋ. Di kpa n Gbɔgni maa tɛi, í ga tɛɛ Izrɛl hina. Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia Tɛɛbul la wia

ref: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
text: Kaa kuari gir bar u kɛraa, ú ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ sag u ni.

ref: Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs
text: Luu saliŋ gbittizi anaazu, di kpa bɛl maa mari ú siraa anaazu la, u naazi n duwɛɛ la ni.

ref: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
text: Gil a daajaŋra ge gba ɛɛ akeesia daazi, di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a maa ni.

ref: The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table. The Lampstand (Exodus
text: I daŋ kpa paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛŋ la di sag a tɛɛbul ni n see, saŋa maa. Fintina daa la wia

ref: Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold
text: Kpa saliŋ himmaa luu fintina daa ni u zɛɛ, di kuari u nuuri duuribɔra la a du lugɔ fiiri n punzee, a ni a daa maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: with three branches on each of its two sides.
text: Ú dɔɔ kela anumbɛl, ahoro du ú keŋkere maa.

ref: There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch
text: Kela anumbɛl la bɛl maa daŋ dɔɔ nuuri duuribɔra ahoro lugɔ daa bɛl banna yir almɔn fiiri ni a pume.

ref: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
text: Saliŋ himmaanii bá kpa di luu a fintina daa ni u kela ani fiiri la maa n du u ni la, á maa ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold.
text: Kuna la ban niŋ kpa di ra mɔnni fintina yakɔssi ni a pɛrɛtujigzi daŋ ɛɛ saliŋ himmaa.

ref: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
text: A du tau nɛnnɛ ka kuari a kuna gunla himmaa miŋ faa baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.”

ref: For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
text: Kpa gessi la n ɛɛ peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa, di suah patiisazi, di gil ba tɔɔhzaa, di kpa tɔ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua.

ref: As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth
text: A dɛkkɔɔ a maa mɛgzi, bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ, u wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi anaazu.

ref: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Gil ba kpa gessihuŋŋunanaa la baŋ ŋmɛɛnɛɛ nɛnnɛ ni gessi la baŋ liiwe aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, zagbiiŋ nii ani u aahmu choihchoih, di suah patiisazi fi, di gil nɛr la n zum nyɛraa nɛnnɛ, tɔɔhzi chɛrubzi di du a ni.

ref: and sew them together into two panels with five sections each.
text: Gil ba kpa anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kaa kpa anue la ge n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent.
text: Kpa anue di nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kpa anumbɛl ge nyɛr choŋŋi dɔŋa ni, di kpa anumbɛlhiŋ la kpɛu a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia see.

ref: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
text: Kpa pebala hɔna baŋ liiwe a aah di kuari kuntɔɔrikuŋ di tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di kaa kpa hɔŋbuglaa di kuari bɛl di tɔ sag a ni.

ref: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
text: Gil ba kpa N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua di tɔu.

ref: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
text: Kpa akeesia daazi di kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia.

ref: Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put
text: di kaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa luu a ge zɛɛ hɔŋribɔra tokkoanɛɛ, di kpa anɛɛgaa du bɛl maa zɛɛ.

ref: For the back wall along the west side use six frames
text: Kuari daabaŋlaa anumbɛl di du a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia harbɔɔ wiicholii tuna la,

ref: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
text: A siraa anɛɛ naa daabaŋlaa la daŋ ɛɛ anɛɛgaa guŋŋ di lii zɛɛ di la chiŋ di ga suu gbitti kpaŋ ni. Gunnɛ bá kuari a maa.

ref: Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
text: Awia, a daabaŋlaa daŋ ɛɛ ŋmantannaazi ani a zɛɛzi saliŋhuŋŋa hɔŋribɔra ɛɛ fidaanumbɛl, anɛɛ du bɛl maa zɛɛ.

ref: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through.
text: Ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a daabaŋlaa la bɛl maa ni. Di luu saliŋ gbittizi di du a ni, á lauri a daakaŋlaa kpogli, di kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a daakaŋlaa ge ni.

ref: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
text: Gil ba kuari a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia gunla miŋ baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.

ref: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
text: Gil ba kpa a tɛɛbul la di chiŋŋi a patiisa har wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di gil ba kpa fintina daa la ge chiŋŋi de wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, a chaŋ dɔŋa.

ref: Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
text: Gil a kuŋgorgaa lau a patiisa, ka kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la n du u biini la di chiŋŋi u har. A patiisa daŋ bargi Bɔnaniinanii la di lii Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la ni.

ref: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
text: Kpa akeesia daazi anue di ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ a ni, di luu saliŋ kuŋgorgaa du a ni, di kpa danyɛ luu a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra.”

ref: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
text: Kpa a daajaŋra di suuzi a gbittizi la n du u keŋkerezi anɛɛ la bɔɔni, di ba waa chiu.

ref: All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans.
text: Kpa danyɛ di luu mbusu lizibɔr kuna naa, viini la ban niŋ ɔɔ paa u hɔɔhri di ra du, sɔɔbulzi, hɛnni la ban ninna du chal di ra mizi, dunozi n dɔɔ nyina ba ɔɔ kpa di ra tɔɔhzi ola ani nimbuurikuna.

ref: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
text: Kpa daazi di kuari mbusu lizibɔr, di gil u dɔɔ bɔɔ gunla miŋ baglii a bizeŋ nyuu la. Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia diŋŋee wia

ref: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
text: Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be bá tɛi ɔlivi nuu la n du yelemm, guŋ gil a fintinazi wer di ra lau saŋa maa.

ref: Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard
text: U keŋkere la hiŋ ge, du guŋ.

ref: for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain
text: ú dɔɔ daabaŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra tokkozi, baŋ kpa danyɛ luu. Luu saliŋhuŋŋa kuŋgorgaa ni lugbidaazi la ban niŋ kpa sagzi a daabaŋlaa maa ni.

ref: Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
text: Kpa peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina ge aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah patiisa, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi tokko, di gil ba tɔɔhzuu di kpa tɔ a diŋŋee dominua. Daabaŋlaa anaazu daŋ hɔŋzi a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra anaazu ni di lawuu kpogli.

ref: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
text: Kuna la n kawɛɛ ban niŋ kpa di ra hum n Tanti Dia la biini la, danyɛɛ bá kpa di luu a maa. Daasiraa ban niŋ kpa lauri a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni a diŋŋee daazi maa, danyɛɛ ba kpa lua. Fintina daa nuu wia

ref: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
text: Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, patiisa la n teŋ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka see baŋgia la, Aarɔn ni u biibaalaa niŋ gil a fintinazi la nine ra lau Kɔraawiizi see, di lii duana di ra la hɔpizaa. Kenne niŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni ba naanna, di hanna la.”

ref: Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yir i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ni u biibaala Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza, ani Itama, di lii Izrɛl hina biini, bá wa ɛɛ n kizeehina di ra humiŋ.

ref: Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them.
text: Ŋɔ nɛra la maa miŋ tɛɛ nunzuma ba zum nonee huma nɛnnɛ la be lugɔ bá nyɛr bɔmbɔga la n wesse tɛɛ Aarɔn ú bɔg. A hɔl la ban niŋ sɔu di lizi u doŋa ha, ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii n be, di ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di ra humiŋ la.

ref: Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests.
text: Bɔmbɔga naabuu bá nyɛr. Bampirii pɛɛŋ, tagtakpurii, tagtajiga, tagtajaŋ, namu ani kirsɔɔ. Gil ba nyɛr a keŋ kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga naa tɛɛ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ani u biizi bá ɛɛ n kizeehina di hum ra tɛŋ.

ref: Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes. The Vest for the High Priest (Exodus
text: Kpa saliŋ gessi ni peezi huna baŋ liiwe, aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina aah lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, aŋhina aah choihchoih ani gessihuŋŋunanaa di nyɛraa. Tagtakpurii la wia

ref: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
text: di pɛr saliŋ himmaa yɔlɔzi anɛɛ lugɔ ŋmɛnni di kpaa lauri a bɔbaataa la. Bampirii pɛɛŋ la wia

ref: and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Gil a bia ɛɛ fidaanɛɛ, bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Jekɔb biibaala la sɔna, di gil ba sɛɛh Izrɛl dizi fidaanɛɛ la sɔna di du bɛl maa ni.

ref: with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
text: Kpa binanaa la yoola n kpolle di margi u ni a hiŋzi dɔŋa lugɔ pichɔŋzi anaazu. A lugli pichɔŋa la daŋ dɔɔ binanaa banna yir rubi ni topaz ani bɛril,

ref: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
text: pichɔnnɛɛhiŋ la daŋ dɔɔ tɛkɔis, saafaya ani ɛmɛral,

ref: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
text: horohiŋ la dɔɔ jasint, aget ani amɛtis,

ref: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings
text: naazuhiŋ la ge dɔɔ krisolait, ɔnigs ani jaspa. Kpa saliŋ ŋmɛnni di baataa du u ni.

ref: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
text: Lau a yɔlɔzi nuuzi anɛɛ la n kawɛɛ la, di vɔɔzi margi a bɔbaataa anɛɛ la n du a vaampɛrɛzi pɛɛŋgargaa la tagtakpurii la see.

ref: Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
text: Kpa ŋmɛmburgu di lau gbittijigzi la n du bampirii pɛɛŋ la ni, di vɔɔzi margi gbittijigzi la n du tagtakpurii la ni, di lawuu vɔɔ mari chara kirsɔɔ la, ú gilɛɛ waa lii a tagtakpurii ni.

ref: Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool
text: Kpa pɛɛmburgu di nyɛr tagtajaŋ ba ɔɔ laali tagtakpurii di sag u ni.

ref: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
text: Fur nyuu zuuribɔr u baambaaŋ. Di muuguu nɛnnɛ u gilɛɛ waa piili.

ref: Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them.
text: A saliŋ bɛlinzi ni a pomegranet nɔna daŋ hiŋzi dɔŋa ni a tagtajaŋ nua bɔmuugii la maa di bar.

ref: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ Aarɔn ɔɔ laaluu saŋa maa di u waa hum kizeehiŋ huma. Di u waa zuu Bɔnaniinanii la biini n see gɛɛ di waa lii, a bɛlinzi daŋ ɔɔ ra gbɔgzi ba ra nuu, ú gilɛɛ waa siu.

ref: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
text: Luu saliŋ himmaa pɛrɛtu, di sɛbi wia naa dau u ni, ‘BA KPAUBUU TƐƐ KƆRAAWIIZI U ƐƐ KUNNANIINANII.’

ref: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
text: Kpa ŋmɛmburgu di vɔɔ mari namu la see.

ref: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
text: Aarɔn daŋ ɔɔ kpau di vɔɔ mari u hile, guŋ gil ń lɛɛ mbusuzi lizaa kuna la Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi di ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la. Haali di ba wa leuwo di ɛɛ wichɔgii maa, di lii a lizaa wia biini gba, ka Aarɔnnɛ niŋ lɛɛ a chɔgri. U daŋ ɔɔ mari u hilee saŋa maa di gil ba mbusuzi la banna lizi la, du wer di su mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi siwii.

ref: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
text: Gil ba nyɛr tagtajaŋra, kirsɔɔzi ani kahurozi tɛɛ Aarɔn biizi, á gil ba dɔɔ sɔŋ ni girme.

ref: Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
text: Kpa bɔmbɔga naa di bɔg i kpɛɛma Aarɔn ni u biibaala. Ka ɛɛ nuu waari ba nyuuni, di kpa nonee sagzi ba ni, di kpa baa tɛŋ ba birgi n kizeehina di ra humiŋ.

ref: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
text: Gil ba nyɛr gessihuŋŋunanaa galiŋkpuree ban niŋ du biini, a chi ba charazi di wa hel ba naapɔga.

ref: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
text: Aarɔn ni u biizi daŋ ɔɔ bɔg a bɔmbɔga naa saŋa maa, di ba waa zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia gɛɛ di ra la mbusu lizibɔr la, ba ga hum ba huma Bɔnaniinanii la. Guŋ gil ba wàá ɛɛ wichɔgaa di dɔɔ chɔgri, di siu. Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u naanna di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
text: Ɛɛ kpu nabal hɔpizi biimaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa di lizi n baaŋ ba ni. Gunnɛ í ɛɛ di lizi mbusu lizibɔr ge doŋa ha, di lizi n baaŋ u ni. Kpa nuu di waari u ni, di lizi u doŋa.

ref: Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil.
text: di kpa huuti sakɔla la baŋ waa yiisi duwɛɛ di ɔɔzi paanuu, di kaa ɛɛ nuu koozi a sau yeŋ ni di halli boforoti di ɔɔzi kɛrɛkɛssizi di ɛɛ nuu waari a ni.

ref: Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
text: Kpaa du kɛɛgɔ biini di lau nabalee ni a pebala anɛɛ la jaa a ni di wa tɛŋ.

ref: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves.
text: Denii í kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaala di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di wa sɔ baa nii.

ref: Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash.
text: Kpa bɔmbɔga la di bɔg Aarɔn, aabuu tagtajaŋ, tagtajiga, tagtakpurii, tagtakpurii himmaa la ani bampirii pɛɛŋ la. Lau a tagtakpurii kirsɔɔ la baŋ suahwɛ nɛnnɛ di kirsuu.

ref: and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
text: Yiili nuuwaarii la di waari u nyuu.

ref: caps, and sashes, then ordain them, because they and their descendants will always be priests.
text: di kpa kahurozi hi baa, ka kpa kirsɔɔzi kirsi Aarɔn ni u biibaala la. Gunnɛ i ɛɛ di lizi baa bá ɛɛ n kizeehina di hanna la.

ref: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
text: Lau a nabal di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu,

ref: Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent.
text: ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, n see.

ref: Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar.
text: Kpa i nonibii lii a nabal chal di faa mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi la ka fug anla n kawɛɛ dau u zɛɛ.

ref: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
text: Ka kpa a nabal ol, u hɔŋ ani u biini kuna maa ge, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga fuuah, á ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa.

ref: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
text: I daŋ lau pebal la bɛl di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni.

ref: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
text: Kɔrguu, di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa.

ref: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
text: Mɔnni a pebal jigzijigzi, di yagli u biini kuna ni u naagballi, di kpaa jaa u nyuu ani u bɔr la n kawɛɛ ni.

ref: Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Denii í fuuh a pebal maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
text: Lau a pebal la n kawɛɛ la, di gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni.

ref: Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: Kɔrgi u ge, di ɛɛ u chal di fɔg Aarɔn ni u biibaala nodige dignipaŋhoori, ba nodige nonibibala ani ba nodige naanibibala. Ka kpa a chal yeŋ la n kawɛɛ di mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa.

ref: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
text: Kpa chal la n chɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr ni la yeŋ di koozi nuuwaarii la ni. Kpaa mizi Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni ba bɔmbɔga maa ni. U ni baa ani ba bɔmbɔga la maa jaa ɛɛ kunnanaananaa.

ref: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: Lizi a pebal dinzɛɛ, u biini kuna nuu, u hiah bɔnanii, u siga ni a nuuri ani u nodig hiih, di kpa a maa kpau dɔŋa ni, ba kizeehina kizee kpai peballɛ guŋ.

ref: and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me.
text: Kpa a kuna naa maa du Aarɔn ni u biibaala nonee, bá lallaa chiŋ dí viigi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa tɛŋ.

ref: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Denii i jaa lɛɛa ba be di jaa mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
text: Kpa pebal naa bampirii di lalluu chiŋ viigi n see, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii, di ɛɛ i hor.

ref: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
text: Aarɔn biibaal la n niŋ ɔɔ kpa n kizee la waa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia u hum Bɔnaniinanii la biini, u daŋ ɔɔ bɔgaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place,
text: Daali Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai pebal ol la bɔnaniinanii la biini.

ref: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: Gil Aarɔn ni u biibaala hee a pebal ol ni paanuu la n du a kɛɛgɔ biini la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it.
text: Aarɔn ni u biibaalaa niŋ ɔɔ di a diwee naa baŋ kpawɛɛ lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu tɛŋ naa. Di ba bɛŋ lɛi, nɛr maa wàá wer dia dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ diunanaananaarɛ n be.

ref: If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
text: Di ba wa dia ka ka hɔɔ wa pizi, bá fuuah, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ diunanaananaarɛ n be.

ref: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
