ref: And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up.
text: Awia, u baŋ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia labuu binni anɛɛhiŋ lugli baagu lugli hɔpizii hɔl.

ref: The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached.
text: U kaa kpa bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la di du Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la biini, di kpa a daajaŋra suuzi a gbittizi bɔɔni, di kpa u tua di tɔ.

ref: The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: Denii u kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia biini, di kpa a patiisa vɔɔ teŋuu, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la.

ref: The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place,
text: Moosis kpa tɛɛbul la di zuu ga chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag patiisa la baŋgia,

ref: after which the bread was set on the table.
text: di kpa a paanuu dau u ni, Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord.
text: di choŋŋi u fintinazi Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain,
text: Moosis kpa mbusu lizibɔr baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la, di zuu chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini a patiisa see,

ref: and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma u ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ u ɛɛ la.

ref: The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: Denii u kpa patiisa vɔɔ a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua la.

ref: Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there.
text: U kaa kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia n kaa ɛɛ U Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la, di fuuh mbusuzi lizaa kuna ni mbusuzi lizaa mia u ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water,
text: U kpa tassazeŋ la di chiŋŋi mbusu lizibɔr ni a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia baambaaŋ di ɛɛ nii du u biini, bá ra sam.

ref: then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet.
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn ni u biibaala ɔɔ ra sanzi ba nonee ni naazi.

ref: In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: Gunnɛ ba ɔɔ sanzi saŋa maa, di ba haŋ wàá zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia gɛɛ di ba wàá ba mbusu lizibɔr la, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: Finally, Moses had the curtains hung around the courtyard and at the entrance. The Glory of the Lord
text: Denii Moosis kuari a diŋŋee bar Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni mbusu lizibɔr la, di kpa u dominua patiisa la vɔɔ, di jaa tuŋ a huma. Kɔraawiizi girme wia

ref: Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord.
text: Denii baama la wa tɔ a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, Kɔraawiizi girme su de.

ref: Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow;
text: Izrɛl hina volaa la maa biini, di a baama faa haŋ wa izi a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia nyuu, ba ge ɔɔ izuu di ra vol,

ref: then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again.
text: ka di a baama waa haŋ wa izi, ba waa naa ra kpuzi, di a hɔl la uŋ izee lɛi.

ref: No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi baama la ɔɔ faa guali a Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ninɛɛ bɔchaaŋ maga. Niŋ ge du u biini hamuŋa ni, Izrɛl hina maa ra na, ba volaa maa biini.

ref: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonee sag mbusu lizaa sel nyuu ni, ú ɛɛ u mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, di ɛɛ u wichɔgaa kinturgaa.

ref: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
text: U daŋ kpu a nabalee n see, Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la kpa u chal tɛŋ, ka kpaa mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa n du n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la.

ref: Skin the bull and cut it up,
text: U daŋ sih a sel di mɔnnuu.

ref: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
text: Kizeehiŋ Aarɔn la biibaala daŋ paa daazi sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di chem niŋ,

ref: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Nɛr la n na lizi mbusu la daŋ yagli u biini kuna ni u gballi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la jaa fuuh u maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it.
text: Ka di u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii di lii u peeza gɛɛ u buuna biini, u daŋ ɛɛ u bal la n kpekke.

ref: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: U daŋ kɔrguu mbusu lizibɔr la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere n see, Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la jaa kpa u chal mizi bar mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Nɛr la n na lizi mbusu la, daŋ yagli u biini kuna ni u gballi, n kizeehiŋ la jaa kpa u maa fuuh, mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
text: Di u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n ɛɛ kunzaahri, guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ u lizi koorikomma gɛɛ koŋaahmu.

ref: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpau ba mbusu lizibɔr la, di wa lau u nyuu miŋŋi tɔri, di fuuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ka gil u chal toŋzi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii.

ref: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
text: U daŋ lizi u chigii la maa bir ha mbusu lizibɔr wiifurii la banna ta hɔɔhri la.

ref: Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Denii u jaa lau u keeri di tɛruu piili ka gilɛɛ waa tɔruu anɛɛ. Ka n kizeehiŋ la jaa fuuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, u ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.”

ref: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di bɛl maa wa ba mbusu lizaa mia ni u wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, a daŋ ɛɛ sakɔla. U daŋ yiili ɔlivi nuu du a ni di kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma sag,

ref: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: di kpaa ga tɛɛ Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ n kizeehina la. N kizeehiŋ la daŋ muraa, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
text: A sau bɔr la n kawɛɛ daŋ jaa ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala hor. Á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia bɔnaniinanii himmaanii, dikuu baŋ lizaa lii diwee la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛŋ la wia.

ref: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
text: Di bɛl maa wa kpa mbusu lizaa mia la baŋ ɔɔzɛɛ lugɔ paanuu n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ba, a dɛkkɔɔ u ɛɛ paanuu tɔg baŋ kpa sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu koozi dɔŋa ni, di kuari gɛɛ kɛrɛkɛssizi baŋ ɛɛ nuu waari a ni.

ref: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
text: Di mbusu lizaa mia ɛɛ paanuu la baŋ kpa maansa hɛna halli, a dɛkkɔɔ a ɛɛ sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
text: I daŋ pussaa di fug nuu waari a ni, mbusu lizaa miarɛ guŋ.

ref: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
text: Di mbusu lizaa mia ɛɛ paanuu baŋ hallɛɛnɛ, a dɛkkɔ uŋ ɛɛ sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu.

ref: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
text: Kpa mbusu hiŋ di tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la, waabuu niŋ kpaa la mbusu lizibɔr di ga tɛŋ.

ref: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: U daŋ lizi mbusu yeŋ á ɛɛ liize hor, di fuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a sɔɔh du sum tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
text: Ka mbusu lizaa mia bɔr la n kawɛɛ la birgi Aarɔn ni u biibaala hotte. A ɛɛ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa bɔnaniinanii himmaa la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii.

ref: Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice.
text: Mbusu lizaa mia kuŋfuuhlii la maa hin niŋ kpa wa tɛŋ, gilɛɛ waa dua yiisi gɛɛ huuhnuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ fuuh mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la maa n dɔɔ yiisi gɛɛ huuhnuu di ra tɛŋ.

ref: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
text: Kpa i lugli mia bina maa di wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ka gilɛɛ waa fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
text: Ɛɛ kpa yazi jaa mbusu lizaa mia kuna maa ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, yazi chigɔɔ tɛɛ n ni n nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la. A dɛkkɔɔ yazi ɔɔ du mbusu lizaa mia kuna maa ni.

ref: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
text: Di i wa kpa lugli mia í wa lizi mbusu n be, i daŋ hallaa di nyaaraa.

ref: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
text: Kpa nuu ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma jaa a ni. Mbusu lizaa miarɛ guŋ.

ref: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuh a mihallaa ni nuu mbusu la á ɛɛ liize hor ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni tɛŋ.”

ref: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Di nɛr maa wa lizi nabal gɛɛ naniina u nauna biini, ú lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ú lizi nau la n kpekke.

ref: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: A hiŋ daŋ kpa u nonee sag a sel nyuu ni mɔɔ ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua. Denii Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ kizeehina la, kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni,

ref: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: u siga ni a nuuri la maa n tɔ u fuuh ani u hiah bɔnanii.

ref: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
text: Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa annii maa jaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la ni di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ.

ref: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Di peezii gɛɛ buunnɛ u ŋɔ u kpa lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ u niina gɛɛ u bal la n kpekke,

ref: If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: di peezii u kpa ba ú wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi,

ref: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: u daŋ kpa u nonii sag u nyuu ni, ka kɔrguu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see. Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: u siga ni a nuuri la maa ani u hiah bɔnanii la, di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛŋ.

ref: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
text: Di u mbusu sel la ɛɛ buunnɛ, ú kpau tɛŋ.

ref: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonii sag a sel nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see. Denii Aarɔn biibaala kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: u siga ni a nuuri la maa ani u hiah bɔnanii la.

ref: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, á ɛɛ diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii sɔɔh n summɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. A nuu maa ɛɛ n hotte.

ref: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
text: A ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛ saŋa maa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina naannaa keŋ. Di ii haŋ wa du bɔr maa, ka i ra kii sel nuu gɛɛ chal dii.”

ref: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonibii lii a chal di mizaa buniidaanɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia bɔnaniinanii patiisa la see.

ref: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
text: A hiŋ daŋ kpa ú nonii sag a bubal nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu bɔr la banna kpu mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa sela n see la. Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la.

ref: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii u chal yeŋ di fɔg a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka keezi fug anla n kawɛɛ la maa ta u zɛɛ.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di unla maa waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ka ɛɛ wii la n waa deŋlee mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa biini, widaulaa naabuu ú hiŋzi.

ref: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Di n Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, a buu a nɛra maa, a dɛkkɔ ú kpa nabalee la n kpekke tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ú ɛɛ bilchɔg mbusu, dikuu u wichɔgaa la wia.

ref: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
text: U daŋ kpa a nabalee ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di kpa u nonii sag u nyuu ni, ka kɔrguu n see.

ref: He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent,
text: Denii n Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la kpa a nabalee la chal yeŋ zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini.

ref: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ jaa kpa a chal yeŋ fɔg nyigzi la n du daahɛgsɔɔhsuma mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Ka jaa fug a nabalee chal la n kawɛɛ la, dau mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la zɛɛ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua la.

ref: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
text: di kpa a maa lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia, bɔr la baŋ kuarɛɛ waa doŋŋe n be, ba ra ta hɔɔhri la, di chem niŋ fuuuh.

ref: When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty.
text: Filaŋkennaa, di Izrɛl hina maa wa ɛɛ wii bɛl di chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la bɛl maa, di ba waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka ba cholloo.

ref: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
text: Di ba wa zum wichɔgii la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la, guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔ a nɛra maa lizi nabalee, ú ɛɛ ba wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel di ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see.

ref: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
text: Denii a nɛra nabɔnzi kpa ba nonee sag a nabalee nyuu ni mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see mɔɔ, ka jaa kɔrguu de.

ref: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
text: N Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la daŋ kpa u chal yeŋ zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini.

ref: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
text: U daŋ kpa ú nonibii lii a chal di mizi buniidaanɛɛ, a patiisa la see.

ref: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
text: U daŋ kpa a chal di faa mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la nyigzi ni, ka fug a chal la n kawɛɛ la maa dau mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la n chigɛ n Tanti Dia dominua la zɛɛ.

ref: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Di u wichɔgaa la wa lii chaaŋ u zumaa, u daŋ lizi bubal la n kpekke.

ref: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel hiŋ chal yeŋ, di fɔg mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka jaa keezi fug anla maa n kawɛɛ la ta u zɛɛ.

ref: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
text: U daŋ fuuh a nuu la maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni gunla uŋ fuuh dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu la. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal la n ɛɛ a wichɔgaa la, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi gil tɛu.

ref: When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty.
text: Di unla maa waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ka ɛɛ wii la n waa dɛkkɛ, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la biini, ka u cholloo.

ref: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Di ba wa gillɔ u zum u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia, a dɛkkɔɔ u kpa buniina la n kpekke di wa lizi mbusu dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia.

ref: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonii sag u wichɔgaa mbusu sel hiŋ nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu bɔr la banna kpu wichɔgaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa sela la.

ref: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
text: U daŋ lizi u nuu maa gunla baŋ ɔɔ lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sel nuu la, n kizeehiŋ fuuah mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni, á sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal la n ɛɛ wichɔgaa la, ń gil tɛu.

ref: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Di u wa ba pebii ni lugɔ u wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa selle, u daŋ ɛɛ ú lor la n kpekke.

ref: Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonii sag u ni mɔɔ, ka kɔrguu ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, bɔr la banna kpu mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa la.

ref: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Denii n kizeehiŋ kpa u nonibii lii u chal yeŋ di fɔg a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr nyigzi la, ka keezi fug anla n kawɛɛ la ta u zɛɛ.

ref: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
text: U daŋ lizi u nuu maa gunla baŋ ɔɔ lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa pebii nuu la, n kizeehiŋ kpaa di jaa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la n chɔɔ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa lizibɔr la ni di fuuh a maa. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal, míŋ̀ Kɔraawiizi gil tɛu.’ ”

ref: You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
text: Di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe n be, alugɔ pir ni bol sesiwaa gɛɛ kuntuuzii, haali uŋ waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka u doŋŋoo n be.

ref: You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
text: Gɛɛ di u gbɔgzi newee doŋa ka waa zummɛ, gɛɛ kunla n niŋ gil u doŋ, haali uŋ waa zummɛ gba, di u wa zumaa, u cholloo.

ref: You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
text: Gɛɛ di nɛr waa nfɛrɛ fɛwɛɛ ka hɛɛhzi lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ winanaa gɛɛ wichɔgaa wiimaa biini, haali uŋ waa kuttɛɛ gba, ka di u wa zumaa, u cholloo.

ref: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
text: Di nɛr maa wa chollo lii annii bɛl maa biini, u daŋ sɛɛ a guŋ wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la chɔgri n be,

ref: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
text: u wichɔgaa hiŋ kim daŋ ɛɛ pelor gɛɛ bulor di lii u sela biini, ú kpa wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. N kizeehiŋ jaa kpau lizi u wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri n be.

ref: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
text: U daŋ kpaa wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, u feli kpa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor la tɛŋ. U daŋ miŋŋi u baŋaa ku, ka gilɛɛ waa tɔri u nyuu,

ref: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: di kpa u chal yeŋ mizi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii, ka u chal la n kawɛɛ la, u daŋ kpaa chuuri mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ. Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la.

ref: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
text: Ka di waa koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ la nawɛɛ, ú lizi sakɔla kookoo tassa suul wa tɛŋ, á ɛɛ u wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa. Ú gilɛɛ waa kpa nuu gɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra sag a ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, á ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ.

ref: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
text: U daŋ kpaa wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, ú muraa nonii suul, di kpaa sag mbusuzi lizaa kuna la n chɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuah tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, wichɔgaa mbusu lizaarɛ la.

ref: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
text: Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a baal, ú na giltɛɛi. A mbusu lizaa kuna la n kawɛɛ la daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ hor, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia la.” Bilchɔg mbusu lizaa wia

ref: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
text: “Di nɛr wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa la uŋ waa kuttɛɛ ɛɛ, di suuh ú turgi kim la n ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, u kim daŋ ɛɛ pebal la n kpekke, di lii u sela biini. U yoola hel gunla banna mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋu kebisau n Tanti Dia biini la. Bilchɔg mbusu lizaarɛ la.

ref: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa u galiŋkpurii du, ka jaa kpa u tagtajaŋ huŋŋunanii la laali sag, di jaa paa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n fuuhwe la hɔɔhri mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di dau mbusu lizibɔr kɛrii,

ref: The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord: You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
text: Di nɛr kugni kuŋ n leuwe ka kanni kara u wia gɛɛ di kanni kara di hɛɛhzi gɛɛ di ɛɛ guŋ dɔŋ wichɔgaa nɛra n niŋ wer ɛɛ,

ref: and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained: It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour
text: “Mbusu naabuu Aarɔn ni u biibaala lizi wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, a hɔl la ban niŋ lizi bɛl maa n kizeehiŋ, di waari u nyuu nuu la. Kuna naabuu u lizi, sakɔla kookoo tassa suul á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia di ba waa lizi n kizeehiŋ maa. Ba ɔɔ kpa u keza chɔɔzi ni, di kaa kpa anla n kawɛɛ duana ni di lizi mbusu.

ref: In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong. Daily Sacrifices (Exodus
text: Kenne n kizeehiŋ jaa kpaa di lizi u bilchɔg mbusu tɛɛ a baal n see, n gil tɛu dikuu wia la uŋ ɛɛwɛ chol la wia.” Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii wia

ref: This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it.
text: Biibambie la maa n lii n kizeehina dee biini ra diubuu, ú ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii.

ref: If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
text: Vii la baŋ kpawɛɛ daali a ol, a dɛkkɔ ba purguu, ka di daansanii ba kpa daaluu, ba daŋ kuguu nɛnnɛ di yagluu ni nii.

ref: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
text: “Kpa widaulaa naa tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biizi. Mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ŋmɛnizii keŋ, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la daŋ ɔɔ sag mbusu lizibɔr la niŋ ni hamuŋa maa guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Niŋ la ge n du mbusu lizibɔr ni la, daŋ ɔɔ ra lawuu saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa.

ref: Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
text: ka wir a keŋ bɔmbɔga naa maa, ka kpa aŋhina laali, di paa a hɔɔhri lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia ga ha bɔr la n waa doŋŋe n be ba kuari la.

ref: The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
text: Niŋ la n du mbusu lizibɔr ni la daŋ ɔɔ ra lawuu saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa. Chɔɔzi maa, n kizeehiŋ daŋ ɔɔ lizi daazi di jaa, di kuari mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii kuŋ la sag a niŋ ni di fuuh a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu nuu la di jaa.

ref: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ a niŋ ɔɔ ra lau saŋaa saŋa maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di gilɛɛ waa dim ŋmɛnɛ maa.” Mbusu lizaa mia wia

ref: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Mbusu lizaa mia ŋmɛnizii keŋ. Aarɔn biibaalaa niŋ ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa mia di ba n be, mbusu lizibɔr la see.

ref: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ ɔɔ mur sakɔla la ni nuu di jaa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la maa n sag mbusu lizaa mia la ni, di fuuh liize mbusu lizaa hor la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a sɔɔh du sum tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
text: Ba gilɛɛ waa kpa yiisi jaa a ni di ra ɔɔzi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii kpaa tɛɛ baa lugɔ ba hotte di lii mbusuzi lizaa kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra fuuh di ra tɛŋ la biini. U ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ alugɔ wichɔgaa ni bilchɔg mbusuzi lizaa hora la.

ref: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
text: Saŋaa saŋa maa, Aarɔn dee biibaala maa daŋ wer dia. Ba hotte di lii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la maa biini baŋ ɔɔ fuuh di ra tɛŋ la. Nɛr la maa gɛɛ kunla maa n niŋ gbɔgzi a mbusu lizaa mia naa, wia daŋ huuzuu.”

ref: The Lord spoke to Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Kpa nuu koozi a ni ka hallaa maansa hɛna biini, di pussaa di koozaa nɛnnɛ a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ.

ref: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
text: N kizeehiŋ mbusu lizaa mia maa, fuuihre ba ɔɔ fuuah, ba gilɛɛ waa dia.” Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa wia

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin: This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
text: “Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala be, ‘Wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ŋmɛnizii keŋ. Ba daŋ ɔɔ kpu wichɔgaa mbusu sel labuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ kpu mbusu lizaa sel di fuuh la. A wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii.

ref: The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent,
text: N kizeehiŋ la n lizi mbusu labuu niŋ diu, bɔnaniinanii la biini n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia diŋŋee la.

ref: and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place.
text: Di nɛr la maa gɛɛ kunla maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi a ol, wia daŋ huuzuu, di u chal ge wa toŋzi u laala yemmaa ni, ú chaguu a bɔnaniinanii hiŋ biini.

ref: None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
text: Ka di wichɔgaa mbusu sel chal la baŋ kpawɛɛ zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini ba lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, a Bɔnaniinanii biini la, ba gilɛɛ waa dia, ka fuuah.’ ”

ref: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni tɛŋ, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii. Bilchɔg mbusu lizaarɛ la.

ref: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
text: U daŋ lizi annii bɛl maa iri di wa lizi mbusu, ú ɛɛ u kɛɛi tɛŋ. U daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la n mizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi sela la chal hor.

ref: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
text: Di a ol yemmaa wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, ba gilɛɛ waa heeu, bá fuuuh. Ka nɛr la maa n waa doŋŋe n be, daŋ wer hee u bɔr la n kawɛɛ.

ref: The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Bilchɔg mbusu lizaa ŋmɛnizii keŋ, u ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii.

ref: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
text: Ba daŋ ɔɔ kpu a bilchɔg mbusu sel, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ kpu mbusu lizaa sel di fuuh la, di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr la keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides,
text: U nuu maanii bá lizi tɛŋ, u dinzɛɛ nuu ani u nuu la n tɔ u biini kuna ni la,

ref: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: u siga anɛɛ la ni a nuuri la n tɔ a ni di dugli u fuuh la, ani u hiah bɔnanii la.

ref: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
text: Biibambie maa n lii n kizeehiŋ dee biini daŋ wer diu, ka a dɛkkɔɔ ba diu bɔnaniinanii la biini, u ɛɛ u naniinanii himmaanii.

ref: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
text: A keŋ widaulaa naa himmaanii ba ra hiŋ di ra lizi wichɔgaa ni bilchɔg mbusuzi. N kizeehiŋ la n lizi a wichɔgaa mbusu la horaa.

ref: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
text: N kizeehiŋ la maa haŋ wa lizi nɛr maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛu, daŋ wer kpa a sel hɔŋ.

ref: just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me.
text: Mbusu lizaa mia la maa baŋ ɔɔzɛɛ gɛɛ di daali gɛɛ di halli ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la n niŋ kpaa tɛŋ la hotte,

ref: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
text: ani mbusu lizaa mia maa, di ba koozaabuu nuu gɛɛ a ɛɛ a hilaarɛ, a gba ɛɛ Aarɔn biibaala maa horaa, bá bɔnnaa mɛgzi. Dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa wia

ref: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
text: Dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa la nɛr n niŋ lizi wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaarɛ keŋ.

ref: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
text: Di u lizuu lugɔ jaamaa mbusu, u daŋ kpa nuu di koozi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ni kɛrɛkɛssizi la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ni di ɛɛ nuu waari a ni, di ŋmir boforoti sakɔla nɛnnɛ di dua nuu.

ref: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
text: Ba daŋ hee u dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol la, a hɔl la maa baŋ lizuu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ la. Bá gilɛɛ wa gil u yemmaa ra chɔɔ hɔɔ ra pizi.

ref: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
text: Ka di u mbusu la ɛɛ nua lizaa gɛɛ u kipar mbusu lizaa, ba daŋ diu a hɔl la maa un lizuu la, ka keezi di u bɔr la n kawɛɛ, di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ.

ref: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
text: Awia, di dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol maa haŋ wa hel hɔpizaa ahoro ka nɛr maa heeu, màá lɛɛ u mbusu hiŋ, u daŋ ɛɛ kundoŋ. Nɛr la maa ge n niŋ heeu, wia daŋ huuzuu.

ref: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi kunla maa n doŋŋe n be, di u ɛɛ newee doŋaa gɛɛ sel doŋaa gɛɛ kundoŋ la maa miŋ kiiwee, ka hee dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa ol la n ɛɛ n hor la, ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be dí ba gilɛɛ waa hee nauna ni peeza gɛɛ buuna nuuri.

ref: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
text: Ba daŋ wer kpa sel la maa n siuwɛ gɛɛ pir sela n lauwɛ nuu di ɛɛ wiimaa, ka ba gilɛɛ waa hee a nuu.

ref: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Nɛr la maa haŋ wa hee ol la baŋ kpawɛɛ lizi mbusu di fuuh ra tɛŋ la nuu, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
text: Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa gɛɛ kunzaahri maa chal.

ref: or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa hee chal, ba duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.” Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ bɔdiilii wia

ref: The Lord also told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the people of Israel: If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me.
text: U daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii du u himmaa nonee wa tɛŋ, a dɛkkɔ ú lizi u nuu ni u bampirii ba, di lalli u bampirii hiŋ chiŋ viigi n see, ú ɛɛ u mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii.

ref: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ fuuh u nuu la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ka a bampirii la waa ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala hotte.

ref: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
text: Aarɔn biibaal la n kpa a dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sel chal ni u nuu tɛŋ labuu dɔɔ u nodig hiih hiŋ.

ref: I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants
text: Di lii Izrɛl hina dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa biini, n kpa mbusu lizaa ol bampirii la baŋ lallɛɛ chiŋ di viigi ni u hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ labuu tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala, á ɛɛ ba bɔdiilaa saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
text: miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, a hɔl la miŋ gillɛ Izrɛl hina lizi ba mbusuzi wa tɛŋ, Bizeŋ Sinaai Hɛribɔduma biini la.

ref: Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
text: Denii u kaa kpa u bampirii la n ɛɛ u diiribɔr la, di lalluu chiŋ viigi Kɔraawiizi see, gunla uŋ ŋɔ u ɛɛ la.

ref: The Lord said to Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast.
text: “Kpogli Aarɔn ni u biibaala, di kpa ba bɔmbɔga, nuuwaarii la, wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nabal ni pebala anɛɛ ani paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ kɛɛgɔ suul di ba,

ref: Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: di chaali a nɛra maa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.”

ref: Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together,
text: Moosis ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la, a nɛra maa jaa chaali Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
text: Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Wii naa miŋ ŋɔ n ɛɛ naa, waabuu Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ń ɛɛ.”

ref: After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves.
text: Denii Moosis lau Aarɔn ni u biibaala lii ba see, di sɔ baa nii.

ref: He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt.
text: Di kpa tagtajaŋ ni tagtajiga laali Aarɔn, di kpa kirsɔɔ kirsuu. Di kaa kpa tagtakpurii laaluu, ka lau u kirsɔɔ la baŋ suahwɛ nɛnnɛ, di kirsi u chara.

ref: Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do.
text: Di kpa pɛɛnnanii bɛl di vɔɔ sag u bampirii, di kpa Urim ni Tumim du a bampirii pɛɛŋ hiŋ biini.

ref: He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
text: Denii u vɔɔu namu, ka kpa saliŋ pɛrɛtunanii la di mari u see, di ra bagli lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la.

ref: Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination.
text: Denii Moosis kpa nuuwaarii mizi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni kuna la maa n du u biini, di ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi horaa.

ref: He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base.
text: Di ɛɛ a nuu yeŋ mizi mbusu lizibɔr ni u kuna maa, a tassazeŋ ni u zɛɛ hɔŋribɔr buniidaanɛɛ, di ra bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi horaa.

ref: He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord.
text: Di yiili a nuu yeŋ waari Aarɔn nyuu di lizi u doŋa, ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛnaniinanii.

ref: Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: Denii u lau Aarɔn biibaala ba see, di kpa tagtajaŋra laali baa, ka kpa kirsɔɔzi kirsi baa, di kpa kahurozi hi baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
text: Denii u jaa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu nabal la, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni.

ref: After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin.
text: Moosis kɔrgi a nabal di kpa u chal di kpa u nonibii lii a yeŋ di faa mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi maa ni di bagli lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte. Ka jaa fug a chal bɔr la n kawɛɛ dau mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ zɛɛ. Guŋ bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kunnaniinaniirɛ, di lizi wichɔgaa maa u ni.

ref: Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire.
text: Moosis lizi a nabal biini kuna nuu maa ani u hiah bɔnanii di jaa u siga ni a nuuri maa ni, di kpaa fuuh mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: Ka kpa a nabal hɔŋ ni u ol ani u biini kuna maa ge lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di ga fuuh gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head,
text: Denii u jaa lau pebal la n ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sel la baŋ ɔɔ fuuh la, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni

ref: Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: Moosis kɔrgi a pebal di kpa u chal mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa.

ref: Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
text: Di kaa kpa u biini kuna ni u gballi di yaglaa di fuuh a pebal maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ, di ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla uŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head,
text: Di kaa lizi a pebal la n kawɛɛ la, unla n ɛɛ u kizee kpai hor, Aarɔn ni u biibaala kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni.

ref: and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot.
text: Moosis kɔrgi a pebal di kpa u chal yeŋ fɔg Aarɔn nodig dignipaŋhoo ni u nodig nonibibal ani u nodig naanibibal.

ref: Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: Moosis kaa lau Aarɔn biibaala ba see di kpa a chal yeŋ di fɔg ba nodige dignipaŋhoori ni ba nodige nonibibala ani ba nodige naanibibala. Denii u jaa kpa a chal di mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi la maa.

ref: He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg.
text: Di kpa u nuu ni u dinzɛɛ nuu ni u nuu la maa n tɔ u biini kuna ni, ni u hiah bɔnanii ni u siga ni a nuu ani u nodig hiih.

ref: Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
text: Lizi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ lii kɛɛgɔ la biini baŋ du paanuuzi wa tɛŋ la, ani paanuukpaŋ baŋ kpa nuu kuari ni kɛrɛkɛsi kpaŋ, di kpaa sag peezi la nuu ni u nodig hiih ni.

ref: Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord.
text: Denii u kpaa du Aarɔn ni u biibaala nonee, ba lallaa chiŋ di viigi, Kɔraawiizi see, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa.

ref: After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony.
text: Denii Moosis lɛɛa ba be di jaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la n sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni di fuuah, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, kizee kpai mbusu lizaarɛ guŋ.

ref: Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
text: Moosis kaa kpa nuuwaarii la yeŋ ani a chal yeŋ lii mbusu lizibɔr la, di mizi Aarɔn ni u biizi ni ba bɔmbɔga, ba ni ba bɔmbɔga maa ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Moses said to Aaron and his sons: The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala be, “Ií daali a ol Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di hee u ni paanuu la n lii Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai mbusuzi lizaa kɛɛgɔ la biini, gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ di ra ŋɔ, ‘Aarɔn ni u biibaala niŋ dia.’

ref: Burn what is left over
text: Ií fuuh anla maa n kawɛɛ.

ref: and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now.
text: Ií du Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua guŋŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di ii waa chaaŋ liwɛɛ di ga hel a hɔl la ii Kɔraawiizi kizee kpai hɔpizaa maga n niŋ su.

ref: We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven.
text: Wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ zinaa naa, Kɔraawiizii bagli guŋ, á ɛɛ u baaŋ lizaa ii ni.

ref: The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
text: Ií daŋ du a Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, wibaŋzi ni hamuŋzi di ɛɛ gunla maa miŋ baglɛɛ la, ka gilɛɛ waa siu. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ ń ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
text: Aarɔn ni u biibaala ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be ŋɔ bá ɛɛ la.

ref: Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders.
text: A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl, Moosis yir Aarɔn ni u biibaala ani Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi.

ref: Then he said to Aaron: Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
text: Denii u ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Lizi nabalee, ú ɛɛ ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel, di lizi pebal ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, á du kpeg nɛnnɛ, di kpaa ba wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them.
text: Kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Ií lizi bubal ú ɛɛ ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, ni nabalee ani pebii, á maa di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ. Á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa.

ref: Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
text: Di kaa lizi nabal ani pebal, a ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa sela di wa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di kpa nuu koozi mbusu lizaa mia ni di jaa. Ií ɛɛ guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaa Kɔraawiizi daŋ ba ii be.’ ”

ref: After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord,
text: Ba kpa kuna la Moosis n baglɛɛ la ba Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, a nɛra maa ba, di wa chi de ba jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Moses said: The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi bagli lugɔ ii ɛɛ, guŋ gil u girme ba ii be.”

ref: Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Tuzi ba mbusu lizibɔr la di wa kpa ii wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ni ii mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la, di lizi i ni i nɛra maa wichɔgaa mbusu. Kpa unla n ɛɛ a nɛra hor la lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ la.”

ref: Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins.
text: Awia, Aarɔn ba mbusu lizibɔr di wa kɔrgi u himmaa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nabalee la.

ref: His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot.
text: U biibaala kpa a chal wa tɛu, u kpa u nonibii liia di fɔg mbusu lizibɔr la nyigzi, ka fug a chal bɔr la n kawɛɛ dau mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ zɛɛ.

ref: But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: Di kpa wichɔgaa mbusu sel la nuu, u siga ani u hiah bɔnanii, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagli Moosis la.

ref: Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
text: Ka u ol ni u hɔŋ waa, ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgiarɛ u fuuah.

ref: After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar.
text: Denii u kɔrgi mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la. U biibaala kpa a chal tɛu u mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar.
text: Ba paagi ol la kpaŋkpaŋa di ra tɛu, di kpa u nyuu jaa, u fuuh a maa mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
text: Ka jaa yagli u biini kuna ni u naagballi di kpaa sag anla ni mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuah.

ref: Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins.
text: A har, Aarɔn kpa a nɛra ge mbusu lizaa sel la ba. Di lau ba buuŋ la n ɛɛ ba wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel la, di kɔrguu, di lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu gunla uŋ felee ɛɛ unla.

ref: And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way.
text: U kaa kpa mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii la ge di lizi mbusu gunla banna ɛɛa la.

ref: He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
text: Di kaa kpa mbusu lizaa mia la ge ba, di ɛɛa nokool suul, di jaa chɔɔzin mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar.
text: Di kɔrgi a nabal ni a pebal, a ɛɛ a nɛra dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu sela. U biibaala kpa a chal tɛu, u kpaa mizi mbusu lizibɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa ni.

ref: His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver
text: Ka u jaa kpa a nabal ni a pebal nuuri bɔra la waa,

ref: on top of the choice ribs.
text: di sag a bampiree ni, di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
text: Denii Aarɔn lalli a bampiree ni u nodige hiiah la chiŋ di viigi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa, gunla Moosis n baglɛɛ la.

ref: Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices.
text: Aarɔn lalli u nonee chaŋ a nɛra di kissi baa. Uŋ wa lizi a mbusuzi maa tuŋ, u jaa lii mbusu lizibɔr tuu.

ref: He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory.
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Baŋ wa liiwɛ, ba kissi a nɛra, Kɔraawiizi girme ba ba be.

ref: The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
text: Kakpaŋ, niŋ lii Kɔraawiizi be di wa fuuh mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la maa ni a nuuri bɔra la, n sag mbusu lizibɔr la ni la. Nɛra la maa n wa na guŋ, ba chaasi ni bɔsɔna di chogli hɛri di pi.

ref: Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to.
text: Aarɔn biibaala Nadab ni Abihu kpa ba nimbuurikuna di buu niŋ, di kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di du a niŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di zuu u ni, dikuu uŋ waa ŋɔ bá ɛɛ guŋ wia.

ref: Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi gil niŋ lii chiŋ wa fuuh baa, ba siuzi u see.

ref: Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said: “I demand respect from my priests, and I will be praised by everyone!” Aaron was speechless.
text: Moosis jaa ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ gil banla maa n na ba n be, zum lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ. N daŋ kpa n girme bagli n nɛra. A dɛkkɔɔ ba ra tɔgziŋ.’ ” Ka Aarɔn siigi.

ref: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.”
text: Moosis yir Aarɔn naara biibaala Misɛl ni Ɛlzafan, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ba ɛŋ, di wa chi ii lulla naa n siuwɛ naa, lii Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la see, di la a nɛra chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia.”

ref: Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala Ɛliaza ni Itama be, “Ií chaazi ii nyuuni di gilɛɛ waa piili ii laala, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi, ka Kɔraawiizi baaŋ kaa fuuh a nɛra maa ni. Ka ii diahina ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra wii banla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ niŋ wa fuuh la lee.

ref: But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die. Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lii Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waari iabuu Kɔraawiizi nuu.” Awia, ba ɛɛ gunla Moosis n baglɛɛ la.

ref: The Lord said to Aaron:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be,

ref: When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change.
text: “I ni i biizi gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ siŋ gɛɛ siŋkpega maa, di ii waa zuu n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia naa biini, di guŋ lɛi, ii daŋ siuzi. Kennaa chɔɔwɔɔ di hanna la di tɛɛ i ni i naanna maa.

ref: You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ii wer zum kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora ani anla n ɛɛ nɛra maa hora, ni anla n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be ani anla n waa doŋŋe u be.

ref: You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
text: A ɛɛ firaarɛ lugɔ ií bagli Izrɛl hina widaulaa la maa miŋ tɛɛ baa di lii Moosis be la.”

ref: Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar.
text: Moosis ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala Ɛliaza ni Itama la n kawɛɛ la be, “Ií kpa mbusu lizaa mia la baŋ wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi aŋhina ka la di ɔɔzi paanuu la baŋ wàá yiisi duwɛɛ la, di dia mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ a nanaananaa himmaa wia.

ref: The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place.
text: Ií dia bɔnaniinanii la biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ni ii biibaala maa diiribɔttɛ de, di lii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la. Gunnɛ u ŋɔ n ɛɛ.

ref: But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
text: Hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ ni bampirii la baŋ ɔɔ lalli chiŋ di viigi la, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpa nuuri bɔra la baŋ ɔɔ kpa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la ba, di wa lallaa chiŋ viigi Kɔraawiizi see, mbusu lizaa kuŋviigiire guŋ. Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii ni ii biizi bɔdiilii saŋa maa gunla Kɔraawiizi n baglɛɛ la.”

ref: When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
text: Denii Moosis n wa pɛɛzi wichɔgaa mbusu buuŋ la wia, di wa na lugɔ ba fuuuhbuu, u baaŋ fuuh Ɛliaza ni Itama, Aarɔn biibaala la n kawɛɛ la ni, u ŋɔ,

ref: “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt.
text: “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii waa wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuna la diwee, bɔnaniinanii la biinei? A ɛɛ naniinanii himmaanii. Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu tɛɛ ia ii kpa ra lizi a nɛra wichɔgaa mbusu u see, ú gil di ra tɛɛ baa.

ref: Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
text: Iiŋ waa u chal kpawɛɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini wia, a dɛkkɔɔ ii faa di a mbusu lizaa kuna la de, gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la.”

ref: Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
text: Aarɔn bir ŋɔ Moosis be, “A daŋ faa par Kɔraawiizi di n faa di a wichɔgaa mbusu naa zinaa? Zinaabuu ba lizi ba wichɔgaa mbusu, di lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ka keŋ wikuna haa vɛɛ ba n be.”

ref: Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
text: Moosis n wa nuu guŋ, a paruu.

ref: any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud.
text: Ií daŋ wer di sel la maa n dɔɔ naafiraa la n bargɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ka u ug di ra hee.

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: You may eat
text: “Ií ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, dí sela la maa n du hɛri naa biini, anniibuu dɛg dii.

ref: The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
text: Ka anla maa n dɔɔ keeri di dɔɔ naazi anaazu, ií ra kia.

ref: Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Nɛr la maa n wa gbɔgzi a siwaa daŋ chag u laala ka doŋ di ra ba duana. A doŋŋoo tɛɛ ia.

ref: Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean.
text: jaza, bajagu, ger, saliŋgbalee ani kaliŋgboŋa.

ref: Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening.
text: Anniibuu ií ra kii, di nɛr maa wa gbɔgzi a siwaa, u doŋŋoo di ra ba duana.

ref: If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening.
text: Di bɛl maa wa siuwɔ chol kummaa ni, huma la maa baŋ kpau di ra hum, di daarɛ, hɔnnɛ, wɛjɛɛ gɛɛ gbɔglɔnnɛ, ka u doŋŋoo di tɛɛ ia. Ií kpau du nii biini, u daŋ doŋ di ra ba duana, ka jaa du wer.

ref: If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean.
text: Di bɛl maa wa chol vii biini, a vii ni kuna la maa n du u biini doŋŋoo, a dɛkkɔɔ ií purguu.

ref: If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
text: Diwii la maa iin niŋ di, di u dɔɔ nii u ni di lii a keŋ vii biini, u doŋŋoo. Kunnyɔɔlii la maa iin niŋ nyɔɔ lii u biini doŋŋoo.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed.
text: Di kunsiwii wa chol kummaa ni, u doŋŋoo, di dalaarɛ gɛɛ viire, ií purguu.

ref: A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean.
text: Bule gɛɛ kɔlɔŋ waa maa nii waa doŋŋe, ka di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi kunsiwaa naa bɛl maa doŋŋoo.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean.
text: Di kunsiwii wa gbɔgzi kundee la maa ban niŋ duu, a waa doŋŋe.

ref: But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
text: Di ii ɛɛ nii siŋ kundee ka annii bɛl maa u siwii chol a ni, a doŋŋoo.

ref: If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening.
text: Sel la maa iiŋ waa kii, di u siuwɔ ka nɛr maa gbɔgzuu, u doŋŋoo di ra ba duana.

ref: If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Nɛr la maa wa diu daŋ chag u kuna, ka doŋ di ra ba duana. Nɛr la maa wa kpa u siwii daŋ chag u kuna ka doŋ di ra ba duana.

ref: Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di kuntuuzii maa, di u ra tuuzi u hia ninɛɛ gɛɛ di u ra vol naazi anaazu ninɛɛ gɛɛ naakpila ninɛɛ u ra vol, ií ra kia.

ref: If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di annii bɛl maa, di wàá doŋ iihinaa n be. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra doŋ iihinaa.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. Ií lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kuna la maa n na tuuzi hɛri di doŋ iihinaa.

ref: I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri, ii ɛɛ nɛra la n na humiŋ. Awia, ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ.

ref: I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ii ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di ra bargi anla n doŋŋe, di ra lii anla n waa doŋŋe ni, di kaa ra bargi sela la iin ninna di ani anla iiŋ wàá ra di.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di haaŋ wa kpogli hia di wa lul biibaal, u daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, gunla uŋ ɔɔ doŋ u baagu maa doŋa ɛɛi biini la.

ref: Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day,
text: A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, bá teŋ a bie hɛŋ.

ref: Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another
text: Di biihaannɛ u lul, a haaŋ daŋ doŋ yauzi anɛɛ, gunla uŋ ɔɔ doŋ u baagu maa doŋa ɛɛi biini la. Denii u kaa kpaŋ guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokkoahoro ni anumbɛl mɔɔ, ka bá lizi u doŋa lii u doŋa ɛɛi biini.

ref: When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Di a biibaal gɛɛ di a biihaaŋ doŋa lizaa hɔpizaa wa bɛrɔɔ, a haaŋ daŋ lizi pepɔl la n di biŋkpaŋ, di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, ú lizi mbusu di fuuuh. A haaŋ daŋ kpa koorikomma gɛɛ koŋaahmu jaa, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor.

ref: After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ a haaŋ. Denii ú doŋa jaa tuŋ n be. Anniibuu ɛɛ haaŋ lulaa widaulaa, di u wa lul biibaal gɛɛ biihaaŋ.

ref: If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Ka di wàá wer na pepɔl, u daŋ lizi koorikommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ, bɛl ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor. Kenne n kizeehiŋ ɛɛ di lizi u wichɔgaa ha, ú doŋa jaa tuŋ.”

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be,

ref: If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests.
text: “Di nɛr maa bɔra wa dɔɔ ŋmɛra gɛɛ kunsɔna gɛɛ kisafa a ra buu, ba kpogluu ba Aarɔn la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ gɛɛ u biibaal bɛl maa be.

ref: If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ binni u ŋmɛr la na nɛnnɛ, di huna la n du a ŋmɛr biini la wa huuhzɔɔ, ka a ŋmɛr ge du luŋ di ɛɛ chofoo, u ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuuliire. Di n kizeehiŋ wa binnuu na nɛnnɛ tuŋ, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ a hiŋ doŋŋoo n be.

ref: But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Di a bɔr huuhzɔɔrɛ ka waa chofoo duwɛɛ, de ge huna waa bittɛ huuhzi, n kizeehiŋ daŋ gil a guŋ hiŋ ga du u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, n kizeehiŋ la kaa binnuu na, di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ a ŋmɛr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa, ka u haa gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ kaa.

ref: Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ híŋ, n kizeehiŋ kaa la ga binnuu na, di a ŋmɛr jaa waa hil, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa ge, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa kaa doŋ, kisafa bɛnnɛ. A baal daŋ chag u laala, wàá ka doŋ n be.

ref: However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest.
text: Di a kisafa kaa wa lii u bɔra maa, a dɛkkɔɔ u kaa kpa u hiŋ ga bagli n kizeehiŋ la.

ref: If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: U daŋ kaa binnuu na, di a kisafa wa lii u bɔra maa, u daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire.

ref: Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest.
text: Di nɛr la maa wa dɔɔ bɔchɔgaa la n na buu, bá kpogluu ba n kizeehiŋ la be.

ref: If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white,
text: U daŋ binnuu nɛnnɛ, di u bɔra yemmaa wa ɔttɔ di huuhzi de huna ge bir huuhzi di du nii,

ref: he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.”
text: u birgi zallaarɛ, u daŋ ŋɔ ú doŋŋoo, wiilbuuliire. U gilɛɛ waa gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u teŋ doŋŋoo.

ref: But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: n kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di a wiila wa lii u bɔra maa, u daŋ ŋɔ a hiŋ waa doŋŋe. Dikuu a maa n bittɛ huuhzi wia, waa doŋŋe.

ref: If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Di n kizeehiŋ wa na a ŋmɛr, u daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo. A ŋmɛr doŋŋoo, u dɔɔ wiilbuuliire.

ref: However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu na, di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ a ŋmɛr wa hillɔɔ di huuhzi, u daŋ ŋɔ a wiila hiŋ waa doŋŋe, denii u jaa ŋɔ u doŋa tunnɔɔ.

ref: If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest.
text: di bɔhɔglii maa kaa wa lii bɔr la a ŋmɛrbinaa n faa duwɛɛ la di huuhzi gɛɛ di aah tama, ú kpa u hiŋ di ga bagli n kizeehiŋ.

ref: If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: U daŋ binni de nɛnnɛ di na, di de du chofoo ka de huna bir huuhzi, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo. U ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuuliire di pozi lii bɔr la a ŋmɛrbinaa la n faa ɔttɛ la.

ref: But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Ka di n kizeehiŋ la wa binnuu nɛnnɛ di na lugɔ a de huna waa huuhzɛɛ waa kaa du chofoo, ka ra hil, guŋwaa, u daŋ gil ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ guŋŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.”
text: Di u waa lii u bɔrahɔŋ maa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo, wiilbuuliire.

ref: But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
text: Ka di a bɔr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u yemmaa, guŋwaa, a ŋmɛrbinaa la pɛllɛ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ waa doŋŋe.

ref: If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white,
text: Di kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ wa baari nɛr maa, de aah gɛɛ di huuhzi,

ref: a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.”
text: n kizeehiŋ daŋ binni a bɔr nɛnnɛ, di a de huna wa bittɔ huuhzi a ŋmɛr ge du chofoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuulii la n pozee lii a bɔr la kuna n baareere. U daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ a hiŋ doŋŋoo. U ɛɛ wiilbuuliire.

ref: But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Ka di u wa binni de di na di de huna waa huuhzɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ka ra hil, guŋwaa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ ú gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binnuu na nɛnnɛ, di u wàá lii u bɔra maa, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ u doŋŋoo.

ref: However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
text: Aŋhinabe di a bɔr waa chɛttɛ, waa kaa lii u bɔra yemmaa, ka hil, u ɛɛ kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ baaraa ɔraarɛ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe. U ɛɛ pɛl bɛnnɛ di lii a kuŋwema gɛɛ niŋ baaraa la biini.

ref: If you have a sore on your head or chin,
text: Di baal gɛɛ haaŋ wa dɔɔ ŋmɛr u nyuu gɛɛ u hama ni,

ref: it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binni a ŋmɛr na nɛnnɛ, di u wa du chofoo, de huna aah lugɔ susau ka du ginini, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u doŋŋoo, u ɛɛ wiilbuuliire.

ref: On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Ka di u wa binni a ŋmɛr na, di waa chofoo duwɛɛ, di huŋbiŋŋe waa u biini duwɛɛ, guŋwaa, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ gil a hindee ga du u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep,
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, u daŋ binni a ŋmɛr, di a ŋmɛr waa u bɔra maa liwɛɛ, huŋaahma lugɔ susau waa u biini liwɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ge,

ref: you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: a dɛkkɔɔ bá fuŋ a hiŋ ka ka a bɔr bɛŋ, n kizeehiŋ la gil ú bir gaa zuu u bɛŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kaa binni a ŋmɛr na hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, di waa u bɔra maa liwɛɛ, waa kaa du chofoo ge, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ ŋɔ waa doŋŋe. A wiila hiŋ daŋ chag u laala, denii u doŋa tuŋ.

ref: Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.”
text: n kizeehiŋ la daŋ binnuu di na, di a ŋmɛr wa lii u bɔra maa, ú gilɛɛ kaa wàá nyiŋŋi huŋsusau, a hiŋ doŋŋoo.

ref: But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: Ka di u wa binnɔɔ di na lugɔ a ŋmɛr waa chɛttɛ, huŋbiŋŋe lii de, a de tunnɔɔ, waa doŋŋe. N kizeehiŋ daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ waa doŋŋe.

ref: If white spots break out on your skin,
text: Di baal gɛɛ haaŋ bɔra wa dɔɔ bɔhuŋŋa parapara,

ref: but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: n kizeehiŋ daŋ binni baa di na, di a wa du fululu, a waa wiilchɔgii la n lii u bɔrahɔŋ ni ɛɛwɛ, a hiŋ waa doŋŋe.

ref: If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean.
text: Di u hile magaa wa gbawɛɛ, waa doŋŋe.

ref: But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say,
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ binnuu nɛnnɛ, di a ŋmɛr ɔttɔɔ di du u nyuu gɛɛ u hile ni di aah ka huuhzi, di ɛɛ lugɔ wiilbuulii,

ref: If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!”

text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpaa lizi mbusu, bɛl ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii hor. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi a haaŋ doŋa tɛu, Kɔraawiizi see.

ref: When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
text: Ií gil Izrɛl hina ni kuna la n doŋŋe bargi dɔŋa ni, bá gilɛɛ waa siu ni doŋa di wàá doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la n du ii be la.’ ”

ref: These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
