ref: Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron: I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
text: “Ŋɔ i kpɛɛma Aarɔn be lugɔ ú ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la n du patiisazeŋ la harbɔɔ la n du N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ nɛra ni la see, u kipar saŋa, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ siu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɔɔ du baama la n guali mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa nɛra ni dakka la tɔa ninɛɛ.

ref: Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me.
text: Kenne Aarɔn ɔɔ ɛɛ di zuu a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la. U daŋ ɔɔ kpa nabalee di wa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di kpa pebal ge ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii.

ref: You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban.
text: U daŋ kpa u tagtajaŋnaniinanii la di laali, ka kpa u galŋa n ɔɔ ra chug u naahiine la di du. Di kpa u kirsɔɔ di kirsi, di vɔɔ namu. Annii ɛɛ bɔmbɔgnanaananaarɛ. Awia, ú ɔɔ sɔ nii mɔɔ ka laalaa.

ref: Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
text: Izrɛl hina daŋ lau bubala anɛɛ tɛɛ Aarɔn, ú lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di kaa lau pebal ge ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii.

ref: Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family.
text: Aarɔn daŋ ɔɔ kpa nabal di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di sɛɛ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tɛɛ u ni u diahina maa.

ref: Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent,
text: Denii ú kpa buuna anɛɛ la di tɛŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel.
text: U daŋ ta kuna dikuu buuna anɛɛ la wia, dí zum unla un niŋ kpu tɛŋ ani unla ban niŋ pur ha, ú chi ba wichɔgaa kaali.

ref: After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin,
text: Aarɔn daŋ kpa buuŋ la baŋ ta kuna lizi tɛŋ la, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu.

ref: the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
text: Ka kpa unla ban ta kuna lizi, u ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih lizaa hor la, di tɛŋ nyinii, ka puruu ha ú wer kpa a nɛra wichɔgaa di chɔ kaali hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family.
text: Di Aarɔn wa kpu nabal la di sɛɛ u ni u diahina chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be tuŋ,

ref: Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place.
text: u daŋ buu niŋ di lii mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n see la di su kunla baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la di ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la n ɛɛ kɔlɔlɔlɔ nonii suul bunɛɛ dí kpaa zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la biini, patiisa la harbɔɔ.

ref: There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there!
text: Denii ú jaa kpa a daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la di du niŋ la biini n see, a nyɔɔzi izi di tɔ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ nɛra ni la ni, ú gilɛɛ wa nau di siu.

ref: Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonibii di lii a nabal chal di mizi a tua la see, di kaa kpa a yeŋ di mizi N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see buniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
text: Denii ú jaa kpu buuŋ la ge di lizi a nɛra wichɔgaa mbusu, dí kpa u chal di zuu a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa dí mizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi n baaŋ u ni la see, gunla himmaa uŋ mizi nabal la chal la.

ref: By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people.
text: Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi a Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la doŋa ha dikuu Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa ni ba dignikpega n chɔguu la wia. U daŋ ɛɛ guŋ himmaa di tɛɛ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u chigɔ a nɛra la doŋŋe chɔɔribɔr la baambaannɛ.

ref: After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat.
text: Aarɔn daŋ jaa lii di ba mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, di wa kpa a nabal ni a buuŋ challi yeŋa di faa de nyigzi la di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih de gba ni.

ref: Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
text: Ka kpa u nonibii di lii a chal di mizi mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ buniidaanɛɛ. Kenne ú ɛɛ di lizi de doŋa la Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa n gillɛ u doŋ la ha, ka ú kaa ɛɛ naniinanii.

ref: After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent.
text: Denii Aarɔn n wa lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la ni n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la ani mbusu lizibɔr la ni di tuŋ, ú kpogli bunyinii la di ba, ba see.

ref: There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins.
text: U daŋ kpa u nonee sag a buuŋ nyuu ni, di sɛɛ Izrɛl hina biinikpola ni dignikpega ani ba wichɔgaa maa chɔgri di du u ni. Denii ú lizi nɛbɛl ú duŋŋuu du hɛribɔduma biini,

ref: Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
text: di ga giluu de, a buuŋ chi a nɛra wichɔgaa la di kaali bɔr la nɛra n waa duwɛɛ.

ref: Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people.
text: U daŋ sɔ nii bɔnaniinanii biini, ka kpa ú hɔpizi biimaa laala di laali. Denii u jaa lii di wa lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ u hiŋ ni a nɛra maa, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni.

ref: The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
text: U daŋ fuuh wichɔgaa mbusu sel la nuu mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp.
text: Baal la n duŋŋi buuŋ la di du hɛribɔduma la, a dɛkkɔɔ ú chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka jaa wer zuu chɔɔribɔr la biini.

ref: The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ií kpa wichɔgaa mbusu nabal la ni buuŋ la challi baŋ kpawɛɛ zuu Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa biini la, di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih mbusu la, di lii chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia, di fuuah. A hɔna, a ola ani a biini kuna maa.

ref: And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp. The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ baal la n fuuah la, chag u laala di sɔ nii, ka jaa wer zuu chɔɔribɔr la biini.

ref: On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work.
text: A kennaa daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ia di hanna la. Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fihiŋ hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ Izrɛl hinuu ni hɔɔhri maa n soge ii be vɔɔ nua, di gilɛɛ waa hum huma.

ref: This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence,
text: A hɔl hinnɛ bá lizi ii wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ ia di lizi ii doŋa ha. Denii ii wichɔgaa doŋa jaa tuŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath.
text: U ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ, a dɛg lugɔ ií vɔɔ nuuzi. U ɛɛ widauliirɛ di tɛɛ ia di hanna la.

ref: He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community.
text: di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia, mbusu lizibɔr la, N Dia kizeehina ani a nɛra maa ni.

ref: You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel. Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
text: Kennaa daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ia di hanna la. Bina maa, kakpannɛ ií ɔɔ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, dikuu Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa maa wia.” Ba ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
text: “Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa be,

ref: Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: di waa u ni ballɛ lɛi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua ú wa lizi mbusu tɛŋ, a baal ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. U bizi challɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa a challi di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la n chigɛ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua kɛraa, ka fuuh a nuu a ɛɛ sɔɔh la n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere
text: Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa n soge ba be, wa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii gɛɛ mbusu maa,

ref: except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people. Do Not Eat Blood The Lord said:
text: ka wɔɔ kpawɛɛ ba mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di wa kpuu tɛŋ, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you.
text: Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri bɛl maa n jaa ba ni di so gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa ni u chal, n daŋ bir har kpuu di duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, sel maa miibɔɔ du u chal biinii, n kpaa tɛɛ ia, ii kpaa di ra lizi mbusu di ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih nɛra ni. Chal ɛɛ miibɔɔrɛ di ra lizi nɛra wichɔgaa ba ni.

ref: Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
text: Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri bɛl maa n soge ba be haŋ wa la kpaana, di ga kpu sel gɛɛ zumbee maa banna di, ú kɔrguu ú chal lii, ú ɛɛ hɛɛhraa tɔ a ni.

ref: The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, sel maa miibɔɔrɛ ú chal. Awiarɛ n na ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa hee sel maa chal, dikuu sel maa miibɔɔ n ɛɛ u chal wia, di nɛr maa haŋ wa heea, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Nɛr la maa n ɛɛ Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa, haŋ wa di kunla maa n siuwɛ gɛɛ pir sela n kpuwɛɛ, daŋ chag u laala ka sɔ nii, ka doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be di ra ba duana, denii ú doŋa jaa tuŋ.

ref: If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
text: Ka di waa u kuna chakkɛ di sɔ nii, u daŋ di guŋ tɔɔrɔɔ.’ ”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to tell the people of Israel: I am the Lord your God!
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, dí Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá ɛɛ Ijip hina la iiŋ faa du ba be la wiɛɛlaa, di gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ Keenan la miŋ kpogli ia di ra la la hina wiɛɛlaa.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings.
text: Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni widaulaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: Don't have sex with any of your close relatives,
text: Nɛr maa ni u lulli himmaa gilɛɛ waa chɔɔ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá gbɛlli i mɛɛ di lau u haaŋ nyiŋŋi. I maarɛ, gilɛɛ wa lawuu ra nyiŋŋi.

ref: And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives.
text: Gilɛɛ wa lau i mɛɛ haaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ i mɛɛ gbɛllaa.

ref: Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá lau i niuhambie di ra nyiŋŋi, di i mɛɛ biere gɛɛ i maa biere, gɛɛ di ba luluubuu ii dia biini gɛɛ yembɛl gba.

ref: Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter
text: Gilɛɛ wàá lau i naana di ra nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, a guŋ daŋ gil ba ra gbɛllii.

ref: Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá gbɛlli i mɛɛbee gɛɛ i mɛɛzeŋ di lau u haaŋ nyiŋŋi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ i maarɛ.

ref: And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá lau haaŋ ni u biihaaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi. Gilɛɛ waa nyiŋŋi u naanna. Dikuu baŋ ɛɛ u lulla himmaa wia. Guŋ ɛɛ biinikpolaa.

ref: As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá kpa i haaŋ kpɛɛma gɛɛ u niwee di ra ɛɛ haaŋ, di i haaŋ haa du de ni miibɔɔ.

ref: When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá lau haaŋ maa di ra nyiŋŋi, di u ra ɛɛ doŋa.

ref: Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá nyiŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ, guŋ daŋ chɔgii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá lau i bie maa di ra tɛɛ ba lizi mbusu ra tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa dɛkkɛ hiŋ chɔg mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá nyiŋŋi baal gunla baal n ɔɔ nyiŋŋi haaŋ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hah gunnɛ werge.

ref: Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves
text: Ií gilɛɛ kpa annii bɛl maa di ra doŋ iihinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, gunnɛ banla min niŋ duŋŋi ii sibɔɔ la ɛɛ di doŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu nɛra la n faa du a hɛri naa biini, mɔɔ ka ii haa ba la faa ra ɛɛ, a hɛri faa doŋ.

ref: Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them.
text: Di ii haŋ wa doŋ a hɛri, u daŋ vɛɛ ia gunla uŋ faa vɛɛ banla n faa du de mɔɔ la.

ref: If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
text: Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wikuna la nɛra la n faa du ɛŋ mɔɔ, ka ií ba la n faa ra ɛɛ la. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra doŋ iihinaa. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too!
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina maa be, ‘Ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ.

ref: Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá vɛɛŋ ka bir di ra kuari vuga gɛɛ di wa kpa lugbia ŋmɛɛri kuari vuga, di ra sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions.
text: Di ii wa kpu sel di lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ií lizuu di hiŋ n widaulaa la miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la, guŋ gil n lɛɛu.

ref: You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day.
text: Ií daŋ hee u maa a hɔl la maa iiŋ kpuu la gɛɛ u hɔpizaa anɛɛ hɔl di tuŋ. Ka di u yemmaa wa kawɔɔ ú hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, a dɛkkɔɔ ií fuuuh.

ref: If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it.
text: Ka di ii wa hee u yemmaa a hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, u doŋŋoo, màá lɛɛ a mbusu lizaa.

ref: In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Nɛr la maa wa heeu daŋ di bilchɔg, dikuu uŋ kpa kunnaniinanii la baŋ tɛŋ di birgi kumpɛɛ wia. Ií duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground.
text: Di ii waa kum ii kooliŋkuna, ii gilɛɛ waa kumaa di ra hel ii kooni nuuzi gɛɛ di bir har di ra kugnaa.

ref: Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa bir har di ra tɔrgi ii grepu kooni daazi nɔna bunɛɛ gɛɛ di wàá paagi anla n choglee. Ií gilaa tɛɛ nyaara ni hɔɔhra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra ŋmɛɛ. Ií gilɛɛ ra kanni kara. Ií gilɛɛ ra dar dɔŋa.

ref: Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi, di ra kanni kara di ra chɔg Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum sɔŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá fini gɛɛ di ra ŋmɛɛ ii dɔŋahina. Ií gilɛɛ wàá vɛɛ ii paahdiiri turgaa di ra ba hɔpizaa.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá see gɛnii nua gɛɛ di wa kpa kuŋ di ra tɔ nyuŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ ú wàá garguu. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, ií ra ɔmiŋ.

ref: Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
text: Ií ra di wibii di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa di nyaara seriya ni nɔŋŋaa gɛɛ di ra ɔm dɔɔna, ka ɔɔ ra di ii dɔŋahina seriya ni wibii.

ref: Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gaagi di ra kanni kara la n niŋ chɔg ii dɔŋahina nɛra biini. Ií gilɛɛ wàá ɛɛ wii la maa n niŋ lizi ii dɔŋahina miibɔɔni. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting.
text: Ií gilɛɛ hah ii dɔŋahina ii bampiree biine. Ka ii ɔɔ ra di baa wibii di gilɛɛ waa gil ba wichɔgaa ra buu ia.

ref: Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa bir kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgi ii dɔŋahina wichɔgaa kim gɛɛ di hah ba, ka nɔŋŋi baa gunla iin nɔŋŋi ii hina la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
text: Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa. Ií gilɛɛ gil sel maa wàá deezi ú duma maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa kundee irizi anɛɛ di ra duu koo kpaŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa laali sisaawa.

ref: If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time.
text: Di baal lau yoŋhaaŋ baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baal ka u haa waa u kim turgee, gɛɛ ba haa wɔɔ tawɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ u dɔɔ u hiŋ di nyiŋŋi. Ií tɔɔri baa ka gilɛɛ waa kpu baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u haa waa u hiŋ dɔɔwɛ.

ref: The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpa a pebal, di lizi bilchɔg mbusu di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih, ń gil a baal wichɔgaa tɛu.

ref: After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years.
text: Di ii wa zuu Keenan hɛri di duu daa maa n na nɔŋ, ií ra kii u nɔna binni ahoro, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo n be.

ref: In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks
text: Ií daŋ kpa u binni anaazuhiŋ nɔna di wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, á ɛɛ a nanaananaa, di ɛɛ chɔlaa mbusu hora.

ref: to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
text: Ka u binni anuehiŋ biini waa, ii daŋ jaa wer di u nɔna. Di ii ɛɛ annii naa maa, ii daazi daŋ ɔɔ nɔŋ werge. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: Don't eat the blood of any animal. Don't practice any kind of witchcraft.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wàá hee ol la chal n haa du u ni. Ií gilɛɛ wàá vug gɛɛ di ra di hiri.

ref: I forbid you to shave any part of your head or beard or to cut and tattoo yourself as a way of worshiping the dead.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa kuu lalii wia di ra mɔnni gɛɛ di ra zɛuzi ii bɔra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't let your daughters serve as temple prostitutes—this would bring disgrace both to them and the land.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli ii biihaana di gil ba birgi sɛnsɛnna. Di ii haŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ, a hɛri maa daŋ su ni sɛnsɛŋ ni biinikpola.

ref: I command you to respect the Sabbath and the place where I am worshiped.
text: Ií ra di n Heezaa Hɔpizii la di ra tɔgzi n jaami bɔr la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't make yourselves disgusting to me by going to people who claim they can talk to the dead.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra la vugra gɛɛ ijɔzi be, ba ra bagli ia wia ŋmɛnizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ gil ii doŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: I command you to show respect for older people and to obey me with fear and trembling.
text: Ií ra ɔmiŋ, di ra tɔgzi nabɔnzi, di ra kpa baa girme. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't mistreat any foreigners who live in your land.
text: Di hɔɔhri wa sogo ii hɛri, ií gilɛɛ ra diŋzuu.

ref: Instead, treat them as well as you treat your own people and love them as much as you love yourself. Remember, you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
text: Ií ra ɛɛ hɔɔhri la maa n soge ii be lugɔ ii biilullii. Ií nɔŋŋuu alugɔ ii dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ge gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: Use honest scales and don't cheat when you weigh or measure anything. I am the Lord your God. I rescued you from Egypt,
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa mɛgzaa kuna la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ kookoo tassazi ni galɔnzi di ra mɛgzi kuna. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, minuu kpogli ia di lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: and I command you to obey my laws.
text: Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa maa. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: Death by stoning is the penalty for any citizens or foreigners in the country who sacrifice their children to the god Molech.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di Izrɛl hinuu maa gɛɛ hɔɔhri maa n na zuu Izrɛl hɛri, haŋ wa kpa u bie lizi mbusu tɛɛ vug la banna yir Mɔlɛk la, ií paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu.

ref: They have disgraced both the place where I am worshiped and my holy name, and so I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people.
text: N daŋ lizi siwii sag a guŋ hiŋ ni, di duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini. Dikuu uŋ kpa u biizi tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk wia, u doŋ N Tanti Diarɛ, di kaa chɔg n sɔnnanii.

ref: Some of you may let them get away with human sacrifice,
text: Di u ɛɛ guŋ, ka a nɛra siigi di giluu, ba wɔɔ kpuwɛɛ,

ref: but not me. If any of you worship Molech, I will turn against you and your entire family, and I will no longer let you belong to my people.
text: n himmaa daŋ lizi siwii sag u ni u diahina ni, di duŋŋi banla maa n chigɛ u har, di nyaa wibii n be, di ra jaami vug Mɔlɛk la, di lii ba nɛra biine.

ref: I will be your enemy if you go to someone who claims to speak with the dead, and I will destroy you from among my people.
text: N daŋ lizi siwii sag nɛr la maa n niŋ la vugra ni ijɔzi be, di nyaa wibii n be, n daŋ duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini.

ref: Dedicate yourselves to me and be holy because I am the Lord your God.
text: Ií sɔ iihinaa di lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: I have chosen you as my people, and I expect you to obey my laws.
text: Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa nɛnnɛ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n ɔɔ gil ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.

ref: If you curse your father or mother, you will be put to death, and it will be your own fault.
text: Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa see u mɛɛ gɛɛ u maa nua, ií kpuu, u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u ni.

ref: If any of you men have sex with another man's wife, both you and the woman will be put to death.
text: Di baal maa nyiŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ, ií kpu ba maa.

ref: Having sex with one of your father's wives disgraces him. So both you and the woman will be put to death, just as you deserve.
text: Di baal maa wa nyiŋŋi u mɛɛ haaŋ, u gbɛlli u mɛɛrɛ. Ií kpu a baal ni a haaŋ maa. Ba wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.

ref: It isn't natural to have sex with your daughter-in-law, and both of you will be put to death, just as you deserve.
text: Di baal maa nyiŋŋi u biibaal haaŋ, ií kpu ba maa. Ba ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, awia ba wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi ba ni.

ref: It's disgusting for men to have sex with one another, and those who do will be put to death, just as they deserve.
text: Di baal haŋ wa lau u dɔŋ baal di chɔɔ gunla baal n ɔɔ chɔɔ haaŋ la, ba maa banɛɛ la ɛɛ wikunaa. Ií kpu baa, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.

ref: It isn't natural for a man to marry both a woman and her daughter, and so all three of them will be burned to death.
text: Di baal haŋ wa kpa bie ni u màá maa kpau di ɛɛ u haana, guŋ ɛɛ biinikpolaa. Ií fuuh u ni a haana maa, guŋ gil biinikpola wàá du ii be.

ref: If any of you have sex with an animal, both you and the animal will be put to death, just as you deserve.
text: Di haaŋ wa gillɔ sel nyiŋŋuu, ii kpu a haaŋ ni a sel maa, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.

ref: If you marry one of your sisters, you will be punished, and the two of you will be disgraced by being openly forced out of the community.
text: Di baal haŋ wa kpa u mɛɛ biihaaŋ gɛɛ u maa biihaaŋ, di nyiŋŋuu, a ɛɛ hiihzii werge maa. Ií duŋŋi baa di lii ii biini. U binni u niuhambie labuu pɛɛ, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.

ref: If you have sex with a woman during her monthly period, both you and the woman will be cut off from the people of Israel.
text: Di baal haŋ wa lau haaŋ la maa n na ɛɛ u baagu doŋa di nyiŋŋi, ií duŋŋi baa ii biini, dikuubɛɛwiai ba chɔg kuŋ doŋaa Gbɔgnii.

ref: The sisters of your father and mother are your own relatives, and you will be punished for having sex with any of them.
text: Gilɛɛ wa lau i nyaana gɛɛ maazeŋ gɛɛ i maabie di ra nyiŋŋi, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ ii lulli gbɛllaa. Ii nɛra banɛɛ la maa daŋ turgi a kim.

ref: If you have sex with your uncle's wife, neither you nor she will ever have any children.
text: Di baal maa haŋ wa lau u naara haaŋ nyiŋŋi, u gbɛlli u naaraa. A baal ni a haaŋ daŋ turgi a kim. Ba daŋ wa siuzi di ba waa biizi lullɛ.

ref: Obey my laws and teachings. Or else the land I am giving you will become sick of you and throw you out.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa, di wer du hɛri la minna la ii ni la biini.

ref: The nations I am chasing out did these disgusting things, and I hated them for it, so don't follow their example.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hiŋ hɛssi la hina minna duŋŋi ka ii zuu de la naana wia. Dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu ba faa ra ɛɛ, n kii baa la.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I have promised you their land that is rich with milk and honey. I have chosen you to be different from other people.
text: Ií ra nuu n be, ‘N daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ. U summɔɔ di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge.’ Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, unla n lizi ia, ii kur hɛssi hina maa ni la.

ref: That's why you must make a difference between animals and birds that I have said are clean and unclean—this will keep you from becoming disgusting to me.
text: Awia, ií zum sela ni zumbizi la n waa doŋŋe ni anla n doŋŋe. Ií gilɛɛ waa di a sedoŋa gɛɛ zumbidoŋa gɛɛ kunla maa n na tuuzi hɛri di ra doŋ iihinaa.

ref: I am the Lord, the holy God. You have been chosen to be my people, and so you must be holy too.
text: Ií ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, di lizi ia ií kur hɛssi hina maa ni, dí ɛɛ n hora.

ref: If you claim to receive messages from the dead, you will be put to death by stoning, just as you deserve.
text: Baal gɛɛ haaŋ la maa n ɛɛ vugri gɛɛ ijɔ di du ii biini, ií paagi bia lɔɔzi baa kpuuzi, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi ba ni.”

ref: The Lord gave Moses these instructions for Aaron's sons, the priests: Touching a dead body will make you unclean. So don't go near a dead relative,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Ŋɔ Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ N Dia kizeehina la be, lugɔ bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa doŋ u hiŋ, u lulli lee wia biini.

ref: or an unmarried sister, who has no husband to take care of her.
text: gɛɛ u niuhambie la n waa yuuwɛ ka du u be lɛi.

ref: Don't make yourself unclean by attending the funeral of someone related to you by marriage.
text: Ú gilɛɛ waa doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be dikuu lula yuuri wia.

ref: Don't shave any part of your head or trim your beard or cut yourself to show that you are mourning.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ n kizeehiŋ maa n na fuŋ u nyuu ni u taŋhuna kɛraa gɛɛ di wàá mɔnni u bɔra.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I have chosen you alone to offer sacrifices of food to me on the altar. That's why you must keep yourselves holy.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii, di gilɛɛ waa chɔg n sɔŋ. Dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu ɔɔ ra kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa la n ɛɛ n diwee la di ra tɛŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ ú ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii.

ref: Don't marry a divorced woman or a woman who has served as a temple prostitute. You are holy,
text: A waa dɛkkɛ n kizeehiŋ n kpa hahsɛnsɛnni gɛɛ suŋguru la n zum baal gɛɛ haaŋ la n yuuwɛ ka ka, di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ nɛnaniinaniirɛ.

ref: because I am holy. And so, you must be treated with proper respect, since you offer food sacrifices to me, the God of holiness.
text: Ií zum lugɔ u ɛɛ nɛnaniinaniirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu kpa míŋ̀ Kɔraawiizi diwee di ra tɛŋ. Ií ra tɔgzuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, di gil n nɛra ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.

ref: If any of you priests has a daughter who disgraces you by serving as a temple prostitute, she must be burned to death.
text: Di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ wa birgi sɛnsɛnni di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, u kpa hiihzii kpu u mɛɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ií fuuh a biihaaŋ.

ref: If you are the high priest, you must not mess up your hair or tear your clothes in order to mourn for the dead.
text: N Kizeehina Nabɔma la baŋ lizɛɛ u lulla biini di waaruu nuu u ra bɔg kizeehiŋ bɔmbɔga la, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u nyuu chaazaa gɛɛ di wàá piili u bɔmbɔga, dikuu unna wii lee wia.

ref: Don't make yourself unclean by going near a dead body, not even that of your own father or mother.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ ú wàá zuu bɔr la lalii n chɔɔwɛ. A waa dɛkkɛ un doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, haali di u mɛɛrɛ gɛɛ u maarɛ gba,

ref: If you leave the sacred place to attend a funeral, both you and the sacred place become unclean, because you are the high priest.
text: gɛɛ di waa lii N Tanti Dia la gɛɛ di waa doŋuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba lizuubuu di kpa n nuu waaruu. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: If you are the high priest, you must marry only a virgin
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ú kpa haaŋ la n waa baal zummɛ.

ref: from your own tribe. Don't marry a divorced woman or any other woman who has already had sex, including a temple prostitute.
text: Ú gilɛɛ waa kpa luhaaŋ gɛɛ haaŋ la n yuuwɛ ka ka, gɛɛ haaŋ la n kpa sɛnsɛŋ di doŋ u hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, see haaŋ la n waa baal zummɛ di lii u himmaa nɛra biini.

ref: In this way, your descendants will be qualified to serve me. Remember—I am the Lord, and I have chosen you.
text: Guŋ gilɛɛ gil ú wàá doŋ u biizi di lii u himmaa nɛra biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii gillɛ u ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to Aaron: No descendant of yours can ever serve as my priest if he is blind or lame, if his face is disfigured, if one leg is shorter than the other,
text: Baal la maa n waa kpeg gilɛɛ waa dugliŋ, di u nyuŋŋɔɔrɛ gɛɛ u naa gɛɛ u nonii siuwɔɔ,

ref: if either a foot or a hand is paralyzed,
text: gɛɛ baal la maa n dɔɔ naasiwii gɛɛ nosiwii

ref: if he is a hunchback or a dwarf, if an eye or his skin is diseased, or if his testicles have been damaged.
text: gɛɛ gee hiŋ gɛɛ kirbii gɛɛ unla n dɔɔ siwiila gɛɛ di dɔɔ ŋmɛr la na wii nii gɛɛ nɛr la lurbee n chɔkkɛ.

ref: but they may not enter the sacred place or serve me at the altar. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes a priest holy.
text: ka uŋ waa kpeg la wia, a waa dɛkkɛ unna dugli n Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa patiisa la gɛɛ di wàá la mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ, di gilɛɛ waa doŋ n Tanti Dia la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu gillɛ ba ɛɛ kunnanaananaa.’ ”

ref: Moses told all of this to Aaron, his sons, and the people of Israel.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ annii naa maa tɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to Aaron and his sons: I am the Lord God, and I demand that you honor my holy name by showing proper respect for the offerings brought to me by the people of Israel.
text: “Kali Aarɔn ni u biibaala lugɔ ba ra tɔgzi mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la Izrɛl hina n kpawɛɛ waa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la, di gilɛɛ wàá chɔg n sɔnnaniinanii la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: None of you may take part in the sacred meals while you have a skin disease or an infected penis, or after you have been near a dead body or have had a flow of semen,
text: Di Aarɔn naana maa wa dɔɔ bɔrahɔŋ wiilbuulaa gɛɛ u hɛŋ na lul, ú gilɛɛ waa di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa di hanna la saŋa la ban niŋ lizi u doŋa ha. Di ba bɛl maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi kunla maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ lalii gɛɛ nɛr la maa banni n liwɛɛ, u doŋŋoo

ref: or if you have touched an unclean creature of any sort, including an unclean person.
text: gɛɛ di u wa gbɔgzi kuntuuzii maa gɛɛ nɛr la maa n doŋŋe.

ref: Once you are unclean, you must take a bath, but you still cannot eat any of the sacred food until evening.
text: Di wiizi wa chollo, wàá ka doŋ, u daŋ jaa wer di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa dikuu aŋ ɛɛ u kundiilaa wia.

ref: I command you not to eat anything that is killed by a wild animal or dies a natural death. This would make you unclean.
text: Bɛl maa gilɛɛ wàá di sel la maa n siuwɛ u hiŋ ni gɛɛ pir sela n lauwɛ, di wàá doŋ u hiŋ. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Obey me, or you will die on duty for disgracing the place of worship. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes a priest holy.
text: N Dia kizeehina la ra hiŋ n widaulaa la min dauwɛ tɛɛ baa la nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ chɔgri mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di wàá siuzi, dikuu baŋ gbɛlliŋ la wia. Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu gillɛ ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.

ref: Only you priests and your families may eat the food offerings; these are too sacred for any of your servants.
text: Nɛr la maa n wàá n kizeehiŋ biilullii ɛɛwɛ, gilɛɛ wàá di mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa, haali di u ɛɛ u hɔɔhrii gɛɛ u balii gbaa, ka ú gilɛɛ waa dia.

ref: However, any slave that you own, including those born into your household, may eat this food.
text: Ka di n kizeehiŋ kpa kebee yau yom, gɛɛ di ba lul yom u dia, a yom daŋ wer di u diwee.

ref: If your daughter marries someone who isn't a priest, she can no longer have any of this food.
text: Di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ yuu nɛr la n wan kizeehiŋ la ɛɛwɛ, ú gilɛɛ waa di mbusu lizaa kunnaananaa bɛl maa.

ref: But if she returns to your home, either widowed or divorced, and has no children, she may join in the meal. Only members of a priestly family can eat this food,
text: Ka di n kizeehiŋ biihaaŋ wa birgi luhaaŋ gɛɛ u jaari vɛɛu di wàá biizi dɔɔwɛ, u bir wa du u mɛɛ dia alugɔ u bichaluu saŋa la, u daŋ wer di u mɛɛ diwee. Nɛr la maa n waa dɛkkɛ, gilɛɛ waa dia.

ref: I warn you not to treat lightly the offerings that are brought by the people of Israel.
text: N Dia kizeehina gilɛɛ waa doŋ mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa

ref: Don't let them become guilty of eating this sacred food. Remember—I am the Lord, the one who makes these offerings holy. Acceptable Sacrifices
text: di wa gil ba ra dia, di wa kpa chɔgri ni dignitɛraa ra sag ba ni, a waa lɔ baa kim. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n gillɛ a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa.’ ”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to tell Aaron and his sons and everyone else the rules for offering sacrifices. He said: The animals that are to be completely burned on the altar
text: “Ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala ni Izrɛl hina maa be, ‘Di ii bɛl maa, di Izrɛl hinuurɛ gɛɛ hɔɔhrii du Izrɛl hɛri, di wa kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, di ra lizi nua gɛɛ u kipar mbusu,

ref: When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, there must be nothing wrong with the animal. This is true, whether the sacrifice is part of a promise or something you do voluntarily.
text: Di nɛr wa lizi nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ di lii lig biini, ú wa lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, di u kipar mbusu lizaarɛ gɛɛ di nua mbusu lizaarɛ, ú lizi unla n kpekke, ń wer lɛɛu.

ref: If one of your cattle or lambs has a leg that is longer or shorter than the others, you may offer it voluntarily, but not as part of a promise.
text: Ka ii daŋ wer lizi sel maa, di naurɛ gɛɛ peezi n zugmeere gɛɛ wàá kpeg, di ú ɛɛ ii kipar mbusu, ka màá lɛɛu di ii ra lizi nua waarɛ.

ref: As long as you live in this land, don't offer an animal with injured testicles.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa lizi sel la maa lure n forgee, baŋ chanzɛɛ, baŋ mɔnnɛɛ gɛɛ baŋ chahwɛɛ di ra tɛŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ ii hɛri biini.

ref: And don't bring me animals you bought from a foreigner. I won't accept them, because they are no better than one that has something wrong with it.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ a guŋ sela naa bɛl maa di ra lii hɔɔhri be di ra tɛŋ. Màá lɛɛa dikuu ii wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waa kpeg.’ ”

ref: The Lord told Moses to say:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: Newborn cattle, sheep, or goats must remain with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day, you may send them up in smoke to me, and I will accept the offering.
text: “Di nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ wa lullɔ, u biifula hiŋ daŋ du u maa be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Ka di jaa lii a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl waa, ii daŋ wer kpau lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't sacrifice a newborn animal and its mother on the same day.
text: Gilɛɛ waa kpu nau gɛɛ peezi ni u bie maa hɔpizikpaŋ.

ref: When you offer a sacrifice to give thanks to me, you must do it in a way that is acceptable.
text: Di ii haŋ wa kpu kummaa di ra jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ií kpuu gunla n dɛkkɛ ń wer lɛɛu.

ref: Eat all of the meat that same day and don't save any for the next day. I am the Lord your God!
text: Ií hee u maa a hɔl hiŋ, ií gilɛɛ waa gil u yemmaa hɔɔ ra pizi. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Obey my laws and teachings—I am the Lord.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ií ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: to say to the community of Israel: I have chosen certain times for you to come together and worship me.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Hɔpizizenaa la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali di ra di, di ra tɔgzi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii keŋ. Heezaa Hɔpizii wia

ref: You have six days when you can do your work, but the seventh day of each week is holy because it belongs to me. No matter where you live, you must rest on the Sabbath and come together for worship. This law will never change. Passover and the Festival of Thin Bread (Numbers
text: Hɔpizaa anumbɛllɛ ií ɔɔ kpa di hum huma, ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ iin niŋ ɔɔ kpa di chaali di jaami. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa bɔr la maa iin niŋ du, u ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Gillikaali ni Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa wia

ref: No one is to work on that day—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness, when sacrifices will be offered to me, so that I will forgive your sins.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa a hɔl, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Nɛra Ni Hɔpizizenne, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.

ref: Passover is another time when you must come together to worship me, and it must be celebrated on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
text: Kɔraawiizi Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la daŋ ɔɔ faari lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl duana wiizi aaih saŋa.

ref: Each day of this festival you must offer sacrifices. Then on the final day you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship. Offering the First Part of the Harvest
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ di lizi diwee mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.’ ”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: After you enter the land I am giving you, the first bundle of wheat from each crop must be given to me. So bring it to a priest
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Di ii wa zuu hɛri la minna nyiŋŋi n tɛɛ ia la, di wa kum ii pattikuna, ií lizi ii milugla la iiŋ kummɛ nyuuni di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ.

ref: and two kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil. Then he will place these on the bronze altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. Together with these, you must bring a liter of wine as a drink offering.
text: di kpa kookoo tassazi anɛɛ sau di ɛɛ ɔlivi nuu buua, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia di jaa u ni, di fuuh tɛŋ, a sɔɔh du sum tɛŋ. Ií daŋ kpa siŋ pirintua ni keza di jaa.

ref: I am your God, and I forbid you to eat any new grain or anything made from it until you have brought these offerings. This law will never change. The Harvest Festival (Numbers
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di ii mifalaa maa, di a huurii gɛɛ a ɔɔzaarɛ gɛɛ baŋ kpaa ɔɔzi paanuu, see a hɔl la iiŋ kpa kuna naa di wa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi mɔɔ. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ, di tɛɛ ii naanna bɔr la maa ban niŋ du, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia

ref: The Lord God said to Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: None of my people are ever to do any work on that day—not now or in the future. And I will wipe out those who do!
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa kɔrai. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ ii naanna, bɔr la maa ban niŋ du di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Seven weeks after you offer this bundle of grain, each family must bring another offering of new grain.
text: Ií kur yauzi aniidaanɛ di lii baŋ di Heezaa Hɔpizii, ka hɔpizi la. A hɔllɛ ii ɔɔ kpa minyuuni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa di wa tɛŋ la.

ref: Bring two loaves of bread to be lifted up in dedication to me. Each loaf is to be made with yeast and with two kilograms of the finest flour from the first part of your harvest.
text: Bɔr la maa iin duwɛɛ, ií ɔɔ kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi anɛɛ ni yiisi di ɔɔzi paanuu anɛɛ, a ɛɛ diulugla mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa di wa tɛŋ.

ref: At this same time, the entire community of Israel must bring seven lambs that are a year old, a young bull, and two rams. These animals must have nothing wrong with them, and they must be offered as a sacrifice to please me. You must also offer the proper grain and wine sacrifices with each animal.
text: Ií ɔɔ lizi peballi aniidaanɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, nabalee, pebala anɛɛ la n kpekke ani mbusu lizaa mia ni siŋ mbusu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii la sɔɔh n summɛ tɛŋ.

ref: Offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and two rams a year old as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
text: Denii ií lizi bubal ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor ani pebizi anɛɛ n di biŋkpaŋkpaŋa, á ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa hor.

ref: The priest will lift up the rams together with the bread in dedication to me. These offerings are holy and are my gift to the priest.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ lalli a pebizi anɛɛ la ni diulugla paanuu la maa chiŋ n see, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa. A ɛɛ sunzinanaananaarɛ tɛŋ, di ɛɛ kizeehiŋ hor.

ref: This is a day of celebration and worship, a time of rest from your work. You and your descendants must obey this law.
text: Ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami a hɔl hiŋ ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii naanna, bɔr la maa ban niŋ du di hanna la.

ref: When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing around the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. Leave it for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God! The Festival of Trumpets (Numbers
text: Di ii ɔɔ waa kum ii kooliŋkuna, ií gilɛɛ waa kum ii kooni kɛraa gɛɛ di kaa bir har di ra kugni. Ií ɔɔ gilaa tɛɛ nyaara ni hɔɔhra. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ” Bensunoniinazi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. It is a solemn day of worship; everyone must go without eating to show sorrow for their sins, and sacrifices must be burned.
text: “A baagu aniidaanɛɛhiŋ naa hɔpizaa fi hɔl daŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizizeŋ. Ií ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa di jaami di vɔɔ nua ka lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛŋ.

ref: This is a time of complete rest just like the Sabbath, and everyone must go without eating from the evening of the ninth to the evening of the tenth. The Festival of Shelters (Numbers
text: U ɛɛ heezaa ni nuuvɔɔi hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ ia. Di chi a baagu hɔpizaa kabɛl hɔl duana ni, di ga hel u hɔpizaa fi hɔl duana ninɛɛ, ii ɔɔ di a Heezaa Hɔpizii.” Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia

ref: Pick the best fruit from your trees and cut leafy branches to use during the time of this joyous celebration in my honor.
text: A lugli hɔpizii hɔl, ii daŋ kpa ii daazi nɔna la n wesse nɛnnɛ, di mɔnni abɛ paŋhoori ni daazi kela la, n dɔɔ paŋhoori nɛnnɛ di ra di iihinaa, di ra chɔliŋ ń see hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Baagu aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔllɛ Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii ra faari. Ii daŋ diu hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: No one is to do any work on the first day of the festival—it is a time when everyone must come together for worship.
text: U lugli hɔpizii daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizii la iin niŋ ɔɔ chaali di jaami, ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa, a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: For seven days, sacrifices must be offered on the altar. The eighth day is also to be a day of complete rest, as well as a time of offering sacrifices on the altar and of coming together for worship.
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, ií ɔɔ ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ra tɛŋ hɔpizi biimaa, ka a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi hɔl, ií kaa chaali jaami ka lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii tɛŋ. Waabuu ii chaalaazi hɔpizaa maa tuna hiŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.

ref: I have chosen these festivals as times when my people must come together for worship and when animals, grain, and wine are to be offered on the proper days.
text: Anniibuu ɛɛ n Hɔpizizenaa la miŋ lizɛɛ, anla iin niŋ gil á ɛɛ ii chaalaazi hɔpizinanaa, ii ɔɔ ra ligzi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa di waa tɛŋ. Aabuu, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusu lizaa mia, siŋ ani mbusuzi la maa n dɛkkɛ hɔpizi biimaa.

ref: These festivals must be celebrated in addition to the Sabbaths and the times when you offer special gifts or sacrifices to keep a promise or as a voluntary offering.
text: A mbusuzi naa lizaa daŋ jaa Kɔraawiizi Heezaa Hɔpizii mbusuzi lizaa, ii sunzaa mbusuzi lizaa, ii nuuzi lizaa ani ii kipar mbusuzi la iin ninna lizi ra tɛŋ la ni.

ref: Remember to begin the Festival of Shelters on the fifteenth day of the seventh month after you have harvested your crops. Celebrate this festival for seven days in honor of me and don't do any work on the first day or on the day following the festival.
text: Awia, di haŋ faari baagu aniidaanɛɛ hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl, di ii wa chaali a hɛri pattikuna maa tuŋ, ií di a hɔpizizeŋ naa, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. A lugli hɔpizii ni a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ daŋ ɛɛ heezaa hɔpizaa.

ref: I command you and all of your descendants to celebrate this festival during the seventh month of each year.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra di hɔpizizenaa naa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ binaa bina maa, di ra tɛŋ. Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Ií ɔɔ ra diu baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ maa biini.

ref: so future generations will know that I made their ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
text: guŋ gil ii naanna zum lugɔ n faa gillɔɔ ii Izrɛl hina faa ra zuu pampannizi biine, saŋa la miŋ faa kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri la. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”

ref: This is how Moses instructed the people of Israel to celebrate the Lord's festivals.
text: Kennaabuu Moosis faa ɛɛ di dau hɔpizizenaa Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ba ra di, di ra tɔgzuu la.

ref: It's possible to pay the owner for an animal that has been killed, but death is the penalty for murder.
text: Unla maa haŋ wa kpu sel daŋ lizi sel di du u bɔɔ, ka unla maa wa kpu nɛr, bá kpu u ge gba.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: You must supply the purest olive oil for the lamps in the sacred tent, so they will keep burning.
text: “Gil Izrɛl hina kpa ɔlivi nuu la n du yelemm di wa tɛi, í du fintinazi la n du n Tanti Dia la biini, guŋ gil a ra lau saŋa maa.

ref: Use your finest flour to bake twelve loaves of bread about two kilograms each,
text: Kpa sakɔla kookoo tassazi tokko ni anaazu sau suul di kuari paanuuzi fidaanɛɛ di ɔɔzaa.

ref: then take them into the sacred tent and lay them on the gold table in two rows of six loaves.
text: Kpaa di dau chɔŋa anɛɛ saliŋ himmaa tɛɛbul la n chigɛ n see ni, anumbɛl ɔɔ du chɔŋ maa biini.

ref: Alongside each row put some pure incense that will be sent up by fire in place of the bread as an offering to me.
text: Ɛɛ daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la n wesse nɛnnɛ di hiini a chɔŋ bɛl maa, di fuuah, á ɛɛ liize mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii di chi tɛɛ paanuu la, a sɔɔh du sum tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Aaron must lay fresh loaves on the table each Sabbath, and priests in all generations must continue this practice as part of Israel's agreement with me.
text: Heezaa Hɔpizii maa, a dɛkkɔɔ ba ɔɔ kpa paanuufalaa di chiŋŋi n see, saŋaa saŋa maa, á ɛɛ n ni Izrɛl hina nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: This bread will always belong to Aaron and his family; it is very holy because it was offered to me, and it must be eaten in a holy place. Punishment for Cursing the Lord
text: A ɛɛ Aarɔn ni u biibaala horaa, bá ɔɔ ra heea bɔnaniinanii himmaa la biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu ɛɛ mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa la bɔnanaananaa himmaa la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra tɛŋ la. A ɛɛ ba horaa saŋa maa.” Nɛr la n na gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi dignitɛraa wia

ref: Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri from the tribe of Dan, had married an Egyptian, and they had a son. One day their son got into a fight with an Israelite man in camp and cursed the name of the Lord. So the young man was dragged off to Moses,
text: Unla maa n ɛɛ Izrɛl hinuu la faa gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi di seeu nua. Awia, ba faa kpogluu ba Moosis be. A baal maa sɔnnɛ Sɛlɔmif, n ɛɛ Dibri biihaaŋ di lii Dan dee biini.

ref: who had him guarded while everyone waited for the Lord to tell them what to do.
text: Ba tɔu dia ka ra kpaŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ŋɔ bá dawuu.

ref: Finally, the Lord said to Moses:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: This man has cursed me! Take him outside the camp and tell the witnesses to lay their hands on his head. Then command the whole community of Israel to stone him to death.
text: “Kpogli unla n gbɛlliŋ la di lii ii chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia. Gil banla maa n nuu gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, kpa ba nonee sag u nyuu ni mɔɔ, ka a nɛra maa paagi bia di lɔɔzuu kpu.

ref: And warn the others that everyone else who curses me will die in the same way, whether they are Israelites by birth or foreigners living among you.
text: Unla maa ge wa gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi, á nɛra maa paagi bia di lɔɔzuu kpu. Di hɔɔhrii gɛɛ di ii biere gba.

ref: Death is also the penalty for murder,
text: Di nɛr maa haŋ wa kpu nɛr, bá kpu u ge.

ref: but the killing of an animal that belongs to someone else requires only that the animal be replaced.
text: Nɛr maa haŋ wa kpu u dɔŋhiŋ sel, ú lizi sel di du u bɔɔ. Gbɔgrɛ lugɔ miibɔɔrɛ niŋ turgi miibɔɔ kim.

ref: Personal injuries to others must be dealt with in keeping with the crime—
text: Di nɛr maa haŋ wa du u dɔŋhiŋ pira, gunla maa uŋ haŋ ɛɛ la, gunnɛ bá ɛɛ u gba,

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I demand equal justice both for you Israelites and for those foreigners who live among you.
text: A gbɔg naa du denii di tɛɛ hɔɔhri ni Izrɛl hinuu maa. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’ ”

ref: When Moses finished speaking, the people did what the Lord had told Moses, and they stoned to death the man who had cursed the Lord.
text: Moosis n wa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ba lau a baal la n gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia, di paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu. Izrɛl hina jaa ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: So when you buy or sell farmland, the price is to be determined by the number of crops it can produce before the next Year of Celebration. Don't try to cheat.
text: I daŋ yawuu binni la maga un niŋ wer lii tɔna mɔɔ, ka a Hindɔɔi Bina bɛl kaa wa hel. U daŋ yooubuu tɛi binni la maga hin niŋ wer kpa i pattikuna la.

ref: When Moses was on Mount Sinai, the Lord told him
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu lugɔ

ref: This is a year of complete celebration, so don't plant any seed or harvest what your fields or vineyards produce.
text: A binni tokkoanɛɛ ni fihiŋ la daŋ ɛɛ Hindɔɔi Bina tɛɛ ia, ií gilɛɛ waa duu di gilɛɛ waa kum kuntɛɛ maa gɛɛ di wàá tɔrgi grepu daa la nɔna iiŋ wàá a kela kɛurɛɛ,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: After you enter the land that I am giving you, it must be allowed to rest one year out of every seven.
text: ú ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di ii wa zuu hɛri la minna nyiŋŋi ń tɛɛ ia la, a dɛkkɔɔ ií ra tɔgziŋ di ɔɔ gil a hɛri ge heezi, binni aniidaanɛɛ maa biini.

ref: but the seventh year you must let your fields and vineyards rest in honor of me, your Lord.
text: Ka binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la waa daŋ ɛɛ heezaa bina tɛɛ a hɛri, u daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi bina. Ií gilɛɛ waa duu ii kooni gɛɛ di wàá kɛuri ii grepu daazi kela.

ref: This is to be a time of complete rest for your fields and vineyards, so don't harvest anything they produce.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kum kuntɛɛri maa gɛɛ di wàá tɔrgi ii grepuzi daazi la baŋ waa kɛurɛɛ nɔna. A hɛri daŋ heezi a guŋ bina hiŋ.

ref: However, you and your slaves and your hired workers, as well as any domestic or wild animals, may eat whatever grows on its own. The Year of Celebration The Lord said to his people:
text: haali ii kundɛɛzaa ni pir sela la maa n du ii hɛri. Kunla maa n lii a hɛri daŋ ɛɛ ii kundiwee. Hindɔɔi Bina wia

ref: or uncle or cousin, or some other family member. In fact, if you ever get enough money, you may buy your own freedom
text: U naara gɛɛ u naara bie gɛɛ mɛɛ bie gɛɛ u lulli himmaa daŋ wer bir yawuu. Gɛɛ di u himmaa wa nyɛɛlɔɔ, u daŋ wer bir yau u hiŋ.

ref: on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is also the Great Day of Forgiveness, trumpets are to be blown everywhere in the land.
text: a baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔpizaa fihiŋ hɔl la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Baaŋfuuih Lizaa Hɔpizeŋ la, gil bá huuh bensunoniina di bar a hɛri maa biini.

ref: This fiftieth year is sacred—it is a time of freedom and of celebration when everyone will receive back their original property, and slaves will return home to their families.
text: Binni tokkoanɛɛ ni fihiŋ la daŋ ɛɛ binnaniinanii di ɛɛ Hindɔɔi Bina tɛɛ nɛr maa n du a hɛri biini. Nɛr la maa n faa yoo u kuna, ba biraa tɛu gɛɛ u naanna. Nɛr ge maa baŋ faa yoowe u birgi yom, bir kaali u nɛra be.

ref: In this time of sacred celebration you may eat only what grows on its own.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ Hindɔɔi Binaa, di ɛɛ binnaniinanii tɛɛ ia. Ií ɔɔ di kunla maa n wa lii a hɛri a heezaa bina hiŋ biini.

ref: During this year, all property must go back to its original owner.
text: Hindɔɔi Bina naa biini, bɛ́l maa bir u dɔŋhiŋ kapɛttɛ kuna la uŋ yoowe la, di wa tɛu.

ref: If it is a long time before the next Year of Celebration, the price will be higher, because what is really being sold are the crops that the land can produce.
text: Di a binni wa kpillɔ, i daŋ gil u yoola tinni, ka di a binni waa kpil, i daŋ gil u yoola tuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, kunla hiŋ yoowe di ra tɛu la, gunna bagli pattikuna la maga un niŋ na di lii a hɛrii.

ref: I am the Lord your God, so obey me and don't cheat anyone.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra fini dɔŋa, ka ií ra ɔm mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: If you obey my laws and teachings, you will live safely in the land and enjoy its abundant crops.
text: Denii a hɛri diwee lɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ii di di piŋ, di wer du ni bɔsɔna.

ref: Don't ever worry about what you will eat during the seventh year when you are forbidden to plant or harvest.
text: Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ pɛɛzi, ‘Bɛɛ ya di binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la biinei, di yaa waa kuna duuwe gɛɛ di kumaawɛi?’

ref: I will see to it that you harvest enough in the sixth year to last for three years.
text: N daŋ kissi ia a binni anumbɛlhiŋ biini, a hɛri lii diwee la iin niŋ di binni ahoro.

ref: In the eighth year you will live on what you harvested in the sixth year, but in the ninth year you will eat what you plant and harvest in the eighth year.
text: Saŋa la iin ninna duu kuna binni ŋmantannaazihiŋ biini la, ii danna di ií diubinaa ka binni kabɛlhiŋ la wa hel.

ref: No land may be permanently bought or sold. It all belongs to me—it isn't your land, and you only live there for a little while.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa yoo a hɛri, wàá ka dɔɔ lɛɛi ŋmɛnɛ maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɛri ɛɛ n hotte, ka ii ge ɛɛ lugɔ hɔɔhra la miŋ kpau tɛɛ ia, ii ra di paah.

ref: When property is being sold, the original owner must be given the first chance to buy it.
text: Di lii hɛri la iin niŋ dɔɔ la maa biini, di nɛr yoo hɛri, di kaa bir waa yawuu, a dɛkkɔɔ ií biruu tɛu.

ref: If any of you Israelites become so poor that you are forced to sell your property, your closest relative must buy it back,
text: Di ii bɛl maa wa nyaawɔ, di yoo u kundɔɔlii, ú lulli himmaa bir yawuu.

ref: if that relative has the money. Later, if you can afford to buy it,
text: Ka di a hiŋ waa nɛr maa dɔɔwɛ ú bir yawuu tɛu, ka u wa dɔɔ daama lugɔ u daŋ kaa wer bir yawuu,

ref: you must pay enough to make up for what the present owner will lose on it before the next Year of Celebration, when the property would become yours again.
text: ú binni na gunla a hɛri yoola n niŋ mag binni la n haa kawɛɛ ka ú bir yawuu la, di jaa turgi gunla maga n kawɛɛ ka a hel, ka jaa bir dɔɔ u kundɔɔlii.

ref: But if you don't have the money to pay the present owner a fair price, you will have to wait until the Year of Celebration, when the property will once again become yours.
text: Ka di waa u turgaa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ, kunla uŋ yoowe la, daŋ haa ɛɛ nɛr la n yawuu la hor, di ga hel Hindɔɔi Bina la, ka u jaa biruu tɛu a Hindɔɔi Bina hiŋ biini, u kaa bir dɔɔ u kuŋ.

ref: If you sell a house in a walled city, you have only one year in which to buy it back.
text: Di baal maa wa yoo dia la n du bolzeŋ baŋ ma koŋlii bar biini, u dɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ lugɔ u daŋ kaa bir yawuu di bina wa bɛrɔɔ.

ref: If you don't buy it back before that year is up, it becomes the permanent property of the one who bought it, and it will not be returned to you in the Year of Celebration.
text: Di bina wa bɛrɔɔ di waa wette yawuu, a dia daŋ ɛɛ unla n yawuu la ni u naanna hor di hanna la. Ba wàá ka wer biruu tɛɛ u yoori la Hindɔɔi Bina la biini.

ref: But a house out in a village may be bought back at any time just like a field. And it must be returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration.
text: Ka diini la n du boljigzi, ba waa koŋlaa mawɛɛ baraa la waa, ba daŋ kpaa lugɔ koolimbolaa. Ba daŋ kaa wer bir yawaa a Hindɔɔi Bina hiŋ biini.

ref: If any Levites own houses inside a walled city, they will always have the right to buy them back.
text: Levi dee la dɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ saŋa maa, ba kaa bir yau ba diini la, n du ba bolzenaa la baŋ duwɛɛ la biini.

ref: And any houses that they do not buy back will be returned to them in the Year of Celebration, because these homes are their permanent property among the people of Israel.
text: Awia, Levi dee daŋ wer bir yau ba kundɔɔlaa, bolzeŋ la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ biini. A dɛkkɔɔ ba biraa tɛɛ baa Hindɔɔi Bina la biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, diini la n du Levi dee bolzenaa la ɛɛ ba kunaa Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: No pastureland owned by the Levi tribe can ever be sold; it is their permanent possession. Help for the Poor The Lord said:
text: Ka ba sela diiribɔra la waa n bar ba bolzenaa la, waa dɛkkɛ baŋ yooa. Aawaa, ɛɛ ba horaa saŋa maa.

ref: If any of your people become poor and unable to support themselves, you must help them, just as you are supposed to help foreigners who live among you.
text: Di Izrɛl hinuu maa wa birgi nyaari, wàá ka wer binni u hiŋ, ií hiinuu gunla iiŋ ɔɔ hiini hɔɔhri gɛɛ paahdiiri, ú wer du ii biini.

ref: Don't take advantage of them by charging any kind of interest or selling them food for profit. Instead, honor me by letting them stay where they now live.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa saguu nii maa, gɛɛ di wàá yoo diwee ra tɛu di ra nyiŋŋi tɔna.

ref: Remember—I am the Lord your God! I rescued you from Egypt and gave you the land of Canaan, so that I would be your God.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri, ń wa kpa Keenan hɛri tɛɛ ia la, di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum.

ref: Suppose some of your people become so poor that they have to sell themselves and become your slaves.
text: Di ii dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu maa ɛɛ nyaari ii biine, di yoo u hiŋ tɛɛ ia, ií gilɛɛ gil ú ra hum lugɔ yom.

ref: Then you must treat them as servants, rather than as slaves. And in the Year of Celebration they are to be set free,
text: Ií ra ɛɛu lugɔ paahdiiri gɛɛ hɔɔhri n ballɛ ú wa so ii be tama. U daŋ hum guŋŋ Hindɔɔi Bina la wa hel.

ref: so they and their children may return home to their families and property.
text: Denii ií ta u ni u biizi ú bir kaali u himmaa diahina be ni u naabaala kundɔɔlii bɔr.

ref: I brought them out of Egypt to be my servants, not to be sold as slaves.
text: Dikuu Izrɛl hina la miŋ kpoglee lii Ijip hɛri la n ɛɛ n balaa wia, a waa dɛkkɛ ií yoo baa lugɔ yoma.

ref: So obey me, and don't be cruel to the poor.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sunni baa, ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.

ref: You can own them, and even leave them to your children when you die, but do not make slaves of your own people or be cruel to them.
text: Ii daŋ wer kpa baa tɛɛ ii biizi bá ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna di birgi ba yoma di hanna la, ka ií gilɛɛ waa sunni ii dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu maa.

ref: Even if some of you Israelites become so much in debt that you must sell yourselves to foreigners in your country,
text: Di hɔɔhri gɛɛ nɛr la maa n ballɛ ú wa so ii be tama, wa birgi dɔɔŋ, ii bɛl birgi nyaari di yoo u hiŋ tɛɛ a guŋ hɔɔhri dee bɛl maa,

ref: you still have the right to be set free by a relative, such as a brother
text: u dɔɔ ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ lugɔ bá bir yawuu haali di u yoo u hiŋ gba. U lulli maa daŋ wer bir yawuu.

ref: by paying your owner for the number of years you would still be a slave before the next Year of Celebration.
text: U ni u yauri la daŋ chi saŋa la uŋ yoo u hiŋ la, di kur a binni maga di ga hel Hindɔɔi Bina. U gil u yoola ɛɛ gunla ban niŋ turgi paahdiiri a binni maa la.

ref: The longer the time until then, the more you will have to pay.
text: Ka di binni la n kawɛɛ la waa kaŋ ka a Hindɔɔi Bina hel, guŋ binni magaa u kur di turgi, ka bir lɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: And even while you are the slaves of foreigners in your own country, your people must make sure that you are not mistreated.
text: Ií danna ɛɛubuu lugɔ paahdiiri bina maa. Ií ra du tau u dɔɔri gilɛɛ waa sunnuu.

ref: If you cannot gain your freedom in any of these ways, both you and your children will still be set free in the Year of Celebration.
text: Haali di ii waa wette ga ŋmɛnizi naa bɛl maa di bir yawuu gba, ka ií ta u ni u biizi ŋmɛnɛɛ Hindɔɔi Bina la biini,

ref: People of Israel, I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of Egypt to be my own servants.
text: dikuu Izrɛl hina n ɛɛ n hora alugɔ balaa wia. Ba ɛɛ n balaa la miŋ kpoglee lii Ijip hɛrii. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.”

ref: Respect the Sabbath and honor the place where I am worshiped, because I am the Lord.
text: Ií ra kpa n Heezaa Hɔpizii la girme di ra tɔgzi N Tanti Dia la werge. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: and I will send rain to make your crops grow and your trees produce fruit.
text: n daŋ ɔɔ gil dooŋ nɛɛ u balaa saŋa, ií hɛri pattikuna lɛɛ, ú daazi ge nɔŋ nɛnnɛ.

ref: I will bless your country with peace, and you will rest without fear. I will wipe out the dangerous animals and protect you from enemy attacks.
text: N daŋ tɛɛ ia bɔsɔna a hɛri biini, ií ɔɔ chɔɔ nɛr maa wàá wer ɔnzi ia, di lizi sechɔgaa ii hɛri, laal ge ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka du de.

ref: You will chase and destroy your enemies,
text: Ii daŋ dau ii dɔma luge, di kpuuzi ba maa ni tokobizi.

ref: I will treat you with such kindness that your nation will grow strong, and I will also keep my promises to you.
text: N daŋ suŋ ii ni di gil ií lul di wazi, di du kpil, di gil n ni ia nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la chi.

ref: I will live among you and never again look on you with disgust.
text: N daŋ du ii be, n Tanti Dia biini. N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá bir luŋ kpu ia.

ref: I will walk with you—I will be your God, and you will be my people.
text: N daŋ du ii biini di ra vol, di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, ii ge ɛɛ n nɛra.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I rescued you from Egypt, so that you would never again be slaves. I have set you free; now walk with your heads held high. Punishment for Disobeying the Lord The Lord said:
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, di lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri, ií gilɛɛ kaa ɛɛ ba yoma. Minuu lɛɛ ia, ii waa kaa ɛɛ yoma, guŋ gil ií wer dɔɔ iihinaa la.” Kɔraawiizi nua vɛɛi dignitɛraa wia.

ref: If you disobey me and my laws, and if you break our agreement,
text: di vɛɛ n widaulaa ni n Gbɔgni wia, di chɔg n ni ia nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la,

ref: I will punish you terribly, and you will be ruined. You will be struck with incurable diseases and with fever that leads to blindness and depression. Your enemies will eat the crops you plant,
text: guŋwaa, kenne n ɛɛ ia. N daŋ kpa ɔnsii werge, wiilchɔgaa ni bɔwema ta ii ni, a chɔg ii siwee, ii siuzi. Ii daŋ duu kuna pɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii dɔmaa niŋ dia.

ref: and I will turn from you and let you be destroyed by your attackers. You will even run at the very rumor of attack.
text: N daŋ lizi siwii di sag ii ni, guŋ gil ii dɔma kpegli ia, banla n hah ia la ra di kora ii ni. Ii daŋ chɔ di nɛr maa waa ia ra duŋŋi.

ref: Then, if you still refuse to obey me, I will punish you seven times for each of your sins,
text: Di annii maa wa ɛɛwɔ ka ii haa waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ, n daŋ tɔɔri ia buniidaanɛɛ, dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: until your pride is completely crushed. I will hold back the rain, so the sky above you will be like iron, and the ground beneath your feet will be like copper.
text: N daŋ tuŋ ii dignikpega jigsaa la, dooŋ waa ka ba, ii hɛri hil di du kpeg alugɔ lugbii.

ref: All of your hard work will be for nothing—and there will be no harvest of grain or fruit.
text: Ii daŋ ɔɔ kuuh pɛɛ, ii hɛri wàá ka gil ii pattikuna lɛɛ, ii daazi gba wàá ka nɔŋ.

ref: If you keep rebelling against me, I'll punish you seven times worse, just as your sins deserve!
text: Di ii haa vɛɛwɔ di dɔɔ dignikpega, ii wàá nuu tɛŋ, n daŋ gil ii tɔɔrɔɔ nyaŋŋi buniidaanɛɛ, gunla n dɛkkɛ ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: I'll send wild animals to attack you, and they will gobble up your children and livestock. So few of you will be left that your roads will be deserted.
text: N daŋ gil pir sechɔgaa zuu ii biini, di lauri ii biizi, di chɔgi ii nauna, ii wàá ka du kpil, ii ŋmɛnizi chɔɔgi pɛɛ.

ref: I'll remain your enemy and punish you even worse.
text: n himmaa daŋ kii ii wia di tɛr ii digna buniidaanɛɛ, dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: War will break out because you broke our agreement, and if you escape to your walled cities, I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and you will be captured by your enemies.
text: Laallɛ ń kpa di wa yoo ia, di turgi ia ii wichɔgaa kim, dikuu iiŋ chɔgi n ni ia nuukpaŋ la wia. Di ii wa chaali ii bolzenaa biine ií lɛɛ iihinaa, n daŋ kpa wiilchɔgaa ta ii ni, di kpa ia du ii dɔma nonee biini.

ref: You will have such a shortage of bread, that ten women will be able to bake their bread in the same oven. Each of you will get only a few crumbs, and you will go hungry.
text: Di maa kaa wàá tɛɛ ia diwee, haana fi daŋ ɔɔ ɔɔzi paanuu diikpaŋ biini, di mɛgzi ra tɛɛ ia. Ii daŋ ɔɔ heea, ka ii wàá piŋ.

ref: I'll really get furious and punish you terribly for your sins!
text: n daŋ kpa baaŋfuuih di tɔɔri ia werge maa buniidaanɛɛ, dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: In fact, you will be so desperate for food that you will eat your own children.
text: Lɔzi danna kpu ia werge maa ii lauri ii biibaala ni ii biihaana di hee.

ref: I'll destroy your shrines and tear down your incense altars, leaving your dead bodies piled on top of your idols. And you will be disgusting to me.
text: N daŋ chɔgi ii vuga kuaribɔra la n du giŋgimee nyuuni, di purgi ii daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔra, di paagi ii lalaa sag ii vugsiwaa la ni kulululu, di kii ii wia werge maa.

ref: I'll wipe out your towns and your places of worship and will no longer be pleased with the smell of your sacrifices.
text: N daŋ purgi ii bolzenaa á chɔɔ burburbur, di chɔg ii vuga kuaribɔra, màá lɛɛ ii mbusuzi lizaa kuna la iiŋ ɔɔ ra fuuh, a sɔɔh du sum la.

ref: Your land will become so desolate that even your enemies who settle there will be shocked when they see it.
text: N daŋ chɔgi ii hɛri, ɔnsii lau ii dɔma la n wa soge de la, bá nuuzi kpu werge.

ref: After I destroy your towns and ruin your land with war, I'll scatter you among the nations.
text: Tokobii n kpa di duŋŋi ia ii yaari hɛssi maa biine. Ii hɛri daŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ, ii bolzenaa maa purgi.

ref: While you are prisoners in foreign lands, your own land will enjoy years of rest and refreshment, as it should have done each seventh year when you lived there.
text: U daŋ na heezaa la uŋ faa waa na ii de dui saŋa la, di u chɔɔ pɛɛ.

ref: In the land of your enemies, you will tremble at the rustle of a leaf, as though it were a sword. And you will become so weak that you will stumble and fall over each other, even when no one is chasing you.
text: Haali nɛr maa n waa ia ra duŋŋi gba, ka ii daŋ gargi dɔŋa di ra chogli alugɔ baŋ kpa tokobi di ra duŋŋi ia. Awia, ii wàá wer chi ii dɔma see.

ref: Many of you will die in foreign lands,
text: Ii banla n kawɛɛ, daŋ siuzi hɛrdumazi biine, ii dɔma hɛssi di ia.

ref: and others of you will waste away in sorrow as the result of your sins and the sins of your ancestors.
text: Ii banla n niŋ ka la, daŋ siuzi ta ii dɔma hɛssi biine, dikuu ii ni ii naabaala wichɔgaa wia.

ref: Then suppose you realize that I turned against you and brought you to the land of your enemies because both you and your ancestors had stubbornly sinned against me. If you humbly confess what you have done and start living right,
text: gunnɛ gillɛ n kii baa di gil ba kaali ba dɔma hɛssi, di ba siwee wa sɔɔnɔɔ ba turgi ba wichɔgaa kim,

ref: I'll keep the promise I made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will bless your land
text: n daŋ liizi n ni Jekɔb, Aizik ani Abraham nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la wia, di liizi a hɛri wia.

ref: and let it rest during the time that you are in a foreign country, paying for your rebellion against me and my laws.
text: Ba daŋ vɛɛ a hɛri ka chɔ, u chɔɔ pɛɛ di heezi. Ba daŋ turgi ba wichɔgaa kim ú su, dikuu baŋ vɛɛ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa wia.

ref: No matter what you have done, I am still the Lord your God, and I will never completely reject you or become absolutely disgusted with you there in the land of your enemies.
text: Haali baŋ du ba dɔma hɛssi la gba, màá vɛɛ baa di kii ba wia, di waa chɔg baa nyaamm, di chɔgi n ni baa nuukpaŋ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.

ref: While nations watched, I rescued your ancestors from Egypt so that I would be their God. Yes, I am your Lord, and I will never forget our agreement.
text: N daŋ kuu ba wia di liizi n ni ba naabaala nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la wia saŋa la miŋ faa kpogli baa di lii Ijip hɛri, hɛssi hina maa sibɔɔ la, ń ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum. Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Moses was on Mount Sinai when the Lord gave him these laws and teachings for the people of Israel.
text: Anniibuu Gbɔgni ni widaulaa la Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di dau tɛɛ u ni Izrɛl hina Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu la.

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If you ever want to free someone who has been promised to me,
text: “Ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Izrɛl hina di kali baa, ‘Di nɛr maa wa kpa nɛr tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dikuu uŋ lɛɛ nua n be wia, di ba ra nyiŋŋi á hiŋ na u hiŋ, a kinnɛ keŋ.

ref: you may do so by paying the following amounts, weighed according to the official standards:
text: Nɛr la n di binni tokkoahoro ni saga, baal kim daŋ ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau fidaanue, haaŋ ge hor ɛɛ fi.

ref: Ten percent of everything you harvest is holy and belongs to me, whether it grows in your fields or on your fruit trees.
text: A hɛri kummaa bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ, di miarɛ gɛɛ daanɔnaa, ɛɛ n horaa. A ɛɛ kunnanaananaarɛ.

ref: If you try to substitute any other animal, no matter how good, for the one you promised, they will both become holy and must be sacrificed.
text: Nɛr la n na lizi nua la gilɛɛ waa kpa sel maa di ra chɛruu. Di u kpa sel maa chɛruu, a maa anɛɛ ɛɛ a nanaananaarɛ.

ref: If you have promised to give someone to me and can't afford to pay the full amount for that person's release, you will be taken to a priest, and he will decide how much you can afford.
text: Di nɛr la n lɛɛ nua la ɛɛ nyaarii werge, wàá wer turgi a guŋ kuna, bá kpogli nɛr la kim ban niŋ turgi la di ba n kizeehiŋ see, waabuu niŋ jaa tɛɛ nɛr la n lɛɛ nua la kim un niŋ wer turgi.

ref: If you promise to sacrifice an animal to me, it becomes holy, and there is no way you can set it free.
text: Di a nua ɛɛ sel la n dɛkkɛ ban niŋ kpa tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii, a guŋ mbusu lizaa daŋ ɛɛ u naniinanii tɛŋ.

ref: Donkeys are unfit for sacrifice, so if you promise me a donkey, you must bring it to the priest,
text: Di a nua lɛɛi sel la doŋŋoo, waa dɛg n lɛɛu, guŋwaa, ba daŋ kpa a sel di ba n kizeehiŋ see,

ref: If you promise a house to me, a priest will set the price, whatever the condition of the house.
text: Di baal wa kpa u dia tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, n kizeehiŋ binnuu di na di u wesso gɛɛ waa wer, gunla maa uŋ wa di u yoola, u yoolaa guŋ.

ref: If you promise part of your family's land to me, its value must be determined by the amount of seed needed to plant the land, and the rate will be ten pieces of silver for every
text: Di nɛbɛl kpa u naabaala hɛri yeŋ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ii daŋ di u yoolaa di mag mia la ban niŋ kpa duu. Saliŋhuŋŋu kebisau tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, daŋ yau baali kookoo tassazi kalfa.

ref: If this promise is made in the Year of Celebration, the land will be valued at the full price.
text: Di Hindɔɔi Binaa u kpau tɛŋ, u yoola la baŋ diu la chigɔɔ.

ref: But any time after that, the price will be figured according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration.
text: Ka di u kpaubuu tɛŋ Hindɔɔi Bina la har, n kizeehiŋ la di u yoola di mag binni la n kawɛɛ, ka Hindɔɔi Bina bɛl kaa hel, u daŋ tuu u yoola.

ref: When the Year of Celebration comes, the land becomes holy because it belongs to me, and it will be given to the priests.
text: Di ba wa bir a hɛri tɛɛ u hiŋ Hindɔɔi Bina la biini, u daŋ ɛɛ u naniinanii alugɔ hɛri baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ɛɛ N Dia kizeehina hor.

ref: If you promise me a field that you have bought,
text: Di nɛbɛl kpa hɛri la uŋ yauwɛ, n waa u naabaala hɛri yeŋ ɛɛwɛ, tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi,

ref: its value will be decided by a priest, according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration, and the money you pay will be mine.
text: N kizeehinnɛ niŋ di u yoola di chi a guŋ saŋa di ga hel Hindɔɔi Bina la, a dɛkkɔ á hiŋ turgi u kim a hɔl hiŋ, u ɛɛ naniinanii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: However, on the next Year of Celebration, the land will go back to the family of its original owner.
text: Ba daŋ biruu tɛɛ a hɛri hiŋ, nɛr la be uŋ yawuu la Hindɔɔi Bina la biini.

ref: Every price will be set by the official standards. Various Offerings The Lord said:
text: A dɛkkɔ kuna yoola maa mag gunla banna mɛgzi saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau n Dia la.

ref: All first-born animals of your flocks and herds are already mine, and so you cannot promise any of them to me.
text: Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa kpa sel maa biilugli di wàá tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu biilugli maa n ɛɛ n hor wia, di naballɛ gɛɛ peezii gɛɛ buunnɛ.

ref: Anything that you completely dedicate to me must be completely destroyed. It cannot be bought back or sold. Every person, animal, and piece of property that you dedicate completely is only for me.
text: Ka kunla maa nɛr n kpawɛɛ tɛŋ, di nɛttɛ, di selle gɛɛ u naabaala hɛrii, wàá wer yoou gɛɛ di bir yawuu. Kunla maa baŋ tɛŋ ɛɛ kunnaniinaniirɛ.

ref: In fact, any humans who have been promised to me in this way must be put to death.
text: Nɛr la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi lugɔ n chɔguu, ba wàá wer bir yawuu, bá kpuu.

ref: If you want to buy back this part of your harvest, you may do so by paying what it is worth plus an additional
text: Di nɛr maa ra nyiŋŋi ú bir yau u hor, di ba bɔnni u yoola bɔra anue, ú turgi u bɔkpaŋ sag.

ref: When you count your flocks and herds, one out of ten of every newborn animal is holy and belongs to me,
text: Di nɛr maa wàá kur u sela, fihiŋ la ɛɛ n hotte, di ɛɛ kunnaniinanii tɛŋ.

ref: no matter how good or bad it is. If you substitute one animal for another, both of them become holy, and neither can be bought back.
text: Ú gilɛɛ waa ligzi a nanaa di ra lii a chɔgaa biini gɛɛ di wàá charaa. Di u charuu, a sel ni unla uŋ kpawɛɛ charuu la maa ɛɛ a nanaananaarɛ, wàá ka wer bir yawaa.’ ”

text: Widaulaa la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, ú tɛɛ Izrɛl hina labuu guŋ.

text: Kur baala la maa n di binni tokko ka ra sag, di hel laal lɔi.

text: Moosis ni Aarɔn faa lɛɛ a baala naa sɔna baŋ tɛɛwɛ la.

text: Izrɛl hina la faa ɛɛ annii maa, Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: But the Levites will camp around the sacred tent to make sure that no one goes near it and makes me furious with the Israelites.
