text: Di a wa ɛɛwɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hina maa daŋ kaa izi di la yembɛl, Levi dee labuu niŋ panzi n Tanti Dia la, di kaa ga baŋuu. Di nɛra la n kawɛɛ la bɛl maa haŋ wa tuzi dugluu, bá kpuu.

ref: Aaron's four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar,
text: Aarɔn biibaala sɔnaa keŋ, Nadabuu faa ɛɛ u biibambilugli, Abihu, Ɛliaza ani Itama hiŋzi.

ref: were the ones to be ordained as priests.
text: Baabuu ba faa waari ba nyuuni nuu di lizi baa ba ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la.

ref: But the Lord killed Nadab and Abihu in the Sinai Desert when they used fire that was unacceptable in their offering to the Lord. And because Nadab and Abihu had no sons, only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with their father Aaron. The Duties of the Levites
text: Ka Nadab ni Abihu faa chogli di siuzi Kɔraawiizi see Sinaai Hɛribɔduma la biini, dikuu baŋ faa kpa niŋ la n waa dɛkkɛ di lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia. Ba faa waa biibaala dɔɔwɛ. Awia, Ɛliaza ni Itamaa faa ra hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehina huma ba mɛɛ Aarɔn de dui saŋa.

text: Lizi Aarɔn ni u biibaala bá ɛɛ n kizeehina. Nɛr la maa n kawɛɛ haŋ wa dugluu, bá kpuu.”

ref: With another blue cloth they will cover the lampstand, along with the lamps, the lamp snuffers, the fire pans, and the jars of oil for the lamps.
text: Ba daŋ kpa pɛɛŋ burgu di yaa tɔ fintina daa la ni u fintinazi, kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɔnni a yakɔssi, pɛrɛtuzenaa ani a ɔlivi nuu viini la maa ni.

ref: All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather and placed on a carrying frame.
text: Ba daŋ kpa hɔŋbuglii di fɔɔzi u ni u kuna maa, ka kpaa sag u daazi la ni.

ref: The gold incense altar is to be covered with a blue cloth, and then with a piece of fine leather, before its carrying poles are put in place.
text: Ba daŋ kaa kpa pɛɛŋ burgu di yaa tɔ mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la, di kpa hɔŋbuglii di yaa tɔ u ni, ka kpa daazi la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra chiu la suuzi a bɔsuuzaa.

ref: Next, Aaron and his sons will take blue cloth and wrap all the objects used in worship at the sacred tent. These will need to be covered with a piece of fine leather, then placed on a carrying frame.
text: Ba daŋ kaa kpa pɛɛŋ burgu di fɔɔzi a Bɔnaniinanii kuna maa, di kpa hɔŋbuglii yaa tɔ a ni di kpaa sag daazi la ban niŋ kpa chia ni.

ref: They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
text: Ba daŋ paa hɔɔhri la n chɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari la, ka kpa pɛɛŋ la n aahwɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii di yaa tɔ u ni.

ref: On that cloth will be placed the utensils used at the altar, including the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather, before the carrying poles are put in place.
text: Denii ba jaa kpa kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum huma mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di kpa nimbuurikuna ni zuunzi la n dɔɔ nyina ba kpaa laari ola, sɔɔbulzi ani hɛnni la baŋ ɔɔ du chal gɛɛ nii di ɛɛ ra mizi la jaa, di hɔŋ u ni. Ka jaa kpa hɔŋbuglii di yaa tɔ u ni, di kpa daazi la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra chiu la suuzi a bɔsuuzaa.

ref: When the camp is ready to be moved, the Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects and the furnishings of the sacred tent. But Aaron and his sons must have already covered those things so the Kohathites won't touch them and die.
text: Di Aarɔn ni u biibaala wa tuŋ annii maa, Izrɛl hina jaa ɛɛ sirya ba izi, Kɔhaf dee la daŋ ba wa kpa a kuna chi, ka ba gilɛɛ wàá gbɔgzi kunnanaananaa himmaa la, di waa siuzi. Baabuu niŋ chi kuna la maa n du n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini.

ref: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet-smelling incense, the grain for the sacrifices, and the olive oil used for dedications and ordinations. Eleazar is responsible for seeing that the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the sacred objects are taken care of.
text: N kizeehiŋ Aarɔn biibaal Ɛliazaa ninna binni fintina nuu la, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la, mbusu lizaa mia la ani nuu la baŋ ɔɔ waari nɛr la ni. Waabuu ninna binni n Tanti Dia la ni kuna la maa n du u biini, ani u kunnanaananaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ kuari u biini la ni.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: for carrying the curtains of the sacred tent, its two outer coverings, the curtain for the entrance to the tent,
text: baabuu niŋ ɔɔ ra chi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la patiisazi maa, kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɔu, hɔŋbuglaa la maa baŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra tɔ u kuna ani u dominua patiisa la,

ref: the curtains hanging around the courtyard of the tent, and the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard. The Gershonites are to do whatever needs to be done to take care of these things,
text: u diŋŋee patiisazi la n bar u ni mbusu lizibɔr la, u dominua hor, u ŋmɛnni ani kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum de huma. Huma la maa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ba kpa kuna naa di hum, Gɛsɔn dee labuu niŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ a maa.

ref: These are the duties of the Gershonites at the sacred tent, and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Duties of the Merarite Clans
text: Gɛsɔn dee la humaa guŋ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Aarɔn biibaal Itama niŋ ɔɔ ra binni ba ni ba ra hum ba huma.” Mɛrari dee huma wia

ref: The Merarites will be responsible for carrying the frames of the tent and its other pieces, including the bars, the posts, and the stands,
text: Ba humaa keŋ, baabuu niŋ ɔɔ ra chi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dolli, saŋa, ligee ani a zɛɛzi hɔŋribɔra la maa,

ref: as well as the posts that support the courtyard, together with their stands, tent pegs, and ropes. The Merarites are to be told exactly what objects they are to carry,
text: di kpa u diŋŋee daazi, daasiraa, ŋmɛnni ani anla maa baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum a huma maa di jaa. Gil bɛl maa zum kuna la un niŋ ɔɔ ra chi.

ref: and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Levites Are Counted Again
text: Mɛrari domee humaa guŋ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini. Aarɔn biibaal Itamaa ninna binni ba ni.” Levi dee domeezi kuraa wia

ref: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelite leaders obeyed the Lord and counted the Levi tribe by families and clans, to find out how many men there were between the ages of
text: Ba faa bagli bɛl maanii u huma ani kuna la un niŋ ɔɔ ra chiu, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ la.

ref: to say to the people of Israel, “Put out of the camp everyone who has leprosy or a bodily discharge or who has touched a dead body. Now that I live among my people, their camp must be kept clean.”
text: Di baallɛ gɛɛ haannɛ, bá lizuu lii a chɔɔribɔr ú gilɛɛ waa doŋ de, dikuu mìŋ́ du ba be wia.”

ref: The Israelites obeyed the Lord's instructions. The Penalty for Committing a Crime (Leviticus
text: Izrɛl hina la ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagli Moosis la, di ligzi a guŋ hina maa, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la biini. Wichɔgaa kinturgaa wia

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you commit a crime against someone, you have sinned against me.
text: ú ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di baal gɛɛ haaŋ wa ɛɛ wia di zuu u dɔŋhiŋ ni, guŋ gil u nyaa wibii n be, a hiŋ di bilchɔgrɛ,

ref: You must confess your guilt and pay the victim in full for whatever damage has been done, plus a fine of
text: di dɛg lugɔ ú sɛɛ chɔgri dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia, di turgi a kim maa, di kaa bɔnni a kim bɔra anue, di kpa bɔkpaŋ sag a kim ni, di kpaa tɛɛ nɛr la uŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ

ref: If the victim has no relative who can accept this money, it belongs to me and will be paid to the priest. In addition to that payment, you must take a ram for the priest to sacrifice so your sin will be forgiven.
text: Ka di nɛr la baŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la siuwɔɔ, waa lulli himmaa dɔɔwɛ ban niŋ turgaa tɛu, guŋwaa, a kim la baŋ turgee la ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hotte. Bá kpa a ni pebal la baŋ ɔɔ kpa lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih nɛra ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia la, di tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ.

ref: When you make a donation to the sacred tent, that money belongs only to the priest, and each priest will keep what is given to him. A Suspicious Husband
text: Baal maa mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la ɛɛ a kizeehiŋ kunaa.” Gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ zum haaŋ la wia n nyaa wibii wia

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ

ref: to say to the people of Israel: Suppose a man becomes jealous and suspects that his wife has been unfaithful, but he has no proof.
text: Di zoma wa lau u jaari u ra aani u haaŋ, di u doŋŋo gɛɛ di waa doŋŋe,

ref: He must take his wife to the priest, together with one kilogram of ground barley as an offering to find out if she is guilty. No olive oil or incense is to be put on that offering.
text: guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ ú kpogli u haaŋ hiŋ di la n kizeehiŋ be, di kpa baali sau kookoo tassa suul baŋ bargɛɛ bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ, dikuu a haaŋ wia. Ú gilɛɛ wa yiili nuu di ra du a ni gɛɛ di wa kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra sag a ni, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ zoma mbusu lizaa mia di ra bagli bilchɔg wia.

ref: The priest will lead the woman to my altar and make her stand there.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpogluu ba, ú wa chi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see.

ref: He will then pour sacred water into a clay jar and stir in some dust from the floor of the sacred tent.
text: Denii u ɛɛ niinaniinanii du hɛna biini, di ɛɛ N Tanti Dia hɛri hɛɛhraa tama, di du a nii biini, á du kpol.

ref: The priest will write these curses on special paper and wash them off into the bitter water,
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ sɛbi nuuseelaa naabuu di du hɔŋ ni, di looraa du a niikpol la biini.

ref: so that when the woman drinks this water, the curses will enter her body.
text: U daŋ gil a haaŋ nyɔɔ niikpol la n na ba nuuseei tɔɔrɔɔ ni la, a zuu u hia di tɛu biinichɔg werge.

ref: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ lɛɛ zoma mbusu lizaa mia la lii u nonee biini, di viiguu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, ka kpau ba mbusu lizibɔr la.

ref: and burn part of it as a sacrifice. After that, the woman must drink the bitter water.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ mur mbusu lizaa mia hiŋ nonii suul, á ɛɛ liize mbusu di fuuah mbusu lizibɔr la ni mɔɔ, ka gil haaŋ la nyɔɔ a nii.

ref: If the woman has been unfaithful, the water will immediately make her unable to have children, and she will be a curse among her people.
text: Di u sɛmmɔɔ di nyaa wibii u jaari be, guŋwaa, di ba gillɔ u nyɔɔ a nii, biinichɔg daŋ ba u be, u naa daŋ siu, u hia su. U sɔŋ chɔgi u nɛra biini.

ref: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
text: Ka di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ a haaŋ waa chɔkkɛ di nyaa doŋa, wàá dɔɔ chɔgri. U daŋ wer lul biizi.

ref: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
text: Di baal waa zom dikuu unna aani u haaŋ wia, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ gil á haaŋ chi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, ú ɛɛ wia naa maa.

ref: If the husband is wrong, he will not be punished; but if his wife is guilty, she will be punished.
text: Baal la wàá dɔɔ chɔgri, ka haaŋ la daŋ di u wichɔgaa kinturgaa tɔɔrɔɔ di u ɛɛ gunnɛ.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
text: “Di u ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, ‘Baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa ra nyiŋŋi ú lɛɛ nua lugɔ u ra nyiŋŋi ú kpa u hinnɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, di birgi Naziri,

ref: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
text: a dɛkkɔɔ ú gil siŋ nyɔɔi ni siŋ la maa n dɔɔ bura ani sinnyɛg. A waa dɛg unna nyɔɔ grepuzi nii gɛɛ di ra di a nɔna gɛɛ a hilaa gba.

ref: During the time that you are a Nazirite, you must never go close to a dead body,
text: Saŋa la maa uŋ kpa u hiŋ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la, a waa dɛkkɛ ú waa dugli lalii.

ref: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
text: Di nɛr wa siu u sibɔɔ di pirguu, guŋ gil u nyuhuna la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la doŋ, a dɛkkɔɔ ú fuŋ u nyuhuna a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl la banna sɔ u doŋa di ra ha la.

ref: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
text: A hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl la, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ba koori kommazi anɛɛ gɛɛ koŋaahma anɛɛ ni, di wa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpa bɛl, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di kpa bɛl ge lizi mbusu di fuuuh, di ra lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih dikuu un na lalii, guŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la wia. A hɔl hiŋ maa, a dɛkkɔɔ ú sɔ u nyuu doŋa ha, ka jaa ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hor.

ref: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ú kaa kpa u hiŋ di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi saŋa la maa uŋ ɛɛ Naziri la, di lii durnya wia biini. Ú daŋ lizi pebii la n di biŋkpaŋ di wa lizi bilchɔg mbusu. Hɔpizaa la waa n bɛrɛɛ la waa jaawɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u doŋ u hinnɛ saŋa la uŋ bargi u hiŋ la.

ref: When you have completed your promised time of being a Nazirite, go to the sacred tent
text: Widaulaa la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ Naziri, di u hiŋ bargaa saŋa la wa tunnɔɔ keŋ. Ba daŋ kpogluu ba n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
text: Denii u kpa u mbusuzi lizaa kuna tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, biŋkpaŋ pebalee la n kpekke, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii hor, ni pelor n di biŋkpaŋ n kpekke, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, ni pebal n kpekke, ú ɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa hor,

ref: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
text: di kpa ba mbusuzi lizaa mia, ba mbusuzi lizaa sinni ani paanuu kɛɛgɔ suul baŋ kpa sakɔla ni ɔlivi nuu koozi dɔŋa ni, n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ, di ɔɔzi ani kɛrɛkɛssizi baŋ ɛɛ nuu waari a ni.

ref: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpaa tɛŋ, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu ani mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii.

ref: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
text: Naziri la daŋ fuŋ u nyuhuna la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la, n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua, di kpaa du niŋ la n du dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu zɛɛ la biini.

ref: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
text: Di a Naziri wa fuŋ u nyuhuna, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ kpa pebal la vaampɛrɛ baŋ daalɛɛ la, di lizi paanuu ani kɛrɛkɛsi la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ, di lii a kɛɛgɔ biini du u nonee.

ref: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
text: N kizeehiŋ la daŋ lallaa chiŋ di viigi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi see, a ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa di jaa bampirii la uŋ viigee ni hiih la baŋ lizɛɛ la ni. A ɛɛ a nanaananaarɛ, di ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ hor. Denii wàá ka ɛɛ Naziri, di jaa wer nyɔɔ siŋ.

ref: The Lord told Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “When Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel, they must say:
text: lugɔ ú ŋɔ Aarɔn ni u biibaala be lugɔ kenne ba ɔɔ ra ŋɔ di ra kissi Izrɛl hina.

ref: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
text: “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ia di kpogli ia nɛnnɛ,

ref: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
text: Ú ra binni ii ni, di ra suŋ ii ni.

ref: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
text: Ú bir u siwee chaŋ ia, di tɛɛ ia bampirsɔna.”

ref: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Awia, ba daŋ ɔɔ kpa n sɔŋ di sag Izrɛl hina ni, ń kissi baa.”

ref: When Moses had finished setting up the sacred tent, he dedicated it to the Lord, together with its furnishings, the altar, and its equipment.
text: Moosis n wa gillɛ ba baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la tuŋ, u waaruubuu nuu, di lizi u ni u bɔmbɔga maa doŋa ha, a ɛɛ kunnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Guŋ himmaanii u ɛɛ mbusu lizibɔr la ni u kuna ani u tassazi maa.

ref: Then the twelve tribal leaders of Israel, the same men who had been in charge of counting the people, came to the tent
text: Denii Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi la n ɛɛ ba domeezi sitɔɔra, di kaa ɛɛ ba dizi sitɔɔra la, n kur baa la faa ba ba mbusuzi lizaa kuna ni.

ref: with gifts for the Lord. They brought six strong carts and twelve oxen—one ox from each leader and a cart from every two.
text: Torkozi anumbɛl baŋ tɔ kuna ani navargazi fidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa ba. Nabɔnzi banɛɛ kpau lizi torkokpaŋ, nabɔma maa ge lizi navarga. Anniibuu ba faa lizi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, u Tanti Dia see.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “Accept these gifts, so the Levites can use them here at the sacred tent for carrying the sacred things.”
text: “Lɛɛ ba mbusuzi hiŋ lii ba be, bá kpaa hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia huma. Kpaa tɛɛ Levi dee gunla maga n niŋ hiini bɛl maa ú hum u huma.”

ref: Then Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites,
text: Awia, Moosis kpa a torkozi ni a navargazi tɛɛ a Levi dee.

ref: who were under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron. Moses gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for their work.
text: ka kpa torkozi anaazu ni navargazi ŋmantannaazi tɛɛ Mɛrari dee, dikuu gunla ba huma n makkɛ la wia. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn biibaal Itama faa ra binni ba maa ni.

ref: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the sacred objects that had to be carried on their shoulders.
text: Ka Moosis faa waa Kɔhaf dee la tɛɛwɛ a bɛl maa, dikuubɛɛwiai baabuu faa dɔɔ kunnanaananaa la chigaa ba vampɛrɛzi ni.

ref: On the day the altar was dedicated, the twelve leaders brought offerings for its dedication.
text: Baŋ wa waari mbusu lizibɔr la nuu, bá kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee la, nabɔnzi la faa ba mbusuzi lizaa kuna ninɛɛ a mbusu lizibɔr.

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to give his offering for the dedication.”
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii, “Hɔpizii maa, nabɔnzi la bɛl daŋ ɔɔ ba u mbusu lizaa kuna ni, bá kpa mbusu lizibɔr la du mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi nonee.”

ref: kilograms, according to the official standards;
text: bubal, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu hor,

ref: rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
text: A hɔpizaa kabɛlhiŋ hɔl la, Gidiɔni biibaal Abidan n ɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee sitɔɔri faa ba u mbusu lizaa kuna ni.

ref: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
text: Moosis n waa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la, ú ŋɔ wia Kɔraawiizi be, u faa nuu u loobiire lii chɛrubzi la n faa du Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la tua baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ nɛra ni la baambaannɛ. Kɔraawiizii ni Moosis faa ŋɔ wia.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
text: “Kali Aarɔn lugɔ di u waa chiŋŋi fintinazi aniidaanɛɛ la, ú gil a ra chaani fintina daa la see.”

ref: Aaron obeyed and placed the lamps as he was told.
text: Aarɔn chiŋŋaa gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
text: Kenne ba faa kuari a fintina daa u du. Salinnɛ ba faa luu di kuari u zɛɛ di ga hel u kela nuuzi. Ba faa kuaruubuu gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n faa bagli Moosis la. Levi dee kpai tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia

ref: The Lord said to Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: The Levites must be acceptable to me before they begin working at the sacred tent. So separate them from the rest of the Israelites
text: “Lizi Levi dee lii Izrɛl hina la biini, di lizi ba doŋa ha, bá ɛɛ nɛnanaa tɛŋ.

ref: and sprinkle them with the water that washes away their sins. Then have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes.
text: Kenne í ɛɛ baa. Mizi baa nii la n na lizi doŋa, di gil ba fuŋ ba bɔra huna maa, di chag ba laala maa, guŋ gil ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be.

ref: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Gil ba kpa nabalee ni sakɔla la baŋ koozi nuu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia kuŋfuuhlii la n dɛkkɛ, di kaa kpa nabalee nɛɛhiŋ ge u ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor.

ref: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
text: Gil Izrɛl hina maa chaali n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see, di gil Levi dee chi u dominua.

ref: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
text: Aarɔn daŋ kpa Levi dee la tɛŋ alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa n lii Izrɛl hina be, di ɛɛ baa sirya, bá ra hum n huma.

ref: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
text: Di Levi dee la wa kpa ba nonee di sagzi nabala la nyuuni ni, kpa bɛl ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor, bɛl ge ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii, di lizi n baaŋfuuih ba ni, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.

ref: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
text: Gil Levi dee la chi Aarɔn ni u biibaala see, í kpa baa tɛŋ alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii.

ref: This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way.
text: Kenne í ɛɛ di bargi Levi dee la lii Izrɛl hina be di tɛŋ, bá ɛɛ n hora.

ref: They are mine and will take the place of the first-born Israelite sons.
text: Baabuu Izrɛl hina la n niŋ kpa bahinaa tɛŋ, di ɛɛ n bɛŋ hora. N kpa baabuu di chɛr Izrɛl hina haaŋ maa biibambilugli.

ref: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
text: Biibambilugli maa n du Izrɛl, di neweere gɛɛ selle, u ɛɛ n hotte. Miŋ faa kpuuzi Ijip hina biibambilugla la, n faa lizi baabuu ba ɛɛ n hora.

ref: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
text: N jaa kpa Izrɛl hina biibambiluglaa di chɛr Levi dee la.

ref: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
text: Izrɛl hina la maa biini, Levi dee labuu n kpa sunzi Aarɔn ni u biibaala, bá ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, di ra ligzi n baaŋfuuih ba ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, wiilchɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa lau baa di ba wa dugli n Tanti Dia Bɔnaniinanii la.”

ref: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
text: Moosis, Aarɔn ani Izrɛl hina maa faa ɛɛ Levi dee la gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
text: Levi dee la faa sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, di chag ba laala. Denii Aarɔn jaa kpa baa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi alugɔ mbusu lizaa kuŋviigii, di lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih ba ni dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, ba jaa ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: A guŋ harbɔɔ, Levi dee la jaa ba di wàá hum ba huma Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Aarɔn ni u biibaala ra binni ba ni. Ba faa kpa baabuu di ra hum gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: The Lord also told Moses,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
text: Ba daŋ wer hiini ba lulla di ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini. Ka ba gilɛɛ wa lɛɛ a huma di ra hum. Kenne í tɛɛ a Levi dee ba huma.”

ref: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Moosis Sinaai Hɛribɔduma la biini. Ba Ijip hɛri lii binni anɛɛ lugli baagu biini, di ŋɔ,

ref: to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover
text: “Gil Izrɛl hina la ra di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la saŋa la miŋ dauwɛ la.

ref: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
text: Bá ra diu baagu naa hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr waa lauri siwee, di ra hiŋ u dii ŋmɛnizi ni u wiɛɛlaa maa gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la.”

ref: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
text: Ba diu Sinaai Hɛribɔduma la biini, a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr ra lauri siwee. A Izrɛl hina faa ɛɛ wiimaa gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la.

ref: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
text: Ka baŋhina faa waa wette ba di a hɔpizii a hɔl, dikuu baŋ gbɔgzi lalii di doŋ wia. Awia, ba ba Moosis ni Aarɔn be a hɔl maa

ref: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
text: di wa ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yaa doŋŋoo dikuu yaa n gbɔgzi lalii wia, ka bɛɛ n baani yaa wàá wer jaa Izrɛl hina ni, di kpa yaa mbusu lizaa kuna di waa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi saŋa la baŋ dauwɛ lai?”

ref: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
text: Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra kpaŋ ka n pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di zum gunla un niŋ ŋɔ ii wia.”

ref: The Lord then told Moses
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, ‘Di ii bɛl maa gɛɛ ii naana bɛl maa wa doŋŋo dikuu uŋ gbɔgzi lalii wia gɛɛ di a hiŋ la ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ, ka u daŋ haa wer di a Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ hiŋ.

ref: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
text: Ba daŋ ɔɔ diubuu baagu nɛɛhiŋ la hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl, di bɔr waa lauri siwee la. Ba daŋ ɔɔ hee pebii la ol ni paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ ani tagkpola.

ref: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ ban niŋ gil a ol yemmaa hɔɔ waa pizi gɛɛ di ku u hog bɛl maa. Di ba waa di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ, ba ra hiŋzi u widaulaa ni u wiɛɛlaa.

ref: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
text: Ka di baal maa waa doŋŋe mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, di waa ŋmɛnɛɛ ge laŋŋɛ, ka vɛɛ a hɔpizii dii, bá duŋŋuu lii u nɛra biini, dikuu uŋ waa u mbusu lizaa kuna kpawɛɛ wa tɛŋ saŋa la n dɛkkɛ la wia. A badee wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u ni.

ref: Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations. The Cloud over the Sacred Tent (Exodus
text: Di hɔɔhri du ii biini ka ra nyiŋŋi ú di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ naa, u daŋ wer diu, ka a dɛkkɔɔ ú hiŋzi u dii ŋmɛnizi ni u widaulaa. Hɔɔhri ni bol bie maa danna hiŋ ŋmɛnikpannɛ.’ ” Baama la n guali Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ni wia

ref: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
text: Gunnɛ u faa haŋ du di ra la. Baama la ɔɔ faa ɛɛu lugɔ niŋ hamuŋa ni.

ref: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
text: Di a baama haŋ wa guali Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni hɔpizaa anɛɛ gɛɛ baagu kpaŋ gɛɛ biŋkpaŋ, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ du ba chɔɔri bɔttɛ. Ka di u haŋ wa izi, ba ge ɔɔ izuu.

ref: The Lord told Moses:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
text: “Luu saliŋhuŋŋu di kuari bensunozi anɛɛ, di kpaa ra yir Izrɛl hina, ba ra chaali ani di ba waa nyiŋŋi izaa di la bɔfalii.

ref: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: Di ba haŋ wa kpau huuh anɛɛ hiŋ maa, Izrɛl hina la maa daŋ chaali i be n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua.

ref: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
text: Ka di kpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ ba huuh, Izrɛl domeezi nabɔnzii niŋ chaali i see.

ref: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
text: Di ba kaa wa huuh nɛɛhiŋ, banla n chɔɔ wiifurii nodig wiikakag la daŋ izi di ra la. A huuihrɛ ninna bagli lugɔ ba izaa helloo.

ref: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
text: Di i ɔɔ wa ŋɔ í chaali a nɛra maa, ɛɛ huuh a bensunozi anɛɛ hiŋ maa, ka a wiraazi kurgi.

ref: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
text: Aarɔn biibaala la n ɛɛ n kizeehina labuu niŋ ɔɔ ra huuah. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulaarɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna maa.

ref: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
text: Di i ni i nɛra wàá lɔ ii dɔm la n na fir ia laal ii himmaa hɛri, ií huuh a bensunozi kakpaŋ. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum daŋ liizi ii wia di lɛɛ ia.

ref: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
text: Ií hinaa dii, ii hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazi ani Baagufalaa Dii Hɔpizaa la, ii daŋ ɔɔ huuah di du mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna la ni, a ɛɛ wiliizaa ii be. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.” Izrɛl hina n izee lii Sinaai Hɛribɔduma wia

ref: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
text: Binni anɛɛ, baagu nɛɛhiŋ la hɔpizaa tokko hɔl, Izrɛl hina n izee lii Ijip hɛri la, baama la izi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni.

ref: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina izi Sinaai Hɛribɔduma di ra juuri, a baama jaa wa hel Paran Hɛribɔduma di chi.

ref: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
text: Ka ba lii de dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Moosis be di ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la wia.

ref: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
text: Juda dee ni sugezi la aŋhina ni ba tuutaa tɔ see. Aminadab biibaal Nasɔnnɛ faa ba nabɔma.

ref: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
text: Zuar biibaal Nɛtanɛl genii faa ra binni Isaka dee ni,

ref: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
text: Hɛlɔn biibaal Ɛliab ge ra binni Zɛbulɔn dee ni.

ref: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
text: Denii ba wil Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, Gɛsɔn ni Mɛrari domeezi la n na chiu la, paaguu chi di lii ra vol.

ref: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
text: Rubin dee ni dizi la n ja ba ni, ni ba tuutaa kaa lii hiŋ. Sɛdur biibaal Ɛlizuruu faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma.

ref: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
text: Zurisadai biibaal Sɛlumiɛllɛ faa ɛɛ Simɛɔn dee la binni.

ref: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
text: Diwɛl biibaal Ɛliasaf ge faa ɛɛ Gad dee la nabɔma.

ref: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
text: Denii Kɔhaf domee la izi di kpa kunnanaananaa la chi di lii, di ra la. Gɛsɔn ni Mɛrari dizi labuu niŋ baŋzi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la mɔɔ ka Kɔhaf domee la haa ba.

ref: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
text: Ɛfram dee sugezi la ni ba tuuta ge kaa lii hiŋ. Amihud biibaal Ɛlisamaa faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma.

ref: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
text: Pɛdazur biibaal Gamaliɛllɛ faa ɛɛ Manasɛ dee nabɔma.

ref: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
text: Gidiɔni biibaal Abidannɛ faa ɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee nabɔma.

ref: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
text: Dan ni dizi la n chɔɔwɛ dugli baa la ge jaa lii ni ba tuuta. Amisadai biibaal Ahiɛzaa faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma.

ref: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
text: Ɔkran biibaal Pagiɛl genii faa ɛɛ Asɛ dee nabɔma.

ref: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
text: Ɛnan biibaal Ahira ge faa ɛɛ Naftali dee nabɔma.

ref: This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
text: Gunnɛ Izrɛl sugezi la ɔɔ faa lii di hiŋzi dɔŋa di ra la.

ref: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ u dakiah Hɔbab, n ɛɛ u hila baal Jɛtro n ɛɛ Midian hinuu biibaal be, “Yaa ra la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ yaa labuu. A hiŋ yaa. Yaa daŋ ga kpoglii nɛnnɛ. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina kunnanaa.”

ref: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
text: Hɔbab ŋɔ, “Akai, maa la. N daŋ bir kaali n himmaa hɛri ni n nɛra be.”

ref: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
text: Ka Moosis ŋɔ u be, “Gaafura, gilɛɛ waa gil yaa. Hinuu zum bɔr la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ya chɔɔ a hɛribɔduma biini. Hinuu yaa sitɔɔri.

ref: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
text: Di yaa nii laŋŋɔ, yaa nii daŋ bɔnni kunnanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n niŋ tɛɛ yaa la.”

ref: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
text: Awia, ba izi lii Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ la zɛɛ. Levi dee la chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di tɔ ba see, ba vol hɔpizaa ahoro di ra nyiŋŋi bɔr, bá so di heezi.

ref: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
text: Di Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la haŋ waa lii, Moosis ɔɔ ŋɔu, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, izi chiŋ! Gil i dɔma yaari, di gil ba ra chɔ di ba wa nai.”

ref: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
text: Di dakka la haŋ wa chi heezaa bɔr la, Moosis ɔɔ ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, bir ba Izrɛl hina la n kpillɛ werge maa, ba wàá wer kur baa la be.”

ref: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
text: A nɛra faa faari di ra nuumi dikuu ba anuula wia. Kɔraawiizi faa nuu, u baaŋ fuuh ba ni werge maa. Denii u gil niŋ wa zuu ba chɔɔribɔr la di di u kɛraa yeŋ.

ref: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
text: A nɛra n wa wiiwe tɛɛ Moosis, u suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi nuu, di gil a niŋ dim.

ref: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
text: Awia, ba faa ra yir de Tabɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, niŋ faa lii Kɔraawiizi benii di waa di ba baambaaŋ. Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ Izrɛl hina zaahra wia

ref: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
text: Hɔɔhrijagazi la n du ba biini la faa faari di ra kɛlli diudumazi, guŋ gil Izrɛl hina gba faari di ra wii di ra ŋɔ, “Di yaa gba faa na ol, yaa daŋ hee!

ref: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
text: Yaa n faa du Ijip hɛri la, yaa faa na nyinnii di ra hee, di faa na kiime irizi, gaabu ani alibaasa iri bɛl banna yir galik di ra di.

ref: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
text: Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, lɔzi jaa ra kpu yaabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa waa kaa na kummaa di ra di, di maana naa bɛŋ lɛi.”

ref: The manna was like small whitish seeds
text: Maana la faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zule.

ref: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
text: U pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii ra di tɔɔrɔɔ kennei? Bɛɛ n ɛɛ di chɔgi i biini, i gil n na binni nɛra naa ninɛi?

ref: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
text: Minuu kpogli ba hizi di lul baa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ ń kpogli baa lugɔ biifulli, di ra la hɛri la hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ, i daŋ kpa tɛɛ ba naabaala lai?

ref: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
text: Lee ń na ol tɛɛ nɛra naa maanɛi? Ba wiiwoo ra duŋ, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Tɛɛ yaa ol yá hee!’

ref: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
text: N bɛŋ waa wer kpogli nɛra naa, ba tɔɔrɔɔ siili n ninɛɛ.

ref: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses

ref: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
text: I ni i biibaala bɛnnɛ ninna binni Bɔnaniinanii ani mbusu lizibɔr la ni, guŋ gil n baaŋfuuihchɔgii la gilɛɛ kaa wàá izi Izrɛl hina ni.

ref: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
text: N himmaanii lizi i lulla Levi dee la di lii Izrɛl hina biini di sunzii, bá ɛɛ n hora, di ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini.

ref: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
text: Ka i ni i biibaala bɛnnɛ ninna hum n kizeehina huma mbusu lizibɔr la ani Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa patiisa la biini. N kpa n kizeehina humaa di ra sunzii. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa dugli kunnaananaa la n du u biini la, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpuu.” Mbusuzi lizaa kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee hora wia

ref: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
text: A ola daŋ ɛɛ i hora gunla bampirii la baŋ ɔɔ viigi ani nodig hiih la, n ɛɛ i hora la.

ref: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
text: Hinuu dɔɔ a mbusuzi lizaa kuna bɔnanaananaa himmaa la baŋ waa fuuh la. Di lii mbusuzi lizaa kuna la maa baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛŋ la, di miarɛ, wichɔgaa gɛɛ bilchɔg mbusu lizaa kunaa, á ɛɛ i ni i biibaala horaa.

ref: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
text: Ií ra dia alugɔ kuna la n ɛɛ nanaananaa himmaa la. Baal maanii niŋ na dia. Kpaa lugɔ kunnanaananaa.

ref: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
text: Annii gba ɛɛ i hora, kuna la maa baŋ lizɛɛ di lii Izrɛl hina mbusu lizaa kuŋviigaa biini di dau a bɛŋ. N kpaabuu di ra tɛɛ i ni i biizi á ɛɛ ii hora di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Nɛr la maa n du i dia, di waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be, daŋ wer dia.

ref: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
text: N kpa ɔlivi nuunanaa ni siŋfalaa la n wesse ani mia la maa baŋ ɔɔ lizi di wàá tɛŋ, a ɛɛ ba lugli pattikuna labuu di ra tɛi.

ref: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
text: A hɛri diulugla maa baŋ ɔɔ kpa ba di waa tɛŋ la, ɛɛ i horaa. Nɛr la maa n du i dia, di waa doŋŋe n be daŋ wer dia.

ref: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
text: Kunla maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛŋ, ú ɛɛ n bɛmbɛŋ kuŋ di lii Izrɛl hɛri ɛɛ i horaa.

ref: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
text: Kummaa biilugli, di neweere gɛɛ di selle, baŋ kpawɛɛ di tɛŋ, ɛɛ i hotte. Ka i daŋ wer gil ba bir yau newea biibambilugla. Di kaa gil bá bir yau sel la maa n doŋŋe n be biiballugli gba.

ref: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
text: Di bie maa wa di baagu, ba daŋ yawuu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau anue, gunla banna mɛgzaa n Tanti Dia biini la.

ref: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
text: Ka nau gɛɛ peezi gɛɛ buuŋ waa biilugla, á ɛɛ a nanaananaarɛ, ba wàá wer bir yawaa. Ɛɛ kpa a challi di mizi mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di fuuh a nuuri á ɛɛ mbusu sefuuhlaa la sɔɔh n summɛ di tɛŋ.

ref: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
text: Mbusu lizaa kunnanaananaa la maa Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ kpa ba di waa tɛŋ la, n kpaabuu di ra tɛɛ i ni i biizi. Guŋ ɛɛ n nii ni i naanna nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ saŋa maa labuu.”

ref: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be, “Hàá dɔɔ kapɛttɛ kuŋ maa gɛɛ di dɔɔ a hɛri yemmaa. Minuu i kundɔɔlii Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
text: N kpa Izrɛl hina kuna maa fi bɔkpaŋ la baŋ ɔɔ lizi tɛŋ labuu di ra tɛɛ Levi dee, á ɛɛ ba kinturgaa dikuu ba huma, baŋ ɔɔ ra hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la wia.

ref: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
text: Levi dee labuu ninna hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia hiŋ huma, di ra di u gbɛllaa tɔɔrɔɔzi maa. Guŋ ɛɛ widauliirɛ tɛɛ i naanna maa. Ba waa na kapɛttɛ maa di lii Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
text: “Ŋɔ Levi dee be, ‘Di ii wa lɛɛ kuna fi bɔkpaŋ la Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ lizi, n kpa tɛɛ ia la, á ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuna la, ií bɔnnaa bɔra fi, di lizi a bɔkpaŋ tɛŋ.

ref: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
text: N daŋ kpa mbusu lizaa naa ú ɛɛ lugɔ patti n ɔɔ lizi u mbusu lizaa mifalaa gɛɛ siŋfalii tɛŋ la.

ref: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ií ɔɔ lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ di ɛɛ a nanaananaa himmaa la di ra tɛŋ.’

ref: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
text: Kaa ŋɔ Levi dee be, ‘Di ii wa lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ di tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ii daŋ kpogli anla n kawɛɛ gunla patti n ɔɔ kpogli u hora, di u wa lizi n hora di tɛŋ tuŋ la.

ref: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
text: Ii ni ii diini hina daŋ wer di a bɔr la n kawɛɛ yemmaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii huma la iinna hum n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini la kinturgaare guŋ.

ref: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
text: Ii wàá di bilchɔg, di ii ɔɔ lizi a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ tɛŋ, ka ra di a bɔra la n kawɛɛ. Ka ii ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa dia, di ii haa waa a bɔra la n wesse nɛnnɛ la lizɛɛ tɛŋ, di ii ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ kpuuzi ia.’ ”

ref: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
text: “N Gbɔg widaulaarɛ keŋ. Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ bá lizi nalor aahmu la n kpekke, u haa waa huma maa hummɛ di wa tɛɛ ia.

ref: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
text: Ií kpau tɛɛ Ɛliaza la n ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la, ba daŋ lawuu lii ba chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di kɔrguu u see,

ref: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
text: Ɛliaza kpa u nonibii lii u chal di chaŋ n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la see di mizi buniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
text: U danna binni ka ba fuuh a nau maa, u hɔŋ, u ol, u chal ani u biini kuna maa.

ref: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
text: N kizeehiŋ daŋ kpa hɛriŋkpol ni hisɔp daa ani peezi huna n aahwɛ di ha a niŋ biini.

ref: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
text: Di guŋ wa tunnɔ, n kizeehiŋ la daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii. U daŋ jaa wer zuu ba chɔɔribɔr la biini ka haa doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana.

ref: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
text: Baal la gba n fuuh a nau la daŋ chag u laala, di sɔ nii, ka ge doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana.

ref: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
text: Baal la n waa doŋŋe n be daŋ paa a nalor hɔɔhri di ga dau bɔr la n waa doŋŋe n be ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ baŋgia. A daŋ chɔɔ de tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, baa ɔɔ kpa di ra du doŋa lizaa nii biini. Aabuu ba kpa di ra lizi nɛra wichɔgaa doŋa.

ref: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
text: Baal la ge n paa a hɔɔhri la gba, daŋ chag u laala, ka doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana. Keŋ daŋ ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni hɔɔhra la maa n du ba be la, di hanna la.

ref: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
text: Nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi lalii maa daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
text: U daŋ ɛɛ a nii di sɔ lizi u doŋa, a hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ hɔl ani a aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, denii u doŋa jaa tuŋ. Ka di waa u hiŋ sɔwɛɛ a hɔpizaa ahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ hɔla la, u doŋa wàá tuŋ.

ref: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
text: Nɛr la maa n gbɔgzi lalii maa ka waa u hiŋ sɔwɛɛ, doŋ n Tanti Diarɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋi a hindee lii Izrɛl hina biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wɔɔ mizɛɛ doŋa lizaa nii la. U doŋŋoo mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi be, u doŋa haa du u ninɛɛ.

ref: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
text: Di nɛr haŋ wa siu tanti dia biini, widaulii la n du denii keŋ. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa zuu a tanti dia biini ani unla maa n du u biini, daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
text: Kunla maa n waa tua dɔɔwɛ ge, daŋ doŋ.

ref: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
text: Di nɛr la maa haŋ wa gbɔgzi nɛr la baŋ kpuwɛɛ gɛɛ u saŋa n helle u siu bossee, gɛɛ di nɛr la maa wa gbɔgzi newee hog gɛɛ ŋmam, daŋ doŋ n be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
text: Denii baal la n waa doŋŋe n be kpa hisɔp daa, di lii a nii di mizi a tanti dia ni kuna la maa n du u biini ani nɛr la maa n gbɔgzi newee hog gɛɛ lalii gɛɛ ŋmam.

ref: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
text: Nɛr la n waa doŋŋe n bee niŋ mizi nɛr la n doŋŋe hɔpizaa ahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ hɔla la. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl, u jaa sɔu di lizi u doŋa. Nɛr la baŋ lizi u doŋa la daŋ chag u laala di sɔ nii, u doŋa tuŋ a duana ni.

ref: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
text: Ka di nɛr la n doŋŋe n be la waa u doŋa lizɛɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ ba duŋŋuu lii ba biini, dikuu uŋ doŋ n Tanti Dia la wia. Baŋ wɔɔ mizɛɛ doŋ lizaa nii la wia, u doŋŋoo n be.

ref: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
text: Keŋ ɛɛ widaulii la n chɔɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa di hanna la. Baal la gba n kpa a doŋa lizaa nii di mizuu la gba daŋ chag u laala. Nɛr la maa ge n gbɔgzi a nii gba daŋ doŋ n be guŋŋ di ra ba duana.

ref: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
text: Nɛr la n doŋŋe n be haŋ wa gbɔgzi kummaa, a kundee ge gba daŋ doŋ n be. Nɛr la maa ge wa gbɔgzuu u gba daŋ doŋ n be di ra ba duana.”

ref: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
text: Lugli baagu hiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina maa wa hel Zin Hɛribɔduma biini, di chɔɔ Kadɛs. Denii Miriam siu, ba huguu.

ref: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
text: Nii faa waa hoo de, a nɛra faa chaali di wa bar Moosis ni Aarɔn di ra nuumi,

ref: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
text: di ŋɔ Moosis be, “Di yaa ni yaa balaa la maa faa siuzɔɔ Kɔraawiizi see, guŋ faa bɔ.

ref: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa di ba hɛribɔduma naa biini, ya ni yaa sela maa wa siuzɛi?

ref: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpogli yaa lii Ijip hɛri di ba bɔkpol naa biinei? De waa mia ni fig daazi ni grepu daazi gɛɛ pomegranet dɔɔwɛ. Nii gba waa hoo yá nyɔɔ!”

ref: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
text: Denii Moosis ni Aarɔn lii a nɛra be di la Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la dominua di ga chol pi hɛri, Kɔraawiizi girme chaani ba ni.

ref: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
text: “Kpa daŋkpala la n teli N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, í ni Aarɔn chaali a nɛra maa. Denii ii ŋɔ wia tɛɛ bital la, ba maa sibɔɔ. Nii daŋ pozi di lii u ni. Gunnɛ ii ɛɛ nii lii a bital ni tɛɛ a nɛra ni ba sela maa, bá nyɔɔ.”

ref: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
text: Awia, Moosis faa kpa a daa di lii a Tanti Dia biini, gunla uŋ ŋɔ u be la.

ref: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
text: U ni Aarɔn chaali a nɛra maa a bital zɛɛ. Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Mmɔri diire, ií ra nuu! A dɛkkɔɔ yá gil nii lii bii naa ni tɛɛ iaa?”

ref: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
text: Denii Moosis lalli u daa la di lɔ a bital bunɛɛ. Nii pozi lii, a nɛra ni ba sela maa nyɔɔ.

ref: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be, “Dikuu iiŋ wan yardɛɛ nɛnnɛ di kpaŋ girme lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ Izrɛl hina be wia, ii wàá kpogli baa zuu hɛri la minna tɛɛ baa la biini.”

ref: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
text: Mɛribaa wia naa faa ɛɛ, denii Izrɛl hina faa nuumi du Kɔraawiizi ni, u bagli baa gunla uŋ ɛɛ naniinanii la. Ɛdɔm koori n tɔ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ wia

ref: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
text: Moosis faa hum u balaa Ɛdɔm hina Koori be di lii Kadɛs, bá ga ŋɔ, “Kenne i lulla Izrɛl hina ŋɔ, ‘I zum tɔɔrɔɔ la n huuzi yaa, yaa di dɔgnyaa.

ref: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
text: Yaa naabaala la Ijip hɛrii, yaa du de binni kpilakpila maa. A Ijip hina sunni yaa ni yaa mɛɛwaa werge maa,

ref: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
text: ka yaa n wa wiiwe du Kɔraawiizi ni, u nuu yaa wiraare, di hum u mɛlika u wa lizi yaa di lii Ijip hɛri. Filaŋkeŋ, bol la banna yir Kadɛs la n du i bol magbɔɔ nua labuu yaa so.

ref: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
text: Yaa ra ɛɛibuu jaande, gil ya ga i hɛri di kaali yaa laŋribɔr. Yaa waa zuu ii kooni gɛɛ ii grepu daazi kooni gɛɛ di wàá nyɔɔ ii kɔlɔŋzi niiri. I ŋmɛnizeŋ bɛnnɛ ya hiŋ guŋŋ di ga lii i hɛri, di yaa waa yemmaa bɛɛwɛ.’ ”

ref: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
text: Ka Ɛdɔm hina ŋɔ, “Ií wàá ga yaa hɛri! Di ii haŋ kur, yaa daŋ lii lɔ ia laal.”

ref: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
text: Izrɛl hina la bir ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ ŋmɛnizeŋ di ga lii, ka di yaa sela wa nyɔɔ ii nii maa, yaa daŋ turgi. Yaa hanna nyiŋŋuu yá vol di ga lii, wiimaa waa ka jaa.”

ref: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
text: Ba kaa kuari ŋɔ, “Ií wàá ga de!” Denii Ɛdɔm hina laallɔɔrakpila n kpekke werge faa vɔɔ laal bá ga chem ba ni.

ref: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
text: Dikuu Ɛdɔm hina n faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá ga ba hɛri biini wia, Izrɛl hina bir ga bɔduma. Aarɔn siu wia

ref: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
text: Izrɛl hina la maa faa izi lii Kadɛs di ga hel Bizeŋ Hɔɔ,

ref: on the Edomite border, the Lord said,
text: n dugli Ɛdɔm magbɔɔ la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis ni Aarɔn be,

ref: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.

text: “Yaa mɛɛ siuwɔɔ hɛribɔduma la biini. U faa waa Kɔra harbɔɔ hiŋra la biini jaawɛ, baabuu faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua la. Ka u siuwɔɔ dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia, di waa biibaal lullɛ.

text: Bɛɛ wiarɛ yaa mɛɛ sɔŋ dim u domee biini, dikuu uŋ waa biibaal lullɛ wiai? Ií tɛɛ yaa, yaa kapɛttɛ di lii yaa mɛɛ lulla biini.”

text: Gil ú chi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani nɛra la maa see, í kpau bagli baa lugɔ waa niŋ jaa wa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri.

ref: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.

text: U daŋ ɔɔ dɛlli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza la n niŋ ɔɔ kpa Urim ni Tumim di ra zum n kipar labuu. Di u wa ŋɔ bá lii, ba daŋ lii, di u wa ŋɔ bá zuu, ba daŋ zuu.”

text: ka jaa kpa u nonii sag u nyuu, di lizuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
