text: Di suŋguru haa du u mɛɛ dia ka ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi lugɔ, u daŋ tɛu kuŋ gɛɛ u daŋ vɛɛ wiibɛl ɛɛi,

ref: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
text: Ka di u mɛɛ wa nuuwɔ di ŋɔ waa sɛɛ, guŋwaa, u nua hiŋ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil tɛu, dikuu u mɛɛ n waa sɛɛwɛ wia.

ref: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
text: u jaari nuu guŋ ka waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu, guŋwaa, wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la haa chigɔɔ.

ref: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
text: Ka di u jaari wa nuu guŋ di ŋɔ wàá sɛɛ, guŋwaa, u nua hiŋ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil tɛu.

ref: Widows and divorced women must keep every promise they make to the Lord.
text: Luhaaŋ gɛɛ haaŋ la u jaari n vɛɛwɛ ka u lɛɛ nua, a nua daŋ chi.

ref: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
text: Di haaŋ du u jaari dia ka ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,

ref: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
text: u jaari nuu guŋ ka waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ gɛɛ di duŋŋuu, guŋwaa, wii la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la haa chigɔɔ.

ref: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
text: Ka di u nuu guŋ di ŋɔ wàá sɛɛ, guŋwaa, u nua la ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, dikuu u jaari n waa guŋ sɛɛwɛ wia, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil tɛu.

ref: Her husband has the final say about any promises she makes to the Lord.
text: U jaari daŋ wer sɛɛ gɛɛ di vɛɛ nua la maa wia uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
text: Ka di u jaari wa nuu guŋ ka wàá wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu, guŋwaa, u sɛɛwɔɔ tɛu lugɔ u nuuŋɔɔlaa la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la haa chigɔɔ.

ref: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
text: Ka di a wa birgoo, ka u haa ŋɔ waa sɛɛ, guŋwaa, waabuu a wia maa chug.”

ref: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
text: Gbɔgni naabuu Kɔraawiizi kpa tɛɛ Moosis, di ra bagli baal ni u haaŋ wia ani mɛɛ ni u biihambie la, n haa du u dia wia.

ref: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
text: “La di ga tɛr Midian hina digna dikuu wia la baŋ kpawɛɛ dau Izrɛl hina la mɔɔ, ka haa ga chɔɔ i naabaala be.”

ref: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií vɔɔ laal dí la ga lɔ Midian hina, di tɛr ba digna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
text: Denii baala kagboŋ lii dee maa biini, ba maa jaa ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ, di ɛɛ laal sirya.

ref: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
text: Denii Moosis jaa gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas tɔ a laallɔɔra kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ la see. U kpa kunnanaananaa la aŋhina ani bensunoniinazi la ban ninna huuh di ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ a laallɔɔra.

ref: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
text: Ba la ga lɔ Midian hina gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Moosis be la, di kpuuzi ba baala maa.

ref: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
text: A Izrɛl hina faa lauri a Midian hina haana, ba biizi ani ba sela, di paagi ba kuna maa kaali.

ref: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
text: Ba faa fuuh a Midian hina bolzenaa ani ba laal chɔɔribɔra la maa di jaa.

ref: Israel's soldiers gathered together everything they had taken from the Midianites, including the captives and the animals.
text: A Izrɛl hina jaa paa a Midian hina kundɔɔlaa ni ba sela, haali di lauri ba nɛra la n haa kawɛɛ la maa di jaa.

ref: Then they returned to their own camp in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, where Moses, Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders met the troops outside camp.
text: Denii Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani a nɛra nabɔnzi maa jaa izi, di lii ba chɔɔribɔr la ga chem ba ni.

ref: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
text: U pɛɛzi baa, “Bɛɛ wiarɛ ii gil a haana naa haa du de ni miibɔɔi?

ref: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
text: Awia, ií kpuuzi a biibaala ani haaŋ la maa n zum baal,

ref: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
text: ka biihaana la maa n haa waa baal zummɛ, ií gil baawaa tɛɛ iihinaa.

ref: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
text: Nɛr la maa n kpu nɛr gɛɛ di gbɔgzi lalii, a hiŋ lii ii chɔɔribɔr la baŋgia di du de hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. A hɔpizaa ahoro ni aniidaanɛɛ hɔla la, ií sɔ iihinaa ni banla iin laurɛɛ ba la, di lizi ii doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be.

ref: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
text: Ií lizi ii laala, kunla maa baŋ kpa hɔŋ ani buuŋ huna gɛɛ daa di kuari doŋa ha, á ɛɛ kunnanaananaa n be.”

ref: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire. After you take it out, sprinkle it with the water that purifies. Everything else should only be sprinkled with the water. Do all of this, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
text: ani kunla maa n waa niŋ na ɔm, ii daŋ wer kpau du niŋ biini u ɛɛ kunnanii, di kaa kpa nii la n na lizi doŋa di yagluu, ú du wer. Ka kunla maa n wàá wer zuu niŋ, ii daŋ ɛɛ nii di yagluu, ú du wer.

ref: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and after that, you will be clean and may return to the camp.” Everything Taken from the Midianites Is Divided
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la, ií chag ii laala, guŋ gil ii ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa n be, ka ii jaa zuu a chɔɔribɔr.” Kuna la baŋ paawɛ laal biini bɔnnaa wia

ref: The Lord told Moses:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
text: Lɛɛ a keŋ kuna naa di lii a laallɔɔra ni a nɛra hordiilaa biini, di kpaa tɛɛ n kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza. N hor diilaare guŋ.

ref: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
text: Awia, yaa ballɔɔ ya wa kpa saliŋ gbittizi, nonibisiga, digni kuna ni baŋaa kuna la yaa n paawɛ di lii a Midian hina be, yá wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di lizi u baaŋfuuih yaa ni dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia.”

ref: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
text: Denii Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza jaa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
text: ani haana la n haa waa baal maa zummɛ ge du kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛ,

ref: The army commanders went to Moses
text: A laallɔɔra sitɔɔra maa la Moosis be,

ref: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
text: di ga ŋɔ u be, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa kur laallɔɔra maanii di na di ba bɛl maa waa leuwe.

ref: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
text: Denii Moosis ni Ɛliaza jaa lɛɛ a kuna la maa baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari la.

ref: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
text: Anla a laallɔɔra n lizɛɛ tɛɛ bahinaa la waa faa waa annii naa ni jaawɛ.

ref: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
text: Denii Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza jaa lɛɛ saliŋ la maa di lii a laallɔɔra sitɔɔra be, di kpaa ga du Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia la biini, bá ra liizi gunla Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛ n ɛɛwɛ.

ref: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
text: di lɛɛ a hɛri dɔɔ. A tuna, ii daŋ jaa wer bir di ba ii hɛri di wa so, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii ɛɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ ií ɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni ii dɔŋahina Izrɛl hinaa. Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa zum lugɔ Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii hɛri la ɛɛ ii hotte.

ref: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
text: Rubin ani Gad dizi faa dɔɔ sela kpilaa werge maa, ba faa na lugɔ Jaza ni Giliad hɛssi wessoo sela dɛɛzaa.

ref: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
text: Denii ba jaa ba Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani a nɛra nabɔnzi be di wa ŋɔ,

ref: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
text: hɛssi la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ di du Izrɛl hina nonee la wessoo tɛɛ sela, i balaa ge dɔɔ sela.

ref: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
text: Di yaa wia parii, kpa a hɛri naa tɛɛ yaa ya so, ú ɛɛ yaa hor, ka ya gilɛɛ kaa waa gi a Jɔɔdan muu naa.”

ref: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Gad ani Rubin dizi la be, “A dɛkkɔɔ ii hɛri hina la laal, ka iawaa so bɔnnaa?

ref: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa bɔhuaih du Izrɛl hina ni, ba gilɛɛ waa gi di ra zuu a hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baa lai?

ref: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
text: Kennaa himmaanii ii mɛɛwaa faa ɛɛ, saŋa la miŋ lizi baa di lii Kadɛs Bania lugɔ ba la ga daani a hɛri la.

ref: They went as far as Eshcol Valley, then returned and told the people that we should not enter it.
text: Baŋ wa la Ɛskɔl Faalim bá ga daani a hɛri na la, ba faa bittɔɔ ba di wa du Izrɛl hina bɔhuaih, dikuu a hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ baa la zuui wia.

ref: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ ba be, “Di ii biine maanii ii ra ŋɔ, guŋwaa, ii ɛɛ sirya Kɔraawiizi see di ga lɔ laal.

ref: but he was so angry with the others that he forced them to wander around in the desert for
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Izrɛl hina ni, u gil ba du hɛribɔduma di juuri guŋŋ binni tokkoanɛɛ. Banla maa n faa ɛɛ guŋ wichɔgaa, di zuu u ni la, faa siuzi de.

ref: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
text: Awia, Moosis jaa kpa de tɛɛ Makir domee la n lii Manasɛ dee biini la, ba so.

ref: Now you people of Reuben and Gad are doing the same thing and making the Lord even angrier.
text: Filaŋkeŋ ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ii mɛɛwaa, a guŋ himmaa wichɔgaarɛ ii dɔɔ, di ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuihchɔgii la kaa fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge maa.

ref: If you reject the Lord, he will once again abandon his people and leave them here in the desert. And you will be to blame!
text: Di ii vɛɛ u hiŋaa, u daŋ gil a nɛra naa maa ta hɛribɔduma naa biini, ba sɔnchɔgii chug ia.”

ref: The men from Reuben and Gad replied: Let us build places to keep our sheep and goats, and towns for our wives and children,
text: Denii ba ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Yaa danna nyiŋŋi yá du liga di tɛɛ yaa sela, di kaa ma bola ge di tɛɛ yaa haana ni biizi.

ref: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
text: Yaawaa bir ba yaa bola, di Izrɛl hinuu maa waa u kapɛttɛ nawɛɛ.

ref: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
text: Yaa ni baa waa kpau di di kapɛttɛ maa, a Jɔɔdan muu keŋkere la hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa hotte ú wiifurii bɔr naa.”

ref: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
text: Ií laallɔɔra maa gi Jɔɔdan muu, Kɔraawiizi tɔ ba see bá ga lɔ yaa dɔma guŋŋ Kɔraawiizi wa kpegli baa,

ref: But if you don't keep your promise, you will sin against the Lord and be punished.
text: Ka di ii wa vɛɛ guŋ ɛɛi, ii daŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, wibii maa u daŋ tɛr ii digna dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
text: Ií ma bolzenaa di tɛɛ ii haana ni ii biizi ani liga tɛɛ ii sela, ka ií ɛɛ wia la maa iiŋ ŋɔ ii daŋ ɛɛ la.”

ref: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
text: Gad ni Rubin dizi la ŋɔ Moosis be, “Yaa nabɔma, yaa daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
text: Yaa haana ni biizi ni yaa sela maa daŋ du Giliad bolzenaa naa biini.

ref: But those of us who are prepared for battle will cross the Jordan and fight for the Lord.
text: Ka yaa maa ɛɛ siryaa, Kɔraawiizi tɔ yaa see, ya gi a Jɔɔdan muu hiŋ, di ga lɔ laal gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”

ref: Then Moses said to Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders,
text: Denii Moosis jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ni Josua ani Izrɛl diini sitɔɔra la be,

ref: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
text: “Di Gad ni Rubin dizi haŋ wa vɔɔ tɔ ii see di gi Jɔɔdan muu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, ii ga wer yoo di lɛɛ a hɛri, ií kpa Giliad hɛri tɛɛ baa, ú ɛɛ ba ge dizi hor.

ref: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
text: Ka di ba waa vɔɔwɛ ii ni baa gi, a dɛkkɔɔ ba na ba kapɛttɛ di lii Keenan hɛri.”

ref: The tribes of Gad and Reuben replied, “We are your servants and will do whatever the Lord has commanded.
text: Denii Gad ni Rubin dizi la ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, ii balaa daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
text: Yaa daŋ gi a Jɔɔdan muu hiŋ, Kɔ́raawiizi tɔ yaa see, yá ga yoo a laal di foozi Keenan hɛri. Ka kuna la n niŋ ɛɛ yaa hora la waa, daŋ du a muu keŋkere naa.”

ref: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
text: Denii Moosis kpa Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn ani Basan hina Koori Ɔɔg hɛssi ani bolzenaa la maa n baraa, di tɛɛ Gad ni Rubin dizi ani Joosɛf biibaal Manasɛ dee yeŋ.

ref: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
text: Denii Gad dee la kaa bir ma bolzeŋkpega Dibɔn, Atarɔf, Aroa,

ref: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
text: Atrɔf Sɔfan, Jaza, Jɔgbɛha,

ref: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
text: Bɛf Nimra ani Bɛf Haran, di kaa ma ba sela duuribɔra.

ref: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
text: Denii Rubin dee la ge bir ma Hɛsbɔn, Ɛlialɛ, Kiriatam,

ref: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
text: ani Sibma, di kpa bola la baŋ faa ra yir Nɛbɔ ni Baal Miɔn. Annii maa sɔnaa ba taa kuari dau.

ref: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
text: Manasɛ biibaal Makir domee la ge la Giliad, di ga lɔ Amɔri hina la n faa soge de la, di duŋŋi baa ka so de.

ref: Jair from the Manasseh tribe captured villages and renamed them “Villages of Jair.”
text: Jayir la n lii Manasɛ dee biini la lɛɛ ba bɔsognaa maa, ka jaa ra yiraa Havɔf Jayir.

ref: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
text: Denii Nɔba ge foozi Kɛnaf ni u boljigzi la maa n baruu la di so, di jaa ra yiraa u himmaa sɔŋ Nɔba.

ref: As Israel traveled from Egypt under the command of Moses and Aaron,
text: Moosis ni Aarɔn n faa tɔ Izrɛl hina see ba lii Ijip di ra ba la, bɔra la baŋ faa chɔɔgɛɛ sɔnaa keŋ.

ref: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii lugɔ ú ɔɔ sɛbi ba chɔɔribɔr maa sɔŋ dau.

ref: After the Israelites left Rameses, they camped at Succoth,
text: A Izrɛl hina lii Ramɛsis di ga chɔɔ Sukɔf.

ref: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
text: Baŋ wa lii Sukɔf ba ga chɔɔ Ɛtam n du a hɛribɔduma kɛrii.

ref: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
text: Baŋ wa lii Ɛtam, ba bir kpa ba Pi Hahirɔf n du Baal Zɛfɔn wiifurii, di wa chɔɔ dugli Migdɔl.

ref: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
text: Baŋ wa lii Pi Hahirɔf, ba ga Muuzeŋaahmu la biini di ga lii Ɛtam Hɛribɔduma, di vol hɔpizaa ahoro, ka ga chɔɔ Mara.

ref: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
text: Baŋ wa lii Ɛlim, ba ga chɔɔ Muuzeŋaahmu la nua.

ref: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
text: Baŋ wa lii a Muuzeŋaahmu ba ga chɔɔ Sin Hɛribɔduma.

ref: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
text: Baŋ wa lii Alus, ba ga chɔɔ Rɛfidim, bɔr la nii n faa waa hoo a nɛra nyɔɔ la.

ref: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
text: Baŋ wa lii Rɛfidim, ba ga chɔɔ Sinaai Hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
text: Baŋ wa lii Zin Hɛribɔduma, ba ga chɔɔ Bizeŋ Hɔɔ la n du Ɛdɔm hɛri magbɔɔ la zɛɛ.

ref: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Aarɔn be lugɔ ú tinni Bizeŋ Hɔɔ nyuu, uŋ wa tinni de, u siu. Keŋ ɛɛwɔɔ saŋa la baŋ lii Ijip hɛri binni tokkoanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi anuehiŋ lugli hɔpizii hɔl.

ref: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
text: Keenan hina koori la n ɛɛ Arad koori di faa ra zuu Nɛgɛv n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma la, faa nuu lugɔ Izrɛl hina ra bau.

ref: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
text: Moab lɛla n chɔɔ Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii di chaŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko n du u baŋgia la bɛl la biinii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ di ba haŋ wa gi Jɔɔdan muu di zuu Keenan hɛri,

ref: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
text: bá duŋŋi a hɛssi hina la maa n soge de la. Bá chɔgi ba vugsɛɛhlaa ni anla maa baŋ luuwɛ ani a kuaribɔra maa n du bia nyuuni la.

ref: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
text: Bá lɛɛ a hɛri di so, dikuubɛɛwiai, n kpaubuu tɛɛ baa, ú ɛɛ ba kundɔɔlii.

ref: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
text: Bá ta kuna di bɔnni a hɛri di hiŋzi gunla ba dizi ni domeezi n makkɛzi. Bá kpa u bɔzeŋ di tɛɛ banla n kpillɛ, di kaa kpa u bɔjiga ge di tɛɛ banla n waa kpil. U bɔr la maa n wa la banla maa be, ba hotte guŋ.

ref: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
text: Ka di Izrɛl hina waa haŋ wa duŋŋi de hina, ka gil baŋhina, ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daabizi di ra chugzi Izrɛl hina siwee, di ɛɛ lugɔ sɔɔhri di ra tɔɔhzi baa. Banla n du de la daŋ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina biinichɔg werge maa a hɛri bɔr la ban niŋ so la.

ref: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
text: Di Izrɛl hina wa vɛɛ ba duŋŋaa, n daŋ chɔgi baa gunla miŋ fɛwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ chɔgi a de hina la.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
text: lugɔ ú ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di ii wa zuu Keenan hɛri la miŋ lizɛɛ dau ia lugɔ ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ la, daŋ dɔɔ magbɔɔni naa.

ref: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
text: U wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔ daŋ ga Zin Hɛribɔduma, di hiini Ɛdɔm hɛri magbɔɔ. U daŋ faari wiifurii, di lii Muuzensiwii wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere.

ref: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
text: Di kaa lii de di ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di la bɔr la banna yir Nuuma Ŋmɛnɛɛ, di kaa lii de di ra la Zin, di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ra la Kadɛs Bania n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag. Denii u kaa bir ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wiicholii, di ga hel Hazar Adar guŋŋ di ga hel Azmɔn.

ref: It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Denii u kaa bir ga di ra la waluu la n du Ijip hɛri magbɔɔ di ga tuŋ Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn.

ref: The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
text: U wiicholii magbɔɔ la daŋ ɛɛ Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn.

ref: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
text: U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ daŋ faari Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, di ga wiifurii Bizeŋ Hɔɔ,

ref: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
text: di kaa chi de ge di ga Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ga Zɛdad,

ref: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
text: di chi de kpau di ra la Zifrɔn, di ga tuŋ Hazar Ɛnan.

ref: The eastern border will begin at Hazar-Enan in the north, then run south to Shepham,
text: U wiifurii magbɔɔ daŋ lii Hazar Ɛnan di ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ra Sɛfam.

ref: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
text: U daŋ ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga hel Habɛl n du Ain wiifurii, di lii de di ga hel Galilii muuzeŋ nua wiifurii,

ref: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
text: di ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di hiini Jɔɔdan muu di ga chug Muuzensiwii. Anniibuu niŋ ɛɛ ii hɛri magbɔɔni.”

ref: Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes.
text: Denii Moosis ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Ií ta kuna di bɔnni a hɛri, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií kpau tɛɛ dizi kabɛl ni keza,

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la waa teŋ na ba kapɛttɛ kunaa.

ref: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
text: A dizi anɛɛ ni keza naa waa teŋ, di ba kapɛttɛɛ Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii kɛrii la, n chaŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko la.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
text: “Nɛra la n niŋ bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ ia ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ sɔnaa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza ani Nun biibaal Josua.

ref: One leader from each tribe will help them,
text: Kaa lizi sitɔɔri di lii dee maa biini ú hiini baa bá bɔnni a hɛri.

ref: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
text: Nɛra naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa lizi, di ŋɔ bá bɔnni a Keenan hɛri la di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ.

ref: That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals.
text: A bolzenaa naa daŋ ɛɛ Levi dee bola, bá ra zuu. A de hɛssi la n baraa daŋ ɛɛ ba sela diiribɔra.

ref: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
text: “Ií daŋ kpa bolzenaa anumbɛl tɛɛ a Levi dee, á ɛɛ hinlɛɛi bolzenaa, di nɛr maa wa foroo kpu u dɔŋhiŋ, ú wer chɔ la de, di lɛɛ u hiŋ. Ií kaa kpa bolzenaa tokkoanɛɛ ani anɛɛ di jaa baa.

ref: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
text: A bola la iin lizɛɛ tɛɛ a Levi dee, di lii hɛri la Izrɛl hina n dɔɔwɛ la, dee la maa n kpillɛ ii daŋ tɛɛ baa bolkpila, banla ge n waa kpil ií tɛɛ baa bola tama.”

ref: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
text: Nɛr la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la lulli himmaanii dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu la. Di u wa nau, ú kpuu.

ref: There are to be six of these Safe Towns,
text: A bolzenaa anumbɛl naabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii hinlɛɛi bolzenaa.

ref: The Lord then told Moses
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: to tell the people of Israel: After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan,
text: lugɔ ú ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di ii wa gi Jɔɔdan muu di la Keenan,

ref: choose Safe Towns, where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection.
text: ií lizi a bolzenaa aŋhina a ɛɛ hinlɛɛi bolzenaa, di nɛr maa wa foroo kpu u dɔŋhiŋ, u daŋ wer chɔ la de di ga suah.

ref: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
text: U daŋ wer lɛɛ u hiŋ lii nɛr la uŋ kpuwɛɛ la nɛra be, di ba ra nyiŋŋi u kpui. Nɛr la maa haŋ wa kpu nɛr, daŋ wer chɔ di la a bolzenaa naa bɛl maa, di lɛɛ u hiŋ, di ba waa u wia biini binnɛɛ, ií gilɛɛ waa kpuu.

ref: They will be places of protection for anyone who lives in Israel and accidentally kills someone. Laws about Murder and Accidental Killing The Lord said:
text: A bolzenaa anumbɛl naabuu niŋ ɛɛ hinlɛɛi bolzenaa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni hɔɔhra ani banla maa n soge ba be la, á ɛɛ suahribɔra tɛɛ nɛr la maa n niŋ fori kpu nɛr, chɔ di ga suah.

ref: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
text: Di nɛbɛl kpa daa kuŋkuarii di lɔ nɛr kpu, a hiŋ ɛɛ nɛkpuurii, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpu a hiŋ ge.

ref: Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
text: gɛɛ u kpa u nonii lɔu kpu, u ɛɛ nɛkpuurii, a hiŋ ge gba dɛg kpuirɛ, di u lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpuu la wa nau, ú kpuu.

ref: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
text: a keŋ wia naa, a dɛkkɔɔ a bol hina binni a biini, di lɛɛ jaa nɛr la n kpu u dɔŋhiŋ la ni, ka gilɛɛ wa lɛɛ di ra jaa siuri la lulli himmaa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu la ni.

ref: If they decide that you are innocent, you will be protected from the victim's relative and sent to stay in one of the Safe Towns until the high priest dies.
text: Á bolzeŋ hina chi nɛr la n kpu u dɔŋhiŋ la har, di kpogluu la u ga du bol la nɛr n ɔɔ chɔ di ga suah la biini. U daŋ du de di ra ba saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la baŋ waari nuu la n niŋ wa siu.

ref: But if you ever leave the Safe Town
text: Ka nɛr la n kpu u dɔŋhiŋ la wa chɔwɔɔ lii a hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ biini,

ref: You must stay inside the town until the high priest dies; only then can you go back home.
text: A nɛkpuuri la dɛkkɔɔ u du a hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ hiŋ guŋŋ di ra ba Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la wa siu mɔɔ, ka u haa wer bir la u bol.

ref: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
text: Di nɛr maa wa kpu nɛr, nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ nɛkpila lii di di nɛr la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la daansɛɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ ba kpu a hiŋ, ka di waa daansɛɛ diire banɛɛ dɔɔwɛ waa, bá gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛr la n kpuu la.

ref: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
text: Nɛkpuuri maa wàá wer kpa kebii char u miibɔɔ, a dɛkkɔɔ baŋ kpuu.

ref: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ kebii nɛr la n kpu u dɔŋhiŋ la be, ka gil ú lii a hinlɛɛi bolzeŋ la biini, di la u himmaa bol di Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la waa siuwɛ lɛi.

ref: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
text: A hɔl bɛl Makir biibaal Giliad domee diini hina nabɔnzi n lii u naabaal Manasɛ n lii Joosɛf naanna domeezi biini, faa la Moosis ni Izrɛl hina diini nabɔnzi be,

ref: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
text: di ga ŋɔ, “Yaa nabɔma, Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ii kpa a hɛri tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, u ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ, di lii kuna tai biini la, u ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ii kpa yaa lulli Zɛlɔfɛhad kapɛttɛ diiribɔr, tɛɛ u biihaana.

ref: But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, the land they receive will become part of that tribe's inheritance and will no longer belong to us.
text: Ka di ba wa yuu Izrɛl hina domee bɛl hina, guŋwaa, ba daŋ kpa yaa naabaala kapɛttɛ kuna la ga jaa a domee la baŋ yuuwɛ la kapɛttɛ ni. Awia, bɔr la baŋ mɔnnɛ tɛɛ yaa la, yeŋ daŋ lii yaa dee nonee.

ref: Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
text: Bina la biini, baŋ ɔɔ bir nɛra kuna di ra tɛɛ baa la, ba daŋ kpa ba kapɛttɛ hiŋ di jaa domee la nɛra baŋ yuuwɛ la hor ni, ba kapɛttɛ wàá ka jaa yaa naabaala kundɔɔlaa ni.”

ref: So Moses told the people that the Lord had said: These men from the Manasseh tribe are right.
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Moosis jaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Gunla Joosɛf dee la n ŋɔwɛɛ la ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ, Zɛlɔfɛhad biihaana daŋ wer yuu nɛr la maa banna nyiŋŋi, ka a hindee lii ba himmaa dee biini.

ref: Tribal land must not be given to another tribe—it will remain the property of the tribe that received it.
text: Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa kpa ba kapɛttɛ la gaa tɛɛ dee bɛl Izrɛl hina biini. A dɛkkɔɔ Izrɛl hina dee maa kpogli ba kapɛttɛ la n ɛɛ ba naabaala hora la.

ref: In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
text: Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa kpa ba kapɛttɛ di la gaa tɛɛ dee bɛl maa. Izrɛl hinuu maa kpogli hɛri la n ɛɛ u hor.”

ref: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons
text: Zɛlɔfɛhad biihaana, Mala, Tirza, Hɔgla, Milka ani Noowa jaa yuu ba mɛɛbizi biizi di lii ba Mɛɛ lulla biini.

ref: and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
text: Joosɛf biibaal Manasɛ domee biini nɛraa ba faa yuugi, ba kapɛttɛ jaa ka ba mɛɛ dee ni domee biini.

ref: These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses and the Israelites while they were camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
text: Gbɔgni ni widaulaa naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa ga Moosis ni di dau tɛɛ Izrɛl hina saŋa la baŋ du Moab lɛla la n dugli Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii, di chaŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko n du u baŋgia bɛl la.

ref: Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
text: Ka iawaa, ií bir har di ra la hɛribɔduma, di hiŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Muuzeŋaahmu la.’

ref: People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us: You have stayed here long enough.
text: “Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la, ŋɔ yaa benii saŋa la yaa n du Bizeŋ Sinaai labuu, di ŋɔ, ‘Ii jaa du bizeŋ naa nyuurɛ birgi,

ref: Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River.
text: awia, ií izi di zuu Amɔri hina hɛri giŋgimee bɔr. Ií ra la banla maa n du Jɔɔdan Waluu biini, banla maa n du bizenaa nyuuni ni wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi, banla maa n du Nɛgɛv la ani banla maa n du muuzeŋ nua biini. Ií ra la Keenan hina ani Lɛbanɔn hina hɛssi, di ga hel Muu Yufretis.

ref: I give you this land, just as I promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Now you must go and take the land. Leaders Were Appointed (Exodus
text: Hɛri naa maanii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala, Abraham, Aizik, Jekɔb ani ba naanna maa la. Ií zuu lɔ baa ka foozi a hɛri, ú birgi ii hor.’ ” Moosis n lizi sitɔɔra wia

ref: After I gave these instructions to the judges, I taught you the Lord's commands. Men Were Sent To Explore the Hill Country (Numbers
text: A saŋa, n faa bagli iabuu wia la maa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ií ra ɛɛ.” Baŋ hum baala bá ga daani giŋgimee hɛri la

ref: You stayed in your tents and grumbled, “The Lord must hate us—he brought us out of Egypt, just so he could hand us over to the Amorites and get rid of us.
text: Ii faa du ii tanti diinii di nuumi ra du dɔŋa di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi hah yaabuu. Awiarɛ u lizi yaa di lii Ijip hɛri, ú kpa yaa du Amɔri hina nonee biini, bá chɔgi yaa.

ref: Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you: Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person.
text: Moosis faa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Yaa n faa du Bizeŋ Sinaai la, n ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ii wikpoglaa siili n ninɛɛ werge, n bɛŋ wàá wer kpoglaa.

ref: God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la gil ii wazi bukagboŋ di jaa, di kissi ia, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la.

ref: But I cannot take care of all your problems and settle all your arguments alone.
text: Ka ɛrɛɛ n bɛŋ ɛɛ di chi ii buntɔga naa, di ra kuari ii wia maanɛi?

ref: Then I took these men, who were already wise and respected leaders, and I appointed them as your official leaders. Some of them became military officers in charge of groups of
text: Awia, n faa lizi sitɔɔra di lii ii dizi la biine, ba ɛɛ nunzunna, ba ra tɔgzi baa, di gil baŋhina ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa binna, baŋhina ɛɛ nɛra kalfazi binna, baŋhina ɛɛ nɛra tokkoanɛɛ ni fizi ani fizi binna, di gil ba ɛɛ dizi nabɔnzi.

ref: and others became judges. I gave these judges the following instructions: When you settle legal cases, your decisions must be fair. It doesn't matter if the case is between two Israelites, or between an Israelite and a foreigner living in your community.
text: Kenne n faa ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ií ɔɔ ra nuu ii lulla kaluzi wia nɛnnɛ, di ra di baa seriya gunla n dɛkkɛ, di ii nɛra bɛnnɛ gɛɛ di ii ni hɔɔhraa, ka ii ra dia guŋ.

ref: And it doesn't matter if one is helpless and the other is powerful. Don't be afraid of anyone! No matter who shows up in your court, God will help you make a fair decision. If any case is too hard for you, bring the people to me, and I will make the decision.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di seriya ni nɔŋŋaa. Ií ɔɔ nuu ra tɛɛ nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɔm nɛr maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ ra di nɛra seriya. Di wii bɛl wa kpollo werge ii be, ií kpau di ba n be, ń binni u biini.’

ref: even though he had always been with us in the desert. During the daytime, the Lord was in the cloud, leading us in the right direction and showing us where to camp. And at night, he was there in the fire.
text: Waabuu ɔɔ faa tɔ ii see, di ɛɛ lugɔ niŋ hamuŋa ni, di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ baama bɔchaaŋ ge, di ra bagli ia bɔr la iin niŋ chɔɔ ani bɔr la iin niŋ ga.”

ref: The Lord had commanded us to leave Mount Sinai and go to the hill country that belonged to the Amorites, so we started out into the huge desert. You remember how frightening it was, but soon we were at Kadesh-Barnea,
text: “Denii yaa jaa izi Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ di ra la Amɔri hina hɛri la n dɔɔ giŋgimee la, gunla Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum n ŋɔ yaa be la. Yaa faa ga hɛribɔduma la n kannɛ, u wia faa kaa dɔɔ ɔnsii werge labuu, ii himmaa siwee na mɔɔ, ka yaa wa hel Kadɛs Bania.

ref: and I told you, “We have reached the hill country. It belongs to the Amorites now, but the Lord our God is giving it to us. He is the same God our ancestors worshiped, and he has told us to go in and take this land, so don't hesitate and be afraid.”
text: Ií na, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpa a hɛrii tɛɛ ia. Ií izi zuu de di foozuu ú birgi ii hor, gunla Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la n ŋɔ ii be la. Ií gilɛɛ gil ɔnsii ni bɔhuaih lau ia.’

ref: Then all of you came to me and said, “Before we go into the land, let's send some men to explore it. When they come back, they can tell us about the towns we will find and what roads we should take to get there.”

text: Ií ra liizi a hɔl la iiŋ chigɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ la. A hɔllɛ u ŋɔ n be, ‘Chaali a nɛra bá ba n be di wa nuu n wiŋɔɔlaa, guŋ gil bá ra ɔmiŋ saŋa la maa ban niŋ du a hɛri di birgi mag, di kpaa ra bagli ba biizi.’

ref: Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain,
text: Ii faa ballɔɔ di wa chi a bizeŋ zɛɛ, ka u maa faa ra lau niŋ zagzagzag, nyɔɔzi tɔ de maa kuull di ga chug chiŋ, bɔr biri limpiriŋ.

ref: and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia di lii a niŋ biini. Ii faa ra nuu u wiŋɔzi, ka ii waa kummaa nawɛɛ lugɔ newee. Loobii bɛnnɛ ii faa nuu.

ref: The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
text: U faa ŋɔ u ni ia nuukpaŋ wiarɛ. Aabuu u Gbɔgni Fi la uŋ ŋɔ ií ra hiŋ, u sɛbaa dau bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ ni la.

ref: That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River. Don't Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n benii a saŋa lugɔ n bagli ia u Gbɔgni, ií ra hiŋaa hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu, ii ga foozi dɔɔ la biini.” Vuga kuaraa wia

ref: not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women,
text: di gilɛɛ waa chɔg iihinaa di waa kuari kummaa, ú ra ɛɛ ii vug, di ii kuaruubuu u li baal gɛɛ haaŋ

ref: animals, birds,
text: gɛɛ sel gɛɛ zumbee

ref: reptiles, or fish.
text: gɛɛ kuntuuzii gɛɛ nyiŋ.

ref: And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship.
text: Di ii wa binni chiŋ di na wiizi gɛɛ baagu gɛɛ chinchiŋwilaa, ií gilɛɛ waa kuaraa. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpaabuu tɛɛ hɛssi la hina n wɔɔ zummɛ la lugɔ ba ra kuari.

ref: But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
text: Ka iawaa, Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu di lii tɔɔrɔɔ n lugɔ ninzeŋ biini, Ijip hɛri. U ɛɛ gunnɛ, ií birgi u kapɛttɛ kuna alugɔ iin jaa ɛɛ zinaa naa.

ref: The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you.
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuhwoo n ni dikuu ii wia. U hɛɛhzi ni biinichɔg lugɔ màá gi Jɔɔdan muu naa di zuu hɛrnanii la unna tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ la.

ref: So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
text: N daŋ siu hɛri naa biini. Màá gi Jɔɔdan muu naa. Ka iawaa daŋ giu di ga foozi a hɛrsum di dɔɔ.

ref: Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form.
text: Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa suuh Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ la u ni ia n ɛɛwɛ la wia. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa ú ra li kummaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kiiwe,

ref: The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ n na di kuna la. U ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ.

ref: Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɔ ia yaari durnya hɛssi hina biine. Ii tama bɛnnɛ niŋ ka ba biine.

ref: There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
text: Denii ii jaa ra kuari vuga la newea n kuarɛɛ, a ɛɛ daazi gɛɛ bia la n waa na gɛɛ di ra nuu wia gɛɛ di ra di gɛɛ di ra nuu sɔɔh.

ref: In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God.
text: Di ii waa di dɔgnya, annii naa maa wa huuzi ia, ii daŋ bir ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, di waa hiŋuu.

ref: The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na suŋ nɛra ni la wia, wàá gil ia ta gɛɛ di kpuuzi ia gɛɛ di suuh nuukpaŋ la u ni ii naabaala n ɛɛwɛ, u hɛɛhzi u wibii dɔɔi wia la.”

ref: When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
text: Vug bɛl ŋmɛnɛ haa wetto lizi hɛri bɛl hina lii hɛri bɛl, ba ɛɛ u hora, gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ ia Ijip hɛri laa? Ii himmaa sibɔɔrɛ u kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii di gil wiilchɔgaa, laal, wizenaa ani nuukpuuri wia la n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, ɛɛ.

ref: The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
text: Chinne u faa du ka gil ii nuu u loobii, ú bagli ia wia. Hɛri genii u faa bagli ia u ninzeŋ, ii nuu u loobii di lii u biini.

ref: The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt.
text: Dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi ii naabaala la wiarɛ u faa lizi ia, di kpogli ia lii Ijip hɛri ni u fɔŋŋazeŋ, di ra bagli lugɔ u du ii benii,

ref: Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
text: di duŋŋi hɛrzenaa la hina n kpekke kaali ia, di ii ra ba la. U ɛɛ gunnɛ ka kpa ba hɛssi tɛɛ ia, a ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuna alugɔ aŋ ɛɛwɛ filaŋkennaa.

ref: So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below.
text: Awia, ií zum di gil a du ii biine zinaa, lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɔɔ chiŋ ni hɛri maa fɔŋŋa. Bɛl maa waa kaa hoo, di waa lɛi.

ref: Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you. Safe Towns
text: Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, guŋ gil wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzi ii ni ii biizi ani ii naanna maa, ka ií wer so hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la, ú ɛɛ ii hor saŋaa saŋa maa.” Hinlɛɛi bolzenaa wia

ref: The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him
text: di wa du waluu la n dugli Bɛf Piɔ la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la. A hɛri naa faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n faa ra di kora Hɛsbɔn la hɛrii, waabuu Moosis ni Izrɛl hina faa kpegli, di ba lii Ijip di ra ba la.

ref: and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River
text: U ni Basan Koori Ɔɔg hɛssii Izrɛl hina faa foozi Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga la. Baabuu faa Amɔri hina koora banɛɛ la.

ref: from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon.
text: A hɛri naa faa lii bolzeŋ Aroa la n du Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ nua labuu guŋŋ di ga hel Bizeŋ Siyɔn, u sɔŋ bɛllɛ Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn,

ref: Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
text: di kpa Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii hɛri, di kaa lii de guŋŋ di ga hel Muuzensiwii la n du Bizeŋ Pisga bɔwillaa la maa jaa.

ref: Moses called together the people of Israel and said: Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully.
text: Moosis faa chaali Izrɛl hina maa, di ŋɔ ba be, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu Gbɔgni naa min niŋ bagli ia zinaa naa. Ií hellaa di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ.

ref: Do not murder.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá kpu nɛr.

ref: The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ni yaa faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ Bizeŋ Sinaai.

ref: That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today.
text: Kɔraawiizi ni yaa mɛɛwaa bɛŋ lɛi faa ɛɛ a nuukpaŋ naa, ka yaa banla maa n du de zinaa naa nuubuu ɛɛ a nuukpaŋ.

ref: The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire,
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ga niŋ biinii bizeŋ la nyuu, di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ia, a chaani, ii na u duula.

ref: but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
text: A saŋa hiŋ, minuu faa du ii ni Kɔraawiizi baambaaŋ, di ŋɔ u wiŋɔɔlii di tɛɛ ia, dikuu iiŋ faa ra ɔm a niŋ, di vɛɛ a bizeŋ nyuu tinnaa la wia. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,

ref: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
text: ‘Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lɛɛ ia di lii Ijip hɛri, saŋa la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma de la.

ref: Do not worship any god except me.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kaa wàá dɔɔ vuga maa di ra jaa n ni.

ref: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa, ú li kuŋ n du chiŋ gɛɛ hɛri gɛɛ nii biini di ra tɛɛ iihinaa.

ref: Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa togni di ra jaamaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ zoma hinnɛ, di ra tɛr banla maa n hahŋ biizi, ba naanna, ba naanatɛɛri ani ba ge biizi digna, dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia,

ref: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
text: ka nɔŋŋi jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la maa, n nɔŋŋiŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni la.

ref: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kpogli mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sɔŋ di ra dua. N daŋ tɛr nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ guŋ digni.

ref: You have six days when you can do your work,
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa hɔpizaa anumbɛl di ra hum ii huma maa,

ref: but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work.
text: ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lawaa ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ ii ni ii biizi ni ii balaa, ii sela ani hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola ra hum huma a hɔl hiŋ, bá ge wer heezi lugɔ ia.

ref: This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
text: Ií ra liizi lugɔ ii faa ɛɛ yomaa Ijip hɛri, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii la di lizi ia di lii de. Awia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ií ra tɔgzi Heezaa Hɔpizii la.

ref: Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
text: A tɔgzi i mɛɛ ni i maa gunla Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ la, í wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzii hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n na tɛi naa biini.

ref: Do not steal.
text: Gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ.

ref: When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me. The People Were Afraid (Exodus
text: Gbɔgni la Kɔraawiizi n faa siiwe tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa bizeŋ la nyuu, di lii niŋ ni baama ani bɔbiri limpiriŋ werge biini labuu guŋ. U faa waa kaa kpa wiimaa di jaa. U faa sɛbaabuu dau bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ ni, di kpaa tɛŋ.

ref: When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me
text: Iiŋ faa nuu a loobii n lii a bɔbiri limpiriŋ werge biini, di a bizeŋ nyuu ra lau niŋ la, ii sitɔɔra ni ii nabɔnzi faa ba n benii,

ref: and said: Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them.
text: di wa ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bagli yaabuu u zenni ni u girme, yaa nuu u loobii di lii niŋ biini. Zinaa, yaa zummɔ lugɔ newee wàá siu, di Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia tɛu.

ref: But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya siuzɛi? Ninzeŋ naa daŋ di yaa, di yaa kaa nuu Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la loobii.

ref: Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it?
text: Newee ŋmɛnɛ haa nuu Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la loobii, di lii niŋ biini, ka haa du dee?

ref: Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
text: Tuzi hel di nuu gunla maa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n na ŋɔ, di ŋɔa tɛɛ yaa. Gunla maa un niŋ ŋɔ, yaa daŋ nuu, di hiŋaa.’

ref: The Lord heard you and said: Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa nuu gunla iiŋ ŋɔ n benii, di ŋɔ, ‘N nuu wia la nɛra naa n ŋɔ i be labuu. Wia la maa baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo.

ref: I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
text: Di ba daŋ dɔɔ nfɛrɛ naa dɔŋ, di ra tɔgziŋ, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni, guŋwaa, wiimaa daŋ kuari tɛɛ ba ni ba biizi nɛnnɛ, saŋa maa.

ref: Now, tell them to return to their tents,
text: La ga ŋɔ dí ba bir la ba tanti diini biine.

ref: but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them. Moses said:
text: Ka hiŋwaa du n be bɔnnaa, ń kpa widaulaa ni Gbɔgni la hin niŋ bagli baa, bá ra hiŋaa hɛri la min niŋ tɛɛ baa la biini di tɛi.’ ”

ref: Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
text: Ií ra hiŋ u wibaglaa la maa, guŋ gil ii nyɛɛli, di dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋra hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia la biini.”

ref: The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Widaulaa ni Gbɔgni la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔ ń bagli ia, ií ra hiŋaa hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ií ga dɔɔ la biinii guŋ,

ref: And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws.
text: guŋ gil ii ni ii biizi ni ii naanna ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, ii de dui saŋa, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni maa minna bagli ia naa, ií wer di ra di iihinaa.

ref: Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
text: Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu di ra du tau, di sɛɛ ra hiŋaa, wichɔgii maa gilɛɛ waa huuzi ia, ka ii wazi werge maa hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la biini, gunla Kɔraawiizi la ii mɛɛwaa n na hum la n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.

ref: Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God!
text: Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ɛɛ kpaŋkpannɛ, bɛl maa waa kaa hoo.

ref: So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength.
text: Ií gil ii bampiree maa lau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di nɔŋŋuu ani ii biine maa, di kpa ii kpegzi maa du u ni.

ref: and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
text: Ií kpaa di bagli ii biizi. Ií ra ŋɔ a wia di ii wa du ii diini gɛɛ di ii waa vol ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ii wa chɔɔwɔ gɛɛ di ii wa izoo.

ref: Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them.
text: Ií sɛbaa, di kpaa vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, á ra liizi ia.

ref: The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build,
text: Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa kpogli ia zuu hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala, Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia, u dɔɔ bolzenaa la iiŋ waa mawɛɛ, a du wer werge,

ref: and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more,
text: a diini suugi kunnanaa la iiŋ waa kuuhwɛ na, kɔlɔnzi iiŋ waa kiwee ani daazi la n na nɔŋ kooni iiŋ waa duuwe. Di ii wa dia di piŋzi,

ref: don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt.
text: ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa suuh Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la wia.

ref: Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
text: Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛŋ, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzi.

ref: Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari nɛra la n bar ia la vuga,

ref: If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you,
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n du ii be la ra zomuu. U baaŋ daŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ú dim ia hɛri naa biini.

ref: so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wia di ŋɔ ií ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la di na, gunla iiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ Massa la.

ref: Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you
text: Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Gbɔgni maa uŋ tɛɛ ia la.

ref: Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
text: Di ii biizi ŋmɛnɛ wa pɛɛzi ia, ‘Gbɔgni naa Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n ŋɔ yá ra hiŋaa naa, zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?’

ref: Then you will answer: We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free.
text: Ií ŋɔ ba be, ‘Yaa faa ɛɛ Ijip koori yomaa, ka Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ yaa, di lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri ani u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii.

ref: We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else.
text: Yaa sibɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi faa gil wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la n kpekke di kaa chum werge, chol Ijip hina, ba koori ani u diahina maa ni.

ref: The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors.
text: U lizi yaabuu di lii de, ú kpogli yaa zuu hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ yaa naabaala la biini.

ref: That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
text: Di yaa ra du tau, di ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa nɛnnɛ, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la sibɔɔ gunla uŋ baglɛɛ la, gunnɛ niŋ gil yaa wia deŋli.’ ”

ref: So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today. The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey (Deuteronomy
text: Awia, ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, ka ra hiŋ a widaulaa ni Gbɔgni naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.

ref: When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ií kpu nɛra la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ kpa du i nonee biini. Ií gilɛɛ waa suŋ ba ni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari ba vuga, á wa birgi sidɛɛzi ii be, di lauri ia.

ref: the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them,
text: Di u wa kpa baa du ii nonee biini, ii kpegli baa, ií chɔgi baa nyaamm. Ií ni baa gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa suŋ ba ni.

ref: If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
text: Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ba daŋ gil ii biibaala vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa, ka ra kuari vuga. Guŋ gil u baaŋ fuuh ii ni, ú chɔgi ia manaŋ.

ref: So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire. The Lord's Chosen People Moses said:
text: Awia, ií purgi ba mbusu lizibɔra ni ba bia la baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛ ba vug Baal, di kuugi ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa la maa, di fuuah.

ref: Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own.
text: Ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛmbɛŋ horaa. U lizi iabuu di lii durnya hɛssi nɛra maa biine, ií ɛɛ u nɛra, di ɛɛ u daama la unna tɔgzi werge maa la.

ref: but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
text: Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋi ia, di kaa hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala la wiarɛ, u lizi ia ani u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii, di lɛɛ ia lii hɛri la biini iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma, Ijip koori faa dɔɔ ia la.

ref: You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations.
text: Awia, a dɛkkɔɔ ií zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. U wia dɔɔ wibiire. U nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la ɔɔ du jiminizi kagboŋa nɛra la n nɔŋŋuu di ra hiŋ u widaulaa benii.

ref: But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you.
text: Ka banla waa n hauh la, ba kinturgaare chɔgaa, u daŋ chɔgi baa manaŋ.

ref: God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase.
text: Ii daŋ na kissaa di kaali nɛra maa, durnya naa biini. Ii baal maa gɛɛ haaŋ maa gɛɛ ii kundɛɛzaa maa wàá nyaa bie.

ref: so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa a kuŋkiilii naa bɛl maa di waa zuu ii diini, di guŋ lɛi, Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi ii nuu maa. Ií kii u wia werge maa, di hauh, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi dau u chɔgaa saŋaa.”

ref: The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs.
text: U daŋ nɔŋŋi ia di kissi ia, di gil ii wazi. U daŋ kissi ii biizi ni ii pattikuna, aabuu ii mia ni siŋfalaa ani nuu. U daŋ gil ii sela wazi, hɛri la biini uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ ii naabaala be lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ia la.

ref: If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors.
text: Di ii ra du a Gbɔgni naa tau nɛnnɛ, di ra hiŋaa, guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ lau u ni ia nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la, di kpogli nɛnnɛ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua di hɛɛhzi tɛɛ ii naabaala la.

ref: You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases. Destroy the Nations and Their Gods Moses said to Israel:
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ guu ia di lii wiila maa biini. Wàá gil wiilchɔgaa la iiŋ zummɛ Ijip hɛri la chol ii ni. Ka u daŋ gil a chol banla maa n hah ia ni.

ref: You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.”
text: Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ ii biine, ‘Hɛssi naa hina kpekkoo kaali yaa. Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ duŋŋi baai?’

ref: But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa. Ií ra liizi gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n dau Ijip hina ni ba koori maa la.

ref: You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much.
text: Ii himmaa siwee na tɔɔrɔɔzenaa ni wizenaa ani nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii, di lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri labuu. Guŋ himmaanii ú ɛɛ nɛra naa iinna ɔm naa.

ref: Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead.
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, u daŋ kpa chirinchaazi di ta ba ni, haali banla n niŋ na bahinaa di chɔ suahzi la gba daŋ siuzi.

ref: So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil ba wia dɔɔ ia ɔnsii, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, du ii benii. U zenni kannɔɔ werge. U wia ge dɔɔ ɔnsii werge.

ref: As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la danna duŋŋi a nɛra tama tama. Wàá gil ii kpu baa kakpaŋ. Di guŋ lɛi, sechɔgaa daŋ wazi, di ra koozi ia.

ref: But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
text: U daŋ kpa ba koora du ii nonee biini, ii dim ba sɔna durnya naa biini. Nɛr maa waa hoo ú ni ia wer lɔ dɔŋa. Ii daŋ kpu ba maa.

ref: After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord,
text: Ií fuuh ba vuga maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa kɛlli saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la baŋ kpawɛɛ bɔgaa la ni, di wa kpaa ra birgi ii hora. A daŋ gil ii chol, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ kuna la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n kiiwe wia.

ref: Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau, di ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. Guŋ gil ii wer dɔɔ miibɔɔni di wazi, di zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua, lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala la biini, di foozuu dɔɔ.

ref: so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
text: U faa kpa lɔzii kpu ia, ka tɛɛ ia maana, diwii la ii ni ii naabaala maa n waa zummɛ, ii di. U ɛɛ gunnɛ u pɛssi ia. Ka u ŋɔ ú bagli iabuu lugɔ diwee bɛŋ lɛi ra tɛɛ nɛr miibɔɔ. Ka Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii bɛl maa gba daŋ wer tɛu miibɔɔ.

ref: So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children.
text: Ií zum gunla baal n ɔɔ ra tɛr u biibaal digni la, gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɔɔ ra tɛrgi ii digna la.

ref: Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
text: Ií ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la widaulaa, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi, di ra tɔgzuu werge maa.

ref: The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kpogli iabuu di ra zuu hɛrsum la n dɔɔ gɔŋa, niiri n chɔɔgɛɛ, bulli n pogzee di ra pal walli biine ani giŋgimee nyuuni.

ref: After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you.
text: Di ii wa diwoo di piŋ, ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, dikuu uŋ tɛɛ ia hɛrsum wia.

ref: Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them,
text: Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa suuh u wia, di vɛɛ u Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.

ref: you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in.
text: Di guŋ lɛi, di ii wa diwoo piŋ, di ma diinanaa so,

ref: You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
text: di ii sela, ii saliŋhuŋŋa, ii saliŋ ani ii kundɔɔlaa maa wa wazɔɔ,

ref: But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free.
text: denii ií jaa dɔɔ barabara, di suuh Kɔraawiizi la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la, iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la wia.

ref: Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink.
text: Waabuu faa kpogli ia di ga hɛribɔduma n wassɛ werge, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii la biini la. A hɛri la n faa waa nii dɔɔwɛ, ka dɔɔ hɛrikuna ni nuunzi la siri n kpolle. U faa gillɔɔ nii lii bikpeg ni, ií nyɔɔ.

ref: He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
text: U faa tɛɛ iabuu maana ií di a hɛribɔduma biini. A ɛɛ kuna la ii naabaala n faa waa zummɛ, ú gil ii pɛssi, di kaa ɛɛ ia di na, a tuna, ii wia maa wer kuari.

ref: When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.”
text: Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ ii biine, ‘Yaa fɔŋŋa ni kpegzii tɛɛ yaa daama naa.’

ref: Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
text: Ama, ií ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu ra tɛɛ ia daama nai fɔŋŋa. Waabuu ra ɛɛ wia naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia haa dɔɔ wibiire zinaa, di tɛɛ nuukpaŋ la u ni ii naabaala n ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
text: Gunla uŋ kpu hɛssi nɛra ii sibɔɔ la, gunnɛ ú kpu ia, dikuu iiŋ waa u nua hiŋŋɛ wia.”

ref: Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra nuu. Ii jaa ra nyiŋŋi Jɔɔdan muu giirɛ, ií ga foozi hɛssi la hina n kaali ia hɛssi. Ba kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge kaali ia, di dɔɔ bolzenaa n kannɛzi werge, a dɔɔ koŋlaa la n gaa chug chiŋ.

ref: Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle.
text: A nɛra ɛɛ Anak hina la n helle kpabaa kpabaanɛ! Ii zum ba wiarɛ di kaa nuu baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ wer chem Anak hina ninɛi?’

ref: But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
text: Ka n na nyiŋŋuu ií zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu tɔ ii see di ra gi Jɔɔdan muu la. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niŋ la n na di kuna. U daŋ chɔgi baa di gɛrgi baa mɔɔ, ii sibɔɔ. Denii ií duŋŋi baa di dim baa manaŋ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.

ref: Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
text: Ií ra liizi gunla iiŋ faa gillɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh hɛribɔduma biini la. Di lii a hɔl la iiŋ lii Ijip hɛri guŋŋ di wa hel ɛŋ la, ii faa ra diubuu mmɔri.

ref: At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you.
text: Iiŋ faa du Bizeŋ Sinaai zɛɛ la, ii faa ɛɛ wiarɛ di gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u faa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpu ia.

ref: he said: Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Tuu manaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i nɛra la hiŋ kpoglee lii Ijip hɛri la chɔkkɔɔ, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Ba wia waa kaa dɔɔ wibii. Ba bir hattɛ kpu n widaulaa la, ka ŋmɛɛri saliŋ di kuari vug tɛɛ bahinaa.’

ref: I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, ‘N na nɛra naabuu, wibii maa. Ba dɔɔ dignikpegaa!

ref: So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel. Moses said:
text: Giliŋ bɔɔiih ka n kpu baa, di dim ba sɔŋ durnya naa biini. Ka gil hìŋ́ Moosis ɛɛ hɛri la hina n niŋ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge mɛɛ. I nɛra daŋ du kpil werge di kaali baa.’

ref: Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them.
text: Awia, n faa bir lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu, di u haa ra lau niŋ zagzagzag, di a nuukpaŋ bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la du n nonee.

ref: I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf.
text: Denii n binni di na lugɔ ii ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni, dikuu iiŋ faa kpa saliŋ di ŋmɛɛri, di kuari vug u li nabii wia. Ii faa bir hattɛ manaŋ di kpu ŋmɛnɛɛ la uŋ ŋɔ ii ra hiŋ la.

ref: So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
text: Awia, n faa kpa a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ la miŋ kpoglee la, di viiri hɛri, a purgi burburbur, ii sibɔɔ.

ref: I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Aarɔn gba ninɛɛ, di hel lugɔ ú chɔguu, ka a saŋa hiŋ, n faa suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ u ge gba.

ref: It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
text: N faa kaa kpa ii wichɔgii kuŋ la, a nabii la iiŋ kuarɛɛ la di fuuh, di purguu, di namuu u bii kɔlɔlɔlɔ lugɔ hɛɛhriikɔl, di kpaa ta nii la n faa lii a bii nyuu di pal ra tuu hɛri la biini.

ref: You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah.
text: Ii faa kaa giluu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh Tabɛra, Massa ani Kibrɔf Hataava maa.

ref: Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command.
text: Kɔraawiizi n faa gillɛ ii lii Kadɛs Bania la, u faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií izi la ga foozi hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia la.’ Ka ii faa diu mmɔri. Ii faa wɔɔ yardɛɛ gɛɛ di hiŋ u nua.

ref: In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
text: Di haŋ lii saŋa la maa miŋ zum ia la, ii kpoŋŋoo di ra di Kɔraawiizi mmɔri.

ref: After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for
text: N faa chɔɔwɔɔ pi Kɔraawiizi see hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, dikuu uŋ ŋɔ ú kpu ia la wia.

ref: and prayed: Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own.
text: N faa suŋŋuu di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, gilɛɛ waa kpu i nɛra. Ba ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ hiŋ yauwɛ lii Ijip hɛri ani i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banonii labuu.

ref: Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin.
text: A liizi i balaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb wia, ka suuh a nɛra naa kpoŋaa, ba biinikpola ani ba wichɔgaa naa wia.

ref: If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.”
text: Di guŋ lɛi, hɛri la biini hiŋ lizi yaa lii la hina daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi n waa wette ú kpogli baa di zuu hɛri la uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ baa la ani uŋ hah baa wiarɛ, u kpogli baa ba hɛribɔduma biini, ú wa kpu.

ref: But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
text: Ka ba ɛɛ i nɛraa, di ɛɛ i kapɛttɛ hiŋ lizɛɛ lii Ijip hɛri ani i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banoniire.’ ”

ref: The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “A guŋ saŋa, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Sɛɛh bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la, di kpaa tinni a bizeŋ nyuu di ba n be. Kuari daazi dakka di jaa.

ref: He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
text: Ń kaa sɛbi wia la n faa du lugli hora la hiŋ purgee la ni. Denii í jaa kpaa du a dakka biini.’

ref: So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain,
text: Awia, n kpa akeesia daa di kuari a dakka, di sɛɛh a bipɛntɛnzi anɛɛ alugɔ lugli hora la, di kpaa tinni a bizeŋ nyuu.

ref: where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain. After the Lord returned the stones to me,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa sɛbi a Gbɔgni Fi la uŋ faa felee sɛbi lugli hora la ni, di faa sii a wia di tɛɛ ia bizeŋ la nyuu di lii ninlau biini, ii chaalaa hɔpizii la. Denii u kpaa tɛŋ.

ref: I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there. Aaron Died (Numbers
text: Awia n jaa lii a bizeŋ nyuu di tuu, di kpa a bipɛntɛnzi du dakka la miŋ kuarɛɛ la biini gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ n be la. A haa du u biini filaŋkeŋ.”

ref: Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name.
text: Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra humuu nɛnnɛ. Ií lawuu kpogli chigigi, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra hɛɛhzi.

ref: Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest.
text: Izrɛl hina faa lii Jaakan hina kɔlɔnzi, di vol guŋŋ di ga hel yembɛl banna yir Mɔsɛra. Aarɔn siu de, ba huguu, ka u biibaal Ɛliaza kpa u gawa, di birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ.

ref: Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams. The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest Moses said to Israel:
text: Ba lii de di vol guŋŋ di ga hel Gudgoda, di kaa lii de di la Jɔtbata hɛri n dɔɔ gɔŋa n dɔɔ niiri.

ref: After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi faa lizi Levi dee di tɛɛ u hiŋ, bá ra chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, di ra humuu, di kpa u sɔŋ di ra kissi nɛra. Gunnɛ ba haa ra ɛɛ haali ni zinaa.

ref: Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.” What the Lord Wants Moses said:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n be, ‘La ga tɔ a nɛra see, bá la ga foozi hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la, ú ɛɛ ba hor.’ ” Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi

ref: People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul,
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, filaŋkeŋ, ií ra nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na nyiŋŋi ii be. Ií ra ɔmuu, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi maa, di nɔŋŋuu, di ra humuu ani ii bampiree maa.

ref: and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
text: Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, á hiini ia.

ref: Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɔɔ chinchiŋ, di kpa hɛri ani kuna la maa n du u ni.

ref: Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi faa nɔŋŋi ii naabaalaa werge, di lizi ia, di lii hɛssi hina maa biine, gunla an duwɛɛ zinaa naa.

ref: Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn.
text: Ií chɛr manni filaŋkeŋ, di gilɛɛ kaa dɔɔ dignikpega.

ref: The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu kaali vuga maa. Waabuu dɔɔra maa Dɔɔri. Waabuu dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge. Waa baŋhina ra tɔgzi kaali baŋhina. Nɛr maa wàá wer tɛu kuna, ka u ɛɛ wia leu.
