ref: The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing.
text: U ɔɔ ra lɛɛ lalbiizi ni luhaana nuuzii, di lɛɛ wibii di ra tɛɛ baa. U ɔɔ nɔŋŋi hɔɔhrii, di ra tɛu diwee ni laala.

ref: And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
text: Awia, ií nɔŋŋi hɔɔhra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii gba faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa Ijip hɛri.

ref: Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
text: Ií ra chɔluu. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia di tɛɛ ia, a wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge ii himmaa sibɔɔ la.

ref: The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u kipar, u widaulaa ani u Gbɔgni saŋa maa.

ref: Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power
text: Ií ra liizi zinaa lugɔ ii biizi lɛi faa na gunla Kɔraawiizi dignitɛraa n duwɛɛ, u zenni, u fɔŋŋazeŋ

ref: when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people.
text: ani u banonii ni wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ Ijip hina baambaaŋ la. Anla uŋ kpawɛɛ dau Ijip koori ni u hɛri hina maa la.

ref: And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
text: Ii na gunla uŋ ɛɛ Ijip hina laallɔɔra ni ba zagra ni a torkozi, di gil Muuzeŋaahmu di baa, saŋa la baŋ faa ra dau ii luge ani gunla uŋ chɔgi baa, ba wia tuŋ nyaamm la.

ref: You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here.
text: Ii biizi lɛi na wia la uŋ ɛɛwɛ di tɛɛ ia hɛribɔduma la biini mɔɔ, ka ii wa hel bɔnnaa

ref: And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
text: ani gunla uŋ ɛɛ Ɛliab n lii Rubin dee biini biibaala Datan ni Abiram la. U faa gillɔɔ hɛri peri, di di ba ni ba diini hina, ba tanti diini ani ba kuna maa, Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ.

ref: With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
text: Ii himmaa siweere faa na wizenaa naa maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land
text: Awia, ií ra hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, guŋ gil ií wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di gi Jɔɔdan muu naa, di ga lɔ a nɛra ka foozi a hɛri, di dɔɔ,

ref: that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time.
text: di wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋra hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la, Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii naabaala ni ba naanna la biini.

ref: It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops.
text: Hɛri la iinna zuu ii foozi la waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Ijip hɛri la iiŋ lii u biini, di ɔɔ faa duu kuna di ra mizaa nii lugɔ kambol kuna la.

ref: But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven,
text: Ka hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ii foozi di dɔɔ naa, dooŋ ɔɔ ra ba denii nɛnnɛ, u dɔɔ bizenaa ni walli.

ref: because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
text: Kɔraawiizi waa u wia ra sɛɛ. U siwee ɔɔ du u ninɛɛ, bina maa biini.

ref: The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him,
text: Awia, di ii ra hiŋ widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra humuu ni ii bampiree ani ii biine maa,

ref: But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods,
text: Ií ra du tau, di guŋ lɛi, ba daŋ dar ia, ií bir di ra kuari vuga, di ra tɔgzaa.

ref: the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ii ni werge maa, ú lau dooŋ, wàá ka ba. A hɛri wàá ka lii diwee, ii siuzi a hɛrsum la Kɔraawiizi n na tɛɛ ia la biini.

ref: Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them.
text: Ií gil n wiŋɔzi naa du ii bampiree ni ii nfɛssi biine, di sɛbaa, di kpaa vɔɔzi ii nonee ni ii hilli, á ra liizi ia.

ref: Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
text: Ií kpaa bagli ii biizi, di ra ŋɔ a wia, di ii wa du ii diini gɛɛ di ii waa vol ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ii wa chɔɔwɔ gɛɛ di ii wa izoo.

ref: Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
text: Ií sɛbaa dau ii dominuuzi daazi ani ii gbessi maa ni,

ref: Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
text: guŋ gil ii ni ii biizi hɔpizaa du kpil, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ ii naabaala la biini, gunla chiŋ n niŋ guali hɛri ni, di birgi mag la.

ref: Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants,
text: Di ii ra hiŋ widaulaa naa maa minna tɛɛ ia naa nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi maa, di lawuu kpogli chigigi,

ref: he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack.
text: guŋwaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ duŋŋi hɛssi naa hina maa n du ii see naa. Ii daŋ kpegli hɛssi la hina n kpillɛ, di du kpeg kaali ia la.

ref: You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Bɔr la maa iin niŋ kpa ii naazi jag, daŋ birgi ii hor. Ii hɛri daŋ chi hɛribɔduma guŋŋ di ga hel Lɛbanɔn, di kaa chi Muu Yufretis di ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn.

ref: No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
text: Newee maa wàá wer karsi ia. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kpa ɔnsii werge ni bɔsai, di ta hɛri la maa iin niŋ la hina ni, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, bá ra ɔm ia.

ref: You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you?
text: Zinaa, n kpa kissaa ni nuuseeire di ra dau ii see, ií lizi bɛl.

ref: Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you.
text: Ii daŋ na kissaa, di ii ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.

ref: But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
text: Nuuseei daŋ di ia, di ii wa vɛɛ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di bir har kpua, ka ra kuari vuga la iiŋ faa waa zummɛ.

ref: After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi wa kpogli ia zuu hɛri la iinna la ii ga foozi di dɔɔ la, ii daŋ sii kissaa naa wia Bizeŋ Gɛrizim nyuu, di sii nuuseei naa ge wia Bizeŋ Ɛbal nyuu.

ref: You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
text: Alugɔ iiŋ zummɛ la, bizenaa naa du Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia bɛl ŋmɛnɛɛ wiicholiire, di dugli Mɔrɛ daazenaa la n du Keenan hina hɛri la n du Jɔɔdan Waluu, di dugli Gilgal la.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there,
text: Ii ra nyiŋŋi Jɔɔdan muu giirɛ, ií ga foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la. Di ii wa foozuu di so de,

ref: be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
text: ií ra du tau, ka ra hiŋ widaulaa ni Gbɔgni naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ di ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.”

ref: Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Gbɔgni naabuu ií ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la ii mɛɛwaa n na hum la n na tɛɛ ia, di ii wa sogo u biini.

ref: But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees.
text: Ií chɔgi a hɛssi hina vuga kuaribɔra la n du bizenaa, giŋgimee nyuuni ani daazenaa n lɔɔwɛ werge zɛɛzi la maa.

ref: Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there.
text: Ií purgi ba mbusu lizibɔra ni ba bia baŋ baŋzɛɛ tɛɛ vug Baal la, di fuuh ba vughaaŋ Asɛra daajaŋra la. Ií purgi ba vuga la baŋ kuarɛɛ la maa, di dim a sɔna a hɛri biini nyaamm.

ref: Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la gunla banna kuari ba vuga la.

ref: The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want.
text: Di bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na nyiŋŋi u sɔŋ du la wa nɛɛwɔ ii be, ii daŋ wer kpu sela la aŋhina Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ ia la, gunla miŋ baglɛɛ la. Ii daŋ heea ii bola gunla maa maga iinna nyiŋŋi.

ref: It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
text: Ií heea gunla iin niŋ hee weema gɛɛ burŋa la. Banla n doŋŋe gɛɛ di ba waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be la, maanii niŋ wer heea.

ref: But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ iiŋ hee a chal. Ií fugaa ta hɛri lugɔ nii.

ref: Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa hee a chal, guŋ gil wiimaa du wer tɛɛ ii ni ii biizi, dikuu wideŋlaa la iin ninna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi sibɔɔ wia.

ref: All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
text: Ií ɔɔ lizi ii mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, a ola ni a challi maa. Ii daŋ ɔɔ fug ii mbusuzi sela challi, di dau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr la zɛɛ, ka ii daŋ wer hee a ola waa.

ref: If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful. Worship the Lord in the Right Way Moses said:
text: Ií ra du tau, di ra hiŋ widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia naa, guŋ gil wichɔgii maa wàá huuzi ii ni ii biizi, dikuu iin ninna ɛɛ wia la n wesse di kaa deŋli, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sibɔɔ wia.

ref: Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ duŋŋi hɛssi la nɛra iinna nyiŋŋi ii lɔ, ka foozi ba hɛssi la. Di ii wa duŋŋi baa ka so ba hɛri,

ref: But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?”
text: Kɔraawiizi wa chɔgi baa ii sibɔɔ, ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi ba vuga wia, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ hɛssi naa hina ra kuari ba vugai? Yaa gba ra nyiŋŋi ya ra ɛɛ guŋ himmaanii.’ Di ii wa ɛɛ guŋ, a daŋ birgi sidɛɛzi di lauri ia.

ref: No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, gunla banna kuari ba vuga la, dikuubɛɛwiai, wikuna la Kɔraawiizi n kiiwee ba ra ɛɛ. Haali ba biibaala ni biihaana maanii ba ɔɔ fuuh, di ra ligzi mbusuzi, di ra tɛɛ ba vuga.

ref: Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
text: Wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ la, ií ɛɛ ania maa ka ra hiŋaa. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa di ra jaa a ni gɛɛ di wa teŋ wiimaa di ra ha.”

ref: Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.”
text: di a widee la wia uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wa ɛɛwɔ, u ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil ya ra kuari vuga,’ vuga la iiŋ faa waa zummɛ,

ref: If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul.
text: ií gilɛɛ waa nuu ra tɛɛ a dɔgtɛɛ naa gɛɛ unla n na a wia deeza biini la. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra nyiŋŋuu ú ɛɛ ia na, di zum di ii nɔŋŋuubuu ni ii bampiree ni ii biine maa gɛɛ.

ref: You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling,
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu dɛkkɛ iinna hiŋ, di ra ɔmuu. Ií ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni di ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra, di ra humuu, di lawuu kpogli chigigi.

ref: because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt. If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
text: A dɔgtɛɛ gɛɛ a deeza biini wia nai hiŋ la dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u amaniye la uŋ lizɛɛ la ra bagluu lugɔ ií vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Waabuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri, bɔr la iiŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la. A hiŋ kipattɛ ií bir har kpu ŋmɛnɛɛ la uŋ ŋɔ ií ra hiŋ la. A dɛkkɔɔ ii lizi wichɔgaa lii ii biini.

ref: And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina maa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa, nɛr maa wàá ka lii ii biini di ɛɛ a guŋ wichɔgaa maa.

ref: After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns.
text: Di ii wa nuuwɔ banna ŋɔ bola la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n tɛɛ ia ŋɔ ií so la bɛl maa biini lugɔ

ref: You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them.
text: biinikpola hina izoore ii biini, di dar ba bol hina, di ra ŋɔ lugɔ bá gaa kuari vuga la ii ni ii mɛɛwaa n faa waa zummɛ,

ref: You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country,
text: ií pɛɛzi di pigzi a wia biini nɛnnɛ. Di a ɛɛ wibii, daansɛɛ du de di ra bagli lugɔ wia naa Kɔraawiizi kiiwe naa ɛɛwɔɔ ii biini,

ref: you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too.
text: guŋwaa, a dɛkkɔɔ ií kpuuzi nɛra la maa n du a bol hiŋ biini. Ií chɔgi a bol ni u nɛra ni u kundɛɛzaa maa nyaamm.

ref: Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gil kuna la maa n dɛg chɔgaa la bɛl maa waa du ii be. Guŋ daŋ gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wàá fuuh ii ni. U daŋ suŋ ii ni di na ii sinyɛna, di gil ii wazi gunla uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala la,

ref: That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
text: dikuu iinna sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni la minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee u sibɔɔ wia.”

ref: Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods. Animals That Can Be Eaten (Leviticus
text: Ii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nɛraa. U lizi iabuu lii durnya hɛssi nɛra maa biine, ií ɛɛ u daama la unna tɔgzi werge maa la.

ref: You can eat any clean bird.
text: Ii daŋ wer di zumbee la maa n waa doŋŋe.

ref: Don't eat any disgusting animals.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di kunla maa n doŋŋe u be.

ref: It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
text: Ii daŋ wer di sel la maa naafiraa n bargɛɛ bɔra anɛɛ, u kaa ug ra hee.

ref: But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean.
text: Ka anla n ukke ra hee, a naafiraa bargi biini la, ií gilɛɛ waa hee nyugma, chooma ani aahri. A waa dɛg ii dii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a doŋŋoo Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
text: Pereku gba doŋŋoo, haali u naafiraa n bargɛɛ gba, ka waa ukke ra hee. U ol waa dɛg heei gɛɛ u siwii waa dɛg gbɔgzaa.

ref: You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water,
text: Kunnyinee la maa n du nii biini di dɔɔ sɔɔhri ni hɛga waa, ii daŋ wer dia.

ref: and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
text: Ka anla n nyaa sɔɔhri ni hɛga la, ií gilɛɛ waa dia. A doŋŋoo, a wer tɛɛ ia.

ref: Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them.
text: Ií ra kii kunzaahrijigzi maa.

ref: However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
text: Ka kunnyinee la maa n dɔɔ keeri, a waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be, ii daŋ wer dia.

ref: You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest Moses said:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa di kunla maa n siu u hiŋ ni. Ii daŋ wer kpau tɛɛ hɔɔhra la maa n du ii bola, bá di gɛɛ ii daŋ wer yoou tɛɛ baa. Iawaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la bɛmbɛŋ horaa. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa bubii di ra daali u maa ilanii biini.” Kuna bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ wia

ref: People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ɔɔ bargi ii pattikuna maa bɔra fi, di lizi a bɔkpaŋ dau bina maa. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ.

ref: Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra di ii mia, siŋfalaa, nuu fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa ani ii sela lugli biizi, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see, bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la. Guŋ daŋ gil ii helli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la tɔgzaa, saŋa maa.

ref: But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest,
text: Di a bɔr nɛɛwɔɔ werge, ii wàá wer la ii kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kissi ia ii na la ni,

ref: then sell this part and take the money there instead.
text: ií kpaa chɛr saliŋhuŋŋu, di kpaa la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi la.

ref: When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too.
text: Ií kpa a saliŋhuŋŋu di yau kunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi, naunaa, peezaa ani siŋ gɛɛ siŋ maa iri baŋ du bura gɛɛ kunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi. Denii ii ni ii diini hina maa dia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la see, ii bɔra sɔɔni ia.

ref: And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa suuh Levi dee la n du ii bola la wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa ba himmaa hɛssi gɛɛ kapɛttɛzi dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse.
text: Binni ahoro maa tuna, ií ɔɔ chaali a bina kuna bɔra fi bɔkpaŋ di dau ii bola.

ref: The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
text: Levi dee la n waa ba himmaa hɛssi gɛɛ kapɛttɛzi dɔɔwɛ la, hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana la n du ii bola la, ba di wa di, di piŋ. Guŋ gil Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kissi ia, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini.”

ref: After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money.
text: Di ii lulli maa wa nyaawɔ ii bola la bɛl maa, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ia la biini, ií gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ sikpegii gɛɛ di waa dɔɔ nokpeg u be.

ref: Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment.
text: Kenne ií ɔɔ ɛɛ. Nɛr la maa kim u dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu n diwee, daŋ gil tɛu. A waa dɛkkɛ u kaa gil u dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu gɛɛ u lulli turgi a kim, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba sii saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ bá gil kima di tɛɛ dɔŋaa.

ref: This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
text: Ii daŋ wer gil hɔɔhra waa turgi ba kima. Ka ii lulla waa, ií ɔɔ gil ba kima tɛɛ baa.

ref: No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kissi ia gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ la. Ii daŋ kpa kebee di ra kim hɛrkpila hina, ka iawaa wàá di ba kima. Ii danna di kora hɛrkpila hina ni, ka hɛri maa hina wàá di kora ii ni.

ref: Instead, be kind and lend them what they need.
text: Ka ií dɔɔ bunya, di ɔɔ kimuu kunla maa wia n tiruu.

ref: Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty.
text: Ií ra du tau di gilɛɛ waa fɛ nfɛrchɔgaa naa di ra du ii nyuuni, di ŋɔ, ‘Binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la n dɛg kima gilaa tɛɛ la duglɔɔrɛ,’ guŋ gil ií waa dɔɔ sikpegii ii lulli la anna nuu ni, di vɛɛ u hiinaa. Aŋhinabe, u daŋ wii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di du ii ni, ii dɔɔ bilchɔg dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
text: Ií tɛu nɛnnɛ ni biinihuŋŋu, ka gilɛɛ waa nuumi. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kissi ia, ii huma maa biini. Wii la maa iin niŋ kpa ii nonee ɛɛ, u daŋ kissi ia.

ref: But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa sel la maa n waa kpeg, di lizi mbusu ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.

ref: If any of you buy Israelites as slaves, you must set them free after six years.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di i dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu yoo u hiŋ tɛi, di haannɛ gɛɛ baallɛ, u humii binni anumbɛl, tau ŋmɛnɛɛ u dɔɔ u hiŋ, binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la biini.

ref: And don't just tell them they are free to leave—
text: Di i waa tau ŋmɛnɛɛ, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ di hɔɔ tɛɛwɛ kummaa.

ref: give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them.
text: Hiinuu nɛnnɛ ni peeza, mia ani siŋ, gunla maa maga Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kissii la.

ref: But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.”
text: Ka di i yom la ŋɔ i be, ‘Maa nyiŋŋi n gilii,’ dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi i ni i diahina ani u duula n paruu wia,

ref: Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
text: guŋwaa, lau u digni pɛli gbera, ka kpa hɛm furuu. U daŋ ɛɛ i balii u de dui saŋa maa. Ɛɛ i balii la n ɛɛ biihambie gba guŋ.

ref: If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ɔɔ lizi ii sela biiballugla, tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil nabala la n ɛɛ biilugla waa hum huma, di gilɛɛ waa fuŋ ii pebala la n ɛɛ biilugla huna.

ref: Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
text: Bina maa, ii ni ii diini hina daŋ ɔɔ heea, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi ŋɔ ií ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some.
text: Ií ɔɔ heea ii bola biine. Banla n doŋŋe ani banla n waa doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be daŋ wer heeu, alugɔ uŋ ɛɛ weema gɛɛ burŋa la.

ref: But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
text: Ka ií gilɛɛ waa hee a challi waa. Ií ɔɔ fugaa ha hɛri alugɔ nii.”

ref: People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií gil Abib baagu ɛɛ baaguzeŋ ii be. Ií ɔɔ ra di Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hor. Abib baagu naa biinii u lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri hamuŋa ni la.

ref: People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you. Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií ra hiŋ wibii dii bɛmbɛŋ. Guŋ gil ií wer dɔɔ miibɔɔni, di dɔɔ hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la biini. Vuga kuaraa wia

ref: Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord. The Harvest Festival (Exodus
text: Ii daŋ ɔɔ ra hee paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ hɔpizaa anumbɛl. Ka hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la waa, ií ɔɔ chaali di jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, ka gilɛɛ waa hum huma maa.” Kuna Kumaa Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia

ref: The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped.
text: Ií ɔɔ lau sel lii ii himmaa sela la iinna dɛɛzi biini, di lizi Gillikaali mbusu la tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la.

ref: Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lizi Gillikaali mbusu la, bola la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ia la, bɛl maa biini,

ref: It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt.
text: di bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la lɛi. Denii ii ɔɔ lizi Gillikaali mbusu la duana ni, di wiizi wa chollo, di ra liizi ii Ijip lii saŋa wia.

ref: Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
text: Ií ɔɔ ɔɔzuu, di heeu bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi la, ka bir di la ii tanti diini chɔɔzi ni.

ref: And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
text: di gilɛɛ waa baŋ bii di ra tɛɛ vug Baal, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la haahbuu.”

ref: When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra daa, mbusu lizibɔr la iiŋ mawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la kɛrii,

ref: go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
text: Ií ɔɔ gil ii ni ii biizi, ii balaa, Levi dee, hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana la n du ii bola la, bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni ia, bɔr la un niŋ lizi tɛɛ ia, ii ra jaamuu la.

ref: The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be. Treat Everyone with Justice Moses said to Israel:
text: Bɛl maa ɔɔ lizi sunzaa di mɛg gunla maga Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n kissuu mɛg, di wa tɛu.” Sitɔɔra wia

ref: Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord.
text: Bina maa biini, ii baala daŋ ɔɔ chaali bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lizɛɛ la buhoro, Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ, Kuna Kumaa ani Pampannizi Hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazi. Baal maa gilɛɛ waa ba Kɔraawiizi see ni nodumazi.

ref: If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted! Put To Death People Who Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa nabal gɛɛ peezi la n waa kpeg, di waa lizi mbusu di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u hah gunnɛ werge.

ref: So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty.
text: ba ŋɔa ii nuu, ií binni a biini nɛnnɛ. Di a wa ɛɛ wibii lugɔ a wikiilii naa ɛɛwɔɔ Izrɛl hɛri,

ref: But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty. Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones. Difficult Cases Moses said to Israel:
text: Banla n di u daansɛɛ labuu niŋ feli paagi bia lɔɔzuu, ka nɛra la maa jaa paagi bia di keezi lɔɔzuu kpu. A dɛkkɔɔ ií lizi a wichɔgaa ii biini. Seriya diiribɔra wia

ref: When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court. The King Moses said:
text: A nɛra maa daŋ nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa. Ba wàá kaa ra gbɛlli sitɔɔra.” Koori wia

ref: People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii wa zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la, di ga dɔɔu, di so u biini, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil ya ge lizi koori, ú ra binni yaa ni alugɔ hɛssi hina la n bar yaa n dɔɔwɛ la,’

ref: Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
text: ií ra du tau, ka lizi nɛr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi. A dɛkkɔɔ ú lii ii lulla biini. Ií gilɛɛ waa lizi unla n waa Izrɛl hinuu ɛɛwɛ.

ref: The king should not have many horses, especially those from Egypt. The Lord has said never to go back there again.
text: A waa dɛg a koori n dɔɔ zagkpila gɛɛ di gil ú nɛra bir la Ijip hɛri, di ga nyiŋŋi aŋhina wa jaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ii benii, ‘Ií gilɛɛ wa bir di ra la de.’

ref: And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
text: A waa dɛg un dɔɔ hahkpila. Di u ɛɛ guŋ, u bampirii daŋ bir, ú leu. A waa dɛg uŋ chaali saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ werge.

ref: The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch.
text: Di u wa kpa a hɛri kora, a dɛkkɔɔ ú sɛbi Gbɔgni naa du hɔŋ biini dau. Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la hor biinii, ú binni ka sɛbaa.

ref: Each day the king must read and obey these laws, so that he will learn to worship the Lord with fear and trembling
text: U daŋ du u be, ú ra karmuu u de dui maa biini, guŋ gil u helli Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la ɔmaa, di ra tɔgzuu, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa nɛnnɛ.

ref: and not think that he's better than everyone else. If the king completely obeys the Lord's commands, he and his descendants will rule Israel for many years.
text: Ú gilɛɛ waa tɔgzi u hiŋ di ra kaali u lulla, di waa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni, ka ga bɔduma. Gunnɛ niŋ gil ú ni u naanna di kora di birgi, Izrɛl hɛri.”

ref: So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said.
text: N daŋ lizi dɔgtɛɛ lugɔi di lii ba lulla biini tɛɛ baa, di ɔɔ kpa n wiŋɔzi du u nua, ú ɔɔ ŋɔ wii la maa min niŋ ŋɔ, di ra tɛɛ baa.

ref: Some Levites may have money from selling family possessions, and others may not. But all Levites serving at the place of worship will receive the same amount of food from the sacrifices and gifts brought by the people. Don't Do Disgusting Things Moses said to Israel:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ u ni baa ra di kuna la maa banna na, di ra mɛgzi, haali baŋ tɛu kebee di lii ba diahina kuŋyoolaa biini gba.” Wia la Kɔraawiizi n hahwɛɛ werge wia

ref: The people of the Levi tribe, including the priests, will not receive any land. Instead, they will receive part of the sacrifices that are offered to the Lord,
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la gɛɛ Levi dee waa maa, gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ hɛri gɛɛ kapɛttɛ, Izrɛl hɛri. Ba kundiilaarɛ niŋ ɛɛ mbusuzi lizaa kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ba kapɛttɛɛ guŋ.

ref: because he has promised to provide for them in this way.
text: Ba wàá dɔɔ kapɛttɛ ba lulla biini. Kɔraawiizii ba kapɛttɛ, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ baa la.

ref: When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
text: Di nɛr kpa nabal gɛɛ peezi di wa lizi mbusu, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɔdiilaare keŋ, u vaampɛrɛ, u hama ani u biini kuna.

ref: In addition, they will receive the first part of your grain harvest and part of your first batches of wine and olive oil. You must also give them the first wool that is cut from your sheep each year.
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa ii lugli mia la iin niŋ kum, ii lugli siŋfalaa, ii ɔlivi nuu ani ii peeza lugli huna la iin niŋ fuŋ la, di tɛɛ baa,

ref: Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu lizi ba ni ba dee, di lii ii dizi la biine, di ŋɔ bá ra hum u huma u sɔŋ biini saŋa maa.

ref: Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped,
text: Di Levi dee hinuu bɛl maa wa izi ii bol bɛl maa un duwɛɛ Izrɛl biini, di la yemmaa ni biinihuŋŋu, Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lizi tɛu,

ref: and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites.
text: u daŋ wer hum Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la huma alugɔ u dɔŋahina Levi dee n na hum de la.

ref: Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii wa zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la biini, ií gilɛɛ waa chanzi a hɛssi hina wiɛɛlaa la Kɔraawiizi n hahwɛɛ werge la.

ref: Don't sacrifice your son or daughter. And don't try to use any kind of magic or witchcraft to tell fortunes or to cast spells or to talk with spirits of the dead.
text: gɛɛ di waa vɔɔ nɛra kabirɛzi gɛɛ di ra la nɛra la n na pɛɛzi lalaa wia be.

ref: The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land.
text: Kɔraawiizi hah nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ wia naabuu. Dikuu wikuna naa wia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ duŋŋi hɛssi hina naa ii sibɔɔ, di lii ba hɛssi biine.

ref: Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things! A Prophet like Moses Moses said to Israel:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ií gilɛɛ dɔɔ chɔgri maa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be.” Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ wia

ref: You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Hɛssi la hina iin niŋ duŋŋi ka foozi ba hɛssi la, nuuwɔɔ ra tɛɛ banla n na vug baa. Ka iawaa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la waa ia tɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ ii ra ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ lizi u dɔgtɛɛ bɛl ii dee biini, ú hum di ra tɛɛ ia, alugɔŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ ií nuu ra tɛu.

ref: You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
text: A wii naabuu ii faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi be Bizeŋ Sinaai la zɛɛ, a hɔl la iiŋ chaali de la, ‘Gilɛɛ kaa gil ya ŋmɛnɛ maa waa nuu Kɔraawiizi loobii gɛɛ di waa na ninzeŋ la maa, di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ siu la.’

ref: Then the Lord told me: Moses, they have said the right thing.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Wii la banna ŋɔ naa wessoo.

ref: Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
text: Di nɛr maa wa vɛɛa, n himmaa daŋ di u seriya.

ref: But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god. Moses said to Israel:
text: Ka di dɔgtɛɛ duma maa waa ŋɔ wia la miŋ waa ŋɔwɛɛ n sɔŋ biini gɛɛ dɔgtɛɛ la maa n na ŋɔ wia vuga sɔŋ biini, a dɛkkɔɔ bá kpuu.’

ref: You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?”
text: Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ zum lugɔ amaniye naa waa Kɔraawiizi be liwɛɛi?’

ref: You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
text: Di dɔgtɛɛ maa wa kpa n sɔŋ di ŋɔ wia, ka a waa ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ di ɛɛ wibii, guŋwaa, amaniye hiŋ waa n be liwɛɛ. A dɔgtɛɛ himmaa kipar wiarɛ u ŋɔ di kanni kara. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɔmuu.”

ref: Israel, the Lord your God has promised that if you obey his laws and teachings I'm giving you, and if you always love him, then he will give you the land he promised your ancestors. When that happens, you must name three more Safe Towns in the new territory.
text: dikuu iiŋ hiŋ Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋuu, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi saŋa maa wia, ii daŋ kaa lizi bolzenaa ahoro di jaa.

ref: Soon you will go into the land and attack the nations. The Lord your God will destroy them and give you their lands, towns, and homes. Then after you are settled,
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa chɔgi nɛra la hɛssi unna tɛɛ ia la, ii duŋŋi baa ka so ba bola ni ba diini biine,

ref: you must choose three of your towns to be Safe Towns. Divide the land into three regions with one Safe Town near the middle of each, so that a Safe Town can be easily reached from anywhere in your land. Then, if one of you accidentally kills someone, you can run to a Safe Town and find protection from being put to death. But you must not have been angry with the person you killed.
text: Widaulii la n chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ nɛr la maa n niŋ kpu u dɔŋhiŋ ka chɔ la de, di lɛɛ u hinnɛ keŋ, nɛr la n foree kpu u dɔŋhiŋ di waa a hiŋ fɛwɛɛ ni wichɔgaa gɛɛ di dɔɔ biinikpola a hiŋ ni mɔɔ.

ref: For example, suppose you and a friend go into the forest to cut wood. You are chopping down a tree with an ax, when the ax head slips off the handle, hits your friend, and kills him. You can run to one of the Safe Towns and save your life.
text: Aŋhinabe, baal ni u dɔŋhiŋ daŋ zuu pir bá ga teŋri daazi, u lalli u kpaŋfɔ di ra ŋmɛŋ daa, u bii foŋ di ga lɔ u dɔŋhiŋ la di kpuu, a baal naa dee daŋ wer chɔ la a bolzenaa naa bɛl maa biini, di lɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: You don't deserve to die, since you did not mean to harm your friend. But he did get killed, and his relatives might be very angry. They might even choose one of the men from their family to track you down and kill you. If it is too far to one of the Safe Towns, the victim's relative might be able to catch you and kill you.
text: Di guŋ lɛi, nɛr la lulli himmaa n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu di turgi a lalii kim, daŋ kpa baaŋfuuih werge di duŋŋuu di ga lawuu, di a bolzeŋ nɛɛwɔ werge, di kpuu. Haali uŋ waa dɛg siu gba, dikuubɛɛwiai, waa nfɛrchɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ a hiŋ ni.

ref: That's why I said there must be three Safe Towns.
text: Guŋ wiarɛ n ŋɔ ii lizi bolzenaa ahoro di tɛɛ iihinaa la.

ref: You will need them, so innocent people won't be killed on your land while they are trying to reach a Safe Town that is too far away. You will be guilty of murder, if innocent people lose their lives because you didn't name enough Safe Towns in the land the Lord your God will give you.
text: Ií ɛɛ guŋ di gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ nɛr maa haahkɛ, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n na tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la biini. Guŋ gilɛɛ wa gil ii waa dɔɔ bilchɔg, dikuu nɛr kpui wia.

ref: But what if you really do commit murder? Suppose one of you hates a neighbor. So you wait in a deserted place, kill the neighbor, and run to a Safe Town.
text: Ka di nɛr hah u dɔŋhiŋ di chɔɔ guuu, di lɔɔzuu kpu ka chɔ kaali a bolzenaa naa bɛl maa,

ref: If that happens, the leaders of your town must send messengers to bring you back from the Safe Town. They will hand you over to one of the victim's relatives, who will put you to death.
text: guŋwaa, u bol nabɔnzi daŋ hum u bɔr, bá bir ba u ni. Bá kpau tɛɛ u lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpuu la, di turgi baal la uŋ kpuwɛɛ la kim, ú kpuu.

ref: Israel, for the good of the whole country, you must kill anyone who murders an innocent person. Never show mercy to a murderer! Property Lines Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa na u sinyɛna. A dɛkkɔɔ ií lizi bilchɔg di lii Izrɛl hɛri, dikuu nɛr n siu haahkɛ siu wia, ka ii wia kuari.

ref: In the land the Lord is giving you, there are already stones set up to mark the property lines between fields. So don't move those stones. Witnesses Must Tell the Truth Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa tuzi magbɔɔ bii la faala hina n baŋŋɛ, hɛri la iin niŋ na, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ di lii hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ií dɔɔ la biini.” Daansɛɛdiire wia

ref: Before you are convicted of a crime, at least two witnesses must be able to testify that you did it.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Nɛkpaŋ daansɛɛ waa tɔg lugɔ bá kuu u wia di tɛr nɛr la baŋ ŋɔ u ɛɛ wichɔgaa digni. Nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro daansɛɛrɛ niŋ wer gil á ɛɛ wibii.

ref: If you accuse someone of a crime, but seem to be lying,
text: Di daansɛɛkara hiŋ chigɔ ú di nɛr wichɔgaa daansɛɛ,

ref: then both you and the accused must be taken to the court at the place where the Lord is worshiped. There the priests and judges will find out if you are lying or telling the truth. If you are lying and the accused is innocent,
text: Sitɔɔra la dɛkkɔɔ bá pigzi a wia biini nɛnnɛ. Di ba wa nawɔɔ lugɔ wibii maa, daansɛɛkaraa u ra di, di kanni kara di ra chug u dɔŋhiŋ la,

ref: then you will be punished without mercy. You will receive the same punishment the accused would have received if found guilty, whether it means losing an eye, a tooth, a hand, a foot, or even your life. Israel, the crime of telling lies in court must be punished. And when people hear what happens to witnesses that lie, everyone else who testifies in court will tell the truth.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa na u sinyɛna. Di nɛr lizi miibɔɔ, bá lizi u hor. Di nɛr chɔg u dɔŋ siwii, bá chɔg u hor. Di nɛr ku u dɔŋ nyiŋ, bá ku u hor. Di nɛr ku u dɔŋ nonii, bá ku u hor. Di nɛr ku u dɔŋ naa, bá ku u hor.”

ref: If you have to go to war, you may find yourselves facing an enemy army that is bigger than yours and that has horses and chariots. But don't be afraid! The Lord your God rescued you from Egypt, and he will help you fight.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di laal wa chol ii ni ii dɔma baambaaŋ, ii na zagra ni torkozi ani laallɔɔra la n kpillɛ kaali ia, ií gilɛɛ waa ɔm baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la, daŋ du ii be.

ref: Before you march into battle, a priest will go to the front of the army
text: Di ii wa ŋɔ ií la laal, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ chi ii see, di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ laallɔɔra la.

ref: and say, “Soldiers of Israel, listen to me! Today when you go into battle, don't be afraid of the enemy, and when you see them, don't panic.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl Hina, ií ra nuu! Zinaa, ii ni ii dɔma ra nyiŋŋuu ií lɔ laal. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɔm baa gɛɛ di waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih gɛɛ di gil ii banchulli waa lɔ, ii bɔra ra sa,

ref: The Lord your God will fight alongside you and help you win the battle.”
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni iabuu ra la ií ga lɔ ii dɔma laal. U daŋ gil ii kpegli baa.’

ref: Then the tribal officials will say to the troops: If any of you have built a new house, but haven't yet moved in, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to live in your new house.
text: Laallɔɔra nabɔnzi daŋ pɛɛzi laallɔɔra la, ‘Nɛbɛl du ɛŋ di ma u dia ka u haa wɔɔ kpawɛɛ du Kɔraawiizi noneea? Á hiŋ bir di ra la dia, aŋhinabe, u daŋ siu a laal biini, ka nɛduma kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee.

ref: If any of you have planted a vineyard but haven't had your first grape harvest, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to enjoy your grapes.
text: Nɛbɛl dɔɔ grepu daazi koore, ka u haa waa faarɛɛ di ra di u sumaa? Á hiŋ bir di ra la dia, aŋhinabe, u daŋ siu laal biini, ka nɛbɛl di u suma.

ref: If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
text: Nɛbɛl ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ haaŋ lugɔ u daŋ kpau, ka u haa wɔɔ kpawɛɛa? Á hiŋ bir di ra la dia, aŋhinabe, u daŋ siu a laal biini, ka nɛbɛl kpau.’

ref: Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
text: A nabɔnzi daŋ kaa ŋɔ keŋ di jaa, ‘Nɛbɛl du ɛŋ ɔnsii lawuuwaa? Á hiŋ bir di ra la dia, aŋhinabe, u daŋ du u dɔŋahina bɔhuaih.’

ref: When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
text: Di a nabɔnzi la wa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ a laallɔɔra tuŋ, ba daŋ lizi sitɔɔra tɛɛ baa.

ref: Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals.
text: Ama, bolzenaa la hina hɛssi la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, á ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la waa, ií kpu ba ni ba kuna la maa n na heezi.

ref: He has commanded you to completely wipe out the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
text: Ií kpu ba maa nyaamm, gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔ ii ɛɛ la. Hitti, Amɔri, Keenan, Pɛriz, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina maa.

ref: If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
text: Di guŋ lɛi, ba daŋ bagli ia wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n kiiwe, baŋ ɔɔ ra kuari ba vuga di ra ɛɛ la. Guŋ gil ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni.

ref: When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down.
text: Di ii wa fɔɔ bolzeŋ maa di birgi, di wa yoo baa di kpegli baa, ií gilɛɛ waa teŋri ba daazi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii daŋ wer di a nɔna. Ií gilɛɛ wa ŋmɛnnaa ra ha. A waa ii dɔma ɛɛwɛ.

ref: You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
text: Ama, ii daŋ wer teŋri anla iin zummɛ lugɔ a waa nɔŋ, di kpaa tegli a bolzeŋ koŋlii ni, di ta pizenaa baruu guŋŋ, di wa kpegli u nɛra.”

ref: Suppose the body of a murder victim is found in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you, and no one knows who the murderer is.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ba wa na nɛr baŋ kpuwɛɛ, u chɔ koo, hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ií dɔɔ la biini, ka ba waa zum nɛr la maa n kpuu,

ref: The judges and other leaders from the towns around there must find out what town is the closest to where the body was found.
text: ii nabɔnzi ni ii sitɔɔra daŋ lii, di mɛgzi di lii bɔr la uŋ chɔɔwɛ la, di ga chug bola la n dugluu la.

ref: The leaders from that town will go to their cattle herds and choose a young cow that has never been put to work.
text: Bol la n dugluu la nabɔnzi daŋ lau nalor la baŋ haa waa kpawɛɛ hum huma gɛɛ di par,

ref: They and some of the priests will take this cow to a nearby valley where there is a stream, but no crops. Once they reach the valley, the leaders will break the cow's neck. The priests must be there, because the Lord your God has chosen them to be his special servants at the place of worship. The Lord has chosen them to bless the people in his name and to be judges in all legal cases, whether property or injury is involved.
text: Levi biibaala la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la, daŋ lii chi see, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la lizi baabuu ŋɔ bá ra hum u huma, di ra kissi nɛra u sɔŋ biini, di ra kuari kaluzi ni nuugbirgazi la n du nɛra baaŋ.

ref: The town leaders will wash their hands over the body of the dead cow
text: Denii nabɔnzi la maa n du bol la n dugli a lalii la, sanzi ba nonee du nalor la baŋaa baŋ kuwee la ni,

ref: and say, “We had no part in this murder, and we don't know who did it.
text: ka ŋɔ, ‘Yaa lɛi kpu baal naa gɛɛ di na baŋ kpuu.

ref: From time to time, you men will serve as soldiers and go off to war. The Lord your God will help you defeat your enemies, and you will take many prisoners.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii ni ii dɔma wa lɔ laal, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa kpa baa du ii nonee, ii lauri baa yoma,

ref: One of these prisoners may be a beautiful woman, and you may want to marry her. But first you must bring her into your home, and have her shave her head, cut her nails, get rid of her foreign clothes, and start wearing Israelite clothes. She will mourn a month for her father and mother, then you can marry her.
text: di wir wɛjɛzi la uŋ nignee ka ba lawuu la. Di u du u dia di wii u mɛɛ ni u maa la n siuzɛɛ la baagu bir, guŋwaa u nuu daŋ wer chɔɔ, ú birgi u haaŋ.

ref: Later on, if you are not happy with the woman, you can divorce her, and she can go free. But you have slept with her as your wife, so you cannot sell her as a slave or make her into your own slave. Rights of a First-Born Son Moses said to Israel:
text: Di u wia wɔɔ pattɛ, ú gil ú ra la bɔr la maa n paruu. Ú gilɛɛ waa yoou gɛɛ di wàá ɛɛu lugɔ yom, dikuubɛɛwiai, u chɔguubuu.” Biibambilugli kapɛttɛ dii wia

ref: Suppose a man has two wives and loves one more than the other. The first son of either wife is the man's first-born son, even if the boy's mother is the wife the man doesn't love. Later, when the man is near death and is dividing up his property, he must give a double share to his first-born son, simply because he was the first to be born. A Son Who Rebels Moses said to Israel:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ u sɛɛ lugɔ haaŋ la uŋ waa nɔŋŋɛɛ la biibaal labuu nabɔma, di tɛu u kundɔɔlaa maa bɔra anɛɛ. A biibaal naabuu luglɛɛ bagli u mɛɛ fɔŋŋa la uŋ dɔɔwɛ. Waabuu dɛg wia la n dɛg biibambilugli. Biibaal la n dɔɔ dignikpega wia

ref: A father and a mother may have a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey them even after he has been punished.
text: Di baal dɔɔ biibaal la n dɔɔ dignikpega, waa u mɛɛ ni u maa nua ra nuu, waa ba dignitɛraa ra sɛɛ,

ref: If a son is like that, his parents must drag him to the town gate, where the leaders of the town hold their meetings.
text: u mɛɛ ni u maa daŋ kpogluu ba, ba bol nabɔnzi see, ba bol dominuuzeŋ.

ref: The parents will tell the leaders, “This son of ours is stubborn and never obeys. He spends all his time drinking and partying.”
text: Ba daŋ ŋɔ a nabɔnzi be, ‘Yaa biibaal naa dɔɔ dignikpegaa, waa yaa nua ra hiŋ. U ra di kebeere basabasa, di nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi.’

ref: The men of the town will stone that son to death, because they must get rid of the evil he brought into the community. Everyone in Israel will be afraid when they hear how he was punished. The Body of a Criminal Moses said to Israel:
text: Denii baala la maa n du ba bol la, paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu. Ií lizi wichɔgaa di lii ii biini. Izrɛl hina maa daŋ nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa.” Gbɔgni irizi wia

ref: If a criminal is put to death, and you hang the dead body on a tree,
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di baal ɛɛ wichɔgaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ba kpuu, bá kpuu, di kpa daa tɔɔuh, di lalluu baŋ,

ref: you must not leave it there overnight. Bury it the same day, because the dead body of a criminal hanging on a tree will bring God's curse on the land. The Lord your God is giving this land to you, so don't make it unclean by leaving the bodies of executed criminals on display.
text: ií gilɛɛ waa gil u ra sag de hɔɔ wa pizi. Ií huguu a hɔl hiŋ maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ sag daa ni di kpu, Kɔraawiizi seeubuu nua. Ií gilɛɛ waa chɔg hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la.”

ref: If you see a cow or sheep wandering around lost, take the animal back to its owner.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di i na i dɔŋhiŋ nabal gɛɛ u peezi n leuwe, gilɛɛ waa giluu, lawuu di ga tɛu. Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ guŋ ɛɛi.

ref: If the owner lives too far away, or if you don't know who the owner is, take the animal home with you and take care of it. The owner will come looking for the animal, and then you can give it back.
text: Di i dɔŋhiŋ hiŋ waa duglɛɛ gɛɛ di haa u hiŋ zummɛ, lau a sel la i dia, di gaa binnuu guŋŋ di wa hel hɔpizii la un niŋ ba u bɔr. Kpau tɛu.

ref: That's what you should do if you find anything that belongs to someone else. Do whatever you can to help, whether you find a cow or sheep or donkey or some clothing.
text: Guŋ himmaanii i ɛɛ, di i dɔŋhiŋ kawee gɛɛ u tagtajaŋ gɛɛ u kundɔɔlii maa wa leuwo, i nau. Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ guŋ ɛɛi.

ref: Women must not pretend to be men, and men must not pretend to be women. The Lord your God is disgusted with people who do that. Don't Take a Mother Bird Moses said to Israel:
text: A waa dɛg haaŋ n na laali baal laala gɛɛ baal n na laali haaŋ laala. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hah nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ keŋ wia naabuu.

ref: If you build a house, make sure to put a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off the roof and is killed, it won't be your fault. Laws against Mixing Different Things Moses said to Israel:
text: Di i wa ma diifalii, ma koŋliikpurii bar u sal, nɛr gilɛɛ wa lii u nyuu chol siu, guŋ gil i dɔɔ bilchɔg.

ref: If you plant a vineyard, don't plant any other fruit tree or crop in it. If you do plant something else there, you must bring to the place of worship everything you harvest from the vineyard.
text: Gilɛɛ waa duu kummaa di ra koozi i grepu daazi ni. Di i ɛɛ guŋ, kuna la hiŋ duuwe la bɛŋ lɛi niŋ doŋ, ka a daazi nɔna gba daŋ doŋ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Don't hitch an ox and a donkey to your plow at the same time.
text: Gilɛɛ wa kpa nabal ni kawee kpau, di ra par.

ref: When you weave cloth for clothing, you can use thread made of flax or wool, but not both together.
text: Gilɛɛ waa laali laala la baŋ kpa peezi huna ni gessihuŋŋunanaa di suah.

ref: And when you make a coat, sew a tassel on each of the four corners. When a Husband Accuses His Wife Moses said to Israel:
text: Kuari yɔɔza du tagtajaŋ la hin niŋ ɔɔ laali la siraa anaazu ni.” Baal ni haaŋ dɔŋa kpai wia

ref: Suppose a man starts hating his wife soon after they are married.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di baal kpa haaŋ, ba chɔɔ, ka wɔɔ kaa ra nyiŋŋi,

ref: He might tell ugly lies about her, and say, “I married this woman, but when we slept together, I found out she wasn't a virgin.”
text: di jaa ra chɔg u nyuu di ra ŋɔ, ‘Miŋ kpa haaŋ naa, yaa chɔɔ, waa suwee.’

ref: If this happens, the bride's father and mother must go to the town gate to show the town leaders the proof that the woman was a virgin.
text: U mɛɛ ni u maa daŋ ba a bol nabɔnzi be, a bolzeŋ dominuuzeŋ, di wa di daansɛɛ lugɔ ba bie hiŋ suwoore.

ref: Her father will say, “I let my daughter marry this man, but he started hating her
text: A biihaaŋ mɛɛ daŋ ŋɔ a nabɔnzi be, ‘N kpa n biihaannɛ tɛɛ baal naa, ka wɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi.

ref: and accusing her of not being a virgin. But he is wrong, because here is proof that she was a virgin!” Then the bride's parents will show them the bed sheet from the woman's wedding night.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, u ra zɔɔzuubuu lugɔ waa n biihaaŋ hiŋ huuzee. Ka n biihaaŋ huuzaa daansɛɛrɛ keŋ.’ Denii u mɛɛ ni u maa yaa wɛjɛ la n na di a guŋ daansɛɛ la di bagli a bolzeŋ nabɔnzi.

ref: The town leaders will beat the man with a whip
text: A nabɔnzi daŋ lau a baal di tɛr u digni.

ref: But if the man was right and there is no proof that his bride was a virgin,
text: Ka di a ɛɛwɔ lugɔ wibiire u jaari hiŋ ŋɔ, ba waa wette bá di u sui daansɛɛ maa,

ref: the men of the town will take the woman to the door of her father's house and stone her to death. This woman brought evil into your community by sleeping with someone before she got married, and you must get rid of that evil by killing her. Laws about Illegal Sex Moses said:
text: ba daŋ kpogluu ba u mɛɛ dia dominua, u bol baala paagi bia lɔɔzuu kpu. U ɛɛ hiihzi wiarɛ Izrɛl hina biini, dikuu uŋ zum baal, di u haa du u mɛɛ dia wia. A dɛkkɔɔ ii lizi wichɔgaa lii ii biini.

ref: People of Israel, if a man is caught having sex with someone else's wife, you must put them both to death. That way, you will get rid of the evil they have done in Israel.
text: Di ba wa lau baal bɛl n nyiŋŋi u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ, a baal ni a haaŋ maa dɛg kpuirɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ií lizi wichɔgaa di lii ii biini.

ref: If a man is caught in town having sex with an engaged woman who isn't screaming for help, they both must be put to death. The man is guilty of having sex with a married woman. And the woman is guilty because she didn't call for help, even though she was inside a town and people were nearby. Take them both to the town gate and stone them to death. You must get rid of the evil they brought into your community.
text: ií kpogli ba nɛra banɛɛ la, di la a bol dominua, di paagi bia lɔɔzi baa kpu. Dikuubɛɛwiai, a biihambie du bolle ka waa wile lɔwɛɛ, bá hiinuu. Baal la ge, dikuu uŋ chɔgi nɛbɛl haaŋ wia. A dɛkkɔɔ ií lizi wichɔgaa di lii ii biini.

ref: If an engaged woman is raped out in the country, only the man will be put to death.
text: Ka di a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ pitte baal lau haaŋ la n dɔɔ baal di ra nyiŋŋi ú yuu di pum, baal la n ɛɛ guŋ la bɛnnɛ dɛg kpui.

ref: Do not punish the woman at all; she has done nothing wrong, and certainly nothing deserving death. This crime is like murder,
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ a biihaaŋ wiimaa. Waa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ di dɛg kpui. A wii naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛbɛl n pig u dɔŋhiŋ, di kpuu.

ref: because the woman was alone out in the country when the man attacked her. She screamed, but there was no one to help her.
text: A baal na a biihaannɛ pir, haali uŋ lɔ wile gba, ka nɛr maa waa hoo de, ú lɛɛu.

ref: Suppose a woman isn't engaged to be married, and a man forces her to have sex with him. If he is caught,
text: Di baal wa huuzi biihaaŋ la n haa waa baal zummɛ, gɛɛ u haa waa baal la un niŋ yuu dɔɔwɛ, di nyiŋŋuu, ba wolo lii,

ref: A man must not marry a woman who was married to his father. This would be a disgrace to his father.
text: A waa dɛg baal n kpa u mɛɛ haaŋ. A waa dɛkkɛ uŋ chɔg u mɛɛ dia.”

ref: If a man's private parts have been crushed or cut off, he cannot fully belong to the Lord's people.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa baŋ varɛɛ gɛɛ di tɔri u hɛŋ waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi nɛra biini zuui.

ref: No one born outside of a legal marriage, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can fully belong to the Lord's people.
text: Nɛr la maa baŋ sɛmmɛ lul, waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi nɛra biini zuui. Haali di ga hel jiminizi fi hina gba.

ref: No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can become part of Israel, the Lord's people.
text: Ammɔn gɛɛ Moab hinuu maa ni ba naanna, di ga hel jiminizi fi hina gba, waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi nɛra biini zuui.

ref: This is because when you came out of Egypt, they refused to provide you with food and water. And besides, they hired Balaam to put a curse on you.
text: Ba faa waa diwee ni nii kpawɛɛ chem ii ni, saŋa la iiŋ lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la. Ba faa kpa Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam la n lii Pɛtɔ n du Mɛsɔpɔtemia hɛrii, ú see ia nua.

ref: But the Lord your God loves you, so he refused to listen to Balaam and turned Balaam's curse into a blessing.
text: Ama, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la faa waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛu, ka gil u nuuseei la birgi kissaa tɛɛ ia, dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi ia wia.

ref: Don't even think of signing a peace treaty with Moab or Ammon.
text: Ii ni baa ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, ii de dui saŋa maa.

ref: But Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners in the country of Egypt. Now you must be kind to Edomites and Egyptians
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli Ɛdɔm hina, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii lullaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa gbɛlli Ijip hina, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii faa ɛɛ hɔɔhraa du ba hɛri.

ref: and let their great-grandchildren become part of Israel, the Lord's people. Keep the Army Camp Acceptable Moses said to Israel:
text: Ba jiminizi ahoro hina waa daŋ wer zuu Kɔraawiizi nɛra biini.” Laallɔɔra chɔɔribɔr kossaa wia

ref: When you men go off to fight your enemies, make sure your camp is acceptable to the Lord.
text: Denii Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii wa du ii chɔɔribɔr laal saŋa, ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wii la maa n niŋ gil ii doŋ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: For example, if something happens at night that makes a man unclean and unfit for worship, he must go outside the camp and stay there
text: Di baal maa wa chɔɔwɔ deezi, u hɛŋ lul, a dɛkkɔɔ ú lii a chɔɔribɔr baŋgia, di ga du de.

ref: until late afternoon. Then he must take a bath, and at sunset he can go back into camp.
text: Di bɔr waa duani, u daŋ sɔ nii ka bir zuu a chɔɔribɔr, di wiizi wa zuuwɔ.

ref: Set up a place outside the camp to be used as a toilet area.
text: Ií lizi bɔr ii chɔɔl hiŋ baŋgia, di ɔɔ gaa fiih gɛɛ di ra bɛɛ zahara de.

ref: And make sure that you have a small shovel in your equipment. When you go out to the toilet area, use the shovel to dig a hole. Then, after you relieve yourself, bury the waste in the hole.
text: Kunla iin niŋ ɔɔ kpa ki bɔɔ di togni du la, daŋ ɛɛ ii kuŋkpoglaa la bɛl. Di ii ɔɔ waa nyiŋŋi ii bɛɛ zahara, ií kpau ki bɔɔ, di kaa kpau gbaari hɛɛhraa tɔ,

ref: You must keep your camp clean of filthy and disgusting things. The Lord is always present in your camp, ready to rescue you and give you victory over your enemies. But if he sees something disgusting in your camp, he may turn around and leave. Runaway Slaves from Other Countries Moses said:
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la du ii benii, di ra gaagi ii chɔɔribɔr la biini, ú guu ia, di kpa ii dɔma du ii nonee biini. A dɛkkɔɔ ii chɔɔribɔr ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hor, ú gilɛɛ waa na wii la maa n waa wer de, di wa bir u har kpu ia.” Gbɔgni irizi wia

ref: When runaway slaves from other countries come to Israel and ask for protection, you must not hand them back to their owners.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di yom chɔwɔɔ wa zuu ia, ií gilɛɛ wa lawuu ra tɛɛ u dɔɔri.

ref: Instead, you must let them choose which one of your towns they want to live in. Don't be cruel to runaway slaves. Temple Prostitutes Moses said:
text: Ií gil u du ii biini bɔr la maa unna nyiŋŋi ani bol la maa biini unna nyiŋŋi ú du. Ií gilɛɛ waa sunnuu.

ref: People of Israel, don't any of you ever be temple prostitutes.
text: A waa dɛg Izrɛl baal gɛɛ haaŋ n ɛɛ vuga kuaribɔra sɛnsɛnni.

ref: The Lord your God is disgusted with men and women who are prostitutes of any kind, and he will not accept a gift from them, even if it had been promised to him. Interest on Loans Moses said:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa sɛnsɛŋ kebee di waa lizi nua maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, u hah ba maanii.

ref: When you lend money, food, or anything else to another Israelite, you are not allowed to charge interest.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa sag ii dɔŋhiŋ nii, di kebeere, di diweere gɛɛ di kummaanii u kim.

ref: You can charge a foreigner interest. But if you charge other Israelites interest, the Lord your God will not let you be successful in the land you are about to take. Sacred Promises to the Lord Moses said:
text: Ka ii daŋ wer sag hɔɔhri waa nii, ka ii dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu waa, ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ. Kɔ́raawiizi la iinna hum la kissi ii huma maa, hɛri la iinna zuu ii foozi di dɔɔ la biini.

ref: People of Israel, if you make a sacred promise to give a gift to the Lord, then do it as soon as you can. If the Lord has to come looking for the gift you promised, you will be guilty of breaking that promise.
text: Di ii wa lɛɛ nua Kɔraawiizi be, ií gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih ni u lizaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, wàá gil tɛɛ ia, guŋ gil ii dɔɔ bilchɔg.

ref: On the other hand, if you never make a sacred promise, you can't be guilty of breaking it.
text: Ka di haa nua lɛɛwɛ, guŋwaa, haa chɔgri dɔɔwɛ.

ref: You must keep whatever promises you make to the Lord. After all, you are the one who chose to make the promises. Eating Someone Else's Produce
text: Nua la maa iin niŋ lɛɛ, a dɛkkɔɔ ii lizuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa ia fittɛ.

ref: If you go into a vineyard that belongs to someone else, you are allowed to eat as many grapes as you want while you are there. But don't take any with you when you leave.
text: Di ii wa zuu ii dɔŋhiŋ grepu daazi koo, ii daŋ wer di a nɔna gunla maa iin niŋ wer, ka ií gilɛɛ wa tɔrgi aŋhina di ra du ii hure biine.

ref: In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
text: Di ii wa zuu ii dɔŋhiŋ mia biini, ii daŋ wer kuugi a nyuuni aŋhina gunla maa maga iin niŋ hee, ka ií gilɛɛ waa kumaa.”

ref: Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di baal wa kpa haaŋ ka u wia wɔɔ ra par, dikuu un na wichɔgii bɛl u ni wia, u sɛbi hahvɛɛri hɔŋ tɛu, ka gil u lii u dia,

ref: Later she married another man,
text: di ga birgi baal bɛl haaŋ.

ref: Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted. Newlyweds Moses said to Israel:
text: guŋwaa, u lugli jaari la n felee vɛɛu la wàá ka wer kpau, dikuu uŋ chɔkkɛ wia. Guŋ ɛɛ kiire Kɔraawiizi be. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa wichɔgaa di waa du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ la ni.

ref: If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife. Loans Moses said to Israel:
text: Di baal kpa haŋfalii a waa birgee, a waa dɛkkɛ uŋ la laal gɛɛ di waa hum bol maa huma. U daŋ du dia bina bir, di ra deŋŋi u haŋfalii siwee, ú dɔɔ bɔsɔna.

ref: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread. Kidnapping Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ nɛr nam bia di ra dau talma, dikuu uŋ di ii kim wia. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, lɔzii ii ra dau u ni u diahina la.

ref: If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community. Skin Diseases Moses said to Israel:
text: Di baal maa wa lau u dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu kpegzi ni, di ra ɛɛu lugɔ yom gɛɛ di yoou, unla n lawuu kpegzi ni la, dɛg kpuirɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ iiŋ lizi keŋ wichɔgaa naa lii ii biini.

ref: I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say.
text: Di bɔrahɔŋ wiilchɔgaarɛ, ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la n niŋ bagli ia ŋɔ ii ɛɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ ií hiŋ wia la miŋ bagli baa la.

ref: And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt. Loans Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií ra liizi gunla Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n dau Miriam, saŋa la iiŋ lii Ijip di ra kaali la.

ref: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that the money will be paid back. But you must not go into their house to get it.
text: Di i wa kpa kuŋ di kim i dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuu maa, gilɛɛ waa zuu u dia di ra lɛɛ u wɛjɛ la uŋ kpawɛɛ di ra dau talma.

ref: Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
text: Chi bossee, ka nɛr la n kpa a wɛjɛ di ra dau talma la, kpau wa tɛi.

ref: Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight.
text: Di a baal ɛɛ nyaarii, gilɛɛ waa gil u wɛjɛ la ra chɔɔ i dia hɔɔ waa pizi.

ref: Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing. Poor People's Wages Moses said:
text: Bir kpa u wɛjɛ hiŋ ga tɛu ú tɔ di chɔɔ, di wiizi wa chollo. U daŋ jaamii, guŋ ɛɛ wiɛɛlaa la n deŋlee Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la be.

ref: If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town.
text: Gilɛɛ waa fini huŋhunni la n ɛɛ nyaari, a ra nuuu, di u ɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ Izrɛl hinuurɛ gɛɛ di u ɛɛ hɔɔhrii, di du i bola la bɛl maa biini.

ref: Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you. The Death Penalty Moses said to Israel:
text: Turguu u huma kebee ka wiizi chol, hɔpizi biimaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ nyaarii di dɛlli a ni. Di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ wii du Kɔraawiizi, i ɛɛ wichɔgaa di di bilchɔg.

ref: Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime. Don't Mistreat the Powerless Moses said to Israel:
text: A waa dɛkkɛ bá kpu mɛɛwaa, dikuu ba biizi wichɔgaa wia gɛɛ bá kpu biizi, dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia. A dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa siu, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia.

ref: Make sure that orphans and foreigners are treated fairly. And if you lend money to a widow and want to keep something of hers to guarantee that she will pay you back, don't take any of her clothes.
text: Ɔɔ lɛɛ wibii di ra tɛɛ hɔɔhri gɛɛ lalbie. Gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ luhaaŋ ge wɛjɛ, di ra dau talma.

ref: You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws. Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií ra liizi lugɔ ii faa ɛɛ yomaa Ijip hɛri. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la lɛɛ ia lii de. Awiarɛ n ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ guŋ la.

ref: If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
text: Di i waa chaali i koo mia, di bɛri aŋhina ni, gilɛɛ wàá bir har di gaa paagaa. Gilaa tɛɛ hɔɔhra gɛɛ lalbiizi gɛɛ luhaana. Guŋ gil Kɔ́raawiizi la hinna hum la kissi i huma maa.

ref: When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor.
text: Di i ɔɔ wa tɔrgi i ɔlivi daazi nɔna kakpaŋ, gilɛɛ kaa wàá tɔrgaa bunɛɛ. Gil anla n kawɛɛ la tɛɛ hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana.

ref: And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left.
text: Di i wa tɔrgi i grepu daazi nɔna kakpaŋ, gilɛɛ kaa waa tɔrgaa bunɛɛ. Gil anla n kawɛɛ la di tɛɛ hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana.

ref: You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
text: Ií ra liizi lugɔ ii faa ɛɛ yomaa Ijip hɛri. Awiarɛ n ŋɔ ií ra ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless. Don't Muzzle an Ox Moses said to Israel:
text: Ka a waa dɛg baŋ viiruu bɛri virma nua butokkoanɛɛ. Di ba viiruu bɛri guŋ, ba gbɛlli ii dɔŋhinnɛ ii sibɔɔ.

ref: Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain. A Son for a Dead Brother Moses said to Israel:
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa vɔɔ navarga la n na fɛrgi mia, a bii ra lii la nua, ú gilɛɛ waa dia wia.

ref: But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
text: Ka di a baal waa nyiŋŋi u kpa u lulli luhaaŋ la, a luhaaŋ daŋ la a bol nabɔnzi see, a bol dominuuzeŋ, di ga ŋɔ, ‘N jaari lulli waa sɛɛwɛ ú gil u lulli sɔŋ du Izrɛl hina biini. Waa nyiŋŋi u ɛɛŋ wia la n dɛkkɛ n jaari n niŋ faa ɛɛ tɛŋ.’

ref: The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her,
text: Denii u bol nabɔnzi yiruu, di ŋɔ wia tɛu. Di u wa vɛɛwɔ ka haa ŋɔ, ‘Maa nyiŋŋi ń kpau.’

ref: she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.”
text: U lulli luhaaŋ hiŋ daŋ la a baal be, nabɔnzi la maa see, di ga foŋ a baal gaukpaŋ, ka puuzi nuuhaari du u siwee, ka ŋɔ, ‘Kenne ba ɔɔ ɛɛ baal la n waa sɛɛwɛ u ma u lulli dia.’

ref: From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.” When Two Men Fight Moses said to Israel:
text: A baal naa dee diahinaa bá ra yir, ‘Dia La Hina Gau Baŋ Foŋŋe, Izrɛl hina biini.’

ref: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts,
text: Di baala banɛɛ ra naa, bɛl haaŋ ba ú wa lɛɛ u jaari u dɔŋhiŋ la be, di wa lau u lure,

ref: you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy. Be Honest in Business Moses said to Israel:
text: ií teŋ u nonii. Ií gilɛɛ waa suŋ u ni.

ref: Don't try to cheat people by having two sets of weights or measures, one to get more when you are buying, and the other to give less when you are selling.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ kuna mɛgzaa kuna anɛɛ ii diini biine. Unla n kannɛ ni unla n du jiga.

ref: If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ií dɔɔ kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɛgzi kuna, á wia dɔɔ wibii nɛnnɛ. Guŋ gil ii dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, n na tɛɛ ia la biini,

ref: But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest. Wipe Out Amalek Moses said:
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hah nɛr la maa n na fini wiarɛ.

ref: People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt?
text: Ií ra liizi wia la Amalɛk hina n kpawɛɛ dau ia, saŋa la iiŋ lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la.

ref: You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
text: Iiŋ faa kuuhwɛ la, ba faa chem ii ninɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ, di kpuuzi banla maa n faa du har la. Ba faa waa Kɔraawiizi ɔmmɛ.

ref: The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wa tɛɛ ia heezaa, di lii ii dɔma la n bar ia hɛri la unna tɛɛ ia, ií dɔɔ, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la be, a dɛkkɔ ií dim Amalɛk sɔŋ di lii durnya naa biini. Ií gilɛɛ waa suuh.”

ref: The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down,
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Di ii wa zuu hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia, ú ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ la, di foozuu so u biini,

ref: and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped,
text: ií kpa diufalaa la iin niŋ lugli kpa a hɛri biini la aŋhina du kɛɛgɔzi biini, di kpaa la bɔr la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ lizi, ií ra jaamuu la.

ref: and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
text: Di ii wa la de, ií ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la n du de a saŋa la be, ‘N na ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la benii zinaa lugɔ n ba hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ yaa labuu.’

ref: The priest will take the basket and set it in front of the Lord's altar.
text: A Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ lɛɛ a kɛɛgɔzi lii ii nonee biine, di kpaa chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr la see.

ref: Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray: My ancestor was homeless, an Aramean who went to live in Egypt. There were only a few in his family then, but they became great and powerful, a nation of many people.
text: Denii ií jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, u sibɔɔ, ‘N naabaal faa ɛɛ Siiria hinuurɛ, di ra juuri, di kpogli u lulla tama di la Ijip hɛri, di ga so de. Ba wa ɛɛ hɛrzeŋ hina, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, di du kpil werge.

ref: The Egyptians were cruel and had no pity on us. They mistreated our people and forced us into slavery.
text: Ka Ijip hina la faa ra sunni yaa werge, di gil yaa di dɔgnya, di gil yaa ra hum humkpega.
