ref: We called out for help to you, the Lord God of our ancestors. You heard our cries; you knew we were in trouble and abused.
text: Denii yaa wii du Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaala n na hum la. U nuu ya wiraa di na yaa dɔgnya ni yaa kuuhni ani yaa sunnaa.

ref: Then you terrified the Egyptians with your mighty miracles and rescued us from Egypt.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa kpa u fɔŋŋazeŋ ni u banonii, ɔnsii werge, wizenaa ani nuukpuuri wia, di lizi yaa lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: You brought us here and gave us this land rich with milk and honey.
text: Waabuu ba yaa ni ɛŋ, di wa tɛɛ yaa hɛri naa n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la.

ref: Now, Lord, I bring to you the best of the crops that you have given me. After you say these things, place the basket in front of the Lord's altar and bow down to worship him.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, filaŋkeŋ, n kpa a hɛri la hiŋ tɛŋ la lugli diweere ń wa tɛi.’ Denii ii jaa kpa a kɛɛgɔzi chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la see, ka tognuu.

ref: Then you and your family must celebrate by eating a meal at the place of worship to thank the Lord your God for giving you such a good harvest. And remember to invite the Levites and the foreigners who live in your town. Ten Percent of the Harvest Moses said to Israel:
text: Denii u ni Levi dee ni hɔɔhra la n du ii biini la gil ii bɔra sɔɔni, dikuu kunnanaa la Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n tɛɛ ii ni ii diinihina la wia.

ref: Every year you are to give ten percent of your harvest to the Lord. But every third year, this ten percent must be given to the poor who live in your town, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. That way, they will have enough to eat.
text: Di ii wa lizi kumpattaa maa bɔra fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa dau, binni ahorohiŋ la n ɛɛ kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa lizaa bina la, ii daŋ kpaa tɛɛ Levi dee ni hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana la maa n du ii biini la, bá dia ii bola biine, di kukki.

ref: Then you must pray: Our Lord and our God, you have said that ten percent of my harvest is sacred. I have obeyed your command and given this to the poor, including the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
text: Denii ii jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, ‘N lizi n kumpattaa la n ɛɛ i horaa lii n dia, di tɛɛ Levi dee, hɔɔhra, lalbiizi ani luhaana, gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Maa i wiŋɔɔlaa la bɛl maa vɛɛwɛ gɛɛ di suuh bɛl maa wia.

ref: I have not eaten any of this sacred food while I was in mourning; in fact, I never touched it when I was unclean. And none of it has been offered as a sacrifice to the spirits of the dead. I have done everything exactly as you commanded.
text: Maa sɛɛwɛ di i hor la yemmaa, saŋa la minna wii ni biinichɔg la gɛɛ di lizi u yemmaa saŋa la min doŋŋe i be la gɛɛ di kpa u yemmaa tɛɛ lalaa. N hiŋ hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la nuarɛ. N hiŋ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔ n ɛɛu.

ref: Our Lord, look down from your temple in heaven and bless us and our land. You promised our ancestors that you would give us this land rich with milk and honey, and you have kept your promise. The Lord Is Your God, and You Are His People Moses said to Israel:
text: Liŋŋi di binni a hɛri lii chiŋ, i duuribɔr la, di kissi i nɛra Izrɛl hina ani hɛri la hiŋ tɛɛ yaa, gunla hiŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala la, hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la.’ ” Kɔraawiizi widaulaa hiŋaa wia

ref: Today the Lord your God has commanded you to obey these laws and teachings with all your heart and soul.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra ŋɔ ii benii zinaa, dí ii ra hiŋ u widaulaa, u Gbɔgni ani ii bampiree ni ii biine maa.

ref: In response, you have agreed that the Lord will be your God, that you will obey all his laws and teachings, and that you will listen when he speaks to you.
text: Zinaa, ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna humuu, di sɛɛ lugɔ ii danna hiŋ u nua, u Gbɔgni ani u widaulaa.

ref: Since you have agreed to obey the Lord, he has agreed that you will be his people and that you will belong to him, just as he promised.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ zinaa lugɔ ii ɛɛ u nɛraa, u kundɔɔlaa la n wesse u be werge maa, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la. A dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ ií ra hiŋ u widaulaa maa.

ref: The Lord created all nations, but he will make you more famous than any of them, and you will receive more praise and honor. You will belong only to the Lord your God, just as he promised.
text: U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ u daŋ gil ii kaali durnya hɛssi hina maa uŋ tawɛɛ. Ií ra chɔluu di ra tɔgzuu. Ii daŋ ɛɛ u bɛmbɛŋ nɛra gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la.”

ref: Moses stood together with the leaders and told the people of Israel: Obey all the laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
text: Moosis chi Izrɛl nabɔnzi naa, di ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií ra hiŋ widaulaa naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.

ref: At this same place, build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God. But don't use stones that have been cut with iron tools.
text: Ií ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Ií gilɛɛ wa kpa lugbii huŋhunni kummaa di waa sɛɛah.

ref: Look for stones that can be used without being cut. Then offer sacrifices to please the Lord, burning them completely on the altar.
text: Ií kpa bia la baŋ waa sɛɛhzɛɛ, di ma Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la mbusu lizibɔr, di ra lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa u ni, di ra tɛu.

ref: Next, offer sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing, and serve the meat at a sacred meal where you will celebrate in honor of the Lord.
text: Ií ra ligzi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi de, di ra dia ni bɔsɔna werge maa, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la sibɔɔ.

ref: Don't forget to write out a copy of these laws on the stone slabs that you are going to set up. Make sure that the writing is easy to read. Curses on Those Who Disobey
text: Ii daŋ sɛbi Gbɔgni naa wiŋɔɔlaa maa a bia ni, a chɔɔ di chaani nɛnnɛ.” Nuuseezi dikuu dignikpega wia

ref: Moses stood together with the priests and said, “Israel, be quiet and listen to me! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
text: Denii Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la ŋɔ Izrɛl hina maa be, “Izrɛl hina, ií siigi ka nuu! Ii jaa birgi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nɛraa.

ref: So you must obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you.”
text: Ií ra sɛɛ u nua, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa maa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.”

ref: That same day, Moses gave them the following instructions:
text: A hɔl hiŋ himmaa, Moosis kaa ŋɔ a nɛra be,

ref: Today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. Always obey them, and the Lord will make Israel the most famous and important nation on earth, and he will bless you in many ways.
text: Ii daŋ na kissaazi naa maa, a du ii be bɔr la maa iinna la, di ii ra sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua.

ref: The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ kissi ia ii bola ni ii kooni maa biine.

ref: You will have plenty of bread to eat.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ kissi ii mia ni diwee la iin niŋ kpaa di daali.

ref: The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
text: U daŋ kissi ii wiɛɛlaa maa.

ref: The Lord will help you defeat your enemies and make them scatter in all directions.
text: Di ii dɔma wa ballɔ bá wa lɔ ia, u daŋ kpegli baa tɛɛ ia. Di ba ga bɔkpaŋ ba, ka bɔkpilaa bá ga di chɔ yaari.

ref: The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kissi ii huma, di gil ii buugazi suugi. U daŋ kissi ia hɛri la unna tɛɛ ia la biini.

ref: If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii chi chigigi, di ɛɛ u nɛnanaananaa gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, di ii ra ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi.

ref: Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
text: Denii durnya nɛra maa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu tɛɛ u hiŋ, di ra ɔm ia.

ref: The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
text: U daŋ gil ii nyɛɛli werge. Ii biizi, ii sela ani ii kooni kuna daŋ wazi werge maa, hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia la biini.

ref: The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil dooŋ ba u balaa saŋa, di lii u dia la n du chiŋ, daama su u biini la. U daŋ kissi ii huma maa, hɛssi hina ba di waa kim ii be, ka iawaa waa kim di lii ba be.

ref: Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ gil ii tɔ hɛssi hina maa see. Wàá gil ii tɔ har. Ii daŋ ɔɔ nyɛɛli saŋa maa. Ii wàá ɛɛ wiimaa huhzi, di ii ra sɛɛ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa, di ra hiŋaa nɛnnɛ.

ref: and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
text: Ii daŋ siuzi, ii bɔrahɔna birgi diwee tɛɛ zumbizi ni pir sela maa. Nɛr maa wàá du de, ú ɔnzaa a kaali.

ref: Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
text: A daŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ wii ani witittaa tɛɛ ii ni ii naanna, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ, “Ama, di ii waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua ra sɛɛ, ii waa u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ, nuuseezi naa maa daŋ di ia, di tɛɛ ia tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: Your businesses and farms will fail.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ see ia nuuzi ii bolzenaa ni ii kooni maa biine.

ref: You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ see ia nua, ii biizi, ii pattikuna ani ii sela, a wàá wazi.

ref: The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
text: U daŋ see ii wiɛɛlaa maa nua.

ref: No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
text: U daŋ see ia nuuzi, di gil ii bugmi, di hau ii ni, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini, guŋŋ bá wa chɔg ia manaŋ, ii wia tuŋ dikuu wichɔgaa la iiŋ ɛɛwɛ, di kizuu ta wia.

ref: He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nyɔɔ ni hɛɛhriichaa lii chiŋ di chol ii hɛri lugɔ dooŋ, di ra ba saŋa la iin niŋ tuŋ nyaamm.

ref: The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see,
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii dɔma kpegli ia. Bɔkpannɛ ii ga lɔ baa, ka bɔkpilaa ii ga di chɔ yaari. Ii wia daŋ gil durnya kossi hina maa nuuzi kpu.

ref: The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you!
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpa Ijip kunsɔna la ha ii ni, á ɛɛ ŋmɛrzenaa, di ra lii nii, di ra huhrgi. Nɛr maa wàá wer chaa ia.

ref: You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused,
text: U daŋ kpa chugla, nyuŋŋaa ani bugmaa ha ii ni.

ref: that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
text: Wibaŋkaŋchiirii ni, ka ii danna largi bɔra alugɔ nyuŋŋa. Wii la maa iin niŋ ɛɛ wàá dɔɔ siwee. Hɔpizii maa, ba danna fir ia di ra ŋmɛɛ ia, ka nɛr maa wàá du de, ú lɛɛ ia.

ref: A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest.
text: Ii daŋ dɔɔ sɛnna di ra nyiŋŋi ii paa baa, ka nɛra baŋhinaa niŋ paa baa. Ii daŋ ma diini, ka ii wàá zuu a biine. Ii daŋ par grepu daazi kooni, ka ii wàá faari a nɔna dii.

ref: Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back.
text: Ba daŋ kpu ii nabala ii see, ka ii wàá heea. Ba daŋ foozi ii kauzi, ka ba wàá biraa tɛɛ ia. Ba daŋ kpa ii peeza tɛɛ ii dɔma, ka nɛr maa wàá lɛɛa tɛɛ ia.

ref: Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
text: Ba daŋ kpa ii biibaala ni biihaana tɛɛ hɛri bɛl hina. Ii pɛɛ ii siwee, di binni ba bir balaa ŋmɛnɛɛ guŋŋ di wa kuuh. Ii wàá dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ií ɛɛ wiimaa.

ref: You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
text: Nɛra la iiŋ waa zummɛɛ niŋ di ii hɛri kuna la iiŋ kpa ii fɔŋŋa di par na. Ii wàá dɔɔ kummaa di nɛfiraa ni nɛsunnaa bɛŋ lɛi, ii de dui saŋa.

ref: What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane,
text: Wia la iin ninna na daŋ gil ii ɛɛ lugɔ chuglahina.

ref: and the Lord will punish you from head to toe with boils that never heal.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil i naahiine ni i naazi ɔrgi kunsɔna la n na wii werge, ba wàá weraa chaa. A daŋ yaari di lii i naapaala ga hel i nyuubaana.

ref: The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ duŋŋi ii ni koori la iiŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ ú ra binni ia la, di kaali hɛrduma la ii ni ii mɛɛwaa n waa zummɛ. Denii ii ra kuari vuga la n ɛɛ daazi ni bia.

ref: People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
text: Ii wia daŋ kpu nɛra nuuzi, ba hah ia, di ra ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ hɛssi la maa biine Kɔraawiizi n niŋ duŋŋi ia ii ga du la.

ref: You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops.
text: Ii daŋ duu kuna werge, ka tamaa bɛnnɛ ii kum, dikuubɛɛwiai, lotorozi daŋ di a maa.

ref: You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms.
text: Ii daŋ par grepu daazi kooni, ka ii wàá nyɔɔ a nɔna siŋ gɛɛ di chaali a nɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, sandulee niŋ dia.

ref: Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
text: Ii daŋ dɔɔ ɔlivi daazi ii hɛri maa biini, ka ii wàá na a nuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɔna maanii niŋ war.

ref: Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
text: Lotorozi kpila miiih daŋ tɔ ii daazi ni ii kooni kuna maa ni, di dia.

ref: Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless.
text: Hɔɔhra la n du ii biini la fɔŋŋa danna jaa, ka iawaa hor hanna tuu zɛɛ.

ref: You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers. More Curses for Disobedience Moses said:
text: Ii danna kim kebee di ra lii ba be, ka baawaa wàá kim di lii ii be. Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nyuu, ii ge ɛɛ lugɔ diŋ.

ref: Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you.
text: Nuuseezi naa maa daŋ di ia. A daŋ di ia di ra ba saŋa la ii wia n niŋ tuŋ, dikuu iiŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua, di vɛɛ u widaulaa hiŋaa la wia.

ref: If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him,
text: Dikuu iiŋ waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la hummɛ ni bɔsɔna ni biinihuŋŋu, saŋa la iiŋ nyɛɛlɛɛ la wia.

ref: he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
text: Lɔzi, niinyɔgzi, laala nyaai ani nyaachɔgiirɛ, ii kpa di ra hum ii dɔma la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil bá wa lɔ ia la. Napattaa baŋaa lugbidaarɛ ú kpa sag ii baŋaazi, di ra ba saŋa la un niŋ kpuuzi ia nyaamm.

ref: Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil hɛri bɛl hina n lii bɔɔnɛɛ ba, di wa lɔ ia. Ba daŋ lii hɛri tuna alugɔ chig n lii chiŋ di ra tuu hɛri, ii wàá ra nuu ba mɔɔri.

ref: They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children.
text: Hɛri la hina n dɔɔ sikpegii, ba waa nabɔnzi ra tɔgzi gɛɛ di ra suŋ bichalli ni.

ref: All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down,
text: Ba daŋ fɔɔ ii bolzenaa maa n du ii hɛri guŋŋ, di ra ba saŋa la a koŋliizenaa la n kpekke, ii yardaa la n niŋ chogli. Ba daŋ fɔɔ bolzenaa la maa n du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ ia la.

ref: while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you.
text: Tɔɔrɔɔ la n niŋ huuzi ia saŋa la ii dɔma n niŋ fɔɔ ia la wia, ii daŋ hee ii biizi. Biizi la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum n tɛɛ ia la ola.

ref: Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children.
text: Wàá sɛɛ kpa u bie la ol unna hee la tɛɛ bɛl maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, kunla maa uŋ dɔɔwɛɛ guŋ. Tɔɔrɔɔ la ii dɔma n niŋ gil u huuzi ia saŋa la baŋ fɔɔ ii bolzenaa maa la wia.

ref: A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children. Disobedience Brings Destruction Moses said to Israel:
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ siryaa ú suahzi hee u biifula ni u dɔŋ, dikuu saŋa la ii dɔma n fɔɔ ia ani tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg la baŋ kpawɛɛ ta ii ni la wia.

ref: like those you were so afraid of in Egypt.
text: U daŋ gil Ijip hina wiila la maa iinna ɔm la chol ii ni, a wàá ta ia.

ref: Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa gil wiila ni hɛhchɔg irizi la wia baŋ waa sɛbɛɛ Gbɔg Hɔnnaa biini, chol ii ni guŋŋ di ra ba ii siuzaa saŋa.

ref: There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left.
text: Iiŋ faa kpillɛ werge lugɔ chinchiŋwilaa la, ka ii daŋ ka tama, dikuu iiŋ waa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua hiŋŋɛ wia.

ref: The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
text: Gunla am par Kɔraawiizi, u gil ii daama ni ii biizi wazi werge la, gunnɛ a paruu, ú gil ii wia bir pɛɛ, ú kpuuzi ia. Ba daŋ duŋŋi ia lii hɛri la biini iinna zuu ií dɔɔ la.

ref: Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi gil ii yaari a hɛssi maa biine, di lii hɛri tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl. Denii ii ra kuari vuga la n ɛɛ daazi ni bia, ii ni ii naabaala n faa waa zummɛ.

ref: Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
text: Chɔɔzi ni, ii daŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Di duanaa faa keŋ!’ Duana ge, ii ŋɔ, ‘Di chɔɔzii faa keŋ!’ Ɔnsii werge la n niŋ lau ia ani wia la ii siwee n ninna na la wiarɛ ii ra ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii bir zuu muugberzenaa kaali Ijip, bɔr la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ii wàá ka la la. Denii ii kpa iihinaa di yoo ra tɛɛ ii dɔma, ií ɛɛ ba yombaala ni haana. Ka nɛr maa wàá yau ia.”

ref: So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai. The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord The Lord Is Your God
text: Kɔraawiizi ni Izrɛl hina nuukpaŋ la uŋ ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ u ni Izrɛl hina ɛɛ Moab hɛri la widaulaarɛ keŋ, di kpa jaa unla u ni baa n faa ɛɛwɛ Bizeŋ Sinaai la.

ref: When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them.
text: Yaa n faa wa hel ɛŋ, Hɛsbɔn Koori Sihɔn ni Basan Koori Ɔɔg faa liwɔɔrɛ bá lɔ yaa, ka yaa kpegli baa.

ref: Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. Keep the Agreement Moses said:
text: Yaa faa foozi ba hɛri, di bɔnnuu tɛɛ Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ.

ref: Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do.
text: Ií ra hiŋ nuukpaŋ naa widaulaa nɛnnɛ, guŋ gil ií nyɛɛli ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini.

ref: Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
text: ii chi ɛnnɛ, ii ni Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii. Nuukpaŋfalii la u ni ia n na ɛɛ zinaa, u hɛɛhzi di ra bagli guŋ la,

ref: When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols.
text: Ii faa na ba vuga la n ɛɛ daazi, bia, saliŋhuŋŋa ani saliŋ la Kɔraawiizi n hahwɛɛ labuu, ba biine.

ref: So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations. If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit.
text: Ií ɛɛ ania, baal gɛɛ haaŋ gɛɛ domee gɛɛ dee maa n du ii biini zinaa naa, bampirii gilɛɛ wa bir di ra lii Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ni, ú gaa kuari a hɛssi naa hina vuga. Guŋ daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ daa lunni siri n kpolle werge.

ref: You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you.
text: Di a hiŋ wa nuu gunla nuukpaŋ naa wiŋɔɔlaa n na bagli, ɔɔ kissi u hinnɛ, di ra fɛ lugɔ u daŋ na u hiŋ, haali unna hiŋ u himmaa kipar ŋmɛnɛɛ gba. Guŋ daŋ gil Kɔraawiizi chɔgi wichɔgɛɛra ni nɛnanaa maa.

ref: The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lizuu lii Izrɛl hina dizi maa biini, di gil hɛhchɔg chol u ni gunla nuukpaŋ naa nuuseezi la baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Gbɔg Hɔnnaa biini n na bagli.

ref: The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land
text: Ii biizi la n niŋ hiŋ ii ni, ni jiminizi la n niŋ ba ni hɔɔhra la n niŋ lii hɛhjaŋa la daŋ na biinichɔg wia la n niŋ huuzi ia, a hɛri biini ani wiila la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ ta ii ni.

ref: has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
text: A hɛri maa daŋ hil di chɔɔ pɛɛ, jilbi ni yazii niŋ tɔ u maa. Ba wàá duu kummaa, kummaa ge wàá lii de, daazi ni kooree gba wàá wer lii de. Ii hɛri daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ bolzenaa Sɔdɔm, Gɔmɔra, Adma ani Zɛbɔyim. A ninɛɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge, u chɔgaa la.

ref: People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
text: Hɛssi hina maa daŋ pɛɛzi, ‘Bɛɛ n gillɛ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ hɛri naa kennei? Bɛɛ n gillɛ u baaŋ fuuh kennei?’

ref: And they will be given this answer: Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement
text: Kenne bá bagli a zɛɛ, ‘Nɛra naa vɛɛ ba ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ labuu. Nuukpaŋ la ba ni Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la n ɛɛwɛ la, saŋa la uŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la.

ref: and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods,
text: Ba faa gaa kuari vugaa, di ra tognaa. Vuga la baŋ faa waa zummɛ. Vuga la uŋ waa baa tɛɛwɛ.

ref: and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa. U baaŋfuuih hiŋ biinii u lizi baa lii ba hɛri, di kpa baa ta hɛrduma biini, ba du de haali ni zinaa.’

ref: The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
text: Wia aŋhina du denii, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la gil a suah, ka u Gbɔg la waa, u pilluubuu, yàá ni yaa naanna ra sɛɛ u wia, saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you,
text: Moosis kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Di kissaazi ni nuuseezi naa maa miŋ kpawɛɛ ra dau ii see zinaa naa maa wa du ii be, ií kpaa du ii biine, bɔr la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n niŋ gil ii yaari hɛssi biine la.

ref: return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today.
text: Di ii ni ii biizi wa bittɔ ba Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la be, di ra sɛɛ u nua ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa gunla miŋ bagli ia zinaa naa,

ref: Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back
text: Haali di ii yaarɔɔrɛ la hɛssi magazi gba, ka Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kaa chaali ia di bir ba ii ni Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
text: U daŋ bir ba ii ni hɛri la n faa ɛɛ ii naabaala hor la, ii foozuu dɔɔ la. U daŋ gil ii nyɛɛli di wazi di kaali ii mɛɛwaa.

ref: You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
text: Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ gil ii ni ii naanna chɛr ii manni, di gilɛɛ kaa dɔɔ dignikpega ka nɔŋŋuu ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa, di wer du a hɛri.

ref: Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
text: U daŋ bir nuuseezi la du ii dɔma la n hah ia, di faa ra fir ia la ni.

ref: You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord,
text: Ii daŋ kaa ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra, di ra hiŋ u widaulaa naa minna tɛɛ ia zinaa naa.

ref: and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi gil ii nyɛɛli, ii wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Ii biizi ni ii sela daŋ wazi, ii kooni kuna lɛɛ werge. U bɔra daŋ kaa sɔɔni, ú gil ii nyɛɛli gunla uŋ faa gillɛ ii mɛɛwaa nyɛɛli la.

ref: But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Choose Life, Not Death Moses said to Israel:
text: Ka a dɛkkɔɔ ii ra sɛɛ u nua, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni naa baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Gbɔg Hɔŋ naa biini. A dɛkkɔɔ ií bir ba u be ni ii biine ni ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa.

ref: You know God's laws, and it isn't impossible to obey them.
text: Wia naa miŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɛɛ ia zinaa naa waa kpol gɛɛ di du bɔɔnɛɛ.

ref: His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.”
text: Chiŋ lɛi u du, ii ra pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ tinni di ga ba u ni hɛri, yá wer nuu wia la n du u biini, di ra sɛɛawɛi?’

ref: And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.”
text: Waa muuzeŋ baŋgia bɛl duwɛɛ ge, ii ra pɛɛzi, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ gi, di ga ba u ni wa tɛɛ yaa, yá nuu di ra sɛɛ u wiai?’

ref: No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
text: Akai, a wiŋɔɔlii dugli iabuu werge maa, di du ii nuuzi ni ii biine, guŋ gil ii ra sɛɛ u wia.

ref: Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster.
text: Ií ra nuu! Winanaa ni wichɔgaa gɛɛ miibɔɔ ni siurɛ n kpa ra dau ii see zinaa la. Ií lizi bɛl.

ref: Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life!
text: Zinaa, n na yir chiŋ ni hɛrii, á diŋ daansɛɛ lugɔ n kpa miibɔɔ ni siu, kissaa ani nuuseezii di ra dau ii see. Awia, ií lizi miibɔɔ, ii ni ii biizi wer dɔɔu,

ref: Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
text: di wer nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra nuu u wiŋɔzi, di lawuu kpogli chigigi. Kɔraawiizii ii miibɔɔ. U daŋ gil ii di biŋkpila hɛri la uŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ ii mɛɛwaa Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la biini.”

ref: Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
text: Denii Moosis lii di ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa,

ref: Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
text: Ií chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega. Ií gilɛɛ waa ɔm gɛɛ di waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ni iabuu ra vol. Wàá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa. Wàá gil ii ta maa.”

ref: Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said: Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people.
text: Denii Moosis yir Josua di ŋɔ u be Izrɛl hina maa see, “Chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ni nɛra naabuu niŋ zuu hɛri la wia Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ tɛɛ ba naabaala lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛɛ baa la. A dɛkkɔɔ i bɔnnuu tɛɛ baa, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ.

ref: The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies. Read These Laws
text: Kɔraawiizi himmaanii niŋ tɔ i see, di du i be. Wàá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa. Wàá gil ii ta maa. Gilɛɛ waa ɔm, gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih.” Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg karmaa wia

ref: Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord.
text: Awia, Moosis faa sɛbi Gbɔg naa, di kpau tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la n ɔɔ ra chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi maa.

ref: Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law. Israel Will Reject the Lord
text: Ba biizi la n waa Gbɔg naa zummɛ la dɛkkɔɔ bá nuu la, di helli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ɔmaa, saŋa la maa iin niŋ du a hɛri naa iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu, ií foozi di dɔɔ naa biini.” Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Izrɛl hina dignikpega wia

ref: The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.” Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Filaŋkeŋ i siu hɔpizii duglɔɔrɛ. Yir Josua, í nuu chi n Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia biini, ń tɛu huma.” Awia, Moosis ni Josua faa la de.

ref: and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ba de lugɔ baama n du miriti di la chiŋ, di wa chi a Tanti Dia dominua.

ref: The Lord said: Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “I daŋ la ga chɔɔ i mɛɛwaa be, ka nɛra naa daŋ bir gaa jaami vuga la baŋ waa zummɛ, hɛri la banna nyiŋŋi bá zuu naa biini. Ba daŋ vɛɛŋ, di chɔgi nuukpaŋ la n ni baa n ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ba ni ń vɛɛ baa, di bir har kpu baa, ka ba kpu baa. Tɔɔrɔɔzenaa kpila ni anuula daŋ huuzi baa, ba pɛɛzi a hɔl hiŋ, ‘Kɔraawiizi n waa hoo yaa be wia lɛi, tɔɔrɔɔzenaa naa chol yaa nii?’

ref: They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
text: Wibii maa, n daŋ bir har kpu baa a hɔl hiŋ, dikuu ba biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la banna ɛɛ, di ra kuari vuga la wia.”

ref: Moses and Joshua, I am going to give you the words to a new song. Write them down and teach the song to the Israelites. If they learn it, they will know what I want them to do, and so they will have no excuse for not obeying me.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ Moosis ni Josua be, “Ií sɛbi yir naa tɛɛ iihinaa, Moosis bagli Izrɛl hina ú yiraa, bá ra yiruu, ú di daansɛɛ tɛŋ ba wia.

ref: I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
text: Di n wa kpogli baa zuu hɛri la n summɛ, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge la biini, miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala la, di ba wa nawɔɔ ra di, di nyɛɛli, ba daŋ bir di ra kuari vuga, di ra tognaa. Ba daŋ vɛɛŋ, di chɔgi n ni baa nuukpaŋ la.

ref: When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me. I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
text: Di hɛhchɔgni ni anuula kpila wa chol ba ni, yir naa daŋ di ba daansɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba naanna wàá suuuh. N zum wia la ban niŋ ɛɛu mɔɔ, ka n haa kpogli baa zuu hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la biini.”

ref: Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
text: Awia, Moosis sɛbi a yir dau a hɔl hiŋ, di bagli Izrɛl hina u yiraa.

ref: The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Nun biibaal Josua, “Chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di gilɛɛ ra ɔm, dikuubɛɛwiai, i daŋ kpogli Izrɛl hina di zuu hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la. N daŋ du i be.”

ref: Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book,
text: Moosis n wa sɛbi Gbɔg naa wiŋɔɔlaa maa di wa tuŋ,

ref: then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
text: kenne u faa ŋɔ Levi dee la n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la be,

ref: This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do.
text: “Ií kpa Gbɔg Hɔnnaa dau Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la kɛrii. U daŋ chɔɔ de di ra di ii daansɛɛ.

ref: I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone.
text: N zum gunla iiŋ kpoŋŋe di dɔɔ dignikpegaa. Di ii kpoŋŋo Kɔraawiizi be n de dui saŋa, ii kpoŋaa daŋ nyaŋŋi, di n siuwɔ.

ref: So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
text: Ií yir ii dizi la maa nabɔnzi ni ba nabɔnzenaa, ń ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ baa, ka yir chiŋ ni hɛri á diŋ daansɛɛ.

ref: I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you. The Song of Moses
text: N zummɔ lugɔ di n wa siuwɔ, ii daŋ haŋ chɔguu kɔrai, di bir har kpu wia naa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia naa. A wàá birgi ka hɛhchɔg chol ii ni, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ii ni, dikuu vuga la iiŋ kuarɛɛ wia.” Moosis yir wia

ref: Moses called a meeting of all the people of Israel, so he could teach them the words to the song that the Lord had given him. And here are the words:
text: Denii Moosis faa kurgi a yir wiŋɔɔlaa maa, di lii u lugli di ga hel u tuna, Izrɛl hina la maa n chaalɛɛ la see.

ref: Israel, I will teach you. My words will be like gentle rain on tender young plants, or like dew on the grass.
text: N baglaa daŋ ɛɛu lugɔ dooŋ n na ba, di chol hɛri lugɔ ŋmɛnii. N wiŋɔzi daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ dooŋ n mussɛɛ kunjigzi n haa ra hel ni, di ɛɛ lugɔ dooŋ n mussɛɛ kooree ni.

ref: Join with me in praising the wonderful name of the Lord our God.
text: N daŋ dargi Kɔraawiizi, ú nɛra bagli u zenni ni u girme wia.

ref: The Lord is a mighty rock, and he never does wrong. God can always be trusted to bring justice.
text: Kɔraawiizii ii guurikpeg lugɔ Bizeŋ, waa lewaa dɔɔwɛ, di ra di wibii. Ú wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Kɔraawiizi wia dɔɔ wibiire, waa dar. U wiɛɛlaa maa deŋloore gunla n dɛkkɛ.

ref: But you lie and cheat and are unfaithful to him. You have disgraced yourselves and are no longer worthy to be his children.
text: Ka ii wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ, ii waa dɛg ii ɛɛ u nɛra. Ii ɛɛ nɛra la n na ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di dɔɔ daraa.

ref: Israel, the Lord is your Father, the one who created you, but you repaid him by being foolish.
text: Kenne dɛkkɛ iin ninna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizia? Gɛnaa ni nfɛrnyaara! Waabuu ii Mɛɛ ni ii Taari, waabuu gillɛ ii ɛɛ hɛri bɛl hina.

ref: Think about past generations. Ask your parents or any of your elders. They will tell you
text: Ií ra liizi faala wia, ii pɛɛzi ii mɛɛwaa ni ii maawaa, bá bagli ia wia la n ɛɛwɛ a saŋa. Ií pɛɛzi nabɔnzi, bá bagli ia faala wia.

ref: that God Most High gave land to every nation. He assigned a guardian angel to each of them,
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu tɛɛ hɛssi hina maa ba hɛssi. Waabuu ɔɔ dau nɛra maa duuribɔra. Di ɔɔ gil mɛlika ra binni hɛri maa hina ni.

ref: but the Lord himself takes care of Israel.
text: Ka Jekɔb naanna waa, u lizi baabuu tɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: Israel, the Lord discovered you in a barren desert filled with howling winds. God became your fortress, protecting you as though you were his own eyes.
text: U faa na baabuu banna juuri hɛribɔduma biini, bɔr la n waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ, peu chaazi de maa nyaamm la. U faa guu baabuu, di binni ba ni gunla un niŋ guu u hiŋ la.

ref: The Lord was like an eagle teaching its young to fly, always ready to swoop down and catch them on its back.
text: Di ɛɛ lugɔ chig la n na bagli u biizi zaaih, di ɔɔ yaa u keeri di ra chamaa la. Kɔraawiizi faa waa sɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hina chol.

ref: Israel, the Lord led you, and without the aid of a foreign god,
text: Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ faa tɔ u nɛra see, di hɛrduma bɛl maa vug faa wɔɔ hiinee.

ref: he helped you capture the land. Your fields were rich with grain. Olive trees grew in your stony soil, and honey was found among the rocks.
text: Giŋgimee nyuuni maa faa ɛɛ ba kundɔɔlaarɛ, ba faa ra di ba kooni kuna. Ba faa na huuhnuurɛ di ra di bia la biine, ba ɔlivizi daazi faa lɛɛ a bia hɛri biini.

ref: Your flocks and herds produced milk and yogurt, and you got choice meat from your sheep and goats that grazed in Bashan. Your wheat was the finest, and you drank the best wine.
text: Ba nauna ni buuna faa dɔɔ ilanii werge, ba peeza ni buuna ani naunaa faa wessoo werge maa. Ba mia ni siŋ faa waa dɔŋ dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Israel, you grew fat and rebelled against God, your Creator you rejected the Mighty Rock, your only place of safety.
text: Kɔraawiizi nɛra faa ra nyɛɛli werge, ka dɔɔ dignikpega, ba faa pɔllɔɔ di piŋ werge. Ba faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n ta baa labuu, di vɛɛ ba Lɛɛri la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la.

ref: You made God jealous and angry by worshiping disgusting idols and foreign gods.
text: Ba vuga kuaraa la faa gillɔɔ Kɔraawiizi bɔra faa ra wii werge maa. Ba wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la faa gillɔɔ u baaŋ fuuh.

ref: You offered sacrifices to demons, those useless gods that never helped you, new gods that your ancestors never worshiped.
text: Ba faa ra lizi mbusuzi di ra tɛɛ tinnanchɔgaa la n waa Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɛ. Vuga la baŋ faa waa zummɛ, vuga la Izrɛl hina n haa waa a nuuzi hiŋŋɛ.

ref: You turned away from God, your Creator; you forgot the Mighty Rock, the source of your life.
text: Ba faa suuh Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n ɛɛ ba Lɛɛri, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la, unla n tɛɛ baa miibɔɔ la wiarɛ.

ref: You were the Lord's children, but you made him angry. Then he rejected you
text: Kɔraawiizi n wa na guŋ, u baaŋ fuuh, u vɛɛ u biibaala ni u biihaana ta.

ref: and said, “You are unfaithful and can't be trusted. So I won't answer your prayers; I'll just watch and see what happens to you.
text: Di faa ŋɔ, ‘Màá ka hiini baa. Denii ń na wii la n niŋ huuzi dignikpega ni wibii nyaara naa.

ref: “My people, I will breathe out fire that sends you down to the world of the dead. It will scorch your farmlands and burn deep down under the mountains.
text: N baaŋfuuih daŋ izi lugɔ ninlau, di fuuh hɛri kummaa. U daŋ zuu hɛri, di ga hel lalaa bol, di ga fuuh bizenaa zɛɛzi maa.

ref: I'll send disaster after disaster to strike you like arrows.
text: N daŋ gil hɛhchɔgni la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ ra chol ba ni, alugɔ minna ta baa n hobee maa.

ref: You'll be struck by starvation and deadly diseases, by the fangs of wild animals and poisonous snakes.
text: Lɔzi ni bɔwemaa niŋ kpuuzi baa, wiilchɔgaarɛ niŋ kpuuzi baa. N daŋ gil sechɔgaa lauri baa di gil hɛrikuna la siri n kpolle werge dunzi baa.

ref: Young and old alike will be killed in the streets and terrified at home.
text: Laal daŋ gil ba ŋmɛnizenaa suugi ni lalaa, ɔnsii werge chol ba ni, ba diini biine. Biipɔllaa ni suŋgure daŋ siuzi, biifulli gɛɛ nɛzɛŋzi gba wàá na bahinaa.

ref: “I wanted to scatter you, so no one would remember that you had ever lived.
text: N daŋ vii kpuuzi baa nyaamm, nɛr maa wàá ka liizi ba wia,

ref: But I dreaded the sound of your enemies saying, ‘We defeated Israel with no help from the Lord.’ ”
text: ka màá sɛɛ gil ba dɔma ra ta bara lugɔ baabuu kpegli n nɛra, ka n himmaanii kpuuzi baa la.’

ref: People of Israel, that's what the Lord has said to you. But you don't have good sense, and you never listen to advice.
text: Izrɛl hina ɛɛ nɛra la n waa nfɛrɛ dɔɔwɛɛ. Ba waa nunzuma maa dɔɔwɛ.

ref: How could one enemy soldier chase a thousand of Israel's troops? Or how could two of theirs pursue ten thousand of ours? It can only happen if the Lord stops protecting Israel and lets the enemy win.
text: Bɛɛ n gillɛ nɛkpaŋ wer kpegli nɛra kagboŋei, nɛra banɛɛ kpegli nɛra kagboŋa fiei? Kɔraawiizi la banna hum labuu vɛɛ baa ta. Unla n ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu kpa baa tɛɛ ba dɔma.

ref: Even our enemies know that only our God is a Mighty Rock.
text: Ba dɔma zummɔ lugɔ ba himmaa vuga la waa kpeg. A waa fɔŋŋazeŋ dɔɔwɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la.

ref: Our enemies are grapevines rooted in the fields of Sodom and Gomorrah. The grapes they produce are full of bitter poison;
text: Ba dɔma la n dɔɔ biinikpola lugɔ Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra hina la, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ grepu daazi la n na nɔŋ nɔŋkpola, a ɛɛ lugɔ siri la,

ref: their wine is more deadly than cobra venom.
text: lugɔ siŋ la baŋ kpa hɛrikuŋ siri di daali.

ref: But the Lord has written a list of their sins and locked it in his vault.
text: Kɔraawiizi ra liizi ba dɔma wiɛɛlaa labuu. U ra kpaŋ saŋa la n dɛkkɛ ú tɛr ba dignaa.

ref: Soon our enemies will get what they deserve— suddenly they will slip, and total disaster will quickly follow.
text: Kɔraawiizii niŋ turgi baa a kim. Saŋa ra bau ban niŋ chol, ba chɔgaa hɔpizi duglɔɔrɛ.

ref: When only a few of the Lord's people remain, when their strength is gone, and some of them are slaves, the Lord will feel sorry for them and give them justice.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra, di u wa nawɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa n tunnɛ. U daŋ suŋ banla n na humuu la ni, di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ ba waa hiini dɔɔwɛ.

ref: But first the Lord will say, “You ran for safety to other gods— couldn't they help you?
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi u nɛra, ‘Lee vuga la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, ii yardaa la duɛi?

ref: You offered them wine and your best sacrifices. Can't those gods help you now or give you protection?
text: Ii mbusuzi lizaa kuna nuurii, ii faa kpa di ra tɛɛa, di ra tɛɛa siŋ. Ií gil a ba wa hiini ia filaŋkeŋ, ií gil a chɔ wa lɛɛ ia!

ref: Don't you understand? I am the only God; there are no others. I am the one who takes life and gives it again. I punished you with suffering. But now I will heal you, and nothing can stop me!
text: N bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi, vug maa waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ. Minuu ɔɔ kpu, di kaa tɛɛ miibɔɔ, di du pira, di kaa chaa. Nɛr maa wàá wer tɔ n wiɛɛlaa ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: “I make this solemn promise: Just as I live forever,
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la, lɔ n bampiriire di hɛɛhzi lugɔ

ref: I will take revenge on my hateful enemies. I will sharpen my sword and let it flash like lightning.
text: di n wa sazi n tokobi la n na nyɛgzi, di kpau ń di seriya, n daŋ turgi n dɔma ba wichɔgaa kim, di tɛr banla n hahŋ la digna.

ref: My arrows will get drunk on enemy blood; my sword will taste the flesh and the blood of the enemy. It will kill prisoners, and cut off the heads of their leaders.”
text: Ba chal daŋ lii n hobee ni, di ra toŋzi. N daŋ kpuuzi banla maa n na diŋ mmɔri la ni n tokobi. Màá gil nɛr la maa n niŋ yooŋ. Haali banla n na pira ni banla baŋ laurɛɛ la maanii niŋ siuzi.’

ref: Tell the heavens to celebrate and all gods to bow down to the Lord, because he will take revenge on those hateful enemies who killed his people. He will forgive the sins of Israel and purify their land.
text: Hɛssi hina, a dɛkkɔɔ ii ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi nɛra. U ɔɔ tɛr nɛra la maa n na kpuuzi baa la dignaa. U ra turgi u dɔmaa ba wichɔgaa kim, ka gil u nɛra waa wichɔgaa di ra tɛɛ baa.”

ref: he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law.
text: u ŋɔ, “Ií ra du tau ka ra hiŋ widaulaa naa maa miŋ tɛɛ ia zinaa naa. Ií dammaa ra tɛɛ ii biizi, bá ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua ni wibii.

ref: The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.” Moses Will See the Land
text: Widaulaa naa waa wipɛɛri ɛɛwɛ. A ɛɛ ii miibɔɔrɛ. Ií ra hiŋaa, di wer du hɛri la iinna gi Jɔɔdan muu ii so la, di birgi.” Moosis n niŋ siu Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ nyuu wia

ref: Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
text: A hɔl hiŋ maanii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be,

ref: Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel.
text: “La ga tinni Abarim bizenaa la n du Moab hina hɛri, a ni bolzeŋ Jɛriko chaŋ dɔŋa la, di ga tinni Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ, di binni Keenan hina hɛri la miŋ ŋɔ ń kpa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la.

ref: Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor.
text: I daŋ siu a bizeŋ nyuu, di ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, gunla i kpɛɛma Aarɔn n siu Bizeŋ Hɔɔ nyuu la,

ref: Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, ii maa faa nyaa wibiire n be, Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ, saŋa la iiŋ faa du Mɛriba niiri bɔr la n dugli bol la banna yir Kadɛs, u du Zin Hɛribɔduma la. Ii faa gbɛllimbuu a nɛra sibɔɔ.

ref: So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
text: Awia, i daŋ chi bɔɔnɛɛ ka binni hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la, ka hàá zuu u biini.”

ref: Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
text: Kissaazi naabuu Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis faa dibi tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, ka siu.

ref: The Lord came from Mount Sinai. From Edom, he gave light to his people, and his glory was shining from Mount Paran. Thousands of his warriors were with him, and fire was at his right hand.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi faa lii Bizeŋ Sinaairɛ di ba, di ɛɛ lugɔ wiizi n liwɛɛ di guali Ɛdɔm hina ni, di ra chaani u nɛra ni, di lii Bizeŋ Paran nyuu. U ni mɛlikazi kagboŋa fii ballɛ, di lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag, di lii u bizeŋ bɔwillaa.

ref: The Lord loves the tribes of Israel, and he protects his people. They listen to his words and worship at his feet. *
text: Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi u nɛraa, di ra guu banla n ɛɛ u hora la. Awia, yaa ɔɔ togni u seere, di ra sɛɛ u widaulaa.

ref: I called a meeting of the tribes of Israel and gave you God's Law.
text: Yaa ra sɛɛ Gbɔg la Moosis n tɛɛ yaa la wiarɛ, u ɛɛ yaa hɛri kunzenne yaa be.

ref: Then you and your leaders made the Lord your king.
text: Kɔraawiizi birgi Izrɛl hina koorii, saŋa la ba dizi ni ba sitɔɔra n chaalɛɛ la.”

ref: Tribe of Reuben, you will live, even though your tribe will always be small.
text: Kenne Moosis ŋɔ Rubin dee wia, “Haali Rubin nɛra n waa kpil la gba, ka ba wàá dim.”

ref: The Lord will listen to you, tribe of Judah, as you beg to come safely home. You fought your enemies alone; now the Lord will help you.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Juda dee wia, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, á nuu ba wile di ra lɛɛ baa. Gil ba ni dizi la n kawɛɛ la, kaa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. Yoo ra tɛɛ baa, di ra hiini baa, bá ra kpegli ba dɔma.”

ref: At Massah and Meribah Spring, the Lord tested you, tribe of Levi. You were faithful, and so the priesthood belongs to the Levi tribe.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Levi dee wia, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, di ba wa ta Urim ni Tumim, gil i kipar chaani i huŋhunna Levi dee la wia n dɔɔ wibii la be. I faa ɛɛ baabuu di na Massa, di gil ba wia dɔɔ wibii Mɛriba niiri la bɔr.

ref: Protecting Israel's agreement with the Lord was more important to you than the life of your father or mother, or brothers or sisters, or your own children.
text: Ba faa ra tɔgzii ani wibii kaali ba mɛɛwaa, maawaa, lulla ani biizi. Ba faa ra hiŋ i widaulaarɛ, di faa dɔɔ wibii i nuukpaŋ la wia biini.

ref: You teach God's laws to Israel, and at the place of worship you offer sacrifices and burn incense.
text: Ba daŋ bagli i nɛra bá ra hiŋ i Gbɔg la. Ba danna lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa, i mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: I pray that the Lord will bless everything you do, and make you strong enough to crush your enemies.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hiini ba dizi bá hel, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. Gil ba wiɛɛlaa maa parii. Kpu ba dɔma maa, di dim baa.”

ref: The Lord Most High loves you, tribe of Benjamin. He will live among your hills and protect you.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Bɛnjamin dee wia, “Dee naabuu Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi, di ra guu baa la. U ra guu baabuu hɔpizi biimaa, di du ba biini.”

ref: Descendants of Joseph, the Lord will bless you with precious water from deep wells and with dew from the sky.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Joosɛf dee wia, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ba hɛri, di tɛɛ baa dooŋ, niiri ra lii hɛri.

ref: Month by month, your fruit will ripen in the sunshine.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ba hɛri, ba daazi nɔna ra aah, di du wer nɛnnɛ, bina maa.

ref: You will have a rich harvest from the slopes of the ancient hills.
text: Bá faala maa giŋgimee la maa tɔ ni daazi nɔna la n summɛ werge.

ref: The Lord who appeared in the burning bush wants to give you the best the land can produce, and it will be a princely crown on Joseph's head.
text: Bá hɛri su ni kunla maa n wesse, di lii Kɔraawiizi kissaa la biini. Waabuu ŋɔ wia lii kasagee la n na lau niŋ la biini la. Kɔ́raawiizi gil kissaazi naa ba Joosɛf dee be, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu sitɔɔri u lulla biini.

ref: The armies of Ephraim and Manasseh are majestic and fierce like a bull or a wild ox. They will run their spears through faraway nations.
text: Joosɛf dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa lugɔ nabal, u nyigzi ɛɛ lugɔ pir nabal nyigzi. Ɛfram ni Manasɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa helloo kpabaa, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa lugɔ nabala. Gunla pir nau n ɔɔ lau nɛr la, gunnɛ bá ɛɛ ba dɔma, di taari baa kaali hɛri tunazi.”

ref: Be happy, Zebulun, as your boats set sail; be happy, Issachar, in your tents.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Zɛbulɔn ni Isaka dizi wia, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, gil Zɛbulɔn kɔɔzaa muuzeŋ biini la wazi, Isaka daama ge wazi bol.

ref: The sea will make you wealthy, and from the sandy beach you will get treasure. So invite the other tribes to celebrate with you and offer sacrifices to God.
text: Ba ɔɔ yir hɔɔhraa ba ba bizeŋ la nyuu, di waa ligzi mbusuzi la n dɛkkɛ de. Ba ɔɔ na ba daamaa lii muuzeŋ biini ani hɛɛhriichaa la n chɔɔ u nua la biini.”

ref: Tribe of Gad, the Lord will bless you with more land. So shout his praises! Your tribe is like a lion ripping up its victim.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Gad dee wia, “Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la n gillɛ ba hɛri du kaŋ. Gad chɔɔwɔɔ guu lugɔ bunyiŋ, ú dum nonii teŋ gɛɛ ú fugzi nyuhɔŋ.

ref: Your leaders met together and chose the best land for your tribe, but you obeyed the Lord and helped the other tribes.
text: A hɛri bɔnanii labuu ba faa lɛɛ dɔɔ. Nabɔma diiribɔttɛ ba tɛɛ baa. Ba faa ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u gbɔgnii, saŋa la Izrɛl sitɔɔra n faa chaalɛɛ la.”

ref: Tribe of Dan, you are like a lion cub, startled by a snake.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Dan dee wia, “Dan ɛɛ bunyiŋbiire, di zaah lii Basan barii.”

ref: The Lord is pleased with you, people of Naphtali. He will bless you and give you the land to the west and the south.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Naftali dee wia, “Naftali wia par Kɔraawiizii, u kissuu werge. Ba hɛri chɔɔwɔɔ lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag, di ga chug Galilii muuzeŋ.”

ref: The Lord's greatest blessing is for you, tribe of Asher. You will be the favorite of all the other tribes. You will be rich with olive oil
text: Kenne u ŋɔ Asɛ dee wia, “Asɛ dee na kissaare kaali dizi maa. Kɔ́raawiizi gil u lulla maa nɔŋŋuu. Ú hɛri dɔɔ ɔlivi daazi nɛnnɛ.

ref: and have strong town gates with bronze and iron bolts. Your people will be powerful for as long as they live.
text: Ú bola dominuuzi dɔɔ lugbia gbessi di ra guuu. Ú fɔŋŋa ni u hɔpizaa mɛgzi.”

ref: Israel, no other god is like ours— the clouds are his chariot as he rides across the skies to come and help us.
text: U kaa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Izrɛl hina, vug maa waa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Unla n ɔɔ ga chiŋ di waa kaali, di du baama biini ni zenni ni girme, di ra ba ú wa hiini ia la.

ref: The eternal God is our hiding place; he carries us in his arms. When God tells you to destroy your enemies, he will make them run.
text: Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa labuu ɛɛ ii guuri. U nonee la n du de saŋa maa labuu kpogli ia. Waabuu ɔɔ tɔ ii see di ra duŋŋi ii dɔma, di ŋɔ ií chɔgi ba maa nyaamm la.

ref: Israel, you will live in safety; your enemies will be gone. The dew will fall from the sky, and you will have plenty of grain and wine.
text: Awia, Jekɔb naanna duwɔɔrɛ ni bampirsɔna, di so bɔɔiih, hɛri la n dɔɔ mia ni siŋ werge la, bɔr la ŋmɛnii n ɔɔ lii chiŋ chol, di gil hɛri sɔɔni la biini.

ref: The Lord has rescued you and given you more blessings than any other nation. He protects you like a shield and is your majestic sword. Your enemies will bow in fear, and you will trample on their backs.
text: Izrɛl hina, bɔsɔna hinaa ia! Nɛr maa waa hoo di ɛɛ lugɔ ia. Hɛri la hina Kɔraawiizi n lɛɛwɛ. Kɔraawiizi himmaanii ii laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ ni ii tokobi. U daŋ guu ia, di kpegli ii dɔma tɛɛ ia. Ii dɔma daŋ ba di waa suŋŋi ia, ií suŋ ba ni, ka ii daŋ fɛrgi baa dau.”

ref: Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan.
text: Denii Moosis lii Moab lɛl di ga tinni Bizeŋ Nɛbɔ, di ga hel Bizeŋ Pisga nyuu, Jɛriko wiifurii. Denii Kɔraawiizi bagluu a hɛri maa, di lii Giliad di ga hel Dan,

ref: He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Naftali maa, Ɛfram ni Manasɛ hɛssi maa, Juda hɛri maa guŋŋ di ga wiicholii di ga hel Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn,

ref: The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
text: di kpa Nɛgɛv ni a paga maa, di lii Jɛriko Waluu, Abɛ Daazi Bolzeŋ di ga chug Zoa.

ref: The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis be, “Hɛri naabuu n hɛɛhzi ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ kpa tɛɛ Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb la, miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpau tɛɛ ba naanna la. N gillɔɔ i nau ni siwii, ka hàá gi di zuu u biini.”

ref: And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis siu Moab hɛri, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa huguubuu Moab hɛri, waluu la n chaŋ Bɛf Piɔ la biini. Haali ni zinaa, nɛr maa waa u ŋmam bɔr zummɛ.

ref: The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved
text: Izrɛl hina faa wii Moosis lee Moab hɛri lɛl la biini, hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ.

ref: Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses. Moses Was a Great Prophet
text: Nun biibaal Josua faa dɔɔ nunzuma werge, dikuu Moosis n faa kpa u nonee sag u ni, di suŋŋi wiizi tɛu la wia. Awia, Izrɛl hina faa nuu ra tɛu, di ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga Moosis be di ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la.

ref: There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him
text: Di haŋ lii a saŋa, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ maa waa kaa lii Izrɛl hɛri lugɔ Moosis. U ni Kɔraawiizi faa ra ŋɔ wiarɛ dɔŋa be, a ra chaani nɛnnɛ.

ref: and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation.
text: U faa ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi n humuu ŋɔ ú ga ɛɛ Ijip hɛri, di du Ijip koori ni u nabɔnzenaa ani a hɛri maa ni labuu Izrɛl hina sibɔɔ.

ref: No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
text: Nɛr maa haa waa fɔŋŋazeŋ baglɛɛ gɛɛ di ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia la n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, Moosis n faa ɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ la.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n wa siuwɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Nun biibaal Josua la n ɛɛ Moosis hiini la be,

ref: My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you.
text: “Josua, n balii Moosis siuwɔɔ. Awia, ɛɛ sirya filaŋkeŋ, di izi tɔ n nɛra Izrɛl hina see, ií gi Jɔɔdan muu di la hɛri la minna nyiŋŋi n tɛɛ baa la.

ref: Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses.
text: N daŋ tɛɛ i ni n nɛra bɔr la maa iin niŋ kpa ii naazi jag, gunla miŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Moosis la.

ref: It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west.
text: Ii hɛri magbɔɔ daŋ chi wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma la guŋŋ di ga chug Lɛbanɔn bizenaa la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag. Di kaa lii Muu Yufretis la n du wiifurii la, di ga Hitti hina hɛri di ra la Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la n du wiicholii la.

ref: Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
text: Nɛr maa wàá wer kpeglii maa, i de dui saŋa. Gunla miŋ faa du Moosis be la, gunnɛ ń du i ge gba be. Màá gilii ta gɛɛ di ɛɛ i wia vɛɛlai maa.

ref: Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
text: Ɛɛ ra karmi Gbɔg Hɔnnaa di ra tɛɛ a nɛra saŋa maa, di gilɛɛ waa gar. Ka ra helluu hɔpizaa ani hamuŋa maa, í wer di ra ɛɛ wia la maa baŋ sɛbɛɛ du u biini la. Denii í nyɛɛli, i wiɛɛlaa maa ge lii siwee nɛnnɛ.

ref: I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go. The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
text: Maa ŋɔ í chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpegaa? Gilɛɛ gil i bɔra waa sa di waa huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la daŋ du i be, bɔr la maa hin niŋ la.”

ref: Joshua ordered the tribal leaders
text: Denii Josua jaa ŋɔ a nɛra sitɔɔra be,

ref: to go through the camp and tell everyone: In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
text: “Ií gaagi a chɔɔribɔr maa di ŋɔ a nɛra maa be lugɔ bá ɛɛ sirya di nyiŋŋi diwee nɛnnɛ, hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, ba daŋ gi Jɔɔdan muu di ga foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n na tɛɛ baa la, di so.”

ref: Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
text: Denii Josua chaali Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ, di ŋɔ ba ge be,

ref: The Lord's servant Moses said that the Lord our God has given you land here on the east side of the Jordan River, where you could live in peace. Your wives and children and your animals can stay here in the land Moses gave you. But all of you that can serve in our army must pick up your weapons and lead the men of the other tribes across the Jordan River. They are your relatives, so you must help them
text: Ii haana ni ii biizi ani ii sela waa daŋ wer du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii bɔnnaa Moosis n tɛɛ ia naa, ka ii laallɔɔra la waa vɔɔ nɛnnɛ, di tɔ see gi a muu di ga hiini ii dɔŋahina Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la,

ref: conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
text: di ra la saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ wa tɛɛ baa a hɛri, Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii paga la bá so gunla uŋ tɛɛ ia la, bá ge wa wer foozi hɛri la Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n na tɛɛ baa la. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ tuŋ, ii daŋ jaa wer bir ba di wa so ii himmaa hɛri naa Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n tɛɛ ia, a Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii naa.”

ref: The men answered: We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us.
text: Denii ba sɛɛ tɛɛ Josua, di ŋɔ, “Wii la maa hin niŋ ŋɔ yá ɛɛ, yaa daŋ ɛɛu. Bɔr la maa ge hin niŋ hum yaa, yaa daŋ la.

ref: Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.” The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
text: Denii Josua suahzi hum baala banɛɛ di lii bolzeŋ Sitim, dí ba la ga daani Keenan hɛri, fɔŋfɔŋ bolzeŋ Jɛriko, di na gunla un duwɛɛ. Awia, ba kpa la ga zuu hahsɛnsɛnni bɛl banna yir Rahab dia, di du de.

ref: But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.”
text: Nɛbɛl ga ŋɔ bolzeŋ Jɛriko koori be, “Na! Izrɛl hina baŋhina ba ɛnnɛ hamuŋa naa, bá wa daani a hɛri naa di na.”

ref: Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
text: Mɔɔ ka a baala chɔɔ a hamuŋa ni, Rahab tinni ba be sal,

ref: I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you.
text: di ŋɔ ba be, “N zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpa hɛri naabuu tɛɛ ia, guŋ wia, ɔnsii lau nɛraa werge maa hɛri naa biini, dikuu ii wia.

ref: We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
text: Yaa nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ Muuzeŋaahmu la hiihzi dikuu ii wia labuu, saŋa la iiŋ waa lii Ijip hɛri la. Di kaa nuu gunla iiŋ kpuuzi Sihɔn ni Ɔɔg la n ɛɛ Amɔri hina koora banɛɛ la n faa du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii labuu.

ref: We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
text: Yaa n wa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii lau yaa werge, nɛr maa bɔra huah dikuu ii wia. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa di koraa chiŋ ani hɛri.

ref: Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show
text: Awia, ii gaafura ka hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi alugɔ ii daŋ suŋ n ni n nɛra maa ni, dikuu kennaa miŋ suŋ ii ni naa wia. Ií ɛɛ wii bɛl di bagliŋ, ń yardi ia

ref: that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
text: lugɔ ii wàá kpuuzi n mɛɛ ni n maa, n niuna, n kpɛɛnna ani ba lulla maa.”

ref: “Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
text: A baala ŋɔ u be, “Kɔ́raawiizi kpuuzi yaa, di yaa waa haŋ wa ɛɛ kennaa yaa n niŋ ŋɔ naa! Di haa yaa wolo wa pillɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi wa hiini yaa, yaa foozi a hɛri, yaa daŋ suŋ i ni di lɛɛi.”

ref: Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall.
text: Denii u jaa kpa ŋmɛŋ di ga tokoro ha, bá ga u ni di tuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u dia la faa choŋŋi a bol koŋliizeŋ ninɛɛ.

ref: Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
text: U faa ŋɔ ba benii, “Ií la giŋgimee bɔr la ga suah de hɔpizaa ahoro, di a nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ia la wa bittɔ ba, ií jaa lii di ra la.”

ref: “I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
text: U ŋɔ, “N sɛɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ labuu.” Ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kaali. Ka u jaa kpa a ŋmɛŋaahmu la di vɔɔ a tokoro.

ref: The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho,
text: A baala la n ga daani a hɛri la, la ga suah a giŋgimee bɔr. A koori nɛra la sɛu di nyiŋŋi baa guŋŋ hɔpizaa ahoro di wa huhzi, ka bir ba bol.

ref: the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened.
text: Denii a baala banɛɛ hiŋ jaa lii a giŋgimee bɔr di wa gi Jɔɔdan muu la, di la ga bagli wia la maa n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Josua.

ref: “We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
text: Ba ŋɔ Josua be, “Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ yaabuu a hɛri maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ɔnsii teŋ lau de nɛra maanii yaa wia.”

ref: Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Josua ni Izrɛl hina maa izi lii bolzeŋ Sitim, bɔr la baŋ chɔɔwɛ la, di la Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia, di ga chɔɔ de mɔɔ, ka haa gi.

ref: Two days later their leaders went through the camp,
text: Hɔpizaa ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra la izi di gaagi ba chɔɔribɔr la biini,

ref: shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
text: Denii ii zum ŋmɛnɛɛ la iin niŋ ga, dikuu ii ŋmɛnɛ maa n haa waa ɛŋ gawɛɛ la wia. Ka ii tɛɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la bɔr lugɔ nogumzi kagboŋaanɛɛ, di gilɛɛ waa dugluu.”

ref: Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
text: Josua jaa ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Bɛl maa sɔ u hiŋ di lizi u doŋa ha ka ɛɛ nɛnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u daŋ kɛrɛ ɛɛ nuukpuuri wia ii biini.”

ref: Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
text: Josua jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la be, “Ií kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di tɔ a nɛra see di ra vol.” Ba jaa kpau di tɔ ba see.

ref: The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Zinaa, n daŋ faari di gil i dɔɔ girme ni zenni Izrɛl hina maa sibɔɔ. Bá zum lugɔ gunla miŋ faa du Moosis be la, gunnɛ n du i gba be.

ref: Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
text: Ŋɔ n kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la be lugɔ di ba wa hel Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii, bá zuu nii la biini tama ka chi.”

ref: Joshua spoke to the people: Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do!
text: Josua ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be, “Ií ba di wa nuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la wiŋɔzi.

ref: The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out.
text: Kenne ií chi zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la du ii benii. Wibii maa, u daŋ duŋŋi Keenan, Hitti, Hivi, Pɛriz, Girgas, Amɔri ani Jɛbus hina ii sibɔɔ,

ref: Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river. The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi la, n ɛɛ durnya maa Dɔɔri, Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la haŋ wa zuu Jɔɔdan muu nii, u palaa daŋ teŋ, chiŋ nii la izi chi bɔkpaŋ alugɔ koŋlii.”

ref: until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water,
text: Di kuna kumaa saŋaa, Jɔɔdan muu la jaa su yaari u kɛraa maa, ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, n haŋ wa kpa ba naazi jag a nii biini,

ref: the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la faa chigɔ a Jɔɔdan muu baambaaŋ bɔhiliirɛ guŋŋ, ka Izrɛl hina maa jaa wa gi.

ref: After Israel had crossed the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
text: A Izrɛl hina maa n jaa wa gi Jɔɔdan muu la tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be,

ref: Tell one man from each of the twelve tribes to pick up a large rock from where the priests are standing. Then tell the men to set up those rocks as a monument at the place where you camp tonight.
text: Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ bɛl maa kpa bii lii Jɔɔdan muu la baambaaŋ, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n chigɛ la, di ga dau bɔr la iin niŋ ga chɔɔ hamuŋa naa.”

ref: Joshua chose twelve men; then he called them together
text: Denii Josua jaa yir nɛra fidibanɛɛ la uŋ lizɛɛ lii Izrɛl hina dee maa biini la,

ref: and said: Go to the middle of the riverbed where the sacred chest is, and pick up a large rock. Carry it on your shoulder to our camp. There are twelve of you, so there will be one rock for each tribe.
text: di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií tɔ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di ga zuu Jɔɔdan muu baambaaŋ, ií bɛl maa kpa bikpaŋ di sag u baŋaa, a bii bɛl maa chi tɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi la.

ref: Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
text: Ii daŋ ŋɔ ba be lugɔ a bia naa gillɔɔ yaa ra liizi saŋa maa lugɔ Jɔɔdan muu la faa teŋŋoo, baŋ faa chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di waa giu la.”

ref: The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
text: Awia, a nɛra ɛɛ gunla Josua n ŋɔ ba be la, di paagi bia fidaanɛɛ di lii Jɔɔdan muu baaŋ. Bɛl maa chi di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi la, gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Josua la, ba jaa chia di la bɔr la baŋ ga chɔɔwɛ la.

ref: Joshua set up a monument next to the place where the priests were standing. This monument was also made of twelve large rocks, and it is still there in the middle of the river. The People of Israel Set Up Camp at Gilgal
text: Josua gil ba kaa paagi bia fidaanɛɛ di ma bɔr chiŋŋi Jɔɔdan muu baambaaŋ, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi kizeehina n faa chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di chi la. A haa chigɔ de haali ni zinaa.

ref: It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho.
text: Biŋfalii lugli baagu, u hɔpizaa fi hɔllɛ a nɛra lii Jɔɔdan muu, di wa chɔɔ bol bɛl banna yir Gilgal n du bolzeŋ Jɛriko wiifurii magbɔɔ.

ref: The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument.
text: Denii Josua jaa kpa bia fidaanɛɛ la baŋ paawɛ lii Jɔɔdan muu biini la di baŋzi de.

ref: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
text: Denii Josua ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “Kɛrɛ bɛl, ii biizi daŋ pɛɛzi ba mɛɛwaa, ‘Bia naa ɛŋ chigaa zɛɛrɛ ɛrɛɛ?’

ref: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
text: Ií kaa ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu faa gillɛ a Jɔɔdan muu chah, ka ii faa wer na bɔhilii di gi, gunla uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ Muuzeŋaahmu chah, yaa faa gi la.

ref: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
text: U ɛɛ gunnɛ, durnya nɛra maa na gunla u fɔŋŋa n kannɛ mag, guŋ gil ii ɔɔ ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la saŋa maa.”

ref: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
text: Denii Amɔri hina koora la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiicholii ni Keenan hina koora la maa n du a muuzeŋ kɛraa la, n wa nuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ Jɔɔdan muu chah, ka Izrɛl hina giu la, ɔnsii lau baa werge maa, ba waa kaa dɔɔ bɔkpega ba ni Izrɛl hina chem.

ref: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Kpa bia di kuari kizizi, di kpaa teŋri Izrɛl hina la hɛna n haa waa teŋree la.”

ref: Joshua made the knives, then circumcised those men and boys at Haaraloth Hill.
text: Denii Josua jaa kuari kizizi di teŋri Izrɛl hina hɛna, bɔr la banna yir Gibia Haaralɔf la.

ref: This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the
text: Denii Josua jaa teŋri ba biizi la baŋ lullɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ ba hel lugɔ ba chi ba mɛɛwaa naazi la hɛna, dikuu baŋ faa waa ba hɛna teŋree wia.

ref: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
text: A baala maa hɛna n wa teŋree tuŋ, ba jaa so de guŋŋ di ga hel saŋa la baŋ wa nyaagɛɛ.

ref: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Zinaa, n lizi yom hiihzi la iiŋ faa ra di Ijip labuu ha.” Awiarɛ ba haa ra yir a bɔr Gilgal, haali ni zinaa la.

ref: Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
text: Izrɛl hina n wa chɔɔ Gilgal di dugli bolzeŋ Jɛriko lɛl la, a baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl duana ni, ba di ba Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la.

ref: The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields. Israel Captures Jericho
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, paanuu la n ɔɔ faa lii chiŋ di ra chol ba ra yiruu maana la, waa kaa chol maa. Izrɛl hina la jaa faari di ra di Keenan hɛri pattikuna la.

ref: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
