text: Josua n waa dugli bolzeŋ Jɛriko, u na baal bɛl n chigɛ u see di kpogli tokobi. Denii Josua tuzi heluu di pɛɛzuu, “I ɛɛ yaa bɛllɛ gɛɛ yaa dɔmɛi?”

ref: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
text: A baal ŋɔ u be, “Maa bɛl maa ɛɛwɛ, n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi laallɔɔra nabɔmaa. N jaa bau.” Kakpaŋ, Josua chol pi, di ra tɔgzuu, ka pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ amaniyee n Dɔɔri dɔɔ ú tɛɛ u baliiwɛi?”

ref: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi laallɔɔra nabɔma hiŋ bir ŋɔ u be, “Lizi i gawa la, bɔnnaa hiŋ chigɛ naa ɛɛ bɔnaniinaniirɛ.” Josua ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
text: Bolzeŋ Jɛriko hina la tɔɔgi ba bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa maa, dikuu Izrɛl hina la wia. Nɛr maa wàá ka wer zuu gɛɛ di na bɔr lii.

ref: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
text: Gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehina baniidaanɛɛ kpa pebala nyigzi di tɔ N Ni N Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl la, i ni i laallɔɔra kaa vol bar a bolzeŋ buniidaanɛɛ, ka a kizeehina ra huuh a nyigzi.

ref: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
text: Di i wa nuuwɔ baŋ huuh a nyigzi, di tɛraa werge, gil a nɛra maa chaasi werge maa, a bolzeŋ koŋlii daŋ chol, Izrɛl hina laallɔɔra maa jaa wer zuu de.”

ref: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
text: Awia, Nun biibaal Josua yir Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maa di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di chi, ka lizi ii biini nɛra baniidaanɛɛ, bɛl maa kpa pebal nyigaa di tɔ u see.”

ref: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
text: Awia, u jaa gil ba chi a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, di bar a bolzeŋ kakpaŋ a hɔl hiŋ, ka bir ba ba chɔɔribɔr hamuŋa ni di wa chɔɔ.

ref: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl chɔɔzimpikke ni, Izrɛl hina izi di vol di bar a bol maa gunla baŋ ɔɔ faa ɛɛ la. Ka a hɔl naa waa, ba volloo bar a bolzeŋ buniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
text: Buniidaanɛɛ hiŋ la, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la jaa huuh nyigzi la werge maa. Denii Josua ge jaa ŋɔ a nɛra maa be ani fɔŋŋa ni, “Ií chaasi werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kpa a bolzenne tɛɛ ia!

ref: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
text: Ií chɔgi a bolzeŋ ani u kuna maa, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ií gil sɛnsɛnni Rahab ani u diahina waa, dikuu uŋ lɛɛ yaa nɛra la yaa n hummɛ bá ga daani a bol mɔɔ la wia.

ref: The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
text: Kunla maa baŋ kpa saliŋ gɛɛ lugbii gɛɛ danyɛ gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu di kuari, ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora. Ií chi aawaa maa di ba Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna dauribɔr.”

ref: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
text: A nɛra n wa nuu a nyigzi wiraa, ba chaasi werge maa, kakpaŋ, bolzeŋ Jɛriko koŋlii maa chol, Izrɛl hina hahzi zuu a bolzeŋ, di kpegli a bol hina.

ref: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Josua karfi Izrɛl hina, di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi nuuseei di nɛr la maa n na nyiŋŋi gɛɛ di ra fɛ lugɔ ú kaa bir ma bolzeŋ Jɛriko naa. A hiŋ biibambinabɔmaa ú kpa di chiŋŋi u zɛɛ. Di kpa ú biibambijiga hiŋ ge di du u dominuuzenaa.”

ref: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa du Josua benii, u sɔŋ yaari a hɛri maa.

ref: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
text: Izrɛl hina wia faa waa wibii dɔɔwɛ, ni kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora wia. Baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Akan, u mɛɛ ɛɛ Kaami, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Zimri di lii Zɛra domee n lii Juda dee biini, faa ŋmɛɛ a laal biini kuna aŋhina. A guŋ faa gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh Izrɛl hina ni.

ref: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
text: Josua ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi piili ba tagtazi ni biinichɔg werge, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa di ra waari ba nyuuni, ka jaa chɔɔ pi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, guŋŋ bɔr wa duani.

ref: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
text: Denii Josua lɔ wile di ŋɔ, “Hoi, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la! Bɛɛ n baani i kpogli yaa di wa gi Jɔɔdan muu naa, di kpa yaa tɛɛ Amɔri hina ba kpuuzɛi? Di yaa faa zummɔ di du keŋkere la hiŋ gba bɔ!

ref: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
text: Kɔraawiizi, ɛrɛɛ ń jaa ŋɔ filaŋkennaa, dikuu Izrɛl hina n chol ba dɔma nonee biini wiai?

ref: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
text: Di Keenan hina ani banla maa n du a hɛri naa haŋ wa nuu guŋ, ba daŋ wa bar yaa, di kpuuzi yaa, yàá sɔŋ dim hɛri naa biini. Ɛrɛɛ nɛra ja ɛɛ di zum i sɔnzeŋ wiai?”

ref: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Izi chiŋ! Ɛrɛɛ i chɔɔ pi gunnɛi?

ref: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
text: Izrɛl hina ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di chɔg n ni baa nuukpaŋ la miŋ ŋɔ ba ra hiŋ labuu! Ba ŋmɛɛ kuna la n dɛg chɔgaa labuu, di kanni kara ka kpaa di suahzi ba kuna biine.

ref: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
text: Awiarɛ Izrɛl hina dɔma wer kpegli baa la. Ba bir hattɛ di ra chɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba birgi kuna la ban niŋ chɔgi labuu. Awia, màá ka du ii be, di ii waa haŋ chɔgi kuna la maa n du ii be, di dɛg chɔgaa la lɛi.

ref: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
text: Izi chiŋ di ŋɔ a nɛra be lugɔ ba sɔ bahinaa, di lizi doŋa ha ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ka ɛɛ sirya di ra kpaŋ kɛrɛ. Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl hina! Kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora ka ii kpaa suah naa, di ii wàá lizɛɛ chaaŋ, ii wàá wer kpegli ii dɔma naa maa.

ref: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
text: Chɔɔzi ni, dee maa lii chi u bɛŋ. N daŋ lizi dee la biini a wichɔgɛɛri n duwɛɛ, a dee domeezi lii chi ba bɛnaa, n kaa lizi domee la biini un duwɛɛ, a domee ge diahina ge lii chi ba bɛnaa, n kaa lizi dia la hina biini un duwɛɛ. A tuna maa ge, a diahina jaa lii di chi kpaŋkpaŋa.

ref: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
text: Di n wa lizi unla n ŋmɛɛ a kuna di suah la, ií fuuh u ni u diahina ani u kuna maa, dikuu uŋ chɔgi Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la wia, guŋ gil Izrɛl hina di hiihzi werge la wia.’ ”

ref: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Josua gil Izrɛl hina dizi la lii wa chi chi. Denii ba lizi Juda dee la.

ref: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
text: Awia, Juda dee domeezi la lii di chi, Kɔraawiizi lizi Zɛra domee. Zɛra domee ge kaa lii chi diini diini, denii u jaa lizi Zimri diahina.

ref: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
text: Josua jaa gil Zimri dia baala lii di chi kpaŋkpaŋa, Kɔraawiizi kaa lizi Akan la n ɛɛ Kaami bie, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Zɛra di lii Juda dee biini la.

ref: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
text: Denii Josua ŋɔ Akan be, “N biibaal, kpa chɔlaa ni girme tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, ka ŋɔ wibii tɛŋ, di bagli wii la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ, gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa di ra suah n ni.”

ref: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
text: Akan sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “A ɛɛ wibiire! N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni. Kenne n ɛɛ,

ref: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
text: Ba wigzaa lii tanti dia la biini di ba Josua ni Izrɛl hina maa be, di wa kpaa dau Kɔraawiizi see.

ref: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
text: Denii Josua ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa kpogli Zɛra biibaal Akan, a saliŋhuŋŋa, a tagtazeŋ, a saliŋ, u biibaala ni u biihaana, u nauna, u kauzi, u peeza, u tanti dia ani kuna la maa un dɔɔwɛ, di la bɔr la banna yir Akɔ Waluu la.

ref: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
text: Josua jaa ŋɔ Akan be, “Ɛrɛɛ i kpa tɔɔrɔɔ du yaa kennei? Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɔɔri i ge filaŋkeŋ.” Denii Izrɛl hina maa paagi bia lɔɔzi Akan ni u diahina maa kpuuzi, di fuuh ba ni ba kuna maa de.

ref: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
text: Ka ba jaa paa bizenaa di wa tɔ Akan ni kulululu. A haa du de di wa lii ni zinaa. Kɔraawiizi baaŋ jaa sɔɔni. Guŋ wiarɛ ba ra yir de Akɔ Waluu di wa lii zinaa la.

ref: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
text: Yaa daŋ murgi baa di ra chɔ, bá ra duŋŋi yaa guŋŋ ba maa wa lii a bolzeŋ biini. Denii ba jaa ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl hina la kaa ra chɔu di ra kaali, gunla baŋ faa felee ɛɛ la.’ Di yaa wa chɔwɔɔ di ra lii ba be,

ref: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
text: ií jaa lii ii saga sognibɔra la, di lɔ a bolzeŋ di kpegli baa. Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ kpau du ii nonee biini.

ref: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
text: Di ii wa kpegli baa, ií fuuh a bolzeŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Gunla miŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ iabuu guŋ.”

ref: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Josua izi di chaali u laallɔɔra la maa, u ni Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra jaa ba ni di ra la Ai.

ref: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
text: U ni a laallɔɔra maa faa vol di ra la bolzeŋ Ai dominuuzeŋ, di ga chɔɔ u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag barii, waluu faa chɔɔ ba ni a bolzeŋ baambaaŋ.

ref: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
text: Ba gil laallɔɔra la maa chi ba chignibɔra, ba chɔɔribɔr du a bolzeŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, ka banla ge n soge saga la du u wiicholii. Ka Josua la ga chɔɔ a waluu biini a hamuŋa ni.

ref: So he called out every man in Ai to go after Joshua's troops. They all rushed out to chase the Israelite army, and they left the town gates wide open. Not one man was left in Ai or in Bethel. Joshua let the men of Ai chase him and his army farther and farther away from Ai.
text: Ai ni Bɛtɛl hina baala maanii faa liwɛɛ di ra duŋŋi Izrɛl hina ka ka a bolzeŋ, u pilli chɔɔ pɛɛ, nɛr maa waa kaa hoo ú ra du u tau.

ref: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Kpa i kandaa tɛr deŋli bolzeŋ Ai, n daŋ kpau du i nonee biini.” Josua ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
text: Josua n haŋ wa kpa u kandaa di tɛr a bol, banla n soge saga la maa izi lii kakpaŋ, di zuu de di kpegluu, di fuuh u maa.

ref: When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked. The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting.
text: Josua ni Izrɛl baala n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ banla n soge saga la fuuh a bolle, nyɔɔzi ra lii la, ba jaa bir chem Ai baala la ni, di ra kpuuzi baa.

text: Izrɛl hina la n wa kpuuzi Ai hina la maa n du baŋgia ni a hɛribɔduma la tuŋ, ba bir zuu a bolzeŋ, di keezi kpuuzi ba banla n kawɛɛ la maa, nyaamm.

text: Josua faa lau bolzeŋ Ai koori labuu di saguu ŋmɛŋ, u zeeli guŋŋ wiizi wa chol. U gil ba lizuu a ŋmɛŋ ni, di kpau ha a bol dominuuzeŋ, di paagi bia tɔ u ni kulululu. Haali ni zinaa, a bɔr haa chɔɔ de. Baŋ karmi Gbɔgni Hɔŋ Bizeŋ Ɛbal nyuu wia

text: Di haŋ lii a hɔl hiŋ, Josua jaa gil Gibiɔn hina ɛɛ Izrɛl hina ni Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr, daateŋra ni niidɔɔra, bɔr la maa Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lizi ŋɔ bá mau. Gunnɛ a haa du ba ni di wa lii ni zinaa.

text: Awia, wiizi jaa chi diindiindiiŋ, baagu ge faa chi diindiiŋ, guŋŋ Izrɛl hina la wa kpegli ba dɔma la tuŋ. Ba faa sɛbi a wia naabuu du Jasaa Hɔŋ biini. Wiizi jaa chi chiŋ baambaaŋ guŋŋ, waa cholle a hɔl waa maa.

ref: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset

text: Baŋ kaa wa lii Ɛglɔn, ba la ga pig bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn ge,

text: di kaa kpegli baa, di kpuuzi ba ni ba koori ani boljigzi la ge maa n baruu la nɛra di jaa. Haali nɛkpaŋ maa faa waa kawɛɛ a bolzeŋ naa biini gunla baŋ faa ɛɛ Ɛglɔn hina la.

ref: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
text: Denii ba kaa bir ba di wa pig bolzeŋ Dɛbir hina ge,

text: di kaa chɔgi u ge ni u koori ani nɛra la maa n faa du boljigzi la n dugluu la, haali nɛr maa faa waa kawɛɛ. Ba faa chɔguubuu gunla baŋ faa chɔgi Libna hina ni ba koori ani Hɛbrɔn hina maa la.

ref: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
text: Josua faa kpegli a hɛri hina maa. U faa kpegli ba koora maa n du giŋgimee bola ni Nɛgɛv n ɛɛ hɛribɔduma la ni wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi hina ani bizenaa bɔwillaa la maa nɛra. Haali nɛr maa faa waa kawɛɛ, gunla Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.

ref: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,

ref: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
