ref: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
text: di kaa tili ŋɔ Keenan hina la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii ni wiicholii koora, Amɔri, Hitti, Pɛriz ani Jɛbus hina la n du giŋgimee hɛri la, Hivi hina la n du Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn zɛɛ, Mizpa hɛri la, lugɔ bá wa hiini baa.

ref: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa. Kɛrɛ saŋa naa dɔŋ, n daŋ kpu ba maa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina. Ií chaahzi ba zagra zaŋŋuzi, di fuuh ba torkozi maa.”

ref: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
text: Awia, Josua ni u laallɔɔra izi di la pol Mɛrɔm la ga pig baa, di lɔ baa.

ref: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
text: Denii Josua bir di ga lɔ Hazɔr hina di kpegli baa, di kpu ba koori ge. Hazɔr naabuu faa ɛɛ a kossi naa maa nyuu hiŋ.

ref: Joshua captured all the towns where the enemy kings had ruled. These towns were built on small hills, and Joshua did not set fire to any of these towns, except Hazor. The Israelites kept the animals and everything of value from these towns, but they killed everyone who lived in them, including their kings. That's what the Lord had told his servant Moses to do, that's what Moses had told Joshua to do, and that's exactly what Joshua did.
text: Gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ la, gunnɛ Moosis ge faa ŋɔ Josua ge hiŋ u nua di ɛɛ. Josua jaa hiŋ u nua nɛnnɛ, di ɛɛ wia la maa dee Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
text: Josua faa wettoo kpegli a hɛri maa, giŋgimee bɔr hɛri, Nɛgɛv, Gɔsɛn hɛri maa, wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi, Jɔɔdan Waluu ani wiifurii nomɛɛl ni nodig wiikakagni, a bizenaa ni a zɛɛzi giŋgimee bɔr la maa,

ref: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
text: Kɔraawiizi himmaanii faa gillɛ ba dɔɔ dignikpega, bá ni Izrɛl hina yoo laal, ka ú wer chɔgi baa, di dim baa nyaamm, waa ba ni sunne. Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis ɛɛ.

ref: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
text: A saŋa naa biinii Josua faa chɔgi Anak dee la n ɔɔ hel kpabaa, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la waa maa, baabuu faa du bolzenaa Hɛbrɔn, Dɛbir, Anab ani Juda ni Izrɛl giŋgimee hɛssi la maa. U faa kpuuzi ba maa nyaamm, di purgi ba bola maa.

ref: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
text: Ba nɛkpaŋ maa faa waa kawɛɛ Izrɛl hɛri, ka baŋhina waa faa ka bolzenaa Gaza, Gaf ani Asdɔd.

ref: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
text: Josua jaa dɔɔ a hɛri maa gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ Moosis be lugɔ ú ɛɛ la. U kpau tɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi la, dee maa dɔɔ u bɔr, u birgi ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ, laal ge wia maa tuŋ, a hɛri jaa sɔɔni.

ref: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
text: Koora naabuu Izrɛl hina faa kpuuzi di lii Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii paga, di faa lɛɛ ba hɛssi ge di jaa. Ba hɛssi faa lii Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ di ga chug Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn, di kpa hɛssi la maa n du Jɔɔdan Waluu wiifurii paga la maa. Koora banɛɛrɛ ba faa kpegli.

ref: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
text: Bɛllɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n faa du bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔn. U faa ra di koraa bolzeŋ Aroa la n du Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ kɛrii, di lii de guŋŋ di ga hel u baambaaŋ, di kaa ga hel Muu Jabɔk n faa ɛɛ ba ni Ammɔn hina magbɔɔ. Giliad hina hɛri yeŋ faa jaa denii.

ref: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
text: Di kaa chi Jɔɔdan Waluu la n lii Galilii muuzeŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag paga guŋŋ di ga hel Bɛf Jɛsimɔf n du Muuzensiwii wiifurii paga la, di kaa ga hel Bizeŋ Pisga zɛɛ. De maanii Koori Sihɔn faa dɔɔ di ra binni.

ref: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
text: Ba faa kaa kpegli Basan Koori Ɔɔg hɛri maanii. Waabuu faa ɛɛ Rɛfa hina n helle kpabaa la tuna hiŋ. U faa ra di kooraa bolzenaa Astarɔf ani Ɛdrɛi ni.

ref: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
text: U faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa di ra binni Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn ni yembɛl banna yir Salɛka ani Basan hɛri maa guŋŋ di ga chug Gɛsur ni Maaka hɛssi magazi, di kpa Giliad yeŋ jaa, di lii de guŋŋ di ga chug Hɛsbɔn Koori Sihɔn hɛri.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
text: Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis ani Izrɛl hina faa kpu Koora Sihɔn, Ɔɔg ani ba nɛra maanii. Ka Moosis faa kpa ba hɛssi tɛɛ Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ, a birgi ba kundɔɔlaa.

ref: Jericho, Ai near Bethel, Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon, Gezer, Debir, Geder, Hormah, Arad, Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, Bethel, Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, Lasharon, Madon, Hazor, Shimron-Meron, Achshaph, Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Jokneam on Mount Carmel, Dor in Naphath-Dor, Goiim in Galilee, and Tirzah. There were
text: ani Tirza koori. A koora naa maa faa du tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kpaŋ. Ba ni ba bolzenaa maanii ba faa chɔgi.

ref: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
text: Josua n wa zɛŋŋɛ werge, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “I jaa zɛŋuu werge, ka hɛrkpila maa haa kawɔɔrɛ lugɔ hin niŋ lɔ a nɛra ka foozi.

ref: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
text: Manasɛ dee yeŋ ni Rubin ani Gad dizi faa di ba kapɛttɛɛ Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la, u ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ. Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis faa bɔnnaa di tɛɛ baa.

ref: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
text: Ba bɔr maga faa lii Aroa n du Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ kɛrii, di kaa kpa bol la n du u baambaaŋ la guŋŋ di ga hel Mɛdɛba lɛl, haali di ga hel bolzeŋ Dibɔn.

ref: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
text: Di kaa kpa bolzenaa la maa n ɛɛ Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n du Hɛsbɔn di ra di kora guŋŋ di ga hel Ammɔn hina magbɔɔ la.

ref: Geshur and Maacah were part of this region, and so was the whole territory that King Og had ruled, that is, Gilead, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far east as Salecah. Og had lived in Ashtaroth part of each year, and he had lived in Edrei the rest of the year. Og had been one of the last of the Rephaim, but Moses had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land.
text: A maa faa ɛɛ Basan Koori Ɔɔg kora diiribɔraa. U faa ra di koraa Astarɔf ani Ɛdrɛi ni. Waabuu faa ɛɛ Rɛfa hina la n helle kpabaa la tuna hiŋ. Moosis faa kpegli nɛra naabuu di duŋŋi baa lii ba sognibɔra.

ref: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
text: Ka a Izrɛl hina faa waa Gɛsur ani Maaka hina la waa duŋŋɛɛ, ba sogo ba benii haali ni zinaa.

ref: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
text: Moosis faa waa Levi dee la waa tɛɛwɛ yemmaa lugɔ ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ baa lugɔ ba kapɛttɛ daŋ ɔɔ lii mbusu lizaa kuna la baŋ ɔɔ fuuh ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, Izrɛl hina n na ba a ni la biinii.

ref: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
text: Bɔra la Moosis n kpawɛɛ di tɛɛ Rubin dee domeezii keŋ,

ref: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
text: Ba bɔr magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ di lii Aroa la n du Aanɔn Gɔmbɔɔluŋ kɛrii la, di kpa bolzeŋ la n du a faalim baambaaŋ ni de lɛl maa di ga bɛri bolzeŋ Mɛdɛba,

ref: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
text: ni bola la maa n du a giŋgimiiwar nyuu, ani Amɔri hina Koori Sihɔn la n di kora Hɛsbɔn hɛri la. Moosis faa kpegli u ni Midian hina koora naa n faa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la maanii. Baabuu, Ɛvi, Rɛkɛm, Zur, Hur ani Rɛba. Kooribiizi la n faa soge a hɛri biinii la.

ref: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
text: Izrɛl hina faa kpu baal bɛl banna yir Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam la n faa ra vug la gbaa.

ref: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
text: Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii kɛrii labuu ɛɛ Rubin dee bɔr magbɔɔ. Bolzenaa ni a boljigzi naabuu faa ɛɛ Rubin dee domeezi maa kapɛttɛzi.

ref: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
text: Bɔra naabuu Moosis faa kpa tɛɛ Gad dee domeezi,

ref: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
text: di kaa lii bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔn di ga hel bolzenaa Ramaf Mizpa ani Bɛtɔnim, di kaa lii bolzeŋ Mahanam di ga hel yembɛl banna yir Dɛbir.

ref: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
text: Aŋhinaa bolzenaa la n du Jɔɔdan Waluu, Bɛf Haram, Bɛf Nimra, Sukɔf ani Zafɔn, di kaa Koori Sihɔn kora diiribɔr la n du Hɛsbɔn la. Ba wiicholii magbɔɔrɛ faa Jɔɔdan muu guŋŋ di ga hel Galilii muuzeŋ n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag.

ref: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
text: A bolzenaa naa ni a boljigzi maanii faa ɛɛ Gad dee domeezi maa kapɛttɛ kuna.

ref: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
text: Bɔra naabuu Moosis faa kpa di tɛɛ Manasɛ dee yeŋ domeezi,

ref: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
text: Di kaa kpa Giliad yeŋ ani Astarɔf ni Ɛdrɛi la n ɛɛ Basan Koori Ɔɔg bolzenaa la. A bɔra naa maanii ba faa kpa di tɛɛ Manasɛ biibaal Makir domeezi yeŋ.

ref: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
text: Kenne Moosis faa bɔnni a hɛri la n du Jɛriko ani Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii, di u faa haa du Moab lɛl biini.

ref: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
text: Moosis faa waa yemmaa mɔnnɛ tɛɛ Levi dee la waa, ú birgi ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ nuarɛ tɛɛ baa lugɔ waabuu ninna tɛɛ baa kunla maa banna nyiŋŋi.

ref: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Kɛniz hinuu Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb ni Juda dee nɛra baŋhina la Josua be Gilgal. Kalɛb ga ŋɔ Josua be, “I zum gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Moosis, di lii n nii wia biini saŋa la yaa n faa du Kadɛs Bania la.

ref: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
text: Ama, n ni banla n faa laŋŋɛ la waa, wa du yaa nɛraa ɔnsii ani bɔhuaih. Miŋwaa faa hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ lugɔ n hiŋ.

ref: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Moosis hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua, di ŋɔ, ‘Hɛri la hiŋ volle la daŋ birgi i ni i biizi kapɛttɛ di hanna la, dikuu hiŋ wette hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum nɛnnɛ ni biinihuŋŋu wia.’

ref: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
text: N haa kpekkoo gunla miŋ faa kpekke, saŋa la Moosis n humiŋ a ŋmɛnijaŋ la. N daŋ haa wer vol guŋ, di haa wer la ga yoo laal gba haali ni zinaa.

ref: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
text: Awia, n na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ í kpa a giŋgimee nyuuni hɛri di tɛŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua di tɛŋ a hɔl hiŋ la. I himmaa faa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ Anak hina la n faa helle kpabaa faa du de, di ma koŋlaa di bar ba bolzenaa, a du kpeg werge la. Ka di Kɔraawiizi chigɔ n har, n daŋ duŋŋi ba maa lii a hɛri, gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”

ref: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
text: Denii Josua kissi Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb, ka kpa bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn hɛri tɛu ú ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ.

ref: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
text: Bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn sɔnnɛ faa Kiriaf Aaba. Anak hina nɛkpeg bɛl banna yir Aaba sɔnnɛ ba faa kpa dawuu. Bampirsɔna jaa du a hɛri.

ref: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
text: U wiifurii nodig wiikakag naa magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Muuzensiwii wiifurii nodig wiikakag tuna,

ref: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
text: di ga de guŋŋ di ga gilli bɔr la banna yir Nuuma Ŋmɛnɛɛ wiifurii nodig wiikakag la, di lii de ga chug Zin Hɛribɔduma, di gilli di ga hel Kadɛs Bania wiifurii nodig wiikakag. Denii u kaa lii de di ga bɛri Hɛzrɔn di ga chug Adar. Di bir kpau guŋŋ bar di ga chug bolzeŋ Kaka.

ref: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
text: U ga de guŋŋ di ga bɛri di ga chug bolzeŋ Azmɔn, di ga choŋŋi Ijip gɔŋ, di ga tuŋ muuzeŋ. Juda hɛri wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.

ref: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
text: U wiifurii magbɔɔrɛ Muuzensiwii di ga hel Jɔɔdan muu nua. U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ ge faari a muuzeŋ bɔr la Jɔɔdan muu n ɔɔ waa zuu la,

ref: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
text: di tinni ga hel yembɛl banna yir Bɛf Hɔgla, di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ra la Bɛf Araba wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di ga hel Bohan Bii la baŋ faa kpa Rubin biibaal Bɔhan sɔŋ di dawuu la.

ref: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
text: Di kaa chi de magbɔɔ di kaa kpau ga Akɔ Waluu di tinni ga hel Dɛbir, di kaa kpau di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag paga guŋŋ di ga hel Gilgal n chaŋ Adumim Ŋmɛnɛɛ n du gɔŋluŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag. Di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ga hel niiri aŋhina banna yir Ɛn Sɛmɛs, di lii de ga hel Ɛn Rɔgɛl.

ref: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
text: U magbɔɔ kaa ga Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu, di hiihni Jɛbus hina bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm wiifurii nodig wiikakag bɔwillii, di lii de tinni giŋgimii la n du Hinɔm Waluu wiicholii, u du Rɛfam Waluu wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag tuna la.

ref: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
text: A magbɔɔ kaa lii a bii nyuu di ga hel Nɛftɔa bulli la. Di lii de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel bola la n du Bizeŋ Ɛfrɔn nyuu la. Di kaa bir tuu di ra la bolzeŋ Baala.

ref: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
text: Denii u magbɔɔ hiŋ mɔŋ di ga wiicholii di lii a bolzeŋ Baala ga hel Bizeŋ Sɛɛ, di ga de hiihni Bizeŋ Jiarim wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii la, di tuu ra la bolzeŋ Bɛf Sɛmɛs, di gilli ga chug bolzeŋ Timna.

ref: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
text: A bɔr magbɔɔ kaa chi de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛkrɔn wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di bir chaŋ bolzeŋ Sikɛrɔn di ga hel Bizeŋ Baala, di kaa kpau guŋŋ di ga chug bolzeŋ Jabniil. Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn nuarɛ u magbɔɔ ga tuŋ.

ref: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
text: Denii u kaa lii de di ga lɔ bolzeŋ la banna yir Dɛbir, de sɔnnɛ faa Kiriaf Sɛfa.

ref: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
text: Di lii gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ Josua be la wia, u faa mɔŋ Juda dee hɛri la yeŋ tɛɛ Jɛfunɛ bie Kalɛb. U kpa Kiriaf Aaba la banna yir bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la tɛu. Anak dee naabaal sɔnnɛ faa Aaba, u sɔnnɛ ba faa kpa dau a bolzeŋ naa.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
text: Denii Kalɛb jaa duŋŋi a Anak dee domeezi Sɛsai ni Ahiman ani Talmai lii de.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
text: Kalɛb ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ wer kpegli Kiriaf Sɛfa, n daŋ kpa n biihaaŋ Aksa tɛɛ a hiŋ ú kpa.”

ref: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
text: Aksa n wa yuu Ɔtniɛl, u ŋɔ u be, “Ŋɔ n mɛɛ be lugɔ ú tɛi hɛri di jaa.” Aksa n ga hel u mɛɛ be, di ra tuu u kawee nyuu. U mɛɛ pɛɛzuu. “A summɔaa? Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ n ɛɛ tɛinɛi?”

ref: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
text: U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛl tɛŋ. I suŋ n ninɛɛ di tɛŋ hɛri lii Nɛgɛv biini. Gaafura! Kpa bulli di jaaŋ.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Kalɛb kpa a bulli la n du chiŋ ani zɛɛ la maa tɛu.

ref: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
text: Juda dee ni u domeezi lulla kapɛttɛ diiribɔraa keŋ.

ref: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
text: Lɛbayɔf, Silhim, Ain ani Rimɔn. A maa kpau du bola tokko ni kabɛl ani a boljigzi.

ref: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: Saaram, Aditam, Gɛdɛra ani Gɛdɛrɔtam. Bolzenaa fidaanaazu ni a boljigzi.

ref: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: Gɛdɛrɔf, Bɛf Dagɔn, Naama ani bolzeŋ Makɛda. A ge du bolzenaa fidaanumbɛl ni a boljigzi.

ref: The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages: Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Haali Asdɔd ni u boljigzi ani Gaza ge ni u boljigzi maa, guŋŋ di ga lii gɔŋ la n du Ijip magbɔɔ, di kaa kpa Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn nua la maa di wa kaali.

ref: The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages: Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
text: Di kaa kpa Kiriaf Baal la, n ɛɛ Kiriaf Jiarim la ani Raba, a ge maa du bolzenaa anɛɛ ni a boljigzi.

ref: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
text: Ka Juda dee la faa waa wette duŋŋi Jɛbus hina la n faa du Jɛrusalɛm la waa, di lii a hɛri biini. Haali ni zinaa, ba ni baabuu haa kpauwɛ so.

ref: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
text: Bɔra naabuu ba faa kpa tɛɛ Ɛfram dee. U magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Atarɔf Adar n du wiifurii di ga hel Chiŋ Bɛf Hɔrɔn,

ref: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
text: Ɛfram faa kaa na bolzenaa ni boljigzi aŋhina di lii Manasɛ hina kapɛttɛ la biini.

ref: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
text: Ba faa waa Keenan hina la waa duŋŋɛɛ di lii Gɛza, ka gil baa ba du ba be di birgi ba yoma, haali zinaa, ba ni baabuu haa du de.

ref: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
text: Manasɛ dee bɔr magbɔɔ faa faarɔɔrɛ di lii Asɛ di ga hel Mikmɛtaf la n du bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm wiifurii la. Di lii de ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga kpa nɛra la n du Ɛn Tapua la di jaa.

ref: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
text: Hɛssi la maa n bar Tapua la maa ɛɛ Manasɛ dee horaa, ka Tapua himmaa la n du Manasɛ magbɔɔ la ɛɛ Ɛfram hina hor.

ref: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
text: Isaka ni Asɛ dizi hɛssi biine, Manasɛ deere faa dɔɔ bola naa, Bɛf San, Ibliam, Ɛndɔ, Taanak, Mɛgidɔ hina ani bola la maa n baraa la, di kpa Dɔɔ la n du muuzeŋ nua la.

ref: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
text: Ka Manasɛ hina la waa, waa wette so bola naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa wette duŋŋi Keenan hina la lii a bola.

ref: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Izrɛl hina jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di ra fir Keenan hina, ba hum ra tɛɛ baa, ka ba faa waa baa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri waa biini.

ref: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
text: Joosɛf dee ge ba Josua be di wa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kissi yaabuu werge, yaa du kpil, ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i mɔŋ a hɛri bɔkpaŋ bɛŋ tɛɛ yaa, ú ɛɛ yaa kapɛttɛi?”

ref: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
text: Josua ŋɔ, “Di Ɛfram hɛri la n ɛɛ giŋgimee bɔr la waa kaŋ tɛɛ ia, guŋwaa, ii la kɔrni la n du Pɛriz ni Rɛfa hina bɔra la biini, di ga mɔŋ bɔr di par di jaa.”

ref: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
text: Denii ba bir ŋɔ u be, “A giŋgimee bɔr hɛri wàá hel yaa, ka Keenan hina la n soge lɛla la biini dɔɔ lugbia torkozii, banla maa n du Bɛf San ni u bola la n baruu ani banla n du Jɛzriil Waluu la.”

ref: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
text: Denii Josua jaa ŋɔ Ɛfram ni Manasɛ dee la n lii Joosɛf dee biini la be, “Iiŋ kannɛ di kaa du kpeg kennaa, n daŋ tɛɛ ia hɛri jaa.

ref: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
text: A giŋgimee nyuu bɔr la gba daŋ ɛɛ ii hor. Haali uŋ ɛɛ kɔr la gba, ka ii daŋ paruu, ú ɛɛ ii kundɔɔlii, di lii u tuna bɛl di ga hel bɛl. Ka Keenan hina la waa, ii daŋ duŋŋi baa lii de, haali baŋ dɔɔ lugbia torkozi di du kpeg la gba.”

ref: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
text: Izrɛl hina n jaa dɔɔ a hɛri maa fɔŋŋa la, ba maa chaali bol la banna yir Silo, di baŋ ba ni Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia,

ref: There were still seven tribes without any land,
text: ka ba faa haa waa Izrɛl hina dizi aniidaanɛɛ la waa tɛɛwɛ bá kapɛttɛ hɛssi.

ref: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
text: Josua ŋɔ tɛɛ banla baŋ lizɛɛ ba ra la bá ga daani a hɛri na la be, “Ií la ga daani a hɛri maa, di sɛbi gunla un duwɛɛ dau, ka bir ba di wa ŋɔ n be, ń ta kuna Kɔraawiizi see bolzeŋ Silo bɔnnaa tɛɛ ia, ú bagliŋ gunla min niŋ bɔnni de tɛɛ dee maa.”

ref: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
text: Awia, a nɛra la ga gaagi a hɛri maa, di bɔnni de bɔra aniidaanɛɛ, di sɛbi u duula maa ni a bolzenaa sɔna, ka bir ba Josua be Silo, bɔr la baŋ baŋzi bá tantizi di chɔɔ la.

ref: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
text: Josua jaa ta kuna Silo, Kɔraawiizi see tɛɛ baa, ka bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi la n kawɛɛ la maa. Hɛri la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Bɛnjamin dee la wia

ref: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
text: Bɛnjamin dee domeezii ba feli bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ. Ba hɛri faa chɔɔ Juda ni Joosɛf dizi hɛssi baambaannɛ.

ref: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
text: A hɛri wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ faarɔɔrɛ lii Jɔɔdan muu, di ga bɛri bolzeŋ Jɛriko wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di ga wiicholi ga hel giŋgimee hɛri, di ga chug Bɛf Avɛn hɛribɔduma.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
text: Di lii bizeŋ la n chaŋ Bɛf Hɔrɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag, a magbɔɔ bir ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag di hiihni wiicholiii paga, di ga lii Kiriaf Baal, ba faa kaa ra yiruu Kiriaf Jiarim la, n ɛɛ Juda hina bolzeŋ. U wiicholii magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.

ref: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
text: U wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔ la faarɔɔrɛ lii Kiriaf Jiarim laŋgara, di kpau guŋŋ di ga lii Nɛftɔa bulli.

ref: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
text: A magbɔɔ kaa tuu ga hel bizeŋ la n chaŋ Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu la zɛɛ, n du Rɛfam Waluu wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere la. Di lii de ga Hinɔm Waluu di hiini Jɛbus hina bolzeŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag bɔwillii la, di ga hel bolzeŋ Ɛn Rɔgɛl.

ref: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
text: Di kaa lii de di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ga hel Ɛn Sɛmɛs niiri, di kaa kpau ga lii yembɛl banna yir Gɛlilɔf n chaŋ Adumim Ŋmɛnɛɛ. Di kaa lii de di kpau guŋŋ di ga hel Bɔhan Bii la. Bɔhan naa faa ɛɛ Rubin biibaallɛ.

ref: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
text: Di kaa lii de di kpau guŋŋ ga hel yembɛl banna yir Bɛf Araba wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii, di lii de tuu ga hel Jɔɔdan Waluu.

ref: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
text: U kaa lii de di ga hel Bɛf Hɔgla wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag bɔwillii di ga de ga chug bɔr la Jɔɔdan muu n gaa zuu Muuzensiwii la. U wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔrɛ faa guŋ.

ref: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
text: Jɔɔdan muu labuu faa ba wiifurii magbɔɔ. Bɛnjamin domeezi kapɛttɛ magbɔɔnii faa guŋ.

ref: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
text: A hɛri bɔnnaa nɛɛhiŋ biini, Simɛɔn dee domeezii ba kaa tɛɛ hiŋ. Ba kapɛttɛ bɔr faa du Juda hɛri biinii.

ref: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
text: Bɛf Lɛbayɔf ani Saruhɛn. A maa du bolzenaa fidaahoro ni a boljigzi.

ref: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
text: Anla n kaa jaau, bolzenaa Ain, Rimɔn, Ɛta ani Asan. A ge du bolzenaa anaazu ani a boljigzi,

ref: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
text: ani boljigzi la maa n baraa la guŋŋ di ga chug Baalaf Bɛɛ baŋ kaa ra yir Rama u du Nɛgɛv la. Bɔra naabuu faa ɛɛ Simɛɔn dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔra.

ref: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
text: Ba faa mɔŋ Juda dee bɔr yenne tɛɛ Simɛɔn dee, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba bɔr la faa kannɔɔ werge. Awia, Simɛɔn dee hiŋ jaa na ba hor di lii Juda dee hor la biini. A hɛri bɔr la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Zɛbulɔn dee wia

ref: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
text: Denii a hɛri magbɔɔ bar ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ga hel bolzeŋ Hanatɔn di ga tuŋ Ifta Ɛl Waluu.

ref: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
text: Anla n faa kaa jaau, Kataf, Nahalal, Simrɔn, Idala ani Bɛtlihɛm. A bolzenaa faa du fidaanɛɛ ni a boljigzi.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
text: Bolzenaa naa ni a boljigzii faa Zɛbulɔn dee domeezi kapɛttɛ. Isaka dee hɛri wia

ref: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
text: U magbɔɔ kaa chi de di bir ga wiifurii di chaŋ bolzeŋ Bɛf Dagɔn di ga chug Zɛbulɔn dee hɛri magbɔɔ ni Ifta Ɛl Waluu, di ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ga chug bolzenaa Bɛf Ɛmɛk ani Nɛyɛl, di bɛri Kabul n du nomɛɛl paga

ref: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
text: ni Ɛbrɔn, Rɛhɔb, Hamɔn ani Kana guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋ Saidɔn.

ref: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
text: Naftali dee domeezi kapɛttɛ diiribɔttɛ faa guŋ. Dan dee hɛri wia

ref: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
text: Izrɛl hinuu maa gɛɛ hɔɔhri la maa n du ba biini wa kpu nɛr di waa kuttɛɛ, daŋ wer chɔ ga zuu a bola naa bɛl maa, lalii la lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpu nɛr la n kpuu la, gilɛɛ wa nau di kpu, di ba waa u seriya diwee nɛra baaŋ.

ref: One day the Lord told Joshua:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Josua be,

ref: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be bá lizi bolzenaa la aŋhina, á ɛɛ bolzenaa la nɛra n niŋ ɔɔ chɔ ga zuu di lɛɛ bahinaa gunla miŋ faa gillɛ Moosis ŋɔ i be la.

ref: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
text: Di lalii la lulli himmaa la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ú kpuu la, wa duŋŋi unla n kpuu la luge, ú wa kpuu turgi a kim, á bol hina gilɛɛ wa kpau ra tɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai, waa kuttɛɛ kpu u nɛr hiŋ.

ref: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
text: U daŋ du a bolzeŋ guŋŋ ba wa diu seriya nɛra baaŋ, di kaa ra ba saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la n du de a saŋa hiŋ n niŋ wa siu. Denii ú jaa bir la u bol la un chɔwɛɛ lii la.”

ref: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
text: Awia, ba jaa lizi bolzeŋ Kɛdɛs n du Naftali giŋgimee bɔr, Galilii hɛri, di lizi bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm n du bolzeŋ Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri bɔr ani bolzeŋ Kiriaf Aaba la n ɛɛ bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, Juda dee giŋgimee hɛri la.

ref: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
text: Bolzenaa la baŋ faa lizɛɛ Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii ani bolzeŋ Jɛriko wiifurii hɛribɔduma lɛl labuu, Bɛza n du Rubin dee hɛri biini ni Ramɔf n du Giliad hɛri, Gad dee bɔr ani Golan n du Basan, Manasɛ dee bɔr.

ref: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
text: Silo la n du Keenan hɛri la, di wa ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Moosis benii lugɔ ií tɛɛ yaa bolzenaa ya so ani bɔra la yaa sela ge n ninna di.”

ref: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
text: Awia, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la wia, Izrɛl hina la faa lizi ba bolzenaa ani ba sela diiribɔra di lii ba himmaa kapɛttɛzi biine, di tɛɛ Levi dee.

ref: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
text: Kɔhaf dee domeezi labuu ba feli bɔnni a bolzenaa tɛɛ, baabuu faa Levi dee di lii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Aarɔn naanna biini. Ba faa tɛɛ baabuu bolzenaa fidaahoro di lii Juda, Simɛɔn ani Bɛnjamin dizi hora biine.

ref: The clans that were descendants of Merari received
text: Rubin, Gad ani Zɛbulɔn dizi kpa bolzenaa fidaanɛɛ tɛɛ Mɛrari naanna.

ref: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
text: Awia, Izrɛl hina hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, lugɔ ú bɔnni bolzenaa ani sela diiribɔra tɛɛ Levi dee la.

ref: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
text: Bolzenaa fidaahoro ni a sela diiribɔraa ba faa kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Aarɔn naanna la.

ref: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
text: Bolzenaa fidaahoro ani a sela diiribɔraa ba lizi tɛɛ Gɛsɔn domeezi la.

ref: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
text: A bolzenaa naa bɛl maanii faa dɔɔ sela diiribɔr di baruu chem.

ref: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa hɛri la maa uŋ faa hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ u daŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la, ba faa wer di kpegli ba dɔma, ka foozi de maa di so.

ref: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ baabuuu bampirsɔna a hɛri maa biini, gunla himmaa uŋ faa hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba naabaala la. Ba dɔma bɛl maa faa waa wette kpegli baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa kpa ba dɔmaa di du ba nonee biini.

ref: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
text: Nuuŋɔɔlinanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maanii wa ɛɛwɛ ni wibii.

ref: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
text: Denii Josua yir Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ ba maa chaali bɔkpaŋ,

ref: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
text: Haali di wa lii ni zinaa, ii haa waa ii lulla Izrɛl hina gillɛ ha tama maa. Ii wettoo du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia labuu.

ref: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ii lulla heezaa gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua la, ií bir la ii bola la n du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia, Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la.

ref: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
text: Ka ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa Moosis n tɛɛ ia la. Ií nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, di ra hiŋ u ŋmɛnizi ani u widaulaa maa. Ií lawuu chigigi, di ra humuu ni ii biine ni ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa.”

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
text: Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba ma mbusu lizibɔttɛ Gɛlilɔf, n dugli Jɔɔdan muu, Keenan hɛri magbɔɔ ba keŋkere la,

ref: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
text: ba maa izi kakpaŋ di ga chaali Silo, di ɛɛ sirya bá la ga lɔ baa laal.

ref: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
text: Awia, Izrɛl hina feli hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas, ú la Giliad di ga huuzi Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la de.

ref: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
text: U ni Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra fii ba faa hum. Dizi fi la biini, nɛkpaŋkpaŋaa ba lizi, bɛl maa faa ɛɛ dia nabɔma, Izrɛl domeezi la biini.

ref: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
text: Baŋ ga hel Giliad hɛri la, ba ŋɔ tɛɛ Rubin, Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ la maa be,

ref: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
text: “Yaa chigɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra maa naarɛ di ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni, di bir har kpuu, ka ma ii himmaa mbusu lizibɔr di vɛɛuwɛi?

ref: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
text: Ii ra liizi yaa wichɔgaa la yaa n ɛɛwɛ Bizeŋ Pɛɔ, Kɔraawiizi kpa wiilchɔgaa tɔɔri u nɛra la. Yaa haa ra di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ dikuu a wia. A wichɔgii naa waa kukkɛɛa?

ref: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
text: Ii daŋ vɛɛ u hiŋaa filaŋkeŋ? Di ii vɛɛ u hiŋaa zinaa, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh Izrɛl hina maa ni kɛrɛ.

ref: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
text: Di ii ra fɛu lugɔ ii hɛri waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi jaamaa, amɔ, ií gi a muu naa di ra ba yaa be Kɔraawiizi hɛri, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia n duwɛɛ, ya bɔnni a hɛri di tɛɛ ia. Ka ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua gɛɛ yaa nua, di kaa waa ma mbusu lizibɔr di ra tɛɛ iihinaa. Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔkpaŋkpaŋ bɛnnɛ du de, bɛl maa waa kaa hoo.

ref: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa waa Izrɛl hina maa duwɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ, saŋa la Zɛra biibaal Akan n faa ŋmɛɛ kuna la baŋ lizɛɛ di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi laa? U bɛŋ lɛi faa siuwɛ dikuu a wichɔgaa hiŋ wia.”

ref: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ bɛnnɛ du de! U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi! U bɛnnɛ zum wii la wia yaa n mau. Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ii ge zum guŋ! Di yaa dɔɔ dignikpegaa ya vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua, amɔ, ií gilɛɛ gil yá kaa du de ni miibɔɔ zinaa.

ref: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
text: Di yaa ma mbusu lizibɔttɛ di tɛɛ yaa hinaa, lugɔ ya bir har kpu Kɔraawiizi, gɛɛ yaa n niŋ kpa de di birgi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mia gɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizibɔr, guŋwaa Kɔ́raawiizi himmaa tɛr yaa digna.

ref: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
text: Awiarɛ yaa ma mbusu lizibɔr, ka waa mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa gɛɛ mbusuzi lizibɔr ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas ŋɔ ba be, “Zinaa, yaa zummɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii, dikuu iiŋ waa wichɔgaa maa ɛɛwɛ di zuu u ni gunla yaa n faa fɛwɛɛ la wia. Ka ii lɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa ha, di lii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ biini.”

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
text: Denii Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhas ani nabɔnzi la jaa gil baa Giliad hɛri, ka bir la Keenan di jaa ga ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ.

ref: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina maa bɔra jaa sɔɔni baa werge maa, ba ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Ba waa kaa ra liizi lugɔ ba ni baa yoo laal, di chɔgi ba hɛri.

ref: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
text: Rubin ani Gad dizi la maa jaa ra yir mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ mawɛɛ la, ‘Daansɛɛ.’ Di kaa ŋɔ, “U ɛɛ daansɛɛrɛ tɛɛ yaa ni baa maa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ du de.”

ref: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
text: Biŋkpila n wa bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi jaa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina heezaa di lii ba dɔma be. A saŋa di Josua jaa zɛŋ werge,

ref: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
text: u chaali Izrɛl hina maa, ba nabɔnzi ani ba sitɔɔra, di ŋɔ ba be, “N jaa zɛŋuu werge filaŋkeŋ.

ref: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
text: Ii himmaa na wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛ hɛssi naa maa hinaa, dikuu ii wia, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu faa naawɛ tɛɛ ia.

ref: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Hɛssi naa maa daŋ birgi ii hora, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ duŋŋi a nɛra maa di lii de filaŋkeŋ, ka ii ga so de, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.

ref: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
text: Awia, ií chiiri zɛɛ, di ra du tau, di ra hiŋ wia la maa un dauwɛ tɛɛ ia, Moosis Gbɔgni Hɔŋ biini la nɛnnɛ. Ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ a hiŋaa tama maa.

ref: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
text: Ií ra du tau, di gilɛɛ wa gil ii ni hɛssi naa hina n haa du ii be naa, wàá kpau wiimaa biini gɛɛ di wàá yirgi ba vuga sɔna di ra hɛɛhzaa. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuaraa gɛɛ di togni ra jaamaa.

ref: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
text: Ií lau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la chigigi, gunla iin lawuu di wa lii zinaa naa.

ref: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
text: Kɔraawiizii duŋŋi nɛkpega la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge di lii hɛssi naa biini di tɛɛ ia, di wa lii ni zinaa, di nɛr maa haa waa wette kpegli ia.

ref: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
text: Ii bɛl maa daŋ wer duŋŋi nɛra kagboŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum labuu naawɛ di ra tɛɛ ia, gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ia la.

ref: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
text: Awia, ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.

ref: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
text: guŋwaa, ii zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, wàá ka duŋŋi a hɛssi naa hina lii ii hɛri naa biini. Ba daŋ du ii be di ɛɛ lugɔ ŋmɛmbizi ni sidɛɛzi, di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ virinzi di ra viiri ii hara ani sɔɔhri di ra tɔɔhzi i siwee guŋŋ ii wa dim, di lii a hɛrsum naa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n tɛɛ ia naa biini.”

ref: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
text: Josua kaa ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ, n saŋa jaa heluu. Ii maa zummɔ ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa lugɔ nuuŋɔɔlinanaa la maa Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia la, bɛl maa waa ɛɛwɛ huhzi. A maanii u ɛɛ, waa bɛl maa ɛɛwɛ huhzi!

ref: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
text: Denii Josua chaali Izrɛl dizi nabɔnzi, sitɔɔra, seriya diire ani ba nabɔnzenaa maa, ba wa chaali bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm Kɔraawiizi see.

ref: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
text: Josua ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Faa la, ii naabaala, di kpa Abraham ni Nahɔ mɛɛ Tɛra jaa, faa sogo Muu Yufretis keŋkere la hinnɛ di faa ra kuari vuga.

ref: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
text: Ka n wa lizi ii naabaal Abraham, di kpogluu gi Muu Yufretis, di la ga zuu Keenan hɛri di tɛu naanna kpila. N tɛubuu Aizik,

ref: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
text: u lul Jekɔb ni Ɛsau. N kpa Ɛdɔm giŋgimee hɛri la tɛɛ Ɛsau, ka Jekɔb ni u biibaala waa la Ijip hɛri di ga so de.

ref: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
text: Miŋ wa kpogli ii naabaala di lii Ijip hɛri, ba wa hel muuzeŋ la, a Ijip hina la kpa torkozi zagra n na tɛrgi ani zagtinna di dau ba luge di wa hel a Muuzeŋaahmu.

ref: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
text: Ba lɔ wile tɛŋ di ŋɔ ń lɛɛ baa, n gil bɔbiri ba wa du ba ni Ijip hina baambaaŋ, di gil muuzeŋ la wa tɔ Ijip hina la ni, di di baa. Ii zum gunla miŋ ɛɛ baabuu. Denii ii du hɛribɔduma di birgi werge.

ref: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
text: Ka n wa kpogli ia zuu Amɔri hina hɛri n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii. Ba wa lɔ ia laal, ka n gil ii kpegli baa. N faa kpu baa, ka ii foozi ba hɛri dɔɔ.

ref: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
text: Denii Zipɔ biibaal Balak n di Moab kora, izi di ɛɛ seriya di vɔɔ laal ú wa lɔ ia, di hum bá ga yir Bɛɔ biibaal Balaam, ú wa see ia nua.

ref: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
text: Ka n faa waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu, ka gil u kissi ia werge maa, n lɛɛ ia lii u nonee biini.

ref: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
text: Denii ii gi Jɔɔdan muu la di wa hel bolzeŋ Jɛriko, a bol hina yoo ia. Gunnɛ Amɔri, Pɛriz, Keenan, Hitti, Girgas, Hivi ani Jɛbus hina maa yoo ia, ka n kpa baa du ii nonee.

ref: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
text: N kaa gil chirinchaazi tɔ ii see, di ga duŋŋi ba ni Amɔri hina koora banɛɛ la. Ii tokobizi ni i hozi lɛi ii kpa ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
text: N tɛɛ iabuu hɛri la iiŋ waa kuuhwɛ ka na, di tɛɛ ia bolzenaa la iiŋ waa a zɛɛzi tiiwe ka ra zuua. N kaa tɛɛ ia grepu daazi kooni ni ɔlivizi kooni iiŋ waa pattɛ ka ra dia.’ ”

ref: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
text: Josua kaa ŋɔ, “Ií ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi di ra humuu ni wibii. Ií kpa ii vuga la ii naabaala n faa ra kuari Muu Yufretis keŋkere la hiŋ ani Ijip hɛri la di ha, ka ra hum Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ.

ref: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
text: Ka di ii waa nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi jaamaa, amɔ, ií lizi kunla iinna nyiŋŋi ii ra jaami zinaa, di vuga la ii naabaala n faa ra kuari a muuzeŋ keŋkere la hiŋ gɛɛ Amɔri hina hɛri iiŋ duwɛɛ naa vuga. Ka miŋwaa ni n diahina maa, Kɔraawiizii ya ra hum.”

ref: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
text: Denii a nɛra ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi ra la ani bɔɔnɛɛ, ya ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u wia, ka ra kuari vuga.

ref: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la himmaanii faa kpogli yaa ni yaa naabaala di lii Ijip hɛri la yaa n faa duwɛɛ di ɛɛ yoma la. U faa ɛɛ wizenaare yaa sibɔɔ, di guu yaa nɛnnɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ volaa ni hɛssi la maa biine yaa n gawɛɛ la.

ref: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
text: Kɔraawiizii faa duŋŋi hɛssi la hina maa ni Amɔri hina la n faa du de mɔɔ la. Awia, yaa gba danna hum Kɔraawiizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu yaa ra jaami.”

ref: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
text: Denii Josua ŋɔ ba be, “Ii wàá wer hum Kɔraawiizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ di kaa ra zom. Wàá gil ii dignikpega ni ii wichɔgaa tɛɛ ia.

ref: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
text: Di ii wa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ka ra hiŋ hɛrdumazi hina vuga, u daŋ gil hɛhchɔg chol ii ni di chɔgi ia, haali uŋ faa suŋ ii ni di ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ ia la gba.”

ref: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
text: Ka a nɛra ŋɔ Josua be, “Akai! Yaa daŋ hum Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
text: Denii Josua ŋɔ ba be, “Ii di ii himmaa daansɛɛrɛ lugɔ ii daŋ hum Kɔraawiizi.” Ba maa sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, yaa sɛɛ gunnɛ wibii maa.”

ref: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
text: Josua jaa ŋɔ, “Amɔ, ií chɔgi hɛrdumazi hina vuga la maa n du ii be la, ka gil ii bampiree lau Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.”

ref: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
text: Awia, a nɛra ŋɔ Josua be, “Yaa daŋ hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la, di ra sɛɛ u nua.”

ref: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Josua ni Izrɛl hina ni Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ nuukpaŋ bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm, u sɛbi Gbɔgni ni widaulaa tɛɛ baa, bá ra hiŋ.

ref: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
text: Josua jaa sɛbi a wia maa di du Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni Hɔŋ la biini. Ka kpa bizeŋ baŋ daazeŋ bɛl n chigɛ dugli Kɔraawiizi bɔnaniinanii la zɛɛ.

ref: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Ií na, bii naa nuu wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa labuu. U daŋ di ii daansɛɛ, di ii wa bittɔ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua hiŋaa.” Josua siu wia

ref: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
text: Denii Josua jaa gil bɛl maa kaali u hɛri.

ref: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
text: Annii maa harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi balii Nun biibaal Josua siu. Binni kalfa ni fii u faa di.

ref: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
text: Hɛri la n ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ di du Timnaf Sɛra, Ɛfram hɛri giŋgimee bɔr n du Giŋgimii Gaas wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag paga labuu ba huguu.

ref: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
text: Josua de dui saŋa la, Izrɛl hina faa ra hum Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ. U siu harbɔɔ gba, ba faa haa ra hum Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, dikuu nabɔnzi la n na wia la Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la n faa haa du de wia.

ref: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
text: Izrɛl hina n waa lii Ijip hɛri la, ba faa paa Joosɛf hogaa di ba, di faa kpaa la bol la banna yir bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm, di ga hugaa hɛri la Jekɔb n faa yauwɛ lii Hamɔ biibaala be la. Saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaa u faa yawuu. A hɛri faa wa ɛɛ Joosɛf naanna kapɛttɛ kuŋ.

ref: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
text: Aarɔn biibaal Ɛliaza ge siu, ba hug u ge Gibia la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ u biibaal Finɛhas la. De du Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri bɔr la.

ref: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
text: Josua n wa siuwɛ, Izrɛl hina pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “Izrɛl dee bɛliirɛ niŋ feli ga pig Keenan hinai?”

ref: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ba be, “Juda deere niŋ feli la. N teŋ kpa a hɛri maanii du ba nonee.”

ref: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
text: Denii Juda hina ŋɔ ba lulla Simɛɔn dee be, “Ií hiini yaa yá yoo Keenan hina naa, di lɛɛ bɔr la Josua n mɔnnɛ tɛɛ yaa la. Di yaa wa lɛɛ de, yaa ge daŋ hiini ia yá yoo di lɛɛ ii bɔr tɛɛ ia.” Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, ba ɛɛ sirya di la ga hiini baa.

ref: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
text: Ba kaa la ga pig Keenan hina la n soge bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di kpegli Sɛsai, Ahiman ani Talmai domeezi.

ref: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
text: Denii Koori Adoni Bɛzɛk lii di ra chɔ, ba duŋŋuu ga lawuu di teŋri u nonibibala ni u naanibibala maa.

ref: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
text: Juda laallɔɔra n wa hel Jɛrusalɛm ge, ba kaa pig baa di kpegli baa. Baŋ wa kpuuzi baa tuŋ, ba jaa fuuh ba bolzeŋ maa.

ref: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
text: A harbɔɔ ni, ba la ga yoo Keenan hina la n du a giŋgimee hɛri ni Nɛgɛv ani wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi.

ref: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
text: Ba kaa lii de di ga pig bolzeŋ Dɛbir.

ref: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
text: Denii ba bɛl banna yir Kalɛb faa ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ kpegli Dɛbir, n daŋ kpa n biihaaŋ Aksa tɛɛ a hiŋ.”

ref: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
text: Kalɛb niwee Kɛnaz biibaal Ɔtniɛllɛ ɛɛ nɛr la n wette pig di kpegli baa. Awia, Kalɛb kpa u biihaaŋ Aksa tɛu.

ref: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
text: A hɔl bɛl, Ɔtniɛl ŋɔ u haaŋ Aksa be, “Ŋɔ i mɛɛ be lugɔ ú tɛi hɛri.” Uŋ wa lii u kawee nyuu di tuu, u mɛɛ Kalɛb pɛɛzuu, “A summɔaa? Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ń ɛɛ tɛinɛi?”

ref: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
text: U ŋɔ u be, “Hiŋ felee tɛŋ hɛri bɛl Nɛgɛv biini la, awia, kaa jaaŋ bulli ge.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Kalɛb kpa a hɛri chiŋ ni u zɛɛ bulli jaau.

ref: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
text: Moosis hila Kɛn hinuu naanna lii bolzeŋ Jɛriko, di hiŋ Juda dee di ga so nɛra la n du Juda Hɛribɔduma n du Nɛgɛv di dugli bol bɛl banna yir Arad biini.

ref: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
text: Denii Juda hina ga jaa ba lulla Simɛɔn dee ni, ba ga lɔ Keenan hina n du Zɛfaf, di kpegli baa, di purgi ba bol maa burburbur. Ba jaa dau a bolzeŋ sɔŋ Hɔma.

ref: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa hiini Juda dee, di tɛɛ baa fɔŋŋa, ba wer foozi giŋgimee hɛri la dɔɔ. Ka ba faa waa wette duŋŋi a nɛra lii a hɛri lɛla la baŋ soge la waa biine, dikuu baŋ dɔɔ laal lugbia torkozi wia.

ref: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
text: Juda dee kpa bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn tɛɛ Kalɛb, gunla Moosis n faa ŋɔ nua tɛu la. Kalɛb jaa duŋŋi Anak domeezi ahoro la n soge de la.

ref: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
text: Ka Bɛnjamin dee waa wette duŋŋi Jɛbus hina lii Jɛrusalɛm, awia, haali ni zinaa, Jɛbus hina ni Bɛnjamin dee la maanii haa soge Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
text: Mɔɔ ka ba la de, ba lizi baalaa ba la Bɛtɛl la baŋ faa ra yir Luuz la, di ga suahzi daanuu na gunla uŋ duwɛɛ.

ref: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
text: Ban laŋŋɛ, ba ga na baal bɛl n lii a bolzeŋ biini di ra ba, ba ŋɔ u be, “Bagli yaa gunla yaa n niŋ ɛɛ di zuu a bol naa. Di i bagli yaa, yaa daŋ suŋ i ni, yaa wàá ɛɛi wiimaa.”

ref: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
text: U bagli baa, ba zuu a bolzeŋ di kpuuzi ba maa, ka gil a baal waa ni u diahina maa.

ref: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a baal izi di la Hitti hina hɛri, di ga tii bolzeŋ bɛl zɛɛ de, di so ka dau u sɔŋ Luuz. A sɔnnɛ u haa di, di wa lii ni zinaa.

ref: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
text: Izrɛl hina n wa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, ba jaa ra fir Keenan hina bá ra hum baa alugɔ yoma. Ka ba faa waa baa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri biini.

ref: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
text: Ɛfram dee ge waa Keenan hina la n soge bol la banna yir Gɛza la duŋŋɛɛ. Ka ba ni baa haa kpau di so de.

ref: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
text: Zɛbulɔn dee gba waa Keenan hina la n soge Kitrɔn ni Nahalal la duŋŋɛɛ, ka gil ba ni baa kpau so, ba ra fir baa, ba ra hum alugɔ yoma.

ref: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
text: Naftali dee gba waa nɛra la n soge Bɛf Sɛmɛs ani Bɛf Anaf duŋŋɛɛ. Ka ba ni Keenan hina la kpau so a hɛri. Naftali dee ɔɔ ra fir baa ba ra hum alugɔ yoma.

ref: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
text: Amɔri hina fir Dan dee la waa, ba mag giŋgimee hɛri, ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá tuu lɛl la biini.

ref: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
text: Amɔri hina fittɔɔ bá so Bizeŋ Hɛrɛz, Aijalɔn, ani Saalbim. Ka Joosɛf naanna Ɛfram ni Manasɛ dizi n wa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa jaa, ba ra fir baa ba ra hum lugɔ yoma.

ref: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
text: Amɔri hina hɛri bɔr magbɔɔ chi Nuuma Ŋmɛnɛɛ di ga lii Sɛla, di bɛri de di ra la.

ref: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
text: Kɔraawiizi mɛlika lii Gilgal di ba Bɔkim di wa ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be, “N lizi iabuu lii Ijip hɛri, di kpogli ia ba hɛri naa, gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ii naabaala, di hɛɛhzi lugɔ n daŋ kpau tɛɛ ia, di ŋɔ lugɔ n ŋmɛnɛɛ maa wàá chɔgi n ni ia nuukpaŋ la.

ref: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
text: N ŋɔ ií gilɛɛ gil ii ni nɛra la n na zuu hɛri naa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. A dɛkkɔɔ lugɔ ii chɔgi ba vuga kuaribɔra maa, ka ii vɛɛ n nua hiŋaa. Bɛɛ ii ɛɛ gunnɛi?

ref: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
text: Awia, n na ŋɔ ii benii, iiŋ vɛɛ n wia naa, màá ka tɔ ii see duŋŋi a nɛra. Ba daŋ du ii biine di birgi lugɔ sɔɔhri. Ba vuga ɛɛ lugɔ sidɛɛzi tɛɛ ia.”

ref: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
text: Awia, ba jaa ra yir a bol Bɔkim. Denii ba lizi mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Josua siu wia

ref: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
text: Ba huguu u hɛri n du Timnaf Sɛra. De faa du Ɛfram hɛri giŋgimee hɛri, Bizeŋ Gaas wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag.

ref: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
text: Josua de dui saŋa jimini hina la nonii n wa kpawɛɛ, jiminifalii hina ge wa lii. Baawaa faa suuh Kɔraawiizi wia ani wia la uŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina,

ref: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
text: Di Izrɛl hina haŋ wa lii bá ga yoo ba dɔma yemmaa, Kɔraawiizi waa ɔɔ chi ba har bá kpegli ba dɔma gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua, di karfi baa la. Biinichɔg werge jaa chol ba ni.

ref: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
text: Ka Izrɛl hina faa waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ ba sitɔɔra hiŋ. Izrɛl hina wia faa nyaa wibiire Kɔraawiizi be. Ba ra kuari vuga. Ba mɛɛwaa faa ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ, ka jiminifalii naa hina waa faa vɛɛ guŋ ɛɛi manaŋ.

ref: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
text: Saŋa maa di Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa lizi sitɔɔri tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, u ɔɔ hiini a hinnɛ ú wer lɛɛ baa lii ba dɔma nonee biini u de dui saŋa. Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ na u nɛra sinyɛnaa, dikuu gunla ba dɔma n na sunni baa, ba ra him wia.

ref: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
text: Ka di a sitɔɔri wa siuwɔ, a nɛra ɔɔ kaa bir wa du ba duulaa, di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa, di kaali jimini la hina n tɔ ba see la. Ba ɔɔ faa ra kuari vugaa di ra sɛɛ a dɔɔra, di vɛɛ ba wichɔgaa gilaa ta.

ref: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge maa. U ŋɔ, “Nɛra naa chɔg nuukpaŋ la n ni ba naabaala n ɛɛwɛ labuu, dikuu baŋ vɛɛ n nua wia,

ref: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
text: màá ka duŋŋi nɛra la n kawɛɛ Josua n haa waa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri biini ka siu la.

ref: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
text: N daŋ kpa baa di ɛɛ Izrɛl hina na, di ba daŋ wer hiŋ n nua gunla ba naabaala n hiŋŋɛ la gɛɛ ba wàá wer hiŋɛi?”

ref: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil a hɛssi hina ka a hɛri, waa sɛɛwɛ Josua kpegli baa gɛɛ di duŋŋi baa lii a hɛri manaŋ, Josua siu har.

ref: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
text: U ra ɛɛ gunnɛ ú ɔɔ wer bagli Izrɛl hina biizi la n izee, ba haa waa laal wia zummɛ mɔɔ, bá zum gunla laal wia n duwɛɛ.

ref: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
text: Hɛssi la hina n faa kawɛɛrɛ keŋ, Filisti hina ni ba koora banue, Keenan hina maa, Saidɔn hina ni Hivi hina la n du Lɛbanɔn bizenaa hɛri, di lii Bizeŋ Baal Hɛmɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
text: Banniibuu Kɔraawiizi gil di ŋɔ ú kpa ɛɛ Izrɛl hina di na, di ba daŋ wer hiŋ u nuuzi ani u widaulaa la un dauwɛ tɛɛ ba naabaala, di lii Moosis be la gɛɛ ba wàá werei?

ref: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
text: Izrɛl hina jaa ra paagi ba biihaana. A nɛra ge biibaala ra paagi ba biihaana. Guŋ gil ba jaa ra kuari ba vuga. Ɔtniɛl wia

ref: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
text: Izrɛl hina ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di suuh Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la wia, ka ra kuari vuga Baal ni vughaana Asɛra hiŋ la wia.

ref: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh werge maa Izrɛl hina ni, u kpa baa du Mɛsɔpɔtemia Koori Kusan Risatam nonee biini, u di kora ba ni, binni ŋmantannaazi.

ref: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
text: Ka Izrɛl hina n wa lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi lugɔ ú lɛɛ baa, u lizi Kalɛb niwee Kɛnaz biibaal Ɔtniɛl, lugɔ ú tɔ ba see di lɛɛ baa lii ba dɔma nonee biini.

ref: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
text: Bampirsɔna jaa du a hɛri binni tokkoanɛɛ mɔɔ ka Ɔtniɛl siu. Ɛhud wia

ref: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
text: Izrɛl hina kaa ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. Awia, u gil Moab Koori Ɛglɔn kpegli baa.

ref: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
text: U ni Ammɔn ni Amalɛk hina ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di ga pig Izrɛl hina, di kpegli baa, di foozi Bolzeŋ Jɛriko.

ref: Then he ruled Israel for
text: Izrɛl hina jaa sɛɛ Moab Koori Ɛglɔn dɔɔra binni fidiŋmantannaazi.

ref: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
text: Uŋ wa tɛu tuŋ, u lii ta banla n chigɛ a kuna di hiŋuu ba la ŋmɛnɛɛ di ŋɔ bá ra kpo.

ref: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. text: Denii Gidiɔn la dia di ga lau bubalee kpu di daali, di kaa kpa paanuu sau lugɔ kookoo tassazi fi, di kuari paanuu n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ, di kpa a ola du kɛɛgɔ biini, di fug a yoma ge du hɛna biini, di kpaa ba wa tɛɛ a mɛlika, a daazeŋ zɛɛ.

ref: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”

text: Denii Gidiɔn ma mbusu lizibɔr de, di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di dau u sɔŋ, ‘Kɔraawiizii Bampirsɔna’. A guŋ mbusu lizibɔr naa haa du Abiɛza bolzeŋ Ɔfra, di wa lii ni zinaa.
