text: Ba maa jaa chi ba chignibɔra di bar Midian hina chɔɔribɔr la, ɔnsii lau Midian hina la, ba ra chɛɛhgi ka ra chɔ.

text: Uŋ wa suŋŋi guŋ, Kɔraawiizi nuu u wiisuŋŋaa hiŋ, di gil u mɛlika hiŋ kaa ba a haaŋ be di u du koo, ka u jaari Manoa faa waa hoo u be de.

ref: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
text: Denii a haaŋ lii chɔ werge maa di la u jaari be di ga ŋɔ, “Na, a baal la n ba n be a hɔl labuu kaa ba n be zinaa!”

ref: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
text: Manoa izi kakpaŋ, di hiŋ u haaŋ ba la a baal be, u ga pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu wa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ n haaŋ laa?” U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, minuu.”

ref: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
text: Denii Manoa jaa pɛɛzuu, “Di wia la maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la haŋ la wa ɛɛ wibii, ɛrɛɛ u de dui wikpoglaa duɛi?”

ref: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
text: Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la ŋɔ, “A dɛkkɔɔ i haaŋ na du tau nɛnnɛ, di hiŋ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la.

ref: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
text: Wàá ka di grepu nɔna gɛɛ di nyɔɔ a siŋ. Gɛɛ wàá ka nyɔɔ siŋkpeg maa gɛɛ di di diwee la maa n doŋŋe. A dɛkkɔɔ ú ra du tau, di hiŋ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la nɛnnɛ.”

ref: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
text: Denii Manoa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hiŋ be, “Gaafura ka so tama, ya lau bubalee kpu di ɛɛ diwee tɛi, í di ka ra la.”

ref: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
text: Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hiŋ ŋɔ, “Haali hiŋ ŋɔ n so naa, ka màá di kummaa. Ka di i wa kpuu, fuuuh, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.” Manoa faa waa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlikaa.

ref: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
text: Denii Manoa pɛɛzuu, “I sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ? N na nyiŋŋuu ya zum i sɔŋ, di annii naa maa wa ɛɛwɔ, ya kpa jaaŋ ni girme tɛi.”

ref: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
text: Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hiŋ bir pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi í zum n sɔnɛi? Di n baglii gba, ka haa wer zum u zɛɛ.”

ref: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
text: Denii Manoa lau a bubalee di la bii bɛl nyuu di ga kpu, di kpa mbusu lizaa mia jaa u ni, di lizi mbusu, di fuuuh tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. U fuuih hiŋ biinii u ni u haaŋ chi de di ra binnuu, Kɔraawiizi jaa ɛɛ nuukpuuri wii bɛl.

ref: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
text: A ninlau n na izi mbusu lizibɔr di ra la chiŋ la, ba ŋɔ ba binni di Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hinnɛ du a ninlau biini di ra tinni chiŋ. Manoa ni u haaŋ n wa na guŋ, ba chol pi hɛri.

ref: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
text: Kɔraawiizi mɛlika hiŋ waa kaa kpa u hiŋ di bagli baa. Denii Manoa jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlikaa lii ba be la.

ref: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
text: U jaa ŋɔ u haaŋ be, “Wibii maa, yaa daŋ siuzi dikuu yaa n na Kɔraawiizi wia!”

ref: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
text: Ka u haaŋ ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi faa ra nyiŋŋi yaa kpui, u faa wàá lɛɛ yaa mbusu lizaa mia ni mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii naa gɛɛ u faa wàá sɛɛ lizi wia naa maa bagli yaa gɛɛ di ŋɔ wia naa maa tɛɛ yaa.”

ref: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
text: Denii u haaŋ hiŋ wa lul biibaal, ba dau u sɔŋ Samsin. A bie ra hel, Kɔraawiizi ra hiinuu u wiɛɛlaa maa biini.

ref: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
text: Kɔraawiizi Duma faari di ra izuu saŋa la un soge Mahanɛ Dan n du bolzenaa Zɔra ni Ɛstayɔl baambaaŋ la.

ref: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
text: Denii a hɔl bɛl Samsin la bol bɛl banna yir Timna. Uŋ ga du de la, u na Filisti hina toloori bɛl.

ref: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
text: Uŋ wa bittɛ ba bol, u ŋɔ u maa ni u mɛɛ be, “Miŋ la Timna la, n ga na ba toloori bɛllɛ, u wia pariŋ. Ií la ga nyiŋŋuu tɛŋ.”

ref: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
text: U maa ni u mɛɛ ŋɔ, “Amɔ, di i binni yaa dee naa biini, hàá na haaŋ di kpaa? Izrɛl hina naa maa biini, haa wer na haaŋ dee? Ka bɛɛwiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi Filisti hina naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa bɛlɛi?” Ka Samsin ŋɔ u mɛɛ be, “Ga nyiŋŋuu tɛŋ, u wiarɛ pariŋ.”

ref: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
text: Di u maa ni u mɛɛ faa waa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ra hum u huma, di ra nyiŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ ú yoo Filisti hina. Baabuu faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa Izrɛl hina ni a saŋa hiŋ.

ref: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
text: Samsin ni u maa ni u mɛɛ ra la Timna. Baŋ wa hel Timna grepu daazi kooni, kakpaŋ bunyimpɔl lii di uuhri di ra chem u ni.

ref: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma izuu werge. Waa kummaa kpoglee, ka la ga lau u nua aahli pɛrgi alugɔ uŋ ɛɛ bubii u be, ka waa u maa ni u mɛɛ be ŋɔwɛɛ wii la uŋ ɛɛwɛ.

ref: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
text: Uŋ wa hel Timna, u la a biihaaŋ be, u nuu ga ŋɔ wia, u wia paruu.

ref: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Samsin bir la ú ga kpau. U ga bɛɛ bɔr la uŋ kpu a bunyiŋ la, ú binni u hoga na gunla an duwɛɛ. Uŋ ga naa, di huuhrɛ ma a maa ni, di du nuu.

ref: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
text: U panzi a huuh pɛɛna yeŋ di di ra la, ka kpa u yeŋ ge di ga tɛɛ u maa ni u mɛɛ, ba ge di. Ka waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ ba be lugɔ a bunyiŋ siwii hiŋ ninɛɛ u lizuu.

ref: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Samsin mɛɛ la a haaŋ dia ú ga nau. Samsin ge gil ba daali diuzenaa gunla haŋfalii jaari n ɔɔ ɛɛ la.

ref: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
text: Uŋ wa ballɛ, biipɔllaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ ba yir di lii a bol biini, bá du u be.

ref: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
text: Ka di ii ge waa wette bagliŋ u zɛɛ, ii daŋ tɛŋ pɛɛnnanaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ani bɔmbɔga ge tokko ni kpɔrgɔ.” Ba ŋɔ, “Ta a dar ya nuu!”

ref: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
text: Denii u jaa ŋɔ, “Kundiiri biinii diwee lii. Kuŋkpeg biinii kunsum lii.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, hɔpizaa ahoro, di ba haa waa u zɛɛ zummɛ bá bagluu.

ref: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
text: A hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ, ba ŋɔ Samsin haaŋ be, “Murgi i jaari ú baglii a wii naa zɛɛ, í ge wa bagli yaa. Di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ fuuh i ni i mɛɛ diahina maa ii siuzi. Ií yir yaabuu ɛŋ ii wa foozi yaa kuna gɛɛ?”

ref: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
text: Denii u haaŋ la ba u be di wa chol chɔɔ u ni di ra wii, ka ŋɔ, “Ajaa i hahmbuu ka ŋɔ i nɔŋŋimbuuwaa? Na, i ta dar bɛllɛ tɛɛ n nɛra, di ŋɔ ba be lugɔ bá baglii u zɛɛ, ka haa sɛɛwɛ bagliŋ u zɛɛ.” U bir ŋɔ u haaŋ hiŋ be, “Maa sɛɛwɛ bagli u zɛɛ tɛɛ n maa ni n mɛɛ gba. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń bagli u zɛɛ tɛɛ hiŋwaai?”

ref: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
text: U haaŋ hiŋ ɔɔ jaa wii di ra duu a hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ maa biini banna di ba hiŋ la. A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, u jaa bagluu u zɛɛ, dikuu uŋ wɔɔ ra gil la wia. Uŋ wa bagluu tuŋ, u ge jaa kpa di ga bagli tɛɛ u nɛra hiŋ.

ref: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
text: Hɔpizi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ mɔɔ ka wiizi chol, a bol baala ba Samsin be di wa ŋɔ, “Beedee n summɛ di kaali huuhnuuwɛi? Beedee n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di kaali bunyinɛi?” Samsin jaa bir ŋɔ ba be, “Di ii faa waa n haaŋ ɔnzɛɛ gɛɛ di pɛɛzuu lɛi, ii faa wàá wer zum n dar naa zɛɛ maa.”

ref: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
text: Denii ba bir kpa Samsin haaŋ hiŋ tɛɛ u badɔŋ la n soge u zɛɛ u haŋfalli saŋa la, u ge bir kpau.

ref: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
text: Ka jaa ŋɔ u be, “N zummɔ nɛnnɛ lugɔ hɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi, awia, n kpaubuu tɛɛ i badɔŋ. Ka u niweere du de, haali di du wer werge maa kaaluu. Awia, kpa waabuu ka gil u kpɛɛma hiŋ.”

ref: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
text: Denii Samsin ŋɔ ba be, “Filaŋkeŋ, ŋmɛnɛɛ chɔɔwɔɔ tɛŋ lugɔ ń turgi Filisti hina naa kim. N daŋ tɔɔri baa werge, bá zum.”

ref: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
text: Denii u jaa du niŋ a ni, ka gil a chɔ di ra bar a Filisti hina kooni, di fuuh ba mia baŋ kummɛ dau ni anla n haa chigɛ, di kaa chɔgi ba grepu daazi ni ɔlivizi daazi kooni maa.

ref: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
text: Filisti hina la pɛɛzi bá zum nɛr la n ɛɛ guŋ. Nɛbɛl ŋɔ, “Timna hinuu hila Samsinnɛ, dikuu uŋ kpa u haaŋ tɛɛ u badɔŋ wia.” A Filisti hina n wa nuu guŋ, ba la ga lau u hilabaal hiŋ ani a biihaaŋ hiŋ maa fuuh.

ref: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
text: Denii Samsin ŋɔ ba be, “Kennaa iiŋ ɛɛwɛ naa wia, n daŋ haŋ tɔɔri ia guŋŋ a kim wa tuŋ, ka n jaa gil ia.”

ref: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
text: Denii u jaa la ga pig Filisti hina fɔŋŋa ni, di kpuuzi ba kpila maa, ka chɔ la ga zuu bii bɛl bɔɔ n du Etam.

ref: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
text: Filisti hina la ga chɔɔ Juda di yaari ga dugli bol bɛl banna yir Lɛhi.

ref: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
text: Denii Juda hina pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ba ii wa pig yaai?” Filisti hina ŋɔ, “Yaa ballɔɔ ya wa lau Samsin di ge ɛɛu gunla himmaa uŋ ɛɛ yaa la.”

ref: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
text: Juda hina kagboŋa bɔra fidaahoroo la a bii bɔɔ hiŋ n du Etam, di ga pɛɛzi Samsin, “Bɛɛ i ra ɛɛ yaa gunnɛi? Haa zummɛ lugɔ a Filisti hinaa ra binni yaa nii?” Ka Samsin ŋɔ, “Wii la baŋ kpawɛɛ dawiŋ kinnɛ n kpa turgi baa.”

ref: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
text: Juda hina la ŋɔ u be, “Yaa ballɔɔ ya wa vɔɔzii, di kpai ga tɛɛ Filisti hina la.” Samsin jaa ŋɔ, “Amɔ, ii hɛɛhzi lugɔ ii himmaa wàá kpuŋ.”

ref: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
text: Denii u na kawee handakaraa n ɛɛ u lɛɛ di chɔɔ hɛri, u lawuu kpa di kpu a Filisti hina kagboŋa anue.

ref: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
text: Denii Samsin ŋɔ, “N kpa kawee handakaraarɛ kpu nɛra kagboŋa anue, a handakaraarɛ n kpa di chaali baa dau suge suge.”

ref: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔwɛɛ tuŋ, u kpa a hog di ha. Ba jaa ra yir de Ramaf Lɛhi.

ref: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
text: A saŋa naa, niinyɔgzi jaa lau Samsin werge maa. U lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Hinuu tɛŋ fɔŋŋa n ɛɛ wizenaa naa, di kpegli n dɔma naa. Niinyɔgzi ra nyiŋŋi n kpuirɛ. Di n siuwɔ, nɛra naa n wɛɛ zummɛ naa daŋ ŋɔ ba kpeglimbuu.”

ref: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi gil bɔɔ bɛl pilli Lɛhi, nii lii u biini, Samsin nyɔɔ, fɔŋŋa ba. U jaa dau a bule hiŋ sɔŋ Ɛn Hakɔrɛ. Haali ni zinaa, a bule naa haa du Lɛhi.

ref: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
text: Denii u wia teŋ yaari a Gaza maa lugɔ u du de. Ba lii di ga bar bɔr la un duwɛɛ la maa, di ga so a bolzeŋ dominuuzeŋ la di ra kpaŋuu di chi hamuŋa maa di ra ba hɔpizaa, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ gil hɔpizi, ya lawuu di kpuu.”

ref: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Samsin ra nyiŋŋi haaŋ bɛl banna yir Dɛlila, u du Sɔrɛk Waluu.

ref: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
text: Denii Filisti hina koora ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Murgi Samsin, ú baglii u fɔŋŋa naa dee un dɔɔwɛ naa zɛɛ ani ŋmɛnɛɛ la yaa n niŋ ga di kpegluu di vɔɔzuu, u wia maa pussi. Di i wetto ɛɛ guŋ tɛɛ yaa, yaa bɛl maa daŋ tɛi saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kagboŋ ni kalfa.”

ref: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
text: Denii Dɛlila ga pɛɛzi Samsin, “Bagliŋ i fɔŋŋa naa dee hiŋ dɔɔwɛ naa zɛɛ. Ɛrɛɛ nɛr wer ɛɛ di vɔɔzii, í wia maa pussɛi?”

ref: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
text: Samsin ŋɔ u be, “Di ba haŋ kpa kurhɔŋfalaa aniidaanɛɛ n haa waa hillɛ di vɔɔziŋ, n daŋ jaa gɛrgi alugɔ baal maa.”

ref: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
text: A saŋa, di baala baŋhina suah a dia biini, Dɛlila yiruu di ŋɔ, “Samsin, a Filisti hinaa ra ba, bá wa lawii!” Ka u chaahzi a kurhɔna manaŋ alugɔ ninlau n ɔɔ gbɔgzi gessi u chah la. Awia, u fɔŋŋa la dee un dɔɔwɛ la zɛɛ waa waa liwɛɛ.

ref: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
text: Denii Dɛlila ŋɔ Samsin be, “I yirimbuu gɛnii. I kanni karaa tɛŋ. Jaande maa, ŋɔ n be gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ vɔɔi.”

ref: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
text: Samsin ŋɔ, “Di nɛr maa haŋ kpa ŋmɛŋfalaa baŋ haa waa kpawɛɛ di ɛɛ wiimaa di vɔɔziŋ nɛnnɛ, n daŋ jaa gɛrgi alugɔ baal maa.”

ref: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
text: Awia, Dɛlila kpa ŋmɛŋfalaa di vɔɔzuu, di baala kaa wa suah a dia biini. U yiruu di ŋɔ, “Samsin, a Filisti hinaa ra ba, bá wa lawii!” U jaa chaahzi a ŋmɛnni lii u nonee alugɔ aŋ ɛɛ gessi.

ref: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
text: Denii Dɛlila ŋɔ Samsin be, “Di haŋ chi saŋa maa di ra ba keŋ, i ɔɔ ra yirimbuu gɛnii di ra dariŋ. text: Guŋ jaa gil u ŋɔ u be wii la maa n du de, di ŋɔ, “Ba haa waa fuŋ maa kpawɛɛ di gbɔgzi n nyuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ Naziri la baŋ kpaŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi n lulli hɔpizii maa. Di ba faa haŋ fuŋ n nyuurɛ, keŋ n fɔŋŋa faa li n ni, n gɛrgi lugɔ baal maa.”

ref: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
text: Denii Dɛlila n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ u ŋɔ wiimaanii tɛu la, u tili kali Filisti koora la, di ŋɔ, “Ií kaa bir ba, u ŋɔ n benii wiimaa.” Awia, Filisti hina koora jaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa la di bir ba u be.

ref: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
text: Dɛlila lawuu dau u naazi di faaruu guŋŋ, u chɔɔ dɔɔ. Dɛlila jaa yir baal bɛl ú wa fuŋ Samsin nyuhumpɛttaa aniidaanɛɛ la. U jaa faari di ra gɛrguu, dikuu u fɔŋŋa n lii u ni wia.

text: Denii Samsin ŋɔ balii la n lau u nonii di ra tɛrgi la be, “Gil n chi bɔr la min niŋ wer dɛlli ligzenaa la n lau a vug diizeŋ naa di chiŋŋi naa ń wer dɛlli a ni.”

ref: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.

ref: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”

text: Denii ba baala banue hiŋ lii, di kpa la bolzeŋ Layis. Baŋ ga hel de, ba na lugɔ a nɛra sogoo ni bampirsɔna gunla Saidɔn hina n duwɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔsɔna nɛnnɛ maa la. Wiimaa faa waa baa titte. ref: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
text: Di ii wa hel de, ii daŋ na nɛra la n na fɛ lugɔ tɔɔrɔɔ maa waa huuzi baa. Ii daŋ na hɛrzeŋ la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ du ii nonee, hɛri la n waa kummaa nyaawɛ.”

ref: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.

text: Ba gil ba bichalli ni ba sela ani ba kuna maa tɔ see, ba hiŋ baa di ra la.

ref: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”

The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves.
text: Nɛr maa faa waa baa duglɛɛ ú lɛɛ baa di lii ba dɔma nonee biini. Ba waa Saidɔn hina duglɛɛ, ba ni nɛra maa ge gba faa waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ. Waluu la n dugli Bɛf Rɛhɔb labuu a keŋ bolzeŋ faa du. Denii Dan dee hiŋ jaa kuari a bol ma, di so de.

ref: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
text: Denii Naomi ŋɔ Ruf be, “I dɔŋhiŋ lawaa bittɔɔ ra la u nɛra ni u vuga be la. Awia, í ge gba bir hiŋuu di ra la bol.”

ref: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
text: Ruf ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ firiŋ ń lii i be! Gil n nii ra la. Bɔr la maa hin niŋ la, n ge gba daŋ la de, bɔr la maa hin niŋ ga du, n ge gba daŋ ga du de, í nɛra birgi n nɛra, yaa maa kpau di ra hum Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la.

ref: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
text: Bɔr la maa hin niŋ du siu, denii n ge gba du siu, bá hugiŋ de. Kɔ́raawiizi tɔɔriŋ werge maa, di n wa vɛɛ nua naa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n niibuu naa. Di siu lɛi, kummaa gilɛɛ waa bargi n nii dɔŋa ni.”

ref: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
text: Naomi n wa zummɛ lugɔ Ruf ra nyiŋŋuu u nuu ra la la, waa kaa sɛɛ ŋɔ wiimaa.

ref: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
text: Denii ba nɛra banɛɛ hiŋ lii di ra la, di vol guŋŋ ka haa ga hel Bɛtlihɛm. Baŋ ga helle, a tir a bol hina maa. Haana la n du de la koobi, di ra ŋɔ, “Naomii kennaa?”

ref: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
text: U ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gilɛɛ kaa ra yiriŋ Naomi. Ií jaa ra yiriŋ Mara, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, gillɔɔ de dui du kpol werge maa di tɛŋ.

ref: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
text: Saŋa la miŋ faa lii ii be ɛŋ la, n faa dɔɔwɔɔ werge maa, ka filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi gillɔ n bir ba bol, di kummaa waa kaa hoo n nonee. Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n chɔgi n wia, ka kpa tɔɔrɔɔ tɛŋ kennaa, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii haa ra yiriŋ Naomei?”

ref: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Bɔaz lii Bɛtlihɛm di ba koo wa jaami a huŋhunna, ka ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi hiini ia!” Ba ge sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissii!”

ref: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
text: Denii Bɔaz pɛɛzi nɛr la n na binni a koo ni la, “Anɛɛ biihaannɛ toloori naanɛi?”

ref: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
text: A baal ŋɔ u be, “Toloori la n lii Moab hɛri di hiŋ Naomi ba labuu.

ref: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
text: U ŋɔ n benii, dí, Jaande maa, gil n hiŋ i huŋhunna har, di ra kuuni mia la baŋ kummɛ ka ka la. Chɔɔzi maanii u lii di hum guŋŋ saŋa naa wa hel, ka u jaa zuu bɔsɔŋ naa di ra heezi la.”

ref: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
text: Denii Bɔaz ga ŋɔ Ruf be, “N biihaaŋ, gil n ŋɔ i be. ‘Gilɛɛ kaa wàá la nɛr maa koo di gaa kuuni mia. Haŋ du ɛŋ bɛŋ, i ni biihaana naa ra hum.

ref: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
text: A binni bɔr la baala n na hum la, di ra hiŋ a biihaana har. N ŋɔ a baala benii lugɔ bá gilɛɛ waa ɛɛi wiimaa. Di niinyɔgzi ɔɔ wa lawii, la ga nyɔɔ nii la baŋ dɔɔwɛ wa chiŋŋi la.’ ”

ref: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
text: Ruf giŋŋi di kpa u hile yag hɛri, ka ŋɔ Bɔaz be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ n wia tirii gunnɛi? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra ɛɛ mìŋ́ hɔɔhri naa nɛnnɛi?”

ref: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
text: Bɔaz ŋɔ u be, “N nuu i wia la maa hiŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ i jaari maa Naomii, saŋa la i jaari n siuwɛ la, gunla hiŋ gil i maa ni i mɛɛ, i himmaa hɛri ani i himmaa nɛra, ka wa du nɛra la hiŋ waa zummɛ benii.

ref: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
text: Kɔ́raawiizi hiinii, di tɛi winanaa, dikuu gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia. Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la tɛi daama, dikuu hiŋ ba u be ŋɔ ú jaari i ni wia.”

ref: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
text: Ruf ŋɔ u be, “N dɔɔri, i hiinimbuu. I gillɔɔ n bɔra sɔɔni, hiŋ ŋɔ wia tɛŋ bɔɔiih kennaa, haali miŋ waa i balaa naa n ɛɛ biihaana naa bɛl maa helle gba.”

ref: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
text: Dii saŋa n wa helle, Bɔaz ŋɔ Ruf be, “Ba wa lɛɛ paanuu di ra lii sinnyɛg naa.” Denii u ni a huŋhunna maa wa so, Bɔaz kpa miɔɔzaa tɛu, u di piŋ ka ka a yeŋ.

ref: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
text: Uŋ wa izee ú kaa gaa kuuni mia la, Bɔaz ŋɔ u balaa la be, “Di u wa lizi anla baŋ vɔɔzɛɛ di dauri bɔkpaŋkpaŋa la gba biine, ka ii gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ wiimaa, di waa duu hiihzi.

ref: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
text: Ama waa, ii ɔɔ lau a nyuuni hiŋ yeŋa ligzi a vɔɔlaa hiŋ biine di ra ta, ú ra kuuni, ka gilɛɛ waa pogzi u ni.”

ref: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
text: Ruf kuuni baali la guŋŋ bɔr wa duani, u lɔa, di na a bii kookoo tassazi fi.

ref: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
text: U kpa a baali la bol di ga bagli u jaari maa Naomi ú na gunla maga uŋ kuunee. Ruf kaa kpa diwee la ge uŋ faa diwee ka ka koo la gba tɛu.

ref: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
text: Denii Naomi pɛɛzuu, “Lee i kuuni i mia naa zinaanɛi? Anɛɛ koore i lanɛi? Kɔ́raawiizi kissi nɛr la n nai, di ɛɛi nɛnnɛ naa.” Ruf ŋɔ u be lugɔ baal la banna yir Bɔaz la koore u ga hum a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
text: Naomi ŋɔ u be, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi Bɔaz, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu ra binni nyinee ani lalaa maa ni. Bɔaz ɛɛ yaa lullii di lii diikpaŋ biini, di kaa ɛɛ nɛr la bɛl n dɛkkɛ un niŋ lɛɛ yaa di ra binni.”

ref: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
text: Denii Ruf ŋɔ Naomi be, “Haali u ŋɔ n benii lugɔ n du u huŋhunna la be, di ra la saŋa la ban niŋ wa kum a koo mia maa tuŋ.”

ref: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
text: Naomi ŋɔ, “Wibiire, n biihaaŋ. Di i ni a biihaana danna hum Bɔaz koo, a daŋ du wer werge maa. Di a faa ɛɛ nɛduma bɛl koore, ba daŋ faa ra tɔɔrii werge.”

ref: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
text: Kenne a ɛɛ, Ruf ni baa hum guŋŋ di ga hel saŋa la a baali ni huuti maa kumaa n wa tunnɛ. Ka u ni u jaari maa haa du.

ref: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Naomi pɛɛzi Ruf, “A waa dɛkkɛ miŋ nyiŋŋi jaari tɛi, í dɔɔ dia di soo?

ref: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
text: A liizi baal naa banna yir Bɔaz, i ni u balaa n faa ra hum, u kaa ɛɛ yaa lulli himmaa la wia. Filaŋkeŋ, a nuu n be. Zinaa duana ni, u daŋ du pila, bɔr la banna hɛl u baali la.

ref: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
text: Awia, sɔ nii di kuari i hiŋ nɛnnɛ. Ɛɛ tulaale fɔgli, di kpa i laala la n wesse werge di laali. Di i wa laalɔɔ tuŋ, í la a pila. Ama, gilɛɛ wa gil u waa zum i wia de mɔɔ, di waa diwee di nyɔɔ tuŋ lɛi.

ref: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
text: Ɛɛ ania maa ka zum bɔr la un niŋ chɔɔ. Di u waa chɔɔ dɔɔ, la ga lau u wɛjɛ la un tɔwɛɛ la pilli u naazi paga, ka chɔɔ u naazi zɛɛ. U daŋ ŋɔ i be gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ.”

ref: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
text: Ruf ŋɔ u be, “N daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ naa.”

ref: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
text: Awia, Ruf kpa la Bɔaz pila la, di ga ɛɛ gunla u jaari maa Naomi n faa bagluu la.

ref: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
text: Saŋa la Bɔaz n wa diwee di nyɔɔ siŋ, u bɔra jaa sɔɔnuu la, u la ga chɔɔ u mia la baŋ chaalɛɛ dau la zɛɛ, di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ. Denii Ruf jaa suahzi ɛɛ manaŋ, di la ga lau u wɛjɛ la pilli u naazi paga, ka chɔɔ u naazi zɛɛ.

ref: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
text: Hɛuh n wa hɛɛhzɛɛ, Bɔaz hassi izi. U ŋɔ ú bir, di haannɛ chɔɔ u naazi zɛɛ.

ref: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
text: Bɔaz pɛɛzi, “Anɛɛwɛi?” U ŋɔ, “Minuu i balii Ruf. Lau i wɛjɛ la yeŋ tɔŋ. Hiŋ ɛɛ yaa lulli la wia, a dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ lɛɛŋ di ra binni n ni.”

ref: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
text: Denii Bɔaz ŋɔ Ruf be, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissii. I filaŋkeŋ winanaa naabuu kaali i lugli winanaa la. Haa sɛɛwɛ chɔ ra hiŋ biipɔllaa la n ɛɛ daama hina gɛɛ nyaara.

ref: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
text: A ɛɛ wibiire lugɔ n ɛɛ i lulli la n dɛkkɛ lugɔ n lɛɛi di ra binni la bɛllɛ. Ama, nɛbɛl haa du denii di ɛɛ i lulli himmaa kaaliŋ.

ref: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
text: Awia, du n be hamuŋa naa, ka hɔpizi ya na. Di u daŋ lɛɛi di ra binni i ni, gɛɛ wàá sɛɛ ú ɛɛ guŋ, n hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ miŋwaa daŋ ɛɛ guŋ. Awia, du ɛŋ hɔɔ ra pizi.”

ref: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
text: U du de. Hɔɔŋ waa pizi, u feli izi, di bɔr haa waa chaanɛɛ, nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa nau, dikuubɛɛwiai, Bɔaz faa waa nyiŋŋi nɛr maa zum lugɔ haaŋ wa chɔɔ u pila labuu.

ref: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
text: Denii Bɔaz ŋɔ u be, “Yaa i wɛjɛ pɛ hɛri.” U ɛɛ guŋ. Bɔaz ɛɛ baali kilozi tokko du u biini, di lau chuguu, ka bir kaali bol.

ref: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
text: di kaa ŋɔ, “U ŋɔ n benii lugɔ waa nyiŋŋi ń bir ba i be ni nodumazi. Awiarɛ u tɛŋ baali naa la.”

ref: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
text: Naomi ŋɔ u be, “N biihaaŋ, a di kanyitti, ka ra kpaŋ wii la n niŋ wa ɛɛ. Bɔaz waa ba heezaa zinaa, di waa a wia naa siwee zummɛ.”

ref: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
text: A guŋ saŋa, Bɔaz izi la a bol dominuuzeŋ di ga so de. Denii Ɛlimɛlɛk lulli la Bɔaz n faa ŋɔ u wia lugɔ waabuu dɛkkɛ un niŋ lɛɛ Ruf di ra binni u ni la, ba de. Bɔaz ŋɔ u be, “N dammu, ba wa so ɛŋ.” U ba di wa so.

ref: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
text: Denii Bɔaz yir a bol nabɔnzi fi, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií wa so ɛŋ.” Ba ba wa so.

ref: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
text: Ba maa n wa soge la, u ŋɔ u lulli la be, “Filaŋkeŋ, Naomi n bittɛ lii Moab hɛri ba naa, u ra nyiŋŋuu ú yoo yaa lulli Ɛlimɛlɛk hɛri bɛl.

ref: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
text: N ɛɛ tamii lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ zum a wia. Awia, di i ra nyiŋŋuu, yawuu nabɔnzi ni nɛra naa maa n soge naa see. Ama, di hɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi waa, í ŋɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra la n dɛg a hɛri yawaarɛ n nii, ka hinuu niŋ feli yawuu.” A baal ŋɔ, “N daŋ yawuu.”

ref: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
text: Bɔaz ŋɔ, “Guŋ wesso werge. Di i wetto yau a hɛri lii Naomi be, gunna bagluu lugɔ i kpa Ruf la n ɛɛ Moab hinuu labuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ a hɛri wer du u jaari la n siuwɛ la dee biini, ú sɔŋ gilɛɛ dim.”

ref: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
text: Awia, a baal ŋɔ u be, “Di guŋwaarɛ, màá wer yau a hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, a daŋ bagli lugɔ n biizi wàá wer wa nau, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ. Awia, híŋwaa yawuu.”

ref: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
text: A baal n wa ŋɔ Bɔaz be, “Híŋwaa yawuu.” U lau u gau lizi di tɛɛ Bɔaz.

ref: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
text: Denii Bɔaz ŋɔ nabɔnzi ni nɛra la maa n faa du de la be, “Ii maanii ɛɛ n daansɛɛ hina lugɔ zinaa, n yau kuna la maa n ɛɛ Ɛlimɛlɛk, Kiliɔn ani Malɔn horaa, di lii Naomi be,

ref: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
text: di kaa kpa Ruf la n ɛɛ Moab hina biihaaŋ, u jaari Malɔn n siuwɛ ka kau la gba, ú jaa ɛɛ n haaŋ. A gunnɛ niŋ gil bá kundɔɔlaa gɛɛ a kapɛttɛ du de, di tɛɛ a lalii. Ú sɔŋ wer du u lulla ni u bol hina maa biini. Ii di a keŋ daansɛɛrɛ zinaa.”

ref: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
text: Nabɔnzi la ni nɛra la n du de la ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, yaa ɛɛ i daansɛɛ hinaa. Kɔ́raawiizi gil a haaŋ naa hinna kpa naa ɛɛ lugɔ Rachɛl ani Lia la n faa lul biizi werge, di gil Izrɛl dee wazi la. Í kaa wer dɔɔ werge a dee biini, di dɔɔ chignibɔr Ɛfraf, di kaa dɔɔ sɔŋ Bɛtlihɛm biini.

ref: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
text: Biizi la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ tɛɛ i ni a haaŋ naa la, gil i diahina ɛɛ lugɔ Pɛrɛz diahina, unla n ɛɛ Juda ni Taama biibaal la.” Koori Deevid naanna wia

ref: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
text: Denii Bɔaz kpa Ruf di la u dia. U nuu n wa chɔɔwɛ, Kɔraawiizi hiinuu, u kpogli hia di lul biibaal.

ref: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
text: A haana ŋɔ Naomi be, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ chɔlaarɛ werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, u tɛibuu biibaal, ú ɛɛ i naana zinaa, di ra binni i ni. Kɔ́raawiizi gil ú izi di du kpeg, di dɔɔ sɔnzeŋ Izrɛl hɛri.

ref: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
text: I biibaal haaŋ naa ra nyiŋŋi i wiarɛ werge, awiarɛ u ɛɛ wizeŋ tɛi di kaali baala baniidaanɛɛ n niŋ faa ɛɛ. A biere niŋ wa tɛi miibɔɔfalii, di kaa birgi i lɛɛri, di kpoglii nɛnnɛ, saŋa la hin niŋ wa zɛŋ.”

ref: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
text: Naomi lau a bie la lɛɛ di sag u naazi, di ra dɛɛzuu.

ref: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
text: Haana la n faa du de la dau u sɔŋ Ɔbɛd, ka ra ŋɔ nɛr maa be, “Ba lul biibaallɛ tɛɛ Naomi.” Waabuu wa izee lul Koori Deevid mɛɛ Jɛssɛ la.

ref: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
text: Ɔbɛd ge biibaallɛ Jɛssɛ, Jɛssɛ ge biibaal ɛɛ Koori Deevid.

ref: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.

text: Denii Samuɛl kpa viibee ni ɔlivi nuu, di yiili waari Sɔɔl nyuu, ka faamuu, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizii lizii ŋɔ í ɛɛ u nɛra sitɔɔri. I danna binni u nɛra ni, di guu baa lii ba dɔma maa be. Kenne niŋ bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi liziibuu, í ra binni u nɛra ni.

ref: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
text: Yaa n na ta dɔŋa zinaa naa, i daŋ ga chem baala banɛɛ ni, di ba dugli Rachɛl ŋmam n du Zɛlza, Bɛnjamin magbɔɔ. Ba daŋ ŋɔ i be lugɔ kauzi la hiŋ liwɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi la, ba naabuu. I mɛɛ waa kaa ra fɔŋ a wia. Ka i wiarɛ jaa tiruu, u ra ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ n bie naa wia birɛi?’

ref: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
text: I daŋ vol guŋŋ di ga hel Tabɔ daazeŋ la di chem baala bahoro n na la Bɛtɛl bá ga lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni. Bɛl daŋ chi bupɔla ahoro, bɛl ge chi paanuuzi ahoro, bɛl ge kpogli siŋ ni hur.

ref: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
text: Ba daŋ jaamii, ka tɛi paanuuzi anɛɛ, lɛɛa.

ref: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
text: A harbɔɔ, i daŋ lii de di la Kɔraawiizi Giŋgimii la n du Gibia, bɔr la Filisti laallɔɔra n wa chɔɔwɛ la. Di i wàá dugli a bol, i daŋ chem Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ni baŋ ta chɔŋ, di lii mbusu lizibɔr giŋgimii la nyuu di ra tuu. Ba danna lɔ janjalanzi ni kemzi, di ra huuh tiitoraa, di ra yigzi kuna, bá bɔra ra pur, bá aah siwii di ra sa, di ra chaasi.

ref: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
text: Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma daŋ izii fɔŋŋa ni, í ni baa jaa kpau, i bɔra ra pur, í aah siwii di ra sa, di ra chaasi. Denii í bir kur gunla hiŋ faa duwɛɛ la ni.

ref: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
text: Di daansɛɛ wia naa maa wa ɛɛwɔ tuŋ, ɛɛ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ŋɔ í ɛɛ.

ref: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
text: Tɔ see di ra la Gilgal ń na ba. N daŋ ba wa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu. Awia, ga so de di ra kpaŋiŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ mɔɔ, ka ń ba di wa baglii wii la hin niŋ ɛɛ.”

ref: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
text: Sɔɔl n wa ta Samuɛl ka bir ŋɔ ú kaali, Kɔraawiizi bir Sɔɔl bampirii, daansɛɛ wia naa maa jaa ɛɛ wibii a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
text: Baŋ ga hel Gibia, ba chem Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la ni, di ba ta chɔŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma izuu fɔŋŋa ni, u ni baa maa jaa kpau, u bɔra ra pur, u aah siwii di ra sa, di ra chaasi.

ref: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
text: Banla maa n faa zumuu mɔɔ la, n wa nau unna ɛɛ gunla, ba ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Beedee widizii huuzi Kis biibaal Sɔɔl kennei? U ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la bɛllɛ gɛɛ?”

ref: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
text: Baal bɛl n du de ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi naa mɛɛwaarɛ babɛlaai?” A guŋ jaa ɛɛ wiŋɔɔlii ba ra ŋɔ, “Sɔɔl ge jaa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la biiniaa?”

ref: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
text: Sɔɔl n wa tuŋ sai ani u chaasaa la, u tinni la a giŋgimii nyuu, mbusu lizibɔr la.

ref: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
text: Denii Sɔɔl naara pɛɛzi u ni u balii la, “Lee ii lanɛi?” U ŋɔ, “Yaa volloo ra nyiŋŋi a kauzi la, ka yaa n ga nyiŋŋaa di ra huhzi la, yaa la Samuɛl be.”

ref: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
text: Sɔɔl naara ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ n be wia la maa Samuɛl n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi.”

ref: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
text: Sɔɔl ŋɔ u naara be, “U ŋɔ yaa benii lugɔ ba na a kauzii.” Ka waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ u be lugɔ Samuɛl ŋɔ u daŋ wa di kora waa. Baŋ tɔ Sɔɔl kora wia

ref: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
text: Samuɛl jaa chaali Izrɛl hina maa Kɔraawiizi see Mizpa,

ref: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
text: di ŋɔ ba be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘N lizi iabuu lii Ijip, di kaa lɛɛ ia lii Ijip hina ani hɛssi la maa hina n faa ra tɔɔri ia la nonee biine.’

ref: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, ii jaa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la, n na lɛɛ ia ra lii ii tɔɔrɔɔzi ani anuulazi maa biine labuu. Ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Akai, tɛɛ yaa koori u ra binni yaa.’ Awia, filaŋkeŋ, dee maa ni u domeezi lii di chi ba bɛnaa Kɔraawiizi see bɔnnaa.”

ref: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
text: Samuɛl n wa gillɛ Izrɛl hina dizi hiŋ maa lii chi ba bɛnaa, Bɛnjamin deere Kɔraawiizi lizi lii a dizi maa biini.

ref: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
text: Denii u gil Bɛnjamin dee hiŋ ge lii chi domeezi, Kɔraawiizi lizi Matri domee ba biini, ka a tuna maa, Kis biibaal Sɔɔllɛ u wa lizi. A nɛra binni, ka ba wɔɔ nawɛɛ.

ref: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
text: Awia, ba kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “A keŋ baal naa du yaa biinii ɛnnaa?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, u du ii biinii, ka u suah bunni biinii.”

ref: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
text: Denii ba chɔ la ga kpogluu ba. Uŋ wa ballɛ, di wa chi ba biini, ba binni, di u saagi ba maa ni.

ref: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
text: Samuɛl jaa ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Ií maa na, baal naabuu Kɔraawiizi lizi ú ɛɛ ii koori. U dɔŋ waa hoo ii biini.” Denii a nɛra maa chaasi di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ a koori naa miibɔɔjaŋ!”

ref: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
text: Denii Samuɛl bagli wia la n dɛg a koori ani anla u ge n ninna ɛɛ, di tɛɛ a nɛra maa. Ka sɛbi a maa du hɔŋ biini, di kpaa dau Kɔraawiizi see. Ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, bɛl maa kaali u bol.

ref: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
text: Sɔɔl ge bir kaali u bol Gibia. Nɛkpega baŋhina Kɔraawiizi n bir ba bampiree, duu di la.

ref: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
text: Ka kalu nyiŋŋe baŋhina izi di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ baal naa dɔŋ ɛɛ di wer lɛɛ yaai?” Ba gbɛlluu di vɛɛ u sunzaa, ka Sɔɔl sigli ba ni.

ref: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
text: Ammɔn koori Nahas faa izi di vɔɔ laal, di ga fɔɔ Jabɛs n du Giliad hɛri. Denii a bol baala maa ŋɔ u be, “Gil yaa nii ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, ka ya sɛɛ di ra humii.”

ref: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
text: Ka Koori Nahas ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ guŋ, di ii wa sɛɛ wikpaŋ bɛl min niŋ dau tɛɛ ia. N daŋ foŋ ii bɛl maa nodig sibii, di du Izrɛl hina maa hiihzi.”

ref: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
text: Jabɛs nabɔnzi ŋɔ u be, “Tɛɛ yaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ ya hum balaa, bá vol Izrɛl hɛri maa, di lizi a keŋ amaniye naa tɛɛ a bola hina maa. Di nɛr maa waa wa ballɛ ú wa lɛɛ yaa, guŋwaa, yaa danna sɛɛ i dɔɔra.”

ref: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
text: Ba jaa hum nɛra, baŋ ga hel Sɔɔl bol Gibia, di lizi a keŋ amaniye tɛɛ baa, a nɛra maa n wa nuu guŋ, ba ra chɛɛhgi bɔr maa.

ref: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
text: Banna chɛɛhgi gunla, di Sɔɔl lii koo di hiŋ u navargazi di ra ba. Uŋ wa nuu a chɛɛhgaa, u pɛɛzi baa, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛwɛ ba ra chɛɛhgi kennei?” Denii ba ŋɔ gunla Jabɛs hina n wa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa la, di tɛu.

ref: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
text: Sɔɔl n wa nuu guŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma izuu fɔŋŋa ni, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
text: Denii u lau navargazi anɛɛ, di kpua, di mɔnnaa jigzijigzi, di kpaa hum nɛra, bá gaagi Izrɛl hɛri, di ra sii, di ra ŋɔ, “Di nɛr la maa waa haŋ sɛɛ ú hiŋ Sɔɔl ani Samuɛl, kenne ba mɔnni u ge gba navargazi!” Ɔnsii jaa lau a nɛra werge maa, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ dau baa wia, ba maa lii nyaamm.

ref: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
text: Sɔɔl ni u nabɔnzi ŋɔ balaa la baŋ hummɛ la be, “Ií la ga kali Jabɛs hina be, ‘Kɛrɛ wibaŋa saŋa, ii daŋ na lɛɛi.’ ” Jabɛs hina n wa nuu guŋ, ba bɔra sɔɔni baa werge maa,

ref: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
text: ba ŋɔ Ammɔn hina la be, “Yaa daŋ ba di wa kpa yaa hinaa tɛɛ ia kɛrɛ, ii ɛɛ yaa gunla maa n par ia.”

ref: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Sɔɔl bargi u nɛra hiŋ sugezi ahoro. Chɔɔzimpikke ni, ba vɔɔ di ga pig Ammɔn hina ba chɔɔribɔr, di kpuuzi baa guŋŋ wiizi wa baŋ. Banla n na bahinaa la maa chɔ di yaari, bɛl maa ga u bɛŋ. Baŋ sɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl kora dii wia

ref: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
text: Izrɛl hina ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “Babɛlaarɛ faa ŋɔ Sɔɔl wàá di kora yaa ni lai? Ií ba ba ni ya kpu baa!”

ref: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
text: Ka Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa kpu nɛr maa zinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaabuu Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii ba dɔma nonee biini.”

ref: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
text: Denii Samuɛl ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií ba ya la Gilgal, di kaa ga sɛɛ lugɔ Sɔɔllɛ yaa koori.”

ref: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
text: Awia, a nɛra maa la Gilgal, di ga sɛɛ lugɔ Sɔɔllɛ bá koori, Kɔraawiizi see, ka lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Sɔɔl ani Izrɛl hina maa jaa di bahinaa werge maa, a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
text: Samuɛl ŋɔ Izrɛl hina maa be, “N nuu ii nuarɛ, di ɛɛ wii la iiŋ ŋɔ n ɛɛ la, di tɛɛ ia koori.

ref: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, ii dɔɔ koorii u ɛɛ ii sitɔɔri. Miŋwaa jaa zɛŋuu, n nyuu maa huuhzi, n biibaala ge du ii be. N ɛɛ ii sitɔɔrii lii n pɔlaa saŋa maa guŋŋ di wa lii zinaa.

ref: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
text: Minuu chigɛ la. Di n ɛɛ wii bɛl leu, ii ŋɔ nɛr maa nuu, Kɔraawiizi ni koori naa uŋ lizɛɛ naa see. Anɛɛ navarga gɛɛ kaweere n foozei? Anɛɛ n finei? Anɛɛ n sunnei? Anɛɛ kunaa n lɛɛ, a tɔɔgi n siweei? Di n ɛɛ annii bɛl maa, n daŋ turgi a kim.”

ref: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
text: Samuɛl ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi ni koori la un lizɛɛ la maanii ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hina zinaa, lugɔ ii waa n wichɔgii maa nawɛɛ.” A nɛra sɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, wibiire, Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ.”

ref: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
text: Denii Samuɛl ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Kɔraawiizii faa lizi Moosis ani Aarɔn, ba kpogli ii naabaala di lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
text: Awia, ií chi guŋ, ń bir ia liize Kɔraawiizi see, di liizi ia wizenaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ, di lɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala maa la.

ref: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
text: Jekɔb ni u diahina n faa la Ijip hɛri, ba gaa sunni baa la, ba faa wiiwoo du Kɔraawiizi lugɔ ú hiini baa. Denii Kɔraawiizi hum Moosis ni Aarɔn, ba la ga kpogli ii naabaala lii Ijip hɛri, ba wa so bɔnnaa.

ref: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
text: Ka ba suuh Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la wia, guŋ gil u faa kpa baa di du Sisɛra n ɛɛ bolzeŋ Hazɔr laallɔɔra nabɔma ni Filisti hina ani Moab hina koora nonee biine, ba ba di wa lɔ baa laal, di kpegli baa.

ref: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
text: Denii ba wii du Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi, yaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di vɛɛi, ka ra kuari vug Baala ani vughaaŋ Astɔrɛfzi. Awia, lɛɛ yaa lii yaa dɔma nonee biini, yá ra humii.’

ref: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi hum Gidiɔn, Barak, Jɛfta ani mìŋ́ Samuɛl, di lɛɛ ia lii ii dɔma maa nonee biine, ii jaa so ni bɔsɔna.

ref: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
text: Ka iiŋ wa na Ammɔn Koori Nahas n na ba ú wa lɔ ia laal, ɔnsii lau ia, ii ŋɔ n be, ‘Yaa ra nyiŋŋi koorii ú ra binni yaa ni, haali Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la n ɛɛ ii Koori gba.’

ref: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
text: Di ii ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi, di ra hiŋ u nua, di ra humuu nɛnnɛ, ii waa u widaulaa ra vɛɛ ka ra hiŋaa, di ii ni ii koori la maa n na binni ia la ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ, ii wiimaa daŋ kuari.

ref: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
text: Ka di ii waa hanna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa, ka ra vɛɛa, u daŋ tɛr ii digna gunla uŋ faa tɛr ii naabaala digna la.

ref: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
text: Awia, ii haa chi diindiiŋ, ka ra binni wizeŋ la Kɔraawiizi n na nyiŋŋi ú ɛɛ, ii himmaa siwee na!

ref: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
text: Lumaŋa lɛiyaa? N daŋ suŋŋi wiizi ú gil dooŋ ni nazaa ba. Di guŋ ɛɛwɔ, ii daŋ zum lugɔ ii ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu u ni, dikuu saŋa la iiŋ ŋɔ ú tɛɛ ia koori la wia.”

ref: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
text: Denii Samuɛl suŋŋi wiizi. Kɔraawiizi gil dooŋ ba, di ra pogzi, ɔnsii ani biinichɔg lau a nɛra, dikuu Kɔraawiizi ni Samuɛl wia.

ref: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
text: A nɛra maa ŋɔ Samuɛl be, “Suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la tɛɛ yaa, ya gilɛɛ waa siuzi, dikuu yaa n kaa ɛɛ wichɔgaa jaa, di ŋɔ yaa ra nyiŋŋi koori la wia.”

ref: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
text: Samuɛl ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Haali iiŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa naa maa, ka ii gilɛɛ wa bir har di ra kpu Kɔraawiizi, ka ra humuu ani ii biine maa.

ref: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kaa wa bir di ra hiŋ vuga. A wàá wer hiini ia gɛɛ di lɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛ maa, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ kumpɛɛri wia.

ref: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.

text: Filisti hina chi ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ, ka pozi Jonatan ni a biipɔllii hiŋ ni werge maa, di ŋɔ, “Ií tuzi hel ka na, yaa daŋ bagli ia wii bɛl!” Denii Jonatan ŋɔ a biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna hiŋ be, “Tinni di ra hiŋiŋ. Kɔraawiizi kpa baabuu du Izrɛl hina nonee!”

text: U jaa ŋɔ, “La ga kali baa, dí bɛl maa lau u nauna ni peeza di ba bɔnnaa, di wa kɔrgaa hee. Ií gilɛɛ ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di ra hee ol ni chal.” Bɛl maa jaa lau u navarga a hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa ni, di ba de, di wa kɔrguu.

ref: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.

text: U yoowoo banni ni, di kpegli Amalɛk hina, di lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii banla maa n ɔɔ faa ra lɔ baa laal la nonee biini. Koori Sɔɔl diahina wia

text: U kandaa daa faa lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daarɛ, u nua bɔpupula tɔgzi ge ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaanumbɛl. Nɛr la n na kpogli u laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ uŋ kpawɛɛ di ra teŋ kandaazi ni hobee tɔ u see.

ref: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
text: Goliaf izi chi di pozi Izrɛl hina ni, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii lii di wa chi di ra nyiŋŋi ii yoo laalɛi? Maa Filisti hinuu ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ, ii ge ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl balaa? Ií lizi unla n na yir u hiŋ baal, ú tuu ba n nuu chem dɔŋa.

ref: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
text: Di u wa wetto kpegliŋ di kpuŋ, guŋwaa, yaa daŋ birgi ii balaa. Ka di n ge wa kpegluu di kpuu, ii ge daŋ birgi yaa balaa, di ra hum yaa.

ref: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
text: Awia, Izrɛl laallɔɔra, ií ba ya karsi dɔŋa zinaa! Ií lizi unla n ŋɔ u ɛɛ baallɛ, ú ba n nuu lɔ dɔŋa!”

ref: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
text: Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra la n wa nuu a Filisti hinuu wiŋɔzi hiŋ, ɔnsii jaa lau baa werge maa, ba bɔra ra sa.

ref: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
text: Deevid faa ɛɛ Ɛfraf hinuu Jɛssɛ biibaallɛ di lii Bɛtlihɛm n du Juda hɛri. Jɛssɛ biibaala faa du ŋmantannaazi. Koori Sɔɔl de dui saŋa la, u faa zɛŋŋɔɔ werge maa.

ref: the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army. David was Jesse's youngest son.
text: Deevidii faa ɛɛ bichala Jɛssɛ biibaala biini. U biibambinabɔnzi bahoroo faa hiŋ Koori Sɔɔl la.

ref: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
text: Ka Deevid waa ɔɔ lii Koori Sɔɔl be, di ra ba Bɛtlihɛm, di waa binni u mɛɛ peeza ka bir ra la.

ref: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
text: Hɔpizii maa chɔɔzi ni duana, Goliaf naa ɔɔ faa liiu chi di ra ŋɔ Izrɛl hina ba, bá karsi dɔŋa, guŋŋ hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ.

ref: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
text: Denii u kpa u penɔɔni kpala di tuu gɔŋ biini, di hɔɔzi loglogbia anue, di du u hur la uŋ ɔɔ laali di ra nɔɔni u peeza la biini, ka jaa kpogli u bilori di tuzi di ra hel Filisti hinuu hiŋ.

ref: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Jɛssɛ ŋɔ u biibaal Deevid be, “Kpa mihallaa kookoo tassazi fi naa ani paanuubire fi naa, di hahzi ga tɛɛ i kpɛɛnna, a laal bɔr.

ref: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
text: Kpa waagazi fi naa, di jaa ra la ga tɛɛ ba nabɔma la n na binni ba ni la. Binni i kpɛɛnna hiŋ di na gunla baŋ duwɛɛ, gil kumbɛl hiŋii lii ba be ba, ń zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ ba du denii.

ref: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
text: Ba du Koori Sɔɔl ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa be, Ɛla Waluu biini, di ra yoo Filisti hina laal.”

ref: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Deevid izi di vɔɔ u bunni di kpa lii ra la, gunla u mɛɛ n ŋɔ u be la, ka jaa gil a peeza hiŋ di du penɔɔni bɛl nonee. Uŋ ga hel bá chɔɔribɔr bɔr, di ba kaa ɛɛ sirya bá ga chi ba chignibɔra, di ra lɔ laal wile.

ref: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
text: Izrɛl laallɔɔra ni Filisti laallɔɔra jaa chi ba chignibɔra, di chaŋ dɔŋa.

ref: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
text: Deevid chug u bunni di chiŋŋi nɛr la n na binni ba kuna di ra tɛɛ baa be, ka chɔ di hel a laal bɔr di ga jaami u kpɛɛnna hiŋ.

ref: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
text: U ni baa n na ŋɔ wia la, di Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hina kpegleg di lii Gaf la liiwɔɔ chi, di ra karsi Izrɛl hina gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la. Deevid nuu guŋ.

ref: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
text: Izrɛl hina n wa nau, ɔnsii werge lau baa, ba chɔ lii u be.

ref: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
text: Izrɛl hina jaa ra ŋɔ, “Ií na a baal! U ɔɔ liiu di ra gbɛlli Izrɛl hina. Nɛr la maa n niŋ wer kpuu, koori ŋɔ u daŋ tɛu daama werge. U daŋ kaa kpa u biihambie ge tɛu, ú ɛɛ haaŋ, di lizi lampoo turgaa lii u mɛɛ dia, Izrɛl hɛri.”

ref: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
text: Deevid pɛɛzi a nɛra la n chigɛ dugluu la, “Bɛɛ bá ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr la n niŋ wer kpu Filisti hinuu naa, di lizi hiihzi naa Izrɛl hina ninɛi? Anɛɛ unla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa, lugɔ u danna gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa laallɔɔrai?”

ref: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
text: Ba bir ŋɔ u be wii la ban niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ baal la n niŋ kpu Goliaf.

ref: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
text: Deevid kpɛɛma Ɛliab nuu u ni baala la n na ŋɔ wia, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ i ba ɛŋ í wa ɛɛi? Anɛɛ i gil a petama la tɛɛ a hɛribɔduma biinei? N zummɔ hinna tɔgzi i hiŋ, di dɔɔ biinikpola. A laal naa lɔi binnaa bɛŋ wiarɛ i kuu ba ɛŋ!”

ref: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? A waa dɛkkɛ min niŋ wer pɛɛzi wii bɛlaa?”

ref: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
text: Denii u jaa bir pɛɛzi nɛbɛl a wii himmaa ni u nyuu. U ge kaa ŋɔ u be gunla himmaa banla n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
text: Denii a nɛra baŋhina nuu gunla Deevid n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di la ga ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, u hum ŋɔ bá ga yiruu.

ref: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
text: Deevid ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ ra ɔm Filisti hinuu naa! N daŋ la ga yoou.”

ref: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
text: Sɔɔl ŋɔ u be, “I ɛɛ bichalaa lugɔ i ni baal naa wer yoo. U ɛɛ laallɔɔrii lii u pɔlaa saŋa maa guŋŋ wa lii zinaa.”

ref: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
text: Ka Deevid ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, mìŋ́ i balii ra binni n mɛɛ peezaa. Di bunyiŋ gɛɛ munu haŋ wa lau a peeza bɛl maa di ra kaali,

ref: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
text: n ɔɔ duŋŋuubuu di ga lɔu ta ka lɛɛu. Di u haŋ wa bir ú lawiŋ ge, n ɔɔ lau u hunaa ka lɔɔzuu kpu.

ref: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
text: N ɔɔ weruu kpu bunyinzi ani munuzi maa. Gunnɛ ń wer kpu Filisti hinuu naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa gba, dikuu unna gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa laallɔɔra wia.

ref: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
text: Kɔraawiizi la n lɛɛŋ lii bunyinzi ani munuzi maa be la, daŋ lɛɛŋ lii Filisti hinuu naa gba be.” Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “A la, Kɔ́raawiizi du i be.”

ref: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
text: Denii Sɔɔl kpa u himmaa laal laala tɛɛ Deevid, di kaa kpa u danyɛ kahuro ge tɛu, u hi.

ref: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
text: Deevid kpa Sɔɔl tokobi di vɔɔ mari a laala, ka waa wette ú vol, dikuu uŋ wàá laalɛɛ mani wia. U ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, màá wer laali a laala, dikuubɛɛwiai, a waŋ manɛɛ.” Awia, u jaa wiraa.

ref: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
text: Goliaf ge lii di ra chem Deevid ni, ka nɛr la ge n kpogli ú laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ la tɔ u see di ra ba.

ref: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
text: Baŋ waa dugluu, u binni Deevid di u ɛɛ bichala, di kaa ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ di dɔɔ alaanfia nɛnnɛ jaa, u ra gbɛlluu.

ref: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
text: Denii u ŋɔ Deevid be, “Nuahinnɛ miŋ, i kpa kpala di ra ba n bee?” Ka jaa yirgi u vuga di ra see Deevid nua,

ref: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
text: di ŋɔ u be, “Ba ɛŋ ń kpui tɛɛ zumbizi ani pir sela a di!”

ref: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
text: Deevid ge ŋɔ Goliaf be, “I kpa kandaa ni tokobii di ra ba n be, ka miŋwaa ra ba i benii ani Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, n ɛɛ Izrɛl laallɔɔra Kɔraawiizi la hiŋ gbɛllɛɛ la sɔŋ biinii.

ref: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
text: Zinaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kpai du n nonee biini, ń kpui, di teŋ i nyuu, ka kpuuzi i laallɔɔra tɛɛ zumbizi ni pir sela, á di. Denii durnya hina maa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la du denii.

ref: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
text: Banla maa ge n chaali bɔnnaa zum lugɔ tokobi ni kandaa lɛi Kɔraawiizi kpa di ra lɛɛ nɛra. A laal ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte, u daŋ kpa ii maa du yaa nonee biini.”

ref: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
text: Ka jaa hau u hur biini di lizi bii du u bilori, di viguu, ka tau, u ga lɔ Goliaf hile di harmi zuu, u chol hɛri pi.

ref: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
text: Deevid faa kpu Goliaf ani bilori, di waa tokobi kpawɛɛ.

ref: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
text: Denii Deevid kɛɛhzi ga chi guali Goliaf ni, di pam Goliaf tokobi, di kpuu. Uŋ wa kpuu tuŋ, u kpa a tokobi teŋ u nyuu. Filisti hina n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba kpegleg siuwɔɔ, ba bir kɛɛhzi.

ref: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
text: Izrɛl ni Juda hina la chaasi, ka duŋŋi baa guŋŋ ga hel Gaf ani Ɛkrɔn dominuuzi. Banla baŋ kpuuzɛɛ ge chɔɔgi Saaram ŋmɛnɛɛ, guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛkrɔn ni Gaf.

ref: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
text: Izrɛl hina gil a Filisti hina duŋŋaa, ka bir ba di wa paagi ba kuna maa ba chɔɔribɔr la.

ref: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
text: Deevid kpa Goliaf nyuu di ba Jɛrusalɛm, ka kpa u dɔŋkuna la ge di dau u himmaa tanti dia biini.

ref: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
text: Deevid n na la ú ga chem Goliaf ni la, Koori Sɔɔl binnuu, ka pɛɛzi u laallɔɔra maa nabɔma Abna, “Anɛɛ biere a biipɔllii naanɛi?” Abna bir ŋɔ, “Jara, maa zum nɛr la biibaal n ɛɛu.”

ref: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
text: A koori ŋɔ, “Pɛɛzi nɛr la biibaal n ɛɛu.”

ref: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
text: Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzuu, “Biipɔllii, anɛɛ biere hinnɛi?” Deevid ŋɔ, “Jara, n mɛɛrɛ i balii Jɛssɛ di lii Bɛtlihɛm.”

ref: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
text: Di haŋ chi a hɔl hiŋ, Koori Sɔɔl gil Deevid du u be. Waa kaa sɛɛ ú la ga du u mɛɛ dia.

ref: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
text: Denii Jonatan ni Deevid jaa ɛɛ dammunaa nuukpaŋ, dikuu Jonatan n nɔŋŋuu alugɔ u hiŋ wia.

ref: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
text: Jonatan wir u tagtajaŋ bɛl uŋ laalɛɛ, tɛɛ Deevid, di kaa kpa u laal tagta, u tokobi, u hoo ani u kurhɔŋ di tɛu.

ref: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
text: Wii la maa Koori Sɔɔl n ɔɔ hum Deevid ŋɔ ú ɛɛ, ɔɔ ɛɛubuu nɛnnɛ. Koori Sɔɔl jaa gil u ɛɛ u laallɔɔra nabɔma. Guŋ sɔɔni a nɛra ni Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi maa bɔra.

ref: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
text: Deevid n wa kpu Goliaf, ka a laallɔɔra maa bir di ra ba bol la, Izrɛl hɛri bola haana maa lii, di yir yira di ra sa di ra lɔ kemzi, di ra yigzi kuna di ra chem Koori Sɔɔl ni ani bɔsɔna.

ref: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
text: Banna sa la, ba ra yir yira di ra ŋɔ, “Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa, Deevid ge kpu kagboŋa fizi.”

ref: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
text: Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuu gunla banna yir la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa. U fɛ u biini, “Ba ra tɛɛ Deevidii kagboŋa fizi, ka ra tɛŋ kagboŋa bɛŋ, bɛɛ bá kaa tɛu di a kora lɛiyɛi?”

ref: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi gil tinnanchɔgii ba di wa izi Koori Sɔɔl kpegzi ni. U ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ u dia biini. A saŋa di Deevid ge sogo di ra lɔ u kem gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra lɔu saŋa maa la. Di Koori Sɔɔl ge kpogli u kandaa.

ref: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biini, “N daŋ yag Deevid pɛli koŋlii.” U tau, ka Deevid du gbaŋ, u tau kir bunɛɛ maa.

ref: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
text: Koori Sɔɔl faa ra ɔm Deevid, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du u be ka kizi waabuu Sɔɔl ha wia.

ref: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
text: Wii la maa Deevid n ɔɔ ɛɛ, ɔɔ ɛɛubuu nɛnnɛ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du u be wia.

ref: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
text: Ka Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa nɔŋŋi Deevid werge, dikuu uŋ ɔɔ tɔ ba see laal biini, ba ra kpegli ba dɔma wia.

ref: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
text: A hɔl bɛl Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “N daŋ kpa n biihambinabɔma Mɛrab tɛi. Ka n na nyiŋŋuu lugɔ í humiŋ nɛnnɛ, di kaa yoo Kɔraawiizi laalzi di jaa.” Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biini, “Màá kpa n nonii gbɔgzuu, ka n daŋ gil Filisti hina ɛɛ guŋ!”

ref: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
text: Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Anɛɛ miŋ gɛɛ n domee gɛɛ n mɛɛ diahina, Izrɛl hina biini lugɔ ń ɛɛ koori hilai?”

ref: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
text: Ka Mɛrab kpai n wa helle, u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl waa kaa sɛɛ kpau tɛɛ Deevid gunla uŋ felee ŋɔ la. Ka bir gil Adriɛl la n lii Mɛhɔla la kpau.

ref: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ bɛl banna yir Mikal, ge bampirii bir lau Deevid, u ra nyiŋŋuu. Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl, u bɔra sɔɔnuu.

ref: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
text: U ŋɔ u biini, “N daŋ gil ú kpau. A guŋ daŋ tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń kpau du Filisti hina nonee biini, bá kpuu.” Ka jaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “I kaa na bɔttɛ lugɔ í ɛɛ n hila.”

ref: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
text: Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi la n wa ŋɔ u be gunla Deevid ge n ŋɔwɛɛ,
