ref: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
text: Koori Sɔɔl ge kaa ŋɔ, “Ií la ga ŋɔ Deevid be lugɔ hila kuna la minna nyiŋŋi u be maanii lugɔ, ú ga kpu Filisti hina baala kalfa, di mɔnni ba hɛna hɔna wa tɛŋ, di turgi n dɔma wichɔgaa kim.” Ka Koori Sɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ Filisti hina kpu Deevid.

ref: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
text: A nabɔnzi n kaa ba Deevid be di wa ŋɔ gunla maa Koori Sɔɔl n ŋɔwɛɛ la, u bɔra jaa sɔɔnuu werge maa un niŋ ɛɛ koori hila wia Mɔɔ ka u haaŋ kpai hɔpizii wa hel,

ref: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
text: Koori Sɔɔl n wa zummɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du Deevid benii, u biihaaŋ Mikal ge kaa ra nyiŋŋuu la,

ref: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
text: u Deevid ɔmaa jaa bir nyaŋŋi, u ɛɛ u dɔm u de dui maa.

ref: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
text: Filisti laallɔɔra sitɔɔra la ɔɔ haa lii di ba waa lɔ baa laal. Saŋa maa, di ba haŋ wa ba, Deevid ɔɔ lii di kpu baa werge maa, kaali Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra sitɔɔra la bɛl maa, guŋ gil u dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa.

ref: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
text: A hɔl bɛl Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u biibaal Jonatan ani u nabɔnzi be lugɔ bá la ga kpu Deevid. Ka Jonatan ge faa nɔŋŋi Deevid wia werge maa, a guŋ waa u bɔra sɔɔnɛɛ.

ref: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
text: N daŋ gil n ni n mɛɛ wa chi pir bɔr la hin niŋ suah la paga, ka ń ŋɔ i wia tɛu, di nuu gunla un niŋ ŋɔ. Di u wa ŋɔ wii maa, n daŋ wa ŋɔ i be.”

ref: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
text: U kpa u miibɔɔrɛ chɛr siu, gunla uŋ wette kpu Goliaf la. Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ gunnɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa kpegli ba dɔma. I na guŋ, i bɔra sɔɔni. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ í ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di kpu nɛnanii pɛɛpɛɛi?”

ref: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
text: Koori Sɔɔl nuu gunla maa Jonatan n ŋɔwɛɛ la, di jaa hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ màá ka kpu Deevid.”

ref: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
text: Denii Jonatan yir Deevid, di bagli wia la maa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u mɛɛ, dikuu u wia la. Ka jaa kpogluu ba u mɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl be, u nuu kaa du ú dia gunla baŋ faa duwɛɛ saŋa maa la.

ref: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
text: Denii laal kaa izi, Deevid la ga lɔ Filisti hina werge maa, ba maa chɔ yaari.

ref: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
text: Koori Sɔɔl tau kandaa, di fɛ lugɔ u vii yaguu di mari koŋlii, ka Deevid du gbaŋ, u tau kir, ka a kandaa ga yag koŋlii di baŋ de. A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa maanii Deevid chɔ lii di ga suah.

ref: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
text: Koori Sɔɔl lizi nɛra bá la Deevid dia di ga guu, di u wa izoo chɔɔzi ni, bá kpuu. Ka u haaŋ Mikal n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ u be, “Di haa haŋ chɔ di suah hamuŋa naa ka hɔpizi, ba daŋ kpui.”

ref: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
text: Awia, Mikal hiinuu, u ga tokoro lii, di chɔ ga suah.

ref: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
text: Denii Mikal kpa vug dau u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni, di kpa buuŋ huna di bɔg u nyuu, ka kpa wɛjɛ tɔu.

ref: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
text: Koori Sɔɔl n hum u balaa lugɔ ba ga lau Deevid ba, baŋ ga helle, Mikal ŋɔ ba be lugɔ u ra wiiu.

ref: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl kaa hum u balaa hiŋ, dí ba bir la ga binni Deevid na, ka ŋɔ ba be, “Ií lalli u ni u kunchɔɔrikuŋ maa ba, ń kpuu.”

ref: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
text: Ka u balaa hiŋ n kpawɛɛ di ga zuu ŋɔ ba binni, di vugrɛ chɔɔ a kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni, buuŋ huna tɔ ú nyuu.

ref: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
text: Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzi Mikal, “Ɛrɛɛ i dariŋ kennaa, di gil n dɔm lii di chɔ kaalɛi?” Denii Mikal ŋɔ u be, “U ŋɔ n benii lugɔ di maa haŋ gil u chɔ, u daŋ kpuŋ.”

ref: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
text: Denii Deevid chɔ la Samuɛl be Rama, di ga ŋɔ u be wii la maa Koori Sɔɔl n ɛɛu. U ni Samuɛl kpa di la yembɛl banna yir Nayɔf, di ga so de.

ref: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
text: Denii Sɔɔl nuu lugɔ Deevid du Nayɔf n du Rama.

ref: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
text: Awia, u hum u balaa dí ba ga lawuu ba. Baŋ ga hel de, ba na Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi n chaali bɔkpaŋ di ra sa, ka ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Samuɛl faa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri. Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi Duma izi baa, ba ge jaa ra ŋɔ a guŋ wiŋɔzi.

ref: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
text: Ba ba wa ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be gunla maa n du de. Denii u kaa lizi nɛra, di hum ba ge de himmaa, baŋ ga hel de, ba ge kaa ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini.

ref: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
text: A tuna maa, u himmaa izi di ra la Rama. Uŋ ga hel kɔlɔŋzeŋ la n du yembɛl banna yir Sɛku, u pɛɛzi, “Lee Samuɛl ni Deevid duɛi?” Ba ŋɔ u be, “Ba du Nayɔf n du Rama.”

ref: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
text: Unna la de la, Kɔraawiizi Duma izi u gba. U ra sa ka ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ waa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini guŋŋ di ga hel Nayɔf.

ref: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
text: Uŋ ga hel de, u wir u koori tagtazi, ka chi Samuɛl see di ra sa, di ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Gunnɛ u kpogli di chɔɔ guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi. Banla n na guŋ ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Koori Sɔɔl ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la bɛllɛ gɛɛ?”

ref: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
text: Denii Deevid chɔ lii Nayɔf n du Rama, di la Jonatan be di ga pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ n ɛɛ di zuu i mɛɛ ni, u ra nyiŋŋi ú lizi n miibɔɔi?”

ref: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
text: Jonatan ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi la a ni bɔɔnɛɛ! Hàá siu! Na, n mɛɛ wàá sɛɛ ɛɛ wizeŋ gɛɛ wijiga maa, di waa n be ŋɔwɛɛ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ú kpa annii suah n ninɛi? Wibii lɛi!”

ref: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
text: Ka Deevid hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ, “Wibii maa, i mɛɛ zum gunla hinna nyiŋŋi n wiarɛ werge maa, aabuu gillɛ u ŋɔ, ‘Màá gil Jonatan zum gunla minna fɛ. Di u zummɔ, u biini daŋ chɔgi werge maa.’ N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ n ni siu waa kaa du nɛɛ.”

ref: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
text: Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “Wii la maa hinna nyiŋŋi, n daŋ ɛɛu.”

ref: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Na, kɛrɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii, a dɛg lugɔ n ni koori kpau di. Ama, gil ń la pir, di di ga nyiŋŋi bɔr suah, di ra ba hɔbil duana ni.

ref: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
text: Di i mɛɛ wa nyiŋŋiŋ huhzi ka ra pɛɛzi n wia, ŋɔ u be, ‘Deevid suŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ ú la u bol Bɛtlihɛm, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba dɔɔ ba domee bina maa mbusu lizaarɛ.’

ref: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
text: Di u wa ŋɔ, ‘Guŋ wesso,’ amɔ, i balii daŋ na u hiŋ. Ka di u baaŋ haŋ wa fuuh waa, guŋwaa, u ra nyiŋŋi n kpuirɛ wibii maa.

ref: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
text: Ɛɛ ania maa ka suŋ n ni, dikuu nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi be la wia. Di n hor waa sum, amɔ, í himmaa kpuŋ! Ka gilɛɛ waa kpaŋ di ra du i mɛɛ nonee biini, ú kpu.”

ref: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
text: Jonatan ŋɔ, “Akai, màá sɛɛ ɛɛ guŋ! Di n zummɔ tama maa lugɔ n mɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi i kpuirɛ wibii maa, màá ŋɔ i bee?”

ref: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
text: Denii Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “Gil ya la pir.” Ba la.

ref: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
text: Jonatan kaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ! Hɔbil saŋa naa dɔŋ, n daŋ pɛɛzi n mɛɛ i wia, di nuu gunla un niŋ ŋɔ. Di u wa ŋɔ winanii maa, n daŋ gil i nuu.

ref: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
text: Ka di n mɛɛ wa fɛ i kpui wia, ka n vɛɛ i be ŋɔi, í chɔ lɛɛ i hiŋ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ. Kɔ́raawiizi du i be gunla uŋ faa du n mɛɛ be la.

ref: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
text: Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ n lulla nɔŋŋaa, haali di Kɔraawiizi waa chɔgi hìŋ́ Deevid dɔma maa dee nyaamm, a hɛri naa biini.

ref: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
text: Gilɛɛ waa gil n nii nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ la wàá chɔgi. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, Kɔ́raawiizi tɛr i digni.”

ref: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
text: Denii Jonatan kaa gil Deevid ŋɔ nua lugɔ ú nɔŋŋuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, Jonatan nɔŋŋi Deevidii alugɔ u hiŋ.

ref: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
text: Jonatan kaa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Kɛrɛ daŋ ɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii. Hàá du de, nɛra na guŋ, dikuu i sognibɔr n niŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ wia.

ref: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
text: Hɔbil, di bɔr waa duani, chɔ di ga suah bɔr la hiŋ faa ga suahwɛ, saŋa la wia naa n faarɛɛ la, di gaa kpaŋiŋ bii Ɛzɛl zɛɛ.

ref: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
text: N daŋ ta hobee ahoro di du de paga alugɔ miŋ na kumbɛl, di ra tau la.

ref: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
text: Denii ń hum biibambie lugɔ ú la ga nyiŋŋi a hobee ba. Di n haŋ wa ŋɔ u be, ‘Binni keŋkere naa, denii a hobee du, paagaa ba.’ Guŋwaa, a ba. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ wiimaa waa hoo un niŋ ɛɛi, siaahmu waa hoo.

ref: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
text: Ka di i haŋ wa nuu miŋ ŋɔ a biibambie be lugɔ a hobee du seere, guŋwaa chɔ di ra la bɔɔnɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii ra lizii a siaahmu biini la.

ref: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
text: Ama, wia la yaa n ŋɔwɛɛ la, a liizaa, di zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ yaa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
text: Denii Deevid suah a pir biini guŋŋ a Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ Dii wa hel. Koori Sɔɔl la ga so ú di a diwee.

ref: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
text: U so u sognibɔr gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra so saŋa maa, di pɛli koŋlii, u ni Jonatan chaŋ dɔŋa. Abna ge so di hiŋ Sɔɔl ni. Ka Deevid waa sognibɔr la chɔɔ pɛɛ.

ref: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Koori Sɔɔl waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Deevid ɛɛ wiibɛllɛ di doŋ Kɔraawiizi be, awiarɛ waa ballɛ.

ref: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, a Baagufalii Hɔpizeŋ Dii hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ hɔl, di Deevid sognibɔr la haa chɔɔ pɛɛ. Denii Koori Sɔɔl jaa pɛɛzi u biibaal Jonatan, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ, dɛɛla ni zinaa maa, Jɛssɛ biibaal waa ballɛ ú wa dei?”

ref: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
text: U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Gil ń la, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa diahina dɔɔ mbusu lizaarɛ bol, n kpɛɛma ge ŋɔ ń ba. Di n wia parii, gil n la ga na n lulla.’ Awiarɛ waa diiribɔr ballɛ la.”

ref: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl baaŋ fuuh Jonatan ni werge maa. U ŋɔ, “Hìŋ́ hahjaga ni dignikpega hiŋ biibaal naa! Filaŋkeŋ n jaa zumuu nɛnnɛ lugɔ i chigɔ Deevid hattɛ. I kpa hiihzii di kpu i hiŋ ani i maa!

ref: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
text: Di Jɛssɛ biibaal naa daŋ haŋ du durnya naa ni miibɔɔ, haa ba kora naa dii maa. Hum bá ga yiruu filaŋkeŋ maa u ba. A dɛkkɔɔ ú siu!”

ref: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
text: Jonatan pɛɛzi u mɛɛ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ŋɔ i kpuuwɛi? Bɛɛ u ɛɛi?”

ref: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
text: Ka Koori Sɔɔl ta Jonatan kandaa, ú vii kpuu. Denii Jonatan jaa zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ u mɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi Deevid kpuirɛ, wibii maa.

ref: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
text: Jonatan baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u lɔ izi a diwee zɛɛ. A hɔl hiŋ waa, Jonatan waa kummaa diwee. U biini chɔgi werge, dikuu u mɛɛ hiihnyaai wia la uŋ ɛɛ Deevid la wia.

ref: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
text: Chɔɔzi ni, Jonatan izi di la a pir, Deevid be, gunla baŋ ta jina la. Unna la la, u lau biibambijiga di hiŋ u hiŋ.

ref: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
text: Denii u ŋɔ a bie be, “Chɔ la ga nyiŋŋi hobee naa min niŋ ta naa ba.” A bie n na la la, u ta hobii du u see.

ref: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
text: A bie n wa hel bɔr la Jonatan n ta a hobii u chol la, Jonatan yiruu, di ŋɔ, “A hobii haa du see!”

ref: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
text: Denii u pozi werge maa di ŋɔ, “A chɔ manaŋ di ga kpau, gilɛɛ waa chi!” A bie la ga kpau di bir ba di wa tɛɛ u dɔɔri hiŋ.

ref: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
text: A bie waa faa waa zum wii la n na ɛɛ. Jonatan ni Deevid bɛnnɛ faa zum wii la banna ɛɛ.

ref: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
text: Jonatan jaa kpa u dɔŋkuna di tɛɛ a bie, ka ŋɔ, “Kpaa di bir a kpo bol.”

ref: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
text: A bie n wa kaalɛɛ tuŋ, Deevid faa izi lii a bii wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, di ba Jonatan be, di wa tognuu buhoro, di willi u nyuu. Ka ba jaa faami dɔŋa di ra wii. Ka Deevidii faa wiiwe werge.

ref: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
text: Jonatan ŋɔ Deevid be, “A la ani bɔsɔna, yaa ŋɔ dammunaa nuarɛ tɛɛ dɔŋa Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini. Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ n nii maa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di kaa ɛɛ i naanna ani n ge naanna maa daansɛɛ hiŋ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.” Denii Deevid kaali, ka Jonatan bir kpo.

ref: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
text: Deevid kpa la Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, bol bɛl banna yir Nɔb. Ahimɛlɛk n wa nau, u hassi, u bɔra ra sa, u pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra vol i bɛnnɛi? Ɛrɛɛ nɛr maa waa i ni jaawɛi?”

ref: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, “Koorii humiŋ di ŋɔ n wa ɛɛ wii bɛl, di ŋɔ n be, ‘Gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa wàá zum a widee.’ Ama, n kali n laallɔɔraa bá ra chemiŋ yembɛl.

ref: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
text: Bɛɛ diweere i dɔɔi? Tɛŋ paanuuzi anue gɛɛ kunla maa hin niŋ wer na.”

ref: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ŋɔ Deevid be, “Maa paanuuduma maa dɔɔwɛ, see paanuunanaananaa la baŋ ɔɔ chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la bɛnnɛ du de, di i laallɔɔra la ni haana waa chɔɔwɛ waa, lɛɛ ga tɛɛ baa.”

ref: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
text: Deevid ŋɔ, “Wibiiire, yaa ni haana waa ɔɔ ra chɔɔ di yaa haŋ wa ɛɛ sirya lugɔ ń lii. Ba haŋ wa ŋɔ ba vol voldumazi gba, ka ba ni haana waa ɔɔ ra chɔɔ, di gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi volaa naa dɔŋ!”

ref: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la kpa a paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, a binaa di wa tɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa kpa a falaarɛ di wa dau a teebulnaniinanii ni, ka lizaa.

ref: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
text: A hɔl naa, di Koori Sɔɔl penɔɔna nabɔma banna yir Dɔwɛg n ɛɛ Ɛdɔm hinuu du de, di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
text: Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk, “Haa kandaa gɛɛ tokobi maa dɔɔwɛ ɛŋŋ? Maa dɔŋkuŋ maa ni ballɛ, dikuu a koori huma la n ɛɛ siaahmu werge maa wia.”

ref: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la ŋɔ, “Tokobi la n ɛɛ Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hinuu, hiŋ kpuwɛɛ Ɛla Waluu labuu du ɛŋ. Waabuu ba kpa yakɔza di bɔɔri, u teli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagtakpurii la har. Di i ra nyiŋŋuu, í kpa. Tokobi maa waa hoo ɛŋ, di u bɛŋ lɛi.” Deevid ŋɔ, “Tokobi maa waa hoo lugɔu, kpau tɛŋ!” Deevid n du Gaf wia

ref: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Deevid chɔ lii Koori Sɔɔl be, di kaali Gaf Koori Akis be.

ref: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
text: Ka Koori Akis balaa ŋɔ u be, “Deevid naa lɛi ɛɛ hɛri naa koori laa? Waa lɛi ba kpa du yira, baŋ ɔɔ waa sa, di ra yir, ‘Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa, ka Deevid kpu kagboŋa fizi laa?’ ”

ref: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
text: Deevid kpa a wia hiŋ maa di du u biini, ɔnsii jaa lawuu werge maa dikuu Gaf Koori Akis wia.

ref: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
text: Uŋ faa du ba nonee biini la, u ɔɔ kutti ɛɛ u hiŋ lugɔ nɛr nyuu n waa hoo, di ra ɛɛ wia lugɔ chuglahiŋ, di ra piizi ba dominuuzenaa gbessi, di gil u nuuhaari pal di ra tuu u taŋhuna ni.

ref: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
text: Koori Akis ŋɔ u nabɔnzi la be, “Ií na a baal naa! U nyuu waa hoo, bɛɛ wiarɛ ii kpogluu di wa tɛnnɛi?

ref: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
text: N nyaa chugla hinaa lugɔ ii kaa kpogli baal naa wa tɛŋ, u ra ɛɛ wia naa dizi n sibɔɔ? A dɛkkɔɔ a baal naa dɔŋ n waa zuu n diaa?”

ref: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
text: Deevid lii bolzeŋ Gaf di chɔ la ga zuu bii bɔɔ bɛl n du Adulam. U kpɛɛnna, u mɛɛ ani ba diahina maa n wa nuu u wia de, ba maa la ga du u be de.

ref: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
text: Banla maa n ɛɛ anuula hina, kindiire ani biinichɔg hina ba, di wa chaali, u birgi ba sitɔɔri. Baala la n faa du u be la du lugɔ kalfaanaazu.

ref: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
text: Deevid lii de di la Mizpa la n du Moab hɛri la, di ga ŋɔ de koori be, “I daŋ gil n maa ni n mɛɛ ba di wa so ii be, ka ń binni na wii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ɛɛ tɛŋŋ?”

ref: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
text: A koori sɛɛ, di gil ba ba wa so u be, di ra la saŋa la maga Deevid n du a bii bɔɔ la.

ref: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Gad ba di wa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Gilɛɛ suah a bii bɔɔ naa, izi la Juda hɛri.” Denii Deevid jaa izi di kpa la Hɛrɛf kɔr biini, di ga du de. Koori Sɔɔl n kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Nɔb biini wia

ref: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Koori Sɔɔl so Gibia giŋgimii nyuu, tamaris daa bɛl bɔsɔŋ, di kpogli u kandaa, u nabɔnzi chaali chi baruu. Ba wa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ba na Deevid ni u laallɔɔraa.

ref: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
text: Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ ba be, “Bɛnjamin dee baala, ii ra nuu! Jɛssɛ biibaal naa daŋ mɔnni hɛssi ni pattibɔra tɛɛ ii maa? U daŋ gil ii maa ɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa ani nɛra kalfazi sitɔɔraa?

ref: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
text: A gunnɛ gillɛ ii maa chi n nii? Nɛr maa sɛɛwɛ ú ŋɔ n be, n biibaal ni Jɛssɛ biibaal n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ wia. N wia waa ii bɛl maa titte gɛɛ ú wa ŋɔ n be, gunla n biibaal n chugzi n balii di ra du ŋɔ ú chɔɔ guuŋ, gunla unna ɛɛ zinaa naa.”

ref: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
text: Denii Dɔwɛg la n ɛɛ Ɛdɔm hinuu la gba faa chi Koori Sɔɔl nabɔnzi la be, di ŋɔ, “N faa na Jɛssɛ biibaal la n ba Ahitub biibaal, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk be, Nɔb.

ref: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi tɛu. U kaa tɛu diwee ge jaa, haali di kpa Goliaf la n ɛɛ Filisti hinuu la tokobi la gba di jaau.”

ref: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
text: Awia, Koori Sɔɔl hum dí ba ga yir Ahitub biibaal Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk ani u mɛɛ ni ba dee la maa n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, n du Nɔb la, bá ba. Ba jaa ba.

ref: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
text: Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ahitub biibaal, a nuu!” U ŋɔ, “Jara, n na nuu.”

ref: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
text: Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ni Jɛssɛ biibaal chi n ni, haali i tɛu paanuu ani tokobi, di kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi tɛuwɛi? U birgi dignikpega hiŋ, di ga suah di guuŋ alugɔ kennaa unna ɛɛ zinaa naanɛi?”

ref: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk ŋɔ koori be, “I nabɔnzi naa maa biini, ú bɛliirɛ dɔɔ wibii lugɔ i hila Deevidei? Waabuu ɛɛ i laallɔɔra la n na binnii la nabɔma, i diahina maa ge ra tɛu tɔgzuu.

ref: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
text: A waa lugɔ a hɔl naa bɛnnɛ n faari di pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ra tɛu. Akai! Gilɛɛ wa kpa wia di ra chug n ni n diahina pɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, maa wiimaa zummɛ di lii a wia naa biini, tama maa.”

ref: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
text: Ka Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk, i ni i diahina maanii niŋ siu.”

ref: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
text: Denii koori ŋɔ laallɔɔra la n na binnuu la be, “Ií bir kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina naa, dikuu baŋ lɛɛwɛ jaa Deevid ni wia. Ba zummɔɔ unna chɔ, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ n be.” Ka koori laallɔɔra la waa sɛɛwɛ bá izi kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina hiŋ.

ref: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
text: Denii u ŋɔ Dɔwɛg be, “Hiŋwaa kpu a kizeehina naa maa.” Ɛdɔm hinuu Dɔwɛg la kpu ba maa. A hɔl hiŋ, baala tokkoanaazu ni banuere u kpu, di ba haa laali ba Kizeehina pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa tagtakpuree.

ref: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
text: U gil ba kpu Nɔb hina la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, baala ni haana, ba bichalli ni biifulli, ba nauna, ba kauzi ani ba peeza maa.

ref: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ahimɛlɛk biibaal Abiata waa na bɔr chɔ la Deevid be.

ref: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
text: Uŋ ga hel de, u ŋɔ Deevid be lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl kpu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maanii nyaamm.

ref: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ Abiata be, “A hɔl la miŋ na Ɛdɔm hinuu Dɔwɛg de la, n zummɔ lugɔ u daŋ ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be. Awia, i mɛɛ ni u diahina maa siu chugimbuu.

ref: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
text: Du n be ɛŋ, di gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Koori Sɔɔl ra nyiŋŋi n nii maa kpuirɛ. I daŋ na i hiŋ n be bɔnnaa.”

ref: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ Deevid be, “Na, Filisti hinaa kpa laal di ga fɔɔ bol bɛl banna yir Keila, di ra paagi ba diwee, ba pilli.”

ref: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
text: Awia, u faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “A dɛkkɔɔ ń la ga yoo Filisti hina naa?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Izi la ga yoo baa, di lɛɛ Keila hina ta.”

ref: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
text: Ka Deevid laallɔɔra la ŋɔ u be, “Haali yaa n du Juda naa, ka ɔnsii lau yaabuu. A kaa ɛɛ lugɔ ya la Keila ga lɔ a Filisti hina naa?”

ref: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
text: Denii Deevid kuari pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, u ŋɔ u be, “Izi la Keila, n daŋ kpa Filisti hina du i nonee, í kpegli baa.”

ref: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
text: Awia, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la Keila, di ga yoo Filisti hina di kpu bakpila maa, ka lauri ba sela maa. U faa lɛɛ Keila hinaa lii Filisti hina nonee biini, ba dɔɔ bahinaa.

ref: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
text: Deevid n wa zummɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl vɔɔ ú kpui jinaa di ra nyiŋŋuu la, u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata be, “Kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina tagtakpurii ifɔd la ba.”

ref: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, mìŋ́ i balii nuuwɔɔ nɛnnɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ɛɛ siryaa ú ba Keila, di wa chɔgi u ni u nɛra maa dikuu n wia.

ref: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
text: Keila hina daŋ kpaŋ du u nonee biiniaa? Koori Sɔɔl daŋ ba ɛŋ gunla i balii n nuuwɛ naa? N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, gil i balii zum.” Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “U daŋ ba.”

ref: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
text: Deevid kuari pɛɛzi, “Keila hina daŋ kpa n ni n laallɔɔra maa du Koori Sɔɔl nonee?” Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ba daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
text: Deevid la ga suah Zif Hɛribɔduma giŋgimee hɛri. Koori Sɔɔl ɔɔ izuu hɔpizi biimaa, di gaagi ra nyiŋŋuu. Ka Kɔraawiizi faa waa sɛɛwɛ kpa Deevid du u nonee biini.

ref: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
text: Deevid faa du Hɔrɛs, Zif Hɛribɔduma biini, di nuu lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ballɔɔ, ú wa kpuu.

ref: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
text: Denii Jonatan izi di la Deevid be Hɔrɛs, di gaa duu bɔkpega ú haa vɛɛ yardi Kɔraawiizi,

ref: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
text: di ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm, dikuubɛɛwiai, n mɛɛ Sɔɔl wàá wer kpui. I daŋ di Izrɛl kora, ń ge ra hiŋ i ni. Haali n mɛɛ gba zum gunnɛ.”

ref: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
text: Denii ba nɛra banɛɛ hiŋ maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ Kɔraawiizi see. Jonatan bir kpo, ka Deevid waa haa du Hɔrɛs.

ref: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
text: Denii Zif hina baŋhina la Koori Sɔɔl be Gibia, di ga ŋɔ, “Deevid la lɛi suah Hɔrɛs giŋgimee hɛri la n du Bizeŋ Hakila barii, Jɛsimɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag laa?

ref: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
text: Denii Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ia, dikuu n wia n tir ia kennaa wia!

ref: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
text: Ií haa la ga binni na nɛnnɛ, di zum bɔra la uŋ ɔɔ ra la ani nɛra la n nau de. Ba ŋɔ n benii lugɔ u dɔɔ nunzumaa werge.

ref: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
text: Ií la ga binni bɔra la maa n ɛɛ bɔsuahlaa, di zumaa nɛnnɛ, ka ba wa ŋɔ n be, n ni ii maa la ga dau u luge di lawuu, haali di Juda hɛri maa gbaa ya pigzi.”

ref: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
text: Denii ba bir tɔ see Koori Sɔɔl ni, di la Zif. A saŋa naa di Deevid ni u laallɔɔra du Mayɔn Hɛribɔduma, di suah Jɔɔdan Waluu n du Jɛsimɔn wiifurii nodig wiikakag.

ref: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra jaa faari di ra nyiŋŋuu. Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u izi chɔ di ga suah giŋgimii bɛl n du Mayɔn Hɛribɔduma. Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuu guŋ, u izi la de di gaa nyiŋŋuu.

ref: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
text: Koori Sɔɔl faa ga a giŋgimii keŋkere bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋuu. Deevid ge ni u laallɔɔra ga u keŋkere bɛl di ra hahzi, bá chɔ, Koori Sɔɔl gilɛɛ waa na baa. Saŋa la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra n waa dugli baa, di ra nyiŋŋi ba lauri baa,

ref: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
text: ka nɛbɛl ba wa ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Jara, ba manaŋ! Filisti hina kaa waa lɔ yaa hɛrii.”

ref: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl gil Deevid nyiŋŋaa, ka la ú ga lɔ Filisti hina. Awiarɛ ba ra yir a bɔr hiŋ Sɛla Hamalɛkɔf la.

ref: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
text: Deevid jaa lii de di la gaa zuu Ɛn Gɛdi bia bɔɔni.

ref: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
text: Saŋa la Koori Sɔɔl n wa yoo Filisti hina ka bir ba la, nɛbɛl ŋɔ u be, “Deevid du Ɛn Gɛdi Hɛribɔduma labuu.”

ref: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
text: Denii u wa hel peliga la n du a ŋmɛnikɛrii, di bii bɔɔ du de, Koori Sɔɔl jaa zuu de, ú bɛɛ zahara. Di Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la ge du a bii bɔɔ lume.

ref: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
text: Deevid laallɔɔra ŋɔ u be, “Zinaa hɔpizii naa wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ kpa i dɔm du i nonee biini, í ɛɛu gunla n parii.’ ” Denii Deevid suahzi di ga mɔŋ Koori Sɔɔl tagta nua, di waa zummɛ.

ref: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
text: Deevid n wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u biini bir chɔgi werge maa, dikuu uŋ mɔŋ Koori Sɔɔl tagta la wia,

ref: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ, ka nyɛgi ba ni lugɔ bá gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl wiimaa. Koori Sɔɔl jaa lii a bii bɔɔ di ra kaali.

ref: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
text: Denii Deevid lii a bii bɔɔ hiŋ biini, di yir Koori Sɔɔl, “Jara,” U bir binni, Deevid jaa chɔɔ pi,

ref: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
text: ka ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i ra nuu nɛra nuuzi lugɔ mìŋ́ Deevid ra nyiŋŋi i kpuirɛi?

ref: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
text: I himmaa siwii nawɔɔrɛ zinaa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi kpaibuu du n nonee, a bii bɔɔ naa biini. Baŋhina ŋɔ ń kpui, n vɛɛ ka ŋɔ, ‘Màá lalli n nonii gbɔgzi n dɔɔri, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu Kɔraawiizi lizi u ɛɛ koori.’

ref: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
text: N mɛ, na i tagta yenne du n nonii la! N mɔŋ u yenne, ka maa sɛɛwɛ ń kpui. Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu i zum filaŋkeŋ lugɔ maa ɛɛwɛ leu gɛɛ di vɛɛi, maa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ di zuu i ni, ka i ra daaziŋ í kpu.

ref: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
text: Kɔ́raawiizii niŋ di n nii maa seriya. Waabuu niŋ turgii i wichɔgaa la maa hinna ɛɛŋ la kim, ka miŋwaa nonii wàá gbɔgzii.

ref: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
text: Gunla baŋ ɔɔ ta sɛɛlii faa maa di ŋɔ la, ‘Wichɔgɛɛra benii wichɔgaa ra lii.’ Awia, màá kpa n nonii gbɔgzii maa.

ref: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
text: Anɛɛ Izrɛl koori lii di ra nyiŋŋi ú lauwɛi? Anɛɛ lugee i ra dawɛi? Nuahiŋ siwii gɛɛ kariŋgbai?

ref: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
text: Kɔraawiizii niŋ di yaa maa seriya. Waabuu niŋ bagli unla hor n waa sum. Waabuu niŋ di wibii di lɛɛŋ lii i nonee biini.”

ref: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
text: ka ŋɔ, “I ɛɛ biinihuŋŋu hinnɛ werge kaaliŋ. I ɛɛmbuu nɛnnɛ, ka miŋwaa ɛɛi chumaa.

ref: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
text: Zinaa, i baglimbuu winanaa la hiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛŋ. Kɔraawiizi kpambuu du i nonee biini, ka haa sɛɛwɛ kpuŋ.

ref: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
text: Di baal wa na u dɔm, ɔɔ giluubuu u kaali di wàá duu piraa? Kɔ́raawiizi kissii werge maa, dikuu kennaa hiŋ suŋ n ni zinaa naa wia!

ref: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
text: N zummɔɔ nɛnnɛ maa lugɔ i daŋ di kora Izrɛl hɛri. Á kora chi nɛnnɛ.

ref: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
text: Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu í ŋɔ nua, di hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, lugɔ hàá kpu n dee maa gɛɛ di dim n sɔŋ lii n mɛɛ diahina biini.”

ref: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ a nua, di hɛɛhzi tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl. Koori Sɔɔl jaa bir kaali bol, ka Deevid ni u laallɔɔra bir kaali ba suahribɔr la.

ref: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
text: Deevid n du a hɛribɔduma la, u nuu lugɔ Nabal ra fuŋ u peeza hunaa.

ref: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
text: Ií ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ i ni i diahina miibɔɔjaŋ! Ú kissi i kundɔɔlaa maa!

ref: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
text: N nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i ra fuŋ i peeza hunaa. Yaa ni i penɔɔna maa n faa du Kamɛl la, yaa ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa wichɔgii maa kpawɛɛ di dau baa, gɛɛ di ŋmɛɛ ba kundɔɔlii bɛl maa gba.

ref: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
text: Pɛɛzi i penɔɔna hiŋ, ba daŋ ŋɔ i be. Yaa ba i benii hɔpizizeŋ dii saŋa naa, suŋ n biipɔllaa naa ni, di tɛɛ i balaa ni mìŋ́ i biibaal Deevid kunla maa hiŋ dɔɔwɛ.’ ”

ref: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
text: Deevid balaa hiŋ n wa hel Nabal be, ba lizi Deevid amaniye hiŋ tɛu, ka jaa ra kpaŋ.

ref: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
text: Nabal pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ Deevid naanɛi? Anɛɛ Jɛssɛ biibaal naanɛi? Zinaa hɔpizii naa, balaa kpila maanii ra chɔ ba dɔɔra.

ref: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń kpa n diwee ni nii ani sela la miŋ kpuwɛɛ, ń tɛɛ n balaa n na fuŋ n peeza huna, di tɛɛ nɛra la miŋ waa zummɛi?”

ref: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
text: Denii Deevid balaa hiŋ bir kaali. Baŋ ga helle, ba bagli gunla maa Nabal n ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
text: Deevid ŋɔ u laallɔɔra be, “Ií kpa ii tokobizi laali!” Ba jaa kpaa, ka u ge himmaa kpa u hor. Laallɔɔra kalfaanaazuu faa hiŋuu di la, ka ba kalfaanɛɛ ge so di ra binni ba diwee ni ba dɔŋkuna.

ref: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
text: Awia, binni a wii naa di na gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ, di guŋ lɛi yaa ni yaa dɔɔri ani u diahina maanii du siaahmu biini. Nɛr maa wàá wer ŋɔ wia tɛu u nuu, dikuu u biinikpola werge wia.”

ref: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
text: Denii u ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií kpaa ra tɔ see n na ba.” Ka waa sɛɛwɛɛ ŋɔ u jaari Nabal be.

ref: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
text: Denii Abigeel tinni u kawee di wa hel bizeŋ bɛl zɛɛ gɔmbɔɔ, di Deevid ni u laallɔɔraa tuuwe ra chem u ni.

ref: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
text: Deevid jaa ra fɛ u biini, “Kuuhni naa maa miŋ kuuhwɛ di binni baal naa kundɔɔlaa hɛribɔduma naa biini, bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa leu naa, ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. U bittɔɔ kpa wichɔgaa di ra turgiŋ n winanaa kim.

ref: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
text: N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, di maa u ni u nɛra maa kpuwɛɛ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ!”

ref: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
text: Abigeel n wa na Deevid, u lii u kawee nyuu tuu manaŋ, di giŋŋi u see, di willi u nyuu.

ref: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
text: Awia, gilɛɛ gil n dɔɔri wàá hagzi biinikpola hiŋ Nabal naa. U sɔŋ duulaa u du la, u sɔŋ hiŋ zɛɛrɛ, Gɛnii, gunnɛ gillɛ u ra ɛɛ gɛnni wia la. N dɔɔri, miŋwaa faa waa i balaa la hiŋ hummɛ la nawɛɛ.

ref: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
text: Jaande maa, ka gil mìŋ́ i balii wichɔgaa tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ haŋ giluu i ni i naanna di Izrɛl kora di hanna la, dikuu hinna yoo u laalzi wia. Gilɛɛ waa gil bá waa na wichɔgii maa i ni, i de dui maa biini.

ref: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
text: Haali nɛbɛl n na nyiŋŋii ú kpui naa gba, ka Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la daŋ lɛɛi gunla nɛr n ɔɔ ra du u kumpazi tau la. Ka i dɔma waa, u daŋ ta baa gunla baŋ ɔɔ ta bilori la.

ref: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
text: Di Kɔraawiizi wa ɛɛ winanaa la maa uŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ hìŋ́ n dɔɔri, di gil i ɛɛ Izrɛl koori la,

ref: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
text: n dɔɔri, i biini wàá chɔgi gɛɛ di tirii, dikuu hiŋ kpu nɛra pɛɛpɛɛ gɛɛ di bir turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim wia. Di Kɔraawiizi wa kissii, n dɔɔri, jaande maa, gilɛɛ waa suuh n wia.”

ref: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ Abigeel be, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la dɛg chɔlaarɛ, uŋ humii zinaa, i wa chem n ni!

ref: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi kissii, dikuu nfɛrnanii naa hiŋ tɛŋ di bir n liize, di gil maa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ di kpu nɛra zinaa, di turgi baa ba wichɔgaa kim naa wia.

ref: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu gillɛ maa ia kpuwɛɛ. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ di i faa waa n ni wa chemme manaŋ, hɔɔ daŋ vii waa pizi, di n kpu Nabal ni baala la maa n ɛɛ u nɛra la nyaamm.”

ref: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
text: Denii Deevid lɛɛ kuna la uŋ kpawɛɛ di ba wa tɛu la, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Bir di ra kpo ni bɔsɔna. N daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.”

ref: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
text: Abigeel n bittɛ la Nabal be, di u du dia di ra di diuzenaa alugɔ koori, u bɔra sɔɔni, u dɛɛzi werge maa. Awia, u faa waa sɛɛwɛ ŋɔ wiimaa tɛu, ka hɔɔ wa pizi.

ref: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, di siŋ la jaa lii Nabal siwee, u haaŋ ŋɔ u be wia la maa n dɛɛ ɛɛwɛ. Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u banchule lɔ werge maa, u bɔra siu, u gbɛr kakpaŋ.

ref: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
text: Hɔpizaa fi harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi lɔu, u siu.

ref: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
text: Awia, Abigeel giŋŋi di willi u nyuu, ka ŋɔ, “Mìŋ́ i baliirɛ keŋ, n ɛɛ siryaa ń humii, di sanzi i balaa naazi.”

ref: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
text: Denii Abigeel izi manaŋ, di tinni u kawee, u balaa banue la n du u be la duu. Ba ni Deevid balaa la maa kpa di la, u ga birgi Deevid haaŋ.

ref: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
text: Deevid faa kpa Ahinoam n lii Jɛzriil, banɛɛ hiŋ maa faa jaa ɛɛ u haana.

ref: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
text: Ka Koori Sɔɔl faa kpa u biihaaŋ Mikal la n faa ɛɛ Deevid haaŋ la, di tɛɛ Layis biibaal Palti n lii bol bɛl banna yir Galim.

ref: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Zif hina la Koori Sɔɔl be Gibia, di ga ŋɔ, “Deevid lɛi suah Bizeŋ Hakila n chaŋ Juda Hɛribɔduma laa?”

ref: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
text: Koori Sɔɔl ga chɔɔ dugli ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl n chɔɔ Bizeŋ Hakila la n chaŋ Jɛsimɔn nyuu, ka Deevid du a hɛribɔduma biini. Uŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl duŋŋi u lugee di ba de la,

ref: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
text: u hum nɛra, bá la ga daani de na, dí Koori Sɔɔl ba denii wibii maa?

ref: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
text: Denii Deevid izi di kpa la bɔr la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra n wa chɔɔwɛ la. U ga na bɔr la Koori Sɔɔl ni u laallɔɔra nabɔma Nɛɛr biibaal Abna n chɔɔwɛ. Koori Sɔɔl faa chɔɔ u laallɔɔra hiŋ baambaannɛ, ka ba chɔɔ baruu.

ref: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
text: Denii Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Hitti hinuu Ahimɛlɛk ni Zɛruya biibaal Abisai n ɛɛ Joab lulli la, “Ú bɛliirɛ niŋ duŋ la Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔribɔrɛi?” Abisai ŋɔ, “N nii daŋ la.”

ref: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
text: Denii Deevid ni Abisai la a laallɔɔra be a hamuŋa ni, di Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔ ba chɔɔribɔr hiŋ di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ, ka u kandaa baŋ di dugli u nyuu. Abna ni u laallɔɔra ge chɔɔ baruu.

ref: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
text: Abisai ŋɔ Deevid be, “Kɔraawiizi kpa i dɔnnɛ du i nonee zinaa. Gil ń yaguu ni n kandaa kakpaŋ di pɛli hɛri, màá tɔɔuh bunɛɛ!”

ref: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
text: Ka Deevid ŋɔ Abisai be, “Gilɛɛ kpuu! Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kpa nonii gbɔgzi nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ, di waa di bilchɔgɛi?”

ref: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
text: Deevid kaa ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la, lugɔ Kɔraawiizi himmaanii niŋ kpuu gɛɛ u saŋaa niŋ wa hel gɛɛ laal biinii bá kpuu.

ref: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
text: Kɔraawiizi gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ lugɔ n wa kpa n nonii di ra gbɔgzi nɛr la uŋ lizɛɛ. Gil ya kpa u kandaa ani u lɔŋgɔm waa di ra la.”

ref: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
text: Denii Deevid kpa kandaa la ni lɔŋgɔm la n dugli Koori Sɔɔl nyuu la, ba kaali, di nɛr maa faa waa baa nawɛɛ gɛɛ di zum guŋ, gɛɛ di izi dɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ ba chɔɔ a guŋ dɔbɛrii.

ref: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
text: Denii Deevid gi a waluu baŋgia bɛl, di ga chi giŋgimii nyuu bɔɔnɛɛ.

ref: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
text: Ka jaa gbooli yir Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra ani Nɛɛr biibaal Abna, di ŋɔ, “Abna, hàá sɛɛ n be gɛɛ?” Abna bir ŋɔ, “Anɛɛ n na yir koorei?”

ref: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
text: Deevid bir ŋɔ u be, “Abna, baal lɛi hiŋ? Anɛɛ n lugɔi, Izrɛl hɛri biinei? Ɛrɛɛ haa i dɔɔri koori guuwei? Nɛbɛl ballɔɔ ú wa kpuu.

ref: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
text: Gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la waa wer. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ i ni i laallɔɔra maanii dɛg kpui, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa wette guu ii dɔɔri la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ u ɛɛ koori la. Ií binni de na, lee a koori kandaa ni u lɔŋgɔm la n chigɛ dugli u nyuu la duɛi?”

ref: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
text: Koori Sɔɔl nuu Deevid loobii, di zum lugɔ waabuu. Di yiruu, “N biibaal Deevid, i loobiire naa?” Deevid sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, minuu, n dɔɔri koori.

ref: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
text: Bɛɛ wiarɛ hìŋ́ n dɔɔri, ra duŋŋi míŋ̀ i balii kennei? Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Bɛɛ bilchɔgrɛ n dɔɔi?

ref: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
text: Awia, Jara, a nuu míŋ̀ i balii wiŋɔzi naa. Di Kɔraawiizii gillɛ i ra yooŋ, guŋwaa, n daŋ lizi mbusu lizaa kuna tɛu. Ka di nɛraa ɛɛ guŋ, nuuseei di baa Kɔraawiizi see! Ba duŋŋimbuu filaŋkeŋ lii hɛri la miŋ di kapɛttɛ Kɔraawiizi be la, ka ŋɔ, ‘La gaa kuari hɛrdumazi vuga.’

ref: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
text: Awia, n na suŋŋiibuu lugɔ i gilɛɛ wa gil n siu bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n waa duglɛɛ. Bɛɛwiarɛ Izrɛl koori lii di ra nyiŋŋi mìŋ́ nɛr la n lugɔ kariŋgbai, gɛɛ kpaaŋ n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi zaahri bizenaa nyuuni lai?”

ref: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Bir a ba, n biibaal Deevid, dikuubɛɛwiai, i vɛɛ n miibɔɔ lizaarɛ zinaa, màá kaa ɛɛ ania ń dui pira maa. N ɛɛ wiarɛ lugɔ gɛnii, di leu werge, wibii maa.”

ref: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
text: Ka Deevid ŋɔ, “Koori kandaarɛ keŋ. Gil i biipɔllaa la bɛl gi wa lɛɛu.

ref: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
text: Nɛr la wia n deŋlee, u kaa dɔɔ wibii daŋ na tɔna Kɔraawiizi be. U kpaibuu du n nonee zinaa, ka màá kpa n nonii di gbɔgzi nɛr la uŋ lizɛɛ u ɛɛ koori.

ref: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
text: Kennaa miŋ vɛɛ i miibɔɔ lizaa zinaa naa, Kɔ́raawiizi vɛɛ n ge miibɔɔ lizaa guŋ, di lɛɛŋ lii tɔɔrɔɔ maa biini!”

ref: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ Deevid be, “N biibaal Deevid, Kɔ́raawiizi kissii. I daŋ ɛɛ wizenaa, i wia kuari.” Denii Deevid bir kaali, ka Koori Sɔɔl ge bir kpo bol.

ref: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
text: Denii Deevid fɛ nfɛrɛ, di ŋɔ, “Hɔpizii bɛl, Koori Sɔɔl daŋ kpuŋ. Wii la n dɛkkɛ min niŋ ɛɛ maanii, miŋ chɔwɛɛ kaali Filisti hɛri. Gunnɛ niŋ gil Koori Sɔɔl gil n nyiŋŋaa Izrɛl hɛri naa biini, ka n na n hiŋ.”

ref: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
text: Koori Sɔɔl n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Deevid chɔwɔɔ kaali Gaf, u jaa gil u nyiŋŋaa.

ref: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ Koori Akis be, “Di i dɔɔ n bila, tɛŋ bɔr i hɛri naa bola naa bɛl biini, ń ga so de. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ míŋ̀ i balii nii so koori bolzeŋ naa biinei?”

ref: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
text: Awia, Koori Akis kpa Ziklag tɛu, de haŋ ɛɛ Juda koora bɔr, di wa lii ni zinaa.

ref: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
text: Deevid faa so Filisti hɛri biŋkpaŋ ni baaguzi anaazu.

ref: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
text: A guŋ saŋa, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la ga lɔ Gɛsur, Girzi ani Amalɛk hina la n faa soge a hɛri faala maa, di lii Suur di ga hel Ijip hɛri la.

ref: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
text: Deevid haŋ wa pig yemmaa, waa ɔɔ gil baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa du de ni miibɔɔ, ka ɔɔ lauri peeza, nauna, kauzi ani nyugmazi, di paa ba laala jaa. Ka ɔɔ kaa bir ba Koori Akis be.

ref: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
text: Koori Akis haŋ wa pɛɛzuu, “Lee i ga lɔ zinaa, di paa kunai?” Deevid ɔɔ ŋɔ, “Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii” gɛɛ “Jɛramiil dee hɛri” gɛɛ “Kɛn hina hɛri.”

ref: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
text: Deevid waa ɔɔ gil baal gɛɛ haaŋ maa du de ni miibɔɔ, ú kpogli baa ba Gaf, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ, “Aŋhinabe, ba daŋ la ga ŋɔ, ‘Kenne Deevid ɛɛ.’ ” Gunnɛ u faa ra ɛɛ, saŋa la uŋ soge Filisti hɛri la.

ref: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
text: Koori Akis yardi Deevid, di ŋɔ u biini, “U himmaa nɛra Izrɛl hina hauhbuu werge maa, guŋ daŋ gil u ɛɛ n balii di hanna la.”

ref: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
text: Denii a Filisti hina izi ga baŋzi ba tantizi di chɔɔ bolzeŋ bɛl banna yir Sunɛm. Koori Sɔɔl ge chaali Izrɛl hina laallɔɔra, ba ge ga chɔɔ Bizeŋ Gilbɔa.

ref: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
text: Koori Sɔɔl n wa na Filisti laallɔɔra la, ɔnsii ni biinichɔg lawuu werge maa.

ref: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
text: U pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi gunla un niŋ ɛɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu, di lii deeza gɛɛ Urim ni Tumim tai biini gɛɛ dɔgtɛɛzi be.

ref: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií nyiŋŋi haaŋ la n ɛɛ vugri ń la u ga vugiŋ.” Ba ŋɔ, “Bɛl du Ɛndɔ.”

ref: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl bɔg hamuŋa ni, di kur. U ni u laallɔɔra banɛɛ kpa di la a haaŋ be. Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Yir lalii la sɔŋ min niŋ yir duma, di pɛɛzuu tɛŋ.”

ref: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
text: Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ u be, “Wibii maa, i zum wii la Koori Sɔɔl n ɛɛwɛnɛ. U duŋŋi vugra ni ijɔzii lii Izrɛl hɛri. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ba í wa heŋ sidɛɛ, di lawiŋ ń siuwɛi?”

ref: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
text: Ka Koori Sɔɔl hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la sɔŋ biini, nɛr maa wàá tɛr i digni dikuu guŋ wia.”

ref: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
text: Denii a haaŋ pɛɛzuu, “Lalbɛliirɛ i ra nyiŋŋi ń yir tɛinɛi?” Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Samuɛl.”

ref: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
text: A haaŋ n wa yir Samuɛl di na u duma n na ba, u lɔ wile werge maa, di ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i dariŋ gunnɛi? Koori Sɔɔllɛ hiŋ!”

ref: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm! Bɛɛ i nai?” A haaŋ ŋɔ, “N na nɛr dumaa n na lii hɛrii.”

ref: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
text: Koori Sɔɔl pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ u duɛi?” U ŋɔ, “U ɛɛ bazɛŋaa, di laali tagtajaŋ di ra ba.” Denii Koori Sɔɔl jaa zum lugɔ Samuɛllɛ, u chɔɔ hɛri di pi.

ref: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
text: Samuɛl ŋɔ Koori Sɔɔl be, “Ɛrɛɛ i tɔɔriŋ, di yiriŋ ba ɛnnɛi?” Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Biinichɔg wergee lawiŋ. Filisti hinaa wa fɔɔŋ ni laal, ka Kɔraawiizi vɛɛŋ ta. Waa kaa sɛɛ ga u dɔgtɛɛzi be di nuu ra tɛŋ gɛɛ di lii deeza gba biini. Awiarɛ n yirii, í wa bagliŋ gunla min niŋ ɛɛ.”

ref: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
text: Denii Samuɛl ŋɔ u be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i yiriŋ, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n vɛɛi, di birgi i dɔmɛi?

ref: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
text: Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ wia la uŋ ga n be ŋɔ lugɔ a daŋ ɛɛi labuu tuŋ. Kɔraawiizi foozi Izrɛl kora labuu lii i be, tɛɛ i dɔŋhiŋ Deevid.

ref: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
text: Dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ u nua hiŋaa, haa Amalɛk hina maa kpuwɛɛ, di chɔgi ba kundɔɔlaa maa nyaamm la wiarɛ, u kpa a keŋ wii naa di ra dawii zinaa la.

ref: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
text: Awia, u daŋ kpa i ni Izrɛl hina maa du Filisti hina nonee. Kɛrɛ, i ni i biibaala daŋ wa jaa mìŋ́ Samuɛl ni. Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa kpa Izrɛl laallɔɔra ge du Filisti hina nonee biini.”

ref: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
text: Kakpaŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Sɔɔl werge, u chol hɛri di tɛr chɔɔ, dikuu gunla Samuɛl n ŋɔwɛɛ la wia. Waa kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa tama maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa waa kummaa diwee di lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ di ga hel hamuŋa.

ref: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
text: A haaŋ n wa ba Sɔɔl be, di na gunla bɔsai ni ɔnsii n lawuu la, u ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, mìŋ́ i balii hiŋ i nuarɛ, di kpa n miibɔɔ chɛr siu, di ɛɛ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔ ń ɛɛ tɛi labuu.

ref: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
text: Jaande maa, a nuu míŋ̀ i balii be, gil n tɛi diwee í di, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ra la.”

ref: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
text: U vɛɛ ka ŋɔ, “Màá di.” Ka u nɛra la hiini a haaŋ di ra fɔrguu lugɔ ú di, u jaa sɛɛ, di izi so u karjaŋ ni.

ref: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
text: A haaŋ ge dɔɔ ú nabii n pɔllɛ nɛnnɛ, u lawuu kpu manaŋ. Di ɛɛ sau di ɔɔzi paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
text: Denii u kpaa wa tɛɛ Sɔɔl ni u nɛra hiŋ ba di. A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa maanii, ba lii kaali.

ref: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
text: Ka Filisti laallɔɔra sitɔɔra hiŋ ŋɔ Koori Akis be ani baaŋfuuih, “Gil a baal bir kaali bɔr la hiŋ tɛu la. Gilɛɛ gil yaa nuu la a laal. Di a haŋ wa chi siaahmu, u daŋ bir di ra yoo yaa. Gunla un niŋ ɛɛ u dɔɔri bɔra kaa sɔɔni maanii, un niŋ bir kpu yaa.

ref: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, Deevid naa wia lɛi a ba kpa di ra yir yira ani chɔlaa lugɔ, ‘Koori Sɔɔl kpu kagboŋaa, ka Deevid kpu kagboŋa fizi laa’?”

ref: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
text: Denii Koori Akis yir Deevid di ŋɔ u be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa labuu lugɔ i wia dɔɔ wibiire n be. A daŋ faa pariŋ lugɔ n nii la a laal. Di haŋ lii a hɔl la hiŋ ba n be di wa lii ni zinaa, maa wichɔgii maa nawɛɛ i ni. Ka n dɔŋa koora la waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ i jaa yaa ni.

ref: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
text: Awia, bir di ra kpo ani bɔsɔna, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wiimaa, ba baana waa fuuh.”

ref: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
text: Ka Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛi? Haŋ lii a hɔl la maa miŋ ba i be la di wa lii ni zinaa, bɛɛ wichɔgiirɛ i na n ninɛi? N dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ n nii wàá wer la ń ga yoo i dɔmai?”

ref: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
text: Koori Akis bir ŋɔ u be, “N zummɔɔ lugɔ i wia dɔɔ wibiire alugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl, ka Filisti hina koora ŋɔ ba wàá sɛɛ lugɔ i ni yaa la a laal.

ref: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
text: Awia, feli izi chɔɔzi ni di lau i dɔɔri balaa la i ni baa n ballɛ la, di biraa kpo.”

ref: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
text: Awia, Deevid ni u laallɔɔra feli izi chɔɔzi ni, di bir ba Filisti hɛri, ka Filisti hina la ge kpa di ra la Jɛzriil.

ref: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
text: Hɔpizaa ahoroo Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la kpa di bir hel Ziklag. A saŋa naa, di Amalɛk hina teŋ wa lɔ Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag, di foozi ba kuna ka fuuh bolzeŋ Ziklag maa,

ref: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
text: Deevid ni u laallɔɔra n wa hel Ziklag, ba na lugɔ a bol maanii fuuhwe, haali ba lauri ba haana ani ba biizi maa kaali.

ref: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
text: Denii Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la jaa chɛɛhgi guŋŋ, ba fɔŋŋa maa wa tuŋ.

ref: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
text: Ba faa lauri Deevid haana banɛɛ Jɛzriil hinuu Ahinoam ani Kamɛl hinuu Nabal luhaaŋ Abigeel maanii kaali.

ref: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
text: Biinichɔg jaa lau Deevid werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia faa ra fuuh u laallɔɔra hiŋ baannɛ. Ba faa ra nyiŋŋi ba paagi bia lɔɔzuu, dikuu baŋ waa kaa na ba biizi wia. Ka Kɔraawiizi la unna hum faa duu bɔkpega.

ref: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
text: Denii Deevid ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata n ɛɛ Ahimɛlɛk biibaal be, “Kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina tagtakpurii ifɔd la wa tɛŋ.” Abiata kpau di wa tɛu.

ref: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
text: Denii Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Ń dau a laallɔɔra naa n wa chɔgi yaa bol naa luge gɛɛ? N daŋ huuzi baa?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Lii dau ba luge, i daŋ huuzi baa, di lɛɛ i nɛra hiŋ.”

ref: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
text: Ba ga na Ijip hinuu bɛl pir biini, di lawuu ba Deevid be, ba tɛu nii ni diwee,

ref: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
text: fig nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ, a hil yeŋ ani grepu nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ, a hil anɛɛ. U dia, fɔŋŋa ba u be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa waa kummaa diwee gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii hɔpizaa ahoro.

ref: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
text: Deevid pɛɛzuu, “I dɔɔrii anɛɛ, lee i liiyɛi?” U ŋɔ, “Ijip hinuurɛ miŋ, n ɛɛ Amalɛk hinuu bɛl yonne. N na wiiu hɔpizaa ahoro n bɛrɛɛ, n dɔɔri hiŋ vɛɛŋ ta.

ref: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
text: Yaa ga lɔ Kɛrɛf hina la n du Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag ani Kalɛb domeere, ka fuuh Ziklag ge jaa.”

ref: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
text: Denii Deevid pɛɛzuu, “I daŋ wer tɔ n see, di ga bagliŋ bɔr la nɛra naa n wa lɔ yaa di paa yaa kuna naa n duwɛɛ?” U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh. Ama, hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ hàá kpuŋ gɛɛ di kpaŋ ga tɛɛ n dɔɔri la.”

ref: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
text: U tɔ Deevid see di la bɔr la baŋ duwɛɛ la, di ba yaari de maa, di ra di ka ra nyɔɔ, di ra sa, dikuu kuna la baŋ paagɛɛ werge lii Filisti ani Juda hina be la wia.

ref: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
text: Deevid lɔ baa chɔɔzimpikke ni guŋŋ hɔɔ waa pizi, ba biipɔllaa kalfaanaazu bɛnnɛ faa wette tinni nyugmazi di chɔ kaali. Ka banla waa maa n kawɛɛ la, waa wette na bɔr chɔ kaali.

ref: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
text: Deevid lɛɛ kuna la maa Amalɛk hina n paagɛɛ la, di kpa ú haana banɛɛ la jaa.

ref: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
text: Ba kummaa faa waa a nɛra be leuwe, haali ba biihaana ani biibaala gba. A maanii Deevid lɛɛ ba.

ref: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
text: U faa bir foozi peeza ani nauna, u nɛra duŋŋaa di tɔ see, ka ra ŋɔ, “Deevid kunaa keŋ.”

ref: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
text: Ka banla ni Deevid n laŋŋɛ la nɛchɔgaa ani kalu nyiŋŋe baŋhina ŋɔ, “Dikuu baŋ vɛɛ de laŋaa la wia, yaa wàá bɔnni a kuna di tɛɛ baa. Ama, bɛl maa kpogli u haaŋ ni biizi waa di ra la.”

ref: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
text: Ka Deevid ŋɔ, “Akai, n lulla, ii gilɛɛ ɛɛ chumaa, dikuu kuna naa Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ yaa naa wia. U guu yaabuu, di kpa yaa dɔma du yaa nonee.

ref: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
text: Akai! Anɛɛ niŋ nuu gunla iinna ŋɔ naanɛi? Banla n soge di ra binni yaa kuna ani banla maa n la a laal la maanii niŋ di mɛgzi. Yaa maa daŋ bɔnnaa di mɛgzi.”

ref: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
text: Kenne Deevid dau tɛɛ Izrɛl hina ba ra hiŋ, haali ni zinaa.

ref: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
text: Deevid n wa hel Ziklag, u kpa a kuna aŋhina tɛɛ Juda nabɔnzi la n ɛɛ u dammuzi, di ŋɔ, “Kuna la miŋ foozee di lii Kɔraawiizi dɔma benii keŋ.”

ref: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
text: A kaa wa ɛɛ lugɔ Filisti ni Izrɛl hina kaa ra lɔ laal, ba kpu Izrɛl hina galga maa Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu, ka baŋhina chɔ.

ref: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
text: Filisti hina faa duŋŋi Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala guŋŋ di ga kpu Jonatan, Abinadab ani Malki Sua.

ref: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
text: A laal faa jaa du kpeg werge, ba bar Koori Sɔɔl, di viruu hobii, di duu pira werge maa.

ref: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
text: Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna be, “Pam i tokobi di tɔɔhŋ kpu, di guŋ lɛi, nɛra naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa daŋ ba wa ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ, di sunniŋ.” Ka ɔnsii faa lau a biipɔllii werge maa, waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpuu. Denii Koori Sɔɔl pam u himmaa tokobi, di bir tɔɔh u hiŋ kpu.

ref: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
text: A biipɔllii n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ, u ge pam u himmaa tokobi di tɔɔh u hiŋ, di siu jaa u ni.
