ref: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
text: Denii Koori Sɔɔl, u biibaala bahoro, u balii ani u laallɔɔra maa faa kpau siu, a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
text: Izrɛl hina la n soge di hiini waluu ani ba banla n du Jɔɔdan muu baŋgia la, n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba laallɔɔra maa chɔwɔɔrɛ la, Koori Sɔɔl ge ni u biibaala maa siu la, ba ge maa chɔ ka ka ba bola. Filisti hina la jaa ba di wa so ba bola hiŋ.

ref: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Filisti hina ba, bá wa wir a lalaa kuna, ba na Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala bahoro la maa n siuwɛ chɔɔ Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu.

ref: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
text: Bolzeŋ Jabɛs Giliad hina n wa nuu gunla Filisti hina la n dau Koori Sɔɔl la,

ref: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
text: ba nɛkpega izi hamuŋa ni di vɔɔ, di la Bɛf San, di ga lizi Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaala hiŋ a koŋlii ni, di kpa baa ba Jabɛs, di wa fuuh baa de.

ref: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
text: Ka paa ba hoga di wa hug tamaris daa zɛɛ, Jabɛs biini. Ka vɔɔ nua hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
text: Koori Sɔɔl siu har, Deevid jaa lii bɔr la uŋ kpegli Amalɛk hina la, di bir ba wa du Ziklag hɔpizaa anɛɛ.

ref: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
text: A hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ, baal bɛl lii Koori Sɔɔl chɔɔribɔr di piili u laala, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa waari u nyuu, di ra bagli u biinichɔg. Uŋ wa hel Deevid be, u giŋŋi u see di jaamuu girme ni.

ref: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
text: Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Lee i liiyɛi?” U ŋɔ, “N chɔwɔɔrɛ lii Izrɛl hina chɔɔribɔr la.”

ref: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
text: Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n ɛɛwɛnɛi? Ŋɔ n be.” U ŋɔ, “Yaa laallɔɔra maanii chɔwɛɛ lii a laal biini yaari. Ba kpila ge maa kaa siu. Haali Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan gba siuwɔɔ.”

ref: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
text: Denii Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ zum lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan gba siuwɔɔwɛi?”

ref: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
text: A biipɔllii hiŋ ŋɔ, “Bizeŋ la banna yir Gilbɔa la nyuurɛ n chi, ka na Koori Sɔɔl n chigɛ dɛlli u kandaa, ka u dɔma la ni ba zagra ni a torkozi baruu tuŋ.

ref: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
text: Uŋ wa bittɛ di ŋɔ u binni, di minuu, u yiriŋ. N pɛɛzuu, ‘Bɛɛ i ŋɔ n ɛɛi?’

ref: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
text: U pɛɛziŋ, ‘Anɛɛ hinnɛi?’ N ŋɔ, ‘Amalɛk hinuurɛ miŋ.’

ref: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
text: Denii u ŋɔ n be, ‘Ba wa kpuŋ, n na piraa werge maa, di ra nyiŋŋi n siu.’

ref: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
text: Denii n tuzi heluu di kpuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ di u wa chol hɛri, wàá ka piri. N jaa pilli u saliŋ kahuro la uŋ hiwee la, di lizi u nonii gbuŋ ge, aabuu keŋ n kpa ba ń wa tɛi, n dɔɔri.”

ref: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
text: Deevid ni u laallɔɔra maa lau ba laala piili ni biinichɔg,

ref: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
text: di wii werge maa di ra tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan ani Izrɛl hina la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra, ka vɔɔ nua guŋŋ di ga hel duana ni, dikuu baŋ siu laal biini wia.

ref: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
text: Deevid ŋɔ a biipɔllii la n wa lizi a amaniye hiŋ be, “Lee i liiyɛi?” U ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ Amalɛk hinuurɛ, ka du i hɛri.”

ref: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
text: Deevid ŋɔ u be, “I wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi i ni, i himmaa nuarɛ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ, i kpu koori la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛnɛ.” Deevid n wii Koori Sɔɔl ni Jonatan lee wia

ref: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
text: Deevid jaa yir biinichɔg yir naa dikuu Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan wia,

ref: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
text: “Yaa sitɔɔra siuwɔɔ chɔɔ Izrɛl hɛri giŋgimee nyuuni! Yaa laallɔkpega werge la chogloore!

ref: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ a wia bolzenaa Gaf biini gɛɛ Askɛlɔn ŋmɛnizi. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil Filisti hina haana bɔra sɔɔni, di gilɛɛ wa gil banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ biihaana bɔra sɔɔni.

ref: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
text: Gilɛɛ gil dooŋ gɛɛ sɔnii wàá chol Gilbɔa giŋgimee ni, gil u kooni chɔɔ pɛɛ saŋa maa! Dikuu laallɔkpega laal pɛrɛtuzenaa chɔɔ denii ni hiihzi, ba waa kaa kpa nuu di ra billi Koori Sɔɔl hor.

ref: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
text: Jonatan hoo faa waa tawɛɛ ra kir, Koori Sɔɔl ge faa kpu nɛkpila werge ni u tokobi, di faa kpuuzi nɛkpega ani u dɔma.

ref: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
text: Koori Sɔɔl ni Jonatan de dui saŋa, nɛra faa nɔŋŋi baabuu, di ra tɔgzi baa, ba faa waa bargɛɛ siu gba biini. Ba faa gbaŋŋɔɔ kaali chigni, di du kpeg kaali bunyinzi.

ref: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
text: Izrɛl haana, ií wii ra tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl, u faa ɔɔ ra tɛɛ iabuu pɛɛŋaahma la yoolazi n kpolle werge, di ra bɔg ia ni saliŋ kuna.

ref: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
text: Laallɔkpega la chogloore ba kpuuzi baabuu laal biini. Jonatannɛ siuwɛ chɔɔ giŋgimee nyuuni.

ref: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
text: N wiiwoo ra tɛi, n badɔŋ Jonatan, i faa nɔŋŋimbuu werge! I nɔŋŋaa faa kpekkoo kaali haana nɔŋŋaa.

ref: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
text: Laallɔkpega chogloore, ba dɔŋkuna bir pɛɛ.”

ref: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Deevid pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “N Dɔɔri, ń la Juda bola naa bɛl di ga soo?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Ɛɛh, a la.” Deevid kaa pɛɛzi, “Ń la ga so u bɛlii?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Ga so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn.”

ref: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
text: Denii Deevid kpogli u haana banɛɛ, u ni baa la de, bɛllɛ faa Jɛzriil hinuu Ahinoam, bɛl genii faa Nabal n lii Kamɛl luhaaŋ Abigeel la.

ref: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
text: Deevid faa kaa kpogli u laallɔɔra la n faa du u be la maa ni ba diinihina, ba maa la ga so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn ani u boljigzi.

ref: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
text: Denii Juda hina ba bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di wa fug nuu waari Deevid nyuu, di tɔu kora, u jaa ɛɛ Juda hina maa koori. Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ bolzeŋ Jabɛs la, n du Giliad hɛri hina hug Koori Sɔɔllɛ,

ref: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
text: u hum ŋɔ ba ga ŋɔ ba be. “Kɔ́raawiizi kissi ia, iiŋ suŋ ii dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl ni, di huguu la wia.

ref: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi ra ɛɛ ia nɛnnɛ di dɔɔ wibii ni ia, n gba daŋ suŋ ii ni di hiini ia guŋ himmaa, dikuu kennaa iiŋ ɛɛwɛ naa wia.

ref: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
text: Awia, ií chiiri zɛɛ di dɔɔ bampirii! Ii Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ, ka Juda hina jaa waari n nyuu nuu, di tɔŋ kora.” Laal n chol Koori Deevid ni Koori Sɔɔl diinihina ni wia

ref: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
text: Ama, Abna la n ɛɛ Nɛɛr biibaal, di kaa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl laallɔɔra sitɔɔri la, faa lau Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf, ba chɔ la Mahanam.

ref: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
text: Denii u ga tɔu kora, u ɛɛ Giliad, Asɛ, Jɛzriil, Ɛfram, Bɛnjamin ani Izrɛl hina maa koori.

ref: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
text: Denii Koori Deevid so bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di di kora Juda dee ni, binni aniidaanɛɛ ni baaguzi anumbɛl.

ref: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ani Isbɔsɛf nabɔnzi izi Mahanam, di kpa la bolzeŋ Gibiɔn.

ref: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
text: Zɛruya biibaal Joab ni Koori Deevid nabɔnzi la ga chem ba ni Gibiɔn pol. Baŋhina so a pol baŋgia bɛl, baŋhina ge so bɛl.

ref: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
text: Denii Abna ŋɔ Joab be, “Lizi i biipɔllaa, ya ge lizi yaa biipɔllaa, bá lɔ dɔŋa ya na.” Joab ŋɔ, “Wibiire i ŋɔ, ya ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
text: Denii Abna lizi nɛra fidibanɛɛ lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, ba chi tɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl biibaal Isbɔsɛf. Joab ge lizi nɛra fidibanɛɛ ba chi tɛɛ Koori Deevid.

ref: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
text: Denii ba zuu dɔŋa, bɛl maa lau u dɔŋhiŋ nyuu, ka pam u tokobi di chug u loŋŋi, ba maa kpau chol, di siu. Awia, ba jaa ra yir bɔr n du Gibiɔn hɛri la, Hɛlkaf Hazurim.

ref: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, a laal faa kpekkoo werge maa. Ka Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra kpegli Abna ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra la.

ref: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
text: Zɛruya biibaala bahoro la faa du denii, baabuu, Joab, Abisai ani Asahɛl la n faa ra chɔ werge lugɔ weema la.

ref: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
text: Abna bir binnuu, ka ŋɔ, “Asahɛl, hinuu naa?” U ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh!”

ref: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
text: Abna ŋɔ u be, “Gil n duŋŋaa! A duŋŋi laallɔɔra naa bɛl, di foozi kuna la uŋ kpoglee.” Ka Asahɛl vɛɛ ka haa ra duŋŋuu.

ref: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
text: Abna kaa ŋɔ Asahɛl be. “Gil n duŋŋaa! Ɛrɛɛ i ra firiŋ ń kpuinɛi? Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ binni i kpɛɛma Joab siweei?”

ref: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
text: Ka Asahɛl vɛɛ ka ra duŋŋuu. Denii Abna kpa u kandaa di bir yaguu, u saagi ga lii u harbɔɔ. U chol siu. Di nɛr maa hanna ba di wa hel bɔr la Asahɛl n siuwɛ hiŋ, ɔɔ chiu.

ref: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
text: Ka Joab ni Abisai ge haa ra duŋŋi Abna guŋŋ di ga hel Amma giŋgimii la n dugli Gia, ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Gibiɔn hɛribɔduma la, di wiizi jaa ra zuu.

ref: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
text: Denii Bɛnjamin dee laallɔɔra la jaa wa bar Abna, di chi giŋgimii bɛl nyuu, ba chigni bɔra.

ref: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”

text: Awia, Koori Deevid faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na, di ŋɔ, “Ń la ga lɔ Filisti hina naa? I daŋ gil n kpegli baa?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “A la, n daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini, wibii maa.”

ref: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
text: Awia, Koori Deevid kpa di la Baal Pɛrazim, di ga kpegli baa, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma alugɔ nii n suwee di kpu nɛra la.” Awia, ba jaa ra yir de Baal Pɛrazim.

ref: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
text: Filisti hina faa gil ba vuga ha de, Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra paagaa kaali.

ref: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
text: Denii Filisti hina kaa kuari ba Rɛfam Waluu, di wa yaari de maa.

ref: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
text: Koori Deevid kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, u ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ deŋli baa la, bar baa di la ba har, di lɔ baa daazi la banna yir balsam la see.

ref: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
text: Di i haŋ wa nuu laallɔɔra naazi gbɔga a balsam daazi nyuuni, lii chem ba ni laal manaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, guŋ daŋ bagli lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi tɔ i seere, ń kpu Filisti laallɔɔra hiŋ.”

ref: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la. U jaa kpu Filisti hina la, di lii Gibiɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛza.

ref: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
text: Koori Deevid kpa pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii vɔɔ u chara di ra sa, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi ni u fɔŋŋa maa.

ref: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa ra di bahinaa, di ra chaasi ani bɔsɔna, di ra huuh ba bensunozi, di chi a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ra ba Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
text: Baŋ chigɛ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka di ra zuu Jɛrusalɛm la, di Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal chigɔ tokoro di ra binni baa. U na gunla Koori Deevid n na sa, di zaahzi ra chiiri ani bɔsɔna, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la, u wia ra fuuh u baaŋ, u ra gbɛlluu.

ref: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
text: Ba la ga zuu Abinadab dia la n hɔŋ giŋgimii ni la, di kpa a Dakka hɔŋ torkofalii ni. Abinadab biibaala Uza ni Ahiore faa ra binni a torkofalii ni.

ref: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
text: di tɔ ba see la Baala n du Juda, bá ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la sɔŋ n sag u ni, u di kora chɛrubzi baambaaŋ la.

ref: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
text: Banna la la, Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra sa, di ra yir yira ni ba fɔŋŋa maa, di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi, di ra yigzi kuna, di ra lɔ pɛrɛtuzi, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi werge maa.

ref: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
text: Ka baŋ wa hel baal bɛl banna yir Nakɔn pila, a navargazi lɔ naa, Uza tɛr u nonii lau a Dakka.

ref: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
text: Kakpaŋ, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Uza ni, dikuu uŋ wɔɔ tɔgzɛɛ wia. U lɔu, u chol hɛri siu chɔɔ a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka kɛrii.

ref: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
text: Denii Koori Deevid baaŋ fuuh dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛr Uza digni ni baaŋfuuih wia. Ba jaa ra yir de Pɛrɛz Uza, haali ni zinaa.

ref: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
text: A hɔl hiŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Deevid dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia, u ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ Dakka naa ɛɛ ba n benei?”

ref: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
text: U faa waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi ú kpa a Dakka ba u be bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, ka jaa bir kpau la Gaf hinuu Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia.

ref: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
text: Denii ba la ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be gunla Kɔraawiizi n kissi Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm ani u diahina maa, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la n du u dia la wia. Awia, Koori Deevid la Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia di ga kpa a Dakka ba Deevid bolzeŋ la, di ra di u hiŋ, u bɔra sɔɔni werge maa.

ref: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
text: Baŋ wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ ni a bol biini, ba kpau ga chiŋŋi Tanti Dia la biini Koori Deevid n gillɛ ba baŋ, ú ɛɛ u chiŋŋi bɔr la. Koori Deevid jaa lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
text: Ka jaa tɛɛ Izrɛl baal ni haaŋ maa paanuubire ni olɔɔzaa ani grepu nɔŋhilaa. Denii bɛl maa jaa kaali u dia.

ref: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
text: Koori Deevid n wa bittɛ la dia ú ga jaami u diahina, Koori Sɔɔl biihaaŋ Mikal lii chem u ni, di ŋɔ u be, “Izrɛl koori nyiŋŋi sɔnzenne tɛɛ u hiŋ zinaa. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ genii, di wir u hiŋ, di ra sa u dia yoŋhaana see!”

ref: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
text: Koori Deevid bir ŋɔ Mikal be, “Kɔraawiizii n faa sa di ra chɔli. U lizimbuu ka vɛɛ i mɛɛ ni u diahina maa, n ɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa sitɔɔri, di ra binni ba ni. Awia, n danna sa di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi saŋa maa.

ref: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
text: Keŋ waarɛ ń jaa du n hiŋ hiihzi werge, i ra fɛ lugɔ maa kummaa ɛɛwɛ. Ka a haana naa waa be, n ɛɛ nɛzenne di dɔɔ girme!”

ref: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
text: N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá vɛɛ u nɔŋŋaa gunla miŋ vɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl nɔŋŋaa, di lizuu ka gil i kpa a kora la.

ref: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
text: Denii u ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan be, “Na, miŋwaa ra zuu diinanii la baŋ kpa hɛriŋkpol daazii di ma, ka Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la waa chi tanti dia biini!”

ref: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
text: Netan bir ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Ɛɛ gunla maa i bampirii n lauwɛ. Kɔraawiizi du i benii.”

ref: That night, the Lord told Nathan
text: A hɔl hamuŋa ni, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Netan be,

ref: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
text: “La ga ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ n ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma dia di tɛŋ n na zuu.

ref: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
text: Maa dia maa biini duwɛɛ di haŋ lii a hɔl la miŋ lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri, di wa lii ni zinaa. Bɔr la maa n ni baa n ɔɔ la, tanti dia biinii n ɔɔ du.

ref: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
text: Bɔr la maa n ni Izrɛl hina n ɔɔ la, n ŋmɛnɛ haa ŋɔ ba sitɔɔri bɛl maa miŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ u ra binni n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni be lugɔ ú ma hɛriŋkpol daazi dia di tɛŋwaa?’

ref: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
text: Awia, ŋɔ n balii Koori Deevid be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, ‘N liziibuu lii peeza nɔɔnaa biini, di gil i di kora n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni.

ref: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
text: N du i benii bɔr la maa hiŋ faa laŋŋɛ, di gil i kpegli i dɔma maa. Filaŋkeŋ, n daŋ gil i dɔɔ sɔnzeŋ alugɔ durnya nɛzenaa n dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
text: N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sognibɔr, di gil bá so de, de ɛɛ ba himmaa hɛri. Nɛr maa wàá kaa ra tɔɔri baa. Biinikpola hina wàá kaa ra fir baa gunla baŋ faa ra ɛɛ baa lugli la,

ref: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
text: di haa ra ɛɛ baa saŋa la maa miŋ lizi baa ba ra binni Izrɛl hina ni la. N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii daŋ gil i ni i naanna ra di kora saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
text: Di i saŋa wa hello i ga chɔɔ i naabaala be, n daŋ gil i himmaa biibaal kpa i gawa, ń gil u kora chi nɛnnɛ.

ref: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
text: Waabuu niŋ wa ma Dia tɛŋ. N daŋ gil u kora chi di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
text: N daŋ ɛɛ u mɛɛ, ú ge ɛɛ n biibaal. Di u haŋ wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, n daŋ tɛr u digni gunla mɛɛ n ɔɔ tɛr u biibaal digni la.

ref: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ tɛɛ i balii lugɔ i daŋ gil u naanna ɛɛ koora. Awia, i balii dɔɔ bɔkpegaa ú suŋŋi wiizi naa.

ref: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
text: Denii Koori Deevid jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la di so, ka ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, anɛɛ ń ni n diahinai, i teŋ ɛɛ wia mag keŋ tɛɛ yaai?

ref: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
text: Ɛrɛɛ ń kaa ŋɔi? I zum mìŋ́ i balii biini maanii, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa.

ref: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
text: Dikuu i wiŋɔɔlii ni i kipar wia, i ɛɛ wizeŋ naabuu, di gil mìŋ́ i balii zumuu.

ref: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, i dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge. Nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi. Yaa himmaa digna nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
text: Hɛri maa hina waa hoo di ɛɛ lugɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina, hiŋ lɛɛwɛ lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, ba ɛɛ i hora la. Nuukpuuri wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa la gillɔɔ i sɔŋ yaari durnya maa biini. I lɛɛ i nɛraa lii Ijip hɛri, di ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wia, di duŋŋi hɛssi hina ni ba vuga ba see, saŋa la baŋ liiwɛ di ra ba la.

ref: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
text: I gillɔɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina ɛɛ i hora di hanna la, i birgi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.

ref: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
text: Guŋ gil i sɔŋ dɔɔ girme, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Denii nɛra jaa ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ra binni Izrɛl hina ni.’ I daŋ gil i balii Koori Deevid domee du de, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, i ɛɛ Kɔraawiizii! I wiŋɔzi dɔɔ wibiire. Hinuu ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ winanaa naa tɛɛ i balii.

ref: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
text: Awia, gil a parii filaŋkeŋ, í kissi i balii naanna, bá du de di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, kenne i ŋɔ nua tɛŋ lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ. Wibii, a keŋ ɛɛi daŋ gil n naanna na kissaa, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
text: Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaayaa faa ra binni Kɛrɛf ni Pɛlɛf hina ni. Koori Deevid biibaala ge faa ra biruu liize.

ref: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
text: Koori Deevid kaa kpegli Moab hina ge. Denii u gil ba chɔɔ hɛri, u kpa ŋmɛŋ mɛgzi baa. U guŋ bɔra anɛɛ nɛra maanii u ɔɔ gil ba kpuuzi, ka ɔɔ gil u horohiŋ waa nɛra du de. Awia, ba birgi u balaa, di ɔɔ lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu.

ref: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
text: Koori Deevid kaa lɔ Rɛhɔb biibaal Hadadɛɛza la n faa ɛɛ Zoba koori laal, saŋa la Koori Hadadɛɛza n faa laŋŋɛ, ú kaa ga gil Muu Yufretis kɛraa bola maa birgi u hora la.

ref: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
text: Siiria hina n lii Damaskus la n wa ballɛ, bá wa hiini Zoba Koori Hadadɛɛza, Koori Deevid faa kpu ba laallɔɔra kagboŋa tokko ni anɛɛ.

ref: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
text: Awia, Koori Deevid jaa kpa u laallɔɔra baŋhina soŋŋi Damaskus n du Siiria hɛri, bá ra guu de, di dɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa, di gil ba ra lizi hɛri kuna di waa tɛu. Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ faa giluu Koori Deevid kpegli u dɔma, bɔr la maa uŋ ɔɔ la.

ref: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
text: Koori Deevid paagi laal saliŋ pɛrɛtuzenaa la n ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔnzi hora, di kpaa ba Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
text: Di lii bolzenaa la banna yir Tɛba ni Bɛrɔtai n faa ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza hora la, Koori Deevid faa paagi danyɛ werge maa.

ref: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
text: Koori Tuu hum u biibaal Joram, ú ga jaami Koori Deevid, dikuu uŋ kpegli Koori Hadadɛɛza laal biini wia. Koori Tuu ni Koori Hadadɛɛza ge faa ra lɔ laallɛ. Joram faa kpa saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa ani danyɛ kuŋkuaraa di wa sunzi Koori Deevid.

ref: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
text: Koori Deevid faa kpa a kuna naabuu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla uŋ faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa uŋ faa foozee lii hɛssi hina la maa uŋ kpeglee be tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la.

ref: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
text: Ahitub biibaal Zadɔk ni Abiata biibaal Ahimɛlɛk genii faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina. Sɛraaya ge faa ra sɛbi a koori hɔna.

ref: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
text: Zɛruya biibaal Joabrɛ faa ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra maa nabɔma, Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge faa sɛbi ba wiɛɛlaa di ra dau.

ref: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
text: A hɔl bɛl, Koori Deevid pɛɛzi, “Nɛbɛl haa kawɔɔrɛ di du de lii Koori Sɔɔl naanna biini, ń ɛɛ winanii bɛl tɛu, dikuu Jonatan wiaa?”

ref: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
text: A saŋa, di Koori Sɔɔl diahina balii bɛl banna yir Ziba faa du de. Denii ba yiruu ba Koori Deevid see, u pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu Ziba laa?” U sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, i baliirɛ miŋ.”

ref: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
text: Koori pɛɛzuu, “Nɛbɛl haa du denii lii Koori Sɔɔl dia, ń ɛɛu winanaa gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi laa?” Ziba ŋɔ, “Jonatan biibaal bɛl haa du denii, di ɛɛ gbɛrii.”

ref: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
text: A koori pɛɛzi, “Lee u duɛi?” Ziba ŋɔ, “U du Ammiɛl biibaal Makir la n du bolzeŋ Lo Dɛba dia.”

ref: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
text: Jonatan biibaal Mɛfibɔsɛf la n ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl naana n wa ba Koori Deevid be, u togni u see di jaamuu girme ni. Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu ba ra yir Mɛfibɔsɛf laa?” U sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, i baliirɛ miŋ.”

ref: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm, n daŋ ɛɛi winanaa, dikuu i mɛɛ Jonatan wia. N daŋ bir kpa i naabaal Koori Sɔɔl hɛri maa tɛi, ka n nii kpau di ra di n dia.”

ref: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
text: Mɛfibɔsɛf togni u see girme ni, di ŋɔ, “Jara, maa nuahiŋsiwii bɔwɛɛ, ka i ra tɛŋ a girme naa dɔŋaa?”

ref: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
text: Denii Koori Deevid yir Koori Sɔɔl balii Ziba, di ŋɔ u be, “N kpa i dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl ani u diahina kundɔɔlaa maanii di ra tɛɛ u naana Mɛfibɔsɛf, á ɛɛ u hora.

ref: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
text: Koora la maa Koori Hadadɛɛza n faa kpeglee la maa n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba la ga di kuu Izrɛl hina be, Izrɛl hina jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ba ni. Awia, Siiria hina la jaa ra ɔm Ammɔn hina hiinaa.

ref: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
text: Denii Koori Deevid lɔ nfɛrɛ di ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ Koori Nahas biibaal Koori Hanun, gunla u mɛɛ n faa ɛɛŋ winanaa la.” Awia, Koori Deevid jaa hum nɛra, bá ga jaami Koori Hanun, u mɛɛ lee. Koori Deevid laallɔɔra hiŋ n ga hel Ammɔn hɛri, di la bá ga jaami Koori Hanun,

ref: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
text: Ammɔn nabɔnzi ŋɔ Koori Hanun be, “I ɛɛ tamiirɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid n na tɔgzi i mɛɛ wiarɛ u gil nɛra naa ba, bá wa jaamii u lee gɛɛ? Ba waa ballɛ lɛi bá wa daani a hɛri na, ka wer kpegli yaa?”

ref: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
text: Awia, Koori Hanun gil ba lauri Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la, di fuŋ ba taŋhuna keŋkerezi, di mɔnni ba bɔmbɔga, bá zɛɛpume baambaana, ka ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ Koori Deevid be guŋ, u hum u balaa bá ga chem ba ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa du baabuu hiihzi werge maa. Koori Deevid tili ba be, di ŋɔ, “Ií du bolzeŋ Jɛriko guŋŋ ii taŋhunazi wa hel mɔɔ, ka ii jaa ra ba.”

ref: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
text: Ammɔn hina n jaa wa zum lugɔ ba wia ra fuuh Koori Deevid baannɛ werge maa la, ba jaa ga kpa Siiria hina laallɔɔra kagboŋa tokko la n na vol naazi lii bolzenaa Bɛf Rɛhɔb ani Zoba, di kpa Maaka koori ge ni u laallɔɔra kagboŋ ni laallɔɔra kagboŋa fidaanɛɛ ge lii Tɔb hɛri jaa.

ref: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
text: Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega! Gil ya dɔɔ bampirii di yoo, di lɛɛ yaa nɛra ani Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la bolzenaa. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ gunla n dɛkkɛ u be.”

ref: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u hum Joab ni u laallɔɔra maa, bá ga lɔ baa.

ref: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
text: Ammɔn hina lii chi, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya ba bolzeŋ dominua, ka Siiria laallɔɔra la n lii Zoba ni Rɛhɔb ani laallɔɔra la ge n lii Tɔb ni Maaka la n ballɛ, bá wa hiini baa la chi a laŋgara.

ref: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
text: Denii Joab na lugɔ a laallɔɔra baŋhina chigɔ u seere, baŋhina ge chi u har. Awia, u lizi u laallɔɔra la baŋhina n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, Izrɛl laallɔɔra biini, u ni baa yoo Siiria hina la.

ref: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
text: Ka gil u niwee Abisai ge tɔ banla n kawɛɛ la see, bá yoo Ammɔn hina la.

ref: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
text: Joab ŋɔ Abisai be, “Di Siiria hina haŋ waa kpegliŋ, í ra chɔ n wile. Ka di Ammɔn hina hiŋ ge waa kpeglii, n ge daŋ wa chɔ i wile.

ref: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
text: Joab ni u laallɔɔra la, bá ga lɔ Siiria laallɔɔra la, ka Siiria laallɔɔra hiŋ bir chɔ.

ref: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
text: Ammɔn hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Siiria hina la bittɔɔ di ra chɔ la, ba ge chɔ lii Abisai be, di bir zuu ba bolzeŋ la biini. Denii Joab bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
text: Siiria hina la n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hina kpegli baabuu la, ba kaa chaali.

ref: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
text: Denii Koori Hadadɛɛza gil ba ga yir Siiria laallɔɔra la n du Muu Yufretis wiifurii baŋgia la di wa jaa, di gil Sobak la n ɛɛ Koori Hadadɛɛza laallɔɔra nabɔma ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, ba la bolzeŋ Hɛlam.

ref: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u chaali Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa, di gi Jɔɔdan muu di la Hɛlam. Siiria laallɔɔra hiŋ ge ɛɛ sirya, bá ni Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra lɔ dɔŋa.

ref: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
text: Wem maga, saŋa la koora n ɔɔ ra la laal la, Koori Deevid hum u laallɔɔra nabɔma Joab ani Izrɛl hɛri laallɔɔra maa, bá ga lɔ Ammɔn hina di kpegli baa, ka fɔɔ bolzeŋ Raba hina ge. Ka Koori Deevid waa faa du Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
text: aŋhinabe, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh, ú pɛɛzii, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ii la ga dugli a bolzeŋ werge maa guŋ, ii lɔ baai? Ií waa zummɛ lugɔ ba daŋ ga ba koŋlaa ni di ra virgi ia hobeea?

ref: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ, a haaŋ hum dí ba ga ŋɔ Koori Deevid be lugɔ u kpogli hiarɛ.

ref: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
text: Awia, Koori Deevid tili Joab be lugɔ ú gil Hitti hinuu Yuria ba wa nau. Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u tau ŋmɛnɛɛ u ba Koori Deevid be.

ref: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
text: Yuria n ballɛ, Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu gunla Joab ni u laallɔɔra n duwɛɛ ani gunla a laal wia n na vol.

ref: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Yuria be, la dia ga sɔ nii. Yuria lii. Koori Deevid jaa kpa sunzaa dí ba ga tɛu.

ref: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
text: Ka Yuria vɛɛ u dia laŋaa, ka chɔɔ Koori Deevid balaa la n ɔɔ chɔɔ ra guu u dominuuzeŋ la be.

ref: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Yuria waa sɛɛwɛ la dia, u pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ haa dia laŋŋɛi? I lii bolle birgi.”

ref: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
text: Yuria ŋɔ u be, “Izrɛl ani Juda hina du laal biinii, Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la gba du bá be de. N nabɔma Joab ni u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi maa chɔɔ lɛl biinii. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ miŋwaa la dia, di ga di, di nyɔɔ, ka n ni n haaŋ chɔɔi? N hɛɛhzii, màá ɛɛ a guŋ widee maa!”

ref: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Yuria be, “Guŋwaa, chɔɔ zinaa, ka kɛrɛ n tai ŋmɛnɛɛ í bir kaali.” U jaa chɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm hɔpizaa anɛɛ.

ref: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
text: Koori Deevid yiruu, u nuu di, di gil u dɛɛzi. Ka a hamuŋa hiŋ, Yuria kaa vɛɛ dia laŋaa, ka kpa u kita lii chɔɔ kooridia guure chɔɔribɔr.

ref: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, Koori Deevid sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ Yuria, dí u kpa ra la ga tɛɛ Joab.

ref: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
text: Kenne Koori Deevid sɛbi a hɔŋ biini, “Kpa Yuria du a laal bɔkpeg, ka chɔ lii u be, bá kpuu.”

ref: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
text: Awia, Joab ni u laallɔɔra n wa fɔɔ a bolzeŋ, u jaa taa Yuria du bɔr la ba dɔma hiŋ n kpekke, di siili ba ni.

ref: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
text: A bolzeŋ laallɔɔra n wa liwɛɛ lɔ Joab ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ, ba faa kpu Koori Deevid laallɔɔra baŋhinaa, haali di kpu Hitti hinuu Yuria gba jaa.

ref: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
text: Denii Joab jaa hum nɛr ú la ga bagli wia la maa n ɛɛwɛ a laal biini tɛɛ Koori Deevid.

ref: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
text: U ŋɔ nɛr la uŋ hummɛ la be, “Di i haŋ wa bagli a koori a laal wiimaa tuŋ,

ref: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
text: Ií waa liizi gunla baŋ faa kpu Gidiɔn biibaal Abimɛlɛk laa? Tɛbɛzii, haaŋ faa kpa nam ga koŋlii ni ta, di lɔu kpu. Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii zum guŋ ka la ga dugli a koŋliiwei?’ Di u wa pɛɛzii keŋ, ŋɔ u be lugɔ ba kpu u balii Hitti hinuu Yuria gbaa jaa.”

ref: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
text: A baal la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ wia la maa Joab n humuu ŋɔ ú wa ŋɔ u be la.

ref: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
text: U ŋɔ, “Yaa dɔma hiŋ faa kpekkoo werge maa kaali yaa, haali ba lii a bol biini di wa lɔ yaa a bol laŋgara. Ka yaa nyaŋŋi baa, di taa baa ga du a bol dominuuzeŋ.

ref: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
text: Jara, ka ba laallɔɔra hiŋ baŋhina ga a koŋlii ni di virgi yaa hobee, di kpu yaa baala la baŋhina. Haali ba kpu i balii Hitti hinuu Yuria gbaa jaa.”

ref: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ a huŋhunni be, “Ga ŋɔ Joab be dí u gilɛɛ gil ú biini chɔgi dikuu guŋ wia, laal waa maa biini, hàá wer zum nɛr la n niŋ siu. Ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú chiiri zɛɛ di lɔ a bolzeŋ hina, di puruu.”

ref: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
text: Batsiiba n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba kpu u jaari Yuria, u wiiu werge maa.

ref: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
text: A lee wia n wa tunnɛ, Koori Deevid jaa gil ba ga kpogli Batsiiba ba u dia, u wa birgi u haaŋ, di lul biibaal tɛu. Ka a wii naa Koori Deevid n ɛɛwɛ naa faa waa Kɔraawiizi pattɛ.

ref: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
text: Dɔɔŋ la dɔɔ peeza ni nauna werge maa,

ref: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
text: Denii a hɔl bɛl, hɔɔhri bɛl wa zuu a dɔɔŋ, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ú lau u peeza gɛɛ u nauna bɛl maa hɔɔhruu. Ka ga lau a nyaari la pekpaŋ la uŋ dɔɔwɛ la di kpu hɔɔhruu.”

ref: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ fuuh a baal wia werge maa, u ŋɔ Netan be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la lugɔ baal la n ɛɛ a guŋ wii naa dɛg kpuirɛ.

ref: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
text: A dɛkkɔɔ u kpa peeza anaazu di bir turgi a peezi kim, dikuu a keŋ sikpegii ni biinikpola wia naa uŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ a baal, waa u ni sunne la wia.”

ref: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
text: Denii Netan ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Hinuu a bádee. Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘N tɔibuu Izrɛl hina kora, di lɛɛi lii Koori Sɔɔl be.

ref: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
text: N kpa i dɔɔri dia ni u haana maanii du i nonee, di kpa Izrɛl ni Juda hina tɛi. Di annii faa waa i siwii suwee, n daŋ faa tɛi aŋhina jaa.

ref: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
text: Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i vɛɛ n widaulaa, ka ɛɛ a keŋ wichɔgaai? I gillɔɔ ba kpu Hitti hinuu Yuria laal biini. I gillɔɔ Ammɔn hina kpuu, ka i kpa u haaŋ.

ref: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
text: Awia, jimini maa biini, i naanna baŋhina daŋ ɔɔ siu siukpega, dikuu hiŋ vɛɛ n nua ka kpa Hitti hinuu Yuria haaŋ wia.’

ref: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
text: N daŋ gil dɔgnya ni tɔɔrɔɔ werge lii i himmaa dia, di chol i ni. N daŋ kpa i haana tɛɛ i lulli himmaa bɛl, u ni baa nyiŋŋi dɔŋa bɔchaaŋ, í sibɔɔ.

ref: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
text: I suahwɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ, ka miŋwaa daŋ gil guŋ ɛɛ bɔchaaŋ yeŋgeleŋ, Izrɛl hina maa na.”

ref: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
text: Denii Netan kpa kaali dia. Ka Kɔraawiizi gil wiila chol a bie la Yuria haaŋ n lullɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid la ni.

ref: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
text: Koori Deevid suŋŋi wiizi lugɔ u faa gil a bie nyaagi. Di ɔɔ vɔɔ nua, di zuu du u diichɔɔlii hamuŋa maa, di ɔɔ chɔɔ hɛri guŋŋ hɔɔ wa pizi.

ref: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
text: U dia nabɔnzi ɔɔ zuu u be di ra suŋŋuu lugɔ u izi a hɛri, ka u vɛɛ, di ɔɔ vɛɛ diwee gba dii.

ref: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl, a bie siu. Ɔnsii lau koori balaa, gunla ban niŋ ɛɛ ŋɔ u be a bie siu wia. Ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Bie naa n faa haa ra nyiŋ gba, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ú nuu yaa fɔrgaa. Ka kennaa n jaa ɛɛ naa waa nyaŋŋɛɛaa? Di u wa nuu guŋ, a guŋ daŋ wer gil u ɛɛ u hiŋ wichɔgii bɛl gba.”

ref: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ u balaa hiŋ n na munni dɔŋa be, u jaa zum lugɔ a bie siuwɔɔ. U pɛɛzi baa, “A bie siuwɔɔ gɛɛ?” Ba ŋɔ “Ɛɛh u siuwɔɔ.”

ref: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
text: U balaa pɛɛzuu, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra ɛɛ kennei? A bie n faa ra nyiŋ, i ra wiiu di vɔɔ nua, ka uŋ wa siuwɛ, i jaa izi di di diwee!”

ref: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
text: U ŋɔ, “A bie n faa haa du de ni miibɔɔ la, n vɔɔ nuarɛ di wii, di faa fɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ na n sinyɛna, di giluu tɛŋ.

ref: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, uŋ jaa siu naa, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń kaa ra vɔɔ nuai? N daŋ kaa wer gil ú dɔɔ miibɔɔa? Akai! Minuu niŋ la u be, waabuu wàá ka wer ba n be.”

ref: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon

text: Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u togni hɛri di jaami Koori Deevid, ka ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, Kɔ́raawiizi kissii. I gillɔɔ n zum zinaa lugɔ i dɔɔ n bilaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, i nuu n suŋŋaarɛ.”

ref: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
text: Denii Joab jaa la Gɛsur, di ga kpogli Absalɔm di bir ba Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
text: Ka Koori Deevid ŋɔ Joab be, “Gil u ra la u dia. Maa nyiŋŋi n nau ni siwii.” Absalɔm jaa kpa la u dia, di waa koori nawɛɛ ni siwii.

ref: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
text: U faa dɔɔ nyuhunaa werge, di ɔɔ ra funaa kakpaŋ, bina maa biini, di a wa sukko werge. Di u wa funaa, a tɔgzi ɔɔ ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaanɛɛrɛ, gunla banna mɛgzaa kooridia la.

ref: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
text: Absalɔm biizi faa du banaazu, baala bahoro ni biihambikpaŋ. U biihaaŋ hiŋ sɔnnɛ faa Taama. U faa ɛɛ toloori werge maa.

ref: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
text: Absalɔm faa du Jɛrusalɛmnɛ binni anɛɛ, di waa Koori Deevid nawɛɛ ni siwii.

ref: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
text: Denii Absalɔm hum Joab bɔr lugɔ ú ba, ú humuu Koori Deevid be, ka Joab vɛɛ balaa. U kaa hum u bɔr, ka u haa vɛɛ.

ref: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
text: Absalɔm ŋɔ u balaa be, “Ií na, n ni Joab kooni pɛli dɔŋaa, u dɔɔ baali. Ií la ga fuuah.” U balaa hiŋ la ga fuuh a koo maa.

ref: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
text: Joab n wa nuu guŋ, u hahzi di kpa la Absalɔm be u dia, di ga pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ wiarɛ i balaa la ga fuuh n kooi?”

ref: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
text: Absalɔm ŋɔ u be, “Na, n hum i bɔttɛ lugɔ í ba ń humii Koori Deevid be, í ga pɛɛzuu lugɔ bɛɛ wiarɛ n lii Gɛsur ba ɛnnɛi? Ka ii vɛɛ balaa. Di n faa haa du de gba bɔ n ɛŋ balaa naa. Awia, la ga ŋɔ u be lugɔ n na nyiŋŋuu ń nuu na dɔŋa. Di u wa nawɔɔ lugɔ n ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, ú kpuŋ.”

ref: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
text: Awia, Joab la Koori Deevid be, di ga ŋɔ gunla maa Absalɔm n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Koori hum dí ba ga yir Absalɔm. Absalɔm n wa ballɛ, u togni jaami Koori Deevid. Koori Deevid faamuu, di suuzuu.

ref: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Absalɔm nyiŋŋi torko, zagra ani baala tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, bá ɔɔ tɔ u see di ra chɔ.

ref: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
text: U ɔɔ feluu izi di ga teŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ la n chɔɔwɛ di gaa zuu a bolzeŋ dominuuzeŋ la. Di nɛr maa haŋ wa kpa u wia di ra ba koori be ú kuari, Absalɔm ɔɔ yir a hinnɛ di pɛɛzuu, “Lee bolle i liiyɛi?” A hiŋ ɔɔ jaa bagluu bol la ni dee la biini uŋ liwɛɛ.

ref: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
text: Absalɔm ɔɔ ŋɔ a hiŋ be, “I hor summɔɔ, ka koori nɛr maa waa hoo ɛŋ ú nuu tɛi.”

ref: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
text: Absalɔm ɔɔ kaa ŋɔ, “Alako ba faa lizimbuu n ɛɛ hɛri naa seriya diiri! Guŋwaa, di nɛr la maa kpa wia ba n be, n daŋ ɔɔ dia ni wibii.”

ref: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
text: Awia, di nɛr maa haŋ wa ba u be, di ŋɔ u tognuu, Absalɔm ɔɔ feluu faamuu, di suuzuu.

ref: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
text: Kenne Absalɔm kpa di ra ɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maa n ɔɔ ba Koori Deevid be, ú di u wia ni wibii la. Guŋ jaa gil ba nɔŋŋuu werge maa kaali Koori Deevid.

ref: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
text: Binni anaazu n wa bɛrɛɛ, Absalɔm ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Jara, tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń la bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn di ga lizi nua bɛl miŋ lɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
text: Saŋa la miŋ faa du Gɛsur la n du Siiria labuu n lɛɛ a nua, di ŋɔ, ‘Di Kɔraawiizi hiiniŋ n wer hel Jɛrusalɛm, n daŋ ga jaamuu bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn biini.’ ”

ref: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “A la ni bampirsɔna.” Absalɔm jaa kpa kaali bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn.

ref: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
text: Denii nɛbɛl wa ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Izrɛl hina maanii chɔwɛɛ di ra hiŋ Absalɔm ka kai.”

ref: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
text: Denii Koori Deevid yir u nabɔnzi la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm la, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ya chɔ lii ɛŋ, di guŋ lɛi, Absalɔm wàá gil yaa. Yá lii manaŋ, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ wa kpuuzi yaa ni a bolzeŋ hina maa ge di jaa!”

ref: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
text: Denii Koori Deevid zɛɛsogna hiŋ ŋɔ u be, “Gunla maa hiŋ nawɛɛ, yaa maa hotte.”

ref: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
text: Koori Deevid ni u nabɔnzi chi ka ra binni u laallɔɔra, Kɛrɛf ni Pɛlɛf hina maa ani Giti hina n lii Gaf laallɔɔra kalfaanumbɛl la maa n duu la maa wa bɛri kaali.

ref: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
text: A koori bir ŋɔ Giti hinuu Ittai la n lii Gaf be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i hiŋ yaa di ra lanɛi? Bir di ra la Koori Absalɔm be. I ɛɛ famaruurɛ, di chɔ wa du ɛŋ.

ref: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
text: I ɛŋ balaa haa waa birgee. Ka ń gil i vol di ra juuriaa? Maa zum n nyuu chaŋribɔr. Awia, bir zuu a bolzeŋ di lauri i hɛri nɛra, i ni baa ra la. Kɔ́raawiizi ga suŋ i ni, di hiinii.”

ref: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
text: Ka Ittai ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, n hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa lugɔ bɔr la maa hin niŋ la, n niibuu, haali di siurɛ ń nii maa kpau siu gba.”

ref: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Guŋwaa, yaa ra la!” Denii Ittai ni u nɛra ani ba lulla maa jaa hiŋ dɔŋa di lii a bol biini.

ref: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
text: Nɛra la maa n du a de hɛri kɛraa la ra wii werge maa, saŋa la Koori Deevid ni u nɛra n wa bɛrɛɛ di ra kaali la. Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ kpa di ga Kidrɔn Waluu, di bir chaŋ hɛribɔduma.

ref: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
text: Zadɔk gba faa jaa ba ninɛɛ. Ka haali Levi dee la maa ge n faa du u be la chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la di ra la. Ba ga chuguu chiŋŋi, Abiata lizi mbusuzi guŋŋ a nɛra maa wa lii a bol biini tuŋ.

ref: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Zadɔk be, “Bir kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ zuu a bolzeŋ biini. Di n wia par Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ gil n bir ba Jɛrusalɛm di wa na a Dakka u Dia biini.

ref: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
text: Ka di n wia wɔɔ pattɛ, n ɛɛ siryaa lugɔ ú ɛɛŋ gunla maa n paruu.”

ref: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ Zadɔk ge be, “Sinaari lɛi hiŋŋ? Bir di ra zuu a bolzeŋ ani bampirsɔna. Kpogli i biibaal Ahimaz ani Abiata biibaal Jonatan, í ni baa ra la.

ref: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
text: N daŋ so a muu yarizi hɛribɔduma naa biini, di ra kpaŋ saŋa la hin niŋ wa ŋɔ wii bɛl tɛŋ.”

ref: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
text: Denii Zadɔk ni Abiata kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ, di bir zuu Jɛrusalɛm ga so de.

ref: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
text: Ka Koori Deevid kpa kuŋ tɔ u nyuu, di wii ra tinni Ɔlivizi Bizeŋ nyuu di ra kaali ni u naadumazi. A nɛra la maa u ni baa n na la la maa, ge kpa kuna tɔɔgi ba nyuuni, di wii ra hiŋuu.

ref: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
text: Koori Deevid n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Ahitɔfɛl ge gba jaa a nɛra la ni Absalɔm n ɛɛ ú kpui sirya la biinii, u suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hin niŋ gil Ahitɔfɛl wiŋɔzi la maa uŋ ga ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Absalɔm, di bir u nfɛrɛ la maa ɛɛ wipɛɛri!”

ref: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
text: Koori Deevid n wa hel a bizeŋ nyuu, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ ra jaami Kɔraawiizi la, di Aaki hinuu Husai la du de di ra kpaŋuu. Haali di lau u laalaa piili, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa waari u nyuu.

ref: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “Di i haŋ hiŋiŋ la, i wia daŋ ɛɛ tɔɔrɔɔ tɛŋ.

ref: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
text: Ka di i wa bittɔ la a bolzeŋ, ga ŋɔ Absalɔm be, ‘N dɔɔri, n daŋ ɛɛ i balii, n faa ɛɛ i mɛɛ baliirɛ, n jaa ra nyiŋŋuu ń ɛɛ i balii filaŋkeŋ.’ I daŋ wer ga a guŋ ni, di hiiniŋ di chɔgi Ahitɔfɛl baglaa la.

ref: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk ni Abiata maa daŋ du de. Ŋɔ ba be wii la maa hin niŋ nuu lii a kooridia.

ref: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
text: Gil ba hum ba biibaala Ahimaz ni Jonatan, bá wa ŋɔ n be wii la maa hiŋ nuuwɛ.”

ref: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
text: Denii Koori Deevid dammu Husai bir kpa ba Jɛrusalɛm. Uŋ wa hel de, di Absalɔm hanna zuu a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
text: Koori Deevid n wa lii a giŋgimii nyubaaŋ di tuu la see tama, u chem Mɛfibɔsɛf balii Ziba ni, di u chigɔ ra kpaŋuu, di kpogli kauzi, a chi paanuuzi kalfaanɛɛ, grepu nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil kalfa ani fig nɔna baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa a hil ge kalfa.

ref: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
text: Koori Deevid pɛɛzi Ziba, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i chi kuna naa banɛi?” Ziba ŋɔ, “Koori diahinaa dɔɔ a kauzi naa, bá ra tinni. A paanuuzi ani daanɔna naa ge ɛɛ a baala horaa, bá kpa di. Banla maa ge n wa kuuhwɛ a hɛribɔduma biini, daŋ wer nyɔɔ a siŋ, fɔŋŋa kaa ba.”

ref: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
text: Denii Koori Deevid pɛɛzuu, “Lee i dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl naana Mɛfibɔsɛf la duɛi?” Ziba ŋɔ u be, “U du Jɛrusalɛm. U ra fɛu lugɔ Izrɛl hina daŋ kpa u naabaal Koori Sɔɔl kora la tɛu.”

ref: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ Ziba be, “Kuna la maa n ɛɛ Mɛfibɔsɛf kuna jaa ɛɛ i horaa.” Ziba ŋɔ, “Ani i huma n dɔɔri, gil n wia ra parii saŋaa saŋa maa.” Simei n see Koori Deevid nua wia

ref: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
text: Koori Deevid n waa dugli bol bɛl banna yir Bahurim, baal bɛl n lii Koori Sɔɔl domee biini lii de ba. U sɔnnɛ faa Simei, u mɛɛrɛ Gɛra. Uŋ faa ra ba hiŋ, u faa ra see Koori Deevidii nua, ka ra ba.

ref: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
text: Haali Koori Deevid nabɔnzi, u laallɔɔra ani u guure maa n baruu gba, ka Simei faa ra taazi ba maanii bia.

ref: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
text: Simei n na see baa a nua la, u ŋɔ, “Vol kaali! Nɛkpuuri ni karkanni naa!

ref: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
text: Hinuu foozi Koori Sɔɔl kora, di kaa lau u diahina maa ge di kpuuzi jaa. Kɔraawiizii hanna turgii i wichɔgaa la maa hiŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl ni u diahina la maa kim la. Kɔraawiizi kpa a koraa tɛɛ i biibaal Absalɔm. I kora dii chɔkkɔɔ, nɛkpuuri naa!”

ref: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
text: Denii Zɛruya biibaal Abisai ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “N dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ vasiwii naa ra chagzii kennaanɛi? Gil n la ga teŋ u nyuu!”

ref: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
text: Ka Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Zɛruya biibaala, bɛɛ n ni ia kpawɛi? Di Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú seeŋ nua, anɛɛ n niŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ u ra ɛɛ gunnɛi?”

ref: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Abisai ni nabɔnzi la maa be, “Ií na! N himmaa biilullii n na nyiŋŋi n kpui, ɛrɛɛ bá kaa ŋɔ Bɛnjamin dee hinuu naa wiai? Ií gil u ra seeŋ nua, Kɔraawiizii tɛu a guŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
text: Aŋhinabe, Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ n ni, di bir tɛŋ winanaa, dikuu zinaa nuuseezi naa wia.”

ref: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
text: Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra hiŋ kpa ba ŋmɛnɛɛ di ra kaali, ka Simei ge ra hiŋ baa, di kpa a giŋgimii nyuu keŋkere bɛl di ra kaali, ka ra chagzuu, di paagi bia di ra vuuruu, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa ra viiruu.

ref: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
text: A tuna maa, Koori Deevid ni nɛra la maa n du u be la kpa di ga hel bɔr la banna la la, di ba maa dee jaa kuuh werge. Ba so de di heezi nɛnnɛ. Absalɔm n du Jɛrusalɛm wia

ref: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
text: A saŋa naa, di Absalɔm ni Izrɛl hina maa teŋ ba Jɛrusalɛm, Ahitɔfɛl ge gba faa jaa ba ninɛɛ.

ref: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
text: Denii Aaki hinuu Husai n ɛɛ Koori Deevid dammu la, la Absalɔm be, di ga ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ koori miibɔɔjaŋ!”

ref: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
text: Ka Absalɔm pɛɛzi Husai, “Kenne ba ra nɔŋŋi dammuua? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ haa i dammu hiŋŋɛ kaalɛi?”

ref: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
text: Husai ŋɔ Absalɔm be, “Akai, nɛr la Kɔraawiizi ni a nɛra naa ani Izrɛl hina maa n lizɛɛrɛ ń hiŋ, di du u be saŋa maa.

ref: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, n dɔɔri, anɛɛ ń na hum, di hiŋ lɛiwɛi? Gunla miŋ hummɛ tɛɛ i mɛɛ la, gunnɛ ń hum tɛɛ i gba.”

ref: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
text: Denii Absalɔm ŋɔ Ahitɔfɛl be, “Bir yaa liize. Ɛrɛɛ i ŋɔ ya ɛɛi?”

ref: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
text: Ahitɔfɛl ŋɔ, “Lau i mɛɛ hahjigzi la uŋ gillɛ ba so di ra binni u dia la nyiŋŋi. Di Izrɛl hina maa haŋ wa nuu guŋ, guŋ daŋ gil i wia ra sɔɔhri i mɛɛ miizi, di du banla maa n du i be la bɔkpega nɛnnɛ.”

ref: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
