text: I haa nɔŋŋi banla n haihbuu, ka hah banla n nɔŋŋiibuu! I gillɔɔ a chaani nɛnnɛ maa lugɔ i laallɔɔra sitɔɔra ani i laallɔɔra maa ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii i be. N nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ i bɔra daŋ faa sɔɔnii, di yaa maa faa siuwɔ zinaa, ka i biibaal Absalɔm du de.

ref: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
text: Awia, lii ga du i laallɔɔra hiŋ bɔkpega. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ di haa haŋ ɛɛ guŋ, di kpa ra ba kɛrɛ chɔɔzi, i laallɔɔra naa bɛl maa wàá ka du i be. Gunnɛ niŋ ɛɛ wichuma werge di kaali hɛhchɔg la maa n huuzii guŋŋ di lii pɔlaa saŋa la.”

ref: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
text: Denii Koori Deevid jaa izi lii di ga so a dominuuzeŋ la nua. Baŋ ga ŋɔ laallɔɔra hiŋ be, “A koori sogo a dominuuzenne,” ba maa ba u be. Koori Deevid n bittɛ ba Jɛrusalɛm wia A saŋa naa, di Izrɛl hina maa chɔwɔɔ kaali ba bola.

ref: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
text: Izrɛl hina wiŋɔzi hiŋ maa hel Koori Deevid. Awia, u hum Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Zadɔk ni Abiata lugɔ ba la ga pɛɛzi Juda nabɔnzi, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii tɔ har ií hiini bá kaa kpogli a koori ba u dianɛi?

ref: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
text: Ii ɛɛ n lullaa, yaa maa ɛɛ chakpaŋ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii tɔ har, ii kaa kpogliŋ banɛi?”

ref: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ dí ba ga ŋɔ Amasa ge be, “Yaa waa chakpaŋ ɛɛwɛ lɛiyaa? Di haŋ lii zinaa, n liziibuu í lɛɛ Joab bɔr di ɛɛ n laallɔɔra sitɔɔri. Di maa haŋ ɛɛ guŋ, Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ!”

ref: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
text: U wiŋɔzi la par Juda baala hiŋ werge maa alugɔ baŋ ɛɛ kpaŋ wia. Ba hum ba ga ŋɔ a koori be, “Í ni i nɛra maa bir di ra ba.”

ref: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
text: Gɛra biibaal Simei n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, di lii Bahurim, hahzi la Jɔɔdan muu ú ga chem Koori Deevid ni.

ref: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
text: N zummɔ lugɔ n ɛɛibuu wichɔgaa. Aabuu gillɛ n feli nɛr maa lii Joosɛf diahina biini di ba ɛŋ, ń wa chem i ni la.”

ref: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
text: Ba gi a muu, bá ga kpogli a koori ni u diahina wa gi, di ɛɛ wia la maa unna nyiŋŋi. Simei n wa gi Jɔɔdan muu la, u chol pi a koori see,

ref: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
text: di ŋɔ u be, “Jara, n na suŋŋiibuu werge maa, suuh wichɔgaa la miŋ ɛɛi, a hɔl la hinna lii Jɛrusalɛm la. Gilɛɛ wa kpaa di ra ɛɛŋ wiimaa gɛɛ di kaa ra liizi a wia kɔrai.

ref: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
text: Koori Deevid bir ŋɔ, “Zɛruya biibaala, bɛɛ n ni ia kpauwɛi? Ii birgi n dɔmaa zinaa! A dɛkkɔ baŋ kpu nɛr Izrɛl biini zinaa? Ii fɛ lugɔ maa zummɛ lugɔ minuu Izrɛl hina koori zinaa?”

ref: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
text: A koori hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Simei, “Hàá siu.”

ref: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
text: U ŋɔ, “Jara, i zummɔ lugɔ n ɛɛ gbɛriirɛ. N faa ŋɔ n balii benii lugɔ ú bɔg n kawee ń tinnuu, n nii la, ka u dariŋ.

ref: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
text: Jara, u chɔg n sɔnnɛ i be. Jara, i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl. Awia, ɛɛ gunla maa n parii.

ref: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
text: N naabaal naanna waa wiimaa dɛkkɛ di lii i be di siu bɛŋ lɛi, ka i tɛɛ i baliirɛ bɔr u jaa banla n na di i be. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ n kaa suŋŋii kummaa.”

ref: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
text: A koori ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ kaa ŋɔ wiimaa. Í ni Ziba ga bɔnni i hɛri la.”

ref: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
text: Mɛfibɔsɛf ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, gil Ziba kpogli u maa. Hiŋ bittɛ ba bol ni bɔsɔna naa gba kukkimbuu.”

ref: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
text: Giliad hinuu Bazilai faa lii Rogelim ba Jɔɔdan muu ú wa hiini Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra bá gi.

ref: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
text: A koori ŋɔ Bazilai be, “Gil n nii maa gi a muu di la Jɛrusalɛm ga so, ń na binni i ni.”

ref: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
text: Ka Bazilai ŋɔ a koori be, “Binni aŋmɛnɛɛ n kaa di lugɔ n hiŋii la Jɛrusalɛmnɛi?

ref: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
text: Maa a keŋ kinturgaa naa dɛkkɛ. Hiŋwaa gil n dui gi Jɔɔdan muu, di la see tama.

ref: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
text: Taŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ ń bir di ra la bol di ga siu dugli n mɛɛ ni n maa ŋmama. Ka n biibaal Kimhannɛ keŋ. Jara, gil i nuu gi di ra la. Gaa dawuu gunla maa n parii.”

ref: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “N nuuwɔɔ, n ni Kimham daŋ la. Wii la maa n parii, n daŋ ɛɛ tɛu. Wii la maa ge hinna nyiŋŋi n be, n daŋ ɛɛu tɛi.”

ref: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
text: Awia, a nɛra maa tɔ see di gi a Jɔɔdan muu, ka a koori ge jaa gi. Koori Deevid faami Bazilai, di suuzuu, ka kissuu. Bazilai jaa bir kpo.

ref: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
text: A koori n faa giwɛɛ di la Gilgal la, Kimham waa faa hiŋuubuu gi. Juda hina laallɔɔra maa ni Izrɛl laallɔɔra yeŋ wa jaa, ba maa du a koori gi.

ref: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Izrɛl baala maa ba a koori be, di waa ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa lulla Juda hina baala ŋmɛɛ koori ni u diahina maa di kpogli baa gi Jɔɔdan muu, di kpa u laallɔɔra maa gba jaai?”

ref: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
text: Juda baala maa ŋɔ Izrɛl baala be, “Yaa ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa ni a koori lullɔɔ nɛnnɛ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii baana fuuh a guŋ wiai? Yaa di a koori diweere gɛɛ di kpa u kumbɛlɛi?”

ref: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
text: Denii Izrɛl baala bir ŋɔ Juda baala be, “Yaa dɔɔ a koorii bufi, gunla iiŋ dɔɔu la, haali di u ɛɛ ii bɛl gba. Ka ɛrɛɛ ii ra gbɛlli yaa gunnɛi? Ií gilɛɛ suuh lugɔ yaabuu felee ŋɔ a koori bir balaa wia!” Ka Juda hina faa ra ŋɔ kpegzi ani baaŋ ni, di kaali gunla Izrɛl hina n na ŋɔ la.

ref: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
text: Denii baal bɛl banna yir Bikri biibaal Siiba n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini, di ɛɛ kalu nyiŋŋi, faa jaa ba ni, huuh bensunoniina werge maa, ka pozi di ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, beedee yaa ni Koori Deevid kora la dɔɔ bɔnnaai? Yaa ni Jɛssɛ biibaala waa kummaa bɔnnaa dɔɔwɛ. Aa! Izrɛl hina, ií ra la ii diini.”

ref: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
text: Awia, Izrɛl hina waa vɛɛ Koori Deevid, ka ga hiŋ Siiba di ra la. Ka Juda hina waa sɛɛ Koori Deevid wia, di du u be, di duu lii Jɔɔdan muu guŋŋ di ga hel Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
text: Koori Deevid n wa bittɛ la u dia Jɛrusalɛm biini, u lau u hahjigzi fi la uŋ faa gillɛ ba ra binni u dia la, di du dia bɛl biini, di gil ba ra guu baa. U ra dɛɛzi baa, ka waa kaa sɛɛ u ni bɛl maa chɔɔ. Waa kaa sɛɛ ba lii chaaŋ maa di ra ba ba siu. Ba faa jaa du lugɔ luhaana.

ref: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Amasa be, “Yir Juda baala lugɔ ba maa chaali n be hɔpizaa ahoro biini, í ge gba jaa ba ni.”

ref: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
text: Ka Amasa n laŋŋɛ ú ga yir Juda laallɔɔra la, u ga birgi kaali saŋa la Koori Deevid n tɛu la.

ref: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ Abisai be, “Bikri biibaal Siiba daŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa kaali gunla Absalɔm n ɛɛwɛ la gba. Awia, lau n laallɔɔra di dau u luge, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ chɔ zuu bolzeŋkpega la biine, yaa wàá ka nau lau.”

ref: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
text: Awia, Joab laallɔɔra, koori guure ani laallɔɔra la maa n kawɛɛ la lii Jɛrusalɛm, di ra dau Siiba luge.

ref: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
text: Baŋ ga hel bizeŋ la n du Gibiɔn, Amasa chem ba ni. Di Joab ge laali u laal kuna di kpa u tokobi suu u too di kirsi u chara. Uŋ volle di ra la see la, a tokobi lii chol.

ref: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
text: Joab ŋɔ Amasa be, “N niwee, jaanjaamu, i du ɛrɛɛ?” Denii Joab jaa tɛr u nonii lau Amasa taŋhuna lugɔ unna nyiŋŋi ú suuzuu la.

ref: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
text: Ka Amasa salli lugɔ Joab kpogli tokobii. Joab tɔɔh u hia, u looree vir lii chol hɛri, Amasa siu kakpaŋ. Awia, waa kaa tɔɔuh bunɛɛ. Ka Joab ni u niwee Abisai haa ra dau Siiba luge.

ref: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
text: Joab laallɔɔra la bɛl wa chi Amasa be, ka ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n nɔŋŋi Joab, di sɛɛ Koori Deevid wia, amɔ, ú ra hiŋ Joab!”

ref: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
text: Amasa chɔɔ u chal biini a ŋmɛnibaaŋ. Joab laallɔɔri hiŋ na lugɔ a laallɔɔra maa ballɔɔ di waa chi de. Awia, u tuuzuu lii a ŋmɛnɛɛ di ga dau pir, di yaa tagta tɔu.

ref: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
text: Uŋ wa tuuzi Amasa lii a ŋmɛnɛɛ tuŋ, a nɛra maa hiŋ Joab di ra dau Siiba luge.

ref: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
text: Siiba ga Izrɛl hina dizi maa biine guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋkpeg la banna yir Abɛl Bɛf Maaka la. Bikri domee baala maa chaali hiŋuu zuu a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
text: Joab ni u laallɔɔra maa n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Siiba du de, ba la ga fɔɔ a bolzeŋ, di ta pizenaa pɛli u koŋlii, di kaa faari di ra ki a koŋlii zɛɛ, ú chol.

ref: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
text: Hahnunzunni bɛl du a bolzeŋ lɔ wile werge maa di ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu! Ií ra nuu! Ií ŋɔ Joab be lugɔ ú ba ɛŋ, n ŋɔ wia tɛu.”

ref: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
text: Joab la, u pɛɛzuu, “Hinuu Joab laa?” U ŋɔ “Ɛɛh, minuu.” A haaŋ ŋɔ, “A nuu gunla i balii n niŋ ŋɔ.” Joab ŋɔ, “N na nuuu.”

ref: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
text: U ŋɔ, “Faala maa, a ba ŋɔu, ‘La bolzeŋ Abɛl di ga na i wia zɛɛ.’ Guŋ himmaanii ba ɛɛ la.

ref: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
text: Yaabuu ɛɛ bampirsɔna ni wibii hina Izrɛl hɛri. I ra nyiŋŋuu i chɔgi bolzeŋ la n ɛɛ Izrɛl bola maa nyuu hiŋ. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi i chɔgi Kɔraawiizi kundɔɔliiyɛi?”

ref: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
text: Joab ŋɔ, “Akai! N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá sɛɛ chɔgi ii bolzeŋ naa!

ref: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
text: Gunlɛi kɔrai! Baal bɛl banna yir Siiba, u ɛɛ Bikri biibaal, n lii Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri, faarɔɔrɛ di ra di Koori Deevid mmɔri. Ií lawuu tɛɛ yaa, ka ń gil bolzeŋ naa.” A haaŋ ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ kpa u nyuu ha danzɛɛkɛrii tɛi.”

ref: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
text: Denii a haaŋ zuu a bol biini di ga ŋɔ a bol hina be gunla unna fɛ. Ba jaa teŋ Siiba nyuu, di tau tɛɛ Joab. Joab huuh bensunoniina lugɔ u laallɔɔra gil a bolzeŋ, ka bir di ra kpo. Denii Joab ge bir kaali Koori Deevid be Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
text: Joab faa ɛɛ Izrɛl laallɔɔra maa nabɔmaa. Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya genii faa ɛɛ a koori guure nabɔma.

ref: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
text: Adoniram genii faa ra binni banla baŋ ɔɔ fir ba ra hum huma la nabɔma. Ahilud biibaal Jɛhɔsafat ge faa sɛbi wia di ra dau.

ref: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
text: Siva ge faa ɛɛ ba seriya dii dia karchi. Zadɔk ni Abiata ge faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina.

ref: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
text: Gibiɔn hina faa waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ. Ba faa ɛɛ Amɔri hina yenne, di faa du tama. Izrɛl hina faa hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ di ŋɔ nua lugɔ ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá kpu baa. Ka Sɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋi ú dim baa, dikuu uŋ nɔŋŋi Izrɛl ni Juda hina werge wia.

ref: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
text: Awia, Koori Deevid faa chaali Gibiɔn hina, di ŋɔ ba be, “Bɛɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi ń ɛɛ tɛɛ ia? N na nyiŋŋuu ń turgi wichɔgaa la baŋ kpawɛɛ ɛɛ ia la kim, guŋ gil ii kissi Kɔraawiizi nɛra.”

ref: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
text: Ba ŋɔ, “Koori Sɔɔl nfɛrɛɛ lugɔ ú dim yaa, yá gilɛɛ ka du Izrɛl hɛri yemmaa.

ref: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
text: Awia, lau u naanna la n ɛɛ baala baniidaanɛɛ tɛɛ yaa, yá kpu baa Gibia la n ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl la Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ la bol.” A koori ŋɔ, “N daŋ kpa baa di tɛɛ ia.”

ref: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
text: Ka Koori Deevid faa gil Jonatan biibaal Mɛfibɔsɛf, Sɔɔl naana waa, dikuu nua la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ u mɛɛ la wia.

ref: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
text: Koori Deevid kpa baa tɛɛ Gibiɔn hina, ba kpu baa dau giŋgimii nyuu, Kɔraawiizi see. Ba nɛra baniidaanɛɛhiŋ maanii ba faa kpau kpu, saŋa la baŋ faari baali kumaa la.

ref: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
text: Denii Sɔɔl hahjiga Aaya biihaaŋ Rizpa, kpa gbɔglɔŋ du pampanni bii nyuu, bɔr la a lalaa n chɔɔwɛ la. Di du de, a baali kumaa saŋa guŋŋ di ga hel sazau dooŋ balaa saŋa. Hɔpizaa saŋa, u ɔɔ duŋŋi zumbizi lii ba be, hamuŋzi ge, u duŋŋi pir sela.

ref: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
text: u izi la Jabɛs Giliad hina be, di ga paa Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan hoga. Giliad hina faa ŋmɛɛabuu lii Bɛf San, bɔr la Filisti hina n faa sag baa ŋmɛŋ, saŋa la baŋ kpu Koori Sɔɔl, Gilbɔa la.

ref: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
text: Ba hug Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaal Jonatan hoga Koori Sɔɔl mɛɛ Kis ŋmam, Zɛla n du Bɛnjamin hɛri, gunla Koori Deevid n faa ŋɔ bá ɛɛ la. Kɔraawiizi jaa nuu ba wiisuŋŋaa tɛɛ a hɛri maa. Izrɛl ni Filisti hina laalzi wia

ref: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
text: Denii laal bɛl kaa wa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Gaf. Bazeŋ bɛl n faa helle kpabaa, di dɔɔ nonibee ani naanibee anumbɛlaa, di ge ɛɛ Rafa naana bɛl,

ref: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
text: Denii Isbi Bɛnɔb n ɛɛ Rafa naana bɛl, u danyɛ kandaa nyuu tɔgzi bɛŋ faa ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau kalfaahoro, u kaa laali tokobifalii, faa fɛ lugɔ u daŋ wer kpu Koori Deevid.

ref: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
text: Ka Zɛruya biibaal Abisai ba wa mɔgli Deevid, di kpa u kandaa yag a Filisti hinuu kpu. Denii Koori Deevid laallɔɔra la hɛɛhzi tɛu, di ŋɔ, “Yaa nii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka la laal, dikuubɛɛwiai, hinuu Izrɛl hina tamii, yaa waa nyiŋŋi ya nyaai.”

ref: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, laal kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, bol bɛl banna yir Gɔb. A saŋaa Husa hinuu Sibɛkai faa kpu Rafa naana bɛl banna yir Saf la.

ref: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
text: Laal bɛl kaa chol ba ni Filisti hina ni, Gɔb. A laal naa biinii Jaarɛ Ɔrɛgim biibaal Ɛlhanan n lii Bɛtlihɛm, faa kpu Gaf hinuu Goliaf la kandaa daa n faa gbosse lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daa la.

ref: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
text: ge faa ɛɛ Izrɛl hinaa chɛɛtɛ. Awia, Koori Deevid niwee Simɛya biibaal Jonatan faa lii kpuu.

ref: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
text: Ba nɛra banaazu naabuu faa ɛɛ Rafa naanna, Gaf. Ba maanii Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra faa kpu laal biini.

ref: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
text: U lɛɛmbuu lii n dɔma n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la be, di lɛɛŋ lii n haahra la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge kaaliŋ la be.

ref: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
text: Yir naabuu Koori Deevid faa yir tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu uŋ lɛɛu lii u dɔma maa ni Koori Sɔɔl nonee biini wia.

ref: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, awia, n daŋ chɔlii hɛssi maa hina be. N daŋ yir yira di ra dargii.

ref: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
text: A yittɛ keŋ, “Kɔraawiizii n guuri, waabuu n kpegzi bɔr.

ref: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
text: Waabuu ra guuŋ, di n du u be, n daŋ na n hiŋ. U ra gberimbuu lugɔ laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ. Waabuu n Lɛɛri, waabuu ra guuŋ di ra lɛɛŋ nɛra la n na fir nɛra werge be.

ref: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
text: N yir Kɔraawiizi la n dɛg chɔlaa labuu, awia, u lɛɛmbuu di lii n dɔma be.

ref: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
text: Siu faa barimbuu alugɔ muuzeŋ nii n na lɔ, niikpeg kpeglimbuu.

ref: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
text: N biinichɔg biini, n yir Kɔraawiizii, di lɔ wile tɛu ú hiiniŋ. U nuu n loobiire lii u Dia biini, di nuu n wiraa.

ref: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
text: Denii hɛri ziigi di zigli, chiŋ ge zɛɛzi zigli, a zigloore dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n fuuhwe wia!

ref: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
text: Nyɔɔzi faa ra lii u miibɔɔni, ninlau n na di kuna ra lii u nua, niŋhɔla ge ta di ra lii de.

ref: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
text: U peri chiŋ di tuu ba, baama biŋŋu du u naazi zɛɛ.

ref: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
text: U tinni chɛrubzi di ra zaah, di so peu keeri ni di ra kaali.

ref: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
text: U kpa bɔbirii tɔ u hiŋ, baama biŋŋe n dɔɔ nii werge baruu.

ref: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
text: Di lii u chachaaŋ la biini, dooŋ pogzi, di ra nyɛgzi.

ref: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
text: Kɔraawiizi pozoore alugɔ dooŋ di lii chiŋ, ba nuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la loobii.

ref: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
text: U taazi u hobeere, u dɔma yaari, u kpa nazaa di gil ba ra chɔ.

ref: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
text: Muuzeŋ zɛɛ lii chɔɔ. Hɛri zɛɛzi ge maa chɔɔ pɛɛ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n nyɛgi u dɔma ni, di kpa baaŋfuuih di ra pogzi ba ni wia.

ref: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
text: U lii chinne tuu di wa lawiŋ, di tɛriŋ lii niivile biini.

ref: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
text: Ba faa fɔɔmbuu saŋa la min du siaahmu biini la, ka Kɔraawiizi faa lɛɛŋ.

ref: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
text: U lɛɛmbuu lii siaahmu biini, dikuu n wia n paruu wia.

ref: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
text: Kɔraawiizi turgimbuu dikuu n wideŋlaa ɛɛi wia. U kissimbuu dikuu miŋ waa wichɔgii maa ɛɛwɛ wia.

ref: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
text: N hiŋ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnizii, maa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ, di bir har kpu Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la.

ref: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
text: U Gbɔgni maanii n hiŋ. Maa u widaulaa la ge vɛɛwɛ ta.

ref: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
text: Maa wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ u be, n ɔɔ lizi n hinnɛ di lii wichɔgaa maa biini.

ref: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
text: Kɔraawiizi turgimbuu dikuu n wideŋlaa ɛɛi ni miŋ waa wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ wia.

ref: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
text: I wia dɔɔ wibiire tɛɛ banla wia n dɔɔ wibii. I wia ge du wer tɛɛ banla n waa wichɔgii maa dɔɔwɛ.

ref: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
text: I dɔɔ biinihuŋŋuu tɛɛ banla n dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu, ka hah banla n ɛɛ biinikpola hina.

ref: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
text: I ra lɛɛ banla n dɔɔ sisɔnaa, ka gil banla n na jigsi la ra tuu zɛɛ.

ref: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ n fintina di ra chaaniŋ, di gil n bɔbiri birgi bɔchaaŋ.

ref: You help me defeat armies and capture cities.
text: Hinuu tɛŋ fɔŋŋa n lɔ n dɔma di kpegli baa.

ref: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
text: Kɔraawiiziwaa, u ŋmɛnizi maanii deŋlee. U ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laal pɛrɛtuzeŋ tɛɛ banla maa n na nyiŋŋi ú guu baa.

ref: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
text: Anɛɛ n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di u bɛŋ lɛiyɛi? U bɛnnɛ ɛɛ yaa guuri.

ref: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
text: Kɔraawiizi tɛmbuu fɔŋŋa, di gil n ŋmɛnɛɛ chaani.

ref: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
text: U gillɔɔ n naazi ɛɛ lugɔ weema naazi, u ɔɔ giluu n chi bizenaa nyuuni di na n hiŋ.

ref: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
text: U ra baglimbuu laal lɔi, ń ɔɔ wer ta hoo la gba n kpekke werge.

ref: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i guumbuu di lɛɛŋ, n ni binnaa la gillɔɔ n du kpeg, i hiinaa gillɔɔ n dɔɔ sɔŋ.

ref: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
text: I kuari ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ u du war tɛŋ, guŋ gil n gilɛɛ waa lɔ naa.

ref: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
text: N duŋŋi n dɔmaa di ga kpegli baa. Maa har bittɛ, di miŋ wa chɔgi baa tuŋ la lɛi.

ref: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
text: N lɔ baabuu ta hɛri, ba waa kaa wer bá izi, ba chɔɔgi n naazi zɛɛ.

ref: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
text: I tɛmbuu fɔŋŋa nɛnnɛ, n lɔ laal di kpegli n dɔma.

ref: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
text: I gillɔɔ n dɔma chɔ lii n be, n chɔgi n haahra.

ref: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
text: Ba lɔ wilee di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa, ka nɛr maa waa baa lɛɛwɛ, di lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ka waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ baa.

ref: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
text: N nam baabuu ba ɛɛ lugɔ nyɔɔ. N na fɛrgi baabuu alugɔ kpɛchɛgaa n chɔɔ ŋmɛnizenaa.

ref: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
text: I lɛɛmbuu lii nɛkpoŋlaa be, di gil n ɛɛ hɛssi maa koori. Nɛra la maa miŋ faa waa zummɛ jaa birgi n balaarɛ.

ref: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
text: Ba maa bɔra huahwɔɔ, ba lii ba diikpega ba, ba bɔra ra sa.

ref: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
text: Kɔraawiizi du denii! Ií ra chɔli n Lɛɛrikpeg! Ií ra sii Kɔraawiizi la n kpekke, di lɛɛŋ la zenni.

ref: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
text: U ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na lɛɛ n nuarɛ, u gillɔɔ hɛssi hina ra sɛɛ n dɔɔra,

ref: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
text: di lɛɛŋ lii n dɔma be. I gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma, di lɛɛŋ lii nɛchɔgaa be.

ref: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
text: U gillɔɔ u koori du kpeg, di bagli u nɔŋŋaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la, di ra tɛɛ unla baŋ waari nuu di lizi la, di ra tɛɛ Koori Deevid ni u naanna saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
text: “Kɔraawiizi Duma ga n ninɛɛ di ra ŋɔ wia, u wiŋɔzi du n nuarɛ.

ref: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, Izrɛl hina Bizeŋ ŋɔ n benii, ‘Koori la n na binni nɛra ni wibii, di kpa Kɔraawiizi ɔmaa di ra binni baa,

ref: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
text: u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baama n waa hoo, wiizi ra fur chɔɔzi ni, wiizi ɔɔ gil kooree ra nyɛgzi, di dooŋ wa chaazɔɔ.’

ref: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
text: Gunnɛ Kɔ́raawiizi kissi n naanna, dikuubɛɛwiai, n nuu ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛɛ. Nuukpaŋ la n waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ, nuuŋɔɔlii la n waa biraa dɔɔwɛ. N winyiŋŋii maanii guŋ. Gunnɛ niŋ gil n na kunla minna tami. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil guŋ ɛɛ wibii maa.

ref: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
text: Ka ba daŋ kpa wichɔgɛɛra ha lugɔ sɔɔhri, ba wàá wer kpa nodumazi gbɔgzaa la.

ref: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
text: Nɛr la maa n niŋ gbɔgzaa, see u kpa lugbii kuŋkuarii gɛɛ kandaa. Ba daŋ fuuah nyaamm.” Koori Deevid laallɔkpega wia

ref: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
text: ka Ɛliaza waa faa chi de chigigi, di yoo a Filisti hina guŋŋ u nonii wa sɔm dar, waa kaa wer ú kpa u tokobi tɔɔh nɛr gba. A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi faa lɔ laal di kpegli Filisti hina werge. A laal n wa tunnɛ, Izrɛl laallɔɔra la bir ba bɔr la Ɛliaza n duwɛɛ la, di wa wir a lalaa laal kuna.

ref: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
text: Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge kaali Bahoro la. Awia, u faa jaa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, haali uŋ faa waa ba ni jaawɛ gba.

ref: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
text: Koori Deevid laallɔkpega la sɔnaa keŋ, Takɛmɔn hinuu Jɔsɛb Basɛbɛf, waabuu faa Laallɔkpega Bahoro la sitɔɔri. U faa kpa u kandaarɛ kpu nɛra kalfa ŋmantannaazi, laalkpaŋ biini.

ref: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
text: Unla n faa hiŋ u ni genii Ahɔ domee hinuu Dɔdai biibaal Ɛliaza. U faa ɛɛ ba laallɔkpega bahoro la bɛllɛ. A hɔl bɛl, u ni Koori Deevid faa karsi Filisti hina n chaali yembɛl banna yir Pas Damim, bá lɔ laal, ka Izrɛl hina faa bir chɔ,

ref: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
text: ka Samma waa faa chi a koo baaŋ chigigi, di yoo Filisti hina la, di kpu baa. Kɔraawiizi faa gil ba kpegli baa nɛnnɛ.

ref: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
text: Kuna kumaa saŋa n wa helle, laallɔkpega tokko ni kpɔrgɔ la bahoro, faa tuu ba Koori Deevid be, Adulam bii bɔɔ, di Filisti laallɔɔra suge bɛl faa chɔɔ Rɛfam Waluu biini.

ref: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
text: A saŋa hiŋ, di Koori Deevid faa du diikpeg biini, ka Filisti laallɔɔra suge bɛl wa chɔɔ Bɛtlihɛm.

ref: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
text: Denii niinyɔgzi wa lau Koori Deevid werge maa, u ŋɔ, “N bɔra daŋ vii sɔɔni, di nɛbɛl vii la kɔlɔŋ la n dugli Bɛtlihɛm dominuuzeŋ la, di ga ɛɛ nii wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ!”

ref: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
text: Denii a laallɔkpega bahoro la izi, di peri Filisti laallɔɔra la baaŋ, di la a kɔlɔŋ di ga ɛɛ nii wa tɛɛ Koori Deevid, ka u vɛɛ a nyɔɔi, ka bizaa ta hɛri tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi,

ref: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
text: ka ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, màá wer nyɔɔa! A daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ baala naa n tulmee naa challɛ n na nyɔɔ gunla!” Awia, u vɛɛ a nyɔɔi. Wizenaa naabuu laallɔkpega bahoro naa faa ɛɛ.

ref: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
text: Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya n lii bolzeŋ Kabziil ge faa ɛɛ laallɔkpega la bɛllɛ. U ge gba faa ɛɛ wizenaare, di kpu Moab hina laallɔkpega banɛɛ. U faa ga tuu bɔɔ bɛllɛ waari hɔpizii, di kpu bunyiŋ.

ref: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
text: U faa kaa kpu Ijip hinuu bɛl n helle kpabaa. Haali a Ijip hinuu n kpogli kandaa gba, ka Bɛnaaya faa kpa guliire lɔu, ka foozi u kandaa hiŋ, di kpuu.

ref: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
text: Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge kaali Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ la bɛl maa, ka u faa waa Laallɔkpega Bahoro La ni jaawɛ. Koori Deevid jaa gil u ɛɛ u guure nabɔma.

ref: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
text: ka ŋɔ, “Jara, asummua?” Koori Deevid ŋɔ u be, “I pila naabuu n na nyiŋŋi ń yau, di ma mbusu lizibɔr tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Aŋhinabe, a wiilchɔgii naa daŋ tuŋ.”

text: Di i ra ɛɛ guŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ hiŋ u nua la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛŋ lugɔ n naanna danna di Izrɛl kora di hanna la, di ba ra du tau, di ra hiŋ u widaulaa ni wibii ba biine ni ba kpegzi ani ba nfɛssi maa.

ref: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
text: Wii bɛl haa jaawɔɔ. A liizi gunla Zɛruya biibaal Joab n ɛɛŋ, di faa kpu Izrɛl laallɔɔra nabɔnzi banɛɛ la. Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ani Jɛta biibaal Amasa. U faa kpu baabuu saŋa la bɔr n sɔɔnɛɛ lugɔ laal biini. Ba challi faa chɔg u kirsɔɔ ni u gawa.

ref: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
text: Awia, tɛr u digni ni nunzuma, ka gilɛɛ wa gil u waa siu ni bampirsɔna.

ref: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
text: Kaa ra liizi lugɔ Gɛra biibaal Simei la n lii Bɛnjamin dee biini la, n lii Bahurim la du i benii. U faa seembuu nua a hɔl la miŋ la Mahanam la. U faa tuuwoo wa huuziŋ Jɔɔdan muu nua, ka n faa kpa Kɔraawiizi sɔnnɛ hɛɛhzi lugɔ màá kpuu ni tokobi.

ref: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
text: Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u dignitɛraa. Zum gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ, di gil bá kpuu.” Koori Deevid siu wia

ref: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
text: Uŋ wa nuu guŋ, u izi bɔg u kawee, di la Koori Akis be, Gaf hɛri, ú ga nyiŋŋi u yoma hiŋ. U faa ga na baabuu de, di kpogli baa bir ba.

ref: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
text: Awia, bá wichɔgaa laŋŋi Joab ani u naanna waa maa ninɛɛ, di hanna la saŋa maa. Ama, Kɔ́raawiizi bɔsɔna du Koori Deevidwaa ni u naanna maa, u dia ani u kooridomee la be, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
text: Gunnɛ a faa ɛɛ, Solomɔn kpa u mɛɛ Koori Deevid gawa di di a kora, u kora ge faa chi chigigi werge maa. Adonija siu wia

ref: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
text: Denii Hagif biibaal Adonija la faa la Koori Solomɔn maa Batsiiba be. Batsiiba pɛɛzuu, “A summɔaa?” Adonija sɛɛ, “Ɛɛh, a summɔɔ.”

ref: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
text: Ka jaa ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ wiibɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi n ŋɔ tɛi.” Batsiiba ŋɔ, “A ŋɔ.”

ref: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
text: U ŋɔ, “I zummɔ lugɔ kora naa ɛɛ n hotte. Izrɛl hina maa faa zummɔ lugɔ minuu ba koori. Ka guŋ waa wette ɛɛ, ka a kora kpa la n niwee be, dikuu guŋ n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipar wia.

ref: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
text: Awia, n dɔɔ wikpaŋ bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi n suŋŋi. Jaande, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ.” Denii Batsiiba tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ dí u suŋŋi.

ref: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
text: Adonija ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, suŋŋi Koori Solomɔn lugɔ ú kpa Sunɛm hinuu Abisag tɛŋ ń kpa, n zummɔ lugɔ wàá vɛɛ.”

ref: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
text: Batsiiba ŋɔ, “Guŋ wesso. N daŋ ŋɔ a koori be tɛi.”

ref: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
text: Awia, Batsiiba la Koori Solomɔn be ú ga lizi Adonija amaniye la tɛu. Uŋ ga zuuwɛ, koori izi tognuu, di jaamuu, ka bir so u koorikara ni, ka gil ba kpa a kara bɛl ge chiŋŋi u nodig, u maa ge so.

ref: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
text: Batsiiba jaa ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ wijiga bɛllɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ń suŋŋii, gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ.” A koori ŋɔ, “N ma, bɛɛwɛi? Suŋŋi, màá vɛɛ.”

ref: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
text: U maa ŋɔ, “Gil Sunɛm hinuu Abisag yuu i kpɛɛma Adonija.”

ref: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
text: Denii Koori Solomɔn bir ŋɔ u maa be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i suŋŋi Abisag di ra tɛɛ Adonijai? Guŋwaa, suŋŋi n kora naa gba tɛu, dikuu uŋ ɛɛ n kpɛɛma wia. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata ni Zɛruya biibaal Joab ge gba chigɛ u hattɛ!”

ref: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
text: Denii Koori Solomɔn hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi kpuŋ, di Adonija waa u miibɔɔ kpawɛɛ turgi u winyiŋŋii naa kim!

ref: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
text: N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, unla n hiiniŋ n wer so n mɛɛ Koori Deevid koorikara naa ni chigigi, di kaa dau koori domee tɛɛ n ni naanna gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua la. Adonija daŋ siu zinaa!”

ref: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
text: Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, u ga kpu Adonija. Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata duŋŋaa ani Joab siu wia

ref: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
text: Denii Koori Solomɔn faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Abiata waa be, “Bir di ra la i koo la n du Anatɔf. I gba dɛg siurɛ, ka màá kpui filaŋkeŋ. I ɔɔ faa chi Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka labuu di tɔ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid see, di kaa hiinuu di tɔɔrɔɔ.”

ref: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
text: Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa lizi Abiata lii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina huma biini. Guŋ faa gil gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ Silo, di ra bagli Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛli dia wia la ɛɛ wibii.

ref: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
text: Joab ni Adonija n faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, haali Joab n faa waa Absalɔm har chigɛ gba, n wa nuu guŋ, u chɔ ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di ga lau mbusu lizibɔr nyigzi la kpogli.

ref: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
text: Ba ga ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be lugɔ Joab chɔwɔɔrɛ la Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia, di ga chi mbusu lizibɔr la kɛrii. Denii Koori Solomɔn tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “La ga kpuu!”

ref: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
text: Awia, Bɛnaaya ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la di ŋɔ Joab be, “A koori ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Wa lii!’ ” Ka Joab bir ŋɔ, “Akai, n daŋ siu ɛŋ.” Bɛnaaya bir la ga kali koori gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Joab digni, dikuu banla uŋ faa kpuwɛɛ, di n mɛɛ Koori Deevid waa zummɛ la wia. U faa kpu baala banɛɛrɛ, Nɛɛr biibaal Abna, Izrɛl laallɔɔra nabɔma ani Jɛta biibaal Amasa, Juda laallɔɔra nabɔma. Ba maanii faa ɛɛ nɛnanaa kaaluu.

ref: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
text: Awia, Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya faa la ga kpu Joab, ba huguu u himmaa hɛri, hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
text: Gunnɛ a ɛɛ, a koori faa kpa Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya du Joab bɔr, u ɛɛ u laallɔɔra nabɔma, di kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zadɔk ge du Abiata bɔr. Simei siu wia

ref: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
text: Denii Koori Solomɔn hum bá ga yir Simei, ú ba. Uŋ wa ballɛ, u ŋɔ u be, “Ma dia Jɛrusalɛm biini di ra zuu, ka gilɛɛ waa la yemmaa.

ref: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
text: A hɔl la maa hin niŋ izi gi Kidrɔn Waluu, zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ i daŋ siu, wibii maa, í wichɔgaa laŋŋi i ni.”

ref: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
text: Simei ŋɔ koori be, “Jara, gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo. Mìŋ́ i balii daŋ ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.” Awia, Simei faa so Jɛrusalɛm birgi werge.

ref: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
text: Ka binni ahoro n wa bɛrɛɛ, Simei yoma banɛɛ baŋhina chɔ kaali Maaka biibaal Gaf Koori Akis be. Denii ba faa ga kali Simei guŋ, di ŋɔ, “I yoma la du Gaf hɛri.”

ref: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
text: Ka Koori Solomɔn n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Simei la Gaf hɛrii ka bir ba la,

ref: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
text: u hum di yiruu, u ba, u ŋɔ u be, “Maa gillɛ i hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini lugɔ a hɔl la maa hin niŋ la yemmaa, í zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ i daŋ siuwaa? A saŋa hiŋ, i faa ŋɔ n benii gunla miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la wessoo, awia i daŋ hiŋ guŋ.

ref: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
text: Ka bɛɛ n gillɛ haa i nua la hiŋŋɛ, ka vɛɛ n widaulii lai?”

ref: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
text: Koori Solomɔn faa kaa ŋɔ Simei be, “I zummɔɔ nɛnnɛ i biini, wichɔgaa la maa hiŋ ɛɛ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid. Filaŋkennaa waa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ turgii í wichɔgaa la kim.

ref: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
text: Ka mìŋ́ Koori Solomɔnwaa daŋ na kissaa, Koori Deevid kora ge chi nɛnnɛ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
text: Denii a koori faa jaa tɛɛ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya ŋmɛnɛɛ, u la ga kpu Simei. Gunnɛ faa ɛɛwɛ, Koori Solomɔn kora faa jaa chi chigigi.

ref: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
text: Izrɛl hina faa haa ra lizi ba mbusuzii giŋgimee nyuuni, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa haa waa Kɔraawiizi Dia mawɛɛ.

ref: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
text: Haali n daŋ tɛi kunla gba hiŋ waa suŋŋɛɛ. N daŋ tɛi daama ani zenni. Koori maa wàá lugɔi, i de dui saŋa.

ref: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
text: Koori Solomɔn faa nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizii, di ra hiŋ gunla u mɛɛ Koori Deevid n bagluu la, ka uŋ faa kpa sela di ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma giŋgimee nyuuni la bɛnnɛ faa kawɛɛ.

ref: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ba Koori Solomɔn be Gibiɔn hamuŋa ni, deeza biini, di wa ŋɔ u be, “Suŋŋi kunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi, ń tɛi.”

ref: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
text: Koori Solomɔn ŋɔ u be, “I faa nɔŋŋi i balii n mɛɛ Koori Deevidii werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra hiŋiibuu ni wibii, u wia maa deŋli, di kaa dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu ge jaa. I haa ra suŋ u ninɛɛ werge maa, di tɛu biibaal u so u koorikara ni zinaa.

ref: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, filaŋkeŋ, i gillɔɔ mìŋ́ i balii Koori Solomɔn kpa n mɛɛ gawa, di di kora. N ɛɛ bichalaa, maa n see ni n har zummɛ.

ref: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
text: Mìŋ́ i baliirɛ keŋ, di du i nɛra la hiŋ lizɛɛ biini, ba kpillɔɔ werge maa, ba wàá wer kur baa.

ref: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
text: Awia, gil i balii ɛɛ nunzunni la n niŋ wer ra zum wia zɛɛzi, di wer ra binni i nɛra ni, di ɔɔ wer zum wideŋlaa ani anla n waa deŋlee. Anɛɛ n niŋ wer binni i nɛra naa n dɔɔ sɔŋ werge naa ninɛi?”

ref: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Dikuu hiŋ suŋŋi keŋ ka gil miibɔɔjaŋ ni daama gɛɛ i dɔma siuzaa, ka ra nyiŋŋi nunzuma, í wer di ra di wibii wia,

ref: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
text: Di i wetto di ra hiŋ n ŋmɛnizi n widaulaa ani n Gbɔgni nɛnnɛ, gunla i mɛɛ Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛwɛ la, n daŋ tɛi miibɔɔjaŋ.”

ref: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
text: Denii Koori Solomɔn hassi izi, di na lugɔ deezaa. U jaa bir la Jɛrusalɛm di ga chi Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la see, di lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi. Ka gil ba daali diuzenaa tɛɛ u balaa ni u nabɔnzi maa. Koori Solomɔn n di seriyakpol bɛl wia

ref: One day two women came to King Solomon,
text: A hɔl bɛl, hahsɛnsɛnna banɛɛ baŋhina faa chi dɔŋa ba Koori Solomɔn be.

ref: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
text: Denii bɛl ŋɔ, “Jara, n ni haannaabuu ra zuu. U sibɔɔrɛ, ka n lul biibaal.

ref: and three days later her baby was born. Nobody else was there with us.
text: A hɔpizaa ahoro hɔl, u ge lul biibaal. N nuu bɛnnɛ du a dia.

ref: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
text: Denii hamuŋa ni, haaŋ naa billi chɔɔ u bie ni, u siu.

ref: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
text: Hɛuh n wa hɛɛhzɛɛ, u izi wa kpa n bie lii n kɛra, di ga dau u kɛra, di mìŋ́ i balii ra chɔɔ dɔɔ, ka kpa u biisiwii la dau n kɛra.

ref: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
text: Denii hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, n izi ŋɔ n lau il du n bie, di u siuwɔ. Ka miŋ wa binnuu na nɛnnɛ, n na lugɔ n bie la miŋ lullɛ la lɛi.”

ref: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
text: Denii a haaŋ la hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai! Biinyinii labuu n bie, i hotte u siwii la.” Ka hahlugli la haa vɛɛ ŋɔ, “Akai! U siwii labuu i hor, u nyinii la ge ɛɛ n hor.” Ba maa faa chi a koori see di ra bil dɔŋa.

ref: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
text: Awia, a koori ŋɔ, “Ií kpa tokobi di wa tɛŋ.” Ba kpa a tokobi wa tɛu.

ref: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
text: U ŋɔ, “Ií lau biinyinii la chah anɛɛ, di kpa u yeŋ tɛɛ unnii, di kpa u yeŋ ge tɛɛ unla hiŋ.”

ref: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, unla bie n ɛɛu la na u sinyɛna werge maa, awia, u ŋɔ a koori be, “Jara, jaande maa, kpa a biinyinii la tɛɛ n dɔŋhiŋ la, gilɛɛ waa kpuu!” Ka unla hiŋ ŋɔ, “Akai! Yaa bɛl maa wàá dɔɔ a biinyinii, ií chauh!”

ref: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
text: Denii a koori jaa ŋɔ, “Ií kpa a biinyinii la tɛɛ a lugli hiŋ la. Ií gilɛɛ waa kpuu, waabuu u maa.”

ref: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
text: Izrɛl hina maa n wa nuu a koori seriya dii la, a kpu ba nuuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi benii u na nunzuma, di ra di seriya ni wibii.

ref: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
text: Koori Solomɔn faa dɔɔ bariizi fidaanɛɛrɛ Izrɛl hɛri maa di wa chem. A bɛl maanii faa dɔɔ u nabɔma, u ɔɔ kɛɛ kuna di waa tɛɛ a koori ni u diahina maa. Ba bɛl maanii ɔɔ faa ɛɛ guŋ baagu bir, bina maa biini.

ref: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.

ref: Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him.
text: U faa di Muu Yufretis wiicholii hɛssi maa koraa, di lii Tifsa guŋŋ di ga hel Gaza n du wiicholii. Bampirsɔna faa du u ni hɛssi hina la maa n baruu la baaŋ.

ref: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
text: Koori Solomɔn de dui saŋa, Izrɛl ni Juda hɛssi maa faa dɔɔ bampirsɔnaa, di chi Dan guŋŋ di ga hel bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba. Nɛr maa faa dɔɔ u grepu ni fig daazii.

ref: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,

ref: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔnnɛ nunzuma ni wia zɛɛ zumaa werge di ga bɛri.

ref: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
text: U faa dɔɔ nunzumaa kaali baal maa, haali di kpa Ɛtan la n faa ɛɛ Ɛzra domee hinuu la gba. Di faa kaa dɔɔ nunzuma kaali Hɛman, Mahɔl biibaala Kalkɔl ani Dada. Awia, u sɔŋ faa yaari hɛssi la maa n baruu la biine.

ref: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
text: U faa bagli daazi wiarɛ, di chi Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpola guŋŋ di ga hel hisɔp la n na fur koŋlaa ni la. U faa kaa bagli nɛra genii sela, zumbizi, kuntuuzaa ani nyinni wia.

ref: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
text: Hɛssi maa koora n faa nuu Koori Solomɔn nunzuma la wia, ɔɔ faa hum nɛraa ba ba di waa nuu u wiŋɔzi.

ref: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
text: Taaya Koori Hiram n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Solomɔn kpa u mɛɛ Koori Deevid gawaa la, u hum u nabɔnzi u be, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ni Koori Deevid faa summɔɔ.

ref: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
text: Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń ma Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la Diarɛ, di tɛu sɔŋ, alugɔ uŋ faa ŋɔ n mɛɛ Koori Deevid be, ‘I biibaal la n niŋ wa kpa i gawa labuu niŋ ma Dia tɛŋ.’

ref: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
text: Awia, tɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ bá teŋri Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpola daazi tɛŋ. N nɛra daŋ wa hiini i nɛra di hum a huma. N daŋ turgi i nɛra hiŋ di mag gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi. I zummɔ genii lugɔ yaa waa nɛr dɔɔwɛ, u zum daazi teŋraa nɛnnɛ lugɔ Saidɔn hina.”

ref: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
text: Hiram n wa nuu Koori Solomɔn tile la, a faa paruubuu werge maa, u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ werge maa zinaa, dikuu uŋ tɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaal la siwee n chaanɛɛ, u di hɛrzeŋ la kora wia.”

ref: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
text: Awia, Koori Hiram faa tili ŋɔ Koori Solomɔn be, “N nuu i tile labuu. N daŋ ɛɛ gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi. N daŋ tɛi a hɛriŋkpola daazi ni daananaa.

ref: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
text: N balaa daŋ tuuzaa lii Lɛbanɔn hɛri tuu muuzeŋ, di vɔɔzaa mari dɔŋa alugɔ muugbessi, a pal di ga hel bɔr la maa hin niŋ bagli. A bɔdeere n balaa ga puraa tɛi. Ama, n winyiŋŋiire lugɔ í ra tɛɛ n ni n diahina diwee.”

ref: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
text: Kɔraawiizii faa tɛɛ Koori Solomɔn nunzuma gunla uŋ ŋɔ nua tɛu la. Bampirsɔna faa du Koori Hiram ni Koori Solomɔn baannɛ. A guŋ wia, ba faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ.

ref: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
text: A koori faa ŋɔ bá sɛɛh bizennanaa, bá chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ zɛɛ.

ref: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
text: Koori Solomɔn, Koori Hiram huŋhunna ani bolzeŋ Gɛbal hina huŋhunna maanii faa teŋri a daazi di kuaraa, di sɛɛhzi a bia ge bá ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ.

ref: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
text: U faa du tokorozii a Dia koŋlaa ni a baŋgizi fɔɔ, ka a biine du war, di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni.

ref: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
text: Awia, Koori Solomɔn faa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hinnɛ tuŋ, di kpa dolzenaa ani hɛriŋkpol daapiahni guu.

ref: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
text: A diini faa hɔŋzi dɔŋa ninɛɛ. U zɛɛ himmaa dia la wassi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi anue. Nɛɛhiŋ la ge hɔŋ u ni di saagi, u wassi faa ɛɛ lugɔ nogumzi anumbɛl. ref: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.

ref: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
text: Di nɛra naa haa ra la Kɔraawiizi Dia la Jɛrusalɛm biini di gaa lizi mbusuzi, ba daŋ kaa ra sɛɛ Juda Koori Rehoboam dɔɔra. Ba daŋ kpuŋ, ka bir di ra hiŋuu.”

ref: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
text: Koori Jeroboam wa pɛɛzi u nabɔnzi, ba biruu liize. U kpa saliŋ kuari nabizi anɛɛ, ka ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Izrɛl hina, tɔɔrɔɔrɛ werge maa lugɔ ii ɔɔ ra la Jɛrusalɛm. Ii vugaa keŋ, aabuu lizi ia lii Ijip hɛri la!”

ref: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
text: Denii u faa kpa bɛl chiŋŋi Bɛtɛl, ka kpa bɛl ge chiŋŋi Dan.

ref: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
text: A guŋ faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, haali a nɛra ɔɔ la Bɛtɛl ni Dan di gaa kuaraa.

ref: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
text: Koori Jeroboam faa ma vuga kuaribɔra giŋgimee nyuuni, di ligzi kizeehina, di lii nɛra maa ni ba dizi biine, haali baŋ faa waa Levi dee ɛɛwɛ.

ref: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
text: Baaguzi ŋmantannaazihiŋ, hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ hɔl, hɔpizii la u himmaa n dauwɛ la, u ɔɔ la Bɛtɛllɛ di ga lizi mbusuzi, mbusu lizibɔr ni. Awia, u faa dau a hɔpizizenne tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, u himmaa ɔɔ faa jaa tinni mbusu lizibɔr la di ra lizi mbusuzi.

ref: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
text: U lɔ wile du mbusu lizibɔr ni, di ŋɔ, “Ee, mbusu lizibɔr, mbusu lizibɔr! Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Ba daŋ lul biibaal lii Koori Deevid dia, ú sɔŋ di Jɔsia. U daŋ kpa kizeehina la n du vuga kuaribɔra giŋgimee nyuuni, di ra lizi mbusuzi la, di lizi mbusuzi i ni. U daŋ fuuh newea hoga i ni.’ ”

ref: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
text: Denii mbusu lizibɔr hiŋ puri chol kakpaŋ, u hɔɔhri la yaari hɛri, gunla Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la n ŋɔwɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini la.

ref: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
text: A koori ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ be, “Jaande maa, suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la, ú chaa n nonii tɛŋ.” A dɔgtɛɛ la suŋŋi wiizi, a koori nonii nyaagi, di bir du u duula.

ref: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
text: Koori Jeroboam ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ be, “Ba ya la n dia ga di. N daŋ sunzii kumbɛl, dikuu gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia.”

text: Ka Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ hiŋ ŋɔ a koori be, “Haali di i daŋ tɛŋ i daama keŋkere gba, ka màá hiŋii gɛɛ di ga hee paanuu gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii gba bɔnnaa.

ref: Then he started home down a different road. An Old Prophet from Bethel
text: Awia, u faa kpa ŋmɛniduma di bir ra kpo. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzɛŋa bɛl n faa du Bɛtɛl wia

text: Denii ba mɛɛ pɛɛzi baa, “Ŋmɛnibɛliirɛ u kpa kaalɛi?” Ba bagluu ŋmɛnɛɛ la Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la n lii Juda n kpawɛɛ la.

ref: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
text: U jaa ŋɔ u biibaala la be, “Ií bɔg kawee tɛŋ.” Baŋ wa bɔguu tuŋ, u tinnuu

text: Ka Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la n lii Juda la ŋɔ, “Màá wer bir har di hiŋii gɛɛ di wer hee paanuu gɛɛ di nyɔɔ nii i be bɔnnaa,

text: A Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzɛŋa ŋɔ u be, “N ge gba ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛrɛ lugɔi. Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ u mɛlika wa ŋɔ n be, ‘Kpogluu bir ba i dia ú wa hee paanuu di nyɔɔ nii.’ ” Ka u faa ra daruubuu.

ref: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzɛŋa la n biruu ba la n wa nuu guŋ, u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua labuu. Kɔraawiizii kpau tɛɛ a bunyiŋ, u lawuu la, dikuu gunla uŋ faa karfuu la wia.”

ref: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
text: A dɔgtɛɛzɛŋa la ŋɔ u biibaala be, “Ií bɔg kawee tɛŋ.” Ba ɛɛ guŋ.

text: Denii u lii ga na, di a dɔgtɛɛrɛ chɔɔ a ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka kawee la ni bunyiŋ la chi u kɛra. A bunyiŋ faa waa a lalii diwee gɛɛ di lau a kawee gba.

ref: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
text: Denii a dɔgtɛɛzɛŋa kpa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la sag a kawee ni, di bir ba u himmaa bolzeŋ la biini, ú ga wii u lee ka huguu.

ref: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
text: U wa kpau hug bɔɔ la baŋ faa kiwee dau, bá wa hug u himmaa la, ka ba wii u lee, di ŋɔ, “Ee, n lulli!”

ref: I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
text: Kɔraawiizi amaniye la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ du mbusu lizibɔr la n du Bɛtɛl ani vuga kuaribɔra la maa n du bolzeŋ Samaria bola ni la, daŋ wa ɛɛ, wibii maa.”

ref: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
text: Haali keŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ gba, ka Koori Jeroboam faa haa waa u wichɔgaa la gillɛ ta. Ka faa haa lizi kizeehinaa lii dizi maa biine, ba du a giŋgimee nyuuni. Nɛr la maa n faa ra nyiŋŋi ú birgi kizeehiŋ, ɔɔ faa sɔubuu, u du a giŋgimee nyuuni.

ref: This sinful thing led to the downfall of his kingdom.
text: Wichɔgaa la Koori Jeroboam diahina n faa ɛɛwɛ labuu faa gillɛ a domee chol, di dim durnya naa biini.

ref: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Jeroboam biibaal Abija faa ra wii.

ref: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
text: Awia, Ahija n wa nuu u naazi gbɔga dominua, u ŋɔ, “A zuu Jeroboam haaŋ, beedee i kutti ɛɛ lugɔ nɛbɛl deei? N dɔɔ amaniyechɔgaarɛ ń tɛi lii Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
text: Bir la ga kali Koori Jeroboam lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘N liziibuu lii n nɛra biini, di gil i ɛɛ Izrɛl sitɔɔri.

ref: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
text: N faa lɛɛ a kora labuu Koori Deevid naanna be tɛi, ka haa lugɔ n balii Koori Deevid la n faa hiŋ n baglaazi ni u biini maa, di faa ɛɛ wideŋlaa n be la.

ref: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
text: I ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa kaali koora la maa n diwee ka dawii la. I kuari vugaa tɛɛ i hiŋ, anla baŋ kpa lugbia kuari. I vɛɛmbuu ta, guŋ gil n baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
text: Dikuu guŋ wia, n daŋ gil hɛhchɔg chol Koori Jeroboam dia ni werge maa, di kpuuzi i naanna la maa n ɛɛ baala, ba nabɔnzi ni bichalli maa. N daŋ dim i diahina maa, ba wia tuŋ alugɔ niŋ n fuuh nabina.

ref: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
text: Izrɛl hina maa daŋ wii u lee ka huguu. U bɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ Koori Jeroboam dia hinuu la ban niŋ hug nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u bɛnnɛ ɛɛ nɛr la n du u dia biini, u wia par Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la.

ref: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lizi koori tɛɛ Izrɛl. Waabuu niŋ dim Koori Jeroboam domee kora.

ref: The people of Israel have made the Lord angry by setting up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. So the Lord will punish them until they shake like grass in a stream. He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr Izrɛl hina digna, bá bɔra ra sa, alugɔ koorii n chigɛ gɔŋ biini. U daŋ lizi Izrɛl hina lii hɛrnanii naa un tɛɛ ba naabaala la biini, di gil ba yaari Muu Yufretis baŋgia, dikuu baŋ fuuh u baaŋ, di ra kuari vughaaŋ Asɛra wia.

ref: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
text: Denii Koori Jeroboam haaŋ la faa izi di bir kpo u bol Tirza. Uŋ haŋ ga kpa u naa di ra jag ba dia dominua daa ni, a bie siu.

ref: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
text: Ba huguu, ka Izrɛl hina maa wii u lee, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga u dɔgtɛɛ Ahija be, di ŋɔ la. Koori Jeroboam siu wia

text: Ba faa sɛbi Koori Jeroboam wiɛɛlaa la n kawɛɛ, u laal lɔizi ani gunla un di u kora labuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.

ref: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.

ref: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
