text: Haali, uŋ faa waa a vuga kuaribɔra chɔkkɛ a giŋgimee nyuuni gba, ka u bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, ú de dui maa biini.

ref: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
text: Izrɛl Koori Baasa faa lɔ Juda hina, di kpegli baa, di foozi Rama, di ma koŋlii baruu, nɛr maa gilɛɛ kaa wer lii gɛɛ zuu Juda koori hɛri.

ref: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
text: Denii Koori Asa jaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ la maa n kawɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna dauribɔra ani u himmaa kooridia hora di jaa, di kpaa hum u nabɔnzi dí ba la Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad la n faa du Damaskus di ra di kora, u mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Tabrimɔn, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Hɛziɔn la be, di ga ŋɔ,

ref: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
text: “Gil n nii dɔɔ nuukpaŋ gunla n mɛɛ ni i mɛɛ n faa dɔɔwɛ la. Awia, n na sunziibuu saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ, ka í gil i ni Izrɛl Koori Baasa nuukpaŋ la tuŋ, gunnɛ niŋ gil ú lizi u laallɔɔra lii n hɛri.”

ref: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
text: Denii Koori Bɛn Hadad nuu Koori Asa nua la, di hum u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi, bá ga lɔ Izrɛl laal. Ba faa ga kpegli Ijɔn, Dan, Abɛl Bɛf Maaka ani hɛri la n dugli Galilii muuzeŋ maa, di kpa Naftali bolzenaa maa jaa.

ref: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
text: Koori Baasa n wa nuu guŋ, u faa gil Rama mai, ka la ga so Tirza.

ref: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
text: Wia la aŋhina n ɛɛwɛ Koori Asa kora dii biini wia la maa uŋ wette di ɛɛ ani bolzenaa la maa uŋ faa ma koŋlaa bar, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Ama, u zɛŋaa saŋa la, wiila faa lau u naazii, u gbɛr.

ref: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
text: Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Jeroboam biibaal Nadab faa di Izrɛl kora. Binni anɛɛ bɛnnɛ u faa di a kora.

ref: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be alugɔ u mɛɛ, di faa gil Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

ref: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
text: Uŋ haŋ faari u kora dii, u kpu Koori Jeroboam lulla maa. U faa waa kpaŋkpaŋ maa gillɛ, ba maanii u faa chɔgi di lii gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Silo hinuu Ahija be, di ŋɔ la.

ref: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
text: A guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ dikuu Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ fuuh werge la wia.

ref: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Wia la aŋhina Koori Nadab n ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
text: Laal faa du Juda Koori Asa ani Izrɛl Koori Baasa baannɛ, ba kossi dii saŋa maa. Izrɛl Koori Baasa wia

ref: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
text: Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni ahorohiŋ biinii, Ahija biibaal Baasa faa di Izrɛl kora, di du Tirza biini, binni tokko ni anaazu.

ref: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di hiŋ Koori Jeroboam hiŋaa la, di gil Izrɛl hina gba ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

ref: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Hanani biibaal Jehu be lugɔ ú ga lizi amaniye naa tɛɛ Koori Baasa, di ŋɔ,

ref: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
text: “I faa waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ, ka n gil i ɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sitɔɔri. Ka filaŋkennaa, i ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ alugɔ Koori Jeroboam, di gil n nɛra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Guŋ gil n baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
text: Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń dim i ni i lulla maa, di gil i dia ɛɛ lugɔ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam dia.

ref: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
text: Nuuzihinaa niŋ di i dia hinuu la maa n niŋ siu a bolzeŋ biini, duuni ge di unla ge n niŋ siu pir biini.”

ref: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
text: Amaniye naa faa ga Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jehu benii di ba Koori Baasa ni u diahina be, dikuu wichɔgaa la maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni la wia. U faa fuuh Kɔraawiizi baannɛ, dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Koori Jeroboam n faa ɛɛwɛ ani uŋ kaa kpu Koori Jeroboam lulla maa wia. Izrɛl Koori Ɛla wia

ref: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
text: Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni anumbɛlhiŋ biinii, Koori Baasa biibaal Ɛla faa di Izrɛl kora, di so Tirza binni anɛɛ.

ref: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
text: U nabɔma Zimri n faa ɛɛ u torkozi yeŋ binni, faa ta u kpui jina. A hɔl bɛl, Koori Ɛla faa du Tirza, Aaza la n faa ra du kooridia tau la dia, di nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi.

ref: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
text: Denii Zimri wa zuu di yag Koori Ɛla ta, di kpuu. Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii guŋ ɛɛ. Ka jaa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
text: Uŋ haŋ faari a kora dii, u faa kpu Koori Baasa lulla maanii. U faa waa ba baal maa gillɛ, haali di u ɛɛ u lulli gɛɛ u dammu gba.

ref: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
text: Awia, Koori Zimri faa chɔgi Koori Baasa waa lulla maanii gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Jehu be, di ŋɔ labuu.

ref: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
text: Koori Baasa ni u biibaal Koori Ɛla faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh, dikuu baŋ faa ra kuari vuga wia.

ref: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
text: Wia la aŋhina Koori Ɛla n faa ɛɛwɛ u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Izrɛl Koori Zimri wia

ref: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
text: Izrɛl hina la n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Koori Zimri ta Koori Ɛla jinaa di kpuu la, ba lizi Ɔmri n ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra nabɔma, di tɔu Izrɛl kora a hɔl hiŋ, ba chaalibɔr la biini.

ref: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
text: Denii Koori Ɔmri ni Izrɛl hina la maa n du u be la, lii Gibɛtɔn di vɔɔ laal di ga fɔɔ Tirza.

ref: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
text: Koori Zimri n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba kpegli a bolzenne la, u chɔ zuu a kooridia diikpeg, ka duu niŋ. Awia, u faa siu,

ref: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, gunla Koori Jeroboam n faa ɛɛwɛ, di gil Izrɛl hina maa ge ɛɛa la wia.

ref: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
text: Wia la aŋhina Koori Zimri n faa ɛɛwɛ u kora dii biini ani u jinachɔgaa wiɛɛlaa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Izrɛl Koori Ɔmri wia

ref: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina la faa bargi bɔra anɛɛ, ba yeŋ chi Ginaf biibaal Tibni har lugɔ ú ɛɛ koori, ka ba yeŋ ge chi Ɔmri har.

ref: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
text: Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kpaŋhiŋ biinii, Ɔmri faa di Izrɛl kora. Binni fidaanɛɛrɛ u faa di a kora. U faa sogo Tirzaa binni anumbɛl.

ref: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
text: U faa hiŋ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wiɛɛlaa ni u wichɔgaa la maa, uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina ɛɛ, di gil Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ faa fuuh, dikuu baŋ faa ra kuari vuga la n waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ wia.

ref: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Wia la aŋhina Koori Ɔmri n faa ɛɛwɛ, u kora dii saŋa, ba faa sɛbi a maanii du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
text: Denii Koori Ɔmri faa siu, ba huguu bolzeŋ Samaria biini. Ka u biibaal Ahab kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Izrɛl Koori Ahab wia

ref: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
text: Juda Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ŋmantannaazihiŋ biinii, Koori Ɔmri biibaal Ahab faa di Izrɛl kora, di faa so Samaria, di di a kora binni tokko ni anɛɛ.

ref: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
text: Koori Ɔmri biibaal Koori Ahab faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, Kɔraawiizi be, di kaali banla maa n feluu di kora la.

ref: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
text: U faa waa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la ɛɛ wizenne, ka faa ga kpa Saidɔn Koori Ɛtbaal biihaaŋ, Jɛzɛbɛl, di faari ra kuari vug Baal, di ra tɔgzuu.

ref: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
text: U faa ma vug Baal diarɛ, Samaria, di ma mbusu lizibɔr u biini.

ref: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
text: Koori Ahab faa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra daarɛ, di kaa ɛɛ wikpila maa jaa, di faa gil Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la baaŋ fuuh werge maa, di kaali Izrɛl koora la maa n diwee ka tɛu la.

ref: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
text: Koori Ahab kora dii saŋa, Bɛtɛl baal bɛl banna yir Hiɛl, bittɔɔ ma bolzeŋ Jɛriko. U biibambilugli Abiram faa siu, uŋ wa chiŋŋi a bol zɛɛ tuŋ. U bichala hiŋ Sɛgub ge faa siu, saŋa la uŋ wa du a bol koŋlii dominuuzenaa tuŋ. Annii naa maa ɛɛwɔɔ gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga Nun biibaal Josua be, di ŋɔ la.

ref: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
text: Tisbi hinuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija la n lii Giliad hɛri la ŋɔ Koori Ahab be, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n ni Izrɛl hina n na hum, u du de saŋa maa labuu lugɔ dooŋ gɛɛ ŋmɛnii wàá ka chol, binni aŋmɛnɛ biini, di maa guŋ wa ŋɔwɛɛ lɛi.”

ref: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Ɛlija be,

ref: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
text: “Lii bɔnnaa, di ga wiifurii, di ga suah Kɛrif Gɔmbɔɔluŋ la n du Jɔɔdan muu wiifurii la.

ref: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
text: I danna nyɔɔ gɔnjiga bɛl nii, ka n gil duglizi ra dɛɛzii de.”

ref: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
text: A duglizi ɔɔ faa wa tɛu paanuu ni ol chɔɔzi ni duana maa. U ɔɔ nyɔɔ nii a gɔŋ biini.

ref: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a gɔŋ hiihzi, dikuu dooŋ n waa ba wia. Ɛlija ni Zarɛfaf luhaaŋ wia

ref: The Lord told Elijah,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be,

ref: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
text: “La bol la banna yir Zarɛfaf n dugli bolzeŋ Saidɔn, di gaa zuu de. N lizi luhaaŋ bɛllɛ de, di ŋɔ ú ra tɛi diwee.”

ref: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
text: Ɛlija la Zarɛfaf. Uŋ gaa hel a bol dominuuzeŋ, di luhaaŋ bɛl ra nyiŋŋi daazi. U yiruu ŋɔ u be, “Jaande maa, ɛɛ nii wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ.”

ref: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
text: A haaŋ n na la ú ga ɛɛ a nii la, u kaa yiruu ŋɔ u be, “Jaande maa, mɔŋ paanuu jaa wa tɛŋ.”

ref: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
text: Ka a luhaaŋ bir ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n du de saŋa maa la, maa paanuu dɔɔwɛ. Sau tama bɛnnɛ n dɔɔ n saulee biini ni nuu tama ge n nuulee biini. N na nyiŋŋi daazi tamaa ń la bol, di ga ɔɔzi paanuu, n ni n biibaal hee, ka siuzi.”

ref: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
text: Ɛlija ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm. La bol ga ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa. Ama, feli ga ɔɔzi paanuujiga lii kunla hiŋ dɔɔwɛ la biini, di wa tɛŋ mɔɔ, ka jaa ga ɔɔzi, í ni i biibaal ge hee.

ref: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘A sau lee wàá nyaa sau maa, a nuu lee ge wàá hil maa, di ga hel a hɔl la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil dooŋ kaa ba hɛri naa.’ ”

ref: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
text: Awia, u kpa la ga ɛɛ gunla Ɛlija n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu la. Hɔpizii maanii diwee ɔɔ du de, tɛɛ Ɛlija, haaŋ la ani u diahina.

ref: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
text: A sau lee waa sau nyaawɛ maa, a nuu lee ge faa waa hillɛ maa, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Ɛlija be, di ŋɔ la.

ref: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, a haaŋ la n dɔɔ a dia la biibaal ra wii. U wiila la ra nyaŋŋi. A tuna maa, u heeza teŋ.

ref: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
text: Denii a luhaaŋ ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ, beedee wiarɛ i kpa ra chuginnɛi. I ballɔɔ í wa liiziŋ n wichɔgaa wia, ka kpu n biibaal gɛɛ?”

ref: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
text: Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Kpa i biibaal la ba.” U lɛɛu u nonee biini, di kpau di tinni la dia la uŋ duwɛɛ chiŋ la, di ga kpau dau u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni.

ref: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
text: Ka lɔ wile tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, i kpa biinichɔgrɛ ta luhaaŋ naa minna zuu u be naa ninɛɛ, di gil u biibaal siwaa?”

ref: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
text: Ka jaa izi di chɔɔ pi a biibaal ni buhoro, ka kaa lɔ wile di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, gil biibaal naa kaa bir dɔɔ miibɔɔ!”

ref: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi nuu Ɛlija suŋŋaa la, a biibaal kaa bir dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
text: Ɛlija kpau tuu tɛɛ u maa, ka ŋɔ u be, “Na, i biibaal la ra nyinuu!”

ref: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
text: Denii a haaŋ ŋɔ Ɛlija be, “Filaŋkennaa, n jaa zumuu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛrɛ hiŋ. U wiŋɔɔlii maa ge hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ɛɛ wibii.”

ref: For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
text: Awia, Ɛlija la ú ga kpa u hiŋ bagli Koori Ahab. A saŋa naa, di lɔchɔgii faa nyaŋŋɔɔ bolzeŋ Samaria biini.

ref: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Ahab haaŋ Jɛzɛbɛl n faa ra kpuuzi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la, Obadia faa lau ba kalfaa, ga suah bia bɔɔni anɛɛ aŋhina biine. Ba tokkoanɛɛ ni fi du bɔɔ naa, ba tokkoanɛɛ ni fi ge du bɛl, ka u ra tɛɛ baa diwee ni nii.

ref: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
text: Koori Ahab ŋɔ Obadia be, “Yá gaagi a hɛri ni bulli ni walli maa na. Aŋhinabe, yaa daŋ na kooree di ra dɛɛzi yaa zagra ni kauzi, gunnɛ niŋ gil yaa wàá kpu yaa sel maa.”

ref: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
text: Awia, ba bɔnni a hɛri bɔr la ban niŋ gaagi la. Koori Ahab ga keŋkere bɛl, Obadia ge ga keŋkere bɛl.

ref: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”

text: Obadia pɛɛzi, “Beedee wichɔgiirɛ n ɛɛi, i ra nyiŋŋi i kpa mìŋ́ i balii, tɛɛ Koori Ahab, ú kpuɛi?

ref: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
text: N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum, u du de saŋa maa la lugɔ koori gillɔɔ ba gaagi durnya hɛssi naa maa biine, di ra nyiŋŋii. Di hɛri bɛl maa hina wa ŋɔwɔɔ lugɔ ba wɛɛ nawɛɛ, u ɔɔ giluu ba hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba wàá wer nai.

ref: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
text: Ka i ra ŋɔ n be filaŋkeŋ lugɔ ń ga ŋɔ n dɔɔri be lugɔ hinuu du ɛŋ.

ref: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”

text: Ka Ɛlija ŋɔ, “Maa Izrɛl ra koozi. I ni i mɛɛwaa domee labuu ra koozuu. Ií vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuuzii, ka ra kuari vug Baala.

ref: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
text: Ií nyiŋŋi nabala anɛɛ tɛɛ yaa. Di gil ba lizi bɛl, di kpuu, di mɔnnuu jigzi sag daazi ni, ka gilɛɛ waa du niŋ. N ge kpu bɛl, di ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”

ref: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
text: Denii ba lau a nabal la baŋ tɛɛ baa la kpu, di kuaruu. Ka jaa yir Baal sɔŋ di lii chɔɔzi maa guŋŋ wiizi wa baŋ. Ba ra pogzi di ra ŋɔ, “Hoi, Baal, nuu yaa be!” Ka ba waa wiimaa nuuwɛ. Nɛr maa waa sɛɛwɛ, ka ba sa di ra bar mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kuarɛɛ la.

ref: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
text: Ba jaa ra pogzi werge, di ra mɔnni bahinaa ni ba tokobizi ni kandaazi, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ la, guŋŋ ba challi waa lii.

ref: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
text: Wibaŋkanchirii n wa bɛrɛɛ, di ba haa aah siwii di ra kaabi ba vug la guŋŋ, ba duaniŋmbusu lizaa saŋa wa hel. Ka ba haa waa wiimaa nuuwɛ, nɛr maa ge waa sɛɛwɛ gɛɛ di hagzi baa.

text: U kpa a bia di ma mbusu lizibɔr, Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, di ki bɔɔ baruu, u du luŋ lugɔ nii pirintuani fidaanaazu, wer suu.

text: U kaa ŋɔ, “Ií kaa ɛɛ guŋ.” Ba kaa kuari ɛɛ guŋ. U kaa ŋɔ, “Ií kaa ɛɛ guŋ buhoro hiŋ.” Ba kaa ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.

ref: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,

text: Awia, u kaa izi di di, ka nyɔɔ. Un na fɔŋŋa lii a diwee be la, u wer vol guŋŋ hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi tokkoanɛɛ, di ga hel Bizeŋ Sinaai n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Bizennaniinanii la.

text: Ɛlisa bir di la Gilgal paga, di lɔchɔgii chol de keŋkere, a saŋa hiŋ. Di u ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi baŋhina n kpauwɛ di ra hum, chaalɔɔ, u ra bagli baa. Denii Ɛlisa ŋɔ u balii be, “Kpa viizeŋ di hɔŋ, di nuugi dɔzi tɛɛ baala naa.”

ref: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
text: Ba bɛl lii la pir ú ga nyiŋŋi tagzi, di ga na kiim. Denii u tɔrgi u nɔna aŋhina, di kpaa du u tagtajaŋ jiffa. Uŋ wa bittɛ ba, u pergaa du a dɔzi, haali nɛr maa n faa waa zum kuna la dizi n ɛɛa.

ref: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
text: Denii ba fug a dɔzi di tɛɛ a baala bá di, ka baŋ wa faarɛɛ di ra di, ba lɔ wile di ŋɔ, “Ee, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ, ba duabuu siri!” Awia, ba vɛɛ a dii.

ref: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
text: Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “Ií nyiŋŋi sau ba.” U kpa a sau di du a vii biini, ka ŋɔ, “Ií bɔnni a dɔzi tɛɛ a nɛra bá di.” A dɔzi jaa du sum.

ref: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
text: Denii u kpaa chiŋŋi a baala see, ba heea ka ka, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
text: Baal bɛllɛ ba faa ra yir Naaman, u ɛɛ Siiria koori laallɔɔra nabɔma. Ba faa ra tɔgzuubuu werge, u dɔɔ sɔŋ Siiria koori be, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ga u benii, Siiria hina lɔ laal di kpegli ba dɔma. U faa dɔɔ bampiriire werge laal lɔi biini, ka faa dɔɔ bɔchɔgaa.

ref: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Siiria laallɔɔra faa ga lɔ Izrɛl hina laal, di lau ba biihambijiga bɛl, ú ga ɛɛ Naaman haaŋ balii.

ref: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
text: Denii Naaman la u nabɔma be, di ga ŋɔ u be gunla a biihambie n ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
text: A koori ŋɔ u be, “La! N daŋ sɛbi hɔŋ tɛi, í ga tɛɛ Izrɛl koori.” Denii Naaman izi di kpa saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi kalfaahoro ni tokkoanɛɛ, saliŋ ge kebisau kagboŋa anumbɛl ani laala ge bɔra fi.

ref: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
text: Wia la n du Siiria koori hɔŋ la uŋ sɛbɛɛ ba ga tɛɛ Izrɛl koori labuu keŋ, “Hɔnnaabuu niŋ bagli lugɔ minuu ra hum n balii Naaman i be, í chaa u bɔchɔgaa.”

ref: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
text: Ɛlisa hum u balii dí u la ga ŋɔ u be, “La ga sɔ i hiŋ naa buniidaanɛɛ, Jɔɔdan muu biini. I bɔchɔgaa la daŋ tuŋ, i bɔrahɔŋ bir chol dɔŋa ni, di vɔgli.”

ref: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
text: Izrɛl koori la n haŋ wa karmi a hɔŋ di waa tuŋ, u lau u laala piili, ka ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizii miŋŋ? N daŋ wer kpu kuŋ ka bir lalluuwaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ a hindee hum nɛbɛl ŋɔ ú ba n be n chaa u bɔchɔgaa? Na gunla unna nyiŋŋi n ni kalu!”

ref: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Izrɛl koori piili u laalaa la, u tili ŋɔ u be, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i piili i laalai? Gil a baal ba n be, denii u zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ du Izrɛllɛ.”

ref: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
text: Awia, Naaman ni u zagra ni torkozi jaa la ga chi Ɛlisa dominua.

ref: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
text: Ka Naaman bir di ra kaali ni baaŋfuuih, di ŋɔ, “N fɛwɔɔ lugɔ u daŋ vii liiu ba n be di wa chi, ka yir Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la sɔŋ, di lalli u nonii guali n ni, di chaa n bɔchɔgaa naa.

ref: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
text: Muuni Abana ni Fapa n du Damaskus niiri waa wer di kaali Izrɛl hɛri niiri maa? N faa wàá wer sɔ a biine, ń bɔra kuaria?” Awia, u faa bir di ra kaali ni baaŋfuuih werge maa.

ref: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
text: Ka Naaman balaa la u be, di ga ŋɔ, “Yaa dɔɔri, di Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa ŋɔ i ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛl, i vii wàá ɛɛuwaa? Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ hàá wer sɔ i hiŋ, í bɔrahɔŋ bir chol dɔŋa ni, gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lai?”

ref: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
text: Denii u jaa tuu la ga muzi Jɔɔdan muu biini, naa buniidaanɛɛ, gunla Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ n bagluu la. U bɔrahɔŋ bir chol dɔŋa ni, di vɔgli alugɔ biifula bɔrahɔŋ.

ref: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
text: Denii Naaman ani u balaa la maa bir la Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la be. U ga chi u see ka ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ, n jaa zumuu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi waa hoo durnya naa yemmaa, di Izrɛl hɛri lɛi. Awia, jaande maa, ka lɛɛ i balii kuna un niŋ sunzii filaŋkeŋ.”

ref: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ ŋɔ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, n na humuu la, lugɔ màá lɛɛ kummaa.” Naaman faa fɔrguu lugɔ u lɛɛa, ka u vɛɛ.

ref: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
text: Denii Naaman jaa ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, haali di haa lɛɛ gba, amɔ, i tɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii hɛɛhraa lugɔ kauzi anɛɛ bunni, n kpa di ra kpo, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ i balii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka kpu kuna di lizi mbusu di fuuh tɛɛ vug maa, di Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ lɛi.

ref: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi ga gil wikpaŋ naa tɛɛ mìŋ́ i balii. Di n ga du n nabɔma zuu Siiria hina vug Rimɔn diizeŋ biini, u dɛlli n nonii ni, n ge tognuu, Kɔ́raawiizi gil n wichɔgaa tɛŋ, dikuu wikpaŋ naa wia.”

ref: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
text: Ɛlisa balii Gɛhazi ŋɔ u biini, “N dɔɔri suŋ Siiria hinuu Naaman la ninɛɛ werge, dikuu uŋ waa u kunsunzaa la uŋ ba a ni la lɛɛwɛ wia. N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de, wibii maa, n daŋ dau u luge di ga lɛɛ a kuna aŋhina u be.”

ref: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
text: Denii Gɛhazi hahzi di ra dau Naaman luge. Naaman n wa nau uŋ chɔwɛɛ di ra ba u be la, u lii u torko biini tuu, di chem u ni, di pɛɛzuu, “A summɔaa?”

ref: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
text: Gɛhazi ŋɔ, “A summɔɔ. N dɔɔrii humiŋ dí n wa ŋɔ i be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi baŋhina n kpauwɛ di ra hum banɛɛrɛ lii Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri di ba u be. Awia, jaande maa, ka kpa saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu ani laala ge bɔra anɛɛ tɛu, ú tɛɛ baa.”

ref: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
text: Naaman ŋɔ, “Jaande maa, lɛɛ a saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi tokkoahoro ni ŋmantannaazi.” U fɔrgi Gɛhazi dí u lɛɛa. Ka jaa kpa a saliŋhuŋŋa di du hure anɛɛ biini, di vɔɔzaa, di kpa laala la di jaa. Di kpaa chug u balaa banɛɛ, ba tɔ Gɛhazi see.

ref: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
text: Ka baŋ ga hel giŋgimii la nyuu Ɛlisa n faa duwɛɛ la, Gɛhazi lɛɛ a kuna di chiŋŋi dia, ka ta a baala ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba kaali.

ref: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
text: Denii u zuu ga chi u dɔɔri Ɛlisa see. Ɛlisa pɛɛzuu, “Gɛhazi, lee i lanɛi?” Gɛhazi ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, maa yemmaa laŋŋɛ.”

ref: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
text: Ka Ɛlisa ŋɔ u be, “N duma faa du i benii saŋa la a baal n lii u torko biini di tuu chem i ni la. Saŋa naabuu dɛkkɛ hin niŋ ga lɛɛ kebee gɛɛ laala ni ɔlivizi ni daanɔna kooni ni peeza ni nauna ani balaa?

ref: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
text: Awia, Naaman bɔchɔgaa la daŋ buu i ni i naanna maa di hanna la.” Denii Gɛhazi lii Ɛlisa be ni bɔchɔgaa, u bɔra maa huuhzi alugɔ gonni.

ref: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
text: A hɔl bɛl, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi baŋhina n kpauwɛ di ra hum, ŋɔ Ɛlisa be, “Na, bɔnnaa yaa nii n ɔɔ ra chaali naa du jigaa werge.

ref: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
text: Awia, gil ya la Jɔɔdan muu. Yaa bɛl maa ga nyiŋŋi daakpaŋkpaŋa, di kuari bɔr di ra zuu de.” U ŋɔ, “Ií ra la.”

ref: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
text: Ka bɛl ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, hàá gil i ni i balaa laa?” Ɛlisa sɛɛ,

ref: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
text: u ni baa kpa di kaali. Baŋ ga hel Jɔɔdan muu, ba faari di ra teŋri daazi.

ref: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ la pɛɛzuu, “Lee u chollei?” Uŋ wa bagluu, Ɛlisa mɔŋ daa di ta de, a kpaŋfɔ bii lii zaali.

ref: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
text: U ŋɔ, “Laau.” A baal bugni di laau. Siiria laallɔɔra nyuŋŋaa wia

ref: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
text: A saŋa, di Siiria koori ni Izrɛl hina ra lɔ laal. Siiria koori ŋɔ u nabɔnzi biruu liize, ú lizi bɔr la un niŋ chɔɔ.

ref: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa tili Izrɛl koori be, di ŋɔ, “A du tau, gilɛɛ waa ga de, dikuubɛɛwiai, denii Siiria hina ra la bá ga chɔɔ.”

ref: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
text: Guŋ faa fuuh Siiria koori la baaŋ werge maa, u chaali u nabɔnzi, di pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ n du yaa biini di chi Izrɛl koori harɛi?”

ref: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
text: Ba bɛl ŋɔ, “Jara, yaa bɛl maa waa u har chigɛ. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa n du Izrɛl labuu ɔɔ bagli wia la maa hiŋ ɔɔ suah di ŋɔ i diichɔɔlii gba biinii di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl koori.”

ref: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
text: A koori faa ŋɔ, “Ií la ga nyiŋŋi bɔr la un duwɛɛ, ń hum laallɔɔra ba ga lawuu.” Ba wa ŋɔ u be lugɔ u du Dɔtan.

ref: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
text: Denii u hum laallɔkpega ni zagra ani a torkozi. Ba la ga fɔɔ a bolzeŋ hamuŋa ni, di baruu chem.

ref: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
text: Chɔɔzimpikke ni, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ balii izi di lii bossee, di na lugɔ Siiria laallɔɔra ni ba zagra ni a torkozii bar a bolzeŋ maa chem. A balii bir la Ɛlisa be, di ga ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri, yaa siuwɔɔ tuŋ! Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛi?”

ref: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
text: A Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm, banla n du yaa be kpillɔɔ kaali banla n du ba be.”

ref: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
text: Denii Ɛlisa suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, pilli u siwee ú wer di ra na.” Kɔraawiizi pilli u balii la siwee, u binni di na lugɔ giŋgimee la nyuuni maanii zagra ni torkozi su, di ra lau niŋ, di bar Ɛlisa chem.

ref: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
text: Ba dɔma la n tuuwe di ra ba u be la, Ɛlisa suŋŋi wiizi, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, gil laallɔɔra naa maa nyuŋŋi!” Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil ba maa nyuŋŋi, gunla Ɛlisa n suŋŋɛɛ la.

ref: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
text: Ɛlisa ŋɔ ba be, “A ŋmɛnɛɛ lɛi keŋ, a bolzeŋ ge gba lɛi keŋ. Ií ra hiŋiŋ, ń ga bagli ia baal la iinna nyiŋŋi la.” Denii u tɔ ba see di la Samaria.

ref: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
text: Baŋ ga zuu a bolzeŋ biini, Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, pilli laallɔɔra naa siwee, bá wer di ra na.” Denii Kɔraawiizi pilli ba siwee, ba na lugɔ bolzeŋ Samaria biinii ba du.

ref: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
text: Izrɛl koori n wa na baa, u pɛɛzi Ɛlisa, “Mmɛ, n kpu baa? N kpu baa?”

ref: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
text: Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ waa kpuuzi baa. I daŋ sɛɛ kpuuzi baala la hiŋ kpa i tokobi ni i hoo di kpegli, di lauriaa? Tɛɛ baa diwee ni nii, bá di, di nyɔɔ ka bir di ra la ba dɔɔri be.”

ref: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
text: Denii u faa daali diuzenaa tɛɛ baa. Baŋ wa diwee di nyɔɔ tuŋ, u ta baa ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba bir kaali ba dɔɔri be. Awia, Siiria laallɔɔra faa waa kaa ra lɔ Izrɛl hina laal. Bolzeŋ Samaria fɔɔi wia

ref: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad kaa chaali u laallɔɔra maa, di la ga fɔɔ bolzeŋ Samaria ni laal.

ref: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
text: Baŋ faa fɔɔ a bolzeŋ di birgi wia, lɔchɔgii faa chol a bol, haali ba ɔɔ faa yoo kawee nyuu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau tokkoanaazu, komma bina ge kookoo tassa suul ɔɔ ɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau anue.

ref: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
text: Izrɛl koori faa wa ga danzɛɛ kɛrii di waa kaali, haaŋ bɛl lɔ wile di ŋɔ, “Jara, hiiniŋ!”

ref: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
text: A koori bir ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi wɛɛ hiinee, ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di hiiniinei, di lii pila gɛɛ bɔr la banna fɛrgi grepu nɔna, a nii ra liiyɛi?”

ref: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
text: A koori kaa pɛɛzuu, “A summɔaa?” U ŋɔ, “Haaŋ naabuu ŋɔ n be, ‘Kpa i biibaal ba ya hee zinaa, ka kɛrɛ ya hee n ge hor.’

ref: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
text: Awia, yaa daali n biibaal la di hee. Ka hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, n ŋɔ u be, ‘Ge kpa i biibaal la ba ya hee, ka waabuu kpa u bie suah.’ ”

ref: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
text: A koori n wa nuu a haaŋ wiŋɔzi la, u tɛr u laala piili. Ka unna vol a koŋlii kɛrii la, a nɛra na lugɔ u laali gbɔglɔŋ tagtaarɛ di du biini.

ref: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
text: Denii u ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi tɛr n digni werge, di maa Safat biibaal Ɛlisa nyuu teŋŋe zinaa!”

ref: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. text: Denii a hɛri nɛra maa faa jaa la vug Baal dia, di ga purgi u maa, di purgi u mbusu lizibɔra ani de vuga la maa, di kpu vug Baal kizeehiŋ Matan, mbusu lizibɔra see. Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa lizi nɛra, bá ra guu Kɔraawiizi Dia.

ref: he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah.
text: U jaa yir laallɔɔra kalfazi nabɔnzi, koori guure, kooridia tauduura ani a hɛri nɛra maa, ba maa chaali di kpogli a koori lii Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga a tauduura dominua la ga zuu a kooridia. A koori faa jaa ga so u koorikara ni.

ref: Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord.
text: Koori Joas faa ɛɛ nɛnnɛɛ Kɔraawiizi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa ra bagluubuu.

ref: The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
text: Ama, kebee la baŋ faa nawɛɛ lii bilchɔg mbusuzi ni wichɔgaa giltɛɛi mbusuzi lizaa biine la waa, faa waa Kɔraawiizi Dia la ballɛ. Aawaa faa ɛɛ kizeehina horaa.

ref: But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Ama, vuga kuaribɔra la faa haa du denii, nɛra haa vɛɛ di ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma de.

ref: and use it to repair the temple whenever you see the need.”
text: Ií gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɛl maa lɛɛ kebee lii kebidaura la be, bá kpaa di kuari ma a Dia bɔra la n chɔkkɛ la.”

ref: But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule,
text: Ka Koori Joas Kora dii binni tokko ni ahorohiŋ biini, di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la faa haa waa a Dia kuarɛɛ.

ref: Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.”
text: Awia, Koori Joas faa yir Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada ani u dɔŋahina kizeehina la, di pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii waa a Dia bɔra la n chɔkkɛ la kuarɛɛi? Ií gilɛɛ kaa dau kebee la maa iiŋ lɛɛwɛ lii kebidaura la be, ií kpaa tɛɛ bá kuari a Dia.”

ref: The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la sɛɛ lugɔ ba wàá ka lɛɛ kebee lii a nɛra be, ba himmaa gba lɛi niŋ kuari a Dia.

ref: Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa kpa dakka bɛl di fur u nuatua, ka kpau chiŋŋi mbusu lizibɔr nodig keŋkere la nɛra n gawɛɛ di ra zuu a Dia biini. Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n na du a Dia dominua tau, ɔɔ kpa kebee la maa baŋ ɔɔ ba a ni Dia la, di ra du a dakka biini.

ref: When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags.
text: Di ba wa nawɔɔ lugɔ, kebee werge du a dakka biini, kooridia karchi ani Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma ɔɔ bau, di wa kur a kebee la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ba Kɔraawiizi Dia la, di kpaa du bɔɔtizi biine.

ref: Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers,
text: Di ba wa zum a kebee maga la, ba ɔɔ kpaa tɛɛ nɛra la baŋ lizɛɛ ŋɔ ba ra binni a huma ni a Dia biini la. A kebee naa biinii ba faa turgi banla n hum a Dia hum, baabuu kapintazi, maara,

ref: the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
text: koŋlii maara ani banla n na sɛɛhzi bia maa. Ba faa yau daapiahni ni bisɛɛhzaarɛ, bá kuari a Dia. Haali ba faa wettoo turgi kima la maa baŋ lɔwɛɛ ka wer kuari a Dia labuu.

ref: While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple.
text: Ba faa waa a kebee la baŋ ba a ni a Dia la kpawɛɛ turgi a Dia saliŋhuŋŋa tassazenaa, kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra mɔnni fintina yakɔssi, niimizaa tassazi, bensunozi ani kuna la baŋ kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa kuari, di du a Dia la kim.

ref: The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
text: Ba faa waa nyiŋŋi bá zum gunla banla baŋ kpa a kebee tɛɛ bá turgi a huŋhunna la n dia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa hummɔɔ ni biinihuŋŋu.

ref: About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem.
text: A saŋa, di Siiria Koori Hazɛl faa laŋŋɔ di ga lɔ bolzeŋ Gaf laal di kpegluu. Denii u faa kaa bir ú wa lɔ Jɛrusalɛm ge.

ref: So Joash collected everything he and his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated to the Lord, as well as the gold in the storage rooms in the temple and palace. He sent it all to Hazael as a gift, and when Hazael received it, he ordered his troops to leave Jerusalem.
text: Ka Juda Koori Joas faa kpa kunnanaananaa la u mɛɛwaa, Koori Jɛhɔsafat, Koori Jɛhɔram, Koori Ahazia ani u himmaa hora la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni saliŋ la maa n faa du Kɔraawiizi Dia ani anla ge maa n faa du a kooridia la, di ga tɛɛ Siiria Koori Hazɛl, ka u gil Jɛrusalɛm laal lɔi.

ref: Everything else Joash did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Ama, Koori Joas kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: At the end of his rule, some of his officers rebelled against him. Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him in a building where the land was filled in on the east side of Jerusalem, near the road to Silla. Joash was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Amaziah became king.
text: U nabɔnzi la n faa kpuubuu, Simiaf biibaal Jɔzabad ani Soma biibaal Jɛhɔzabad. Ba faa huguu u mɛɛwaa hugribɔr, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Amazia faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled
text: Koori Ahazia biibaal Juda Koori Joas kora dii binni tokko ni ahorohiŋ biinii, Koori Jehu biibaal Jehoahaz ge faa di Izrɛl kora, di du bolzeŋ Samaria biini, binni fidaaniidaanɛɛ.

ref: and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
text: Ka kaa ŋɔ u be, “Pilli wiifurii tokoro la.” U pilluu. Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “Ta hobii!” U tau. Ɛlisa jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi hobiire, u hobii la un niŋ kpa di kpegli Siiria hina labuu guŋ. I daŋ chɔgi Siiria hina maa nyaamm, bolzeŋ Afɛk hɛri.”

ref: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, dikuu uŋ faa hiŋ Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la wia. Koori Jehoahaz faa waa sɛɛwɛ gilaa ta.

ref: The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge maa, u gil Siiria Koori Hazɛl ni u biibaal Bɛn Hadad faa dɔɔ ba fɔŋŋa, di birgi werge maa.

ref: Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz
text: Denii Koori Jehoahaz faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú hiinuu. Kɔraawiizi nuu u suŋŋaa la, dikuu u faa na gunla Siiria koori n na tɔɔri Izrɛl hina labuu werge maa.

ref: by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa lɛɛ Izrɛl hina lii Siiria hina dɔɔra la biini. Izrɛl hina faa jaa ra zuu ni bampirsɔna, gunla baŋ faa felee du la.

ref: Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled
text: Juda Koori Joas kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Jehoahaz biibaal Jehoas, faa di Izrɛl kora, di du Samaria, binni fidaanumbɛl.

ref: Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Ama, Koori Jehoahaz kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ wette ɛɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna la biine.

ref: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king. King Jehoash of Israel
text: Koori Jehoahaz faa siu, ba huguu u mɛɛwaa hugribɔr, bolzeŋ Samaria biini, ka u biibaal Jehoas kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Izrɛl Koori Jehoas wia

ref: “Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand
text: U ŋɔ Izrɛl koori hiŋ be, “Kpa a hoo.” Uŋ wa kpau la, Ɛlisa kpa u nonee di sag a koori nonee ni.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord by doing just like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. U faa waa sɛɛwɛ ú gil Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la.

ref: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Ama, Koori Jehoas kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, u ni Juda Koori Amazia laal lɔi wia, ba faa sɛbaabuu di du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna la biine.

ref: Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king. Elisha the Prophet Dies
text: Koori Jehoas faa siu, ba huguu Izrɛl koora hugribɔr, bolzeŋ Samaria biini, ka u biibaal Jeroboam nɛɛhiŋ kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa siu wia

ref: Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa faa ra wii wiilkpega la n niŋ kpuu. Izrɛl Koori Jehoas faa la ú ga nau. Uŋ ga na Ɛlisa, di u ra nyiŋŋi u siu, Koori Jehoas faa ra wii, di ra ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri! N dɔɔri! Hinuu faa Izrɛl hina guuri la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge!”

ref: Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa kaa ŋɔ, “Kpa hobee la!” A koori kpaa. Ɛlisa ŋɔ, “Kpaa di yag hɛri.” U kpaa di yag buhoro, ka gil.

ref: Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa baaŋ faa fuuh u ni werge maa, u ŋɔ, “A dɛkkɔɔ i vii yag a hɛri naa bunue gɛɛ bunumbɛl, guŋ bagli lugɔ i daŋ vii kpegli Siiria hina, di chɔgi baa nyaamm. Ka filaŋkennaa waa, buhoro bɛnnɛ, í wer kpegli baa.”

ref: Elisha died and was buried. Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlisa jaa siu, ba huguu. A guŋ saŋa, di Moab hina nɛchɔgaa ɔɔ faa wa zuu Izrɛl hɛrii wem maga di ra foozi ba kuna.

ref: Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up. Israel Defeats Syria
text: Denii a hɔl bɛl, Izrɛl hina baŋhina faa ra nyiŋŋi ba hug lalii bɛl. Ba wa ŋɔ ba binni, di nɛchɔgaa gaa ba, ba kpa a lalii ta Ɛlisa ŋmam biini, ka chɔ kaali. A lalii n ga gbɔgzi Ɛlisa hoga, u bir na miibɔɔ, di izi chi. Izrɛl hina ni Siiria hina laal wia

ref: Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz.
text: Siiria Koori Hazɛl faa sunni Izrɛl hinaa werge maa, Koori Jehoahaz kora dii saŋa.

ref: But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi faa ɛɛ baabuu nɛnnɛ, di ɔɔ ra suŋ ba ni, dikuu u ni Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb nuukpaŋ la wia. Haali ni zinaa, u haa waa nyiŋŋi ú chɔgi baa gɛɛ di vɛɛ baa ta.

ref: Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria.
text: Siiria Koori Hazɛl faa siu, ka u biibaal Bɛn Hadad kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
text: Denii Izrɛl Koori Jehoas faa lɔ Siiria hina laal, di kpegli baa buhoro maa, di bir foozi bola la maa Koori Hazɛl n faa foozee laal biini lii u mɛɛ Koori Jehoahaz be la.

ref: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
text: Waabuu faa bittɛ di lɛɛ Izrɛl hina hɛri magbɔɔni lii Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere, di ga chug Muuzensiwii, n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag. ref: Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel.
text: Koori Jehoahaz biibaal Izrɛl Koori Jehoas, kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Joas biibaal Amazia faa di Juda kora.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. U faa waa sɛɛwɛ ú gil Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la.

ref: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
text: Koori Jeroboam faa siu, ba huguu koora hugribɔr, ka u biibaal Zɛkaria faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
text: U faa ɛɛ wideŋlaare Kɔraawiizi be. Ka u faa waa ɛɛwɛ hel u naabaal Koori Deevid. U wiɛɛlaa maa biini, u faa ra hiŋ gunla u mɛɛ Koori Joas n faa ɛɛwɛ labuu.

ref: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Ama, u faa waa vuga kuaribɔra la chɔkkɛ. Nɛra faa haa ra lizi mbusuzii, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma de.

ref: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
text: A kora n faa wa du u nonee chigigi, u kpu nabɔnzi la maa n faa kpu u mɛɛ la.

ref: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
text: Ama, u faa waa u mɛɛ kpuura biibaala waa kpuwɛɛ, gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ Moosis Gbɔgni hɔŋ biini, bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ, “A waa dɛkkɛ bá kpu mɛɛwaa, dikuu ba biizi wichɔgaa wia gɛɛ bá kpu biizi, dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia. A dɛkkɔɔ bɛl maa siu, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia.”

ref: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
text: I kpegli Ɛdɔm hinaa, di jaa ra ta barabara di ra jigsi, ka n na ŋɔ i benii, so i bol pɛrɛtɛ! Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra nyiŋŋi tɔɔrɔɔ la n niŋ gil i ni Juda hina maa cholei?”

ref: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
text: Denii Koori Amazia faa hum u balaa Izrɛl Koori Jehoas be, di ŋɔ, “Ba n nii chem di lɔ dɔŋa!”

ref: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
text: Ka Izrɛl Koori Jehoas bir ŋɔ Juda Koori Amazia be, “A hɔl bɛllɛ Lɛbanɔn sɔɔhpuza tili Lɛbanɔn hɛriŋkpol daa be, di ŋɔ, ‘Kpa i biihaaŋ tɛŋ ń tɛɛ n biibaal.’ Ka Lɛbanɔn sechɔgii bɛl lii di wa fɛrgi a sɔɔhpuza kpu.

ref: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
text: Ka Koori Amazia faa waa nuuwɛ tɛu. Awia, Izrɛl Koori Jehoas jaa ɛɛ sirya lii, ú ni Juda koori ga chem dɔŋa ni bolzeŋ Bɛf Sɛmɛs n du Juda hɛri, di lɔ dɔŋa.

ref: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,

text: Koori Jehoas kora dii saŋa, wia la aŋhina uŋ ɛɛwɛ ani u bampirsi wiɛɛlaa uŋ faa wette ɛɛ nɛnnɛ, u ni Juda Koori Amazia laal lɔi la, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna la biine.

text: Denii Juda hina maa faa lau u biibaal Uzzia n di binni fidaanumbɛl, di tɔu kora, u kpa u mɛɛ gawa.

text: Waabuu faa bittɛ ma Ɛlaf, di bir jaa Juda bola ni, Koori Amazia siu har. Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam nɛɛhiŋ wia

text: Kɔraawiizi faa na gunla yoma gɛɛ nɛra la n dɔɔ bahinaa la n faa ra di dɔgnya werge Izrɛl hɛri, ka nɛr maa faa waa hoo ú hiini baa.

ref: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi n faa waa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ dim Izrɛl sɔŋ hɛri naa biini wia, u faa ga Koori Jehoas biibaal Koori Jeroboam benii, di lɛɛ baa.

ref: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Koori Jeroboam kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, uŋ lɔ laal di kpegli u dɔma ani uŋ wette bir lɛɛ bolzenaa Damaskus ani Hamaf n faa ɛɛ Juda hora, di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la. Ba faa sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
text: Koori Pɛkahia kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, ba sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Izrɛl Koori Pɛka wia

ref: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
text: Juda Koori Uzzia kora dii binni tokkoanɛɛ ni fihiŋ biinii, Koori Mɛnahɛm biibaal Pɛkahia, faa di Izrɛl kora, di so bolzeŋ Samaria. Binni anɛɛrɛ u faa di a kora, bolzeŋ Samaria biini.

ref: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
text: U faa ɛɛ wideŋlaare Kɔraawiizi be, gunla u mɛɛ Koori Amazia n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Ka u faa waa vuga kuaribɔra la chɔkkɛ. Nɛra faa haa ra lizi mbusuzii di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma de.

ref: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi faa kpa bɔchɔgaa ta u ni, a du u ni guŋŋ u wa siu. Awia, u faa du u bɛŋ diarɛ. Ka u biibaal Jɔtam faa dɔɔ a kooridia fɔŋŋa, di ra binni a hɛri hina maa ni.

ref: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Koori Uzzia kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
text: Koori Uzzia faa siu, ba huguu di dugli u mɛɛwaa hugribɔr, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini, ka u biibaal Jɔtam faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Izrɛl Koori Zɛkaria wia

ref: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
text: Juda Koori Uzzia kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ŋmantannaazihiŋ biinii, Koori Jeroboam nɛɛhiŋ biibaal Zɛkaria faa di Izrɛl kora, di du Samaria. U faa di a koraa baaguzi anumbɛl.

ref: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
text: Jabɛs biibaal Salum faa suahzi ta Koori Zɛkaria kpui jina, di faa kpuu nɛra see, ka kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
text: Gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Jehu, “I naanna daŋ so Izrɛl koorikara naa ni, jiminizi anaazu” la, jaa ɛɛ wibii. Izrɛl Koori Salum wia

ref: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
text: Jabɛs biibaal Salum faa di Izrɛl koraa, Juda Koori Uzzia kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kabɛlhiŋ biini. U faa di a koraa baagu kpaŋ, bolzeŋ Samaria biini.

ref: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
text: Juda Koori Uzzia kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kabɛlhiŋ biinii, Gadi biibaal Mɛnahɛm faa di Izrɛl kora. U faa di a koraa bolzeŋ Samaria biini, binni fi.

ref: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. U kora dii saŋa maa biini, u faa waa Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la, gillɛ.

ref: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
text: Denii Asiiria Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa, faa wa fɔɔ Izrɛl hɛri ni laal. Ka Koori Mɛnahɛm faa tɛu saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi kagboŋa tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anaazu, ka ú chi u har, ú kora la wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, a hɛri biini.

ref: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
text: Koori Jɔtam faa ɛɛ gunla n deŋleere Kɔraawiizi be, gunla u mɛɛ Koori Uzzia n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Koori Mɛnahɛm kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
text: Koori Mɛnahɛm faa siu, ba huguu, ka u biibaal Pɛkahia kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Izrɛl Koori Pɛkahia wia

ref: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
text: Koori Pɛkahia faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge, di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni. U faa waa Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la, gillɛ.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa waa Nɛbat biibaal Koori Jeroboam wichɔgaa la uŋ faa gillɛ Izrɛl hina maa ɛɛ la, gillɛ.

ref: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
text: Izrɛl Koori Pɛka kora dii biinii, Asiiria Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa faa ba, di wa lɔ bolzenaa Ijɔn, Abɛl Bɛf Maaka, Janoa, Kɛdɛs ani Hazɔr hina laal, di kpegli baa. U faa kaa kpegli Giliad, Galilii ani Naftali hɛssi maa, di lauri a nɛra maa kaali Siiria hɛri.

ref: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
text: Denii baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Ɛla biibaal Hosia faa suahzi ta Koori Pɛka kpui jina, di kpuu, ka kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Koori Uzzia biibaal Koori Jɔtam kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biinii guŋ ɛɛ.

ref: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
text: Koori Pɛka kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, ba sɛbaabuu du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine. Juda Koori Jɔtam wia

ref: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
text: Izrɛl Koori Pɛka la mɛɛ n faa ɛɛ Rɛmalia la, kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Uzzia biibaal Jɔtam faa di Juda kora.

ref: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Ka u faa waa vuga kuaribɔra la chɔkkɛ, ka nɛra faa haa ra lizi mbusuzi, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma de. Koori Jotannɛ faa kaa bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia Chiŋ Dominuuzeŋ la.

ref: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Koori Jɔtam kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
text: A saŋa naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa gil Siiria Koori Rɛzin ani Rɛmalia biibaal Izrɛl Koori Pɛka faa la ga pig Juda hina ni laal.

ref: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
text: Koori Jɔtam faa siu, ba huguu u mɛɛwaa hugribɔr, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Ahaz faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
text: Rɛmalia biibaal Koori Pɛka kora dii binni fidaaniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Koori Jɔtam biibaal Ahaz, faa di Juda kora.

ref: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
text: Koori Ahaz faa siu, ba huguu u mɛɛwaa hugribɔr, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini, ka u biibaal Hɛzɛkia faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Yuria faa ɛɛ gunla maa Koori Ahaz n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
text: U faa ra hiŋ Izrɛl koora hiŋaa labuu, haali di lau u biibaal lizi mbusu di fuuh tɛɛ vuga, di ra chanzi wikuna la nɛra la Kɔraawiizi n faa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri n na ɛɛ, di Izrɛl hina faa ra ba la.

ref: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
text: U faa ra lizi mbusuzii, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma vuga kuaribɔra, giŋgimee nyuuni ani daazenaa maa zɛɛzi.

ref: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Siiria Koori Rɛzin faa kaa bir foozi bolzeŋ Ɛlaf tɛɛ Siiria hina, dikuu uŋ faa wette duŋŋi Juda hina de wia. Ɛdɔm hina faa la ga so de, di wa lii ni zinaa.

ref: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
text: Koori Ahaz faa hum nɛra Asiiria Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa be, di ŋɔ, “N ɛɛ i baliirɛ, di ra sɛɛ i dɔɔra. Ba wa lɛɛŋ lii Siiria Koori Rɛzin ni Izrɛl Koori Pɛka la n na lɔŋ laal la nonee biini.”

ref: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
text: Koori Ahaz faa kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia ni kooridia diini la biine, banna chiŋŋi daama kuna la, di tɛɛ ba ga sunzi Asiiria koorizeŋ la.

ref: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
text: Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa faa nuu u suŋŋaa la, di la ga fɔɔ Damaskus hina ni laal, di kpegli baa, di lauri baa kaali yembɛl banna yir Kir, ka faa kpu Koori Rɛzin ge.

ref: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
text: Denii Koori Ahaz faa la Damaskus, ú ga na Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa. U faa ga na mbusu lizibɔr bɛl de, di faa kuari u duula di dau kuŋ ni, di kpau hum, ba ga tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Yuria.

ref: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Yuria faa ma mbusu lizibɔr gunla maa Koori Ahaz n baglɛɛ la di tuŋ, mɔɔ ka a koori haa bir lii Damaskus ba.

ref: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
text: A koori n wa lii Damaskus ba di wa na mbusu lizibɔr, u tuzi hel u zɛɛ, di lizi mbusuzi u ni.

ref: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
text: U faa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni mbusu lizaa mia, di ta siŋ, di kpa dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa sela chal di mizi mbusu lizibɔr ni.

ref: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
text: Danyɛ mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la faa chigɔ mbusu lizibɔfalii la ni Kɔraawiizi Dia baambaannɛ. Awia, Koori Ahaz faa kpau di ga chiŋŋi ufalii la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere.

ref: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
text: Denii Koori Ahaz faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Yuria be, “Mbusu lizibɔfaliizeŋ naa ninɛɛ i ɔɔ ra lizi chɔɔzi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, duaniŋ mbusu lizaa mia, koori mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni u mbusu lizaa mia, a hɛri nɛra maa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni ba mbusu lizaa mia ani mbusuzi lizaa siŋ. I daŋ ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni mbusuzi lizaa sela maa chal, di mizi mbusu lizibɔr naa ni. Ka n ge ɔɔ kpa mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari naa, di ra vug.”

ref: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
text: Koori Ahaz faa wil a torkozi kɛraa daapiahni la, ka koo tassazenaa la n faa hɔŋzi a ni la, di kaa koo danyɛ Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ la lii danyɛ nabala fidaanɛɛ la ni uŋ faa hɔŋŋɛ la, di hɔŋ bii ni.

ref: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
text: U kaa gil ba wil Heezaa Hɔpizii pampanni la baŋ faa baŋŋɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia la. Ba faa kaa tɔ koori dominua la uŋ ɔɔ faa ga di ra zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la, guŋ par Asiiria koorizeŋ.

ref: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Koori Ahaz kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
text: Juda Koori Ahaz kora dii binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Ɛla biibaal Hosia, faa di Izrɛl kora bolzeŋ Samaria biini, binni kabɛl.

ref: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, ka u faa waa lugɔ Izrɛl koora la n di a kora ka tɛu la.

ref: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
text: Denii Asiiria Koorizeŋ Salmanɛsa faa ba ú wa lɔ Koori Hosia laal, haali uŋ faa ɛɛ u koorijiga, di ɔɔ lizi hɛri kuna di ra tɛu gba.

ref: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
text: Ka Asiiria koorizeŋ la faa wa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Koori Hosia ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔ hinnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa hum u nɛraa ba la Ijip koori So be, ba nuu ga ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Guŋ wia, u faa waa kaa ra lizi hɛri kuna di ra tɛu, gunla uŋ ɔɔ faa ra ɛɛ, bina maa la. Awia, Koorizeŋ Samlanɛsa faa wa lawuu, di tɔu dia.

ref: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
text: Koori Hosia kora dii binni kabɛlhiŋ biinii, Asiiria koorizeŋ la faa jaa kpegli bolzeŋ Samaria hina, di lauri Izrɛl hina kaali Asiiria. U faa ga soŋŋi baŋhinaa bolzeŋ la banna yir Hala, baŋhina ge so dugli Muu Habɔ n du Gɔzan barii, baŋhina ge so Mɛdi hina bolzenaa.

ref: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
text: Annii maa faa ɛɛwɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Izrɛl hina faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di zuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la n lɛɛ baa, di lii Ijip koori dɔɔra biini la ni. Ba faa ra kuari vugaa,

ref: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
text: di ra hiŋ gunla nɛra la Kɔraawiizi n faa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri, n faa ra hiŋ ani wichɔgaa la Izrɛl koora n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
text: Izrɛl hina la faa suahzɔɔrɛ di ɛɛ wia la n waa deŋlee, di zuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la ni. Ba faa ma vuga kuaribɔraa ba boljigzi ni ba bolzenaa maa biine.

ref: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
text: Ba faa baŋzi vug Baal bia ani vughaaŋ Asɛra daazii, giŋgimee nyuuni ani daazenaa maa zɛɛzi.

ref: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
text: A vuga kuaribɔra maanii ba ɔɔ faa ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma gunla hɛssi la hina Kɔraawiizi n duŋŋɛɛ, di ba faa ra ba, n na ɛɛ la. Ba faa ɛɛ biinikpola wiarɛ werge maa, a guŋ faa gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh ba ni.

ref: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
text: Ba faa ra kuari vugaa, haali Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ga u dɔgtɛɛzi ni u sinaara benii, di karfi Izrɛl ani Juda hɛssi hina maa, di ŋɔ, “Ií gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi, ka ra hiŋ n wiŋɔɔlaa ni n widaulaa, gunla n Gbɔg n na bagli, n dau tɛɛ ii naabaala bá ra hiŋ la ani anla miŋ ga n dɔgtɛɛzi be di ŋɔ la.”

ref: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
text: Ka ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ ba nuu, ka gil ba digna du kpeg gunla ba naabaala n faa waa Kɔraawiizi la banna hum yardɛɛ la.

ref: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
text: Ba faa vɛɛ u baglaa ani u ni baa nuukpaŋ la u ni ba mɛɛwaa n faa ɛɛwɛ ani karfaa la uŋ karfi baa labuu. Ba faa ra hiŋ vuga n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛɛ, guŋ wia, ba ge gba himmaa faa waa tɔna kaa dɔɔ. Ba faa ra chanzi a hɛssi la n bar baa la hinaa, haali Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ ba be, “Ií gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ gunla banna ɛɛ la.” Ka ba faa vɛɛ, ka ra ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ba gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ la.

ref: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
