text: Babilɔn laallɔɔra la maa koori guure nabɔma n faa ra binni ba ni la, purgi koŋlaa la n bar Jɛrusalɛm la.

ref: He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar.
text: Koori guure nabɔma Nɛbuzaradan jaa lauri nɛra la n kawɛɛ a bolzeŋ biini ni banla maa n chɔwɛɛ zuu Babilɔn koori la, di kaali Babilɔn.

ref: Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
text: Ama, a koori guure nabɔma faa gil banla n ɛɛ nyaara werge la baŋhinaa a hɛri, bá ra binni ba grepu daazi kooni ani ba kooni ni.

ref: The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia.
text: Babilɔn hina faa purgi danyɛ ligee ni torkozi la ani danyɛ Kolzeŋ la banna yir Muuzeŋ, n faa du Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la, di chia kaali Babilɔn.

ref: They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense,
text: Ba faa kaa chi a viini, a sɔɔbulzi, fintina yakɔssi mɔnni kuna, tassazi ani danyɛ kuna la maa, baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum a Dia biini, di kaali.

ref: as well as the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to take everything made of gold or silver.
text: A koori guure nabɔma faa paagi nimbuurikuna ni kuna mizaa tassazi la gba maanii, di kaali. A maanii ba faa kpa saliŋ himmaa gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋa di kuari.

ref: The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed.
text: Ligee anɛɛ la, Kolzeŋ la ani torkozi la maa Koori Solomɔn n faa kpa danyɛ kuari du Kɔraawiizi Dia la, faa kannɔɔ werge, ba wàá wer mɛgzaa.

ref: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
text: A koori guure nabɔma faa lauri Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Sɛraaya ni u harbɔɔhiŋra Zɛfania ani a Dia dominua tauduura bahoro la maa yoma.

ref: Then he arrested one of the army commanders, the king's five personal advisors, and the officer in charge of gathering the troops for battle. He also found
text: Banla n faa haa ka a bolzeŋ biini, u faa lauri ba laallɔɔra nabɔma ni koori zɛɛsogna ge banue. U kaa lauri ba laallɔɔra nabɔma karchi n na binni laallɔɔra hɔna ni ani baala tokkoahoro, n faa du a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to rule the few people still living in Judah.
text: Denii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza, faa lizi Ahikam biibaal Gɛdalia la naabaal n ɛɛ Safan, u ra binni nɛra la uŋ gillɛ Juda hɛri ni.

ref: When the army officers and troops heard that Gedaliah was their ruler, the officers met with him at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah from Maacah.
text: A laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni a laallɔɔra maa, n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Babilɔn koori lizi Gɛdaliarɛ u ɛɛ ba hɛri nabɔma la, ba ba u be Mizpa. Baabuu faa Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl, Karia biibaal Jɔhanan, Nɛtɔfaf hinuu Tanumɛf biibaal Sɛraaya, Maaka hinuu biibaal Jaazania ani ba laallɔɔra.

ref: Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
text: Gɛdalia faa hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ tɛɛ ba ni ba laallɔɔra, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm Babilɔn nabɔnzi la. Ií so a hɛri, di hum ra tɛɛ Babilɔn koorizeŋ, gunnɛ ii wia kuari.”

ref: Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia.
text: A bina hiŋ, baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Nɛtania biibaal Ismɛl, u naabaal n ɛɛ Ɛlisama, n faa ɛɛ kooridiiri ni baala fi, ba di wa kpu Gɛdalia ani Juda ni Babilɔn laallɔɔra la n faa du u be, Mizpa la.

ref: After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (Jeremiah
text: Guŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, a nɛra nɛdumazi, nɛzenaa ani laallɔɔra nabɔnzi maa, faa chɔ kaali Ijip hɛri, dikuu banna ɔm Babilɔn hina wia. Koori Jɛhɔyachin lizaa wia

ref: Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
text: U faa ŋɔ wia ni sisɔna di tɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔyachin, ka tɛu nabɔmuu kaali koora la maa n du u be, Babilɔn la.

ref: Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day.
text: Awia, Koori Jɛhɔyachin faa wir u nɛra tɔi dia laala ta, ka kpa u himmaa laala di laali. U ni a koori ɔɔ jaa kpau di ra di, ú de dui maa biini.

ref: Japheth was the father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
text: Jafɛf ge biibaalaa faa Goma, Magɔg, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Mɛsɛk ani Tiras.

ref: Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan.
text: Abraham hahjiga Kɛtura biibaalaa faa Zimran, Jɔksan, Mɛdan, Midian, Isbak ani Suua. Jɔksan ge biibaalaa faa Siiba ani Dɛdan.

ref: Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior.
text: Kus ge faa lul Nimrɔd la n faa ɛɛ durnya naa maa laallɔɔrikpeg la.

ref: Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
text: Mizram naannaa faa Lidia, Anam, Lehab, Naftu,

ref: Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
text: Goma ge biibaalaa faa Askɛnaz, Rifaf ani Togama.

ref: Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
text: Javan ge biibaalaa faa Ɛlisɛ, Taasis, Saiprɔs ani Roods hina.

ref: Ethiopia was the ancestor of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah was the ancestor of Sheba and Dedan.
text: Kus biibaalaa faa Sɛba, Havila, Sabta, Raama ani Sabtɛka. Raama ge biibaalaa faa Siiba ani Dɛdan.

ref: Canaan's oldest son was Sidon; his other son was Heth.
text: Keenan ge biibambiluglii faa Saidɔn, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Hɛf, baabuu nɛra la ba naanna n di ba sɔna,

ref: Shem was the ancestor of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech; they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
text: Sɛm ge biibaalaa faa Ɛlam, Assur, Aafagzad, Luud ani Aram. Aram ge biibaalaa faa Uz, Hul, Gɛta ani Mɛsɛk.

ref: Arpachshad was Shelah's father and Eber's grandfather.
text: Aafagzad ge biibaallɛ faa Sɛla, Sɛla ge biibaal ɛɛ Ɛba.

ref: Eber named his first son Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided into tribal regions. Eber's second son was Joktan,
text: Biibaala banɛɛrɛ Ɛba ge faa lul. Bɛl sɔnnɛ faa Pɛlɛg, u zɛɛrɛ Bargaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, durnya hina faa bargi dɔŋa ninɛɛ u de dui saŋa, bɛl ge sɔnnɛ faa Jɔktan.

ref: the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
text: Ɔfir, Havila ani Jobab. Bannii maa faa ɛɛ Jɔktan biibaalaa.

ref: Shem's descendants included Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and Abram, later renamed Abraham. Abraham's Family (Genesis
text: ani Abram la baŋ faa bittɛ dau Abraham la. Abraham naanna wia

ref: Abraham was the father of Isaac and Ishmael.
text: Biibaala banɛɛrɛ Abraham faa lul. Baabuu Aizik ani Ismɛl.

ref: Midian was the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. Esau's Family (Genesis
text: Midian ge biibaalaa Efa, Ɛfɛ, Hanɔk, Abida ani Ɛldaa. Kɛtura naannaa faa bannii maa. Ɛsau naanna wia

ref: Abraham's son Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
text: Abraham biibaal Aizik faa dɔɔ biibaala banɛɛrɛ, Ɛsau ani Jekɔb.

ref: Esau was the father of Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
text: Ɛsau ge biibaalaa faa Ɛlifaz, Riwɛl, Jɛyus, Jalam ani Kɔra.

ref: Reuel was the father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. The First Edomites and Their Kings (Genesis
text: Riwɛl ge biibaalaa faa Nahaf, Zɛra, Samma ani Miza.

ref: Before kings ruled in Israel, Bela son of Beor ruled the country of Edom from its capital of Dinhabah.
text: Koora la maa n faa di kora Ɛdɔm hɛri, mɔɔ ka Izrɛl koori maa haa wa di koraa keŋ, Bɛɔ biibaal Bɛla la bolzeŋ sɔnnɛ faa Dinhaba.

ref: Seir was the father of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
text: Sɛɛ ge biibaalaa faa Lɔtan, Sobal, Zibiɔn, Ana, Disɔn, Ɛza ani Disan.

ref: Lotan was the father of Hori and Homam; Lotan's sister was Timna.
text: Lɔtan biibaalaa faa Hɔri ani Hɔmam. U niuhambie ge sɔnnɛ faa Timna.

ref: Shobal was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon was the father of Aiah and Anah.
text: Sobal ge biibaalaa faa Alvan, Manahaf, Ɛbal, Sɛfɔ ani Ɔnam. Zibiɔn ge biibaalaa faa Aaya ni Ana.

ref: Anah was the father of Dishon and the grandfather of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
text: Ana biibaallɛ faa Disɔn. Disɔn ge biibaalaa faa Hɛmdan, Ɛsban, Itran ani Kɛran.

ref: Ezer was the father of Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan was the father of Uz and Aran.
text: Ɛza biibaalaa faa Bilhan, Zaavan ani Akan. Disan ge biibaalaa faa Uz ani Aran. Ɛdɔm koora wia

ref: After Bela's death, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king.
text: Koori Bɛla n wa siuwɛ, Zɛra biibaal Jobab la n faa lii bolzeŋ Bɔzra la, kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: After Jobab's death, Husham from the land of Teman became king.
text: Koori Jobab ge n wa siuwɛ, Tɛman hinuu Husam la kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: After Husham's death, Hadad son of Bedad became king and ruled from Avith. Earlier, Bedad had defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab.
text: Koori Husam ge n wa siuwɛ, Bɛdad biibaal Hadad la n faa kpegli Midian hina, Moab hɛri biini la, kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Ba faa dau u bolzeŋ sɔŋ Avif.

ref: after Samlah's death, Shaul from the town of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king;
text: Koori Samla ge n wa siuwɛ, Sual n lii bol bɛl banna yir Rɛhɔbɔf la n du Muu Yufretis la, kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: and after Shaul's death, Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king.
text: Koori Sual ge n wa siuwɛ, Akbɔ biibaal Baal Hanan kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: After Baal Hanan's death, Hadad ruled from Pai. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
text: Baal Hanan n wa siuwɛ, Hadad kpa u gawa, di di a kora. Ba faa dau u bolzeŋ sɔŋ Pau. U haaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Mɛhɛtabɛl, u ɛɛ Matrɛd biihaaŋ, Matrɛd ge maarɛ faa Mɛ Zahab.

ref: The Edomite clans were Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
text: Koori Hadad ge siu. Ɛdɔm kooraa faa Timna, Alva, Jɛtɛf,

ref: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
text: Ɔhɔlibama, Ɛla, Pinɔn,

ref: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
text: Kɛnaz, Tɛman, Mibzar,

ref: Magdiel, and Iram.
text: Magdiɛl ani Iram.

ref: Judah and his Canaanite wife Bathshua had three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. But the Lord had Er put to death, because he disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
text: Juda ge biibaala maa faa du banue. U haaŋ Keenan hinuu Batsua biibaala faa du bahoro, Ɛr, Ɔnan ani Sɛla. Juda biibambilugli Ɛr faa dɔɔ biinikpolaa werge maa Kɔraawiizi be. Awia, u faa kpuu.

ref: Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar also had two sons: Perez and Zerah.
text: Ka Juda biibaal haaŋ Taama, faa lul Pɛrɛz ani Zɛra tɛu. Awia, Juda biibaala maa faa du banue.

ref: Perez was the father of Hezron and Hamul.
text: Pɛrɛz ge biibaalaa Hɛzrɔn ani Hamul.

ref: Zerah was the father of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda.
text: Zɛra ge biibaalaa Zimri, Ɛtan, Hɛman, Kalkɔl ani Dada. Ba ge maa faa du banue.

ref: Achan, who was a descendant of Zerah and the son of Carmi, caused trouble for Israel, because he kept for himself things that belonged only to the Lord.
text: Kaami biibaallɛ Ekan la n faa gillɛ tɔɔrɔɔ huuzi Izrɛl hina, dikuu uŋ faa kpa kuna n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora la wia.

ref: Ethan's son was Azariah. The Ancestors of King David
text: Ɛtan ge biibaallɛ Azaaria. Koori Deevid dee wia

ref: Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
text: Hɛzrɔn biibaalaa Jɛramiil, Ram ani Kalɛb.

ref: Ram was the father of Amminadab and the grandfather of Nahshon, a tribal leader of Judah.
text: Aminadab mɛɛrɛ Ram, Aminadab ge biibaallɛ Nasɔn la n faa ɛɛ Juda hina nabɔma la.

ref: Nahshon's descendants included Salma, Boaz,
text: Salmɔn mɛɛrɛ Nasɔn, Bɔaz ge mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Salmɔn,

ref: Jesse also had two daughters: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah was the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
text: Ba niuhambizii Zɛruya ani Abigeel. Zɛrua biibaala bahoroo faa Abisai, Joab ani Asahɛl.

ref: Abigail's husband was Jether, who was a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa. The Descendants of Hezron
text: Abigeel ge biibaallɛ faa Amasa la mɛɛ n faa ɛɛ Jɛta, n lii Ismɛl dee biini la. Hɛzrɔn naanna wia

ref: Hezron's son Caleb married Azubah, and their daughter was Jerioth, the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
text: Hɛzrɔn biibaal Kalɛb faa kpa Azuba, di lul biihaaŋ, u sɔŋ faa di Jɛriɔf. Jɛriɔf ge faa lul biibaala bahoro, Jɛsa, Sobab ani Aadɔn.

ref: After the death of Azubah, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son Hur
text: Azuba n wa siuwɛ, Kalɛb kpa Ɛfraf di lul biibaal, u sɔŋ di Hur.

ref: was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
text: Hur ge biibaallɛ faa Uri, Uri ge biibaal faa ɛɛ Bɛzalɛl.

ref: After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa. The Descendants of Jerahmeel
text: Hɛzrɔn n wa siuwɛ, Kalɛb kpa u mɛɛ luhaaŋ Ɛfraf, di lul biibaal, u sɔŋ di Asur la n faa tii Tɛkua zɛɛ la. Jɛramiil naanna wia

ref: Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
text: Hɛzrɔn biibambiluglii faa Jɛramiil, u ge biibaalaa keŋ. U biibambiluglii faa Ram, di kpa Buna, Ɔrɛn, Ɔzɛm ani Ahija.

ref: Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam.
text: Jɛramiil faa kaa dɔɔ haaŋ bɛllɛ, u sɔŋ di Atara. U ge lul biibaal, u sɔŋ di Ɔnam.

ref: Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
text: Jɛramiil biibambilugli Ram la biibaalaa, Maaz, Jamin ani Ɛka.

ref: Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada. Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur.
text: Ɔnam ge biibaalaa Samai ani Jada. Samai ge biibaalaa Nadab ani Abisur.

ref: Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid.
text: Abisur haaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Abiheel, u ge lul Aban ani Mɔlid.

ref: Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children;
text: Nadab ge biibaalaa Sɛlɛd ani Apam. Sɛlɛd faa waa biizi lullɛ ka siu.

ref: Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
text: Apam biibaallɛ Isi, u ge biibaallɛ Sɛsan. Sɛsan ge biibaallɛ Alai.

ref: Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children,
text: Samai niwee Jada biibaalaa Jɛta ani Jonatan. Jɛta faa waa biizi lullɛ, ka siu.

ref: but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
text: Jonatan biibaalaa Pɛlɛf ani Zaza. Jɛramiil naannaa faa bannii maa.

ref: Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai,
text: Sɛsan faa kpa u biihaaŋ tɛu. U lul biibaal, ba ra yiruu Atai.

ref: the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad.
text: Atai biibaallɛ Netan, Netan ge biibaallɛ Zabad,

ref: Zabad's descendants included Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Eleasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, and Elishama. The Descendants of Caleb
text: Salum ge biibaallɛ Jɛkamia, Jɛkamia ge biibaal jaa ɛɛ Ɛlisama. Kalɛb naanna wia

ref: Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, had the following descendants: Mesha, Ziph, Mareshah, Hebron,
text: Jɛramiil niwee Kalɛb biibambiluglii Mɛsa, u ge biibaallɛ Zif, Zif ge biibaallɛ Marɛsa, u ge biibaallɛ Hɛbrɔn.

ref: and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
text: Hɛbrɔn biibaalaa Kɔra, Tapua, Rɛkɛm ani Sɛma.

ref: Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai,
text: Sɛma biibaallɛ Raham, Raham ge biibaallɛ Jɔkiam. Rɛkɛm ge biibaallɛ Samai.

ref: the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
text: Samai biibaallɛ Mayɔn. Mayɔn ge biibaallɛ Bɛf Zur.

ref: Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez.
text: Kalɛb hahjiga Efa biibaalaa Haran, Mɔza ani Gazɛz. Haran ge biibaallɛ Gazɛz.

ref: Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
text: Jadai ge biibaalaa Rɛgɛm, Jɔtam, Gɛsan, Pɛlɛt, Efa ani Saaf.

ref: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
text: Kalɛb hahjiga Maaka biibaalaa Siibɛ ani Tirhana.

ref: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
text: U faa kaa lul Madmana mɛɛ Saaf ani Makbɛna ni Gibia mɛɛ Siva. Kalɛb ge biihaannɛ Aksa.

ref: All of these were Caleb's descendants. Hur, the oldest son of Caleb and Ephrath, had three sons: Shobal, Salma, and Hareph, who settled the town of Beth-Gader.
text: U biibambinɛɛhiŋ Salma ge tii Bɛtlihɛm zɛɛ, u biibambihorohiŋ Harɛf ge tii Bɛf Gada zɛɛ.

ref: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
text: Sobal la n tii Kiriaf Jiarim zɛɛ naannaa, Harɔɛ hina ani Manahaf hina yeŋ

ref: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
text: ni Kiriaf Jiarim domeezi, Iti, Put, Suma ani Misra hina. Bannii biinii Zɔra ani Ɛstayɔl hina lii.

ref: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
text: Salma la n tii Bɛtlihɛm zɛɛ naannaa, Nɛtɔfaf, Atrɔf Bɛf Joab, Manahaf hina yeŋ ani Zɔri hina.

ref: Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
text: Domeezi la n faa ɛɛ karchizi nɛnnɛɛ faa ra zuu bol bɛl banna yir Jabɛz. Baabuu Tiraf, Simiaf ani Sukaf hina. Ba faa ɛɛ Kɛn hina di lii Hammaf, Rɛkab mɛɛ dia.

ref: David's other sons included Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
text: Ɛlisama, Ɛliada ani Ɛlifɛlɛt. Bannii ge maa faa du baala kabɛl.

ref: David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter. The Descendants of King Solomon
text: Koori Deevid biibaalaa bannii maa, di u hahjigzi biibaala waa jaawɛ. Ba niuhambiere Taama. Koori Solomɔn naanna wia

ref: Jehoiakim was the father of Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.
text: Jɛhɔyakim ge faa lul biibaala banɛɛ, Jɛhɔyachin ani Zɛdɛkia. Koori Jɛhɔyachin naanna wia

ref: Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel,
text: Koori Jɛhɔyachin la baŋ faa lɔ laal di lawuu kaali Babilɔn hɛri la naanna faa du baniidaanɛɛ. Baabuu Sɛɛltiɛl,

ref: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
text: Malkiram, Pɛdaaya, Sɛnaza, Jɛkamia, Hɔsama ani Nɛdabia.

ref: Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
text: Pɛdaaya biibaalaa Zɛrubabɛl ani Simei. Zɛrubabɛl ge biibaalaa Mɛsulam ani Hanania, ba niuhambiere Sɛlɔmif.

ref: He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.
text: Zɛrubabɛl biibaala baŋhinaa Hasuba, Ɔhɛl, Bɛrɛkia, Hasadia ani Jusab Hɛsɛd. Ba ge du banue.

ref: the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
text: Sɛkania naanna genii keŋ, Sɛmaaya ni u biibaala, Hatus, Igal, Baria, Niaria ani Safat. Ba ge maa faa du banumbɛl.

ref: Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
text: Niaria ge biibaalaa Ɛliɔnai, Hɛzɛkia ani Azrikam. Ba ge nɛra bahoro.

ref: Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
text: Ɛliɔnai ge biibaalaa Hɔdavia, Ɛliasib, Pɛlaaya, Akub, Jɔhanan, Dɛlaaya ani Anani. Ba ge maa faa du baala baniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Judah was the father of five sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
text: Juda naannaa keŋ, Pɛrɛz, Hɛzrɔn, Kaami, Hur ani Sobal.

ref: Shobal was the father of Reaiah, the grandfather of Jahath, and the great-grandfather of Ahumai and Lahad. These men all belonged to the Zorathite clan.
text: Sobal biibaal Rɛyaaya biibaallɛ Jahaf, Jahaf ge biibaalaa, Ahumai ani Lahad. Zɔra hina naabaalaa faa la.

ref: Ashhur, who settled the town of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
text: Asur la n tii Tɛkua zɛɛ la faa dɔɔ haana banɛɛrɛ, Hɛla ani Naara.

ref: daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
text: U ni Naara lul Ahuzam, Hɛfa, Tɛmɛni ani Haahastari. Naara naannaa faa bannii.

ref: Ashhur and Helah were the parents of Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
text: Hɛla ge biibaalaa, Zɛrɛf, Zɔha, Ɛtnan

ref: Koz, the father of Anub and Zobebah, was also the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.
text: ani Kɔz n ɛɛ Anub ni Hazobɛba mɛɛ ani Harum biibaal Ahahɛl domeezi.

ref: Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family.
text: Jabɛz maa faa dawuubuu sɔŋ naa, dikuu u lullaa n faa nuu werge wia. Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge ba dia biini.

ref: One day he prayed to Israel's God, “Please bless me and give me a lot of land. Be with me so I will be safe from harm.” And God did just what Jabez had asked.
text: Jabɛz faa lɔ wilee tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, kissiŋ, di gil n hɛri yaa. Gil i nonii tɔ n ni, di gil wifittii gilɛɛ waa huuziŋ, di liziŋ lii tɔɔrɔɔ maa biini.” Denii Kɔraawiizi nuu u suŋŋaa.

ref: Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton,
text: Suha kpɛɛma Kɛlub biibaallɛ Mɛhir la ge biibaal n ɛɛ Ɛstɔn la.

ref: whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
text: Ɛstɔn biibaalaa, Bɛf Rafa, Pasia ani Tɛhina la biibaal n tii bolzeŋ Ir Nahas zɛɛ la. Rɛka hinaa faa bannii maa.

ref: Kenaz was the father of Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had two sons: Hathath and Meonothai,
text: Kɛnaz biibaalaa Ɔtniɛl ani Sɛraaya. Ɔtniɛl ge biibaala, Hataf ani Mɛɔnɔtai.

ref: who was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who settled a place called “Valley of Crafts” because the people who lived there were experts in making things.
text: Miɔnɔtai ge biibaallɛ Ɔfra. Sɛraaya ge biibaallɛ Joab la n tii Gɛ Harasim n faa du waluu biini la.

ref: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah was the father of Kenaz.
text: Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb biibaalaa, Iru, Ɛla ani Naam. Ɛla ge biibaallɛ faa Kɛnaz.

ref: A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
text: Baal bɛl banna yir Hɔdia faa kpa Naham niuhambie la. Ba naannaa Gam domee n faa du Keila ani Maakaf domee n faa du Ɛstɛmɔa.

ref: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
text: Simɔn biibaalaa, Amnɔn, Rina, Bɛn Hanan ani Tilɔn. Isi ge naannaa, Zɔhɛf ani Bɛn Zɔhɛf. Sɛla naanna wia

ref: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
text: Ba faa ɛɛ viimaaraa di du Nɛtam ni Gɛdɛra hɛssi. Ba faa sogo denii di hum huma di ra tɛɛ a koori. Simɛɔn naanna wia

ref: Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
text: Simɛɔn naannaa keŋ, Nɛmuɛl, Jamin, Jarib, Zɛra ani Sual.

ref: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
text: Sual biibaallɛ Salum, Salum biibaallɛ Mibsam, Mibsam ge biibaallɛ Misma.

ref: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
text: Misma ge naannaa keŋ, Hamuɛl Zakur ani Simei.

ref: Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim.
text: Bɛf Makabɔf, Hazar Susim, Bɛf Biri ani Saaram. Anniibuu faa ɛɛ ba bola guŋŋ di wa hel Koori Deevid kora dii saŋa.

ref: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
text: Bola la n faa soge ba kɛraa genii Etam, Ain, Rimɔn, Tɔkɛn ani Asan. A faa du bola anue

ref: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
text: ani boljigzi la maa n baraa la guŋŋ di ga chug Baalaf. Ba bolaa faa annii maa. Ba faa sɛbi ba naana wiarɛ dau.

ref: As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza.
text: Baala naa sɔna baŋ yirgɛɛ naabuu faa ɛɛ ba domeezi nabɔnzi. Ba diini hina faa wazɔɔrɛ werge maa.

ref: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
text: Awia, ba faa lii di ga so Gɛdɔ kɛraa, a waluu wiifurii paga, bá sela ɔɔ wer na kooree di ra di.

ref: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
text: Ba faa na kooriinanaarɛ de, a de hɛri ge kaa du war. Koozaa maa faa waa hoo de, bampirsɔna ge du de. Ham hina baŋhina faa feloore so de mɔɔ.

ref: They killed the last of the Amalekites and lived there from then on.
text: di kpu Amalɛk hina la n kawɛɛ, ka jaa so de haali ni zinaa.

ref: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph,
text: Jekɔb biibambilugli Rubin naannaa keŋ, Rubinnɛ faa ɛɛ Jekɔb biibambilugli, ka u lau u mɛɛ haaŋ bɛl nyiŋŋi. Awia, ba faa lɛɛ u nabɔmuu tɛɛ u niwee Joosɛf ni u biibaala. Guŋ wia, ba waa u sɔŋ sɛbɛɛ jaa gunla baŋ lul baa di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni la.

ref: Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
text: Jekɔb biibambilugli Rubin biibaalaa keŋ, Hanɔk, Palu, Hɛzrɔn ani Kaami.

ref: The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
text: Baal ge biibaal ɛɛ Bɛɛra la Asiiria hina Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa n faa lauwɛ kaali hɛrduma la. Bɛɛraa faa Rubin naanna sitɔɔri.

ref: The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon,
text: Azaz biibaallɛ Bɛla, Bɛla ge biibaallɛ Sɛma, Sɛma ge biibaallɛ Jowɛl. Ba faa sogo Aroa hɛrii guŋŋ di ga lii Nɛbɔ ani Baal Miɔn hɛssi.

ref: and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
text: Ba faa sogo wiifurii pagaa guŋŋ di ga chug hɛribɔduma la n faa chɔɔwɛ, guŋŋ di ga lii Muu Yufretis, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba sela faa wazɔɔrɛ werge, Giliad hɛri biini.

ref: When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead. The Descendants of Gad
text: Koori Sɔɔl kora dii saŋaa Rubin dee faa lɔ Hagri nɛra laal, di kpegli baa. Awia, ba faa lɛɛ a Hagri nɛra hɛri, n du Giliad hɛri wiifurii, di so. Gad naanna wia

ref: The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah.
text: Gad dee faa sogo Rubin dee wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ, Basan hɛri biini, guŋŋ di ga lii Salɛka, n du wiifurii.

ref: Some of the clan leaders were Joel, Shapham, Janai, and Shaphat.
text: A domeezi nabɔnzi baŋhinaa keŋ, Jowɛl, Safam, Janai ani Safat, ba du Basan.

ref: Their relatives included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.
text: Ba domeezi aniidaanɛɛ nabɔnzii keŋ, Maikil, Mɛsulam, Siiba, Jɔrai, Jakan, Zia ani Ɛba.

ref: They were all descendants of Abihail, whose family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.
text: Huri biibaal Abiheel biibaalaa keŋ, Jaroa biibaallɛ Giliad, Giliad ge biibaallɛ Maikil, Maikil ge biibaallɛ Jɛsisai, Jɛsisai ge biibaallɛ Jadɔ, Jadɔ ge biibaallɛ Buz.

ref: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
text: Baŋhina genii Abdiɛl biibaal Ahi, Ahi ge biibaallɛ Guni la n faa ɛɛ ba domee nabɔma la.

ref: The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon.
text: Gad nɛra la faa sogo Giliad ani Basan hɛssi ni boljigzi la n baraa chem labuu, haali Sarɔn sela diiribɔra maa.

ref: Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
text: Annii maanii ba faa sɛbi dau, di hiŋzi gunla baŋ lul baa, Juda Koori Jɔtam ani Izrɛl Koori Jeroboam kossi dii saŋa.

ref: They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
text: Ba faa lɔ Hagri dizi, Jɛtur, Nafis ani Nɔdab nɛra laal.

ref: Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies.
text: Ba faa yardi Kɔraawiizii, di suŋŋuu ú hiini baa a laal biini. U kpa Hagri dizi ani banla maa ni baa n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, di du ba nonee biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa lɔ wilee tɛu.

ref: Many of the Hagrites died in battle, because God was fighting this battle against them. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh lived in that territory until they were taken as prisoners to Assyria. The Tribe of East Manasseh
text: Ba faa kpu bakpila ge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, a laal faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte. Ba faa jaa so ba hɛri hiŋ guŋŋ di ga hel saŋa la baŋ wa lauri ba ge, di kaali hɛrduma la. Manasɛ dee yeŋ wia

ref: East Manasseh was a large tribe, so its people settled in the northern region of Bashan, as far north as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
text: Manasɛ dee yeŋ faa kpillɔɔ werge maa. Ba faa sogo Basan hɛri biinii guŋŋ di ga lii Baal Hɛmɔn ani Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn.

ref: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers. The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
text: Ba domeezi nabɔnzii faa keŋ, Ɛfɛ, Isi, Ɛliɛl, Azriɛl, Jɛrɛmia, Hɔdavia ani Jadiɛl. Ba faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra la n dɔɔ bampireere, di dɔɔ sɔŋ, ba domeezi biine.

ref: The people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh were unfaithful to the God their ancestors had worshiped, and they started worshiping the gods of the nations that God had forced out of Canaan.
text: Ama, ba faa waa wibii dɔɔwɛ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n faa ra hum la be, ka faa ra kuari hɛssi hina la Kɔraawiizi n duŋŋɛɛ, di ba ra ba la vuga.

ref: So God sent King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria to attack these Israelite tribes. The king led them away as prisoners to Assyria, and from then on, he forced them to live in Halah, Habor, Hara, and near the Gozan River.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, faa gil Asiiria hina Koorizeŋ Tiglaf Pilɛsa, wa kpegli Rubin ni Gad dizi ani Manasɛ dee yeŋ, di lauri baa, di kpogli baa kaali Hala, Habɔ, Hara ani Gɔzan muu hɛssi. Ba haa du a bɔra, haali ni zinaa.

ref: Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: Kɔhaf ge biibaalaa, Amram, Izhar, Hɛbrɔn ani Uziɛl.

ref: Amram was the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
text: Amram ge biibaala du banɛɛ, Aarɔn ni Moosis ani biihambikpaŋ, Miriam. Aarɔn ge biibaalaa, Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza ani Itama.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia took Jehozadak to Babylon as prisoner when the Lord let the people of Judah and Jerusalem be dragged from their land.
text: Jɛhɔzadak naabuu ba faa lau kaali, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n faa gillɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza lauri Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina, di kaali hɛrduma la. Levi naanna baŋhina wia

ref: Levi's three sons had sons of their own.
text: Levi biibaalaa, Gɛsɔn, Kɔhaf ani Mɛrari.

ref: Gershon was the father of Libni and Shimei.
text: Gɛsɔn biibaala sɔnaa keŋ, Libni ani Simei.

ref: Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: Kɔhaf ge biibaalaa, Amram, Izhar, Hɛbrɔn ani Uziɛl.

ref: Merari was the father of Mahli and Mushi. These descendants of Levi each became leaders of their own clans.
text: Mɛrari ge biibaalaa, Mali ani Musi. Levi dizi baŋ sɛbɛɛ di hiŋzi dɔŋa mɛɛwaarɛ keŋ,

ref: Kohath's descendants included Amminadab, Korah, Assir, Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir, Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
text: Asir ge biibaallɛ Tahaf, Tahaf ge biibaallɛ Uriɛl, Uriɛl ge biibaallɛ Uzzia, Uzzia ge biibaallɛ Sual.

ref: Elkanah was the father of Amasai and Ahimoth.
text: Ɛlkana naannaa keŋ, Ɛlkana biibaalaa Amasai ani Ahimɔf,

ref: Ahimoth's descendants included Elkanah, Zophai, Nahath, Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah.
text: Nahaf ge biibaallɛ Ɛliab, Ɛliab ge biibaallɛ Jeroham, Jerɔham ge biibaallɛ Ɛlkana, Ɛlkana ge biibaallɛ Samuɛl.

ref: Samuel was the father of Joel and Abijah, born in that order.
text: Samuɛl biibaala faa du banɛɛ, u biibambiluglii Jowɛl, di kpa Abija hiŋ.

ref: Merari's descendants included Mahli, Libni, Shimei, Uzzah, Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah. The Temple Musicians
text: Uza ge biibaallɛ Simia, Simia ge biibaallɛ Hagia, Hagia ge biibaallɛ Asaaya. Kɔraawiizi Dia yiryitta wia

ref: After King David had the sacred chest moved to Jerusalem, he appointed musicians from the Levi tribe to be in charge of the music at the place of worship.
text: A baala naabuu Koori Deevid faa lizi, ba faa ra binni yira yiraa ni, Kɔraawiizi Dia, Jɛrusalɛm biini, saŋa la baŋ faa kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la, di wa chiŋŋi de la.

ref: The rest of the Levites were appointed to work at the sacred tent. The Descendants of Aaron
text: Levi naanna la n kawɛɛ labuu ba faa lizi, bá ra hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini. Aarɔn naanna wia

ref: Only Aaron and his descendants were allowed to offer sacrifices and incense on the two altars at the sacred tent. They were in charge of the most holy place and the ceremonies to forgive sins, just as God's servant Moses had commanded.
text: Ama, Aarɔn ni u naannaa ɔɔ faa ra lizi mbusuzi, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔra la ni, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ, a Tanti Dia Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la biini, di ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ. Guŋ ɔɔ gil Kɔraawiizi gil Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa di ra tɛɛ baa, gunla u balii Moosis n faa baglɛɛ la.

ref: Aaron's descendants included his son Eleazar, Phinehas, Abishua, Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, and Ahimaaz. The Towns for the Levites (Joshua
text: Ahitub ge biibaallɛ Zadɔk, Zadɔk ge biibaallɛ Ahimaz. Levi dee sognibɔr wia

ref: Aaron's descendants belonged to the Levite clan of Kohath, and they were the first group chosen to receive towns to live in.
text: Bɔra naabuu ba faa bɔnni tɛɛ Aarɔn naanna la n lii Kɔhaf domee biini, ba so, de ɛɛ ba hɛri. Baabuu ba faa feli bɔnni tɛɛ.

ref: They received the town of Hebron in the territory of Judah and the pastureland around it.
text: Ba faa tɛɛ baabuu bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn n du Juda hɛri ani u kɛraa sela diiribɔra maa.

ref: But the farmland and villages around Hebron were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
text: Ama, ba faa kpa a bolzeŋ kɛraa boljigzi ni a koonii tɛɛ Jɛfunɛ biibaal Kalɛb.

ref: So Aaron's descendants received the following Safe Towns and the pastureland around them: Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Hilen, Debir, Ashan, and Beth-Shemesh.
text: Asan, Jutta, Bɛf Sɛmɛs ani a sela diiribɔra la maanii tɛɛ Aarɔn naanna.

ref: From the Benjamin tribe they were given the towns of Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth and the pastureland around them. Thirteen towns were given to Aaron's descendants.
text: Di kaa lizi bolzenaa Gibiɔn, Gɛba, Alɛmɛf, Anatɔf ani a sela diiribɔra ge maa, di lii Bɛnjamin dee bɔr biini tɛɛ baa. Bola la maa baŋ faa bɔnnɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔhaf domeezi, faa du fidaahoro.

ref: The rest of the Levite clan of Kohath received ten towns from West Manasseh.
text: Ba faa tɛɛ Kɔhaf naanna la n kawɛɛ labuu bola fi, di lii Manasɛ dee yeŋ domeezi bɔr biini.

ref: The Levite clan of Gershon received thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh in Bashan.
text: Gɛsɔn naanna domeezi maanii, ba faa tɛɛ bola fidaahoro, di lii Isaka, Asɛ ani Naftali dizi bɔra biine, di kaa tɛɛ baa lii Manasɛ dee yeŋ ge bɔr la n du Basan biini.

ref: The Levite clan of Merari received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
text: Di faa lii Mɛrari naanna ge bɔr biini, domeezi maanii ba faa tɛɛ bola fidaanɛɛ lii Rubin, Gad ani Zɛbulɔn dizi bɔra biine.

ref: So the people of Israel gave the Levites towns to live in and the pastureland around them.
text: A bola naa ni a sela diiribɔraa, Izrɛl hina la faa kpa tɛɛ Levi dee la.

ref: All the towns were chosen with the Lord's help, including those towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
text: Di lii Juda, Simɛɔn ani Bɛnjamin dizi bola la, baŋ felee yirgi labuu, ba faa kpa bɔnni baa.

ref: Some of the families of the Kohath clan received their towns from the tribe of Ephraim.
text: Ba faa tɛɛ Kɔhaf domeezi yenne bola ni hɛssi di lii Ɛfram dee bɔr biini.

ref: The Gershonite clan received two towns from the tribe of East Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, including the pastureland around them.
text: Gɛsɔn domeezi la ge kaa na bola naa lii Manasɛ dee yeŋ la be, Golan n du Basan hɛri ni Astarɔf ani a sela diiribɔra.

ref: Finally, the Gershonites received three towns from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, including the pastureland around them.
text: Di kaa lii Naftali ge dee bɔr biini, ba bolaa faa Kɛdɛs n du Galilii, Hamɔn, Kiriatam ani a sela diiribɔra maa.

ref: The rest of the Merari clan received the towns of Rimmono and Tabor and their pastureland from the tribe of Zebulun.
text: Levi dee la n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ Mɛrari domee hina la genii ba tɛɛ bola naa, di lii Zɛbulɔn dee hɛri, Jɔkniam, Kaata, Rimɔn ani Tabɔ ni a sela diiribɔra.

ref: Issachar was the father of four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
text: Isaka biibaalaa keŋ, Tola, Pua, Jasub ani Simrɔn. Ba faa du biibaala banaazu.

ref: Tola was the father of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, who were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their clan. There were
text: Tola ge biibaalaa, Uzi, Rɛfaaya, Jɛriɛl, Jamai, Ibsam ani Samuɛl. Ba maa faa ɛɛ ba lulla biini nabɔnzii. Koori Deevid kora dii saŋa la, baala la n faa lii Tola dee biini, ba domeezi laallɔɔra baŋ sɛbɛɛ di hiŋzi dɔŋa, faa du baala kagboŋa tokko ni banɛɛ ni kalfaanumbɛl.

ref: Ephraim mourned for his sons a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
text: Ba mɛɛ Ɛfram faa wii baa hɔpizikpila. Awia, u lulla faa ba di wa tig u bampirii.

ref: Uzzi was the father of Izrahiah and the grandfather of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, who were also family leaders.
text: Uzi ge biibaallɛ, Izrahia. Izrahia biibaalaa, Maikil, Obadia, Jowɛl ani Issia. Ba nɛra banue naa maanii faa ɛɛ koora.

ref: Zophah was the father of Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
text: Zɔfa biibaalaa, Sua, Hanɛfa, Sual, Bɛri, Imra,

ref: Benjamin was the father of three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
text: Bɛnjamin biibaala faa du bahoro, Bɛla, Bɛka ani Jɛdiɛl.

ref: Bela was the father of Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their father's clan. The number of soldiers in their clan was
text: Bɛla biibaalaa, Ɛzbɔn, Uzi, Uziɛl, Jɛrimɔf ani Iri. Ba faa du nɛra banue, di ɛɛ ba domeezi ge nabɔnzi. Di lii ba dee la biini, baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ di hiŋzi ba lulaa ŋmɛnizi, ba laallɔɔra faa du baala kagboŋa tokko ni anɛɛ ani tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni banaazu.

ref: Becher was the father of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
text: Bɛka ge biibaalaa, Zɛmira, Joas, Ɛliɛza, Ɛliɔnai, Ɔmri, Jɛrɛmɔf, Abija, Anatɔf ani Alɛmɛf. Bɛka biibaalaa faa bannii maa.

ref: Ephraim was the father of Shuthelah and the ancestor of Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath,
text: Ɛfram naannaa keŋ, Ɛfram biibaallɛ Sutɛla, Sutɛla ge biibaallɛ Bɛrɛd, Bɛrɛd ge biibaallɛ Tahaf, Tahaf ge biibaallɛ Ɛliada, Ɛliada ge biibaallɛ Tahaf,

ref: Jediael was the father of Bilhan and the grandfather of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
text: Jɛdiɛl ge biibaallɛ Bilhan. Bilhan ge biibaalaa, Jɛyus, Bɛnjamin, Ɛhud, Kɛnaana, Zɛtan, Taasis ani Ahisaha.

ref: They were family leaders in their clan, which had
text: Jɛdiɛl biibaala naa maanii faa ɛɛ ba domeezi nabɔnzi. Ba laallɔɔra faa du baala kagboŋa fidaaniidaanɛɛ ani kalfaanɛɛ.

ref: Ulam was the father of Bedan. These were all descendants of Gilead, the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh.
text: Ulam biibaallɛ Bɛdan. Giliad biibaalaa keŋ, Makir biibaallɛ Giliad, Manasɛ biibaallɛ Makir.

ref: Ir was the father of Shuppim and Huppim, who also belonged to this clan. Dan was the father of Hushim. The Descendants of Naphtali
text: Ir naannaa Supi ni Hupi domeezi. Ahɛ naanna ge ɛɛ Husim domeezi. Naftali naanna wia

ref: Naphtali's mother was Bilhah, and he was the father of Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. The Descendants of Manasseh
text: Naftali biibaalaa keŋ, Jaziɛl, Guni, Jɛza ani Silɛm. Ba faa ɛɛ Bilha naannaa. Manasɛ naanna wia

ref: Manasseh and his Syrian wife were the parents of Asriel and Machir the father of Gilead.
text: Manasɛ naannaa keŋ, Asriɛl faa ɛɛ u naannaa, di lii u hahjiga la n ɛɛ Siiria hinuu la be. Waabuu faa kaa lul Giliad mɛɛ Makir.

ref: Machir found a wife for Huppim and one for Shuppim. Machir had a sister named Maacah. Zelophehad was also a descendant of Manasseh, and he had five daughters.
text: Makir faa nyiŋŋi haana tɛɛ Hupim ani Supim. Makir niuhambie sɔnnɛ faa Maaka. U naana bɛl ge sɔnnɛ faa Zɛlɔfɛhad. Biibaala bɛnnɛ waabuu faa lul.

ref: Machir and his wife Maacah were the parents of Peresh and Sheresh. Peresh was the father of Ulam and Rekem.
text: Makir haaŋ Maaka faa lul biibaala banɛɛ, di dau bɛl sɔŋ Pɛrɛs, bɛl ge Sɛrɛs. Sɛrɛs ge biibaalaa Ulam ani Rakɛm.

ref: Gilead's sister Hammolecheth was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
text: Giliad niuhambie Hamɔlɛkɛf ge faa lul Ishɔd, Abiɛza ani Mala.

ref: Shemida, another descendant of Manasseh, was the father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam. The Descendants of Ephraim
text: Sɛmida biibaalaa, Ahian, Sɛkɛm, Likhi ani Aniam. Ɛfram naanna wia

ref: Zabad, and Shuthelah. Ephraim had two other sons, Ezer and Elead. But they were killed when they tried to steal livestock from the people who lived in the territory of Gath.
text: Tahaf biibaallɛ Zabad, u ge biibaallɛ Sutɛla. Ɛfram faa kaa dɔɔ biibaala banɛɛ, Ɛza ani Ɛliad. Gaf hina faa kpu baa, saŋa la baŋ faa tuuwe la bá ga foozi ba sela la.

ref: Some time later his wife gave birth to another son, and Ephraim named him Beriah, because he was born during a time of misery.
text: Denii u ni u haaŋ faa kaa chɔɔ, u kpogli hia di lul biibaal, u dau u sɔŋ Bɛria, dikuu nyuchɔgii n faa du u dia wia.

ref: Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah. She built the towns of Lower Beth-Horon, Upper Beth-Horon, and Uzzen-Sheerah.
text: Ɛfram biihaaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Siira n faa ma bola banna yir Chiŋ Bɛf Hɔrɔn ni Zɛɛ Bɛf Hɔrɔn, di kpa Uzɛn Siira jaa.

ref: Ephraim also had a son named Rephah, and his descendants included Resheph, Telah, Tahan,
text: Ɛfram faa dɔɔ biibaal bɛllɛ ba ra yiruu Rɛfa, Rɛfa ge biibaallɛ Rɛsɛf, Rɛsɛf ge biibaallɛ Tɛla, Tɛla ge biibaallɛ Tahan, Tahan ge biibaallɛ Ladan.

ref: Nun, and Joshua.
text: Nun ge biibaallɛ Josua.

ref: The descendants of Ephraim took over the territory as far south as Bethel, as far east as Naaran, and as far west as Gezer. Their territory included all the villages around these towns, as well as Shechem, Ayyah, and the nearby villages.
text: Ba hɛssi ni ba bolaa faa Bɛtɛl ani u boljigzi la n baruu. Aŋhinaa faa Naaran n du wiifurii, Gɛza ni u kɛraa boljigzi ge n du wiicholii ani bolzeŋ Sɛkɛm ni u kɛraa boljigzi guŋŋ di ga lii Aiya ni u boljigzi maa.

ref: The descendants of Manasseh settled in the territory that included Beth-Shan, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor, and the nearby villages. The descendants of Joseph lived in these towns and villages. The Descendants of Asher
text: Bola la n faa du Manasɛ hɛri magbɔɔnii, Bɛf San, Taanak, bolzeŋ Mɛgidɔ, Dɔɔ ani a boljigzi maa. Jekɔb biibaal Joosɛf la naannaa faa ra zuu a bola naa maa. Asɛ naanna wia

ref: Asher had four sons, Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and one daughter, Serah.
text: Asɛ ge biibaalaa keŋ, Imna, Isva, Isvi ani Bɛria. Ba niuhambiere Sɛra.

ref: Beriah was the father of Heber and Malchiel the father of Birzaith.
text: Bɛria ge biibaalaa, Hɛba ni Malkiɛl la n faa ɛɛ Birzaf mɛɛ la.

ref: Heber was the father of three sons, Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and one daughter, Shua.
text: Hɛba biibaalaa, Jaflɛt, Soma, Hɔtam ani ba niuhambie Sua.

ref: Japhlet was the father of Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
text: Jaflɛt biibaalaa keŋ, Pasak, Bimhal ani Asvaf.

ref: Shomer was the father of Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
text: Soma ge biibaalaa, Ahi, Roga, Huba ani Aram.

ref: And Japhlet's brother Hotham was the father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
text: U niwee Hɛlɛm ge biibaalaa, Zɔfa, Imna, Sɛlɛs ani Amal.

ref: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
text: Bɛza, Hɔd, Samma, Silsa, Itran ani Bɛɛra.

ref: Jether was the father of Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
text: Jɛta ge biibaalaa, Jɛfunɛ, Pispa ani Ara.

ref: Ulla was the father of Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
text: Ula ge biibaalaa, Ara, Haniɛl ani Rizia.

ref: Benjamin had five sons, who were born in the following order: Bela, Ashbel, Aharah,
text: Bɛnjamin biibambiluglii Bɛla, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Asbɛl, horohiŋ ɛɛ Ahara,

ref: Nohah, and Rapha.
text: naazuhiŋ ɛɛ Nɔha, nuehiŋ ɛɛ Rafa.

ref: Bela was the father of Addar, Gera, Abihud,
text: Bɛla biibaalaa, Adar, Gɛra, Abihud,

ref: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
text: Abisua, Naaman, Ahoa,

ref: Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
text: Gɛra, Sɛfufan ani Huram.

ref: Elpaal was the father of Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who settled the towns of Ono and Lod, as well as the nearby villages.
text: Ɛlpaal biibaalaa, Ɛba, Misam ani Sɛmɛd la n faa ma bolzenaa Ono, Lɔɔd ni a kɛraa boljigzi

ref: Beriah and Shema were family leaders in the clan that lived in the town of Aijalon and that forced out the people of Gath.
text: ani Bɛria ni Sɛma n faa ɛɛ ba diini nabɔnzi, di ga so bolzeŋ Aijalɔn, ka faa duŋŋi bolzeŋ Gaf hina la.

ref: Beriah's descendants included Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha.
text: Maikil, Ispa ani Jɔha. Bannii maanii faa ɛɛ Bɛria biibaala.

ref: Elpaal's descendants included Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab.
text: Ismɛrai, Izlia ani Jobab. Bannii ge maanii faa ɛɛ Ɛlpaal naanna.

ref: Shashak's descendants included Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel.
text: Ifdɛya ani Pɛniɛl ge faa ɛɛ Sasak naanna.

ref: Jeroham's descendants included Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri.
text: Jaarɛsia, Ɛlija ani Zikri ge faa ɛɛ Jeroham naanna.

ref: These were the family leaders in their ancestor's clan, and they and their descendants lived in Jerusalem.
text: Bannii maanii faa ɛɛ ba diini nabɔnzi ni koora baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ, di hiŋzi ba lulaa ŋmɛnizi, ba faa du Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: Jeiel settled the town of Gibeon. He and his wife Maacah lived there
text: Gibiɔn mɛɛ Jɛyɛl faa du bolzeŋ Gibiɔnnɛ. U haaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Maaka.

ref: along with their sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
text: U biibambiluglii Abdɔn. Bannii hiŋzi, Zur, Kis, Baal, Nɛɛr, Nadab,

ref: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
text: Gɛdɔ, Ahio, Zɛka

ref: and Mikloth the father of Shimeah. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives. The Descendants of King Saul
text: ani Simiam mɛɛ Miklɔf. Ba ge gba faa sogoo di dugli ba lulla n du Jɛrusalɛm la.

ref: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
text: Nɛɛr biibaallɛ Kis, Kis ge biibaallɛ Koori Sɔɔl, Koori Sɔɔl ge biibaalaa Jonatan, Malki Sua, Abinadab ani Ɛs Baal.

ref: Jonathan was the father of Meribbaal, the grandfather of Micah,
text: Jonatan biibaallɛ Mɛrib Baal n ɛɛ Maika mɛɛ.

ref: and the great-grandfather of Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
text: Maika ge biibaalaa keŋ, Pitɔn, Mɛlɛk, Taaria ani Ahaz.

ref: Saul's other descendants were Jehoaddah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza,
text: Ahaz biibaallɛ Jehoada, Jehoada ge biibaalaa Alɛmɛf, Azmavɛf ani Zimri. Zimri ge biibaallɛ Mɔza.

ref: as well as Azel's six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
text: Azɛl biibaala faa du banumbɛl. Ba sɔnaa keŋ, Azrikam, Bɔkɛru, Ismɛl, Sɛɛria, Obadia ani Hanan.

ref: Azel's brother Eshek was the father of Ulam, Jeush, and Eliphelet.
text: Azɛl niwee Ɛsɛk ge biibaalaa keŋ, U biibambiluglii Ulam, nɛɛhinnɛ Jɛyus, horohinnɛ Ɛlifɛlɛt.

ref: Ulam's sons were brave soldiers who were experts at using a bow and arrows. They had a total of
text: Ulam biibaala faa ɛɛ laallɔɔraa nɛnnɛ, di zum hozi tai. Ba faa dɔɔ biikpila ani naanna kpila maanii. Ba maa faa du kalfa ni tokkoanɛɛ ni fi. Bannii maanii faa ɛɛ Bɛnjamin naanna.

ref: And the first people to return to their towns included priests, Levites, temple workers, and other Israelites.
text: Ama, banla n felee bir wa so ba himmaa bɔdɔɔlaa, ba bola biinee faa, Izrɛl hina baŋhina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna.

ref: People from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
text: Banla n lii Juda, Bɛnjamin, Ɛfram ani Manasɛ dizi biini du Jɛrusalɛmnɛ,

ref: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives were the guards at the temple gates. Shallum was the leader of this clan,
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuguuree, Salum, Akub, Talmɔn, Ahiman ani ba niuna. Ba sitɔɔrii faa Salum.

ref: and for a long time they had been the guards at the King's Gate on the east side of the city. Before that, their ancestors guarded the entrance to the Levite camp.
text: Baabuu faa ra guu koori dominuuzeŋ n du a bolzeŋ wiifurii, haali ni zinaa. Banniibuu faa ɛɛ dominuuzenaa guure di lii Levi dee biini.

ref: Shallum son of Kore, as well as the other men in the Korahite clan, guarded the entrance to the temple, just as their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: Kɔrɛ biibaallɛ Salum, Ɛbiasaf ge biibaallɛ Kɔrɛ, Kɔra ge biibaallɛ Ɛbiasaf ani u dɔŋahina dominuuzenaa guure n lii ba dia biini, di ɛɛ Kɔra naanna. Baabuu faa ra guu Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua, gunla ba mɛɛwaa n faa ra guu Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia dominua la.

ref: Phinehas son of Eleazar had supervised their work because the Lord was with him.
text: A lugli saŋa la, Ɛliaza biibaal Finɛhasii faa ɛɛ a dominuuzenaa guure sitɔɔri, Kɔraawiizi faa ra hiinuu.

ref: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was also one of the guards at the temple.
text: Mɛsɛlɛmia biibaal Zɛkariaa faa ra guu Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia dominua.

ref: and now they guarded the temple gates.
text: Ba ni ba naanna noneere ba faa kpa Kɔraawiizi Dia la dominuuzi guui du.

ref: There was one full-time guard appointed to each of the four sides of the temple.
text: A dominuuzi guure faa du a keŋkerezi maanii. Wiifurii, wiicholii ani a wiifurii nomɛɛl ni nodig wiikakagni maa.

ref: Their assistants lived in the villages outside the city, and every seven days a group of them would come into the city and take their turn at guard duty.
text: Ba lulla la n faa du ba bola ɔɔ faa liiu saŋazi, di ba waa hiini baa, alugɔ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: The four full-time guards were Levites, and they supervised the other guards and were responsible for the rooms in the temple and the supplies kept there.
text: Ama, a dominuuzi guure sitɔɔra banaazu baŋhina waa n faa ɛɛ Levi dee, ba faa tɛɛ baabuu ba huma, ba ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia diini ni u daama kuna dauribɔra ni.

ref: They guarded the temple day and night and opened its doors every morning. The Duties of the Levites
text: Ba ɔɔ faa chiu di ra guu Kɔraawiizi Dia, hamuŋa maa guŋŋ bɔr wa chaani, dikuu aŋ ɛɛ ba huma wia. Baabuu faa ra kpogli a Dia saafiibii, di ɔɔ ra pilluu chɔɔzi maa.

ref: Some of the Levites were responsible for the equipment used in worship at the temple, and they had to count everything before and after it was used.
text: A Levi dee baŋhina noneere ba faa kpa kunnanaananaa la baŋ faa kpawɛɛ ra hum Kɔraawiizi Dia huma du. Baabuu ɔɔ faa ra kuraa, di ba wa kpaa di ra lii gɛɛ di bir di ra zuu.

ref: But only the priests could mix the spices.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina baŋhina noneere ba faa kpa kunsɔɔhrisuma koozaa du.

ref: Mattithiah, Shallum's oldest son, was a member of the Levite clan of Korah, and he was in charge of baking the bread used for offerings.
text: Levi dee hinuu bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Matitia, u faa ɛɛ Kɔra domee hinuu Salum biibambiluglii. Ba faa tɛubuu ba mbusu lizaa paanuu ɔɔzaa huma.

ref: The Levites from the Kohath clan were in charge of baking the sacred loaves of bread for each Sabbath.
text: Kɔhaf domee baŋhina genii ɔɔ faa ɛɛ ba Heezaa Hɔpizii paanuu sirya, di dau tɛɛbul ni.

ref: The Levite family leaders who were the musicians also lived at the temple. They had no other responsibilities, because they were on duty day and night.
text: Banla n faa ɛɛ yiryitta, di ɛɛ Levi dee domee nabɔnzi la waa, faa du Kɔraawiizi Dia diibizi biinii. Ba faa waa kaa gil ba dɔɔ huma maa, dikuu baŋ ɔɔ faa ra hum huma hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi maa wia.

ref: All of these men were family leaders in the Levi tribe and were listed that way in their family records. They lived in Jerusalem. King Saul's Family (
text: Bannii maanii faa ɛɛ Levi dee domeezi nabɔnzi, ba sɛbi ba sɔna di hiŋzi ba lulaa ŋmɛnizi, ba faa du Jɛrusalɛm. Koori Sɔɔl naabaala ni u naanna wia

ref: the father of Shimeam. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives.
text: ani Simiam mɛɛ Miklɔf. Ba ge gba faa sogoo di dugli ba lulla n du Jɛrusalɛm la.

ref: Jeiel had settled the town of Gibeon, where he and his wife Maacah lived.
text: Gibiɔn mɛɛ Jɛyɛl faa du bolzeŋ Gibiɔnnɛ. U haaŋ sɔnnɛ faa Maaka,

ref: They had ten sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
text: u biibambiluglii Abdɔn. Bannii hiŋzi, Zur, Kis, Baal, Nɛɛr, Nadab,

ref: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth
text: Gɛdɔ, Ahio, Zɛkaria

ref: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
text: Nɛɛr biibaallɛ Kis, Kis ge biibaallɛ Koori Sɔɔl, Koori Sɔɔl ge biibaalaa Jonatan, Malki Sua, Abinadab ani Ɛs Baal.

ref: The descendants of Ahaz included Jarah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel and his six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
text: Azɛl biibaala faa du banumbɛl. Ba sɔnaa keŋ, Azrikam, Bɔkɛru, Ismɛl, Sɛɛria, Obadia ani Hanan.

ref: The Philistines fought against Israel in a battle at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
text: A kaa wa ɛɛ lugɔ Filisti ni Izrɛl hina kaa ra lɔ laal, ba kpu Izrɛl hina galga maa Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu, ka baŋhina chɔ.

ref: Saul died because he was unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord. He even asked advice from a woman who talked to spirits of the dead,
text: Koori Sɔɔl faa siuwɔɔ dikuu u wia n faa waa wibii dɔɔwɛ Kɔraawiizi be wia. U faa waa u nuuzi ra hiŋ, haali di la vugri be, di ga pɛɛzi,

ref: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons and killed three of them: Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
text: Filisti hina faa duŋŋi Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala guŋŋ di ga kpu Jonatan, Abinadab ani Malki Sua.

ref: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
text: A laal faa jaa du kpeg werge, ba bar Koori Sɔɔl, di viruu hobii, di duu pira.

ref: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want those godless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Then Saul stuck himself in the stomach with his own sword and fell on the blade.
text: Koori Sɔɔl ŋɔ biipɔllii la n kpogli u dɔŋkuna be, “Pam i tokobi di tɔɔhŋ kpu, di guŋ lɛi, nɛra naa n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ naa daŋ ba wa ɛɛŋ chɛɛtɛ, di sunniŋ.” Ka ɔnsii faa lau a biipɔllii werge maa, waa sɛɛwɛ ú kpuu. Denii Koori Sɔɔl pam u himmaa tokobi, di bir tɔɔh u hiŋ kpu.

ref: When the soldier realized that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
text: A biipɔllii n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Koori Sɔɔl siuwɔɔ, u ge pam u himmaa tokobi tɔɔh u hiŋ, di siu jaa u ni.

ref: Saul, three of his sons, and all his male relatives were dead.
text: Awia, Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaala bahoro ani u diahina maa, faa kpau siu.

ref: The Israelites who lived in Jezreel Valley learned that their army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead. They ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites left behind.
text: Izrɛl hina la maa n faa du a waluu, n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ ba laallɔɔra maa chɔwɔɔrɛ la, Koori Sɔɔl ge ni u biibaala maa siu la, ba ge maa chɔ ka ka ba bola. Filisti hina la jaa ba di wa so ba bola hiŋ.

ref: The next day the Philistines came back to the battlefield to carry away the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers. When they found the bodies of Saul and his sons on Mount Gilboa,
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Filisti hina ba, bá wa wir a lalaa kuna, ba na Koori Sɔɔl ani u biibaala la n siuwɛ chɔɔ Bizeŋ Gilbɔa nyuu.

ref: they took Saul's weapons, pulled off his armor, and cut off his head. Then they sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the news among their people and to thank the idols of their gods.
text: Ba teŋ Koori Sɔɔl nyuu, di wir u laal laala, ka hunzi nɛra Filisti hina bola maa, lugɔ bá sii guŋ amaniyesuma, ba vuga diini biine ani ba nɛra maa be.

ref: They put Saul's armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of their god Dagon.
text: Ba kpa u dɔŋkuna la ga dau ba vuga dia, ka kpa u nyuu ge sag ba vug Dagɔn dia biini.

ref: When the people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
text: Bolzeŋ Jabɛs Giliad hina n wa nuu gunla Filisti hina la n dau Koori Sɔɔl,

ref: some brave men went to get his body and the bodies of his three sons. The men brought the bodies back to Jabesh, where they buried them under an oak tree. Then for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
text: ba baala la maa n faa ɛɛ laallɔkpega maa izi, di la ga paagi Koori Sɔɔl ni u biibaala di ba Jabɛs, di wa hug baa daazeŋ bɛl zɛɛ, ka vɔɔ nua hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: instead of asking the Lord. So the Lord had Saul killed and gave his kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
text: ka vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzaa. Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa kpuu, ka kpa u kora tɛɛ Jɛssɛ biibaal Koori Deevid.

ref: The Jebusites said, “You won't be able to get in here!” But David captured the fortress of Mount Zion, which is now called the City of David.
text: A Jɛbus dee ŋɔ Koori Deevid be, “Hàá wer na bɔr zuu ɛŋ.” Haali ani a maa, ka Koori Deevid faa wettoo kpegli a Bolzeŋ Ziɔn diikpeg la. Ba jaa ra yiruu Deevid Bolzeŋ.

ref: Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives,
text: Izrɛl hina dizi maa chaali, di ba Koori Deevid be bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn, di wa ŋɔ, “Na, yaa ɛɛ i challɛ.

ref: So we have come to crown you king of Israel.” David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now king of Israel. This happened just as the Lord's prophet Samuel had said. David Captures Jerusalem (
text: Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi maa n wa ba Koori Deevid be bolzeŋ Hɛbrɔn la, u ni baa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ Kɔraawiizi see, ka ba waaruu nuu, di tɔu Izrɛl kora, gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ga Samuɛl be, di ŋɔ nua la. Koori Deevid n kpegli Jɛrusalɛm hina wia

ref: David had told his troops, “The first soldier to kill a Jebusite will become my army commander.” And since Joab son of Zeruiah attacked first, he became commander.
text: Denii Koori Deevid faa ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ tɔ a laal see, di lɔ Jɛbus dee laal, waabuu niŋ birgi n laallɔɔra nabɔma.” Zɛruya biibaal Joab faa feli lii. Awia, u faa birgi u laallɔɔra nabɔma.

ref: The Lord had promised that David would become king, and so everyone in Israel gave David their support. Certain warriors also helped keep his kingdom strong.
text: Banla n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid laallɔkpega n dɔɔ sɔnnɛ keŋ. Ba ni Izrɛl hina maanii faa chigɛ Koori Deevid har, di hiinuu u di kora a hɛri maa ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua la.

ref: Jerusalem was called Jebus at the time, and David led Israel's army to attack the town.
text: Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra maa izi di la Jɛrusalɛm, bá ga lɔ Jɛbus dee la n du de la.

ref: Later, David moved to the fortress—that's why it's called the City of David.
text: Koori Deevid ga zuu a diikpeg la di du de. Ba jaa ra yiruu, Deevid Bolzeŋ.

ref: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side. The Three Warriors (
text: Denii Koori Deevid jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ faa du u benii. Koori Deevid Laallɔkpega wia

ref: Another time he killed an Egyptian who was over two meters tall and was armed with a spear. Benaiah only had a club, so he grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
text: U faa kaa kpu Ijip hinuu bɛl n helle kpabaa, u jaŋzi faa ɛɛ naapezi aniidaanɛɛ ni keza. Haali a Ijip hinuu n kpogli kandaa lugɔ kɔɔrɛɛ daa gba, ka Bɛnaaya faa kpa guliire di lɔu, ka foozi u kandaa hiŋ di kpuu.

ref: and he said, “I'm very thirsty. I wish I had a drink of water from the well by the gate to Bethlehem.”
text: Denii niinyɔgzi wa lau Koori Deevid werge maa, u ŋɔ, “N bɔra daŋ vii sɔɔni, di nɛbɛl vii la kɔlɔŋ la n dugli Bɛtlihɛm dominuuzeŋ la ga ɛɛ nii wa tɛŋ ń nyɔɔ!”

ref: The first of these warriors was Jashobeam the son of Hachmoni, the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle he killed
text: Koori Deevid laallɔkpega la sɔnaa keŋ, Hakmɔn domee hinuu Jasɔbiannɛ faa a nabɔnzi la maa sitɔɔri. U faa kpa kandaarɛ di kpu nɛra kalfaahoroo laalkpaŋ biini.

ref: Another one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite.
text: Unla n faa hiŋ u ni genii Ahɔ domee hinuu Dɔdai biibaal Ɛliaza. U faa ɛɛ ba laallɔkpega bahoro la bɛllɛ.

ref: except Eleazar, who stayed with David. They took their positions in a nearby barley field and defeated the Philistines! The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
text: ka u ni u laallɔɔra waa chi a koo baaŋ chigigi di yoo Filisti hina la, di kpu baa. Kɔraawiizi faa gil ba kpegli baa nɛnnɛ.

ref: One time the Three Warriors went to meet David among the rocks at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
text: A hɔl bɛl, a laallɔkpega tokko ni kpɔrgɔ la bahoro faa tuu ba Koori Deevid be, bii la n dugli Adulam bii bɔɔ, di Filisti laallɔɔra suge bɛl faa chɔɔ Rɛfam Waluu biini.

ref: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in a fortress,
text: A saŋa hiŋ, di Koori Deevid faa du a diikpeg biini, ka Filisti laallɔɔra suge wa chɔɔ Bɛtlihɛm.

ref: and said, “Drinking this water would be like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
text: “Kɔ́raawiizi gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ n waa nyɔɔ nii naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, a daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ baala naa n tulmee naa challɛ n na nyɔɔ gunla!” Awia, u vɛɛ a nyɔɔi. Wizenaa naabuu laallɔkpega bahoro naa faa ɛɛ.

ref: and was more famous than the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was their commander, but he never became one of the Three Warriors.
text: Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge di kaali Bahoro la. Awia, u faa jaa ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, haali uŋ faa waa ba ni jaawɛ gba.

ref: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. One time he killed two of Moab's best fighters, and one snowy day he went into a pit and killed a lion.
text: Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaaya n lii bolzeŋ Kabziil ge faa ɛɛ laallɔkpega la bɛllɛ. U ge gba faa ɛɛ wizenaare di kpu Moab hina laallɔkpega banɛɛ. U faa ga tuu bɔɔ bɛl waari hɔpizii, di kpu bunyiŋ.

ref: Benaiah did things like that; he was just as brave as the Three Warriors,
text: Bɛnaaya gba faa dɔɔ sɔnnɛ alugɔ laallɔkpega Bahoro la. Wizenaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛɛ guŋ.

ref: even though he never became one of them. And he was certainly as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. So David made him the leader of his own bodyguard.
text: Waabuu ba faa ra tɔgzi werge kaali Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ la bɛl maa, ka u faa waa Laallɔkpega Bahoro La ni jaawɛ. Koori Deevid jaa gil u ɛɛ u guure nabɔma.

ref: Several of these warriors were from King Saul's own tribe of Benjamin. They were experts at using a bow and arrows, and they could shoot an arrow or sling a stone with either hand.
text: Ba faa vɔɔ laallɛ ni hozi, di faa zum hozi ni bilorizi taazaa ni ba nodige ni nomɛɛla maa werge. Ba faa ɛɛ Koori Sɔɔl lullaa di lii Bɛnjamin dee biini.

ref: Men from the tribe of Gad also joined David at his fortress in the desert and served as his warriors. They were also brave soldiers—fierce as lions and quick as gazelles. They were always prepared to fight with shields and spears.
text: Banniibuu faa lii Gad dee biini di chɔ ga zuu Koori Deevid, di jaa u laallɔɔra ni, u diikpeg, hɛribɔduma biini. Ba faa zum laal lɔirɛ nɛnnɛ, di ɛɛ laal lɔi sirya, di zum laal pɛrɛtuzi ni kandaazi kpoglaa nɛnnɛ. Ba wia faa dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ alugɔ bunyinzi, ka faa du gbaŋ ge alugɔ sejigzi n du bia nyuuni.

ref: All these men were army officers; some were high-ranking officers over a thousand troops, and others were officers over a hundred troops.
text: Bannii naabuu faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra nabɔnzi di lii Gad dee biini. Ba jigahiŋ ɔɔ faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kalfa nabɔmaa. Ba nabɔnzeŋ hiŋ ge ɔɔ faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋ nabɔma.

ref: Earlier, they had crossed the Jordan River when it flooded, and they chased out the people who lived in the valleys on each side of the river. Warriors from the Benjamin and Judah tribes
text: Baabuu faa gi Jɔɔdan muu, lugli baagu biini, saŋa la uŋ faa suwee werge la, di faa ga duŋŋi banla n soge a walli biine, wiifurii ni wiicholii maa.

ref: One time a group of men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah went to the fortress where David was staying.
text: A hɔl bɛl Bɛnjamin ni Juda dizi la ge baŋhina faa ba Deevid be, u diikpeg la biini.

ref: David met them outside and said, “If you are coming as friends to fight on my side, then stay and join us. But if you try to turn me over to my enemies, the God our ancestors worshiped will punish you, because I have done nothing wrong.”
text: Deevid faa lii ga chem ba ni, di ŋɔ ba be, “Di ii ballɔɔ ni bampirsɔna ií wa hiiniŋ, n ɛɛ siryaa n ni ia ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, ka di ii ballɔɔ ii wa liziŋ tɛɛ n dɔma, filaŋkennaa miŋ waa kalu maa ra lɔ naa, guŋwaa, Kɔ́raawiizi la yaa mɛɛwaa n na hum la di ia seriya.”

ref: Some of the warriors who joined David were from the tribe of Manasseh. They had earlier gone with David when he agreed to fight on the side of the Philistines against King Saul. But as soon as the Philistine rulers realized that David might turn against them and rejoin Saul, they sent David away to the town of Ziklag.
text: Manasɛ dee laallɔɔra baŋhina ge faa chɔ di ga zuu Koori Deevid, saŋa la u ni Filisti hina n faa laŋŋɛ bá ga lɔ Koori Sɔɔl laal la. Ka u ni u laallɔɔra la faa waa Filisti hina la hiinee, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba nabɔnzi faa wɔɔ yardɛɛ, awia, ba faa duŋŋuu. Ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Yaa nyuunii ya kpa turgi kim, di u wa bittɔ chɔ kaali u dɔɔri Koori Sɔɔl be.”

ref: and brave soldiers, and so David made them officers in his army. They fought on his side when enemy troops attacked.
text: Ba faa hiini Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔraa, ba kpegli ŋmɛɛna sugezi, dikuu baŋ faa ɛɛ laallɔkpega ni sitɔɔra, u laallɔɔra biini wia.

ref: Other Israelites from as far away as the territories of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought cattle and sheep to slaughter for food. They also brought donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen that were loaded down with flour, dried figs and raisins, wine, and olive oil. Everyone in Israel was very happy.
text: Haali ba dɔŋahina gba n faa lii bɔɔnɛɛzi, alugɔ Isaka, Zɛbulɔn ani Naftali hɛssi, faa gillɔɔ kauzi, zagra, nyugmazi ani navargazi chi diwee di waa tɛɛ baa. Ba faa dɔɔ kuŋkpila maanii lugɔ sau, fig ni grepu nɔŋhilaa baŋ ɛhzɛɛ mari dɔŋa, siŋ, nuu, nauna ani peeza, dikuubɛɛwiai, bɔsɔna faa du Izrɛl hɛrii.

ref: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
text: Bannii maa faa ɛɛ laallɔɔraa, di faa lizi bahinaa di ra hum laal huma. Ba faa ba Hɛbrɔnnɛ di wa ɛɛ sirya lugɔ bá tɔ Koori Deevid Izrɛl maa kora. Izrɛl hina la maa gba n faa kawɛɛ, la faa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ lugɔ bá tɔ Koori Deevid a kora.

ref: The soldiers stayed in Hebron three days, eating and drinking what their relatives had prepared for them.
text: A laallɔɔra faa di hɔpizaa ahoroo Koori Deevid be, di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba lulla faa tɛɛ baabuu a guŋ kuna.

ref: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
text: Koori Deevid ni a nɛra faa la bolzeŋ Baala, ba ra yiruu Kiriaf Jiarim la, de du Juda hɛri la, bá ga kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ n sag u ni la, u ra di kora chɛrubzi baambaaŋ la.

ref: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
text: A hɔl hiŋ, ɔnsii lau Koori Deevid dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia, u ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ Dakka naa ɛɛ ba n benei?”

ref: The people agreed this was the right thing to do.
text: Denii nɛra la maa n faa chaalɛɛ la sɛɛ, dikuu guŋ n faa deŋlee ba maa be wia.

ref: The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart,
text: Denii ba faa la ga lizi a Dakka la lii Abinadab dia, di kpau hɔŋ torkofalii ni, di gil Uza ni Ahio ra du u tau, di ra bagli a nauna ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
text: Koori Deevid ni Izrɛl hina maa jaa ra sa, di ra yir yira ni ba fɔŋŋa maa, di ra lɔ kemzi, janjalanzi, di ra yigzi kuna, di ra lɔ pɛrɛtuzi, di ra huuh bensunozi di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi werge maa.

ref: But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling.
text: Ka baŋ wa hel baal bɛl banna yir Kidɔn pila, a navargazi lɔ naa, Uza tɛr u nonii di lau a Dakka.

ref: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Uza ni, u lɔu ta de, u siu u see, dikuu uŋ tɛr u nonii lau a Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka wia.

ref: David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
text: Denii Koori Deevid baaŋ fuuh, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛr Uza digna ni baaŋfuuih wia. Ba jaa ra yir de Pɛrɛz Uza haali ni zinaa.

ref: So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
text: Awia, u faa waa a Dakka kpawɛɛ ba u be, bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, ka jaa bir kpau la Gaf hinuu Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm dia.

ref: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
text: Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka hiŋ jaa du Ɔbɛd Ɛdɔm diahina be baaguzi ahoro. Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa kissi u diahina ani kuna la maa un dɔɔwɛ.

ref: David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
text: Awia, Koori Deevid ni u laallɔɔra la jaa izi di la Baal Pɛrazim, di faa ga kpegli baa, ka jaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n kpegli n dɔma alugɔ nii n suwee di kpu nɛra la.” Awia, ba jaa ra yir de Baal Pɛrazim.

ref: David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
text: Denii Koori Deevid faa ɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n bagluu la. Ba jaa kpu Filisti laallɔɔra la, di lii Gibiɔn guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛza.

ref: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace.
text: A saŋaa Taaya Koori Hiram hum u balaa Koori Deevid be, di gil ba kpa hɛriŋkpol daazi, ba ni kapintazi ani maara, bá wa ma kooridia tɛu.

ref: After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters.
text: Koori Deevid kaa kpa hahkpila Jɛrusalɛm biini di jaa, di lul biibaala ni biihaana kpila.

ref: From then on, David became even more famous, and the Lord made all the nations afraid of him.
text: Awia, Koori Deevid sɔŋ faa yaari a hɛssi maa. Kɔraawiizi gil a hɛssi maa hina faa ra ɔmuu.

ref: When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle.
text: Filisti hina n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ ba waari Koori Deevid nyuurɛ nuu, di tɔu Izrɛl maa kora la, ba laallɔɔra maa vɔɔ lii, di gaa nyiŋŋuu. Koori Deevid n wa nuu guŋ, u lii la ú ga chem ba ni.

ref: The Philistines had already camped in Rephaim Valley and were raiding the nearby villages.
text: Di Filisti hina la ballɔ wa lɔ Rɛfam Waluu hina laal, di foozi ba kuna.

ref: David asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help me win?” The Lord told David, “Yes, attack them! I will give you victory.”
text: Awia, Koori Deevid faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi di na, di ŋɔ, “Ń la ga lɔ Filisti hina naa? I daŋ gil n kpegli baa?” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “A la, n daŋ kpa baa du i nonee biini.”

ref: Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
text: Filisti hina faa gil ba vuga ha de, Koori Deevid ŋɔ lugɔ ba fuuh a maa.

ref: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Filisti hina kaa wa fɔɔ a waluu hina ni laal, di foozi ba kuna.

ref: David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are.
text: Koori Deevid kaa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ deŋli baa di la, bar baa di la keŋkere bɛl, di lɔ baa balsam daazi la see.

ref: Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
text: Di i haŋ wa nuu laallɔɔra naazi gbɔga a balsam daazi nyuuni, lii chem baa ni laal, dikuubɛɛwiai, guŋ daŋ bagli lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi tɔ i seere, ń kpu Filisti laallɔɔra hiŋ.”

text: Koori Deevid n wa ma diini u Bolzeŋ la biini tuŋ, u jaa kuari bɔr di baŋ tanti dia ú du Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la.

text: Ií ra dargi Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ girme la. Ií kpa sunzaa kuna ba u be. Ií ra giŋŋi unla n ɛɛ naniinanii la, di u wa ballɔ.

text: Muuzeŋ ani kunnyinee la maa n du i biini la, ií ge gba ra ɛɛ guŋ. Kooni ani kuna la maa n du ii biine, ií ra di iihinaa alugɔ nɛra!

text: N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina sognibɔr, di gil bá so de, de ɛɛ ba himmaa hɛri, nɛr maa wàá kaa ra tɔɔri baa. Biinikpola hina wàá kaa ra fir baa gunla baŋ faa ra ɛɛ baa lugli la,

text: N daŋ gil u ra binni n dia ni n kora ni, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa. U kora wàá tuŋ maa.’ ”

text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi. Yaa himmaa digna nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
text: Hɛri maa hina waa hoo di ɛɛ lugɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina, hiŋ lɛɛwɛ lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, ba ɛɛ i hora la. Nuukpuuri wia la hiŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa la gillɔɔ i sɔŋ yaari durnya maa biini. I lɛɛ i nɛraa lii Ijip hɛri, di ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wia, di duŋŋi hɛssi hina la n du ba see, saŋa la baŋ liiwɛ di ra ba la.

ref: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
text: I gillɔɔ i nɛra Izrɛl hina ɛɛ i hora di hanna la, i birgi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.

ref: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,

ref: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ tɛɛ i balii lugɔ i daŋ gil u naanna ra di kora. Awia, i balii dɔɔ bɔkpegaa ú suŋŋi wiizi naa.

ref: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu Kɔraawiizi di ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ ɛɛ winanaa naa tɛɛ i balii.

ref: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
text: Awia, a pariibuu filaŋkeŋ lugɔ i kissi i balii naanna, bá du de di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu kissi baa, awia, ba daŋ na kissaa di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

text: ka ma mbusu lizibɔr de tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi u ni. U faa suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi nuu tɛu, di gil ninlau lii chiŋ, di wa fuuh mbusu lizaa kuna hiŋ de.

text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia a mɛlika be, u bir kpa u tokobi suu u too biini.

ref: When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place,
text: Koori Deevid n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi nuu u suŋŋaa labuu, Jɛbus hinuu Arauna pila la, u lizi mbusuzi de.

ref: David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.” David Prepares To Build the Temple
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Ɛnnɛ dɛkkɛ bá ma Kɔraawiizi Dia ni mbusu lizibɔr, Izrɛl hina ɔɔ ra fuuh kuna u ni, di ra lizi mbusuzi.” Kɔraawiizi Dia mai sirya ɛɛi wia

text: Koori Deevid faa gil ba chaali hɔɔhra la maa n du Izrɛl hɛri. U binni ba biini di lizi bisɛɛhra bá sɛɛhzi bia, bá kpa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia.

ref: He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
