ref: He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.” That's why David did all these things before he died. David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “N biibaal Solomɔn haa ɛɛ bichalaa, waa wia zummɛ nɛnnɛ. Dia naa ge yaa n niŋ ma tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi naa, dɛkkɔɔ uŋ wesse werge di dɔɔ girme ni sɔŋ, hɛssi hina maa be. Awia, n daŋ ɛɛ u sirya nɛnnɛ.” Denii Koori Deevid jaa ɛɛ u sirya nɛnnɛ mɔɔ ka siu.

ref: David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel.
text: Awia, u yir u biibaal Solomɔn, di ŋɔ dí u ma Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la.

ref: He said: My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped.
text: Kenne Koori Deevid ŋɔ Solomɔn be, “N biibaal, n na nyiŋŋuu ń vii ma Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la sɔŋ.

ref: But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘I kpu nɛraa werge maa, di kaa yoo laalkpila. Awia, hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma Dia di tɛŋ sɔŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i kpu nɛraa werge n sibɔɔ, hɛri naa biini.

ref: But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful.
text: Ama, i daŋ lul biibaal la n niŋ wa ɛɛ bampirsɔna hiŋ, di na heezaa. N daŋ gil u na heezaa lii u dɔma maa be. U sɔŋ daŋ di Solomɔn. N daŋ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina bampirsɔna, bá so bɔɔiih u kora dii saŋa.

ref: Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
text: Waabuu niŋ wa ma n Dia. U daŋ ɛɛ n biibaal, ń ge ɛɛ u mɛɛ. N daŋ gil u kora chi di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.’

ref: Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him.
text: Awia, n biibaal, Kɔ́raawiizi du i be filaŋkeŋ, í wer ma a Dia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum, gunla uŋ ŋɔ i daŋ ɛɛ la.

ref: May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi tɛi laakal ani wia zɛɛ zumaa, di u wa gillɔ i ra di kora Izrɛl hina ni, guŋ gil í ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg.

ref: If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
text: Di i ra hiŋ Gbɔgni ni widaulaa la maa Kɔraawiizi n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, u tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la nɛnnɛ, i wia maa daŋ kuari. Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di gilɛɛ gil ɔnsii waa lawii gɛɛ i bɔra waa huah.

ref: I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with
text: I dɔɔ huŋhunna kpilaa, bisɛɛhra, maara ani kapintazi. Di kaa dɔɔ nɛra la ge n zum huma maa nɛnnɛ.

ref: gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
text: Banla n zum saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ ani lugbia huma maanii i dɔɔ, ba du kpil werge maa. Awia, faari a huma filaŋkeŋ. Kɔ́raawiizi du i be.”

ref: David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon.
text: Denii Koori Deevid faa ŋɔ Izrɛl sitɔɔra maa be lugɔ ba hiini u biibaal Solomɔn.

ref: David said: The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people.
text: Kenne u ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la waa ii be duwɛɛ lɛiyaa? Waa ia tɛɛwɛ bampirsɔna lɛi, ii so bɔɔiih? U kpa hɛri naa nɛraa du n nonee biini, ba sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra dɔɔra.

ref: Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
text: Awia, ií aah siwii di ra hum Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum ni ii biine, ii kpegzi ani ii nfɛssi maa. Ií faari di ra ma u Dia, ii wer kpa U Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka ani kuna la maa n ɛɛ kunnanaananaa, di ɛɛ u hora la, di wa du a Dia la yaa n niŋ ma di tɛɛ u sɔŋ girme la biini.”

ref: David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel.
text: Koori Deevid n wa zɛŋŋɛ werge maa, u gil u biibaal Solomɔn di Izrɛl kora.

ref: Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites.
text: U faa chaali Izrɛl hɛri sitɔɔra maa, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee.

ref: Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him.
text: Baabuu niŋ ɔɔ kaa chi chɔɔzi ni duana maa, di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi, di ra chɔluu,

ref: David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
text: Koori Deevid faa bargi Levi dee la bɔra ahoro, di hiŋzi ba domeezi, Gɛsɔn, Kɔhaf ani Mɛrari. Gɛsɔn domee wia

ref: Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei.
text: Gɛsɔn domee hinaa, Ladan ani Simei.

ref: Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
text: Ladan biibaalaa, Jɛhiɛl, u biibambilugli, di kpa Zɛtam ani Jowɛl.

ref: They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran.
text: Simei ge biibaalaa, Sɛlɔmɔf, Haziɛl ani Haran. Ladan domeezi nabɔnzii faa la.

ref: Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
text: Jahafuu u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Ziza. Ka Jɛyus ani Bɛria waa faa waa biibaala kpila lullɛ. Awia, ba faa kur baa lugɔ domeekpaŋ. Kɔhaf domee wia

ref: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: Kɔhaf ge biibaalaa, Amram, Izhar, Hɛbrɔn ani Uziɛl.

ref: Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name.
text: Amram ge biibaalaa, Aarɔn ni Moosis. Ba faa lizi Aarɔn ni u naannaa, bá ra lizi kunnanaananaa himmaa la doŋa, a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hora, bá ɔɔ kaa ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuna ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra humuu di ra kissi nɛra u sɔŋ biini, saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel.
text: Gɛsɔm naannaa, Subɛl, u biibambilugli.

ref: Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
text: Hɛbrɔn ge biibaalaa, Jɛria, u biibambilugli, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ Amaria, horohiŋ Jahaziɛl, naazuhiŋ Jɛkamiam.

ref: Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish.
text: Mɛrari biibaalaa, Mali ani Musi. Mali ge biibaalaa, Ɛliaza ani Kis.

ref: Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons.
text: Ɛliaza faa waa biibaal maa lullɛ ka siu. Biihambizii u faa lul. Ba naara Kis biibaala faa paa baa.

ref: David said: The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
text: Koori Deevid faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la tɛɛ u nɛraa bampirsɔna, di jaa wa du ba be Jɛrusalɛm biini, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place.
text: Awia, Levi dee waa kaa dɔɔ lugɔ ba ra chi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia ani kuna la maa, baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra hum huma u biini la.”

ref: will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure.
text: Levi dee humaa faa lugɔ ba ɔɔ ra hiini Aarɔn naanna, di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, di ra du Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee ani u diibizi tau. Bá ɔɔ lizi kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ, di ra hum huma a Dia biini la doŋa ha, á ɛɛ kunnanaananaa saŋa maa.

ref: They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
text: Baabuu faa ra du paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, sau la baŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra lizi mbusuzi, kɛrɛkɛssizi la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛ, a ɔɔzaa ni a koozaa ni kuna mɛgzaa ni.

ref: They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done.
text: di ba wa fuuh kuna di lizi mbusu, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Heezaa Hɔpizii gɛɛ Baagufalii Hɔpizizenaa ani Hɔpizizenaa aŋhina. Baabuu faa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ ba ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma saŋa maa, gunla n dɛkkɛ ban niŋ mag ani ŋmɛnizi la baŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ baa la.

ref: They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
text: Awia, Levi dee faa ra hum ba humaa nɛnnɛ, Kɔraawiizi Ni Chemaa Tanti Dia ani u Bɔnaniinanii la biini. Ba ɔɔ kaa hiini ba lulla Aarɔn naannaa, ba ra hum huma Kɔraawiizi Dia biini.

ref: Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
text: Aarɔn naanna sugezii keŋ, Aarɔn biibaalaa faa Nadab, Abihu, Ɛliaza ani Itama.

ref: But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
text: Nadab waa ni Abihu faa feli ba mɛɛrɛ siu, di ba waa biibaala maa lullɛ. Awia, Ɛliaza ani Itama faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina.

ref: David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
text: Ɛliaza naana Zadɔk ani Itama naana Ahimɛlɛkii faa hiini Koori Deevid, u bargi baa di du ba huma bɔra, bá ra hum.

ref: groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders.
text: fidikabɛlhiŋ chol Pɛtahia ni, tokkohiŋ chol Jɛhɛzkɛl ni,

ref: However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
text: Awia, ba faa ta kunaa, bá zum banla n niŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia nabɔnzi ani kizeehina.

ref: As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
text: Nɛtanɛl biibaal, Sɛmaaya la n faa ɛɛ Levi ni karchi la, sɛbi ba sɔna a koori ni a nabɔnzi see, di dau. text: Kennaabuu ba faa lizi baa, ba ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma, di ba ɔɔ wa zuu u Dia la biini. Widaulaa la ba naabaal Aarɔn n faa dauwɛ tɛɛ baa, gunla Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la n faa bagluu lugɔ u ɛɛ labuu guŋ. Levi dee la n kawɛɛ wia

ref: The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites.

ref: Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
text: Ba faa waa domee bɛl maa kpila gɛɛ tama dui binnɛɛ, ka ta kuna, di lizi baa, bá ra binni a dominuuzenaa.

ref: Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms.

ref: Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road. The guards were assigned the following work schedule:

ref: Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms,

ref: four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
text: Ama, diŋŋee la waa n faa du wiicholii la, banaazuu ɔɔ faa chi u ŋmɛnɛɛ, banɛɛ ge chi u biini.

ref: These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari. Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
text: Kennaabuu ba faa bargi a dominuuzenaa guure sugezi hiŋ n lii Kɔra ani Mɛrari dizi biini la. Kɔraawiizi Dia huma aŋhina wia

ref: The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
text: Ba dɔŋahina Levi dee la baŋhinaa faa ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna diini ani kuna la baŋ ɔɔ kpa di waa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la diini ni.

ref: Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan.
text: Gɛsɔn biibaal Ladan, faa ɛɛ domee kpila naabaallɛ, di kpa u biibaal Jɛhiɛli diahina jaa.

ref: Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
text: Jɛhiɛli biibaala Zɛtam ni u niwee Jowɛllɛ faa ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna diini ni.

ref: Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: Amram, Izhar, Hɛbrɔn ani Uziɛl naanna la ge humazii keŋ,

ref: Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury.
text: Moosis biibaal Gɛsɔm naana Subɛllɛ faa ɛɛ daama kuna diini nabɔma.

ref: Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders.
text: Sɛlɔmif ni u lullaa faa ra binni daama kuna la maa Koori Deevid, domeezi nabɔnzi n faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa ni kalfazi nabɔnzi ani laallɔɔra nabɔnzi baŋhina n lizɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ni.

ref: And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple.
text: A kuna aŋhinaa anla baŋ faa yoo laal di foozi, di kpaa wa tɛɛ ŋɔ bá bir kuari Kɔraawiizi Dia la.

ref: Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah. Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
text: Haali anla gba Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Samuɛl, Kis biibaal Sɔɔl, Nɛɛr biibaal Abna ani Zɛruya biibaal Joab n lizɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la maanii faa du Sɛlɔmif ni u lulla nonee biini.

ref: Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
text: Di lii Izhar naanna biini, Kɛnania ni u biibaalaa ba faa lizi, ba ɛɛ nabɔnzi ni sitɔɔra, Izrɛl hina ni. Baawaa huma faa waa hoo Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini.

ref: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count the people, but he stopped when the Lord began punishing Israel. So the total number was never included in David's official records. Officials in Charge of the King's Property
text: Zɛruya biibaal Joab faa jaa faari di ra kur a nɛra, ka waa wette kur baa tuŋ. Kɔraawiizi faa tɔɔri baa werge, dikuu a nɛkuraa naa wia. Awia, ba faa waa ba maga sɛbɛɛ du Koori Deevid wiɛɛlaa hɔŋ biini. Kooridia kuna binna wia

ref: in the third month, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest,
text: Baaguzi ahorohiŋ biini, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada biibaal Bɛnaayaa faa ɛɛ ba laallɔɔra nabɔma. U suge baala faa du kagboŋa tokko ni anaazu.

ref: who was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and whose son Ammizabad was also an army commander;
text: Bɛnaaya naabuu faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, ba Laallɔkpega Tokko Ni Kpɔrgɔ la biini, di faa ɛɛ ba maa nabɔma. U biibaal Amizabad faa ra binni u suge ni.

ref: in the fourth month, Asahel the brother of Joab, whose son Zebadiah took over command after him;
text: Baaguzi anaazuhiŋ biini, Joab niwee Asahɛl biibaal Zɛbadia wa lɛɛ u bɔr, di ra binni a nɛra ni. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni anaazuu faa du u suge biini.

ref: in the fifth month, Shamhuth from the Izrah clan;
text: Baaguzi anuehiŋ biini, Izhar naana Samhuf. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni anaazuu faa du u ge suge biini.

ref: in the sixth month, Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa;
text: Baaguzi anumbɛlhiŋ la biini, Tɛkua hinuu Ikɛs biibaal Ira. U faa dɔɔ baala kagboŋa tokko ni anaazuu u ge suge biini.

ref: in the seventh month, Helez from Pelon in the territory of Ephraim;
text: Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, Pɛlɔn hinuu Hɛlɛz, di lii Ɛfram naanna biini. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni anaazuu u faa dɔɔ u suge biini.

ref: in the ninth month, Abiezer from Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin;
text: Baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ biini nabɔmaa faa Anatɔf hinuu Abiɛza, u lii Bɛnjamin dee biini. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni banaazuu u faa dɔɔ.

ref: in the tenth month, Maharai from Netophah of the Zerah clan;
text: Baaguzi fihiŋ biini nabɔmaa faa Nɛtɔfaf hinuu Maharai, di lii Zɛra dee biini. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni banaazuu u faa dɔɔ.

ref: in the eleventh month, Benaiah from Pirathon in the territory of Ephraim;
text: Baaguzi fidikpaŋhiŋ biini nabɔmaa faa Piratɔn hinuu Bɛnaaya, di lii Ɛfram dee biini. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni anaazuu u faa dɔɔ.

ref: in the twelfth month, Heldai from Netophah, who was a descendant of Othniel. David Assigns Tribal Leaders
text: Baaguzi fidaanɛɛhiŋ biini nabɔmaa faa Nɛtɔfaf hinuu Hɛldai, di lii Ɔtniɛl lulla biini. Baala kagboŋa tokko ni banaazuu u faa dɔɔ. Izrɛl dizi nabɔnzi wia

ref: When David decided to count the people of Israel, he gave orders not to count anyone under
text: Koori Deevid faa waa nɛra la n di binni tokko gɛɛ n haa waa guŋ helle kutte, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ gil Izrɛl hina du kpil werge maa alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa.

ref: Azmaveth the son of Adiel was in charge of the king's personal storage rooms. Jonathan the son of Uzziah was in charge of the king's other storerooms that were in the towns, the villages, and the defense towers in Israel.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Adiɛl biibaal Azmavɛfuu faa ɛɛ a kooridia kuna dauribɔra nabɔma. Uzzia biibaal Jonatan genii faa ɛɛ ba kɛraa bola ani diijaŋra la n kpekke kuna dauribɔra nabɔma.

ref: Ezri the son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who farmed the king's land.
text: Kɛlub biibaal Ɛzri labuu faa ɛɛ ba huŋhunna la n ɛɛ patta nabɔma.

ref: Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi from Shepham was in charge of storing the wine.
text: Simei n lii Rama labuu faa ra binni daazi la nɔna baŋ kpawɛɛ di ra daali siŋ ni. Sɛfam hinuu Zabdi genii faa ra binni ba siŋ chigni bɔra wia biini.

ref: Baal Hanan from Geder was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the western foothills, and Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.
text: Baal Hanan n ɛɛ Gɛda hinuu labuu faa ra binni ɔlivi ani fig daazi la n faa du wiicholii giŋgimee zɛɛzi la ni. Joas genii faa ra binni ba ɔlivizi nuu wia biini.

ref: Shitrai from Sharon was responsible for the cattle that were kept in Sharon Plain, and Shaphat son of Adlai was responsible for those kept in the valleys.
text: Sitrai n lii Sarɔn labuu faa ɛɛ sela n na di Sarɔn hɛri kooree la nabɔma. Adlai biibaal Safat genii faa ɛɛ anla n na di de walli biine la nabɔma.

ref: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, Jehdeiah from Meronoth was in charge of the donkeys, and Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the sheep and goats.
text: Ɔbil n lii Ismɛl dee biini labuu faa ra binni ba nyugmazi ni. Jɛdɛya n lii Mɛrɔnɔf la genii faa ra binni ba kauzi ni.

ref: These were the men in charge of David's royal property. David's Personal Advisors
text: Hagri hinuu Jaziz labuu faa ra binni ba peeza ni. Bannii maanii faa ɛɛ nabɔnzi di ra binni Koori Deevid kuna ni.

ref: David's uncle Jonathan was a wise and intelligent advisor. He and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni taught David's sons.
text: Koori Deevid naara Jonatannɛ faa ra bir nɛra liize, di kaa ɛɛ wia zɛɛ zunni ani karchi. Hakmɔn biibaal Jɛhiɛl genii faa ra binni kooribiibaala ni.

ref: Ahithophel and Hushai the Archite were two of David's advisors.
text: Ahitɔfɛllɛ faa ra bir koori liize. Aaki hinuu Husairɛ faa ɛɛ koori dammu.

ref: Jehoiada the son of Benaiah was the king's advisor after Ahithophel, and later, Abiathar was his advisor. Joab was commander of Israel's army.
text: Bɛnaaya biibaal Jɛhɔyada ni Abiataa faa wa kpa Ahitɔfɛl bɔr. Joab faa ɛɛ a koori laallɔɔra nabɔma.

ref: David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
text: Denii Koori Deevid faa yir Izrɛl hɛri nabɔnzi maa, ba wa chaali Jɛrusalɛm. Baabuu nabɔnzi la n na binni ba dizi ni, sugezi nabɔnzi la n na hum a koori, kagboŋa ni kalfazi nabɔnzi maa ani nabɔnzi la n na binni u ni u biizi kuna, ba sela ni, kooridia nabɔnzi, baala la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ani laallɔkpega maa ni.

ref: After everyone was there, David stood up and said: Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple,
text: Koori Deevid jaa izi chi ba see di ŋɔ, “Yaabalaa, ií ra nuu n be. N na nyiŋŋuu ń ma dia di kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la chiŋŋi u biini, ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la naazi kara. N ɛɛ siryaa ń mau.

ref: but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, ‘Hiŋ lɛi niŋ ma dia tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i ɛɛ laallɔɔrii, di kpu nɛra werge laal biini.’

ref: The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings.
text: Ama, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la lizimbuu lii yaa diahina maa biini, ń ɛɛ Izrɛl hina koori di hanna la. U lizi Judaa u ɛɛ nabɔma. A Juda domee biinii u lizi yaa diahina. A paruubuu u liziŋ lii n mɛɛ biibaala biini, n di Izrɛl maa kora.

ref: The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel.
text: Kɔraawiizi tɛmbuu biibaalakpila, di lizi Solomɔn lii ba biini, ú di kora Kɔraawiizi nɛra Izrɛl hina ni.

ref: The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n benii, ‘I biibaal Solomɔnnɛ niŋ ma n Dia ni u diŋŋizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, n lizuubuu ú ɛɛ n biibaal, ń ge ɛɛ u mɛɛ.

ref: My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
text: Awia, yaa balaa, n na ŋɔ ii benii Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum ani u nɛra naa maa n chaalɛɛ naa see, lugɔ ii ra hiŋ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n bagli ia la nɛnnɛ, ii wer dɔɔ hɛrnanii naa, di wa giluu dau ii biizi, ú ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuŋ di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever.
text: Ka hìŋ́ n biibaal Solomɔn, a jaami Kɔraawiizi la mìŋ́ i mɛɛ n na hum la, di sɛɛ u wia ani i biini maa. Kɔraawiizii zum nɛr maa biini ani u liizee. Di i ra nyiŋŋuu i daŋ nau, ka di i vɛɛ u wia, u daŋ gilii ta, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
text: Zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi liziibuu, í ma u Dia. Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di hum a huma.”

ref: After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place.
text: Denii Koori Deevid faa jaa kpa hɔŋ la baŋ kuarɛɛ, di ra bagli gunla Kɔraawiizi Dia n niŋ du la, di tɛɛ Solomɔn. U kuna dauribɔra, u diini maa ani Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la, bɔr la baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋ nɛra ni la.

ref: He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
text: Di faa kaa kpa gunla unna fɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋizi ge ni u kɛraa diini ani kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lizi di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la dauribɔra n niŋ du la hɔŋ, di tɛu.

ref: David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship.
text: U kaa bagluu gunla un niŋ bɔnni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee gunla ban ninna hum huma Kɔraawiizi Dia biini ani kuna la ban niŋ kpa di ra hum a huma.

ref: He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects,
text: Koori Deevid kaa bagli saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa gunla maga ban niŋ kpa di kuari a dia hɛnni ni u huŋhunni kuna maa.

ref: David then said to Solomon: The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built.
text: Koori Deevid ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizii bagliŋ annii maa, n sɛbaa dau. U gillɔɔ n zum gunla maa u Dia n niŋ du.”

ref: But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him.
text: Koori Deevid kaa ŋɔ u biibaal Solomɔn be, “Chiiri zɛɛ, di dɔɔ bɔkpega, di hum a huma. Gilɛɛ waa ɔm, i bɔra waa huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la du i benii. U ŋmɛnɛ maa waa gilii ta, di u Dia mai huma waa tunnɛ.

ref: The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee la ɛɛ siryaa, bá hum Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ huma. Nɛr la maa ge n zum nonii huma nɛnnɛ, di ra nyiŋŋi u hum, daŋ hiinii di hum a huma. A nɛra maa ni ba nabɔnzi daŋ hiŋ gunla maa hin niŋ ɔɔ bagli.”

ref: That's why I have done my best to get everything Solomon will need to build it—gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, onyx, turquoise, colored gems, all kinds of precious stones, and marble.
text: Awiarɛ n ɛɛ ania di nyiŋŋi kuna la maa Solomɔn n niŋ kpa ma a Dia. Saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋu, danyɛ, lugbia, daazi, binanaa la yoola n kpolle irizi, bia la ba niŋ kpa bɔguu ani bihuŋŋukpega.

ref: and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
text: ani kuna la maa banla n zum nonee huma n niŋ kuari la. Awia, anɛɛ n niŋ lizi kuna ni biinihuŋŋu zinaa, di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizɛi?”

ref: After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts
text: Denii ba domeezi nabɔnzi, Izrɛl dizi nabɔnzi, ba laallɔɔra kagboŋa ni kalfazi nabɔnzi ani a koori huŋhunna nabɔnzi maa lizi kuna ba kipar ni.

ref: Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
text: Banla maa n dɔɔ binanaa la yoola n kpolle, faa kpaabuu du Kɔraawiizi Dia daama kuna dauribɔr. Levi dee hinuu Jɛhiɛl n lii Gɛsɔn domee biinii, faa ra binni de ni.

ref: David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated. David Praises the Lord
text: A nɛra bɔra faa sɔɔni, dikuu gunla ba nabɔnzi n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa lizaabuu ni biinihuŋŋu. Koori Deevid gba bɔra faa sɔɔni werge maa. Koori Deevid wiisuŋŋaa wia

ref: Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord: I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped.
text: Koori Deevid faa chɔli Kɔraawiizi a nɛra la n chaalɛɛ la maa see, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la yaa mɛɛ Jekɔb n na hum la, dɛg chɔlaarɛ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world,
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, hinuu dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ni kpegzi, di dɔɔ girme, zenni ani sɔŋ. Kuna la maa n du chiŋ ni hɛri ɛɛ i horaa, hinuu ra di kora kummaa ni.

ref: and you rule with strength and power. You make people rich and powerful and famous.
text: Daama ni girme lii i benii, hinuu dɔɔ kummaa fɔŋŋa. Hinuu dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ani kpegzi, di ra tɛɛ nɛr maa zenni ani fɔŋŋa.

ref: We thank you, our God, and praise you.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, yaa ra jaamiibuu, di ra dargi i sɔnzeŋ la.

ref: But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours.
text: N ni n nɛraa babɛlaai, ya tɛi kunai? Hinuu tɛɛ yaa kummaa, yaa bir kpaa ra tɛi.

ref: We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
text: Yaa ɛɛ hɛrduma hina ni hɔɔhraa i be, gunla yaa naabaala n faa duwɛɛ la. Yaa hɔpizaa hɛri naa biini ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laalii, yaa waa tamii dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, kuŋkpila naa yaa n lizɛɛ, ya ma i Dia di tɛi sɔnnanii naa, lii i benii, di ɛɛ i kuna.

ref: But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest.
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, n zummɔ lugɔ hinuu ɛɛ nɛr maa di ra na, banla wia n dɔɔ wibii wia ɔɔ pariibuu. N tɛibuu kuna naa maa ni wibii ani biinihuŋŋu. Filaŋkeŋ, n nawɔɔrɛ n bɔra sɔɔni, gunla i nɛra naa n du ɛnnaa n sɛɛwɛ lizi kuna tɛi ba kipar ni.

ref: Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaala Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n faa ra hum la, gil manni naa du i nɛra bampiree, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa, di gil ba bampiree lawii ni wibii.

ref: And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
text: Gil n biibaal Solomɔn nɔŋŋii ni u biini maa, di ra hiŋ gunla maa hin niŋ bagluu, ú wer ma Dia naa miŋ ɛɛ u sirya dau naa.”

ref: David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king. Solomon Is Crowned King
text: Denii Koori Deevid ŋɔ nɛra la n chaalɛɛ la be, “Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la!” Awia, ba maa chɔli ba mɛɛwaa Kɔraawiizi la baŋ faa ra hum la, di giŋŋi willi ba nyuuni, Kɔraawiizi ni a koori see.

ref: The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar. That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, ba di, di nyɔɔ Kɔraawiizi see ani bɔsɔna werge. Denii ba kaa ŋɔ a nɛra maa be bunɛɛhiŋ lugɔ Deevid biibaal Solomɔnnɛ ba lizi, ú ɛɛ koori. Ba ɛɛ nuu waari u nyuu, Kɔraawiizi see, ú ɛɛ ba koori, di waari Zadɔk ge, ú ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ.

ref: So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him.

Ba ɔɔ kpa paanuurɛ sag mbusu lizaa tɛɛbul la n waa doŋa dɔɔwɛ Kɔraawiizi be la ni, di choŋŋi fintinazi la n hɔŋzi saliŋ fintina daa ni la duana maa. Yaa ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la n na nyiŋŋuu. Ka iawaa vɛɛubuu ta.

ref: That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
text: Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii, di ɛɛ yaa sitɔɔri. U kizeehinaa niŋ huuh bensunozi di yir yaa, yaa ni ia lɔ laal. Izrɛl baala, ií gilɛɛ gil ii ni Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii wàá wer kpegluu.”

ref: But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front.
text: A saŋa, di Koori Jeroboam gillɔ u laallɔɔra baŋhina bar di ga so saga Juda hina la harbɔɔ, bá wer fɔɔ baa, ka baŋhina ge chi ba see.

ref: Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
text: Denii Juda laallɔɔra la faa kpegli Izrɛl laallɔɔra, dikuu baŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la wia.

ref: Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
text: Koori Abija ni u laallɔɔra faa duŋŋi Koori Jeroboam laallɔɔra la, di ga foozi ba bolzenaa Bɛtɛl, Jɛsana, Ɛfrɔn ani a kɛraa boljigzi maa.

ref: Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
text: Koori Jeroboam faa waa kaa wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa maa, Koori Abija de di saŋa la. Denii Kɔraawiizi tɛr u digni, u siu.

ref: Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
text: Koori Abija kora dii saŋa, u wiɛɛlaa ni u wiŋɔɔlaa maa, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ido Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right.
text: Koori Asa faa ɛɛ gunla n wesse di par Kɔraawiizi la unna hum labuu.

ref: He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah.
text: U faa chɔgi hɛrdumazi vuga mbusu lizibɔra ani a kuaribɔra la n du giŋgimee nyuuni labuu, di purgi vuga la n ɛɛ bia, di teŋri vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi la baŋ baŋzɛɛ la ta.

ref: Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings.
text: U faa ŋɔ Juda hina benii, dí ba ra ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la kipar, di ra hiŋ u Gbɔgni ani u baglaazi.

ref: The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns.
text: U faa ma koŋlaa bar Juda bolzenaa, dikuu a hɛri n faa dɔɔ bampirsɔna wia. U ni nɛr maa faa waa laal dɔɔwɛ a guŋ saŋa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛubuu bampirsɔna.

ref: He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
text: U faa ŋɔ Juda hina be, “Ií gil ya ma koŋlaa bar bolzenaa naa, á du kpeg, di dɔɔ tauduura sognibɔra a chine, di dɔɔ dominuuzenaa la n dɔɔ lugbidaazi, bá ra karaa. A hɛri naa haa ɛɛ yaa hotte, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na humuu, u tɛɛ yaa bampirsɔna.” Awia, ba maa, guŋ gil ba nyɛɛli.

ref: Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
text: Awia, Koori Asa ni u laallɔɔra faa lii bá ga chem baa, di faa ga ɛɛ sirya Zɛfata Waluu la n dugli Marɛsa la.

ref: Asa prayed: Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
text: Denii Koori Asa faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la unna hum, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, nɛr maa waa hoo lugɔi un niŋ hiini gɛrgi, ú wer chi di huuzi fɔŋŋa hiŋ. Hiini yaa, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum. I ninɛɛ yaa dɛlli. I sɔŋ biinii yaa ba yá wa chem laallɔɔrakpila naa. N Dɔɔri, hinuu yaa ra hum, gilɛɛ gil newee kpeglii.”

ref: The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa hiini Koori Asa ni Juda hina, ba kpu Itiopia hina la. Itiopia hina la n kawɛɛ faa ra chɔ,

ref: but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back! The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians.
text: ka Koori Asa ni u laallɔɔra la faa duŋŋi baa guŋŋ di ga hel Gɛra, di kpu bakpila maa. Kɔraawiizi ni u laallɔɔra faa kpegli baa. Denii Juda laallɔɔra la faa paagi ba kuna werge maa di kaali.

ref: The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns.
text: Ba faa jaa chɔgi boljigzi la maa n du Gɛra kɛraa la, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii chol a bola hina ni. A laallɔɔra faa paagi kuna werge di lii a boljigzi biine, dikuubɛɛwiai, kuna faa du a biinee werge.

ref: They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
text: Ba faa kaa fɔɔ ba senɔɔna chɔɔribɔra di lɔ baa, ka duŋŋi pekpila, bukpila ani nyugmazi, di bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma izi Ɔdɛd biibaal Azaria,

ref: At once, Azariah went to Asa and said: Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
text: u lii di ga chem Koori Asa ni, di ŋɔ u be, “Jara, Juda ani Bɛnjamin dee, ií ra nuu n be. Kɔraawiizi du ii benii, di ii du u be. Di ii ra nyiŋŋi u bɔr, ii daŋ nau, ka di ii vɛɛu ta, u ge daŋ vɛɛ ia ta.

ref: For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law.
text: Saŋa bɛl n bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi himmaa faa waa Izrɛl hina be duwɛɛ. Ba faa waa u Dia kizeehiŋ gba dɔɔwɛ ú ra bagli baa gɛɛ di dɔɔ u gbɔg gba.

ref: But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
text: Ka tɔɔrɔɔ n wa huuzi baa, ba bir Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la be, di nyiŋŋi u bɔr, di nau.

ref: There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, gaagaa faa dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, tɔɔrɔɔ ni koozaa faa su hɛssi maanii.

ref: Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
text: Hɛri bɛl hina ɔɔ faa ra kpegli bɛl hinaa, bolzeŋ bɛl hina kpegli bɛl hora, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii faa gillɛ tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg chol ba ni.

ref: As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
text: Koori Asa n wa nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii naa lii Ɔdɛd biibaal Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Azaria be, u faa dɔɔ bɔkpega, di chɔgi vuga la maa n du Juda ni Bɛnjamin hɛssi la. Haali di lizaa lii bola la maa baŋ kpeglee, a du Ɛfram giŋgimee hɛri la. Ka bir kuari Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la n faa chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua jaŋgal see la ma.

ref: Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
text: Ka faa jaa chaali Juda ni Bɛnjamin dee maa ni nɛra la maa n lii Ɛfram, Manasɛ ani Simɛɔn dizi la n wa soge ba be la. Nɛkpila maanii faa ballɛ di wa jaa Koori Asa ni, di so Izrɛl hɛri, u kora dii saŋa, dikuu baŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du u benii wia.

ref: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem.
text: A nɛra maa faa wa chaali Jɛrusalɛm, Asa kora dii binni fidaanuehiŋ, baaguzi ahorohiŋ biini.

ref: The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns.
text: Ba faa hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini lugɔ ba danna hiŋ u ni, di chaasi, di huuh bɛŋkunazi ni bensunozi.

ref: Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
text: Juda hina maa bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ a guŋ wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ ni biinihuŋŋu, di faa ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi bɔr siaahmu ni, di nau. Awia, Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa bampirsɔna ba sogaa biini.

ref: Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
text: Koori Asa faa wir u naa Maakaa lii wiche biini, dikuu uŋ faa baŋ vughaaŋ Asɛra n chummɛ daa, di ra kuaruu wia. Koori Asa faa ŋmɛŋ a daarɛ ta, di kuuguu, di kpau ga fuuh Kidrɔn Waluu biini.

ref: As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel.
text: Haali, uŋ faa waa a vuga kuaribɔra chɔkkɛ a giŋgimee nyuuni Izrɛl gba, ka u bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, ú de dui maa biini.

ref: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
text: U faa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ kuŋkuaraa la, u ni u mɛɛ n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi labuu du Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini.

ref: There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
text: Laal faa waa kaa hoo, di Koori Asa kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anuehiŋ biini lɛi.

ref: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
text: Denii Koori Asa jaa kpa saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia daama dauribɔra ani u himmaa kooridia hora di jaa, di kpaa hum dí ba la Siiria Koori Bɛn Hadad la n faa du Damaskus di ra di kora la be, di ga ŋɔ,

ref: “I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
text: “Gil n nii dɔɔ nuukpaŋ gunla n mɛɛ ni i mɛɛ n faa dɔɔwɛ la. Awia, n na sunziibuu saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ naa, ka gil i ni Izrɛl Koori Baasa nuukpaŋ la tuŋ. Gunnɛ niŋ gil ú lizi u laallɔɔra lii n hɛri.”

ref: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept.
text: Koori Bɛn Hadad nuu Koori Asa nua la, di hum u laallɔɔra nabɔnzi, bá ga lɔ Izrɛl laal. Ba faa ga kpegli Ijɔn, Dan, Abɛl Mam ani Naftali bolzenaa la n ɛɛ ba kuna dauribɔra la maa.

ref: When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
text: Koori Baasa n wa nuu guŋ, u faa gil Rama mai.

ref: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood. Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
text: Koori Asa n wa nuu guŋ, u gil Juda hina maa la Rama, di ga chi bia ani daazi la maa Koori Baasa n faa kpawɛɛ di ra ma la ba. U kpaa ma Gɛba ni Mizpa.

ref: Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said: You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hanani faa ba Koori Asa be, di wa ŋɔ, “Dikuu hiŋ dɛlli Siiria koori ka gil Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum wia, hàá ka wer kpegli Siiria laallɔɔra.

ref: Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them.
text: Itiopia ni Libia hina laallɔɔra faa kpillɔɔ, di dɔɔ laal torkozi ni zagtinna, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge maa. Ka hiŋ faa dɛlli Kɔraawiizi wia, u faa kpa baabuu du i nonee biini.

ref: The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
text: Kɔraawiizi ra du nɛr maa wiɛɛlaa taurɛ durnya naa biini, di ra tɛɛ banla maa bampiree n lawuu nɛnnɛ fɔŋŋa. Ka i ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ. Awia, di haŋ lii zinaa di ra la, i daŋ du laal biini.”

ref: When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people. Asa Dies (
text: Koori Asa n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ faa fuuh Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hanani ni werge maa, u lawuu tɔ dia. A guŋ saŋaa Koori Asa faa jaa ra sunni a nɛra baŋhina werge maa. Koori Asa siu wia

ref: Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
text: Koori Asa kora dii saŋa, u wiɛɛlaa di lii u lugli saŋa di ga hel u tuna, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda ani Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help.
text: U kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni kabɛlhiŋ biini, wiila aŋhina faa lau u naazii. Haali u wiila hiŋ n faa ɛɛ siaahmu werge gba, ka u faa waa Kɔraawiizi suŋŋɛɛ ú hiinuu, ka faa ra nyiŋŋi alaanfia nɛchaara be.

ref: Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
text: Ba huguu bii bɔɔ bɛl uŋ faa tukke dau u hiŋ, Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ la biini. Ba faa kpaubuu dau kunchɔɔrikuŋ la baŋ mizɛɛ ni kunsɔɔhrisuma aŋhina ni tulaalenanaa. U lee biini, u nɛra faa chem ninzenne di wiiu.

ref: He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
text: U faa gillɔɔ laallɔɔra du Juda bolzenaa la maa, baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa la biine. Di faa gil baŋhina so Juda hɛri yeŋa ani Ɛfram bola la u mɛɛ Koori Asa n faa kpeglee di foozi la.

ref: When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat
text: Ka faa ra hum Kɔraawiizi la u mɛɛ n faa ra hum la, di ra hiŋ u baglaazi, ka gil Izrɛl hina wiɛɛlaa.

ref: and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected,
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil u kora chi nɛnnɛ, u dɔɔ a hɛri fɔŋŋa. Juda hina maa ɔɔ faa kpa kuna di wàá sunzuu, u faa dɔɔ daama ani girme werge maa.

ref: he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
text: U bampirii faa lau Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ nɛnnɛ. U faa kaa chɔgi vuga kuaribɔra ani vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa, Juda hɛri.

ref: Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along.
text: U faa gil Levi dee, Sɛmaaya, Nɛtania, Zɛbadia, Asahɛl, Sɛmiramɔf, Jɛhɔnatan, Adonija, Tobija, Tɔb Adonija ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina Ɛlisama ni Jɛhɔram jaa ba ni.

ref: They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
text: Ba faa kpa Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni hɔŋ la, di gaagi Juda hɛri bola maa, di ra bagli a nɛra.

ref: The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa gil ɔnsii chol hɛssi hina la maa n bar Juda hina ni. Awia, ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá ba wa lɔ Koori Jɛhɔsafat laal.

ref: where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers
text: ani diwee ni ba kunnyiŋŋaa aŋhina werge Juda bolkpila maa biine. U faa gillɔɔ nɛra la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ du Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans. Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had
text: Kennaabuu u faa lizi u laallɔɔra lii domeezi biine. Di lii Juda domee biini, Adnaa faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaahoro sitɔɔri,

ref: Jehohanan was second in command, with
text: Jɛhɔhanan faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ ni tokkoanaazu sitɔɔri,

ref: Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with
text: Zikri biibaal Amasia la n kpa u hiŋ tɛɛ lugɔ u danna hum Kɔraawiizi la, ge ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ sitɔɔri,

ref: Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had
text: Di lii Bɛnjamin domee biini, Ɛliada n faa ɛɛ laallɔkpeg, faa ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfaanɛɛ nabɔma,

ref: Jehozabad was second in command, with
text: di kpa Jɛhɔzabad, u ge ɛɛ laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokkoanaazu,

ref: These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
text: A laallɔɔra naabuu a koori faa dɔɔ di jaa banla n faa du a bola la baŋ ma koŋlaa baraa, Juda hɛri maa la.

ref: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
text: Denii Izrɛl Koori Ahab ni Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat, faa kpa la Ramɔf Giliad.

ref: One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead,
text: Binni aŋhina n wa bɛrɛɛ, u la bolzeŋ Samaria, ú ga na Koori Ahab. Koori Ahab faa kpu peeza ani nauna di hɔɔhri u ni u nɛra, ka suŋŋuu lugɔ ú ga lɔ Ramɔf Giliad laal.

ref: and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?” “Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command.
text: Izrɛl Koori Ahab, faa pɛɛzi Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat, “I daŋ la ga hiiniŋ ya lɔ Ramɔf Giliad hinaa?” Juda Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ, “N nii maa ɛɛ kpannɛ, n nɛra ɛɛ i nɛraa. Yaa daŋ hiinii lɔ a laal.”

ref: But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
text: Koori Jɛhɔsafat ŋɔ Izrɛl koori be, “Pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi na mɔɔ.”

ref: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
text: Ka Koori Jɛhɔsafat pɛɛzi, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ maa waa hoo ɛŋ, yaa n niŋ pɛɛzuu naa?”

ref: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.

text: Denii Koori Jɛhɔsafat faa siu, ba huguu u naabaala hugribɔr la, Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini. Ka u biibaal Jɛhɔram faa kpa u gawa di di a kora.

ref: King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah.
text: Koori Jɛhɔram niwizii faa Azaria, Jɛhiɛl, Zɛkaria, Azariahu, Maikil ani Sɛfatia. Izrɛl Koori Jɛhɔsafat biibaalaa faa bannii maa.

ref: years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
text: Koori Jɛhɔram kora dii saŋa, Ɛdɔm hina faa vɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra sɛɛirɛ, ka tɔ ba himmaa koori.

ref: The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa gil Filisti ni Lɔrbizi la n faa soge dugli Itiopia hina la n faa soge muuzeŋ nua la, faa ba wa lɔ Koori Jɛhɔram laal.

ref: Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
text: Ba mɛɛ faa tɛɛ baabuu saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, kuna la n dɔɔ tɔna ani Juda bolzeŋkpega la. Ama, u faa kpa a koraa tɛɛ Jɛhɔram, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu faa u biibambinabɔma.

ref: After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders.
text: Saŋa la Koori Jɛhɔram n wa chigɛ nɛnnɛ, u kpu u niuna maa ani Izrɛl nabɔnzi baŋhina.

ref: Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong,
text: U faa ra hiŋ Izrɛl koora ŋmɛnizii, gunla Koori Ahab diahina n faa ɛɛwɛ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa kpa Koori Ahab biihaannɛ, di faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa di zuu Kɔraawiizi ni.

ref: but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
text: Ka nua la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid la wia, u faa waa nyiŋŋi ú chɔgi Koori Deevid dia. U faa ŋɔ nuarɛ lugɔ u daŋ ɔɔ gil u naana bɛl di kora di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night,
text: Awia, Koori Jɛhɔram, u nabɔnzi ani u laal torkozi maa faa la de. Ka Ɛdɔm hina la faa go u ni u torkozi nabɔnzi la, ka u izi hamuŋa ni di suahzi ga ba baambaaŋ chɔ.

ref: but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time. Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
text: Haali ni zinaa, Ɛdɔm hina waa kaa ra sɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra. A guŋ saŋa himmaanii bolzeŋ Libna hina gba faa waa kaa ra sɛɛ Juda hina dɔɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, Koori Jɛhɔram faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la u naabaala n faa ra hum la wiarɛ ta.

ref: Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
text: U faa kaa ma vuga kuaribɔra genii Juda hɛri giŋgimee nyuuni, di gil Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina leu, di ra kuari vugkpila, ka gil Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa.

ref: One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said: I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather.
text: Koori Jɛhɔram faa na hɔŋ lii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija be. A hɔŋ ra ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi la i naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ra hum la ŋɔ, ‘Haa i mɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔsafat gɛɛ i naabaal Juda Koori Asa hiŋaa la hiŋŋɛ,

ref: Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
text: ka hiŋ Izrɛl koora hiŋaa la, di kaa gil Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina ra kuari vuga gunla Koori Ahab n faa ra ɛɛ la. I kaa kpu i himmaa niuna n ɛɛ i mɛɛ domee hina di bɔi.

ref: Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr i ni i nɛra, i biizi ani i haana digna, di chɔgi kuna la maa hiŋ dɔɔwɛ.

ref: You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
text: Hiwiilchɔgii daŋ lau i looree, di tɔɔrii guŋŋ a wa lii chaaŋ.’ ”

ref: They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
text: Ba faa wa lɔ baa laal di kpegli baa, ka chi kuna la maa n du a kooridia, u biibaala ani u haana maa kaali. Ba faa waa biibaal maa gillɛ tɛu, di u biibambijiga Ahazia bɛŋ lɛi.

ref: After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease.
text: Annii maa harbɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi faa gil hiwiilchɔgii la n waa chaai dɔɔwɛ, wa lau Koori Jɛhɔram looree.

ref: About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
text: A guŋ saŋa biini, binni anɛɛ n wa helle, a wiila faa gil u looree wa lii chaaŋ, u faa siu ni bɔwiila werge. U nɛra faa waa ninzeŋ chemme di kpau girme, ú lee biini, gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ u naabaala la.

ref: and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot,
text: Koori Jehu n gaa tɛr Koori Ahab diahina digna, u na Juda nabɔnzi ani Koori Ahazia lulla biibaala la n ɔɔ ra binni Koori Ahazia ni la, u faa kpu ba maa.

ref: then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord. There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah. Queen Athaliah of Judah (
text: Ka Koori Jehu ni u laallɔɔra la jaa lii di ra nyiŋŋi Koori Ahazia. Ba faa ga nau, di u suah bolzeŋ Samaria biini. Ba lawuu wa tɛɛ Jehu, u gil ba kpuu. Ba faa huguu nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “U ɛɛ Koori Jɛhɔsafat la n faa nɔŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ni u biini maa la naannaa.” Guŋ wia, nɛr maa faa waa kaa hoo Koori Ahazia domee la biini, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa nɛnnɛ, lugɔ ú wer di kora. Wiche Atalia ni Joas wia

ref: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi be alugɔ Koori Ahab n faa ɛɛwɛ la, dikuubɛɛwiai, u mɛɛ n faa wa siuwɛ la, Ahab domee hinaa faa ɛɛ nɛra la n na biruu liize, guŋ gil u chol.

ref: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
text: Ba nuarɛ Koori Ahazia faa kaa hiŋ, u ni Izrɛl Koori Ahab biibaal Koori Joram faa la, di ga lɔ Siiria Koori Hazɛl laal, Ramɔf Giliad hɛri, ka Siiria hina faa du Koori Joram pira la.

ref: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
text: Koori Ahazia n faa laŋŋɛ u ga na Koori Joram la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi gil u kora chol. Koori Ahazia n ga helle la, u ni Koori Joram faa lii bá ga chem Nimsi biibaal Jehu ni, unla Kɔraawiizi n faa lizɛɛ lugɔ ú chɔgi Koori Ahab domee la.

ref: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
text: Ka Koori Jɛhɔram biihaaŋ Jɛhɔsɛba, faa suahzi lau Koori Ahazia biibaal Joas lii a kooribiibaala biini, saŋa la baŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi bá kpu baa la. U faa kpa u ni nɛr la n na kpogluu la suah chɔɔribɔr bɛl biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, Koori Jɛhɔram biihaaŋ Jɛhɔsɛba n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada haaŋ, di ɛɛ Koori Ahazia niuhambie, faa lau a bie suah. Awia, Atalia faa waa wette nau kpu.

ref: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
text: Koori Ahazia maa Atalia n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ u biibaal siuwɔɔ la, u faa jaa ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ u dim Juda kooridiahina maa.

ref: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
text: U ni baa faa suah Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, binni anumbɛl. A saŋa, di Atalia dɔɔ a hɛri fɔŋŋa di ra di kora.

ref: These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem
text: Ba faa gaagi Juda hɛri maa, di chaali Levi dee ani Izrɛl domeezi nabɔnzi lii a bolzenaa maa biine. Baŋ wa chaali Jɛrusalɛm,

ref: Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada ni u biibaala faa kpogli a koori biibaal hiŋ di lii baŋgia, di kpa koorikahuro hiu, di kpa Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Hɔŋ la tɛu, ka sii lugɔ waabuu jaa koori, di fug nuu waari u nyuu, ka chaasi di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔ́raawiizi tɛɛ a koori miibɔɔjaŋ!”

ref: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
text: Kenne ii ɛɛ, di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee la haŋ la huma Heezaa Hɔpizii la. Ii daŋ bargi iihinaa bɔra ahoro, ii bɔkpaŋ ra du dominuuzenaa la tau.

ref: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
text: A hɛri nɛra maa bɔra jaa sɔɔni werge maa, a bolzeŋ maa faa jaa ɛɛ surumm, dikuu baŋ kpu Wiche Atalia wia.

ref: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
text: A binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa bagli u fɔŋŋa. U faa gillɔɔ u ni laallɔɔra kalfazi nabɔnzi ɛɛ nuukpaŋ. Baabuu Jeroham biibaal Azaria, Jɛhɔhanan biibaal Ismɛl, Ɔbɛd biibaal Azaria, Adaaya biibaal Maasɛya ani Zikri biibaal Ɛlisafat.

ref: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
text: ba ni a koori faa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini. Denii Jɛhɔyada ŋɔ ba be, “A koori biibaallɛ dɛkkɛ un niŋ kpa u gawa di di a kora, gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ Koori Deevid naannaa niŋ ɔɔ di a kora la.

ref: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
text: Bɔkpaŋ du kooridia, bɔkpaŋ ga chi dominua la banna yir Dia Zɛɛ Dominua la. Ka banla n kawɛɛ ge jaa du Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋizi la biine.

ref: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
text: Nɛr maa gilɛɛ waa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini, di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la n dɔɔ huma a hɔl la bɛŋ lɛi. Baa waa daŋ wer zuu de, dikuu baŋ sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be wia. Ka banla maa n kawɛɛ la waa, bá ra hiŋ gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa la.

ref: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
text: Levi dee labuu niŋ ɔɔ kpogli ba dɔŋkuna chi bar a koori, di ra guuu. Nɛr la maa n niŋ zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, ií kpuu. Ií ɔɔ du a koori be, bɔr la maa unna la.”

ref: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
text: A Levi dee ni Juda hina la maa ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada n bagli baa la. Ba bɛl maa faa kpogli u baala, banla n faa ra la huma Heezaa Hɔpizii ani banla n na izi huma, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa waa a suge bɛl maa tawɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ, bá kpo.

ref: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
text: Denii u faa kpa kandaazi, laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ani a jigzi la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ɛɛ Koori Deevid hora la, di tɛɛ a laallɔɔra kalfazi nabɔnzi.

ref: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
text: U faa gillɔɔ a guure bɛl maa kpogli u dɔŋkuŋ, di chi bar a koori, di dugli mbusu lizibɔr la ni Kɔraawiizi Dia wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere, di ga hel wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag keŋkere.

ref: As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple.
text: Wiche Atalia n wa nuu a nɛra n na kɔɔ di ra chɔ, ka ra chaasi di ra chɔli a koori la, u lii la ba be, Kɔraawiizi Dia la,

ref: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
text: di ga na, di a koorii chigɛ pɛli ligii la n ɛɛ koora hor la. Ka a nabɔnzi ni bensunohuuhra chi u kɛra. A hɛri nɛra maa ge bɔra sɔɔni, ba ra huuh bensunozi. Ka yiryitta tɔ ba see di ra lɔ kuna di ra chɔluu werge maa. Denii Wiche Atalia tɛr u koorilaala piili, ka ra pogzi, di ra ŋɔ, “Hɛri chɔkkɔɔ! Hɛri chɔkkɔɔ!”

ref: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada faa hum laallɔɔra kalfazi nabɔnzi la, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ií lawuu lii baŋgia, a tauduura la be. Ií kpu nɛr la maa ge n na hiŋuu.” Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa kpuu Kɔraawiizi Dia naa biini.”

ref: She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
text: Awia, ba lawuu ga hel kooridia dominuuzeŋ la banna yir Zagra Dominua la, di kpuu de.

ref: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada jaa gil Koori Joas ni a nɛra ni Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ nuukpaŋ lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛra.

ref: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
text: Denii a hɛri nɛra maa faa jaa la vug Baal dia, di ga purgi u maa, di purgi u mbusu lizibɔra ani de vuga la maa, di kpu vug Baal kizeehiŋ Matan, mbusu lizibɔra see.

ref: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada, faa jaa kpa Kɔraawiizi Dia wikpoglaa maa wia du Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la nonee biini, gunla Koori Deevid n baglɛɛ la. Baabuu niŋ ɔɔ kaa ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Moosis hɔŋ biini la. Ba daŋ ɔɔ dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di ra yir yira a saŋa gunla Koori Deevid n dauwɛ la.

ref: Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
text: U faa lizi Kɔraawiizi Dia doominuuguure genii, bá gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr la maa n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be, wàá zuu de.

ref: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
text: U jaa yir laallɔɔra kalfazi nabɔnzi, nabɔnzenaa, a hɛri nabɔnzi ani a hɛri nɛra maa, ba kpogli a koori lii Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga a kooridia dominua la banna yir Chiŋ Dominuuzeŋ la di zuu, di lau a koori soŋŋi a koorikara ni.

ref: While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right.
text: Koori Joas faa ɛɛ wideŋlaare Kɔraawiizi be, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Jɛhɔyada de dui maa biini.

ref: Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
text: Koori Joas ni Jɛhɔyada ɔɔ faa kpaa di ra tɛɛ huŋhunna la n na hum Kɔraawiizi Dia huma la. Ba faa kpaa di kpa maara, kapintazi ani nɛra la n zum lugbia ni danyɛ huma, bá bir kuari a Dia.

ref: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
text: Ba huguu koora hugribɔr, Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la biini, dikuu winanaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ Izrɛl hɛri tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni u Dia la wia. Koori Joas biinikpola wia

ref: And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
text: A saŋa naa, di hahbiinikpola hiŋ Wiche Atalia hiŋra faa ku Kɔraawiizi Dia, di zuu paa a Dia kunnanaananaa la, di ga hum vug Baal la huma.

ref: Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
text: Jɛhɔyada faa nyiŋŋi haana banɛɛrɛ tɛu, u lul biibaala ni biihaana.

ref: Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Koori Joas faa ra nyiŋŋi u kaa bir kuari Kɔraawiizi Dia la, ú du wer.

ref: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
