text: U ɔɔ faa lizi mbusuzii di fuuh a kuna Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu biini, di lau u biibaala ra lizi mbusuzi di ra fuuh baa, di ra chanzi wikuna la nɛra la Kɔraawiizi n faa duŋŋɛɛ lii a hɛri n na ɛɛ, di Izrɛl hina faa ra ba la.

ref: Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them. The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed
text: Hɔpizikpaŋ biini, Rɛmalia biibaal Izrɛl Koori Pɛka, faa kpu Juda laallɔɔra kagboŋa kalfa ni tokko, dikuu Juda hina n faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la wia.

ref: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
text: Haali ii jaa ra nyiŋŋi ii gil Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina birgi ii yoma. Ka ii waa zummɛ lugɔ ii gba ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ninɛɛaa?

ref: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
text: Awia, ií ra nuu n be, nɛra naa iin laurɛɛ naa ɛɛ ii lullaa. Ií gil ba bir kaali, di guŋ lɛi, Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛr ii digna ni baaŋfuuih werge.”

ref: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
text: Denii Ɛfram nabɔnzi baŋhina, Jɛhɔhanan biibaal Azaria, Mɛsilɛmɔf biibaal Bɛrɛkia, Salum biibaal Jɛhizkia ani Hadlai biibaal Amasa, faa lii chem a laallɔɔra ni, di ge hau ba ni, di ŋɔ,

ref: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
text: “Ií gilɛɛ wa kpogli nɛra la iin laurɛɛ la di ra ba ɛŋ, di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ di bilchɔg Kɔraawiizi be. Ii ra nyiŋŋuu yaa wichɔgaa kaa jaa yaa bilchɔg nii? Yaa chɔgri teŋ kannɔɔ werge, u baaŋ ge kaa ra fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge maa.”

ref: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
text: Awia, a laallɔɔra faa gil a nɛra ani ba kuna la maa baŋ paagɛɛ la, a nabɔnzi ni nɛra la maa n chaalɛɛ la sibɔɔ.

ref: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help (
text: Denii a baala la sɔna baŋ yirgɛɛ la faa lɛɛ a nɛra, di binni a kuŋfoozaa biini, di lizi laala laali banla n faa ra vol chakpalli. Ba faa tɛɛ baabuu laala, gawa, diwee, niinyɔɔlii ani nuu la baŋ kpawɛɛ ra tɔ ŋmɛra. Banla ge maa n faa gɛrgɛɛ, ba kpa baa soŋŋi kauzi ni, di bir kpogli baa la ba himmaa hɛri Jɛriko la banna yir Abɛ Daazi Bolzeŋ la, ka bir kaali Samaria.

ref: Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places. Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help.
text: ka Filisti hina ge faa wa lɔ ba giŋgimee zɛɛ bola ni Juda wiifurii nodig wiikakag hina, di paagi ba kuna. Ba faa kpegli Bɛf Sɛmɛs, Aijalɔn, Gɛdɛrɔf, di kpa Soko bolzenaa jaa, Timna, Gimzo ani a kɛraa boljigzi maa hina jaa, ka so a biine.

ref: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa du Juda hinaa hiihzi, dikuu Juda Koori Ahaz wia. U faa gillɔɔ biinikpola wiɛɛlaa nyaŋŋi Juda biini, di faa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa.

ref: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
text: Koori Ahaz faa kpa Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna la aŋhina, kooridia hora ani anla uŋ lɛɛwɛ u nabɔnzi be, di tɛɛ Asiiria koorizeŋ la. Ka guŋ gba faa wɔɔ hiinee.

ref: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
text: Haali Koori Ahaz n faa du tɔɔrɔɔ biini la gba, ka u faa nyaa wibiire Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
text: U faa lizi mbusuzii di ra tɛɛ Siiria hina la n faa kpegluu la vuga, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa fɛwɔɔrɛ, “Siiria koora vuga hiini baabuu, awia, n danna kuaraa, á hiini n ge.” Ka aabuu faa gillɛ u ni Izrɛl hina maa chol la.

ref: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
text: Koori Ahaz faa wa chaali Kɔraawiizi Dia bɔmbɔga la di kaali, ka kar a Dia dominuuzi, ka ma vuga mbusu lizibɔra ŋmɛnikɛraa maa, Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
text: Juda bola maa biinee u faa ma vuga kuaribɔra, di ra lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa di ra tɛɛa. Aabuu faa gillɛ Kɔraawiizi la u naabaala n na hum la baaŋ fuuh werge maa la.

ref: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
text: U kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ, u huŋhunnaa di lii u lugli di ga hel u tuna, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Juda ni Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
text: Koori Ahaz faa siu, ba huguu bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, ka ba faa wɔɔ hukke Izrɛl koora hugribɔr la, ka u biibaal Hɛzɛkia faa kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
text: U faa ɛɛ wideŋlaare Kɔraawiizi be, gunla u naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
text: Denii ba jaa zuu ga ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be, “Yaa lizi Kɔraawiizi Dia maa ni mbusuzi lizaa kuna fuuhribɔr, u kuna ni paanuunanaananaa la baŋ ɔɔ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi tɛɛbul la, ni u ge kuna maa doŋaa ha.

ref: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa gillɔɔ Levi dee la du a Kɔraawiizi Dia la, di ɔɔ kpogli kuŋyigzaa, kemzi ani janjalanzi, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ga Koori Deevid, u sinaari Gad ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Netan be, di bagli la.

ref: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
text: Saŋa la a mbusuzi lizaa n wa tunnɛ, a koori ni nɛra la maa n du de la giŋŋi hɛri, di jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
text: U faa kaa chaali Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee, Kɔraawiizi Dia wiifurii diŋŋee la biini,

ref: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
text: di ŋɔ, “Ií ra nuu n be, Levi dee! Ií sɔ iihinaa di lizi ii doŋa, di lizi Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n na hum la Dia ge doŋa ha. Ií lizi kunla maa n gillɛ a Bɔnaniinanii la doŋ.

ref: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
text: Yaa naabaala faa waa Kɔraawiizi ra hiŋ ni wibii. Ba faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ u be, di vɛɛu. Ba faa bir hattɛ kpu u Dia la,

ref: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
text: Guŋ wia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina ni, u gil ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii, nɛra nuuzi kpu ba wia alugɔ ii himmaa siwee n nawɛɛ naa.

ref: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
text: Guŋ wiarɛ ba kpu yaa naabaala, ka lauri yaa biizi ni yaa haana kaali hɛrduma la.

ref: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
text: Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń ni Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, ú baaŋfuuih werge la tuŋ yaa ni.

ref: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
text: N biibaala, ií gilɛɛ wa vɛɛ ii huma di ra ta, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi lizi iabuu ŋɔ ií chi u see, di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra tɛu, di tɔ u nɛra la see di ra humuu.”

ref: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
text: Baŋ wa chaali ba lulla, di sɔ bahinaa di lizi doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be la, ba zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la, bá lizi u doŋa ha, ka ú ɛɛ kunnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be, gunla a koori n ŋɔwɛɛ, di lii Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii biini la.

ref: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la faa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la, bá lizi u doŋa ha, ú ɛɛ kunnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be. Ba faa paagi kuna la maa baŋ nawɛɛ an doŋŋe a Dia biini lii diŋŋee. Levi dee la faa chi a maa la Kidrɔn Waluu,

ref: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
text: ka ba faa faari a Dia doŋa lizaa hai, a baagu lugli hɔpizii hiŋ. U hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl, ba hel Kɔraawiizi jaŋgal la. Ba kaa kpa hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi ge, di lizi a Dia himmaa ge doŋa ha, ú ɛɛ kunnaniinanii Kɔraawiizi be, di faa jaa tuŋ a huma maa, a baagu lugli hiŋ hɔpizaa fidaanumbɛlhiŋ hɔl.

ref: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
text: Yaa kossi kuna la maa Koori Ahaz n faa lizɛɛ, u wibii nyaai saŋa labuu, di lizi a maa doŋa. A maanii chigɛ Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la see, filaŋkeŋ.”

ref: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzimpikke ni, Koori Hɛzɛkia chaali a bolzeŋ nabɔnzi, ba la Kɔraawiizi Dia la.

ref: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
text: Ba faa lau nabala aniidaanɛɛ, pebala aniidaanɛɛ, peballi aniidaanɛɛ ani bubala aniidaanɛɛ ba, bá wa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ u kora diiribɔr, Kɔraawiizi Dia ani Juda maa. A koori faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n ɛɛ Aarɔn naanna la be lugɔ ba kpa a sela lizi mbusu, Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la ni.

ref: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
text: ka lau buuna la ban niŋ kpa lizi wichɔgaa mbusu ge, di ba a koori ni nɛra la n chaalɛɛ la see. Ba kpa ba nonee sagzi a ni.

ref: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la jaa kɔrgaa, di kpa a chal waari mbusu lizibɔr ni, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa kuna tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, a koorii faa ŋɔ dí ba ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
text: Awia, Levi dee la faa chi kpogli Koori Deevid kunlɔɔlaa la, ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ge faa kpogli ba bensunozi.

ref: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa ŋɔ lugɔ bá lizi mbusu, di fuuh a kuna, mbusu lizibɔr la ni. Baŋ faari mbusu lizaa la, ba ra yir yira di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di ra huuh bensunozi, di ra lɔ Izrɛl Koori Deevid kunlɔɔlaa la di ra du.

ref: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia ni a nabɔnzi la faa ŋɔ Levi dee la be lugɔ bá kpa Koori Deevid ni Sinaari Asaf wiŋɔzi la, di chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Awia, ba faa yir yira ni bɔsɔna di chɔli Kɔraawiizi, di willi ba nyuuni di jaami.

ref: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋwaa, ii jaa kpa iihinaarɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Awia, ií kpa ii mbusu lizaa ni ii jaaŋ tɛɛi kuna ba Kɔraawiizi Dia.” A nɛra faa kpa ba mbusuzi lizaa ni ba jaaŋ tɛɛi kuna ni kuna la banla ge bampiree n tɛɛ baa lugɔ bá kpa lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ba.

ref: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la faa waa kpil lugɔ ba wer kir mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa la maa. Awia, ba lulla Levi dee la faa hiini baa guŋŋ a huma wa tuŋ. Denii ba kaa lizi a kizeehina baŋhina jaa, di sɔ ba doŋa ha. Levi dee la siweere faa aahwɛ ni bahinaa sɔi di lizi ba doŋa ha wia kaali Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la.

ref: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
text: Mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa ni ola nuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu ani sintaalii la n ɔɔ jaa mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa ni la, faa kannɔɔ werge maa. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia huma faa kaa bir chi nɛnnɛ.

ref: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia ni a nɛra maa bɔra faa sɔɔni, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ baa la wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wia maanii faa ɛɛwɛ manaŋ.

ref: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
text: Guŋ wia, ba faa sii Izrɛl hɛri maa, di lii bolzeŋ Bɛɛsiba guŋŋ di ga hel Dan, di ra yir a nɛra maa lugɔ bá ba Jɛrusalɛm, di wa di Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la Gillikaali Hɔpizizeŋ la. Nɛkpila faa wɔɔ ra di gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ dau la.

ref: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
text: A koori ni u nabɔnzi faa gil ba balaa kpa a hɔna gaagi Izrɛl ni Juda hɛssi maa biine. Kenne ba faa sɛbi a hɔna biine, “Izrɛl hina, iabuu kawɛɛ di lii Asiiria hina laal la baŋ wa lɔ yaa la biini. Awia, ií bir ba Kɔraawiizi la Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb n na hum la be, ú ge bir ba ii be.

ref: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
text: Ií gilɛɛ dɔɔ dignikpega gunla ii naabaala n faa dɔɔwɛɛ la. Ií ra sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔɔra. Ií ba u Dia la uŋ lizi u doŋa ha, u ɛɛ Diinaniinanii la biini saŋaa saŋa maa la. Ií ra jaami Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Guŋ daŋ gil ú lizi u baaŋfuuih werge la ii ni.

ref: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
text: Di ii bittɔ ba u be, u daŋ gil banla n lauri ii lulla ni ii biizi la na ba sinyɛna, di gil ba kaa bir ba hɛri naa biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la ra na nɛra sinyɛnaa. Wàá bir u har kpu ia, di ii bittɔ ba u be.”

ref: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
text: Ama, baala baŋhina faa lii Asɛ, Manasɛ ani Zɛbulɔn dizi biine, di sɔɔni siwii, ka la Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
text: Juda ge biini, Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa faa du a nɛra benii, ú tɛɛ baa nuukpaŋ, bá wer ɛɛ wia la maa a koori ni u nabɔnzi n ŋɔ ba ɛɛ, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
text: Denii nɛkpila maa faa chaali Jɛrusalɛm biini, baaguzi anɛɛhiŋ biini, bá di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa la.

ref: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
text: Ba faa purgi vuga mbusu lizibɔra ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔra la maa Jɛrusalɛm biini, di paagaa ga ta Kidrɔn Waluu biini.

ref: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa nuu Koori Hɛzɛkia suŋŋaa la, di gil a nɛra wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, waa baa tɔɔrɛɛ.

ref: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
text: Izrɛl hina la n faa du Jɛrusalɛm la, faa di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ ani bɔsɔna werge maa, ka Levi dee la ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la yir yira hɔpizi biimaa, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di lɔ kuna di ra du.

ref: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa du Levi dee la bɔkpega, dikuu baŋ baglɛɛ lugɔ ba zum Kɔraawiizi humaa nɛnnɛ wia. Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ biini, ba faa ra di ba diiribɔra, di ra lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la.

ref: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
text: Juda hina la maa n faa chaali de la bɔra faa sɔɔni. Baabuu Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee, banla maa n faa lii Izrɛl, hɔɔhra la n faa du Izrɛl ani Juda hina maa.

ref: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
text: Bɔsɔna werge faa du Jɛrusalɛmnɛ, di lii Izrɛl Koori Deevid biibaal Koori Solomɔn saŋa la guŋŋ di wa hel a guŋ saŋa hiŋ. Guŋ dɔŋ faa haa waa ɛɛwɛ Jɛrusalɛm biini maa.

ref: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la faa izi chi, di kissi a nɛra. Kɔraawiizi faa nuu ba suŋŋaa lii u bolnaniinanii la n du chiŋ la.

ref: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa bargi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la, di tɛɛ bɛl maa u huma. Banla n ninna lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, banla n ninna lizi dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi, banla n niŋ ɔɔ tɔ nɛra see bá ra jaami, banla n ninna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ ani banla ge n niŋ chi u Dia dominuuzenaa yir yira di ra chɔluu.

ref: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
text: Ba bichalli, ba haana ani biibaala ni biihaana la maa sɔnaa faa jaa ba lulla ŋmɛnizi wia hɔna biine, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maanii faa sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni wibii.

ref: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
text: U faa ŋɔ banla n du Jɛrusalɛm biini la benii lugɔ ba ɔɔ kpa sunzaa kuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la hora di ra ba. Gunnɛ niŋ gil ba ɔɔ wer di ra hum gunla Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni la n na bagli la.

ref: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
text: A Hɔpizizeŋ dii n wa tunnɛ, Izrɛl hina la maa n faa du de la, lii di la Juda bola di ga purgi vuga bia, di ŋmɛnni vughaaŋ Asɛra daabaŋlaa ge ta, di chɔgi a giŋgimee nyuuni vuga kuaribɔra ani mbusu lizibɔra la maa n du Juda, Bɛnjamin, Ɛfram ani Manasɛ hɛssi maa biine la. Baŋ wa chɔgi a maa tuŋ, Izrɛl hina la bir kpo ba bola.

ref: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
text: A koori himmaanii faa lizi sela lii u himmaa sela biini, bá kpa di ra lizi mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa chɔɔzizi, duaninzi, Heezaa Hɔpizii la, Baagufalii Hɔpizizeŋ ani Hɔpizizenaa dii la maa wia baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni Hɔŋ biini la.

ref: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
text: Izrɛl hina la n wa nuu guŋ, ba sɛɛ kakpaŋ, di lizi mia la baŋ felee kum, siŋfalaa, nuu, huuhnuu ani pattikuna la maa baŋ felee kum ba, ni biinihuŋŋuu. Ba faa ba kuna ninɛɛ werge, di faa bargi kuna la maa ge baŋ dɔɔwɛ bɔra fizi, di kpa a bɔkpaŋkpaŋa wa tɛɛ baa.

ref: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
text: Nɛra la n lii Izrɛl ni Juda, ka so Juda bola la ge maa faa kpa ba kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa lii ba nauna, peeza biine ani kunnanaananaa la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la ba. Ba chaalaa dauri kulululuzi.

ref: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
text: Ba faa faarɔɔrɛ di ra lizi a kuna baaguzi ahorohiŋ biini guŋŋ di ga hel baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini.

ref: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia ni u nabɔnzi n wa na kuna la baŋ lizɛɛ puugi la, ba chɔli Kɔraawiizi, ka kissi Izrɛl hina la.

ref: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la kuna la n puugee kulululuzi la wia.

ref: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Azaria la n lii Zadɔk naanna biini la ŋɔ, “Saŋa la a nɛra n faarɛɛ lizi a kuna di ra ba Kɔraawiizi Dia la, yaa na diweere werge di di, ka ka, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kissi u nɛraa. Aabuu baani a ka werge la.”

ref: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa ŋɔ dí ba ma kuna dauri bɔra diini Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. Ba faa ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
text: Banla ge n faa ra hiini baabuu, Jɛhiɛl, Azazia, Nahaf, Asahɛl, Jɛrimɔf, Jɔzabad, Ɛliɛl, Ismakia, Mahaf ani Bɛnaaya. Koori Hɛzɛkia ni Kɔraawiizi Dia nabɔma Azariaa faa lizi baa.

ref: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
text: Imna biibaal Kɔrɛ n ɛɛ Levi naana di faa ra guu Wiifurii Dominuuzeŋ labuu ba lizi u ra binni sunzaazi kuna la baŋ ɔɔ kpa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ni. Di faa kaa ra bɔnni kuna la baŋ kɛɛwɛ ani anla baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la.

ref: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, ba ɔɔ bɔnnaabuu tɛɛ ba baala la n di binni ahoro ka ra sag la, ba sɔna du ba lulla ŋmɛnizi wia hɔna biine, ba maa ɔɔ wer zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini, di ra hum ba hɔpizi biimaa huma, gunla baŋ bargi baa la.

ref: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la waa n faa ɛɛ Aarɔn naanna, ka du koolimbola la n du a bol kɛraa ani bola aŋhina la, ba lizi baalaa, ba ɔɔ bɔnni a kuna tɛɛ unla la maa n ɛɛ baal di du ba biini ani banla maa sɔna baŋ sɛbɛɛ du Levi dee lulla ŋmɛnizi wia hɔna biine la.

ref: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
text: Wia la maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia la huma wia biini gɛɛ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa hiŋaa nɛnnɛ biini, u faa hiŋ Kɔraawiizii ni biinihuŋŋu. Guŋ wia, u faa nyɛɛlɔɔrɛ.

ref: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
text: Denii Asiiria nabɔnzi hiŋ faa kpa Juda hina mɔɔri di mɔɔ guŋ tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina la n soge ba koŋlii ni la lugɔ bá faa ɔnzi baa, di gil ba bɔra huah, bá wer kpegli baa, di dɔɔ a bolzeŋ fɔŋŋa.

ref: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
text: Ií waa nuuwɛ gunla n ni n mɛɛwaa n faa ɛɛ hɛssi aŋhina nɛra laa? A hɛssi hiŋ vuga faa wettoo lɛɛ baa lii n nonee biiniaa?

ref: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
text: Ba faa chaali huŋhunna kpila maa, ba gber a bulli ni gɔŋ la n na pal a hɛri biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Asiiria koora wa na nii werge nyɔɔi?”

ref: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia faa jaa aah siwii di ma a koŋlii la n bar a bolzeŋ la bɔra la n purgee la, di ma diijaŋra hɔŋzi u ni. U faa kaa ma koŋlii bɛl genii lugli hor la harbɔɔ, di ma bɔwillaa ge bar Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la. U faa kuari dɔŋkuna ni laal pɛrɛtuzi ge kpila werge maa.

ref: and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
text: U faa lizi laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ba ra binni a nɛra ni, ka chaali ba maa a bolzeŋ koŋlii dominua bossibaaŋ, di du baa bɔkpega, di ŋɔ,

ref: Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful,
text: “Ií chiiri zɛɛ, di gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra huah. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm Asiiria koorizeŋ ni u laallɔɔrakpila naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, fɔŋŋa la n du yaa be la, kaali unla n du ba benii.

ref: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib ni u laallɔɔra la faa la gaa fɔɔ bolzeŋ Lakis la, u hum u nabɔnzi baŋhina Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia ani nɛra la maa n du u be Jɛrusalɛm la ni amaniye naa,

ref: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
text: “Mìŋ́ Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib ra ŋɔ i benii lugɔ bɛɛ ninɛɛ i dɛllɛi, di haa du Jɛrusalɛm la baŋ fɔɔwɛ biinei?

ref: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
text: Awia, ií gilɛɛ gil Koori Hɛzɛkia dar ia, ii leu. Ií gilɛɛ yarduu, dikuubɛɛwiai, hɛri maa vug haa waa wette lɛɛ u nɛra lii n nonee gɛɛ n mɛɛwaa nonee biini. Ɛrɛɛ á jaa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi la iawaa n na hum la wer lɛɛ ia lii n nonee biinei?”

ref: The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
text: Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib nabɔnzi la faa kaa ŋɔ wia, di gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni u balii Koori Hɛzɛkia maa.

ref: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
text: A koorizeŋ faa kaa sɛbi hɔna chagzi Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la, di ŋɔ, “Gunla a hɛssi la hina vuga n faa waa wette lɛɛ baa lii n nonii biini la, gunnɛ Koori Hɛzɛkia gba vug wàá wer lɛɛ u nɛra lii n nonii biini.”

ref: People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah. Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies (
text: Nɛkpila maa faa kpa sunzaa kuna ba Jɛrusalɛm, di wa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di kaa wa sunzi Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia kuna la n dɔɔ tɔna werge. Di chi a saŋa hiŋ di ra la, a hɛssi maa hina faa jaa ra tɔgzuu. Koori Hɛzɛkia wiila ni u jigsi wia

ref: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, wiila lɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia, u ra nyiŋŋi u siu. Denii u suŋŋi wiizi, Kɔraawiizi nuu u wiisuŋŋaa, di ɛɛ wizeŋ tɛu.

ref: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
text: Ka Koori Hɛzɛkia faa ra jigsi, dikuu guŋ wia, u baga waa hoo winanaa la Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ tɛu la be. Awia, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ faa fuuh u ni Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina maa ni werge.

ref: Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king. Hezekiah's Wealth (
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia ni Jɛrusalɛm hina maa biine faa chɔgi, ba bir lii ba jigsi la biini. Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa waa kaa tɛr ba digna, Koori Hɛzɛkia de dui saŋa.

ref: Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa jaa ɛɛ dɔɔŋ, ba ra tɔgzuu werge maa. Awia, u faa ma u saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, binanaa la yoola n kpolle, u dɔzi tiuzaa kuna, u laallɔɔra pɛrɛtuzenaa ani kuŋkpila maa n dɔɔ tɔna dauribɔra diini.

ref: Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep.
text: U kaa ma kuna dauribɔra diini, ú ra chiŋŋi mia, siŋfalaa ani nuu, di du liga ú ra tɔ u nauna, di ma lonni ge ú ra tɔ u peeza ni buuna.

ref: God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
text: U faa ma bolkpilaa, di dɔɔ sela ni a dizi kpilakpila werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛubuu daama werge.

ref: It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful!
text: Koori Hɛzɛkiaa faa gber Gihɔn bule palli bɔr la, ka faa peri bɔr, u pal ga de di ra tuu Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la wiicholii barii. U wiɛɛlaa maa faa nyɛɛlɔɔrɛ.

ref: Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful. Hezekiah Dies (
text: Ka Babilɔn nabɔnzi n faa hum nɛra bá wa pɛɛzuu wizenaa la Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛ a hɛri biini la, Kɔraawiizi faa gil u ɛɛ u kipar, ú ɛɛu na, di zum wii la n du u bampirii.

ref: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia wiɛɛlaa maa ni gunla uŋ faa hum Kɔraawiizi, ba faa sɛbaabuu du Amɔz biibaal, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya wia nai lugɔ deeza biini la n du Juda ni Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa siu, ba huguu giŋgimii la nyuu Koori Deevid naanna ŋmama n duwɛɛ la. Uŋ wa siuwɛ, Juda ani Jɛrusalɛm hina maanii faa tɔgzuu. Ka u biibaal Manasɛ kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
text: Ka Koori Manasɛ faa gillɔɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina leu, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge maa kaali hɛssi la hina Kɔraawiizi n faa chɔkkɛ, di Izrɛl hina ra ba la.

ref: The people obeyed Manasseh, but they worshiped the Lord at their own shrines.
text: Ka a nɛra faa haa vɛɛ ka ra lizi mbusuzi a vuga kuaribɔra a giŋgimee nyuuni, di jaa ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la bɛŋ.

ref: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Koori Manasɛ kora dii saŋa, wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ ani u wiisuŋŋaa la uŋ suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la unna hum ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi wiŋɔɔlaa baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum sɔŋ biini la maanii, ba faa sɛbi du Izrɛl Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him.
text: Ka u biinichɔg werge hiŋ biini, u faa sɔɔni siwii, Kɔraawiizi la u naabaala n na hum la be, di suŋŋuu ŋɔ ú hinuu.

ref: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
text: U faa bittɔɔ ma vuga kuaribɔra la n du giŋgimee nyuuni, u mɛɛ Koori Hɛzɛkia n faa purgee la. Haali u kaa ma vug Baala mbusu lizibɔra, di baŋzi vughaaŋ Asɛra daazi ge, di ɔɔ faa kaa giŋŋi di ra jaami chinchiŋwilaa maa.

ref: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
text: U faa ma banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ vuga mbusu lizibɔraa Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini, bɔr la wia Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ, “N sɔŋ daŋ du Jɛrusalɛm biini di hanna la saŋa maa la.”

ref: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋizi anɛɛ la maa biinee, u faa ma mbusu lizibɔra tɛɛ chinchiŋwilaa maa.

ref: and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago, God had told David and Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever.
text: Koori Manasɛ faa sɛɛh vug bɛllɛ di chigni Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, bɔr la wia Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Koori Deevid ni u biibaal Solomɔn, “A Dia naa ni Jɛrusalɛm la miŋ lizɛɛ lii Izrɛl dizi maa biinee, ń kpa n sɔŋ du, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
text: N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka gil Izrɛl hina lii hɛri la miŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la, di ba danna du tau di ra ɛɛ gunla maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, di ra hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa n balii Moosis n tɛɛ baa la.”

ref: The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ wia tɛɛ Koori Manasɛ ni u nɛra, ka ba waa nuuwɛ.

ref: So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil Asiiria laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ba wa lɔ baa di lau Koori Manasɛ, di kpa gɔrga du u miizi, ka kpa danyɛ yɔlɔzi vɔɔzuu, di kpogluu kaali Babilɔn.

ref: The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
text: Kɔraawiizi nuu u suŋŋaa la, di gil u bir ba Jɛrusalɛm di kaa waa di u kora la. Denii Koori Manasɛ faa jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la unna hum labuu Kɔraawiizi wibii maa.

ref: Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
text: Guŋ n ɛɛwɛ la harbɔɔ, u faa bir ma Koori Deevid bolzeŋ la bossee koŋlii la n du Gihɔn bulli la n du a waluu wiicholii barii la guŋŋ di ga hel dominua la banna yir Nyiŋ Dominua la, di kaa kpa guŋŋ di ga bar Ɔfɛl giŋgimii la. ref: The message said: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
text: “Kenne Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Sairus ra ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la gillɔɔ n di kora durnya maa ni. U lizimbuu lugɔ n ma u Dia bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm la n du Juda hɛri biini la tɛu. Nɛr la maa n du ii biini di ɛɛ u nɛr, Kɔ́raawiizi la unna hum la du u be, di gil ú wer bir la Jɛrusalɛm.’ ”

ref: Nebuchadnezzar also carried off many of the valuable things in the Lord's temple, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.

ref: During Jehoiakim's rule, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia invaded Judah. He arrested Jehoiakim and put him in chains, and he sent him to the capital city of Babylon.
text: Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa wa lɔu laal, di kpa danyɛ yɔlɔzi vɔɔzuu, di kpogluu kaali Babilɔn.

ref: The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi faa gil Babilɔn koori wa lɔ baa laal, di kpu ba biipɔllaa Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini. U faa waa biipɔllii gɛɛ toloori gɛɛ nɛzɛŋa maa sinyɛna nawɛɛ. Ba maanii Kɔraawiizi faa kpa du Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee biini.

ref: Nebuchadnezzar carried off everything that was left in the temple; he robbed the treasury and the personal storerooms of the king and his officials. He took everything back to Babylon.
text: U faa paa Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna, a zenaa ni a jigzi ani a Dia daama kuna ni a koori ni u nabɔnzi daama kuna maanii kaali Babilɔn.

ref: In the spring of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had Jehoiachin arrested and taken to Babylon, along with more of the valuable items in the temple. Then Nebuchadnezzar appointed Zedekiah king of Judah. King Zedekiah of Judah (
text: Kuna duui saŋa n wa helle, Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza hum ba ga lawuu, ka paagi Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna la yoola n kpolle jaa, di ba Babilɔn. Ka faa gil Koori Jɛhɔyachin naara Zɛdɛkia kpa u gawa, di di Juda ani Jɛrusalɛm kora. Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia Wia

ref: The survivors were taken to Babylonia as prisoners, where they were slaves of the king and his sons, until Persia became a powerful nation.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord his God and refused to change his ways, even after a warning from Jeremiah, the Lord's prophet.
text: U faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ di zuu Kɔraawiizi la unna hum la ni. U faa waa siwii sɔɔnɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia la n faa ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia la be.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had forced Zedekiah to promise in God's name that he would be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn and refused to turn back to the Lord God of Israel, so he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
text: U faa ra di Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛzaa mmɔri, haali uŋ faa gillɛ u hɛɛhzi ni Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ lugɔ u danna sɛɛ u dɔɔra la gba. U faa dɔɔ dignikpegaa Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la be, di bir har kpuu.

ref: The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship.
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, Juda sitɔɔra, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani a nɛra maa wibii nyaai faa ra nyaŋŋuu. Ba ra hiŋ a hɛssi nɛra hiŋaa la, di ra kuari vuga, di ra chɔgi Kɔraawiizi Dia la uŋ lizi u doŋa ha, u ɛɛ kunnaniinanii u be, Jɛrusalɛm biini la ni wikuna.

ref: But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi la ba naabaala n na hum la faa hunzi u dɔgtɛɛzii ba be digiidigii, dikuu unna na ú nɛra ani u duuribɔr la sinyɛna wia.

ref: But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem. Jerusalem Is Destroyed (
text: Ka ba faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la chɛɛtɛ, di ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la, di ra mam baa guŋŋ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ jaa waa fuuh ba ni, waa kaa dɔɔ laafaa.

ref: Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall.
text: U faa jaa fuuh Kɔraawiizi Dia la, di purgi Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii, di fuuh ba kooridiini, di chɔgi ba daama kunnanaa maa.

ref: In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord had Cyrus send a message to all parts of his kingdom. This happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had promised.
text: Lugli bina la, baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Sairus, faa wa di koraa Pɛsia hɛri. Kɔraawiizi faa gil u nua la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Jɛrɛmia la wa ɛɛ wibii. Kɔraawiizi faa bir Koorizeŋ Sairus nfɛrɛ, di gil u sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ u kora diiribɔra maa, di ŋɔ bá sii, di karmuu nɛr maa nuu.

ref: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven, who is also the God of Israel, has made me the ruler of all nations on earth. And he has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over and encourage any of his people who want to go back to Jerusalem and help build the temple.
text: Nɛr la maa n du ii biini di ɛɛ u nɛr, Kɔ́raawiizi la unna hum la du u be, di gil ú bir la Jɛrusalɛm n du Juda, di ga ma Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la Dia. Waabuu Kɔraawiizi la n du Jɛrusalɛm biini la.

ref: Everyone else must provide what is needed. They must give money, supplies, and animals, as well as gifts for rebuilding God's temple.
text: Banla maa n haa kawɛɛ di du yemmaa di ɛɛ hɔɔhra, di ra nyiŋŋi hiinaa bá bir la, a dɛkkɔɔ bá dɔŋahina tɛɛ baa saliŋhuŋŋa, saliŋ, kuna, sela ani sunzaazi, bá ga du Kɔraawiizi Dia, Jɛrusalɛm biini.”

ref: The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
text: Denii ba dɔŋahina maa hiini baa ni saliŋhuŋŋa kundaalikuna, saliŋ kuna, sela ani sunzinanaa, bá ga du Kɔraawiizi Dia.

ref: King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods.
text: Koorizeŋ Sairus la paagi tassazi ni kapuzi ni kuna la maa Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n faa paagɛɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia n du Jɛrusalɛm, di ga du u vuga dia la, di lii tɛɛ baa jaa.

ref: Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
text: Denii Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Sairus gil Mitrɛdaf la n na dau ba kebee la, kur a kuna maa tɛɛ Juda hina sitɔɔri Sɛsbazar.

text: saliŋ tassabizi tokko ni kpɔrgɔ,

text: . Aabuu Sɛsbazar faa paa, u ni nɛra la baŋ faa laurɛɛ la Babilɔn ka ba bir ba Jɛrusalɛm la.

text: Awia, Jus hɛri nabɔma faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ba gilɛɛ kaa di diwee la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, di Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ waa haŋ wa du de, di kpa Urim ni Tumim di ra hum lɛi.

ref: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
text: Baŋ wa hel Kɔraawiizi Dia n du Jɛrusalɛm la, denii diini nabɔnzi baŋhina faa lizi kebee, kuna la baŋ wette na, di kpaa hiini, bá bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia la, ú chigni bɔbinii la.

ref: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani a nɛra baŋhina so Jɛrusalɛm biini di dugluu. Yiryitta, Kɔraawiizi Dia guure ani huŋhunna faa so bola la n duglɛɛrɛ. Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la ge faa so bola la ba naabaala n faa soge la.

ref: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
text: Baaguzi aniidaanɛɛ n wa helle, Izrɛl hina la maa n bittɛ ba ba bola di wa so la, chaali bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
text: Denii Jɔzadak biibaal Jesua ni u dɔŋahina Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl ni u lulla kaa faari di ra ma Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la mbusu lizibɔr la, bá wer di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa di ra tɛu u ni, gunla Kɔraawiizi balii Moosis n sɛbɛɛ u Gbɔgni Hɔŋ biini la.

ref: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
text: Haali baŋ faa ra ɔm nɛra la maa n soge bar baa la, ka ba faa ma mbusu lizibɔr hinnɛ, di chiŋŋi u zɛɛ bɔbinii la. Hɔpizii maa, ba ɔɔ faa jaa kpu sela, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi u ni, chɔɔzi ni duana maa.

ref: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
text: Denii ba ɔɔ kaa wer di di Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ la, di kpu sela lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, gunla baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ ŋɔ ba ra ɛɛ hɔpizi biimaa la.

ref: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
text: Annii maa har, ba ɔɔ faa kaa lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa, Baagufalii mbusuzi ani mbusuzi la maa baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi ba hɔpizizenaa baŋ ɔɔ ra di diuzenaa, di ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi ani ba sunzaazi maa labuu.

ref: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
text: Haali baŋ faa haa waa Kɔraawiizi Dia la zɛɛ chiŋŋɛɛ, ka ba faa faarɔɔrɛ di ra lizi mbusu kuŋfuuhlaa di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, a baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ lugli hɔpizii hɔl. Kɔraawiizi Dia la bir kuaraa ma wia

ref: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
text: Denii nɛra la tɛɛ maara ni kapintazi kebee, di kaa tɛɛ bolzenaa Saidɔn ni Taaya hina diwee, sinni ani ɔlivi nuu, ka ba nyiŋŋi hɛriŋkpol daazi lii Lɛbanɔn hɛri, di kpaa ga muuzeŋ biini ba Jɔpa, gunla Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Sairus n faa tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ ŋɔ bá ɛɛ la.

ref: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
text: Baŋ bittɛ ba Kɔraawiizi Dia Jɛrusalɛm, baaguzi anɛɛhiŋ biini Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl, Jɔzadak biibaal Jesua ni ba lulla, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la ani Levi naanna la maa baŋ faa laurɛɛ la Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba Jɛrusalɛm la faari huma, di faa lizi Levi dee la baala la n di binni tokko gɛɛ ka sag, bá ra binni huŋhunna la n niŋ ma a Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ ni.

ref: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
text: Levi dee Jesua ni u biizi ni u lulla ni Kadmiɛl ni u biizi la n ɛɛ Hɔdavia naanna ani Hɛnadad domee la maanii faa kpauwɛ, di ra binni a huŋhunna ni, ba ra ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ.

ref: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
text: Maara la n wa chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dia zɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maa faa bɔg, di kpogli ba bensunozi, Levi dee la ge n lii Asaf dee biini ge faa kpogli dawossi, di chi ba chignibɔra, di lɔa ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi gunla Koori Deevid n faa ɛɛ Izrɛl koori n dauwɛ la.

ref: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
text: Ba faa ra yir yira di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, di ra jaamuu werge maa, di ra ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi wia wessoo, u nɔŋŋaa la uŋ nɔŋŋi Izrɛl hina la waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.” Denii a nɛra maa chaasi werge maa, di ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, dikuu baŋ wette chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi Dia la zɛɛ wia.

ref: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi kizeehina banla n binɛɛ, Levi dee ani domeezi nabɔnzi la n faa na Kɔraawiizi Diibinii la, faa ra chɛɛhgi werge maa, baŋ wa na a Dia zɛɛ chiŋŋaa wia. Ama, baŋhina waa bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ werge maa, ba ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.

ref: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
text: Banna chaasi gunla, nɛr maa waa ɔɔ kaa wer zum banla n na chaasi ni bɔsɔna ani banla ge n na wii di ra chɛɛhgi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba kɔɔi la faa ra la bɔɔnɛɛrɛ werge maa.

ref: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.

ref: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
text: Denii a nɛra la n soge bar baa la waa du baa bɔhuaih ni ɔnsii, lugɔ bá gilɛɛ wer ma a Dia.

ref: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
text: Denii ba faa kpa kebee kpa Pɛsia hɛri karchizenaa lugɔ bá chɔgi ba huma hiŋ, di haŋ lii Koorizeŋ Sairus kora dii saŋa maa guŋŋ Dariɔs ge kaa wa di Pɛsia kora, di ba haa waa gillɛ. Ba dɔma n waa sɛɛ lugɔ bá bir ma Jɛrusalɛm wia

ref: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
text: Denii Aatazɛgzis ge n kaa wa di yagboŋkora Pɛsia, Bislam, Mitrɛdaf, Tabiil ani ba balaa faa sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ a koori. Ba faa sɛbi a hɔnnɛ Aram hina mɔɔri biini, ba wa karmuu di bagli u zɛɛ tɛu.

ref: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
text: Hɔnnaabuu ba faa sɛbi. “Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis, i hɔnnɛ keŋ, di lii i balaa la n du Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga la.

ref: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
text: Jara, yaa ŋɔ yá ŋɔ i benii i zum lugɔ Jus hina la n lii i be di wa so ɛŋ la, kaa biruu ba Jɛrusalɛm di waa ma dignikpega hina ni wichɔgɛɛra bol la. Ba bittɔɔ kuari u koŋlaa ni a zɛɛzi di ra ma.

ref: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
text: Jara, yaa ra nyiŋŋuu i zum lugɔ di ba haŋ wa bir ma a bolzeŋ ni u koŋlaa naa maa, ba wàá ka sɛɛ turgi lampoo gɛɛ di lizi hɛri kuna gɛɛ di kɛɛ kuna gba. A guŋ daŋ gil kebee wia du kpol tɛi.

ref: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
text: Awia, yaa n ɛɛ i balaa wia, yaa waa nyiŋŋi bá lɔi sɔkpassi. Awiarɛ yaa sɛbi hɔnnaa di ra tɛi, í zum wii la n du de,

ref: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
text: di gil ba pigzi hɛri naa kooribinaa faala wia hɔna biine di na. A daŋ gil i zum lugɔ a bolzeŋ naa hina ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa, koora ni ba hɛssi hina be, faala maa. Awiarɛ ba faa chɔguu la.

ref: If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
text: Yaa ŋɔ ya ŋɔ i benii i zum lugɔ, di ba bittɔ ma a bolzeŋ naa ni u koŋlaa maa, hàá ka dɔɔ fɔŋŋa Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga ni.”

ref: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
text: Denii a koorizeŋ bir sɛbi hɔnnaa, “Nabɔma Rɛhum, karchi Simsai ani ii dɔŋahina la maa n du bolzeŋ Samaria ni Muu Yufretis wiicholii yeŋa maa, ii hɔnnɛ keŋ. N na jaami ia.

ref: After your letter was translated and read to me,
text: Hɔŋ la iiŋ sɛbɛɛ la, ba karmuubuu di biruu du n mɔɔri biini tɛŋ.

ref: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
text: N gillɔɔ ba pigzi di na lugɔ a bolzeŋ hina ɔɔ ra vɛɛ koora nuuzii, di dɔɔ dignikpega di ra koozi wia, di lii faala maa.

ref: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
text: Awia, ii gilɛɛ gil ba kaa bir ma a bol, di miŋ lɛi wa tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
text: Baŋ haŋ wa karmi Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis hɔŋ la tɛɛ nabɔma Rɛhum, karchi Simsai ani ba balaa la, ba hahzi di la a Jus hina hiŋ be, Jɛrusalɛm, di ga fir baa lugɔ ba gilɛɛ kaa ma a bolzeŋ.

ref: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
text: Denii ba gil Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ mai, guŋŋ di wa hel Pɛsia hɛri koorizeŋ la banna yir Dariɔs la kora dii binni anɛɛhiŋ biini.

ref: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
text: A keŋ saŋaa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hagai ni Ido naana Zɛkaria faa faari di ra ŋɔ wia, di ra du Jus hina la n du Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm la ni, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la sɔŋ biini.

ref: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
text: Denii Sɛɛltiɛl biibaal Zɛrubabɛl ni Jɔzadak biibaal Jesua kaa faari di ra ma Kɔraawiizi Dia, Jɛrusalɛm. A dɔgtɛɛzi banɛɛ naa faa du ba benii di ra hiini baa.

ref: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
text: A guŋ saŋa hiŋ, Tatɛnai la n faa ɛɛ Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga hɛri nabɔma, Sɛtar Bɔzɛnai ani ba balaa izi di ga pɛɛzi baa, “Anɛɛ n tɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ ŋɔ ii kaa kuari di ra ma Kɔraawiizi Dia naa, di kaa du u kuna maanɛi?”

ref: Give us the names of the workers!”
text: Di kaa pɛɛzi baa nɛra la n na ma a Dia sɔna.

ref: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la faa ra binni Jus hina sitɔɔra ninɛɛ. Awia, Pɛsia nabɔnzi faa waa gillɛ ba gil a Dia mai, ka ra kpaŋ gunla ban niŋ sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ Koorizeŋ Dariɔs, ú ge bir sɛbi tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ u loobii.

ref: Governor Tattenai, Shethar Bozenai, and their advisors sent a report to Darius,
text: Hɔnnaabuu Tatɛnai la n faa ɛɛ Muu Yufretis wiicholii hɛri nabɔma, Sɛtar Bɔzɛnai ani ba babalaa nabɔnzi faa sɛbi tɛɛ Koorizeŋ Dariɔs.

ref: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
text: Wia la baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ labuu keŋ, “Koorizeŋ Dariɔs, yaa bɔsɔna jaannɛ keŋ.

ref: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
text: Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu i zum lugɔ yaa la Juda hɛrii, di ga na gunla Jus hina n bittɛ kuari Kɔraawiizizeŋ Dia la di ra ma. Ba kpa bizenaa ni dollii di ra ma u koŋlaa. Ba aah siwiire di ra mau nɛnnɛ. A mai ge ra la manamanaŋ.

ref: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
text: Yaa pɛɛzi ba sitɔɔra lugɔ anɛɛ n tɛɛ baa ŋmɛnɛɛ ba bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia naa, di ra du u kuna maa,

ref: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
text: di kaa pɛɛzi ba sitɔɔra sɔna, ya wer sɛbaa tɛi, í zum.

ref: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
text: Ba ŋɔ yaa be, ‘Yaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la ni hɛri maa balaarɛ. Yaa bir kuari u Dia la Izrɛl koorizeŋ bɛl n faa mawɛɛ biŋkpila maa n bɛrɛɛ, di ra mau.

ref: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
text: Ka yaa naabaala n faa fuuh Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la baaŋ wia, u faa kpa baabuu du Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee biini, u faa lɔ baa laal di kpegli baa, di purgi u Dia hiŋ, ka lauri baa kaali Babilɔn hɛri.

ref: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
text: Awia, Sɛsbazar bir kuari Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ zɛɛ chiŋŋi u bɔbinii la, Jɛrusalɛm biini. Di haŋ lii a hɔl hiŋ di wa lii zinaa, ba haa wɔɔ mawɛɛ tuŋ.’

ref: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
text: Jara, di a parii, gil ba pigzi koora faala wia hɔna biini, Babilɔn hɛri. Denii í zum, di wibii maanii Sairus faa sɛbi dau lugɔ bá bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini, ka i jaa gil ya nuu gunla hiŋ lauwɛ, a wia naa biini.”

ref: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
text: Denii Koorizeŋ Dariɔs ŋɔ dí ba pigzi ba faala koora wia la baŋ sɛbɛɛ dau Babilɔn hɛri la biini.

ref: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
text: Ba pigzi guŋŋ di wa na a guŋ hɔŋ, bolzeŋ la baŋ faa ra yir Ɛkbatana n du Mɛdi hɛri la. Kenne ba faa sɛbi u ni,

ref: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
text: “Koorizeŋ Sairus kora dii lugli bina biini, kenne u faa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Dia la n du Jɛrusalɛm la wia, Ií bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia la n faa du Jɛrusalɛm la, di chiŋŋi u zɛɛbinii la ni, u ɛɛ mbusuzi lizibɔr. Ií mau, ú chiŋ laŋaa ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoahoro, ú wassi ge ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
text: Ií ɔɔ kpa bizenaa di ma solaa ahoro di hɔŋ dɔŋa ni, ka ɔɔ kpa dolli ge sag a ni u ge ɛɛ solkpaŋ. A kora kebeere ba kpa di turgi a Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ kim maa.

ref: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
text: Di kaa kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa kuna la maa Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n paawɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia n du Jɛrusalɛm, di kpaa ba Babilɔn la, ba kaa bir kpa a maa la Jɛrusalɛm, di ga du Kɔraawiizi Dia biini.” Koorizeŋ Dariɔs n ŋɔ bá kaa faari a huma wia

ref: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
text: Denii Koorizeŋ Dariɔs bir sɛbi tɛɛ baa di ŋɔ, “Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga nabɔma Tatɛnai, Sɛtar Bɔzɛnai ani ii balaa nabɔnzi la maa n du de la, ii gilɛɛ kaa wàá la Kɔraawiizi Dia la.

ref: Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
text: Ií gilɛɛ ka kpa ii nuuzi di du a Dia mai wia biini. Ií gil a Jus hina nabɔma ni ba sitɔɔra bir ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ, di chiŋŋi u zɛɛbinii la ni.

ref: And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil.
text: Hɔpizii maa, ií ɔɔ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n du Jɛrusalɛm kuna la maa banna nyiŋŋi. Di naballii gɛɛ pebalaa gɛɛ peballii ba ra nyiŋŋi, ba kpa lizi mbusuzi di fuuh tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n du chiŋ, ií tɛɛ baa. Di huuti genii gɛɛ yazi gɛɛ siŋ gɛɛ nuurɛ, ba ra nyiŋŋi,

ref: I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
text: bá ɔɔ wer lizi mbusuzi la n na par Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ, di ra suŋŋuu winanaa ra tɛɛ mìŋ́ koori ni n biibaala.

ref: If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump.
text: Wii la n kaa jaau lugɔ, di nɛr maa haŋ wa bir n widaulii naa, bá pam u dia dola, di sɛɛh u nua bɛl di yaguu, di lalluu baŋ chiŋ. Ka ba purgi u dia ú birgi hul, dikuu a wichɔgii naa wia.

ref: I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully. The Temple Is Dedicated
text: Kɔraawiizi la n gillɛ u Sɔŋ du u biini la, waabuu niŋ chɔgi koori gɛɛ nɛr la maa n niŋ ŋɔ u bir n widaulii naa gɛɛ di chɔgi Kɔraawiizi Dia naa Jɛrusalɛm biini. Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Dariɔsii dau guŋ. Ií hiŋuu nɛnnɛ.” Kɔraawiizi Dia kpai du u nonee biini wia

ref: With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia.
text: Awia, Jus hina nabɔnzi la jaa wer na bɔr di ra ma a dia. Wiimaa ge kuari di ra tɛɛ baa, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Hagai ni Ido naana Zɛkaria n faa du baa bɔkpega wia. Ba jaa ma a Dia tuŋ, gunla Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la n ŋɔwɛɛ ani Pɛsia hɛri Koorizenaa Sairus, Dariɔs ani Aatazɛgzis n faa dauwɛ la.

ref: On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
text: Ba faa ma Kɔraawiizi Dia hinnɛ tuŋ, baagu la banna yir Adar la hɔpizaa ahorohiŋ hɔl, Dariɔs kora dii binni anumbɛlhiŋ biini.

ref: The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani banla maa baŋ faa laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba la, jaa di bahinaa ni bɔsɔna, dikuu baŋ kpa a Dia du Kɔraawiizi nonee wia.

ref: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Baŋ faa ŋɔ ba kpa a Dia di du Kɔraawiizi nonee la, ba kpu nabala kalfa ni pebala kalfaanɛɛ ani peballi kalfaanaazuu, di kpaa lizi mbusu kuna tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Baŋ ŋɔ ba lizi ba wichɔgaa giltɛɛi mbusu ge, bubala fidaanɛɛrɛ ba kpa lizi mbusu. Bubal kpaŋ maa faa chi tɛɛ dee maa.

ref: Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written. The Passover
text: Denii ba faa bargi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la di du sugezi, bá ra hum ba huma Kɔraawiizi Dia la n du Jɛrusalɛm la biini, gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ Moosis hɔŋ biini la. Gillikaali dii wia

ref: Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
text: Lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl, Izrɛl hina la baŋ faa laurɛɛ kaali la n bittɛ ba la, di Gillikaali.

ref: The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la maa sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. Levi dee kpu Gillikaali pebii, di lizi ba ni banla n bittɛ ba la ni ba lulla la n ɛɛ kizeehina la maa mbusu, tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina la maa n bittɛ ba la, ni banla maa n gil widoŋa la banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ n na ɛɛ la, ka ra jaami Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la maa, di a Gillikaali hɔpizii diwee hiŋ.

ref: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
text: Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ Hɔpizizenaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la faa tɛɛ baabuu bɔsɔna werge, dikuu uŋ faa bir Asiiria koorizeŋ la bampirii, u faa hiini baa, ba wer ma Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la Dia wia.

ref: Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest. Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
text: Ɛzra naa faa lii Babilɔnnɛ di ba. U faa ɛɛ baglii, di zum Moosis gbɔg la Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum n faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis labuu nɛnnɛ. Kɔraawiizi faa du u benii di nɔŋŋuu. Awia, kunla maa uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi di ŋɔ koorizeŋ la be, a koori ɔɔ tɛubuu.

ref: Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
text: Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biini, Izrɛl hina baŋhina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee, yiryitta, Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua guure ani u Dia balaa baŋhina ge izi ba Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month.
text: A bina lugli baagu, lugli hɔpiziirɛ u faa lii Babilɔn, di faari u ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋ volaa, di zuu Jɛrusalɛm a baagu anuehiŋ la lugli hɔpizii hɔl. Ɛzra faa wettoo vol a ŋmɛnɛɛ naa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi la uŋ faa ra hum la du u benii.

ref: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
text: Hɔnnaabuu Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis faa sɛbi tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra, n faa ɛɛ bagli, di zum Kɔraawiizi widaulaa ni u Gbɔgni ŋmɛnizi la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la.

ref: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
text: “Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzisii sɛbi hɔnnaa di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra, n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la Gbɔg bagli. N na jaamii.

ref: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
text: Awia, n ni n zɛɛsogna baniidaanɛɛ ra hum iabuu, ii la Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm di ga daani na gunla banna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg la n du i be la.

ref: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, di ii waa la, ii kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa la n ni n zɛɛsogna n kpawɛɛ ra sunzi Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, u Dia du Jɛrusalɛm la di ra la.

ref: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
text: Ií kaa kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa la maa iin nawɛɛ lii Babilɔn hɛri ani sunzaazi la Izrɛl hina ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina n lizɛɛ, dikuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la Dia n du Jɛrusalɛm biini la wia di ra la.

ref: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
text: Kebee gunla maa iiŋ wa nawɛɛ, ii ɛɛ ania di kpaa yau nabala, pebala, peballi, mia ani siŋ di kpaa lizi mbusuzi ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, u Dia mbusu lizibɔr la ni, Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
text: Denii i ni i lulla Jus hina jaa wer kpa saliŋhuŋŋa la ni saliŋ la maa n kawɛɛ di ɛɛ gunla maa iinna nyiŋŋi, á par Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.

ref: Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple.
text: Ií kpa kuna la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ia la ga tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, Jɛrusalɛm, bá kpaa di ra jaamuu u Dia biini.

ref: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
text: Di ii waa nyiŋŋi kunla maa lugɔ ii kpa ra hum Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la Dia la huma, ií lizuu lii n daama dauribɔr biini.

ref: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
text: Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis dauwɔɔ lugɔ Muu Yufretis wiicholii hɛri daama dauribɔra binna maa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la Gbɔg bagli, kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi di lii ii be nɛnnɛ,

ref: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
text: Ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ, kunla maa Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ n na nyiŋŋi ii tɛɛ baa, bá kpa hum u Dia la huma, ií ɔɔ nyiŋŋaa tɛɛ baa, u baaŋ gilɛɛ waa fuuh n ni n biibaal maa ni.

ref: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina gɛɛ Levi dee gɛɛ u Dia yiryitta gɛɛ u Dia guure gɛɛ nɛr la maa n na hum u Dia la huma maa lampoo gɛɛ hɛri kuna gɛɛ kuŋkɛɛlaa.

ref: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
text: Ka hìŋ́ Ɛzra, kpa nunzuma la Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la n tɛi la, di lizi i nabɔnzi ni i sitɔɔra la n zum Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔgni la, bá ra binni Muu Yufretis wiicholii paga nɛra maa ni, di ra di baa seriya, ka bagli banla maa ge n waa a Gbɔgni zummɛ.

ref: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
text: Nɛr la maa n ŋɔ wàá hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la hinna hum la Gbɔg gɛɛ n gbɔg, a dɛkkɔɔ bá tɛr u digni manaŋ, di kpuu gɛɛ di duŋŋuu gɛɛ di foozi u kuna maa gɛɛ di tɔu dia.” Ɛzra n chɔli Kɔraawiizi wia

ref: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.

ref: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.

ref: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.

text: Yaa n wa hel Jɛrusalɛm, yaa faa heezoore hɔpizaa ahoro.

text: A hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl la, yaa kpa la Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la Dia, di ga mɛgzi a saliŋhuŋŋa, a saliŋ ani kunnanaananaa la maa, di kpaa tɛɛ Yuria biibaal Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Mɛrɛmɔf.
