ref: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
text: Baŋ wa ɛɛ annii maa tuŋ, Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra ba mìŋ́ Ɛzra be, di wa ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee la haa waa bahinaa bargɛɛ lii nɛra la baŋ soge dugli la ni ba wikuna ɛɛi biini, aabuu Keenan, Hitti, Pɛriz, Jɛbus, Ammɔn, Moab, Ijip ani Amɔri hina maa n na ɛɛ la.

ref: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
text: Ba paagi ba biihaanaa, di nyiŋŋi baŋhina ge tɛɛ ba biibaala. Awia, ba gillɔɔ nɛra la n ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa koozi nɛra la n bar baa la biini. Ba sitɔɔra ni ba nabɔnzi tɔ see, ba wibii nyaai naa biini.”

ref: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
text: Miŋ wa nuu wia naa, a chɔgi n biini werge maa, n lau n laala piili, di kpuzi n nyuhuna ni n taŋkulo huna ka so, n bɔra huah.

ref: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
text: Nɛra la maa n faa nuu Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la wiŋɔzi, ɔnsii lau baa ba bɔra ra sa la, ba jaa chaali bariŋ, dikuu banla baŋ faa laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn la n bittɛ ba la wibii nyaai naa wia. Denii n faa so ni bɔhuaih, guŋŋ duana mbusu lizaa wa hel.

ref: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
text: Duana mbusu lizaa n wa helle, n izi di lii bɔr la miŋ faa soge ni bɔhuaih ni n laalipiilaa la, di giŋŋi, di yaa n nonee chiŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la,

ref: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
text: di suŋŋuu ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, hiihzi lawimbuu werge maa, n ŋmaabi. Awia, màá wer lalli n nyuu i sibɔɔ. Yaa wichɔgaa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ, yaa chɔgri ge ga chug baama.

ref: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
text: Di lii yaa naabaala saŋa la guŋŋ di wa lii zinaa, yaa bilchɔg kannɔɔ werge maa, dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia. Ba faa kpu yaa ni yaa koora ani i kizeehinaa, di lauri baŋhina birgi yoma, di paagi yaa kuna maa, yaa birgi sɔkpassi kuna hɛrdumazi koora nonee biine, alugɔ zinaa naa.

ref: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, i suŋ yaa ninɛɛ saŋa kpurii naa biini, di gil yaa baŋhina ka, di du de ni bɔsɔna, Diinaniinanii naa biini. I lɛɛ yaabuu lii tɔɔrɔɔ biini, di gil yaa na bɔchaaŋ.

ref: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
text: Yaa faa ɛɛ yomaa, ka haa yaa gillɛ ha a tɔɔrɔɔ biini. I bagli yaabuu i nɔŋŋaa Pɛsia hina koorizenaa see, di tɛɛ yaa miibɔɔfalii. Yaa na ŋmɛnɛɛ di kaa wer ma hìŋ́ Kɔraawiizizeŋ Dia n faa puree la. Di gil yaa so Juda hɛri ni Jɛrusalɛm biine ni bɔsɔna.

ref: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ annii naa maa harɛi? Yaa gbɛlli i widaulaa la

ref: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
text: hiŋ ga i balaa n ɛɛ i dɔgtɛɛzi be tɛɛ yaa, saŋa la hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, ‘Hɛri la iinna zuu ii dɔɔ la, ɛɛ hɛri la n doŋŋee, dikuu u nɛra wikuna wia. Dikuu ba wiɛɛlaa la miŋ kiiwe la wia, ba gillɔɔ ba wichɔgaa doŋa su a hɛri maa.

ref: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
text: Awia, ii gilɛɛ waa kpa ii biihaana di ra tɛɛ ba biibaala gɛɛ di waa kpa ba biihaana di ra tɛɛ ii biibaala. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ii ni baa wàá ɛɛ dammunaa nuukpaŋ, ŋmɛnɛ maa. Guŋ daŋ gil ii dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, di di a hɛri kunnanaa guŋŋ di wa gilaa tɛɛ ii biizi, a ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna, di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.’

ref: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
text: Wia naa n ɛɛ yaa be naa zɛɛ bɔttɛ lugɔ yaa wiɛɛlaa ani yaa bilchɔg n kannɛ werge wia, ka Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, haa yaa digna tɛrgɛɛ di hel gunla yaa wichɔgaa n makkɛ, ka gil yaa bannii ka, di haa du de.

ref: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
text: Awia, a dɛkkɔ yaa n niŋ kaa chɔgi i widaulaa, di kaa gil yaa ni banla n na ɛɛ i wikiilaa ra paagi dɔŋaa? Di yaa kaa ɛɛ guŋ, i baaŋ wàá fuuh yaa ni werge maa, í chɔgi yaa, bɛl maa wàá ka kaa?

ref: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum, i wia deŋloore! Yaa banniibuu kawɛɛ zinaa. Yaabuu keŋ di chi i see, di di bilchɔg. Yaa bɛl maa waa dɛkkɛ lugɔ u chi i see gba.”

ref: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
text: Ɛzra n faa ra suŋŋi wiizi, di ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, ka faa ra wii di chol hɛri, Kɔraawiizi Dia la see la, Izrɛl baala ni haana ani bichalli kpila maa faa wa baruu. Ba ge gba maa faa ra wii werge.

ref: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,

ref: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, gil yaa ni Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ɛɛ nuukpaŋ u see, yá duŋŋi a keŋ haana ni ba biizi, gunla hìŋ́ Ɛzra ani banla n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la widaulaa n niŋ bagli. Gil ya ɛɛ gunla u Gbɔg n na bagli.

ref: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
text: Ɛzra, izi chiŋ, a wii naa du i noneere. Yaa daŋ chi i har. Awia, dɔɔ bɔkpega, di ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
text: Denii Ɛzra izi hɛɛhzi di du Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani Izrɛl hina maa, lugɔ bá hiŋ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la. Ba hɛɛhzi guŋ.

ref: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
text: Awia, Ɛzra jaa lii Kɔraawiizi Dia la see, di la Ɛliasib biibaal Jɛhɔhanan chɔɔribɔr. Uŋ faa du de la, waa diwee, waa nii ge nyɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa haa ra wiiu, dikuu banla baŋ laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba la wibii nyaai wia.

ref: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. text: nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ chaalaa naa balaa hɔpizaa ahoro biini, u daŋ nyaa u kundɔɔlaa maa, gunla nabɔnzi n dauwɛ, ka bá lizuu lii banla n bittɛ ba la biini.

ref: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
text: A hɔpizaa ahoro biini, Juda ni Bɛnjamin dee baala maa chaali Jɛrusalɛm. A baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ, u hɔpizaa tokko hɔl, di a nɛra maa chaalɔɔ di so Kɔraawiizi Dia la bossee. Ba maa biine faa chɔgi werge maa, dikuu a wii n faa ɛɛ siaahmu ani dooŋ n faa ra ba werge wia.

ref: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra izi chi, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ii waa wibii dɔɔwɛ. Ií paagi hɛrdumazi biihaanaa. Guŋ kaa gil Izrɛl hina bilchɔg nyaŋŋi.

ref: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, ii sɛɛ ii wichɔgaa chɔgri, Kɔraawiizi la ii naabaala n faa ra hum la be, ka ra ɛɛ u kipar. Ií bargi iihinaa lii nɛra la n bar ia ani ii hɛrdumazi haana la be.”

ref: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
text: Denii a nɛra maa sɛɛ werge maa, di ŋɔ, “I di wibiire! Firaarɛ ya ɛɛ gunla hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
text: Ka nɛra la n chaali bɔnnaa kpillɔɔ werge maa. A ge kaa ɛɛ yuu, awia, yaa wàá wer so baŋgia. A wii naa ge waa kaa ɛɛ hɔpizikpaŋ gɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ wiɛɛlii, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa kpila maa jaa a wii naa biinii.

ref: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
text: Ií gil yaa nabɔnzi chi a nɛra maa naazi di ɛɛ wiimaa. Denii bá gil unla maa n dɔɔ hɛrduma haaŋ u bol lii ba, saŋa la baŋ dauwɛ, di kpa bol maa nabɔnzi ni sitɔɔra jaa, guŋŋ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la baaŋ wa sɔɔni yaa ni, dikuu a wii naa wia.”

ref: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
text: Asahɛl biibaal Jonatan ni Tikva biibaal Jazɛya bɛnnɛ faa di a wii naa mmɔri. Mɛsulam ni Sabɛtai la n faa lii Levi dee biini sɛɛ jaa baa.

ref: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,

text: Harim ge naanna biini, Maasɛya, Ɛlija, Sɛmaaya, Jɛhiɛl ani Uzzia.

ref: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
text: Pasur naanna biini, Ɛliɔnai, Maasɛya, Ismɛl, Nɛtanɛl, Jɔzabad ani Ɛlasa.

ref: Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah , Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
text: Levi dee ge biini, Jɔzabad, Simei, Kɛlaaya, ba kaa ra yiruu Kɛlita la, Pɛtahia, Juda ani Ɛliɛza.

ref: Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife. These temple guards had foreign wives: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
text: Yiryitta ge biini, Ɛliasib. Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuguure ge biini, Salum, Tɛlɛm ani Uri.

ref: Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
text: Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ biini, Parɔs naanna, Ramia, Izia, Malkija, Mijamin, Ɛliaza, Malkija ani Bɛnaaya.

ref: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
text: Ɛlam ge naanna, Matania, Zɛkaria, Jɛhiɛl, Abdi, Jɛrɛmɔf ani Ɛlija.

ref: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
text: Zatu ge naanna, Ɛliɔnai, Ɛliasib, Matania, Jɛrɛmɔf, Zabad ani Aziza.

ref: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
text: Bɛbai ge naanna, Jɛhɔhanan, Hanania, Zabai ani Atlai.

ref: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
text: Bani ge naannaa, Mɛsulam, Maluk, Adaaya, Jasub, Sɛɛl ani Jɛrɛmɔf.

ref: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
text: Pahaf Moab naanna, Adna, Kɛlal, Bɛnaaya, Maasɛya, Matania, Bɛzalɛl, Binui ani Manasɛ.

ref: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
text: Hasum ge naannaa, Matɛnai, Mattatta, Zabad, Ɛlifɛlɛt, Jɛrɛmia, Manasɛ ani Simei.

ref: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
text: Nɛbɔ naanna, Jɛyɛl, Matitia, Zabad, Zɛbina, Jaddai, Jowɛl ani Bɛnaaya.

ref: These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
text: A nɛra naa maanii faa paa hɛrdumazi haana, baŋhina ni ba hora faa lul biizii, ka ba duŋŋi ba ni a biizi maa.

ref: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
text: Hakalia biibaal Nɛhɛmia wiŋɔɔlaarɛ keŋ. Binni tokko n wa helle, baagu la banna yir Kislɛv biini, Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii saŋa, di mìŋ́ Nɛhɛmia faa du bolzeŋ la banna yir Susa.

ref: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
text: Denii n niwee Hanani ni baala baŋhina lii Juda ba. N pɛɛzi baa gunla Jus hina la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali Babilɔn, ka ba bir ba Juda la wia ani gunla Jɛrusalɛm wia n duwɛɛ.

ref: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
text: Denii ba ŋɔ n be, “Banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ ka ba bir ba Juda la, du tɔɔrɔɔ ni hiihzi biinii. Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maanii purgee, ba fuuh u dominuuzenaa ge maa.”

ref: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
text: Miŋ wa nuu wia naa, n so di wii ni biinichɔg, di vɔɔ nua hɔpizaa anɛɛ, di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ,

ref: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
text: di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ, di dɔɔ sɔŋ, i wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la, i ɔɔ ra hiŋ i ni i nɛra nuukpaŋ labuu. I nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ banla n nɔŋŋii di ra hiŋ i widaulaa la be.

ref: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
text: Keŋŋi digna, di pilli i siwee nuu i balii n suŋŋii di ra tɛɛ i balaa Izrɛl hina, wibaŋa ni hamuŋa maa. N ŋɔ n sɛɛ chɔgrii lugɔ yaa Izrɛl hina, di kpa n ni n mɛɛ diahina maa jaa, ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu i ni.

ref: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
text: Yaa ɛɛ biinikpola wiarɛ di zuu i ni. Yaa waa sɛɛwɛ hiŋ i wiŋɔɔlaa, i widaulaa ani i Gbɔgni la hiŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ i balii Moosis la.

ref: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
text: A liizi i baglaazi la hiŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis, di ŋɔ, ‘Di ii wanna hiŋ ni wibii, n daŋ gil ii maa yaari hɛrdumazi biine.

ref: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
text: Ka di ii daŋ bir ba n be ni wibii, di ra hiŋ n wiŋɔɔlaa, haali ii banla gba baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛhjaŋa la, n daŋ chaali ia di bir ba bɔr la miŋ lizɛɛ, n sɔŋ du de la.’

ref: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
text: Ba ɛɛ i balaa ni nɛra la hiŋ kpa i fɔŋŋazeŋ ni i banonii di lɛɛu.

ref: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
text: Kɔraawiizi, keŋŋi digna di nuu mìŋ́ i balii naa ni i balaa la maa n na kpa i sɔŋ girme wiisuŋŋaa. Gil mìŋ́ i balii na n kipar zinaa, di gil n wia par baal naa.” Minuu faa ra kpogli a koorizeŋ siŋ libee.

ref: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
text: Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biini, baagu la banna yir Niisan la, n kpa siŋ la ń ga tɛu, di u ra di. U ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa nawɛɛ n biini n chɔkkɛ.

ref: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
text: Denii u pɛɛziŋ, “Zinaa ɛrɛɛ i biini chɔgi, hiŋ waa wiiyɛi? A daŋ ɛɛ biinichɔg wiarɛ.” Uŋ pɛɛzi gunla, ɔnsii lawiŋ,

ref: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
text: ka n ŋɔ u be, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi gil i du de saŋa maa. Bɛɛ n baani n biini wàá chɔgɛi? Bolzeŋ la miŋ liwɛɛ, n naabaala ŋmama du de la maanii purgee, u dominuuzenaa ge maa fuuh.”

ref: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
text: A koorizeŋ pɛɛziŋ, “Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ tɛinɛi?” Denii n suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ,

ref: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
text: ka ŋɔ a koorizeŋ be, “Jara, di n wia parii, nuu n suŋŋaa, di gil n la Juda, n naabaala hɛri la baŋ hug baa la, di ga kuari a bolzeŋ ma.”

ref: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
text: A saŋa, di a koorizeŋ ni u haaŋ sogo, u pɛɛziŋ, “Ɛrɛɛ í ga birgi mag ani saŋa bɛɛ i bir banɛi?” A paruu, u tɛŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ. Awia, n tɛu saŋa la min niŋ la ka bir ba.

ref: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
text: Denii n kaa suŋŋuu ŋɔ ú tɛŋ hɔna, ń kpa la ga tɛɛ Muu Yufretis baŋgia hɛri nabɔnzi, bá gil nɛra tɔ n see di binniŋ guŋŋ ń ga hel Juda ni alaanfia.

ref: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
text: N kaa ŋɔ u be lugɔ ú tɛŋ hɔŋ, ń ga tɛɛ baal la banna yir Asaf la n na binni koori kɔrni la, ú tɛŋ daazi ń teŋri ga kuari gbessi du diikpeg la n dugli Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuzenaa, a bolzeŋ koŋliizeŋ ani n dia. Kɔraawiizi n faa du n be wia, kunla maa miŋ suŋŋɛɛ lii a koori be, u tɛmbuu.

ref: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
text: Denii n faa kpa la Muu Yufretis baŋgia hɛri nabɔnzi la be, di ga kpa a hɔna tɛɛ baa. A koorizeŋ faa gillɔɔ laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ni banla n tinni zagra faa tɔ n see ga hel de.

ref: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
text: Denii baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Sanbalat, u lii Bɛf Hɔrɔn ni u dɔŋhiŋ bɛl banna yir Tobia, n faa ɛɛ Ammɔn hina nabɔma bɛl, nuu lugɔ nɛbɛl ballɔɔ, ú wa kuari Izrɛl hina bolzeŋ la ma. A guŋ faa ra fuuh ba baana werge maa. Nɛhɛmia n gaagɛɛ binni Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa wia

ref: Three days after arriving in Jerusalem,
text: N kpa la Jɛrusalɛm, di ga du de hɔpizaa ahoro.

ref: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
text: N ni baala tama izi hamuŋa bɛl, ka maa nɛr maa be ŋɔwɛɛ gunla Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ du n bampirii lugɔ ń wa ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm. A saŋa, kuntinnaa faa waa hoo, di kawee la miŋ tinnɛɛ la bɛŋ lɛi.

ref: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
text: Hamuŋa ni, n ga Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la lii, di kpa la unla banna yir Hohobia Kɔlɔŋ la, di kaa lii de di kpa la unla banna yir Nabina Dominuuzeŋ la. Aabuu n binni, di na gunla Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maa n purgee ni gunla u dominuuzenaa maa n fuuhwe.

ref: On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey.
text: N lii de la Bule Dominuuzeŋ la, di lii de ga hel Koori Pol la. Ka bɔr faa waa hoo, n kawee ga.

ref: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
text: Awia, n tuu a waluu a hamuŋa ni, di binni a koŋlii. A tuna, n kaa bir ga a Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la zuu a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
text: A nabɔnzi faa waa zum bɔr la maa miŋ kaalɛɛ gɛɛ wii la minna ɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa haa waa Jus hina gɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina gɛɛ nabɔnzenaa gɛɛ ba nabɔnzi gɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ hum a huma la be ŋɔwɛɛ, wii la miŋ ballɛ ń wa ɛɛ.

ref: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
text: Awia, n ŋɔ ba be, “Ií na tɔɔrɔɔ la biini yaa n duwɛɛ. Jɛrusalɛm maanii purgee chɔɔ, u dominuuzenaa maa fuuh. Ií gil ya kuari Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii la ma. Di yaa ɛɛ guŋ, yaa wàá ka du hiihzi biini.”

ref: Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said. Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
text: N jaa ŋɔ ba be gunla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ n ni ani wii la koorizeŋ la n ŋɔ n be. Ba sɛɛ, di ŋɔ, “Ií gil ya faari di kuari a koŋlii ma.” Awia, ba faari di ra hum a hunnanii naa.

ref: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
text: Sanbalat la n ɛɛ Bɛf Hɔrɔn hinuu, Tobia la n ɛɛ Ammɔn hina nabɔma ani Gɛsɛm la n ɛɛ Lɔrbi la n wa nuu guŋ, ba ra mam yaa, di ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ, di ra ŋɔ, “Beedee ii ra ɛɛ kennei? Ii ra di a koorizenne mmɔri gɛɛ?”

ref: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
text: Denii n ŋɔ ba be, “Kɔraawiizi La N Na Di Kora Chiŋ la daŋ tɛɛ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ ani fɔŋŋa, yá wer mau, dikuu yaa n ɛɛ u balaa wia. Yaa daŋ bir mau. Ama, iawaa nonii waa Jɛrusalɛm kapɛttɛ ni jaawɛ.”

ref: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
text: Kenne ba faa bir kuari a bolzeŋ koŋliizeŋ ma. Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Ɛliasib ni u dɔŋahina, faa kuari dominuuzeŋ la banna yir Peeza Dominuuzeŋ la ma, di kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee, ka du u gbessi. Ba faa ma a koŋliizeŋ guŋŋ di ga hel dominuuzeŋ la banna yir Kalfa Diijaŋ ni Hananɛl Diijaŋ la, di kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee.

ref: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
text: Bolzeŋ Jɛriko baala ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n kaa ra hiŋ. Baŋ wa hel see, Imri biibaal Zakur ge ma hiŋ.

ref: The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Hasɛnaa biibaala ge kuari Nyinni Dominuuzeŋ la hiŋ, di du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra.

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
text: Yuria biibaal Mɛrɛmɔf, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Hakɔz, ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Bɛrɛkia biibaal Mɛsulam, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Mɛsɛzabɛl, ge faa kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ. Baana biibaal Zadɔk ge kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ.

ref: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
text: Tɛkua baala ge kuari ma a koŋlii bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Banna ma la, ba nabɔnzenaa la n du a bol waa sɛɛwɛ bá hum huma la ba binna n tɛɛ baa la.

ref: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Denii Pasia biibaal Jɔyada ni Bɛsɔdɛya biibaal Mɛsulam ge kaa kuari Jɛsana Dominuuzeŋ la hiŋ. Ba faa du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra.

ref: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
text: Gibiɔn hinuu Mɛlatia, Mɛrɔnɔf hinuu Jadɔn ani Gibiɔn ni Mizpa baala, ge ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel Muu Yufretis Wiicholii nabɔma dia.

ref: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
text: Hahaaya biibaal Uziɛl, n faa ɛɛ saliŋ luuri, kuari ma bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Hanania la ge n faa ɛɛ tulaale kuari, la genii faa ma bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ. Gunnɛ ba faa ɛɛ, di kuari Jɛrusalɛm koŋliizeŋ la maa ma guŋŋ di ga hel u bɔr la banna yir Koŋlii War la.

ref: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Denii Hur biibaal Rɛfaaya, n faa ɛɛ nabɔma di ra binni Jɛrusalɛm keŋkere bɛl, ge faa kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ.

ref: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
text: Harumaf biibaal Jɛdaaya ge kuari ma u bɔr la n dugli u dia, di hiŋ. Hasabnɛya biibaal Hatus ge kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ.

ref: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
text: Harim biibaal Malkija ni Pahaf Moab biibaal Hasub genii kuarɛɛ ma u bɔr la n hiŋŋɛ ani u bɔr la banna yir Paanuu Ɔɔzibɔra Diijaŋ la.

ref: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
text: Halɔhɛs biibaal Salum la n faa ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm keŋkere bɛl nabɔma ni u biihaana ge kuari ma u yeŋ hiŋ.

ref: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
text: Baal la baŋ faa ra yir Hanun ge ni Zanoa hinaa ge faa ma u bɔr la banna yir Waluu Dominuuzeŋ la. Baŋ wa kuaruu ma, ba du de domininuuzeŋ gbessi ni a kattibɔra. Ba faa kuaruubuu ma guŋŋ nogumzi kagboŋ, di ga hel u bɔr la banna yir Kpaga Dominuuzeŋ la.

ref: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Rɛkab biibaal la baŋ faa ra yir Malkija n faa ɛɛ Bɛf Hakɛrɛm paga nabɔma, genii faa kuari Kpaga Dominuuzeŋ la, di du u dolli, gbessi, lugbidaazi ani u kattibɔra.

ref: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
text: Baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Kol Hɔzɛ biibaal Salum, n faa ɛɛ Mizpa paga nabɔma ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la banna yir Bule Dominuuzeŋ la. U faa kuaruubuu ma, di tɔ u nyuu, di du u gbessi ni a kattikuna. U kaa kuari ma Silɔam Pol koŋlii la n dugli Koori Kambol guŋŋ di ga hel lɔŋa la n lii Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ di tuu ra la la.

ref: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
text: Azbuk biibaal Nɛhɛmia la n faa ɛɛ Bɛf Zur paga yeŋ nabɔma ge faa kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n kawɛɛ la ma guŋŋ di chaŋ Koori Deevid Ŋmam, di ga hel pol la baŋ kiwee ani Laallɔkpega Dia la.

ref: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
text: Levi dee ni ba sitɔɔri Bani biibaal Rɛhum ge kuari ma hiŋ. Hasabia la n faa ɛɛ Keila paga yeŋ nabɔma, ge faa kuari ma ba paga koŋlii yeŋ di hiŋ.

ref: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
text: Baŋ ga hel de, Jesua biibaal Ɛza, n faa ɛɛ Mizpa nabɔma ge faa kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n du ba dɔŋkuna dia see guŋŋ di ga hel a koŋlii sirii.

ref: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
text: Baal bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Zabai ge biibaal Baruk faa aah siwii, di faari a sirii di kuaruu ma guŋŋ di ga hel Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Ɛliasib dominua.

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
text: Yuria biibaal Mɛrɛmɔf, u naabaal ɛɛ Hakɔz, ge faa ma lii Ɛliasib dia dominua ga hel a dia tuna.

ref: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la n soge bar Jɛrusalɛm, ge ma a koŋlii yeŋ di hiŋ.

ref: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
text: Bɛnjamin ni Hasub ge faa kuari ma a koŋlii bɔra la n du ba dia see. Maasɛya biibaal Azaria, u naabaallɛ faa Anania, ge faa ma a koŋlii bɔr la n dugli u dia.

ref: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
text: Hɛnadad biibaal Binui ge kuari a koŋlii ma lii Azaria dia guŋŋ di ga hel a koŋlii sirii.

ref: Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Uzai biibaal Palal ge kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma chaŋ a koŋlii sirii ni diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ lii kooridia chiŋ n dugli guuri diŋŋee la. Parɔs biibaal Pɛdaaya ge kuari ma hiŋ.

ref: He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived. Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia balaa la n faa du Ɔfɛl giŋgimii la ge kuari a koŋlii ma guŋŋ di ga hel u wiifurii, di chaŋ Nii Dominuuzeŋ la, di ra la u diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ la zɛɛ.

ref: The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
text: Tɛkua baala ge kaa ma a koŋlii guŋŋ lii diijaŋ la n saagɛɛ, di ga hel Ɔfɛl koŋlii la. Ba mai nɛɛhinnɛ guŋ.

ref: Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ge kuari ma a koŋlii bɔr la n pɛli Zagu Dominuuzeŋ la di ra la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag. Bɛl maa ma u dia see.

ref: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
text: Ima biibaal Zadɔk ge ma a koŋlii bɔr la n chaŋ u dia hiŋ. Sɛkania biibaal Sɛmaaya la n faa ɛɛ Wiifurii Dominuuzeŋ guuri ge ma a koŋlii yeŋ hiŋ.

ref: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
text: Sɛlɛmia biibaal Hanania ni Zalaf biibambinumbɛlhiŋ, Hanun ge kaa kuari a koŋlii yeŋ ma hiŋ. Bɛrɛkia biibaal Mɛsulam ge kuari a koŋlii bɔr la n chaŋ u dia ma.

ref: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
text: Saliŋ luuri Malkija ge kuari ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel Kɔraawiizi Dia balaa ni kɔkɔɔza dia n chaŋ Mifkad Dominuuzeŋ guŋŋ di ga chug dia la n du u sirii chiŋ la.

ref: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
text: Saliŋ luura ni kɔkɔɔza ge kuari a koŋlii tuna ma, di lii u sirii chiŋ dia guŋŋ di ga chug Peeza Dominuuzeŋ.

ref: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
text: Sanbalat n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa Jus hina bittɔɔ kuari a koŋlii di ra ma la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ.

ref: In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
text: Awia, u jaa chi u dɔŋahina ni bolzeŋ Samaria hina laallɔɔra be, di ŋɔ, “Beedee Jus hina nɛvɛɛlaa naa ra ɛɛ gunnɛi? Ba kaa ra nyiŋŋuu bá bir kuari ba koŋlii naa maa? Ba daŋ lizi mbusuzii gɛɛ? Ba daŋ maubuu tuŋ hɔpizi kpaŋaa? Ba daŋ kaa wer kpa bifuuhlaa naa di maa?”

ref: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
text: Denii Ammɔn hinuu Tobia n chigɛ u kɛra la ge ŋɔ, “Beedee koŋliire ba ra ma kennei? Di nyɛgɛ gba haŋ tinni ba bia koŋlii naa ni gba, u daŋ chol.”

ref: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
text: Awia, n suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, nuu yaa be, dikuu banna gbɛlli yaa wia. Gil chagzaa naa banna chagzi yaa naa laŋŋi ba ni. Kpa baa du ba dɔma nonee, bá lɔ ba laal, di lauri baa kaali hɛrdumazi.

ref: Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
text: Gilɛɛ gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, di gilɛɛ suuh ba wichɔgaa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba chagzi yaa banla n na mau.”

ref: The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again.
text: Awia, yaa faa ma a koŋlii guŋŋ di ga hel u galga, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra maanii faa aah siwii.

ref: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
text: Denii Sanbalat, Tobia, Lɔrbizi, Ammɔn ani Asdɔd hina maa n faa wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa wettoo di ra ma Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii hiŋ, di ra fargi u bowooni, ba baana fuuh werge maa.

ref: and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem.
text: Awia, ba maa ta jina bá ga lɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina, di koozi wia du yaa ni.

ref: But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
text: Ka yaa faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, di lizi nɛra ba ra guu yaa wibaŋa ni hamuŋa maa.

ref: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
text: A biinii, Juda hina ŋɔ, “A maara bɔra ra huauh, hembugle la ge du kaŋ werge. Awia, yaa wàá wer kuari a koŋlii ma.”

ref: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
text: Yaa dɔma ge ŋɔ, “Mɔɔ ka ba zum guŋ gɛɛ di na yaa, di yaa zuu ba biini kpu baa, a huma tuŋ.”

ref: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
text: Denii Jus hina la n soge dugli baa la, ba di wa ŋɔ yaa be nua bufi, di ŋɔ, “Bɔr la maa iin niŋ ga, ba daŋ teŋ yaa di lɔ yaa.”

ref: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
text: Awia, n gil baŋhina lii domeezi biini, di vɔɔ ni ba tokobizi, kandaazi ani hozi, di ga guu ba bariizi koŋlii bɔra la baŋ faa haa waa mawɛɛ tuŋ la.

ref: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
text: Miŋ binni wia guŋŋ di wa kaali, n izi chi, ka ŋɔ nabɔnzenaa, nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa be, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm baa. Ií ra liizi Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, u wia kaa dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la, ka izi naa tɛɛ ii lulla, ii biizi, ii haana ani ii diini.”

ref: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
text: Yaa dɔma n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ yaa zum ba jina la baŋ tawɛɛ la wiarɛ, Kɔraawiizi ge kaa chɔguu la, yaa jaa bir la a koŋlii bɔr, bɛl maa kaa gaa hum u huma.

ref: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
text: Di lii a hɔl hiŋ, n huŋhunna hiŋ yeŋ ɔɔ ra humuu, ka ba yeŋ ge laali ba laal laala di kpogli kandaazi, laal pɛrɛtuzi ani hozi di guu. Nabɔnzi la ge chi Juda hina la

ref: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
text: n na ma a koŋlii la har. Banla n na chi kuna ɔɔ kpa nonii bɛllɛ di ra hum, ka kpa bɛl ge di kpogli dɔŋkuŋ.

ref: Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
text: A maara bɛl maa ge ɔɔ kpa u tokobi vɔɔ u chara ka ra hum. Nɛr la n ɔɔ faa ra huuh bensuno la ge ɔɔ chi n kɛra.

ref: I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another.
text: Denii n ŋɔ a nabɔnzenaa, nabɔnzi ani a nɛra maa be, “Huma la bɔr wassɔɔ, yaa waa ɔɔ chi a koŋlii zɛɛ dugli dɔŋa.

ref: If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
text: Di ii wa nuu bensunoniina wiraa bɔr la maa, ií ra ba yaa be de. Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la daŋ naa tɛɛ yaa!”

ref: Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
text: Awia, yaa yeŋ ɔɔ faa ra humuu, ka yaa yeŋ ge kpogli kandaazi, di lii chɔɔzimpikke guŋŋ di ga hel saŋa la bɔr n ɔɔ waa lauri siwee, chinchiŋwilaa ra lii la.

ref: I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, n ŋɔ a nɛra be lugɔ baal maa ni u hiini ɔɔ du Jɛrusalɛm hamuŋa ni di ra guu yaa, ka di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ bá ra hum.

ref: I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
text: Miŋ gɛɛ n niuna gɛɛ n huŋhunna gɛɛ a guure n faa du n be la, bɛl maa faa waa u laala witte, ka ɔɔ kpogli u dɔŋkuŋ, haali di u waa la ú ga ɛɛ nii gba.

ref: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
text: A saŋa hiŋ, baala ni ba haana faa nuumi di ra du ba dɔŋa Jus hina.

ref: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
text: Baŋhina ra ŋɔ, “Yaa biizi kpillɔɔ werge. Yaa ra nyiŋŋi miarɛ yá di, di piri.”

ref: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
text: Denii baŋhina ge faa ra ŋɔ, “Yaa kpa yaa kooni, yaa grepu daazi kooni ani diinii dau talma, ka ya wer na mia nɛnnɛ a hel yaa dii, lɔchɔgii saŋa.”

ref: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
text: Baŋhina ge ŋɔ, “Yaa kim kebeere turgi yaa kooni ni yaa grepu daazi kooni lampoo tɛɛ koori.

ref: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
text: Yaa maa ɛɛ nɛdeekpannɛ. Gunla ba biizi n duwɛɛ, gunnɛ yaa gba biizi du. Ka aabuu la, yaa biizii yaa kpa birgi yoma. Yaa biihaana baŋhinaa yaa kpa yoo, ba birgi yoma. Yaa waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa kooni ni yaa grepu daazi kooni maanii birgi nɛra baŋhina hora.”

ref: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
text: Miŋ wa nuu ba nuumaa naa, n baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
text: Denii n fɛ a wia nfɛrɛ guŋŋ ka hau a nabɔnzenaa ni a nabɔnzi ni, di ŋɔ ba be, “Ɛrɛɛ ii ra sag ii himmaa lulla nii gunnɛi?” Denii n chaali nɛkpila ya binni a wia biini.

ref: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
text: N ŋɔ ba be, “Filaŋkennaa, yaa bittɔɔ yau yaa lulla Jus hina la baŋ faa yoowe tɛɛ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la. Ka ii kaa biruu ra yoo baa, ka ba kaa wa yoo baa tɛɛ yaa.” Denii ba maa faa so kirkirkir, dikuu baŋ waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ ba ŋɔ wia.

ref: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
text: Denii n kaa ŋɔ, “Wii naa iinna ɛɛ naa waa deŋlee. A dɛkkɔɔ iinna hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa. Guŋ daŋ gil yaa dɔma la n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la, wàá na bɔr di ra ɛɛ yaa chɛɛtɛ.

ref: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
text: Miŋwaa ni n lulla ni n huŋhunna ra kim a nɛraa kebee ni mia, ka yaa wàá fir baa bá turgi.

ref: Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
text: Ií gil ba kima maa tɛɛ baa, di kebeere gɛɛ mia gɛɛ siŋ gɛɛ ɔlivi nuurɛ. Ií bir kpa ba kooni, grepu daazi kooni maa ani ba diini tɛɛ baa manaŋ!”

ref: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
text: Ba ŋɔ, “Yaa daŋ bir kpaa tɛɛ baa. Yaa wàá ka lɛɛ baa kummaa di jaa. Yaa daŋ hiŋ i nua.” Denii n faa gil Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la maa chaali, di gil nabɔnzenaa ni nabɔnzi hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ hiŋ.

ref: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
text: Denii n lizi n tagta di zigluu, ka ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Kenne Kɔ́raawiizi zigli nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ nua naa hiŋaa. U dia ni u kundɔɔlaa maa daŋ lii u nonii.” Awia, a nɛra maa ŋɔ, “Ami!” Ka ba jaa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ, di ɛɛ gunla baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ ɛɛ la.

ref: I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed.
text: Di lii Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis kora dii binni tokkohiŋ biinii, ba liziŋ n ɛɛ nabɔma Juda hɛri guŋŋ di wa hel u binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛhiŋ. Binni fidaanɛɛrɛ guŋ, di n ni n lulla bɛl maa haa waa diwee la baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma la diwee.

ref: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
text: Ka nabɔma la n faa diwee mɔɔ ka a wa heliŋ lawaa, ɔɔ faa ra sunni a nɛraa werge maa. U ɔɔ faa lɛɛ baabuu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau tokkoanɛɛ, diwee ani siŋ hɔpizii maa. A nabɔma harbɔɔhiŋra ge ɔɔ faa kpogli baabuu di ra sunni, ka miŋwaa waa guŋ ɛɛwɛ, dikuu minna ɔm Kɔraawiizi wia.

ref: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
text: Ama, miŋwaa faa kpa n siaahmu maanii du a koŋlii mai wia biini. N huŋhunna maanii chaali a koŋlii zɛɛ, yaa ra hum a huma. Yaa waa hɛri maa lɛɛwɛ.

ref: Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
text: Hɔpizii maa, nau, penanaa anumbɛl ani zagkpilaa ba ɔɔ faa daali tɛŋ. A hɔpizaa fi maa, siŋ maa deere ba ɔɔ faa daali su bɔr. Annii maa biini, ka maa ɔɔ faa lɛɛ kummaa lii a hɛri nabɔma kuntɛɛlaa biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra tɔɔrɔɔ faa nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ.

ref: I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, gil n wia parii, í ra liizi n wia, dikuu gunla miŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ nɛra naa wia.

ref: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates.
text: Sanbalat, Tobia ani Gɛsɛm la n ɛɛ Lɔrbi la ni yaa dɔma n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ n bittɔɔ kuari a koŋlii ma, haali di tɔɔgi u bowooni maa, ka n haa waa u dominuuzenaa gbessi waa duwɛɛ la,

ref: Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way.
text: Sanbalat ni Gɛsɛm tili ŋɔ n be, “Ba ya na dɔŋa bola la bɛl n du Ono Lɛl biini.” Ka ba faa ra ɛɛ dawarii bá ɛɛŋ wichɔgii bɛl.

ref: So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.”
text: Denii n faa hum n balaa bá ga ŋɔ ba be, “N na ɛɛ wizeŋ bɛllɛ, awia, màá wer tuu ba ii be de. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ń gil a huma ka tuu ba ii benei?”

ref: They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
text: Bunaazu maanii ba faa tiliŋ keŋ himmaa, n ge ɔɔ bir ŋɔ a wikpaŋ.

ref: Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter,
text: Denii bunue hiŋ, Sanbalat hum u balii, di sɛbi hɔŋ ŋɔ ú kpa wa tɛŋ, ka waa u nua tɔwɛɛ.

ref: which said: A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true!
text: Kenne u faa sɛbi a hɔŋ biini, “Hɛssi maa hina nuuwɔɔ lugɔ i ni Jus hina la ɛɛ nuukpannɛ di ra nyiŋŋi ii du dɔŋ, awiarɛ ii bir kuari a koŋlii di ra ma. Gɛsɛm ge ŋɔ wibiire! Yaa kaa nuu lugɔ hinuu ra nyiŋŋi i birgi ba koori.

ref: You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
text: A guŋ wia, i lizi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzii, bá sii i wia tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina, di ŋɔ, ‘Koori du Judaa!’ Filaŋkeŋ, a koorizeŋ daŋ nuu a wii naa. Awia, ba ya ta jina.”

ref: I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
text: Denii n tili ŋɔ u be, “Wia naa maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa waa wibii ɛɛwɛ. I himmaa laakal wiŋɔɔlaarɛ.”

ref: Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
text: Ba ra ɔnzi yaabuu, di ra fɛ, “Ba bɔra daŋ huah a huma humaa wia, bá gil a humaa.” Awia, n suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, tɛŋ fɔŋŋa filaŋkeŋ!”

ref: One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
text: A hɔl bɛl, n la Dɛlaaya biibaal Sɛmaaya dia, u naabaal genii faa Mɛhɛtabɛl. U faa suah diarɛ, wàá ka wer lii baaŋ. U ŋɔ n be, “Gil ya la ga suah Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, ka tɔɔgi u dominuuzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ra nyiŋŋuu bá wa kpui hamuŋa naa.”

ref: I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
text: Denii n ŋɔ u be, “Mìŋ́ baal du keŋ di chɔ ra suah? Ń chɔ ga suah Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, dikuu n miibɔɔ wiaa? Akai, màá ɛɛ guŋ!”

ref: Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me
text: N faa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi lɛi hum Sɛmaaya. Sanbalat ni Tobiare lɔu paah, di ŋɔ ú wa ŋɔ wia du n ni.

ref: and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
text: Ba kpaubuu ú wa ɔnziŋ, ń ɛɛ wichɔgaa lugɔ kennaa uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, bá jaa chɔg n sɔŋ, di duŋ hiihzi.

ref: Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me. The Work Is Finished
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, a liizi gunla Tobia ni Sanbalat n ɛɛwɛ. A liizi gunla dɔgtɛɛ Noadia la n ɛɛ haaŋ ni dɔgtɛɛzi la maa n faa ra nyiŋŋi bá ɔnziŋ la wia. A koŋlii mai tunaa wia

ref: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken
text: Baagu la banna yir Ɛlul, u hɔpizaa tokko ni anuehiŋ hɔllɛ, ba faa ma a koŋlii tuŋ. Hɔpizaa tokkoanɛɛ ni fidaanɛɛrɛ ba faa kpa mau tuŋ.

ref: When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
text: Yaa dɔma ani hɛssi la maa hina n bar yaa n wa nuu guŋ, ɔnsii faa lau baa, ba bɔra huah, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa zummɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la hiinaare gillɛ a huma hum.

ref: All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Juda hina nabɔnzenaa faa ra sɛbi hɔna kpila di ra tɛɛ Tobia, u ge bir sɛbi ra tɛɛ baa.

ref: Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
text: Jus hinuu Ara biibaal Sɛkania n faa ɛɛ u hila wia, Juda hina kpila maanii faa chigɛ u har. Di kaa kpa jaa, u biibaal Jɛhɔhanan ge faa kpa Mɛsulam biihaannɛ. A Mɛsulam ge mɛɛrɛ faa Bɛrɛkia.

ref: The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
text: A nɛra ɔɔ faa bagli wipazi la maa Tobia n ɛɛwɛnɛ tɛŋ, ka bir ga ŋɔ u be gunla n ge n ŋɔwɛɛ. Tobia sɛbi hɔna tɛŋ, di ra ɔnziŋ.

ref: Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Jɛrusalɛm faa ɛɛ bolzenne werge, ka u nɛra faa waa kpil, u diini ge faa waa kuarɛɛ ma.

ref: kilograms of gold,
text: , tassazi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi,

ref: This is a list of how many returned from each family group:
text: Gibiɔn naanna faa du tokkoanaazu ni fidaanue,

ref: This is a list of how many returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns:
text: Sɛnaa naanna faa du kagboŋa ahoro ani kalfa kabɛl ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ,

ref: from Nebo;
text: Bɛsai, Mɛyunim, Nɛfusim,

ref: This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites:
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuguure, Salum, Ata, Talmɔn, Akub, Hatita ani Sobai naanna ge maa faa du kalfa ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni ŋmantannaazi,

ref: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
text: Awia, Jus hɛri nabɔma faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ba gilɛɛ kaa di diwee la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, see Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ wa du de, di kpa Urim ni Tumim di ra hum.

ref: Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave
text: Nɛra la maa n faa kawɛɛ ge tɛɛ saliŋ kilozi kalfa ni tokkoahoro ni ŋmantannaazi,

ref: bowls to be used in the temple, and
text: ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina bɔmbɔga kalfaanue ni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ,

ref: And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee, Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuguure, yiryitta, nɛkpila, Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna ani Izrɛl hina maa faa so Juda bola ni u bolzenaa.

ref: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Ɛzra la n faa ɛɛ ba karchi, jaa chi janjiga nyuu. Ba du a jannɛ dikuu a guŋ hɔpizii naa wia. U faa ra karmi a hɔnnɛ ka baala naa chi u nodig, Matitia, Sɛma, Anaaya, Yuria, Hilkia ani Maasɛya. Banla ge n faa chigɛ u nomɛɛllɛ, Pɛdaaya, Misɛl, Malkija, Hasum, Hasbadana, Zɛkaria ani Mɛsulam.

ref: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
text: Denii Ɛzra pilli a hɔŋ. Uŋ chigɛ jaŋ nyuu la wia, nɛra maanii faa wette nau. Uŋ ŋɔ u pilli a hɔŋ, nɛr maanii izee chi.

ref: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
text: Denii Ɛzra ŋɔ, “Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizizeŋ.” A nɛra maa lalli ba nonee chiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Ami! Ami!!” Ka ba maa giŋŋi di willi jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
text: Ba faa karmɔɔrɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg Hɔŋ biini, di bagli a Gbɔgni maa zɛɛzi nɛnnɛ tɛɛ baa, bá zum.

ref: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
text: Denii Nɛhɛmia la n faa ɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma, Ɛzra la n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ, di kaa ɛɛ ba karchi ani Levi dee la n faa ra bagli a nɛra la jaa ŋɔ ba be, “Zinaa hɔpizii naa ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinaniirɛ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Bɛl maa gilɛɛ ka gil ú biini chɔgi, ú ra wii.” Dikuubɛɛwiai, baŋ faa ra karmi Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni Hɔŋ la, a nɛra biine chɔkkɔɔ, ba ra wii.

ref: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
text: Denii Nɛhɛmia jaa ŋɔ ba be, “Ií ra la gaa di iihinaa, di di diwee la iinna nyiŋŋi, di nyɔɔ siŋ la ge n par ia. Ka kpa aŋhina tɛɛ banla n waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ, bá ge di. Zinaa hɔpizii naa ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinaniirɛ Kɔraawiizi be. Awia, bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa gil u biini ra chɔgi. Bɔsɔna la Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ ia labuu ɛɛ ii fɔŋŋa.”

ref: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
text: Levi dee la jaa tig a nɛra bampiree, di ŋɔ, “Ií maa ɛɛ bɔɔiih, dikuubɛɛwiai, zinaa hɔpizii naa ɛɛ hɔpizinaniinaniirɛ Kɔraawiizi be. Ií gilɛɛ gil ii biine chɔgi.”

ref: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
text: Denii a nɛra maa la ga di, di nyɔɔ, di di bahinaa nɛnnɛ, ka kpa aŋhina ge tɛɛ nɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba nuu wia la maa baŋ karmɛɛ tɛɛ baa la zɛɛrɛ.

ref: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
text: A baagu hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ, domeezi nabɔnzi, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ani Levi dee maa faa la Ɛzra la n ɛɛ ba karchi be, bá ga helli gunla Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la n na bagli.

ref: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
text: Ba faa na a Gbɔg Hɔŋ, Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ Moosis la biini lugɔ di Izrɛl hina waa di Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ la, bɛl maa ɔɔ lii u dia di gaa zuu pampanni biini, guŋŋ ba wa ɛɛ wiimaa tuŋ.

ref: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
text: Denii a nɛra lii ga mɔnni a daazi kela ba, di wa du pampannizi ba salli ni diŋŋizi, Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋizi, bɔwar la n dugli Nii Dominuuzeŋ ani unla n dugli Ɛfram Dominuuzeŋ la biine.

ref: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
text: Banla maa baŋ faa laurɛɛ kaali hɛrdumazi la n bittɛ ba bol la, du pampannizi di zuu a biine. Di haŋ lii Nun biibaal Josua de dui saŋa guŋŋ di wa hel a guŋ hɔpizii hiŋ, Izrɛl hina waa kaa ɛɛ a keŋ wii naa maa, di a hɔl naa lɛi. A hɔl hiŋ, ba bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ werge maa.

ref: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
text: Di haŋ lii a hɔpizizenaa faaraa hɔl di ga hel u tuna, hɔpizi biimaanii Ɛzra ɔɔ faa karmi Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg Hɔŋ la yeŋ. Denii ba faa di a hɔpizizenaa naa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ la, ba maa chaali, gunla a Gbɔg Hɔŋ n baglɛɛ la.

ref: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
text: A baagu himmaa hɔpizaa tokko ni anaazuhiŋ hɔl, Izrɛl hina maa chaali di vɔɔ nua, ka laali gbɔglɔŋ laala, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa waari ba nyuuni.

ref: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
text: Banla maa n ɛɛ Izrɛl dee la faa bargi bahinaarɛ lii hɔɔhra maa be. Denii ba chi de di sɛɛ chɔgri, dikuu ba ni ba naabaala maa wichɔgaa wia.

ref: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
text: Gunnɛ ba kaa chi de himmaa di karmi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la Gbɔg Hɔŋ la, karfizi ahoro a hɔl hiŋ, di kaa kpa karfizi ahoro di sɛɛ chɔgri, dikuu ba wichɔgaa maa wia, ka jaami Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la.

ref: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
text: Ba faa kuari chignibɔttɛ de izi chiŋ alugɔ bimbinni. Levi dee naabuu faa chigɛ de, Jesua, Bani, Kadmiɛl, Sɛbania, Buni, Sɛrɛbia, Bani ani Kɛnani. Baabuu faa gbooli Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la werge maa.

ref: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
text: Ka Levi dee naa, Jesua, Kadmiɛl, Bani, Hasabnɛya, Sɛrɛbia, Hɔdia, Sɛbania ani Pɛtahia faa chi a chignibɔr hiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “Ií izi chi di chɔli Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Ií ra chɔluu saŋaa saŋa maa! Ií gil nɛr maa ra chɔli u sɔŋ la n dɔɔ girme werge la, haali u girme n kaali newee chɔlaa gba.

ref: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
text: I bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Hinuu ta chinchiŋ, chinchiŋwilaa, hɛri maa ani kuna la maa n du u biine, muuzenaa ni kuna la maa n du a biine. Hinuu tɛɛ kummaa miibɔɔ, u du de. Kuna la maa n du chinchiŋ ra jaamiibuu.

ref: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
text: Hinuu Kɔraawiizi la n lizi Abram lii bol la banna yir Ur la n du Babilɔn hɛri, di bir dau u sɔŋ Abraham.

ref: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
text: I nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ u wia dɔɔ wibiire i be, awiarɛ i ŋɔ nua tɛu lugɔ i daŋ gil u naanna wa dɔɔ Keenan, Hitti, Amɔri, Pɛriz, Jɛbus ani Girgas hina maa hɛri. I gillɔɔ i wiŋɔzi hiŋ ɛɛ wibii, dikuu i wia n dɔɔ wibii wia.

ref: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
text: I faa na gunla yaa naabaala n na di dɔgnyaa Ijip hɛri, di kaa nuu ba wile lɔi, di lii Muuzeŋaahmu la nua.

ref: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
text: Baŋ faa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ Ijip hɛri la, i faa ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wiarɛ di gil Ijip koori, u nabɔnzi ani nɛra la maa n du u hɛri la di dɔgnya, dikuubɛɛwiai, i nawɔɔrɛ gunla Ijip hina n faa ra sunni yaa naabaala barabara ni. I faa na sɔnnɛ tɛɛ i hiŋ di wa lii ni zinaa.

ref: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
text: I faa gillɔɔ a muuzeŋ bargi bɔra anɛɛ, ka ba ga de di vol bɔhilii gi. Ka ba dɔma la n faa ra duŋŋi ba luge, bá lauri baa la waa, i faa gillɔɔ ba ɛɛ lugɔ bia, a muuzeŋ di ba maa.

ref: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
text: Hɔpizaa, i ɔɔ faa kpa baama la n du miriti lugɔ venne di tɔ ba see, hamuŋa ge i kpa niŋ n lugɔ vem, di tɔ ba see, u ra chaani baa, ba ra vol.

ref: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
text: I faa lii chinne tuu Bizeŋ Sinaai, di ŋɔ wia ɛɛ baa. Di tɛɛ baa i Gbɔg ni i widaulaa la n wesse werge.

ref: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
text: I ŋɔ ba gil i Heezaa Hɔpizii la ɛɛ naniinanii, di ga i balii Moosis be, di kpa i widaulaa ni i Gbɔgni la tɛɛ baa.

ref: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
text: Lɔzi n waa kpu baa, i tɛɛ baabuu paanuu lii chiŋ. Niinyɔgzi ge n waa kpu baa, i tɛɛ baabuu nii lii bizeŋ ni. Denii i kaa ŋɔ ba be lugɔ bá la ga foozi hɛri la hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ tɛɛ baa la.

ref: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
text: Ka yaa naabaala kpoŋaa ni ba dignikpega wia, ba faa waa i widaulaa hiŋŋɛ.

ref: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
text: Ba faa kuari vugrɛ u ɛɛ lugɔ nabii, di ŋɔ, ‘Vug la n lɛɛ yaa lii Ijip hɛri labuu keŋ!’ Na gunla baŋ chagzii mag!

ref: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
text: Binni tokkoanɛɛ biini, i kpogli baabuu nɛnnɛ hɛribɔduma biini, di faa tɛɛ baa kunla maa n dɛkkɛ, Ba laalaa waa kɔzɛɛ maa, ba naazi ge waa ɔrgɛɛ.

ref: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
text: I gil ba lul biibaala di du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa n du chiŋ. I kpogli baabuu di la ba ni hɛri la hiŋ ŋɔ nua tɛɛ ba mɛɛwaa lugɔ baabuu niŋ ŋmɛnɛ dɔɔu la.

ref: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
text: Ka baŋ faa kpoŋŋe di dɔɔ dignikpega wia, ba dii mmɔri, di bir har kpu i Gbɔg. Di kpu i dɔgtɛɛzi la n na karfi baa, di ra bagli baa wia, bá bir di ra hiŋii la. Ba ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu i ni, di chagzii werge maa.

ref: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
text: Denii i kpa baa tɛɛ ba dɔma, ba dɔma hiŋ sunni baa. Ba dɔma hiŋ n waa sunni baa la, ba bir lɔ wile tɛi. I lii chiŋ nuu ba wile, dikuu i nɛsunaa werge wia, di tɛɛ baa lɛɛra, ba lɛɛ baa lii ba dɔma nonee biine.

ref: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
text: Ka baŋ wa na ba hiŋ tuŋ, ba kaa bir ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu i ni. I kaa kpa baa du ba dɔma nonee, ba dɔma hiŋ di kora ba ni. Denii ba kaa wii tɛi, i kaa nuu ba wiraa lii chiŋ. Dikuu i nɛsunaa wia, i ɔɔ faa lɛɛ baabuu saŋa kpila maa.

ref: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
text: I faa di baabuu kanyitti, biŋkpila maa biine. I gillɔɔ i dɔgtɛɛzi ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa, i Duma la fɔŋŋa biini, ka ba vɛɛ nuui. Denii i kpa baa du hɛrdumazi hina la n bar baa la nonee biine.

ref: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
text: Ka dikuu i nɛsunaa wia, haa baa vɛɛwɛ ta gɛɛ haa gillɛ ba wia tuŋ durnya biini. I ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na suŋ nɛra ninɛɛ, di ra na ba sinyɛna!

ref: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
text: Filaŋkennaa, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, unla n dɔɔ girme di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, i wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, i ra hiŋ nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la. Tɔɔrɔɔ naa n chol yaa ni yaa koora, sitɔɔra, i kizeehina, i huŋhunna, yaa naabaala ani i nɛra maa, di lii Asiiria koora kora dii saŋa maa guŋŋ di wa lii zinaa, gilɛɛ gil a ɛɛ wijigzi i be.

ref: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
text: Annii maa n huuzi yaa naa biini, ka i wia dɔɔ wibiire, i ɛɛ wii la n deŋlee, ka yaa waa ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

ref: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
text: Yaa naabaala, yaa koora, yaa sitɔɔra ani i kizeehina vɛɛ i Gbɔg hiŋaarɛ. Ba waa i wiŋɔɔlaa ni i karfaazi hiŋŋɛ.

ref: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
text: Haali baŋ faa soge ba himmaa hɛri gba, i kissi baabuu, di tɛɛ baa daama ni hɛrsum. Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi gɛɛ di ra humii.

ref: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
text: Dikuu yaa wichɔgaa ɛɛi wia, pattikuna werge la maa n ɔɔ lii de, ɛɛ koora la hiŋ tɛɛ yaa la horaa. Ba ra di koraa yaa ni yaa sela maa ni, gunla maa n par baa. Yaa biine chɔkkɔɔ werge maa!” A nɛra n ɛɛ nuukpaŋ wia

ref: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
text: “Dikuu annii maa wia, yaa ra ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, di sɛbuu ra dau, di gil yaa sitɔɔra, Levi dee ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina kpa ba nonee jaguu.”
