ref: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah. The Agreement
text: Maluk, Harim ani Baana.

ref: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
text: ni ba nabɔnzenaa maa jaa hɛɛhzi, di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be lugɔ ba daŋ hiŋ u Gbɔg la, u widaulaa, u baglaazi ani u kiizi la uŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ u balii Moosis la. Di ba waa guŋ wa ɛɛwɛ, nuuseei di baa.

ref: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
text: Di hɛrdumazi hina wa kpa ba kooliŋkuna gɛɛ ba kunyoolaa di ba yaa bol, bá wa yoo Heezaa Hɔpizii gɛɛ hɔpizinaiinanii maa, yaa wàá yawaa. Binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ waa maa biini, yaa wàá par. Kima la maa nɛra n di yaa ge, yaa daŋ gilaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
text: Bina maa, yaa bɛl maa daŋ ɔɔ kɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu kebisaujiga, bá kpa hiini turgi Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna.

ref: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
text: Paanuu la baŋ ɔɔ kpa dau tɛɛbul ni la, hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa mia, hɔpizi biimaa mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, Heezaa Hɔpizii mbusuzi lizaa kuna, Baagufalii Hɔpizizenaa ani hɔpizizenaa aŋhina, mbusunanaa aŋhina, Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa giltɛɛi mbusuzi lizaa ani kuna la maa ban niŋ kpa di ra hum Kɔraawiizi Dia huma maa, yaabuu dɔɔ a maa kɛɛi.

ref: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
text: Yaa ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee ani nɛra la maa n kawɛɛ daŋ ɔɔ ta kuna bina maa, di na dee la n niŋ ɔɔ ba daahilaa ni, bá ɔɔ kpa di fuuh kuna Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ u Gbɔg Hɔŋ biini la.

ref: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
text: Bina maa, yaa daŋ ɔɔ kpa yaa lugli pattikuna ani daazi lugli nɔna maa, ba i Dia.

ref: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
text: Di kaa lii gunla baŋ sɛbɛɛ i Gbɔg Hɔŋ biini la, yaa bɛl maa daŋ ɔɔ kpa u biibambilugli, u nauna, peeza ani buuna hora, di wa tɛɛ i kizeehina la n na hum i Dia la.

ref: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
text: Di kaa jaa annii maa ni, yaa daŋ ɔɔ kpa yaa kooni lugli mia sau, yaa daazi lugli nɔna, lugli siŋ ani nuu wa tɛɛ i kizeehina, i Dia biini. Yaa daŋ ɔɔ kpa yaa pattikuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa tɛɛ Levi dee la, di lii bola la maa biine yaa n na par la, dikuubɛɛwiai, baabuu ɔɔ ra lɛɛa.

ref: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
text: I kizeehina la n lii Aarɔn naanna biini labuu ɔɔ ra hiŋ a Levi dee, ba ra lɛɛ a kuna fi maa bɔkpaŋ. Di ba wa lɛɛa tuŋ, bá ɔɔ kpa a fi bɔkpaŋ ga du i Dia kuna dauribɔr.

ref: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
text: Izrɛl hina ni Levi dee daŋ ɔɔ lizi mia, sinfalii ani ɔlivi nuu, bá kpa du i Dia kuna dauribɔr biini. Denii i kizeehina, dominuuzenaa guure ani yiryitta maa du. Yaa wàá vɛɛ i Dia ta maa.”

ref: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
text: A nɛra sitɔɔra ni domeezi faa so Jɛrusalɛm biini. Banla maa ge n kawɛɛ la, ba ta kunaa di lizi domeekpaŋ lii domeezi fi maa biine, ba so bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm la n ɛɛ naniinanii la biini. Ka banla maa n jaa ka la, jaa ga so ba himmaa bola.

ref: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
text: Denii a nɛra jaa chɔli banla maa n lizi bahinaa ŋɔ ba daŋ la ga so Jɛrusalɛm biini la.

ref: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
text: Denii Izrɛl hina baŋhina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, Levi dee, Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna ani Solomɔn balaa naanna faa so ba himmaa hɛssi, Juda bola biine. Juda hɛri sitɔɔra la n faa soge Jɛrusalɛm biini la sɔnaa keŋ,

ref: From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez,
text: Pɛrɛz naanna la n soge Jɛrusalɛm biini faa du baala la n ɛɛ nɛkpega kalfaanaazu ni tokkoahoro ni ŋmantannaazi,

ref: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
text: u lullaa faa Gabai ni Salai. A Bɛnjamin dee la maa n faa soge Jɛrusalɛm biini la faa du kalfa kabɛl ni tokko ni ŋmantannaazi,

ref: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
text: Zikri biibaal Jowɛllɛ faa ba sitɔɔri, Hasɛnua biibaal Juda ge faa ra hiŋ ba hɛri karchizi nabɔma ni a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
text: Hilkia biibaal Sɛraaya. U naabaalaa faa Mɛsulam, Zadɔk, Mɛrayɔf ani Ahitub n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma.

ref: from his clan who served in the temple. The third priest to settle there was Adaiah son of Jeroham. His ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah.
text: . Adaaya, u mɛɛrɛ Jeroham, u naabaal ɛɛ Pɛlalaaya. U naabaala baŋhinaa faa Amzi, Zɛkaria, Pasur ani Malkija

ref: clan leaders among his relatives. The fourth priest to settle there was Amashsai son of Azarel. His ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer.
text: . Ba maa ɛɛ ba domeezi nabɔnzi. Amassai, u mɛɛrɛ Azarɛl, u naabaal ɛɛ Azai. U naabaala baŋhinaa faa Mɛsilɛmɔf ani Ima.

ref: brave warriors from their clans, and their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim. Levites
text: . Ba karchizi nabɔmaa faa Hagɛdɔlim biibaal Zabdiɛl.

ref: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
text: Levi dee, Sɛmaaya, u mɛɛrɛ faa Hasub, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Azrikam. U naabaala baŋhinaa faa Hasabia ani Buni.

ref: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
text: Sabɛtai ni Jɔzabad n faa ɛɛ a Levi dee sitɔɔra baŋhinaa faa ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia baŋgia huma ni.

ref: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
text: Maatania, u mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Mika, u naabaal ge faa ɛɛ Zabdi. Zabdi ge mɛɛ faa ɛɛ Asaf. Asaf naabuu faa ɛɛ yiryitta ni wiisuŋŋaa sitɔɔri. Bakbukia genii faa ra hiini Matania. Abda, u mɛɛrɛ faa Samua, u naabaalaa faa Galal ani Jɛdutun.

ref: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
text: Dominuuguure genii faa, Akub, Talmɔn ani ba lullaa. Ba faa du baala kalfa ni tokkoahoro ni fidaanɛɛ,

ref: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
text: Izrɛl dizi maa n kawɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la faa jaa so ba naabaala hɛssi, Juda bolzenaa ani boljigzi maa biine.

ref: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia balaa faa so Ɔfɛl giŋgimii nyuu. Ziha ni Gispa faa ra binni ba ni.

ref: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
text: Levi dee nabɔma n faa du Jɛrusalɛmnɛ Bani biibaal Uzzi, u naabaallɛ faa Hasabia. U naabaalaa faa kaa ɛɛ Matania ni Mika ge. Uzi faa ɛɛ Asaf naanna la bɛl n faa ra yir yira Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, jaamaa saŋa.

ref: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
text: Koorii faa dɔɔ a yiryitta fɔŋŋa, di gil ba ra lɛɛ dɔŋa, ba hɔpizii maa wiɛɛlaa biini.

ref: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
text: Mɛsɛzabɛl biibaal Pɛtahia, n lii Zɛra domee biini di ɛɛ Juda dee hinuurɛ faa chigɛ Izrɛl hina naa Pɛsia hina seriya diiribɔr.

text: Baŋhina so Ɛn Rimɔn, Zɔra, Jamuf,

text: Zanoa, Adulam ani boljigzi la n baraa. Ba faa so Lakis di dugli ba kooni, di kaa so Azɛka ni u boljigzi. Ba faa sogo Bɛɛsibaa guŋŋ di ga hel Hinɔm Waluu.

text: Levi dee la sugezi aŋhina n lii Juda ge faa so Bɛnjamin.

ref: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
text: Sallu, Amɔk, Hilkia ani Jɛdaaya. Baabuu faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi, Jesua saŋa la.

ref: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,

ref: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
text: Bakbukia, Uni ani ba balaa ge ɔɔ chi chaŋ baa, di ra sɛɛ a yira.

ref: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
text: Jesua biibaallɛ Jɔyakim, Jɔyakim ge biibaallɛ Ɛliasib, Ɛliasib ge biibaallɛ Jɔyada.

ref: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
text: Jɔyada ge biibaal ɛɛ Jonatan, Jonatan biibaal ɛɛ Jadua.

ref: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,

text: Hilkia domee hor ɛɛ Hasabia, Jɛdaaya domee hor faa ɛɛ Nɛtanɛl.

ref: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
text: Ba faa sɛbi Levi dee ni Kɔraawiizi kizeehina domeezi nabɔnzi sɔnaa dau, di lii Ɛliasib, Jɔyada, Jɔhanan ani Jadua nabɔmuu dii saŋazi. Pɛsia Koorizeŋ Dariɔs kora dii saŋaa ba faa sɛbaa tuŋ.

ref: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
text: Ba faa sɛbi domeezi nabɔnzi sɔnaa lii Levi naanna biini guŋŋ di ga hel Ɛliasib biibaal Jɔhanan saŋa, di du ba Faala Hɔŋ biini.

ref: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
text: Levi dee la sitɔɔraa faa Hasabia, Sɛrɛbia, Kadmiɛl biibaal Jesua ani banla n ɔɔ faa chi chaŋ baa, ka ba ra jaami Kɔraawiizi di ra chɔluu la. Keŋkere bɛl hina sɛɛ di ra du a keŋkere bɛl hina gunla Kɔraawiizi balii Koori Deevid n faa sɛbɛɛ du hɔŋ biini la.

ref: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
text: Matania, Bakbukia, Obadia, Mɛsulam, Talmɔn ani Akubrɛ faa ra guu diibizi la banna dau kuna la n dugli dominuuzenaa la.

ref: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
text: Ba faa hum ba humaa Jesua biibaal Jɔyakim naabaal n ɛɛ Jɔzadak, Nɛhɛmia n faa ɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma ani Ɛzra n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ni karchi de dui saŋazi. Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii kpai du Kɔraawiizi nonee wia

ref: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
text: Baŋ wa ma Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii la tuŋ di ŋɔ ba kpau du Kɔraawiizi nonee, ba faa gillɔɔ Levi dee lii bɔra la maa baŋ duwɛɛ la ba Jɛrusalɛm, di wa di a guŋ hɔpizii hiŋ, di yir yira, di lɔ danyɛ pɛrɛtuzi, kemzi ani janjalanzi, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ ni bɔsɔna.

ref: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
text: Baŋhina faa lii Bɛf Gilgal, Gɛba ani Azmavɛf bariirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a yiryitta faa ma ba bolaa bar Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la n wa sɔ bahinaa di lizi ba doŋa ha, ka ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa la, ba jaa ɛɛ a nɛra, a koŋlii dominuuzenaa ani a koŋlii ge maa guŋ.

ref: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
text: Annii maa n wa tunnɛ, denii n gil Juda hina nabɔnzi tinni a koŋlii nyuu, ka n gil yiryitta sugezenaa anɛɛ jaa ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ. A suge bɛl ge tinni a koŋlii nodig keŋkere, di ra la Hul Dominuuzeŋ la.

ref: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
text: Hɔsaaya ni Juda nabɔnzi yeŋ hiŋ ba ni.

ref: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
text: Kenne ba faa hiŋ dɔŋa ni, Azaria, Ɛzra, Mɛsulam,

ref: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
text: Juda, Bɛnjamin, Sɛmaaya, Jɛrɛmia

ref: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
text: ani u ni u domee nɛra baŋhina, baabuu, Sɛmaaya, Azarɛl, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nɛtanɛl, Juda ani Hanani. Ba maanii faa kpogli kunlɔɔlaa la Kɔraawiizi balii Koori Deevid n baglɛɛ la. Karchi Ɛzraa faa tɔ ba see,

ref: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
text: di lii a koŋlii Bule Dominuuzeŋ la, ba faa chi ta chɔŋ guŋŋ di ga tinni Koori Deevid Bolzeŋ lɔŋa la baŋ ɔɔ ga tinni Koori Deevid sal, di ga hel Nii Dominuuzeŋ la n du wiifurii la.

ref: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
text: A yiryitta suge bɛl ge ta chɔŋ di ga keŋkere bɛl. N ni a nɛra yeŋ faa ra hiŋ ba ni, a koŋlii nyuu guŋŋ di ga bɛri Paanuu Ɔɔzibɔr Diijaŋ la, di ga hel a Koŋlii War la,

ref: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
text: di ga de gilli la Ɛfram Dominuuzeŋ, di kpa la Jɛsana Dominuuzeŋ, di lii de la Nyinni Dominuuzeŋ, di kaa lii de la Hananɛl Diijaŋ ani Kalfa Diijaŋ la, di chi de la Peeza Dominuuzeŋ la. Baŋ ga hel Guuri Dominuuzeŋ la, ba chi de.

ref: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
text: A yiryitta suge anɛɛ la n kpa jaaŋ di tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, jaa zuu so ba sognibɔra, Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. Denii n ge ni nabɔnzi la yeŋ,

ref: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
text: di kpa Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, baabuu, Ɛliakim, Maasɛya, Miniamin, Mikaaya, Ɛliɔnai, Zɛkaria ani Hanania, n kpogli bensunozi.

ref: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
text: Banniibuu ge kaa hiŋ di zuu, Maasɛya, Sɛmaaya, Ɛliaza, Uzi, Jɛhɔhanan, Malkija, Ɛlam ani Ɛza. Denii Jɛzrahia jaa tɔ a yiryitta see, ba ra yir yira.

ref: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
text: A hɔl hiŋ, ba lizi mbusuzii werge maa Kɔraawiizi be ni bampirsɔna, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa bɔsɔna werge maa wia. Gunnɛ haana ni bichalli ge gba bɔra faa sɔɔni, ba ra kɔɔ werge. Awia, a kɔɔi faa lii Jɛrusalɛm biini di la bɔɔnɛɛ werge maa.

ref: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
text: A saŋa hiŋ, ba ɔɔ faa lizi baalaa, ba ra binni ba kuna dauribɔra diini la baŋ kɛɛ kuna, diulugla ani kuna fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa di ra dau la ni. Baabuu faa ra lɛɛ kɛɛizi la di ra lii kooni la n dugli bolzenaa la maa, a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee hora gunla Gbɔg n baglɛɛ la. Juda hina bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la n na hum wia.

ref: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
text: Ba ɔɔ sɔ bahinaarɛ di lizi ba doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa gunla yiryitta ni dominuuguure n ɔɔ ɛɛ mɔɔ, ka ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma, gunla Koori Deevid ni u biibaal Koori Solomɔn n dauwɛ la.

ref: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
text: Di lii Koori Deevid ni Asaf de dui saŋa la, nɛra faa du denii di ra bagli yiryitta gunla ban niŋ ɔɔ ra yir chɔlaa yira, di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaaŋ.

ref: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
text: Zɛrubabɛl ni Nɛhɛmia de dui saŋa la, Izrɛl hina maanii ɔɔ faa kɛɛ kuna hɔpizi biimaa di ra tɛɛ a yiryitta ni dominuuguure. Ba ɔɔ faa kaa lizi a yeŋ tɛɛ Levi dee, ba ge bir lizi a yeŋ tɛɛ Aarɔn naanna.

ref: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
text: A hɔl la baŋ karmi Moosis Hɔŋ la a lii chaaŋ nɛnnɛ nɛr maa nuu lugɔ ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ dí ba ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa gil Ammɔn gɛɛ Moab hinuu maa waa jaa Kɔraawiizi nɛra ni,

ref: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa waa sɛɛwɛ kpa diwee ni nii tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, saŋa la baŋ faa lii Ijip hɛri di ra ba la. Ammɔn ni Moab hina hiŋ faa kpa Balaamnɛ ŋɔ ú see Izrɛl hina nua, ka Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la gil a nuuseei birgi kissaa.

ref: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
text: A nɛra n wa nuu a Gbɔg naa, ba faa waa kaa sɛɛ hɔɔhra ni banla n waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ so Izrɛl hɛri la jaa ba ni di ra jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
text: Mɔɔ ka guŋ ɛɛ, Ɛliasib la n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ labuu ba faa gil u ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna dauribɔra la ni. U ni Tobia faa summɔɔ.

ref: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
text: Ɛliasib faa kpa a kuna dauribɔr bɛl n kannɛ tɛɛ Tobia. U biinii ba faa ra dau mbusu mia, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna, mia bɔra fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa, siŋfalaa ani nuuri la n ɛɛ Levi dee, yiryitta, dominuuguure ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina hora la.

ref: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
text: Annii naa maa n faa ra ɛɛ la, di mìŋ́ Nɛhɛmia waa hoo Jɛrusalɛm biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, n bittɔɔ la Babilɔn ń ga na Koorizeŋ Aatazɛgzis. U kora dii binni tokko ni kpɔrgɔ ni anɛɛhiŋ biinii faa guŋ. Ka saŋa bɛl wa hel la n suŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ,

ref: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
text: di bir ba Jɛrusalɛm. Denii n wa nuu gunla Ɛliasib n ɛɛ wichɔgaa, dikuu uŋ kpa Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna dauribɔr tɛɛ Tobia wia.

ref: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
text: N baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa, n paa Tobia kuna la maa n du a diibee la, di ha bossee,

ref: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
text: ka ŋɔ bá lizi a kuna dauribɔra doŋa ha, a ɛɛ nanaananaa, ka n bir kpa a kuna la maa baŋ faa lizɛɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la bir du de. Aabuu, mbusu lizaa mia, daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ani a Dia kuna maa.

ref: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
text: N kaa nuu lugɔ ba faa waa kaa ra binni Levi dee la ni. Awia, a Levi dee ni yiryitta la n faa ra binni wiijaamaa wikpoglaa ni la maa faa bittɔɔ kaali di gaa par ba kooni.

ref: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
text: Denii n faa nyɛgi a nabɔnzi ni, di pɛɛzi baa, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii gil Kɔraawiizi Dia tai?” Denii n faa jaa chaali Levi dee ni yiryitta la maa di lii ba kooni, di ba Kɔraawiizi Dia, di wa gil bɛl maa kaa ra hum u huma.

ref: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
text: Denii Izrɛl hina maa kaa bir faari di ra lizi mia bɔra fizi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa, siŋfalii ani ɔlivi nuu di ra ba a dauribɔra diini.

ref: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
text: N lizi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Sɛlɛmia, Zadɔk la n faa ɛɛ karchi ani Pɛdaaya la n faa ɛɛ Levi dee hinuu, ba faa ra binni Kɔraawiizi Dia kuna dauribɔra ni. N kaa lizi Zakur biibaal Hanan, u naabaal faa ɛɛ Matania, u faa ra hiini baa. N faa yardi baabuu, di zum lugɔ ba daŋ ɔɔ wer bɔnni diwee ni kuna ra tɛɛ ba dɔŋahina huŋhunna nɛnnɛ.

ref: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, a liizi wia la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ ni biinihuŋŋu, dikuu i Dia naa ani u huma wia.

ref: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, n nawɔɔrɛ Juda baala n faa ra fɛrgi grepuzi a nii ra lii, Heezaa Hɔpizii la. Baŋhina ge kpa daazi nɔna, mia ani sinni, di vɔɔzaa sag kauzi ni di ra ba Jɛrusalɛm. Denii n nyɛgi ba ni siaahmu ni lugɔ bá gilɛɛ ra yoo kuna a Heezaa Hɔpizii.

ref: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
text: Taaya baala la n faa soge Jɛrusalɛm la ɔɔ faa chi nyinni ni ba kuna irizi maa dee di waa yooa Jɛrusalɛm, a Heezaa Hɔpizii di ra tɛɛ Juda hina.

ref: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
text: Denii n faa nyɛgi ba nabɔnzi ni, di ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ biinikpola wiarɛ ii ra ɛɛ, di ra chɔgi a Heezaa Hɔpizii gunnɛi?

ref: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
text: Keŋ lɛi ii naabaala faa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi tɛr ba digna, di gil ba puri bolzeŋ naa maa laa? Ka ii kaa ra zuu Kɔraawiizi ni filaŋkeŋ, ú baaŋ kaa fuuh Izrɛl hina ni werge, dikuu iinna chɔgi a Heezaa Hɔpizii wia.”

ref: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
text: Awia, n faa ŋɔ bá ɔɔ tɔɔgi Jɛrusalɛm dominuuzenaa, di a Heezaa Hɔpizii waa faari duana ni. Bá gilɛɛ kaa waa pillaa, di a Hɔpizii waa tunnɛ. Denii n faa gil n himmaa baala baŋhina ɔɔ chi a bol dominuuzenaa la lugɔ bá gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa chi kuna di waa zuu a bolzeŋ biini, di ra yooa a Hɔpizii hiŋ.

ref: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
text: Kakpaŋkpaŋa bɛnnɛ kɔkɔɔza la n ɔɔ ra yoo kuna irizi maa dee la ɔɔ wa chɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm koŋlii baŋgia hamuŋa ni, ka hɔpizi Heezaa Hɔpizii.

ref: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
text: Ka n hau ba ni, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ɔɔ wa chɔɔ a bol koŋlii baŋgiai? Di ii kaa ɛɛ guŋ, màá gil ia.” Awia, di haŋ lii a hɔl hiŋ, ba waa kaa ba de a Heezaa Hɔpizii hɔl maa.

ref: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
text: Denii n gil Levi dee la sɔ bahinaa di lizi di ba doŋa ha, di ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa, ka la gaa guu a bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa. Nɛra gilɛɛ kaa wàá chɔgi a Heezaa Hɔpizii wia. Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, a liizi n wia dikuu a keŋ gba wia, di suŋ n ni dikuu i nɔŋŋaa werge la wia.

ref: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, n kaa na lugɔ Juda baala kpila maa faa paagi haanaa lii Asdɔd, Ammɔn ani Moab hɛssi.

ref: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
text: Ba biizi yeŋ faa ra mɔɔ Asdɔd hina mɔɔri gɛɛ a nɛra baŋhina mɔɔri. Ba faa waa wette di ra mɔɔ Juda hina mɔɔri.

ref: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
text: Denii n faa hau ba ni ka see baa nuuzi, di lɔɔzi baa, di tɛrgi ba nyuhuna kpuzi. Ka gil ba hɛɛhzi ni Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ lugɔ ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka gil ba biibaala paa hɛrdumazi biihaana gɛɛ ba biihaana yuu hɛrdumazi biibaala.

ref: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ya kaa nuu lugɔ ii ge ra ɛɛ biinikpola wia naa dɔŋaa, di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la nua, ka gaa paagi hɛrdumazi haanaa?

ref: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
text: Ɛliasib la n faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma biibaal Jɔyada ge biibaal bɛl faa kpa Sanbalat la n ɛɛ Bɛf Hɔrɔn hinuu biihaannɛ. Awia, n duŋŋuu lii Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, a liizi gunla a nɛra n ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di chɔgi i kizeehina huma ani i ni i kizeehina ni Levi dee nuukpaŋ la.

ref: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
text: Denii n sɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni Levi dee la, di lizi ba doŋa ha, ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa di lii kuna la maa n ɛɛ hɛrdumazi hina hora, di gil ba doŋ la ni, di tɛɛ baa huma, bɛl maa ni u hor.

ref: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
text: N kaa bagli saŋazi la ban ninna kɛɛ daazi la baŋ kpawɛɛ ra fuuh mbusuzi lizaa kuna ni diulugla kɛɛi. Awia, Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, gil n wia parii.

ref: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Zɛgzis sogo u diikpeg, Susa biini u koorikara ni, di ra di kora.

ref: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
text: Un di a kora guŋŋ binni ahoro wa hel, u gil ba daali diuzenaa ú tɛɛ u nabɔntɔga ni u huŋhunna nabɔnzi. Pɛsia ni Mɛdia hɛssi laallɔɔra nabɔnzi, kooribiizi ani hɛssi la unna di kora a ni la gba nabɔntɔga maanii faa du a diuzenaa dii bɔr.

ref: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
text: Annii harbɔɔ, a koori kaa gil ba daali diuzenaa u tɛɛ nɛra la maa n du u bolzeŋkpeg Susa la, nɛdumazi ni nɛtɔga maa. U kooridia kambol la baŋ duu daananaa la biinii ba faa chaali, di di a diuzenaa naa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
text: U faa gillɔɔ ba bɔg de ani patiisananaa. Aŋhina ɛɛ burgu, aŋhina ge huuhzi. Gessihuŋŋunanaa ni anla n lugɔ zagbiiŋ niirɛ ba faa kpa vɔɔzaa, ka kpa saliŋhuŋŋa gbittizi ge sagzi a ligee la baŋ kpa binanaa aŋhina di kuari, a chi di hiŋzi dɔŋa ni la. Karjannanaa baŋ kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu di kuari maanii faa du de. Ba faa kuari a hɛrii ni binanaa, aŋhina huuhzi, aŋhina aah, aŋhina ge ɛɛ burgu, ani anla n na nyɛgzi ani binanaa irizi yoola n kpolle werge maa.

ref: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
text: Saliŋ libizi biinee ba faa du siŋ di ra tɛɛ nɛra. A libizi bɛl maa faa waa u dɔŋ liwɛɛ. A siŋ ge faa pur, di ra bagli a koorizeŋ bunya.

ref: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
text: A koorizeŋ haaŋ banna yir Vasti ge faa gillɔɔ ba daali diuzenaa ú tɛɛ haana la maa n faa du Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis dia la.

ref: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ hɔl la, Koori Zɛgzis bɔra sɔɔnuu werge maa, dikuu uŋ nyɔɔ siŋ la wia. Denii u ŋɔ Mɛhuman, Bizta, Habɔna, Bigta, Abagta, Zɛtar ani Kakas n ɛɛ nɛvaraa di ra humuu la be

ref: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
text: lugɔ ba ga kpogli u haaŋ Vasti, di gil u kpa u wiche kahuro hi di ba u see, ú kaa bagli nɛtɔga la ni a nɛra maa, bá na u wessi, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa wessoo werge.

ref: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
text: Nɛvaraa naa n ga ŋɔ Vasti be gunla Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis n ŋɔwɛɛ la, ka u vɛɛ, di ŋɔ wàá la. A koorizeŋ n wa nuu guŋ, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
text: Banniibuu ɔɔ du u be di ra hiinuu saŋa maa. Ba sɔnaa keŋ, Kasina, Sɛtar, Admata, Taasis, Mɛrɛs, Masɛna ani Mɛmukan. Nabɔntɔga baniidaanɛɛ naabuu faa ɛɛ Pɛsia ni Mɛdia hɛssi hina nabɔnzi la n faa ɛɛ koori zɛɛsogna di kaa ɛɛ a hɛri hina sitɔɔra nabɔnzi.

ref: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
text: Baŋ wa chaalɛɛ, a koorizeŋ pɛɛzi baa, “Di lii yaa widaulaa biini, ɛrɛɛ n dɛkkɛ lugɔ ya dau Wiche Vastei? Waa sɛɛwɛ u hiŋ n nua la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ nɛvaraa ŋɔ ba tɛu la.”

ref: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
text: Denii Mɛmukan izi chi a koori ni u dɔŋahina nabɔntɔga la see di ŋɔ, “Jara, i haaŋ Vasti ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. A waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ wiarɛ zuu hìŋ́ koori bɛŋ ni, ka a hɛssi nabɔntɔga ni nɛra la maa n du Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora hɛssi la maa biini ninɛɛ u ɛɛ a wia zuu.

ref: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
text: Wiche naa wiɛɛlaa naa daŋ zuu a hɛssi naa maa haana digna, guŋ gil bá ɔɔ ra gbɛlli ba janna, di ra ŋɔ lugɔ Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis ŋɔ bá yir u haaŋ Vasti ú ba, ka u vɛɛ.

ref: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
text: Zinaa hɔpizii naa, Pɛsia ni Mɛdi hina nabɔntɔga haana la n nuu Wiche Vasti wiɛɛlaa naa, daŋ jaa ra ɛɛ hìŋ́ koori nɛtɔga la guŋ himmaa. Ba danna gbɛlli ba janna, ba janna ge baana ra fuuh ba ni.

ref: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
text: Awia, Jara, di a parii, ŋɔ nua di gil ba sɛbuu du Pɛsia ni Mɛdi hina widaulaa n waa birgaa dɔɔwɛ ŋmɛnɛ maa biini lugɔ a waa dɛkkɛ koori siwii n niŋ kaa na Vasti ŋmɛnɛ maa. Di kaa kpa jaa, gil koori nyiŋŋi haaŋ la n bɔu di gil ú lɛɛ u bɔr.

ref: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
text: Di ba wa ŋɔ koori widaulifalii naa tɛɛ u hɛri naa n kannɛ werge maa naa hina, haana maa danna tɔgzi ba janna.”

ref: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
text: U hunzi nɛra u kora hɛssi maa biini dí ba sii a widaulii tɛɛ baa. U faa gillɔɔ ba sɛbaa hɛri maa sɛbaa biini. Iri maa ge himmaa mɔɔri biinii u faa gil ba kaa sɛbaa tɛɛ ba maa, di ŋɔ ra tɛɛ nɛra maa ba mɔɔri biini lugɔ baal maanii ninna di nabɔmuu u diahina ni.

ref: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ di Koori Zɛgzis baaŋ jaa sɔɔni tama, u liizi Vasti ni u wiɛɛlaa la ani widaulii la un dauwɛ dikuu u wia la.

ref: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
text: Denii u himmaa balaa la n na binni u ni la ŋɔ u be, “Jara, gil ba nyiŋŋi suŋgure la n haa waa baala zummɛ di wa tɛi.

ref: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
text: Lizi nabɔnzi i kora hɛssi la maa biine, bá nyiŋŋi suŋgure bá ba i kora bolzeŋkpeg Susa, í du baa i dia haana bɔr la. Gil ba kpa baa du Hɛgai la n ɛɛ i nɛvarii la n na binni haana la nonee biini. Gil ba ra ɛɛ gunla maa n niŋ gil ba wessi jaa werge maa.

ref: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
text: Ba biini, unla wia n waa parii werge, gil ú ɛɛ wiche di lɛɛ Vasti bɔr.” Koori n wa nuu gunla baŋ ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la, a paruu, u hiŋ guŋ.

ref: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
text: Baal bɛl faa du bolzeŋkpeg Susa diikpeg naabuu di ɛɛ Jus hinuu, ba ra yiruu Mɔdɛkai. U faa lii Bɛnjamin dee biinii, di ɛɛ Jayir biibaal. A Jayir ge mɛɛrɛ faa Simei, Simei ge mɛɛrɛ faa Kis.

ref: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
text: A Kis naabuu faa jaa nɛra ni Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n laurɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali u hɛri la. Ba ni Jus hina Koori Jɛhɔyachinnɛ ba faa lauri a saŋa hiŋ.

ref: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
text: Mɔdɛkai faa dɔɔ u mɛɛzeŋ biihaaŋ bɛllɛ, u sɔnnɛ Hadassa, u ra dɛɛzuu alugɔ u himmaa bie, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ɛɛ lalbiere a saŋa. U sɔŋ bɛllɛ faa Ɛsta. U faa ɛɛ toloorii werge maa. Mɔdɛkai faa kpaubuu birgi u himmaa bie saŋa la u maa ni u mɛɛ n siuwɛ la.

ref: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
text: Baŋ wa sii wia la koori n ŋɔwɛɛ ani u widaulii la tɛɛ nɛra la, ba jaa nyiŋŋi biihaana kpila maa di ba Susa diikpeg la, di wa tɛɛ Hɛgai la n na binni haana la n du kooridia haana bɔr la. Ɛsta ge faa jaa ba ninɛɛ.

ref: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
text: Ɛsta wia faa par Hɛgai werge, u ra nyiŋŋi u wia. Denii u ɛɛ manaŋ di ra tɛu kuna la un niŋ kpa di ra ɛɛ u hiŋ di du wer, ani diwee la n wesse werge. Hɛgai faa lizi biihaana baniidaanɛɛ di lii a kooridia, ba ɛɛ u balaa, u kpa baa du a bɔr diinanaa la biine.

ref: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
text: Ɛsta faa waa baglɛɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ Jus hinuurɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Mɔdɛkai faa karfuubuu guŋ wia.

ref: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
text: Hɔpizii maa, Mɔdɛkai ɔɔ ga a haana bɔr diŋŋee kɛrii ú zum gunla Ɛsta n duwɛɛ ani wia la n na ɛɛ u be.

ref: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
text: Mɔɔ ka a suŋguru bɛl maa la Koori Zɛgzis be di ga chɔɔ, see uŋ kpa kuna la baŋ baglɛɛ, di ra kuari u hiŋ baaguzi fidaanɛɛ. Mɛr nuufɔglii labuu ba ɔɔ fɔgli baaguzi anumbɛl. Baaguzi anumbɛl ge, ba kaa kpa tulaalezi ni kuna la n na kuari bɔrahɔŋ ge di ra kuari bahinaa.

ref: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
text: Kenne bɛl maa ɔɔ ɛɛ ka la a koori be. Kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi lii a haana bɔr, ba ɔɔ kpaubuu tɛu, ú kpa la a kooridia.

ref: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
text: Duanaa u ɔɔ la de di ga chɔɔ, di bir ba ba haana duuribɔr hiŋ keŋkere bɛl chɔɔzi ni. Di u wa ballɔ, nɛvarii bɛl ge n na binni koori hahjigzi nonee biinii ba ɔɔ duu. U sɔnnɛ Saasgaz. A biihaaŋ naa dee wàá ka bir la a koori be, di u wia waa a koori pattɛ, u bagli u sɔŋ ŋɔ bá yiruu lɛi.

ref: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
text: Ɛsta faa du wer Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis be di kaali haana la maa. U wia paruu, u nɔŋŋuu di kaali u dɔŋahina la n waa baala zummɛ la. Awia, u faa gil ba kpa Wiche kahuro hiu, di gil u lɛɛ Vasti bɔr.

ref: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
text: A koori faa gil ba daali diuzenaa n kannɛ werge dikuu Ɛsta wia. U yir u nabɔntɔga ni u huŋhunna nabɔnzi bá wa di. U faa gillɔɔ ba sii lugɔ a hɔpizii ɛɛ heezaa hɔpiziirɛ u kora hɛssi maa biine, di sunzi nɛra kuna di ra bagli u bunya. Mɔdɛkai n lɛɛ koori miibɔɔ wia

ref: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
text: Baŋ kaa wa gil suŋgure la chaali bunɛɛhiŋ, di Mɔdɛkai jaa birgi kooridia nabɔma.

ref: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
text: Saŋa la Mɔdɛkai n birgi kooridia nabɔma la, di koori huŋhunna nabɔnzi banɛɛ, banna yir Bigtana ni Tɛrɛs, n ɔɔ chi di ra du u dominua tau la baana fuuh, ba jaa ta jina bá kpu Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis.

ref: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
text: Wia naa n wa chol Mɔdɛkai digna, u baglaa tɛɛ Wiche Ɛsta, u ge baglaa tɛɛ a koori di kpa sɔŋ tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai.

ref: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
text: Baŋ wa pigzi a wia biini, a ɛɛ wibii. Ba faa sag a nabɔnzi banɛɛ hiŋ ŋmɛŋ, gunla baŋ ɔɔ ra kpu nɛra la. Ba faa sɛbi wia naa maanii du ba Koora Faala Hɔŋ biini, a koori see.

ref: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
text: Wia naa maa n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis tɛɛ Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal Haman nabɔmuu kaali u nabɔntɔga maa.

ref: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
text: Koori huŋhunna nabɔnzi la maa n du kooridia dominua la maa giŋŋi, di kpa girme tɛɛ Haman gunla koori n ŋɔwɛɛ la, ka Mɔdɛkai waa faa waa sɛɛwɛ giŋŋuu gɛɛ di tɔgzuu.

ref: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
text: Koori huŋhunna nabɔnzi la n du a koori dominua la pɛɛzi Mɔdɛkai, “Ɛrɛɛ i vɛɛ koori nuai?”

ref: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
text: Hɔpizii waa maa, ba ɔɔ ŋɔ Mɔdɛkai be lugɔ ú hiŋ koori nua hiŋ, ka u ɔɔ vɛɛ guŋ. Awia, ba baglaa tɛɛ Haman, ba na di u daŋ gil gɛɛ wàá gilɛi, dikuubɛɛwiai, Mɔdɛkai ŋɔ ba benii lugɔ u ɛɛ Jus hinuurɛ.

ref: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
text: Haman n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ Mɔdɛkai wàá giŋŋuu gɛɛ di tɔgzuu la, u baaŋ fuuh werge maa.

ref: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
text: Ka uŋ wa zummɛ nɛra la dee Mɔdɛkai nɛra n ɛɛwɛ, Mɔdɛkai bɛŋ kpui faa waa haŋ paruu ga tuŋ. Awia, u faa nyiŋŋi ŋmɛnɛɛ la un niŋ ga di kpu Mɔdɛkai nɛra Jus hina la n du Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora hɛssi maa biine la.

ref: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
text: Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora dii binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, lugli baagu Niisan biinii ba ta kuna banna yir pur, bá lizi hɔpizii ani baagu Haman see. Baagu fidaanɛɛhiŋ Adar labuu a pur tai chol u ni.

ref: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
text: Denii Haman ŋɔ Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis be, “Jara, nɛra baŋhina yaari yaa kora hɛssi maa biinee, ba naana wia kur iri maa hora ni, ba waa koori widaulaa ge ra hiŋ. Di i gil ba wia tɛɛ baa, a wàá du wer.

ref: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
text: Jara, di i sɛɛwɔ gil ba sɛbi widaulii di kpu ba maa, n daŋ kpa saliŋhuŋŋa kilozi kagboŋa kalfa ahoro ni tokkoanɛɛ í tɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
text: Awia, a koori lizi u nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, uŋ kpawɛɛ ra jag kuna ni la tɛɛ Jus hina dɔm Haman n ɛɛ Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal la.

ref: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
text: Koori ŋɔ Haman be, “Gil a kebee wia, ka ɛɛ a nɛra gunla maa hinna nyiŋŋi.”

ref: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
text: Lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔl la, ba yirgi banla n na sɛbi koori hɔna la, ba chaali. Ba gil ba sɛbi gunla Haman n baglɛɛ tɛɛ koora, hɛssi nabɔnzi ani u nɛra dizi maa nabɔntɔga. Ba faa sɛbi wia naabuu a hɛssi bɛl maa sɛbaa ni u nɛra irizi maa mɔɔri biini. Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis sɔnnɛ ba faa kpa sɛbaa, di kaa kpa u nonibisig la jag a ni di tɛɛa fɔŋŋa.

ref: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
text: Denii ba kpa a hɔna di hunzi ba huŋhunna la n ɔɔ ra chɔ werge di ra la tilekpega ni nɛra be la, ba tɛɛ hɛssi la hina maa di ra ŋɔ ba be lugɔ ba kpu Jus hina la maa, di dim baa kɔrai, biipɔllaa, suŋgure, nabɔnzi ani haana ni bichalli maa, hɔpizikpaŋ biini, di paagi ba kuna ge jaa. Baagu fidaanɛɛhiŋ Adar hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ guŋ.

ref: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
text: A huŋhunna lii di ra hahzi, dikuu koori nua la wia. Baŋhina ge kpa a widaulifalii la di yaari Susa diikpeg biini. A koori ni Haman so di ra nyɔɔ siŋ, ka Susa bol biini nɛra maa ɛɛ kinchaŋ, di ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa a wii wia.

ref: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
text: Mɔdɛkai n wa nuu gunla maa baŋ dauwɛ la, u lɔgɔ lii werge maa u lau u laala piili, ka kpa gbɔglɔŋ laala laali, di ɛɛ hɔɔhri waari u nyuu maa. Denii u jaa vol di ra gaagi a bolzeŋkpeg biini maa di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa ni biinichɔg.

ref: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
text: Uŋ wa hel koori dominua, waa sɛɛwɛ u zuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba waa ɔɔ sɛɛ nɛr la maa n laali gbɔglɔŋ laala zuu de.

ref: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
text: Hɛri la maa koori widaulifalii naa n haŋ wa hel, biinichɔg werge maa ɔɔ lau Jus hina la n du de labuu, ba ra vɔɔ nuuzi di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa. Bakpila maa ɔɔ chɔɔgi hɛrii ni ba gbɔglɔnzi, di ɛɛ hɔɔhri waari ba nyuuni maa.

ref: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
text: Biihambizi la n ɛɛ Ɛsta balaa ni nɛvaraa la n na du u tau la n wa ŋɔ Mɔdɛkai wia tɛu, biinichɔg faa lawuubuu werge maa. Denii u gil ba kpa laala aŋhina ga tɛu ú laali ka wir a gbɔglɔŋ la, ka u vɛɛa.

ref: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
text: Ɛsta yir koori nɛvaraa la bɛl n na binnuu, u sɔŋ di Hatak la, di humuu ú ga pɛɛzi Mɔdɛkai, ú bagli wii la n na tɔɔruu ani u zɛɛ.

ref: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
text: Denii Hatak kpa la Mɔdɛkai be, di u sogo a bolzeŋ bɔchaaŋ la n chɔɔ koori dominua nɛra ɔɔ ra so de la.

ref: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
text: Mɔdɛkai bagli wii la maa n huuzuu ani kebee la maga Haman n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ turgi di du koori daama kuna dauribɔr, ka bá kpu Jus hina maa la.

ref: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
text: U kaa kpa hɔŋ la n na bagli lugɔ ba dim Jus hina maa, la di gil u wia yaari Susa la bɛl tɛɛ Hataki ú ga tɛɛ Ɛsta, di chaani u wia siwee maa tɛu. U kaa ŋɔ a nɛvarii be lugɔ ú la Ɛsta be di ga ŋɔ u be, siaahmu maa lugɔ ú la koori be di ga suŋŋuu, ú na Jus hina la sinyɛna, di suŋ ba ni.

ref: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
text: Hatak bir la ga bagli wii la maa Mɔdɛkai n ŋɔwɛɛ la tɛɛ Ɛsta.

ref: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
text: “Koori zɛɛsogna ni nɛra la maa n du u kora hɛssi la zummɔ lugɔ widauliirɛ lugɔ nɛr la maa, baal gɛɛ haaŋ, n niŋ zuu koori be u dia biini diŋŋee la, di koori wɔɔ yittɛ lɛi, dɛg kpuirɛ. Ama, di koori lalli u saliŋ daŋkpala tɛruu waa, guŋ bɛnnɛ niŋ wer lɛɛu. Hɔpizaa tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ zinaa, di koori haa wan yittɛ.”

ref: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
text: Hitaki n wa ŋɔ wia la Ɛsta n ŋɔwɛɛ naa tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai,

ref: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
text: kenne Mɔdɛkai ŋɔ ba bir ga ŋɔ Ɛsta be, “Wiche, gilɛɛ waa fɛ lugɔ hin du kooridia la wia, i bɛnnɛ niŋ na i hiŋ lii a Jus hina maa biini.

ref: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
text: Di i siigɔɔ wia naa biini, Jus hina daŋ na lɛɛi di lii yembɛl, ka ba daŋ chɔgi hiŋwaa ni i mɛɛ diahina maa. Di kennaa wiarɛ i wa ɛɛ koori haaŋ, i zummɔaa?”

ref: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
text: Denii Ɛsta ŋɔ ba bir ga ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai.

ref: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
text: “La ga chaali Jus hina la maa n du bolzeŋkpeg Susa la ii vɔɔ nua tɛŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa di gɛɛ di wàá nyɔɔ nii hɔpizaa ni hamuŋzi ahoro maa. N ni n balaa ge daŋ ɛɛ guŋ. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ la koori be, haali guŋ n niŋ chɔgi a widaulii la. Di n daŋ siu gba, ń siu.”

ref: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
text: Denii Mɔdɛkai izi kaali di ga ɛɛ gunla maa Ɛsta n ŋɔ ú ɛɛ la.

ref: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
text: Ba nuuvɔɔi hɔpizaa ahoro la n wa tunnɛ, Ɛsta kpa u Wiche laala bɔg, di zuu kooridia biini diŋŋee la ga chi u sognibɔr dominua. A saŋa, di koori sogo u koorikara ni, u siwee chaŋ u dominua.

ref: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
text: Uŋ wa na Wiche Ɛsta n chigɛ a loŋ biini, u wia paruu, u kpa u saliŋ daŋkpala la n du u nonii la tɛruu. Ɛsta tuzi heluu di ga gbɔgzi a daŋkpala nua.

ref: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
text: Denii a koori pɛɛzi, “N haaŋ Ɛsta, a summɔaa? Bɛɛ i ra nyiŋŋei? Haali di hɛssi la maa minna di kora a ni la kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi, a daŋ ɛɛ i hora.”

ref: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
text: Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di i sɛɛwɔ, gil i ni Haman ba n dia di wa di diuzenaa miŋ daalɛɛ ń tɛi zinaa.”

ref: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
text: A koorizeŋ ŋɔ, “Ií yir Haman ú ba ɛŋ manaŋ, yá ɛɛ Ɛsta kipar.” Awia, koori ni Haman kpa la diuzenaa la Ɛsta n gillɛ ba daali la bɔr, bá ga di.

ref: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
text: Baŋ waa nyɔɔ siŋ la, koori kaa pɛɛzi Ɛsta, “Too, i winyiŋŋiire ɛrɛɛ? I daŋ nau. Haali di n kora hɛssi kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi, i daŋ naa.”

ref: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
text: Di n wia parii, Jara, i ra nyiŋŋi i tɛŋ n winyiŋŋii, guŋwaa, gil í ni Haman ba kɛrɛ di wa di diuzenaa min niŋ daali tɛɛ ia. Di ii wa ballɔ, n daŋ jaa bagli wii la minna nyiŋŋi.” Haman baaŋ n na fuuh Mɔdɛkai ni wia

ref: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
text: Haman n wa lii de a hɔl hiŋ, u bɔra sɔɔnuu werge maa, u ra munzi pɛɛpɛɛ. Ka uŋ wa na Mɔdɛkai kooridia dominua, di na lugɔ waa sɛɛwɛ izi gɛɛ di ɛɛ lugɔ ɔnsii lawuu u see, u baaŋ fuuh Mɔdɛkai ni werge maa.

ref: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
text: Ka Haman lau u hiŋ di kaali dia. Uŋ ga hel dia, u yir u dammuzi ni u haaŋ Zɛrɛs,

ref: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
text: di ta bara dikuu u daama werge ni u biibaala kpila ani gunla maa koori n kpau girme, haali di tɛu nabɔmuu u dɔŋahina nabɔntɔga ni huŋhunna nabɔnzi ni wia.

ref: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
text: Haman kaa ŋɔ, “A maa lɛi gba. N bɛnnɛ Wiche Ɛsta yir n jaa koori ni di ga di diuzenaa la un daalɛɛ la. U kaa yir n ni koorii lugɔ kɛrɛ yá kaa wa di.

ref: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
text: Ka miŋ ɔɔ ra na Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai kooridia dominua la wia, annii maa wanna tɛɛ bɔsɔna.”

ref: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
text: A hɔl hiŋ hamuŋa, a koori waa wette chɔɔ dɔɔ, awia u gil ba kpa u kora wia hɔŋ n na bagli u kora wiɛɛlaa di wa karmi tɛu.

ref: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
text: Koori pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ sɔnnɛ Mɔdɛkai faa na dikuu keŋ wiai? Bɛɛ kinturgaare ba tɛuwɛi?” U balaa ŋɔ, “Ba waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ tɛu.”

ref: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
text: A koori pɛɛzi, “Anɛɛ n du diŋŋee biinei?” A saŋa di Haman haŋ zuu kooridia diŋŋee la n dugli bossee la, ú wa ŋɔ wia koori be lugɔ ú tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ ba kpu Mɔdɛkai ŋmɛŋsagri daa la ni uŋ gillɛ ba baŋ la.

ref: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
text: U balaa ŋɔ, “Hamannɛ chigɛ diŋŋee biini.” A koori ŋɔ, “Ií yiruu ú ba.”

ref: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
text: Haman n wa zuuwɛ, koori pɛɛzuu, “Bɛɛ n dɛkkɛ ba ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr la wia n na par koori, ú tɛu sɔnɛi?” Haman fɛ u biini, “Nɛr du de koori n na nyiŋŋi ú tɛɛ sɔŋ di miŋ lɛiyaa?”

ref: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
text: Awia, u ŋɔ koori be, “Jara, di i ra nyiŋŋi í tɛɛ nɛr sɔŋ,

ref: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
text: gil ba kpa i himmaa laala la hinna laali la ba ani zagu bɛl hiŋ tinnɛɛ ka ka. Ba kpa pɛrɛtujiga pɛli u hile di ra bagli lugɔ i kunnɛ.

ref: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
text: Í jaa gil i nabɔnzenaa himmaa la bɛl kpa a koorilaala naa di bɔg baal la hinna nyiŋŋi í tɛɛ sɔŋ la, di gil u tinni a zagu. Denii í gil nabɔnzeŋ la tɔ u see, di tɛrguu di ra gaagi a bolzeŋ biini maa ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni, ‘Kenne koori ŋɔ ba ɛɛ ra tɛɛ baal la am paruu, ú tɛu sɔŋ.’ ”

ref: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
text: Koori ŋɔ Haman be, “Izi manaŋ, di gil ba tɛi a laala ni a zagu, í ɛɛ gunla hiŋ baglɛɛ naa, di tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai la n ɛɛ Jus hinuu la. Waabuu ɔɔ ra so n dia dominua la. A du tau, di ɛɛ wia la maa hiŋ baglɛɛ la. Gilɛɛ waa gil bɛl maa ɛɛi.”

ref: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
text: Awia, Haman nyiŋŋi a koorilaala ni u zagu, di bɔg Mɔdɛkai, di gil u tinni a zagu, u kpogluu ra gaagi a bolzeŋ biini maa di ra ŋɔ kpegzi ni, “Kenne ba ɛɛ ra tɛɛ baal la am par koori ú tɛu sɔŋ.”

ref: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
text: A guŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, Mɔdɛkai bir la kooridia dominua ga so, ka Haman hahzi di kaali u dia ni biinichɔg ni hiihzi werge maa.

ref: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
text: Uŋ wa hel dia, u bagli wii la maa n ɛɛwɛ tɛɛ u haaŋ Zɛrɛs ni u dammuzi. Ba karfuu, di ŋɔ, “Mɔdɛkai jaa ra kpegliibuu la. U ge n ɛɛ Jus hinuu naa, i nuu wàá weraa ɛɛ, i wia daŋ chɔgi.”

ref: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
text: Baŋ haa ra ŋɔ wia la, di koori nɛvaraa ballɔ wa yir Haman, u ni baa hahzi kaali a diuzenaa Wiche Ɛsta n gillɛ ba daali la dii bɔr.

ref: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
text: Haman ni a koori jaa la bá ni Wiche Ɛsta ga di.

ref: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
text: Baŋ kaa waa nyɔɔ siŋ a hɔpizaa anɛɛhiŋ naa ge, a koori kaa pɛɛzi Wiche Ɛsta, “N haaŋ Ɛsta, i winyiŋŋiire bɛɛ? Haali di n hɛssi naa kezaa i ra nyiŋŋi gba, n daŋ tɛi.”

ref: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
text: Wiche Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di n wia ra parii, i bɔra sɔɔni, amɔ í lɛɛ n ni n nɛra ha. N winyiŋŋiire guŋ.

ref: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
text: Ba ɛɛ siryaa bá kpu n ni n nɛra maa, yaa wia tuŋ kɔrai. Di ba faa yoo yaabuu yá birgi yoma, a faa wàá tiriŋ. N daŋ vii tɔ n nua, dikuubɛɛwiai, a tɔɔrɔɔ dii faa waa kunla min niŋ kuu u wia di ra tɔɔri hiŋ koori ɛɛwɛ.”

ref: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
text: Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis pɛɛzi u haaŋ Ɛsta, “A hinnɛ anɛɛ? Babɛliirɛ lɔ bampirii ú ɛɛ kennei?”

ref: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
text: Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Yaa chɔgri ni yaa dɔnnɛ bachɔgii Haman naa!” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, ɔnsii werge lau Haman, koori ni u haaŋ see.

ref: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
text: Denii koori la izi ni baaŋfuuih werge di gil u siŋ ka zuu kooridia kambol la biini. Ka Haman n teŋ zummɛ lugɔ koori tuŋ u wiarɛ la, u ka har a dia biini di ra fɔrgi Wiche Ɛsta, ú lɛɛ u miibɔɔ.

ref: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
text: Saŋa la koori n haŋ lii u dia kambol la biini di bir wàá zuu, di Haman ra nyiŋŋi ú giŋŋi di chɔɔ karjaŋ la Ɛsta n dɛlli u ni la di fɔrguu. Koori la n wa na guŋ, u koobi di ŋɔ, “Ee, akubani! U daŋ pum n haaŋ haali n nuu n kpauwɛ soo?” Koori nua n haŋ waa chol hɛri, di ba teŋ kpa kuŋ di vɔɔ Haman siwee.

ref: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
text: Awia, ba ga kpu Haman a ŋmɛŋsagri daa la uŋ baŋŋɛ ú kpu Mɔdɛkai la ni. Denii koori baaŋ jaa sɔɔni tama.

ref: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
text: A hɔl himmaanii Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kpa Jus hina dɔm Haman la kundɔɔlaa maa tɛɛ u haaŋ Ɛsta. Ɛsta ge bagli tɛɛ koori lugɔ Mɔdɛkai ɛɛ u lullii. Di haŋ lii a hɔl hiŋ, Mɔdɛkai ɔɔ jaa weruu zuu di ga chi koori see.

ref: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
text: Koori lizi u nonibisig la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, u kpa ra jag hɔna ni, u birgi widaulii la tɛɛ Mɔdɛkai. Haman benii koori faa lɛɛu. Ɛsta faa gil Mɔdɛkai dɔɔ fɔŋŋa Haman kundɔɔlaa maa ni.

ref: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
text: Ɛsta kaa giŋŋi koori see di ra wii, di ra fɔrguu, ú chɔgi Agag hinuu Haman jinachɔgii la uŋ tawɛɛ ú chɔgi Jus hina maa la.

ref: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
text: Denii koori kaa kpa u saliŋ daŋkpala la di tɛr Ɛsta, u izi chi u see,

ref: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
text: di ŋɔ, “Jara, di a parii di deŋli i be, n wia kaa sɔɔni i bɔra, gil bá kaa sɛbi widaulifalii hɔŋ, di bɔnni i hɛssi la maa di ra chɔgi unla Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal Haman n faa felee sɛbi ŋɔ bá chɔgi Jus hina la maa n du i hɛssi maa la.

ref: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
text: Ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di lau n hiŋ, di wia wa huuzi n nɛrai? Màá wer so di ra binni ka ba kpu n diahina.”

ref: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
text: Koori Zɛgzis jaa ŋɔ u haaŋ Ɛsta ni Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai be, “N gillɔɔ ba sag Haman ŋmɛŋsagri daa la uŋ baŋŋɛ dikuu u jinachɔgii la un tawɛɛ, ú kpa ɛɛ Jus hina la wia. N kpa u kundɔɔlaa maanii tɛɛ Ɛsta.

ref: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
text: Ka widaulii la baŋ kpa mìŋ́ koori sɔŋ sɛbi, di kpa n nonibisig jag a ni la waa kaa dɔɔ biraa. Ama, ii daŋ wer sɛbi widaulifalii di hiini a Jus hina gunla maa n wesse ii be. Ií kpa n sɔŋ di sɛbuu, di kpa n nonibisig la di jag u ni, ú dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.”

ref: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
text: Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis sɔnnɛ Mɔdɛkai faa kpa di sɛbi a hɔna, di kaa kpa u fɔŋŋa nonibisig la jagaa. Koori balaa n tinni zagra baŋ dɛɛzɛɛ a ɛɛ koori hora di ra chɔ werge labuu ba kpa bɔnnaa.

ref: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
text: Mɔdɛkai lii a koori see ni u bɔmbɔga n ɛɛ burgu di koozi a huŋŋa, di kaa tɔ wɛjɛ bɛl baŋ kpa pɛɛnnanii di nyɛr, u ɛɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ nii, di hi saliŋkahuro, a maa lugɔ koorilaala. A hɔl hiŋ, bolzeŋkpeg Susa hina di bahinaa werge maa ni bɔsɔna.

ref: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
text: Jus hina la waa be, bɔsɔna, bɔpuraa ani girme saŋaa di faa tɛɛ baa.

ref: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
text: Bolzeŋ maa biini, hɛssi maa biine ani bɔr la maa baŋ karmi a koori widaulii naa, Jus hina bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu, ba chaali di ra di diuzenaa di ra di bahinaa werge maa. Nɛkpila n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ faa birgi Jus hina, dikuu baŋ jaa ra ɔm baa werge la wia.

ref: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
text: Baagu Adar la hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ, koori widaulii naa fɔŋŋa faari. A hɔllɛ Jus hina dɔma faa ra fɛ lugɔ ba daŋ kpegli baa, di kpu baa. Ka wia la bir, Jus hina la kpegli nɛra la n hah baa la.

ref: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
text: Jus hina la n du ba bolzenaa la maa n du Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis kora hɛssi la maa chaali, bá yoo nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ba dimaa la. Nɛra maa faa waa wette ba ni baa yoo, dikuubɛɛwiai, iri maa faa ra ɔm baabuu.

ref: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
text: A hɛssi maa nabɔntɔga ni koora, hɛssi nabɔnzi ani koori huŋhunna maa faa chi Jus hina la har, dikuu banna ɔm Mɔdɛkai werge wia.

ref: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
text: Mɔdɛkai faa ɛɛ nɛtɔgrɛ kooridia. U sɔŋ faa yaari a koori hɛssi maa, u fɔŋŋa ra jaa saŋa maa.

ref: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
text: Jus hina la faa kpa tokobizii yoo ba dɔma di kpu baa, di chɔgi baa werge maa. Ba faa ɛɛ nɛra la n hah baabuu ba kipar.

ref: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
text: A hɔl hiŋ maanii ba kali koori nɛra la maga Jus hina n kpuwɛɛ Susa diikpeg biini.

ref: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
text: Koori ŋɔ u haaŋ Ɛsta be, “Jus hina la kpu nɛra kalfaanuere, di kpa Haman biizi fi jaa, Susa diikpeg naa biini. An du kennaa, nɛra baŋmɛnɛɛ ba kpu hɛssi la n kawɛɛ la biinei? Too, filaŋkeŋ bɛɛ i kaa ra nyiŋŋei? N daŋ ɛɛu tɛi.”

ref: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
text: Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Jara, di i sɛɛwɔ, tɛɛ Jus hina la n du Susa la ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ ba kɛrɛ kaa kpa zinaa widaulii naa di hum huma, di kpa Haman biibaala fi la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la sag ŋmɛŋsagri daazi ni.”

ref: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
text: Denii koori ŋɔ ba ɛɛ guŋ. Ba dau a widaulii Susa biini, di kpa Haman biibaala fi la baŋ kpuwɛɛ la di sag ŋmɛŋsagri daazi ni, nɛ́r maa na.

ref: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
text: Jus hina chaali Susa biini baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la, di kaa kpu baala kalfaahoro, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ kpa ba kummaa.

ref: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
text: Baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaahoro hɔllɛ ba ɛɛ guŋ. Hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la, ba heezi di di diuzenaa, ba bɔra faa sɔɔni baa werge, ba gil u birgi ba hɔpizizeŋ bɛl. Purim Hɔpizizeŋ dii wia

ref: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
text: Ka Jus hina la n faa du Susa lawaa chaalɔɔrɛ hɔpizaa fidaahoro ni fidaanaazu hɔla, ka jaa heezi hɔpizaa fidaanue hɔl la di di diuzenaa, ba bɔra sɔɔni baa werge maa.

ref: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
text: Awiarɛ Jus hina la n du boljigzi la gil baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu hɔl la ɛɛ hɔpizizeŋ ba be, ba ɔɔ ra di diuzenaa ba bɔra sɔɔni baa, ba ra sunzi dɔŋa kuna.

ref: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
text: Mɔdɛkai faa sɛbi wia naabuu dau, di sɛbi hɔna tɛɛ Jus hina la maa n du Koori Zɛgzis hɛssi maa biine, banla n duglɛɛ ni banla n du bɔɔnɛɛ,

ref: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
text: di ra kali baa lugɔ ba gil baagu Adar hɔpizaa fidaanaazu ni fidaanue hɔla la ɛɛ hɔpizizenaa, bá ra dia bina maa,

ref: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
text: di ra liizi saŋa la Jus hina n na lɛɛi lii ba dɔma be ani baagu la biini ba biinichɔg n birgi bɔsɔna, ba wiraa hɔpizii la birgi hiŋ dii hɔpizii. U sɛbɔɔrɛ tɛɛ baa bá gil hɔpizaa naa ɛɛ diuzenaa dii ni bɔsɔna hɔla, di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa diwee di ra sunzi nyaara.

ref: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
text: Awia, Jus hina la sɛɛ gunla Mɔdɛkai n sɛbɛɛ la lugɔ a hɔpizizenaa dii du de di hanna la.

ref: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, Agag hinuu Hamɛdata biibaal Haman n ɛɛ Jus hina maa dɔm la, faa ta jinaa ú chɔgi baa, di faa ta kuna banna yir pur, ú zum hɔpizii la un niŋ chɔgi baa, ba wia tuŋ.

ref: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
text: Ka u jina naa n wa zuu koori digna, u faa gillɔɔ ba sɛbi hɔna di bagli lugɔ ba gil Haman nfɛrchɔgaa la un dɔɔwɛ Jus hina ni la bir laŋŋi u ni, di bir ŋɔ ba sag u ni u biibaala ŋmɛŋsagridaazi ni.

ref: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
text: Awia, ba faa ra yir a hɔpizaa naa Purim, dikuu wii la maa baŋ sɛbɛɛ a hɔnnaa biini ni wii la maa ban nawɛɛ ani wii la maa n ɛɛ baa la wia.

ref: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
text: Denii Abiheel biihaaŋ Wiche Ɛsta ni Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai la kpa fɔŋŋa la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ di sɛbi hɔŋ di chi hɔnnɛɛhiŋ naa n na ŋɔ Purim wia naa har.

ref: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
text: di ŋɔ bá dau Purim hɔpizaa naa saŋazi gunla Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai ni Wiche Ɛsta n faa dauwɛ tɛɛ baa ani gunla baŋ faa dau hɔpizaa tɛɛ bahinaa ni ba dee lugɔ ban niŋ ɔɔ vɔɔ nua di ra wii, dikuu biinichɔg la n faa huuzi baa la wia.

ref: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
text: Ɛsta widaulii gillɔɔ gunla baŋ faa ŋɔ Purim ni u ŋmɛnizi wia chi nɛnnɛ. Ba faa sɛbuubuu du hɔna biine.

ref: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
text: Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis faa tɛɛ u nɛra la n faa du u kora diiribɔr maanii kima, haali di ga chug muuzeŋ gba.

ref: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
text: Ba kaa sɛbi u wiɛɛlaa la maa uŋ kpa u fɔŋŋa ni u zenni ɛɛ, ni gunla maa un lalli Mɔdɛkai chiŋ di tɛu nabɔmuu. A maanii ba faa sɛbi du Mɛdia ni Pɛsia Koora Faala Hɔna biine.

ref: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
text: Jus hinuu Mɔdɛkai labuu faa ɛɛ nabɔnzeŋ di ra hiŋ Koorizeŋ Zɛgzis ni. U faa ɛɛ nɛzenne Jus hina biini. U dɔŋahina faa ra tɔgzuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa hummɔɔ ba wia kuari, u ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa ba maa bɔra sɔɔni werge maa.

ref: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
text: Baal bɛllɛ faa du de, u sɔnnɛ Joob. U faa du hɛri bɛl banna yir Uz. U faa ra jaami Kɔraawiizii, u wia dɔɔ wibii u be. Joob faa ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ, di ra du tau ni wichɔgaa ɛɛi.

ref: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
text: Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi Sitaani, “Lee i liiyɛi?” Sitaani ŋɔ, “Hɛrii n du di gaagi ra bar.”

ref: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
text: U biibaala ɔɔ faa ra daali diuzenaare ba diini ka ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, ba ɔɔ yir ba niuhambizi bahoro la, ba ba, ba maa di ka nyɔɔ.

ref: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
text: Di ba diuzenaa dii haŋ wa tuŋ, Joob ɔɔ faa hum ba bɔttɛ, di sɔ lizi ba doŋa ha, bá ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa Kɔraawiizi be. Joob lugli ɛɛi na wia

ref: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,

ref: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
text: Sitaani pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi, “I ŋɔ pɛɛrɛ u ra jaamii?

ref: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
text: I ra guu u ni u diahina ni u kundɔɔlaa maanii nɛnnɛ, di kissuu u wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Guŋ gil u sela wazi, di yaari a hɛri maa biini.

text: Ka di i gillɔ u kuna naa maa tuŋ, u daŋ seei nua, i sibɔɔ.”

ref: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything

ref: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,

text: Uŋ faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di a balii bɛl ballɔ di wa ŋɔ, “Dooŋ pozi peeza la ni i balaa la ninɛɛ, di fuuh ba maa, ka n bɛnnɛ liiwɛ, di chɔ ba ń wa kalii!”

ref: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
text: U ge n faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia, di a balii bɛl kaa ba, di wa ŋɔ, “Babilɔn hina ŋmɛɛna sugezi ahoro ballɔɔ di wa lɔ yaa, di kpu i balaa maa, ka tig i nyugmazi la maa kaali. N bɛnnɛ liiwɛ di chɔ ba ń wa kalii.”

ref: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
