ref: But if you punish the guilty, things will go well for you, and you will prosper.
text: Ka banla n ɔɔ tɛr bilchɔg hina digna, daŋ na kissaa.

ref: Don't fail to rescue those who are doomed to die.
text: Lɛɛ banla baŋ laurɛɛ bá ga kpuuzi pɛɛpɛɛ la, di gilɛɛ wa gil bá kpuuzi baa.

ref: Don't say, “I didn't know it!” God can read your mind. He watches each of us and knows our thoughts. And God will pay us back for what we do. –
text: Di ii ŋɔ, “Yaa waa a wia zummɛ.” Kɔraawiizii zum newea maa bampiree, di ra naa. Waabuu ra binni ii de dui ni, di zum lugɔ ii zummɔɔ! U daŋ kpa nɛra maa wiɛɛlaa di di baa seriya. Tokko ni anumbɛlhiŋ

ref: Giving an honest answer is a sign of true friendship.
text: Hiŋ bittɛ sɛɛ wibii wiŋɔzi, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ i badɔŋ n faamii.

ref: Honey is good for you, my children, and it tastes sweet.
text: N bie, a di huuhnuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wessoo, anla n lii a pɛɛna ni di ra toŋzi la summɔɔ tɛi.

ref: Wisdom is like honey for your life— if you find it, your future is bright. –
text: Guŋ himmaanii nunzuma du sum tɛi. Di i nau, i kɛrɛ bɛl de dui daŋ du wer, i tamii ge wàá tuŋ maa. Tokko ni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ

ref: Get your fields ready and plant your crops before starting a home.
text: Par i kooni tuŋ mɔɔ, ka haa ma i dia.

ref: Don't be a cruel person who attacks good people and hurts their families.
text: Gilɛɛ waa du alugɔ biinikpola hina la n ɔɔ chɔɔ guu, bá ŋmɛɛ banla wia n deŋlee diini kuna.

ref: Even if good people fall seven times, they will get back up. But when trouble strikes the wicked, that's the end of them. –
text: Gunla maa maga banla wia n deŋlee n niŋ chol, ka ba daŋ izi, ka hɛhchɔg daŋ chɔgi biinikpola hina waa. Tokko ni ŋmantannaazihiŋ

ref: Don't accuse anyone who isn't guilty. Don't ever tell a lie
text: Gilɛɛ waa di daansɛɛkara di ra chug nɛr la, n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Don't be happy to see your enemies trip and fall down.
text: Gilɛɛ gil a ɛɛi bɔsɔna di i dɔm wa chollo, di gilɛɛ gil i bɔra sɔɔni di u lɔ naa jiŋli,

ref: The Lord will find out and be unhappy. Then he will stop being angry with them. –
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi biini daŋ chɔgi dikuu i wia, guŋ gil u baaŋ wàá ka fuuh u ni. Tokko ni kabɛlhiŋ

ref: or say to someone, “I'll get even with you!”
text: Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ, “N daŋ ɛɛu gunla uŋ faa ɛɛŋ la! N daŋ turguu a kim!”

ref: I once walked by the field and the vineyard of a lazy fool.
text: N ɔɔ ga yaara hina ni nfɛrnyaara kooni nuuzii,

ref: Thorns and weeds were everywhere, and the stone wall had fallen down.
text: kooree ni sɔɔhri sug a maa biine, a koŋlaa maa chogli.

ref: When I saw this, it taught me a lesson:
text: Denii n binnaa, di fɛ nfɛrɛ, di helli wii naa lii de,

ref: Sleep a little. Doze a little. Fold your hands and twiddle your thumbs.
text: daari di chɔɔ dɔɔ tama, di kɔrgi i bɔra heezi tama,

ref: Suddenly poverty hits you and everything is gone!
text: ka hinna chɔɔ dɔɔ la, nyaari daŋ chol i ni alugɔ ŋmɛɛŋchɔgii.

ref: Here are some more of Solomon's proverbs. They were copied by the officials of King Hezekiah of Judah.
text: Koori Solomɔn sɛɛliizi aŋhina, Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia karchizenaa n binnɛɛ ka sɛbuu keŋ.

ref: God is praised for being mysterious; rulers are praised for explaining mysteries.
text: Yaa ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizii dikuu u wisuahlaa wia, di ra tɔgzi koora dikuu a zɛɛzi baglaa wia.

ref: Who can fully understand the thoughts of a ruler? They reach beyond the sky and go deep in the earth.
text: Gunla nɛr maa n wàá wer zum chiŋ maga ni hɛri luŋzi maga la, gunnɛ nɛr maa wàá wer zum koori biini wia.

ref: Silver must be purified before it can be used to make something of value.
text: Lizi saliŋhuŋŋa doŋa ha, ka nɛr la n zum nonii huma kpau kuari kunnanii,

ref: Evil people must be removed before anyone can rule with justice.
text: gunnɛ di ba duŋŋi biinikpola hina lii koori be, u kora daŋ chi, dikuu wibii dii wia.

ref: Don't try to seem important in the court of a ruler.
text: Gilɛɛ waa kpa i hiŋ zenni koori see gɛɛ di wàá tɔgzi i hiŋ,

ref: It's better for the ruler to give you a high position than for you to be embarrassed in front of royal officials. Be sure you are right
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, di u wa ŋɔ i be lugɔ i tinni wa so nabɔmbɔr, aabuu bɔ, uŋ kpa i bɔr hiŋ tɛɛ nabɔma.

ref: When you and someone else can't get along, don't gossip about it.
text: Awia, di i ni i dɔŋhiŋ di mmɔri, gil i nuu bɛŋ ŋɔa. Gilɛɛ waa kali nɛr maa,

ref: The right word at the right time is like precious gold set in silver.
text: Wiŋɔzi ŋɔi nɛnnɛ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ kpa saliŋ margi saliŋhuŋŋu ni.

ref: Listening to good advice is worth much more than jewelry made of gold.
text: Nunzunni n hau nɛr la digna n na nuu wia, wessoo kaali baŋaa kuŋ baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari tɛɛ nɛr.

ref: A messenger you can trust is just as refreshing as cool water in summer.
text: Balii la wia n dɔɔ wibii ra sɔɔni bɔraa alugɔ wem maga pechule. U wia ɔɔ sɔɔni u dɔɔri bɔraa.

ref: Patience and gentle talk can convince a ruler and overcome any problem.
text: Kanyitti ɔɔ weruu tɛɛ koori laakal, wiŋɔzi bɔɔiih ge ra bir nɛr la wia n kpolle nfɛrɛ.

ref: Eating too much honey can make you sick.
text: Di i na huuhnuu, diu mɛgzi, di i diu werge, i daŋ hɛɛhzi.

ref: Don't visit friends too often, or they will get tired of it and start hating you.
text: Di i ra la i dɔŋhiŋ dia digiidigii, i wia daŋ wa bazuu.

ref: Telling lies about friends is like attacking them with clubs and swords and sharp arrows.
text: Kara kannaa chug nɛra ra du baabuu pira, alugɔ hiŋ kpa gulii lɔɔzi baa gɛɛ hiŋ kpa tokobi du baa pira gɛɛ hiŋ kpa hobidiilaa taazi baa.

ref: If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink.
text: Di lɔzi waa kpu i dɔm, nyiŋŋi diwee tɛu ú di. Di niinyɔgzi lawuu, ɛɛ nii tɛu ú nyɔɔ.

ref: This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads. And the Lord will reward you.
text: Di i wetto ɛɛ guŋ tɛu, hiihzi daŋ lawuu. Kɔraawiizi daŋ turgii a kim.

ref: As surely as rain blows in from the north, anger is caused by cruel words.
text: Gunla wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag peu n ɔɔ ba dooŋ ni la, gunnɛ zɔɔza ra fuuh baaŋ.

ref: It's better to stay outside on the roof of your house than to live inside with a nagging wife.
text: Sakɛrii sogaare bɔ, i ni hahkalu hiŋ n kpau dia.

ref: Good news from far away refreshes like cold water when you are thirsty.
text: Amaniyesuma n lii hɛhjaŋa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ niisɔŋ tɛɛ niinyɔgzi hiŋ.

ref: When a good person gives in to the wicked, it's like dumping garbage in a stream of clear water.
text: Di nɛnanii sɛɛwɔ tɛɛ biinikpola hiŋ, guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ kpa siri du kɔlɔŋ gɛɛ baŋ pur bule.

ref: Don't eat too much honey or always want praise.
text: Gunla huuhnuu dii werge n waa wer la, gunnɛ sɔŋ nyiŋŋaa werge waa wer.

ref: Losing self-control leaves you as helpless as a city without a wall.
text: Nɛr la n wàá wer lau u hiŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bolzeŋ la baŋ lɔwɛɛ di purgi u koŋlaa.

ref: Expecting snow in summer and rain in the dry season makes more sense than honoring a fool.
text: Gunla dooŋ n waa dɛg lumaŋa gɛɛ kuna kumaa saŋa la, gunnɛ gɛnii waa dɛg tɔgzaa.

ref: A curse you don't deserve will take wings and fly away like a sparrow or a swallow.
text: Nuuseei wàá wer dii, di wɛɛ dɛkkɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zumbee n ɔɔ zaah di waa kaali, ka waa togni la.

ref: Horses and donkeys must be beaten and bridled— and so must fools.
text: Virma dɛg zaguu, kabarga ge dɛg kawee, gunnɛ bulaali dɛg gɛnii ge!

ref: Don't make a fool of yourself by answering a fool.
text: Gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ gɛnii pɛɛzaazi, di guŋ lɛi, i daŋ gɛni lugɔu.

ref: But if you answer any fools, show how foolish they are, so they won't feel smart.
text: Di gɛnii ŋɔ gɛnni wiŋɔzi, bir ŋɔ gɛnni wiŋɔzi chemuu, ú zum lugɔ waa wiimaa zummɛ.

ref: Sending a message by a fool is like chopping off your foot just to spite yourself.
text: Hiŋ yatti gɛnii di kpa tile tɛu, ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ alugɔ hiŋ teŋri i naazi gɛɛ hiŋ nyɔɔ siri.

ref: A fool with words of wisdom is like an athlete with legs that can't move.
text: Gunla gbɛrii naazi n waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ la, gunnɛ gɛnii sɛɛliizi waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Are you going to honor a fool? Why not shoot a slingshot with the rock tied tight?
text: Gɛnii tɔgzaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr n vɔɔ bii mari bilori ni.

ref: A thornbush waved around in the hand of a drunkard is no worse than a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
text: Gɛnii sɛɛlii chummɔɔ lugɔ sɔɔh n tɔɔh nɛr la n nyɔɔ siŋ dɛɛzi nonii, di ku du.

ref: Dogs return to eat their vomit, just as fools repeat their foolishness.
text: Gunla nuahiŋ n ɔɔ ug ka bir paagaa di la, gunnɛ gɛnii ɔɔ ra dammi u wiɛɛlaa.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who says, “I'm really smart!”
text: Gɛniirɛ dɔɔ tamii werge kaali nɛr la n na fɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ nunzunnii.

ref: Don't be lazy and keep saying, “There's a lion outside!”
text: Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ dawarii, lugɔ di u lii baŋgia, bunyiŋ daŋ lawuu.

ref: A door turns on its hinges, but a lazy person just turns over in bed.
text: Gunla gbera n ɔɔ ra birgi di ra la see ni har la, gunnɛ yaara hiŋ ɔɔ chɔɔ u kunchɔɔrikuŋ ni di ra birgi.

ref: Some of us are so lazy that we won't lift a hand to feed ourselves.
text: Diwee dii gba ɔɔ ra huah yaara hiŋ bɔraa.

ref: A lazy person says, “I am smarter than everyone else.”
text: Yaara hiŋ ɔɔ ra fɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ nunzunnii, di kaali nɛra baniidaanɛɛ la n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wia nɛnnɛ.

ref: It's better to take hold of a mad dog by the ears than to take part in someone else's argument.
text: Hiŋ kpa i nua jaa kalu la n waa i hor ɛɛwɛ biini, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hiŋ lau nuahiŋ hɔɔhri digna.

ref: It's no crazier to shoot sharp and flaming arrows
text: Chuglahiŋ n na taazi hobee la n na kpu,

ref: than to cheat someone and say, “I was only fooling!”
text: ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n dar u dɔŋ ka ŋɔ, “N na duau!”

ref: Where there is no fuel a fire goes out; where there is no gossip arguments come to an end.
text: Di nindaazi bɛllɔ tuŋ, niŋ ɔɔ dimuu, di zɔɔza ge tunnɔ, kalu ɔɔ tunuu.

ref: Troublemakers start trouble, just as sparks and fuel start a fire.
text: Gunla hɔla n ɔɔ wo di mazi, daazi gil niŋ ra lau la, gunnɛ kalu nyiŋŋi ɔɔ ra du kalu.

ref: There is nothing so delicious as the taste of gossip! It melts in your mouth.
text: Zɔɔza wiŋɔzi summɔɔ alugɔ lɔgmɛnanaa nɛr n ɔɔ ligli, a zuu u bɔra nɛnnɛ.

ref: Hiding hateful thoughts behind smooth talk is like coating a clay pot with a cheap glaze.
text: Nɛr n ɔɔ kpa wiŋɔnanaa di suah u biinikpola la, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ baŋ kpa kunnyɛgzaa faa vii, hàá wer zum lugɔ chuurii ba kpa mau la.

ref: The pleasant talk of an enemy hides more evil plans
text: Machɔgaa hiŋ ɔɔ kpa wiŋɔsumaa suah u manni, ú dar nɛra.

ref: than can be counted— so don't believe a word!
text: Di u waa ŋɔ nɔŋŋaa wiŋɔzi gba, gilɛɛ waa yarduu, wichɔgaa kpila maanii su u biini.

ref: If you dig a pit, you will fall in; if you start a stone rolling, it will roll back on you.
text: Di nɛr he u dɔŋhiŋ sidɛɛ, u daŋ bir lau u himmaa, di u billi bii ú ta u dɔŋhiŋ ni, u daŋ bir ba u ni.

ref: Watch out for anyone who tells lies and flatters— they are out to get you.
text: Karkanni hah banla uŋ kanni karaa di ra chug, nuusum ge ra ba chɔgaa ni.

ref: Don't brag about tomorrow! Each day brings its own surprises.
text: Gilɛɛ waa jigsi dikuu kɛrɛ wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, haa zum wii la n niŋ ba.

ref: Don't brag about yourself— let others praise you.
text: Gilɛɛ waa chɔli i hiŋ, gil nɛra chɔlii.

ref: Stones and sand are heavy, but trouble caused by a fool is a much heavier load.
text: Bii tɔkkɔɔ, hɛɛhraa gba du tɔg, ka gɛnii n fuuh i baannɛ tɔkkɛ kaali a maa.

ref: An angry person is dangerous, but a jealous person is even worse.
text: Baaŋ chummɔɔ, baaŋfuuihchɔgaa ɛɛ lugɔ muu n suwee gi, ka zomaa chummɛ kaali a maa.

ref: A truly good friend will openly correct you.
text: Hiŋ hau nɛr ni u sibɔɔrɛ bɔ, uŋ fɛ lugɔ i baga lɛi u wia.

ref: You can trust a friend who corrects you, but kisses from an enemy are nothing but lies.
text: I dammu n dui piraa bɔ, ka di i dɔm faamii, di jaamii, a du tau!

ref: If you have had enough to eat, honey doesn't taste good, but if you are really hungry, you will eat anything.
text: Huuhnuu ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ aŋ sɛppɛ tɛɛ nɛr la n piŋŋɛ, ka diukpola gba summɔɔ tɛɛ nɛr la lɔzi n na kpu.

ref: When you are far from home, you feel like a bird without a nest.
text: Nɛr la maa n lii u dia ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zumbee n lii u daŋ biini.

ref: The sweet smell of incense can make you feel good, but true friendship is better still.
text: Gunla tulaale ni daahɛgsɔɔhsuma sɔɔh n summɛ nɛr be la, gunnɛ badɔŋ baglaa du sum.

ref: Don't desert an old friend of your family or visit your relatives when you are in trouble. A friend nearby is better than relatives far away.
text: Gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ i dammu ni i mɛɛ dammu di ra ha. Dikuubɛɛwiai, di wia wa huuzii, baabuu niŋ hiinii manaŋ, di kaali i lulli la n du bɔɔnɛɛ.

ref: My child, show good sense! Then I will be happy and able to answer anyone who criticizes me.
text: N bie, n bɔra daŋ sɔɔniŋ di i birgi nunzunni! Denii ń wer ŋɔ wia chem n haahra nɛnnɛ, di ba waa ŋɔ n wia.

ref: Be cautious and hide when you see danger— don't be stupid and walk right into trouble.
text: Nɛr la n dɔɔ nfɛrɛ nɛnnɛ ɔɔ na siaahmuu n na ba, di suah u hiŋ, ka nfɛrnyaari ɔɔ zuu u biinii di tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: You deserve to lose your coat if you loan it to someone to guarantee payment for the debt of a stranger.
text: Di nɛr gɛnnɔ, di chi tɛɛ hɔɔhri u di kim, u himmaa kunnɛ bá lɛɛ dau talma.

ref: A loud greeting early in the morning is the same as a curse.
text: Di i feloo kɔɔ chɔɔzi i dɔŋhiŋ chɔɔzimpikke ni, guŋ daŋ fuuh u baaŋ alugɔ nuuseei.

ref: The steady dripping of rain and the nagging of a wife are one and the same.
text: Hahkalu nyiŋŋi ge wia ra fuuh baannɛ alugɔ domarima.

ref: It's easier to catch the wind or hold olive oil in your hand than to stop a nagging wife.
text: U laafaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hiŋ ŋɔ i laafi peu gɛɛ hiŋ mur nuuteela.

ref: Just as iron sharpens iron, friends sharpen the minds of each other.
text: Gunla baŋ ɔɔ kpa lugbii di sazi u dɔŋ la, gunnɛ nɛr ɔɔ helli nunzuma lii u dɔŋhiŋ be.

ref: Take care of a tree, and you will eat its fruit; look after your master, and you will be praised.
text: Nɛr la n na binni fig daa ni daŋ wer di u nɔna, gunnɛ ba ra tɔgzi nɛr la ge n na du u nabɔma tau.

ref: You see your face in a mirror and your thoughts in the minds of others.
text: Gunla nɛr n ɔɔ na u duula digii biini la, gunnɛ u nfɛrɛ ra bagli u manni.

ref: Death and the grave are never satisfied, and neither are humans.
text: Gunla lalaa bol n waa su la, gunnɛ newee siwii waa su.

ref: Gold and silver are tested in a red-hot furnace, but we are tested by praise.
text: Ninne ba ɔɔ kpa ŋmɛɛri saliŋhuŋŋu ni saliŋ, bá zum a wessi, gunnɛ ba ɔɔ kpa chɔlaa ɛɛ newee na.

ref: No matter how hard you beat a fool, you can't pound out the foolishness.
text: Hàá wer bargi gɛnii lii u gɛnni ni, haali di i chɔguu alugɔ mia, tugree biini gba.

ref: You should take good care of your sheep and goats,
text: Zum gunla i sela n duwɛɛ, di ra du a tau nɛnnɛ,

ref: After the hay is cut and the new growth appears and the harvest is over,
text: Di ba haŋ wa paa kɔlaa, di ŋmɛnni bizenaa nyuuni kooree, kooriifalaa ɔɔ liiu, di ra hel.

ref: you can sell lambs and goats to buy clothes and land.
text: I daŋ na peeza huna suah i laala, di yoo buuna yau hɛri.

ref: From the milk of the goats, you can make enough cheese to feed your family and all your servants.
text: I daŋ na buuna ilanii a hel i ni i diahina ani i balaa.

ref: Wicked people run away when no one chases them, but those who live right are as brave as lions.
text: Biinikpola hiŋ ɔɔ ra chɔu, di nɛr maa wɔɔ ra duŋŋi, ka unla n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi, ɔɔ dɔɔ bampiriire alugɔ bunyiŋ.

ref: In time of civil war there are many leaders, but a sensible leader restores law and order.
text: Di hɛri maa nɛra waa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ba ɔɔ dɔɔ koorikpilaa, ka unla sitɔɔra n ɛɛ nunzunna, u ɔɔ dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa chi nɛnnɛ.

ref: When someone poor takes over and mistreats the poor, it's like a heavy rain destroying the crops.
text: Koori la n na sunni nyaara, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ dooŋ la n na chɔgi kuna.

ref: Criminals don't know what justice means, but all who respect the Lord understand it completely.
text: Biinikpola hina waa wibii zɛɛ zummɛ, ka banla n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi zum u zɛɛrɛ nɛnnɛ.

ref: It's better to be poor and live right, than to be rich and dishonest.
text: Hiŋ nyaawɛ ka ɛɛ wibii hiŋ, aabuu bɔ hiŋ dɔɔwɛ ka i wia waa deŋlee.

ref: It makes good sense to obey the Law of God, but you disgrace your parents if you make friends with worthless nobodies.
text: Biipɔllii la n na hiŋ Gbɔg ɛɛ nunzunnii, ka unla n na hiŋ nɛjagazi, kpa hiihzii ra kpu u mɛɛ.

ref: If you make money by charging high interest rates, you will lose it all to someone who cares for the poor.
text: Nɛr la n na kim nɛra kebee di ra sag nii, u daama daŋ wa mag nɛr la n nɔŋŋi nyaari wia nonee biini.

ref: God cannot stand the prayers of anyone who disobeys his Law.
text: Nɛr la maa n vɛɛ gbɔg hiŋaa, Kɔraawiizi kii u wiisuŋŋaarɛ.

ref: By leading good people to sin, you dig a pit for yourself, but all who live right will have a bright future.
text: Di i dar nɛr la wia n deŋlee u ɛɛ wichɔgaa, i daŋ chol i himmaa sidɛɛ biini, ka unla wia n dɔɔ wibii, daŋ di winanaa kapɛttɛ.

ref: The rich think highly of themselves, but anyone poor and sensible sees right through them.
text: Dɔɔŋ ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ nunzunnii, ka nyaari la n zum wia zɛɛ zum u mannii.

ref: When an honest person wins, it's time to celebrate; when crooks are in control, it's best to hide.
text: Di nɛr la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa nyɛɛli, nɛr maa bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔnuu. Ka di biinikpola hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ sitɔɔri, nɛr maa ɔɔ chɔu di ra suah.

ref: If you don't confess your sins, you will be a failure. But God will be merciful if you confess your sins and give them up.
text: Nɛr la n na suah u wichɔgaa wàá nyɛɛli, ka unla n ɔɔ vɛɛa, di sɛɛ chɔgri, Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ u ni.

ref: The Lord blesses everyone who is afraid to do evil, but if you are cruel, you will end up in trouble.
text: Nɛr la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi saŋa maa, nuu sumaa, ka unla n kpoŋŋe daŋ na siaahmu werge.

ref: A ruler who mistreats the poor is like a roaring lion or a bear hunting for food.
text: Koori la n dɔɔ biinikpola nyaara ni, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ n na pogzi, gɛɛ amani n nyɛkkɛ di ra lauri baa.

ref: A heartless leader is a fool, but anyone who refuses to get rich by cheating others will live a long time.
text: Koori la n gɛnnɛɛrɛ ra fir u nɛra, ka unla n hah wikara, daŋ di kora di birgi.

ref: Don't give help to murderers! Make them stay on the run for as long as they live.
text: Nɛr n na di tɔɔrɔɔ werge, dikuu uŋ kpu nɛr wia, u himmaa bɔɔrɛ u ra ki. Nɛr maa gilɛɛ mɔgluu.

ref: Honesty will keep you safe, but everyone who is crooked will suddenly fall.
text: Nɛr la wia n deŋlee daŋ na u hiŋ, ka unla wia n waa deŋlee daŋ chol.

ref: Work hard, and you will have a lot of food; waste time, and you will have a lot of trouble.
text: Patti la n aah siwii di ra hum, daŋ na diwee werge di ra di, ka gɛnii waa, ɔɔ ra chɔgi u saŋaa humpɛɛri ni.

ref: God blesses his loyal people, but punishes all who want to get rich quick.
text: Banla wia n dɔɔ wibii daŋ na kissaa werge, ka banla n hahzee di ra nyiŋŋi daama manaŋ, daŋ zuu tɔɔrɔɔ biini.

ref: It isn't right to be unfair, but some people can be bribed with only a piece of bread.
text: Di i binni nɛr siwee ka di seriya, guŋ waa wer. Ka baŋhina ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ wichɔgaarɛ, dikuu baŋ lɛɛ kunjiga bɛl wia.

ref: Don't be selfish and eager to get rich— you will end up worse off than you can imagine.
text: Kpossiiri ɔɔ ra yali siweere ú birgi daama hiŋ manaŋ, ka waa zummɛ lugɔ nyaarii niŋ ba u ni.

ref: If you cheat your parents and don't think it's wrong, you are a common thief.
text: Hiŋ kpa fɔŋŋa di ra ŋmɛɛ i mɛɛ ni i maa, ka ra ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ a ra ɛɛi?” A guŋ ɛɛ siaahmuu alugɔ hiŋ kpu nɛr.

ref: Selfish people cause trouble, but you will live a full life if you trust the Lord.
text: Kposiiri ɔɔ koozi wiarɛ du nɛra, ka unla n yardi Kɔraawiizi daŋ nyɛɛli.

ref: Only fools would trust what they alone think, but if you live by wisdom, you will do all right.
text: Gɛniirɛ ra yardi u hiŋ, unla n na hiŋ nunzuma dɔɔ u hinnɛ.

ref: Giving to the poor will keep you from poverty, but if you close your eyes to their needs, everyone will curse you.
text: Nɛr la maa n na sunzi nyaara kuna wàá nyaa maa. Ka nuuseezi daŋ di unla n ɔɔ bir har kpu baa.

ref: When crooks are in control, everyone tries to hide, but when they lose power, good people are everywhere.
text: Di biinikpola hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ sitɔɔri, nɛr maa ɔɔ chɔu di ra suah, ka di hɛhchɔg wa chol u ni, banla ge n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi la ɔɔ nyɛɛluu.

ref: If you keep being stubborn after many warnings, you will suddenly discover you have gone too far.
text: Nɛr la maa n kpoŋŋe di vɛɛ baglaa, daŋ ŋmɛnɛ zuu wia biini, wàá na lɛɛi.

ref: If you love wisdom your parents will be glad, but chasing after bad women will cost you everything.
text: Nɛr la n na nyiŋŋi nunzuma ɔɔ tɛɛ u mɛɛrɛ bɔsɔna, ka di u ni sɛnsɛnna ra kpau, u daama ɔɔ tunuu.

ref: An honest ruler makes the nation strong; a ruler who takes bribes will bring it to ruin.
text: Koori la n na di wibii ɔɔ giluu u hɛri chi nɛnnɛ, ka unla n na nyiŋŋi kebee ɔɔ ra chɔguubuu.

ref: Flattery is nothing less than setting a trap.
text: Di i ra chɔli nɛra ni nuusum, sidɛɛrɛ i ra he i hiŋ la.

ref: Your sins will catch you, but everyone who lives right will sing and celebrate.
text: Biinikpola hiŋ wichɔgaa ɔɔ biruu diu, ka nɛr la wia n deŋlee ɔɔ lii wia biinii, di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna.

ref: The wicked don't care about the rights of the poor, but good people do.
text: Banla wia n deŋlee ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu nyaari na wibii, ka biinikpola hina waa baga lɛi guŋ wia.

ref: Sneering at others is a spark that sets a city on fire; using good sense can put out the flames of anger.
text: Chɛɛtɛ ɛɛra daŋ wer koozi bolzeŋ, ka nunzunna waa ɔɔ sɔɔni baannɛ.

ref: Be wise and don't sue a fool. You won't get satisfaction, because all the fool will do is sneer and shout.
text: Di nunzunni ni gɛnii la seriya diiribɔr, gɛnii la ɔɔ ra mamuu, di ra kɔɔ di ra chagzi, bampirsɔna waa ɔɔ du de.

ref: Don't be a fool and quickly lose your temper— be sensible and patient.
text: Gɛnii ɔɔ giluu u baaŋfuuih lii chaaŋ werge maa, ka nunzunni ɔɔ weruu di kanyitti di lau u hiŋ.

ref: A ruler who listens to lies will have corrupt officials.
text: Di koori ra nuu kara, u zɛɛsogna maa daŋ ɛɛ biinikpola hina.

ref: The poor and all who abuse them must each depend on God for light.
text: Kunnaabuu nyaara ni banla n na sunni baa maa dɔɔ, Kɔraawiizii tɛɛ ba maa siwee ba ra na.

ref: Kings who are fair to the poor will rule a long time.
text: Koori la n na di nyaari seriya ni wibii, daŋ di kora di birgi.

ref: Correct your children, and they will be wise; children out of control disgrace their mothers.
text: Hiŋ tɛr bie digni di deŋluu ra tɛubuu nunzuma, ka bie pɔɔih kpa hiihzii ra kpu u maa.

ref: Crime increases when crooks are in power, but law-abiding citizens will see them fall.
text: Di biinikpola hina haŋ wàá di nabɔmuu, wichɔgaa ɔɔ nyaŋŋuu. Ka nɛra la wia n deŋlee, daŋ du de di na ba cholaa.

ref: If you correct your children, they will bring you peace and happiness.
text: Di i tɛr i biizi digna, ba daŋ tɛi bɔsɔna ni bampirsɔna.

ref: Without guidance from God law and order disappear, but God blesses everyone who obeys his Law.
text: Hɛri la nɛra n waa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ, ɛɛ kuntaalaarɛ, ka bɔsɔna hinaa banla n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua.

ref: Even when servants are smart, it takes more than words to make them obey.
text: Nua bɛŋ kpai dɛɛzi balii wàá wer hinuu, see dignitɛraa n jaawɛ. Aŋhinabe u daŋ nuu i wiŋɔzi hiŋ zɛɛ, ka wàá hiŋaa.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks without thinking.
text: Gɛniirɛ dɔɔ tamii kaali nɛr la n hahzee di ra ŋɔ wia.

ref: Slaves that you treat kindly from their childhood will cause you sorrow.
text: Balii la baŋ pɔɔhwɛ lii u bichalli saŋa, daŋ ŋmɛnɛ tɛi biinichɔg.

ref: A person with a quick temper stirs up arguments and commits a lot of sins.
text: Nɛr la baaŋ n waa birgi fuuih, ɔɔ ra izi kaluu di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa werge.

ref: Too much pride brings disgrace; humility leads to honor.
text: Barabara hiŋ ɔɔ di hiihzii, ka sisɔna hiŋ waa, ɔɔ na girmee.

ref: If you take part in a crime you are your worst enemy, because even under oath you can't tell the truth.
text: Di i ra hiini ŋmɛɛŋ, i hinnɛ i ra du pira, di i pilli u wolo, ba daŋ tɛr i digni, ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ seei nua, di i kaa tɔ u wolo ge.

ref: Don't fall into the trap of being a coward— trust the Lord, and you will be safe.
text: Newee ɔmaa ɛɛ sidɛɛrɛ, ka nɛr la maa n yardi Kɔraawiizi, na u hinnɛ.

ref: Many try to make friends with a ruler, but justice comes from the Lord.
text: Nɛkpila maa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi ba wia par koorii, ka Kɔraawiizi benii newee ɔɔ na wibii.

ref: Good people and criminals can't stand each other.
text: Banla wia n deŋlee, ɔɔ hah biinikpola hinaa, biinikpola hina ge hah baa.

ref: These are the sayings and the message of Agur son of Jakeh. Someone cries out to God, “I am completely worn out! How can I last?
text: Wiŋɔzi naa lii Jakɛ biibaal Agur benii, u ŋɔ tɛɛ Itiɛl ni Ukal.

ref: I am far too stupid to be considered human.
text: Minuu newea maa bambuguu, maa newee nunzuma dɔɔwɛ.

ref: I never was wise, and I don't understand what God is like.”
text: Maa nunzuma hellee gɛɛ di zum Dɔɔrinaniinanii la wia.

ref: Has anyone gone up to heaven and come back down? Has anyone grabbed hold of the wind? Has anyone wrapped up the sea or marked out boundaries for the earth? If you know of any who have done such things, then tell me their names and their children's names.
text: Anɛɛ la Kɔraawiizi bol ka bir banɛi? Anɛɛ n lau peu kuŋŋei? Anɛɛ n kpa u banaaga fɔɔ niirɛi? Anɛɛ n dau hɛri magbɔɔnɛi? U sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ, u biibaal ge sɔnnɛ ɛrɛɛ? Ŋɔ n be, di i zummɔ!

ref: Everything God says is true— and it's a shield for all who come to him for safety.
text: Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii maa ɛɛ wibiire, u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laal pɛrɛtu, di tɛɛ nɛr la maa n chɔwɛɛ di wa zuuu.

ref: Don't change what God has said! He will correct you and show that you are a liar.
text: Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiŋɔdumazi di ra jaa u wiŋɔzi ni, di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ nyɛg i ni, di gil i birgi kara hiŋ.

ref: There are two things, Lord, I want you to do for me before I die:
text: “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, wia anɛɛrɛ n na suŋŋii mɔɔ, ka n siu, jaande maa, gilɛɛ waa kpolliŋ.

ref: Make me absolutely honest and don't let me be too poor or too rich. Give me just what I need.
text: Gilɛɛ wa gil n ŋmɛnɛ maa waa kanni kara, di gilɛɛ waa gil n ɛɛ nyaari gɛɛ daama hiŋ, ka ra tɛŋ n hɔpizi biimaa diwee.

ref: If I have too much to eat, I might forget about you; if I don't have enough, I might steal and disgrace your name.
text: Aŋhinabe, di n ɛɛ dɔɔŋ, n daŋ suuh i wia, di ŋɔ, ‘Anɛɛ Kɔraawiizɛi?’ Ka di n nyaawɔ ge, n daŋ ŋmɛɛ, di chɔg u sɔnnaniinanii la.

ref: Don't tell a slave owner something bad about one of the slaves. That slave will curse you, and you will be in trouble.
text: Gilɛɛ waa chɔg balii u dɔɔri see. Di i ɛɛ guŋ, a hiŋ daŋ bir seei nua, í na wia.

ref: Some people curse their father and even their mother;
text: Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ ra see ba mɛɛwaarɛ nuuzi, ba waa ba maa waa ra jaami ani ba huma.

ref: others think they are perfect, but they are stained by sin.
text: Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ fɛ lugɔ ba waa doŋŋe, ka doŋa bɛnnɛ su ba bampiree.

ref: Some people are stuck-up and act like snobs;
text: Nɛra baŋhina dɔɔ barabaraa ga bɛri, di ra gbɛlli nɛra werge.

ref: others are so greedy that they gobble up the poor and homeless.
text: Nɛra baŋhina ɔɔ dɔɔ sikpegiire, di ra sunni nyaara ni anuula hina, gunnɛ ba ɛɛ di ra di.

ref: Greed has twins, each named “Give me!” There are three or four things that are never satisfied:
text: Kpaŋkpaŋziglii dɔɔ biihaana banɛɛ, ba maa ra wii, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Tɛŋ, tɛŋ!’ Kuna ahoro aŋhina ge du de, akai, a du anaazuu! A waa diwee ra piŋ, aabuu,

ref: The world of the dead and a childless wife, the thirsty earth and a flaming fire.
text: ŋmam, hahbara, hɛri la n hillɛ di ra nyiŋŋi donii ani niŋ, a ŋmɛnɛ haa waa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ, a kukkɔɔrɛ!

ref: Don't make fun of your father or disobey your mother— crows will peck out your eyes, and buzzards will eat the rest of you.
text: Nɛr la n na ɛɛ u mɛɛ chɛɛtɛ, di ra gbɛlli u maa, duglizi daŋ foŋzi u siwee, duuni dia.

ref: How eagles fly so high or snakes crawl on rocks, how ships sail the ocean or people fall in love.
text: gunla chig n ɔɔ ra lɛɛli chiŋ la, gunla hɛrikuŋ n ɔɔ ra goomi bii nyuu la, gunla muugberzeŋ n ɔɔ sag nii nyuu di ra la la, ani gunla baal ni haaŋ n ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi dɔŋa la.

ref: An unfaithful wife says, “Sleeping with another man is as natural as eating.”
text: Kenne hahsɛnsɛnni ɔɔ ra ɛɛ, u ɔɔ sɛmuu, di sɔ nii ka ŋɔ, ‘Maa wichɔgaa maa ɛɛwɛ!’

ref: There are three or four things that make the earth tremble and are unbearable:
text: Kuna ahoroo ɔɔ gil hɛri zigli, anaazu ge ɔɔ gil a ra nuuu,

ref: A slave who becomes king, a fool who eats too much,
text: aabuu, yom n birgi koori, gɛnii la n dɔɔ kunla maa unna nyiŋŋi,

ref: a hateful woman who finds a husband, and a slave who takes the place of the woman who owns her.
text: haaŋ la biini n kpolle n yuuwɛ, gɛɛ balii n wa foozi u dɔɔri jaari.

ref: On this earth four things are small but very wise:
text: Kunjigzi anaazuu du hɛri naa, ka a dɔɔ nunzumaa werge,

ref: Ants, who seem to be feeble, but store up food all summer long;
text: aabuu, minni, a waa kpeg, ka a ɔɔ chaali diweere dau di ra kpaŋ yuu,

ref: badgers, who seem to be weak, but live among the rocks;
text: kachazi waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ, ka bia bɔɔnii a ra suah,

ref: locusts, who have no king, but march like an army;
text: lotorozi waa koori dɔɔwɛ, ka ɔɔ ra voluu lugɔ laallɔɔra,

ref: lizards, which can be caught in your hand, but sneak into palaces.
text: ger lawaa waa kpol, ka u du koora diinii.

ref: Those fearless lions who rule the jungle,
text: aabuu, bunyiŋ, waabuu ɛɛ sela koori, waa bɛɛ ka ra tɛɛ kummaa bɔr,

ref: those proud roosters, those mountain goats, and those rulers who have no enemies.
text: zabal n ɔɔ ra vol barabara ni, bubal, ani koori la u laallɔɔra n baruu.

ref: If you are foolishly bragging or planning something evil, then stop it now!
text: Di i faa ɛɛ gɛnii di ra kpa i hiŋ zenni, gɛɛ di ta wichɔgaa jina, willi i nyuu ni hiihzi!

ref: If you churn milk you get butter; if you pound on your nose, you get blood— and if you stay angry, you get in trouble.
text: Gunla baŋ ɔɔ yiigi nail la n du kɔŋkɔŋ biini, a wa lii nuu la, di lɔ nɛr miizi chal lii la, gunnɛ nɛr baaŋfuuih ɔɔ izi kalu.”

ref: These are the sayings that King Lemuel of Massa was taught by his mother.
text: Wiŋɔzi naa lii Koori bɛl banna yir Lɛmuɛl, u maa n bagluubuu keŋ,

ref: My son Lemuel, you were born in answer to my prayers, so listen carefully.
text: “I ɛɛ n biinɔŋŋiirɛ, Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ n wiisuŋŋaarɛ. Ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔ i benei?

ref: Don't waste your life chasing after women! This has ruined many kings.
text: Gilɛɛ waa kpa i fɔŋŋa di ra chɔɔ haana, di kpa i kebee ra chɔg ba ni, ba chɔgi kooraa.

ref: Kings and leaders should not get drunk or even want to drink.
text: A nuu, Lɛmuɛl, koora waa dɛg siŋ nyɔɔi gɛɛ di ra kɛlli siŋkpega.

ref: Drinking makes you forget your responsibilities, and you mistreat the poor.
text: Di ba haŋ wa nyɔɔ siŋ, ba ɔɔ suuh gbɔgnii, di vɛɛ wia la n dɛg nɛra ɛɛi.

ref: Beer and wine are only for the dying or for those who have lost all hope.
text: Nɛra la n na siu kunnɛ siŋkpeg, di kaa ɛɛ banla biine n chɔkkɛ werge kuŋ,

ref: Let them drink and forget how poor and miserable they feel.
text: gil bá nyɔɔ di suuh ba nyaari ni ba biinichɔg wia.

ref: But you must defend those who are helpless and have no hope.
text: Ɛɛ ŋɔ wia lɛɛ banla n wàá wer ŋɔ wia lɛɛ bahinaa la, di ɔɔ di wibii ra lɛɛ banla n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Be fair and give justice to the poor and homeless. In Praise of a Good Wife
text: Ɛɛ ŋɔ wia di ra di seriya ni wibii di ra lɛɛ baa, di ra lɛɛ nyaara ni dɔgnya hina.” Hahpa chɔlaa wia

ref: A truly good wife is the most precious treasure a man can find!
text: Hahpa nai kpolloo! U dɔɔ tɔnaa werge kaali rubizi!

ref: Her husband depends on her, and she never lets him down.
text: U jaari ɔɔ yarduubuu, u jaari ŋmɛnɛ wàá nyaa maa.

ref: She is good to him every day of her life,
text: U de dui maa biini, winanaarɛ ɔɔ ra ɛɛu, waa ɔɔ ra tɔɔruu.

ref: and with her own hands she gladly makes clothes.
text: U ɔɔ ra humuu saŋa maa, di ra kuari peezi huna ni gessihuŋŋunanaa wɛjɛ.

ref: She is like a sailing ship that brings food from across the sea.
text: U ɔɔ la bɔɔnɛɛzii ga chi diwee di ra ba, gunla kɔkɔɔza n ɔɔ kpa muugberzenaa di ra ɛɛ la.

ref: She gets up before daylight to prepare food for her family and for her servants.
text: U ɔɔ feluu izi chɔɔzimpikke ni, di daali diwee tɛɛ u diahina, di ɔɔ bagli u balaa ba humazi.

ref: She knows how to buy land and how to plant a vineyard,
text: Hahpa ɔɔ liiu nyiŋŋi hɛrnanii yau di kpa u huma tɔna yau grepu daazi koo.

ref: and she always works hard.
text: U ɔɔ dɔɔ bɔkpega ni fɔŋŋaa, di ra hum werge.

ref: She knows when to buy or sell, and she stays busy until late at night.
text: U ɔɔ aah siwiire u kɔɔzaa dɔɔ tɔna, u ɔɔ humuu guŋŋ hɛuh wa hɛɛhzi.

ref: and she helps the poor and the needy.
text: U ɔɔ ra hiini nyaaraa, di yaa nonee di ra lɛɛ anuula hina.

ref: Her family has warm clothing, and so she doesn't worry when it snows.
text: Gbaŋgbaŋ wia waa ɔɔ tiruu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u diahina maanii dɔɔ waari laala.

ref: She does her own sewing, and everything she wears is beautiful.
text: U ɔɔ nyɛr u himmaa chɔɔribɔr kumpɛɛri kunaa, u ɔɔ bɔg u hinnɛ ni pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa ni anla n aahwɛ lugɔ zagbiiŋ niirɛ.

ref: Her husband is a well-known and respected leader in the city.
text: U jaari ɔɔ dɔɔ sɔnnɛ nɛnnɛ, di ra so bol nabɔnzi biini.

ref: She makes clothes to sell to the shop owners.
text: U ɔɔ ra nyɛr bɔmbɔga ni belentizii, di yooa ra tɛɛ kɔkɔɔza.

ref: She is strong and graceful, as well as cheerful about the future.
text: U ɔɔ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ni girmee, waa wii la n niŋ wa ɛɛ kɛrɛ ra ɔm.

ref: Her words are sensible, and her advice is thoughtful.
text: Nunzuma wiŋɔzii u ɔɔ ra ŋɔ, u baglaa ge ra tɛɛ nfɛrɛ.

ref: She takes good care of her family and is never lazy.
text: U ɔɔ ra du wia la maa n na ɛɛ u dia taurɛ nɛnnɛ, waa yaara dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Her children praise her, and with great pride her husband says,
text: U biizi ɔɔ ra chɔluubuu, u jaari ge ɔɔ ra chɔluu, di ra ŋɔ,

ref: “There are many good women, but you are the best!”
text: “Hahpazi suwoore, ka hinuu kaali ba maa.”

ref: Charm can be deceiving, and beauty fades away, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves to be praised.
text: Nuusum daŋ wer ɛɛ daraa, toloori ge dɔɔ tunaa, ka haaŋ la n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi dɛg chɔlaarɛ.

ref: Show her respect— praise her in public for what she has done.
text: Turguu wia la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ kim. Nɛra maa ra tɔgzuu.

ref: When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
text: Nunzunni la n faa ɛɛ Koori Deevid biibaal, di ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm koori la wiŋɔɔlaarɛ keŋ,

ref: Nothing makes sense! Everything is nonsense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense!
text: Kenne u ŋɔ, “Wipɛɛrii, wipɛɛrii! De dui ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ! Wiimaa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ!”

ref: What is there to show for all of our hard work here on this earth?
text: Bɛɛ tɔnaa newee ɔɔ na di lii u huŋhunnaa maa biini, uŋ aah siwii ra hum durnya naa biinei?

ref: People come, and people go, but still the world never changes.
text: Jiminizi ra bau, jiminizi ra kaali, ka durnya waa duulaa u duula.

ref: The sun comes up, the sun goes down; it hurries right back to where it started from.
text: Wiizi haa ra furuu di ra chol, di ra la bɔr la uŋ futtɛ la, ú kaa ga fur.

ref: The wind blows south, the wind blows north; round and round it blows over and over again.
text: Peu ɔɔ tau ra la wiifurii nodig wiikakag, di bir ta ra la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ta ra bar saŋa maa.

ref: All rivers empty into the sea, but it never spills over; one by one the rivers return to their source.
text: Niiri maa pallɔɔ di ra zuu muuzeŋ, ka waa su. A ɔɔ biruu la bɔr la aŋ liiwɛ, di kaa ga faari.

ref: All of life is far more boring than words could ever say. Our eyes and our ears are never satisfied with what we see and hear.
text: Wiimaa ɛɛ kuuhni la nɛr n wàá wer bagli u wiarɛ. Yaa siwee waa wia nawɛɛ ra piŋ, yaa digna gba waa nuuwɛ ra piŋ.

ref: Everything that happens has happened before; nothing is new, nothing under the sun.
text: Wii la n felee ɛɛ, daŋ kaa ɛɛ, wii la baŋ ɛɛwɛ, ba daŋ kaa kuari ɛɛu, wifalii maa waa hoo durnya naa biini.

ref: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
text: Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu, “Na, wifalii bɛllɛ keŋ!” Akai, a widee ɛɛwɔɔ birgi mɔɔ, ka ba lul yaa.

ref: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
text: Ba waa faala hina wia ra liizi, haali banla ban niŋ haa lul gba, banla n niŋ hiŋ baa wàá liizi ba wia. Nunzuma ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ

ref: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
text: Mìŋ́ Nunzunni naa faa ɛɛ Izrɛl koorii di so Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do.
text: N ɛɛ aniaa ń pigzi di helli wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biini, ń zum a zɛɛzi. Kɔraawiizi waa yaa tɛɛwɛ labananii.

ref: I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: N na wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biinii. N na ŋɔ i benii lugɔ a ɛɛ wipɛɛrii. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

ref: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
text: Hàá wer deŋli kunla n golle gɛɛ di kur kuna la i siwee n waa na.

ref: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
text: Denii n ŋɔ n biini, “N birgi nɛzenne, di dɔɔ nunzuma werge kaali nɛr la maa n faa di kora Jɛrusalɛm, mɔɔ ka n wa diu. N zum kuna la nunzuma ni zumaa n ɛɛwɛnɛ.”

ref: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: N aah siwii ń zum gunla zumaa ni gɛnaa n kuttɛ ani gunla nunzuma ni chugla n kuttɛ. Denii n na lugɔ guŋ gba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ minna duŋŋi peu.

ref: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
text: Gunla i nunzuma n na jaa la, gunnɛ wia ra tirii werge, gunla i zumaa n kannɛ, gunnɛ wia ra tɔɔrii.

ref: I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense.
text: Denii n ŋɔ ń di n hiŋ, di na gunla bɔsɔna n duwɛɛ. Ka n wa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ wipɛɛrii a ge gba.

ref: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
text: N kaa na lugɔ mamaa ɛɛ gɛnni wiarɛ. Hindii gba waa ɔɔ hiinii.

ref: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
text: Miŋ aah siwii lugɔ n dɔɔ nunzuma la wia, n kpa siŋ di ra deŋŋi siwee, di ra di n hiŋ. N fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ gunnɛ niŋ gil nɛra ra di bahinaa, saŋa kpurii naa newea n dɔɔwɛ durnya biini naa.

ref: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
text: N wettoo ɛɛ wizenaa. N ma diinii, di par grepu daazi kooni.

ref: I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees.
text: N kuari kambolnanaarɛ, di duu daazi irizi la n na nɔŋ,

ref: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
text: di ki bulli, ń na dua nii.

ref: I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem.
text: N yau yomkpilaa, ba lul baŋhina ge n dia jaa. N faa dɔɔ selaa kaali nɛr la maa n faa felee du Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
text: N faa kaa chaali saliŋhuŋŋa ani saliŋ lii hɛssi la miŋ faa ra di kora a ni la daama kuna dauribɔra. Baala ni haana ɔɔ faa yir yira di ra deŋŋi n siwee. N kaa dɔɔ haana la baal maa n ninna kɛlli ú dɔɔ.

ref: I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise.
text: Wibii maa, n faa ɛɛ nɛzenne. N zenni faa kaali nɛr la maa n faa felee du Jɛrusalɛm labuu werge maa. N nunzuma faa waa gillɛ n ɛɛ wia huhzi maa.

ref: I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work.
text: Kunla maa miŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi, an naubuu. N faa waa sideŋŋa maa vɛɛwɛ. N bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ dikuu kunla maa miŋ hummɛ di na wia. N tɔna maanii faa guŋ.

ref: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
text: Denii n pessi wia la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ la ani gunla miŋ aah siwii di ɛɛa la wia, di na lugɔ a faa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii. A faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu, a faa waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ. Nunzuma ni gɛnaa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii

ref: I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity.
text: A tuna maa, koori wàá wer ɛɛ wiimaa kaali anla koora la n tɔ u see n ɛɛwɛ la. Awia, n faari di ra pessi nunzuma dɔɔi zɛɛ gɛɛ chugla ni gɛnaa zɛɛzi.

ref: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
text: Ee, n na lugɔ nunzumaa bɔ gɛnaa gunla bɔchaaŋ n bɔ bɔbiri la.

ref: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
text: Nunzunna ɔɔ ra na bɔr la banna lau, ka gɛnaa waa guŋ duwɛɛ. N kaa na lugɔ labakpannɛ chɔɔwɛ tɛɛ ba maa.

ref: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
text: Denii n fɛ n biini, “N ni gɛnaa maanii labakpaŋ huuzi. Awia, bɛɛ tɔnaa n na lii n nunzuma werge la biinei?” Awia, n ŋɔ n biini, “Maa kummaa nawɛɛ, a maa ɛɛ wipɛɛrii.”

ref: This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: Awia, n de dui faa waa kaa wa dɔɔ zɛɛ tɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, wan tɛɛwɛ kummaa, di tɔɔrɔɔ bɛŋ lɛi. N de dui maa faa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peure n na duŋŋi.

ref: Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all.
text: Kuna la maa miŋ faa hummɛ na, faa waa kaa ɛɛ kummaa n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, n zummɔ lugɔ n daŋ gilaa tɛɛ n kapɛttɛ diiri.

ref: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
text: Aŋhinabe, u daŋ ɛɛ nunzunni gɛɛ gɛnii. Ka waabuu niŋ dɔɔ kuna la maa miŋ kuuhwɛ na. Kuna la maa n nunzuma n tɛŋ durnya naa biini, a maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
text: Awia, n biini faa faari chɔgi, dikuu miŋ kuuhwɛ werge la wia.

ref: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
text: Nɛr ɔɔ kpa u nunzuma ni u zumaarɛ di hum na kuna, ka a ɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ gilaa tɛɛ nɛr la n waa a kuuhni kuuhwɛ. A guŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A guŋ waa wer!

ref: What do we really gain from all of our hard work?
text: Nɛr ɔɔ ra humuu ni kafɔŋ u miibɔɔ saŋa. Ka bɛɛ tɔnaa ɔɔ na durnya naa biinei?

ref: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
text: Nɛr de dui biini maa, u wiɛɛlaa maa ɔɔ ra tɛubuu kafɔŋ ni biinichɔg. Haali hamuŋa, ka u nfɛrɛ waa ɔɔ chɔɔ bɔkpaŋ. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
text: Winanii la maa nɛr n niŋ wer ɛɛu lugɔ u ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di lii u kuuhni biini. Ka a gba, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi benii a lii.

ref: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
text: Ɛrɛɛ i ɛɛ na di ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di u be lɛi a liiyɛi?

ref: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Kɔraawiizii ra tɛɛ banla wia n paruu nunzuma ni zumaa ani bɔsɔna. Ka u ɔɔ giluu wichɔgɛɛra ra hum, di ra na kuna di ra dau, ú wa kpaa tɛɛ banla wia n paruu. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

ref: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
text: Wiimaa dɔɔ saŋaa, di dɔɔ u hɔpizii durnya naa biini.

ref: There is a time for birth and death, planting and reaping,
text: Lulaa ni siu dɔɔ a saŋazii, kuna duui ni a kpuzaa ge dɔɔ a saŋazi,

ref: for killing and healing, destroying and building,
text: kpui dɔɔ saŋa, chaai dɔɔ saŋa, purgaa dɔɔ saŋa, mai ge dɔɔ saŋa,

ref: for crying and laughing, weeping and dancing,
text: biinichɔg ni bɔsɔna dɔɔ a saŋazi, lee wiraa ni saizi ge dɔɔ a saŋazi,

ref: for throwing stones and gathering stones, embracing and parting.
text: bia yaaraa ni a chaalaa dɔɔ a saŋazi, dɔŋa koraa ni dɔŋa vɛɛ koraa dɔɔ a saŋazi,

ref: There is a time for finding and losing, keeping and giving,
text: kuna nyiŋŋaa ni a lewaa dɔɔ a saŋazi, a dawaa ni a kpai ha ge dɔɔ a saŋazi,

ref: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
text: nɔŋŋaa ni hahzi dɔɔ a saŋazi, laal ni bampirsɔna ge dɔɔ a saŋazi.

ref: What do we gain by all our hard work?
text: Bɛɛ tɔnaa huŋhunni ɔɔ na di lii u kuuhni biinei?

ref: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
text: N na buntɔga la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ chug neweare.

ref: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
text: Saŋazi la n dɛkkɛɛ u dau tɛɛ wiimaa. U gillɔɔ newea dɔɔ kɛkɛluu, bá zum wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ ŋmɛnɛbɛl. Ka waa baa tɛɛwɛ bá wer zum u wiɛɛlaa zɛɛ nɛnnɛ di ga tuŋ, á kpu baa lɔzi.

ref: I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life,
text: Awia, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ newea hor maanii ba dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di aah siwii ra hum ba humazi, baŋ haa dɔɔ miibɔɔni naa.

ref: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ newea maa ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di ra di bahinaa lii kuna la baŋ kuuhwɛ na biini. Kɔraawiizi sunzaarɛ guŋ.

ref: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
text: N zummɔ lugɔ wii la maa Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ waa chɔgaa dɔɔwɛ maa. Newea wàá wer kpa wiimaa jaa a ni gɛɛ di lizi a yemmaa ha. Wikpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa n na bagli neweare lugɔ, bá ra ɔmuu werge.

ref: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
text: Wii la maa n ɛɛwɛɛ gɛɛ n niŋ haa wa ɛɛ, faa ɛɛwɔɔ mɔɔ. Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ giluu wia bir di ra ɛɛ digiidigii.

ref: Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice.
text: N kaa na lugɔ durnya naa biini, biinikpolaa ɔɔ du bɔr la n dɛkkɛ wibii dii ni wideŋlaa n niŋ du.

ref: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
text: Denii n fɛ n biini, “Kɔraawiizi daŋ di nɛnanaa ni nɛchɔgaa maa seriya, dikuubɛɛwiai, wiimaa ni wiɛɛlii maa daŋ ɛɛu, saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ tɛabuu.”

ref: I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals.
text: Denii n kaa fɛ n biini, “Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ neweare di ra na, bá zum lugɔ ba waa sela bɔwɛɛ.

ref: Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense.
text: A tuna maa, newea ni sela maa heeza ɛɛ kpannɛ. Bɛl maa ɔɔ siwuu. Kɔraawiizi taabuu a ɛɛ iri kpaŋ. Newee waa sel bɔwɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, de dui waa zɛɛ dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ bɛl maa.

ref: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
text: Bɔkpannɛ a maa ra la. Waabuu hɛɛhraa biini. Denii a maa lii, a daŋ bir kaali de.

ref: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
text: Ɛrɛɛ nɛr maa wer zum lugɔ newee duma ra la chinne, ka sel duma ra zuu hɛrɛi?”

ref: We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
text: Denii n na lugɔ wizeŋ la newea n ninna ɛɛu, ban ninna di kuna la baŋ kuuhwɛ na labuu ni bɔsɔna. Ba wàá ka wer ɛɛ wiimaa. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá wer zum wii la n niŋ ɛɛ, ba siu har.

ref: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
text: Denii n kaa binni nɛsunnaa la n su durnya naa biini, di na banla banna sunni la n na wii, ka nɛr maa waa hoo ú tig ba bampiree. Nɛr maa wàá hiini baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra la n na sunni baa la dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa.

ref: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
text: N na lugɔ banla n siuzɛɛ nuu sumaa, kaali nyinee.

ref: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
text: Ka banla n bɔ ba maanii, banla baŋ haa waa lullɛ. Baabuu haa waa durnya naa wichɔgaa nawɛɛ la.

ref: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: N kaa helli wii la wia nɛra n aah siwii ra hum bá nyɛɛli. Ba dɔŋahina kuna dɔɔi wiarɛ ba ra ɛɛ guŋ. Ka a maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

ref: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
text: Aŋhinabe gunnɛ, ka hiŋ dɔɔ tama, ka dɔɔ nfɛrkpaŋ, aabuu bɔ hiŋ kpa i nonee ra hum saŋa maa, di ra duŋŋi peu.

ref: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
text: Wii bɛllɛ n kaa pessi de dui biini, u ɛɛ pɛɛ.

ref: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
text: Baal bɛllɛ faa du de, u bɛŋ. Waa biibaal gɛɛ maa bie dɔɔwɛ. Ka u aah siwii ra hum saŋa maa, ka u siwii waa su u daama la uŋ dɔɔwɛ wia. Anɛɛ wiarɛ u aah siwii ra hum kennei, ka waa sɛɛwɛ ra di u hiŋ naanɛi? A keŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, di ɛɛ biinichɔg werge maa.

ref: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
text: Nɛra banɛɛ wia bɔ nɛkpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba huma wia daŋ dɔɔ siwee.

ref: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
text: Di bɛl wa chollo, u dɔŋhiŋ daŋ lalluu. Ka di nɛkpaŋ du u bɛŋ di wa chol, wichɔgiirɛ werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa waa hoo, ú lalluu.

ref: If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night.
text: Di bɔr sɔɔnɔɔ, nɛra banɛɛ daŋ chɔɔ pɛli dɔŋa, ba bɔra wenzi di duŋŋi waari. Ka ɛrɛɛ waari ɛɛ lii i ni, di i chɔɔ i bɛnnɛi?

ref: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
text: Nɛra banɛɛ daŋ wer lɛɛ bahinaa lii siaahmu la n niŋ kpegli nɛkpaŋ biini. Kubooroobi la baŋ kpa gessibee ahoro ŋmɛɛni chaih kpolloo.

ref: You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice.
text: Biipɔllii la n ɛɛ nyaari ka zum wiarɛ bɔ koorizɛŋa la n gɛnnɛ, waa baglaa ra nuu.

ref: Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king.
text: Aŋhinabe, a biipɔllii lii nɛra tɔi diarɛ di wa di kora, gɛɛ ba luluu ni nyaari, u kora diiribɔr biini.

ref: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
text: N na lugɔ banla maa n du durnya naa biini, ra hiŋ a biipɔllii la n niŋ wa kpa koori gawa labuu.

ref: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Aŋhinabe, nɛra la koori n na di kora ba ni waa maga dɔɔwɛ. Ka di u wa siuwɔ, nɛr maa wàá chɔluu, dikuu u wiɛɛlaa wia. Guŋ gba ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu.

ref: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
text: Di i ra la Kɔraawiizi Dia, a du tau nɛnnɛ. Hiŋ la de di gaa helli wia, aabuu bɔ hinna lizi mbusuzi gunla gɛnaa n na ɛɛ la. Baabuu banla n waa zummɛ lugɔ wideŋlaa kuttɔɔ wichɔgaa ni la.

ref: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
text: Ɛɛ fɛ nfɛrɛ ka ra ŋɔ wia, di gilɛɛ hahzi ŋɔ nua ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. U du chinne, i ge du hɛri, awia, gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ wia ra bɛri.

ref: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
text: Di i ra fɔŋ wia ni werge, guŋ daŋ wer gil i ra deezi deezichɔgaa. Di i kaa ra ŋɔ wia ge werge, guŋ daŋ gil i ŋɔ gɛnni wia.

ref: It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it.
text: Hiŋ waa nua ŋɔwɛɛ, aabuu bɔ hiŋ ŋɔu, ka hɔɔ hiŋŋɛ.

ref: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
text: Gilɛɛ wa gil i wiŋɔɔlaa ra dui wichɔgaa ɛɛi biini, di gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ be lugɔ i ra duau. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ í gil Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh i ninɛi? Gilɛɛ gil u wàá chɔgi kuna la maa hiŋ kuuhwɛ na la.

ref: Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
text: Gunla maa hinna deezi gɛɛ hinna hum humpɛɛri gɛɛ hinna ŋɔ wia, ka a dɛkkɔɔ í ra ɔm Kɔraawiizi werge. Daama ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ

ref: Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do.
text: Gilɛɛ wa gil a tirii, di i wa na gɔminanti n na fir nyaara, waa wibii lɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ baa gɛɛ di ra tɛɛ baa wia la n dɛg baa. Nabɔma maa dɔɔ u nabɔmaa u ra guuu. Nabɔnzenaa ge ɔɔ kaa guu ba maa.

ref: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
text: A koori himmaa gba, a hɛri kumpattaa ninɛɛ u dɛlli.

ref: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
text: Di i nɔŋŋi kebee, i siwii waa ba sui maa, di i ra nyiŋŋi í birgi daama hiŋ, ka hàá wer na kuna la maa hinna nyiŋŋi. Pɛɛrɛ a maa.

ref: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
text: Di i dɔɔ daama werge, nɛkpilaa ninna dii. Tɔna la maa hinna na maanii, banna yirii daama hiŋ.

ref: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
text: Aŋhinabe, huŋhunni daŋ na diwee ra di, di ra kukki, gɛɛ wàá na, ka u daŋ wer chɔɔ dɔɔ nɛnnɛ hamuŋa ni. Ka daama hiŋ waa kuŋkpila wia, waa dɔɔ ra chɔɔ.

ref: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
text: Wichuma werge bɛllɛ n na durnya biini. Nɛra ɔɔ ra dau kebeere di ra ba saŋa la ban niŋ wàá nyiŋŋaa,

ref: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
text: ka a maa ɔɔ wa lewuu, dikuu ŋmɛnichuma bɛl uŋ kpaa ga wia, wàá ka dɔɔ kummaa ú gil dau u biizi.

ref: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
text: Gunla newee n waa ɔɔ kpogli kummaa ba durnya naa la, gunnɛ waa ɔɔ kaa kpogli kummaa lii u biini kaali. Haali uŋ ɔɔ hum huma werge maa gba, ka wàá wer kpa kummaa kaali.

ref: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
text: A gunna wiiu werge! Gunla newee n ɔɔ ba, gunnɛ ɔɔ kaa kaali. U ɔɔ ra kuuuh di ra ɛɛ ania ka u kuuhni ɔɔ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
text: U ɔɔ du bɔbirii, u biini chɔgi, kafɔŋ lawuu, u baaŋ na fuuh, u ra wii.

ref: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
text: Wii la miŋ nawɛɛrɛ keŋ, winanii la nɛr n niŋ wer ɛɛu lugɔ ú ra di, di ra nyɔɔ, di kpa kuna la uŋ kuuhwɛ na la, di ra di u hiŋ, miibɔɔkpurii naa Kɔraawiizi n tɛu naa biini. Newee labaa guŋ.

ref: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ nɛr daama, di gil u ra di a suma, a dɛkkɔɔ ú ra tɛu jaaŋ ka ra di kuna la uŋ kuuhwɛ na la. Kɔraawiizii sunzuu.

ref: God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
text: Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n tɛu bɔsɔna wia, waa ɔɔ kaa ra fɔŋ werge gunla u miibɔɔ n kpusse wia.

ref: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
text: N pessoore di na lugɔ wichɔgaa du durnya naa biinii werge.

ref: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
text: Kɔraawiizi ɔɔ tɛɛ nɛbɛllɛ daama ni girme. Wibii maa, ɔɔ tɛubuu kuna la maa unna nyiŋŋi, ka waa ɔɔ gil u ra di a suma. Ka hɔɔhri bɛllɛ ɔɔ lɛɛa di ra di. A guŋ ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. A gunna wiiu werge.

ref: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
text: Nɛr daŋ wer dɔɔ biizi kalfa, di dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, ka di waa bɔsɔna dɔɔwɛ di wa siu, ba wɔɔ hukke nɛnnɛ, guŋwaa, bie la n siu u maa hia, ka ba luluurɛ bɔu. Wii la miŋ nawɛɛrɛ guŋ.

ref: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
text: di kaali nɛr la n waa de dui suma ra di, haali di u di binni kagboŋa anɛɛ gba. Ani a maa, ka bɔkpannɛ ba maa ra la.

ref: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
text: Nɛra ɔɔ ra hum ba humaa bá na kumbɛl di, ka ba waa ɔɔ wer bá naa, á kukki baa.

ref: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: A ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hinna duŋŋi peu. A wessoo í gil kunla hiŋ dɔɔwɛ su i siwii, ka gil a dumazi nyiŋŋaa di ra jaa saŋa maa.

ref: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
text: Wii la maa n na ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizii dau guŋ faala maa. Nɛr maa zummɔ lugɔ u ni nɛr la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa kaaluu wàá wer di mmɔri.

ref: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
text: Gunla maa maga nɛr n niŋ di mmɔri, ka pɛɛrɛ, wàá na hiinaa maa.

ref: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
text: Anɛɛ n niŋ wer zum wia la n dɛg yaa, yaa de dui naa n ɛɛ pɛɛ naa biinei? Miibɔɔ la n ɔɔ kaali lugɔ laalii lai? Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ zum wia la n niŋ waa ɛɛ durnya naa biini, yaa siu harɛi?

ref: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
text: Sɔnnanii bɔ tulaale la yoola n kpolle, gunnɛ i siwaa hɔpizii bɔ i lulaa hɔpizii.

ref: It's better to go to a funeral than to attend a feast; funerals remind us that we all must die.
text: Hinna la dia la biini banna wii lee, bɔ unla biini banna di diuzenaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ nyinee ra liizi lugɔ ba daŋ siuzi.

ref: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
text: Biinichɔg bɔ mamaa, u daŋ gil i nyɛm, ka ɔɔ giluu i wia zɛɛ zumaa ra jaa.

ref: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
text: Nunzunni n na hau i ni, aabuu bɔ gɛnaa n na chɔlii.

ref: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
text: Di gɛnii haŋ waa mam, a ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ niŋ n na fuuh sɔɔhri a ra pogzi. A ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
text: Wiimaa tunaa bɔ u luglaa, kanyittii bɔ jigsi.

ref: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
text: A lau i hiŋ, di i baaŋ wa fuuhwo, gɛniirɛ kpa wia ra du u biini.

ref: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
text: Gilɛɛ waa pɛɛzi, di ra ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ n baani wia faa bɔ werge maa, faala lai?” Nunzunni wipɛɛzaa lɛi guŋ.

ref: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
text: Nunzuma daŋ wer guui lugɔ kebee n ɔɔ guui la, di gil i dɔɔ i hiŋ. Zumaa tɔnaa la.

ref: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
text: A fɛ Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa wia. Nɛr daŋ wer deŋli kunla Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ u golaa?

ref: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
text: Di i wia ra kuari nɛnnɛ, gil i bɔra sɔɔni. Ka di tɔɔrɔɔ wa ballɔ, a liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizii ɔɔ gil bɔsɔna ni tɔɔrɔɔ maa ra ba. Hàá wer zum wii la n niŋ wa ɛɛ.

ref: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
text: N de dui ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, ka n wettoo na wiimaa. Nɛnanaa ɔɔ weruu siuzi ka nɛra baŋhina du de birgi, haali baŋ ɛɛ nɛchɔgaa gba.

ref: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
text: Awia, gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nɛnanii werge gɛɛ di wàá ɛɛ nunzunni werge. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i kpu i hinnɛi?

ref: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
text: Gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ biinikpola werge gɛɛ di wàá gɛŋ werge. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i siu manannɛi?

ref: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
text: Gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ mannizi naa bɛl maa werge. Di i ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi di ra ɔmuu, i wiimaa daŋ kuari.

ref: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
text: Wia la nunzuma dɔɔi n ɔɔ ɛɛ tɛɛ nɛr, kaali wia la bolzeŋ nabɔnzi fi n niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ a bolzeŋ.

ref: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
text: Gilɛɛ ra nuu wia la maa nɛra n na ŋɔ, di guŋ lɛi, i daŋ nuu i balii n na chagzii,

ref: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
text: N kpa n nunzumaa ɛɛ annii naa maa na. N faa ra fir n hinnɛ ń dɔɔ nunzuma, ka guŋ faa kaalimbuu.

ref: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
text: Ka n faa aah siwiire werge maa, ń zum wia, di pigzi ra helli wia, di aah siwii ra fir n hiŋ, ń na nunzuma ni n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzi, di helli gunla biinikpola ni gɛnaa n ɛɛ bambugri.

ref: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
text: Denii n na wii bɛl n chummɛ werge kaali siu, waabuu haaŋ la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ sidɛɛ. Nɔŋŋaa la uŋ nɔŋŋii la daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ asau di lawii. U nonee la uŋ kpawɛɛ korii la, daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ baŋ kpa yɔlɔzi vɔɔzii. Ka baal la wia n na par Kɔraawiizi, daŋ wer lɛɛ u hiŋ, ka u daŋ lau wichɔgɛɛri waa.

ref: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
text: A Nunzunni ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ɛɛh, n na wia naabuu tama, saŋa la minna nyiŋŋi n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzi la.

ref: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
text: N nyiŋŋi n pɛɛzaazi zɛɛzii, ka maa bɛl maa nawɛɛ. Baala kagboŋ biini, nɛkpannɛ n na ń wer tɔgzi. Ka haana waa biini, maa kpaŋkpaŋ maa nawɛɛ.

ref: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
text: Wii la maa miŋ helleere keŋ, Kɔraawiizi ta yaabuu, yaa wia chaani, ka yaa gil yaa wia du kpol.”

ref: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
text: Nɛr la n dɔɔ nunzuma bɛnnɛ ɔɔ zum wia zɛɛzi. Nunzumaa ɔɔ gil ba ra munzi, di gil ba nyɛmaa tuŋ. A tɔgzi koori

ref: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
text: Ɛɛ gunla koori n ŋɔ í ɛɛ, ka gilɛɛ hahzi ŋɔ nua ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
text: Koori daŋ wer ɛɛ wii la maa unna nyiŋŋi. Awia, chɔ lii u be, de waa wer.

ref: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
text: Koori dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa di ra ɛɛ wia, nɛr maa wàá wer diu mmɔri.

ref: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
text: Di i hanna hiŋ u widaulaa, wichɔgii maa wàá huuzii. Nɛr la n zum wia, u zum gunla ni saŋazi la un niŋ ɛɛ gunnɛ.

ref: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
text: Wiimaa ɛɛi dɔɔ u saŋaa ni ŋmɛnɛɛ la n dɛg u ɛɛi. Ka yaa zumaa waa kaŋ.

ref: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
text: Nɛr maa wàá wer vɛɛ siu gɛɛ di vɛɛ hɔpizii la un niŋ siu. Laal la yaa n wàá wer chɔ di lii u biinii guŋ, yaa wàá wer fini di lii u biini maa.

ref: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
text: Minna fɛ wia la maa banna ɛɛ durnya naa biini nfɛrɛ labuu n na annii maa. Durnya naa biini, baŋhina dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa, baŋhina ge ra di tɔɔrɔɔ dikuu ba fɔŋŋa hiŋ wia.

ref: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
text: Wibii maa, n na baŋ hugzi biinikpola hinaa, ka nɛra la n hug baa ka bir di ra kpo la, a chɔli baa bolzeŋ la himmaa biini baŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la. A maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛra hahzi di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaai? Ba ra ɛɛ gunnɛ, dikuu baŋ waa wichɔgɛɛra digna ra tɛrgi manamanaŋ wia.

ref: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
text: Wichɔgɛɛri daŋ wer ɛɛ wichɔgaa kalfa, ka haa du de ni miibɔɔ. Wibii maa, n zum gunla banna ŋɔu, “Di i ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, wiimaa daŋ kuari.

ref: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
text: A wàá kuari tɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra waa. Ba miibɔɔni ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ laalii. Ba daŋ siuzi di ba haa ɛɛ biipɔllaa, dikuu baŋ waa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ wia.”

ref: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
text: Ka annii ɛɛ wijagazii. Na wia la n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini. Saŋa bɛl, ba ɔɔ kpa nɛchɔgii dignitɛraarɛ di tɛr nɛnanii digni. Nɛchɔgii na nɛnanii kinturgaa. Annii maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ.

ref: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
text: Awia, wii la miŋ sɛɛwɛɛ lugɔ ya ra di yaa hinaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, sideŋŋa la bɛŋ yaa n dɔɔwɛ yaa de dui biinii, dii ni nyɔɔi, á tɛɛ yaa bɔsɔna. Yaa daŋ wer ɛɛ keŋ, di lii kuuhni la yaa n na kuuh, yaa de dui durnya naa biini naa.

ref: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
text: Di n haŋ wa ŋɔ n ɛɛ ania dɔɔ nunzuma, ń wer zum wia la n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini, n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ di i sogo hamuŋa ni hɔpizaa maa gba,

ref: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
text: ka hàá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa zɛɛ. Gunla maa hin niŋ aah siwii, ka hàá wer zum a zɛɛ maa. Nunzunna daŋ ŋɔ ba zummɔɔ, ka ba waa zummɛ.

ref: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
text: Annii maa wia, n fɛ nfɛrɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ka n nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii dɔɔ nunzunna ani nɛra la wia n deŋlee wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋa, haali ba nɛnɔŋŋaa ni ba nɛhahzi. Nɛr maa wàá wer zum wia la n du see di ra ba.

ref: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
text: Labakpannɛ nɛra maa dɔɔ, nɛra la wia n deŋlee, biinikpola hina, nɛnanaa, nɛchɔgaa, banla n waa doŋŋe, banla n doŋŋe, banla n na lizi mbusuzi ani banla n waa ra lizi. Nɛnanii waa nɛchɔgii bɔwɛɛ. Nɛr la n ɔɔ hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua waa unla n waa gunna ɛɛ bɔwɛɛ.

ref: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
text: Labakpannɛ ɔɔ huuzi ba maa. A wii naa waa deŋlee alugɔ wia la maa n na ɛɛ durnya naa biini. Nɛra de dui biini saŋa waa maa, wichɔgaa ni chuglaa su ba nfɛssi biine. Kakpaŋ, di ba siuzɔɔ.

ref: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
text: Ka nɛr la maa n du nyinee biini, u dɔɔ tamiirɛ. Nuahiŋ nyinii bɔ bunyiŋ siwii.

ref: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
text: Wibii maa, nyinee zummɔ lugɔ ba daŋ siuzi, ka lalaa waa, waa wiimaa zummɛ. Ba wàá ka na kinturgaa maa, ba wàá ka liizi ba wia maa.

ref: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
text: Ba nɔŋŋaa, ba hahzii ani ba winyiŋŋaa maanii siuwɛ. Ba waa kaa jaa durnya wiɛɛlaa bɛl maa biini.

ref: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
text: A di i diwee di dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di ra nyɔɔ i siŋ, í bɔra ra kazi. A guŋ waa chummɛ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
text: Dɔɔ bɔsɔna ni biinihuŋŋu saŋa maa.

ref: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
text: Gil i ni haaŋ la hiŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ la ra di iihinaa, i de dui saŋa naa Kɔraawiizi n tɛi, waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ naa biini. A di i hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, tɔna la maa hin niŋ na lii i kuuhni biinii guŋ.

ref: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
text: Wii la maa hinna ɛɛ, aah siwii di ra ɛɛu, dikuubɛɛwiai wiɛɛlii gɛɛ nfɛrɛ fɛi gɛɛ wia zɛɛ zumaa gɛɛ nunzuma waa hoo lalaa bol. Denii i ra la la.

ref: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
text: N kaa na wikpaŋ bɛl durnya naa biini. Banla n gbaŋŋɛ di ra chɔ lɛi ɔɔ di, banla n dɔɔ bampirii ge lɛi ɔɔ wer lɔ laal di kpegli ba dɔma. Nunzunna ge waa ɔɔ wer ba hum di na kuna di. Banla n dɔɔ nfɛrɛ ge lɛi ɔɔ ɛɛ dɔɔna. Banla n wer wiɛɛlaa ge lɛi ɔɔ ra na nabɔmuu. Ka nyuchɔgii ɔɔ huuzi nɛr maanii.

ref: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
text: Hàá wer zum i hɔpizii. Gunla sidɛɛ n ɔɔ lau zumbee a pirguu la, gɛɛ sɔzaa n ɔɔ lau nyinni gunla, gunnɛ wichɔgaa ɔɔ pirgi yaa saŋa la yaa n waa gunna fɛ. Nunzumaa bɔ gɛnaa

ref: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
text: Denii n kaa na wii bɛl, gunla durnya naa hina n na fɛ nunzuma wia.

ref: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
text: Boljiga bɛllɛ faa du de, u nɛra waa kpil. Koorizeŋ bɛl n kpekke faa vɔɔ laal di wa fɔɔu, ú purgi u koŋlaa ka zuu u biini.

ref: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
text: Nɛbɛl faa du u biini, di ɛɛ nyaari, ka faa dɔɔ nunzuma, di lɛɛ a bol hina. Ka nɛr maa faa waa u wia liizee.

ref: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
text: Saŋa maa, aŋ ŋɔu lugɔ nunzumaa bɔ fɔŋŋa, ka nɛr maa waa ɔɔ ra fɛ nyaara wia lugɔ ba ɛɛ nunzunnaa, di ra nuu ba wiŋɔɔlaa.

ref: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
text: Hinna nuu nunzunni wiŋɔɔlaa n du bɔɔiih, aabuu bɔ gɛnaa koori n na pogzi.

ref: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
text: Nunzuma wiɛɛlaa ra ɛɛ winanaarɛ werge kaali dɔŋkuna, ka wichɔgɛɛri kpaŋkpaŋ daŋ wer chɔgi winaŋkpila.

ref: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
text: Gunla nakɛɛhsiwaa n ɔɔ gil tulaale ra hɛhzi la, gunnɛ gɛnaa tama maa, ɔɔ wer chɔgi nunzuma la n kannɛ werge.

ref: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
text: Nunzunna hotte wideŋlaa ɛɛi, gɛnaa ge hotte gɛnni wiɛɛlaa.

ref: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
text: Di ba wa chem hɔɔhra ni ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba ɔɔ na ba gɛnaarɛ, ba wiɛɛlaa ɔɔ giluu nɛr maa zum lugɔ ba ɛɛ gɛnaarɛ.

ref: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
text: Di i koori wa nyɛg i ni, ka i gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ u humaa. Di i lau i hiŋ, u daŋ wer gil i wichɔgaa tɛi.

ref: Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair:
text: Wichɔgii bɛl miŋ kaa na durnya naa biinii keŋ, kooraa ra ɛɛ a wii naa.

ref: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
text: Gɛnaarɛ ba ɔɔ tɛɛ nabɔmuu, ka gil dɔɔna.

ref: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
text: N na yoma n tinni zagra, ka nabɔnzenaa ra vol lugɔ yoma.

ref: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
text: Di i ki bɔɔ, i daŋ wer chol u biini. Di i ra purgi koŋlii, hɛrikuŋ daŋ wer dumii.

ref: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
text: Di i ra hum bia purgaa bɔr, bia daŋ dui pira. Di i ra pergi daazi, i daŋ wer na pira.

ref: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
text: Di i kpaŋfɔ waa di, i vɛɛ u sazaa ka kpogluu ra hum, i daŋ kuuh werge. Nunzuma wiarɛ hiŋ felee lauri i wiɛɛlaa dau.

ref: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
text: Tɔna maa waa hoo, hiŋ ŋɔ i helli hɛrikuŋ pɛssaa, ka u feli dumii.

ref: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
text: Nunzunna wiŋɔɔlaa ɔɔ giluu ba ra tɔgzi baa, ka gɛnaa waa wiŋɔɔlaa ra chɔgi baabuu.

ref: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
text: Gɛnni wiŋɔzii ba ɔɔ kpa faari, a tuna maa, a birgi chugla himmaa.

ref: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
text: Gɛnii waa wia ŋɔwɛɛ ra kuuh. Nɛr maa waa zum wii la n na ba, nɛr maa ge wàá wer bagli yaa, wii la n niŋ ɛɛ yaa siu har.

ref: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
text: Nɛr la n gɛnnɛ werge, waa u dia ŋmɛnɛɛ zummɛɛ, niŋ chɔgi u hiŋ ni humkpega.

ref: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
text: Di hɛri maa koori wa ɛɛ biipɔllii, u nabɔnzi ra di diuzenaa hamuŋa maa, a hɛri hina du tɔɔrɔɔ biinii.

ref: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
text: Di nɛr dɔɔ yaara werge, wàá wer magzi u sal, u daŋ lul guŋŋ di wa chol.

ref: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
text: Hɔpizizeŋ dii ra tɛibuu bɔsɔna, siŋ gil i bɔra ra kazi, ka hàá wer na bɛl maa di haa kebii dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
text: Gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ koori wia i biini gba, gɛɛ di wàá ŋɔ dɔɔŋ wia i chɔɔribɔr. Aŋhinabe, zumbee daŋ ga baglaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
text: Kpa i kebee ra hum huma hɛrdumazi biini, ŋmɛnɛbɛl i daŋ na tɔna.

ref: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
text: Kpa i kebee du kuŋkpila ani bɔkpila biine. Haa zum hɔpizii la nyuchɔgii n niŋ huuzii durnya naa biini.

ref: Rain clouds always bring rain; trees always stay wherever they fall.
text: Bɔr la maa paga daa n niŋ chol, denii ú chɔɔ. Di baama wa biroo ni donii, dooŋ daŋ ba.

ref: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
text: Di i ra kpaŋ ŋɔ bɔr wa du wer, hàá duu kuna, hàá kumaa ge.

ref: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
text: Gunla hiŋ waa peu ŋmɛnɛɛ zummɛ, gɛɛ gunla biifula n ɛɛwɛ di ra hel u maa hia biini la, gunnɛ hàá wer zum Kɔraawiizi wiɛɛlaa, unla n ta kummaa la.

ref: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
text: A duu kuna chɔɔzi ni duana maa. Hàá wer zum di a maa daŋ lii nɛnnɛ gɛɛ aŋhina daŋ lii kaali aŋhina.

ref: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
text: Bɔchaaŋ wessoo, di ra par siwee.

ref: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
text: Gil i bɔra sɔɔni i de dui saŋa. Gunla hin niŋ du de di birgi mag, ka i ra liizi lugɔ siurɛ í siu di birgi werge. Tamii maa waa hoo.

ref: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
text: Biipɔllaa, ií ra di ii pɔlaa tɔna. Ií gil ii bɔra ɔɔ sɔɔni ia, ii pɔlaa saŋa. Ií ra ɛɛ wia la iinna nyiŋŋi, di ra hiŋ ii bampiree wilaulaa. Ka ií ra liizi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ di ii wiɛɛlaa, maa seriya.

ref: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil wiimaa ra tir ia gɛɛ di gil ii bɔra ra wii. A wàá birgi ka ii pɔlaa saŋa tuŋ.

ref: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
