ref: The king's power reaches from the city of Zoan as far south as Hanes.
text: Haali baŋ hum nabɔnzenaa ba la bolzenaa Zoan ni Hanɛs gba,

ref: But Egypt can't protect you, and to trust that nation is useless and foolish.”
text: ka ba maa daŋ wa di hiihzi dikuu Ijip hina n wàá wer hiini baa tama maa wia. Ba wàá dɔɔ tɔna maa tɛɛ baa, hiihzii ba di.”

ref: This is a message about the animals of the Southern Desert: “You people carry treasures on donkeys and camels. You travel to a feeble nation through a troublesome desert filled with lions and flying fiery dragons.
text: Amaniye la miŋ nuuwɛ lii Kɔraawiizi be, u ra bagli wiifurii nodig wiikakag hɛribɔduma sela wiarɛ keŋ, “Nabɔnzenaa la baŋ hummɛ Ijip hɛri la ra voluu di ra la, a ra nuu baa. Hɛribɔduma labuu ba ga, bɔr la bunyinzi, hɛrikunchɔgaa ani nyugzenzenaa n duwɛɛ. Ba kauzi ni nyugmazi chi daama kuna werge maa, bá ga tɛɛ Ijip hɛri koorizeŋ ú hiini baa. Ka pɛɛrɛ, ba wàá na hiinaa maa u be.

ref: Egypt can't help you! That's why I call that nation a helpless monster.” Israel Refuses To Listen
text: Ijip hɛri la waa hiinaa maa dɔɔwɛ. Awia, n na yiruubuu ‘Nyugzenzeŋ la n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ.’ ”

ref: The Lord told me to write down his message for his people, so that it would be there forever.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “La ga sɛbi Ijip hɛri wia naa dau bipɛntɛŋ ni, di sɛbaa dau hɔŋ ge ni, á ɛɛ daansɛɛ tɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ haa wa du de, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: They have turned against the Lord and can't be trusted. They have refused his teaching
text: N biizi naa ɛɛ dignikpega ni karkannaa. Biizi la n waa nyiŋŋi bá nuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baglaa.

ref: and have said to his messengers and prophets: Don't tell us what God has shown you and don't preach the truth. Just say what we want to hear, even if it's false.
text: Ba ŋɔ n dɔgtɛɛzi be, ‘Ií gilɛɛ kaa ra na wia lugɔ deeza biini, di gilɛɛ kaa bagli wibii ŋmɛnizi di ra tɛɛ yaa. Ií ra ŋɔ wia la n na par yaa, di gilɛɛ di wibii ra tɛɛ yaa.

ref: Stop telling us what God has said! We don't want to hear any more about the holy One of Israel.
text: Ií gilɛɛ teŋ yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ, di gilɛɛ kaa kpa Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii wia huuzi yaa.’ ”

ref: Now this is the answer of the holy One of Israel: “You rejected my message, and you trust in violence and lies.
text: Awia, kenne Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔ, “Dikuu iiŋ vɛɛ gunla miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ naa, ka kpa ii tamii maa du nɛsunnaa ni kara ni la wia,

ref: This sin is like a crack that makes a high wall quickly crumble
text: ii wichɔgii naa daŋ birgi tɔɔrɔɔ tɛɛ ia, alugɔ koŋlii n la chiŋ, di peri chi, di ra nyiŋŋi u chol, di wa chol kakpaŋ, birim!

ref: and shatter like a crushed bowl. There's not a piece left big enough to carry hot coals or to dip out water.” Trust the Lord
text: Di u wa chollo, u daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ vii baŋ vigzee, u ga chol di ŋmuuri la, u keŋlii gba wàá ka wer buu niŋ gɛɛ di kaa wer ɛɛ nii gba.”

ref: The holy Lord God of Israel had told all of you, “I will keep you safe if you turn back to me and calm down. I will make you strong if you quietly trust me.” Then you stubbornly
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la, di ɛɛ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií bir ba n be wa heezi. Anniibuu niŋ gil ii na lɛɛi. Ií gil ii bampiree sɔɔni di yardiŋ. Anniibuu niŋ gil ii dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.

ref: As few as five of them, or even one, will be enough to chase a thousand of you. Finally, all that will be left will be a few survivors as lonely as a flag pole on a barren hill. The Lord Will Show Mercy
text: Ba laallɔɔra kpaŋkpaŋ daŋ gil ii nɛra kagboŋ chɔ, banue ge gil ii maa chɔ, ka ii jaa chɔ ka ka tuuta daajaŋ a bizeŋ nyuu.”

ref: The Lord God is waiting to show how kind he is and to have pity on you. The Lord always does right; he blesses those who trust him.
text: Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi haa ra kpaŋ iabuu, ú ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ ia, di ɛɛ sirya ú na ii sinyɛna. U ɛɛ wibii hinnɛ saŋa maa. Banla maa n na kpaŋuu lugɔ ú wa hiini baa, nuu sumaa.

ref: People of Jerusalem, you don't need to cry anymore. The Lord is kind, and as soon as he hears your cries for help, he will come.
text: Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, ii banla n soge Jɛrusalɛm, ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka wii. Wibii maa, di ii wiiwo yir Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ hiini ia. Di u haŋ wa nuu ii wiisuŋŋaa, u daŋ ɔɔ sɛɛ kakpaŋ.

ref: The Lord has given you trouble and sorrow as your food and drink. But now you will again see the Lord, your teacher, and he will guide you.
text: Haali Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ tɔɔrɔɔ birgi ii diwee, biinichɔg ge birgi ii niinyɔɔlii la gba, ka u himmaa daŋ bagli ia, ii wàá ka nyiŋŋi u bɔr.

ref: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice saying, “This is the road! Now follow it.”
text: Di ii wa leu ŋmɛnɛɛ, ii daŋ nuu loobii bɛl ii harbɔɔ n na ŋɔ, “A ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ keŋ. Ií hiŋuu di ra la!”

ref: Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold like garbage; you will throw them away like filthy rags.
text: Denii ii chɔgi ii vuga baŋ kuarɛɛ, di kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa tɔa la, di kpaa ha lugɔ haaŋ doŋa wɛjɛ, ka ŋɔ, “Ií kaali de!”

ref: The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi jaa gil dooŋ ba, saŋa la iin niŋ waa duu kuna, di gil a lii du binanaa, di lɛɛ nɛnnɛ di wazi, ii sela gba na kooriinanaa di ra di a kipar.

ref: Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
text: Nabala ni kauzi n na par ii kooni la daŋ na diunanaa baŋ kuarɛɛ nɛnnɛ, di ra di.

ref: On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains.
text: Saŋa la ban niŋ wa kpu ii dɔma werge, ba diikpega la n jaŋŋɛ la chiŋ, chogli la, niiri danna bul bizenaa ni giŋgimee maa nyuuni.

ref: Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once. Assyria Will Be Punished
text: Baagu daŋ bir chaani alugɔ wiizi, wiizi ge chaanaa la bir ɛɛ u guŋ dɔŋ buniidaanɛɛ. A saŋaa Kɔraawiizi jaa vɔɔzi u nɛra bɔra uŋ gillɛ a kuugi la, di chaa baa.

ref: The Lord is coming from far away with his fiery anger and thick clouds of smoke. His angry words flame up like a destructive fire;
text: Ií na! Kɔraawiizi Sɔŋ lii bɔɔnɛɛrɛ di ra ba. U baaŋ ra fuuh werge maa, nyɔɔzi ra lii di tɔ bɔr maa kulululu. Baaŋfuuih wiŋɔzii u ra ŋɔ, u nuuzuŋŋi ɛɛ lugɔ ninlau.

ref: he breathes out a flood that comes up to the neck. He sifts the nations and destroys them. Then he puts a bridle in every foreigner's mouth and leads them to doom.
text: U heeza dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa lugɔ gɔnzeŋ n suwee, di hel baŋaa. U zigli a durnya hɛssi maanii, ú chɔgaa, di kpa kabargazi du a hɛssi nɛra nuuzi, di tɛrgi baa ra la bá ga leu.

ref: The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
text: Denii ii jaa yir yira lugɔ baŋ ɔɔ ra yir yira hamuŋa ni, di ra di hɔpizizenaa la. Ií bɔra daŋ sɔɔni lugɔ saŋa la tiitorii huuhra n du nɛra di ra la Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ la nyuu, Izrɛl hina Bizeŋ la.

ref: The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nɛra nuu u zenni loobii, di gil ba na gunla uŋ lalli u banonii baaŋ ni, di kpa ninlau n na di kuna werge, baama n na pogzi, nazaa ani dobizenaa di tuu ra ba.

ref: When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ ŋɔ wikpaŋ di gil Asiiria hina maa ŋmuuri. U daŋ kpa u kooridaŋkpala di lɔ baa.

ref: He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
text: Too, saŋa maa, di u wa lalli u daŋkpala yag baa, di tɛr ba digna la, u nɛra danna yir yirsuma, di ra lɔ kemzi, di ra yigzi lɔŋgɔma. Gunnɛ ú ɛɛ di lɔ Asiiria hina laal, ni u banonii.

ref: Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
text: U teŋ kuari bɔttɛ birgi, ú fuuh Asiiria koorizeŋ. Ba kiubuu, u du luŋ di kaa du war jaa, bá du daazi de werge, Kɔraawiizi heeza n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ jilbi ni ninlau gil a ra lau zagzagzag.

ref: You are in for trouble if you go to Egypt for help, or if you depend on an army of chariots or a powerful cavalry. Instead you should depend on and trust the holy Lord God of Israel.
text: Wia daŋ huuzi banla n ɔɔ ra la Ijip hɛri, di gaa nyiŋŋi hiinaa, banla n dɛlli zagra, banla n yardi laal torkokpila ni ba zagtinna la n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la. Ba waa hiinaa ra nyiŋŋi Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii be, gɛɛ di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú hiini baa.

ref: The Lord isn't stupid! He does what he promises, and he can bring doom. If you are cruel yourself, or help those who are evil, you will be destroyed.
text: Waabuu dɔɔ nunzuma, u daŋ wer gil hɛhchɔg chol, gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, gunnɛ ú ɛɛ. U daŋ hau biinikpola hina ni, di hau banla n na hiini wichɔgɛɛra ni.

ref: The Egyptians are mere humans. They aren't God. Their horses are made of flesh; they can't live forever. When the Lord shows his power, he will destroy the Egyptians and all who depend on them. Together they will fall.
text: Newea lɛi Ijip hinaa? Ba waa Kɔraawiizi ɛɛwɛ. Ba zagra ɛɛ ola bɛnnɛ, a waa dunzi ɛɛwɛ. Di Kɔraawiizi haŋ wa tɛr u nonii, unla n na hiini nɛra, daŋ jiŋli, unla ge baŋ hiinee, daŋ chol, ba maa kpau siu.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said to me, “I will roar and attack like a fearless lion not frightened by the shouts of shepherds trying to protect their sheep. That's how I will come down and fight on Mount Zion.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Aizaaya be, “Di bunyiŋ gɛɛ u biipɔl lau peezi, u baga waa hoo penɔɔna pogzaa be, haali di ba kpillɔ gunla maa di ra kɔɔ werge gba, ka u ɔɔ chɔɔu di ra di u kuŋ. Guŋ himmaanii niŋ wa ɛɛ saŋa la Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la n niŋ ba wa naa kalu, Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will protect Jerusalem like a mother bird circling over her nest.” Come Back to the Lord
text: Gunla zumbee n ɔɔ zaah ra bar u daŋ, di ra du u biizi tau la, gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la wa zaah ra bar Jɛrusalɛm, di ra du u tau, di lɛɛu u dɔma be.”

ref: People of Israel, come back! You have completely turned from the Lord.
text: Hoi, Izrɛl hina, haali iiŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la gba, ka ii bir ba u be.

ref: The time is coming when you will throw away your idols of silver and gold, made by your sinful hands.
text: A saŋa, ii maa daŋ vɛɛ saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa vuga la iiŋ kpa nonee kuari, guŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa la.

ref: The Assyrians will be killed, but not by the swords of humans. Their young men will try to escape, but they will be captured and forced into slavery.
text: Asiiria hina daŋ tuŋ laal biini, ka a wàá lugɔ neweare niŋ kpu baa. Akai! Kɔraawiizi tokobii niŋ kpu baa, ba daŋ chɔ lii laal biini, bá lauri ba biipɔllaa, di gil ba gaa hum humkpega.

ref: Their fortress will fall when terror strikes; their army officers will be frightened and run from the battle. This is what the Lord has said, the Lord whose fiery furnace is built on Mount Zion.
text: Ɔnsii werge daŋ lau ba koorizeŋ, ú chɔ, ɔnsii kaa lau ba laallɔɔra nabɔnzi ge, bá gil tuutazi ka chɔ. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ, waabuu ba ra jaami Jɛrusalɛm la, u niŋ ra lau de, mbusuzi lizaa wia.

ref: They will be a place of safety from stormy winds, a stream in the desert, and a rock that gives shade from the heat of the sun.
text: Bɛl maa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ lɔɔ di tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, di pechɔgii maa haŋ wa ta ba ni ba chɔ ga zuu. Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ gɔŋa n na pal hɛribɔduma la dooŋ n waa ba, gɛɛ bizenzeŋ n na tɔ baa bɔsɔŋ hɛrhilii biini.

ref: Then everyone who has eyes will open them and see, and those who have ears will pay attention.
text: Denii a nɛra wàá ka tɔɔgi ba siwee. Ba daŋ pilli siwee, di keŋŋi digna ge nuu wia,

ref: All who are impatient will take time to think; everyone who stutters will talk clearly.
text: di dɔɔ kanyitti di ra nuu wia, di zum a zɛɛ. Banla ge n ɔɔ ra mɛuli wàá kaa ra mɛuli, ka jaa ra ŋɔ wia a ra chaani.

ref: Fools will no longer be highly respected, and crooks won't be given positions of honor.
text: Nɛra wàá kaa ra tɔgzi gɛnaa, ba wàá kaa ra tɔgzi karkanna ge.

ref: Fools talk foolishness. They always make plans to do sinful things, to lie about the Lord, to let the hungry starve, and to keep water from those who are thirsty.
text: Gɛnii ɔɔ ra ŋɔ gɛnni wiarɛ, di dɔɔ nfɛrɛchɔgaa werge. Waa ɔɔ ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnizi, ka ra bagli nɛra wia la n waa deŋlee Kɔraawiizi hiŋaa biini. Waa ɔɔ sɛɛ tɛɛ banla lɔzi n na kpu diwee, bá di, waa ɔɔ tɛɛ banla niinyɔgzi n na kpu nii, bá nyɔɔ.

ref: Cruel people tell lies— they do evil things, and make cruel plans to destroy the poor and needy, even when they beg for justice.
text: Karkanni ni u kara maa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. U ɔɔ suahzuu di ta jina dí na gunla un niŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di kanni kara chɔgi nyaara, haali di ba hor summɔ gba.

ref: But helpful people can always be trusted to make helpful plans. Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
text: Ama, girme hiŋwaa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu gunla un niŋ ɛɛu, a hiini nɛra, di lau guŋ wiɛɛlaa nɛnnɛ. Jɛrusalɛm haana wia

ref: You may not have worries now, but in about a year, the grape harvest will fail, and you will tremble.
text: Di bina ni tama wa jaawɔ, ii banla wiimaa n waa ia titte la siwii daŋ jaa aah, ii bɔra ra sa. Ií grepuzi daazi daŋ vɛɛ nɔnaa, ii wàá naa tɔrgi.

ref: Slap your breasts in sorrow because of what happened to the fruitful fields and vineyards,
text: Ií lɔ ii bampiree ni biinichɔg di ra wii, dikuu ii koonanaa ni daazi la n faa ra nɔŋ werge

ref: The palace will be deserted, the crowded city empty. Fortresses and towers will forever become playgrounds for wild donkeys and pastures for sheep. God's Spirit Makes the Difference
text: Koori diahina maa daŋ chɔ ka ka u diikpeg, bolzeŋ la nɛra n faa su u biini la, ba maa daŋ chɔ ka giluu. Diikpeg ni diijaŋ la n la chiŋ maa, daŋ birgi diŋgela di hanna la. Bol sela maa jaa ra zuu de di ra di a hinaa, di ra di kooree.

ref: Honesty and justice will prosper there,
text: Wibii daŋ du hɛribɔduma biini, wideŋlaa du hɛrsum la biini.

ref: You, the Lord's people, will live in peace, calm and secure,
text: N nɛra daŋ jaa so ni bɔsɔna, di du bɔɔiih bɔr la maa baŋ duwɛɛ, wichɔgii maa wàá ka huuzi baa.

ref: even if hailstones flatten forests and cities.
text: Haali dobizenaa n niŋ wa chɔgi kɔr la, bolzeŋ la ge maa puri chol,

ref: You will have God's blessing, as you plant your crops beside streams, while your donkeys and cattle roam freely about.
text: ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ haa kissi u nɛra werge maa. Ba daŋ ɔɔ duu ba kuna gɔŋa kɛraa, ba nauna ni kauzi ge gaagi di ra di a kipar.

ref: You defeated my people. Now you're in for trouble! You've never been destroyed, but you will be destroyed; you've never been betrayed, but you will be betrayed. When you have finished destroying and betraying, you will be destroyed and betrayed in return.
text: Wia daŋ huuzi hinla n na kpu nɛra, ka ba waa hiŋwaa kpuwɛɛ! Wia daŋ huuzi hinla n na ɛɛ sɔsɔgɔ, ka nɛra haa waa hiŋwaa ɛɛwɛ sɔsɔgɔ! Di i haŋ wa gil nɛra kpui, ba daŋ jaa kpui. Di i haŋ wa gil sɔsɔgɔ ɛɛi, ba daŋ jaa ɛɛ i ge sɔsɔgɔ!

ref: Please, Lord, be kind to us! We depend on you. Make us strong each morning, and come to save us when we are in trouble.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, suŋ yaa ni di hiini yaa! Yaa ra binni i siweere. Tɛɛ yaa fɔŋŋa hɔpizibii maa, di ra lɛɛ yaa tɔɔrɔɔ saŋa.

ref: We attack our enemies like swarms of locusts; we take everything that belongs to them.
text: Hɛssi nɛra, nɛra daŋ jaa paagi i kuna maa nyaamm alugɔ lotorozi n ɔɔ tuŋ pattikuna gunla.

ref: You, Lord, are above all others, and you live in the heavens. You have brought justice and fairness to Jerusalem;
text: Kɔraawiizi zenni kaali kummaa, awia, u duuribɔttɛ chiŋ. U daŋ gil wibii ni wideŋlaa su bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm werge maa.

ref: you are the foundation on which we stand today. You always save us and give true wisdom and knowledge. Nothing means more to us than obeying you. The Lord Will Do Something
text: Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ ii fɔŋŋa a saŋa. U danna lɛɛ ia werge maa, di ra tɛɛ ia sichaana ani nunzuma ge werge. U ɔmaarɛ niŋ ɛɛ ii wizeŋ.

ref: Listen! Our bravest soldiers are running through the streets, screaming for help. Our messengers hoped for peace, but came home crying.
text: Ií na! Ba baala la n dɔɔ bampiree werge ra wiiu, ba bola ŋmɛnizenaa biine. Nabɔnzi la baŋ hummɛ lugɔ ba ga kuari wia ra wiiu werge maa ni biinichɔg.

ref: No one travels anymore; every road is empty. Treaties are broken, and no respect is shown to any who keep promises.
text: Ŋmɛnizenaa maanii ba gil ta, nɛr maa waa kaa ra volaa. Nɛra ra chɔgi nuukpaŋ la ba ni nɛra n ɛɛwɛ, di jaa ra gbɛlli ba jinazi baŋ tawɛɛ, ba waa kaa ra tɔgzi nɛr maa.

ref: Fields are dry and barren; Mount Lebanon wilts with shame. Sharon Valley is a desert; the forests of Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
text: A hɛri maanii chɔɔ pɛɛ di birgi diŋgela. Lɛbanɔn hɛri kɔr daazi maanii hillɛ, Sarɔn gba hɛrnanaa la maanii jaa birgi hɛribɔdumazi. Basan ni Bizeŋ Kamɛl daakpega maa paŋhoori wattɔɔ.

ref: But the Lord says, “Now I will do something and be greatly praised.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Filaŋkeŋ n daŋ izi di bagli n zenni la n kaali kummaa zenni la.

ref: Your deeds are straw that will be set on fire by your very own breath.
text: Wia la iiŋ ta jina ii ɛɛ, ani anla iinna ɛɛ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ zɔga. Ii himmaa heeza daŋ birgi ninlau di fuuh ia.

ref: You will be burned to ashes like thorns in a fire.
text: Hɛssi hina daŋ fuuh nyaamm, hɔɔhri bɛŋ ka, alugɔ sɔɔhri baŋ ŋmɛnnɛɛ di du niŋ a ra lau zagzagzag la.

ref: Everyone, both far and near, come look at what I have done. See my mighty power!” Punishment and Rewards
text: Ii banla n du bɔɔnɛɛ, ií ra nuu gunla miŋ ɛɛwɛ! Ii banla ge n duglɛɛ, ií ra tɔgzi n fɔŋŋa la!”

ref: But there will be rewards for those who live right and tell the truth, for those who refuse to take money by force or accept bribes, for all who hate murder and violent crimes.
text: Nɛr la n niŋ wer du denii unla wia n deŋlee, u ra di wibii, waa nɛra ra fini di ra na tɔna, waa kuna ra lɛɛ nɛra be, waa sɛɛwɛ ra tɛɛ nɛra la n ɔɔ ra ta jina bá ga kpu nɛr, di ɔɔ tɔ u siwee ú gilɛɛ wa na wia la n niŋ lul wichɔgaa.

ref: They will live in a fortress high on a rocky cliff, where they will have food and plenty of water. The Lord Is Our King
text: Wiimaa wàá wer ɛɛ a hindee u sognibɔr. De ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ diikpeg bɛl n du giŋgimii nyuu. Ba daŋ tɛu diwee ú di, u niinyɔɔlii gba wàá tuŋ maa.

ref: With your own eyes you will see the glorious King; you will see his kingdom reaching far and wide.
text: Ii daŋ wa na koori la wessi werge, di kaa na hɛri ge n chɔɔwɛ yɛlɛlɛlɛ kaali.

ref: You will never again have to see the proud people who spoke a strange and foreign language you could not understand.
text: Ii wàá ka na a nɛkpoŋlaa la maa. Ba wàá ka mɔɔ ba mɔɔri la iiŋ waa nuu la tɛɛ ia ii nua huhzi.

ref: Look to Mount Zion where we celebrate our religious festivals. You will see Jerusalem, secure as a tent with pegs that cannot be pulled up and fastened with ropes that can never be broken.
text: Ii daŋ binni Jɛrusalɛm, bolzeŋ la yaa n na di yaa hɔpizizenaa u biini la, di na lugɔ u ɛɛ bolzeŋ la nɛra du u biinii ni bampirsɔna. U daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ tanti dia la baŋ baŋŋɛ, waa panzaa dɔɔwɛ, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá panzi u daasiraa gɛɛ di chaahzi u ŋmɛnni.

ref: The Lord is our judge and our ruler; the Lord is our king and will keep us safe.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ yaa seriya diirii, di ɛɛ yaa gbɔgtɛɛri, di ɛɛ yaa koori, waabuu niŋ lɛɛ yaa.

ref: But your nation is a ship with its rigging loose, its mast shaky, and its sail not spread. Someday even you that are lame will take everything you want from your enemies.
text: Yaa dɔma muugbessi pergoore, di kuugi, Daazi la n lauri ba muugbessi wɛjɛzi, peu ra ta a ni a ra vol la kuugoore, a wɛjɛzi hiŋ sag de yɔgɔyɔgɔ, a wàá wer yaa. Kɔraawiizi nɛra daŋ bɔnni ba dɔma daama la. Haali gbɛraa gba daŋ na ba hora!

ref: The Lord will forgive your sins, and none of you will say, “I feel sick.”
text: Nɛra la maa n du Bolzeŋ Ziɔn ŋmɛnɛ wàá ka ŋɔ ba bɔra ra wii baabuu. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: The Lord is terribly angry with the nations; he has condemned them to be slaughtered.
text: Kɔraawiizi izoore ni baaŋ, ú chɔgi hɛssi hina maa. U baaŋ hiŋ na fuuh ba laallɔɔra maa ninɛɛ. U daŋ chɔgi ba maa nyaamm, di gil ba kpuuzi ba maa.

ref: Their dead bodies will be left to rot and stink; their blood will flow down the mountains.
text: Ba daŋ kpa ba lalaa haazi bɔr maa, ba sɔɔh tɔ a hɛri maa puihpuihpuih, ba challi ra pal bizenaa la nyuuni.

ref: Each star will disappear— the sky will roll up like a scroll. Everything in the sky will dry up and wilt like leaves on a vine or fruit on a tree. Trouble for Edom
text: Chinchiŋwilaa maa n du chiŋ daŋ ŋmɛɛri, chiŋ ge piŋŋi alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ piŋŋi hɔnsɛbii la. Chinchiŋwilaa maa daŋ chogli lugɔ grepu daa paŋhoori n ɔɔ war gunla. Lugɔ fig nɔŋhɛɛlaa n ɔɔ chogli gunla.

ref: After the sword of the Lord has done what it wants to the skies above, it will come down on Edom, the nation that the Lord has doomed for destruction.
text: Di n tokobi la wa hum u huma tuŋ chiŋ, u daŋ jaa tuu Ɛdɔm hina la miŋ di ba chɔgaa seriya tuŋ la ni.

ref: The sword of the Lord is covered with blood from lambs and goats, together with fat from kidneys of rams. This is because the Lord will slaughter many people and make a sacrifice of them in the city of Bozrah and everywhere else in Edom.
text: Kɔraawiizi tokobi la maa ɛɛ challɛ, nuuri faa u maa. Peballi, buuna chal ani pebala siga nuurii faau la. Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ mbusu lizaarɛ bolzeŋ Bɔzra. U daŋ kpu sekpila Ɛdɔm hɛri.

ref: Edom's leaders are wild oxen. They are powerful bulls, but they will die with the others. Their country will be soaked with their own blood, and its soil made fertile with their own fat.
text: A nɛra nɛkpega n lugɔ nabalkpoŋlaa, naballi ani nabalzenaa maa daŋ siu. Chal danna pal ba hɛri maa, a nuuri ge gil nyɔɔ wàá ka wer izi de.

ref: The Lord has chosen the year and the day, when he will take revenge and come to Zion's defense.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi lizi a saŋaa, ú tɛr ba digna, di turgi wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina la kim, gunna bagli lugɔ Jɛrusalɛm hor summɔɔ.

text: De daŋ ɛɛ kukuballi ni duglizi duuribɔr, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil Ɛdɔm hɛri chɔɔ pɛɛ gunla hɛri n faa waa duula dɔɔwɛ, di chɔɔ woo la.

ref: Edom will be called “Kingdom of Nothing.” Its rulers will also be nothing.
text: Koori wàá du de di ra binni a hɛri, ba sitɔɔra maa tuŋ.

ref: Its palaces and fortresses will be covered with thorns; only wolves and ostriches will make their home there.
text: Sɔɔhri ni paŋhoori la n dɔɔ sɔɔhri daŋ lii ba diikpega ni ba bolkpega maa biine, de jaa birgi hohobiazi ni kukuballi duuribɔr.

ref: Wildcats and hyenas will hunt together, demons will scream to demons, and creatures of the night will live among the ruins.

ref: Owls will nest there to raise their young among its shadows, while families of vultures circle around.
text: Kikiuzi du a daŋa de, di he hala, di teezaa di yaa a keeri tɔ a biifulli ni. Kɔlli ge ɔɔ chaali de, bɛl maa ni u cheeŋ.

ref: In The Book of the Lord you can search and find where it is written, “The Lord brought together all of his creatures by the power of his Spirit. Not one is missing.”
text: Binni Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, di karmi gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, A sela ni a zumbizi naa maanii niŋ du de, bɛl maa ni u cheeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi himmaanii dau guŋ, u Duma genii niŋ chaalaa ba dɔŋa be.

ref: The Lord has decided where they each should live; they will be there forever, generation after generation.
text: U himmaanii mɛgzi a sela duuribɔr tɛɛa, de birgi a zuuribɔr á du de di hanna la, saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: Thirsty deserts will be glad; barren lands will celebrate and blossom with flowers.
text: Bɔsɔna daŋ du hɛribɔduma ni hɛri la n hillɛ pergi biine, á fur kooree, daazi fii di du wer.

ref: Deserts will bloom everywhere and sing joyful songs. They will be as majestic as Mount Lebanon, as glorious as Mount Carmel or Sharon Valley. Everyone will see the wonderful splendor of the Lord our God. God Changes Everything *
text: Hɛribɔduma ra yir yira di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna. U daŋ du wer lugɔ Lɛbanɔn bizenaa, di du sum alugɔ Kamɛl ni Sarɔn hɛssi. Nɛr maa daŋ na Kɔraawiizi girme, u zenni ni u fɔŋŋa.

ref: Here is a message for all who are weak, trembling, and worried:
text: Ií du nɛra la bɔra n huahwɛ, bɔkpega, bá wer chi nɛnnɛ.

ref: “Cheer up! Don't be afraid. Your God is coming to punish your enemies. God will take revenge on them and rescue you.”
text: Ií ŋɔ tɛɛ banla maa bɔra n huahwɛ, ɔnsii lau baa la, “Ií chiiri zɛɛ, di gilɛɛ ra ɔm! Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la daŋ ba di wa tɛr ii dɔma digna di turgi ba wichɔgaa kim, ka lɛɛ ia.”

ref: Scorching sand will turn into a lake, and thirsty ground will flow with fountains. Grass will grow in deserts, where packs of wild dogs once made their home. God's Sacred Highway
text: Bɔr la wiizi n lɔwɛɛ u hil, daŋ birgi pol, hɛssi la n nyaa nii la maa ge furgi bulli, bɔra la hohobiazi n faa ra chɔɔ la fur kooree la n ɔɔ ra lii nii bɔr.

ref: A good road will be there, and it will be named “God's Sacred Highway.” It will be for God's people; no one unfit to worship God will walk on that road. And no fools can travel on that highway.
text: Ŋmɛnizeŋ daŋ du de, ba ra yiruu, ‘Ŋmɛninaniinanii.’ Wichɔgɛɛri maa wàá vol u ni. Gɛnaa wàá wer dar banla n na hiŋuu.

ref: No lions or other wild animals will come near that road; only those the Lord has saved will travel there.
text: Bunyiŋ maa wàá du de, sechɔgii bɛl maa ŋmɛnɛ wàá vol u ni. Banla Kɔraawiizi n lɛɛwɛ bɛnnɛ niŋ ga de kaali bol.

ref: The people the Lord has rescued will come back singing as they enter Zion. Happiness will be a crown everyone will always wear. They will celebrate and shout because all sorrows and worries will be gone far away.
text: Ba daŋ zuu Jɛrusalɛm ni bɔsɔna, di ra yir yira, di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna la n waa tuna dɔɔwɛ maa. Ba bɔra daŋ sɔɔni di hanna la, biinichɔg ni himaa wàá ka du de.

ref: Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil Koori Hɛzɛkia dar ia, di u ŋɔwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ ia! Hɛrbɛlii vugrɛ haa wette lɛɛ u hɛri lii Asiiria koorizeŋ nonee biinei?

ref: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted out in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!

ref: What happened to the gods of Hamath, Arpad, and Sepharvaim? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?

ref: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.

ref: Three of the king's highest officials came out of Jerusalem to meet him. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
text: Juda hina bahoro lii bá ga chem u ni. Hilkia biibaal Ɛliakim n na binni kooridia wikpoglaa, seriya diiribɔr karchi Sɛbna ani Asaf biibaal Joa la n na binni ba wikpoglaa hɔna ni la, lii bá ga chem u ni.

ref: The Assyrian commander told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.

ref: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
text: Na! I dɛlli Ijip koori ninɛɛ. Ka u ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kɔlii daŋkpala. Di i dɛlli u ni, u daŋ ku di dui pira. Gunnɛ Ijip koori du tɛɛ banla maa n dɛlli u ni.

ref: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord, your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
text: Gɛɛ di i ŋɔ n be, ‘Yaa dɛlli Kɔraawiizii la yaa n na hum la ninɛɛ.’ U vuga kuaribɔra ni u mbusu lizibɔra lɛi Koori Hɛzɛkia faa chɔgi, ka ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be, ‘Ií ra jaami Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la n du Jɛrusalɛm bɛŋ laa?’

text: Awia, ba filaŋkeŋ, i ni n dɔɔri Asiiria koorizeŋ la na dɔŋa. N daŋ tɛi zagra kagboŋa anɛɛ, di i daŋ wer na a tinna!

ref: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
text: Di kaa kpa jaa, n ballɔɔ ń wa lɔ hɛri naa hina laal di chɔguu, di maa wiimaa nuuwɛ lɛi lii Kɔraawiizi bee? U himmaanii ŋɔ ń wa fɔɔ a hɛri naa, di chɔguu.”

ref: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you!”

text: Ií gilɛɛ waa nuu Koori Hɛzɛkia be. Asiiria koorizeŋ ra ŋɔu lugɔ ií gil u ni ia dɔɔ nuukpaŋ, ií ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra. Ii bɛl maa daŋ jaa ra di u himmaa grepu ni fig daazi nɔna, di ra nyɔɔ nii u himmaa kɔlɔŋ biini

ref: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards and raise your own grain.

ref: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.

ref: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.

ref: When these leaders came to me,

ref: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.

ref: Meanwhile the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.

ref: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?

ref: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia faa lɛɛ a hɔŋ lii a koorizeŋ balaa la be, di karmuu. Ka jaa kpau ga zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, di yaau dau Kɔraawiizi see,

text: ka suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ,

text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum, hinla n soge chɛrubzi baambaaŋ, i bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi la n na di kora durnya kossi maa ni. Hinuu ta chiŋ ni hɛri.

ref: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.

ref: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted and sneered at me, the holy One of Israel.
text: Anɛɛ i ra gbɛlli di ra chagzɛi? Anɛɛ ninɛɛ i pozei? Anɛɛ i ra maarei? Mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii labuu i ra ɛɛ gunla!

ref: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And here is what you have said about yourself, “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
text: I hum i balaarɛ ba wa chagziŋ. I ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i kpa i zagkpila ni a torkozii di tinni bizenaa nyuuni, haali Lɛbanɔn bizenaa la nyuuni, di teŋri de hɛriŋkpola la n jaŋŋɛ ani daananaa la maa n wesse la. I zuuwɔɔ la bɔɔnɛɛ, di ga hel u kɔr bɔra la n wesse werge.

ref: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
text: I ta barabaraa lugɔ, i ki kɔlɔnzii hɛrdumazi biine, di nyɔɔ a niiri. Di kaa ŋɔ lugɔ, i laallɔɔra fɛrgi Muu Naallɛ, u hil.

text: Haa nuuwɛa? N dau gunnɛ saŋa maa. Awiarɛ filaŋkeŋ n jaa ɛɛ guŋ la. N tɛibuu fɔŋŋa i puri bolzenaa la baŋ ma koŋlaa bar la.

ref: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or like tender young grass growing on a flat roof or like a field of grain before it matures.
text: Gunnɛ faa gillɛ a bola zuura waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ, ɔnsii faa lau baa, ba di hiihzi la. Ba faa gɛrgɔɔrɛ lugɔ kooriibii, ba faa waa fɔŋŋa maa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ kooree n lii sal, wiizi lɔ a ni a hil la.

ref: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
text: Ama, n zum i wiimaanii, i wiɛɛlaa ni bɔr la hinna la. Di zum gunla, i baaŋ n na fuuh n ni, werge maa.

ref: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
text: Dikuu i baaŋ n na fuuh n ni, n kaa nuu i jigsaa ge wia, n daŋ kpa n gɔrga gori i miizi, di kpa n kabarga ge du i nua, di gil i bir kaali gunla hiŋ ballɛ la.’ ”

ref: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year, you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be, “Kenne niŋ ɛɛ daansɛɛ wii tɛi, dɛɛnnaa ni bina, i daŋ di mitɛɛri. Ka biŋhorohiŋ waa, i himmaa daŋ duu mia, di kumaa di duu grepu daazi, di di a nɔna.

ref: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
text: Ii banla n ka Juda, daŋ nyɛɛli lugɔ daazi la lunne, n zuu hɛri nɛnnɛ, di nɔŋ.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
text: Banla n kawɛɛ la daŋ lii Jɛrusalɛm, baŋhina ge lii Bizeŋ Ziɔn. Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu niŋ aah siwii guŋ ɛɛ.”

ref: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Asiiria koorizeŋ wia, “Wàá zuu a bolzeŋ naa biini. Wàá ta hobikpaŋ maa ɛŋ. U laallɔɔra wàá dugli bol naa, gɛɛ di wer baruu, gɛɛ di ta pee tinni zuu ɛŋ.

ref: After this, King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
text: Awia, Asiiria Koorizeŋ Sɛnakɛrib faa bir har, di la u bolzeŋ Ninɛvɛ, di ga so de.

ref: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
text: A hɔl bɛl, u du u vug la banna yir Nisrɔk dia, di ra jaamuu. Denii u biibaala Adramɛlɛk ni Sarɛza wa kpuu ni tokobi, ka chɔ gilli Ararat hɛri. Gunnɛ a ɛɛ, u biibaal Ɛsahadɔn kpa u gawa, di di a kora.

ref: Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed,
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia bir u siwee chaŋ koŋlii, ka suŋŋi wiizi di ŋɔ,

ref: You, Lord, will save me, and every day that we live we will sing in your temple to the music of stringed instruments. Isaiah's Advice to Hezekiah
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛŋ, ka ya jaa wer kpa janjalanzi lɔ, di yir yira chɔluu u Dia biini, yaa de dui biini, saŋa maa.

ref: About this time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. So I went in and told him, “The Lord says you won't ever get well. You are going to die, and so you had better start doing what needs to be done.”
text: Saŋa bɛl n wa helle, wiila lɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia, u ra nyiŋŋi u siu. Amɔz biibaal, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa ba u be di wa ŋɔ, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Kossi i dia nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, hàá ka nyaagi, i daŋ siu.’ ”

ref: I thought I would never again see you, my Lord, or any of the people who live on this earth.
text: Màá ka na Kɔraawiizi, nyinee biini. Màá ka na nɛra, gɛɛ di kaa du ba be durnya naa biini.

ref: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried hard.
text: “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, a liizi lugɔ n humiibuu ni wibii ani n biini maa, di ɛɛ wia la maa n deŋlee i be.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u wii werge maa.

ref: Then the Lord sent me
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya be,

ref: with this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will let you live
text: lugɔ ú bir la Koori Hɛzɛkia be di ga ŋɔ, “Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la i naabaal Koori Deevid n faa ra hum la ŋɔ, ‘N nuu i wiisuŋŋaa labuu, di kaa na i sinii ge. N daŋ chaai. N daŋ gil i kaa di binni fidaanue jaa.

ref: There's nothing I can say in answer to you, since you are the one who has done this to me. My life has turned sour; I will limp until I die.
text: Ka ɛrɛɛ ń ŋɔi? U ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛŋ. U himmaanii ɛɛ guŋ. N daŋ sɔɔni siwii di hiŋuu n binni la n kawɛɛ biini maa dikuu aŋ kpolle tɛŋ wia.

ref: while I protect you and your city from the king of Assyria.
text: N daŋ lɛɛ i ni bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm maa lii Asiiria koorizeŋ nonee biini, di guuu.’ ”

ref: Now I will prove to you that I will keep my promise.
text: Aizaaya bir ŋɔ u be gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ ɛɛ ú zum lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ gunla un ŋɔ nua la. U ŋɔ,

ref: Do you see the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway built for King Ahaz? I will make the shadow go back ten steps. Then the shadow went back ten steps. King Hezekiah's Song of Praise
text: “Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil chunchugle naa bir la har keeriilɔŋa fi, Ahaz keeraa la ni.” Denii a wiizi n faa ra chol la bir la har keeriilɔŋa fi.

ref: This is what Hezekiah wrote after he got well:
text: Kenne Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia faa sɛbi di chɔli Kɔraawiizi u nyaagaa saŋa la,

ref: I thought I would die during my best years and stay as a prisoner forever in the world of the dead.
text: “N Dɔɔri, n de dui n jaa chi nɛnnɛ naa, a dɛkkɔɔ miŋ siuwɛ, ka n binni la n kawɛɛ la bir pɛɛa?

ref: My life was taken from me like the tent that a shepherd pulls up and moves. You cut me off like thread from a weaver's loom; you make a wreck of me day and night.
text: Ba faa wil n diarɛ di lɛɛu lii n be, gunla baŋ ɔɔ wil penɔɔni lɔɔ ta la. N miibɔɔ faa tunnɔɔ alugɔ suahri gessi, u lawiŋ teŋ kɔɔrɛɛ ni. Di lii hɔpizaa di ga hel hamuŋa, u gil n miibɔɔ tuŋ.

ref: Until morning came, I thought you would crush my bones just like a hungry lion; both night and day you make a wreck of me.
text: N di kanyittii kpaŋii guŋŋ di ga hel chɔɔzinnua, ka u purgi n hoga gunla bunyiŋ n ɔɔ purgi hoga la. Di lii hɔpizaa di ga hel hamuŋa, u gil n miibɔɔ tuŋ.

ref: I cry like a swallow; I mourn like a dove. My eyes are red from looking to you, Lord. I am in terrible trouble. Please come and help me.
text: N wiiwoo lugɔ koŋkoroŋbee gɛɛ kagchagii, N jaa ra nuumi lugɔ chɔɔziŋkomma n na wii. N binni chinne guŋŋ n siwee wa dim. Siaahmu biinii n du. N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, wa lɛɛŋ!”

ref: Your words and your deeds bring life to everyone, including me. Please make me healthy and strong again.
text: N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, anniibuu gillɛ newea du de. N gba ra na miibɔɔrɛ di lii a biini. I chaambuu di gil n dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: It was for my own good that I had such hard times. But your love protected me from doom in the deep pit, and you turned your eyes away from my sins.
text: Ajaa n suma dii wiarɛ n faa ra di a dɔgnya la. I nɔŋŋaa wiarɛ i lɛɛŋ lii siu be, di bir i har kpu n wichɔgaa.

ref: No one in the world of the dead can thank you or praise you; none of those in the deep pit can hope for you to show them how faithful you are.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, lalaa wàá wer chɔlii. Di nɛr siuwɔ, wàá wer yir yira chɔlii. Banla n du lalaa bol wàá wer dɔɔ i wibii tamii.

ref: Only the living can thank you, as I am doing today. Each generation tells the next about your faithfulness.
text: Nyinee bɛnnɛ niŋ wer chɔlii alugɔ kennaa minna ɛɛ zinaa naa. Mɛɛwaa ra bagli ba biizii i wibii dɔɔi wia.

ref: I had told King Hezekiah's servants to put some mashed figs on the king's open sore, and he would get well.
text: Denii Aizaaya faa ŋɔ, “Ií lug fig nɔna tɔ u kunsɔŋ la, ú nyaagi.”

ref: Then Hezekiah asked for proof that he would again worship in the Lord's temple.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia faa pɛɛzi Aizaaya, “Bɛɛ n niŋ bagli lugɔ n daŋ wer la Kɔraawiizi Diai?”

ref: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
text: Denii Koori Hɛzɛkia faa lɛɛ a nabɔnzi ni bɔsɔna werge maa. Di faa kpa u daama kuna dauribɔra maa bagli baa, u saliŋhuŋŋa, u saliŋ, u dɔzi tiuzaa kuna, nuunanaa, u laal dɔŋkuna ani kuna la maa n faa jaa u daama ni. Kummaa faa waa kawɛɛ u dia ni u kora biini, di wɔɔ kpawɛɛ bagli baa.

ref: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah was well, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Baladan biibaal Babilɔn Koori Mɛrɔdak Baladan, faa sɛbi hɔna, di kpa sunzaa jaa, di hum u balaa Koori Hɛzɛkia be, dikuu uŋ faa nuu u wiila ni u nyaagaa maa la wia.

ref: I asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa wa pɛɛzi Koori Hɛzɛkia, “Ɛrɛɛ a baala naa wa ŋɔi? Lee genii ba liiyɛi?” Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ lugɔ hɛhjannɛ ba lii, Babilɔnnɛ ba lii.

ref: “What did you show them?” I asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
text: Aizaaya pɛɛzuu, “Beedee ba na i kooridia biinei?” U ŋɔ, “N dia kummaanii ba na. N daama kummaa waa hoo, di maa kpawɛɛ bagli baa.”

ref: Then I told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Denii Aizaaya ŋɔ Koori Hɛzɛkia be, dí Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,

ref: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
text: “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, wibii maa, kunla maa n du i kooridia naa, daama la maa i naabaala n nyiŋŋee dau di wa lii ni zinaa, ba daŋ wa chi a maa kaali Babilɔn hɛri. Kummaa wàá ka ka.

ref: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
text: I naanna la n ɛɛ i himmaa challɛ bá lauri kaali Babilɔn hɛri, di ga vari baa, bá ra hum Babilɔn kooridia.” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told me, “The message you brought from the Lord is good.”
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia ŋɔ Aizaaya be, “Kɔraawiizi amaniye naa hiŋ wa tɛŋ naa wessoo.” U faa fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ bɔsɔna daŋ du de, ú kora chi chigigi u de dui biini.

ref: Our God has said: “Encourage my people! Give them comfort.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Tɛɛ n nɛra bɔsɔna, tɛɛ baa bɔsɔna.

ref: Speak kindly to Jerusalem and announce: Your slavery is past; your punishment is over. I, the Lord, made you pay double for your sins.”
text: A du Jɛrusalɛm hina bɔkpega. Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ ba tɔɔrɔɔ dii werge la tunnɔɔ. N jaa gil ba wichɔgaarɛ tɛɛ baa. N tɛr ba dignaa naa bunɛɛ, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.”

ref: Someone is shouting: “Clear a path in the desert! Make a straight road for the Lord our God.
text: Ba daŋ nuu nɛbɛl n na sii hɛribɔduma biini, di ra ŋɔ, “Yaa Dɔɔri ra bau. Ií ra ɛɛ sirya ú ra ba! Ií ra ɛɛ wia á ra deŋli ni a ŋmɛnizi.

ref: Fill in the valleys; flatten every hill and mountain. Level the rough and rugged ground.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɔ walli maa, di kaa bul giŋgimee ni bɔra la n la chiŋ. U daŋ wa kuari ŋmɛninyirmanyirmazi la á du kpantalaŋ.

ref: Then the glory of the Lord will appear for all to see. The Lord has promised this!”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi girme la jaa lii baaŋ, newea maa wer nau. Kɔraawiizi himmaanii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Someone told me to shout, and I asked, “What should I shout?” We humans are merely grass, and we last no longer than wild flowers.
text: Loobii bɛl ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ wia kpegzi ni!” N ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ wiarɛ ń ŋɔ kpegzi ninɛi?” U ŋɔ, “Newee maa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kooree, ba wessi maa ɛɛ lugɔ fiiri.

ref: At the Lord's command, flowers and grass disappear, and so do we.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi wa heezoo du a ni, a kooree ɔɔ yɔluu, a fiiri chogli. Wibii maa, newea ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kooree.

ref: Flowers and grass fade away, but what our God has said will never change. Your God Is Here!
text: Kooree ɔɔ yɔluu a fiiri chogli, ka Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la Wiŋɔɔlii lawaa, ɔɔ haŋ du denii di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: There is good news for the city of Zion. Shout it as loud as you can from the highest mountain. Don't be afraid to shout to the towns of Judah: “Your God is here!”
text: Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, iin dɔɔ amaniyesuma ii lizi la, ií tinni bizeŋ nyuu di sii werge. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, ií ŋɔ tɛɛ Juda bola hina, dí Kɔraawiizi la banna hum labuu ra ba la.

ref: Look! The powerful Lord God is coming to rule with his mighty arm. He brings with him what he has taken in war, and he rewards his people.
text: Ií ra nuu! Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra bau ni fɔŋŋa. U kpa fɔŋŋaa di ra di kora. Kinturgaa la un niŋ turgi u nɛra du u benii.

ref: The Lord cares for his nation, just as shepherds care for their flocks. He carries the lambs in his arms, while gently leading the mother sheep. Who Compares with God?
text: U ra binni u nɛraa lugɔ penɔɔni, di ɔɔ kpa a pebizi kpogli, ka ra nɔɔni peniinazi la n kpogli hizi nɛnnɛ.

ref: Did any of you measure the ocean by yourself or stretch out the sky with your own hands? Did you put the soil of the earth in a bucket or weigh the hills and mountains on balance scales?
text: Anɛɛ mɛgzi muuni niiri u nopaal biinei? Anɛɛ n tɛr u nonii di mɛgzi chiŋ magai? Anɛɛ n mɛgzi hɛri maa hɛɛhraa kuŋ biinei, di mɛgzi bizenaa ani giŋgimee maa tɔgzizi lai?

ref: Has anyone told the Lord what he must do or given him advice?
text: Anɛɛ n zum Kɔraawiizi nfɛrɛi gɛɛ ú wer bagluu wiai?

ref: Did the Lord ask anyone to teach him wisdom and justice? Who gave him knowledge and understanding?
text: Anɛɛ Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi, ú chaani u siweei? Anɛɛ n bagluu ŋmɛnizi la n deŋleenei? Anɛɛ n bagluu nunzuma ni wia zɛɛzi zumaai?

ref: To the Lord, all nations are merely a drop in a bucket or dust on balance scales; all of the islands are but a handful of sand.
text: Wibii maa, a hɛssi naa maa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ dobii n toŋŋe u be, a fukkɔɔ lugɔ nyɔɔ. U mɛgzi muu baaŋ hɛrjigzii a du fug alugɔ hɛɛhriikɔl.

ref: The cattle on the mountains of Lebanon would not be enough to offer as a sacrifice to God, and the trees would not be enough for the fire.
text: Lɛbanɔn kɔr daakpila la gba waa mbusu lizaa niŋ chemaa helle, u sela waa kpil lugɔ ba kpaa lizi mbusu di fuuh tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: God thinks of the nations as far less than nothing.
text: Kɔraawiizi waa be, a hɛssi naa maa waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ. A ɛɛ kumpɛɛrii, a waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Who compares with God? Is anything like him?
text: Anɛɛ ya jaa wer kpa mɛgzi Kɔraawiizɛi? Beedee í kpau mɛgzɛi?

ref: Is an idol at all like God? It is made of bronze with a thin layer of gold, and decorated with silver.
text: Vugwaa, sɛɛhrii ɔɔ sɛɛuh, luuri ge ɔɔ kaa ŋmɛɛri saliŋ tɔ u ni, di kuari saliŋhuŋŋu yɔlɔzi laaluu.

ref: Or special wood may be chosen because it doesn't rot— then skilled hands take care to make an idol that won't fall on its face. God Rules the Whole Earth
text: Nɛr la n wàá wer na saliŋ gɛɛ saliŋhuŋŋu, ɔɔ nyiŋŋi daa la n wàá wer pɔɔh manannɛ, di tɛɛ sɛɛhri la n zum huma nɛnnɛ, ú sɛɛuh u chi nɛnnɛ, wàá wer chol.

ref: Don't you know? Haven't you heard? Hasn't it been clear since the time of creation?
text: Ii waa zummɛ, gɛɛ ii waa nuuwɛ, di lii lugli laa? Ii waa wia naa zɛɛ zummɛ lii durnya luglaa saŋa laa?

ref: God is the one who rules the whole earth, and we that live here are merely insects. He spread out the heavens like a curtain or an open tent.
text: Waabuu soge u koorikara ni chinchiŋ, durnya nɛra maa ɛɛ lugɔ huuhni u be. U yaa chinne lugɔ patiisa, di kaa yaau lugɔ tanti dia.

ref: God brings down rulers and turns them into nothing.
text: U ɔɔ giluu durnya naa koorizenaa tuu zɛɛ, di gil ba bir pɛɛ.

ref: They are like flowers freshly sprung up and starting to grow. But when God blows on them, they wilt and are carried off like straw in a storm.
text: Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ kuna la baŋ duuwe gɛɛ baŋ chɔɔzɛɛ, a lunne waa hɛri zuuwɛ nɛnnɛ, ka Kɔraawiizi gil peu ta a ni a maa war, vem kpaa kaali alugɔ zɔga.

ref: The holy God asks, “Who compares with me? Is anyone my equal?”
text: Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Anɛɛ ii wer kpaŋ mɛgzɛi? N ni anɛɛ n mɛgzɛɛnɛi?”

ref: Look at the evening sky! Who created the stars? Who gave them each a name? Who leads them like an army? The Lord is so powerful that none of the stars are ever missing. The Lord Gives Strength
text: Ií lalli ii nyuuni binni chiŋ na. Anɛɛ n ta kuna naa maanɛi? Kɔraawiizii ta a kuŋkpila naa maa, di zum a maa maga ni a sɔna. U kpegzi n kannɛ, u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge wia, bɛl maa waa leuwe.

ref: You people of Israel say, “God pays no attention to us! He doesn't care if we are treated unjustly.” But how can you say that?
text: Ee, Izrɛl hina! Ɛrɛɛ i ra nuumi di ra ŋɔ, “Tɔɔrɔɔ naa yaa n na di naa, Kɔraawiizi wɔɔ ra naa? U baga waa hoo yaa dɔgnya dii bee?”

ref: Don't you know? Haven't you heard? The Lord is the eternal God, Creator of the earth. He never gets weary or tired; his wisdom cannot be measured.
text: Ii waa zummɛ, gɛɛ ii waa nuuwɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du denii di hanna laa? Waabuu ta hɛri naa maa. U ŋmɛnɛ maa waa kuuih dɔɔwɛ, nɛr maa wàá wer zum u nunzuma maga.

ref: The Lord gives strength to those who are weary.
text: Waabuu ɔɔ tɛɛ banla n kuuhwɛ fɔŋŋa, di tɛɛ gɛrga fɔŋŋa.

ref: Even young people get tired, then stumble and fall.
text: Haali biipɔllaa gba ɔɔ wa kuuuh, di lɔɔzi naazi ra jiŋli, di ra chogli.

ref: But those who trust the Lord will find new strength. They will be strong like eagles soaring upward on wings; they will walk and run without getting tired.
text: Ka banla n dɛlli Kɔraawiiziwaa, daŋ kaa bir dɔɔ fɔŋŋafalii. Ba daŋ yaa keeri di ra zaah alugɔ chigni, ba danna chɔ, ka ba wàá kuuh, di ra vol, ka ba bɔra wàá yɔɔri.

ref: Be silent and listen, every island in the sea. Have courage and come near, every one of you nations. Let's settle this matter!
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Muu baaŋ hɛrjigzi hina, ií gil kɔɔi ka keŋŋi digna di ra nuu n be. Ií ɛɛ sirya di ba seriya diiribɔr, di wa ŋɔ ii hor! Ií gil yaa maa chaali di zum unla hor n summɛ.

ref: Who appointed this ruler from the east? Who puts nations and kings in his power? His sword and his arrows turn them to dust blown by the wind.
text: Nɛbɛllɛ lii wiifurii keŋkere di ra ba. Anɛɛ n lizuu di tɛu fɔŋŋa ú wer yoo laal di kpegli nɛra, haali u gil u wer kpegli hɛssi hina ni ba koorai? U kpa u tokobii kpuuzi baa, u hoo ge yaari baa alugɔ peu n lɔ nyɔɔ ni zɔga yaari la.

ref: He goes after them so quickly that his feet barely touch the ground— he doesn't even get hurt.
text: U duŋŋi baa di ra la, ka wiimaa wɔɔ ɛɛwɛ, di ra chɔ alugɔ u naazi n waa hɛri ra hel.

ref: Who makes these things happen? Who controls human events? I do! I am the Lord. I was there at the beginning; I will be there at the end.
text: Anɛɛ n ɛɛ keŋ di gil guŋ du denei? Anɛɛ n yir newea maa di lii lugli la, ba ɛɛ u kipar lai? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n faa du nɛra be lugli la, di haa du ba be tuna saŋa labuu.

ref: Islands and foreign nations saw what I did and trembled as they came near. What Can Idols Do?
text: Muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛrjigzi hina na gunnɛ ɔnsii lau baa, hɛri naa tunazi hina maa na guŋ, ba bɔra ra sa. Ba chaali dɔŋa di ra ba.

ref: Worshipers of idols comfort each other, saying, “Don't worry!”
text: Bɛl maa ra hiini u dɔŋhiŋ di ra du dɔŋa bɔkpega.

ref: Woodcarvers, goldsmiths, and other workers encourage one another and say, “We've done a great job!” Then they nail the idol down, so it won't fall over. The Lord's Chosen Servant
text: Sɛɛhrii ra du salinluuri bɔkpega, unla n kpa silii di ra lɔ saliŋ ú vɔgli ge ra du unla n na lɔ lugbii bɔkpega. Ba maa ŋɔ gunla baŋ margi ba kuŋ la wesso, di kpaahzi a vug ú chi chigigi.

ref: Israel, you are my servant. I chose you, the family of my friend Abraham.
text: Ama, ii Izrɛl hinawaa ɛɛ n balaarɛ, ii ɛɛ banla miŋ lizɛɛ lii n dammu Abraham dee biini labuu.

ref: From far across the earth I brought you here and said, “You are my chosen servant. I haven't forgotten you.”
text: N lizi iabuu lii a hɛri tuna, di yir ia lii bɔɔnɛɛ, di ŋɔ ii be, ‘Ií ɛɛ n balaarɛ.’ Maa ia vɛɛwɛ, ka lizi ia tɛɛ n hiŋ.

ref: Don't be afraid. I am with you. Don't tremble with fear. I am your God. I will make you strong, as I protect you with my arm and give you victories.
text: Awia, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. N du ii benii. Ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra huah. Minuu ɛɛ ii Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi. N daŋ tɛɛ ia fɔŋŋa di hiini ia. N banonii daŋ ɔɔ lɛɛ ia di lau ia kpogli nɛnnɛ.

ref: Everyone who hates you will be terribly disgraced; those who attack will vanish into thin air.
text: Banla maa n hah ia daŋ di hiihzi di ŋmaabi. Banla maa ni ia n dɔɔ kalu daŋ siuzi ba wia tuŋ.

ref: You will look around for those brutal enemies, but you won't find them— they will be gone.
text: Haali iin ninna nyiŋŋi ii dɔma bɔr, ka ii wàá na baa. Banla n niŋ lɔ ia laal la wia daŋ tuŋ.

ref: I am the Lord your God. I am holding your hand, so don't be afraid. I am here to help you.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. N lau ii nodigee kpogli ka ŋɔ ii be, ‘Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. N daŋ hiini ia.’ ”

ref: People of Israel, don't worry, though others may say, “Israel is only a worm!” I am the holy God of Israel, who saves and protects you.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Izrɛl hina, haali iiŋ gɛrgɛɛ alugɔ haalauri di du tama la, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. N himmaanii niŋ hiini ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii, ii Lɛɛri, Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will let you be like a log covered with sharp spikes. You will grind and crush every mountain and hill until they turn to dust.
text: Ií ra nuu! N na kuari iabuu ii ɛɛ lugɔ milɔɔri daazi aŋhina dizi n dɔɔ nyina, a ɛɛ a falaa di ra di. Ií daŋ purgi bizenaa, di bul giŋgimee a birgi nyɔɔ.

ref: A strong wind will scatter them in all directions. Then you will celebrate and praise me, your Lord, the holy God of Israel. The Lord Helps the Poor
text: Ií daŋ hɛlaa, peu kpaa, vem lɔa yaari. Ama, iawaa daŋ na bɔsɔna mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi wia, di ra chɔli mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la.

ref: When the poor and needy are dying of thirst and cannot find water, I, the Lord God of Israel, will come to their rescue. I won't forget them.
text: Di nɛra waa di dɔgnya di nyiŋŋi nii huhzi bá nyɔɔ, ba loobee hil, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ nuu ba wiisuŋŋaa, mìŋ́ unla Izrɛl hina n na hum la, wàá gil baa ta.

ref: I will make rivers flow on mountain peaks. I will send streams to fill the valleys. Dry and barren land will flow with springs and become a lake.
text: N daŋ gil niiri ra pal bizenaa la n hillɛ nyuuni, bulli ge furgi walli. N daŋ gil hɛribɔduma birgi polli, bulli ra pal hɛri bɔhilaa.

ref: I will fill the desert with all kinds of trees— cedars, acacias, and myrtles; olive and cypress trees; fir trees and pines.
text: N daŋ gil hɛriŋkpola, akeesia, mɛrtil ani ɔlivi daazi fur hɛribɔduma, di gil daananaa ge fur hɛrsɛb di tɔ kɔr.

ref: Everyone will see this and know that I, the holy Lord God of Israel, created it all. Idols Are Useless
text: Denii nɛra jaa na di zum, ba daŋ binni a wia biini di zum a zɛɛ nɛnnɛ lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ guŋ, di zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii labuu gillɛ a maa wer ɛɛ.”

ref: I am the Lord, the King of Israel! Come argue your case with me. Present your evidence.
text: Kɔraawiizi, Izrɛl hina koori ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií wa lizi ii loobii, di ŋɔ ii hor.

ref: Come near me, you idols. Tell us about the past, and we will think about it. Tell us about the future, so we will know what is going to happen.
text: Ií kpa ii vuga la ba, á ŋɔ yaa be gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ. Ií gil a bagli yaa gunla wia n faa duwɛɛ, ya wer binni a biini, di zum gunla a tuna n niŋ wa du, gɛɛ a ŋɔ wia la n niŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa ɛɛ tɛɛ yaa.

ref: Prove that you are gods by making your predictions come true. Do something good or evil, so we can be amazed and terrified.
text: Di a wetto ŋɔ yaa be wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ, denii ya jaa zum lugɔ a ɛɛ vugaa di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, wibii maa. Ií gil a ɛɛ winanii gɛɛ wichɔgii bɛl a tir yaa, ɔnsii lau yaa.

ref: You idols are nothing, and you are powerless. To worship you would be disgusting.
text: Ka vuga waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ, a wiɛɛlaa maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ. Nɛr la maa n na kuari vuga, n kii u wiarɛ.

ref: I, the Lord, appointed a ruler in the north; now he comes from the east to honor my name. He tramples kings like mud, as potters trample clay.
text: N du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag nɛbɛllɛ bɔkpega, u ra ba, unla n lii wiifurii di ra yir n sɔŋ. U ra fɛrgi koora alugɔ banna fɛrgi hɛɛhraa la, alugɔ viimaari n na fɛrgi chuuri la.

ref: Did any of you idols predict what would happen? Did any of you get it right? None of you told about this or even spoke a word.
text: U bɛlii vugrɛ faa luglɛɛ ŋɔ wii naa, ya wer zum, lugɔ wibiirei? Bɛl maa faa waa guŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, nɛr maa faa waa wiimaa nuuwɛ lii ii be.

ref: I was the first to tell the people of Jerusalem, “Look, it's happening!” I was the one who announced this good news to Zion.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii faa felee lizi guŋ amaniye tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií na, ii nɛraa gaa ba la, ba ra ba bolle.’

ref: They are nothing, and they can do nothing— they are merely a passing breeze.
text: Ií ra nuu! A maa ɛɛ karaa, a wiɛɛlaa ɛɛ pɛɛ, a maa ɛɛ peure di ɛɛ daraa.”

ref: Here is my servant! I have made him strong. He is my chosen one; I am pleased with him. I have given him my Spirit, and he will bring justice to the nations.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N huŋhunnii keŋ, unla miŋ chigɛ u har. N lizuubuu tɛɛ n hiŋ, u wia parimbuu werge. N daŋ kpa n Duma du u ni, ú gil wibii dii du hɛssi maa biine.

ref: He won't shout or yell or call out in the streets.
text: Wàá ra pogzi gɛɛ di ra kɔɔ gɛɛ ba ra nuu u loobii ŋmɛnizi biine.

ref: He won't break off a bent reed or put out a dying flame, but he will make sure that justice is done.
text: Di nɛr ɛɛwɔ lugɔ koorii n luuwe, ka wàá kuu ha. Di nɛr ge ɛɛwɔ lugɔ fintina n na lii nyɔɔzi, ka wàá dimuu. U daŋ gil wibii dii du de.

ref: He won't quit or give up until he brings justice everywhere on earth, and people in foreign nations long for his teaching.
text: Wàá kuuh maa, u bɔra ge wàá huah di ra ba saŋa la un niŋ gil wibii dii wa du durnya. Muu baaŋ hɛrjigzi hina danna kpaŋ u baglaa, siaahmu ni.”

ref: I am the Lord God. I created the heavens like an open tent above. I made the earth and everything that grows on it. I am the source of life for all who live on this earth, so listen to what I say.
text: Kɔraawiizii ta chiŋ, di yaau, di ta hɛri ge, di kuari kuna la maa n du u biini, di tɛɛ newea maa heeza ni miibɔɔ. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u balii be,

ref: I chose you to bring justice, and I am here at your side. I selected you and sent you to bring light and my promise of hope to the nations.
text: “Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii yirii, di tɛi fɔŋŋa, í ra di wibii. N daŋ lau i nonii kpogli, di ra binni i ni. N daŋ ga i be, di gil n ni nɛra maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, di gil bɔchaaŋ ba hɛssi hina maa be.

ref: You will give sight to the blind; you will set prisoners free from dark dungeons.
text: I daŋ pilli nyuŋŋa siwee, di lizi banla baŋ tɔ diini biine, di kaa lizi banla n du bɔbiri werge biini.

ref: My name is the Lord! I won't let idols or humans share my glory and praise.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi, n sɔnnɛ guŋ! Màá gil ba kpa girme la n dɛgiŋ tɛɛ vug maa, gɛɛ di kpa chɔlaa la ban niŋ chɔliŋ tɛɛ vuga.

ref: Everything has happened just as I said it would; now I will announce what will happen next. Sing Praises to the Lord
text: Na, wia la miŋ felee ŋɔ la wa ɛɛ wibiire. Wifalaarɛ n kaa ra ŋɔ i be. Mɔɔ ka a wa ɛɛ, n daŋ ŋɔa tɛi.” Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa yir

ref: Tell the whole world to sing a new song to the Lord! Tell those who sail the ocean and those who live far away to join in the praise.
text: Ií yir yirfalii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi! Durnya nɛra maa, ií ra chɔluu. Ií banla n du muugberzenaa biine di ra hum, kuna la maa n du muuni biine, muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛrjigzi ni banla maa n soge a biine la, ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi!

ref: The Lord is marching out like an angry soldier, shouting with all his might while attacking his enemies. The Lord Will Help His People
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ lii alugɔ laallɔkpeg, alugɔ laallɔɔri bɔra n ɔɔ ra nyurgi gunla. U daŋ lɔ laal wile, di bagli u dɔma u fɔŋŋa.

ref: For a long time, I, the Lord, have held my temper; now I will cry out and groan like a woman giving birth.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N siigɔɔrɛ birgi, N lau n hinnɛ di faa di kanyitti. Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, n ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ haaŋ n na lul, di ra hɛm di ra lɔ wile di ra sigzi la.

ref: I will destroy the mountains and what grows on them; I will dry up rivers and ponds.
text: N daŋ chɔgi bizenaa ni giŋgimee maa, di gil daazi ni kooree hil. N daŋ gil muuni maa hil, di gil a gbatarni maa ge hiihzi.

ref: I will lead the blind on roads they have never known; I will guide them on paths they have never traveled. Their road is dark and rough, but I will give light to keep them from stumbling. This is my solemn promise.
text: N daŋ kpogli nyuŋŋa ga ŋmɛnizi la baŋ waa zummɛ. N daŋ gil bɔbiri birgi bɔchaaŋ, di gil hɛri bɔchɔgaa birgi bɔnanaa tɛɛ baa. N daŋ ɛɛ guŋ, wibii maa. Màá vɛɛ n nuuzi la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Everyone who worships idols as though they were gods will be terribly ashamed. God's People Won't Obey
text: Ama, banla n na tɔgzi vuga di kpaa birgi ba dɔɔra lawaa daŋ bir har di di hiihzi werge maa.” Izrɛl hina n ɛɛ nyuŋŋa ni dignitaŋa hina wia

ref: You people are deaf and blind, but the Lord commands you to listen and to see.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Dignitaŋa hina, ií ra nuu! Nyuŋŋa, ií binni nɛnnɛ na!

ref: The Lord always does right, and so he wanted his Law to be greatly praised.
text: A par Kɔraawiizii, dikuu u wideŋlaa wia, u gillɔɔ u Gbɔg dɔɔ sɔŋ ni girme.

ref: But his people were trapped and imprisoned in holes with no one to rescue them. All they owned had been taken, and no one was willing to give it back.
text: Ka na gunla a nɛra n duwɛɛ. Ba kpegli baabuu, di paagi ba kuna maa. Ba fɔɔ baabuu du bɔɔni ni nɛra tɔi diini biine. Ba waa hiini dɔɔwɛ. Ba lauri baabuu yoma, ka nɛr maa waa hoo, ú ŋɔ, “Ií gil ba bir kaali.”

ref: Israel sinned and refused to obey the Lord or follow his instructions. So the Lord let us be robbed of everything we owned.
text: Anɛɛ n gillɛ ba kpegli Izrɛl hina, di paagi ba kunai? Kɔraawiizi la baŋ faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu u ni werge la lɛiyaa? Ba vɛɛ u ŋmɛnizi hiŋaarɛ, ba waa u Gbɔg hiŋŋɛ.

ref: He was furious with us and punished our nation with the fires of war. Still we paid no attention. We didn't even care when we were surrounded and scorched by flames.
text: Awiarɛ u baaŋ faa fuuh ba ni werge, u gil ba lɔ baa laal, ba di tɔɔrɔɔ alugɔ baŋ du niŋ biini. Ka ba waa a zɛɛ zummɛ. U faa fuuh baa, ka ba wàá wiimaa hellee lii a biini.

ref: Descendants of Jacob, I, the Lord, created you and formed your nation. Israel, don't be afraid. I have rescued you. I have called you by name; now you belong to me.
text: Izrɛl hina, unla n ta ia la, ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. N lɛɛ iabuu. N yir ii sɔnaa, di lizi ia, ii ɛɛ n hora.

ref: When you cross deep rivers, I will be with you, and you won't drown. When you walk through fire, you won't be burned or scorched by the flames.
text: Di niiri biinii ii ra zuu, n daŋ du ii be, di muunii ii ra gi, ka a wàá di ia. Di niŋ biinii ii ra vol, ka wàá wer fuuh ia, u ninlau gba wàá haahri ia.

ref: I am the Lord, your God, the Holy One of Israel, the God who saves you. I gave up Egypt, Ethiopia, and the region of Seba in exchange for you.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum, Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la, n ɛɛ ii Lɛɛri la. N daŋ kpa Ijip hina chɛr ia, di kaa kpa Itiopia ni Sɛba hina jaa.

ref: To me, you are very dear, and I love you. That's why I gave up nations and people to rescue you.
text: Iiŋ ɛɛ kumpazi di dɔɔ girme n be ni miŋ nɔŋŋi ia la wia, n daŋ kpa nɛra char ia, di kaa kpa hɛssi hina char ii miibɔɔni.

ref: Don't be afraid! I am with you. From both east and west I will bring you together.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, n du i benii. N daŋ chaali ii dee la maa lii wiifurii ni wiicholii, di ba.

ref: They are my people— I created each of them to bring honor to me.” The Lord Alone Is God The Lord said:
text: N sɔŋ sag ba ninɛɛ, ba ɛɛ n nɛra la miŋ tawɛɛnɛ, nɛ́ra ra tɔgziŋ dikuu ba wia.”

ref: Bring my people together. They have eyes and ears, but they can't see or hear.
text: Ií tɛɛ n nɛra la n dɔɔ siwee ka nyuŋŋi, di dɔɔ digna ka taŋzi la ŋmɛnɛɛ bá ba.

ref: Tell everyone of every nation to gather around. None of them can honestly say, “We told you so!” If someone heard them say this, then tell us about it now.
text: Gil hɛssi hina maa chaali. Ba biini, u bɛliirɛ faa ŋɔ wia la n faa ɛɛwɛ mɔɔ ni annii n na ɛɛ filaŋkennaanɛi? Gil ba nyiŋŋi ba daansɛɛ hina ba, bá wa di baa wibii, ba dɔŋahina nuu di sɛɛ lugɔ wibiire.

ref: My people, you are my witnesses and my chosen servant. I want you to know me, to trust me, and understand that I alone am God. I have always been God; there can be no others.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Izrɛl hina, iabuu n daansɛɛ hina, di kaa ɛɛ n balaa la min lizɛɛ ii wer zumiŋ di yardiŋ, di kaa zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ n bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Vug maa faa waa hoo ka n du de, bɛl maa ge wàá ka du de n har.

ref: I alone am the Lord; only I can rescue you.
text: N bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi, Lɛɛri maa waa hoo di min lɛi.

ref: I promised to save you, and I kept my promise. You are my witnesses that no other god did this. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N bagli iabuu wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ. Aŋ waa ɛɛ la, n lɛɛ ia, di bagli ia lugɔ minuu ɛɛ guŋ. Hɛrduma bɛl maa vug lɛi du ii be, di ɛɛ guŋ. Iabuu n daansɛɛ hina. Minuu Kɔraawiizi. Mìŋ́ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I am God now and forever. No one can snatch you from me or stand in my way. The Lord Will Prepare the Way
text: Wibii maa, minuu Kɔraawiizi di lii faala maa di hanna la. Nɛr maa wàá wer lɛɛ u hiŋ lii n nonee biini. Wii la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ, nɛr maa wàá wer biruu.” Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa dɔɔi ni Izrɛl hina wibii nyaai wia

ref: I, the Lord, will rescue you! I am Israel's holy God, and this is my promise: For your sake, I will send an army against Babylon to drag its people away, crying as they go.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi, Izrɛl hina Lɛɛri ni ba Dɔɔrinaniinanii la ŋɔ, “N daŋ kuu ii wia di gil ba lɔ Babilɔn laal, di kpegli baa. Ba bɔsɔna chaasaa la daŋ birgi wiraa.

ref: I am the Lord, your holy God, Israel's Creator and King.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi, ii Dɔɔrinaniinanii la. Izrɛl hina taari ni ii koori.”

ref: I am the one who cut a path through the mighty ocean.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ra ŋɔ, unla n faa gillɛ muuzeŋ la peri, ŋmɛnɛɛ chɔɔ u baaŋ la,

ref: I sent an army to chase you with chariots and horses; now they lie dead, unable to move. They are like an oil lamp with the flame snuffed out. Forget the Past The Lord said:
text: unla n faa gillɛ a nii tɔ Ijip hina, ba zagra, ba laal torkozi ani ba laallɔɔra ni, di di baa, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka izi la. Ba dimmoo lugɔ baŋ dim fintina la.

ref: Forget what happened long ago! Don't think about the past.
text: “Ií suuh wibinaa wia, di gilɛɛ gil ii nfɛssi haa du a ni.

ref: I am creating something new. There it is! Do you see it? I have put roads in deserts, streams in thirsty lands.
text: Ií ra nuu! N kaa ra ɛɛ wifaliirɛ filaŋkeŋ. Waa ra ba la, ii wɔɔ nawɛɛa? N na dau ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ hɛribɔduma, di gil niiri ra pal de.

ref: Every wild animal honors me, even jackals and owls. I provide water in deserts— streams in thirsty lands for my chosen people.
text: Pir sela ra tɔgzimbuu, hohobiazi ni kikiuzi ra tɔgziŋ, dikuu miŋ gillɛ niiri ra pal hɛribɔduma biini di tɛɛ n nɛra la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hiŋ, ba nyɔɔ wia.

ref: I made them my own nation, so they would praise me.
text: N ma baabuu tɛɛ n hiŋ, bá ra chɔliŋ bombombom!

ref: I, the Lord, said to Israel: You have become weary of me, but not from worshiping me.
text: Izrɛl hina, ani a maa, ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ ii yir n sɔŋ. N wia bazi iabuu.

ref: You have not honored me by sacrificing sheep or other animals. And I have not burdened you with demands for sacrifices or sweet-smelling incense.
text: Ii waa kaa kpa peeza ba ií wa lizi mbusu di fuuah tɛŋ, gɛɛ di kaa ra tɔgziŋ ni mbusu lizaa. Maa ia fittɛ ŋɔ ii kpa mbusuzi lizaa mia wa tɛŋ, gɛɛ di gil n wia bazi ia dikuu daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuih wia.

ref: You have not brought delicious spices for me or given me the best part of your sacrificed animals. Instead, you burden me down with your terrible sins.
text: Ii waa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma maa yauwɛ tɛŋ, gɛɛ di kpa ii mbusu lizaa sela nuuri werge tɛŋ, a su n siwii. Ka i gillɔɔ ii wichɔgaa ɛɛ lugɔ buntɔga tɛŋ, di gil n lɔgɔ lii ii wichɔgaa wia.

ref: But I wipe away your sins because of who I am. And so, I will forget the wrongs you have done.
text: Ka minuu ra dinzi ii wichɔgaa dikuu n himmaa wia. Maa kaa ra liizaa ŋmɛnɛ maa.

ref: Meet me in court! State your case and prove that you are right.
text: Ií liiziŋ wia la iiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, yá di mmɔri. Ií bagli wii la n gillɛ ii hor du sum.

ref: Your earliest ancestor and all your leaders rebelled against me.
text: Ii mɛɛlugli faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, ii sitɔɔra ge vɛɛŋ.

ref: That's why I don't allow your priests to serve me; I let Israel be destroyed and your people disgraced.
text: Awia, n daŋ gil n Dia nabɔnzi di hiihzi, N daŋ kpa Izrɛl hina du ba dɔma nonee, bá chɔgi baa, di chagzi baa.”

ref: People of Israel, I have chosen you as my servant.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N balaa Izrɛl hina, miŋ lizɛɛ, ií ra nuu!

ref: I am your Creator. You were in my care even before you were born. Israel, don't be terrified! You are my chosen servant, my very favorite.
text: Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n ma ia ii maawaa hizi, di ta ia la, di ɔɔ ra hiini ia la, ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm! N lizi iabuu, ii ɛɛ n balaa ni n nɛnɔŋŋaa.

ref: I will bless the thirsty land by sending streams of water; I will bless your descendants by giving them my Spirit.
text: N daŋ bizi nii ta hɛri bɔhilii, di gil u ra pal gɔŋa la ni hɛrhilii maa biine. N daŋ kpa n Duma di du ii dee maa ni werge maa, di kissi ii naanna ge maa.

ref: They will spring up like grass or like willow trees near flowing streams.
text: Ba daŋ lul biizi ba hel nɛnnɛ lugɔ daajaŋra n chigɛ gɔŋa kɛraa.

ref: They will worship me and become my people. They will write my name on the back of their hands.
text: Nɛbɛl daŋ ba wa ŋɔ, ‘N ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi hotte.’ Bɛl ge ra yir u hiŋ Jekɔb. Bɛl ge daŋ sɛbi u nonii ni, ‘Kɔraawiizi hotte miŋ.’ Ba daŋ kpa Izrɛl sɔŋ di dau bahinaa.”

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the first and the last, the one and only God. Israel, I have rescued you! I am your King.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Izrɛl Koori ni ba Lɛɛri, di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Minuu lugli, minuu tuna. Kɔraawiizi maa waa hoo, di miŋ lɛi.

ref: Can anyone compare with me? If so, let them speak up and tell me now. Let them say what has happened since I made my nation long ago, and let them tell what is going to happen.
text: Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kpa u hiŋ di mɛgzi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizɛi? Gil ú sii guŋ, wibii maa. Gil ú bagli gunla maa n faa ɛɛwɛ lii saŋa la miŋ faa soŋŋi faala hina la, ni gunla n niŋ haa ba. Ɛɛh, ú bagli wia la n niŋ ba.

ref: Don't tremble with fear! Didn't I tell you long ago? Didn't you hear me? I alone am God— no one else is a mighty rock. Idols Can't Do a Thing The Lord said:
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra ra sa, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Maa felee ŋɔ wii naa tɛɛ ia saŋa maa? Iabuu n daansɛɛ hina. Fɔŋŋa dɔɔri bɛl kaa du denii di miŋ lɛiyaa? Akai, vug maa waa hoo ii dɛlli u ni di miŋ lɛi. Maa bɛl maa zummɛ.”

ref: Those people who make idols are nothing themselves, and the idols they treasure are just as worthless. Worshipers of idols are blind, stupid, and foolish.
text: Banla maa n na kuari vuga waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ, kuna la banna tɔgzi waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ. Banla n na kuaraa ɛɛ nyuŋŋaa. Ba waa wiimaa zummɛ, ba daŋ di hiihzi guŋ wia.

ref: Why make an idol or an image that can't do a thing?
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛr ma vug gɛɛ di sɛɛuh, ka waa tɔna maa dɔɔwɛ tɛuwɛi?

ref: Everyone who makes idols and all who worship them are mere humans, who will end up sadly disappointed. Let them face me in court and be terrified. Idols and Firewood
text: Nɛr la maa n na kuaraa daŋ di hiihzi, banla n na kuaraa ɛɛ neweare. Ií gil ba maa chaali seriya diiribɔr. Ɔnsii daŋ lau baa ba bɔra ra sa, bá chol di di ŋmaabi.

ref: A metalworker shapes an idol by using a hammer and heat from the fire. In his powerful hand he holds a hammer, as he pounds the metal into the proper shape. But he gets hungry and thirsty and loses his strength.
text: Luuri ɔɔ kpa lugbiirɛ du niŋ, di kpa silii luuu, di kpa u fɔŋŋa kuaruu. Di u wa ɛɛ guŋ, lɔzi ɔɔ lawuubuu, u fɔŋŋa tuŋ, niinyɔgzi ge lawuu, u bɔra ra yɔɔri.

ref: Some woodcarver measures a piece of wood, then draws an outline. The idol is carefully carved with each detail exact. At last it looks like a person and is placed in a temple.
text: Sɛɛhri ɔɔ kpa daarɛ mɛgzuu, di zum gunla un niŋ sɛɛuh, di kpa siah sɛɛuh, di kuaruu, u du newee duula, di du wer, ú kpau chiŋŋi vug dia.

ref: Either cedar, cypress, oak, or any tree from the forest may be chosen. Or even a pine tree planted by the woodcarver and watered by the rain.
text: Hɛriŋkpolaa ɔɔ teŋri, gɛɛ di lizi daananaa aŋhina lii kɔr biini di kuari vug gɛɛ di chɔɔzi aŋhina ka ra kpaŋ dooŋ ú ba, á hel.

ref: Some of the wood is used to make a fire for heating or for cooking. One piece is made into an idol, then the woodcarver bows down and worships it.
text: A ɛɛ nindaazi tɛu u ra chem di ra ŋmaani ka ra ɔɔzi paanuu. Di ɔɔ kaa kpa a daa yeŋ di sɛɛh vug, di ra kuaruu, di ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra.

ref: He enjoys the warm fire and the meat that was roasted over the burning coals.
text: A daazi yenne ɔɔ kpa daali u diwee, di ɔɔzi ol di di piŋ. Di ɔɔ ŋmaani a niŋ ge ka ŋɔ, “Niŋ naa ŋmaanaa summɔ oo!”

ref: Afterwards, he bows down to worship the wooden idol. “Protect me!” he says. “You are my god.”
text: Ka jaa kpa a daazi anla n kawɛɛ sɛɛh vug di ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra ka ra kuaruu, di suŋŋuu, di ra ŋɔ, “Lɛɛŋ! Hinuu n dɔɔri.”

ref: They don't have enough sense to say to themselves, “I made a fire with half of the wood and cooked my bread and meat on it. Then I made something worthless with the other half. Why worship a block of wood?”
text: Ba bɛl maa waa nfɛrɛ dɔɔwɛ, bɛl maa waa nunzuma dɔɔwɛ lugɔ ú wer chi di ŋɔ, “N kpa a daa yenne chem niŋ, di ɔɔzi paanuu ni ol hee. A dɛkkɔɔ miŋ kaa kpa u yeŋ di sɛɛh kunla Kɔraawiizi n kii u wiaa? Gɛɛ di ra togni kunla baŋ kpa daa kuariaa?”

ref: How can anyone be stupid enough to trust something that can be burned to ashes? No one can save themselves like that. Don't they realize that the idols they hold in their hands are not really gods? The Lord Won't Forget His People
text: Hɔɔhrii u ra di, u nfɛrɛ ra daruu, wàá wer lɛɛ u hiŋ gɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Kunnaa miŋ kpoglee naa wanna dar lɛiyaa?”

ref: People of Israel, you are my servant, so remember all of this. Israel, I created you, and you are my servant. I won't forget you.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Izrɛl hina, ií ra liizi wia naa nɛnnɛ, dikuu iiŋ ɛɛ n balaa wia. N ma iabuu, ii ɛɛ n balaarɛ, Izrɛl hina, màá suuh ii wia maa.

ref: Turn back to me! I have rescued you and swept away your sins as though they were clouds. Sing Praises to the Lord
text: N dinzi ii wichɔgaarɛ lugɔ baama, di dinzi ii wichɔgaa ge maa alugɔ kɔɔl. Ií bir ba n be, dikuubɛɛwiai, n lɛɛ iabuu.”

ref: Tell the heavens and the earth to start singing! Tell the mountains and every tree in the forest to join in the song! The Lord has rescued his people; now they will worship him. The Lord Created Everything
text: Chiŋ, a chaasi ni bɔsɔna! Durnya hɛribɔluŋe, ií ra chaasi werge! Bizenaa maa, ií ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna! Kɔrni ni a daazi maa, ií ge gba ra ɛɛ guŋ. Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ u nɛra Izrɛl hinaa, di bagli baa u girme.

ref: Israel, I am your Lord, the source of your life, and I have rescued you. I created everything from the sky above to the earth below.
text: Ii Lɛɛri Kɔraawiizi la n ma ia du ii maawaa hizi la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Minuu Kɔraawiizi, minuu ta kummaa, N bɛnnɛ yaa chiŋ, n bɛnnɛ yaa hɛri gba.

ref: I make liars of false prophets and fools of fortunetellers. I take human wisdom and turn it into nonsense.
text: Minuu ɔɔ chɔgi dɔgtɛɛkara wia, di gil vugra ge birgi gɛnaa, nunzunna zumaa birgi gɛnni wia.

ref: I will make the message of my prophets come true. They are saying, “Jerusalem will be filled with people, and the Lord will rebuild the towns of Judah.”
text: Ka ɔɔ gil n balii waa wiŋɔɔlii maa ɛɛ wibii, di gil u wiŋɔɔlii maa ɛɛ gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ. N ŋɔ Jɛrusalɛm wiarɛ lugɔ u daŋ bir su nɛra. N daŋ bir ma Juda bola la baŋ purgee la. N daŋ kaa gil a bir du a duula.

ref: I am the one who commands the sea and its streams to run dry.
text: N dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa ń gil muuzeŋ ni gɔŋa maa hiihzi.

ref: I am also the one who says, “Cyrus will lead my people and obey my orders. Jerusalem and the temple will be rebuilt.”
text: Minuu ŋɔ Sairus be, ‘I ɛɛ n penɔɔnii. I daŋ hiŋ n kipar di ŋɔ bá bir ma Jɛrusalɛm, di kaa ŋɔ bá chiŋŋi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia la ge zɛɛ.’ ”

ref: The Lord said to Cyrus, his chosen one: I have taken hold of your right hand to help you capture nations and remove kings from power. City gates will open for you; not one will stay closed.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Sairus la uŋ lizɛɛ, ú ɛɛ koori la be, “N lau i nodigre di gil i kpegli hɛssi ni ba koora, di paagi ba dɔŋkuna maa. N daŋ pilli ba bola dominuuzenaa tɛi, ba wàá ka wer karaa maa.

ref: As I lead you, I will level mountains and break the iron bars on bronze gates of cities.
text: N daŋ tɔ i see, di bul bizenaa la maa n du i ŋmɛnɛɛ, di ŋmuuri ba danyɛ dominuuzenaa, di kuugi a lugbidaazi maa.

ref: I will give you treasures hidden in dark and secret places. Then you will know that I, the Lord God of Israel, have called you by name.
text: N daŋ tɛi daama la n du bɔbiri, daama n la suahwɛ. Denii i jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum labuu yir i sɔŋ.

ref: Cyrus, you don't even know me! But I have called you by name and highly honored you because of Israel, my chosen servant.
text: N balii Izrɛl la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hiŋ la wiarɛ n yir i sɔŋ la, di tɛi sɔnzeŋ, haali hiŋ wan zummɛ gba.

ref: Only I am the Lord! There are no other gods. I have made you strong, though you don't know me.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi, Dɔɔri waa kaa hoo di jaa n ni. Di min lɛi, Dɔɔri maa waa kaa hoo. N daŋ tɛi fɔŋŋa, haali hiŋ wan zummɛ gba.

ref: Now everyone from east to west will learn that I am the Lord. No other gods are real.
text: Guŋ gil durnya hina maa, di lii wiifurii di ra la wiicholii, nɛra wer zum lugɔ vug maa waa hoo di mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi lɛi.

ref: I create light and darkness, happiness and sorrow. I, the Lord, do all this.
text: Minuu ta bɔchaaŋ ni bɔbiri maa, di gil bɔsɔna ni tɔɔrɔɔ maa du de. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ɛɛ annii maa.

ref: Tell the heavens to send down justice like showers of rain. Prepare the earth for my saving power to sprout and produce justice that I, the Lord, create. The Lord's Mighty Power The Lord said:
text: Chinchiŋ, gil baamazi nɛɛ wideŋlaa alugɔ dooŋ, di gil hɛri ge lɛɛa. Kɔ́raawiizi nɛlɛɛi ni wideŋlaa su hɛri maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ta a maa.

ref: Israel, you have no right to argue with your Creator. You are merely a clay pot shaped by a potter. The clay doesn't ask, “Why did you make me this way? Where are the handles?”
text: Wia daŋ huuzi unla maa ni u Taari n na di hɔɔzi. Vii ni u maari daŋ wer di hɔɔzia? Chuuri daŋ wer pɛɛzi maari, ‘Bɛɛ i ra ɛɛ gunnɛi? I nonee waa huma zummɛa?’

ref: Children don't have the right to demand of their parents, “What have you done to make us what we are?”
text: Wia daŋ huuzi unla maa n niŋ pɛɛzi u mɛɛ ni u maa, ‘Bɛɛ i lulɛi?’ ”

ref: I am the Lord, the Creator, the holy God of Israel. Do you dare question me about my own nation or about what I have done?
