text: N daŋ kpai du nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi i miibɔɔ lizaa la nonee, banla hinna ɔm la. N daŋ kpai du Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra nonee biini.

ref: You and your mother were born in Judah, but I will throw both of you into a foreign country, where you will die,
text: N daŋ fir i ni i maa, ii kaali hɛrduma la baŋ waa ii bɛl maa lullɛ. Denii ii maa ga siuzi.

ref: Jehoiachin, you are unwanted like a broken clay pot. So you and your children will be thrown into a country you know nothing about.
text: Denii n ŋɔ, “Koori Jɛhɔyachin ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ vii n purgee, ba kpa ha, nɛr maa waa kaa ra nyiŋŋuuwaa? A gunnɛ gillɛ ba lauri u ni u biizi maa kaali hɛrduma la baŋ waa zummɛa?

ref: Land of Judah, I am the Lord. Now listen to what I say!
text: N na yir hɛri naa himmaanii, ú nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii naa!

ref: Erase the names of Jehoiachin's children from the royal records. He is a complete failure, and so none of them will ever be king. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘Sɛbi baal naa wia dau alugɔ biinyaarii, baal la n wàá nyɛɛli u de dui saŋa. U naana bɛl maa wàá nyɛɛli, bɛl maa wàá so Koori Deevid koorikara ni gɛɛ di Juda kora maa.’ ”

ref: You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Wiarɛ huuzi n nɛra sitɔɔra la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ penɔɔna la n na kpu di ra yaari peeza la.”

ref: You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ ra tɛɛ penɔɔna la n na nɔɔni u peezaa la, “Dikuu iiŋ yaari n peeza di duŋŋaa ha, ii waa a tau duwɛɛ wia, n daŋ tɛr ii digna, dikuu wichɔgaa la iiŋ ɛɛwɛ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will bring the rest of my people home from the lands where I have scattered them, and they will grow into a mighty nation.
text: N himmaa daŋ chaali n peeza la maa n kawɛɛ lii hɛssi la maa miŋ duŋŋaa du la, di bir ba a diiribɔr, denii á wa lul di wazi werge.

ref: I promise to choose leaders who will care for them like real shepherds. All of my people will be there, and they will never again be frightened.
text: N daŋ lizi sitɔɔra lugɔ penɔɔna, bá ra binni a ni nɛnnɛ. Ɔnsii ni bɔsai wàá ka lawaa gɛɛ bɛl maa leu. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Someday I will appoint an honest king from the family of David, a king who will be wise and rule with justice.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ lizi Koori Deevid naana la wia n deŋlee di ɛɛ lugɔ Daa Kel. U danna di kora ni nunzuma, di ra di wibii, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa a hɛri maa biini.

ref: As long as he is king, Israel will have peace, and Judah will be safe. The name of this king will be “The Lord Gives Justice.”
text: Juda hina daŋ na lɛɛi u kora dii saŋa, Izrɛl hina ge so ni bampirsɔna. Sɔŋ naabuu ba ra yiruu, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Ɛɛ Yaa Lɛɛri.’

ref: A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living God who rescued Israel from Egypt.
text: Awia, hɔpizaa ra bau, nɛr maa wàá ka ŋɔ, ‘N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, unla n lizi Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri la.’

ref: Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land. Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
text: Ka ba daŋ ɔɔ kpa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa la sɔŋ, di hɛɛhzi mìŋ́ unla n lizi baa lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ani a hɛssi la maa miŋ gillɛ ba yaari la biine. Denii ba jaa bir wa so ba himmaa hɛri.” Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛkara hina wia

ref: When I think of the prophets, I am shocked, and I tremble like someone drunk, because of the Lord and his sacred words.
text: A dɔgtɛɛzi naa wia gillɔɔ n biini chɔgi, n bɔra ra sa. N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sinnyɔɔri, dikuu Kɔraawiizi ni u wiŋɔɔlaa n ɛɛ naniinanii wia.

ref: Those unfaithful prophets misuse their power all over the country. So God turned the pasturelands into scorching deserts. The Lord Will Punish Unfaithful Prophets
text: Sɛnsɛnna su a hɛri maanii, a hɛri hil werge, dikuu nuuseei la wia, u sela diiribɔra maa hil. A dɔgtɛɛzi ra hiŋ wichɔgaa ŋmɛnizi, di kpa ba fɔŋŋa ra ɛɛ wia la n waa deŋlee.

ref: The Lord told me to say: You prophets and priests think so little of me, the Lord, that you even sin in my own temple!
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N dɔgtɛɛzi ni n kizeehina maa wan zummɛ. Haali n Dia biini gba, n na ba biinikpola wiɛɛlaarɛ.

ref: Now I will punish you with disaster, and you will slip and fall in the darkness. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Awia, ba ŋmɛnizi danna hɛhrgi, ń duŋŋi baa du bɔbiri, bá chol. N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg ha ba ni, bina la biini min niŋ tɛr ba digna la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: The prophets in Samaria were repulsive to me, because they preached in the name of Baal and led my people astray.
text: N na keŋ wikuna naabuu Samaria dɔgtɛɛzi biini. Baŋ kpa vug Baal sɔŋ, di ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi n nɛra Izrɛl hina, di ra du ba ni, di gil ba leu.

ref: And you prophets in Jerusalem are even worse. You're unfaithful in marriage and never tell the truth. You even lead others to sin instead of helping them turn back to me. You and the people of Jerusalem are evil like Sodom and Gomorrah.
text: N kaa na wikunaa werge maa, Jɛrusalɛm dɔgtɛɛzi la ge biini, banna sɛm, di ra kanni kara. Ba kaa ra du wichɔgɛɛra bɔkpega, guŋ gil ba bɛl maa wàá sɛɛ lii u wichɔgaa biini. Ba maa ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛraa lugɔ Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra hina n be.”

ref: You prophets in Jerusalem have spread evil everywhere. That's why I, the Lord, promise to give you bitter poison to eat and drink. The Lord Gives a Warning The Lord said:
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ra ŋɔ a dɔgtɛɛzi naa wia, “N daŋ gil ba di diukpola, di nyɔɔ nii la n dɔɔ siri, dikuubɛɛwiai, Jɛrusalɛm dɔgtɛɛkara hina gillɔɔ wichɔgaa yaari a hɛri maa.”

ref: Don't listen to the lies of these false prophets, you people of Judah! The message they preach is something they imagined; it did not come from me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ waa nuu gunla dɔgtɛɛkara hina naa n na ŋɔ ra tɛɛ ia. Ba gillɔɔ ii dɔɔ tamipɛɛri. Ba ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wiarɛ ra lii ba himmaa nfɛssi biine, alugɔ baŋ chɔɔwɛ naa deeza biini, ka a waa ɔɔ lii n be.

ref: These prophets go to people who refuse to respect me and who are stubborn and do whatever they please. The prophets tell them, “The Lord has promised everything will be fine.”
text: Ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ ra tɛɛ banla n na gbɛlliŋ labuu, ‘Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií daŋ dɔɔ bampirsɔna.’ Di kaa ŋɔ tɛɛ banla ge n dɔɔ dignikpega, ‘Wichɔgii maa wàá huuzi ia.’

ref: But I, the Lord, tell you that these prophets have never attended a meeting of my council in heaven or heard me speak.
text: Ka n ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘A dɔgtɛɛzi naa bɛl maa waa n wolo ni n nfɛrɛ zummɛ. Ba waa kaa zum n wiŋɔzi ge bɛl maa zɛɛ gɛɛ di dɔɔ kanyitti lugɔ bá nuu n wiŋɔzi.

ref: They are evil! So in my anger I will strike them like a violent storm.
text: Na, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ dooŋ pekpeg. U daŋ ta biinikpola hina nyuuni ni,

ref: I won't calm down, until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday you will understand exactly what I mean.
text: wàá teŋ, di waa wii la minna nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ la tunnɛ. A zɛɛ daŋ chaani nɛnnɛ tɛɛ nɛra, saŋa bɛl n na ba biini.’ ”

ref: I did not send these prophets or speak to them, but they ran to find you and to preach their message.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Miŋ lɛi hum a dɔgtɛɛzi naa, ka ba la. Maa baa tɛɛwɛ amaniye maa, ka ba kpa n sɔŋ di ra ŋɔa.

ref: If they had been in a meeting of my council in heaven, they would have told you people of Judah to give up your sins and come back to me.
text: Ka di ba faa zum wii la n du n biinii, ba daŋ faa wer sii n amaniye tɛɛ n nɛra, di hiini baa, bá gil ba wichɔgaa ni biinikpola wiɛɛlaa, ba de dui biini.

ref: I am everywhere— both near and far,
text: N ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la n du yemmaanii, bɔkpaŋ bɛŋ lɛi n du.

ref: in heaven and on earth. There are no secret places where you can hide from me.
text: Nɛr maa wàá wer suah bɔr la miŋ wàá nau, ii waa zummɛ lugɔ n du chiŋ ni hɛri yemmaanɛa?

ref: These unfaithful prophets claim that I have given them a dream or a vision, and then they tell lies in my name.
text: N nuu wii la maa dɔgtɛɛkara hina naa n kpa n sɔŋ di ra ŋɔu, di ra ŋɔ lugɔ n tɛɛ baabuu amaniye ba deeza biini.

ref: But everything they say comes from their own twisted minds. How long can this go on?
text: Ɛrɛɛ wia naa n du a dɔgtɛɛkara hina naa bampiree, ba ra ŋɔa naa birgi magɛi? Ba ɔɔ ra sii ba himmaa karaa.

ref: They tell each other their dreams and try to get my people to reject me, just as their ancestors left me and worshiped Baal.
text: Ba ra fɛu lugɔ ba deezazi la baŋ baglɛɛ ra tɛɛ dɔŋa la daŋ gil n nɛra suuh n wia, gunla ba naabaala n faa suuh n wia, dikuu vug Baal kuaraa wia la.

ref: Their dreams and my truth are as different as straw and wheat. But when prophets speak for me, they must say only what I have told them.
text: Gil dɔgtɛɛ la n deezee la bagli u deeza, ka gil unla n dɔɔ n wiŋɔɔlii, ŋɔu ni wibii. Kɔlii ni mibii ɛɛ kpannɛa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: My words are a powerful fire; they are a hammer that shatters rocks.
text: N wiŋɔɔlii waa ɛɛwɛ lɛi lugɔ niŋ, di kaa ɛɛ lugɔ silii baŋ kpawɛɛ ra purgi biaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: These unfaithful prophets claim I give them their dreams, but it isn't true. I didn't choose them to be my prophets, and yet they babble on and on, speaking in my name, while stealing words from each other. And when my people hear these liars, they are led astray instead of being helped. So I warn you that I am now the enemy of these prophets. I, the Lord, have spoken. News and Nuisance The Lord said to me:
text: Wibii maa, n ni banla n ɔɔ kpa deezikara di ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi nɛra ra du ba ni la, dɔɔ wiarɛ. Ba ɔɔ ŋɔabuu di ra dar n nɛra ba ra leu, ka minlɛi lizi baa di hum baa. A waa ɔɔ dɔɔ hiinaa tama maa tɛɛ a nɛra. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.” Amaniyekara ni dɔgtɛɛkara hina wia

ref: Jeremiah, when a prophet or a priest or anyone else comes to you and asks, “Does the Lord have news for us?” tell them, “You people are a nuisance to the Lord, and he will get rid of you.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “Di nɛra naa gɛɛ n dɔgtɛɛzi gɛɛ n kizeehina wa pɛɛzii, ‘Bɛɛ amaniyee lii Kɔraawiizi benei?’ Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunni Kɔraawiizi be, awia, u daŋ vɛɛ ia ta.’

ref: If any of you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” I will punish you and your families, even if you are a prophet or a priest.
text: Di n dɔgtɛɛ gɛɛ n kizeehiŋ gɛɛ nɛr maa haŋ waa ŋɔ, ‘Amaniye naa lii Kɔraawiizi benii,’ n daŋ tɛr a hiŋ ni u diahina digna.

ref: Instead, you must ask your friends and relatives, “What answer did the Lord give?” or “What has the Lord said?”
text: Kenne ii bɛl maa ɔɔ ra ŋɔ di ra tɛɛ u dammu gɛɛ u lulli, ‘Ɛrɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nai?’ gɛɛ ‘Ɛrɛɛ u ŋɔi?’

ref: It seems that you each have your own news! So if you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” you are twisting my words into a lie. Remember that I am your God, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Ka ii gilɛɛ kaa wàá ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi amaniyee,’ dikuubɛɛwiai, baal maa wiŋɔzi ɔɔ ɛɛ u himmaa amaniyee. Awia, ii ɔɔ lau Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la yaa n na hum la wiŋɔzii, di bir.

ref: But if you disobey me and say, “Here is news from the Lord,”
text: Ka di ba vɛɛ n wiŋɔɔlii ka ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi amaniyee keŋ,’ guŋwaa, ŋɔ ba be lugɔ

ref: I will pick you up and throw you far away. And I will abandon this city of Jerusalem that I gave to your ancestors.
text: wibii maa, n daŋ lau baa, di kpa baa ta bɔɔnɛɛ, di vɛɛ bolzeŋ la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ba ni ba naabaala la maa.

ref: You will never be free from your shame and disgrace.
text: N daŋ gil ba di hiihzi la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ, baŋ wàá suuh u wia maa.”

ref: The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple.
text: Saŋa la Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n wa lauri Jɛhɔyakim biibaal, Juda Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni u nabɔnzi ani banla n zum nonee huma, di kpogli baa lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la, Kɔraawiizi faa bagliŋ kɛɛgɔzi anɛɛ n su fig nɔna, di chi u Dia dominua, alugɔ deeza biini.

ref: One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
text: A kɛɛgɔ bɛl biini, fig nɔna la aahwɔɔ nɛnnɛ, di dɛg dii. Bɛl ge biini, a faa waa wer, di dɛg dii tama maa.

ref: “Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?” “Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛziŋ, “Jɛrɛmia, bɛɛ i nai?” N ŋɔ, “Fig nɔnaa n na. Aŋhina wessoo werge, ka aŋhina ge waa wer, a waa dii gba dɛkkɛ tama maa.”

ref: Then the Lord told me to say:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: People of Judah, the good figs stand for those of you I sent away as exiles to Babylonia,
text: “Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Juda hina la miŋ gillɛ ba lauri kaali Babilɔn hɛri la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ a fig nɔnnanaa la.

ref: where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down.
text: N danna binni ba ni nɛnnɛ ba de dui biini. N daŋ kaa bir ba ba ni hɛri naa. N daŋ kuari baa chiŋŋi nɛnnɛ, màá kpu baa. N daŋ duu baa, màá kpuzi baa ta alugɔ kunduulaa.

ref: I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
text: N daŋ gil ba bampiree lawiŋ lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi. N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum, bá ge ɛɛ n nɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ bir ba n be ni ba biine maa.

ref: The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt.
text: Ka gunla a fig nɔna la n waa wer, a waa wer dii la, gunnɛ ń kpa dau Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia ni u nabɔnzi ni banla maa n ka Jɛrusalɛm la, haali di ba du a hɛri naa biini gɛɛ di Ijip gbaa ba du.

ref: I will punish them with a terrible disaster, and everyone on earth will tremble when they hear about it. I will force the people of Judah to go to foreign countries, where they will be cursed and insulted.
text: N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg ta ba ni, ɔnsii lau hɛssi hina maa durnya naa biini. Nɛra danna ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ, di ra lɔ baa mɔmɔsia, di kpa ba sɔŋ ra kuari wisuma, di kpa ba sɔŋ ra see dɔŋa nuuzi, bɔr la maa miŋ yaari baa, ba du.

ref: War and hunger and disease will strike them, until they finally disappear from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.
text: N daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii ta ba ni, ba maa tuŋ hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ba ni ba naabaala la biini.’ ”

ref: The Lord has sent prophets to you time after time, but you refused to listen.
text: Haali Kɔraawiizi n hum u balaa dɔgtɛɛzi ii be saŋa kpila maa, ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛɛ baa.

ref: They told you that the Lord had said: Change your ways! If you stop doing evil, I will let you stay forever in this land that I gave your ancestors.
text: Ba ɔɔ ŋɔ ii benii lugɔ ii bɛl maa bir lii u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ni u wikuna ɛɛi maa biini. Guŋ gil ii wer so hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala, ú ɛɛ ii kundɔɔlii di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa la.

ref: I don't want to harm you. So don't make me angry by worshiping idols and other gods.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vug maa gɛɛ di waa sɛɛ u dɔɔra. Ií gilɛɛ gil n baaŋ waa fuuh, dikuu ii nonee kuŋkuaraa wia, ń gilɛɛ waa tɔɔri ia.

ref: But you refused to listen to my prophets. So I, the Lord, say that you have made me angry by worshiping idols, and you are the ones who were hurt by what you did.
text: Ka ii waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ, ka gil n baaŋ fuuh dikuu kuna la iiŋ kuarɛɛ la wia, di gil wia huuzi ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: and now I will let you be attacked by nations from the north, and especially by my servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. You and other nearby nations will be destroyed and left in ruins forever. Everyone who sees what has happened will be shocked, but they will still make fun of you.
text: n daŋ chaali nɛra la maa n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ni n balii Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza, bá wa lɔ hɛri naa ni anla maa n baruu la hina laal. N daŋ chɔgi a maa nyaamm, di gil ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, nɛra nuuzi kpu, di gil ba bola chɔɔgi diŋgelli di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will put an end to your parties and wedding celebrations; no one will grind grain or be here to light the lamps at night.
text: N daŋ lizi bɔsɔna ni hindii kɔɔi, haŋfalaa ni ba janna loobee, nanni gbɔga ani fintinazi chaanaa ba biini.

ref: This country will be as empty as a desert, because I will make all of you the slaves of the king of Babylonia for
text: A hɛri naa maa daŋ chɔɔ diŋgela, ka hɛssi naa hina maa jaa gaa hum Babilɔn koori di ra la binni tokkoahoro ni fi.

ref: When that time is up, I will punish the king of Babylonia and his people for everything they have done wrong, and I will turn that country into a wasteland forever.
text: Di a binni tokkoahoro ni fihiŋ wa su a maga, n daŋ jaa bir tɛr Babilɔn koori ni u hɛri hina maa digna, dikuu ba bilchɔg wia, di gil de chɔɔ diŋgela, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: My servant Jeremiah has told you what I said I will do to Babylonia and to the other nations, and he wrote it all down in this book. I will do everything I threatened.
text: N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔgni la maa miŋ ŋɔ a daŋ chol hɛssi hina ni la, di tɛr Babilɔn hina digna, saŋa la miŋ ga Jɛrɛmia be di ŋɔ hɛhchɔgni la maa wia baŋ sɛbɛɛ du hɔnnaa biini la.

ref: I will pay back the Babylonians for every wrong they have done. Great kings from many other nations will conquer the Babylonians and force them to be slaves. The Cup Full of God's Anger
text: Ba daŋ birgi yoma tɛɛ hɛrkpila hina ni ba koorizenaa maa. N daŋ kaa kpa ba wiɛɛlaa kim turgi baa, gunla n dɛkkɛ.” Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di hɛssi hina seriya wia

ref: The Lord God of Israel showed me a vision in which he said, “Jeremiah, here is a cup filled with the wine of my anger. Take it and make every nation drink some.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “Siŋ ni libeere keŋ, lugɔ n baaŋ n suu. Kpau la hɛssi la hina maa be miŋ humii la, di gil ba maa nyɔɔu.

ref: They will vomit and act crazy, because of the war this cup of anger will bring to them.”
text: Di ba wa nyɔɔu, ba danna jiŋli, di birgi chugla hina, dikuu laal la miŋ kpawɛɛ ra ba ba ni wia.”

ref: I took the cup from the Lord's hand, and I went to the kings of the nations and made each of them drink some.
text: Denii n lɛɛ a siŋ ni libee Kɔraawiizi be, di kpau la ga tɛɛ hɛssi la hina be uŋ humiŋ la, ba nyɔɔu.

ref: I started with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and the king and his officials were removed from power in disgrace. Everyone still makes insulting jokes about them and uses their names as curse words.
text: Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda bola maa ni ba koora ani ba nabɔnzi maanii ń gil ba nyɔɔu. Guŋ gil bá hɛssi birgi hɛribɔdumazi, ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii ni nuukpui werge. Nɛra kpa ba sɔŋ di ra see dɔŋa nuuzi. Gunnɛ ba haa ra ɛɛ haali ni zinaa.

ref: The second place I went was Egypt, where everyone had to drink from the cup, including the king and his officials, the other government workers, the rest of the Egyptians,
text: Banla maa n niŋ nyɔɔ a sinnɛ keŋ, Ijip koori, u balaa, u nabɔnzi ani Ijip hina maa,

ref: and all the foreigners who lived in the country. Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod.
text: di kpa hɔɔhra maa, Uz koora maa, Filisti koora maa, banla n lii Askɛlɔn, Gaza, Ɛkrɔn ani banla n ka Asdɔd la,

ref: Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon,
text: di kpa Ɛdɔm, Moab ani Ammɔn hɛssi hina,

ref: and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea.
text: di kpa Taaya ni Saidɔn koora maa ani koora la n du a muuzeŋ baŋgia kɛraa,

ref: After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert,
text: di kpa Lɔrbizi koora maa ni hɔɔhra la maa n du hɛribɔduma la koora maa,

ref: and the countries in the north, both near and far. I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
text: di kpa koora la maa n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, n duglɛɛ gɛɛ n du bɔɔnɛɛ, di hiŋzi dɔŋa. Ba maa har, Sɛsak koori gba daŋ nyɔɔu.

ref: The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
text: Awia, ŋɔ ba be, “Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, ‘Ií nyɔɔ werge di dɛɛzi, di ra hɛɛhzi, di chogli, ii wàá ka izi maa, dikuu laal la min niŋ kpa ta ii ni la wia.’

ref: The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink.
text: Ka di ba wa vɛɛwɔ lugɔ ba wàá lɛɛ a siŋ i be di nyɔɔ, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ a dɛkkɔ ií nyɔɔu!

ref: Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
text: Na, n faarɔɔrɛ kpa hɛhchɔg di ra ta n himmaa bolzeŋ la n sɔŋ n sag u ni la ninɛɛ. Ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ màá tɛr ii digna. Akai, màá gil ii digna tɛraa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil laal chol durnya nɛra maa ni. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.’

ref: The Lord told me to say: From my sacred temple I will roar like thunder, while I trample my people and everyone else as though they were grapes.
text: Awia, ŋɔ wia naa n niŋ wa huuzi baa naa du ba ni. ‘Kɔraawiizi daŋ pozi lii u bol, u daŋ pozi lii u duuribɔnaniinanii lugɔ nazaa, di pozi u hɛri ni werge. U danna kɔɔ lugɔ nɛra la n ɔɔ ra fɛrgi ba grepuzi, di ra pogzi durnya hina maa ni.

ref: My voice will be heard everywhere on earth, accusing nations of their crimes and sentencing the guilty to death. Disaster Is Coming
text: Denii a pogzaa hel durnya maa. Kɔraawiizi ni durnya nɛra maanii dɔɔ wia, u daŋ di bɛl maa seriya, di kpu wichɔgɛɛra maa.’ ” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says: You can see disaster spreading from far across the earth, from nation to nation like a horrible storm.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Ií na! Hɛhchɔg ra yaaruu lugɔ dooŋ pekpeg di lii hɛri bɛl di ra la bɛl.”

ref: When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn. The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
text: A saŋa hiŋ, banla Kɔraawiizi n kpuwɛɛ la daŋ yaari bɔr maa. Nɛr maa wàá wii ba lee gɛɛ di chaali baa gɛɛ di hug baa gba, ka ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nabina n chɔɔ hɛri.

ref: The Lord's people are his flock, and you leaders were the shepherds. But now it's your turn to be butchered like sheep. You'll shatter like fine pottery dropped on the floor. So roll on the ground, crying and mourning.
text: N nɛra binna n lugɔ penɔɔna, ií ra chɛɛhgi! N nɛra sitɔɔra, ií chɔɔ hɛɛhraa biini ra billi. Dikuubɛɛwiai, ii kɔrgaa saŋa helloo, ba daŋ ŋmɛnni ia lugɔ pebala.

ref: You have nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. *
text: N nɛra sitɔɔra n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ penɔɔna, wàá dɔɔ bɔr la ban niŋ chɔ la.

ref: Listen to the cries of the shepherds, as the Lord's burning anger turns peaceful meadows into barren deserts.
text: Ii waa bampirsɔna dɔɔwɛ ii hɛri, dikuu Kɔraawiizi n kpa u baaŋ chɔgi ii hɛri wia.

ref: Like a lion leaving its den, the Lord has abandoned his people to the destruction of war.
text: Kɔraawiizi vɛɛ u nɛraa ta alugɔ bunyiŋ n chɔ u bɔzuulii. Laal nuukpuuri wia ni Kɔraawiizi baaŋ gillɔɔ a hɛri birgi hɛribɔduma.

ref: The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said,
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina, u dɔgtɛɛzi ani a nɛra maa nuu wia la maa mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa, Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la.

ref: Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
text: Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim n wa di Juda kora, a waa birgee ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
text: Ka ii zum nɛnnɛ lugɔ di ii kpuŋ, ii daŋ lɛɛ nɛr la n waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ haahkɛ di chug ii ni a bolzeŋ naa ni nɛra la maa n du u biini. Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizii humiŋ wibii maa lugɔ ń wa ŋɔ wia naa maa, ií nuu.”

ref: Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you.
text: “Lii chi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ nɛra la n lii Juda bola maa di ba bá wa jaamiŋ n Dia biini la. Ŋɔ ba be wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ í ŋɔ tɛɛ baa la. Gilɛɛ wa mɔŋ a bɛl maa ra ta tama maa.

ref: Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins.
text: Aŋhinabe, baŋhina daŋ nuu, di bir lii ba wichɔgaa la banna ɛɛ biini, guŋ gil màá ka kpa hɛhchɔg la miŋ faa ra ta u jina lugɔ n kpa ta ba ni, dikuu wichɔgaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛɛ la wia ta ba ni.”

ref: Tell them that I have said: You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ dí n ŋɔ a nɛra be, “A dɛkkɔ ii ra hiŋ n Gbɔg la miŋ kpawɛɛ dau ii see la.

ref: Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once,
text: Di ii waa sɛɛwɛ ii nuu tɛɛ n balaa dɔgtɛɛzi la, miŋ hum ii be digiidigii la,

ref: I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word. Jeremiah on Trial
text: guŋwaa, n daŋ chɔgi n Dia naa gunla miŋ chɔgi Silo la. Bolzeŋ naa ge daŋ ɛɛ nuuseei kuŋ tɛɛ durnya hɛssi hina maa.”

ref: The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial.
text: Juda hina nabɔnzi n wa nuu a wia naa, ba izi lii kooridia di kpa la Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga chi ba chigni bɔra u Dominuuzeŋfalii.

ref: While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi ŋɔ tɛɛ a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa, “Baal naa dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi bolzeŋ naabuu du u ni. Ii himmaa nuu gunla uŋ ŋɔwɛɛrɛ!”

ref: Then I told the judges and everyone else: The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, ií char ii manni ni ii wiɛɛlaa maa, ka ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la nua. Di ii ɛɛ guŋ, wàá ka gil hɛhchɔg la uŋ faa ŋɔ u daŋ chol ii ni la, chol ii ni.

ref: You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right.
text: Ama, miŋwaa du ii noneere. Ií ɛɛŋ wii la maa iiŋ nawɛɛ lugɔ u wessoo di deŋli.

ref: The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
text: Denii a nabɔnzi ni a nɛra maa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi be, “Baal naa waa kpui dɛkkɛ! Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la sɔŋ biinii u ŋɔ wia tɛɛ yaa.”

ref: Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that
text: A hɛri nabɔnzi baŋhina lii chi nɛra la n chaalɛɛ la see, di ŋɔ ba be,

ref: years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said: “I, the Lord All-Powerful, say Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.”
text: “Mɔrɛsɛf hinuu Maika faa ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi Juda hinaa, saŋa la Juda Koori Hɛzɛkia n faa di kora la. U faa ŋɔ Juda hina maa benii lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ba daŋ par Ziɔn alugɔ koo. Jɛrusalɛm birgi hembugle, di chɔɔ kulululu. Kɔraawiizi Dia giŋgimii ge birgi kɔr.’

ref: Then the leaders continued: No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would. People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
text: Koori Hɛzɛkia ni Juda hina faa waa Maika kpuwɛɛ. Awia, Koori Hɛzɛkia wia faa par Kɔraawiizi, waa kaa gil hɛhchɔg la uŋ faa ŋɔ u wia la chol ba ni. Ka yaa himmaa ra nyiŋŋuu hɛhchɔg chuma chol yaa ni.”

ref: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me: Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck.
text: “Kpa kurhɔna ni daazi kuari napattaa baŋaa daa, di kpau du i baŋaa.

ref: Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah.
text: Ɛdɔm, Moab ani Ammɔn hɛssi ni Taaya ani Saidɔn bola koora nabɔnzi ba Jɛrusalɛmnɛ bá wa na Koori Zɛdɛkia. Awia, kpa tile naa tɛɛ baa, bá ga tɛɛ ba koora.

ref: So have them tell their kings that I have said: I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel,
text: Tili baa ba dɔɔra be, di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií ga ŋɔ ii dɔɔra be,

ref: and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth,
text: n himmaa fɔŋŋazeŋ ni n banoniire n kpa ta hɛri, newea ani sela la maa n du u ni. Aŋ kpaubuu tɛɛ nɛr la maa wia n pariŋ.

ref: and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
text: Durnya hɛssi nɛra maa daŋ humuu, di hum u biibaal ni u naana maa guŋŋ di ra ba saŋa la u hɛri n niŋ chol. Denii ú hɛri nɛra birgi hɛrkpila ni koorizenaa balaa.

ref: This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease.
text: Ka di hɛri bɛl nɛra gɛɛ koora maa waa haŋ wa sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, n daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii tɛr ba digna guŋŋ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza wa chɔgi baa nyaamm. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar.
text: Awia, ií gilɛɛ nuu ra tɛɛ ii dɔgtɛɛkara hina, ii vugra, ii nɛra la n ɔɔ ra bagli ii deeza zɛɛzi ani hila la n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ií gilɛɛ waa hum Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza la.

ref: If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed.
text: Wiŋɔzi la baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ ia la maa ɛɛ karaa, a daŋ wer lizi ia hɛri naa biini, di gil n duŋŋi ia lii u biini, ií siuzi.

ref: But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
text: Ka hɛri la maa nɛra n niŋ sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, di ra humuu, n daŋ gil a guŋ hɛri naa nɛra haa du ba himmaa hɛri biini, di par a di. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said: Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
text: A keŋ amaniye naa himmaanii n lizi tɛɛ Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia, di ŋɔ, “Í ni i nɛra maa ra sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra, di ra humuu, denii ií maa dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned.
text: Bɛɛ n baani í ni i nɛra gil laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ gil a kpu hɛri la maa hina, n niŋ vɛɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra sɛɛi, kpu iai?

ref: Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies.
text: Ií gilɛɛ wa nuu di ra tɛɛ dɔgtɛɛkara hina la n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ii gilɛɛ waa sɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza dɔɔra la. Ba ra dar iabuu.

ref: Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
text: Kɔraawiizi sɔnnɛ ba kpa di kanni guŋ kara di ra tɛɛ ia la. Waa lɛi hum baa. Awia, u daŋ duŋŋi ia lii bɔnnaa, bá kpu ii ni a keŋ dɔgtɛɛkara hina naa maa. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said: Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying!
text: Denii n jaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni a nɛra maa be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií gilɛɛ wa nuu ra tɛɛ dɔgtɛɛkara hina la n na ŋɔ dí ba daŋ paagi n Dia kuna, di bir lii Babilɔn ba filaŋkeŋ maa la. Karaa ba ra kanni.

ref: If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra nuu ba be! Ií ra hum Babilɔn koori, di na iihinaa! Bɛɛwiarɛ bolzeŋ naa purgei?

ref: If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem.
text: Di ba ɛɛ n dɔgtɛɛzii wibii maa, di dɔɔ n wiŋɔɔlii, gil ba suŋŋi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ lugɔ n gilɛɛ gil bá wàá paagi kuna la n kawɛɛ n Dia, Juda kooridia ani Jɛrusalɛm biine di ra kaali Babilɔn.

ref: will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: ‘Ba daŋ paagaa kaali Babilɔn, a du de guŋŋ di ra ba hɔpizii la min niŋ ba a bɔr. Denii n bir kpaa ba di wa du bɔnnaa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening,
text: A bina himmaa biini, Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii baaguzi anuehiŋ biinii, Azur biibaal Hanania dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ n lii Gibiɔn ŋɔ wia n be Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni a nɛra maa see, di ŋɔ,

ref: he told me that the Lord had said: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves.
text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ chɔgi Babilɔn koori la fɔŋŋa.

ref: And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia.
text: Binni anɛɛ biini, n daŋ paagi kuna la maa Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n paawɛ lii n Dia kaali Babilɔn la, di bir ba.

ref: King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
text: N daŋ kaa kpogli Jɛhɔyakim biibaal Juda Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni banla maa baŋ laurɛɛ lii Juda kaali Babilɔn la, di bir ba, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ chɔgi Babilɔn koori fɔŋŋa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
text: Denii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia bir ŋɔ Hanania be, Kɔraawiizi kizeehina ni nɛra la maa n chigɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la see,

ref: Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home.
text: “Guŋ wesso! Kɔ́raawiizi ɛɛ guŋ! Kɔ́raawiizi gil i wiŋɔzi naa maa ɛɛ wibii lugɔ u daŋ bir paagi kuna la maa baŋ paagɛɛ lii Kɔraawiizi Dia biini kaali Babilɔn ni banla baŋ laurɛɛ kaali de la, di bir ba.

ref: But let me remind you and everyone else
text: Ama, a nuu gunla min niŋ ŋɔ tɛɛ i ni nɛra naa maa n du ɛnnaa.

ref: that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease.
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la n ŋɔ wia saŋa kpila maa n bɛrɛɛ, mɔɔ ka n ge nii saŋa wa hel naa, ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ laal, hɛhchɔg ni wiilchɔgii daŋ chol hɛrkpila ni ba kossi maa ni.

ref: Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
text: Ka dɔgtɛɛ la maa n na ŋɔ bampirsɔna wia, di u wiŋɔzi hiŋ haŋ wa ɛɛ wibii, guŋwaa, waabuu Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ himmaa.”

ref: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it.
text: Denii Hanania lau napattaa baŋaa daa la n du n baŋaa la lizi, di kuuguu ta,

ref: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
text: ka ŋɔ a nɛra maa be, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Keŋ himmaanii ń lizi buntɔga la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n chug hɛssi hina maa la, binni anɛɛ biini.’ ” A guŋ n wa ɛɛwɛ tuŋ, mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa kaali.

ref: and a little while later, the Lord told me
text: Hanania n wa lizi a daa n baŋaa la, a waa birgee ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: to go back and say to Hananiah: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la daŋ kpa napattaa lugbii hora du hɛssi maa hina baŋaazi, bá ra hum Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza. N daŋ gil pir sela gba ra sɛɛ u dɔɔra.”

ref: Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N na nyiŋŋi n liziibuu durnya naa biini. I daŋ siu bina naa biini, dikuu hiŋ ŋɔ ń nɛra vɛɛŋ wia.’ ”

ref: Two months later, Hananiah died.
text: A bina hiŋ baaguzi aniidaanɛɛhiŋ biinii, dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ Hanania siu.

ref: I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia.
text: Saŋa la Koori Jɛhɔyachin ni u maa n ɛɛ wiche, koori zɛɛsogna ani Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina sitɔɔra, di kpa banla n zum nonee huma, ba lauri lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali la harbɔɔrɛ, a wii naa ɛɛ.

ref: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
text: N kpa hɔnnaabuu tɛɛ Safan biibaal Ɛlasa ni Hilkia biibaal Gɛmaria, banla Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia n hummɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza be la. Kenne a hɔŋ ŋɔ,

ref: that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you
text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ ra tɛɛ banla maa uŋ gillɛ ba lauri lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la.

ref: to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them.
text: ‘Ií ma diini so, di dau kooni, á lii diwee tɛɛ ia, ií ra di.

ref: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
text: Ií paagi haana di lul biizi, di nyiŋŋi haana tɛɛ ii biibaala, di gil ii biihaana ge yuu, di lul biizi, ii wazi, di gilɛɛ waa ka tama de.

ref: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
text: Ií ra nyiŋŋi bampirsɔna ni nyɛɛlaa ra tɛɛ bolzeŋ la miŋ la ii ni la biini. Ií ra suŋŋi wiizi, ú kissi de, ii ge gba na kissaa, ii wia maa nyɛɛli.

ref: I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, n zum jinazi la miŋ tawɛɛ dikuu ii wiarɛ, anla n niŋ gil ii nyɛɛli. Ii tɔɔraa wia lɛi. Jinazi la n niŋ gil ii dɔɔ tamii kɛrɛ bɛl wiarɛ.

ref: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
text: Denii ii yiriŋ, di ba wa suŋŋiŋ, ń nuu tɛɛ ia.

ref: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
text: Ii daŋ nyiŋŋiŋ di naŋ, dikuu iin niŋ nyiŋŋiŋ ni ii biine maa wia.

ref: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
text: Aŋhinabe, ii daŋ ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ yaabuu dɔgtɛɛzi, Babilɔn.”

ref: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
text: Awia, ii banla maa miŋ duŋŋɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm kaali Babilɔn la, ií ra nuu n wiŋɔzi.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i kpa i himmaa sɔnnɛ, di sɛbi hɔna tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hina, Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Maasɛya biibaal Zɛfania ani kizeehina maa.

ref: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
text: A hɔŋ biini, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi liziibuu i lɛɛ Jɛhɔyada bɔr, di ɛɛ u kizeehiŋ, di ra binni u Dia. Lau chuglahiŋ la maa n na yir u hiŋ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ, di duu daa, di du u baŋaa ge yɔlɔzi.

ref: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
text: Bɛɛ n baani haa a kennaa kpawɛɛ dau Jɛrɛmia la n lii Anatɔf, di ra yir u hiŋ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ lai?

ref: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
text: Kenne u tili ŋɔ yaa be Babilɔn. A daŋ birgi. Awia, ií ma diini so, di dau kooni, á lii diwee tɛɛ ia, ii ra di.”

ref: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ Zɛfania n wa na Sɛmaaya hɔŋ la, u karmuu tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia.

ref: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
text: “La ga ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ nɛra la maa baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrduma la, ‘Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Nɛhɛlam hinuu Sɛmaaya wia. Dikuu uŋ ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi ia di du ii ni, haali miŋ wɔɔ hummɛ, ka u gil ii yardi kara wia,

ref: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: n daŋ tɛr u ni u naanna digna. U nɛr maa wàá ka ka nɛra naa biini, ú na winanaa la min niŋ ɛɛ tɛɛ n nɛra, dikuu uŋ ŋɔ bá vɛɛŋ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
text: “Sɛbi wia naa maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi naa du hɔŋ biini.

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
text: “N nuu ɔnsii wiraare, u ɛɛ ɔnsii werge wiraa, waa bampirsɔna hor ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
text: Lɔ nfɛrɛ na, baal daŋ wer lulaa? Ka bɛɛ n baani n na baal maa n lau u hia alugɔ hilula n lɔ haannɛi? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ nɛr maa siwee chogli wogliwoglei?

ref: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
text: Hɔpizichuma ra bau, hàá wer kpa hɔpizii maa mɛgzuu. U daŋ ɛɛ hɔpizichuma tɛɛ n nɛra, ka n daŋ lɛɛ baa lii u biini.

ref: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
text: Di a hɔpizii wa hello, n daŋ lizi baa lii hɔɔhraa sunnaa ni ba wichɔgaa la maa n vɔɔzi baa la biini. N daŋ lizi baa lii hɛrdumazi la baŋ duwɛɛ la biine. Ba wàá ka ɛɛ yoma. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
text: Bá jaa ra hum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum ni Koori Deevid naana la min niŋ tɔ kora.

ref: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
text: N nɛra Izrɛl hina, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, ií gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra ra sa. Izrɛl hina, wibii maa, n daŋ lɛɛ ia lii hɛhjaŋa la baŋ lauri ia kaali la biine. Ii daŋ kaa bir ba bol, di wa dɔɔ bampirsɔna, di so pɛrɛtɛ. Nɛr maa wàá ka ɔnzi ia.

ref: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
text: N daŋ ba ii be, di wa lɛɛ ia. N daŋ dim hɛssi hina la maa miŋ yaari ia ii ga du ba biine la, ka màá dim iawaa. Màá vɛɛ ii digna tɛraa, ka di n waa tɛr ii digna, n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ ni wibii. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ii ŋmɛra waa chaai dɔɔwɛ, a ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá wer tuŋ.

ref: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
text: Nɛr maa waa hoo un ninna binni ia, ii ŋmɛra naa waa chaai dɔɔwɛ, ii waa chaai tamii dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
text: Banla maa ii ni baa n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ suuh ii wiarɛ, ba baga lɛi kaa ii wia. N lɔ iabuu alugɔ ii dɔm, di tɛr ii digna manaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii bilchɔg kannɔɔ, ii dɔɔ biinikpola ge werge maa.

ref: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
text: Ka banla maa n chɔgi ia, ba dɔma daŋ chɔgi baa. Ba daŋ lauri ii dɔma maa kaali hɛrdumazi. Banla maa n foozi ii kuna, ba daŋ foozi ba hora. Banla maa n na sunni ia, n daŋ sunni baa.

ref: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
text: N daŋ kaa gil ii dɔɔ alaanfia, di chaa ii ŋmɛra la, haali ii dɔma n na ŋɔ, ‘Ziɔn hina ɛɛ kuntaalaarɛ, nɛr maa baga waa hoo ba be.’ Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ kuari n nɛra soŋŋi ba himmaa hɛri, di suŋ dia maa hina ni. Nɛra daŋ bir ma Jɛrusalɛm maa, bá kooridia chi bɔr la n dɛkkɛ.

ref: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
text: Ba daŋ yir yira, di ra chɔliŋ, di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna. N daŋ kissi baa, bá wazi jaa, ba wàá ka tama. N daŋ kissi baa, bá dɔɔ girme, ba wàá kaa ra gbɛlli baa.

ref: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
text: Ba biizi daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ faala hina, ń kaa kuari ba bola maa ma, á chi chigigi. N daŋ tɛr banla maa n faa ra sunni baa la digna.

ref: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
text: Ba koori daŋ lii ba himmaa hɛri, ba sitɔɔri ge gba lii ba himmaa nɛra biini. Di n wa yiruu, u daŋ ba n be. Anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛ ba n be, di mɔɔ yittɛi? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: You will be my people, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Awia, ii daŋ ɛɛ n nɛra, n ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.”

ref: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
text: Ií na, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ pezeŋ n tawɛɛ ra ba, peu n na ba kpegzi ni di ra kɔɔ, ú wa lɔ wichɔgɛɛra nyuuni.

ref: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
text: Kɔraawiizi baaŋ la wàá bir har, di waa u kipar maa nawɛɛ. Di saŋa bɛl wa hello, ii daŋ zum a zɛɛ.

ref: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ń ɛɛ Izrɛl hina dizi maa Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum, ba ge ɛɛ n nɛra.

ref: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
text: Nɛra la n chɔwɛɛ lii siu biini, ba wia daŋ pariŋ hɛribɔduma biini, n daŋ ba wa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina heezaa.”

ref: Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say: Israel, I will always love you; that's why I've been so patient and kind.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ba yaa benii, saŋa bɛl n bɛrɛɛ, di wa ŋɔ, “N nɔŋŋi iabuu ni nɔŋŋaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ, di haa vɛɛ ra bagli ia n nɔŋŋaa.

ref: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
text: Izrɛl hina, n daŋ kaa kuari ia soŋŋi, ii kaa kpa kuŋyigzaa, di ra sa ni bɔsɔna.

ref: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
text: Samaria giŋgimee la nyuunii, ii kaa dau ii kooni, di duu ii grepu daazi. Ii banla n niŋ duua, daŋ di a nɔna.

ref: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
text: Saŋa bɛl ra bau, tauduura lɔ wile Ɛfram giŋgimee nyuuni, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií ba ya la Bizeŋ Ziɔn n du Jɛrusalɛm, Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum la be.’ ”

ref: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií yir yira ni bɔsɔna, di ra tɛɛ Izrɛl hina n ɛɛ Jekɔb naanna. Ií chaasi ra tɛɛ hɛri la n kaali hɛssi maa. Ií gil bá nuu iinna chɔluu, di ra ŋɔ, ‘N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, lɛɛ i nɛra Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ.’

ref: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
text: N daŋ lizi baa lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di chaali baa lii bɔr maa. Gbɛraa ni nyuŋŋa maanii niŋ jaa ba ni. Haana la n kpogli hizi ni banla n na nyiŋŋi lulaa. Ba daŋ du kpil werge, di bir ba a hɛri.

ref: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
text: Min niŋ kpogli baa di ra ba la, ba danna wii, di ra suŋŋi wiizi. N daŋ tɔ ba see, gɔŋa n dɔɔ niiri kɛraa, ŋmɛnizi la n du kpantalaŋ ni, ba wàá lɔɔzi naazi di jiŋli. N ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hina mɛɛ, Ɛfram ge ɛɛ n biibambilugli.”

ref: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Durnya hɛssi hina, ií ra nuu n be, di gil n wiŋɔzi naa yaari la hɛhjaŋa muuzenaa nuuzi. N yaari n nɛraa, ka n daŋ bir chaali baa, di ra binni ba ni alugɔ penɔɔni n na binni u peeza la.

ref: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
text: Ba daŋ ba Bizeŋ Ziɔn nyuu, di waa yir yira ni bɔsɔna, ba bɔra ra pur, dikuu kuna la miŋ tɛɛ baa wia. Mia, siŋfalii, nuu, peeza ani nauna la miŋ tɛɛ baa wia. Ba daŋ jaa ɛɛ lugɔ kambol n sɔɔnɛɛ nɛnnɛ, bá dɔɔ kunla maa banna nyiŋŋi.

ref: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
text: Denii suŋgure jaa ra sa ni bɔsɔna, biipɔllaa ni nɛzɛŋzi maa jaa. N daŋ gil ba wiraa birgi bɔsɔna, di tɛɛ baa bɔsɔna, ka gil biinichɔg.

ref: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
text: N daŋ tɛɛ n kizeehina diunanaa werge, di tɛɛ n nɛra kuna la maa banna nyiŋŋi werge. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ba nuu nɛbɛl loobiire Rama, unna wii werge maa. Rachɛllɛ ra wii dikuu u biizi wia, ba laafuu ra huhzi, dikuu u biizi la n waa hoo wia.”

ref: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Gil wiraa ka lau i hiŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, i daŋ na i huma kinturgaa. Ba daŋ lii ba dɔma hɛri bir ba. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
text: N nuuwɔɔ Izrɛl hina n na ŋɔ ni biinichɔg, ‘Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, yaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sekpoŋlii, ka i bagli yaabuu gunla yaa n ninna sɛɛ i dɔɔra. Awia, bir yaa ni ba, yaa ɛɛ siryaa yá bir ba i be.

ref: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
text: Yaa faa bir hattɛ kpui, yaa kaa ra nyiŋŋuu yá bir ba i be filaŋkeŋ. Hiŋ wa tɛr yaa digna tuŋ la, yaa willi yaa nyuunii ni biinichɔg. Yaa faa di hiihzii, di ŋmaabi, dikuu yaa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa yaa bichalli saŋa maa wia.’ ”

ref: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, ii ɛɛ n biinɔŋŋaarɛ, biizi la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ werge. Di n haŋ wa yir ii sɔna, anna fɛ ii wiarɛ ni nɔŋŋaa. N bampirii lau iabuu, n daŋ suŋ ii ni.

ref: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
text: Ií baŋ kuna ŋmɛnikɛraa, á ra bagli bɔra. Á ra bagli ŋmɛnɛɛ la iin niŋ ga. Izrɛl hina, ií bir ba, ií bir ba ii bola.

ref: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
text: Ɛrɛɛ ií juuri di birgi magɛi, biizi la wia n waa wibii dɔɔwɛi? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ ɛɛ wifalii bɛl durnya naa biini, ú kur werge maa, alugɔ haaŋ n na guu baal.” Kɔraawiizi nɛra kɛrɛbɛl nyɛɛlaa wia

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, “Di n wa lii ii ni hɛrdumazi la baŋ lauri ia kaali la, di bir ba, ii nɛra la n du Juda hɛri ni u bola daŋ kaa ra ŋɔ wia naa, ‘Kɔ́raawiizi kissi Bizennaniinanii Ziɔn la n ɛɛ u duuribɔr la.’

ref: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
text: Nɛra daŋ kpau so Juda ni u bola maa, patta ni banla maa n kpogli ba peeza di vol ra gaagi.

ref: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
text: N daŋ tɛɛ banla n kuuhwɛ la fɔŋŋa, di tɛɛ banla maa n huahgɛɛ diwee, bá di.”

ref: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
text: Denii nɛra jaa ŋɔ, “Yaa chɔɔgi dɔzii, di izi fogofogo.”

ref: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ gil nɛra ni sela su Izrɛl ni Juda hɛssi maa.

ref: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
text: Gunla miŋ haŋ sɔɔni bɔra di kpuzi baa, di taa baa ha, di kpegli baa, di chɔgi baa, di kpa hɛhchɔg ta ba ni la, gunnɛ n sɔɔni bɔra di lau baa bá chi chigigi lugɔ kunduulaa.

ref: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
text: A guŋ saŋa, nɛra wàá ka ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛwaa di grepu nɔnnyɛgaa, ka ba biizi nyina lɛɛ ra nyiiri.’

ref: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
text: Ka bɛl maa daŋ siu, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa wia, unla maa n di a grepu nɔnnyɛga, u himmaa nyinaa niŋ nyiiri.”

ref: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ń ni Izrɛl ni Juda hina ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii.

ref: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
text: Wàá ɛɛ lugɔ nuukpaŋ la n ni ba naabaala n faa ɛɛwɛ, saŋa la miŋ kpogli baa lii Ijip hɛri la. Haali miŋ faa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ ba jaari gba, ka ba chɔgi a guŋ nuukpannɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Nuukpaŋfalii la n ni Izrɛl hina n niŋ ɛɛu keŋ, n daŋ kpa n Gbɔg du ba biine, di sɛbaa du ba bampiree biine. N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum, bá ge ɛɛ n nɛra. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
text: A wàá ka ɛɛ lugɔ nɛr maa n niŋ bagli u niwee gɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ, di ŋɔ, ‘A wesso hiŋ zum Kɔraawiizi,’ dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maanii niŋ zumiŋ, nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa. N daŋ suŋ ba ni, di gil ba wia la n waa deŋlee la tɛɛ baa. Màá ka liizi ba wichɔgaa wia maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Minuu ɔɔ gil wiizi ra chaani hɔpizaa, di gil baagu ni chinchiŋwilaa ra chaani hamuŋa. Minuu ɔɔ koozi muuzeŋ u ra lɔ, di ra kɔɔ la. N sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.

ref: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Gunla wiizi furaa ni u cholaa n niŋ du de di hanna la la, gunnɛ Izrɛl ge du de di birgi mag.”

ref: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Di nɛr maa daŋ wer mɛgzi chiŋ, di kaa wer pigzi zum gunla miŋ chiŋŋi hɛri zɛɛ, guŋwaa, n ge gba daŋ wer vɛɛ Izrɛl naanna maa ta, dikuu wia la maa baŋ ɛɛwɛ wia.”

ref: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ban niŋ kuari Jɛrusalɛm ma, ú ɛɛ n bolzeŋ, di chi Hananɛl Diijaŋ di ga hel Sirii Dominuuzeŋ la.

ref: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
text: U magbɔɔ daŋ lii de wiicholii di ga hel Garɛb giŋgimii, di bir ga hel Gɔa.

ref: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
text: Waluu la banna hug nɛra, di kaa ra ta hɔɔhri de la maa ni bɔwillaa la maa, di ga hel Kidrɔn Waluu n du wiifurii, guŋŋ di ga hel Zagu Dominuuzeŋ, daŋ ɛɛ bɔnaninanii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka puri a bolzeŋ gɛɛ di chɔguu.”

ref: The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia.
text: Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia kora dii binni fi hinnɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wia tɛŋ. Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ge kora dii binni fidiŋmantannaazi hinnɛ guŋ.

ref: At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards.
text: A saŋa, di Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra ballɔ wa fɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm, di faa tɔŋ du Juda kooridia tauduura diŋŋee.

ref: Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said: I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem.
text: Juda Koori Zɛdɛkiaa faa tɔŋ de, di ra nyiŋŋi u na n chollibɔr, di ŋɔ n ɔɔ siiu, di ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil Babilɔn koori kpegli a bolzeŋ,

ref: King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face.
text: Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia wàá na bɔr chɔ. Ba daŋ kpau du Babilɔn koori nonee. U daŋ nau siwii ni, ú nuu ŋɔ wia.

ref: Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: U daŋ lau Koori Zɛdɛkia kaali Babilɔn, denii u ga du ka ń jaa ɛɛu gunla minna nyiŋŋi. Di u hanna yoo Babilɔn hina, ka wàá wer kpegli baa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be lugɔ

ref: Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
text: n naara Salum biibaal Hanamɛl daŋ ba n be di wa ŋɔ, “Yau n koo la n du Anatɔf, dikuubɛɛwiai, hinuu n lulli himmaa, i dɛg lugɔ í yawuu.”

ref: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
text: Gunla himmaa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la, n baal Hanamɛl ba n be a diŋŋee biini, di wa ŋɔ, “Yau n koo la n du Anatɔf, n du Bɛnjamin hɛri la. Dikuubɛɛwiai, a dɛkkɔɔ hiŋ yawuu, ú ɛɛ i hor.” N jaa zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔliirɛ guŋ.

ref: from Hanamel, and so I did. The price was
text: Awia, n yau a koo Hanamɛl be, di turguu saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau fidaaniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything.
text: “Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, hinuu kpa i fɔŋŋazeŋ ta chiŋ ni hɛri, wiimaa waa kpol i be.

ref: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
text: N kpaa tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal Baruk naabaal n ɛɛ Masɛya la. N baal Hanamɛl ni banla n di daansɛɛ di jag ba nonee, Jus hina la n soge a diŋŋee la maa sibɔɔ.

ref: I told Baruch that the Lord had said: Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
text: “Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ í kpa hɔna naa, unla baŋ tɔwɛɛ ni unla n waa tɔwɛɛ la maa, di du tɔg biini, á wer birgi.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ diini, kooni, daazi ani grepu daazi kooni maanii, bá kaa yau hɛri naa biini.” Jɛrɛmia wiisuŋŋaa wia

ref: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Hinuu bagli nɔŋŋaa ra tɛɛ nɛra kagboŋa, ka ɔɔ tɛrgi nɛra digna dikuu ba mɛɛwaa wichɔgaa wia. Hinuu dɔɔ sɔŋ ni kpegzi werge. I sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.

ref: With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
text: I ɔɔ ra ta jinananaarɛ, di ra ɛɛ wizenaa. I zum nɛr maa wiɛɛlaarɛ, di ɔɔ turgi bɛl maa u wiɛɛlaa kim.

ref: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
text: I faa ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wiarɛ Ijip hɛri, haali di haa ra ɛɛa wa lii ni zinaa, Izrɛl hina ni newea maa biini, a guŋ gil i dɔɔ sɔŋ bɔr maa.

ref: You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt.
text: I kpa witittaa ni nuukpuuri wiarɛ du yaa dɔma ɔnsii werge, di kpa i fɔŋŋa ni i banonii lizi i nɛra Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
text: Hinuu tɛɛ baa hɛrsum naa hiŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ i daŋ tɛɛ ba naabaala la.

ref: But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster.
text: Baŋ wa ballɛ di wa lɛɛ a hɛri dɔɔ, ka ba wɛɛ hiŋŋɛ gɛɛ di hiŋ i Gbɔg. Ba waa gunla hiŋ ŋɔ ba ɛɛ la ɛɛwɛ. Awiarɛ i kpa hɛhchɔg naa ta ba ni la.

ref: Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
text: Babilɔn hina wa teŋri daazii teli a bolzeŋ koŋlii ni, di ta pizenaa bar a bolzeŋ maa, bá wer tinni zuu de, di lɔ baa. Laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgii daŋ gil bá kpegli a bolzeŋ. I nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ wii la maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, hinuu ŋɔ di n yau a koo naa, nɛra naa n di u daansɛɛ naa see, haali Babilɔn hina n na ba bá wa foozi a bolzeŋ dɔɔ gba.”

ref: The Lord explained:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
text: “N ɛɛ newea maa Kɔraawiizii, wii bɛl kpolloo tɛŋŋ?

ref: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
text: Awia, n na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa bolzeŋ naa du Babilɔn laallɔɔra ni ba Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee, bá kpegluu.

ref: The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
text: Ba daŋ wa pig a bolzeŋ, di fuuh u ni diini la nɛra n na fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma a salli ra tɛɛ vug Baal, di ta siŋ ra tɛɛ vuga aŋhina ge, di ra fuuh n baaŋ la wia.

ref: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
text: Haali ba kpa ba vuga la miŋ kiiwee chiŋŋi n Dia biini, di doŋuu.

ref: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
text: Ba ma mbusu lizibɔraa tɛɛ vug Baal, Bɛn Hinɔm Waluu biini, di kpa ba biizi lizi mbusuzi ra tɛɛ vug Mɔlɛk. Maa ba be ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ bá ɛɛ guŋ, maa fɛwɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ sɛɛ ɛɛ a keŋ wiɛɛlaa naa, di gil Juda hina ɛɛ wichɔgaa.”

ref: Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrɛmia, a nɛra ra ŋɔu lugɔ laal, lɔzi ani wiilchɔgiirɛ niŋ gil bolzeŋ naa zuu Babilɔn koori nonee biini. A nuu gunla miŋ dɔɔwɛ n ŋɔ.

ref: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
text: N daŋ chaali baa lii bɔra la maa miŋ kpa n baaŋ di yaari baa, ba ga du la, di bir ba ba ni bɔnnaa, bá wa so pɛrɛtɛ.

ref: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
text: Ba daŋ ɛɛ n nɛra, ń ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum.

ref: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
text: Kennaa miŋ haŋ kpa tɔɔrɔɔ ni dɔgnya ta nɛra naa ni naa, gunnɛ ń gil ba nyɛɛli, gunla miŋ ŋɔ nua la.

ref: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
text: A nɛra ra ŋɔu lugɔ hɛri naa daŋ du lugɔ hɛribɔduma, bɔr la newea gɛɛ sela n waa duwɛɛ, ka bá kpau tɛɛ Babilɔn hina. Ka ba daŋ kaa yau kooni u biini.

ref: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ka saŋa bɛl daŋ wa hel, nɛra bir kpa ba saliŋhuŋŋu di ba waa yau kooni. Ba daŋ jag nonibee di di daansɛɛ Bɛnjamin hɛri, boljigzi la n bar Jɛrusalɛm, Juda bola ani giŋgimee hɛssi bola la n du wiicholii ni Nɛgɛv la, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil ba bir nyɛɛli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
text: Yiriŋ, n daŋ sɛɛ, di ŋɔ i be wizenaa ni wisuahlaa la hiŋ waa zummɛ.

ref: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
text: Annii maa har, n daŋ chaa baa, bá dɔɔ alaanfia, di dɔɔ bampirsɔna werge, di so pɛrɛtɛ.

ref: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
text: N daŋ kpogli Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa lii bɔra la baŋ lauri baa kaali la, di bir ba, di wa kuari baa soŋŋi, gunla baŋ faa duwɛɛ la.

ref: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
text: N daŋ lizi ba wichɔgaa la maa baŋ ɛɛŋ ba ni, di gil ba wichɔgaa ni baŋ vɛɛŋ la tɛɛ baa.

ref: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
text: Jɛrusalɛm daŋ gil n dɔɔ sɔŋ, bɔsɔna ani girme, bá ra chɔliŋ durnya hɛssi hina maa n nuu winanaa la miŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛu la sibɔɔ. Denii ɔnsii lau baa bá bɔra ra sa, di ba wa nuu gunla la miŋ gillɛ a bolzeŋ nyɛɛli di dɔɔ bampirsɔna wia.”

ref: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛra ra ŋɔ bɔnnaa wiarɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ diŋgelaa. Nɛra gɛɛ sela waa hoo de. Wibiire ba ŋɔ. Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda bolzenaa maanii chɔɔwɛ woo. Newea ni sela waa hoo de. Ka ii daŋ kaa wa nuu,

ref: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
text: nɛra n ninna chaasi ni bɔsɔna, di ra nuu haŋfalii ni u jaari loobee ni banla n kpa kuna ra ba, bá wa jaamiŋ, n Dia biini. Ba danna ŋɔ, ‘Ií ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la jaaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wia wessoo, u nɔŋŋaa waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ.’ N daŋ gil a hɛri naa nyɛɛli werge maa, gunla uŋ faa duwɛɛ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ gil nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl ni Juda hina la, su u maga.

ref: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
text: A saŋa hiŋ, n daŋ lizi koori la wia n deŋlee lii Koori Deevid naanna biini. Waabuu ninna ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee, di ra di wibii, a hɛri maa biini.

ref: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Juda hina daŋ na lɛɛi, Jɛrusalɛm hina ge so pɛrɛtɛ. Sɔnnaabuu ba wa kpa ra yir a bolzeŋ, ‘Kɔraawiizii Yaa Lɛɛri.’ ”

ref: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Koori Deevid ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá nyaa nɛr la n niŋ di Izrɛl kora

ref: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
text: gɛɛ n kizeehina la n ɛɛ Levi dee la gba wàá nyaa nɛr la n niŋ ɔɔ wa chi n see, di ra lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, di ra fuuh mbusuzi lizaa mia kuna, di lizi mbusuzi lizaa kuna di ra tɛŋ.”

ref: Then the Lord told me:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
text: “N ni hɔpizaa ni hamuŋa ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ba saŋa la n dɛg u balaa. A keŋ nuukpaŋ naa wàá wer chɔgi maa.

ref: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
text: Gunnɛ n ni Koori Deevid ni Levi dee la n ɛɛ n kizeehina di ra humiŋ la, nuukpaŋ la wàá wer chɔgi maa la.

ref: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
text: N daŋ gil n balii Koori Deevid naanna ni Levi dee la n na humiŋ la du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa baŋ wàá wer kur gɛɛ gunla baŋ wàá wer kur hɛɛhriichaa la.”

ref: The Lord also said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
text: “I nuu gunla nɛra naa n na ŋɔ lugɔ n vɛɛ Izrɛl ni Juda la miŋ lizɛɛ tɛɛ n hinnɛ. Awia, ba ra gbɛlli baabuu. Ba waa kaa ra yir baa hɛri bɛl hina.

ref: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
text: Di n ni hɔpizaa ni hamuŋa faa waa nuukpaŋ ɛɛwɛ, di dau chiŋ ni hɛri gbɔgni,

ref: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
text: guŋwaa, n daŋ faa vɛɛ Jekɔb ni n balii Koori Deevid naanna, di vɛɛ u biibaal bɛl lizaa ú di kora Abraham, Aizik ani Jekɔb naanna ni. N daŋ bir kpogli baa lii bɔra la baŋ lauri baa kaali la, di ba, di suŋ ba ni, di gil ba nyɛɛli.”

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
text: Saŋa la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u laallɔɔra, u kossi ani nɛra la maa n du u kora diiribɔr n faa ra naa Jɛrusalɛm hina ni bola la maa n baruu la,

ref: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, “La Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia be, di ga ŋɔ u be lugɔ n na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa bolzeŋ naa du Babilɔn koori nonee, ú fuuuh.

ref: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
text: Awia, hàá na bɔr chɔ, ba daŋ lawii wa tɛu. I daŋ na Babilɔn koori ni siwii, í nuu so ŋɔ wia tɛɛ dɔŋa, ka ba kpoglii kaali Babilɔn.

ref: Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle.
text: Ama, Koori Zɛdɛkia, a nuu gunla minna ŋɔ i wia. Ba wàá kpui laal biini.

ref: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
text: I daŋ siu ni bampirsɔna. Gunla baŋ ɔɔ faa fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di hug i naabaala la n di kossi mɔɔ ka tɛi, di tɛɛ baa girme la, guŋ himmaanii bá fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma tɛi. Ba danna wii i lee, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa koori siuwɔɔ!’ Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
text: Denii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia ŋɔ wia naa maa tɛɛ Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia, Jɛrusalɛm biini.

ref: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
text: Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra la n haa ra yoo Jɛrusalɛm ni bolzenaa la n kawɛɛ Juda hɛri, ba ra yiraa Lakis ni Azɛka la, a bɛnnɛ faa haa dɔɔ koŋliikpega baraa, Juda hɛri. Yoma n niŋ na bahinaa wia

ref: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
text: Awia, a nɛra maa ni ba sitɔɔra sɛɛ lugɔ ba daŋ gil ba yoma na bahinaa, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka lau baa ɛɛ yoma. Ba jaa sɛɛ, di ta baa.

ref: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
text: Ka a harbɔɔ, ba bir ba nfɛssi, di kaa lauri baa di wa ɛɛ yoma.

ref: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
text: “Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ni ii naabaala ɛɛ nuukpannɛ, saŋa la miŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri la, hɛri la baŋ faa ɛɛ yoma la. N faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ
