ref: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
text: binni aniidaanɛɛ maa biini, bɛ́l maa ɔɔ ta Hibru hinuu la n kpa u hiŋ yoo tɛu. Di u wa humii binni anumbɛl, tau ŋmɛnɛɛ, ú dɔɔ u hiŋ. Ka ii mɛɛwaa faa waa sɛɛwɛ tɛŋ gɛɛ di hiŋ n nua.

ref: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
text: Ka ii kaa bir ii nfɛssi, di gbɛlliŋ. Ii maa kaa bir lau ii yoma la iiŋ tawɛɛ a par baa la, di fir baa, ba kaa ɛɛ yoma.

ref: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ii gbɛllimbuu. Ii waa sɛɛwɛ ta ii lulla Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛɛ, bá dɔɔ bahinaa. Awia, miŋwaa daŋ ta ia ŋmɛnɛɛ, ii dɔɔ iihinaa, bá kpu ia laal biini, wiilchɔgii ni lɔchɔgii jaa. N daŋ gil hɛssi hina maa nua kpu ii wia.

ref: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
text: Saŋa la Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim n wa di Juda kora la, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
text: “La ga yir Rɛkab domee hina, bá ba Kɔraawiizi Dia diibizi la bɛl biini, di wa tɛɛ baa siŋ bá nyɔɔ.”

ref: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
text: Denii n la ga yir Habazinia biibaal Jɛrɛmia ge biibaal Jaazania ni u lulla ni u biibaala maa, baabuu Rɛkab domee hina,

ref: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
text: di kpogli baa wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Igdalia biibaal Hanan biibaala chɔɔribɔr. A dia naa faa hiŋ a nabɔnzi hor la n hɔŋ Salum biibaal Maasɛya la n ɛɛ dominuuguuri hor ninɛɛ.

ref: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
text: Denii n kpa siŋ ni libizi tɛɛ baa, di ŋɔ, “Ií lɛɛ siŋ nyɔɔ!”

ref: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
text: Ka ba bir ŋɔ, “Yaa waa sinna nyɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa naabaal Rɛkab biibaal Jonadab ŋɔ yaa benii, ‘Ií ni ii naanna ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ siŋ.’

ref: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ yaa benii lugɔ yá gilɛɛ waa ma diini, di gilɛɛ waa dau kooni gɛɛ di waa duu grepu daazi kooni. Dí ya ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ annii bɛl maa, ka ɔɔ ra zuu tanti diini biine. Denii ya wer dɔɔ miibɔɔjaŋ, di du hɛri la yaa n ɛɛ famaraa naa biini.

ref: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
text: Ka Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n wa zuu hɛri naa di lɔ yaa, di lɛɛu dɔɔ la, yaa ŋɔ, ‘Ií ba ya chɔ lii Babilɔn ni Siiria laallɔɔra be, di kaali Jɛrusalɛm.’ Awiarɛ yaa ka Jɛrusalɛm biini la.”

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
text: “La ga ŋɔ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina be lugɔ di ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá helli wia, amɔ, ba wàá helli wia, di hiŋ n wiŋɔzia? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
text: Jonadab naanna faa hiŋ u nuarɛ, di vɛɛ siŋ nyɔɔi di wa lii ni zinaa. Ka n na ŋɔ wiarɛ di ra tɛɛ ia digiidigii, ka iawaa waa sɛɛwɛ ii nuu tɛŋ, di hiŋ n nua.

ref: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
text: N hum n dɔgtɛɛzii ii be, digiidigii. Ba ŋɔ ii be lugɔ ií bɛl maa gil u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa, di chɛr u manni. Ií gilɛɛ waa kuari vuga, di waa sɛɛ a dɔɔra. Denii ii wer du hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii ni ii naabaala la biini. Ka ii waa sɛɛwɛ nuu n be, di hiŋ n nua.

ref: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
text: Ka Jonadab naanna waa hiŋ u nuarɛ. Ka iawaa, waa sɛɛwɛ ii hiŋ n nua.

ref: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ ií ra nuu! N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔgni la maa miŋ ŋɔ a wia la, di ta Juda hina ni nɛra la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm ni. N ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ baa, ka ba waa nuuwɛ, di yir baa, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ.”

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
text: Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa ŋɔ Rɛkab domee hina la be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ii hiŋ ii naabaal Jonadab nuarɛ, di ɛɛ wia la maa uŋ dauwɛ tɛɛ ia la.

ref: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
text: Juda Koori Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biinii, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
text: “Kpa hɔŋ sɛbi wia la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi, di ra bagli Izrɛl ni Juda ani hɛssi la maa n kawɛɛ hina wia, di lii saŋa la miŋ faarɛɛ ŋɔ wia ra tɛi, Koori Jɔsia kora dii saŋa, di wa lii ni zinaa la.

ref: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
text: Aŋhinabe, di Juda hina wa nuu gunla minna nyiŋŋi ń kpa hɛhchɔgni ta ba ni, ba bɛl maa daŋ gil biinikpola wiɛɛlaa. Denii ń gil ba biinikpola ni ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.”

ref: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
text: Denii mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia yir Nɛria biibaal Baruk, di ŋɔ wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la di ra tɛu, u sɛbaa ra dau hɔŋ ni.

ref: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
text: Awia, n ŋɔ Baruk be, “Ba wan tɛɛwɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ lugɔ n kaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia biini.

ref: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
text: Awia, la Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ga karmi Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ i sɛbi dau a hɔŋ ni la tɛɛ a nɛra, ba nuuvɔɔi hɔpizii hɔl. Karmuu tɛɛ Juda hɛri nɛra la maa n lii bola di ba de la, bá maa nuu.

ref: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
text: Aŋhinabe, ba daŋ suŋŋi wiizi, di gil ba biinikpola wiɛɛlaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ɔnzi baabuu ni u baaŋfuuihchɔgii.”

ref: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
text: Gɛmaria biibaal Mikaaya, u naabaal ge ɛɛ Safan, n wa nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa la maa Baruk n karmɛɛ lii a hɔŋ biini la,

ref: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
text: u izi la kooridia karchi diibee la n du kooridia biini, bɔr la nabɔnzi la maa n faa chaalɛɛ la. Baabuu karchi Ɛlisama, Sɛmaaya biibaal Dɛlaaya, Akbɔ biibaal Ɛlnatan, Safan biibaal Gɛmaria, Hanania biibaal Zɛdɛkia ani ba nabɔnzi la maa n kawɛɛ.

ref: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
text: Mikaaya n wa ŋɔ wia la maa uŋ nuuwɛ Baruk n karmɛɛ, lii a hɔŋ biini tɛɛ a nɛra wa tuŋ,

ref: Then the officials sent Jehudi and Shelemiah to tell Baruch, “Bring us that scroll.” When Baruch arrived with the scroll,
text: a nabɔnzi maa hum Nɛtania biibaal Jɛhudi, u naabaal n ɛɛ Kusi biibaal Sɛlɛmia, dí u ga ŋɔ Baruk be, “Kpa hɔŋ la hiŋ karmɛɛ tɛɛ a nɛra la ba.” Awia, Baruk kpa a hɔŋ di la.

ref: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
text: Ba ŋɔ u be, “Gaafura, ka so hɛri di karmuu tɛɛ yaa.”

ref: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
text: Baŋ wa nuu wia la uŋ karmɛɛ tɛɛ baa la, ɔnsii lau baa, ba bir binni dɔŋa, ka ŋɔ Baruk be, “Yaa daŋ ga bagli wia naa tɛɛ koori.”

ref: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
text: Denii ba ŋɔ Baruk be, “Bagli yaa gunla hiŋ ɛɛwɛ sɛbi wia naa maa. Jɛrɛmiaa ŋɔa, i sɛbiaa?”

ref: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
text: Baruk ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, waabuu ŋɔa, n sɛbaa dau hɔnnaa ni.”

ref: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
text: Denii a nabɔnzi ŋɔ Baruk be, “Í ni Jɛrɛmia chɔ ga suah, di gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa ra zum bɔr la iiŋ duwɛɛ.”

ref: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
text: ka ŋɔ u biibaal Jɛramiil, Azriɛl biibaal Sɛraaya ani Abdiil biibaal Sɛlɛmia be lugɔ bá ga lau karchi Baruk ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia ba. Ka Kɔraawiizi faa kpa baa suah.

ref: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
text: A koori n wa fuuh a hɔŋ tuŋ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
text: “Kaa kpa hɔŋ bɛl, di sɛbi wia la maa hiŋ faa felee sɛbi dau unla Koori Jɛhɔyakim n fuuhwe la, di kaa dau u ni.

ref: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be lugɔ ń ŋɔ Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim be, ‘I fuuh a hɔnnɛ ka pɛɛzi Jɛrɛmia lugɔ bɛɛwiarɛ u sɛbi lugɔ Babilɔn koori daŋ ba wa chɔgi hɛri naa, di kpu a newea ni sela maanɛi?

ref: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
text: Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ra ŋɔ hìŋ́ Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim wia lugɔ i ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá dɔɔ nɛr la n niŋ so Koori Deevid koorikara ni. Di i wa siuwɔ, ba daŋ kpai ha bossee, wiizi kpui bɔchaaŋ, hamuŋa ge, ŋmɛnii chol i ni.

ref: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
text: N daŋ tɔɔri i ni i balaa ni i biizi maa, dikuu ii biinikpola wia. N daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg la maa miŋ ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ chol ii ni banla n du Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina maa la, di ta ii ni, dikuu iiŋ waa nuuwɛ tɛŋ wia.’ ”

ref: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia kaa kpa hɔŋ bɛl tɛɛ Nɛria biibaal karchi Baruk. N kaa kuari ŋɔ wia la himmaa n faa du unla Koori Jɛhɔyakim n fuuhwe la biini, Baruk sɛbaa dau, di faa kpa wiŋɔɔlaa kpila n lia jaa.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
text: Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa tɔ Jɔsia biibaal Zɛdɛkiaa Juda kora. Jɛhɔyakim biibaal Koori Jɛhɔyachin bɔttɛ u faa lɛɛ di a kora.

ref: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
text: Ka u ni u balaa gɛɛ u nɛra faa waa sɛɛwɛ bá hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, gunla mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ baa la.

ref: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
text: Ka Babilɔn laallɔɔra daŋ bir ba wa pig a bolzeŋ naa, di kpegluu di fuuh u maa.

ref: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
text: Haali di ii faa wettoo kpegli Babilɔn hina laallɔɔra maa gba, ka banla n na pira, di chɔɔgi ba tanti diini biine, daŋ haa lii di fuuh a bolzeŋ naa maa nyaamm.”

ref: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
text: Babilɔn laallɔɔra la n wa kuu Ijip koori laallɔɔra wia di chɔ lii Jɛrusalɛm di wa tuŋ,

ref: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
text: mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia jaa izi a bolzeŋ di ra la Bɛnjamin hɛri, ń ga lɛɛ n kapɛttɛ kuna n nɛra be.

ref: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
text: Ka miŋ ga hel Bɛnjamin dominuuzeŋ, de guure nabɔma Sɛlɛmia biibaal Irija la naabaal n ɛɛ Hanania n wa naŋ, u lawiŋ, ka ŋɔ, “I chɔwɔɔrɛ ra zuu Babilɔn hina!”

ref: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
text: N ŋɔ u be, “Karaa, màá chɔwɛɛ lɛi ra zuu Babilɔn hina.” Ka Irija waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛŋ, ka lawiŋ di kpogliŋ ba nabɔnzi be.

ref: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
text: Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia gil ba ga liziŋ ba u kooridia. Miŋ wa ballɛ, u suahzi pɛɛziŋ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ wiibɛllɛ uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ yaa gɛɛ?” N ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh, ba daŋ kpai du Babilɔn koori nonee biini.”

ref: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
text: Denii n pɛɛzi Koori Zɛdɛkia, “Bɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ n ɛɛ i ni i nabɔnzi ni a nɛra naa maa, i gil ba tɔŋ diai?

ref: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
text: Lee Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la n ŋɔ wia waa huuzii, di ŋɔ lugɔ Babilɔn koori wàá ba di wa lɔ i ni i hɛri hina la duɛi?

ref: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
text: Jara, nuu n suŋŋaa naa, ka gilɛɛ kaa wàá la n ni Jonatan dia, di i ɛɛ guŋ, n daŋ ga siu de.”

ref: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
text: Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia gil ba tɔŋ dia u koori diŋŋee la biini, u ra binni n ni. Hɔpizii maa, ɔɔ gil ba tɛŋ paanuu lii paanuu kuara be, guŋŋ a maa wa tuŋ a bolzeŋ biini.

ref: One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah
text: Denii Matan biibaal Sɛfatia, Pasur biibaal Gɛdalia, Sɛlɛmia biibaal Jɛhukal ani Malkija biibaal Pasur, nuu wia la maa mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ a nɛra lugɔ

ref: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
text: Denii a nabɔnzi ŋɔ a koori be, “Baal naa dɛg kpuirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ra du a laallɔɔra la n ka a bolzeŋ naa ni a nɛra maanii bɔhuaih, dikuu wia la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ ra tɛɛ baa naa wia. A baal naa waa nɛra naa ni winanaa ra nyiŋŋi, ba chɔgaarɛ u ra nyiŋŋi.”

ref: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
text: Koori Zɛdɛkia ŋɔ, “Too, a du ii be, gunla maa iin niŋ ɛɛu, ii ɛɛu. Màá tɔ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ.”

ref: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
text: Denii ba lau mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia, di kpaŋ du a koori biibaal Malkija kɔlɔŋ la n du guure diŋŋee la biini. Ŋmɛnnii ba faa kpa vɔɔzi n vaampɛrɛzi, ka kpaŋ du a kɔlɔŋ hiŋ biini. Nii faa waa hoo u biini, kpɛchɛgaa bɛnnɛ faa du de, n naazi jaa ra muzi.

ref: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
text: “Jara, nɛra naa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa, dikuu gunla baŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia wia. Ba kpaubuu ta kɔlɔŋ biini, bɔr la lɔzi n niŋ kpuu, ú siu, dikuu diwee n waa kaa hoo bolzeŋ naa biini wia.”

ref: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
text: Awia, Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk lau a baala, u ni baa la diibee bɛl n du a kooridia daama kuna dauribɔr zɛɛ. Baŋ ga hel de, u kpa yakɔssi ni tagtakɔssi mil dɔŋa lugɔ ŋmɛŋ, di lawuu taŋ a kɔlɔŋ biini.

ref: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
text: Ka ŋɔ n be, “Kpa yakɔssi naa du i lugbɔɔni, ŋmɛnni la gilɛɛ waa dui pira.” N kpaa du gunla uŋ bagliŋ la.

ref: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
text: Ba lau a ŋmɛnni, di tɛrgiŋ lii a kɔlɔŋ biini. N jaa du a kooridia guure diŋŋee la. Koori Zɛdɛkia n kaa pɛɛzi Jɛrɛmia wia

ref: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
text: Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia hum mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia bɔr. Ba kpogliŋ ga Kɔraawiizi Dia dominuuzi ahorohiŋ la, di ba. A koori ŋɔ, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń pɛɛzii wii bɛl. Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa ra suah n ni.”

ref: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
text: N jaa ŋɔ, “Di n dii wibii hàá kpuŋŋ? Haali di n baglii wia gba, ka hàá nuu.”

ref: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
text: Ka Koori Zɛdɛkia suahzi hɛɛhzi di ŋɔ nua tɛŋ, “N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa, di tɛɛ yaa miibɔɔ la sɔŋ biini lugɔ màá kpui gɛɛ di kpai tɛɛ banla n na nyiŋŋi i kpui la.”

ref: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
text: Denii n ŋɔ Koori Zɛdɛkia be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina la n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di i sɛɛ Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi dɔɔra, guŋwaa, i daŋ na i hiŋ, bolzeŋ naa ge wàá fuuh, i ni i diahina ge wàá siu.

ref: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
text: Ka di hàá sɛɛ a Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi dɔɔra, guŋwaa, n daŋ kpa a bolzeŋ naa du ba nonee, bá fuuh u maa. I ge gba himmaa wàá wer chɔ lii ba nonee biini.”

ref: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
text: Koori Zɛdɛkia bir ŋɔ n be, “N na ɔm Jus hina la n chɔwɛɛ ga zuu Babilɔn hina labuu. Aŋhinabe, Babilɔn hina daŋ kpaŋ du ba nonee, bá sunniŋ werge.”

ref: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
text: Denii n ŋɔ u be, “Ba wàá kpai du ba nonee biini. Hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, di ɛɛ wia naa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛi naa. Denii wiimaa kuari tɛi. Hàá siu.

ref: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
text: Ka di i vɛɛ dɔɔra sɛɛi, kenne Kɔraawiizi bagliŋ,

ref: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
text: haana la maa n kawɛɛ Juda kooridia la maanii, bá lauri tɛɛ Babilɔn koori laallɔɔra nabɔnzi. A haana naa daŋ ŋɔ i be, ‘I dammuzi la hiŋ yardɛɛ dariibuu, di lawii. I nir fotogozi biini, i dammuzi vɛɛi ta.’

ref: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
text: I haana ni i biizi maanii bá lauri wa tɛɛ a Babilɔn hina. I himmaa gba wàá na bɔr chɔ. Babilɔn koori daŋ lawii, ka bá fuuh a bolzeŋ naa.”

ref: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
text: Denii Koori Zɛdɛkia ŋɔ n be, “Gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa waa nuu yaa wiŋɔzi naa. Di ba haŋ wa nuua, ba daŋ kpui.

ref: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
text: Di a nabɔnzi wa nuuwɔ lugɔ n nii ŋɔ wiarɛ, ba ba i be wa pɛɛzii, ‘Bɛɛ wiarɛ i ni koori so di ŋɔ lai? Gilɛɛ wa kpa wiimaa di ra suah yaa ni, di guŋ lɛi, yaa daŋ kpui.’

ref: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
text: Ŋɔ ba be, ‘N faa ra suŋŋi a koorii lugɔ u gilɛɛ kaa gil ba kpaŋ la Jonatan dia, ń ga siu de.’ ”

ref: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
text: Denii a nabɔnzi maa ba n be, di wa pɛɛziŋ, n ŋɔ ba be gunla maa a koori n ŋɔ n be lugɔ n ŋɔ la. Ba waa kaa ŋɔ wiimaa, dikuu baŋ waa wia la n ni a koori n ŋɔwɛɛ la biini zummɛ wia.

ref: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
text: Denii n du a kooridia guure diŋŋee hiŋ guŋŋ di wa hel a hɔl la baŋ kpegli Jɛrusalɛm hina la.

ref: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
text: Saŋa la Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia ni u laallɔɔra n wa na baa, ba jaa izi hahmuŋa ni, di chɔ lii a bol. A koori kambol biinii ba faa ga di ga lii a dominua la n du a koŋlaa anɛɛ baambaaŋ la, di chɔ ra la Jɔɔdan Waluu paga.

ref: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
text: “La ga ŋɔ Itiopia hinuu Ɛbɛd Mɛlɛk be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N na nyiŋŋuu ń kpa hɛhchɔg ta bolzeŋ naa hina ni, nyɛɛlaa waa lɛi, guŋ gil ń nua la su u maga. A guŋ saŋa, guŋ daŋ ɛɛ i sibɔɔ.

ref: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
text: “Ií lawuu di ra binni u ni nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa ɛɛu wichɔgii maa. Di u haŋ wa ŋɔ ii ɛɛ wiimaa tɛu, ií ɛɛ a widee.”

ref: In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls. After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
text: Denii Babilɔn koori nabɔnzi la maa ba a bolzeŋ Baambaaŋ Dominuuzeŋ la, di wa so ba nabɔmbɔra. Nɛra la ge n faa kaa jaa ba ninɛɛ, Samga hinuu Nɛgal Sarɛza, Babilɔn koori nabɔnzi maa nabɔma Nɛbɔ Sasɛkim, u nabɔnzeŋ bɛl Nɛgal Sarɛza ani u nabɔnzi la maa n kawɛɛ.

ref: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
text: Ka Babilɔn laallɔɔra dau ba luge guŋŋ di ga lau Koori Zɛdɛkia, Jɛriko lɛl biini. Di kpogluu ba Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza be, bolzeŋ Ribla n du Hamaf hɛri, u di u seriya de, u chol.

ref: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
text: A Riblaa Babilɔn koori faa kpu Koori Zɛdɛkia biibaala u sibɔɔ, di kaa kpu Juda hina nabɔnzenaa maa ge de jaa.

ref: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
text: Uŋ wa ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ, u foŋzi Koori Zɛdɛkia sibee, ka gil ba kpa danyɛ yɔlɔzi duu, ka ŋɔ bá kpogluu kaali Babilɔn.

ref: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
text: Denii Babilɔn hina jaa fuuh a kooridia ni a nɛra maa diini, ka purgi Jɛrusalɛm koŋlaa maa.

ref: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
text: Nɛbuzaradan n ɛɛ koori guure nabɔma, lauri nɛra la n kawɛɛ a bolzeŋ biini, di kpa banla maa n faa chɔwɛɛ ga zuuu la, di kaali Babilɔn.

ref: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.

ref: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ, “Bɛɛ n baani ii ra ɛɛ keŋ wichɔgaa naa, di ra nyiŋŋi ii kpa hɛhchɔgzeŋ ta baala, haana ani biizi maa ni, ba bɛl maa wàá kaa kai?

ref: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: Bɛɛ n baani ii gil n baaŋ fuuh, dikuu daahɛgsɔɔhsuma la iinna fuuh, di ra tɛɛ vuga la n du Ijip hɛri, bɔr la iiŋ ballɛ wa so lai? Ii daŋ chɔgi iihinaa. Durnya hɛssi hina maa danna ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ, di kpa ii sɔŋ ra see nɛra nuuzi.

ref: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
text: Ii suuh biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la ii mɛɛwaa, ii koora ani wichezi n ɛɛwɛ Juda bola ni biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la ii ge gba ni ii haana n ɛɛwɛ Juda hɛri ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la wiarɛa?

ref: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
text: Haali ni zinaa, ii haa waa sɛɛwɛ sɔɔni siwii gɛɛ di kpaŋ girme gɛɛ di hiŋ n Gbɔgni miŋ tɛɛ ii ni ii mɛɛwaa la gba.

ref: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: Ka Juda hina la n kawɛɛ di aah siwii lugɔ bá la Ijip ga so la, n daŋ gil ba maa siuzi lɔchɔgii gɛɛ laal biini, ba nɛdumazi ni ba nɛzenaa maa. Ba danna ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ di kpa ba sɔŋ ra see nɛra nuuzi bɔr maa, ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge maa.

ref: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
text: N daŋ kpa laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii, di tɛr banla n du Ijip hɛri la digna, gunla miŋ faa tɛr Jɛrusalɛm hina digna la.

ref: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
text: Juda hina la n kawɛɛ di la Ijip ga so la, bɛl maa wàá lii gɛɛ di dɔɔ miibɔɔ lugɔ u kaa bir ba Juda, bɔr la banna nyiŋŋi lugɔ ba kaa bir ba wa so la. Ba bɛl maa wàá bir ba, see ba tama la n ɛɛ hɔɔhra hɛrdumazi biine la bɛŋ.’ ”

ref: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
text: Baala la maa n zummɛ lugɔ ba haana fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsumaa ra tɛɛ vuga ni haana la maa n du de la ani Izrɛl hina la maa n du Ijip hɛri wiifurii nomɛɛl ni nodig wiikakagni faa kpillɔɔ werge. Ba faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be,

ref: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
text: “Yaa wàá nuu amaniye naa hiŋ lizɛɛ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ biini, di tɛɛ yaa naa.

ref: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
text: Yaa daŋ ɛɛ wia la maa yaa n ŋɔwɛɛ la. Yaa daŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche, di ta siŋ tɛu gunla himmaa yaa naabaala, koora ani yaa nabɔnzi n faa ɛɛwɛ Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la. A guŋ saŋa, yaa faa dɔɔ diweere werge maa, di dɔɔ daama, wiimaa faa waa yaa ra tɔɔri.

ref: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
text: Ka di haŋ lii saŋa la yaa n waa kaa ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di lizi siŋ ra tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche la, yaa waa kaa dɔɔ kummaa, see laal ni lɔchɔgiirɛ ra kpuuzi yaa.”

ref: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
text: A haana kaa ŋɔ, “Yaa n ɔɔ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ra tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche, di ta siŋ ra tɛu la, yaa janna waa zummɛ lugɔ yaa ɔɔ ta kaanzaa a ra liu, di ta siŋ ra tɛuwaa?”

ref: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
text: “Mbusuzi la ii ni ii naabaala, koora, nabɔnzi ani a hɛri hina n lizɛɛ Juda bola ni Jɛrusalɛm ŋmɛnizenaa biine la, ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi waa a wia zummɛ gɛɛ u suuh a wiarɛaa?

ref: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
text: Kɔraawiizi n waa kaa wa wer ú di ia kanyitti dikuu ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ni wikiilaa la iiŋ ɛɛwɛ wia, ii hɛri la birgi nuuseerikunnɛ, di birgi diŋgela. Nɛr maa waa kaa so de di wa lii ni zinaa.

ref: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
text: Dikuu iiŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa zuu Kɔraawiizi ni, di vɛɛ u hiŋaa gɛɛ u Gbɔgni ni u widaulaa wiarɛ, hɛhchɔg naa iin nawɛɛ naa chol ii ni la.”

ref: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií ni ii haana maa wiɛɛlaa teŋ baglɔɔrɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔ nua, saŋa la iiŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ii daŋ haŋ hiŋ nuuzi la iiŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ di ŋɔ lugɔ ii daŋ fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma, di ta siŋ tɛɛ Chiŋ Wiche labuu.’ Ií ra ɛɛ guŋ, di ɛɛ gunla iiŋ ŋɔ nua la!

ref: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
text: Jus hina la maa n du Ijip hɛri, ií ra nuu gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n hɛɛhzɛɛ ni n sɔnzeŋ, lugɔ Jus hinuu la maa n du Ijip hɛri yemmaa, ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka yir n sɔŋ gɛɛ di hɛɛhzi, di ŋɔ, ‘N hɛɛhzi Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, di du de saŋa maa la.’

ref: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
text: Màá ka gil ii nyɛɛli, n daŋ kpu ia. Ii maa daŋ siuzi laal gɛɛ lɔchɔgii biini. Ii bɛl maa wàá ka du de.

ref: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
text: Ka ii nɛtama bɛnnɛ niŋ lii a siu biini, di lii Ijip ba Juda. Denii banla n niŋ na bahinaa la, jaa zum lugɔ n hotte ɛɛ wibii gɛɛ ba hotte ɛɛ wibii.

ref: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii zum wibii maa lugɔ n daŋ tɛr ii digna bɔnnaa, guŋ gil nua la miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ n daŋ chɔgi ia la su u maga.

ref: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
text: N daŋ kpa Ijip Koori Hɔfra tɛɛ u dɔma la n na nyiŋŋi u kpui la, gunla miŋ faa kpa Juda Koori Zɛdɛkia du Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza nonee, u dɔm la n faa ra nyiŋŋi u kpui la.”

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
text: Juda Koori Jɔsia biibaal Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biini, di Nɛria biibaal Baruk faa jaa sɛbi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia wiŋɔzi du hɔŋ biini. Denii n ŋɔ u be

ref: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
text: lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Baruk,

ref: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
text: i ra ŋɔu, ‘N lɔgɔ liwɔɔrɛ! Kɔraawiizi kpa biinichɔgrɛ jaa n tɔɔrɔɔ ni. N jaa hɛmuu guŋŋ di wa pɛssi, maa heezaa dɔɔwɛ!’

ref: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
text: Ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, ‘N na purgi kunla miŋ mawɛɛnɛ, di kaa ra kpuzi kuna la maa miŋ duuwee hɛri naa maa biini.

ref: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: I ra nyiŋŋi wizenaareaa? Gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg ta nɛr maa ni. Ka n daŋ gil i chɔ lɛɛ i miibɔɔ, bɔr la maa hin niŋ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
text: Gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia be, di ra bagli hɛssi wiarɛ keŋ,

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
text: Ijip hɛri wia. Wia naabuu u ŋɔ di ra du Ijip Koori Nɛkɔ ni u laallɔɔra ni. Waabuu Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa kpegli bolzeŋ Kakɛmis n du Muu Yufretis nua la. Jɔsia biibaal Juda Koori Jɛhɔyakim kora dii binni anaazuhiŋ biinii guŋ ɛɛ.

ref: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
text: Ií bɔg ii zagra, di tinnaa! Ií chi ii chignibɔra di hi ii laal kahurozi! Ií sazi ii kandaazi di kpa ii laal kuna laali.”

ref: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ n nai? N nawɔɔrɛ ɔnsii n lau baa, ba bittɔɔ ra chɔ, ba kpegli ba laallɔɔraa. Ba ra chɔu manamanaŋ, ba waa kɛɛwɛ ra binni har, ɔnsii werge su bɔr maa.

ref: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
text: Banla n gbaŋŋɛ ni banla n kpekke wàá na bɔr chɔ. Muu Yufretis wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ ba lɔɔzi naazi chogli.

ref: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
text: Anɛɛ izee keŋ lugɔ Muu Naal alugɔ muu n suwee di yaarɛi?

ref: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
text: Ijip izoore lugɔ Muu Naal, di ɛɛ lugɔ muuni n suwee di ra lɔ werge. Ijip ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ izi tɔ hɛri ni, di chɔgi bolzenaa ni a nɛra maa.’

ref: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
text: Zagra, ií ra chɔ! Laal torko zuura, ií ge ra chɔ ni baaŋ! Laallɔɔra, ií ge lii ra la! Banla n lii Itiopia ni Libia, di kpogli laal pɛrɛtuzi, banla n lii Lidia di zum hoo tai!

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la, hɔpiziirɛ zinaa. Zinaa, u daŋ turgi u dɔma ba kim, zinaa, u daŋ tɛr u dɔma digna. U tokobi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ sechɔgii n diwee guŋŋ di wa piŋ, di nyɔɔ chal guŋŋ di wa dɛɛzi. Zinaa, Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la kpa u dɔmaa lizi mbusu hɛri la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di dugli Muu Yufretis la.

ref: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
text: Ijip hina, ií la Giliad di ga nyiŋŋi tagzi! Ii tagzi maa ɛɛ pɛɛrɛ, kummaa wàá wer chaa ia.

ref: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
text: Durnya hɛssi hina maa daŋ nuu ii hiihzi dii wia, di nuu ii wiraa. Laallɔɔri daŋ jiŋli, di yag u dɔŋhiŋ, bá maa kpau chol.”

ref: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
text: “Sii wia naa Ijip bola ni Migdɔl, di kaa siia Mɛmfis ni Tapanɛs biine, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií chi ii chignibɔra di ɛɛ sirya, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba kpa tokobii di kpu banla n bar ia labuu.’

ref: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
text: Bɛɛ n niŋ gil ii laallɔɔra maa choglei? Ba wàá wer chi, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi daŋ taagi baa ha.

ref: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
text: Ba danna jiŋli digiidigii, di chogli dɔŋa ni, Ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil yá izi, di bir kaali yaa himmaa nɛra be, yaa himmaa hɛssi biine, di chɔ lii yaa dɔma tokobi be.’

ref: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
text: Awia, ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Kɔɔi bɛnnɛ Ijip koori ra kɔɔ, waa bɔr nawɛɛ.’

ref: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ɛɛ koorii. Minuu Kɔraawiizi la n du de saŋa maa. Gunla Bizeŋ Tabɔ n saagi bizenaa maa ni la, Bizeŋ Kamɛl saagi muuzeŋ ni la, gunnɛ nɛr la n niŋ wa lɔ ia la fɔŋŋa du.

ref: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
text: Ijip hina, ií bali ii kuna ɛɛ sirya, ba daŋ lauri ia kaali hɛrduma. Mɛmfis daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma, nɛr maa wàá ka du de.

ref: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
text: Ijip ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nalor n wesse, wogogua bɛl lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di wa dumuu.

ref: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
text: Haali laallɔɔra la uŋ ga kpawɛɛ gɛrgɔɔrɛ lugɔ nabizi. Ba waa chigɛ yoo, ba maanii bittɛ chɔ. Ba labachɔgii hɔpizii helloo, ba siu saŋaa guŋ.

ref: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
text: Ijip hina ra fuuri alugɔ hɛrikuŋ n na chɔ, dikuu ba dɔm n na ba fɔŋŋa ni wia. Ba daŋ kpogli kpaŋfɔzi ba lugɔ baala n na teŋri daazi.

ref: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
text: Ba daŋ wa teŋri u kɔrzeŋ daazi maa ta, haali uŋ tɔwɛɛ werge gba. Ba kpillɔɔ kaali lotorozi, ba wàá wer kur baa.

ref: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
text: Ijip hina daŋ di hiihzi, ba kpa baabuu du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag nɛra nonee.”

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N na nyiŋŋuu ń tɛr Tɛbɛs hina vug Amɔn, Ijip koori, Ijip hina ni ba vuga ani banla n dɛlli Ijip koori la digna.

ref: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
text: N daŋ kpa baa tɛɛ nɛra la n na nyiŋŋi ba kpui la. Baabuu Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni u nabɔnzi. Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello, nɛra daŋ kaa ba di wa so Ijip hɛri lugɔ saŋa la baŋ faa soge de la.” Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra

ref: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
text: “N nɛra Izrɛl hina, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, ii bɔra ra sá. N daŋ lɛɛ ia lii a hɛhjaŋa la biini. N daŋ lɛɛ ii naanna lii hɛri la baŋ lauri baa kaali la. Ii daŋ bir ba bol di wa du ni bampirsɔna, di so pɛrɛtɛ, nɛr maa waa kaa ra koozi ia.

ref: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N daŋ ba wa lɛɛ ia. N daŋ dim hɛssi la hina maa miŋ yaari ia la biine, ka màá dim iawaa. Màá gil ii digna tɛraa, ka di n wa tɛr ii digna, n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ ni wibii. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ tɛɛ mìŋ́ u dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia, di ra bagli Filisti hina wia, mɔɔ ka Ijip koori faa ba wa lɔ Gaza hina laal la.

ref: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
text: U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Na gunla dɔma n na chaali wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag alugɔ muu n suwee. Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muu n suwee taali di ra ba, ba daŋ wa tɔ Filisti hɛri ni kuna la maa n du de. A nɛra danna lɔɔgi wile, banla maa n du a hɛri danna chɛɛhgi.

ref: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
text: Ba daŋ nuu zagra n na chɔ, a naazi ra gbɔgzi, ba dɔma torkozi chira ra gbɔgzi. Mɛɛwaa wàá bir hiini ba biizi, dikuu ɔnsii werge wia, ba bɔra daŋ huah.

ref: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
text: Saŋa helloo ń dim Filisti hina maa, di kpu banla n kawɛɛ, banla n niŋ faa hiini Taaya ni Saidɔn hina la. Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋuu ú dim Filisti hina, banla n kawɛɛ di lii Krit muuzeŋ nua la.

ref: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
text: Gaza hina daŋ gbaari ba nyuuni, di ra wii. Askɛlɔn hina daŋ siigi. Ɛrɛɛ Filisti hina la n kawɛɛ la wii di birgi magɛi?

ref: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
text: A nɛra wiiwoo di ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi! Ɛrɛɛ í kpa i tokobi, di kpuuzi yaa birgi magɛi? Kpau du u too, ú du de ra heezi.’

ref: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
text: Ka mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia bir ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ú ɛɛ di heezei, Kɔraawiizi n tɛu huma ú hummɛi? Waabuu ŋɔ u lɔ Askɛlɔn hina ni nɛra la maa n du muuzeŋ nua la.’ ”

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔ Moab hɛri wia, “Wiarɛ huuzi Nɛbɔ hina, dikuu ban niŋ puri ba bol wia. Ba lau bolzeŋ Kiriatam hinaa, di purgi ba diikpeg, ba ŋmaabi.

ref: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
text: Ba wàá ka chɔli Moab hina, ba bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔn hina ta a hɛri chɔgaa jinaa, Bol la banna yir Madmɛn, ba daŋ chɔgii, di kpa tokobi dau i nɛra luge.

ref: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
text: Ií ra nuu Hɔrɔnam hina wile, banna chɛɛhgi dikuu chɔgaa werge wia.

ref: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
text: Moab maanii ba purgi, ií ra nuu bichalli chɛɛhgaa.

ref: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
text: Ií ra nuu ba chɛɛhgaa ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Luhif. Biinichɔg werge chɛɛhgaa ŋmɛnɛɛ la n na la Hɔrɔnam.

ref: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
text: Ba ra ŋɔu, ‘Ií chɔ lɛɛ iihinaa. Ií ra chɔ lugɔ hɛribɔduma kawee!’

ref: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
text: Moab hina, dikuu iiŋ yardi ii wiɛɛlaa ni ii daama wia, ba daŋ wa lauri ii ge gba kaali hɛrduma. Ba daŋ chi ii vug Kɛmɔs kaali, di lau u kizeehina ni u nabɔnzi kaali.

ref: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
text: A bola maanii bá chɔgi, haali walli ni lɛla maanii bá chɔgi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
text: Ií chi yazi di ga yaari Moab hɛri maa, dikuu un niŋ chɔɔ pɛɛ wia. U bola daŋ birgi diŋgelli, nɛr maa wàá ka du a biine.”

ref: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
text: Kɔ́raawiizi see nɛr la maa n wàá hum Kɔraawiizi huma ni biinihuŋŋu! U nuuseei di nɛr la maa n wàá sɛɛ kpa u tokobi kpu Moab hina!

ref: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Moab hina sogoo ni bampirsɔna, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa haa waa baa laurɛɛ kaali hɛrduma. Ba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ siŋ n du golii biini, ba haa wɔɔ fɛɛnɛɛ maa. U sunzi ŋmɛnɛ haa waa chɔkkɛ, u haŋ du sum di hanna la.

ref: But now, I will send enemies to pour out the wine and smash the jars!
text: Ka saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ gil nɛra la ga fug Moab hina alugɔ baŋ fug siŋ, tɔga biine. Kummaa wàá kaa ka, ba daŋ purgi a tɔga maa.

ref: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
text: Vug Kɛmɔs wia daŋ dɔɔ Moab hina hiihzi, gunla Izrɛl hina baŋhina n faa yardi vug Bɛtɛl, di di hiihzi la.

ref: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
text: Moab baala, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ŋɔ, ‘Yaa ɛɛ laallɔkpegaawɛi?’

ref: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
text: Moab hina dɔma daŋ wa lɔ baa, di zuu chɔgi ba bola maa, di kpu ba biipɔlnanaa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Koora Maa Koori, di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
text: Moab hina cholaa helloo, hɛhchɔg daŋ chol ba ni manaŋ.

ref: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
text: Banla maa n soge bar baa, ií wii ra tɛɛ baa. Banla maa n na nuu ba sɔŋ, ií ŋɔ, ‘Daŋkpalzeŋ la kuugoore, u girme tunnɔɔ!’

ref: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
text: Dibɔn hina, ií lii ii girme bɔr, di tuu wa so hɛrhilii. Moab chɔgri du ɛnnɛ, di purgi u diikpega.

ref: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
text: Aroa hina, ií chi ŋmɛnikɛrii di ra du tau. Ií pɛɛzi banla n chɔwɛɛ ra kaali, ‘Bɛɛ n ɛɛwɛnɛi?’

ref: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
text: Ba daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Moab hina cholloo, di di hiihzi. Ií wii di ra lɔɔgi wile! Ií sii Muu Aanɔn nua lugɔ Moab maanii purgee!’

ref: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
text: Kɔraawiizi di giŋgimee nyuuni bolzenaare seriya, aabuu Hɔlɔn, Jaaza, Mɛfaaf,

ref: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
text: Dibɔn, Nɛbɔ, Bɛf Diblatam,

ref: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
text: Kiriatam, Bɛf Gamul, Bɛf Miɔn

ref: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
text: Moab hina fɔŋŋazeŋ tunnɔɔ, n chɔgi u fɔŋŋa maanii. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ií gil Moab hina nyɔɔ siŋ di dɛɛzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba bir hattɛ kpuŋ. Moab hina daŋ chɔɔ ba himmaa hɛɛhzaa biini, di ra billi, nɛra ra mam.

ref: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
text: Moab hina, ií lii ii bola di gaa zuu bizenaa nyuuni. Ií ɛɛ lugɔ komma la n du u daŋ bii bɔɔ nua.

ref: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
text: Yaa nuu Moab hina jigsi wiarɛ, ba kpoŋaa werge wia, di ra na bahinaa werge, di ra binni nɛra pɛɛ.

ref: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
text: Awia, n daŋ wii tɛɛ Moab ni Kir Harɛsɛf hina maa.

ref: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
text: Sibma hina, n wiiwoo ra tɛɛ ia, di kaali gunla miŋ wiiwe tɛɛ Jaza hina la. Bolzeŋ Sibma ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ grepu daa, di ta kela ga hel Muuzensiwii, haali di ga hel Jaza muuzeŋ. Ka filaŋkeŋ, nɛchɔgaa ballɔɔ di wa chɔgi i nɔŋaahma ni i grepuzi maa.

ref: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
text: N lizi bɔsɔna ni hindiire lii Moab hɛrsum la biini. N gillɔɔ siŋ waa kaa ra lii ba siŋ kuaribɔra, nɛr maa waa kaa ra kuaraa di ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna. Haali banna chaasi gba, ka bɔsɔna chaasaa lɛi.

ref: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
text: Wiraa lii Hɛsbɔnnɛ di ga hel Ɛlialɛ ni Jahaz, Zoa hina gba ra nuu, di lii Zoa guŋŋ di ga hel Hɔrɔnam ni Ɛglaf Sɛlisiya, haali Nimrim niiri maa hil.

ref: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N daŋ tɔ Moab hina ŋmɛnɛɛ, ba wàá kaa ra lizi mbusuzi giŋgimee nyuuni, di fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma di ra tɛɛ ba vuga. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
text: N na wiiu n biini ra tɛɛ Moab ni Kir Harɛsɛf hina alugɔ nɛr n na huuh tiitorii di ra wii lee, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daama maanii tunnɛ.

ref: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
text: Wiimaa waa kaa du Moab salli ni bossibaana, di wiraa bɛŋ lɛi, dikuubɛɛwiai, n purgi Moab maanii alugɔ golii la nɛr maa n waa kaa ra nyiŋŋi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
text: Ií na, Moab maanii purgee chɔɔ! Ií nuu gunla banna chɛɛhgi! Moab hina bir ba haraa ni hiihzi! Moab hina birgi chɛɛtɛ kunaa, ba wia dɔɔ ɔnsii ni nuukpui werge, banla maa n bar baa la be.”

ref: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Hɛri bɛl hina daŋ ba di wa gbaari Moab hina kaali, gunla chig n ɔɔ wa lau kuŋ la.

ref: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
text: Ba daŋ kpegli Kɛriɔf hina, di foozi ba diikpega. A hɔl hiŋ, Moab hina laallɔɔra biine daŋ chɔgi alugɔ hilula n lɔ haaŋ la.

ref: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
text: Ba daŋ dim Moab hɛri hina, dikuu u nɛra n diŋ mmɔri wia.

ref: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Unla maa n niŋ chɔ lii a ɔnsii biini, u daŋ chol bɔɔ biini, unla maa n niŋ lii a bɔɔ biini ge, sidɛɛ daŋ lawuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, Moab hina dignitɛraa bina helloo. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
text: Banla n chɔwɛɛ lii laal biini du bolzeŋ Hɛsbɔnnɛ di ra nyiŋŋi lɛɛi, bolzeŋ la Koori Sihɔn n faa ra di kora la, maanii fuuhwe. A niŋ fuuh Moab hina la n na nyiŋŋi laal lɔi hɛri magaa guŋŋ di ga lii ba bizenaa nyuuni maa.

ref: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
text: Wia daŋ wa huuzi ia, Moab hina! Nuuseei daŋ di ia, vug Kɛmɔs kuara maanii ba chɔgi. Ba lauri ii biibaala ni biihaana maanii kaali hɛrduma.

ref: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ka hɔpizii bɛl ra bau min niŋ kaa gil Moab hina nyɛɛli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.” Moab hina seriya dii tunaa guŋ.

ref: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
text: Wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ di ra bagli Ammɔn hina wiarɛ keŋ, “Lee Izrɛl hina baala duɛi? Nɛr maa waa hoo un niŋ wer yoo lɛɛ ba hɛriaa? Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ba gil nɛra la n na kuari vug Mɔlɛk wa lɛɛ Gad dee hɛri sonei?

ref: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
text: Ka saŋa bɛl ra bau, min niŋ lɔ laal wile di du Ammɔn hina bolzeŋ Raba ni. Ba daŋ purguu ú chɔɔ kululu, di fuuh u boljigzi la maa n baruu. Denii Izrɛl hina duŋŋi banla n faa duŋŋi baa la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
text: Hɛsbɔn hina, ií ra chɛɛhgi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba chɔg Airɛ! Raba hina, ií ra wii! Ií kpa gbɔglɔŋ tagtaazi di laali ra wii, ií du a bol koŋlaa biini di chɔ ra bar, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ kpa vug Mɔlɛk kaali hɛhjaŋ, u ni u Kizeehina ni u nabɔnzenaa maa.

ref: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
text: Wibiinyaara, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra ta barabarai? Ii fɔŋŋa ra tunuu. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii dɛlli ii fɔŋŋa di ŋɔ lugɔ nɛr maa wàá kur lɔ iai?

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
text: N daŋ gil ɔnsii werge lii banla n bar ia la be di chol ii ni. Ba daŋ duŋŋi ii bɛl maa, nɛr maa wàá wer chaali banla n chɔwɛɛ la.

ref: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
text: Ka a harbɔɔ, n daŋ bir gil Ammɔn hina kaa nyɛɛli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.” Ɛdɔm hina wia

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ di ra bagli Ɛdɔm hina wia, “Nunzuma waa kaa hoo Tɛman gɛɛ? Nunzunna baglaa tunnɔɔ gɛɛ? Ba nunzuma pɔɔhwɔɔ gɛɛ?

ref: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
text: Ií bir chɔ ga suah bia bɔɔluŋe biine, ii banla maa n du Dɛdan, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ kpa hɛhchɔg di wa ta Ɛsau dee ni, saŋa la min niŋ tɛr ba digna la.

ref: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
text: Di banla n na tɔrgi grepuzi faa wa tɔrgaa, ba wàá gil aŋhinaa? Di ŋmɛɛna faa ballɔ hamuŋa ni, gunla maga banna nyiŋŋi lɛi ba ŋmɛɛa?

ref: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
text: N daŋ foozi Ɛsau dee kummaa, di lizi ba suahribɔra chaaŋ, guŋ gil ba wàá wer suah. Ba biizi, lulla ani ba dɔŋahina maa daŋ siu, ba wia tuŋ nyaamm.

ref: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
text: Ií gil ii lalbiizi tɛŋ, n daŋ guu baa, ii luhaana gba daŋ wer yardiŋ.”

ref: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Di banla n waa dɛkkɛ lugɔ n tɔɔri baa la ra nyɔɔ tɔɔrɔɔ nii la, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ màá tɛr ii dignai? Wibii maa, ii daŋ haŋ nyɔɔ a tɔɔrɔɔ niirɛ.

ref: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
text: N hɛɛhzi n hinnɛ lugɔ Bɔzra daŋ puri, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, nɛra nuuzi kpu, bá ra ɛɛu chɛɛtɛ, di kpa u sɔŋ ra see dɔŋa nuuzi. U bolzenaa maa ge purgi di birgi diŋgelli, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
text: Mìŋ́ Jɛrɛmia nuu amaniyee lii Kɔraawiizi be, uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ, “N hum baliirɛ hɛssi hina maa be lugɔ bá chaali di wa lɔ Ɛdɔm hina laal!

ref: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
text: N daŋ gil ii gɛrgi hɛssi hina maa be, nɛr maa wàá kaa ra tɔgzi ia.

ref: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
text: Ii barabara dar iabuu. Nɛr maa waa ia ra ɔm gunla iinna fɛ lugɔ bá ra ɛɛ la. Ii banla n du bia la n jaŋŋɛ la chiŋ werge nyuuni, di ra zuu a bɔɔni la. Haali iiŋ du chiŋ alugɔ chig gba, ka n daŋ gil ii lii de di tuu hɛri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
text: Ɛdɔm wia daŋ dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, nɛr la maa n niŋ ga de nua daŋ kpu, ɔnsii lawuu, dikuu u chɔgaa wia.

ref: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
text: Gunla baŋ faa chɔg Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra ani bola la maa n baraa la, gunnɛ bá chɔg Ɛdɔm, nɛr maa wàá ka du. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
text: Alugɔ bunyiŋ n lii Jɔɔdan muu kɔr biini di ra la sela diiribɔr la n wesse la, gunnɛ ń duŋŋi Ɛdɔm hina lii ba hɛri kakpaŋ. Anɛɛ ń lizi u ɛɛ kennei? Anɛɛ n lugɔŋ, ú karsinnɛi? Sitɔɔri bɛliirɛ n niŋ wer diŋ mmɔrɛi?

ref: Listen to my plans for you, people of Edom. Your children will be dragged off and your country destroyed.
text: Awia, ii ra nuu jina la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tawɛɛ Ɛdɔm hina wia, gunla minna nyiŋŋi ń dau Tɛman hina. N daŋ tuuzi ba biizi kaali, di chɔgi ba sela diiribɔra maa dikuu ba wia.

ref: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
text: Di nɛra wa nuu Ɛdɔm hina cholaa wia, durnya maa daŋ zigli. Ba wiraa daŋ hel Muuzeŋaahmu.

ref: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
text: Dɔma daŋ wa pig bolzeŋ Bɔzra hina alugɔ chig n tuuwe ú lau kuŋ. A hɔl hiŋ, ɔnsii daŋ lau Ɛdɔm laallɔɔra alugɔ hilulaa n lɔ haaŋ la.”

ref: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ bolzeŋ Damaskus wia. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Bolzenaa Hamaf ni Aapad hina biine chɔkkɔɔ, dikuu baŋ nuu amaniyechɔgaa wia. Kafɔŋ chol ba ni, alugɔ muuzeŋ n na koozi.

ref: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
text: Damaskus hina bɔra huahwɔɔ, ba bir chɔ ni bɔsai. Ba bɔra ra waazi, biinichɔg lau baa werge maa alugɔ hilulaa n lɔ haaŋ la.

ref: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
text: Bolzeŋ la n faa dɔɔ sɔŋ werge maa, di dɔɔ bɔsɔna la maanii chɔɔ pɛɛ.

ref: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
text: Wibii maa, a hɔl hiŋ, ba daŋ kpu ba biipɔllaa maa di ta ŋmɛnikɛraa, chɔgi ba laallɔɔra maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
text: N daŋ du Damaskus koŋlaa maa niŋ, ú fuuh Koori Bɛn Hadad kooridia la maa.” Kɛda Dee ni Bolzeŋ Hazɔr Hina Wia

ref: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ di ra bagli Kɛda dee ni Hazɔr kossi la Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n faa lɔ laal la wia. U ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií izi di ga lɔ Kɛda dee laal, di chɔgi nɛra la maa n soge wiifurii la.

ref: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi karfi iabuu lugɔ ii chɔ di ga suah bia bɔɔluŋe biine, ii banla n du bolzeŋ Hazɔr! Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ta ii jinachɔgiirɛ.”

ref: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ií izi di lɔ hɛri la hina n soge pɛrɛtɛ, di dɛlli bahinaa la. Hɛri la hina n waa dominuuzenaa gɛɛ lugbidaazi dɔɔwɛ, di so ba bɛŋ la.

ref: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
text: Ií lauri ba nyugmazi ani ba sela maa. N daŋ yaari banla n fuŋ ba nyuuni, di kpa hɛhchɔg ta ba ni bɔr maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
text: Bolzeŋ Hazɔr daŋ birgi hohobiazi duuribɔr, di chɔɔ diŋgela di hanna la. Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka so de.” Ɛlam hɛri wia

ref: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ n be, “N daŋ kpu hotaara la maa n gillɛ Ɛlam hina du kpeg werge maa la.

ref: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
text: N daŋ gil dɔma lii bɔr maa di wa lɔ Ɛlam hina. N daŋ yaari baa bɔr maa, hɛri maa wàá ka, di ba wàá du u biini.

ref: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N daŋ chiŋŋi n koorikara Ɛlam biini, ka kpu ba koori ni ba nabɔnzenaa.

ref: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
text: Ka di saŋa bɛl wa hello, n daŋ kaa gil Ɛlam hina nyɛɛli. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Babilɔn hɛri ani nɛra la maa n du de la wia tɛɛ mìŋ́ u dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia,

ref: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
text: “Sii hɛssi maa biine, lalli tuuta chiŋ di sii guŋ, gilɛɛ wa mɔŋ wiimaa ra ta, ka ŋɔ, ‘Ba daŋ kpegli Babilɔn hina. Ba daŋ kpa hiihzi kpu ba vug Maduk. Babilɔn vuga maanii niŋ di hiihzi, ba vuga la miŋ kiiwe maanii bá purgi.’

ref: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
text: Hɛri bɛl nɛra daŋ lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ba wa pig baa, di chɔgi a hɛri, ú chɔɔ pɛɛ. Nɛr maa wàá kaa du de, newea ni sela maanii niŋ chɔ lii de.

ref: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
text: Di a saŋa wa hello, Izrɛl ani Juda hina maa daŋ kpau, di wii sinii di ra nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la bɔr.

ref: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
text: Ba daŋ pɛɛzi Bizeŋ Ziɔn ŋmɛnɛɛ bɔr, di bir ba siwee chaŋuu. Ba daŋ ba, bá ni mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ nuukpaŋ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ, nuukpaŋ la baŋ wàá chɔgi maa.

ref: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
text: N nɛra leuwoo lugɔ peeza, a nɔɔna gillɔɔ a leu, di gil a du bizenaa nyuuni di ra bar. A du bizenaa ni giŋgimee nyuuni di ra juuri, a waa kaa zum a chɔɔribɔr bɔr.

ref: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
text: Nɛr la maa haŋ wa naa, ɔɔ lɔabuu. A dɔma ɔɔ ŋɔu, ‘Yaa waa bilchɔg dɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, di zuu Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ a diiribɔr himmaa ani ba naabaala tamii la ninɛɛ.’

ref: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
text: Izrɛl hina, ií chɔ lii Babilɔn hɛri, ií chɔ lii de! Ii ɛɛ nɛra la n niŋ feli lii.

ref: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
text: N daŋ du hɛssi aŋhina n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag nɛra bɔkpega, bá ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di wa pig Babilɔn hina. Ba daŋ wa chi ba chignibɔra di kpegli baa. Ba hobee daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ nɛra la n zum laal lɔi nɛnnɛ, ba waa tawɛɛ ra kir.

ref: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
text: Ba daŋ wa paagi Babilɔn hina kuna kaali, banla n niŋ paagaa la daŋ na ba kipar. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
text: Babilɔn hina, ii foozi n hɛri kunaa ii bɔra sɔɔni ia, ii ra baruu alugɔ nau la n na fɛrgi sɔgmia gɛɛ zagu la n na wii,

ref: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
text: ka ii bolzeŋkpeg daŋ di hiihzi, di ŋmaabi. Babilɔnnɛ niŋ gɛrgi kaali hɛssi maa. U daŋ ɛɛ hɛribɔduma, wàá dɔɔ nii.

ref: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
text: Dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wia, nɛr maa wàá ka so de, ka u maa chɔɔ pɛɛ. Nɛr la maa n niŋ wa ga Babilɔn, ɔnsii werge daŋ lawuu, ú nua kpu.

ref: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
text: Ií lɔ laal wile di ra bar a bolzeŋ maa! U di kuurɛ, u diijaŋraa la n la chiŋ maa purgi chogli, ba purgi u koŋlaa maanii. Guŋ n ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi kinturgaa wia, ií turguu a kim, di dawuu gunla ban dau baŋhina la.

ref: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa gil bá duu gɛɛ di kum kuna a hɛri. Dikuu nɛr la n na sunni nɛra tokobi wia, gil nɛr maa bir kaali u himmaa nɛra be, u himmaa hɛri.”

ref: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ peeza bunyinzi n duŋŋɛɛ, a yaari. Asiiria koorizenne felee wa lɔ baa, ka Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza jaa keezi ba di wa purgi ba hoga.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ tɛr Babilɔn koori ani u hɛri hina maa digna, gunla miŋ tɛr Asiiria koorizeŋ digna la.

ref: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
text: Ka n daŋ bir gil Izrɛl hina ba ba himmaa hɛri, di kaa wa so. Ba daŋ na diwee Bizeŋ Kamɛl nyuu ni Basan hɛri. Ba daŋ na diwee gunla maga banna nyiŋŋi, lii Ɛfram ni Giliad giŋgimee nyuuni, di di piŋ.

ref: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
text: A guŋ saŋa wa hello, ba daŋ pigzi di nyiŋŋi Izrɛl hina bilchɔg, ka ba wàá na bɛl maa, di nyiŋŋi Juda hina wichɔgaa, ka ba wàá na bɛl maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ gil banla miŋ gillɛ la wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.’ ”

ref: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií la ga lɔ Mɛratam hɛri ani banla n du Pɛkɔd la. Ií dau ba luge, di kpu baa nyaamm. Ií ɛɛ wia la maa miŋ ŋɔ ii ɛɛ la.

ref: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
text: Ba nuu laal gbɔgaa a hɛri biini, chɔgaa werge gbɔga!

ref: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
text: Babilɔn hina faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ silii, di ra nyiŋŋi ba purgi durnya naa maa burburbur! Ka filaŋkeŋ, ba waa kaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, ba kpegli baabuu! Na gunla Babilɔn wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, hɛssi hina maa nuuzi kpu.

ref: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
text: N he iabuu sidɛɛ, Babilɔn hina, u lau iabuu di ii waa zummɛ. Ba na iabuu di lau ia, dikuu iiŋ di mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi mmɔri wia.

ref: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
text: N pilli n dɔŋkuna diarɛ, di lizi n baaŋfuuihchɔgii dɔŋkuna, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la, dɔɔ humaa ń hum Babilɔn hɛri.

ref: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
text: Ií lii bɔɔnɛɛ wa lɔ baa, di purgi ba buugazi, di chaali kuna la iiŋ paagɛɛ dau kulululu lugɔ mia. Ií chɔgi a hɛri maa, di gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa wàá ka de.

ref: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
text: Ií kpu ba laallɔɔra maa! Ií kɔrgi baa! Wiarɛ huuzi Babilɔn hina! Ba digna tɛraa saŋa helloo.

ref: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
text: Ií ra nuu, nɛra la n lii Babilɔnnɛ di ba Jɛrusalɛm. Ba ra bagli gunla Kɔraawiizi n tɔɔri Babilɔn hinaa, dikuu baŋ chɔg u Dia wia.

ref: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
text: Chaali hotaara bá ga yoo Babilɔn hina, banla maa n zum hoo tai nɛnnɛ. Ií la ga chɔɔ bar a bolzeŋ maa, di gilɛɛ wa gil nɛr maa wa na bɔr di ra chɔ. Ií bir turgi baa ba wiɛɛlaa kim, di dau baa gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ la. Dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ta barabaraa du mìŋ́ Izrɛl Dɔɔrinaniinanii la.

ref: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
text: Awia, ba biipɔllaa maanii bá kpu ta ŋmɛnibaana, di kaa kpu ba laallɔɔra maa ge a hɔl hiŋ.

ref: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
text: Babilɔn hina, ii kpoŋŋoo werge, awia, n chigɛ ii ninɛɛ. Hɔpizii la min niŋ tɛr ii digna la helloo. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
text: Ii kpoŋaa daŋ gil ii jiŋli di chogli, ka nɛr maa wàá lalli ia chiŋ. N daŋ du ii bolzenaa maa niŋ, ú fuuh kuna la maa n bar ia la nyaamm.”

ref: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ba ra sunni Izrɛl ni Juda hina maanii. Nɛra la n lauri baa la ra du ba taurɛ nɛnnɛ, ba wàá sɛɛ ba na bɔr kaali.

ref: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
text: Ka ba Lɛɛri kpekkoo, u sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ. U daŋ aah siwii di lɛɛ ba nua, di gil bɔsɔna du ba hɛri, ka kpa tɔɔrɔɔ ta Babilɔn hina ni.”

ref: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Babilɔn hina daŋ siu! Ba nabɔnzi ni ba nunzunna daŋ siu!

ref: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
text: Ba dɔgtɛɛkara hina daŋ siu! Ba daŋ birgi gɛnaa! Ba laallɔɔra maa daŋ siu! Ɔnsii lau baabuuu werge maa!

ref: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
text: Ba zagra ni anla n na tɛrgi torkozi daŋ siu ani famaraa la maa n du ba biini la! Ba daŋ birgi haana! Ba daama kuna daŋ siu! Ba daŋ paagaa kaali!

ref: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
text: Hil daŋ chi! Bá gɔŋa maa hil! Dikuubɛɛwiai, Babilɔn ɛɛ vuga hɛrii, vuga la n niŋ gil ba birgi chuglahina, dikuu ɔnsii werge wia.

ref: Never again will people live in your land— only desert animals, jackals, and unclean birds.
text: Awia, hɛribɔduma sela ni munuzii niŋ du de, kukuballi ra zuu de. Nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka so de, di lii jimini bɛl di ra la bɛl.

ref: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
text: Gunla baŋ faa chɔg Sɔdɔm ni Gɔmɔra ani bola la maa n baraa la, gunnɛ bá chɔg Babilɔn, nɛr maa wàá ka du. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
text: Ií na, laallɔɔra lii wiifuri nomɛɛl wiikakagrɛ di ra ba. Ba du hɛrkpeg hina ni koorikpila n du bɔɔnɛɛrɛ bɔkpega.

ref: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
text: Ba kpogli hozi, kandaazi ani ba tokobizii, di dɔɔ sihilii werge, ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ. Di ba haŋ tinni ba zagra, ba gbɔga ɔɔ ɛɛu lugɔ muuzeŋ n ɔɔ ra kɔɔ la. Ba ɛɛ siryaa bá wa lɔ Babilɔn hina.

ref: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
text: Babilɔn koori nuu ba wiarɛ, u nonee maa yɔɔri. U biini chɔgi werge, u bɔra ra waazuu alugɔ hilulaa n lɔ haaŋ la.

ref: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
text: Alugɔ bunyiŋ n lii Jɔɔdan muu kɔr biini di ra la sela diiribɔr la n wesse la, gunnɛ ń duŋŋi Babilɔn hina lii ba hɛri kakpaŋ. Anɛɛ ń lizi u ɛɛ kennei? Anɛɛ n lugɔŋ, ú karsinnɛi? Sitɔɔri bɛliirɛ niŋ wer diŋ mmɔrɛi?

ref: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
text: Awia, ii ra nuu jina la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n tawɛɛ Babilɔn hina wia, gunla minna nyiŋŋi ń dau Babilɔn hɛri hina. N daŋ tuuzi ba biizi kaali, di chɔgi ba sela diiribɔr maa dikuu ba wia.

ref: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
text: Di nɛra wa nuu Babilɔn hina cholaa wia, durnya maa daŋ zigli. Hɛssi hina maa daŋ nuu ba wiraa.”

ref: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N daŋ du nɛchɔgii bɔkpega, ú ba wa lɔ Babilɔn hina laal.

ref: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
text: N daŋ gil hɔɔhra la Babilɔn, di ga chɔgi baa alugɔ peu n ɔɔ paa kpaga kaali la. Di a keŋ hɔpizii naa wa hello, ba daŋ la ga baruu, di lɔu, di chɔguu, ú birgi diŋgela.

ref: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa tɛɛ ba laallɔɔra bɔr, ba waa taazi ba hozi gɛɛ di wa kpa ba laal kuna di ra laali. Ií gilɛɛ waa gil ba biipɔllaa! Ií kpu ba laallɔɔra maa!

ref: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
text: Ba daŋ du baa pira, bá siuzi chɔɔ ba bolzenaa ŋmɛnizi.
