ref: You will put on sackcloth to show your sorrow, but terror will overpower you. Shame will be written all over your faces, and you will shave your heads in despair.
text: Ba daŋ laali gbɔglɔnzi, ɔnsii lau baa. Hiihzi kpu baa werge maa, ba fuŋ ba nyuuni.

ref: Your silver and gold will be thrown into the streets like garbage, because those are the two things that led you into sin, and now they cannot save you from my anger. They are not even worth enough to buy food.
text: Ba daŋ kpa ba saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa ta a bolzeŋ biini ŋmɛnizenaa alugɔ kpaga, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wàá wer lɛɛ baa a hɔl la n baaŋ n niŋ fuuh ba ni la. A wàá wer kpu ba lɔzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, aabuu du baa wichɔgaa biini.

ref: You took great pride in using your beautiful jewelry to make disgusting idols of foreign gods. So I will make your jewelry worthless.
text: Ba faa kpa ba saliŋ kuŋkuaraa wiarɛ su siwii werge, di kpaa ra kuari vuga la miŋ kiiwe la n ɛɛ kundoŋa. Awia, n daŋ gil ba daama birgi kundoŋa tɛɛ baa.

ref: They will break into my temple and leave it unfit as a place to worship me, but I will look away and let it happen.
text: N daŋ bir n har kpu baa, ka ŋmɛɛna wa zuu mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia, di chɔguu.”

ref: Your whole country is in confusion! Murder and violence are everywhere in Israel,
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, “Kuari yɔlɔzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛkpui su a hɛri maanii, kalu ge su a bolzeŋ maa.

ref: so I will tell the most wicked nations to come and take over your homes. They will put an end to the pride you have in your strong army, and they will make your places of worship unfit to use.
text: N daŋ gil hɛssi la hina la n dɔɔ biinikpola werge wa lɛɛ ba diini dɔɔ, di doŋ ba jaamibɔra la banna tɔgzi la, di kaa chɔgi ba vuga kuaribɔra la maa, á bir pɛɛ.

ref: You will be terrified and will desperately look for peace—but there will be no peace.
text: Ɔnsii werge lau n nɛra, bá bɔra ra sa. Ba danna nyiŋŋi bɔsɔna, ka ba wàá nau.

ref: One tragedy will follow another, and you'll hear only bad news. People will beg prophets to give them a message from me. Priests will stop teaching my Law, and wise leaders won't be able to give advice.
text: Tɔɔrɔɔzenaa daŋ hiŋzi dɔŋa. Ba danna nuu amaniyechɔgaa wia hunehune digiidigii, di ra fɛ lugɔ n dɔgtɛɛ bɛl daŋ ŋɔ wia lugɔ deeza biini tɛɛ baa. Akai, guŋ wàá ɛɛ. Ba wàá ka na baglaa maa ge gba lii n kizeehina be. Ba nabɔma bɛl maa ge gba wàá ka karfi baa wiimaa ni.

ref: Even your king and his officials will lose hope and cry in despair. Your hands will tremble with fear. I will punish you for your sins and treat you the same way you have treated others. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Koori daŋ wii, ú sitɔɔri ge bɔra huah. Ɔnsii lau a nɛra, bá bɔra ra sa. N daŋ tɛrgi ba digna dikuu ba wiɛɛlaa wia, di kaa di baa seriya gunla baŋ di ba dɔŋahina seriya la. Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Six years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the leaders of Judah were meeting with me in my house. On the fifth day of the sixth month, the Lord God suddenly took control of me,
text: Baŋ lauri yaa la hɛrduma la, binni anumbɛlhiŋ, u baaguzi anumbɛl hɔpizaa anuehiŋ hɔl, di n ni Juda hɛri nabɔnzi maa faa sogo n dia. Denii Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la fɔŋŋa wa zuu mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ni.

ref: and I saw something in the shape of a human. This figure was like fire from the waist down, and it was bright as polished metal from the waist up.
text: N na kumbɛl alugɔ newee, di lii u chara barii di ra tuu, u ɛɛ lugɔ ninlau, di lii u chara di ra tinni ge ra nyɛgzi lugɔ danyɛ baŋ vɔglɛɛ.

ref: It reached out what seemed to be a hand and grabbed my hair. Then in my vision the Lord's Spirit lifted me into the sky and carried me to Jerusalem. The Spirit took me to the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard, where there was an idol that disgusted the Lord and made him furious.
text: N kaa na uŋ tɛr kumbɛl lugɔ nonii di wa lau n nyuhuna. Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma lalliŋ chiŋ, n du hɛri ni chiŋ baambaaŋ. U kpaŋ ga hel Jɛrusalɛm, di ga tuuŋ ú Dia diŋŋee diisee wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominua la, baŋ ma vug bɛl, u wia ra fuuh Kɔraawiizi baaŋ werge maa la. Kenne n na lugɔ deeza biini.

ref: Then I saw the brightness of the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River.
text: Denii n ŋɔ ń binni, di Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la girme chaanɔɔ gunla miŋ faa felee nau lugɔ deeza biini, lɛl la biini la.

ref: God said to me, “Ezekiel, son of man, look north.” And when I did, I saw that repulsive idol by the altar near the gate.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, binni wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag barii na.” Awia, n binni di na vug la u wia n na fuuh Kɔraawiizi baaŋ werge la n chigɛ dominua nua la n na la mbusu lizibɔr la.

ref: God then said, “Do you see the terrible sins of the people of Israel? Their sins are making my holy temple unfit as a place to worship me. Yet you will see even worse things than this.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, i na gunla Izrɛl hina n na ɛɛa? I na wikuna la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n kiiwe la banna ɛɛ, guŋ duŋŋiŋ lii n Bɔnaniinanii la biini, di ra la bɔɔnɛɛa? Hiŋwaa ra ba, i daŋ haa na wichɔgaa la n kaali annii!”

ref: Next, I was taken to the entrance of the courtyard, where I saw a hole in the wall.
text: Denii u kpaŋ ga hel u Dia diŋŋee bɛl dominua, di bagliŋ bɔɔ bɛl n du a koŋlii ni.

ref: God said, “Make this hole bigger.” And when I did, I realized it was a doorway.
text: U kaa ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, fur a koŋlii na.” Denii n fur a koŋlii di na dominua bɛl.

ref: “Go in,” God said, “and see what horrible and evil things the people are doing.”
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, “Zuu ga na ba wikuna la miŋ kiiwe banna ɛɛ bɔnnaa.”

ref: Inside, I saw that the walls were covered with pictures of reptiles and disgusting, unclean animals, as well as with idols that the Israelites were worshiping.
text: Awia, n zuu ga na a dia koŋlaa maa ni, di ba kuari hɛrikuna, gerni ani sedoŋa irizi maa. N kaa na vuga ni a irizi Izrɛl hina la n na kuari.

ref: Seventy Israelite leaders were standing there, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each of these leaders was holding an incense burner, and the smell of incense filled the room.
text: N na Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi tokkoahoro ni fi n chigɛ a see, Safan biibaal Jaazania chi ba biini. Bɛl maa ge faa kpogli nimbuurikunnɛ, di ra fuuh daahɛgsɔɔhsuma. Nyɔɔzi faa ra lii a daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ni, di tɔ bɔr maa.

ref: God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel.
text: U kaa ŋɔ u n be, “Newee biibaal, haa nawɛɛ gunla Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi n du diibiri naa, di ra kuari ba vugaa? Ba ra ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizi waa yaa ra na, Kɔraawiizi lii a hɛrii.’ ”

ref: But I will show you something even worse than this.”
text: Denii u kaa ŋɔ, “Kaa wa na anla n ɛɛ wikuna werge miŋ kiiwe banna ɛɛ kaali annii.”

ref: He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa kpaŋ la u Dia wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominua nua, di haana baŋhina sogo de di ra wii, dikuu ba vug Tamuz n siuwɛ wia.

ref: God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
text: U ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, haa nawɛɛa? Ka i daŋ haa na wikuna miŋ kiiwe kaali annii!”

ref: God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, haa nawɛɛa? Juda hina ra ɛɛ wikuna la miŋ kiiwee, witamaa waa? Kalu su a hɛri maanii, di gil n baaŋ na fuuh werge maa. Na gunla banna chagziŋ!

ref: So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
text: Awia, n daŋ tɔɔri baa ni baaŋfuuih, màá suŋ ba ni gɛɛ di gil baa. Haali di ba ra chɛɛhgi di ra suŋŋiŋ gba, ka màá nuu tɛɛ baa maa.”

ref: After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
text: Denii n nuu Kɔraawiizi n pozee werge maa, di ŋɔ, “Lau nɛra la n na binni a bolzeŋ ni la ba ɛŋ. Kali baa bɛl maa kpa u laal kuna.”

ref: I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
text: N na baala banumbɛl n liiwɛ kpogli ba laal kuna, di lii Kɔraawiizi Dia chiŋ dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la, bɛl maa kpogli dɔŋkuŋ. Baal bɛl faa du ba biini, di laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagta, ka pɛgli kuŋwar bɛl ban niŋ wer sɛbi u ni. Ba maa jaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la ga chi mbusu lizibɔr la baŋ kpa danyɛ kuari la kɛrii.

ref: The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la girme n na chaani la, izi chɛrubzi la baambaaŋ, di ga chi Kɔraawiizi Dia la dominua. Kɔraawiizi jaa yir a baal la n laali a pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagta, ka kpogli kunsɛbikuŋ la,

ref: “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
text: di ŋɔ u be, “Gaagi Jɛrusalɛm biini maa di lɛgzi nɛra la maa n na wii di ra him la hilli, dikuu wikuna la miŋ kiiwe, a nɛra n na ɛɛ a bol biini la wia.”

ref: He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.” The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
text: Ií kpuuzi ba maa, nabɔnzi, biipɔllaa, bichalli, biihaana ani haana maa, haali di bichaljigzi gbaa, ií kpu ba maa. Ama, ií gilɛɛ waa gbɔgzi unla waa maa hile n lɛkkɛ. Awia, ií faari ii huma n Dia naa biini.” Uŋ ŋɔ gunla, ba faari di ra kpuuzi a sitɔɔra la n du Kɔraawiizi Dia see la.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ ba be, “Ií chɔg n Dia, di gil ú diŋŋizi la suugi ni lalaa. Ií la!” Ba faa jaa la a bol biini, di ga ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n bagli baa la.

ref: I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
text: Banna kpuuzi baa la, di n chigɔ n bɛŋ. Denii n chol pi ka lɔ wile, di ŋɔ, “Hoi! Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, amɔ, i baaŋ n fuuh Jɛrusalɛm hina ni naa, guŋ daŋ gil í kpu Izrɛl hina la maa n kawɛɛa?”

ref: The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing.
text: Denii u ŋɔ n be, “Izrɛl ni Juda hina maa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ werge maa. Ba hɛssi maanii suugi nɛkpui, wibii nyaai ge su a bolzeŋ. Ba ra ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizi wàá ra na! U lii a hɛrii.’

ref: And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
text: Awia, màá ka suŋ ba ni, màá gil baa. N daŋ turgi baa ba wichɔgaa la maa kim.”

ref: Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
text: Denii, baal la n laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagta, ka kpogli kunsɛbii la bir ba, di wa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi, n tuŋ i huma la hiŋ ŋɔ ń hum labuu.”

ref: I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne.
text: Mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl kaa binni na kumbɛl n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ koorikara bɛl, baŋ kpa binanii safaaya la kuari, u guali chɛrubzi la nyuu.

ref: The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ a baal la n laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagta la be, “Ga zuu chira la n du chɛrubzi la zɛɛ la baambaaŋ, di lizi niŋhɔla nokoola anɛɛ, di kpaa yaari a bolzeŋ maa ni.” Denii n na binni ka u ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard,
text: Saŋa la a baal n wa zuu a chira baambaaŋ la, di chɛrubzi la chigɔ Kɔraawiizi Dia wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii, baama wa su a biini diŋŋee la maa.

ref: and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi girme la n na chaani la faa kaa izi chɛrubzi la nyuu ga tɔ u Dia dominua. Baama naa faa su u Dia hiŋ maa. U girme hiŋ faa gillɔɔ a diŋŋee maa chaani di ra nyɛgzi.

ref: The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
text: Chɛrubzi la keeri gbɔgza faa ra li Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ loobiire. Haali di i du bossee paga diŋŋee la gba, ka i daŋ nuu.

ref: One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
text: Denii chɛrubzi la bɛl tɛr u nonii lizi a niŋhɔla aŋhina a baambaaŋ, di kpaa du a baal la n laali a pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanii tagta la nonee, u kpaa lii.

ref: I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings,
text: Chɛrubzi la bɛl maa faa dɔɔ noneere alugɔ newee hora, a du a keeri zɛɛzi.

ref: and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite.
text: N kaa binni na chira anaazu, bɛl maa chi chɛrubzi anaazu la bɛl maa kɛra. A chira ra nyɛgzi werge maa alugɔ binanii krisolait la.

ref: Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
text: A chira anaazu maa ge li dɔŋa. Ka a bɛl maa ge ɔɔ ɛɛ lugɔ chira anɛɛ n suu dɔŋa ni, di kaŋli.

ref: so that they could move in any direction without turning. The wheels moved together whenever the creatures moved.
text: Di a chɛrubzi haŋ wàá la bɔr la maa, a maa ɔɔ kpawuu la bɔra anaazu la bɛl maa, di a waa bittɛ.

ref: I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes.
text: A chɛrubzi ni a chira la maanii dɔɔ siwee di bar. Haali a bɔrahɔna maanii dɔɔ siwee bar. A harbɔɔni, nonee ni a keeri la maanii dɔɔ siwee.

ref: And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
text: N kaa nuu loobii bɛl n yiraa, “Chira N Na Birgi Manamanaŋ.”

ref: Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle.
text: A chɛrubzi bɛl maanii dɔɔ siwee bɔra anaazu, lugli hor ɛɛ nabal siwee, nɛɛhiŋ ɛɛ newee siwee, horohiŋ ge ɛɛ bunyiŋ siwee, naazuhiŋ ɛɛ chig siwee.

ref: These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
text: Di a chɛrubzi wa chigɔ, a chira ge ɔɔ chiu, di a wa zaahwɔ, a ge ɔɔ hiŋaabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a kunnyinee hiŋ dunzi faa du a chira la ninɛɛ.

ref: Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi girme la kaa lii u Dia dominua la ga chi guali a chɛrubzi ni.

ref: They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
text: N kaa ra binni ka a chɛrubzi yaa a keeri zaah chiŋ, a ni chira la maa ga hel Kɔraawiizi Dia wiifurii keŋkere dominua la. Denii Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la girme faa ga guali a ni.

ref: I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River.
text: A kunnyinee naa dizi himmaanii n faa na aŋ du Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la be naazi zɛɛ, saŋa la miŋ faa du Muu Kɛbar nua la. N faa zum lugɔ chɛrubzii.

ref: They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
text: A siwee bɔrazi la gba ra li anla miŋ faa nawɛɛ Muu Kɛbar labuu. A kunnyinee bɛl maa ɔɔ zaauh deŋli di ra la.

ref: and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
text: n jaa bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n faa pillɛɛ tɛŋ la, tɛɛ baa.

ref: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, a nɛra naabuu ra bagli nɛra wikuna ni biinikpola wiɛɛlaa ɛɛi a bolzeŋ naa biini la.

ref: They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’
text: Ba kaa ra ŋɔ a nɛra be, ‘Yaa diini mai duglɔɔrɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Jɛrusalɛm ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ vii, yaa ɛɛ lugɔ ol du u biini.’

ref: The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders: I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma iziŋ werge maa, di ŋɔ dí n kali Izrɛl hina be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina, kenne ii ra ŋɔa? Ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi zum ii nfɛssi maanii.

ref: You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies!
text: Ií kpuuzi nɛraa werge maa yaari bolzeŋ naa biini ŋmɛnizi maa.”

ref: This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem,
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “Bolzeŋ naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ vii, banla iiŋ kpuuzɛɛ la ge ɛɛ lugɔ ol du u biini. N daŋ duŋŋi ia lii de.

ref: and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear.
text: Ii ra ɔm laallɛ, ka n daŋ kpa ia du u biini.

ref: Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies.
text: N daŋ duŋŋi ia lii Jɛrusalɛm biini du hɛrduma hina nonee biini, di tɛr ii digna.

ref: You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: N daŋ di ia seriya, bá kpuuzi ia guŋŋ ga hel ii hɛri magbɔɔni. Denii ii zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel.
text: Jɛrusalɛm wàá wer lɛɛ ia gunla vii n ɔɔ lɛɛ ol n du u biini la. N daŋ di ia seriya di ga hel Izrɛl hɛri magbɔɔni.

ref: You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
text: Gunnɛ ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii vɛɛ n widaulaa ni n Gbɔgni hiŋaarɛ, ka ra chanzi wichɔgaa la banla n soge bar ia n na ɛɛ la.”

ref: Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.” A Promise of Hope
text: Too, miŋ haa ra ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzi baa la, denii Bɛnaaya biibaal Pɛlatia chol, di siu. Denii n chol pi, ka lɔ wile werge maa, di ŋɔ, “Hoi, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, Izrɛl hina la n kawɛɛ la maanii í kpu nyaamm gɛɛ?”

ref: The Lord replied:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them.
text: “Newee biibaal, nɛra la n kawɛɛ du Jɛrusalɛm la ra ŋɔ í ni i dɔŋa Izrɛl hina la baŋ laurɛɛ ba ga du hɛrdumazi la wiarɛ, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Ba du bɔɔnɛɛrɛ, ba wàá ka wer jaami Kɔraawiizi, awia, u kpa hɛri labuu tɛɛ yaa.’ ” Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrdumazi la wia

ref: But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia: It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Awia, ŋɔ banla n du hɛrdumazi la be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, dí, haali miŋ duŋŋi baa yaari durnya hɛssi maa gba, ka filaŋkennaa waa, n daŋ jaa du ba be, di guu baa bɔr la maa baŋ duwɛɛ.

ref: And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again.
text: Awia, ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ chaali baa lii hɛssi la baŋ yaarɛɛ la di ba, di kaa wa bir kpa Izrɛl hɛri la tɛɛ baa.

ref: When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much.
text: Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ba bir la ba himmaa hɛri la, ba daŋ ga chɔgi ba vugkuna la miŋ kiiwe werge la maa ta.

ref: Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me
text: Denii ń jaa tɛɛ baa bampirfalaa ni nfɛrfalaa, di lizi ba dignikpega la, ka tɛɛ baa bampiree la n niŋ nɔŋŋiŋ.

ref: and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
text: Gunnɛ bá jaa ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa la maa. Ba daŋ birgi n nɛra, n ge birgi Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum.

ref: But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
text: Ama, ba banla waa n niŋ haa nɔŋŋi ba vuga ni wikuna la miŋ kiiwe wia la, n daŋ turgi baawaa ba wichɔgaa kim, gunla n dɛkkɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them
text: Denii a chɛrubzi faa zaah ni a chira maa di ra la chiŋ. Ka Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la girme la n na nyɛgzi la guali a ni.

ref: left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi girme hiŋ kaa izi a bolzeŋ biini di ga guali u wiifurii paga bizeŋ nyuu.

ref: Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away,
text: A deeza biini, Kɔraawiizi Duma n lalliŋ la, u kpaŋ la Babilɔn hɛri, bɔr la baŋ lauri Juda hina lii ba hɛri, ba ga du la. Denii Kɔraawiizi wia la miŋ nawɛɛ alugɔ deeza biini la jaa tuŋ,

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen.
text: “Newee biibaal, i du nɛra la n kpoŋŋe werge biinii. Ba dɔɔ siweere ka ba waa na, di dɔɔ digna, ka ba waa wia ra nuu, dikuu baŋ kpoŋŋe wia.

ref: So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are.
text: Awia, newee biibaal, bali i kuna alugɔ i ra la hɛrdumaa. Ɛɛ guŋ bɔchaaŋ maga, nɛra wer nai. Aŋhinabe, di ba nai, ba daŋ zum a zɛɛ, haali baŋ kpoŋŋe werge naa maa.

ref: After you have done this, return to your house. Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile.
text: Bali i kuna di bɔr haa chaanɔɔ, bá wer nai, di ɛɛ sirya alugɔ hɛrdumaa i ra la. Lii ŋmɛnɛɛ duana ni bá ra binnii, gunla baŋ ɔɔ lauri nɛra di ra la hɛrdumazi la.

ref: Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching.
text: Gil bá ra binnii, ka í fur i dia koŋlii di kpa i kuna ga de lii.

ref: Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
text: Ban ninna binni la, lalli i kuna sag i vaampɛrɛ di ra kaali, di bɔr ra lauri siwee. Kpa kuŋ tɔ i siwee, di gilɛɛ waa na a hɛri. Annii maanii niŋ ɛɛ karfaa tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.”

ref: I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
text: Denii n ɛɛ gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ń ɛɛ la, di bali n kuna ɛɛ sirya ń kaali hɛrduma, di bɔr haa chaanɔɔ. Denii bɔr n wa duanɛɛ, a nɛra faa ra binniŋ, ka n fur a koŋlii, di kpa n kuna ga de lii, di lallaa sag n vaampɛrɛ, di bɔr ra lauri siwee, n jaa ra kaali.

ref: The next morning, the Lord
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ chɔɔzi ni, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing.
text: “Newee biibaal, Izrɛl hina naa n kpoŋŋe werge dɛɛ pɛɛziibuu, ‘Bɛɛ i ra ɛɛ gunnɛi?’

ref: So he sent me back to tell them: The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
text: Awia, ŋɔ ba be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘A guŋ dɔɔ amaniyee lii n be tɛɛ Koori Zɛdɛkia ni Izrɛl hina la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm la.’

ref: I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
text: Kali baa lugɔ i chigɔɔ tɛɛ baa, di ra bagli wia la n niŋ wa huuzi baa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba daŋ ɛɛ nɛra la baŋ laurɛɛ kaali hɛrdumazi, lugɔ baŋ lɔ nɛra laal di lauri la.

ref: The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving.
text: Koori Zɛdɛkia gba daŋ ga koŋlii la ban niŋ fur tɛu lii, di bɔr ra lauri siwee, di kpa u kuna sag u vaampɛrɛ, di kpa kuŋ tɔ u siwee di ra kaali, wàá ka wer na a hɛri.

ref: The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there.
text: N daŋ ta n asau lawuu, di kpau la Babilɔn hɛri la uŋ wàá wer na, denii ú siu.

ref: His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
text: N daŋ gil u balaa ni u binna ni u laallɔɔra maa yaari bɔr maa, di gil nɛra nyiŋŋi baa, di kpuuzi baa bɔr la maa ban niŋ du.

ref: The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things.
text: Di n wa gillɔ ba yaari hɛrdumazi la, ba daŋ zum lugɔ n bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way. A Sign of Fear
text: Ama, màá gil laal, lɔchɔgii ani wiilchɔgii la min niŋ gil a chol ba ni la kpu baa. Denii ba wer kali hɛrdumazi la ban niŋ la la hina lugɔ ba faa ra ɛɛ n wikiilaare. Denii bá jaa wer zum lugɔ n bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink.
text: “Newee biibaal, gil í bɔra ra sa werge, di i waa di diwee di ra nyɔɔ nii.

ref: Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent.
text: Kali nɛra la n du a hɛri la be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ banla n du Jɛrusalɛm ni Izrɛl hɛri wia. Ba daŋ ɔɔ ra di ba diwee ni biinichɔg, di ra nyɔɔ nii ni bɔhuaih, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba hɛssi maanii niŋ chɔgi di chɔɔ pɛɛ, dikuu ba biinikpola werge wia.

ref: Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord. The Words of the Lord Will Come True
text: N daŋ gil ba dɔma chɔgi ba bolzenaa la maa, ba hɛri maa birgi diŋgela. Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.”
text: “Newee biibaal, sɛɛlii bɛliirɛ Izrɛl hina ɔɔ ra ta lai? Ba ɔɔ ra ŋɔu dí, ‘Saŋaa ra bɛri, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi maa birgi kara hina.’

ref: Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true!
text: Ŋɔ ba be, lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ gil a sɛɛlii naa tuŋ, Izrɛl hina wàá ka tau maa. Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ saŋa helloo, wia la maa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi n ɔɔ faa na lugɔ deeza biini, di baglaa la jaa ɛɛ.

ref: The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages.
text: Di lii Izrɛl hina biini, kara winaalaa lugɔ deeza biini ni daraa wàá ka du de.

ref: I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Ka n daŋ ŋɔ n kipar, di gil a widee ɛɛ manaŋ. Izrɛl hina, ii de dui naa biini iiŋ kpoŋŋe naa, n daŋ gil wii la maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la ɛɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future.
text: “Newee biibaal, Izrɛl hina ra ŋɔu lugɔ i winaalaa lugɔ deeza biini la, daŋ di biŋkpila mɔɔ ka haa wa ɛɛ. Wibirgaa wiarɛ u ra bagli.

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
text: “Newee biibaal, karfi Izrɛl hina dɔgtɛɛzi la n na ŋɔ gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ la. Ba himmaa nfɛssi wiarɛ ba ra ŋɔ. Kali baa, ‘Ií ra nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa!’

ref: I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages!
text: Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ wia werge maa daŋ huuzi a dɔgtɛɛgɛnaa la n na kanni kara, di lii ba himmaa nfɛssi biine, ka ba waa ɔɔ na wiimaa la.

ref: Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city.
text: Izrɛl hina, ii dɔgtɛɛzi naa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyɛgɛzi n du diŋgelli.

ref: They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me.
text: Ii waa laŋŋɛ ga kuari ii koŋlii purgaa la ma tɛɛ Izrɛl hina, á wer chi Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la biini.

ref: Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true.
text: Wia la maa baŋ ɔɔ na lugɔ deeza biini di ŋɔa la, ɔɔ ɛɛ karaa. Ba ɔɔ ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizii ŋɔwɛɛ,’ di n ge lɛi. Ka ba ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ ń gil ba wiŋɔzi la ɛɛ wibii.

ref: They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
text: Ii waa wikara winaalaa lugɔ deeza biini nawɛɛ, di ŋɔ daraa wia, ka ŋɔ dí minuu ŋɔwɛɛ? Di n ge waa wiimaa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ ia.”

ref: So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Ii wiŋɔzi waa deŋlee, ii winaalaa lugɔ deeza biini ge ɛɛ kara. Awia, n daŋ tɔɔri ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
text: N daŋ tɔɔri Izrɛl hina dɔgtɛɛzi la n ɔɔ ra na kara lugɔ deeza biini, ka ba kpaa di ra dar nɛra ba ra leuzi la. Dikuu guŋ wia, ba wàá ka jaa Izrɛl hina nabɔnzi biini gɛɛ bá sɛbi ba sɔna jaa Izrɛl hina biini gɛɛ bá ŋmɛnɛ kaa bir ba Izrɛl hɛri. Denii bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.

ref: Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint.
text: Dɔgtɛɛzi la ɔɔ dar n nɛraa, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Bɔsɔna du denii,’ haali bɔsɔna n waa hoo gba. A guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ a nɛra n ma dia, u koŋlaa waa kpeg, ka dɔgtɛɛzi la ra ɛɛ lugɔ ba kpa hɔɔhrii hamuu.

ref: But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse.
text: Awia, ŋɔ nɛra la n ham a koŋlii la be, dí u daŋ chol. Dozeŋ daŋ ba, ń gil dobee viiruu, pezeŋ ge ta u ni, ú chol.

ref: People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
text: Di a koŋlii wa chollo, a nɛra danna pɛɛzii, ‘Lee a hɔɔhri la baŋ hamuu la duɛi?’ ”

ref: That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “N baaŋ daŋ fuuh werge maa, ń gil pezeŋ ta, dozeŋ ba, dobia chogli di viiri a koŋlii purgi.

ref: The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
text: N daŋ purgi ii koŋlii la iiŋ ham hɔɔhri la nyaamm, ú zɛɛ chɔɔ kpantalaŋ. Di u wa chollo, u daŋ kpu ia. Gunnɛ ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead,
text: N baaŋ daŋ fuuh koŋlii la wia ni nɛra la n hamuu hɔɔhri la ni. N daŋ ŋɔ ii be, ‘A koŋlii ni nɛra la wia tunnɔɔ,

ref: because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Women Who Wear Magic Charms The Lord said:
text: ba faa ɛɛ Izrɛl dɔgtɛɛkara hinaa, di ra dar nɛra lugɔ bɔsɔna daŋ ba Jɛrusalɛm, haali wiimaa n waa hoo di ra bagli guŋ gba la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ!’

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination.
text: Too, newee biibaal, tɛɛ i nɛra la n kpa ba himmaa nfɛssi di ra bagli gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ la haana chɔgri, di ŋɔ ba be gunla n niŋ wa huuzi baa, di du ba ni.

ref: Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies.
text: Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Wia daŋ huuzi haana la n na dar nɛra. Ba kuari sɛbɛzii di ra du nɛra nonee, di kuari ziŋgaabo kabirɛ chimuzi tɛɛ baa, á wer gil ba dɔɔ fɔŋŋa nɛra ni. Ii ɛɛ tamiirɛ lugɔ ii daŋ wer lauri n nɛra guŋ, ka tɔɔrɔɔ wàá huuzi iaa?

ref: They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
text: Haali ii chɔg n sɔŋ di dar n nɛra, dikuu iinna nyiŋŋi baali nokoola suul ni paanuu tama ba be wia, di kaa kanni kara ra tɛɛ n nɛra, ba ge sɛɛ di ra jaa ia. Di kpuuzi banla n waa siu dɛkkɛ, ka gil banla n dɛg siu.’ ”

ref: I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “N hah ii ziŋgaabo kabirɛzi la maa iiŋ kpawɛɛ di ra dar nɛra, di kpaa he lugɔ sidɛɛzi, di ra lauri nɛra lugɔ zumbizi labuu. N daŋ chaahzaa lii ba nonee ni, ka gil ba dɔɔ bahinaa alugɔ zumbee n foozee ŋmɛmbee ni la.

ref: I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
text: N daŋ piili ii chimuzi la ka lɛɛ n nɛra lii ii nonee biini. Ii wàá ka dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ba ni. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ii daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin.
text: Ii kpa kara labuu di gil nɛnanaa bɔra huah, haali miŋ waa nyiŋŋi ba biine chɔgi gba. Ka du nɛchɔgaa bɔkpega lugɔ bá gilɛɛ waa gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi, di wer na bahinaa.

text: Dikuu hiŋ suuh wia la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ tɛi i bichalli saŋa la, ka fuuh n baaŋ la wia, n daŋ turgii i wichɔgaa la maa kim. Sɛnsɛnchɔgaa ni wia la miŋ kiiwe lɛi i ɛɛ di jaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.”
text: Nɛr la maa n na ta sɛɛliizi, daŋ ɔɔ chanzi hìŋ́ Jɛrusalɛm wia sɛɛlii naa, di ŋɔ, ‘Gunla u maa n duwɛɛ, gunnɛ u biihaaŋ gba du.’

ref: You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, i maa faa hah u jaari ni u biizii. I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ i kpɛɛnna ni i niuna la n hah ba janna ni ba biizii. Wibiire lugɔ i maa ɛɛ Hitti hinuurɛ, i mɛɛ ge ɛɛ Amɔri hinuu.

ref: Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages.
text: I kpɛɛmaa bolzeŋ Samaria la ni u biihaana n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la. I niwee genii Sɔdɔm la ge ni u biihaana n du wiifurii nodig wiikakag la.

ref: You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
text: I wichɔgaa la ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ba hora, di ɛɛ n wikiilaa werge maa. Guŋ bɛŋ lɛi, ka i kpa saŋa kpuriire di ɛɛ wichɔgaa kaali baa werge maa.

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ lugɔ i niwee Sɔdɔm ni u biihaana la faa waa biinikpola dɔɔwɛ alugɔ kennaa i ni i biihaana n dɔɔu naa.

ref: They were arrogant and spoiled; they had everything they needed and still refused to help the poor and needy.
text: Na, i niwee Sɔdɔm wichɔgaarɛ keŋ, u ni u biihaana faa ra jigsuu di ra di werge, ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ, di ɔɔ vɛɛ nyaara ni gɛrga hiinaa.

ref: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
text: Ba faa ra tɔgzi bahinaarɛ, di ra ɛɛ wia la miŋ kiiwe n see. Guŋ wiarɛ n kpu baa, i na la.

ref: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
text: Bolzeŋ Samaria wichɔgaa faa waa i wichɔgaa naa duglɛɛ. I ɛɛ n wikiilaare werge maa kaali i lulla la, a ɛɛ lugɔ ba wiarɛ deŋlee kaalii n be.

ref: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
text: A dɛkkɔɔ í di hiihzi werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, i wichɔgaa la chummɔɔ werge kaali i lulla hora, dikuu guŋ wia, a daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ a wiarɛ deŋlee kaalii! Guŋ wia, i daŋ di hiihzi, di ŋmaabi.

ref: Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem.
text: Ka n daŋ kaa gil Sɔdɔm, bolzeŋ Samaria ani ba biihaana nyɛɛli, di kaa gil í gba nyɛɛli,

ref: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
text: guŋ gil i di hiihzi di ŋmaabi, í lulla na lugɔ baawaa bɔwɔɔrɛ.

ref: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
text: I lulla Sɔdɔm, bolzeŋ Samaria ani ba biihaana maanii ń kaa gil ba bir nyɛɛli, a saŋa hiŋ. I gba ni i biihaana daŋ kaa bir nyɛɛli.

ref: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
text: Saŋa la hiŋ faa ɛɛ nɛnanii di ra jigsi la, i faa ra gbɛlli i lulli Sɔdɔmnɛ,

ref: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
text: mɔɔ ka i biinikpola wiɛɛlaa wolo wa lii chaaŋ. Haali Ɛdɔm hina, Filisti hina ani i dɔŋahina maa ra ɛɛi chɛɛtɛ, di faa ra gbɛllii.

ref: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
text: I daŋ di i sɛnsɛŋ tɔɔrɔɔ, dikuu n wikiilaa la maa hiŋ ɛɛwɛ wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
text: Ama, n daŋ liizi a nuukpaŋ la n nii n ɛɛwɛ i bichalli saŋa la wia, di kaa kuari bɛl, ú du de di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
text: Denii í wer ra liizi wichɔgaa la maa hiŋ ɛɛwɛ la, hiihzi lawii. N daŋ gil i lulla Sɔdɔm ni bolzeŋ Samaria birgi i biihaana, haali guŋ n faa waa n nii nuukpaŋ la biini jaawɛ gba.

ref: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Ama, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ kaa bir gil n nii nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la chi nɛnnɛ, denii í jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: I daŋ ɔɔ ra liizi i wichɔgaa la wia, á gil i nua kpu, hiihzi lawii, saŋa la min niŋ wa lizi i wichɔgaa mbusu tɛi la. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
text: “Newee biibaal, ta sɛɛlii tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.

ref: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
text: Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, dí chigzeŋ bɛl keeri n kpekke werge, u huna du jaŋ di du wer nɛnnɛ, ba Lɛbanɔnnɛ wa ku hɛriŋkpol

ref: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
text: nyubaaŋ kelchɔr, di kpau ga hel bolzeŋ bɛl kɔkɔɔza n suwee, di chɔɔzuu de.

ref: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
text: Denii u kpa Izrɛl hɛri daa bɛl bii duu hɛri la n summɛ, nii du de saŋa maa, ú wer hel.

ref: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
text: U lii manaŋ di hel, di lɔɔ taari hɛri. Denii u kela fur deŋli a chig, ka u lunne lau hɛri di ra tuu zɛɛ. U dɔɔ kela ni paŋhoori.

ref: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
text: Ka a chigzeŋ bɛl ge n dɔɔ keekpega ni huna werge, a du wer nɛnnɛ ba, a daa bir u lunne ni u kela la maa chaŋuu, ú tɛɛa nii.

ref: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
text: Ba faa duubuu hɛri bɔnanii, nii kɛrii, ú wer fur kela di nɔŋ, di ɛɛ daananii.’

ref: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
text: Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘U daŋ helaa? Ba wàá kpuzuu di tɔrgi u nɔna, ú siwaa? U kelfalaa la maa daŋ siu. Fɔŋŋa lɛi bá kpa gɛɛ nɛkpila lɛi niŋ kpuzuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, u kpuzaa wàá du kpol.

ref: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
text: Haali di ba kaa chɔɔzuu, u daŋ wer izaa? Di wiifurii peu wa ta u ni, wàá yɔl di siwaa? U daŋ siu u chignibɔr la manaŋ.’ ”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
text: “Ŋɔ Izrɛl dignikpega hina naa be, ‘Ií waa sɛɛlii naa zɛɛ zummɛa? Babilɔn koorii la Jɛrusalɛm ga lau u koori ni u nabɔnzenaa maa bir kaali Babilɔn.

ref: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
text: Denii Babilɔn koori la ga gil u ni a Jɛrusalɛm kooribiizi la bɛl ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, dí u gil u hɛɛhzi lugɔ wàá vɛɛ a nuukpaŋ wia maa. U faa kaa lauri a hɛri sitɔɔra kaali.

ref: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
text: U ɛɛ gunnɛ Izrɛl hina ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ kaa wàá dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. Gunla Izrɛl hina n niŋ ɛɛ du de maanii lugɔ bá ni Babilɔn koori n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ.

ref: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
text: Ka Juda koori la faa vɛɛ Babilɔn koori la nua, ka hum u balaa baŋhina bá la Ijip ga suŋŋi ba laallɔɔrakpila ni ba zagra. Amɔ, baal naa daŋ wer chɔgi nuukpaŋ la ka nuu sumaa?’

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
text: Akai! Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl koori la daŋ siu Babilɔn hɛri, a koori la n tɛu kora ka u gbɛlluu, di chɔgi u nuu nuukpaŋ la hɛri.

ref: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
text: Ijip koori ni u laallɔkpega la wàá wer hiini Izrɛl koori, saŋa la Babilɔn koori n niŋ wa vɔɔ laal di ta pizenaa, di ki bɔɔjaŋra, bá kpuuzi nɛkpila la.

ref: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
text: Dikuu Izrɛl koori n hɛɛhzɛɛ, di ŋɔ nua ka chɔgi ba nuukpaŋ la wia, wàá wer na bɔr lɛɛ u hiŋ.’ ”

ref: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzi, di ra ŋɔ, “N daŋ tɛr Izrɛl koori la digni werge maa, dikuu uŋ chɔgi nuukpaŋ la uŋ kpa n sɔŋ hɛɛhzi ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ hiŋ la wia.

ref: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
text: N daŋ lawuu alugɔ asau n lau kuŋ, di la u ni Babilɔn hɛri ga tɛr u digni, dikuu uŋ nyaa wibii n be wia.

ref: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Izrɛl laallɔɔra la n ninna chɔ maanii bá kpu a laal biini. Banla n niŋ ka ge daŋ chɔ yaari a hɛri kɛraa maa. Denii í zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “N daŋ mɔŋ hɛriŋkpol nyuu kelchɔr la n na fur, di ga chɔɔzi Izrɛl hɛri bizeŋ la n la chiŋ werge maa la nyuu.

ref: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
text: U daŋ hel, di ta kela, di ɛɛ daazeŋ di ra nɔŋ nɛnnɛ. Zumbizi maa ni a dizi ra du daŋa u nyuu, de birgi a chɔɔribɔr.

ref: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
text: Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, daazi ni a dizi maa daŋ zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ɔɔ teŋri daajaŋra ta, ka gil a kpuree ge hel di du jaŋ. Minuu ɔɔ gil daalɛɛri siu, ka gil a hilaa ge fur. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ, awia, n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
text: “Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra ta sɛɛlii naa Izrɛl hɛrɛi? ‘Ba mɛɛwaa ɔɔ ra di grepu nyɛgaa, ka ba biizi nyina ɔɔ lɛɛ ra nyiiria?’

ref: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ ŋɔ, ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka ta sɛɛlii naa Izrɛl hɛri.

ref: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
text: Minuu dɔɔ nɛr maa miibɔɔ. Mɛɛwaa ni ba biizi miibɔɔni du n benii. Awia, nɛr la maa n niŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, a hinnɛ niŋ siu.

ref: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
text: Too, di nɛbɛl du de u wia deŋli, u ra di wibii di ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ,

ref: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
text: waa Izrɛl hina vuga kuna ra di gɛɛ di ra kuaraa. Waa u dɔŋahina haana ra sɛm gɛɛ waa haaŋ la n na ɛɛ doŋa lauwɛ di nyiŋŋi.

ref: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
text: Waa nɛr maa ra fir, di bir nɛra talmazi ra tɛɛ baa. Waa ŋmɛɛ, ka ɔɔ ra tɛɛ lɔzima diwee di ra tɛɛ banla n waa laala dɔɔwɛ laala.

ref: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
text: Di a hiŋ kpa kebee kim nɛr, ka waa ɔɔ saguu nii werge, waa wikara ra ɛɛ, ka ra di nɛra seriya ni wibii.

ref: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
text: Di ra hiŋ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi widaulaa, di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni wibii. A hindee wia deŋloore, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
text: Ama, ka di a baal dɔɔ biibaal, u ra ŋmɛɛ di ra foozi nɛra kuna, di ra kpuuzi nɛra di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa naa dizi,

ref: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
text: u mɛɛ n haa waa ɛɛwɛ, di ra di vuga kuaribɔra la n du bizenaa nyuuni di chɔg u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ,

ref: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
text: di ra fir nyaara ni anuula hina, di ra ŋmɛɛ, waa kaa bir ba talma kuna ra tɛɛ baa. Vugaa u dɛlli, di ra ɛɛ n wikiilaa,

ref: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
text: di ɔɔ kpa kebee ra kim nɛra, ka ra nyiŋŋi tɔna ba be werge maa. Amɔ, a dɛkkɔ a guŋ hiŋ n du de ni miibɔɔaa? Akai! Ba daŋ kpuu, dikuu wikuna naa maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia, ú sɔnchɔgii bir chug u hiŋ.

ref: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
text: Ka di a guŋ wichɔgɛɛri naa ge dɔɔ biibaal, u na u mɛɛ wichɔgaa ni u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la maa unna ɛɛ, ka vɛɛ a ɛɛi,

ref: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
text: di u vɛɛ vuga kuaribɔra kuna dii, gɛɛ di vɛɛ Izrɛl hina vuga ni dɛllaa, di vɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ chɔgaa.

ref: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
text: Waa nyaara ge ra fir gɛɛ di ra lɛɛ talma. Waa ŋmɛɛ, ka ɔɔ ra tɛɛ lɔzima diwee, di ra tɛɛ banla n waa laala dɔɔwɛ laala.

ref: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
text: Waa wichɔgaa ra ɛɛ, waa nii werge ra sag. Di ra hiŋ n Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa. Wàá siu dikuu u mɛɛ wichɔgaa wia, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
text: Ka ii ɔɔ pɛɛzuu, ‘Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ mɛɛ wichɔgaa kinturgaa wàá wer turgi u biibaal ninɛi?’ Akai! Di a biibaal ra ɛɛ nɛnnɛ, u wia deŋli, di ra hiŋ n widaulaa nɛnnɛ, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
text: Nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa, waabuu niŋ siu. Màá kpa biibaal mɛɛ wichɔgaa kim turgi u biibaal, gunnɛ màá kpa biibaal wichɔgaa kim turgi u mɛɛ. Nɛr la maa wia n deŋlee daŋ na u wideŋlaa kinturgaa, biinikpola hiŋ ge na u biinikpola kinturgaa.

ref: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
text: Ka di biinikpola hiŋ gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi, ka bir ra hiŋ n widaulaa, di ra ɛɛ winanaa ni wideŋlaa, wàá siu, ka u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ, wibii maa.

ref: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
text: Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ gil u wichɔgaa la maa tɛu, ka ú dɔɔ miibɔɔ, dikuu wideŋlaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia.

ref: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kaa pɛɛzi lugɔ i ɛɛ tamii lugɔ n bɔra daŋ sɔɔni di biinikpola hina ra siuzaa? Akai! N na nyiŋŋuu lugɔ ba biine chɔgi ba wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, ka dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
text: Ka di nɛr la n na ɛɛ wideŋlaa ge wa bittɔ di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa, di ra ɛɛ wikiilaa la biinikpola hiŋ n na ɛɛ la, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔa? Akai! U winanaa la maa uŋ faa ra ɛɛ la daŋ ɛɛ pɛɛ, ka ú siu dikuu u wichɔgaa ni u wibii nyaai wia.

ref: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
text: Ka ii ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi wia waa deŋlee.’ Ee! Ií ra nuu, Izrɛl hina! N wiarɛ waa deŋlee gɛɛ ii wiarɛ waa deŋleei?

ref: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
text: Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee wa bittɔ di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u daŋ siu dikuu a wia. Wibii maa, u daŋ siu dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia.

ref: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
text: Ka di biinikpola hiŋ ge wa bittɔ lii u biinikpola wiɛɛlaa biini, di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa, di ra di wibii, u daŋ na u hiŋ.

ref: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
text: U daŋ na miibɔɔ, dikuu uŋ zummɛ lugɔ wichɔgaarɛ u faa ra ɛɛ di gilaa ta, ka jaa ra ɛɛ winanaa wia, wàá siu wibii maa, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
text: Ka Izrɛl hina haa vɛɛwɔɔ di ra ŋɔ lugɔ n wia waa deŋlee. Ee! Izrɛl hina, ii wiarɛ waa wibii dɔɔwɛ gɛɛ n wiai?

ref: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
text: Awia, Izrɛl hina, nɛr maanii ń di u wiɛɛlaa seriya. Awia, ii gil ii biine chɔgi ii wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, á gilɛɛ chɔgi ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
text: Ií gil ii wichɔgaa la maa iiŋ ɛɛwɛ la, ka dɔɔ nfɛrfalaa ni bampirfalaa! Izrɛl hina, bɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra nyiŋŋi ii siuzɛi?

ref: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
text: N kipar lɛi nɛr maa siu, awia, ii gil ii biine chɔgi dikuu ii wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, ka dɔɔ miibɔɔ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, “Yir biinichɔg yir naa dikuu Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra wia,

ref: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
text: di ŋɔ, ‘Ii maa faa ɛɛ bunyinniinakpegre bunyinzi biini. U chɔɔ bunyimpɔla biinii, di dɛɛzi u biizi.

ref: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
text: U dɛɛzi u bie bɛllɛ, u hel dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, di helli sela lauraa ni newea heei.

ref: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
text: Denii hɛssi hina nuu u wia, di ki bɔɔ lawuu, di kpa gɔrgazi, tɛrguu kaali Ijip hɛri.

ref: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
text: U maa n wa nawɛɛ lugɔ waa kaa dɔɔ tamii la, u lau u bie la bɛl dɛɛzuu u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa.

ref: He hunted with other lions and learned to eat people.
text: U ɔɔ ra guuzi u dɔŋahina biini, dikuu uŋ jaa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa wia. Di helli sela lauraa ni newea heei.

ref: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
text: Awia, nɛra lii hɛssi kɛraa maa wa fɔɔu ni laal, di ta asau bá lawuu, di lawuu ba bɔɔ la biini.

ref: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
text: Ba faa duu gɔrgazi tɛrguu du dakkazeŋ biini, di kpau ga tɛɛ Babilɔn koori. Denii ba tɔu dia, awia, nɛr maa faa waa kaa nuu u wiraa Izrɛl bizenaa la nyuuni.

ref: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
text: I maa la faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ grepu daa hiŋ duuwe i koo biini, nii kɛrii. U faa dɔɔ kelkpilaa di nɔŋ nɛnnɛ, dikuu uŋ dugli nii wia.

ref: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
text: U kela faa du kpeg lugɔ a wer ɛɛ koori daŋkpala. U hel la chiŋ kaali daazi maa. Ba wer ra nau nɛnnɛ, dikuu u jaŋzi ni u kelkpila la wia.

ref: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
text: Ka ba wa kpuzuu ni baaŋ ta. Wiifurii peu ta u ni, u yɔl, ba kaari u nɔna, u kelkpega la hil, niŋ fuuah.

ref: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
text: Ba chɔɔzuubuu hɛribɔduma la n hillɛ werge, di nyaa nii.

ref: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
text: Denii niŋ lau u kelzenaa la bɛl di wa fuuh u nɔna la maa. Kelkpeg maa waa kaa ka u ni, ú wer ɛɛ koori daŋkpala.’ A biinichɔg yittɛ keŋ, bá ra yiruu saŋa maa.”

ref: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
text: Yaa binni aniidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi anue hɔpizaa fi hɔl, baŋ lauri yaa kaali hɛrdumazi la, Izrɛl hɛri nabɔnzi baŋhina ba mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, bá wa pɛɛzi Kɔraawiizi amaniye bɛl. Denii ba so n see di ra kpaŋ.

ref: Just then, the Lord God said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Izrɛl nabɔnzi naa be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Ii ballɔɔ ii wa pɛɛziŋ wiaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ màá sɛɛ ii pɛɛziŋ wiimaa.’

ref: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
text: Newee biibaal, i ɛɛ siryaa í di baa seriyaa? Di baa! Gil ba zum n wikiilaa la ba naabaala n faa ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ a hɔl la miŋ lizi Izrɛl hina ba ɛɛ n hora la, n lalli n banoniire hɛɛhzi tɛɛ Jekɔb naanna, di kpa n hiŋ bagli baa saŋa la baŋ du Ijip hɛri la, di lalli n banonii ŋɔ lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la.

ref: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
text: Denii n faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ baa lugɔ n daŋ lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri, di la hɛri bɛl miŋ lizɛɛ u du sum, di dɔɔ diwee ni kunnanaa werge, di kaa du wer kaali hɛssi maa la.

ref: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
text: Denii n faa ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ií bɛl maa lizi u hiŋ lii vuga la miŋ kiiwe ka ii ra tɔgzaa la kuaraa biini. Ií gilɛɛ gil Ijip hina vuga chɔgi ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, n bɛnnɛ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum.’

ref: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
text: Ka ba ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa di vɛɛŋ, ba waa n baglaa la nuuwɛ. Ba waa sɛɛwɛ ba kpa ba vuga la banna tɔgzi la ha gɛɛ di vɛɛ Ijip hina vuga kuaraa. Awia, n faa ŋɔ n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ba ni, ń tɔɔri baa werge maa, di ba haa du Ijip hɛri la.

ref: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
text: Ka n faa waa sɛɛwɛ ń ɛɛ gunla miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la, dikuu miŋ waa nyiŋŋi ń chɔgi n sɔŋ nɛra la ni Izrɛl hina n duwɛɛ la be wia. Ba siwiire n lizi n hiŋ bagli baa, di ŋɔ nua lugɔ n daŋ lizi Izrɛl hina lii Ijip hɛri.

ref: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
text: Awiarɛ n faa lizi baa lii Ijip hɛri, di kpogli baa ba hɛribɔduma la.

ref: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
text: N faa tɛɛ baa n widaulaa, di bagli baa n Gbɔgni. Nɛr la maa n niŋ sɛɛ di ra hiŋaa daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
text: N faa kaa tɛɛ baa n Heezaa Hɔpizaa la, á ɛɛ n ni baa nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ la daansɛɛ kuna. N faa ɛɛ gunnɛ bá zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii gillɛ ba ɛɛ nɛnanaananaa.

ref: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
text: Ka Izrɛl hina la faa dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛŋ hɛribɔduma la biini. Ba faa chɔgi n Gbɔgnii di vɛɛ n widaulaa hiŋaa, haali a hiŋaa n niŋ tɛɛ baa miibɔɔ la gba. Ba faa kaa ra chɔgi n Heezaa Hɔpizaa la werge maa. Guŋ wia, n faa ŋɔ ba be lugɔ n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ba ni, n kpu baa nyaamm a hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
text: Ka n faa kaa kuari lau n hiŋ, dikuu miŋ waa nyiŋŋi n sɔŋ chɔgi hɛssi la hina n na gunla miŋ kpogli baa lii Ijip hɛri la be wia.

ref: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
text: N faa ŋɔ ba benii guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa chɔgi n Gbɔgnii di vɛɛ n widaulaa hiŋaa, di chɔgi n Heezaa Hɔpizaa ge werge, dikuu baŋ faa ra tɔgzi ba vuga la wia.

ref: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
text: Ka ba wia faa dɔɔŋ sinyɛna, maa baa kpuwɛɛ a hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
text: Denii n faa karfi Izrɛl hina biizi lugɔ ba gilɛɛ waa hiŋ ba naabaala wiɛɛlaa la, di waa kpa vuga kuaraa ra chɔg bahinaa.

ref: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
text: Minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la. Ií ra hiŋ n widaulaa ni n Gbɔgni.

ref: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
text: Dí ra tɔgzi n Heezaa Hɔpizaa la, á ɛɛ hɔpizinanaananaa ii be, gunnɛ niŋ gil á ɛɛ n ni ia nuukpaŋ la yaa n ɛɛwɛ la daansɛɛ kuna. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum la.

ref: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
text: Ka ba biizi la gba faa dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛŋ. Ba faa chɔg n Gbɔgnii di vɛɛ n widaulaa la hiŋaa, haali a hiŋaa n niŋ faa tɛɛ baa miibɔɔ gba. Ka ba faa ra chɔgi n Heezaa Hɔpizii labuu. Guŋ wia, n faa ŋɔ ba be lugɔ n baaŋ daŋ fuuh ba ni, ń kpu baa nyaamm a hɛribɔduma biini.

ref: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
text: Ka n faa kaa kuari lau n hiŋ, dikuu miŋ waa nyiŋŋi n sɔŋ chɔgi hɛssi la hina n na gunla miŋ kpogli baa lii Ijip hɛri la be wia.

ref: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
text: Ama, n faa lalli n banoniire hɛɛhzi a hɛribɔduma biini lugɔ n daŋ gil ba yaari hɛssi maa biine,

ref: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
text: dikuu baŋ faa chɔg n Gbɔgni di vɛɛ n widaulaa la hiŋaa, di chɔgi n Heezaa Hɔpizaa werge, ka ra kuari vuga la ba naabaala n faa ra kuari la wia.

ref: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
text: Awiarɛ n tɛɛ baa Gbɔgni la n waa wer ni widaulaa la n wàá wer tɛɛ baa miibɔɔ la.

ref: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
text: N gillɔɔ ba doŋ n be dikuu ba sunzaazi, baŋ kpa ba biibambilugla di ra lizi mbusuzi wia, ń gil ɔnsii werge chol ba ni. N ɛɛ gunnɛ ń tɛr ba digna, bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
text: Awia, newee biibaal, ŋɔ Izrɛl hina la be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ii naabaala faa gbɛllimbuu di vɛɛŋ.

ref: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
text: Miŋ ba ba ni hɛri la miŋ hɛɛhzɛɛ ŋɔ n daŋ tɛɛ baa la, ba wa na giŋgimiizenaa ni daazi la n lɔɔwɛ nɛnnɛ, di lizi mbusuzi, di fuuh n baaŋ werge maa, dikuu baŋ lizi mbusuzi di ra tɛɛ ba vuga la wia. Ba kpa ba daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ni sinnii di waa tɛɛa.

ref: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
text: Denii n pɛɛzi baa, beedee a vuga kuaribɔr naa iinna la naanɛi?’ ” Ba ra yiruubuu Bama haali ni zinaa. Seriya dii ni kuari sogaa wia

ref: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
text: Iiŋ ɔɔ kpu ii biibaala di fuuh lizi mbusuzi di ra tɛɛ a vuga la, guŋ gillɔɔ ii wia chɔgi n be haali ni zinaa, dikuu ii vuga hiŋ wia. Izrɛl hina, n sɛɛ ii wiaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ lugɔ màá sɛɛ ii pɛɛziŋ wiimaa.

ref: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
text: Haali ii ɔɔ ra ŋɔu, ‘Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu yaa ni hɛssi la maa hina n soge bar yaa la ɛɛ kpaŋ, di ra kuari daazi ni bia.’ Akai, guŋ ŋmɛnɛ wàá ɛɛ.

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ lugɔ n danna di kora ii ni, ni fɔŋŋa ni baaŋfuuih werge.

ref: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
text: N kpegzi ni n baaŋ daŋ gil n bir chaali ia lii hɛssi la maa iiŋ yaarɛɛ ga du la.

ref: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
text: N daŋ kpogli ia ba bɔr la banna yir ‘Hɛssi Hɛribɔduma’ la, di wa di ia seriya de, yaa maa sibɔɔ.

ref: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
text: Gunla miŋ faa di ii naabaala seriya Ijip hɛribɔduma biini la, gunnɛ ń di ii gba seriya. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
text: N daŋ dɔɔ ii fɔŋŋa, di gil ii ra hiŋ n ni ia nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la nɛnnɛ.

ref: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ lizi banla n dɔɔ dignikpega, di ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa di ra zuu n ni la lii ii biini. N daŋ lizi baa lii hɛri la baŋ duwɛɛ la biini. Ama, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka bir ba Izrɛl hɛri. Gunnɛ ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kaa ra ŋɔu, “Izrɛl hina, bɛ́l maa la gaa kuari u vuga. Ka a harbɔɔ ni, ii daŋ wa nuu tɛŋ wibii maa, di gil n sɔnnaniinanii chɔgaa ni ii sunzaazi ni ii vuga kuaraa la.

ref: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
text: Izrɛl hina maa daŋ waa jaamiŋ n Bizennaniinanii Ziɔn nyuu. Denii ii maa waa humiŋ, ń sɛɛ ii wia, di ra nyiŋŋi ii mbusuzi ni ii sunzinanaa ani ii sunzinanaananaa jaa.

ref: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
text: Saŋa la min niŋ wa lizi ia lii hɛssi la iiŋ yaarɛɛ la biine, di chaali ia, n daŋ sɛɛ ii wia alugɔ mbusuzi lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa. Denii hɛssi hina na lugɔ n ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ du ii biini.

ref: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
text: Di n jaa wa gil ii ba hɛri la miŋ lalli n banonii hɛɛhzi lugɔ n daŋ tɛɛ ii naabaala la, gunnɛ ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
text: Ii daŋ ɔɔ liizi ii wikuna la maa iiŋ faa ɛɛwɛ, a ɛɛ hiihzi wia, di chɔg iihinaa la, á guŋ gil ii hah iihinaa.

ref: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
text: Izrɛl hina, ii daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi, di n wa suŋ ii ni dikuu n sɔŋ girme wia, haali iiŋ dɔɔ biinikpola ni wichɔgaa werge maa la gba. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.” Wia la n na ba á wa huuzi wiifurii nodig wiikakag hina wia

ref: The Lord said,
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
text: Ŋɔ wiifurii nodig wiikakag kɔr la be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu, ‘N na nyiŋŋuu ń fuuih, í daalɛɛri ni a hilaa maa fuuh. Kummaa wàá wer dimuu. U daŋ di di lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ga hel wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di haahri nɛr maa.

ref: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
text: Nɛr maa daŋ na lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii chɔguu, nɛr maa wàá wer dimuu.’ ”

ref: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
text: Denii mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ŋɔ, “Eei, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa! Ba ra ŋɔ n wiarɛ lugɔ sɛɛliizii n na ta.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
text: “Newee biibaal, tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm chɔgri, di ŋɔ wia du bɔra la banna jaami ni, di ŋɔ wii la n niŋ wa huuzi Izrɛl hina,

ref: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
text: di ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ ii dɔmnɛ. N daŋ pam n tokobi lii u too biini, di kpu ii nɛra la wia n deŋlee ni banla wia n waa deŋlee maa.

ref: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
text: Newee biibaal, gil i biini chɔgi, í ra uuri werge maa, a nɛra see alugɔ i tamii n tunnɛ la!

ref: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
text: Di ba wa pɛɛzii, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ i ra uurei? Ŋɔ ba be, ‘N na uuruu dikuu biinichɔg wia la miŋ nuuwɛ anna ba la wia. Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, ɔnsii daŋ lau nɛr maa, ba bɔra huah werge maa. Ba bampirsi daŋ tuŋ, ba bɔra ra sa, ba naahiine ra lɔ dɔŋa kpakpakpakpa.’ Wibii maa, annii maa daŋ ɛɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
text: Nɛra kpui wiarɛ n sazuu. N billuubuu u ra nyɛgzi alugɔ dooŋ! Filaŋkeŋ, ii daŋ kaa mamaa? N nɛra gbɛlli n karfaa ni n dignitɛraa maanii.

ref: My sword has been polished; it's sharp and ready to kill.
text: Ba ra billi a tokobii, bá kpa hum huma, ba sazuubuu di billuu, ba kpau du nɛkpuuri nonee biini.

ref: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
text: Newee biibaal, lɔ wile di ra chɛɛhgi werge maa, dikuu a tokobi n na ba n nɛra ni Izrɛl nabɔnzi maa ni wia. Ba daŋ kpu ba ni n nɛra la maa n kawɛɛ. A viigi i nyuu alugɔ i tamii n tunnɛ la.

ref: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N ɛɛ n nɛraa di ra na, di ba wàá gillɛ ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, wia naa maa daŋ huuzi baa.’

ref: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
text: Newee biibaal, ra lɔ kpaa werge, ka ŋɔ tɛɛ baa wii la maa n niŋ wa ɛɛ. Ka jaa kpa a tokobi la zɛuli, naa bunɛɛ gɛɛ buhoro. A tokobi ra bagli siu ni ɔnsii la dee n niŋ wa huuzi baa wiarɛ.

ref: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
text: U daŋ gil n nɛra bɔra huah, bá ra jiŋli. N ɛɛ tokobi siryaa ba bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa. U ra nyɛgzuu werge maa pilpilpil lugɔ nazaa, ú kpu baa.

text: Tokobi, kɛu la nodig ni nomɛɛl, bɔr la maa i nua n deŋlee.

ref: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
text: N daŋ jaa ra lɔ kpaa, n baaŋ n niŋ jaa sɔɔni wia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
text: “Newee biibaal, dau ŋmɛnizi anɛɛ, á lii bɔkpaŋ, di ra bagli bɔra la Babilɔn koori n niŋ wa kpa ú tokobi ga ba la. Nyiŋŋi daa baŋ bɔr la a ŋmɛnizi n bargɛɛ, di ra bagli unla n na la a bolzeŋ biini la.

ref: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
text: Gil a ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl ɛɛ unla laallɔɔra n niŋ ga, di ga lɔ Ammɔn hina bolzeŋ Raba laal. Á ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl ge ɛɛ unla laallɔɔra n niŋ ga la Juda hɛri bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm la baŋ ma koŋlii bar la.

ref: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
text: Denii Babilɔn koori la jaa wa chi a ŋmɛnichechema ú pɛɛzi na, di zum wii la n du de. U daŋ taazi hobee, di pɛɛzi u vuga ge gunla n dɛkkɛ. Ka jaa pessi sel la baŋ kpawɛɛ lizi mbusu la hiah, di na ŋmɛnɛɛ la un niŋ ga.

ref: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
text: U nodig daŋ kpogli hobii la baŋ sɛbi Jɛrusalɛm sɔŋ u ni la, di ra bagluu bɔr la un niŋ ga dauri dolzenaa, di lɔ laal wile, di kaa dauri dolzenaa la ban niŋ kpa purgi a bolzeŋ dominuuzenaa, di ta pizenaa bar a bolzeŋ koŋlii, di ki bɔɔjaŋra la.

ref: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
text: Ama, Jɛrusalɛm hina daŋ fɛ lugɔ karaa, dikuu ba ni Babilɔn hina nuukpaŋ la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia. Ka Babilɔn koori la daŋ liizi baa ba nuukpaŋ chɔgaa la wia, di lauri baa yoma.

text: Awia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Dikuu ii wichɔgaa la wia, nɛr maa ra na ii chɔgrii, di ra bagli ii wichɔgaa ba wiɛɛlaa maa biini. Ii cholloo, n daŋ kpa ia tɛɛ ii dɔma.

ref: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
text: Eei, i ɛɛ Izrɛl koori biinikpola hinnɛ di ɛɛ nɛchɔgii. I dignitɛraa werge hɔpizii la helloo.
