text: N daŋ kpa n baaŋfuuihchɔgii la tɛr ba digna, di turgi gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ la kim. Di guŋ wa huuzi baa, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
text: “Newee biibaal, Taaya hina bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ werge maa, dikuu Jɛrusalɛm n cholle la wia. Ba ra mam ka ra chaasi, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Unla n dɔɔ kɔkɔɔzi ŋmɛnizi fɔŋŋa la cholloo. Jɛrusalɛm n cholle naa wia, yaa daŋ birgi daama hina!’

ref: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
text: Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Taaya hina, ii birgi n dɔmaa. N daŋ gil hɛrkpila maa hina hah ia, di ra nyiŋŋi ba chɔgi ia, gunla muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ ra lɔ ú kɛraa la.

ref: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
text: Ba daŋ wa purgi bolzeŋ Taaya koŋlaa ni ba diijaŋra la n la chiŋ la maa nyaamm, di gbaari u maa maa, ka gil ú ɛɛ lugɔ bital.

ref: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Laal genii niŋ chɔgi u bola la maa n du a muuzeŋ baŋgia. Denii ba jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, “N daŋ gil Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza la n ɛɛ Koora Maa Koori la, ni u laallɔɔra, u zagra ni a torkozi ani laallɔɔra la n niŋ tinni zagra maa lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wa fɔɔ Taaya hina ni laal.

ref: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
text: U daŋ gil ba chɔgi di kpu nɛra la n du Taaya bola la n du a muu baŋgia la. Ii dɔma daŋ ki bɔɔni, di ta pizenaa pɛgli ii koŋlaa, ka kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa gber ia alugɔ koŋlii.

ref: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
text: U daŋ gil ba kpa dolzenaa ni dɔŋkuna purgi ii koŋlaa ni ii diijaŋra la n la chiŋ la maa.

ref: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
text: U zagkpila daŋ lɔ nyɔɔ tɔ a bolzeŋ maa. A laal zagra torkozi ni a torkozenaa danna kɔɔ, a bolzeŋ la n purgee la koŋlaa ra zigli, di a wa ga u dominuuzenaa ra zuu.

ref: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
text: U laallɔɔra ni ba zagra daŋ su bol biini ni u ŋmɛnizi maa. Ba daŋ kpa tokobizi kpu ii nɛra. Ka jaa purgi a bolzeŋ silminti ligzenaa la maa.

ref: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
text: Ba daŋ paagi ii daama kuna la maa iiŋ dɔɔwɛ la, di chɔgi ii diinanaa la maa, di purgi a koŋlaa. Ba daŋ paagi a daazi ni bia, haali a hembugle maa di ga ta muuzeŋ biini.

ref: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
text: N daŋ gil ii yira la iinna tɔgzi la maa tuŋ. Nɛr maa wàá ka nuu ii nɛra n na lɔ kemzi.

ref: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
text: N daŋ gil a bolzeŋ ɛɛ lugɔ bital, di ɛɛ bɔr la nyinlaura n ninna nyiŋ ba asauzi. Ii wàá ka wer mau maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ Taaya hina be, “Ɔnsii daŋ lau ii banla n soge muuzeŋ nua, ii bɔra ra sa, dikuu banla banna kpu ba ra lɔɔgi wilezi wia.

ref: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
text: A muuzeŋ kɛraa bola koora daŋ tuu ba koorikassi ni, di wir ba koori bɔmbɔgnanaa la baŋ tɔɔhzɛɛ nɛnnɛ dau. Ɔnsii daŋ lau baa werge, bá so hɛri ba bɔra ra sa werge maa, dikuu wia la n na ɛɛ i be la wia.

ref: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
text: Filaŋkeŋ, muuzeŋ kɛraa hina maa bɔra a sau, dikuu hìŋ́ Taaya n cholle la wia. Ɔnsii werge lau a muuzeŋ baaŋ hɛssi hina, ba bɔra huah, dikuu hiŋ cholle wia.’ ”

ref: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil Taaya birgi diŋgela. Nɛr gɛɛ kummaa gba wàá ka du de. Muuzeŋ vile wa tɔ a bolzeŋ maa ni.

ref: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
text: N daŋ gil i tuu lalaa bol ga jaa faala hina ni. N daŋ gil i tuu hɛri ga zuu chɔgaa la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la biini, í ni lalaa ra zuu. Guŋ gil nɛr maa ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka du i biini durnya naa biini.

ref: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N daŋ gil ii Taaya hina laba chum, ií dim. Ba danna nyiŋŋi ia, ka ba ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka wer na ia. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
text: “Newee biibaal, yir lee yir naa tɛɛ bolzeŋ Taaya la

ref: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
text: n soge muuzeŋ nua, u ni nɛra la n soge muuzenaa nuuzi durnya maa biini, di ra di kɔɔzi la, dí Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ, Bolzeŋ Taaya ŋɔ lugɔ u wessoo werge.

ref: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
text: U sogo muuzeŋ baannɛ, u maara kuaruubuu u du wer alugɔ muuzeŋgbernanii.

ref: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
text: Ba kpa daananaarɛ lii Bizeŋ Hɛmɔn nyuu kuaruu. Daazi la banna yir hɛriŋkpol lii Lɛbanɔn labuu ba kpa kuari daajaŋ la baŋ kpawɛɛ baŋ u baambaaŋ la.

ref: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
text: Haali ba faa kpa Basan hɛri daakpega sɛɛh daajaŋra la baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra saa a muugbera la. Saiprɔs hɛri daananaarɛ ba kpa pɛ a muugbera biini, ka jaa kpa bala nyina kuari de.

ref: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
text: Ijip hɛri pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaarɛ ba faa kpa kuari u muugbera wɛjɛ, peu ra taau, ú wer ra vol, u kaa ɛɛ tuuta. Saiprɔs hɛri pɛɛnnanaa la n ɛɛ burgu ni zagbiiŋ niirɛ, ba kpa kuari wɛjɛzi, tɔi chunchugli.

ref: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
text: I muugbersaara la faa lii Saidɔn ni Aavad hɛrzenaare. Banla ge n faa zum muugbera huma lii hìŋ́ Taaya biinii, di faa ɛɛ i muugbersaara.

ref: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
text: Nabɔnzi la n dɔɔ nunzuma lii Gɛbal, di faa ra kuari i muugbessi gba. Nɛra ɔɔ lii hɛrkpilaa zuu muugbessi ba, i ni baa ra yuu di ra yau kuna.

ref: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
text: Baala faa lii Pɛsia, Lidia ani Libia hɛssii wa birgi i laallɔɔra. Ba kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ni ba kahurozii sagzi i koŋlaa ni, guŋ gil i dɔɔ girme.

ref: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
text: Baala la ge n lii Aavad ni Hɛlɛk hɛssi ɔɔ tinni a koŋlaa nyuuni di ra du tau. Gamad hɛri baala faa ra binni i diijaŋra la n la chiŋ la ni. Ba kpa ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa sagzi i koŋlaa ni, gunna bagli i wessi ni i girme.

ref: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
text: I ni Taasis hina faa ba kpa saliŋhuŋŋa, lugbia, kpana ani a dizi maa, di waa chɛr i daama kuna.

ref: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
text: Kɔkɔɔza ɔɔ faa lii Giris, Tubal ani Mɛsɛk hɛssii, di kpa yoma ni danyɛ, di waa chɛr i kuna.

ref: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
text: Baŋhina ge lii Bɛf Togama, di lauri zagra la n na hum huma, laal zagra ani kauzi di waa chɛr i kuna.

ref: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
text: I ni Roods hɛri hina gba faa ra yuu kuna di tɛɛ dɔŋa. Nɛra ge lii muu kɛraa hɛssi di kpa bala nyina ni pomegranet daazi, di waa chɛr i kunyoolaa.

ref: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
text: Juda ni Izrɛl hɛssi hina maanii i ni baa faa ra yau di ra yoo kuna dɔŋa be. A ba kpa mia, huuhnuu, ɔlivi nuu ani nuusɔɔhrinanii bɛl banna fɔgli, di wàá chɛr i kunyoolaa.

ref: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
text: Damaskus hina gba nii faa ra yau di ra yoo kuna, dikuu i daama kuna werge la wia. A ba faa kpa siŋ lii bol bɛl banna yir Hɛlbɔn ni peeza huna ge lii Zahaa ba.

ref: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
text: Lɔrbizi ni Kɛda sitɔɔra ge ɔɔ lauri pebizi, pebala ani buunaa di waa yoo i be.

ref: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
text: Siiba ni Raama hɛssi kɔkɔɔza ge gba ɔɔ kpa daahɛgsɔɔhsuma ni a irizi, binanaa ani salinnɛ di waa chɛr i kunyoolaa.

ref: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
text: Bolzenaa Haran, Kanɛ ani Ɛdɛn, di kpa Siiba kɔkɔɔza ni bolzenaa Asur ni Kilmad hina maanii ɔɔ faa waa chɛr i kuna.

ref: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
text: A ba faa kpa bɔmbɔgnanaa, wɛjɛ burguzi, kuna baŋ tɔɔhzɛɛ, dia kumpɛɛri kuna, ŋmɛnni ani a dizi baŋ pɛttɛ nɛnnɛɛ di waa chɛr i kuna.

ref: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
text: Taasis hɛri muugbessi labuu faa ra chi i kunyoolaa. I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muugbera la n du muuzeŋ baaŋ, buntɔga suu werge maa.

ref: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
text: I muugbersaara la saaibuu di ra zuu a muuzeŋ baambaaŋ. Ka wiifurii pezeŋ daŋ chɔgii a muuzeŋ baambaaŋ.

ref: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
text: Muugbersaara la maanii niŋ gil ba muugbessi, muugbersaara nabɔnzi ni a huŋhunna maa daŋ chi baŋgia.

ref: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
text: Ba maa ra wii werge di ra tɛi, di ɛɛ hɛɛhraa di ra waari ba nyuuni, di chɔɔ hɔɔhri biini ra billi.

ref: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
text: Ba daŋ fuŋ ba nyuuni, di tɔ gbɔglɔnzi dikuu i wia. Ba daŋ wii werge maa ni biinichɔg tɛi.

ref: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
text: Ban ninna wii ni biinichɔg werge labuu, bá yir lee yir naa ra tɛi. ‘Bolzeŋ bɛl faa du denii kaali Taaya naa, muuzeŋ tɔ u nii?’

ref: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
text: I kunyoolaa la hiŋ faa kpawɛɛ la hɛrdumazi la, faa kuari hɛrkpila maa hinaa. I daama werge la faa gillɔɔ a hɛssi koora birgi daama hina.

ref: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, i ɛɛ muugbera la n pergeere chɔɔ muu zɛɛ, i ni i kunyoolaa ni i nɛra maanii a muuzeŋ di.

ref: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
text: Nɛra la maa n soge a muuzeŋ kɛraa la bɔra faa huahwɔɔ werge maa, dikuu i cholzeŋ la wia. Ɔnsii lau ba koorizenaa, ba bɔra ra sa werge maa, ba hɔrmi.

ref: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
text: Hɛssi kɔkɔɔza ra viigi ba nyuuni, dikuu hiŋ chol cholchuma, i ŋmɛnɛ maa n wàá ka izi wia.”

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Taaya koori be, dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Dikuu i barabara werge wia, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ vugrɛ, di so koorikara ni muuzeŋ baambaaŋ. Ka i ɛɛ neweere, haa vug ɛɛwɛ, haali hinna fɛ lugɔ i dɔɔ nunzumaa lugɔ vug la.

ref: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
text: I fɛ lugɔ i dɔɔ nunzumaa kaali Danɛl, wiimaa waa i ni suahwɛ.

ref: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
text: Dikuu i nunzuma ni i wia zɛɛzi zumaa la wia, i birgi daama hiŋ werge maa, di dɔɔ saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋa werge maa.

ref: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
text: Hiŋ zum kɔɔzaa werge la wia, i daama waazɔɔrɛ werge maa, guŋ gil i ra jigsi.

ref: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
text: Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, Hinna fɛ lugɔ i dɔɔ nunzumaa lugɔ vug la wia,

ref: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
text: n daŋ gil hɔɔhra la n dɔɔ sikpegii werge, wa lɔi laal, di chɔgi i nunzuma ni i girme la maa.

ref: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
text: Ba daŋ kpui, í siu siuchuma, bá kpai ha muuzeŋ biini.

ref: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
text: I daŋ kaa wer ŋɔ i ɛɛ vugrɛ, nɛra la n niŋ kpui la bee? Baa waa zummɔɔ lugɔ haa vug ɛɛwɛ, neweere hiŋ.

ref: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
text: I daŋ siu lugɔ nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ hɔɔhra nonee biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
text: “Newee biibaal, a wii dikuu Taaya koori wia, di ŋɔ u be, ‘Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ i faa wessoo kaali nɛra maa, di dɔɔ nunzuma werge maa.

ref: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
text: I faa du Ɛdɛnnɛ, kambol la Kɔraawiizi n kuarɛɛ nɛnnɛ, daazi du de, di faa laali binanaa naa, rubi, topaz, ɛmɛrald, kisolɛt, ɔnigs, jaspa, safaaya, tɛkɔis ani bɛril bɔmbɔgaa! Saliŋ kuna biinii i faa du. Ba faa kuaraabuu tɛi a hɔl la miŋ mai la.

ref: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
text: N faa liziibuu, di gil i ɛɛ lugɔ n chɛrub la bɛl, i ra binni mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi bizennaniinanii la ni, di ra vol n binanaa la n na nyɛgzi biini.

ref: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
text: I faa waa chɔgri maa dɔɔwɛ lii saŋa la miŋ mai la, guŋŋ di wa hel a hɔl la miŋ zummɛ lugɔ i ɛɛ biinikpola hinnɛ la.

ref: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
text: I soochi dii werge la faa gillɔɔ i ra nyiŋŋi kalu, di dɔɔ wichɔgaa. Awia, n faa duŋŋiibuu, lii mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi bizennaniinanii la nyuu. Haali mɛlika la n faa ra guui la gba, duŋŋiibuu lii n binanaa la n na nyɛgzi la biini.

ref: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
text: I faa ra jigsuu, dikuu hiŋ ɛɛ bunɔɔŋ la wia. I girme werge la faa chɔgi i nunzumaa. Awiarɛ n kpai ta hɛri, í ɛɛ daansɛɛ kuŋ tɛɛ durnya koora maa.

ref: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
text: I wichɔgaa ni i kɔɔzichɔgaa la gillɔɔ i chɔgi i jaamibɔra. Awiarɛ n faa gil niŋ fuuh i bolzeŋ maa nyaamm, u birgi hɔɔhri nɛkpila maa see la.

ref: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
text: A hɛssi la maa hina n faa zumii la bɔra huah werge maa dikuu i wia. I wia tunnɔɔ ni biinichɔg werge maa. I ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka du de.’ ” Wia la n niŋ wa huuzi bolzeŋ Saidɔn wia

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
text: Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Bolzeŋ Saidɔn, n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ, i benii ń ga na girme. Nɛra daŋ zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi, saŋa la min niŋ wa tɔɔrii, ka bagli n nanni i biini la.

ref: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ gil wiilchɔgaa chol i ni, di gil bá kpu nɛkpila maa ge i ŋmɛnibaana. A lalaa daŋ yaari i biini maa, bá ra lɔi laal bɔr maa. Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
text: Hɛssi la hina n bar Izrɛl la wàá ka ɛɛ ba dɔma, di ɛɛ lugɔ choŋgolaa ni sɔɔhri n na wii werge. Denii bá zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.’ ”

ref: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Di n wa chaali n nɛra Izrɛl hina lii hɛssi la baŋ yaarɛɛ la biine, ba bir ga so hɛri la miŋ faa kpawɛɛ tɛɛ n balii Jekɔb la, n daŋ bagli n nanni n nɛra Izrɛl hina biini, durnya hina maa na.

ref: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
text: Ba daŋ wa so ba hɛri ni bɔsɔna, di ma diini, di dau grepu daazi kooni ge gba jaa, a nɔŋ di ra tɛɛ baa. Di ba jaa wa na minna tɔɔri hɛssi la hina maa n faa ra tɔɔri baa la, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.”

ref: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
text: A binni fi baagu fihiŋ, hɔpizaa fidaanɛɛ hɔl, saŋa la baŋ lauri yaa kaali hɛrduma la, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
text: “Newee biibaal, hau Ijip koori ni, di ŋɔ wia la maa n niŋ wa huuzi u ni Ijip hɛri maa du ba ni.

ref: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
text: Ŋɔ dí kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ, ‘Ijip koori, n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ. I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyugzeŋ, di chɔɔ muu biini. I ra ŋɔu lugɔ Muu Naal la ɛɛ n hotte, minuu kuaruu.

ref: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
text: N daŋ kpa gɔrgazi di du i nua lawii. Nyinni margi i hɔŋ maa ni, ń tɛrgi i ni nyinni la maa n margi i bɔrahɔŋ la ni lii baŋgia.

ref: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
text: N daŋ gil i ni nyinni la maa n du i muu la ta hɛribɔduma. I daŋ chol baŋgia, nɛr maa wàá hugii. N daŋ kpai tɛɛ hɛri naa pir sela ni u zumbizi, á di.

ref: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
text: Denii Ijip hina maa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ijip hina faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ koori daŋkpala tɛɛ Izrɛl hina.

ref: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
text: Ba faa lawiibuu kpogli, ka i peri lugɔ daapiah di tɔɔh ba kugzi. Ba faa kaa dɛllii, ka i ku, ba chol di guzi ba charazi.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ gil laallɔɔra wa kpu i nɛra ni ba sela maa.

ref: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
text: Ijip hɛri daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma, wàá ka dɔɔ tɔna. Denii bá jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi. Dikuubɛɛwiai, i ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Muu Naal ɛɛ n hotte, minuu kuaruu.’

ref: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
text: Awia, n jaa birgi i ni i muu la maa dɔmnɛ. N daŋ chɔgi Ijip hɛri maa ú chɔɔ pɛɛ, di chi bolzeŋ Migdɔl ga hel bolzeŋ Aswan, guŋŋ ga hel i ni Itiopia hɛri magbɔɔ.

ref: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
text: A daŋ di binni tokkoanɛɛ, di nɛr gɛɛ sel gba waa kaa vol a de hɛri hiŋ. De daŋ birgi hɛribɔduma.

ref: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
text: Izrɛl hina wàá ka dɔɔ tamii lugɔ ba yardi Ijip hina lugɔ bá hiini baa. Ijip hɛri cholaa la daŋ gil Izrɛl hina liizi lugɔ ba faa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, saŋa la baŋ faa ŋɔ lugɔ Ijip hina hiini baa la. Denii Izrɛl hina jaa zum lugɔ Minuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la.”

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
text: “Newee biibaal, Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza laallɔɔra faa fɔɔ Taaya hinaa ni laal, ka a du kpol tɛɛ baa. U faa gillɔɔ u laallɔɔra chi buntɔga, ba vaampɛrɛzi ge maa forgi, ka u ni u laallɔɔra la waa tɔna maa nawɛɛ a laal biini.

ref: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpa Ijip hɛri tɛɛ Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza. U daŋ foozi di ŋmɛɛ ba daama ni kuna la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ, di turgi u laallɔɔra.

ref: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: N kpa Ijip hɛrii tɛu, ú birgi u huma tɔna, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ni u laallɔɔra faa chɔg Taayaa tɛŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: Di guŋ wa ɛɛwɔ, n daŋ kaa gil Izrɛl hina dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. Ka gil hìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ŋɔ wia bɔr la nɛr maa n niŋ nuu i loobii. Gunnɛ ba jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ wia ra bau! Lɔ wile ŋɔ, ‘Ɔnsii werge hɔpizii ra bau!’

ref: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
text: A hɔpizii duglɔɔrɛ, a hɔpiziirɛ Kɔraawiizi hum u huma. A hɔl, baama daŋ bir biri, tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ chol hɛssi hina maa ni.

ref: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
text: Laal daŋ chol Ijip hɛri, bá kpu nɛra ni tokobizi. Biinichɔg werge lau Itiopia hina. Di ba wa kpu Ijip hina kpila maa, ba daŋ chi ba daama kaali, ka purgi a bola á birgi diŋgelli.

ref: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
text: Ba daŋ kpuuzi Itiopia, Libia, Lidia ani Lɔrbizi hɛssi hina ni n nɛra baŋhina ani Ijip hina a laal biini.”

ref: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Hɛssi la hina ni Ijip hina n dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la daŋ chol laal biini, Ijip hina laallɔɔra fɔŋŋa la wia banna jigsi la daŋ tuŋ. Ba daŋ kpu baa laal biini, di lii Migdɔl guŋŋ di ga hel Aswan. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
text: A hɛssi daŋ birgi diŋgelli jaa durnya hɛssi diŋgelli ni. A bolzenaa ge purgi di jaa bolzenaa la n purgee ge ni.

ref: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Di n wa gillɔ ba fuuh Ijip hɛri, ka gil banla maa n na hiinuu, siuzi la, ba daŋ jaa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
text: Di a hɔl wa hello Ijip hɛri chɔgi, n daŋ hum n balaa bá kpa muugbessi ga ɔnzi Itiopia hina, dikuu banna fɛ lugɔ wiimaa wàá huuzi baa wia. Bɔsai werge maa daŋ chol ba ni, Ijip tɔɔrɔɔ hɔpizii la n niŋ ba wibii maa la wia.”

ref: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “N daŋ gil Babilɔn Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza kpu Ijip hina kpila maa.

ref: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
text: N daŋ gil Muu Naal ni u gɔŋa maa hiihzi, di kpa a hɛri du nɛchɔgaa nonee biini. N daŋ gil hɔɔhra wa chɔgi Ijip hɛri ni kuna la maa n du de la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu, “N daŋ purgi Ijip hina vuga ni anla maa baŋ mawɛɛ lugɔ newea, a du Mɛmfis la. Sitɔɔri wàá ka du Ijip hɛri maa. N daŋ gil ɔnsii lau a hɛri hina maa.

ref: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ chɔgi Ijip wiifurii nodig wiikakag, ú birgi diŋgela, di gil niŋ fuuh bolzeŋ Zoan n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la, di tɛr bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs hina digna werge maa.

ref: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
text: Gunnɛ n baaŋ kaa fuuh bolzeŋ Pɛlusiɔm la n ɛɛ Ijip hina bolkpeg la ni, di gil ba kpu bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs hina kpila maa.

ref: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
text: N daŋ fuuh Ijip hɛri, di gil bolzeŋ Pɛlusiɔm hina di dɔgnya werge maa, di purgi bolzeŋ Tɛbɛs koŋlaa la n baruu la nyaamm. Mɛmfis hina ge daŋ du siaahmu biini di hanna la.

ref: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
text: Hɛliɔpɔlis ni Bubastis bolzenaa biipɔllaa maanii niŋ siu laal biini, ka ba lauri banla n kawɛɛ kaali.

ref: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
text: A hɔl la min niŋ wa chɔgi Ijip fɔŋŋa ni u kpegzi la wia unna jigsi la tuŋ, Bɔbiri daŋ tɔ Tapanɛs. A hɔl, baama daŋ tɔ Ijip hɛri, ka bá lauri u boljigzi la hina maa kaali.

ref: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
text: Kenne ń tɛr Ijip hina digna werge maa, bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
text: “Newee biibaal, n kpegli Ijip koorii. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ miŋ ku u nonii, ka ba wɔɔ vɔɔwɛ ú choŋŋi, di kaa du kpeg di wer lau tokobi gba.

ref: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
text: Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, dí, n ɛɛ Ijip koori dɔmnɛ. N daŋ kuugi u nonee maa, u kpeg la ni unla n kuwee la gba, di gil a tokobi lii u nonii chol hɛri.

ref: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
text: N daŋ gil Ijip hina yaari durnya hɛssi maa biine.

ref: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ tɛɛ Babilɔn koori la fɔŋŋa werge maa, ka gil Ijip koori waa gɛrgi. Ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi, di n wa kpa n tokobi du Babilɔn koori nonii, ú viiguu Ijip hɛri.

ref: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
text: N daŋ gil Ijip hina yaari durnya hɛssi maa biine. Denii bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Ijip koori ni u nɛra maa be, ‘Anɛɛ n niŋ wer kpa u hiŋ di mɛgzi ii zennei?

ref: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
text: Asiiria faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ hɛriŋkpol daa bɛl n du Lɛbanɔn Kɔr, u kela du wer, u lɔɔ nɛnnɛ, u hel saagi u dɔŋahina maa ni a kɔr biini.

ref: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
text: Nii du de di gil u ra hel, bulli ge gil u ra hel jaŋzi ni. A gɔŋa faa pal ra bar u zɛɛ maa, di pal ra zuu a kɔr daazi maa zɛɛzi.

ref: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
text: Awia, u faa helloo kaali daazi la maa n du a kɔr biini. U kela hel nɛnnɛ di du jaŋra, di yɛl, dikuu nii n du de nɛnnɛ wia.

ref: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
text: Zumbizi maa faa du daŋaa u kela ni, pir sela maa gba ra lul a biizi u bɔsɔŋ. Hɛrzenaa maa hina ge faa ra so u chunchugli di ra heezi.

ref: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
text: A daa naa dee faa helloo kaali Kɔraawiizi kambolnanii la n du Ɛdɛn biini hɛriŋkpola maa. Hàá wer kpa daananaa maa mɛgzi u kela. Haali daa maa faa waa hoo hin niŋ kpa mɛgzi u kela. Daa maa ge faa waa hoo a kambolnanii biini di du wer heluu.

ref: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
text: N faa gillɔɔ u du wer nɛnnɛ, di dɔɔ kelkpila werge. N kambolnanii hiŋ daazi faa ra nyiŋŋi á du u duula la.

ref: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ ŋɔ ii be gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ a daa naa n helle di gaa chug baama, di ra tɔgzi u hiŋ naa wia.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
text: N daŋ kpau du hɛrduma koori nonee biini. U daŋ ɛɛ a daa gunla n dɛkkɛ, dikuu u biinikpola wia. N vɛɛubuu,

ref: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
text: hɛrdumazi hina la n dɔɔ sikpegii kaali hɛssi maa hina la wa teŋuu ta, di giluu. Uŋ cholle la, u kela vuuri bizenaa nyuuni ni walli maa biine. A kuugi chɔɔ a hɛri faalime maa biine. Hɛssi maa hina chɔ lii u chunchugli biini ka kau.

ref: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
text: Zumbizi maa togni a daa la n cholle la ni, ka pir sela maa ge ra vol u kela la ni.

ref: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
text: Awia, daa maa gilɛɛ kaa ra tɔgzi u hiŋ dikuu un na nii bɔr chi di hel, di du jaŋ saagi u dɔŋahina ni wia. Daa maa n na nii nɛnnɛ ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka hel guŋ dɔŋ, a maanii dɛkkɛ an niŋ siuzi zuu hɛri, di ga jaa lalaa ni.’ ”

ref: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “A hɔl la baŋ huguu la, n faa gillɔɔ bulli tɔ u ni alugɔ banna wii u lee. N gillɔɔ u muuni ni gɔŋa palaa teŋ, waa kaa ra na nii. Dikuu uŋ siuwɛ wia, n gillɔɔ bɔbiri tɔ Lɛbanɔn bizenaa ni, u kɔr daazi maa siuzi.

ref: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
text: Saŋa la uŋ cholle la, n faa gillɔɔ hɛssi hina la maa bɔra ra sa. Saŋa la miŋ huguu la, daazi la gba maa n faa du a Ɛdɛn kɔr biini, anla n wesse werge lii a Lɛbanɔn hɛri, a lunne zuu hɛri bɔr la n sɔɔnɛɛ la nɛnnɛ la maa, bɔra faa sɔɔnɔɔrɛ a ŋmam biini.

ref: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
text: Banla maa n faa ra zuu u bɔsɔŋ, ba nuu dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la maa nuubuu zuu a ŋmam biini, di ga jaa banla maa baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la ni.

ref: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Ɛdɛn kɔr daazi la, ú bɛliirɛ bá kpa i wessi ni i zenni mɛgzi naanɛi? Ka i ge gba ni Ɛdɛn daazi maanii niŋ zuu a ŋmam biini ga chɔɔ banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi, ba waa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la biini. Ijip koori ni u harbɔɔ hiŋraa guŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
text: Binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi fidaanɛɛ, lugli hɔpizii la baŋ lauri yaa la hɛrdumazi la hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
text: “Newee biibaal, yir lee yir tɛɛ Ijip koori, di ŋɔ u be, ‘I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ bunyiŋ hɛssi hina maa biini, ka i ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nyugaa n du muuzeŋ biini di ra lɔ nii, di ra koozuu ni i naazi, di ra puruu.’

ref: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
text: Awia, kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ ta asau lawii, di gil nɛkpila tɛrgii lii baŋgia.

ref: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
text: N daŋ kpai ta hɛri, di gil durnya zumbizi ni pir sela maa wa dii.

ref: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
text: N daŋ gil i ola yaari bizenaa nyuuni, di gil i hoga ge suugi walli.

ref: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
text: N daŋ gil i chal pal pɔɔh a hɛri guŋŋ di ga chug bizenaa, di gil i ola suugi faalime.

ref: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
text: Di mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi wa chɔgi i wia tuŋ kɔrai la, n daŋ tɔ chiŋ, di gil chinchiŋwilaa biri. N daŋ gil baama bɛl tɔ wiizi ni, baagu ge wàá ka chaani.

ref: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: N daŋ gil kuna la maa n du chiŋ di ra chaani la biri, di gil i hɛri maa biri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
text: N daŋ gil hɛrkpila hina maa biine chɔgi, di n wa gillɔ hɛssi la hiŋ waa zummɛ la hina nuu i chɔgaa wia.

ref: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
text: N daŋ gil i wia huah hɛrkpila hina bɔra werge, koora bɔra danna sa, ɔnsii lau baa dikuu i wia, di n wa viigi n tokobi ba see. I cholli hɔpizii la, ba bɛl maa bɔra danna sa werge, dikuu u miibɔɔ wia.’ ”

ref: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
text: A guŋ wia, kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Babilɔn koori daŋ kpa u tokobi wa lɔi laal.

ref: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
text: N daŋ gil laallɔɔra lii hɛssi la hina n dɔɔ sikpegii werge, kpa ba tokobizi wa kpu i nɛra maa. Ba daŋ kpu i nɛra maa di chɔgi kuna la maa hiŋ kuu a wia di ra jigsi la.

ref: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
text: N daŋ kaa kpu i nauna maa n du niizenaa kɛraa, nɛra wàá ka koozi a niiri ni ba naazi, gɛɛ nauna puraa ni a naazi maa maa.

ref: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Denii ń kaa gil Ijip niiri la maa chol yelemm, di gil a kaa ra pal bɔɔiih alugɔ nuu. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
text: Di n wa gillɔ Ijip hɛri maa chɔɔ pɛɛ, di chɔgi kuna la n du u biini, di kpu nɛra la maa n du de la, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
text: Wibii maa, lee yir naabuu bá yir dikuu u wia. Hɛssi hina la maa biihaana daŋ yiruu, di wii ra tɛɛ Ijip hɛri ni u nɛra maa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
text: Binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, lugli baagu hiŋ, hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ, baŋ lauri yaa la hɛrdumazi la hɔllɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
text: “Newee biibaal, wii ra tɛɛ Ijip nɛkpila. Kpa baa ga jaa hɛrkpega nɛra ni, di hug baa, bá ga jaa lalaa ni.

ref: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
text: Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Ii fɛwɔɔrɛ lugɔ iabuu wesse kaali nɛra maa? Ií tuu la ga chɔɔ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la be, lalaa bol.’

ref: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
text: Ijip hina ni banla maa n siuwɛ a laal biini labuu niŋ kpau chol. N pam n tokobii ń kpu ba maa.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
text: Ba ŋmama la du a bɔɔluŋ hiŋ biinii, u laallɔɔra ŋmama bar u ŋmam. Banla n faa gillɛ ɔnsii lau nɛra werge a hɛri biini labuu ba kpu ni tokobi la.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
text: Ɛlam chɔɔwɔɔ jaa banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ laal biini la ni, u laallɔɔra ŋmama baruu. Ba bɛl maa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu ba maa laal biini. Ba de dui saŋa, ba faa gillɔɔ ɔnsii werge lau nɛra, ka filaŋkeŋ, ba siuzɔɔrɛ chɔɔ, ba ni banla maa n siuzɛɛ laal biini la, kpau di hiihzi.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
text: Mɛsɛk ni Tubal gba maanii ba faa hug de, ba laallɔɔra ŋmama bar baa. Ba bɛl maa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu ba maa laal biini, ka baabuu faa ra ɔnzi nɛra werge ba de dui saŋa la.

ref: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
text: Ba faa waa baa hukke ni girme gunla baŋ faa ra hug nabɔnzenaa saŋa la. Ba ɔɔ faa kpa ba laal kunaa jaa ba ni hugzi, ba nyuuni sil ba tokobizi, ba laal pɛrɛtuzenaa ge tɔ ba bɔra. Nabɔnzenaa naa faa kpekkoo werge, di ɔnzi nɛra ba de dui saŋa la.

ref: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
text: Ijip koori, gunnɛ bá kpu i ge, í ga chɔɔ banla n waa mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba kpu baa ni tokobi la be.

ref: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
text: Ɛdɔm hina gba, ba koora ani ba sitɔɔra maa faa chɔɔ denii. Haali baŋ faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge la gba, ka ba ni nɛra la maa baŋ faa kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la maanii chɔɔ de. Ba ni banla n faa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ la maanii faa du a lalaa bol.

ref: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
text: Wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag hɛssi sitɔɔra ni Saidɔn hina maanii ba faa hug de. Ba ni banla maa n siuwɛ laal biini la di hiihzi, haali baŋ faa kpa ba kpegzi di ra ɔnzi nɛra werge, ba de dui saŋa la. Ba faa waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ, ba ni banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la chɔɔ de, di ra di hiihzi lalaa bol.

ref: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
text: Ijip koori ni u laallɔɔra maa n niŋ wa na baa, u bampirii daŋ tig werge maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, u laallɔɔra bɛŋ lɛi faa siuwɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ra ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Haali miŋ faa gillɛ Ijip koori kpa ɔnsii ta nɛra ni werge, u de dui saŋa la, ka n daŋ gil bá kpu u ni u nɛkpila la maa, di hug baa banla n waŋ zummɛ ni banla baŋ kpuwɛɛ ni tokobi la biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
text: Di u wa na ba dɔm n na ba, u ɔɔ huuh bensunoniinaa karfi nɛr maa.

ref: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
text: Màá ka liizi u wichɔgaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la bɛl maa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, u jaa ɛɛ wia la n dɛkkɛ ni wideŋlaare, u daŋ na miibɔɔ wibii maa.

ref: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
text: Saŋa la baŋ faa lau yaa kaali hɛrduma la binni fidaanɛɛhiŋ, baaguzi fi hɔpizaa anuehiŋ hɔl, baal bɛl faa chɔ lii bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm, di wa ŋɔ n be, “Jɛrusalɛm cholloo!”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ i nɛra be gunla n ɔɔ ɛɛ, di n wa gillɔ laal chol hɛri maa hina ni. Ba ɔɔ lizi ba bɛllɛ u ɛɛ ba guuri.

ref: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
text: Uŋ nuu a bensunoniina wiraa ka waa hagzɛɛ la, u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi u hiŋ ni. Di u faa hagzɔɔrɛ, u daŋ faa lɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
text: Ama, di a guuri wa na ba dɔm n na ba ka u siigi, waa a bensunoniina huuhwɛ di karfi a nɛra, ka ba wa kpu ba bɛl maa, a hiŋ daŋ siu dikuu u wichɔgaa wia, ka u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi a guuri ni.

ref: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
text: Newee biibaal, n gillɔɔ i ɛɛ Izrɛl hina guuri. Awia, a nuu nɛnnɛ gunla maa min niŋ ŋɔ, di karfi baa tɛŋ.

ref: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
text: Di n wa ŋɔ biinikpola hiŋ daŋ siu, ka hɔɔ karfɛɛ ú gil u biinikpola la, ka lɛɛ u hiŋ, u daŋ siu dikuu u biinikpola la wia, ka u wichɔgaa daŋ laŋŋi i ni.

ref: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
text: Ama, di i karfuu waa, ka u vɛɛ, waa u wichɔgaa gillɛ ta, u daŋ siu dikuu u wichɔgaa hiŋ wia, ka i daŋ lɛɛ i hiŋ.

ref: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
text: Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee haŋ wa bir lii u wideŋlaa hiŋ biini di ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u daŋ siu dikuu a wia.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, i hɛri hina ɔɔ ra ŋɔ i wiarɛ, di ba wa chem dɔŋa a bolzeŋ koŋlaa kɛraa gɛɛ ba diini dominuuzi. Ba ɔɔ ra ŋɔ dɔŋa benii, ‘Ií ba ya la ga nuu wia la n lii Kɔraawiizi be filaŋkeŋ.’

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
text: Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ kenne ba ra ŋɔ, ‘Yaa biinikpola ni wikuna werge siili yaa ninɛɛ. Awiarɛ, yaa maa ra kɔgi! Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ na miibɔɔ naanɛi?’

ref: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
text: Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, ‘N bɔra waa ɔɔ sɔɔni biinikpola hina siu wia, ka anna nyiŋŋuu ba gil ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, ka na miibɔɔ. Izrɛl hina! Ií gil ii wichɔgaa ta! Ií gilaa ta! Di gil ii biinikpola wiɛɛlaa la. Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ií siuzɛi?’

ref: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
text: Newee biibaal, ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ i hɛri hina lugɔ di nɛr la wia n deŋlee ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa ka wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u wideŋlaa la wàá wer lɛɛu, gunnɛ biinikpola hiŋ ge biinikpola wiɛɛlaa wàá gil ú chol, di u wa bittɔ lii a biini. Di nɛr la wia n deŋlee wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u daŋ siu. U wideŋlaa la uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la wàá wer lɛɛu.

ref: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
text: Di n haŋ wa kali nɛr la wia n deŋlee lugɔ u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ, wibii maa, ka u dɛlli u wideŋlaa la ni di ɛɛ wichɔgaa, màá ka liizi u wideŋlaa la bɛl maa uŋ faa ɛɛwɛ la wia. U daŋ siu dikuu wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia.

ref: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
text: Di n haŋ kali biinikpola hiŋ lugɔ u daŋ siu wibii maa, ka u bir lii u wichɔgaa biini, di ra ɛɛ wia la n dɛkkɛ ni wideŋlaa,

ref: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
text: alugɔ di u wa bir talma la uŋ lɛɛwɛ ka kpa kebee kim nɛr la, di bir kpa nɛr la kuna uŋ faa ŋmɛɛwɛ ga tɛu, di ra hiŋ widaulaa la n na tɛɛ miibɔɔ la, di gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi, u daŋ dɔɔ miibɔɔ wibii maa, wàá siu.

ref: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
text: Ka i nɛra ra ŋɔu, ‘Kɔraawiizi wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ.’ Ka ba wiarɛ waa wibii dɔɔwɛ.

ref: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
text: Ama, di biinikpola hiŋ ge wa gil ú wichɔgaa ɛɛi, ka bir ra ɛɛ winanaa, u daŋ na miibɔɔ dikuu guŋ wia.

ref: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
text: Ka Izrɛl hina, ii ra ŋɔu lugɔ n wiɛɛlaa waa deŋlee. N daŋ kpa bɛl maa wiɛɛlaa diu seriya.” Jɛrusalɛm cholaa wia

ref: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
text: A duana ni mɔɔ ka a baal ba la, Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa faa iziŋ werge, di pilli n nua ń wer ŋɔ wia di u wa ballɔ chɔɔzi ni. Awia, n nua faa pilli, waa kaa mar.

ref: Then the Lord said:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ n be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
text: “Newee biibaal, nɛra la n du Izrɛl hɛri bolzenaa la n purgee la ra ŋɔu, ‘Abraham faa ɛɛ nɛkpannɛ, ka faa wer dɔɔ a hɛri naa maa! Ka yaa kpillɔɔ, awia, a hɛri jaa ɛɛ yaa hotte, wibii maa.’

ref: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
text: Awia, ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu lugɔ ii ra hee ola ni a challii, di ra kuari vuga, haali di ɔɔ ra kpuuzi nɛra. Awia, ii ɛɛ tamii lugɔ a hɛri daŋ wer ɛɛ ii hor, wibii maa?

ref: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
text: Ii dɛlli ii tokobizii, di ra ɛɛ wia la miŋ kiiwe, bɛl ra chɔgi u dɔŋhiŋ haaŋ. A dɛkkɔ a hɛri n ɛɛ ii horaa?’

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
text: Ŋɔ ba be, ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ ba daŋ kpa tokobi kpu banla n kawɛɛ bolzenaa la n purgee la biine. N daŋ kpa banla ge n du kooni la tɛɛ pir sela á di. Banla n suahzi bizenaa nyuuni ni bia bɔɔni la, wiilchɔgaarɛ niŋ kpuuzi ba ge.

ref: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
text: N daŋ chɔgi a hɛri ú birgi diŋgela, di chɔɔ pɛɛ, ba fɔŋŋa la baŋ faa ra jigsi u wia la tuŋ. Izrɛl bizenaa la maa daŋ chɔgi, nɛr maa wàá ka wer tinni a nyuuni.

ref: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
text: Di n wa gillɔ ba hɛri birgi diŋgela dikuu ba wiɛɛlaa la miŋ kiiwe, ka ba ra ɛɛa la wia, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
text: Awia, n nɛra ɔɔ bau wa so i be di ra nuu wia la hinna ŋɔ, ka ba wàá ra hiŋ. Ba nuuzi summɔɔ werge maa, ka ba bampiree nɔŋŋi wichɔgaa ni kebee wia.

ref: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
text: I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr la n na deŋŋi ba siweere alugɔ nɛbɛl loobii n ɔɔ du sum, u ra lɔ gilgo di ra yir nɔŋŋaa yira, di ra deŋŋi nɛra siwee la. Ba ɔɔ nuu gunla maa hiŋ ŋɔwɛɛnɛ, ka ba wàá ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
text: Ama, di annii maa wa huuzi baa, wibii maa, denii bá zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa du ba biinii.”

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
text: “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ wii la n niŋ wa huuzi Izrɛl penɔɔna du ba ni. Ŋɔ ba be lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘Tɔɔrɔɔ werge daŋ huuzi Izrɛl penɔɔna la n na binni bahinaa ka gil ba peeza la. Penɔɔna lɛi dɛkkɛ banna binni peeza nii?

ref: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
text: Iabuu ra nyɔɔ a ilaniiri, di ra laali laala la baŋ kpa a huna kuari, haali di ɔɔ kpuuzi anla n pɔllɛ nɛnnɛ ra hee, ka ii waa a peeza ni ra binni.

ref: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
text: Ii waa kaa ra du anla n gɛrgɛɛ tau gɛɛ di ra chaa anla n na wii. Ii waa ɔɔ sɛɛ ii vɔɔzi anla naazi n kuugee gba gɛɛ di ɔɔ ɛɛ ania lugɔ ii gaagi nyiŋŋi anla n leuzee gba. Ka ɔɔ ra firaa di ra tɔɔraa werge maa.

ref: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
text: Dikuu n peeza n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ wia, a maa yaarɔɔrɛ, pir sela lauraa ra di.

ref: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
text: A yaari bizenaa ni giŋgimee la n la chiŋ maa nyuunii, durnya naa yemmaa. Ka nɛr maa waa wette ú la ga du a tau, di nyiŋŋaa.

ref: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
text: mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, dikuu n peeza n nyaa nɔɔni, pir sela maa lauraa di ra di, n penɔɔna ge wàá nyiŋŋee, ka ra binni bahinaa, ka gilaa ta wia,

ref: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu lugɔ n ɛɛ ii dɔmnɛ. Awia, ii daŋ turgi n peeza la kim. Màá ka gil ii nɔɔnaa, ii wàá ka wer dɛɛzi iihinaa. N daŋ lɛɛa lii ii be, màá ka gil ii heea.’

ref: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
text: Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘N himmaa daŋ nyiŋŋi n peeza di ra binnaa.

ref: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
text: Gunla penɔɔni n ɔɔ ra binni u peeza la n yaarɛɛ la, gunnɛ ń na binni n peeza. N daŋ lɛɛa lii bɔra la maa aŋ faa yaarɛɛ hɔpizichɔgii la n biree la biini.

ref: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
text: N daŋ lizi a maa lii hɛrdumazi biine, di chaalaa kpoglaa ba a himmaa hɛri. N daŋ tɔ a see di bir ba a ni Izrɛl hɛri bizenaa nyuuni ni gɔŋa biine, di wa dɛɛzaa kooriinanaa biine.

ref: They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills.
text: N danna nɔɔnaa kooriinanaa biine, Izrɛl bizenaa nyuuni. Denii a chɔɔ bɔnanaa di ra di kooriinanaa, Izrɛl bizenaa nyuuni.

ref: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
text: N himmaa danna nɔɔnaa, di tɛɛa bɔr á chɔɔ ra heezi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
text: N daŋ nyiŋŋi anla maa n faa leuzee ni anla maa n yaarɛɛ la, á bir ba. N daŋ vɔɔzi anla maa n na pira ŋmɛra, di chaa anla n na wii la. Ama, n daŋ kpu anla waa maa n pɔllɛ di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la, dikuubɛɛwiai, n ɛɛ penɔɔni la n ɔɔ ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋleere.’ ”

ref: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N peeza, n daŋ di ii bɛl maa seriya, di bargi a nanaa lii a chɔgaa ni, di bargi peeza lii buuna ni.

ref: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
text: A waa ia kukkɛɛ iinna kooriinanaa ra di, ka ra fɛrgi anla n kawɛɛ? A waa ia kukkɛɛ iinna niinanii di ra nyɔɔ, ka ra vuugi anla n kawɛɛ, á puraa?

ref: That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ń peeza ra di anla iiŋ fɛrgɛɛ laa, di ra nyɔɔ nii la iiŋ puttɛ laa?

ref: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
text: Ii taagi anla n na wii labuu lii kɛrii, di yagzaa lii a peeza biini.

ref: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
text: Awia, n daŋ lɛɛa lii a tɔɔrɔɔ hiŋ biini, nɛr maa wàá ka wer tɔɔraa gɛɛ di chɔgaa gba, di di a peeza bɛl maa seriya, di bargi a nanaa lii a chɔgaa ni.

ref: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la jaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum, n balii Koori Deevid ge ɛɛ ba koori, di ra binni ba ni. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
text: N ni baa daŋ ɛɛ bɔsɔna nuukpaŋ, ka ń duŋŋi pir sela la maa lii a hɛri biini. Gunnɛ n nɛra jaa wer dɔɔ bɔsɔna, haali di ba sogo hɛribɔduma biini gɛɛ di chɔɔ kɔrni gba biine, ka ɔnsii wàá ka lau baa.

ref: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
text: N daŋ kissi n nɛra ni bola la maa n bar n giŋgimiinaniinanii la. N daŋ tɛɛ baa dooŋ, saŋa la maa baŋ ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋuu, á ɛɛ kissaa werge maa.

ref: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
text: Hɛri la daazi maa danna nɔŋ nɛnnɛ, kooliŋkuna ge lɛɛ nɛnnɛ. Á nɛra so pɛrɛtɛ, a hɛri biini. Di n wa lɛɛ baa lii ba dɔma nonee, ba wàá ka ɛɛ yoma la, ba daŋ zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
text: N daŋ tɛɛ baa hɛri la ge n summɛ werge, bá wer ra na diwee, lɔzi ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka kpu baa gɛɛ hɛrdumazi hina kaa ɛɛ baa chɛɛtɛ.

ref: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Gunnɛ ba zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum la du ba benii. Denii Izrɛl hina maa zum lugɔ ba ɛɛ n nɛraa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ra ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
text: Ii ɛɛ n peeza la minna dɛɛzuu, di ɛɛ n nɛra, n ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iinna hum. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ra ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
text: “Newee biibaal, hau Ɛdɔm hɛri ni, di ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa huuzuu du u ni,

ref: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
text: di ŋɔ lugɔ kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ɛdɔm hɛri, n ɛɛ i dɔmnɛ. N daŋ chɔgii, í birgi diŋgela.

ref: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ purgi i bolzenaa la maa, í birgi diŋgela. Denii í zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
text: I faa ɛɛ Izrɛl hina dɔmnɛ saŋa maa, di gil ba kpu baa, bá hɛhchɔg saŋa la n faa ɛɛ ba tuna dignitɛraa dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia la.

ref: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ kpai tɛɛ bá kpu, hàá wer chɔ lii u biini. Dikuu hiŋ waa nɛkpui ra ɔm wia, ba daŋ dau i luge kpui.

ref: I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it.
text: N daŋ gil Ɛdɔm hɛri hɛssi la maa birgi diŋgelli, di kpu banla maa n na ga de la.

ref: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ gil i birgi diŋgela di hanna la, nɛra wàá ka so i bola biine. Denii i zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
text: Ɛdɔm hina, ii faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Izrɛl, Juda ani ba hɛssi maa daŋ birgi ii hora. Haali mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi n faa du ba be gba.

ref: and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you!
text: Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ tɔɔri ia gunla iiŋ faa kpa baaŋ, zoma ani hahzi huuzi baa la wia. N daŋ gil ba zumiŋ, di n waa di ia seriya.

ref: And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take.
text: Denii ií zum lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la nuu hahzi wia la maa iiŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ du Izrɛl hɛri bizenaare. Ii faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Izrɛl hɛri birgi diŋgelaa, ba kpaubuu tɛɛ yaa alugɔ diwee yá di.

ref: You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
text: Ii faa jigsɔɔrɛ ŋɔ wia werge maa du n ni, n nuu guŋ.’ ”

ref: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
text: Dikuu ii bɔra n sɔɔnɛɛ werge dikuu Izrɛl hina kapɛttɛ n faa birgi diŋgela la wia, gunnɛ ń ɛɛ ii gba. Awia, Ɛdɔm hina, ii hɛri daŋ birgi diŋgela, ii bizenaa ani ii hɛri maa. Denii hɛssi hina maa zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ Izrɛl hɛri bizenaa be lugɔ a ra nuu gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n na ŋɔ,

ref: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
text: ‘Ii dɔma ɛɛ iabuu chɛɛtɛ di ra ŋɔ lugɔ tibaarikala, a faala bizenaa jaa birgi yaa horaa!’

ref: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
text: Awia, Izrɛl bizenaa, ií ra nuu gunla mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n na ŋɔ. N ŋɔwɔɔrɛ ra tɛɛ bizenaa, giŋgimee, faalime, walli, diŋgelli ani bolzenaa la baŋ chɔwɛɛ ka kaa, hɛssi hina la n bar ia la paagi a kuna, ka ra ɛɛ ia chɛɛtɛ la wia,

ref: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
text: Ka Izrɛl hɛri bizenaa lawaa daazi daŋ kaa fur, di nɔŋ tɛɛ n nɛra Izrɛl hina, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wàá ka birgi ka ba bol.

ref: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
text: Ii wia tirimbuu, n daŋ suŋ ii ni, bá par ii nyuuni duu kuna,

ref: The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them.
text: di gil Izrɛl hɛri hina wazi werge, ba bola la maa n faa purgee la bir ma di su nɛra.

ref: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: N daŋ gil nɛra ni sela wazi werge maa, di so ii nyuuni ra lul, di du kpil. N daŋ kaa gil nɛra so ii nyuuni gunla baŋ faa soge de la, di gil ii nyɛɛli kaali gunla iiŋ faa duwɛɛ la. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.

ref: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
text: N daŋ gil n nɛra Izrɛl hina kaa bir waa vol ii ni. Ba daŋ dɔɔ ia, ií ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna, ii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka gil bá nyaa ba biizi.

ref: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔu, dikuu nɛra n na ŋɔ lugɔ hìŋ́ Izrɛl hɛri ra di nɛraa, di gil i nyaa biizi wia,

ref: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
text: N ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka gil i nuu hɛrdumazi hina chɛɛtɛ, gɛɛ di kaa di nɛra gbɛllaa tɔɔrɔɔ, gɛɛ di chɔgi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’ ”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
text: “Newee biibaal, saŋa la Izrɛl hina n faa soge ba himmaa hɛri la, ba doŋuubuu dikuu ba manni ni ba wiɛɛlaa wia. Ba manni faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ haaŋ n faa ra ɛɛ doŋa n sibɔɔ.

ref: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
text: Ba faa chɔgi a hɛrii ni nɛkpui ani vuga kuaraa, dikuu guŋ wia, n baaŋ faa fuuh ba ni werge maa.

ref: and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved.
text: N faa gillɔɔ ba yaari hɛssi maa biine. N faa di baabuu seriya, dikuu ba manni ni ba wiɛɛlaa wia.

ref: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
text: Bɔr la maa baŋ ɔɔ la, ba ɔɔ chɔgi n sɔnnaniinaniirɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra ɔɔ faa ŋɔ ba wiarɛ, ‘Kɔraawiizi nɛraa keŋ, ka u duŋŋi baa lii u hɛri.’

ref: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
text: Awia, ŋɔ Izrɛl hina be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘Izrɛl hina, ii wia lɛi n na nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ wia naa, ka n sɔnnaniinanii la iiŋ chɔkkɛ hɛssi hina la be, iiŋ laŋŋɛ la wiarɛ.

ref: I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home.
text: N daŋ lizi ia lii a hɛssi hina biine, di chaali ia lii a hɛssi maa biine, di ba ii himmaa hɛri.

ref: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
text: N daŋ kpa niinanii mizi ia, ii doŋa lii. N daŋ lizi ii doŋa maa lii ii vuga be.

ref: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
text: Denii ń jaa tɛɛ ia bampirfalaa ni nfɛrfalaa, di lizi ii dignikpega la, ka tɛɛ ia bampiree la n niŋ nɔŋŋiŋ.

ref: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
text: N daŋ kpa n Duma du ii ni, ú gil ii wer ra hiŋ n widaulaa, di ra du tau ni n Gbɔgni hiŋaa, gunla miŋ bagli ia la.

ref: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
text: Denii ii wa so hɛri la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ ii naabaala la. Ii daŋ birgi n nɛra, n ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la iin ninna hum.

ref: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
text: N daŋ lɛɛ ia lii wia la maa n gillɛ ii ra doŋ biini. N daŋ gil ii mia lɛɛ werge, lɔchɔgii ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá ka chol ii ni.

ref: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
text: N daŋ gil ii daazi nɔŋ nɛnnɛ, ii kooni kuna ge lɛɛ nɛnnɛ, guŋ gil ii wàá ka di hiihzi hɛssi hina be, dikuu lɔchɔgii wia.

ref: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: A waa lugɔ ii wiarɛ n na nyiŋŋi ń ɛɛ wia naa. Ee, Izrɛl hina, ií gil hiihzi lau ia werge maa dikuu ii manni wia! Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.’

ref: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
text: Kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘A hɔl la min niŋ lizi ia lii ii wichɔgaa biini la, n daŋ bir soŋŋi ia ii bola la biine, ii bir maa.

ref: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
text: Ii daŋ bir par diŋgelli la maa n faa chɔɔ pɛɛ la, banla maa n faa ra ga de la sibɔɔ.’

ref: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
text: Nɛra daŋ ŋɔ, ‘Hɛri naa n faa chɔɔ pɛɛ la, waabuu jaa bir du lugɔ Ɛdɛn kambolnanii la! A bolzenaa la n faa purgee birgi diŋgelli la maanii ba jaa bir ma, a du kpeg di su nɛra la!

ref: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Denii hɛssi hina la n kawɛɛ bar ia la, jaa zum lugɔ minuu bittɛ ma bola la n faa purgee la, di bir duu kuna hɛssi la n faa ɛɛ diŋgelli, di chɔɔ pɛɛ la. Minuu ŋɔ guŋ, n daŋ ɛɛ guŋ wibii maa.’

ref: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, ‘N daŋ kaa nuu Izrɛl hina wiisuŋŋaa, di ɛɛ keŋ tɛɛ baa. N daŋ gil ba nɛra wazi di du kpil werge alugɔ peeza.

ref: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Gunla mbusu lizaa peeza n ɔɔ faa mag Jɛrusalɛm diuzenaa dii saŋa la, gunnɛ bolzenaa la n purgee la su nɛra. Denii bá zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
text: Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa faa izi mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl. U Duma kpaŋ ga chiŋŋi waluu bɛl hoga n suwee baambaaŋ.

ref: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
text: U faa kpogliŋ bar a hoga biini, n naa kpilakpila, a faa hil werge maa.

ref: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
text: Denii u jaa pɛɛziŋ, “Newee biibaal, a hoga naa daŋ kaa wer dɔɔ miibɔɔa?” N ŋɔ, “Ee, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa, i bɛnnɛ zummɛ.”

ref: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
text: Denii u ŋɔ n be, “Ŋɔ wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ hoga naa, di ŋɔ a be lugɔ a ra nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii!

ref: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
text: Ŋɔ a be lugɔ kenne mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, dí n daŋ heezi du ii ni, ií kaa dɔɔ miibɔɔ.

ref: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
text: N daŋ tɛɛ ia diah ni olsiah, di kpa hɔna tɔɔgi ia, di heezi du ii ni, ií kaa dɔɔ miibɔɔ. Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu Kɔraawiizi.”

ref: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
text: Awia, n faa ŋɔ wia du a ni gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ n be la. Saŋa la minna ŋɔ a wia la, n nuu kɔɔi bɛl guŋ kparkparkpar, nɛr maa hoga ba waa choŋŋi dɔŋa ni.

ref: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
text: Minna binni la, di diah, ola ani hɔna ge ballɔ, wa tɔɔgi a maa ni, ka a faa haa waa heezi.

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, ŋɔ n wiŋɔɔlaa tɛɛ peu. Kali peu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ ú lii bɔr maa ba, wa zuu nɛra naa baŋ kpuwɛɛ naa ni, di gil ba bir dɔɔ miibɔɔ.”

ref: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
text: u wassi ɛɛ nogumzi ŋmantannaazi, u kɛraa daazi gbossi ɛɛ nogumzi anɛɛgaa. A dominuuzeŋ jaŋgal hiŋ chaŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia la.

ref: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
text: A wiifurii dominuuzeŋ la biini dɔɔ tauduura chignibɔra ahoro, u kɛraa. Ahoro hiŋ maa mɛgzi dɔŋa, a koŋliisaagaa kɛraa sezi ge gbossi mɛgzi dɔŋa.

ref: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
text: Denii a baal mɛgzi a dominuuzeŋ, u wassi ɛɛ nogumzi fi, u jaŋzi ge ɛɛ nogumzi fidaahoro.

ref: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
text: Denii u faa kaa mɛgzi a tauduura chignibɔra la bɛl harbɔɔ koŋlii chiŋ ga chug bɛl, de ɛɛ nogumzi tokko ni anue, di lii a sal koŋlii vollibɔr ga chug bɛl.

ref: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
text: Di lii a dominuuzeŋ ga hel a jaŋgal tuna faa ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi.

ref: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
text: Ba faa furgi tokorjigzii a diini baŋgizi koŋlaa ni a biine koŋlaa la n du a baambaana la ni. Ba faa zɛuzi abɛ daazii dau a koŋliisaagaa ni. Baŋgia diŋŋee wia

ref: The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw
text: Denii a baal faa jaa kpogliŋ zuu a baŋgia diŋŋee. N faa na baŋ ma diini aŋhina, di kuari vollibɔr bar a diŋŋee. Diini tokko ni kpɔrgɔɔ faa hiini a vollibɔr.

ref: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
text: A dominuuzenaa jaŋgalli la n faa bar a biini diŋŋee la jaŋzi faa du nogumzi tokko ni anuezi, a wassi ge faa du nogumzi anuezi.

ref: This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was
text: A vollibɔr faa bar a baŋgia diŋŋeere. Baŋgia diŋŋee naa faa tuu zɛɛrɛ kaali biini diŋŋee la.

ref: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
