ref: Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard.
text: Denii u mɛgzi dominuuzeŋ la n chaŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la baŋ gawɛɛ ra zuu a baŋgia diŋŋee la jaŋzi ni u wassi.

ref: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also

ref: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.

ref: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was

text: A baal faa kaa kpogliŋ la a wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii, n kaa na dominuuzeŋ bɛl n chaŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag. U mɛgzi u kɛraa daazi ni u jaŋgal, a ni anla maa mɛgzaazi ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
text: Ba faa ma tinnibɔra aniidaanɛɛ lugɔ lɔŋa, a tinni ga chug a dominuuzeŋ, u jaŋgal faa chaŋaa. Ba faa kaa zɛuzi abɛ daazi dau u koŋliisaagaa keŋkere bɛl maa ni.

ref: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
text: Denii u faa kaa kpogliŋ ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag dominuuzeŋ la zuu biini diŋŋee la, di mɛgzi a dominuuzeŋ, u ni anla maa mɛgzaazi ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
text: U jaŋgal faa chaŋ baŋgia diŋŋee la, ba faa zɛuzi abɛ daazi dau u dominuuzeŋ kɛraa daazi ni, di ma tinnibɔra ŋmantannaazi lugɔ lɔŋa, a tinni ga chug a dominuuzeŋ. Biini diŋŋee wiifurii dominuuzeŋ

ref: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
text: U jaŋgal chaŋ baŋgia diŋŋee la, ba faa zɛuzi abɛ daazi dau u dominuuzeŋ kɛraa daazi ni, di ma tinnibɔra ŋmantannaazi lugɔ lɔŋa, a tinni ga chug a dominuuzeŋ.

text: alugɔ u tauduura chignibɔra, u koŋliisaagaa ani u jaŋgal la dɔɔ tokorozi bar. U jaŋzi faa du nogumzi tokkoanɛɛ ni fi, u wassi ge du nogumzi tokko ni anue.

ref: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
text: A jaŋgal chaŋ baŋgia diŋŋee la, ba faa zɛuzi abɛ daazi dau u dominuuzeŋ kɛraa daazi ni, di ma tinni bɔra ŋmantannaazi lugɔ lɔŋa, a tinni ga chug a dominuuzeŋ. Diini la biine banna ɛɛ mbusu lizaa kuna siryazi wia

ref: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right.
text: A dominua jaŋgal biini faa dɔɔ tɛɛbulzi anaazuu, anɛɛ chi keŋkere naa, anɛɛ ge chi keŋkere naa. A ninɛɛ ba faa ra kpu mbusu lizaa sefuuhlaa, wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa ani bilchɔg mbusu lizaa sela.

ref: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
text: A dominua jaŋgal koŋlii harbɔɔ kɛrii n dugli lɔŋa la n du wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominuuzeŋ la, tɛɛbulzi anɛɛrɛ faa chigɛ de ge. A lɔŋa keŋkere la hiŋ ge, tɛɛbulzi anɛɛrɛ faa chigɛ de.

ref: and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar. Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables
text: Ba faa kpa gɔrgakpara, bɛl maa jaŋzi ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga, baŋzi de koŋlaa ni bar. A tɛɛbulzi ninɛɛ ba faa kpa mbusu lizaa ola di ra sag. Kɔraawiizi kizeehina diini wia

ref: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.

ref: The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
text: A jaŋgal wassi faa du nogumzi tokkoo, di chi u see di ra la u har ge du nogumzi fidaanɛɛ. Lɔŋa fii i ɔɔ tinni, ka zuu u biini. Silminti ligee faa du u dominuuzeŋ kɛraa daazi keŋkerezi bɛl maa.

ref: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was

ref: and the nearest buildings ten meters away.
text: ani Kɔraawiizi kizeehina diini la wassi faa ɛɛ nogumzi tokkoo bar Kɔraawiizi Dia hiŋ.

ref: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.

ref: The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms.
text: N faa na baŋ ma koŋlii chiŋŋi bar Kɔraawiizi Dia lugɔ dia zɛɛ, u ɛɛ diibizi zɛɛzi. U chiŋ laŋaa faa ɛɛ nogumzi anumbɛl.

ref: The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls
text: A diibizi baŋgia koŋlii gbossi faa ɛɛ nogumzi anuere. Bɔwoo la n faa du a diibizi ni Kɔraawiizi Dia baambaaŋ

ref: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
text: Dominuuzi lii a bɔwoo wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ni wiifurii nodig wiikakag, ba ga ra zuu a diibizi. A diibizi zɛɛ n ga choŋŋi a bɔwoo wassi faa ɛɛ nogumzi anuere bar.

ref: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
text: Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee wiifurii la ni u see maa wassi ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa.

ref: Finally, the man measured the length of the west building, including the side rooms on each end, and it was also
text: A tuna, a baal mɛgzi a wiicholii dia la jaŋzi, di kpa diibizi la n du u tunazi la jaa, a ge ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa. Jaŋgal la n chaŋ diŋŋee la, Bɔnaniinanii, Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa

ref: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.

ref: The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated
text: Di chi Kɔraawiizi Dia biini koŋlaa zɛɛzi ga chug chiŋ maanii, ba faa zɛuzi

text: A bɛl maa dɔɔ gberkpara.

text: A diini see faa dɔɔ biini vollibɔttɛ, u wassi ɛɛ nogumzi fi, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kalfa. A dominuuzi faa chaŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag.

ref: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.

ref: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.

ref: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
text: Denii a baal ŋɔ mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl be, “Wiifurii nomɛɛl ni wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkerezi ni diini naa n chaŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia diŋŋee naa, ɛɛ a Kɔraawiizi kizeehina diinii. Aabuu mbusuzi lizaa mia, wichɔgaa mbusuzi ani bilchɔg mbusuzi lizaa kuna, dikuubɛɛwiai, de ɛɛ bɔnaniinaniirɛ.

ref: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
text: Di Kɔraawiizi kizeehina haŋ wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia hum ba huma tuŋ, bá wir ba huma bɔmbɔga dau de mɔɔ, ka haa lii zuu baŋgia diŋŋee la biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ bɔmbɔgnanaananaarɛ. A dɛkkɔɔ bá laali bɔmbɔgdumazi mɔɔ, ka haa wer la bɔra la nɛra n chaalɛɛ la.”

ref: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.

text: U mɛgzi a wiifurii keŋkere, u jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kalfaanue.

text: U kaa bir mɛgzi wiicholii keŋkere la, de ge kaa ɛɛ guŋ.

text: U mɛgzi a bɔr keŋkerezi anaazu la maa. U faa dɔɔ koŋliire bar u maa. U jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kalfaanue, u wassi ge guŋ. A koŋlii teŋ kunnanaananaa lii anla n waa ananaananaa ɛɛwɛ la ni.

ref: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
text: Denii a baal kpogli mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ba dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii la,

ref: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
text: n na Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la girme n nyɛgzɛɛ lii wiifurii di ra ba. U loobii ra gbɔgzi alugɔ niizeŋ n na pal guŋ gbuŋgbuŋgbuŋ, a hɛri la maa ra nyɛgzi, dikuu a girme wia.

ref: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
text: Wii naa Kɔraawiizi n pillɛɛ bagliŋ n nau lugɔ deeza biini naa, faa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ unla miŋ felee na, saŋa la uŋ faa ra ba ú wa chɔgi bolzeŋ la ni anla miŋ faa nawɛɛ Muu Kɛbar nua la. Denii n faa chol pi hɛri.

ref: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi girme la faa ga dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii la, di zuu u Dia.

ref: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Duma la lalliŋ chiŋ ga tuu a biini diŋŋee la biini, ka u girme la jaa su u Dia maa.

ref: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, gil ba gil ba vuga ni ba koorisiwaa kuaraa la wia ha, ka ń jaa du ba biini di ra la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
text: Newee biibaal, bagli gunla maa n Dia la n duwɛɛ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina la. Hiihzi kpu baa dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia. Gil ba pessi gunla uŋ duwɛɛ.

ref: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
text: Di hiihzi wa lau baa dikuu gunla baŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia, gil ba zum a Dia duula, gunla baŋ mau, u dominuuzi la baŋ gawɛɛ ra zuu ani anla baŋ gawɛɛ ra lii, u duula maa, u widaulaa ani u gbɔgni maa. Sɛbaa dau ba see, bá na gunla maa un duwɛɛ, di hiŋ u widaulaa.

ref: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
text: N Dia hiŋ gbɔgrɛ keŋ. Bɔra la maa n bar a bizeŋ nyuu ɛɛ naniinanii himmaanii. A Dia gbɔgrɛ guŋ. Mbusu lizibɔr la wia

ref: According to the official standards, the altar in the temple had the following measurements: Around the bottom of the altar was a gutter
text: Nogumzii ba faa kpa mɛgzi mbusu lizibɔr gunla baŋ mɛgzi Kɔraawiizi Dia la. U gɔɔta luŋzi faa ɛɛ nogume, u wassi ge guŋ, u gir ge wassi ɛɛ nopaal wassi maga, di bar u kɛraa. U chiŋ laŋaa genii keŋ,

ref: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
text: Guŋ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, i daŋ ɔɔ lau bubal, nabalee ani pebal lii i kundɛɛzaa biini hɔpizi biimaa, di lizi wichɔgaa mbusu. A dɛkkɔ sel naa bɛl maa n kpekke nɛnnɛ.

ref: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, ŋmɛnizi la hin niŋ hiŋ di lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni gunla hin niŋ mizi chal mbusu lizibɔr la ni, di ba wa maubuu keŋ,

ref: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
text: a dɛkkɔ i lizi nabalee, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa hor tɛɛ Levi dee la n ɛɛ n kizeehina lii Zadɔk naanna biini la n ɔɔ ba waa hum n see la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
text: I daŋ kpa u chal yeŋ fɔg mbusu lizibɔr nyigzi anaazu la ni, u chiŋ kuna sagribɔr siraa anaazu la ani gir la n baruu la. Gunnɛ í ɛɛ di lizi n baaŋ u ni.

ref: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
text: I daŋ kpa a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa nabalee lii n Dia baŋgia yembɛl baŋ kuarɛɛ, di ɔɔ ra fuuah de la, fuuuh.

ref: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
text: Di hɔɔ wa pizɔɔ, i daŋ kpa bubal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di lizi mbusu lizibɔr doŋa gunla baŋ faa kpa nabalee ɛɛu la.

ref: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
text: Di i wa lizi de doŋa tuŋ, i daŋ lau nabalee ni pebal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ lii i kundɛɛzaa biini, di lizi mbusu.

ref: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
text: I daŋ kpaa ba n see, n kizeehina la ɛɛ yazi mizaa, ka fuuah lizi mbusu.

ref: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
text: N kizeehina daŋ kpa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ, di lizi n baaŋ u ni, di kpau du n nonee.

ref: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ tuna, di lii a hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazihiŋ hɔl di ra la, n kizeehina daŋ ɔɔ kpa n nɛra mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusu lizaa kuna, di ra fuuh mbusu lizibɔr ni. Denii ń jaa sɛɛ lɛɛ ia. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
text: Denii a baal bir kpogli mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl la Kɔraawiizi Dia baŋgia dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii la, di u tɔwɔɔ.

ref: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Dominua naa waa daŋ haŋ tɔu di hanna la. Bá gilɛɛ waa pilluu maa. Nɛr maa wàá ka ga de zuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina n na hum la ga denii zuu.

ref: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
text: A sitɔɔri bɛnnɛ niŋ wa so a dominua di diunanaananaa la n see. Jaŋgal dominua labuu u ɔɔ ga zuu, di kaa ga de lii.”

ref: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
text: Denii a baal kpogliŋ ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominua la, di ba Kɔraawiizi Dia la see. N binni di na Kɔraawiizii girme n nyɛgzɛɛ di ra su a Dia maa. N chol pi.

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, a binni nɛnnɛ, di ra nuu gunla maa min niŋ ŋɔ i be nɛnnɛ, n Dia widaulaa wia. A nuu n Dia dominua ni u Bɔnaniinanii bɔra la maa baŋ gawɛɛ ra lii la wia nɛnnɛ.

ref: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
text: Ŋɔ Izrɛl hina naa n ɛɛ dignikpega hina naa be lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la wàá ka sɛɛ wikiilaa la iinna ɛɛ la wia, a jaa kukkuu!

ref: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
text: Ii gillɔɔ hɔɔhra la n waa ba hɛna teŋree, di ɛɛ nɛra la n waa n nua ra hiŋ la, zuu n Dia chɔguu, saŋa la iiŋ kpa diwee, nuuri ani challi lizi mbusu la. Awia, ii kpa wikunaa chɔgi n ni ia nuukpaŋ la.

ref: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
text: Iin niŋ faa kpa n kunnanaananaa di ra hum gunla n dɛkkɛ n Dia biini la, ka ii gillɔɔ hɔɔhra waa binni n Dia la huma ni.”

ref: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
text: Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Hɔɔhri maa hɛŋ n waa teŋŋe, waa n nua ra hiŋ, wàá ka zuu n Dia, haali banla gba n du Izrɛl hina biini la.

ref: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
text: Awia, Levi dee la ni Izrɛl hina n faa vɛɛŋ ka gaa kuari vuga la, daŋ di ba wichɔgaa tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
text: Ama, ba daŋ ɔɔ haa ra hum n Dia la biini, di ra binni u dominuuzi ni, di ra hum u biini. Ba daŋ haa ra kpu nɛra mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa ni mbusuzi lizaa sela di ra tɛɛ baa, di chi ba see di ra hum baa.

ref: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
text: Ka baŋ faa ra hum baa ba vuga sezi, di gil Izrɛl hina ɛɛ wichɔgaa la wia, n lalli banoniire hɛɛhzi lugɔ ba daŋ di ba wichɔgaa tɔɔrɔɔ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
text: Ba gilɛɛ kaa wàá dugliŋ di ra humiŋ lugɔ n kizeehina gɛɛ di wàá dugli n kunnanaananaa la, gɛɛ n mbusunanaananaa himmaa lizaa kuna la. Ba daŋ di wikiilaa la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
text: Ka n daŋ gil ba ra binni n Dia hunjigzi maa ni.”

ref: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
text: “Ka Levi dee la n ɛɛ kizeehina lii Zadɔk naanna biini, di ra hum n Dia la biini huma nɛnnɛ ni wibii, saŋa la Izrɛl hina n faa vɛɛŋ, di lii n be la, daŋ dugliŋ di ra humiŋ. Ba daŋ chi n see di ra lizi nuuri ni challi mbusuzi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
text: Ba bɛnnɛ niŋ ɔɔ zuu n Dia la, ba bɛnnɛ niŋ ɔɔ dugli n mbusu lizibɔr la, di ra hum n see.

ref: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
text: Di ba ɔɔ waa zuu biini diŋŋee dominuuzi la, a dɛkkɔ ba ɔɔ laali pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa laala, a waa dɛkkɛ ban niŋ ɔɔ laali peezi huna laala, di ba waa hum n huma, a biini diŋŋee la dominuuzi gɛɛ n Dia biini.

ref: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
text: Ba daŋ ɔɔ kpa pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa namuzi vɔɔzi ba nyuuni, di nigni pɛɛŋhuŋŋunanaa galinzi. A waa dɛkkɛ ba ɔɔ laali laala la n niŋ gil weŋ fur baa.

ref: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
text: Di ba waa lii ba zuu baŋgia diŋŋee la nɛra la n duwɛɛ la, a dɛkkɔɔ ba wir bɔmbɔga la baŋ bɔkkɛ di hum n huma la dau diinanaananaa la biine, ka bir kpa laalidumazi laali, guŋ gilɛɛ wa gil ba bɔmbɔgnanaananaa la waa tɛɛ a nɛra tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ baŋ ɔɔ gil ba nyuhuna sug werge gɛɛ di gbaaraa. Ama a dɛkkɔɔ baŋ ɔɔ ŋmɛnnaa a mɛgzi.

ref: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
text: Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la bɛl maa ŋmɛnɛ gilɛɛ waa nyɔɔ siŋkpega mɔɔ, ka ra zuu a biini diŋŋee la.

ref: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ ba ra kpa luhaana gɛɛ haana la ba janna n vɛɛwɛ, ka ba daŋ wer kpa Izrɛl hina biihaana la n waa baala zummɛ gɛɛ ba dɔŋa kizeehina luhaana.

ref: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
text: Baabuu niŋ ɔɔ bagli n nɛra, bá wer zum kuna la n ɛɛ n hora ani anla n ɛɛ nɛra maa hora, di bagli baa gunla ban niŋ ɔɔ bargi kundoŋa lii anla n waa doŋŋe ni.

ref: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
text: Baabuu niŋ ɔɔ di naari maa wia seriya, gunla miŋ bagli baa la. Ba danna hiŋzi n hɔpizizenaa diuzenaa Gbɔgni ni n widaulaa, di gil n Heezaa Hɔpizaa la ɛɛ nanaananaa.

ref: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
text: N kizeehiŋ maa waa dɛkkɛ u dugli lalii di doŋ u hiŋ, see a lalii n ɛɛ u mɛɛ gɛɛ u maa gɛɛ u bie gɛɛ u niwee gɛɛ u kpɛɛma la n ɛɛ baal gɛɛ u niuhambie la n haa waa yuuwɛ.

ref: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
text: Haali di ba wa lizi u doŋa, ka u daŋ haa di hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ mɔɔ.

ref: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: A hɔl la un niŋ kaa zuu n Dia biini diŋŋee la ú ga hum, u daŋ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu tɛɛ u hiŋ, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
text: N bɛnnɛ ɛɛ n kizeehina kapɛttɛ kuŋ. Ií gilɛɛ waa tɛɛ baa kapɛttɛ kuŋ maa Izrɛl hɛri. Minuu ba kundɔɔlii.

ref: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
text: Ba daŋ ɔɔ di mbusuzi lizaa mia, wichɔgaa mbusuzi ani bilchɔg mbusuzi lizaa kuna, ni kuna la maa baŋ lizɛɛ tɛŋ Izrɛl hɛri.

ref: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
text: Diulugla la n wesse nɛnnɛ ni kumpazi la maa iiŋ ɔɔ sunziŋ la ɛɛ n kizeehina horaa. Di ii ɔɔ wa ɔɔzi paanuu saŋa maa, ii ɔɔ lizi lugli hora tɛɛ n kizeehina, guŋ daŋ gil n ɔɔ kissi ii diini hina.

ref: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
text: A waa dɛkkɛ n kizeehina hee zumbee gɛɛ sel la maa n siuwɛ u hiŋ ni gɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ n kpuu.”

ref: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
text: Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ dii hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ la n ɔɔ lugli baaguzi aniidaanɛɛ hɔpizaa fidaanuehiŋ hɔl la, u daŋ ɔɔ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, mbusuzi lizaa mia ani nuu.”

ref: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
text: Bɔnanii naa biini, ií mɛgzi yembɛl de jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, u wassi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi. Denii n Dia la n ɛɛ naniinanii la chi.

ref: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Izrɛl hina sitɔɔra, ii ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ birgi werge maa! Ií gil ii kalu ni ii nɛsunnaa la, ka ra ɛɛ wia la n wesse di deŋli. Ií ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ kaa wàá duŋŋi n nɛra ra lii ba hɛri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ra ŋɔ ii be guŋ.

ref: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
text: Tassazeŋ la iiŋ ɔɔ kpa ra mɛgzi kuŋhilaa la ni garwa la iiŋ ɔɔ kpa di ra mɛgzi nii kuna la dɛkkɔɔ aŋ mɛgzɛɛ.

ref: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
text: Ii daŋ ɔɔ kaa ɛɛ guŋ a baagu hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ hɔl tɛɛ nɛr la maa n waa zummɛ ka ɛɛ wichɔgaa gɛɛ uŋ waa kuttɛɛ. Gunnɛ ií ɔɔ ɛɛ lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia doŋa ha.

ref: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
text: Kuna naabuu ii ɔɔ kpa ra lizi mbusuzi. Di ii wa kum huuti gɛɛ baali, ií ɔɔ lizi a bɛl maa tassazeŋ ni keza lii tassazenaa kalfa maa biini, di wa tɛŋ.

ref: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
text: Ɔlivi nuu wia. Di ii wa tɔrgi ii ɔlivi nɔna lizi a nuu, ií bargaa bɔra kalfa, di kpa a bɔkpaŋ wa tɛŋ.

ref: The people of Israel will bring you these offerings.
text: Izrɛl hina maanii niŋ ɔɔ lizi a mbusuzi lizaa kuna naa hiini a hɛri sitɔɔri.

ref: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
text: A sitɔɔri humaa lugɔ ú ɔɔ lizi mbusuzi lizaa mia ni mbusuzi lizaa sin kuna, ii hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazi, ii baagufalaa, ii Heezaa Hɔpizaa ni Izrɛl hina hɔpizizenaa dii saŋazi maa. U daŋ ɔɔ lizi mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlaa, wichɔgaa mbusuzi lizaa, mbusuzi lizaa mia ani dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, di lizi n baaŋ Izrɛl hina ni.”

ref: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
text: A diuzenaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ la ge bɛl maa hɔl, u daŋ ɔɔ lizi nabala aniidaanɛɛ ni pebala ge aniidaanɛɛ la n kpekke nɛnnɛ lizi mbusu di fuuah tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. U daŋ ɔɔ kaa kpa bubal ge lizi wichɔgaa mbusu, a hɔpizii naa bɛl maa.

ref: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Lugli baagu hɔpizi kpaŋ hɔl, ií ɔɔ lau nabalee la n kpekke nɛnnɛ, di lizi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia doŋa ha.

ref: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ daŋ ɔɔ kpa a wichɔgaa mbusu lizaa sel naa chal yeŋ fɔg n Dia dominua daazi ni mbusu lizibɔr chiŋ kuna sagribɔr siraa anaazu la ani biini diŋŋee dominua daazi la.

ref: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
text: Biŋfalii lugli baagu hɔpizaa fidaanaazuhiŋ hɔl, ii daŋ ɔɔ faari Gillikaali diwee la dii. Ii daŋ ɔɔ di a hɔpizizenaa naa diwee, hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Paanuu la n waa yiisi dɔɔwɛɛ nɛr maa ɔɔ ra hee a saŋa naa.

ref: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, a sitɔɔri daŋ ɔɔ nyiŋŋi nabal lizi u ni Izrɛl hina maa wichɔgaa mbusu.

ref: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
text: A sitɔɔri daŋ ɔɔ kaa lizi mia tassazenaa fi jaa nabal ni pebal maa ni, di kaa lizi nuu pirintuani anaazuu jaa a tassazeŋ maa ni, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa mia.

ref: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ra ŋɔ, “Ba daŋ ɔɔ tɔ biini diŋŋee dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii la, hɔpizaa anumbɛl la biini banna hum huma la, ka Heezaa Hɔpizii ni Baagufalii Hɔpizii la waa biine, ba ɔɔ pilluu.

ref: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
text: A sitɔɔri daŋ ɔɔ ga a jaŋgal dominua la zuu ga chi pɛli a daazi. N kizeehina daŋ ɔɔ lizi u mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhlii ni u dɔŋa be chaalaa mbusuzi lizaa kuna. U daŋ ɔɔ chi u dominua zɛɛ daa ni jaami mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi, ka bir ga bɔr la uŋ gawɛɛ zuu la lii. Ka ba wàá tɔu, di duana lɛi.

ref: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
text: A nɛra la ge n kawɛɛ la daŋ ɔɔ chi a dominua harbɔɔ, di ra jaami Heezaa Hɔpizaa ni a Baagufalaa jaamaa hɔpizaa la n see.

ref: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
text: A Heezaa Hɔpizii la, a sitɔɔri daŋ ɔɔ lizi peballi anumbɛl ni pebal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: U daŋ ɔɔ kaa kpa mbusu lizaa mia tassazeŋ jaa pebal la ni. Ka jaa mɛgzi gunla maga ge unna nyiŋŋi jaa peballi la bɛl maa ge ni, di kaa kpa nuu pirintuani anaazu jaa mbusu lizaa mia tassazeŋ maa ni.

ref: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
text: Baagufalii maa dii hɔpizii, u daŋ ɔɔ lizi nabalee, peballi anumbɛl ani pebal la n kpekke nɛnnɛ lizi mbusu.

ref: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: U daŋ ɔɔ kaa kpa mbusu lizaa mia tassazeŋ jaa nabal la ni pebal la bɛl maa ni, ka jaa mɛgzi gunla maga ge unna nyiŋŋi jaa pebalee la bɛl maa ni, di kaa kpa nuu pirintuani anumbɛl jaa a mia tassazeŋ ni.

ref: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
text: Di a sitɔɔri ɔɔ waa zuu, jaŋgal dominua labuu u ɔɔ ga zuu, di kaa bir ga de himmaa lii.

ref: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
text: Di a hɛri hina waa, wa ballɔ bá wa jaamiŋ ba diuzenaa dii saŋa, di unla maa wa ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominua la zuu, ú bir ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag dominua la lii. Di unla ge wa ga wiifurii nodig wiikakag dominua la zuu, ú bir ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag hor la lii, di u wa jaamɔɔ tuŋ. A waa dɛkkɛ bɛl maa n bittɛ ga bɔr la uŋ gawɛɛ zuu la, di bir lii.

ref: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
text: A sitɔɔri ni a nɛraa niŋ ɔɔ kpau zuu, di bir kpau lii.

ref: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: Hɔpizizenaa ni diuzenaa dii saŋa, mbusu lizaa mia daŋ ɛɛ mia tassazeŋ jaa nabal la ni pebal la bɛl maa ni. Ka jaa mɛgzi gunla maga ge unna nyiŋŋi jaa pebii la bɛl maa ge ni, di kaa kpa nuu pirintuani anaazu jaa a mia tassazeŋ ni.

ref: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
text: Di a sitɔɔri waa nyiŋŋi ú sunziŋ, di mbusu lizaa kuŋfuuhliire gɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa horaa, dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii labuu ba ɔɔ pilli tɛu, ú zuu di lizi mbusu, gunla himmaa uŋ ɔɔ ɛɛ Heezaa Hɔpizii la. U daŋ bir ga de lii ka ba lawuu tɔ.

ref: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
text: Hɔpizii maa, ii daŋ ɔɔ lizi pebii la n di biŋ kpaŋ, di du kpeg nɛnnɛ, ú ɛɛ mbusu lizaa sefuuhlii tɛŋ. Ií ɔɔ ra ɛɛ guŋ chɔɔzi maa.

ref: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
text: Ii daŋ ɔɔ lizi sau kilozi anɛɛ ni nuu pirintua, di buu á sau a pɛssi, di lizi mbusu chɔɔzi maa. Keŋ mbusu naa lizaa n be ɛɛ widauliirɛ di hanna la.

ref: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
text: Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ di a sitɔɔri wa kpa hɛri bɛl maa sunzi u biibaal maa, de daŋ ɛɛ a biidee ni u naanna maa kapɛttɛ.

ref: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
text: Ama, di u wa kpa u kapɛttɛ kuŋ bɛl sunzi u balii bɛl waa, a balii daŋ wer dɔɔu guŋŋ Hindɔɔi Bina la wa hel, ka ú kaa birgi a sitɔɔri hor. U kapɛttɛ ɛɛ u biibaala bɛŋ hotte.

ref: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
text: A sitɔɔri ge ŋmɛnɛ maa gilɛɛ waa lɛɛ nɛr maa kapɛttɛ kuŋ, ka duŋŋuu lii de. U himmaa kundɔɔlaa biinii ú ra tɛɛ u biibaala ba kapɛttɛzi, guŋ gilɛɛ wa gil n nɛra bɛl maa wàá nyaa u hɛri.”

ref: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
text: Denii a baal kaa kpogli mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl, yaa ga a dominuujiga la n du a dominuuzeŋ la kɛrii zuu a diinanaananaa la n chaŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina hora la, di bagliŋ yembɛl n du wiicholii tuna.

ref: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
text: Denii u kaa kpogliŋ zuu baŋgia diŋŋee la, di kpaŋ bar u siraa anaazu la maa, n na a diŋŋee siraa maa.

ref: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
text: Ba faa kpa biarɛ ma koŋliikpuree bar a diŋŋizi anaazu hiŋ biine, bɔra du de ba ra chem niŋ.

ref: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
text: Denii a baal kaa ŋɔ n be, “A bɔra naabuu ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia huŋhunna la kɛŋluzi, bá ɔɔ ra daali a nɛra mbusuzi lizaa kuna.”

ref: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
text: A baal bir kpogli mìŋ́ Ɛzɛkiɛl ba Kɔraawiizi Dia dominua, n wa na nii n pallɛ ra lii a Dia dominua daa zɛɛ wiifurii keŋkere, dikuu Kɔraawiizi Dia la n chaŋ wiifurii wia. A nii faa ra lii a Dia wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii zɛɛrɛ, mbusu lizibɔr la wiifurii nodig wiikakag keŋkere.

ref: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
text: Denii u kaa kpogliŋ ga wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag dominua la lii, di kpogliŋ bar ga hel baŋgia dominua la n chaŋ wiifurii la. A nii faa pal ra lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii.

ref: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
text: U pɛɛziŋ, “Newee biibaal, i na wia naabuu naa?” Ka faa jaa kpogliŋ la a muu baŋgia.

ref: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
text: Miŋ ga hel de, n na daazi werge a muu baŋgia bɛl maa.

ref: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
text: U ŋɔ n be, “A muu naa pallɔɔ ga wiifurii keŋkere di gaa zuu Jɔɔdan Waluu la, di jaa ga de gaa zuu Muuzensiwii la. Di a nii haŋ gaa zuu a Muuzensiwii biini, u nii la n ɛɛ yazi la ɔɔ birgi niinaniirɛ, di du sum.

ref: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Nyinlaura daŋ ɔɔ chi a Muuzensiwii kɛrii guŋŋ di ga lii Ɛn Gɛdi guŋŋ di ga hel bɔr la banna yir Ɛn Ɛglam la. Bɔra daŋ du de bá ra nyiŋ ba asauzi. Nyiŋ maa deere niŋ su de, gunla aŋ su Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn la.

ref: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
text: Ama, gbatarni la n chɔɔ u kɛraa la waa niiri daŋ haa dɔɔ yazi.

ref: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
text: Daazi ge maa ni a dizii niŋ du a muu baŋgia bɛl maa di ra nɔŋ. A paŋhoori ŋmɛnɛ maa wàá war gɛɛ á nɔŋ huhzi. A daŋ ɔɔ nɔŋ baagu maa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Diarɛ a nii pal lii di waa zuua. A nɔna daŋ ɛɛ diwee, a paŋhoori ge ɛɛ tagzi.” A hɛri magbɔɔni wia

ref: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
text: Ii daŋ bɔnnaabuu a mɛgzi dɔŋa, dikuubɛɛwiai, n lalli n banoniire hɛɛhzi lugɔ n daŋ kpau tɛɛ ii naabaala, ú birgi ii hor di ɛɛ ii kapɛttɛ kuŋ. A hɛri naa daŋ birgi ii kundɔɔlii.

ref: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
text: Bɔra naabuu niŋ ɛɛ a hɛri magbɔɔni, U wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ la daŋ ga wiifurii lii Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, ga chug bolzeŋ Hɛtlɔn ŋmɛnikɛrii, di bɛri Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ ga hel bolzeŋ Zɛdad,

ref: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
text: di kaa ga bolzenaa Bɛrɔta ni Sibram la n du Damaskus ni Hamaf hɛssi baambaaŋ la guŋŋ di ga hel Tikɔn la n du Hauran magbɔɔ la.

ref: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
text: Awia, wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag la magbɔɔ daŋ lii Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn ga chug bolzeŋ Hazar Ɛnan, di hiini Damaskus wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ. Hamaf magbɔɔ chɔɔ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag barii. Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ u wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag magbɔɔ.

ref: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
text: A wiifurii magbɔɔ ge daŋ ga Damaskus ni Hauran hɛssi bambaaŋ, di hiini Jɔɔdan muu la n chɔɔ Giliad ni Izrɛl hɛssi baambaaŋ la ga hel wiifurii muuzeŋ la guŋŋ di ga hel Taama. Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ wiifurii la ge magbɔɔ.

ref: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
text: A wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii magbɔɔ la ge daŋ lii Taama guŋŋ di ga chug Mɛriba Kadɛs niiri la, di hiini Ijip Waluu di ga chug Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn. Waabuu niŋ ɛɛ wiifurii nodig wiikakag magbɔɔ.

ref: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
text: Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛnnɛ niŋ ɛɛ wiicholii magbɔɔ di chɔɔ guŋŋ la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag di ga hel yembɛl n du Hamaf Ŋmɛnɛɛ wiicholii.

ref: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ii bɔnni hɛri naa tɛɛ ii dizi la maa.

ref: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
text: A dɛkkɔɔ ii bɔnni a hɛri naa tɛɛ iihinaa ani hɔɔhra la maa n wa soge ii be di lul biizi la. Ií kpa baa lugɔ bol biizi, dikuu baŋ lul baa Izrɛl hɛri la wia. Ii ni baa maanii bá bɔnni a hɛri tɛɛ Izrɛl hina biini.

ref: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Dee la maa biini hɔɔhri maa n soge, denii ií tɛu u kapɛttɛ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
text: Ba daŋ gil hɛri bɛl, u ni Juda dee hor la du magbɔɔ di lii wiifurii ga hel wiicholii barii, ú ɛɛ sunzinanii tɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi. Ú wassi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, ú jaŋzi lii wiifurii ga hel wiicholii, ú ni dizi hɛssi la bɛl maa mɛgzi. N Dia la daŋ chi u baambaaŋ.

ref: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
text: A bɔnnaa biini baambaaŋ, ii daŋ mɛgzi bɔnanii bɛl, de jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, ú wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi, ií kpa tɛŋ.

ref: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
text: Bɔnanii naa daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehina hor. Ú wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag barii jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, ú wiicholii barii wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi. Ú wiifurii keŋkere ge wassi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi, ú wiifurii nodig wiikakag barii jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue. N Dia la chi u baambaaŋ.

ref: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
text: A hɛri naa daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehina la miŋ lizɛɛ ba ra humiŋ, ba lii Zadɔk naanna biini di faa ra humiŋ ni wibii la hor. Ba faa waŋ vɛɛwɛ saŋa la Izrɛl hina ni Levi dee n faa vɛɛŋ la.

ref: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
text: A hɛri naa daŋ ɛɛ sunzinanii di ɛɛ bɔnaniinanii kaali a maa, di lii a bɔnanii naa biini tɛɛ baa. De ni Levi dee hor la daŋ du magbɔɔ, di hiini n kizeehina hor la.

ref: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
text: Levi dee la daŋ dɔɔ ba hor de, ú jaŋzi ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, ú wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi. Ú jaŋzi maa ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue, ú wassi ge ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi.

ref: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
text: A hɛri naa ŋmɛnɛ maa waa dɛkkɛ baŋ yoou gɛɛ di kpau chɛr kummaa gɛɛ di sunzi nɛr. Denii ɛɛ a hɛri maa bɔnaniinanii, dikuubɛɛwiai, de ɛɛ naniinaniirɛ, di ɛɛ n hor.

ref: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
text: A hɛri bɔr la n kawɛɛ la wassi n ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa anue, u jaŋzi ge ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anue la, daŋ ɛɛ nɛr maa bɔr. Bá ra ma diini gɛɛ ú ɛɛ ba sela diiribɔr. Bolzeŋ la daŋ chi de baambaaŋ.

ref: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
text: A bolzeŋ keŋkere bɛl maa daŋ mɛgzi, ú jaŋzi ni u wassi maa ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa anaazu ni kalfaanuezi.

ref: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
text: A hɛri bɔr la n kawɛɛ, u ni bɔnaniinanii la du magbɔɔ la jaŋzi daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa fi, ú wiifurii keŋkere, ú jaŋzi ge ɛɛ guŋ himmaa u wiicholii barii. Denii a bolzeŋ huŋhunna ra na ba diwee.

ref: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
text: A bolzeŋ huŋhunna maanii ninna par de. Ba daŋ lii Izrɛl dizi maa biine.

ref: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
text: Awia, a hɛri la maa n du a baambaaŋ la baŋ lizɛɛ tɛŋ la wassi ni u jaŋzi maa daŋ ɛɛ kpaŋ, u daŋ ɛɛ nogumzi kagboŋa tokko ni anuezi, bɔr la ban niŋ ma bolzeŋ la jaa.

ref: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
text: A hɛri bɔr la n kawɛɛ du a bɔnaniinanii ni a bolzeŋ bɔr la keŋkerezi anɛɛ la maa, daŋ ɛɛ Izrɛl hina sitɔɔri la hor. U kundɔɔlii daŋ chɔɔ lii wiifurii ga chug Jɔɔdan muu, di lii wiicholii ge ga chug Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn. A bɔnnaa baambaannɛ niŋ ɛɛ n hɛrnaniinanii ni n Dia bɔr.

text: Sitɔɔraa, hɛssi nabɔnzii, laallɔɔra nabɔnzii ani nabɔnzi la maa n jaawɛ, wa bar baa, di na lugɔ niŋ la waa ba bɔrahɔna ɛɛwɛ wiimaa gɛɛ ba nyuhuŋ kpaŋ gba waa nyursɛɛ, ba tagtazi waa fuuhwe, ba waa nyɔɔzi gba ra sɔɔhri.

ref: So all of them came and stood in front of it.
text: Ba maa n wa chaalɛɛ bá kuari Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza vug la uŋ chiŋŋɛɛ la, ba ga chi a vug see.

ref: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
text: Denii u chaali u hɛri nabɔnzi maa, sitɔɔra, hɛssi nabɔnzi, nabɔnzi la n na biruu liize, kebibinna, sitɔɔra, seriya diire ani nabɔnzi la maa n du u kora diiribɔr biini. Bá wa faari di kuari vug la uŋ chiŋŋɛɛ la.

ref: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
text: Denii siiri sii di ŋɔ werge maa, “Hɛssi hina, nɛra maa ani mɔɔrizi maa, kenne koorizeŋ ŋɔ ií ɛɛ,

ref: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
text: di ii haŋ wa nuu nyigaa, tiitorii, kem, janjalaŋ, kaloopezi ani duarikuna iri maa wiraa, a dɛkkɔɔ ií chɔɔ hɛri di jaami vug la Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n chiŋŋɛɛ la.

ref: Anyone who refuses will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace.
text: Unla maa waa haŋ wa sɛɛ chɔɔ di jaamuu, ba daŋ kpau ha ninzeŋ biini.”

ref: As soon as the people heard the music, they bowed down and worshiped the gold statue that the king had set up.
text: Awia, baŋ haŋ waa nuu a kuna naa maa wiraa, a nɛra maa maa chɔɔ, di jaami kunla Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n kpa saliŋ kuari chiŋŋi la.

ref: Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar.
text: Kenne a ɛɛ, banla n zum chinchiŋwilaa wikpoglaa la baŋhina na ŋmɛnɛɛ bá chɔgi Jus hina la wia.

ref: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
text: Ba ŋɔ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza be, “Jara, Kɔ́raawiizi tɛi miibɔɔjaŋ, í du de di hanna la!

ref: You commanded everyone to bow down and worship the gold statue when the music played.
text: Jara, i du gbɔgrɛ lugɔ di unla maa haŋ wa nuu nyigaa, tiitorii, kem ani duarikuna la maa wiraa, a dɛkkɔɔ u chɔɔ, di jaami saliŋ vug la,

ref: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
text: di unla maa haŋ wa vɛɛ guŋ ɛɛi, bá kpau ha ninzenzeŋ biini.

ref: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
text: Ka Jus hina la hiŋ tɛɛ Babilɔn paga nabɔmuu la, Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo waa, waa sɛɛwɛ. Ba waa i vuga ra hum gɛɛ di ra jaami saliŋ vug la hiŋ chiŋŋɛɛ la.”

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said,
text: Koorizeŋ la baaŋ fuuh werge maa, u ŋɔ bá yir ba nɛra bahoro hiŋ. Denii ba kpogli baa ba u be,

ref: “I hear that you refuse to worship my gods and the gold statue I have set up.
text: u pɛɛzi baa, “Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo, wibiire ii waa n vuga ra hum gɛɛ di ra jaami saliŋ vug la miŋ chiŋŋɛɛ laa?

ref: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, di ii haŋ wa nuu nyigaa, tiitorii, kem ani duarikuna la maa wiraa, ií ɛɛ sirya di jaamuu nɛnnɛ. Ka di ii wa vɛɛwɔ, ba daŋ kpa ia ha ninzenzeŋ biini manaŋ, ń na, di vug bɛl du denii ú wer lɛɛ ia ha, lii n nonee biini gɛɛ?”

ref: The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves.
text: Denii Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo bir ŋɔ u be, “Jara, yaa waa wii maa dɔɔwɛ, ya ŋɔ mɔgli yaa hinaa.

ref: But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
text: Haali di waa guŋ wa ɛɛwɛ gba, ka yaa ra nyiŋŋuu i zum lugɔ yaa wàá hum i vuga gɛɛ di sɛɛ saliŋ vug la hiŋ chiŋŋɛɛ la dɔɔra maa.”

ref: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
text: Denii Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza baaŋ fuuh, Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo ni werge maa, u manni bir kur ba ni. U gil ba bir kuari niŋ la du, u ra lau zagzagzag, di kaali gunla uŋ faa duwɛɛ la, buniidaanɛɛ.

ref: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
text: Denii u ŋɔ u laallɔɔra la baŋhina n dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge be lugɔ bá vɔɔzi baa, di kpa baa ha a ninzenzeŋ biini.

ref: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
text: Kakpaŋ, Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza jeŋki naazi, di pɛɛzi banla n na biruu liize la, dikuu u nua n kpuwɛɛ wia, di ŋɔ, “Baala bahoro lɛi yaa vɔɔzi ha a niŋ biini laa?” Ba bir ŋɔ, “Jara, gunnɛ a ɛɛ.”

ref: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
text: U ŋɔ, “Ií na, n na baala banaazu n volle ra bar a niŋ biini, ba waa fuuhwe, ka naazuhiŋ la du lugɔ mɛlika.”

ref: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
text: Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza jaa tuzi hel a ninzenzeŋ dominua, di ga gbooli werge maa, “Sadrak, Mɛsak, ani Abɛdnigo, Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la balaa, ií lii ba ɛŋ!” Awia, Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo lii a niŋ biini.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
text: Denii Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ŋɔ, “Chɔlaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo n na hum la hotte, unla n hum u mɛlika di lɛɛ u balaa! Ba yarduubuu, di vɛɛ mìŋ́ koori wiŋɔɔlii. A par baabuu lugɔ bá kpa ba miibɔɔni chɛr siu kaali ban niŋ hum di jaami vuga aŋhina, see ba himmaa Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.

ref: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
text: Awia, n du gbɔgrɛ lugɔ hɛri bɛl maa nɛra gɛɛ mɔɔri iri maa hina, n niŋ kaa ŋɔ wiimaa zuu Kɔraawiizi la Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo n na hum la ni, bá mɔnni baa jigzijigzi, di purgi ba diini á chɔɔ kulululu, dikuubɛɛwiai, vug maa wàá wer lɛɛ nɛra keŋ dɔŋ maa.”

ref: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
text: Denii Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza kaa bir jaa Sadrak, Mɛsak ani Abɛdnigo nabɔmuu, Babilɔn paga maa.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
text: Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza sɛbi hɔŋ tɛɛ hɛssi maa nɛra ni mɔɔri maa nɛra n du durnya naa. Kenne u ŋɔ, “N na jaami ia!

ref: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
text: A ɛɛmbuu bɔsɔna werge, n ŋɔ ń kali iabuu wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la n ɛɛwɛ tɛŋ.

ref: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
text: U ɛɛ wizenaare werge, u nuukpuuri wia dɔɔ fɔŋŋa! Kɔraawiizi kora waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ, u ra di koraa jiminizi maa ni.

ref: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
text: Mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza faa sogo n diarɛ di dɔɔ bampirsɔna, di nyɛɛli.

ref: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
text: Awia, n faa ŋɔ Babilɔn nunzunna maa wa bagli a deeza zɛɛ tɛŋ.

ref: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
text: Baabuu hila, banla n zum chinchiŋwilaa wia ani vugra maa, ba wa chaali. N kali baa n deeza hiŋ, ka ba waa wette bá bagliŋ u zɛɛ.

ref: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
text: A tuna maa, Daniɛl, ba kaa ra yiruu n vug sɔŋ Bɛltisaaza, vuga la n kpekke duma du u ni, ba n be, n bagluu a deeza.

ref: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
text: Hila maa Koori Bɛltisaaza, n zummɔ lugɔ vuga la n kpekke dumaa du i ni. Wisuahlii maa waa hoo di du kpol tɛi. N deezaa keŋ, bagliŋ u zɛɛ.

ref: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
text: N chɔɔwɔɔ deezi, di na daazeŋ bɛl n chigɛ durnya baambaaŋ. U kannɔɔ di hel werge maa guŋ hibibi.

ref: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
text: U hel di du kaŋ, di du kpeg werge di ga chug chiŋ, guŋ gil durnya nɛra maa nau.

ref: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
text: U paŋhoori faa du wer nɛnnɛ, u nɔna du kpil werge, di ɛɛ diwee tɛɛ durnya kummaa. Pir sela faa chɔɔ u chunchugli, zumbizi ge du daŋa u kela maa ni, newea ni kunyinee maa iri ra di u nɔna.

ref: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
text: Miŋ faa chɔɔwɛ di haa ra fɛ a winaalii naa nfɛrɛ, n kaa na mɛlika n lii Kɔraawiizi bol di ra tuu.

ref: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
text: U sii werge maa, di ŋɔ, ‘Ií teŋ a daa ha, di kɛuri u kela maa, di nɛɛri u paŋhoori, di yaari u nɔna. Ií duŋŋi sela la maa n chɔɔ u zɛɛ ni zumbizi la maa n du u kela ni la.

ref: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
text: Ka kpa lugbii ni danyɛ yɔlɔzi vɔɔzi u zɛɛkantirii ni u lunne, á ka hɛri, kooree biini. Gil ŋmɛnii chol baal naa ni werge, di gil u ni sela ni kooree du.

ref: Give him the mind of a wild animal for seven long years.
text: Gil newee nfɛrɛ la un dɔɔwɛ la birgi sel nfɛrɛ, guŋŋ binni aniidaanɛɛ.

ref: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
text: Mɛlikazii faa sii a keŋ jina naa wia, di ŋɔ lugɔ kenne niŋ ɛɛ, guŋ gil newea maa wer sɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu dɔɔ newea kossi maa fɔŋŋa, di kpaa ra tɛɛ nɛr la maa wia n paruu, haali nɛra la gba n ɛɛ nɛdumazi.’

ref: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
text: Deeza naabuu mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza deezi. Bɛltisaaza, bagliŋ ú zɛɛ filaŋkeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, nunzunna la n du n kora biini la bɛl maa waa wette bagliŋ u zɛɛ. Ka hiŋwaa daŋ wer, dikuubɛɛwiai, vuga la n kpekke dumaa du i ni.” Daniɛl n bagli a deeza zɛɛ

ref: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
text: Denii Daniɛl, ba kaa ra yiruu Bɛltisaaza, ɛɛ kinchaŋ tama, ɔnsii lawuu. Awia, a koori ŋɔ, “Bɛltisaaza, gilɛɛ gil a deeza ni u zɛɛ wia dɔɔi ɔnsii.” Bɛltisaaza ŋɔ, “Jara, a faa ɛɛ lugɔ a deeza ra bagli i dɔma wiarɛ, ka gilɛɛ ɛɛ i hor!

ref: You saw a tree that grew so big and strong that it reached up to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
text: Daa la hiŋ nawɛɛ u hel di du kaŋ, di du kpeg werge di ga chug chiŋ, durnya nɛra maa nau,

ref: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
text: u dɔɔ paŋhoonanaa nɛnnɛ ni nɔna werge, di ra tɛɛ kummaa diwee, di ra tɛɛ pir sela bɔsɔŋ, zumbizi daŋa du u kela ni la,

ref: Your Majesty, that tree is you. Your glorious reputation has reached heaven, and your kingdom covers the earth.
text: Jara, hinuu a daa! I zenni ni i fɔŋŋa werge la nyaŋŋɔɔrɛ, haali di ga chug chiŋ, i kora ge yaa la bɔɔnɛɛ.

ref: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
text: Jara, hin na mɛlikananiinanii n lii Kɔraawiizi bol di ra tuu, di ra ŋɔ, ‘Ií teŋ a daa di chɔguu, ka gil u zɛɛkantirii, di kpa lugbii ni danyɛ yɔlɔzi vɔɔzuu pir kooree biini, ka u lunne du hɛri biini. Gil ŋmɛnii chol a baal naa ni werge maa, di gil u du lugɔ pir sela guŋŋ binni aniidaanɛɛ.’

ref: Your Majesty, God Most High has sent you this message, and it means
text: Jara, u zɛɛ ni wii la Kɔraawiizi la N Kaali Kummaa la n dauwɛ tɛibuu keŋ.

ref: that you will be forced to live with the wild animals, far away from humans. You will eat grass like a wild animal and live outdoors for seven years, until you learn that God Most High controls all earthly kingdoms and chooses their rulers.
text: Ba daŋ duŋŋii lii newea biini, i gaa zuu pir sela be. I danna di kooree lugɔ nauna, ŋmɛnii chol i ni werge. Binni aniidaanɛɛ daŋ wa bɛri mɔɔ, ka i haa sɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu dɔɔ newea kossi maa fɔŋŋa, di kpaa ra tɛɛ nɛr la maa uŋ lizɛɛ.

ref: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
text: A mɛlika n ŋɔ bá gil a daa zɛɛkantirii ni u lunne la zɛɛrɛ lugɔ ba daŋ kaa bir wa tɛi kora, di i wa sɛɛwɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizii koori.

ref: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
text: Awia, Jara, gil n baglaa naa sɔɔni i bɔra. Gil i biini chɔgi dikuu i wichɔgaa wia, di gilaa ta, di ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee, di ra na dɔgnya hina sinyɛna. Aŋhinabe, guŋ daŋ gil i nyɛɛli di ra la.” A deeza n wa ɛɛ wibii wia

ref: But before I could finish speaking, a voice from heaven interrupted: King Nebuchadnezzar, this kingdom is no longer yours.
text: U faa haa ra ŋɔ wia naabuu, ka nuu loobii bɛl n lii Kɔraawiizi bol, di ra ŋɔ, “Nɛbukadnɛɛza, kenne ba dau tɛi, ba lɛɛ i kora fɔŋŋaa i be.

ref: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
text: Ba daŋ duŋŋii lii nɛra biini, í ni pir sela gaa zuu. I ra di kooree lugɔ nauna. Binni aniidaanɛɛ daŋ wa bɛri mɔɔ, ka i haa sɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa labuu dɔɔ newea kossi maa fɔŋŋa, di kpaa ra tɛɛ nɛr la maa uŋ lizɛɛ.”

ref: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
text: Wia la baŋ ŋɔwɛɛ du Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ni la, wa ɛɛ kakpaŋ. Ba faa wa duŋŋuubuu lii nɛra biini, u gaa di kooree lugɔ nauna. Ŋmɛnii faa lii Kɔraawiizi bol di chol u ni, u bɔra maa pɔɔh, guŋŋ u huna maa wa hel lugɔ chig huna, u nonibifiiri ni naanibifiiri ge hel lugɔ zumbee hora.

ref: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
text: A binni aniidaanɛɛ n wa bɛrɛɛ, mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza lalli n siwee chaŋ Kɔraawiizi bol, n nfɛrɛ bir ba. Denii n chɔli Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la, di tɔgzuu, di kpau girme. Waabuu unla n du de saŋa maa la. U daŋ di kora di hanna la, u kora daŋ haŋ du denii saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
text: Durnya newea maa waa kummaa ɛɛwɛ u be. U ɔɔ kpa u fɔŋŋaa dau chinchiŋ fɔŋŋazi ni newea la n du hɛri naa, gunla n paruu. Nɛr maa wàá wer karsuu gɛɛ di ŋɔ u be, “Bɛɛ i ɛɛ gunnɛi?”

ref: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
text: Saŋa la n nfɛrɛ n wa bittɛ ba la, denii n bir du wer, di dɔɔ girme werge, dikuu n kora girme wia. Banla n na biriŋ liize ni n nabɔnzenaa nyiŋŋi n bɔr, di bir soŋŋiŋ n koorikara ni, n zenni bir kaali gunla miŋ faa duwɛɛ la.

ref: That's why I say: “Praise and honor the King who rules from heaven! Everything he does is honest and fair, and he can shatter the power of those who are proud.”
text: Awia, filaŋkeŋ, mìŋ́ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza ra tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi la n du chiŋ la girmee, dikuubɛɛwiai, u wiɛɛlaa maa deŋloore, u ŋmɛnizi maa dɔɔ wibii. U ɔɔ giluu nɛra la maa n na jigsi bir dɔɔ sisɔna.

ref: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
text: Bɛlsaaza n wa di kora, u gil ba ɛɛ diuzenaa tɛɛ u nabɔnzenaa kagboŋ, u ni baa di, di nyɔɔ siŋ.

ref: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
text: Koori Bɛlsaaza n na nyɔɔ siŋ la, u ŋɔ dí ba ga kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu libizi la u mɛɛ Koorizeŋ Nɛbukadnɛɛza n faa paagɛɛ lii Jɛrusalɛm, Kɔraawiizi Dia biini la, di ba, ú ni u nabɔnzi, u haana ani u hahjigzi kpaa nyɔɔ siŋ.

ref: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
text: Banna nyɔɔ a siŋ la, ba ra chɔli vuga la baŋ kpa saliŋ, saliŋhuŋŋa, danyɛ, lugbia, daazi ani bia di kuari la.

ref: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.

text: Denii n na nyiŋŋi n zum senaazu hiŋ la ge zɛɛ nɛnnɛ, unla n faa kur anla maa ni, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge, u dɔɔ lugbia nyina ni danyɛ naanibifiiri, di purgi u kuŋkpeglaa maa, di liglaa, di fɛrgi a bɔra la n kawɛɛ la.

ref: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
text: N kaa ra nyiŋŋi n zum nyigzi fi la n du u nyuu la wia ni unla hiŋ n kaa wa lii, di faa kuugi lugli nyigzi ahoro la. U dɔɔ siwee ni nua la n na ŋɔ barabara wiŋɔzi la, u wia dɔɔ ɔnsii werge di kaali a maa la.

ref: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
text: Minna binni la, di nyigaa naa ra lɔ Kɔraawiizi nɛra la laal, di ra kpegli baa,

ref: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
text: guŋŋ Unla N Du De Saŋa Maa la wa ba, di wa di seriya, di lɛɛ bilii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la nɛra, dikuubɛɛwiai, saŋa la ban niŋ dɔɔ a kora helloo.

ref: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
text: Kenne u bagliŋ a zɛɛ, ‘Senaazu hiŋ la ɛɛ kornaazuhiŋ la n niŋ wa diu. U daŋ kur kossi la maa ni, di chɔgi hɛri maa, di fɛrguu purgi.

ref: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
text: Nyigzi fi la ɛɛ koora fi n niŋ lii kora naa biinii. Koori bɛl wa di, di lii ba har, di kur lugli hora la ni, di kpegli baa.

ref: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
text: U daŋ ŋɔ wia zuu Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la ni, di ra sunni u nɛra, di ra nyiŋŋi ú bir hɔpizizenaa ni gbɔgni la n du de. U daŋ dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi nɛra fɔŋŋa guŋŋ binni ahoro ni keza.

ref: But he will finally be judged, and his kingdom completely destroyed.
text: Ka ba daŋ wa diu seriya, di foozi u fɔŋŋa, di chɔgi u kora nyaamm, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.

ref: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
text: Denii bá kpa kossizenaa ni a fɔŋŋazi ani a zenni werge maa n du durnya naa maa biini, fɔŋŋa tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la nɛra. U kora daŋ ɛɛ kora la n niŋ du de hanna la, hɛssi nabɔnzi maa ra jaamuu, di ra sɛɛu dɔɔra.’

ref: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
text: A wii tunaa keŋ. Mìŋ́ Daniɛl nfɛrɛ faa ra kooziŋ werge, n siwee bir chogli, ka n kpa a wii du n biini.”

ref: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
text: Koori Bɛlsaaza kora dii binni ahorohiŋ biinii, mìŋ́ Daniɛl faa kaa na wia lugɔ deeza biini, unla miŋ felee na la har.

ref: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
text: Denii n binni na pebal n chigɛ a muu kɛrii, di dɔɔ nyigjaŋra anɛɛ. A nyigaa bɛl faa du jaŋ kaali unla hiŋ, ka tɔ har lii.

ref: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
text: N na binni a pebal, ka u ra gbuuri wiicholii, wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag ani wiifurii nodig wiikakag kuna maa. Bɛl maa faa waa wette kpegluu gɛɛ di wer lɛɛ u hiŋ lii u fɔŋŋa biini. U ɛɛ gunla maa n paruu, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa jaa.

ref: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
text: Minna fɛ nfɛrɛ ń zum wii naa zɛɛ, kakpaŋ, di buuŋ lii wiicholii ra chɔ werge maa, haali u naazi gba waa hɛri ra gbɔgzi, u dɔɔ nyigzeŋkpaŋ, u baŋ u siwee baambaaŋ.

ref: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
text: Denii u kpa u fɔŋŋa maa di kiiri werge, di ra ba pebal la miŋ faa nawɛɛ a muu nua la ni.

ref: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
text: N ŋɔ n binni, di u gaa naa a pebal ni baaŋ werge maa, di kuugi u nyigzi anɛɛ la, di lau a maa purgi. A pebal faa waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ ú wer naau. A buuŋ ta a pebal hɛri, di fɛrguu, ka nɛr maa faa waa hoo ú mɔgluu ta.

ref: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
text: A buuŋ faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa werge di ra jigsi. U fɔŋŋa n wa nyaŋŋɛɛ, u nyigaa la faa ku, ka nyigzi anaazu faa kaa lii lɛɛ u bɔr, bɛl chaŋ wiifurii, bɛl chaŋ wiicholii, bɛl chaŋ wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag, bɛl ge chaŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag.

ref: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
text: A nyigzi anaazu hiŋ bɛl kaa fur nyigjiga bɛl, u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge guŋŋ di ga hel wiifurii nodig wiikakag ni wiifurii, di ra la Izrɛl Hɛrnanii la.

ref: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
text: U hel di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di lɔ Kɔraawiizi laallɔɔra, aabuu chinchiŋwilaa. Haali di hur a chinchiŋwilaa aŋhina ha hɛri, di fɛrgaa.

ref: It humiliated heaven's army and dishonored its leader by keeping him from offering the daily sacrifices. In fact, it was so terrible that it even disgraced the temple and wiped out true worship. It also did everything else it wanted to do.
text: Nɛra faa ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa de, ka gil hɔpizi biimaa mbusuzi himmaa lizaa, di duŋŋi wiijaamaa himmaa. A nyigaa faa nyɛɛli u wiɛɛlaa maa biini.

ref: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
text: Denii n nuu mɛlika bɛl n pɛɛzi u dɔŋhiŋ bɛl, di ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ winaalii naa wia ɛɛ, di birgi magɛi? Ɛrɛɛ wichɔgaa werge naa lɛɛ hɔpizi biimaa mbusuzi lizaa bɔr, di birgi magɛi? Ɛrɛɛ bá fɛrgi Kɔraawiizi laallɔɔra ni Kɔraawiizi Dia, di birgi magɛi?”

ref: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
text: Mìŋ́ Daniɛl n faa ra pessi n winaalii hiŋ lugɔ deeza biini, ń zum u zɛɛ la, n ŋɔ n binni kakpaŋ, di kunnɛ chigɛ n see alugɔ newee.

ref: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
text: N nuu newee loobii n na yir lii Muu Ulai biini, di ra ŋɔ, “Gebrɛl, bagli baal naa a winaalii naa zɛɛ.”

ref: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
text: Mɛlika Gebrɛl n na ba n be di waa dugliŋ, ɔnsii lawiŋ werge, n chol pi. U ŋɔ n be, “Newee biibaal, zum lugɔ a winaalii naa lugɔ deeza biini naa ɛɛ hɛri tunaa wiarɛ.”

ref: While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet
text: Uŋ faa haa ra ŋɔ a wia n be la, di n chɔɔwɔ pi, di chɔɔ dɔbɛrii. Denii u gbɔgziŋ, di lalliŋ n izi chi.

ref: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
text: U ŋɔ n be, “N daŋ baglii gunla n niŋ wa ɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi baaŋ saŋa. A winaalii naa ra bagli hɛri tunaa saŋa wiarɛ.

ref: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
text: A pebal la hiŋ nawɛɛ uŋ dɔɔ nyigzi anɛɛ la, chigɔɔ tɛɛ Mɛdi ni Pɛsia kossi.

ref: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
text: A buuŋ la ge chi tɛɛ Giris hina koora, u nyigzeŋ la ge n chigɛ u siwee baambaaŋ la, chi tɛɛ ba koorilugli.

ref: After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
text: A nyigzeŋ la n kuwee, ka anaazu lii u bɔr la ge chigɔɔ tɛɛ kossi anaazu n niŋ wa lii u kora diiribɔr biini, ka a fɔŋŋa wàá hel u hor la.

ref: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
text: Di a keŋ kossi tunaa saŋa waa dugli, ba kpoŋaa ni ba biinikpola nyaŋŋi lugɔ bá tɛrgi ba digna la, koori la wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii, di ɛɛ nɛchɔgii werge, di nyaa wibii, daŋ wa du de.

ref: He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well.
text: U daŋ dɔɔ fɔŋŋa werge, ka a wàá ɛɛ u himmaa fɔŋŋa. U daŋ chɔgi bɔr werge, di nyɛɛli u wiɛɛlaa maa biini. U daŋ kpuuzi nɛzenaa ni Kɔraawiizi nɛra.

ref: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
text: U daŋ gil nɛdaraa nyaŋŋi, di kpa u hiŋ bɔmbɔ nɛr maa. Saŋa la baŋ wa fɛwɛɛ lugɔ ba sogoo nɛnnɛ la, a saŋaa ú wa kpu bakpila maa, di karsi Koora Maa Koori. Ba daŋ kpuu, ka a wàá lugɔ newee fɔŋŋaa bá kpa kpuu.

ref: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
text: Duaninzi ni chɔɔzizi wia la baŋ pillɛɛ baglii la ɛɛ wibiire, gil aawaa ɛɛ wolo wia filaŋkeŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, a wàá ɛɛ manaŋ.”

ref: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
text: Kuuhni ni wiila werge lɔ mìŋ́ Daniɛl dau hɔpizikpila maa, ka n kaa izi di gaa hum huma la koori n tɛŋ la. N nua kpu, dikuu a winaalii wia, maa wette ń zum u zɛɛ.

ref: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
text: U kora dii lugli bina biinii, n faa karmi gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ u hɔŋ biini tɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ Jɛrɛmia, u ra bagli gunla Jɛrusalɛm n niŋ chɔɔ diŋgela, binni tokkoahoro ni fi.

ref: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.
text: N suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi la minna hum, di sɛɛ chɔgri, dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi, i zenni kannɔɔ, i wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge. I wia dɔɔ wibiire i ni nɛra nɔŋŋaa nuukpaŋ la wia, di tɛɛ banla n nɔŋŋii, di ra hiŋ i widaulaa la.

ref: But we have sinned terribly by rebelling against you and rejecting your laws and teachings.
text: Yaa ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ zuu i ni. Yaa ɛɛ biinikpola wiarɛ, di dɔɔ dignikpega, di bir har kpu i widaulaa ni i Gbɔgni.

ref: We have ignored the message your servants the prophets spoke to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and everyone else.
text: Yaa waa sɛɛwɛ nuu tɛɛ i dɔgtɛɛzi la n ɛɛ i balaa la n wa kpa i sɔŋ, di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ yaa koora, yaa sitɔɔra, yaa mɛɛwaa ani nɛra la maa n du a hɛri.

ref: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, i ɔɔ ra na nɛra sinyɛnaa di gil yaa wichɔgaa ra tɛɛ yaa, haali yaa n ɔɔ dɔɔ dignikpega di vɛɛi gba.

ref: and rejected your teachings that came to us from your servants the prophets.
text: Kɔraawiizi la yaa n na hum, yaa waa i nua ni i Gbɔgni la hiŋ ga i balaa dɔgtɛɛzi be tɛɛ yaa la hiŋŋɛ.

ref: Everyone in Israel has stubbornly refused to obey your laws, and so those curses written by your servant Moses have fallen upon us.
text: Izrɛl hina maa chɔg i Gbɔgnii, di bir har kpui, di vɛɛ a hiŋaa. Awia, nuuseezi la hiŋ ŋɔ a daŋ di yaa, ba sɛbaa du i balii Moosis Gbɔgni hɔŋ biini la, di yaabuu, dikuu yaa n ɛɛ wichɔgaa di zuu i ni wia.

ref: You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened.
