text: Koorizeŋ Dariɔs koora dii binni anaazuhiŋ la biini, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ wiarɛ tɛɛ Zɛkaria baaguzi kabɛlhiŋ Kislɛv la hɔpizaa anaazuhiŋ hɔl.

ref: It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
text: lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ Dia Kizeehina ni u dɔgtɛɛzi be, di ŋɔ, “Ya gil yaa biine chɔgi, yá ra vɔɔ nua baaguzi anuehiŋ la biini, gunla yaa n faa ra ɛɛ biŋkpila maa biini laa?”

ref: It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests: For
text: “Pɛɛzi a hɛri hina maa ni a kizeehina, dí, baŋ faa vɔɔ nuuzi di wii ni biinichɔg baaguzi anue ni aniidaanɛɛ hina la biine, binni tokkoahoro ni fi naa, n wiarɛ ba faa vɔɔ a nuuzia?

ref: And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment?
text: Baŋ faa ra di di ra nyɔɔ la, bahinaarɛ ba faa ɛɛ guŋ di ra tɛɛ.”

ref: My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
text: Wia naabuu Kɔraawiizi faa gil u dɔgtɛɛzi la n tɔ see la sii, saŋa la Jɛrusalɛm ani bola la n baruu la n faa su nɛra, ba so pɛrɛtɛ, daama sua, nɛra faa so wiifurii nodig wiikakag paga ni wiicholii ge giŋgimee zɛɛzi la.

ref: So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another!
text: “Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ií ra di wibii di ra na dɔŋa sinyɛna di ra suŋ dɔŋa ni.

ref: Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa fir luhaaŋ gɛɛ lalbiizi gɛɛ hɔɔhri gɛɛ nyaari. Ií gilɛɛ waa fɛ nfɛrchɔgaa ii biine, di ra du dɔŋa ni.’

ref: But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry
text: Ba faa dɔɔ dignikpega, di vɛɛ n Gbɔg gɛɛ n wiŋɔɔlaa la mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ n ga n Duma be, di hum n dɔgtɛɛzi lugɔ bá ŋɔ la. Awia, mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ baaŋ faa fuuh werge maa.

ref: and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
text: Miŋ yir baa la, ba vɛɛ nuuirɛ. Awia, di ba yiriŋ, n gba wàá nuu. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
text: N faa kpa venne di yaari baa durnya hɛssi maa biine, ba faa ga ɛɛ hɔɔhra. Ba hɛri faa chɔɔ diŋgela, nɛr maa faa waa wette ú ba de. Kenne ba ɛɛ, a hɛrsum birgi diŋgela la.”

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ kaa ŋɔ mìŋ́ Zɛkaria be,

ref: I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
text: N daŋ bir la Jɛrusalɛm, n bolzennaniinanii la, di ga du de. Ba danna yiruu Wibii Bolzeŋ, di ra yir mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ bizeŋ la Bizennaniinanii.

ref: while boys and girls play in the streets.
text: Biibaala ni biihaana daŋ su a bolzeŋ ŋmɛnizenaa maa di ra dua.

ref: This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Aŋhinabe, wia naa daŋ ɛɛ witittaa tɛɛ banla n niŋ ka a bolzeŋ a guŋ saŋa, ka a waa ɛɛ witittaa n be.

ref: I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west,
text: N daŋ lɛɛ n nɛra lii hɛssi la n du wiifurii ni wiicholii la biine,

ref: and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
text: di bir ba ba ni Jɛrusalɛm, bá wa du de di ɛɛ n nɛra, ń ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum. N daŋ dɔɔ wibii di ra ɛɛ wideŋlaa ba be. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, ii banla n na nuu wiŋɔɔlaa naa n dɔgtɛɛzi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ ka ba chiŋŋi n Dia zɛɛ la, ií aah siwii di chiiri zɛɛ, di ma mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Dia la.

ref: Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
text: Mɔɔ ka a saŋa faa hel, ba faa waa newee gɛɛ sel maa ra turgi. Nɛr maa faa waa wette u hum u huma dikuu u dɔm wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, n faa gillɔɔ nɛra hah dɔŋa.

ref: My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋwaa, màá ka ɛɛ n nɛra naa n kawɛɛ naa gunla miŋ faa ra ɛɛ la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky.
text: Di ba duu kuna, a daŋ lii di lɛɛ nɛnnɛ, grepu daazi ge nɔŋ nɛnnɛ. Dooŋ ba nɛnnɛ, á hɛri lii kuna nɛnnɛ. Annii naa maanii ń kpa tɛɛ banla n kawɛɛ la, a ɛɛ ba kapɛttɛ kuna.

ref: People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
text: Juda ni Izrɛl hina, iiŋ faa ɛɛ nɛra la hɛssi hina n faa ra see nuuzi la, n daŋ jaa lɛɛ ia, di kissi ia. Ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm, ka chi chigigi.”

ref: When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “Saŋa la ii naabaala n faa fuuh n baaŋ, n faa ta jinaa ń tɔɔri baa werge. N faa waa n nfɛrɛ bittɛ ka ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, n siwii aahwɔɔ ń ɛɛ winanaa tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda hina. Awia, ií gilɛɛ ra ɔm.

ref: But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace.
text: Ií ra ɛɛ annii naa, ií ra ŋɔ wibii bɛŋ di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, di ra di seriyazi ni wibii.

ref: Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things. A Time of Celebration
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra ta jinachɔgaa dikuu ii dɔŋahina wia gɛɛ di hɛɛhzi ra kanni kara. N kiichɔgiirɛ annii maa ɛɛi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ kaa ŋɔ n be,

ref: People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
text: “Baagu anaazuhiŋ, anuehiŋ, aniidaanɛɛhiŋ ani fihiŋ la biine iiŋ ɔɔ ra vɔɔ nuuzi la daŋ ɛɛ bɔsɔna ni sideŋŋa saŋazi, di ɛɛ hɔpizizenaa dii la n dɔɔ bɔsɔna tɛɛ Juda hina. Awia, ií nɔŋŋi wibii ni bampirsɔna.”

ref: I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “Nɛkpila ni ba dizi daŋ lii bolzenaa di haa ba Jɛrusalɛm,

ref: Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
text: denii bolzeŋ bɛl hina la bolzeŋ bɛl hina be, di ga ŋɔ, ‘Ií gil ya la ga jaami Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, di suŋŋuu ú kissi yaa. Ií ba ya kaali.’

ref: Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness.
text: Denii nɛkpila ni ba dizi ani hɛssi la n kpekke hina ba Jɛrusalɛm, bá wa nuu wia lii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ be, di jaamuu.”

ref: When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ra ŋɔ, “A hɔpizaa hiŋ biini, hɔɔhra fi daŋ lii durnya hɛssi ni mɔɔrizi biine, di ba Jus hinuu be di wa lau u tagta ka ŋɔ, ‘Yaa waa ra nyiŋŋuu yaa nii ɛɛ kpaŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa nuuwɔɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi du i benii.’ ”

ref: This is a message from the Lord: His eyes are on everyone, especially the tribes of Israel. So he pronounces judgment against the cities of Hadrach and Damascus.
text: Wia la n lii Kɔraawiizi be di ra ba á wa huuzi Hadrak hɛri ni bolzeŋ Damaskusii keŋ. Newea ni Izrɛl dizi maa dɛlli Kɔraawiizii.

ref: Judgment will also fall on the nearby city of Hamath, as well as on Tyre and Sidon, whose people are clever.
text: Haali Hamaf ni Hadrak n du magbɔɔ gba, Taaya ni Saidɔn hina, n dɔɔ nunzuma werge gba dɛlluubuu.

ref: Tyre has built a fortress and piled up silver and gold, as though they were dust or mud from the streets.
text: Taaya hina ma diikpegaa tɛɛ bahinaa, di chaali saliŋhuŋŋa ni saliŋ lugɔ kpaga, di su ba bola maa.

ref: Now the Lord will punish Tyre with poverty; he will sink its ships and send it up in flames.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ paagi u kundɔɔlaa maa, di chɔgi u muuzeŋ gbessi la n gillɛ u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la maa. Ninne niŋ fuuh u maa kpɛlɛŋ.

ref: Both Ashkelon and Gaza will tremble with fear; Ekron will lose all hope. Gaza's king will be killed, and Ashkelon emptied of its people.
text: Bolzeŋ Askɛlɔn hina daŋ na guŋ, ɔnsii lau baa, bolzeŋ Gaza hina ra miŋŋi, dikuu ba biine n chɔkkɛ wia. Bolzeŋ Ɛkrɔn hina gba tamii daŋ tuŋ, bá lɔgɔ lii baa. Gaza hina daŋ nyaa ba koori, Askɛlɔn hina maa chɔ.

ref: A mob of half-breeds will settle in Ashdod, and the Lord himself will rob Philistia of pride.
text: Hɔɔhraa niŋ wa foozi Asdɔd di so. N daŋ chɔgi Filisti hina jigsi la maa baŋ dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: No longer will the Philistines eat meat with blood in it or any unclean food. They will become part of the people of our God from the tribe of Judah. And God will accept the people of Ekron, as he did the Jebusites.
text: Ba wàá ka ra hee ola la n dɔɔ chal gɛɛ di ra di diukiilaa. Banla maa n kawɛɛ daŋ ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi hora, di ɛɛ sitɔɔra Juda biini. Ɛkrɔn hina daŋ birgi n nɛra lugɔ Jɛbus hina.

ref: God says, “I will stand guard to protect my temple from those who come to attack. I know what's happening, and no one will mistreat my people ever again.” The Lord Tells about the Coming King
text: N daŋ guu n Dia, dikuu laallɔɔra n na ba bá wa lɔu laal wia. Màá ka gil biinikpola hiŋ maa wa dɔɔ n nɛra di ra sunni baa. Filaŋkennaa waa, n na du ba taurɛ. Kɛrɛbɛl koori wia

ref: Everyone in Jerusalem, celebrate and shout! Your king has won a victory, and he is coming to you. He is humble and rides on a donkey; he comes on the colt of a donkey.
text: Bolzeŋ Ziɔn hina, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia werge! Jɛrusalɛm hina, ií ra chaasi ni bɔsɔna! Ií binni na, ii koori ra ba ii benii. U wia deŋloore, ú wer lɛɛ ia. U ɛɛ sisɔna hinnɛ, di tinni kawee ra ba, kaupɔl bɛllɛ u tinni di ra ba.

ref: I, the Lord, will take away war chariots and horses from Israel and Jerusalem. Bows that were made for battle will be broken. I will bring peace to nations, and your king will rule from sea to sea. His kingdom will reach from the Euphrates River across the earth. The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ lizi laal torkozi lii Izrɛl, di lizi laal zagra la lii Jɛrusalɛm. Ba daŋ kuugi laal hozi la. Ii koori daŋ sii bampirsɔna wia tɛɛ durnya hɛssi hina. U kora daŋ chi muuzeŋ bɛl di ga hel bɛlhiŋ, di lii Muu Yufretis di ga hel hɛri tunazi.”

ref: When I made a sacred agreement with you, my people, we sealed it with blood. Now some of you are captives in waterless pits, but I will come to your rescue
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Ka iawaa, dikuu nuukpaŋ la n ni ia n kpa mbusu lizaa sela chal ɛɛ la wia, n daŋ lizi ii nɛra lii hɛrduma nɛra tɔi dia biini.

ref: I will use Judah as my bow and Israel as my arrow. I will take the people of Zion as my sword and attack the Greeks. The Lord Will Protect His People
text: N daŋ kpa Juda birgi lugɔ laallɔɔri hoo, di kpa Izrɛl birgi lugɔ u hobee. N daŋ kpa Bolzeŋ Ziɔn baala birgi lugɔ tokobizi, di yoo Giris baala.”

ref: Like a cloud, the Lord God will appear over his people, and his arrows will flash like lightning. God will sound his trumpet and attack in a whirlwind from the south.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ izi di guali u nɛra ni, ú hobii ra nyɛgzi alugɔ nazaa. Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la daŋ huuh u bensunoniina, wiifurii nodig wiikakag dooŋ ni pekpeg biinii ú ga ba.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful will protect his people, and they will trample down the sharpshooters and their slingshots. They will drink and get rowdy; they will be as full as a bowl at the time of sacrifice.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ guu baa. Ba daŋ kpu ba dɔma. Ba danna chaasi laal biini lugɔ baŋ nyɔɔ siŋ di ra dɛɛzi la. Ba daŋ kpu ba dɔma, bá challi ra pal lugɔ baŋ kpu sela lizi mbusu, di fug a chal lii tassa biini waari mbusu lizibɔr ni la.

ref: The Lord God will save them on that day, because they are his people, and they will shine on his land like jewels in a crown.
text: Di a hɔpizii wa hello, Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ u nɛra, gunla penɔɔni n ɔɔ lɛɛ u peeza la. Ba danna nyɛgzi u hɛri biini alugɔ koorikahuro binanaa la yoola n kpolle la.

ref: How lovely they will be. Young people will grow there like grain in a field or grapes in a vineyard.
text: A hɛri daŋ du wer di dɔɔ kɛlli. U mia ni siŋ daŋ gil u suŋgure ni biipɔllaa hel nɛnnɛ.

ref: I, the Lord, am the one who sends storm clouds and showers of rain to make fields produce. So when the crops need rain, you should pray to me.
text: Ií suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú tɛɛ ia dooŋ, dooŋ balaa saŋa. Waabuu gillɛ dooŋ a tiŋ, di ba ra tɛɛ nɛra, di gil kooni kuna biri, di ra hel nɛnnɛ.

ref: You can't believe idols and fortunetellers, or depend on the hope you receive from witchcraft and interpreters of dreams. But you have tried all of these, and now you are like sheep without a shepherd.
text: Karaa vuga ra kanni, vugra ra na kara wipillaa, di ra bagli deeza la n ɛɛ kara zɛɛzi. Ba nɛra bampirtigaa waa tɔna dɔɔwɛ. Awia, a nɛra ra gaaguu lugɔ peeza n leuwe, ba ra fir baa alugɔ peeza la n waa nɔɔni dɔɔwɛ.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am fiercely angry with you leaders, and I will punish you. I care for my people, the nation of Judah, and I will change this flock of sheep into charging war horses.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “N baaŋ fuuhwoo penɔɔna la ni, n daŋ tɛrgi a guŋ sitɔɔra la digna. Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ binni Juda domee la n ɛɛwɛ lugɔ peeza la ni, di gil bá ɛɛ lugɔ laal biini zagkpega.

ref: From this flock will come leaders who will be strong like cornerstones and tent pegs and weapons of war.
text: Juda dee biinii bii la n na faari dia zɛɛ la lii, ba biinii tanti daasirii lii, ba biinii laal hoo lii, ba biinii sitɔɔri maa lii.

ref: They will join in the fighting, and together they will trample their enemies like mud. They will fight, because I, the Lord, will be on their side. And they will crush the enemy cavalry.
text: Ba maa daŋ kpau ɛɛ lugɔ laal biini nɛkpega, di ra fɛrgi bol biini ŋmɛnizenaa la n dɔɔ kpɛchɛgaa la. Dikuu Kɔraawiizi n du ba be wia, ba daŋ lɔ ba dɔma di kpegli banla n tinni zagra la.

ref: I will strengthen the kingdoms of Judah and Israel. And I will show mercy because I am the Lord, their God. I will answer their prayers and bring them home. Then it will seem as though I had never rejected them.
text: N daŋ gil Juda hina du kpeg, di lɛɛ Joosɛf diahina. N daŋ gil ba kaa du ba dubinii la, dikuu miŋ na ba sinyɛna wia. Ba daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ miŋ faa waa baa vɛɛwɛ ta, dikuubɛɛwiai, minuu Kɔraawiizi la banna hum. N daŋ nuu ba wiisuŋŋaa.

ref: Israel will be like a tribe of warriors celebrating with wine. When their children see this, they will also be happy because of me, the Lord.
text: Izrɛl hina daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ fɔŋŋazeŋ hina, ba bɔra daŋ sɔɔni baa alugɔ baŋ nyɔɔ siŋ la. Ba biizi daŋ na guŋ ba bɔra sɔɔni, bá dɔɔ bampirsɔna dikuu Kɔraawiizi wia.

ref: I will give a signal for them to come together because I have rescued them. And there will be as many as ever before.
text: N daŋ yir baa, di chaali baa. Wibii maa, n daŋ lɛɛ baa, bá bir du kpil gunla baŋ faa duwɛɛ la.

ref: Although I scattered my people in distant countries, they won't forget me. Once their children are raised, they will return—
text: Haali miŋ gillɛ ba yaari hɛssi biine gba, ka ba danna liizi n wia a hɛhjaŋa biine. Ba ni ba biizi daŋ piri, di bir ba.

ref: I will bring them home from Egypt and Assyria, then let them settle as far as Gilead and Lebanon, until the land overflows with them.
text: N daŋ bir ba ba ni, di lii Ijip hɛri, di chaali baa lii Asiiria hɛri, di ba ba ni Giliad ni Lɛbanɔn hɛssi biine, ka bɔr waa du de, di hel baa.

ref: My people will go through an ocean of troubles, but I will overcome the waves and dry up the deepest part of the Nile. Assyria's great pride will be put down, and the power of Egypt will disappear.
text: Tɔɔrɔɔzeŋ daŋ huuzi baa alugɔ muuzeŋ nii n ɔɔ ra lɔ werge la, ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil a nii sɔɔni. N daŋ gil Muu Naal nii maa hiihzi. Asiiria hina ge jigsi ni Ijip hina fɔŋŋa la maa tuŋ.

ref: I'll strengthen my people because of who I am, and they will follow me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
text: N daŋ tɛɛ n nɛra fɔŋŋa, ba danna jaamiŋ, di nuu ra tɛŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: Lebanon, open your gates! Let the fire come in to destroy your cedar trees.
text: Lɛbanɔn hina, ií pilli ii dominuuzi, niŋ zuu di ii hɛriŋkpol daazi maa!

ref: Cry, you cypress trees! The glorious cedars have fallen and are rotting. Cry, you oak trees of Bashan! The dense forest has been chopped down.
text: Daananaa, ií ra wii di ra lɔɔgi wile werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, hɛriŋkpol daazi la chogloore, daananaa la maa chɔkkɔɔ. Daazenaa la n du Basan, ií ra wii di ra chɛɛhgi werge, dikuubɛɛwiai, kɔrzeŋ la daazi maanii ba ŋmɛnni ha.

ref: Listen! Shepherds are crying. Their glorious pastures have been ruined. Listen! Lions are roaring. The forests of the Jordan Valley are no more to be found. Worthless Shepherds
text: Ií ra nuu penɔɔna n na chɛɛhgi, dikuu ba sela diiribɔra la n wesse la maa n chɔkkɛ wia. Ií ra nuu bunyinzi n na wii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a chɔɔribɔr la n ɛɛ kɔr di du Jɔɔdan muu kɛrii la chɔkkɔɔ. Penɔɔna banɛɛ wia

ref: The Lord my God said to me: Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter!
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi la miŋ Zɛkaria n na hum la ŋɔ n be, “Ií ra dɛɛzi peeza la ban niŋ kpuuzi la nɛnnɛ.

ref: The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
text: Banla n yauzaa la ɔɔ kɔrgaabuu ka ba waa baa ra ɛɛ wiimaa. Banla n ɔɔ yooa la ra ŋɔ, ‘Ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi, yaa birgi daama hinaa!’ A nɔɔna himmaa wàá ra gil.

ref: Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
text: Guŋ himmaanii n ge gba wàá ka na nɛra la n du a hɛri la sinyɛna. N daŋ kpa bɛl maa du u dɔŋhiŋ ni u koori nonee biini, bá ra fir baa ka màá lɛɛ baa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.”
text: Awia, miŋ Zɛkaria ra dɛɛzi peeza la ban niŋ kpu la nɛnnɛ, fɔŋfɔŋ anla banna sunni. Denii n kpa daŋkpalli anɛɛ di ra yir bɛl Nisunaa, di kaa ra yir bɛl ge Nuukpaŋ, di ra nɔɔni a peeza.

ref: In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them.
text: Baagu kpaŋ biini, di n teŋ duŋŋi penɔɔna bahoro. N faa waa kaa wer dɔɔ kanyitti ni a peyaura. Ba ge n hahŋ wia,

ref: Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
text: n ŋɔ, “Màá ka ɛɛ ii nɔɔni. Anla n niŋ siuzi, á siuzi. Anla n niŋ ta, á ta. Anla n kawɛɛ la ge ra hee dɔŋa.”

ref: On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people.
text: Denii n kpa daŋkpala la minna yir Nisunaa la di kuuguu, di chɔgi Kɔraawiizi ni nɛra nuukpaŋ la baŋ ɛɛwɛ la.

ref: The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord.
text: A hɔl hinnɛ n chɔgi a nuukpaŋ, sela la n na di tɔɔrɔɔ la na guŋ, di zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔzii.

ref: I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ n be, “Kpaa du Kɔraawiizi Dia kebee dauribɔr la.” Denii n kpa a saliŋhuŋŋa kebisau tokko ni kpɔrgɔ la baŋ ŋɔ a kannɔɔ la, di du Kɔraawiizi Dia kebee dauribɔr la.

ref: Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
text: Denii n kuugi daŋkpala la minna yir Nuukpaŋ la ge, di ra chɔgi Juda ni Izrɛl hina nuukpaŋ la.

ref: Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ n be, “Kaa ra ɛɛ lugɔ penɔɔni la n gɛnnɛ.

ref: Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, n daŋ lizi penɔɔni la n waa sela tau ra du tɛɛ a hɛri hina. U baga wàá du peleulaa ni gɛɛ wàá ra du a bizi tau gɛɛ di ra chaa anla n na wii la gɛɛ di ra dɛɛzi anla n kpekke, ka sela la n wesse werge la olaa ú ra hee. U daŋ ɔɔ foŋzi a naafiraa.

ref: You worthless shepherd, deserting the sheep! I hope a sword will cripple your arm and blind your right eye.
text: Wia daŋ huuzi penɔɔnijaga la n chɔwɛɛ ka ka u peeza! Ba daŋ kpa tokobi ŋmɛŋ u nonii ni u nodig siwii! U nonii daŋ siu, ú nodig siwii tɔ kɔrai.”

ref: This is a message from the Lord about Israel: I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans.
text: Wia la n lii Kɔraawiizi be di ra bagli Izrɛl wiarɛ keŋ. Kɔraawiizi la n ta chiŋ di yaau, di ta hɛri, di tɛɛ newee miibɔɔ la, ra ŋɔu,

ref: I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked.
text: “N daŋ gil Jɛrusalɛm ɛɛ lugɔ siŋ n du libee biini, hɛssi hina la maa n baruu la nyɔɔ dɛɛzi, di ra jiŋli. Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm maanii bá fɔɔ.

ref: But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it. When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem,
text: A hɔl la hɛssi hina la maa n niŋ pig Jɛrusalɛm la, n daŋ gil u ɛɛ lugɔ bizeŋ la baŋ wàá wer ziigi. Banla n niŋ ŋɔ ba kpau daŋ na pira.

ref: I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ gil ɔnsii zuu ba zagra, di gil a tinna ra chugli. N danna du Juda hina tau nɛnnɛ, ka n daŋ gil ba dɔma zagra maa nyuŋŋi. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
text: Denii Juda hina sitɔɔra la ŋɔ ba biine, ‘Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ La ra tɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm hinaa fɔŋŋa.’

ref: At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ gil Juda sitɔɔra birgi lugɔ niŋ n na di kɔr gɛɛ lugɔ niŋ n na di sɔgmia n hillɛ chi koo. Ba daŋ kpu hɛssi hina la maa n bar baa la, ka Jɛrusalɛm hinawaa, wiimaa wàá ɛɛ baa.

ref: But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself.
text: N daŋ feli mɔgli Juda laallɔɔra, guŋ gil Koori Deevid diahina ni Jɛrusalɛm hina girme wàá kaali Juda hina girme.

ref: I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ guu Jɛrusalɛm hina, bá gɛrgi fɔŋŋa ɛɛ lugɔ Koori Deevid fɔŋŋa, Koori Deevid diahina ɛɛ lugɔ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi di tɔ ba see lugɔ n mɛlika.

ref: I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem. Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ izi di chɔg hɛssi la maa hina n niŋ pig Jɛrusalɛm hina. Wiraa tɛɛ nɛr la baŋ yag kandaa wia

ref: I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born.
text: N daŋ gil Koori Deevid diahina ni Jɛrusalɛm hina dɔɔ nɛsunaa ni wiisuŋŋaa duma. Ba daŋ binni mìŋ́ unla baŋ yag kandaa, bá biine chɔgi werge maa, bá ra wii dikuu n wia alugɔ nɛr n ɔɔ ra wii u biikpaŋ wia la. Ba biine daŋ chɔgi werge alugɔ mɛɛ ni maa n ɔɔ ra wii dikuu ba biibambilugli n siuwɛ wia.

ref: On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, chɛɛhgaa werge maa daŋ su Jɛrusalɛm biini, gunla banna wii Hadad Rimɔn, bolzeŋ Mɛgidɔ lɛl biini la.

ref: Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan,
text: A hɛri hina biine daŋ chɔgi werge, domee maa ra wii. Baala ni haana ra wii ba bɛnaa. Koori Deevid domee ni ba haana, Netan domee ni ba haana,

ref: and all other families as well.
text: ani domeezi la n kawɛɛ la ni ba haana.”

ref: In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “A hɔl hiŋ, bulli danna bul nii, di tɛɛ Koori Deevid diahina ni bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm zuura kpaa, di lizi ba wichɔgaa ni ba doŋa maa ta.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says: When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, n daŋ chɔgi vuga maa a hɛri, a sɔna dim, ba wàá ka liizi a wia. N daŋ lizi dɔgtɛɛkara hina ni dumchɔgii maa lii a hɛri. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
text: Di dɔgtɛɛkara hiŋ maa haŋ wa ŋɔ u wiŋɔɔlaa lii Kɔraawiizi benii, u maa ni u mɛɛ la n luluu la daŋ ŋɔ u be, ‘A dɛkkɔɔ ba kpui, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi be lɛi a lii.’ U maa ni u mɛɛ daŋ tɔɔuh kpu, di u kaa waa ŋɔ wia di ŋɔ a lii Kɔraawiizi benii.

ref: Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, hiihzi daŋ lau dɔgtɛɛ maa, dikuu u winaalaa lugɔ deeza biini wia. Wàá laali dɔgtɛɛ laala la n dɔɔ huna di wer dar nɛra.

ref: Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
text: U daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ maa dɔgtɛɛ ɛɛwɛ, n ɛɛ kooluure, hɛrii ɛɛ n bɔdiilii di lii n pɔlaa saŋa maa.

ref: And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.” A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
text: Di nɛr pɛɛzuu u bɔra pirazi wia, u daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u dammuzi diinii u naa.” Penɔɔni kpui ni peeza yaaraa wia

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said: My sword, wake up! Attack my shepherd and friend. Strike down the shepherd! Scatter the little sheep, and I will destroy them.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ daŋ ŋɔ, “Tokobi, izi lɔ penɔɔni la n na humiŋ la. N daŋ lɔ penɔɔni la, ú peeza maa yaari, ń chɔgi a biizi.”

ref: Nowhere in the land will more than a third of them be left alive.
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ, “Hɛri naa maa biini, di ba bargi u nɛra bɔra ahoro, ba daŋ kpu ba bɔra anɛɛ ka ka ba bɔkpaŋ.

ref: Then I will purify them and put them to the test, just as gold and silver are purified and tested. They will pray in my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “You are my people,” and they will reply, “You, Lord, are our God!”
text: N daŋ lizi ba bɔkpaŋ naa doŋa ha, gunla baŋ ɔɔ kpa saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu du niŋ di lizi a doŋa ha la. Ba daŋ yir n sɔŋ, ń nuu di sɛɛ. Di yir baa n nɛra, bá ge yiriŋ Kɔraawiizi la banna hum.”

ref: The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people.
text: Hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di ia seriya la ra bau. Jɛrusalɛm hina, ii dɔma daŋ paagi ii kuna, di bɔnnaa ii sibɔɔ.

ref: But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
text: Kɔraawiizi daŋ chaali hɛssi hina maa bá wa lɔ Jɛrusalɛm. Ba daŋ kpegluu, di pigzi u diini di paagi kuna, di punzi u haana. A bolzeŋ hina keza maanii bá lauri kaali, ka ka ba keza.

ref: The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle.
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi izi di yoo a hɛssi hina gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ laal hɔpizii la.

ref: He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, u daŋ chi Ɔlivizi Bizeŋ nyuu Jɛrusalɛm wiifurii, a bii daŋ peri anɛɛ di chi u wiifurii di la u wiicholii, waluuzeŋ chɔɔ a baaŋ. U yeŋ la wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag u yeŋ ge la wiifurii nodig wiikakag.

ref: Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
text: Ií daŋ ga n bizeŋ waluu di chɔ, dikuu un niŋ du jaŋ di ga hel boljiga Azɛl wia. Ií daŋ chɔ gunla iiŋ faa chɔwɛɛ saŋa la hɛri n ziglee Juda Koori Uzzia kora dii saŋa la. Denii Kɔraawiizi la minna hum la ni mɛlikazi la maa kpau ba.

ref: It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, bɔchaaŋ wàá du de. Waari gɛɛ kɔɔl wàá du de.

ref: And the Lord has decided when it will happen—this time of unending day.
text: A hɔpizii naa daŋ kur. Wàá dɔɔ hɔpizaa gɛɛ hamuŋa. Kɔraawiizi bɛnnɛ zum a hɔpizii. Di bɔr waa biri, ka u daŋ chaani.

ref: In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.
text: A hɔl hiŋ, nii la n dɔɔ miibɔɔ daŋ pal lii Jɛrusalɛm, u yeŋ pal di ra la Muuzensiwii, u yeŋ ge ra la Muuzeŋ Mɛditerenɛn, wem ni waari saŋazi maa.

ref: Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
text: A saŋa Kɔraawiizi daŋ di kora durnya maa ni. A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi kpannɛ niŋ du de, ú bɛŋ sɔŋ ka.

ref: Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out.
text: Wiilchɔgii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ kpa ta hɛssi hina la maa n lɔ Jɛrusalɛm hina laal labuu keŋ. Ba bɔrahɔna danna pɔɔh di ba haa ra nyiŋ. Ba siwee ni ba nuuzuŋŋa maanii niŋ pɔɔh.

ref: The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other,
text: A hɔl hiŋ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ du baala ɔnsii werge maa. Baal maa daŋ lau u dɔŋhiŋ nonii bá lɔ dɔŋa.

ref: Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
text: Durnya hɛssi hina la n niŋ ka di lii banla n lɔ Jɛrusalɛm la, danna ba de di waa jaami Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Koori, di ɛɛ Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la binaa bina maa. Ba daŋ ɔɔ ra di Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ la gba de.

ref: No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Di durnya hɛri bɛl maa hina wa vɛɛwɔ lugɔ bá la Jɛrusalɛm di ga jaami Koorizeŋ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ, ba wàá na dooŋ.

ref: This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
text: Ijip hina ni hɛssi hina la maa n vɛɛwɛ bá la Jɛrusalɛm di ga di a Pampannizi Hɔpizizeŋ naa, digna tɛraarɛ guŋ.

ref: At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
text: Vii la maa n du Jɛrusalɛm ni Juda maa daŋ ɛɛ kunnaniinanii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ. Banla maa n niŋ ba, bá wa lizi mbusu, daŋ kpa a viini aŋhina daali ba mbusu lizaa ola. A hɔl hiŋ, nɛr maa wàá ka ɛɛ kɔkɔɔzi Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ Dia biini.

ref: I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel. The Lord's Love for Israel
text: Kɔraawiizii pilli wia naa bagli Malakai, u ŋɔ tɛɛ Izrɛl hina. Gunla Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋi Izrɛl hina wia

ref: Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob
text: Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N nɔŋŋi iabuu. Ka ii pɛɛzi, ‘I nɔŋŋi yaabuu, wibii maa?’ ” Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ, “Ɛsau faa waa Jekɔb kpɛɛma ɛɛwɛ lɛiyaa? Ka Jekɔb ni u naannaa n nɔŋŋi,

ref: instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam.
text: ka faa hah Ɛsau, di gil u giŋgimee hɛri birgi hɛribɔduma tɛɛ hohobiazi.”

ref: Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.” But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
text: Aŋhinabe, Ɛsau naanna Ɛdɔm hina daŋ ŋɔ, “Haali baŋ puri yaa bola gba, ka yaa daŋ bir maa.” Ka kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Di ba maa, ka n daŋ bir purgaa. Nɛra daŋ yir ba hɛri Biinikpola Hina Hɛri, nɛra la Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n na fuuh ba ni saŋa maa la.

ref: Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.” Judgment against Priests
text: Ii himmaa siwee daŋ na guŋ, ií ŋɔ, ‘Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa, haali hɛssi la hina n dugli Izrɛl hɛri la gba ni.’ ” Kɔraawiizi n hau u kizeehina ni wia

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔ u kizeehina be, “Biibambie dɛkkɔɔ u ra kpa u mɛɛ girme, balii ge ra ɛɛ u dɔɔri guŋ. Di minuu ii mɛɛ, lee girme la n dɛgiŋ la duɛi? Di minuu ii dɔɔri, ɛrɛɛ ɔmaarɛ ii ra ɔminnɛi? Hoi, n kizeehina! Iabuu ra gbɛlli n sɔŋ. Ka ii pɛɛzi, ‘Ɛrɛɛ yaa ra gbɛlli i sɔnɛi?’

ref: You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
text: Ii kpa diwee la n doŋŋe mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi benii, di dau n mbusu lizibɔr la ni. Ii kaa pɛɛzi, ‘Ɛrɛɛ yaa ɛɛ di chugii doŋai?’ Ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la waa girme kuŋ ɛɛwɛ.

ref: But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you.
text: Iiŋ ɔɔ kpa sela la n nyuŋŋɛɛ gɛɛ n gbɛttɛ gɛɛ n na wii, di waa lizi mbusuzi la, lewaa lɛiyaa? Di ii kpaa gaa tɛɛ ii hɛri nabɔma, u bɔra daŋ sɔɔni ii wiaa? U daŋ hiini iaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ra pɛɛzi ia guŋ.

ref: I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
text: Too, di ii suŋŋi mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ ń suŋ ii ni, n daŋ nuuwaa? Di ii kpa keŋ kuna lizi mbusu, n daŋ lɛɛawaa? Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings.
text: Ee, di ii bɛl vii tɔ n Dia dominuuzi, guŋ gil ii gilɛɛ ra chem ninjagazi mbusu lizibɔr ni, a vii bɔ! N bɔra waa sɔɔnɛɛ ii wia. Awia, màá lɛɛ ii mbusu lizaa kuna.

ref: But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
text: Ka ii ra chɔg n sɔŋ, di ra ŋɔ n mbusu lizibɔr wia keŋ, ‘U doŋŋoo.’ Ii ra gbɛlli u diwee ge.

ref: You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these?
text: Ií ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Wibaziire!’ Ii mir nuuzi di ra du u ni. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.” Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Iiŋ ɔɔ kpa sela la n boŋŋee ni anla n gbɛttɛ gɛɛ anla n na wii, di waa lizi mbusuzi la, ń lɛɛawaa?

ref: Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
text: Nɛr la n dɔɔ sebal la n wesse u sela biini, di ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpau tɛŋ, ka bir lizi unla n waa kpeg wa tɛŋ, nuuseezi daŋ diu. N ɛɛ koorizenne, a dɛkkɔɔ hɛssi hina maa ra ɔmiŋ. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.”

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔ tɛɛ kizeehina, “Kizeehina, ii karfaarɛ keŋ.

ref: You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests.
text: Di ii waa haŋ nuu, di ii waa haŋ aah siwii di ra tɔgzi n sɔŋ, n daŋ see ia nua, di see kuna la miŋ kissi ia ii dɔɔ la nua. Ɛɛh, n teŋ seeabuu nua, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa siwii aahwɛ di ra tɔgziŋ.

ref: I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
text: N daŋ kuu ii wia, di tɛr ii naanna digna. N daŋ kpa ii hɔpizizenaa mbusu lizaa sela fihbina faa ii siwee, bá kpa ii ni a maa ha hul nyuu.

ref: I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi.
text: Denii ii zum lugɔ minuu karfi ia wia naa, guŋ gil ń ni Levi dee nuukpaŋ la du de di ra la. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name.
text: Nuukpaŋ la miŋ gillɛ yaa dɔɔ la faa du ba benii. Miibɔɔ ni bɔsɔna nuukpannɛ n kpa tɛɛ baa. Guŋ gil ba ra tɔgziŋ, di ra ɔmiŋ werge.

ref: He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
text: Ba baglaa maa faa ɛɛ wibiire, ba ŋmɛnɛ maa faa waa kara nuuwɛ lii ba nuuzi. N ni baa faa du de ni bampirsɔna, ba wia deŋli. Ba faa bir nɛkpila lii ba wichɔgaa biini.

ref: You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ kizeehina n dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi wia zumaa, nɛra ge ra na baglaa lii ba be, dikuu baŋ ɛɛ mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ balaa wia.

ref: But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi.
text: Ka iawaa gil a ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ ta, ii baglaa ge gil nɛkpila leuzi. Ii chɔgi n ni Levi dee nuukpaŋ labuu.

ref: So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike. A Broken Agreement
text: Awia, n gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina hah ia, di ra du ia hiihzi nɛra maa see, dikuu iiŋ waa n ŋmɛnizi hiŋŋɛ ka nɔŋŋi baŋhina kaali baŋhina, n Gbɔgni hiŋaa wia biini. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.” Juda hina wia n nyaa wibii

ref: Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors?
text: Mɛɛkpaŋ lɛi yaa maa dɔɔa? Kɔraawiizikpaŋ lɛi ma yaa maa? Ka ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ yaa waa kaa ra hiŋzi nuuŋɔɔlaa la yaa n duwɛɛ tɛɛ dɔŋai? Guŋ gillɔɔ yaa naabaala ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ la chɔgi.

ref: You people in Judah and Jerusalem have been unfaithful to the Lord. You have disgraced the temple that he loves, and you have committed the disgusting sin of marrying the worshipers of other gods.
text: Juda hina waa kaa ra hiŋzi ba nuuŋɔɔlaa. Ba ɛɛ wikiiliire Izrɛl hɛri ni bolzeŋ Jɛrusalɛm biini. Juda hina paagi haana la n na kuari hɛrdumazi vugaa, guŋ gil Kɔraawiizi Dia la un nɔŋŋɛɛ la chɔg.

ref: I pray that the Lord will no longer let those who are guilty belong to his people, even if they eagerly decide to offer the Lord a gift.
text: Baal la maa n ɛɛ keŋ, di u du gunla maa, Kɔ́raawiizi lizuu lii Jekɔb nɛra biini, haali di u kpa mbusu lizaa kuna gba di wàá tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ.

ref: And what else are you doing? You cry noisily and flood the Lord's altar with your tears, because he isn't pleased with your offerings and refuses to accept them.
text: Wii la bɛl iiŋ kaa ra ɛɛu keŋ, ii kpa siniire taali mbusu lizibɔr la ni. Ii ra wiiu di ra chɛɛhgi, dikuu uŋ waa kaa kɛɛ di ra binni ii mbusu lizaa kuna gɛɛ di ra lɛɛa ni bɔsɔna di lii ii be wia.

ref: And why isn't God pleased? It's because he knows that each of you men has been unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young. You promised that she would be your partner, but now you have broken that promise.
text: Ii ɔɔ pɛɛzi, “Ɛrɛɛ?” Guŋ ɛɛwɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ra di ii ni ii bichalhaanaa daansɛɛ, dikuu ii chɔgi ii ni baa nuuŋɔɔlaa labuu, haali baŋ ɛɛ ii cheena, haana la ii ni baa n ŋɔ nuuzi ka kpa dɔŋa la.

ref: Didn't God create you and your wife to become like one person? And why did he do this? It was so you would have children, and then lead them to become God's people. Don't ever be unfaithful to your wife.
text: Kɔraawiizi lɛi gillɛ baal ni u haaŋ ɛɛ kpaŋaa? U gillɔɔ ba bɔrahɔna ni ba dunzi ɛɛ kpaŋ. Bɛɛ wiarɛ u ɛɛ gunnɛi? Dikuu unna nyiŋŋi ii biizi ra hiŋuu wia. Awia, ii ra du iihinaa tau wiimaa biini, di gilɛɛ waa chɔgi nuuŋɔɔlaa la ii ni ii bichalhaana n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ dɔŋa la.

ref: You have worn out the Lord with your words. And yet, you ask, “How did we do that?” You did it by saying, “The Lord is pleased with evil and doesn't care about justice.”
text: Ii wiŋɔzi bazi Kɔraawiizii. Ii pɛɛzɔɔrɛ, “Ɛrɛɛ yaa ŋɔ a bazuuwei?” Kenne ii ŋɔ, “Banla maa n ɛɛ wichɔgaa wia wessoo Kɔraawiizi be, ba wia paruu,” di kaa ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi la n na di seriya ni wibii la haa du denii naa?”

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send my messenger to prepare the way for me. Then suddenly the Lord you are looking for will appear in his temple. The messenger you desire is coming with my promise, and he is on his way. A Day of Change
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ií ra nuu! N daŋ hum n huŋhunni bɛl n niŋ tɔ see, di wa ɛɛ sirya ń na ba. Denii kakpaŋ, ii Dɔɔri la iinna binni u ŋmɛnɛɛ la ba u Dia, nuukpaŋ balii la wia n na par ia la daŋ ba.”

ref: On the day the Lord comes, he will be like a furnace that purifies silver or like strong soap in a washbasin. No one will be able to stand up to him.
text: Ka anɛɛ n niŋ wer chi u see u balaa hɔpizii naanɛi? Anɛɛ n niŋ wer na u hiŋ a saŋai? U daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ zugzi niŋ gɛɛ chagri fanfanni.

ref: The Lord will purify the descendants of Levi, as though they were gold or silver. Then they will bring the proper offerings to the Lord,
text: U daŋ so lugɔ nɛr la n ɔɔ ŋmɛɛri saliŋhuŋŋu di lizi a doŋa ra ha. Gunnɛ ú lizi Levi dee doŋa ha, ka kuari baa lugɔ saliŋ ni saliŋhuŋŋu. Denii Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ nɛra la wia n deŋlee, ba waa lizi mbusuzi kuna di ra tɛu,

ref: and the offerings of the people of Judah and Jerusalem will please him, just as they did in the past. Don't Cheat God
text: Kɔraawiizi jaa sɛɛ di lɛɛ Juda ni Jɛrusalɛm hina mbusuzi lizaa kuna gunla uŋ faa ra lɛɛa faala la.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said: I'm now on my way to judge you. And I will quickly condemn all who practice witchcraft or cheat in marriage or tell lies in court or rob workers of their pay or mistreat widows and orphans or steal the property of foreigners or refuse to respect me.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Awia, n daŋ ba ii be di wa di ia seriya. N daŋ ɛɛ manaŋ di wa di banla n na di hiri, banla n na sɛm, banla n na di daansɛɛkara, banla n na fini ba paahdiire, banla n na sunni luhaana ni lalbiizi ani banla n waa hɔɔhra ra di seriya ni wibii, dikuu baŋ wanna ɔm wia.” Kɔraawiizi finaa wia

ref: Descendants of Jacob, I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I never change. That's why you haven't been wiped out,
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi waa birgaa dɔɔwɛ. Awia, Jekɔb naanna, maa ia ra dim.

ref: even though you have ignored and disobeyed my laws ever since the time of your ancestors. But if you return to me, I will return to you. And yet you ask, “How can we return?”
text: Di haŋ chi ii naabaala ge naabaala saŋa la maa, ii vɛɛ n widaulaarɛ. Ií bir ba n be, ń ge bir ba ii be di lɛɛ ia. Ka ii pɛɛzi, ‘Ɛrɛɛ ya ɛɛ di bir ba i benei?’

ref: You people are robbing me, your God. And, here you are, asking, “How are we robbing you?” You are robbing me of the offerings and of the ten percent that belongs to me.
text: ‘A wesso newee n na fini mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizia? Ka gunnɛ ii ra ɛɛŋ la.’ Ka ii pɛɛzi, ‘Ɛrɛɛ yaa ra finiinei?’ Ií ra finimbuu dikuu iiŋ wanna tɛɛ ii kuna fifi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa ni sunzaazi la iin niŋ tɛŋ wia.

ref: That's why your whole nation is under a curse.
text: Ii hɛri hina naa maanii n see nua, dikuu iinna finiŋ wia.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I challenge you to put me to the test. Bring the entire ten percent into the storehouse, so there will be food in my house. Then I will open the windows of heaven and flood you with blessing after blessing.
text: Ií kpa ii kuna fifi bɔkpaŋkpaŋa maa ba n Dia kuna dauribɔr, gúŋ gil diwee du de. Ií ɛɛŋ guŋ na, n daŋ kissi ia, ii na kuna werge maa. Ii wàá wer dɔɔ diini ii dawaa.

ref: I will also stop locusts from destroying your crops and keeping your vineyards from producing.
text: N daŋ gil purmaazi gilɛɛ waa di ii pattikuna, ii grepu daazi ge nɔŋ nɛnnɛ.

ref: Everyone of every nation will talk about how I have blessed you and about your wonderful land. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
text: Denii hɛssi hina maa yir ia bɔsɔna hina, dikuu ii hɛri n niŋ du sum werge wia.

ref: You have said horrible things about me, and yet you ask, “What have we said?”
text: Ií chagzimbuu. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizii ŋɔ guŋ. Ka ii pɛɛzi, ‘Ɛrɛɛ yaa chagziinɛi?’

ref: Here is what you have said: “It's foolish to serve the Lord God All-Powerful. What do we get for obeying God and from going around looking sad?
text: Ii ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Yaa hummɔɔ ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ka a ɛɛ pɛɛ. Beedee tɔnaa yaa na lii u widaulaa hiŋaa biini, ka ra bar lugɔ nɛra la n na wii Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ seei?

ref: See how happy those arrogant people are. Everyone who does wrong is successful, and when they put God to the test, they always get away with it.” Faithfulness Is Rewarded
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, yaa ra yir barabara hinaa bɔsɔna hina. Aahna lɛi lugɔ wichɔgɛɛra ɔɔ ra nyɛɛluu. Banla ge n na karsi Kɔraawiizi ra lii wia biini.’ ”

ref: All those who truly respected the Lord and honored his name started discussing these things, and when God saw what was happening, he had their names written as a reminder in his book.
text: Ka banla n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi la ŋɔ wiarɛ di ra tɛɛ dɔŋa, Kɔraawiizi keŋŋi digna di ra nuu. Ba sɛbi banla n na ɔm Kɔraawiizi di ra tɔgzuu la sɔnaa du hɔŋ biini Kɔraawiizi see, bá ra liizi ba wia.

ref: Then the Lord All-Powerful said: You people are precious to me, and when I come to bring justice, I will protect you, just as parents protect an obedient child.
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ba daŋ ɛɛ n hora hɔpizii la min niŋ chaali n nɛra la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ werge maa la. N daŋ na ba sinyɛna di lɛɛ baa, gunla baal n ɔɔ na u bie la n na humuu sinyɛna, di lɛɛu la.

ref: Then everyone will once again see the difference between those who obey me by doing right and those who reject me by doing wrong.
text: Denii ii na gunla Kɔraawiizi n na ɛɛ nɛra la wia n deŋlee, a kur gunla unna ɛɛ biinikpola hina wia la. Banla n na hum Kɔraawiizi ni banla n wɔɔ ra hum wia wàá ɛɛ kpaŋ.”

ref: The day of judgment is certain to come. And it will be like a red-hot furnace with flames that burn up proud and sinful people, as though they were straw. Not a branch or a root will be left. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
text: Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hiŋ la ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Wibii maa, Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la ra bau. U danna haahri alugɔ ninzeŋ. Barabara hina ni wichɔgɛɛra maa daŋ ɛɛ lugɔ kɔlaa. A hɔl hiŋ ba daŋ du baa niŋ, ba yemmaa wàá ka ka.

ref: But for you that honor my name, victory will shine like the sun with healing in its rays, and you will jump around like calves at play.
text: Ka ii banla n na tɔgzi n sɔŋ lawaa, wideŋlaa daŋ lii ii be di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa alugɔ wiizi n futtɛ di ta naazi la n na chaa nɛra. Ii daŋ lii di zaahzi ra chiiri alugɔ baŋ ɔɔ pilli nabizi a lii lig biini, di zaahzi ra chiiri jorob jorob la.

ref: When I come to bring justice, you will trample those who are evil, as though they were ashes under your feet. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
text: Denii ii fɛrgi biinikpola hina dau, ba ɛɛ lugɔ hɔɔhri ii naapaala biine, hɔpizii la min niŋ ɛɛ a wia naa. Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Fɔŋŋa Maa Hinnɛ ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: Don't ever forget the laws and teachings I gave my servant Moses on Mount Sinai.
text: Ií ra liizi n balii Moosis Gbɔgni ni widaulaa la miŋ kpawɛɛ tɛu Bizeŋ Sinaai nyuu, ú tɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa la.

ref: I, the Lord, promise to send the prophet Elijah before that great and terrible day comes.
text: Ií ra nuu! N daŋ hum n dɔgtɛɛ Ɛlija ii be mɔɔ, ka mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizizeŋ la wia n dɔɔ ɔnsii werge la ba.

ref: He will lead children and parents to love each other more, so that when I come, I won't bring destruction to the land.
text: U daŋ bir mɛɛwaa bampiree du ba biizi ni, biizi ge hora bir du ba mɛɛwaa ni. Di guŋ lɛi, n daŋ see a hɛri nua, ú chɔgi.”

ref: “A virgin will have a baby boy, and he will be called Immanuel,” which means “God is with us.”
text: “Toloori bɛl n waa baal zummɛ daŋ kpogli hia di lul biibaal, bá ra yiruu Imanuɛl.” U sɔŋ hiŋ zɛɛrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi du yaa benii.”

ref: From David to the time of the exile in Babylonia, the ancestors of Jesus were: David, Solomon , Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram; Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, Josiah, and Jehoiachin and his brothers.
text: Jɔsia ge biibaalaa Jɛkɔnia ni u niuna. A saŋa, di Jus hina dɔma lauri baa kaali Babilɔn hɛri.

ref: From the exile to the birth of Jesus, his ancestors were: Jehoiachin, Shealtiel, Zerubbabel, Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Zadok, Achim; Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan, Jacob, and Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus, who is called the Messiah.
text: Jekɔb ge lul Joosɛf. Joosɛf naa faa ɛɛ Mɛɛri la jaarii. Mɛɛri ge lul Yeesu, ba kaa ra yiruu Kristo.

ref: more to the birth of the Messiah. The Birth of Jesus (Luke
text: Azɔ ge biibaallɛ Zadɔk. Zadɔk ge biibaallɛ Akim. Akim ge biibaallɛ Ilayud.

ref: This is how Jesus Christ was born. A young woman named Mary was engaged to Joseph from King David's family. But before they were married, she learned that she was going to have a baby by God's Holy Spirit.
text: Yeesu Kristo lulaa wiarɛ keŋ. Joosɛf faa kpa Yeesu maa Mɛɛrii. U faa haa waa u dia zuuwɛ ú nuu chɔɔ, ka u kpogli hia Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini.

ref: Joseph was a good man and did not want to embarrass Mary in front of everyone. So he decided to quietly call off the wedding.
text: U jaari la ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ. Awia, uŋ wa zummɛ lugɔ u kpogli hiarɛ la, u faa waa nyiŋŋi u duu hiihzi, ka ŋɔ ú vii suahzi vɛɛu.

ref: While Joseph was thinking about this, an angel from the Lord appeared to him in a dream. The angel said, “Joseph, the baby that Mary will have is from the Holy Spirit. Go ahead and marry her.
text: Joosɛf n faa ra fɛ guŋ nfɛrɛ la, di Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl ba u be, u nau deeza biini. A mɛlika ŋɔ, “Deevid naana Joosɛf, gilɛɛ ra ɔm Mɛɛri kpai, dikuubɛɛwiai, hia la uŋ kpoglee la, Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biinii u kpogluu.

ref: Then after her baby is born, name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
text: U daŋ lul biibaal. Di u wa luluu, í dawuu Yeesu, dikuubɛɛwiai, waabuu niŋ wa lɛɛ u nɛra lii ba wichɔgaa biini.”

ref: So the Lord's promise came true, just as the prophet had said,
text: Wia naa maa ɛɛwɔɔ ka wia la Kɔraawiizi n faa gillɛ u dɔgtɛɛ sɛbi dau la wer ɛɛ wibii. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,

ref: After Joseph woke up, he and Mary were soon married, just as the Lord's angel had told him to do.
text: Denii Joosɛf n wa izi dɔɔ la, u la ga kpa Mɛɛri gunla Kɔraawiizi mɛlika la n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: But they did not sleep together before her baby was born. Then Joseph named him Jesus.
text: Ka u ni u haaŋ hiŋ waa chɔɔwɛ mɔɔ ka u wa lul. Biibaallɛ u lul. Joosɛf dau u sɔŋ Yeesu.

ref: When Jesus was born in the village of Bethlehem in Judea, Herod was king. During this time some wise men from the east came to Jerusalem
text: Uŋ lul Yeesu la, Bɛtlihɛm n du Juda hɛri labuu u luluu. Baal la n faa ɛɛ koori a saŋa hiŋ sɔnnɛ faa Hɛrɔd. Denii nunzunna baŋhina lii wiifurii hɛri bɛl di ba Jɛrusalɛm di waa pɛɛzi nɛra,

ref: and said, “Where is the child born to be king of the Jews? We saw his star in the east and have come to worship him.”
text: “Ba lul bie la n niŋ ɛɛ Jus hina koori labuu. Lee u duɛi? U chinchiŋwilii lii yaa hɛrii yaa nau, di ba ya wa jaamuu.”

ref: When King Herod heard about this, he was worried, and so was everyone else in Jerusalem.
text: Koori Hɛrɔd n wa nuu guŋ, a tir u ni Jɛrusalɛm hina maa.

ref: Herod brought together the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses and asked them, “Where will the Messiah be born?”
text: U chaali Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Kɔraawiizi Hɔnzunna la maa, di pɛɛzi baa bɔr la ban niŋ faa lul Kristo la Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ ŋmɛnɛ ba la.

ref: They told him, “He will be born in Bethlehem, just as the prophet wrote,
text: Ba ŋɔ, “Bɛtlihɛm n du Juda hɛrii bá luluu. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ faa sɛbi gunnɛ dau, di ŋɔ,

ref: ‘Bethlehem in the land of Judea, you are very important among the towns of Judea. From your town will come a leader, who will be like a shepherd for my people Israel.’ ”
text: ‘Juda hɛri bola maa boljiga Bɛtlihɛm, i dɔɔ sɔnnɛ Juda hɛri nabɔnzi be, dikuubɛɛwiai, i binii ń lizi nabɔma bɛl n niŋ waa binni n nɛra Izrɛl hina ni la wa lii.’ ”

text: Saŋa la yaa naabaala n faa du hɛribɔduma la, Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Moosis la faa kpa lugbiirɛ di luu hɛrikuŋ, di kpau du daa ni, di lawuu lalli chiŋ. Gunnɛ bá wa lalli Mìŋ́ Newee Biibaal ge chiŋ.

ref: Then everyone who has faith in the Son of Man will have eternal life.
text: Di ba wa lalliŋ guŋ, nɛr la maa n niŋ yardiŋ, a hiŋ daŋ na Kɔraawiizi miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: God loved the people of this world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who has faith in him will have eternal life and never really die.
text: Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi durnyaa werge maa. Awiarɛ u gil mìŋ́ u Biikpaŋkpaŋ ba. U ɛɛ gunnɛ, di hinla maa sɛɛ n wia di yardiŋ, í gilɛɛ siu, ka í na Kɔraawiizi miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: God did not send his Son into the world to condemn its people. He sent him to save them!
text: Kɔraawiizi n humiŋ durnya naa biini, u faa waŋ hummɛ dikuu unna nyiŋŋi u di ia seriya, ii chol wia. U humimbuu ń ba di wa wer na ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ ia, ka u wer lɛɛ ia.

ref: No one who has faith in God's Son will be condemned. But everyone who doesn't have faith in him has already been condemned for not having faith in God's only Son.
text: Nɛr la maa n niŋ sɛɛ Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la wia, Kɔraawiizi wàá ka di a hiŋ seriya u chol. Ka nɛr la maa n wàá sɛɛ tɛŋ, Kɔraawiizi teŋ di a hiŋwaa seriyaa tuŋ. U teŋ cholloo, dikuu uŋ waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi Biikpaŋkpaŋ la wia.

ref: The light has come into the world, and people who do evil things are judged guilty because they love the dark more than the light.
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi seriya dii du. Bɔchaaŋ ba durnyaa. Ka newea haa ra nyiŋŋi bɔbiri werge di kaali bɔchaaŋ la, dikuu ba hunchɔgaa wia.

ref: People who do evil hate the light and won't come to the light, because it clearly shows what they have done.
text: Nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa, waa nyiŋŋi bɔchaaŋ wia. Wàá sɛɛ lii bɔchaaŋ ú wolo lii.

ref: But everyone who lives by the truth will come to the light, because they want others to know that God is really the one doing what they do. Jesus and John the Baptist
text: Nɛr la maa ge n na ɛɛ winanaa ɔɔ ra lii bɔchaannɛ, nɛ́ra zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi hiinaa biinii u wer di ra ɛɛ wiimaa.” Yeesu ni Jɔɔn wia

ref: Later, Jesus and his disciples went to Judea, where he stayed with them for a while and was baptizing people.
text: Annii tuna, Yeesu ni u hiŋra izi de di la Juda hɛri di ga birgi de tama, di ra sɔ nɛra Kɔraawiizi nii.

ref: They went to John and said, “Rabbi, you spoke about a man when you were with him east of the Jordan. He is now baptizing people, and everyone is going to him.”
text: Ba maa izi di la Jɔɔn be, di ga ŋɔ u be, “Yaa Nabɔma, baal la n faa du i be Jɔɔdan muu keŋkere, i ŋɔ u wia tɛɛ yaa la, u gba ra sɔ nɛraa Kɔraawiizi nii. Nɛkpila maa ra la u be.”

ref: John replied: No one can do anything unless God in heaven allows it.
text: Jɔɔn ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi waa nɛr maa tɛɛwɛ wii maa ŋmɛnɛɛ, wàá wer na u ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: You surely remember how I told you that I am not the Messiah. I am only the one sent ahead of him.
text: Ii gba faa du denii di nuu gunla miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ maa Kristo la ɛɛwɛ. Ka Kɔraawiizi humimbuu ŋɔ ń tɔ Kristo la see di ba.

ref: At a wedding the groom is the one who gets married. The best man is glad just to be there and to hear the groom's voice. That's why I am so glad.
text: Nɛr la maa n kpa haŋfalii, waabuu dɔɔ u kuŋ. Ka u dammu ɔɔ chiu ra nuu u wiŋɔzi, u bɔra a sɔɔnuu werge maa dikuu u wia. Gunnɛ n ge bɔra sɔɔniŋ werge maa di wa tuŋ la.

ref: Jesus must become more important, while I become less important. The One Who Comes from Heaven
text: A dɛkkɔ waabuu n na zenni di ra jaa, ka míŋwaa wia ra tuŋ.

ref: God's Son comes from heaven and is above all others. Everyone who comes from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all others.
text: Unla n lii Kɔraawiizi be la, u ɛɛ yaa maa nabɔmaa. Unla ge n lii hɛri ɛɛ hɛri hotte di ra ŋɔ hɛri wia. Ka Kɔraawiizi be hinuu la ɛɛ kummaa nabɔmaa.

ref: He speaks about what he has seen and heard, and yet no one believes him.
text: U ra bagli wia la maa un nawɛɛ di nuu lii Kɔraawiizi benii. Ka nɛra waa sɛɛwɛ ra tɛu.

ref: But everyone who does believe him has shown that God is truthful.
text: Unla maa n wa sɛɛ u wia, ɔɔ wer zum u himmaa biinii lugɔ Kɔraawiizi wia dɔɔ wibiire.

ref: The Son was sent to speak God's message, and he has been given the full power of God's Spirit.
text: Unla Kɔraawiizi n hummɛ u lii u be ba la, waabuu ɔɔ ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi tɛubuu u Dumnanii werge di wa tuŋ.

ref: The Father loves the Son and has given him everything.
text: Kɔraawiizi nɔŋŋi u Biibaal labuu werge, di tɛu fɔŋŋa werge kummaa ni.

ref: Everyone who has faith in the Son has eternal life. But no one who rejects him will ever share in that life, and God will be angry with them forever.
text: Nɛr la maa n yardi Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la, Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ a hinnɛ u miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la. Nɛr la maa ge n waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu, wàá na u miibɔɔ la. Kɔraawiizi baaŋ daŋ haŋ du a hiŋ ninɛɛ, di hanna la saŋaa saŋa maa.”

ref: But Jesus' disciples were really the ones doing the baptizing, and not Jesus himself. Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
text: Ama, Yeesu himmaa faa waa ɔɔ ra sɔ a nɛra Kɔraawiizi nii la. U hiŋraa faa ɔɔ ra sɔ baa a nii.

ref: This time he had to go through Samaria,
text: Banna la la, ba ŋɔ bá ga Samaria hɛri.

ref: “You are a Jew,” she replied, “and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink of water when Jews and Samaritans won't have anything to do with each other?”
text: A haaŋ pɛɛzuu, “Hiŋ ɛɛ Jus hinuu, ka ɛrɛɛ i ra suŋŋi mìŋ́ Samaria hinuu niiyɛi?” U ŋɔ gunnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Jus hina faa ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Samaria hinaa. Ba faa waa ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi bá ni baa ra kpau wiimaa bɔr.

ref: “Sir,” the woman said, “you don't even have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where are you going to get this life-giving water?
text: U ŋɔ, “N mɛ, haa jaayir dɔɔwɛ, a kɔlɔŋ ge du luŋ. Ɛrɛɛ í ɛɛ na nii naa dee n dɔɔ miibɔɔ di tɛnnɛi?

ref: Our ancestor Jacob dug this well for us, and his family and animals got water from it. Are you greater than Jacob?”
text: Yaa naabaal Jekɔbuu faa tɛɛ yaa kɔlɔŋ naa. U ni u biizi ni u sela maanii ɔɔ faa na nii u biini di ra nyɔɔ. Amɔ, hinuu ɛɛ nɛzeŋ kaali a Jekɔbaa?”

ref: But no one who drinks the water I give will ever be thirsty again. The water I give will become in that person a flowing fountain that gives eternal life.”
text: Ka nii naa dee miŋ dɔɔwɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra naa, di i nyɔɔu, niinyɔgzi wàá ka kpui maa. Nii la min niŋ tɛi la ɛɛ bulee, di ra bul i biini saŋa maa, di ra tɛi miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.”

ref: The woman replied, “Sir, please give me a drink of that water! Then I won't get thirsty and have to come to this well again.”
text: Haaŋ la ŋɔ, “N mɛ, tɛŋ a nii ń nyɔɔ, niinyɔgzi gilɛɛ kaa waa kpuŋ maa, ń kaa waa dɔɔ nii.”

ref: Jesus told her, “Go and bring your husband.”
text: Yeesu ŋɔ, “La ga yir i jaari ba.”

ref: The woman answered, “I don't have a husband.” “That's right,” Jesus replied, “you're telling the truth. You don't have a husband. You have already been married five times, and the man you are now living with isn't your husband.”
text: I janna la hiŋ faa yuuwɛ la du baala banue. Ka baal la be hiŋ duwɛɛ filaŋkennaa, i jaari lɛi. Awia, i ŋɔ wibiire.”

ref: The woman said, “Sir, I can see that you are a prophet.
text: Denii haaŋ la ŋɔ, “N mɛ, ajaa i ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛllɛa?

ref: Jesus said to her: Believe me, the time is coming when you won't worship the Father either on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
text: Yeesu ŋɔ, “Gil ń ŋɔ wibii maa tɛi. Saŋa bɛl, ba wàá ka waa jaami yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi bizeŋ naa nyuu, ba wàá ka waa jaamuu Jɛrusalɛm gba.

ref: You Samaritans don't really know the one you worship. But we Jews do know the God we worship, and by using us, God will save the world.
text: Ka ii Samaria hina, ii waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ nɛnnɛ ka ra jaamuu. Yaa Jus hinawaa zumuubuu nɛnnɛ di ra jaamuu. Yaa Jus hina benii Kɔraawiizi ga di lɛɛ nɛra.

ref: But a time is coming, and it is already here! Even now the true worshipers are being led by the Spirit to worship the Father according to the truth. These are the ones the Father is seeking to worship him.
text: Ka saŋa bɛl daŋ wa hel, a saŋa jaa ra dugluu gba, bánla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi jaama himmaa, kpa biinihuŋŋu di ra jaamuu ú Duma fɔŋŋa biini. Yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋi guŋ hinaa bá ra jaamuu.

ref: God is Spirit, and those who worship God must be led by the Spirit to worship him according to the truth.
text: Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ Dumaa. Banla maa n na jaamuu, bá ra jaamuu u Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini, di ra jaamuu ani biinihuŋŋu.”

ref: The woman said, “I know that the Messiah will come. He is the one we call Christ. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.”
text: Haaŋ la ŋɔ, “N zummɔ lugɔ Mɛsia banna yir Kristo la, daŋ ba. Di u wa ballɔ, u daŋ bagli yaa wiimaa.”

ref: “I am that one,” Jesus told her, “and I am speaking to you now.”
text: Yeesu ŋɔ, “I nuubuu ra ŋɔ wia la. Minuu a Kristo.”

ref: The disciples returned about this time and were surprised to find Jesus talking with a woman. But none of them asked him what he wanted or why he was talking with her.
text: Denii Yeesu hiŋra jaa bir ba u be. Baŋ wa nawɛɛ lugɔ u ni haaŋ bɛllɛ ra ŋɔ wia la, a tir baa. Ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá pɛɛzi Yeesu kunla unna nyiŋŋi haaŋ la be gɛɛ́ wii la n baani u ni haaŋ la ra ŋɔ wia.

ref: The woman left her water jar and ran back into town, where she said to the people,
text: Haaŋ la gil u vii ta de, ka bir kaali bol di gaa yirgi nɛra, di ra ŋɔ,

ref: “Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! Could he be the Messiah?”
text: “Ií ba wa na baal bɛl n wette ra bagliŋ wii la maa miŋ ɛɛwɛ. Kristoo nii.”

ref: Everyone in town went out to see Jesus.
text: Ba izi lii bol biini di ba wa na Yeesu.

ref: While this was happening, Jesus' disciples were saying to him, “Teacher, please eat something.”
text: Haaŋ la n kaali bol la, Yeesu hiŋra ŋɔ u be, “Yaa Nabɔma, lɛɛ diwee di.”

ref: But Jesus told them, “I have food you don't know anything about.”
text: U vɛɛ ka ŋɔ ba be, “N dɔɔ diwee aŋhina dee iiŋ waa a wia zummɛ.”

ref: His disciples started asking each other, “Has someone brought him something to eat?”
text: U hiŋra la jaa ra pɛɛzi dɔŋa, “Nɛbɛllɛ ballɛ wa tɛu diwee u di gɛɛ?”

ref: Jesus said: My food is to do what God wants! He is the one who sent me, and I must finish the work that he gave me to do.
text: Yeesu ŋɔ, “N diweere lugɔ ń ɛɛ unla n humiŋ la kipar, di hum u huma la maa tuŋ.

ref: You may say there are still four months until harvest time. But I tell you to look, and you will see that the fields are ripe and ready to harvest.
text: Ba ra ŋɔu lugɔ baaguzi anaazuu kawɛɛ ka kuna kumaa saŋa hel. Ka miŋwaa ra ŋɔ ii benii, ‘Ií binni na. Kuna kumaa saŋa helloo, dikuubɛɛwiai, a biiwɔɔ.’

ref: Even now the harvest workers are receiving their reward by gathering a harvest that brings eternal life. Then everyone who planted the seed and everyone who harvests the crop will celebrate together.
text: Nɛr la maa n kummɛ di ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ra na u kinturgaare. Neweare a hiŋ kum la, di ra lɛɛ baa bá wer na Kɔraawiizi miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la, ú ni unla n duuwe maa bɔra sɔɔni baa.

ref: So the saying proves true, “Some plant the seed, and others harvest the crop.”
text: Sɛɛlii bɛl ra bagli wibii bɛllɛ, ‘I daŋ duu mia, i dɔŋhiŋ ge kumaa.’

ref: A lot of Samaritans in that town put their faith in Jesus because the woman had said, “This man told me everything I have ever done.”
text: Samaria hina la n du a bol bakpila yardi Yeesu. Haaŋ la n ŋɔ ba be lugɔ u bagluubuu wii la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ la wia, ba wer chi de yardi Yeesu.

ref: They came and asked him to stay in their town, and he stayed on for two days.
text: Ba ba u be di waa suŋŋuu ú du ba be tama mɔɔ. U la ga du ba be hɔpizaa anɛɛ di ra bagli baa.

ref: Many more Samaritans put their faith in Jesus because of what they heard him say.
text: Baŋ wa nuu u baglaa la, nɛkpila maa yardi.

ref: They told the woman, “We no longer have faith in Jesus just because of what you told us. We have heard him ourselves, and we are certain that he is the Savior of the world!” Jesus Heals an Official's Son (Matthew
text: Ba ŋɔ haaŋ la be, “Yaa gba yardɔɔrɛ. Hinuu felee ŋɔ u wia tɛɛ yaa. Ka yaa himmaa digna jaa nuu u wiarɛ filaŋkeŋ. Awiarɛ yaa yardi. Yaa zummɔ lugɔ durnya Lɛɛrii, ɛnɛ maa.” Yeesu n chaa nabɔma bɛl biibaal

ref: Jesus had said, “Prophets are honored everywhere, except in their own country.” Then two days later he left
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ waa girme dɔɔwɛ u himmaa hɛri.”

ref: and went to Galilee. The people there welcomed him, because they had gone to the festival in Jerusalem and had seen everything he had done.
text: Uŋ wa hel de, de hina jaamuu nɛnnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba gba faa la Jɛrusalɛmnɛ di ga di ba Gillikaali Hɔpizizenaa la, di na u wiɛɛlaa la maa uŋ ɛɛwɛ de, a saŋa.

ref: While Jesus was in Galilee, he returned to the village of Cana, where he had turned the water into wine. There was an official in Capernaum whose son was sick.
text: U kaa ba Keena la n du Galilii hɛri la, bol la uŋ faa gillɛ nii birgi siŋ la, di wa du de. Baal bɛl ge faa du Kapɛniɔm, di ɛɛ nɛzeŋ. U faa hummɔɔ ra tɛɛ de hɛri hina nabɔma. U biibaal ge faa ra wiiu.

ref: And when the man heard that Jesus had come from Judea, he went and begged him to keep his son from dying.
text: Uŋ wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Yeesu lii Juda hɛrii di bir ba Galilii hɛri la, u izi la u be di gaa suŋŋuu werge maa ú ba wa chaa u biibaal la tɛu. U biibaal la faa ra nyiŋŋi siwaarɛ.

ref: Jesus told the official, “You won't have faith unless you see miracles and wonders!”
text: Yeesu ŋɔ u be, “Di maa wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia ra ɛɛ di ra bagli ia, ii wàá yardiŋ.”

ref: The man replied, “Lord, please come before my son dies!”
text: A nabɔma kaa suŋŋuu, di ŋɔ, “N Mɛ, jaande maa, di haa ballɛ manaŋ, n bie la daŋ siu.”

ref: Jesus then said, “Your son will live. Go on home to him.” The man believed Jesus and started back home.
text: Yeesu ŋɔ, “A la dia. I bie la nyaagɔɔrɛ.” Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, a baal yarduu di bir kpo.

ref: Some of the official's servants met him along the road and told him, “Your son is better!”
text: Uŋ haa du ŋmɛnɛɛ ra ba la, u balaa wa chem u ni di ŋɔ u be, “I bie la nyaagɔɔrɛ.”

ref: He asked them when the boy got better, and they answered, “The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock.”
text: U pɛɛzi baa saŋa la a bie n nyaagɛɛ. Ba ŋɔ, “Dɛɛla wibaŋa karfi kpaŋ saŋaa, u bɔra waa kaa wenzi, u nyaagi.”

ref: The boy's father realized that at one o'clock the day before, Jesus had told him, “Your son will live!” So the man and everyone in his family put their faith in Jesus.
text: Baal la zum lugɔ a dɛɛla saŋa hiŋ dɔnnɛ Yeesu ŋɔ u be, dí u bie daŋ nyaagi la. Denii u ni u diahina maa yardi Yeesu.

ref: This was the second miracle that Jesus worked after he left Judea and went to Galilee.
text: Yeesu n lii Juda hɛri di ba Galilii hɛri la, u wizenaa nɛɛhinnɛ guŋ uŋ ɛɛwɛ de.

ref: Later, Jesus went to Jerusalem for another Jewish festival.
text: Annii tuna, Jus hina hɔpizizeŋ bɛl wa hel. Yeesu izi di bir la Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: In the city near the sheep gate was a pool with five porches, and its name in Hebrew was Bethzatha.
text: Pol bɛl faa du Jɛrusalɛm, ba ra yiruu Bɛtzata, u dugli Peeza Dominuuzeŋ. Ba faa ma sognibɔra anue lugɔ jaŋgalli, a pol nua.

ref: Beside the pool was a man who had been sick for
text: Baal bɛl ge du a wiila hina biini. U wiiwɔɔ binni tokko ni fidiŋmantannaazi.

ref: You have not believed his message, because you refused to have faith in the one he sent.
text: U wiŋɔzi gba waa hoo ii bampiree, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii waa sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ unla uŋ hummɛ ii be la.

ref: When Jesus saw the man and realized that he had been crippled for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be healed?”
text: Yeesu nau un chɔɔ de, di zum lugɔ u wiiwɔɔ birgi. Awia, u la u be di ga pɛɛzuu, “I ra nyiŋŋi í nyaagia?”

ref: The man answered, “Sir, I don't have anyone to put me in the pool when the water is stirred up. I try to get in, but someone else always gets there first.”
text: Wiila hiŋ la ŋɔ, “Ɛɛh. Ka nii la n ɔɔ waa birgi gunla, maa ɔɔ na nɛr ú kpaŋ du u biini, ń nyaagi. Di u wa izoo ra birgi, anna nyiŋŋi lugɔ ń zuu u biini, ka bɛl ɔɔ feliŋ zuu.”

ref: Jesus told him, “Pick up your mat and walk!”
text: Denii Yeesu ŋɔ u be, “Izi kpa i kalaŋ di ra la.”

ref: Right then the man was healed. He picked up his mat and started walking around. The day on which this happened was a Sabbath.
text: Yeesu n haŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, di baal la nyaagɔɔ, di izi kpa u kalaŋ di ra la. Ba Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ faa.

ref: When the Jewish leaders saw the man carrying his mat, they said to him, “This is the Sabbath! No one is allowed to carry a mat on the Sabbath.”
text: Unna la, Jus hina baŋhina ga ŋɔ u be, “Yaa Heezaa Hɔpiziirɛ keŋ. Ka i kpa i kalaŋ chi. Yaa kiire i ra chɔgi la.”

ref: But he replied, “The man who healed me told me to pick up my mat and walk.”
text: A baal ŋɔ, “Nɛr la n chaaŋ la, waabuu ŋɔ ń kpa n kalaŋ chi di ra la.”

ref: They asked him, “Who is this man that told you to pick up your mat and walk?”
text: Ba pɛɛzuu, “Anɛɛ n ŋɔ dí i kpa i kalaŋ chi di ra lanɛi?”

ref: But he did not know who Jesus was, and Jesus had left because of the crowd.
text: Baal la waa zum nɛr la n chaau la. Yeesu n chaau tuŋ la, u bir kaali, dikuu nɛkpila n faa du a pol wia, a baal waa kaa wer ú zumuu.

ref: Later, Jesus met the man in the temple and told him, “You are now well. But don't sin anymore or something worse might happen to you.”
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Yeesu wa huuzuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, di ŋɔ u be, “Haa nawɛɛa? I nyaagɔɔrɛ. Awia, gilɛɛ kaa ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Di i kaa wa ɛɛ wichɔgaa, i daŋ kaa di tɔɔrɔɔ kaali gunla hiŋ faa diu la.”

ref: The man left and told the leaders that Jesus was the one who had healed him.
text: A baal jaa la Jus hina la be di ga ŋɔ, “Yeesuu chaaŋ la.”

ref: They started making a lot of trouble for Jesus because he did things like this on the Sabbath.
text: Yeesu n ɔɔ ra ɛɛ guŋ ba Heezaa Hɔpizii la wiarɛ a Jus hina ɔɔ ra tɔɔruu.

ref: But Jesus said, “My Father has never stopped working, and this is why I keep on working.”
text: Yeesu kaa ŋɔ ba be, “N Mɛɛ ra hum u humaa saŋa maa. N ge gba ra hum guŋ.”

ref: Now the leaders wanted to kill Jesus for two reasons. First, he had broken the law of the Sabbath. But even worse, he had said God was his Father, which made him equal with God. The Son's Authority
