text: Un la de di ga na gunla Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa ni u hiinaa n du ba be, ba wer ra ɛɛ winanaa, u bɔra sɔɔni ba wia werge maa. U ra hiini baa di ŋɔ ba be, dí ba ɛɛ ania di lau bampirkpaŋ di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi di gilɛɛ waa leu u ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
text: A Banabas ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ di dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ni yarda nɛnnɛ. Awiarɛ u wer di ra hiini baa guŋ. Nɛkpila maa sɛɛ Yeesu wia di bir ba bampiree di ra hiŋuu.

ref: Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
text: Banabas la Taasus di gaa nyiŋŋi Sɔɔl.

ref: He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
text: Uŋ wa nau, u lawuu ba Antiɔk. Ba ni Yeesu hiŋra ɔɔ chaali dɔŋa guŋŋ a wa hel bina. Ba bagli nɛkpila maa Kɔraawiizi wia Antiɔk biini. Denii ba lugli ra yir baa Yeesu hiŋra. A sɔŋ zɛɛrɛ Kristo nɛra.

ref: During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch.
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi baŋhina lii Jɛrusalɛm a saŋa di ba Antiɔk.

ref: One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor.
text: Bɛl sɔnnɛ Agabus. U izi ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini dí lɔzi daŋ chol durnya maa biini. A lɔzi faa chol Koorizeŋ Klaudius saŋa.

ref: The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea.
text: Denii Yeesu hiŋra ɛɛ nuukpaŋ ŋɔ bá kɛɛ kebee di ŋɔ, “Gunla maa hinla maa n nawɛɛ, í kpa ba ya hiini yaabalaa la n du Juda hɛri la.”

ref: So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
text: Ba ba. Ba kpa tɛɛ Banabas ni Sɔɔl bá kpa ga tɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra nabɔnzi la.

ref: At that time King Herod caused terrible suffering for some members of the church.
text: Jus hina koori bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Hɛrɔd izi lau Yeesu hiŋra baŋhina a saŋa hiŋ di tɔɔri baa,

ref: He ordered soldiers to cut off the head of James, the brother of John.
text: di gil ba kpa kandaa di kpu Jɔɔn kpɛɛma Jems.

ref: When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread.
text: Guŋ par a Jus hina werge. Awia, u kaa gil ba lau Pitta ge. A saŋa ɛɛ ba hɔpizizenaa la baŋ ɔɔ ra di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ hɔpizizenaa labuu.

ref: He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
text: U gil ba tɔu dia mɔɔ, ka di ba wa di ba Gillikaali diwee la tuŋ ú jaa lizuu tɛɛ a nɛra bá ɛɛu ba kipar. U gil soojazi banaazaa bɔra anaazu ra du u tau.

ref: While Peter was being kept in jail, the church never stopped praying to God for him. Peter Is Rescued
text: Pitta n du nɛra tɔi dia la, ka Yeesu hiŋra ra suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi werge maa di ra tɛu.

ref: The night before Peter was to be put on trial, he was asleep and bound by two chains. A soldier was guarding him on each side, and two other soldiers were guarding the entrance to the jail.
text: Hɛrɔd faa dau hɔpizii la un niŋ lizi Pittaa tɛɛ a nɛra. A hamuŋa ka hɔpizii la hel, Pitta chɔɔ soojazi banɛɛ baaŋ di ra chɔɔ dɔɔ. Yɔlɔzi anɛɛ du u nonee ni. A diibinna ge chi a nɛra tɔi dominua la di ra du a dia tau.

ref: Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared, and light flashed around in the cell. The angel poked Peter in the side and woke him up. Then he said, “Quick! Get up!” The chains fell off his hands,
text: Denii Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl ba u be, dia la maa chaani. U lɔ Pitta kɛra di lalluu dɔɔ di ŋɔ, “Izi manaŋ.” U yɔlɔzi la lii u nonee chol hɛri. U izi.

ref: and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.”
text: Denii mɛlika la ŋɔ, “Kpa i kuna laali di kpa i gawa du.” U laali u kuna di kpa u gawa du. U kaa ŋɔ, “Kpa i wɛjɛ tɔ di ra hiŋiŋ.”

ref: They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
text: Ba ga bɛri lugli diibinni la ni di kaa wa bɛri nɛɛhiŋ la ge ni di ga hel bossee dominua la lugbii gbera la. U pilli u hiŋ ni. Ba lii di kpa ŋmɛnɛɛ bɛl di ra la. Baŋ waa hel see, mɛlika la gil Pitta.

ref: Peter now realized what had happened, and he said, “I am certain that the Lord sent his angel to rescue me from Herod and from everything the Jewish leaders planned to do to me.”
text: Denii u nfɛrɛ jaa ba lugɔ wibii himmaanii. U ŋɔ, “Filaŋkeŋ n jaa zumuu lugɔ n Dɔɔrii hum u mɛlika u ba wa lɛɛŋ ɛnɛ maa. Hɛrɔd nonee biinii u lɛɛŋ, Jús hina gilɛɛ ɛɛŋ gunla baŋ faa ra fɛ la.”

ref: Then Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John whose other name was Mark. Many of the Lord's followers had come together there and were praying.
text: U jaa ra la Jɔɔn la banna yir Maak la maa Mɛɛri dia, di nɛkpila chaali de, di ra suŋŋi wiizi.

ref: Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer.
text: U lɔ dominua di ɛɛ gaafura. A dia balii bɛl banna yir Roda ba.

ref: When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
text: Uŋ wa zum Pitta loobii, u bɔra sɔɔni werge maa di wa bɛri. Waa kaa pilli dominua la gba ka chɔ zuu dia biini di kali nɛra la lugɔ, “Pittaa chigɛ dominua.”

ref: “You are crazy!” everyone told her. But she kept saying it was Peter. Then they said, “It must be his angel.”
text: Ba pɛɛzuu, “I ra chugluu gɛɛ?” U kaa ŋɔ siaahmu maa dí wibii maa. Ka ba ŋɔ, “Amɔ, u mɛlikaa.”

ref: But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
text: Ka Pitta haa ra lɔ dominua di ra ɛɛ gaafura la. Ba wa pilli, di Pittaa. A tir baa.

ref: Peter motioned for them to keep quiet. Then he told how the Lord had led him out of jail. He also said, “Tell James and the others what has happened.” After that, he left and went somewhere else.
text: U vig baa nonee bá siigi, ka bagli baa gunla Kɔraawiizi n lizuu nɛra tɔi dia la biini. Uŋ wa bagli baa tuŋ, u ŋɔ, “Ií ŋɔ wia naa tɛɛ Jems ni yaabalaa la.” Denii u kaa bir kaali yembɛl.

ref: The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ a soojazi izi di Pitta waa hoo. Ba ra nyiŋŋuu di ra kɔɔ bɔr maa.

ref: Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while. Herod Dies
text: Hɛrɔd ŋɔ, Ií nyiŋŋuu ba, ka ba nyiŋŋuu huhzi. U pɛɛzi a nɛra tɔi dia binna la u wia, ka ŋɔ dí ba kpu baa. Koori Hɛrɔd siu wia Denii Koori Hɛrɔd izi a Juda hɛri di la Siizaria di ga du de.

ref: Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon were very angry with each other. But their country got its food supply from the region that he ruled. So a group of them went to see Blastus, who was one of Herod's high officials. They convinced Blastus that they wanted to make peace between their cities and Herod,
text: A saŋa hiŋ, Koori Hɛrɔd na baaŋ du Taaya ni Saidɔn hina ni werge. Denii ba maa chaali di feli la u dia nabɔma Blastus be di ga lizi ba amaniye tɛu mɔɔ, ka la Hɛrɔd ge be di ga suŋŋuu ú gil u ni baa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. Ba diwee n ɔɔ ra lii a koori hɛri la wiarɛ ba ra nyiŋŋi u ni baa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ la.

ref: and a day was set for them to meet with him. Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech.
text: Hɛrɔd tɛɛ baa hɔpizii la ban niŋ bir ba. A hɔpizii n wa helle u laali u koori piŋŋozi zɛɛɛ di so u koorikara ni di ŋɔ wisuma aŋhina tɛɛ baa.

ref: The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!”
text: Nɛra la ra koobi di ra ŋɔ, “Kaabaako! Newee lɛi ŋɔ wia naa. Kɔraawiizii ŋɔa.”

ref: At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ Hɛrɔd lɛɛ a girme tɛɛ u hiŋ. Waa sɛɛwɛ bá kpa Kɔraawiizi girme. Awia, Kɔraawiizi mɛlika bɛl wa gil wiila wa lɔu dau kakpaŋ. Haalauri di u biini kuna u siu.

ref: And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
text: Banabas ni Sɔɔl n wa ɛɛ gunla nɛra la n faa hum baa bá la Jɛrusalɛm ga ɛɛ la tuŋ, ba lau Jɔɔn Maak u ni baa izi Jɛrusalɛm di bir la Antiɔk.

ref: The church at Antioch had several prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon, also called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who was Herod's close friend, and Saul.
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ani Kɔraawiizi wibagla baŋhina faa du Yeesu hiŋra biini Antiɔk. Ba sɔnaa faa Banabas ni Simɛɔn, ba kaa ra yiruu Nɛbiŋŋu, ni Lusiɔs la n lii Sairini, ni Manɛn la baŋ faa dɛɛzɛɛ Hɛrɔd mɛɛ dia la, ni Sɔɔl.

ref: While they were worshiping the Lord and going without eating, the Holy Spirit told them, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to do the work for which I have chosen them.”
text: Banniibuu faa ra vɔɔ nua di ra hum Kɔraawiizi huma. Denii Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ŋɔ ba be, “Ií lizi Banabas ni Sɔɔl ii biini bá hum huma aŋhina miŋ dau baa.”

ref: Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way. Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
text: Baŋ wa vɔɔ nua di jaami Kɔraawiizi tuŋ, ba jaa kpa ba nonee sagzi Banabas ni Sɔɔl ni ka hum baa bá ga hum a huma. Banabas ni Sɔɔl n la Saiprɔs hɛri wia

ref: After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus.
text: Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii n hum baa gunla, ba kpa la Sɛlusia di ga zuu muugbera bɛl de di ra la hɛrjiga bɛl n du muu baambaaŋ ba ra yir de Saiprɔs.

ref: They arrived at Salamis and began to preach God's message in the synagogues. They also had John as a helper.
text: Baŋ wa hel de, ba lii di la Salamis di gaa ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia Jus hina jaamaa diini biine. Jɔɔn la ge faa du ba be di ra hiini baa.

ref: Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet.
text: Ba vol di gaagi a hɛri maa di wa hel Pafɔs. Jus hinuu bɛl faa du de. U sɔnnɛ faa Bajesus, ka Giris hina ra yiruu Ɛlimas. U ɔɔ ra ɛɛ ziŋgaabo wia di ra dar nɛra lugɔ u ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛllɛ.

ref: He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul.
text: A hɛri nabɔma Sɛjiɔs Pɔɔlɔs benii u faa du. A nabɔma hiŋ faa dɔɔ nfɛrɛɛ di ra nyiŋŋi u nuu Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la. Awia, u yir Banabas ni Sɔɔl bá ba u be. Ba ba.

ref: But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
text: Ka ziŋgaabo hiŋ la ra di baa hɔɔzi. Waa nyiŋŋi u nabɔma la sɛɛ Yeesu wia.

ref: Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
text: Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii izi Pɔɔl ni. A Sɔɔllɛ Giris hina kaa ra yir Pɔɔl la. U binni u siwee tiiih

ref: and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord?
text: ka ŋɔ, “Ee! Sitaani hiŋ! Winanaa maa dɔm! I dɔɔ daraa ni wichɔgaarɛ werge. Gilɛɛ kpa i wichɔgaa naa di tɔ Kɔraawiizi wia ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.” Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand.
text: Na! Filaŋkeŋ Kɔraawiizi daŋ baglii u fɔŋŋa í nyuŋŋi, á birgi tama ka i kaa na wiizi. Kakpaŋ, u siwee biri.” U ra largi di ra nyiŋŋi nɛbɛl ú ra tɛrguu.

ref: When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord. Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
text: Nabɔma la n wa na guŋ, u yardi gunla bam bagluu Yeesu wia la. A wiŋɔzi wia tiruu werge maa. Bolzeŋ Antiɔk n du Pisidia wia

ref: Paul and the others left Paphos and sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
text: Denii Pɔɔl ni banla n du u be zuu muugbera di lii Pafɔs di ra la Pɛga la n du Pamfilia hɛri la. Jɔɔn la gil baa de ka bir kaali Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
text: Ba ge lii Pɛga di la Antiɔk la n du Pisidia hɛri la. Ba Heezaa Hɔpizii n wa helle ba zuu ba jaamaa dia biini di ga so.

ref: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
text: Nɛra baŋhina karmi Moosis Gbɔgni ni dɔgtɛɛzi Hɔna tama. Denii a jaamaa dia nabɔnzi gil nɛra ŋɔ Pɔɔl ni Banabas be, “Yaabalaa, di ii dɔɔ wihiinii maa iin niŋ ŋɔ dí hiini nɛra naa, ií ŋɔu tɛɛ baa.”

ref: Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said: People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen!
text: Pɔɔl izi di lalli u nonii ka jaa ŋɔ ra tɛɛ baa, “N dɔŋa Izrɛl hina ni ii banla maa n na jaami Kɔraawiizi, ií ra nuu n be.

ref: The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out,
text: Kɔraawiizi la Izrɛl hina naa n na hiŋ la faa lizi yaa naabaalaa durnya nɛra maa biini tɛɛ u hiŋ, di gil ba wazi saŋa la baŋ faa ɛɛ hɔɔhra di du Ijip hɛri la. Denii u wa lizi baa a Ijip hɛri biini ni u fɔŋŋa,

ref: Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
text: Awia, ií ra dazi wia la Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la á gilɛɛ waa na ia. Ba faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ,

ref: He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people.
text: Hɛssi aniidaanɛɛ nɛraa u duŋŋi Keenan hɛri biini ka kpa ba hɛssi tɛɛ u nɛra.

ref: Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
text: ka Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ kora la u be di tɛɛ Deevid u di. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Deevid wia di ŋɔ, ‘Jɛssɛ biibaal Deevid naa wia ra parimbuu werge maa. U daŋ hum n kipar huma la maa di ra tɛŋ.’

ref: God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus.
text: A Deevid dee biinii Yeesu lii. Kɔraawiizi humuu Izrɛl hina be ú ɛɛ ba Lɛɛri gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ baa la.

ref: But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized.
text: Mɔɔ ka Yeesu ba, Jɔɔn faa ra bagli Izrɛl hina maanii dí ba gil ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia ka ú sɔ baa Kɔraawiizi nii.

ref: Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
text: Jɔɔn huma n faa ka tama ka á tuŋ la, u pɛɛzi nɛra la, ‘Anɛɛ ii ra yirinnɛi? Miŋ lɛi unla iinna kpaŋ la. A hiŋ haa du harbɔɔ. Maa dɛg min niŋ lizi u gawa gba tɛu.’

ref: Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone.
text: Yaabalaa, ii banla n ɛɛ Abraham biizi ani ii wiijaama maa, yaa benii Kɔraawiizi durnya lɛɛi wiŋɔzi naa ba.

ref: The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
text: Jɛrusalɛm hina la ni ba nabɔnzi n wa na Yeesu, ba waa zummɛ lugɔ ba Lɛɛrii. Baŋ ɔɔ ra karmi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi wiŋɔzi ba Heezaa Hɔpizii la maa, ka ba waa ɔɔ ra zum a zɛɛ nɛnnɛ. Awiarɛ ba di u kpui seriya gunla a dɔgtɛɛzi n sɛbɛɛ ŋɔ guŋ daŋ wa ɛɛ la.

ref: They did exactly what the Scriptures said they would. Even though they couldn't find any reason to put Jesus to death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed. After Jesus had been put to death, he was taken down from the cross and placed in a tomb.
text: Baŋ wa ɛɛu wii la maa baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini ŋɔ guŋ daŋ wa ɛɛ la, ba ba wa lizuu daakaŋlii la ni di hug.

ref: But God raised him from death!
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi lalluu siu biini.

ref: Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
text: Nɛra la n faa hiŋuu di lii Galilii hɛri di ba Jɛrusalɛm la ɔɔ faa ra nau hɔpizikpila maa biini. Baabuu di daansɛɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra filaŋkeŋ lugɔ u izi siu biinii.

ref: God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news
text: Yaa ge kpa amaniyesuma naa di ba ii be, ií zum gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa naabaala la,

ref: that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus, “You are my son because today I have become your Father.”
text: gunnɛ u ɛɛ tɛɛ yaa banla n ɛɛ ba biizi la, di lalli Yeesu siu biini. Ba sɛbi u wiarɛ Yira Hɔŋ biini, u bɔra anɛɛhiŋ, di ŋɔ, ‘N biibaallɛ hiŋ, zinaabuu n lulii.’

ref: God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said, “I will make to you the same holy promises that I made to David.”
text: Ba kaa sɛbi u wia yembɛl di feli bagli lugɔ u daŋ izi siu biini, ú bɔrahɔŋ gilɛɛ pɔɔh. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘N daŋ ɛɛi winanaa la miŋ faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ Koori Deevid la.’

ref: And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
text: A guŋ wiarɛ ba kaa sɛbi a hɔŋ yembɛl di ŋɔ, ‘Hàá gil i biinaniinanii la bɔrahɔŋ pɔɔh.’

ref: When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed.
text: Deevid ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipattɛ guŋŋ ka wa siu. Ba huguu ba lalaa be. U bɔrahɔŋ pɔɔh.

ref: But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
text: Ka nɛr la Kɔraawiizi n lallɛɛ siu biini la, waabuu bɔrahɔŋ waa pɔɔhwɛ.

ref: My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins.
text: Awia, yaabalaa, ií maa zum nɛnnɛ zinaa lugɔ a Yeesu huma wiarɛ yaa wer di ra ŋɔ ii be lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil ii wichɔgaa tɛɛ ia la.

ref: “Look, you people who make fun of God! Be amazed and disappear. I will do something today that you won't believe, even if someone tells you about it!”
text: ‘Ii banla n na ɛɛ nɛra chɛɛtɛ la, ií binni wia la minna ɛɛ naa, a daŋ wa tir ia ii siuzi. N daŋ ɛɛ wii bɛl í de dui saŋa iiŋ wàá yardi, haali di ba kali ia gba.’ ”

ref: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ anniizi maa tuŋ, u ni Banabas izi ra lii a jaamaa dia biini. Banna lii la, a nɛra suŋŋi baa, dí ba kaa bir ba ba Heezaa Hɔpizii la n na ba la, di kaa wa ŋɔ a wia bá kaa nuu.

ref: After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
text: Ba maa lii a dia biini. Jus hina ni wiijaama kpilakpila maa hiŋ Pɔɔl ni Banabas. Pɔɔl ni Banabas ŋɔ wia tɛɛ baa di ŋɔ bá ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnɛɛ nɛnnɛ, ú nɛsunaa ni u hiinaa du ba be.

ref: The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord.
text: Ba Heezaa Hɔpizii la n kaa wa hel, a bol hina galga maa jaa ba bá wa nuu Kɔraawiizi wia la.

ref: When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
text: Jus hina la n wa na nɛkpila la, a ra ɛɛ baa bɔwii werge. Ba ra di Pɔɔl ni Banabas hɔɔzi di ra gbɛlli ba wiŋɔzi.

ref: But Paul and Barnabas bravely said: We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles.
text: Awia, Pɔɔl ni Banabas ŋɔ bampirii ni, “A faa dɛkkɔɔ yaa n ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia tɛɛ ii Jus hina mɔɔ. Yaa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ tɛɛ ia, ka ii vɛɛ di di ii himmaa seriya di ŋɔ ii waa dɛg Kɔraawiizi miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la dɔɔi. Awia, yaa daŋ gil ia filaŋkeŋ, ka la banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ be di ga ŋɔa bá ge nuu.

ref: The Lord has given us this command, “I have placed you here as a light for the Gentiles. You are to take the saving power of God to people everywhere on earth.”
text: Kenne Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ yaa be, ‘N humiibuu í ɛɛ lugɔ fintina di ra chaani banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ, durnya maa wer na lɛɛi.’ ”

ref: This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
text: Banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la n wa nuu guŋ, ba bɔra sɔɔni. Ba ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi wia la. Banla Kɔraawiizi n faa felee lizi bá dɔɔ u miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la yardi Yeesu.

ref: The message about the Lord spread all over this region.
text: Kɔraawiizi wia yaari a bɔr maa.

ref: But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
text: Ka Jus hina la nyiŋŋi haana baŋhina n ɛɛ wiijaama di ɛɛ nɛzenaa ni a bol nabɔnzi baŋhina di lizi amaniye la tɛɛ baa. Ba baana fuuh werge. A birgi tɔɔrɔɔ tɛɛ Pɔɔl ni Banabas. Ba duŋŋi baa ba hɛri.

ref: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
text: Ban duŋŋi baa la, Pɔɔl ni Banabas peezi ba naazi doŋa ha bá zum lugɔ ba benii a lii, ka kpa ba Aikonium.

ref: But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
text: Ka Yeesu hiŋra la n du Antiɔk la bɔra sɔɔni. Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ge du ba ni werge.

ref: Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord.
text: Pɔɔl ni Banabas n ba Aikonium la, ba zuu Jus hina jaamaa dia de di ra bagli baa Kɔraawiizi wia. Ba baglaa la dɔɔ fɔŋŋa. Nɛkpila maa sɛɛ Yeesu wia di yarduu. Jus hina ni Giris hina maanii sɛɛwɛ.

ref: But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
text: Ka Jus hina baŋhina waa yardɛɛ di ŋɔ wikpila tɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la, di chɔg ba wia, ba waa kaa ra tɔgzi baa.

ref: Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
text: Ka Pɔɔl ni Banabas du de guŋŋ di haa vɛɛ ra ŋɔ gunla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ nɛra ni di ra hiini baa. Denii Kɔraawiizi ge ra jaa baa fɔŋŋa ba wer ra ɛɛ wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia nɛra zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ ba ra ŋɔ.

ref: The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles.
text: A bol biini, baŋhina ra hiŋ Jus hinaa, baŋhina ge ra hiŋ Yeesu huŋhunna la. Ba faa waa nuukpaŋ dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
text: Denii banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ baŋhina ni Jus hina ni ba nabɔnzi baŋhina ta jina bɛl bá lɔɔzi baa bia di du baa tɔɔrɔɔ.

ref: In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk.
text: A hɔl bɛl ba ra ŋɔ a wia Listra, di gbɛrii bɛl sogo. U naazi siuzi. Ban luluu maa, gunnɛ u du. Waa wette u vol.

ref: The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man
text: U so di ra nuu gunla Pɔɔl n na ŋɔ. Pɔɔl binnuu tiiih, di zum lugɔ u dɔɔ yardaa un niŋ wer chaau.

ref: and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
text: U ŋɔ u be kpegzi ni, “Izi chi.” U haŋ lɔ izi di ra vol.

ref: When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!”
text: Nɛkpila du de. Baŋ wa na gunla Pɔɔl n ɛɛwɛ la, ba ra kɔɔ werge di ra ŋɔ ba mɔɔri biini, “Vugaa ba yaa be lugɔ newea.”

ref: The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
text: Ba kpa Banabas di ra yir ba vugzeŋ bɛl banna yir Zeyus di kaa kpa Pɔɔl ge di ra yir ba vug bɛl ge banna yir Hɛmɛs, dikuubɛɛwiai, Pɔɔllɛ ɔɔ ra ŋɔ wia.

ref: The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates.
text: Zeyus kuaribɔr faa du a bol nuarɛ. U kizeehiŋ kpa fiiri aŋhina baŋ ɔɔ kpa di mil dɔŋa di kpa laali nɛra di ra kpa baa girme ani naunaa di ba laŋgara di ra nyiŋŋi ú ni a nɛra maa kpu nauna la di kuari a Zeyus ni Hɛmɛs la.

ref: When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
text: Pɔɔl ni Banabas n wa nuu a wia, a tir baa werge maa ba lau ba wɛjɛzi piili ka chɔ zuu nɛkpila la baaŋ di ŋɔ kpegzi ni,

ref: Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
text: “Yaabalaa, bɛɛ wiarɛ ii ra ɛɛ kennei? Neweare yaa maa. Amaniyesumaa yaa kpa ba ii be, di ŋɔ ií gil wipɛɛri naa maa ha ka bir ra hiŋ unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa di ta chiŋ ni hɛri ni muuzeŋ ani kuna la maa n du a biine.

ref: In times past, God let each nation go its own way.
text: Faala la, u faa bir u hattɛ kpu durnya maa ba maa ra hiŋ ba kipar ŋmɛnizi.

ref: But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
text: Ka u faa haa ra ɛɛ yaabuu winanaa, yaa zum lugɔ u haa du denii di ra tɛɛ yaa dooŋ, diwee ra lii yaa ra di, di ra piŋ, yaa bɔra ra sɔɔni.”

ref: Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
text: Haali ban ŋɔ wia naa maa gba, ka ba vuga kuaraa la faa haa aah nɛra la siweere werge maa. Pɔɔl ni Banabas n ŋɔ gunla, ka ba faa haa ra nyiŋŋi ba kuari ba kuaraa labuu guŋŋ ka wa gil.

ref: Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
text: Denii Jus hina baŋhina lii Antiɔk di ba Aikonium di wa ŋɔ wia aŋhina, di wer bir Listra hina liize, ba baana fuuh du Pɔɔl ni. Ba paa bia lɔɔzuu di tuuzuu lii ba bol biini, di ra fɛ lugɔ u siuwɔɔ.

ref: But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe. Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
text: Ka Yeesu hiŋra wa chaali u be di baruu, u izi chiŋ di bir zuu a bol biini. Hɔpizi u ni Banabas la Dɛbɛ. Pɔɔl ni Banabas n bittɛ ba Antiɔk n du Siiria hɛri wia

ref: Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia.
text: Ban du Dɛbɛ la, ba lizi amaniyesuma la tɛɛ ba ge. Nɛkpila sɛɛ Yeesu wia de di ra hiŋ. Ba kaa izi de di bir la Listra ni Aikonium ni Antiɔk

ref: They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.”
text: di gaa du Yeesu hiŋra bɔkpega di ŋɔ ba be, dí ba ra hiŋ Yeesu ŋmɛnɛɛ nɛnnɛ, bá gilɛɛ waa leu, di kaa ŋɔ dí ba daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ werge mɔɔ ka haa wa zuu Kɔraawiizi Kora biini.

ref: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
text: Banna vol bola la, ba ligzi nɛra a bola biini bá ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra nabɔnzi. Baŋ ɔɔ ligzi baa la, ba ɔɔ vɔɔ nuarɛ di suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa ka kpa baa du Kɔraawiizi la baŋ yardɛɛ la nonee ú ra hiini baa.

ref: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
text: Denii ba izi de di ga Pisidia di ra la ga hel Pamfilia hɛri,

ref: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
text: di ŋɔ wiŋɔzi la Pɛga biini, ka kaa ra la Atalia.

ref: and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
text: Baŋ wa lii de, ba zuu muugbera bɛl di bir la Antiɔk. Antiɔk biinii ba faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baa, ú nɛsunaa ni u hiinaa du ba be, bá ra hum huma naa baŋ hummɛ tuŋ naa.

ref: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
text: Baŋ wa ballɛ la, ba chaali Yeesu hiŋra la maa di bagli baa gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n hiini baa di pilli ŋmɛnɛɛ tɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ ba ge wer yardi Yeesu di na lɛɛi.

ref: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
text: Denii ba du Yeesu hiŋra la be de di birgi.

ref: Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught.
text: Nɛra baŋhina lii Juda hɛri di ba Antiɔk di waa ŋɔ babalaa Yeesu hiŋra be, “Di ii waa Moosis Hɔŋ la ra hiŋ di ra teŋri ii hɛna, Kɔraawiizi wàá lɛɛ ia.”

ref: This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders. The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
text: Pɔɔl ni Banabas ra di baa hɔɔzi werge maa dikuu a wii wia. Awia, ba ŋɔ dí a wesso Pɔɔl ni Banabas ni Antiɔk hina baŋhina n la Jɛrusalɛm di ga na Yeesu huŋhunna la ni nabɔnzi la di pɛɛzi baa a wii.

ref: The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy.
text: Ba hum baa, ba ra la. Banna la la, ba ga Fonisia hɛri ni Samaria hɛri di ra la di ra ŋɔ babalaa maa be lugɔ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ jaa bir ba bampireere di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi. Ba amaniye hiŋ gil ba bɔra sɔɔni werge.

ref: When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do.
text: Ba wa hel Jɛrusalɛm. Yeesu hiŋra ni u huŋhunna ni nabɔnzi la maa chaali di jaami baa. Ba bagli gunla maa Kɔraawiizi n hiini baa ba ɛɛ la di tɛɛ baa.

ref: But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
text: Denii Yeesu hiŋra la n ɛɛ Farisizi la izi di ŋɔ, “Di banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ ra nyiŋŋi ba hiŋ, amɔ, i daŋ gil ba teŋri ba hɛna ka ra hiŋ Moosis Hɔŋ la.”

ref: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
text: Yeesu huŋhunna la ni nabɔnzi la chaali dɔŋa di kaa ra ŋɔ a wia,

ref: They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said: My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him.
text: di ra di hɔɔzi. Pitta wa izi di ŋɔ, “Yaabalaa, ii zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi faa lizimbuu ŋɔ ń la ga lizi amaniyesuma la di tɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ bá ge nuu di yardi Yeesu. N ga lizaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us.
text: Kɔraawiizi n wette zum nɛra maa bampiree biini wiarɛ u kpa u Dumnanii di tɛɛ baa gunla uŋ faa kpau tɛɛ yaa la di bagli lugɔ ba wia paruubuu.

ref: God treated them in the same way that he treated us. They put their faith in him, and he made their hearts pure.
text: Waa binnɛɛ lugɔ yaa kuttɔɔ ba ni. Baŋ yardi Yeesu wiarɛ u gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors.
text: Bɛɛ wiarɛ ii ŋɔ ií fir Kɔraawiizi kennei? Ii ŋɔ ií kpa buntɔga naa yaa ni yaa naabaala maa n faa waa wette chi naabuu di chug Yeesu hiŋra laa?

ref: But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
text: Akai! Guŋ waa wer. Yaa n yardi Yeesu u ge suŋ yaa ni di hiini yaa la wiarɛ u lɛɛ yaa. Ba ge gba gunnɛ.”

ref: Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
text: Banla maa n chaali de la waa kaa di baa hɔɔzi, ka jaa ra nuu Banabas ni Pɔɔl be. Ba bagli baa wizenaa ni nuukpuuri wia la Kɔraawiizi n hiini baa ba wer ɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ biini.

ref: After they had finished speaking, James said: My friends, listen to me!
text: Baŋ wa bagli baa tuŋ, Jems ŋɔ, “Yaabalaa, ií nuu n be.

ref: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
text: Saimɔn Pitta ŋɔ yaa benii gunla Kɔraawiizi n felee lizi nɛra tɛɛ u hiŋ durnya maa biini ú sɔŋ du ba ni labuu,

ref: This agrees with what the prophets wrote,
text: dɔgtɛɛzi la maanii faa ŋɔ guŋ di sɛbi Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini di ŋɔ,

ref: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
text: ‘Mìŋ́ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ n daŋ kaa bir ba ii be di wa ma Koori Deevid dia la n faa cholle la. U bɔpurgaa la maanii ń kuari ma ú chi nɛnnɛ,

ref: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
text: Awia, gunla miŋwaa n nawɛɛ, a waa wer yaa n kpa Moosis Gbɔg naa hiŋaa wia di ra tɔɔri banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ ka bir ba bampiree di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la.

ref: We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Ka ií gil ya sɛbi hɔŋ bɛl tɛɛ baa di ŋɔ bá gil vuga wia á gilɛɛ kaa kpa doŋa sag ba ni, di gil sɛnsɛŋ wia ge di gilɛɛ ra di kunla baŋ hanzi u baŋaa u siu ni chal,

ref: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, banla n na bagli Moosis Gbɔg wia du bol maanii. Ba Heezaa Hɔpizii maanii ba karmi u hɔŋ la ba jaamaa diini biini guŋŋ di wa lii ni zinaa.” Hɔŋ baŋ sɛbɛɛ tɛɛ nɛra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ n sɛɛ Yeesu wia la

ref: The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers.
text: Denii Yeesu huŋhunna la ni nabɔnzi la ni Yeesu hiŋra la maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di ŋɔ bá lizi daansɛɛ hina ba biini, bá du Pɔɔl ni Banabas di la Antiɔk. Ba lizi nabɔnzi banɛɛ ba biini. Bɛl sɔnnɛ Judas, ba kaa ra yiruu Basabas. Bɛl ge sɔnnɛ Silas.

ref: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
text: Denii ba sɛbi hɔŋ bɛl di kpa tɛɛ baa. A hɔŋ biini ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Ii balaa Yeesu huŋhunna la ni nabɔnzi la maa ra jaami ia. Yaabalaa la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ di du Antiɔk ni Siiria ni Silisia hɛri la.

ref: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
text: Yaa nuuwɔ lugɔ yaa nɛra baŋhina ŋɔ wia aŋhinaa tɛɛ ia di tɔɔri ia. Ba waa yaa pɛɛzɛɛ mɔɔ ka ŋɔ guŋ. A tir ia. Ii bampiree waa kaa ɛɛ kpaŋ.

ref: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
text: Awiarɛ yaa maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di ŋɔ ya lizi yaa daansɛɛ hina di gil bá du yaa nɛnɔŋŋaa Banabas ni Pɔɔl di ba ii be.

ref: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
text: Banabas ni Pɔɔl ɔɔ ra hum yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo humaa ani bampirkpaŋ. Ba baga lɛi ba miibɔɔni wia, ka ra humaa.

ref: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
text: Yaa lizi Judas ni Silas di hum baa bá wa ŋɔ anniizi tɛɛ ia.

ref: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
text: Yaa ni Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii jinaa keŋ. Yaa ŋɔ yaa wàá kpa wikiilaa maa di tɛɛ ia see anla n niŋ hiini ia.

ref: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
text: Awia, ií ra kii kuna la baŋ kpuwɛɛ di ra tɛɛ vuga ani chal ani kuna la baŋ ɔɔ hanzi a baŋaa a siuzi la ani sɛnsɛŋ wia. Di ii ra kii anniizi, ii daŋ wer dɔɔ nuukpaŋ dɔŋa be. Kɔ́raawiizi hiini ia.”

ref: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
text: Baŋ wa kpa hɔŋ la tɛɛ Pɔɔl ni Banabas waa, ba jaa ta baa. Ba la Antiɔk di ga chaali Yeesu hiŋra maa di kpa hɔŋ la tɛɛ baa bá karmi.

ref: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
text: Baŋ wa karmuu, ba bɔra sɔɔni baabuu, dikuubɛɛwiai, a hɔŋ du baabuu bɔkpega werge.

ref: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
text: Judas ni Silas ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzii. Awia, ba wettoo di ra ŋɔ wikpila Yeesu hiŋra la be, di ra hiini baa di ra du baa bɔkpega.

ref: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
text: Baŋ wa birgi de tama, babalaa la ŋɔ dí ba bir la babalaa la n hum baa la be.

ref: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
text: ka Pɔɔl ni Banabas haa du ba be Antiɔk. Ba ni nɛkpila ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia di ra tɛɛ nɛra di kaa ra bagli nɛra. Pɔɔl ni Banabas dɔŋa bargaa wia

ref: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ tama, Pɔɔl ŋɔ Banabas be, “Gil ya la yaabalaa la maa n du bola la maa yaa n faa gaagɛɛ di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia la be di ga na gunla ba maa n duwɛɛ.”

ref: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
text: Banabas ra nyiŋŋi ŋɔ Jɔɔn la banna yir Maak la hiŋ baa la.

ref: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
text: Ka Pɔɔl faa waa gunna nyiŋŋi. Uŋ faa vɛɛ u huma Pamfilia di bir kpo saŋa la uŋ faa du ba be la wiarɛ Pɔɔl biini waa kaa huuhzi lugɔ ú kaa hiŋ baa la.

ref: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
text: A jaa ɛɛ baa kinchaŋ. Ba bargi dɔŋa ni. Banabas kpa Maak di zuu muugbera bɛl di la Saiprɔs.

ref: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
text: Pɔɔl ge lizi Silas. Yeesu hiŋra suŋŋi wiizi tɛɛ baa di kpa baa du u nonee, ú nɛsunaa ni u hiinaa du ba be.

ref: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
text: Ba wa hel Dɛbɛ ni Listra, di Yeesu hiŋri bɛl faa du de. U sɔnnɛ faa Timoti. U maa faa ɛɛ Jus hinuurɛ di ra hiŋ Yeesu. U mɛɛ ge ɛɛ Giris hinuu.

ref: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
text: Timoti la faa dɔɔ sɔnnɛ babalaa la n du Listra ni Aikonium la be.

ref: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
text: Pɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ Timoti hiŋuu ra la, ka kuu Jus hina la n du de barii la wia di gil ba teŋ Timoti hɛŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maa zummɔɔ u mɛɛ n ɛɛ Giris hinuu.

ref: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
text: Ba kpa ra la. Banna la la, di ba wa zuu bol maa, ba ɔɔ ŋɔ ba be kiizi la Yeesu huŋhunna la ni Jɛrusalɛm hina nabɔnzi n ŋɔwɛɛ la wia,

ref: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
text: di ra du baa bɔkpega bá ra hiŋ nɛnnɛ. Yeesu hiŋra na nɛra di ra jaa hɔpizibii maa. Pɔɔl n na wia lugɔ deeza biini lii Troas wia

ref: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
text: Pɔɔl ni u dɔŋahina ga Firijia ni Galesia barii di ra la, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii waa sɛɛwɛ ba zuu Eesia hɛri di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia de.

ref: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
text: Ba ba Misia di ŋɔ bá zuu Bitinia hɛri ka Yeesu Duma bir baa.

ref: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
text: Ba ga Misia di ra la ga hel Troas.

ref: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
text: Pɔɔl na wia aŋhina hamuŋa ni lugɔ deeza biini. U na Masɛdɔnia hiŋ bɛl n chigɛ di ra fɔrguu di ra ŋɔ, “Ba Masɛdɔnia hɛri di wa hiini yaa.”

ref: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
text: Pɔɔl n wa na a wia tuŋ, u ni yaa ɛɛ sirya ya la de, dikuubɛɛwiai, denii yaa chi zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ra nyiŋŋuu ya la ga lizi amaniyesuma la tɛɛ baa. Lidia nfɛrɛ biraa Filipai biini wia

ref: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
text: Yaa zuu muugbera di lii Troas di deŋli la Samotiresia. Hɔɔ wa pizi yaa kaa izi de la Niapɔlis

ref: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
text: di kaa izi de ge la Filipai. Filipai la ɛɛ Masɛdɔnia hɛri nyuu bɔttɛ u nɛra dɔɔ fɔŋŋa la dee Room hina n dɔɔwɛ la. Yaa birgi de tama.

ref: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
text: Heezaa Hɔpizii n wa helle, yaa lii a bol biini di la muu nua di ga nyiŋŋi bɔr la n ɛɛ wiijaami bɔr di so di ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ haana baŋhina n chaalɛɛ de.

ref: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
text: Haana la n du de di ra nuu yaa wiŋɔzi la bɛl sɔnnɛ faa Lidia. Tayatairaa u lii, di ɛɛ kuna la baŋ ɔɔ lii gara la yoori, di ɛɛ wiijaami. Uŋ wa nuu Pɔɔl wiŋɔzi, Kɔraawiizi pilli u siwee, u wer sɛɛ a wiŋɔzi.

ref: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
text: Yaa sɔ u ni u diahina maa Kɔraawiizi nii. U suŋŋi yaa di ŋɔ, “Di ii yardɔɔ lugɔ n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizii nɛnnɛ, amɔ, ií ba wa du n dia.” Uŋ wa suŋŋi yaa werge, yaa sɛɛ. Ban tɔ Pɔɔl ni Silas di Filipai wia

ref: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
text: A hɔl bɛl yaa ra la a wiijaami bɔr. Yoŋhaaŋ bɛl wa huuzi yaa. Tinnanchɔgii bɛl ɔɔ ra izuu, u ra na sinai di ra vug nɛra. U dɔɔra ra na kebee werge.

ref: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
text: A yoŋhaaŋ ra hiŋ yaa ni Pɔɔl harbɔɔ di pogzi ra ŋɔ, “Baala naa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizizeŋ balaarɛ. Kɔraawiizi miibɔɔ tɛɛi wiŋɔzii ba ŋɔ di ra tɛɛ ia la.”

ref: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
text: Hɔpizii maa u ɔɔ ɛɛ guŋ. A wa bazi Pɔɔl. U bir ŋɔ tinnanchɔgii la n ɔɔ ra izuu la be, “N na ŋɔ i benii Yeesu Kristo sɔŋ biini, wa lii haaŋ naa ni.” A tinnanchɔgii wa lii kakpaŋ.

ref: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
text: U dɔɔra n wa zummɛ lugɔ ba wàá ka na tɔna maa u be la, ba la ga lauri Pɔɔl ni Silas fɔŋŋa ni di tɛrgi baa la ba jaamaa bɔr la ba bol nabɔnzi n ɔɔ chaali la,

ref: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
text: di ra dau naana wia la Room hina n na kii la.”

ref: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
text: Nɛkpila la n du de la maa ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di hiŋ ba nua di ra chagzi baa. A Room sitɔɔra lau ba laala wir ba ni ka ŋɔ dí ba lɔɔzi baa daazi.

ref: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
text: Ba lɔɔzi baa werge ka jaa tɔ baa nɛra tɔi dia, ka ŋɔ a dia nabɔma be di ú ra du ba tau nɛnnɛ ra tɛɛ baa.

ref: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
text: U kpogli baa zuu a nɛra tɔi dia diisee di du ba naazi daazi.

ref: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
text: Hɛuh n wa hɛɛhzɛɛ, Pɔɔl ni Silas ra jaami Kɔraawiizi di yir yira di ra tɛu, a nɛra la baŋ tɔ a dia la ra nuu.

ref: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
text: Denii kakpaŋ hɛri zigli werge maa, a nɛra tɔi dia maa zigli, u dominuuzi maa pilli, banla baŋ tɔ dia la maa yɔlɔzi pur.

ref: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
text: A nɛra tɔi dia nabɔma izi dɔɔ, di a nɛra tɔi dia hiŋ dominuuzi maa pillɔɔ. U pam u kizee di ŋɔ ú kpu u hiŋ. U niikoo a nɛra la baŋ tɔ dia la maa chɔwɔɔrɛ lii.

ref: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
text: Ka Pɔɔl pogzi werge di ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ ɛɛ i hiŋ wiimaa. Yaa maanii haa du de.”

ref: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
text: U ŋɔ dí ba kpa fintinazi ba. Ba kpaa ba. U chɔ zuu ba be. Ɔnsii n lawuu werge wia u bɔra maa ra sa. U chɔɔ hɛri Pɔɔl ni Silas see di ra jaami baa,

ref: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
text: ka izi kpa baa lii di pɛɛzi baa, “Yaabalaa, ɛrɛɛ ń ɛɛ di lɛɛ n hiŋ lii Kɔraawiizi baaŋ biinei?”

ref: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
text: Ba ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia ra tɛɛ u ni banla maa n du u dia.

ref: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
text: Denii u lau baa a hamuŋa hiŋ di yagli ba bɔra baŋ lɔɔzɛɛ a mɔnni la. Ba sɔ u ni u diahina maa Kɔraawiizi nii a hamuŋa hiŋ.

ref: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
text: Denii u lau baa zuu u dia di ɛɛ diwee tɛɛ baa ba di. U ni u diahina maa bɔra sɔɔni werge dikuu baŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wia.

ref: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, Room sitɔɔra la hum ba balaa ba wa ŋɔ nɛra tɔi dia nabɔma la be, “Tɛɛ nɛra la ŋmɛnɛɛ bá lii.”

ref: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
text: U ga ŋɔ Pɔɔl be, “Room sitɔɔra la hum nɛraa ba wa ŋɔ n be dí n tɛɛ ia ŋmɛnɛɛ ii lii. Awia, ií wa lii. Kɔ́raawiizi la ii ni.”

ref: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
text: Ka Pɔɔl bir ŋɔ banla Room sitɔɔra n hummɛ nɛra tɔi dia nabɔma be la, “Baŋ wa di yaa seriya, ba waa nawɛɛ yaa n ɛɛ wichɔgii maa, ka lɔɔzi yaa nɛra baaŋ di tɔ yaa dia. Yaa ɛɛ Room hinaa ka ba ɛɛ yaa guŋ, ka jaa ra nyiŋŋi ba suahzi lizi yaa. Akai. Màá sɛɛ guŋ. Ií ga ŋɔ ba be bá himmaa wa lizi yaa.”

ref: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
text: A nɛra bir la ga ŋɔ guŋ Room sitɔɔra la be di bagli baa lugɔ ba ɛɛ Room fɔŋŋa diiree. A sitɔɔra n wa nuu guŋ, kafɔŋ lau baa.

ref: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
text: Ba izi la ga fɔrgi baa bá gil tɛɛ baa ka lau baa lii di suŋŋi baa werge lugɔ bá izi kaali.

ref: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
text: Baŋ lii a nɛra tɔi dia biini, ba ga zuu Lidia dia. Baŋ wa na babalaa la maa, ba du baa bɔkpega ka izi ra la.

ref: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
text: Banna la hiŋ ba ga Amfipɔlis ni Apɔlɔnia di ga hel Tɛsalɔnika. Jus hina jaamaa dia bɛl du denii.

ref: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
text: Pɔɔl zuu ba be jaamaa dia la biini gunla uŋ ɔɔ ra ɛɛ bola maa la. Gunnɛ u ɛɛ ba Heezaa Hɔpizaa ahoro maa

ref: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
text: di ra di baa hɔɔzi di ra bagli baa Kristo wia lii Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, bá zum lugɔ Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la faa baglɔɔrɛ lugɔ Kristo daŋ wa di tɔɔrɔɔ di siu ka izi siu biini. Uŋ wa bagli baa guŋ, u ŋɔ, “Yeesu naa miŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ u wia di ra tɛɛ ia naa, waabuu a Kristo.”

ref: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
text: Baŋhina sɛɛ tɛu. Giris wiijaama kpila ni hahgandawa kpila maa sɛɛ di wa jaa u ni Silas ni.

ref: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
text: Denii Jus hina bɔra ra wii. Ba ga nyiŋŋi nɛkpakpalli baŋhina n ɔɔ du yawa bɔr la bá hiini baa. Ba chaali nɛra werge di koozi a bol maa u ra kɔɔ. Ba la Jasɔn dia bá ga lau Pɔɔl ni Silas lii di tɛɛ nɛra la

ref: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
text: di ga nyiŋŋi baa huhzi de, ka lau Jasɔn ni Yeesu hiŋra baŋhina, di tɛrgi baa la ba bol nabɔnzi be, di wa ŋɔ, “Nɛra la n ɔɔ vol di ra koozi wia la ba bɔnnaa gbaa.

ref: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
text: Jasɔn gil ba wa du u dia. Ba maa ra chɔgi yaa Koorizeŋ Siiza gbɔgnii di ra ŋɔ dí koori bɛllɛ kaa du de. Waabuu Yeesu.”

ref: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
text: Nɛkpila la ni bol nabɔnzi la n wa nuu guŋ, a tir baa.

ref: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
text: Ba gil Jasɔnwaa dau kebee mɔɔ ka ba gil baa ba lii. Pɔɔl ni Silas n la Biria wia

ref: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
text: Denii Yeesu hiŋra la ɛɛ manaŋ di ta Pɔɔl ni Silas ŋmɛnɛɛ hamuŋa ni bá la Biria. Ba la Biria di ga zuu Jus hina jaamaa dia de.

ref: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
text: Jus hina la n du de la waa dignikpega hina ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Tɛsalɔnika Jus hina la. Ba aah siwii di ra nuu wiŋɔzi la di ra pessi Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini wia hɔpizibii maa bá zum, di ba wiŋɔzi la ɛɛ wibii gɛɛ a waa wibii ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
text: Bakpila maa yardi ba wiŋɔzi hiŋ. Giris hahgandawa kpila ni baala kpila gba yardi.

ref: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
text: Tɛsalɔnika Jus hina n wa nuuwɛ lugɔ Pɔɔl kaa ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia Biria, ba izi la de ge di gaa ɛɛ nɛra ba baana ra fuuh.

ref: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
text: Denii Yeesu hiŋra la ɛɛ manaŋ di ta Pɔɔl ŋmɛnɛɛ dí ú ra la muuzeŋ la barii, ka Silas ni Timoti ge so a bol.

ref: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
text: Baŋhina du Pɔɔl ra la ga hel Atɛns maa, ka Pɔɔl ŋɔ dí ba bir la ga ŋɔ Silas ni Timoti be, dí ba ba u be manaŋ. Ba kaali. Pɔɔl ni Silas n la Atɛns wia

ref: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
text: Pɔɔl n du Atɛns di ra kpaŋ baa la, u binni di vugaa gbigi de maa. U biini chɔgi.

ref: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
text: U izi la ba jaamaa dia di ga di Jus hina ni wiijaama la n du de la hɔɔzi di ɔɔ ra la jaamaa bɔr hɔpizibii maa di ga ŋɔ wia ra tɛɛ banla maa uŋ ɔɔ huuzi de la.

ref: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
text: Banla n na hiŋ Ɛpikurus ni Stois ŋmɛnɛɛ la waa diu hɔɔzi di pɛɛzi, “Bɛɛ wiŋɔzii wiŋɔbala naa hiŋ ge ra ŋɔ kennei?” Baŋhina ge ŋɔ, “Vuga aŋhina yaa n waa a wia zummɛ wiarɛ u ra ŋɔ.” Unna ŋɔ Yeesu ni siu biini izaa wia werge wiarɛ ba ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
text: Ba ga lawuu di la ba seriya diiribɔr bɛl banna yir Arɛɔpagus di wa ŋɔ u be, “Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ya kaa nuu baglifalii la hinna bagli la.

ref: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
text: Wia la yaa n nuuwɛ i be la tir yaabuu. Awia, yaa ra nyiŋŋuu ya zum a zɛɛ nɛnnɛ.”

ref: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
text: Gunnɛ Atɛns hina ni ba hɔɔhra ɔɔ ra ɛɛ. Ba ɔɔ aah siwiire bá nuu wifalaa di kaa aah siwii bá ŋɔ ba hor.

ref: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
text: Denii Pɔɔl lii chi Arɛɔpagus la baambaaŋ di ŋɔ, “Atɛns hina, mim binni ii wia maa, n zummɔ lugɔ ii ra tɔgzi wiarɛ werge,

ref: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, n gaagi ii bol maanii, di na ii mbusu lizibɔra ni ii vuga, di wa na mbusu lizibɔr bɛl iim mawɛɛ, ka sɛbi wia aŋhina di du u ni, dí Kɔraawiizi la iiŋ waa zummɛ la mbusu lizibɔttɛ keŋ. A Kɔraawiizi la iiŋ ŋɔ ii waa zummɛ ka ra jaamuu la, u wiarɛ n ŋɔ ń ŋɔ tɛɛ ia la.

ref: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
text: Kɔraawiizi la n ta hɛri ni kummaa n du u ni di kaa ɛɛ chiŋ ni hɛri maa dɔɔri la, waabuu waa ɔɔ ra zuu diini la newea n mawɛɛ a ɛɛ jaamaa diini la.

ref: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
text: A waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ newea n hum huma di ra tɛu wiarɛ u wer du de. Akai. Waabuu ra tɛɛ newea miibɔɔ. U benii nɛra maa na ba heeza ni ba kummaa.

ref: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
text: Nɛkpannɛ u faa ta. Newea maa ni ba dee maa lii u ni di yaari hɛri maa. Kɔraawiizi feloore dau ba maa saŋazi ni ba duuribɔra.

ref: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
text: U ɛɛ gunnɛ bá ra nyiŋŋi u bɔr di ra largi bɔr maa bá nau. Ka Kɔraawiizi waa bɔɔnɛɛ duwɛɛ. U dugli yaa maanii.

ref: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
text: Baŋ ɔɔ ŋɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa wiarɛ yaa maa wer du de di ra heezi di ra hum huma la, wibiire ba ɔɔ ŋɔ. Ii nɛra la n ɔɔ ra sɛbi hɔna la gba di wibiire di ŋɔ, ‘Yaa gba ɛɛ u biizii.’

ref: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
text: Di yaa ɛɛ u biizi, a waa dɛkkɛ yaa n kaa ra binni lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ɛɛ kuna la nɛra n kpa saliŋ ni lugbia ni bia di kpa nfɛrɛ kuari labuu.

ref: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
text: Kɔraawiizi faa waa nɛra wichɔgaa wia ra hagzi saŋa la baŋ faa waa u wia zummɛ la. Ka filaŋkeŋ u ra karfi nɛr maanii yemmaa dí ba gil ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia di gilaa ha,

text: dikuubɛɛwiai, u lizi hɔpiziirɛ dau un niŋ di durnya nɛra maa seriya di di wibii tɛɛ baa, di kaa lizi nɛr la n niŋ wa di baa seriya la. U lalli a hinnɛ siu biini ya zum lugɔ wia naa ɛɛ wibiire.”

ref: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ siu biini izaa la wia, baŋhina jaa ra ɛɛu chɛɛtɛ. Baŋhina ge ra ŋɔ, “Yaa haa ra nyiŋŋuu ya nuu i wiŋɔzi hiŋ.”

ref: When Paul left the council meeting,
text: Denii Pɔɔl izi lii ba biini di kaali.

ref: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
text: Nɛra baŋhina ba wa jaa u ni di ra hiŋuu di sɛɛ u wiŋɔzi la. Bɛl sɔnnɛ faa Dionisius. U faa ɛɛ Arɛɔpagus seriya diiri bɛllɛ. Bɛl ge ɛɛ haaŋ. U sɔnnɛ faa Damaris. Ba ni baŋhina jaa u ni.

ref: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
text: Denii Pɔɔl izi Atɛns di la Kɔrint

text: di ga huuzi Jus hinuu bɛl n faa lii Pɔntus di la ga so Room, ka kaa izi Room ge di ba Kɔrint dikuu Klaudius n duŋŋi Jus hina maa Room biini wia. U sɔnnɛ Akuila. U haaŋ ge sɔnnɛ Pirsila. Pɔɔl la ba dia di ga jaami baa,

ref: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
text: di du ba dia di ra hum, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maa faa ra hum humkpannɛ. Tantizii ba faa ra kuari.

ref: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.

ref: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
text: Silas ni Timoti n wa lii Masɛdɔnia hɛri ba, Pɔɔl jaa wer izi di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi wia daansɛɛ nɛnnɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra. A du u bampiriire werge. U ra ŋɔ Jus hina be lugɔ Yeesu la ɛɛ a Kristoo.

ref: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
text: Ka baŋ waa nyiŋŋi ba chɔgi u huma di ra gbɛlluu la, u lau u wɛjɛ zigli ka ŋɔ, “A wia lii ii benii. Ii wichɔgaa laŋŋi ii ni. N ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ tɛɛ ia, ii vɛɛ. Awia, n daŋ la banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la be.”

ref: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, u gil baa ka kaali wiijaami bɛl dia n dugli a jaamaa dia. A baal sɔnnɛ faa Titiɔs Justus.

ref: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
text: Jaamaa dia nabɔma Krispus ni u diahina maa yardi Yeesu. Nɛkpila maa n du Kɔrint nuu wiŋɔzi la di sɛɛ di yardi u wiŋɔzi hiŋ ka ba sɔ baa Kɔraawiizi nii.

ref: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
text: A hɔl bɛl hamuŋa ni Pɔɔl na wia aŋhina lugɔ deeza biini. Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ u be, “Gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Haa ra ŋɔ n wiŋɔzi di ra tɛɛ nɛra. Gilɛɛ siigi.

ref: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
text: N chigɔ i hattɛ. N dɔɔ nɛkpila maanii bol naa biini. Awia, n daŋ kissii kpɛrɛkpɛrɛ ni.”

ref: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
text: Denii Pɔɔl du de biŋkpaŋ ni baaguzi anumbɛl di ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia ra tɛɛ nɛra.

ref: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
text: Saŋa la Galio n di nabɔmuu Akaaya la, Jus hina ɛɛ nuukpaŋ di ra tɔɔri Pɔɔl, di lawuu ba ba seriya diiri dia

text: di wa ŋɔ, “Guŋ la baal naa n na bagli nɛra ŋɔ bá ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la, guŋ daŋ gil ba ra chɔgi yaa kiizi.”

ref: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
text: Pɔɔl ra nyiŋŋi u ŋɔ u hor, ka Galio ŋɔ Jus hina la be, “Aa! Ii Jus hina naa! Di baal naa vii hum hunchɔgii bɛllɛ, n daŋ vii di kanyitti di nuu tɛɛ ia.

ref: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
text: Ka ii himmaa wiazi ni nɛra sɔna ni ii kiizi wiarɛ ii ba. Awia, màá di wia naa seriya. Ií himmaa binni a biini.”

ref: Then he sent them out of the court.
text: U duŋŋi ba maa ba lii a seriya dia biini.

ref: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
text: Denii nɛra lau jaamaa dia nabɔma Sɔstɛnis di ra lɔɔzuu. A seriya dii dia danzɛɛ kɛriirɛ ba faa ra lɔɔzuu la, ka Galio waa baa hagzɛɛ maa. Pɔɔl ni Silas n bittɛ ba Antiɔk wia

ref: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
text: Pɔɔl haa birgi babalaa hiŋ be a bol mɔɔ ka haa lii ba be. U ni Pirsila ni Akuila zuu muugbera bɛl di ra la Siiria hɛri. Pɔɔl faa lɛɛ nua bɛllɛ. Awia, Sɛŋkiriaa ba fuŋ u nyuu mɔɔ ka ba ra la

ref: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
text: di ga hel Ɛfɛsus. Pɔɔl gil Pirsila ni Akuila de ka ga zuu jaamaa dia di ra di Jus hina hɔɔzi.

ref: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
text: Ba ŋɔ dí ú so a bol tama. U vɛɛ

text: di ga hel Siizaria, di lii di la Jɛrusalɛm ga jaami Yeesu hiŋra de ka la Antiɔk.

ref: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
text: U ga birgi de tama, ka lii de di ra gaagi bola Galesia hɛri ni Firijia hɛri maa di ra du Yeesu hiŋra maa bɔkpega di ra la.

ref: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
text: Denii Jus hinuu bɛl n lii Alɛgzandria ba Ɛfɛsus. U sɔnnɛ faa Apɔlɔs. U zum wia ŋɔirɛ werge di wer di ra bagli Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ wia nɛnnɛ.

ref: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
text: U faa helli Yeesu ŋmɛnɛɛ wiarɛ. A du u bampirii werge, u ra ŋɔa, a maa ra deŋli. Ka niisɔɔlii la wia uŋ ɔɔ ra bagli la, Jɔɔn niisɔɔliirɛ. U bɛŋ wiarɛ u zum.

ref: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
text: U ba Ɛfɛsus di waa ŋɔ wia Jus hina jaamaa dia biini ni bɔkpega ni. Pirsila ni Akuila du de di nuu di lawuu la ba dia di ga bagluu Kɔraawiizi wia la uŋ faa waa zummɛ ú ra ŋɔa á ra deŋli nɛnnɛ.

ref: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Denii Apɔlɔs ra nyiŋŋi u la Akaaya. Babalaa duu bɔkpega ú ra la di sɛbi hɔŋ tɛu ú ga tɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra la n du de bá sɛɛ di lɛɛu. U la de di ga wer hiini banla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ ba ni di hiini ba wer yarduu la werge,

ref: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
text: Denii Apɔlɔs n wa du Kɔrint la, Pɔɔl ga a hɛri baaŋ di ba Ɛfɛsus, di wa huuzi Yeesu hiŋra baŋhina de

ref: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
text: di pɛɛzi baa, “Iiŋ yardi Yeesu, ii na Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii lii u bee?” Ba ŋɔ, “Akai. Yaa waa u wia zummɛ gba.”

ref: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
text: U kaa pɛɛzi baa, “Ban sɔ ia Kɔraawiizi nii, niisɔi bɛlii deere ba sɔ iai?” Ba ŋɔ, “Jɔɔn niisɔi labuu ba sɔ yaa.”

ref: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
text: Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Jɔɔn ɔɔ faa ŋɔu lugɔ nɛ́ra gil ba biine chɔgi dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia di gilaa ha ka ú sɔ baa Kɔraawiizi nii, ka ŋɔ, ‘Nɛbɛl du n hattɛ di ra ba. Di u wa ballɔ, ií yardi a hiŋ. Waabuu Yeesu.’ ”

ref: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: Ɛfɛsus hina la n wa nuu guŋ, ba gil ba sɔ baa Kɔraawiizi nii bá ra hiŋ Yeesu.

ref: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
text: Pɔɔl kpa u nonee sag ba ni. Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii zuu ba ni. Ba ra mɔɔ mɔɔdumazi di ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia u fɔŋŋa biini.

ref: There were about twelve men in this group.
text: Ba faa du nɛra fidibanɛɛ.

ref: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
text: Pɔɔl ɔɔ zuu ba jaamaa dia di ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ni bampirsi ni baaguzi ahoro maa biini di ra di nɛra hɔɔzi di fɔrgi baa bá sɛɛ a wiŋɔzi.

ref: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
text: Ka baŋhina waa sɛɛwɛ tɛu dikuu ba dignikpega wia. Ba waa sɛɛwɛ ba hiŋ Kɔraawiizi nua, ka ra gbɛlli u Ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋaa nɛkpila maa be. Awia, Pɔɔl gil baa ka lau Yeesu hiŋra la bargi lii ba be, di la Tiranus sukuru, di jaa di nɛra mmɔri a sukuru biini.
