text: Gunnɛ u bagli baa de hɔpizibii maa guŋŋ binni anɛɛ maa biini. Jus hina ni Giris hina la maa n du Eesia hɛri nuu Kɔraawiizi wia.

ref: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa kpa fɔŋŋa du Pɔɔl ni u wer di ra ɛɛ wizenaa,

ref: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
text: haali nɛra kpa aŋkitizi ni kirsɔɔzi uŋ gbɔgzɛɛ di ga tɛɛ ba wiila hina ba nyaagi, tinnanchɔgaa ge lii ba ni.

ref: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
text: Jus baala baŋhina faa gaagi kpa Yeesu sɔŋ di ra duŋŋi tinnanchɔgaa la. Ba ɔɔ ŋɔ tinnanchɔgaa la be, “Yeesu la Pɔɔl n ɔɔ ra ŋɔ u wia la sɔŋ biini, ií wa lii.”

ref: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
text: Jus hinuu bɛl baŋ faa ra yir Skiva, u faa ɛɛ ba Kizeehina nabɔma bɛl, biibaala baniidaanɛɛrɛ faa gaagɛɛ ra ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
text: A hɔl bɛl, baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tinnanchɔgii hiŋ bɛl be, u ŋɔ ba be, “N zum Yeesuu, di kaa zum Pɔɔl ge. Ka maa iawaa zummɛ.”

ref: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
text: Tinnanchɔgii hiŋ la izi di lɔɔzi baa werge di kpegli baa di vɛgzi ba laala haazi. Ba ni ŋmɛra ni bɔwiilazi chɔ kaali.

ref: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: Jus hina ni Giris hina maa n du Ɛfɛsus nuu a wia. Ɔnsii lau baa. Ba ra tɔgzi yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu sɔŋ.

ref: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
text: Banla n yardɛɛ la kpila maa ba di waa huuhzi ba biine di ra sɛɛ chɔgri Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
text: Baŋhina faa ra hum ziŋgaabo humaa. Ba kpa ba hɔna maa di wa fuuh nɛkpila maa see ka kur ba hɔna la kebee, a hel ba kebinanaa kagbonzi bɔra adunu.

ref: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
text: Kennaa baŋ ɛɛwɛ naa gillɔɔ Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii ra yaari bɔr maa di wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di ra jaa.

ref: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
text: Denii Pɔɔl fɛ nfɛrɛ lugɔ a dɛkkɔ uŋ ga Masɛdɔnia ni Akaaya di la Jɛrusalɛm, di ŋɔ, “Di n wa la Jɛrusalɛm naa, n daŋ la Room ge.”

ref: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
text: U hum u balaa Timoti ni Ɛrastus bá la Masɛdɔnia hɛri, ka ge du Eesia hɛri di birgi tama.

ref: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
text: A saŋa, dɔm izi Ɛfɛsus dikuu Yeesu hiŋaa wia.

ref: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
text: Luuri bɛl du de. U sɔnnɛ faa Dimitrius. U ɔɔ kpa lugbii di luu kuna lugɔ ba vugzeŋ bɛl banna yir Diana. U ni babalaa ɔɔ ra na kebee werge maa ba huma hiŋ biini.

ref: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
text: Denii Dimitrius yirgi babalaa ni banla maa n du a huma biini di ŋɔ ba be, “Yaabalaa, ii zummɔ lugɔ huma naa biinii yaa daama ra lii.

ref: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ ii siwee ra na, ii digna ge ra nuu gunla Pɔɔl n na bagli nɛra ɛŋ. Ɛfɛsus bɛŋ lɛi u ra ɛɛ guŋ. Eesia hɛri maanii u ra ɛɛ guŋ di ra bir nɛkpila bampiree ba ra sɛɛ gunla unna ŋɔ la. Kenne u ɔɔ ra ŋɔ, dí kuna la newea n ɔɔ luu la waa vuga ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
text: Unna ŋɔ kennaa, nɛra daŋ waa gbɛlli yaa huma naa, yáa vugzeŋ Diana jaami dia ge bir pɛɛ, ú himmaa ta. Wàá ka na girme. Eesia hɛri hina ni durnya maa n na maŋkuruu kennaa, a guŋ wàá du wer.”

ref: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: A nɛkpila n wa nuu guŋ, ba baana fuuh werge maa. Ba izi di ra pogzi werge di ra ŋɔ, “Aa! Yaa Ɛfɛsus hina dɔɔri vughaaŋ Diana ɛɛ vugzenne.”

ref: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
text: Dɔm izi a bolzeŋ hina maa. Nɛra lau Masɛdɔnia hina baŋhina n du Pɔɔl ba, ba sɔnaa Geyus ni Aristakus, di taagi baa la ba jaamaa bɔzeŋ bɛl.

ref: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
text: Pɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋi u la ga zuu a nɛra biini, ka Yeesu hiŋra waa sɛɛwɛ ú la de.

ref: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
text: Eesia hɛri nabɔnzi baŋhina ɛɛ Pɔɔl dammuzii, ba hum nɛra bá ga fɔrguu di ú jaande maa, ú gilɛɛ waa zuu a nɛra biini.

ref: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
text: Ka a nɛra du de di ra kɔɔ basabasa. Baŋhina ra ŋɔ wii naa, baŋhina ge ra ŋɔ annii. Ka ba galga maa waa zum wii la n baani ba ba de.

ref: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
text: A nɛra baŋhina gil Jus hina daansɛɛ hiŋ bɛl banna yir Alɛgzanda la lii. U vig baa nonii bá siigi.

ref: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Ka baŋ wa zummɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ Jus hinuurɛ, ba maa kpa loobikpaŋ di ra pogzi di ra ŋɔ, “Aa! Aa! Yaa Ɛfɛsus hina Dɔɔri Diana ɛɛ vugzenne.” Ba pogzi guŋŋ haali karfizi anɛɛ maa biini.

ref: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
text: Ba kupo jaa wa lii di ra laafi baa. Ba siigi. U ŋɔ ba be, “Ɛfɛsus hina, ií ra nuu ɛŋ. Nɛr maa zummɔ lugɔ yaa bolle dɔɔ yaa dɔɔri Diana jaamidia ni u vugbii la n lii chiŋ di chol hɛri la.

ref: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
text: A waa bilii dɔɔwɛ. Awia, ií gil a kɔɔi filaŋkeŋ di gilɛɛ fir ɛɛ wii la iiŋ waa zummɛ.

ref: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
text: Nɛra naa waa yaa dɔɔri jaamidia kummaa ŋmɛɛwɛ. Ba wɔɔ kaa gbɛlli ge, ka ii lau baa ba ɛŋ.

ref: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
text: Di Dimitrius ni u dɔŋahina dɔɔ ba wii, seriya dii dia la pillɔɔrɛ zinaa. A sitɔɔra ge du de. Ii gil ba la gaa sami dɔŋa.

ref: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
text: Di ba ga ɛɛ guŋ tuŋ di wii bɛl haa du de, a hɔl la nabɔnzi n wa chaalɛɛ la, bá kpa ŋɔ ba be.

ref: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
text: Ka kennaa iinna ɛɛ zinaa naa, ba daŋ kpaa pɛɛzi yaa. Di ba kpaa pɛɛzi yaa, yaa ge n waa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ ya ŋɔ naa, ba daŋ ŋɔ dí yaabuu gillɛ nɛra ra izi dɔm.”

ref: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u ta nɛra la, ba lii.

ref: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
text: A dɔm n wa sɔɔnɛɛ, Pɔɔl yir Yeesu hiŋra, ba ba. U du baa bɔkpega ka gil baa ka la Masɛdɔnia hɛri

ref: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
text: di gaa gaagi de maa di bagli baa gunla ban ninna hiŋ, ka kaa lii de di la Giris hɛri,

ref: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
text: di ga di baaguzi ahoro de ka kaa ra nyiŋŋi u zuu muugbera bɛl di la Siiria hɛri ka Jus hina ta jina bɛl bá lawuu. Awia, u kaa ŋɔ ú ga Masɛdɔnia hɛri di izi kpa ra la.

ref: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
text: Pirus biibaal Sɔpatɛr n lii Biria la hiŋuu ra la. Tɛsalɔnika hina Aristakus ni Sɛkundus, Geyus la n lii Dɛbɛ la, Timoti, Eesia hɛri hina Tichikus ni Trɔfimus la

ref: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
text: tɔ yaa see di gaa kpaŋ yaa Troas.

ref: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
text: Ba hɔpizaa la baŋ ɔɔ ra di Paanuu La N Waa Yiisi Dɔɔwɛ hɔpizizenaa la n wa bɛrɛɛ, yaa izi Filipai di zuu muugbera bɛl di du nii la biini hɔpizaa anue ka ga huuzi baa Troas di du de hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Pɔɔl Troas laŋaa tuna wia

ref: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
text: Alaadi hɔl yaa maa chaali di di. Pɔɔl ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ hɔpizi ú kaali. Awia, u ni baa ŋɔ wia guŋŋ hɛuh wa hɛɛhzi.

ref: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
text: Yaa maa faa du dia bɛl n du chiŋ biini, di faa choŋŋi fintinakpila de di so.

ref: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
text: Biipɔllii bɛl so tokoro nua. U sɔnnɛ faa Yutikus. Denii dɔɔ wa lawuu ka Pɔɔl faa haa ra ŋɔ wia la haali guŋŋ u chɔɔ dɔɔ la di wa ziigi lii chinchiŋ dia la wa chol bossee. Ba tuu ga lalluu di u siuwɔ.

ref: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
text: Pɔɔl ge tuu di ga chɔɔ u ni di faamuu ka ŋɔ a nɛra be, “Ií gilɛɛ kaa ra fɔŋ. U dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛ.”

ref: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
text: U kaa tinni di zuu a dia di mɔnni paanuu di di, ka u ni baa haa ŋɔ wia la guŋŋ, hɔɔ wa pizi, u kaali.

ref: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
text: Ba kpa biipɔllii la di la dia. Ba bampiree jaa tig werge dikuu uŋ izi siu biini la wia. Pɔɔl n lii Troas di la Mailitus wia

ref: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
text: Yaa ge zuu muugbera bɛl di la Asɔs ya ga kpa Pɔɔl di du yaa be de. U faa ra nyiŋŋuu u vol di la de. Awiarɛ u ŋɔ dí ya ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
text: Uŋ ga chem yaa ni Asɔs la, yaa lawuu du yaa be a muugbera biini di ra la ga hel Mitilini.

ref: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
text: Hɔpizi yaa kaa lii de di ga hel Kiɔs. Hɔɔ kaa pizi yaa hel Samɔs. Hɔɔ n kaa pizi ge yaa hel Mailitus.

ref: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
text: Yaa bɛri Ɛfɛsus ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, Pɔɔl faa ra nyiŋŋuu u wer hel Jɛrusalɛm manaŋ di huuzi ba hɔpizizeŋ Pɛntikɔs Hɔpizizeŋ la. U faa waa nyiŋŋi u birgi Eesia hɛri.

ref: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
text: Ka uŋ wa hel Mailitus la, u tili Ɛfɛsus hina be di yir Yeesu hiŋra nabɔnzi, ba ba u be.

ref: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
text: U ŋɔ ba be, “Ii himmaa zum gunla miŋ faa duwɛɛ saŋa la miŋ faa ba Eesia hɛri la guŋŋ di wa hel zinaa.

ref: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
text: N kpa n hinnɛ fugzi di ra hum n Dɔɔri huma. N biini ɔɔ faa ra chɔguu werge dikuu ii wia n na wii. Jus hina ge ɔɔ faa ra tɔɔriŋ di ra ta ba jinazi,

ref: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
text: ka maa n huma la vɛɛwɛ ka bagli ia wia la maa n niŋ hiini ia. Maa wiimaa kpawɛɛ suah ii ni. N bagli nɛraa jaamaa bɔra di kaa bagli baŋhina nɛra diini.

ref: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
text: Filaŋkeŋ n na la Jɛrusalɛmnɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii kpa de laŋaarɛ du n bampirii. Wàá gil n vɛɛ. Maa zum wii la maa n niŋ ga huuziŋ de.

ref: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
text: Keŋ bɛnnɛ n zum. Bol la maa miŋ ɔɔ la, Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ɔɔ baglimbuu lugɔ tɔɔrɔɔ ni yɔlɔzii chɔɔ de di ra guŋŋ.

ref: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Ka n baga lɛi n miibɔɔ wia. N Dɔɔri Yeesu huma la un lizɛɛ dawiŋ la, aabuu n na binni ń wer humaa tuŋ. U ŋɔ dí n di daansɛɛ tɛɛ nɛra, bá zum amaniyesuma la wia lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ suŋ ba ni di hiini baa.

ref: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
text: Filaŋkennaa, n zummɔ lugɔ ii bannii miŋ faa ɔɔ du ii be di bagli Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ra tɛɛ la la, ii wàá ka wa naŋ maa.

ref: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
text: Awia, n ŋɔ ń ŋɔ ii benii zinaa lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋaa wiimaa waa hoo miŋ waa sɛɛwɛ bagli ia.

ref: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
text: Awia, ii wiimaa waa kaa hoo n nonee ban niŋ wa kpa pɛɛziŋ.

ref: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
text: Awia, ií ra du iihinaa tau, di ra du Kɔraawiizi peeza la ge u Dumnanii n ŋɔ ií ɛɛ a binna la tau. Kɔraawiizi kpa u himmaa challɛ yau baa. Awia, ií ra binni ba ni nɛnnɛ.

ref: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
text: Minna kaali naa, n zummɔ lugɔ nɛchɔgaa daŋ zuu ii biini lugɔ pir sechɔgaa n ɔɔ zuu peeza ni di lauraa la,

ref: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
text: ii baŋhina ge izi di ŋɔ wichɔgaa di ra dar nɛra bá gil Yeesu hiŋaa ka ra hiŋ ia.

ref: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
text: Awiarɛ n ŋɔ ií ra du tau nɛnnɛ la di gilɛɛ waa suuh binni ahoro la miŋ faa du ii be di bagli ia saŋa maa di ɔɔ ra wii dikuu ii wia la.

ref: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, n kpa iabuu du Kɔraawiizi nonee biini, ú kpogli ia nɛnnɛ, di gil u nɛsunaa wiŋɔzi zuu ii bampiree nɛnnɛ, di hiini ia ií wer du kpeg, di wer di u suma la un dauwɛ tɛɛ banla maa un lizi doŋa maa ba ni ha, ba ɛɛ u bɛŋ hora la.

ref: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
text: N faa waa ii kebee ni ii kummaa kɛkɛluu ra ɛɛ.

ref: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
text: Ii zummɔ lugɔ miŋ faa du ii be la, n himmaa kuuhni biinii n faa ra di n diwee di ra tɛɛ n balaa ge ba ge ra di.

ref: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
text: N ɛɛ annii naa maanii ń bagli ia gunla ii ge n ninna ɛɛ di ra hiini banla maa n waa kpeg di ra liizi yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu wiŋɔzi la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la, ‘Hinna sunzi nɛra kuna, aabuu niŋ tɛi bɔsɔna kaali hinna lɛɛ kuna nɛra be.’ ”

ref: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
text: Pɔɔl n wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, u giŋŋi hɛri, u ni ba maa ra jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
text: Ba ra wii werge ka lawuu di ra jaamuu.

ref: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
text: Ba biine chɔgi werge maa dikuu uŋ ŋɔ ba be dí ba wàá ka nau maa la wia. Baŋ wa jaamuu tuŋ, ba duu la muugbera la zɛɛ.

ref: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
text: Yaa n wa bargi dɔŋa, yaa zuu a muugbera di deŋli di la Kɔs. Hɔpizi yaa la Roods di kaa lii de ge di la Patara,

ref: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
text: di ga na muugbera bɛl de unna la Fonisia, di zuu u ge di ra la.

ref: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
text: Yaa n waa dugli hɛrjiga bɛl banna yir Saiprɔs, yaa ga u wiifurii nodig wiikakag di la Siiria hɛri di ga chi Taaya. Muugbera hiŋ la ra lizi u bunni de,

ref: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
text: A saŋa n wa helle, yaa kaa izi de. Ba ni ba haana ni ba biizi maa du yaa ŋmɛnɛɛ di ga lii a bol biini. Yaa maa giŋŋi muuzeŋ la kɛrii di jaami Kɔraawiizi, ka ba ta yaa.

ref: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
text: Yaa zuu muugbera la ka ba ge kaali ba diini.

ref: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
text: Yaa lii Taaya la di ba wa hel Tɔlɛmayis di lii a muugbera biini di ga jaami yaabalaa de ka du ba be hɔpizikpaŋ.

ref: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
text: Hɔpizi yaa kaa zuu muugbera la di la Siizaria di lii ga zuu Filip dia di du de. A Filip ɛɛ nɛra baniidaanɛɛ la baŋ faa lizɛɛ Jɛrusalɛm la bɛllɛ. U ɔɔ faa gaagi ra ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi wia.

ref: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
text: Yaa birgi de. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ bɛl lii Juda hɛri ba. U sɔnnɛ faa Agabus.

ref: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
text: U ba yaa be di wa lau Pɔɔl kirsɔɔ pur, di kpau vɔɔ u himmaa nonee ni u naazi ka ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ŋɔ dí kenne Jus hina la n du Jɛrusalɛm la wa lau kirsɔɔ naa hiŋ di vɔɔu, di kpau du nɛra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ nonee biini la.”

ref: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
text: Yaa n wa nuu guŋ, yaa ni banla maa n du de la maa ra fɔrgi Pɔɔl werge ú gilɛɛ waa la Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
text: Ka Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ ii ra ɛɛ keŋ di ra wii di ra chɔg n biini gunnɛi? Di ba daŋ lawiŋ vɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm, bá lau! Di ba daŋ kaa kpuŋ genii bá kpu. Di ba daŋ haŋ ɛɛŋ annii maa dikuu n Dɔɔri Yeesu sɔŋ wia, a wan titte. N feloore sɛɛ annii naa maa n bampirii.”

ref: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
text: Yaa fɔrguu huhzi ka giluu ka ŋɔ, “Di Kɔraawiizi kiparuu guŋ, amɔ, í ra la.”

ref: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
text: Denii yaa ɛɛ sirya ka izi di la Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
text: Yeesu hiŋra baŋhina n lii Siizaria ge du yaa di kpogli yaa la baal la dia yaa n niŋ ga du la. A baal ɛɛ Saiprɔs hinuurɛ. U sɔnnɛ Ŋmɛsɔn. U ɛɛ banla n faa felee di ra hiŋ Yeesu la bɛllɛ. Pɔɔl n laŋŋɛ ga jaami Jems wia

ref: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
text: Yaa n hel Jɛrusalɛm, yaabalaa jaami yaa nɛnnɛ.

ref: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
text: Hɔpizi yaa ni Pɔɔl maa la ya ga jaami Jems, di Yeesu hiŋra nabɔnzi la maa chaali u dia.

ref: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
text: Pɔɔl jaami baa ka ŋɔ wiimaa Kɔraawiizi n hiinuu u wer ɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la biini di tɛɛ baa.

ref: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
text: Baŋ wa nuu a wia, ba ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Denii ba ge ŋɔ u be, “Yaa kpɛɛma, na! Jus hina kpila maanii yardi Yeesu filaŋkeŋ ka haa aah siwii ra hiŋ Moosis Gbɔg.

ref: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
text: Ba ɔɔ ra nuu i wiarɛ lugɔ hinna bagli Jus hina la maa n du banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ be la lugɔ bá gilɛɛ kaa hiŋ ba naana wia la.

ref: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
text: Ba daŋ nuu lugɔ i ballɔɔ. Ɛrɛɛ í ɛɛ naanɛi?

ref: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
text: Awia, gil ya baglii gunla hin niŋ ɛɛ. Baala banaazuu du yaa be di lɛɛ nua Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
text: Hiŋ baa la Kɔraawiizi Dia, í ni baa ga kpau ɛɛ wia la, di lizi ii doŋa ha, ka ií turgi a wia kim tɛɛ baa ka bá fuŋ ii nyuuni. Di i haŋ wer ɛɛ guŋ, nɛra maa daŋ zum lugɔ karaa ba kanni chugii di ŋɔ i wia la. Ba daŋ jaa na di i himmaa ra hiŋ Moosis Gbɔg labuu.

ref: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Banla ge n yardi Yeesu ka ba waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la, yaa sɛbi hɔnnɛ tɛɛ baa di ŋɔ bá ra kii kuna la baŋ kpawɛɛ tɛɛ vuga ni chal ni kunla baŋ hanzi u baŋaa u siu la ni sɛnsɛŋ wia.”

ref: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, Pɔɔl lɛɛ a baala banaazu du u be. Hɔpizi, ba la ga kpau ɛɛ a wia, bá doŋa lii ka ba zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia, Pɔɔl ga bagli hɔpizaa la maga ban niŋ ɛɛ a wia, ka bá lizi ba maa mbusuzi. A ɛɛ hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ. Pɔɔl lawaa wia

ref: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
text: A hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ n waa tuŋ, Jus hina baŋhina n lii Eesia hɛri wa na Pɔɔl Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini di kpa dɔm du nɛkpila la n du de la ni, ka la ga lau Pɔɔl

ref: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
text: di pogzi di ra ŋɔ, “Yaabalaa, ií ba wa hiini yaaoo! Baal la n ɔɔ ra gaagi yemmaa di ŋɔ wia ra chɔgi yaa Jus hina wia ni Moosis Gbɔg la ni Kɔraawiizi bɔnaniinanii la wia la, waabuu keŋ. U lau banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ labuu di zuu Kɔraawiizi Dia gba di kpa doŋa du Kɔraawiizi bɔkiilii la ni.”

ref: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
text: Ba waa zummɛ ka ŋɔ guŋ. Ba na hɔɔhribaal bɛl ni Pɔɔllɛ bol la biini. U ɛɛ Ɛfɛsus hinuurɛ, u sɔŋ di Trɔfimus. Baŋ wa na Pɔɔl Kɔraawiizi Dia la, ba fɛ lugɔ Pɔɔl kpogli hɔɔhribaal labuu zuu de.

ref: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
text: Dɔm izi su bol maa. Nɛra chɔ ba di wa chaali werge di lau Pɔɔl tɛrguu lii Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. Baŋ wa liwɛɛ la, ba lau a dia gbessi tɔ manaŋ.

ref: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
text: Nɛkpila la ra nyiŋŋi ba kpuu, ka nɛra teŋ tili ŋɔ Room soojazi nabɔma be dí a bolzeŋ maa izoore di ra du dɔm.

ref: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
text: A nabɔma ɛɛ manaŋ di lizi soojazi ni ba nabɔnzi di chɔ ba ba be. Nɛra la n wa na u ni soojazi la n na ba, ba gil Pɔɔl lɔɔzaa.

ref: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
text: U wa hel Pɔɔl be u ŋɔ bá lawuu vɔɔ yɔlɔzi anɛɛ ka pɛɛzi nɛra, “Baal naa, anɛɛwɛi? Bɛɛ u ɛɛi?”

ref: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.

ref: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”

ref: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
text: Pɔɔl pessi banla maa n chaalɛɛ de la di wa zum lugɔ ba yeŋ ɛɛ Sajusizii, ba yeŋ ge ɛɛ Farisizi. U ŋɔ ni bɔkpega tɛɛ sitɔɔra la maa, “Yaabalaa, n ɛɛ Farisii. Banla n luliŋ ge ɛɛ Farisizii. N binnɔɔrɛ lugɔ nɛra daŋ izi siu biini. A guŋ tamii wiarɛ ii ra di n seriya la.”

ref: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.

text: U ŋɔ, “Di banla i ni baa n dɔɔ wii la wa ballɔ, n daŋ di i seriya.” Denii u ŋɔ bá tɔu Hɛrɔd diizeŋ la biini di gil soojazi ra duu tau de.

ref: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
text: Hɔpizaa anue n wa bɛrɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma Ananias ni a bol nabɔnzi baŋhina lau kiizunni bɛl banna yir Tɛtulus di ba a hɛri nabɔma be Siizaria bá wa bagli wia la Pɔɔl n ɛɛwɛ.

ref: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
text: Ba yir Tɛtulus la ú lii di ŋɔ u wia. U lii di ŋɔ, “N dɔɔri Fɛligs, hiŋ dɔɔ nunzuma di ra binni yaa wiarɛ laal waa kaa izi yaa be. Zinaa yaa wettoo na bɔr heezi birgi. I kuari yaa hɛrii werge di ra tɛɛ yaa.

ref: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
text: Awia, yaa ni banla maa n du yeŋa maa ra jaamii werge maa.

ref: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
text: Maa nyiŋŋi n ŋɔ wia werge di tɔi ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka n na suŋŋiibuu í di kanyitti di nuu n be.

ref: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
text: Baal naa wia waa wer. U ra gba wiarɛ werge. Bɔr la maa Jus hina n duwɛɛ durnya naa biini, ɔɔ ga du dɔmnɛ ba biini. U ɛɛ banla n na hiŋ hiŋfalii bɛl ba ra yir baa Nazirizi la bɛllɛ. Waabuu ba nabɔma.

ref: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
text: ka ŋɔ bánla nuu n dɔɔ wii la ba i be. Di i pɛɛzi a baal, u daŋ baglii wia naa maa miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ chɔguu naa.”

ref: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
text: A Jus hina ge maa hiŋ u nua di ŋɔ, A maa ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
text: Denii a hɛri nabɔma tɛr Pɔɔl nonii ú lii di ŋɔ u hor. Pɔɔl lii di ŋɔ u be, “Hiŋ birgi yaa hɛri di di yaa seriyazi di ra tɛɛ yaa wia n bɔra sɔɔnɔɔ hin niŋ diŋ seriya naa.

ref: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
text: A hɔl la miŋ la Jɛrusalɛm ń wa jaami Kɔraawiizi la, n hɔpizaa fidaanɛɛrɛ keŋ zinaa. Pɛɛzi baa na. A waa guŋ kaalɛɛ.

ref: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
text: Hɔpizaa la maa biini, ba wan nawɛɛ minna di nɛr maa hɔɔzi Kɔraawiizi Dia biini. Ba wan nawɛɛ miŋ kaa ra du dɔm ba jaamaa diini biine ni a bolzeŋ yemmaa.

ref: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
text: Wia naa maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ra chugiŋ naa, ba waa daansɛɛ maa dɔɔwɛ ban niŋ ɛɛ di bagli lugɔ a ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
text: Unnii bɛnnɛ n sɛɛ lugɔ wibiire. Hiŋaa la banna yir hiŋfalii la, waabuu n na hiŋ. Kɔraawiizi la yaa naabaala n faa ra hiŋ labuu n na hiŋ guŋ. Gbɔg la ni wia la maa Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la n faa sɛbɛɛ la, a maanii n na hiŋ,

ref: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
text: di yardi Kɔraawiizi lugɔ u daŋ ŋmɛnɛ lalli nɛchɔgaa ni nɛnanaa maa siu biini. Nɛra naa gba yardi gunnɛ.

ref: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
text: N ɔɔ aah siwiire ra hiŋ ń wer dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu Kɔraawiizi ni nɛra maa be saŋa maa, bá gilɛɛ wa na wiimaa di kpa chugiŋ.

ref: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
text: N faa lii hɛri naabuu di du yembɛl biŋkpila maa biini. Filaŋkenne n haa ba. Kebee aŋhinaa n kpogli ba ń wa sunzi n hɛri hina, di kaa ŋɔ ń lizi mbusuzi aŋhina tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
text: A wiarɛ n faa ra ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dia biini, saŋa la baŋ naŋ de la. Baŋ wa naŋ la, di n jaa ɛɛ wia la miŋ faa ra ɛɛ, ń doŋa lii n ni di tuŋ. Ba faa waa n ni nɛkpila ni kɔɔi wia maa nawɛɛ.

ref: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
text: Jus hina baŋhina n lii Eesia hɛri labuu naŋ de. Di baabuu vii du ɛŋ, ba daŋ vii ŋɔ i nuu. Di n ɛɛ baa wichɔgii maa, ba daŋ vii baglii a wibaluu maa.

ref: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
text: Bannii n du ɛnnaa ge, di ba na n wichɔgaa maa ban niŋ kpa sag n ni saŋa la miŋ faa du ba ni sitɔɔra be la la, bá bagli.

ref: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
text: Ba wàá wer na wiimaa ŋɔ di unnii minna nyiŋŋi n bagli naa lɛi. A hɔl la min chigɛ ba be la n ŋɔwɔɔrɛ ni bɔkpega ni, ‘Siu biini izaa wiŋɔzi wiarɛ n du ii be ii ra pɛɛziŋ wia zinaa la.’ ”

ref: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
text: Fɛligs n zum hiŋaa la wia nɛnnɛ la, u ŋɔ ú laŋŋi a Jus hina di ŋɔ, Ií gil soojazi nabɔma Lisias ba mɔɔ. Di u wa ballɔ, n daŋ di ii wia naa seriya tuŋ.

ref: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
text: U gil soojazi nabɔma bɛl kpa Pɔɔl di la ka ŋɔ, “Ií ra du u tau ka gilɛɛ waa tɔɔruu. Ií ɔɔ tɛɛ u dammuzi ŋmɛnɛɛ bá ba di waa hiinuu.”

ref: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
text: Aŋ wa ɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ, Fɛligs kpa u haaŋ Drusila di ba. U haaŋ hiŋ ɛɛ Jus hinuurɛ. Fɛligs hum nɛra bá lau Pɔɔl ba. Ba lawuu ba. U waa bagli Fɛligs Yeesu Kristo hiŋaa wia ani gunla un niŋ yarduu.

ref: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
text: Ka uŋ wa ŋɔ winanaa hiŋaa wia di ŋɔ u hinlawaa wia di kaa ŋɔ hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di durnya seriya wia, kafɔŋ lau Fɛligs werge maa. U ŋɔ, “A la filaŋkeŋ. Di n kaa wa na bɔr, n daŋ kaa yirii.”

ref: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
text: U faa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ Pɔɔl tɛu kebee. Awiarɛ u ɔɔ faa ra yiruu u nuu ra ŋɔ wia.

ref: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
text: Binni anɛɛ n wa bɛrɛɛ Pɔsiɔs Fɛstus wa lɛɛ Fɛligs bɔr di ɛɛ a hɛri nabɔma. Fɛligs n na nyiŋŋi ŋɔ Jus hina dɔɔ u bila wia, u gil ba faa haa tɔ Pɔɔl dia.

ref: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
text: Denii a Hɛri Nabɔma Fɛstus n wa ba ba hɛri la di wa du de hɔpizaa ahoro, u lii Siizaria di la Jɛrusalɛm.

ref: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
text: Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Jus hina nabɔnzi ba u be di wa ŋɔ Pɔɔl wia,

ref: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
text: ka suŋŋuu dí u ɛɛ wii bɛl tɛɛ baa di gil Pɔɔl ba Jɛrusalɛm. Ba kaa ra ta jina bɛl bá so u saga ŋmɛnɛɛ di kpuu.

ref: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
text: Ka Fɛstus ŋɔ, “Ba tɔ Pɔɔllɛ dia Siizaria. N himmaa daŋ bir la de filaŋkeŋ.

ref: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
text: Awia, ií gil ii nabɔnzi duŋ la. Di a baal ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ba daŋ baglaa tɛŋ de.”

ref: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
text: Hɛri Nabɔma Fɛstus kaa di hɔpizaa ŋmantannaazi gɛɛ fi ba be ka bir la Siizaria. Hɔɔ wa pizi u zuu seriya diiribɔr di ga so, ka ŋɔ dí ba lau Pɔɔl ba.

ref: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
text: Ba lawuu ba. Jus hina la n lii Jɛrusalɛm la wa baruu ka jaa ra ŋɔ wiŋɔzenaa kpila maa di ra du u ni, ka ba waa daansɛɛ maa dɔɔwɛ lugɔ a wia ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
text: Pɔɔl ge ŋɔ u hor di ŋɔ, “Maa Jus hina Gbɔg chɔkkɛ. Maa kaa ɛɛ wichɔgaa di du Kɔraawiizi Dia ni gɛɛ Room koorizeŋ ni.”

ref: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
text: Fɛstus n na nyiŋŋi u lau Jus hina dammuzi wia, u pɛɛzi Pɔɔl, i ra nyiŋŋuu i la Jɛrusalɛm bá ga dii seriya de ń ge nuuwaa?

ref: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
text: Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Akai! N na suŋŋuu ń la Koorizeŋ Siiza be ú ga diŋ seriya. Jus hina na, i gba zummɔ lugɔ maa baa ɛɛwɛ wichɔgii maa.

ref: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
text: Di n vii ɛɛ wichɔgiirɛ di dɛg kpui, n vii wàá vɛɛ guŋ siu. Ka di wia naa baŋ kpawɛɛ ra sag n ni naa waa wibii ɛɛwɛ, nɛr maa wàá wer kpaŋ du ba nonee bá kpuŋ. Koorizeŋ seriya diiribɔttɛ n na suŋŋi í gil n la.”

ref: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
text: Denii Fɛstus ni u nabɔnzi n wa ŋɔ u wia tuŋ, Fɛstus ŋɔ u be, “Koorizeŋ Siiza seriya bɔttɛ i suŋŋi. Awia, denii í la.” Baŋ kpogli Pɔɔl la Koori Agripa ni Bɛnis be wia

ref: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
text: Aŋ kaa wa ɛɛ hɔpizaa anɛɛ, koori bɛl banna yir Agripa ni Bɛnis ba Siizaria di wa jaami Fɛstus.

ref: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
text: Baŋ wa birgee tama, Fɛstus kpa Pɔɔl wia bagli ra tɛɛ a koori di ra ŋɔ, “Fɛligs faa tɔ baal bɛllɛ dia. U haa du de.

ref: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
text: Saŋa la miŋ faa la Jɛrusalɛm la, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi ni Jus hina nabɔnzi ba n benii di wa ŋɔ u wia tɛŋ, di ra nyiŋŋi lugɔ ń di u seriya ú chol.

ref: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
text: Ka n ŋɔ ba be lugɔ Room hina waa ɔɔ sɛɛ bá di nɛr kpui seriya, di u ni nɛra la n kpa wia ra chuguu la waa bɔkpaŋ soge di di a wia, bá ŋɔ ba hor ú ge wer hɔɔ u nua lɛi.

ref: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
text: Baŋ wa chaalɛɛ ba ɛŋ, maa sɛɛwɛ n laŋŋi baa. Hɔpizi n ba wa so seriya diiribɔr, ka ŋɔ bá kpa a baal ba.

ref: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
text: Banla u ni baa n dɔɔ wii la n wa liwɛɛ di ŋɔ u wia, wichɔgaa la miŋ faa ra tami lugɔ ba daŋ ŋɔ la, ba waa a guŋ ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
text: Ba himmaa wiazi hiŋaa ani baal bɛl banna yir Yeesu wiarɛ ba kpa ra ŋɔ. A baal faa siuwɔɔ, ka Pɔɔl ɔɔ ŋɔ lugɔ u izi siu biinii.

ref: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
text: Miŋ waa wia naa biini zummɛ nɛnnɛ lugɔ min niŋ di a seriya la, n pɛɛzuu ŋɔ u daŋ la Jɛrusalɛm bá ga diu seriya de gɛɛ?

ref: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
text: Waa guŋ sɛɛwɛ, ka suŋŋiŋ dí ń gil ba haa ra du u tau mɔɔ ka ú wa la koorizeŋ be ú ga diu seriya. Awia, n ŋɔ bá ra du u tau mɔɔ ka ń wa gil u la Koorizeŋ Siiza be.”

ref: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
text: Agripa ŋɔ, “N gba ra nyiŋŋi n nuu baal naa wiŋɔzii.” Fɛstus ŋɔ, “Kɛrɛ i daŋ nuu.”

ref: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ Agripa ni Bɛnis ba wa zuu seriya diiribɔr la. Ba zuui la dɔɔ girme werge. Ba ga so banla n niŋ di seriya sognibɔr la. Soojazi nabɔnzi ni a bol nabɔnzi maa ba di ge waa so. Ba maa n wa chaalɛɛ la, Fɛstus ŋɔ bá lau Pɔɔl ba. Ba lawuu ba.

ref: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
text: Fɛstus ŋɔ, “Koori Agripa ani i bannii maa n du ɛnnaa, baal la Jus hina nɛkpila maa n ŋɔ u wia di ra tɛŋ bɔnnaa ani Jɛrusalɛm di ra ŋɔ werge maa, dí a waa wer uŋ kaa du de la, waabuu keŋ.

ref: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
text: Ka miŋ wa diu seriya, maa wiimaa nawɛɛ min niŋ kpa sag u ni di ŋɔ lugɔ u dɛg kpuirɛ. U ge n wa suŋŋi koorizeŋ seriya bɔr laŋaa la, n ŋɔ n daŋ gil u la.

ref: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
text: Ka gunla min niŋ sɛbi n dɔɔri koorizeŋ di ŋɔ u wia bá kpa di di u seriya la, aabuu tiriŋ. Awiarɛ n ŋɔ ú lii ií maa nuu u wia. Koori, hinuu n na nyiŋŋi i nuu wiimaa nɛnnɛ di bagliŋ gunla min niŋ sɛbi hɔŋ la.

ref: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
text: Di n gillɔ u la ba be, ka maa wichɔgaa la uŋ ɛɛwɛ baglɛɛ, a daŋ ɛɛu lugɔ maa nfɛrɛ kpawɛɛ di ra hum n huma.”

ref: Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.” Paul stretched out his hand and said:
text: Koori Agripa ŋɔ Pɔɔl be, “N tɛi ŋmɛnɛɛ. Ŋɔ i hor.” Pɔɔl lii lalli u nonii di ŋɔ bá siigi. Ba siigi. U jaa ra ŋɔ u hor, dí,

ref: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
text: “Koori Agripa, n bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ zinaa lugɔ min niŋ wer ŋɔ n hor tɛi, di wer baglii wia la maa Jus hina n kpawɛɛ ra sag n ni,

ref: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, i zum yaa naana wiarɛ. Awia, n na suŋŋii í di kanyitti ka nuu tɛŋ.

ref: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
text: di zum lugɔ Jus hiŋaa la n kpolle werge labuu n faa ra hiŋ. N faa ɛɛ Farisii. Di ba vii sɛɛwɔ bá ŋɔ, ba daŋ vii baglii guŋ.

ref: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
text: Ka ba gil n chi ɛŋ i ra di n seriya, dikuu miŋ yardi nua bɛl Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa naabaala lugɔ u daŋ ŋmɛnɛ lalli lalaa ba siu biini la wia.

ref: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
text: Jus hina dizi fidaanɛɛ la maanii yardi guŋ. Awiarɛ ba ɔɔ ra hum Kɔraawiizi siaahmu ni, saŋa maa la. Ka ba bir di ra diŋ seriya dikuu n gba n yardi guŋ wia. Binni nau!

ref: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
text: Ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ a tir ii ge, miŋ ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi daŋ wer lalli lalaa ba siu biinei?

ref: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
text: N himmaa faa waa Yeesu n lii Nazarɛf wia naa ra sɛɛ. Awia, n binni lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ n himmaa ni Yeesu hiŋra n na naa.

ref: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
text: N ni baa naa Jɛrusalɛm biini. Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzi benii n faa lɛɛ fɔŋŋa di wer lauri Kɔraawiizi biinanaa bakpila maa di tɔ dia. Baŋ ɔɔ faa ra di ba kpui seriya la, n ge ɔɔ faa sɛɛ jaa sitɔɔra la ni lugɔ bá kpu baa.

ref: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
text: Di n wa na baa jaamaa dia maa biini, aŋ faa ra tɔɔri baa saŋa maa bá vii hɔɔ di vɛɛ ba hiŋaa hiŋ. Ba wia n faa ra fuuh n baaŋ werge maa wiarɛ n ɔɔ faa lii kɛrii gba di gaa tɔɔri banla maa n du bola la n waa hoo Jus hina hɛri biini la.

ref: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
text: A hɔl bɛl n na la Damaskus. Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Nabɔnzii faa humiŋ di tɛŋ ba fɔŋŋa n na la.

ref: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
text: Koori, minna la, wiizi ga baŋ. Denii bɔr chaani, n ni banla maa n duŋ di ra la la ni werge maa, di kaali gunla wiizi n na chaani la.

ref: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
text: Yaa maa chogli hɛri. N nuu loobii bɛl n kpa yaa Jus hina mɔɔri biini di pɛɛziŋ, ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, bɛɛ wiarɛ i ra tɔɔriŋ kennei? I yoombuu ra huhzi. I ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nakpoŋlii la baŋ ɔɔ ra tɛrgi u ra yoo, di bir ra tɔɔri u hiŋ la.’

ref: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
text: N pɛɛzi, ‘N Dɔɔri, anɛɛ hinnɛi?’ N Dɔɔri hiŋ ŋɔ, ‘Minuu Yeesu la hinna tɔɔri la.

ref: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
text: Izi chiŋ. N ba i benii í naŋ ka ń wer humii í di daansɛɛ di ra tɛɛ nɛra alugɔ i nambuu zinaa, di kaa wa di daansɛɛ gunla hin niŋ kaa wa naŋ la.

ref: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
text: N daŋ humii í la banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la be, di kissii ba ni, di kaa kissii Jus hina gba ni.

ref: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
text: N daŋ humii í ga pilli ba siwee, bá bir ba bampiree lii bɔbiri di ba bɔchaaŋ, di lii Sitaani fɔŋŋa biini di ba Kɔraawiizi be, ú gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa, di gil ba jaa banla n yardi Kɔraawiizi, n lizi ba doŋa maa di ha, ka gil ba ɛɛ u biizi di ra di u kapɛttɛ la ni.’

ref: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
text: di di daansɛɛ tɛɛ Damaskus hina mɔɔ, ka la Jɛrusalɛm di kaa ga ɛɛ guŋ daansɛɛ tɛɛ ba ge, ka jaa ra gaagi Juda hɛri bola ni bola la n waa hoo Jus hina hɛri biini, di ra ŋɔ ba be bá gil ba wichɔgaa, ka bir ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi di ra ɛɛ winanaa nɛ́ra zum lugɔ ba bir ba bampireere wibii maa.

ref: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
text: Awiarɛ Jus hina lawiŋ Kɔraawiizi Dia la biini, di faa ra nyiŋŋi ba kpuŋ la.

ref: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi n hiiniŋ wiarɛ n haa du de di wer chi ɛnnaa, di haa di daansɛɛ ra tɛɛ nabɔnzenaa ni bichalli maa la. N wiŋɔzi ɛɛ wia la Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi ni Moosis n faa ŋɔ a daŋ wa ɛɛ labuu. A bɛnnɛ n na ŋɔ.

ref: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
text: Ba faa ŋɔ Kristo daŋ di tɔɔrɔɔ di siu mɔɔ ka feli lalaa maa izi siu biini, di wer bagli bɔchaaŋ wia tɛɛ Jus hina ni banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la maa.”

ref: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
text: Pɔɔl n wa ŋɔ guŋ, Fɛstus pozi u ni di ŋɔ, “Pɔɔl, i ra chugluu! I zumaa wergee gillɛ i ra chugli la.”

ref: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
text: Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri Fɛstus, maa chugli lɛi. Wibiire n na ŋɔ. Chugla wiŋɔzi lɛi annii.

ref: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
text: Koori Agripa zum wia naa maa minna ŋɔ naabuu. Awiarɛ maa u be wiŋɔzi ŋɔi ra ɔm la. Maa tamɛɛ lugɔ a wii bɛl maa bar u hattɛ. A faa waa ɛɛwɛ ra suah.

ref: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
text: Koori Agripa, i yardi Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi laa? N zummɔ lugɔ i yardi baabuu.”

ref: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
text: Agripa ŋɔ, “Witama naabuu i ŋɔ tɛŋ, ka ra nyiŋŋi n sɛɛ tɛi, di birgi Yeesu hiŋria?”

ref: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
text: Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Di i daŋ nuu tama ka sɛɛ gɛɛ wergee í nuu ka sɛɛ, a maa lugɔi. Ka n na nyiŋŋuu i ni bannii maa n na nuu n wiŋɔzi naa du gunla min duwɛɛ naa. Ama, maa ŋɔ ií du lugɔ n ni n yɔlɔzi naa waa.”

ref: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
text: Denii a koori ni hɛri nabɔma la ni Bɛnis ni babalaa maa izi lii.

ref: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
text: Baŋ wa liwɛɛ, ba ra ŋɔ u wia dɔŋa be, “Baal naa waa wiimaa ɛɛwɛ di dɛg kpui gɛɛ yɔlɔzi gba vɔɔi.”

ref: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
text: Koori Agripa ŋɔ Fɛstus be, “Baal naa vii waa Koorizeŋ Siiza seriya diiribɔr laŋaa suŋŋɛɛ, n daŋ vii ŋɔ í pilluu ú ra la.”

ref: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
text: Baŋ wa ŋɔ a wia tuŋ, ba ŋɔ ba daŋ gil Pɔɔl zuu muugberzeŋ bɛl di la Itali hɛri. Ba kpa u ni nɛra baŋhina baŋ tɔ dia, di tɛɛ koorizeŋ soojazi nabɔma bɛl, ú kpogli baa ra la. U sɔnnɛ faa Juliɔs.

ref: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
text: N ni baa maa ga zuu muugbera bɛl n lii Adramitum di ra la Eesia hɛri bola la n du a muuzeŋ la nua. Masɛdɔnia hɛri hinuu bɛl n lii Tɛsalɔnika ge faa du yaa be yaa nuu maa ra la. U sɔnnɛ faa Aristakus.

ref: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ yaa wa hel Saidɔn. Juliɔs la ɛɛ Pɔɔl nɛnnɛ, di tɛu ŋmɛnɛɛ ú la u dammuzi be de, bá ga kpogluu tama ka ú bir di ra ba. U la ka bir ba.

ref: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
text: Yaa kpa ra la. Peu gaa ta di ra chem yaa ni, yaa bir ga hɛrjiga Saiprɔs harbɔɔ ú tɔ yaa peu la.

ref: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
text: Yaa ba nii la n dugli Silisia ni Pamfilia hɛri la di giu di ga hel Mira la n du Lisia hɛri la.

ref: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
text: Soojazi nabɔma la wer na Alɛgzandria muugbera bɛl n na la Itali hɛri, di gil yaa zuuu di ra la.

ref: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
text: Yaa waa wette ya na manaŋ, ka ra la bɔɔiih guŋŋ hɔpizaa anɛɛ. A nuu yaa mɔɔ ka yaa wer hel Sinaidus. Peu waa sɛɛwɛ yaa deŋli la. Yaa bir la hɛrjiga bɛl banna yir Krit paga, bɔr la peu n waa ta werge, di ga bɛri Salmɔni,

ref: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
text: di ga dugli muu kɛrii di ra la. A kaa nuu yaa werge ka yaa haa hel bɔr la n dugli Lasia ba ra yir de Fɛɛ Hevins la.

ref: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
text: Yaa birgi de werge. Jus hina Hɔpizizeŋ la banna vɔɔ nua la wa bɛri yaa ni gba. Di a saŋa wa bɛrɔɔ, muuzeŋ la waa ɔɔ kaa ɛɛ zuui. Awia, Pɔɔl karfi baa

ref: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
text: di ŋɔ, “Di yaa ra la filaŋkeŋ yaa daŋ ga zuu tɔɔrɔɔ biini yaa ni yaa muugbera ni u bunni maa ta.”

ref: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
text: Ka soojazi nabɔma la waa nuuwɛ tɛɛ Pɔɔl ka ra hiŋ a muugbera balaa nabɔma ni a muugbera hiŋ nuuzi.

ref: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
text: Baabuu ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ bɔr la waa wer ban niŋ lau muugbera la chiŋŋi de, a pezenaa saŋa la. Ka Krit muugbessi chignibɔr bɛl du de, ba ra yir de Fonigs. Ba galga maa ra ŋɔ dí ba izi ra la bá vii wer hel de mɔɔ, di ga du de ka á pezenaa saŋa wa bɛri. Denii niŋ wer gber baa pezenaa la ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, de faa chaŋ wiifurii nodig wiikakag wiicholii ni wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wiicholiire. Pekpeg n gaa ta muuzeŋ biini wia

ref: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
text: Denii peu la n wa bittɛ lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag di jaa ra ta tama tama, ba binni lugɔ ba jaa na ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ bá ra la. Ba lalli a muugbera lugbii la n ɔɔ lawuu chiŋŋi la ka ra la ga ga muu kɛrii di ra kaali.

ref: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
text: Tama, di pezenzeŋ bɛl izoo. Waabuu ɔɔ lii wiifurii nomɛɛl wiikakag wiifurii, di chum werge la.

ref: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
text: U lii a hɛri barii di waa yag yaa muugbera. Yaa yoou huhzi. A muugbera waa kaa wer ra la see, ka hanna la bɔr la a peu n tawɛɛ ra la la.

ref: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
text: Yaa wa hel hɛrjiga bɛl banna yir Kauda harbɔɔ. U gber yaa a peu tama ka u haa ra yoo yaa. Yaa kuuh werge maa,

ref: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
text: ka haa wer lalli gberjiga la n choŋŋi harbɔɔ di ra hiŋ la, di vɔɔu nɛnnɛ. Baŋ wa vɔɔu la, ba kaa vɔɔzi muugbera la maa. Bɔdɛdɛrɛ bɛl du de ba ra yiruu Sirtis. Ba maa ra fɔŋ lugɔ peu la daŋ taa baa la bá ga far. Awia, ba gil wɛjɛzeŋ la n du a muugbera nyuu la tuu hɛri ka peu la taa baa guŋŋ ba ra la.

ref: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizɛɛ, di a peu haa ra ta werge. Ba lizi muugbera la bunni di ra ta a nii biini.

ref: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
text: Hɔɔŋ kaa pizi, ba kaa lizi a muugbera kuna aŋhina ge di kaa ta.

ref: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
text: Hɔpizikpila maa biini, di yaa waa wette na wiizi. Yaa waa chinchiŋwilaa gba nawɛɛ. Ka peu la haa vɛɛ ra ta werge. Yaa waa kaa ɛɛ tamii lugɔ yaa daŋ wer lɛɛ yaa hinaa.

ref: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
text: Denii bam birgee ka ba haa waa diwee diwee la, Pɔɔl izi ba baaŋ di ŋɔ ba be, “N nabɔnzi, di ii vii nuu wii la miŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ ŋɔ ií gilɛɛ gil ya lii Krit mɔɔ la, wii naa vii wàá na yaa, yaa kuna maa chɔgi keŋ.

ref: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
text: Ka n na suŋŋi ia ií nuu n be, di gil ii bɔra sɔɔni. Muugbera naawaa daŋ chɔgi, ka ii bɛl maa wàá siu.

ref: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
text: Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔŋ, di gil n na hum u huma labuu bagliŋ guŋ. U gillɔɔ u mɛlika bɛl ba n be dɛɛla hamuŋa ni,

ref: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
text: di wa ŋɔ, ‘Pɔɔl, i daŋ chi Koorizeŋ Siiza see. Kɔraawiizii dau guŋ. Awia, gilɛɛ ra ɔm. Bannii maa i ni baa n du muugbera naa biini naa ge, Kɔraawiizi nuuwɔɔ tɛi di ŋɔ u daŋ lɛɛ ba gba.’

ref: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
text: Awia, yaabalaa, ií maa gil ii bɔra sɔɔni. N yardi gunla Kɔraawiizi uŋ ŋɔ n be labuu, guŋ himmaanii niŋ ɛɛ.

ref: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
text: Ama, yaa daŋ wa ta hɛrjiga bɛl.”

ref: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
text: Ba jaa kpa a muugbera lugbia maa ta nii la biini, di pur u kuna la ge n ɔɔ gil u ra deŋli la, ka kpa wɛjɛzeŋ la di kaa vɔɔ chiŋ, di lawuu bir, peu ra ta u ni, ú wer ra la.

ref: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
text: A muugbera balaa baŋhina ra nyiŋŋi ba chɔ lii muugbera la biini, di gil muugberjiga la tuu nii la biini, di ra nyiŋŋi ba dar yaa lugɔ ba daŋ kpa lugbia di lau a muugbera see ge.

ref: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
text: Ba jaa ra fɔŋ lugɔ a muugbera daŋ lii bia ni di purgi. Ba lau muugbera la lugbia anaazu di gil a tuu a nii biini a muugbera har, á lawuu chiŋŋi, ka ra suŋŋi wiizi hɔ́pizi, bɔ́r chaani baa.

ref: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
text: Ka Pɔɔl ŋɔ soojazi ni ba nabɔma be, “Di nɛra naa lii muugbera naa biini, ii wàá na iihinaa.”

ref: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
text: Soojazi la ga chaahzi muugberjiga la ŋmɛnni, u chol nii la biini.

ref: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
text: Awia, n na suŋŋi iabuu, ií nyiŋŋi diwee di, di wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa di wer na iihinaa wia naa biini, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii yemmaa waa ba ɛŋ tai.”

ref: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ, u kpa paanuu di suŋŋi wiizi du u ni, ba maa see, ka mɔnnuu ra hee.

ref: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
text: Denii ba maa bampiree ɛɛ kpaŋ. Ba jaa ra di.

ref: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
text: Ba maa n wa diwee piŋ, ba kpa mia la maa fug chaari nii la biini, ka muugbera la jaa wer du fug.

ref: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
text: Hɔɔŋ wa pizi baa, muugbera balaa la waa wette bá zum hɛri la. Ka baŋ wa na a muu bɔfɔɔlii bɛl, de hɛri mɛgzi dɔŋa ni, ba ta jina dɔŋa be, bá vii wer ga de di gi.

ref: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
text: Banna la la, ba waa de helle, ka zuu bɔtizaa bɛl. A muugberzeŋ nyuu zuu hɛɛhriichaa biini di far de chi. Waa wette lii. Nii ra yag u harbɔɔ werge, u ra purgi.

ref: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
text: Denii a soojazi ta jina bá kpu banla baŋ vɔɔzi yɔlɔzi la maa, bá gilɛɛ wer sɔŋŋi kaali di lɛɛ bahinaa.

ref: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
text: Ka ba nabɔma kuu Pɔɔl wia di ŋɔ bá gil baa, ka ŋɔ dí banla maa n zum sɔŋŋaa, bá zaah chogli nii la biini, di tɔ see ra lii.

ref: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
text: Banla ge n kawɛɛ, bá kpa muugbera daazi ni kummaa ban niŋ wer kpa a muugbera biini di zaali nii la ni, di hiŋ baa lii. Ba maa ɛɛ guŋ di wer lɛɛ bahinaa lii nii la biini.

ref: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
text: Yaa n wa lii nii la biini, yaa jaa zum lugɔ hɛrjiga la banna yir Mɔlta labuu.

ref: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
text: Nɛra la n du a hɛri suŋ yaa ni, di hiini yaa werge. Dooŋ n na ɛɛ la, waari ra kpu yaa, ba chem niŋ tɛɛ yaa, di lau yaa ba a niŋ zɛɛ.

ref: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
text: Pɔɔl ga paa daazi di wa du a niŋ biini. Duŋkpola bɛl faa du a daazi biinii. Aŋ wa wenzee, u lii di dum Pɔɔl nonii.

ref: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
text: A hɛri hina n wa na a duŋkpola n dum u nonii di kpogli la, ba ŋɔ dɔŋa be, “Baal naa nii ɛɛ nɛkpuurii. U wettoo lɛɛ u hiŋ muu la biini, ka Kɔraawiizi waa nyiŋŋi u du de.”

ref: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
text: Pɔɔl zigli a duŋkpola ha niŋ la biini, ka wiimaa wɔɔ ɛɛwɛ.

ref: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
text: A nɛra tami lugɔ u nonii hiŋ daŋ ɔr u chol siu filaŋkeŋ maa. Ka baŋ wa binnuu guŋŋ, wiimaa wɔɔ ra ɛɛ la, ba bir ra binni lugɔ u nii ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dee bɛllɛ.

ref: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
text: A hɛri koori sɔnnɛ faa Publiɔs. U hɛssi dugli de. Ba kpa yaa la u be. U lɛɛ yaa dau di hɔɔhri yaa hɔpizaa ahoro.

ref: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
text: A koori mɛɛ faa chɔɔ diarɛ di ra wii. U bɔra maa wenzi. Binchiiraarɛ faa lawuu. Pɔɔl zuu u be di suŋŋi wiizi tɛu, ka kpa u nonee sag u ni. U nyaagi.

ref: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
text: Uŋ wa chaa baal la, banla maa n du a hɛri biini di ra wii la, ba ba yaa be. Yaa chaa ba maa.

ref: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
text: Ba ra hɔɔhri yaa werge. Saŋa la yaa n kaa waa nyiŋŋi ya zuu muugbera kaali la, ba tɛɛ yaa kuna la maa yaa n faa waa dɔɔwɛ la, yaa kpa zuu ra la. Pɔɔl n hel Room wia

ref: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
text: Yaa du a hɛri baaguzi ahoro, ka zuu Alɛgzandria muugbera bɛl baŋ faa vɔɔwɛ chiŋŋi a hɛri biini, ka pezeŋ la saŋa wa bɛri. A muugbera sɔnnɛ Vugbiinɛɛri.

ref: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
text: Yaa n wa hel Sirakus, yaa di hɔpizaa ahoro de,

ref: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
text: ka kaa izi de di ra la ga hel Rɛgim. Hɔpizi, peu lii wiifurii nodig wiikakag di ra ta. Yaa jaa wer di ra la. Hɔɔ kaa pizi, yaa ga hel Putioli.

ref: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
text: Yeesu hiŋra baŋhina du de. Yaa n wa huuzi baa, ba suŋŋi yaa ŋɔ ya so ba be hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ mɔɔ. Yaa so de. Ba kpogli yaa hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ la, ka yaa jaa kpa ra la Room.

ref: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
text: Yeesu hiŋra la n du Room la nuu yaa wia, di lii ra chem yaa ni, di wa hel bɔr la banna yir Apius Yawa ni Diini Ahoro la. Pɔɔl n wa na baa, u jaami Kɔraawiizi werge, di jaa wer dɔɔ bampirii.

ref: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
text: Yaa n wa zuu Room biini, ba lau Pɔɔl di du u bɛŋ dia, di gil soojakpaŋ du u be, di ŋɔ ú ra du u tau.

ref: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
text: Uŋ wa du de hɔpizaa ahoro, u yir Jus hina nabɔnzi la n du de la, ba ba. U ŋɔ ba be, “Yaabalaa, maa yaa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ wiimaa. Maa yaa naabaala naana wii bɛl maa chɔkkɛ, ka ba lawiŋ vɔɔ Jɛrusalɛm, di kpaŋ du Room hina nonee biini.

ref: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
text: Room hina nabɔnzi ge n wa di n seriya, ba waa wiimaa nawɛɛ bá chugiŋ lugɔ n dɛg kpuirɛ, ka ra nyiŋŋi ba pilliŋ ń lii.

ref: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
text: Ka Jus hina waa sɛɛwɛ. Awiarɛ n suŋŋi Koorizeŋ Siiza seriya diiribɔr laŋaa la. Maa wiimaa dɔɔwɛ ń kpa chug baa, ka ba firiŋ n ɛɛ guŋ.

ref: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
text: Awiarɛ n suŋŋi ia ŋɔ ií ba ɛŋ wa naŋ, ya ŋɔ wia tɛɛ dɔŋa. N na nyiŋŋuu ii zum lugɔ nɛr la Jus hina n ɔɔ ra binni u ŋmɛnɛɛ la wiarɛ ba kuu vɔɔŋ yɔlɔzi naa.”

ref: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
text: Denii ba ŋɔ Pɔɔl be, Yaa haa waa hɔŋ maa nawɛɛ Jus hina hɛri unna bagli i wia. Yaabalaa bɛl maa ge waa de liwɛɛ ba ɛŋ, di wa ŋɔ lugɔ i ra ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ.

ref: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
text: Yaa ge ra nyiŋŋuu ya nuu i wiŋɔzi la, dikuubɛɛwiai, bɔr maanii ba ra gbɛlli ii hiŋfalii naa.

ref: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
text: Ba dau hɔpizii. A hɔpizii wa hel, ba chaali werge maa di ba bɔr la Pɔɔl n duwɛɛ la. U haŋ chi chɔɔzi maa di bagli baa Kɔraawiizi Kora wia guŋŋ bɔr wa duani, di liizi baa wia la maa Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi n faa sɛbɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, bá vii sɛɛ lugɔ Yeesu wiarɛ ba faa ra ŋɔ la.

ref: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
text: Baŋ wa nuu u wiŋɔzi la, baŋhina sɛɛ, baŋhina ge waa sɛɛwɛ.

ref: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
text: Ba waa nuukpaŋ dɔɔwɛ, ka jaa ra nyiŋŋi ba lii. Denii Pɔɔl ŋɔ ú keezi ŋɔ wikpaŋ tɛɛ baa ka bá kaali, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii faa ga u dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya benii di ŋɔ wia tɛɛ ii naabaala.

ref: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
text: U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘La ga ŋɔ nɛra naa be dí ba daŋ ŋɔ wia á zuu ba digna, ka ba wàá wer zum a zɛɛ. Ba daŋ aah siwii bá na a wia ŋmɛnɛɛ, ka ba wàá wer zum a zɛɛ,

ref: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛra naa gillɔɔ ba bampiree du tɔg werge, di gil ba digna ge du kpeg, di kaa tɔ ba siwee ge. Di guŋ lɛi, ba siwee daŋ vii na, ba digna ge nuu, bá zum a zɛɛ di bir ba bampiree di ra hiŋiŋ, ń chaa baa.’

ref: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
text: Uŋ wa ŋɔ guŋ tuŋ, ba lii ra kaali di ra di dɔŋa hɔɔzi werge.

ref: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
text: Denii Pɔɔl du Room binni anɛɛ biini, di du diihayii biini. Nɛra ɔɔ wer ba u be.

ref: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
text: U bagli Kɔraawiizi Kora wia ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo wia di ra tɛɛ baa. Wii la maa n du u biini, a maanii u wer ŋɔ tɛɛ baa, ka nɛr maa wɔɔ tɔwɛɛ ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
text: Mìŋ́ Yeesu Kristo balii Pɔɔllɛ a sɛbi hɔnnaa. A par Kɔraawiizii u yiriŋ ń wa ɛɛ u huŋhunni, di liziŋ du amaniyesuma huma naa biini.

ref: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
text: Amaniyesuma la ɛɛ wia la uŋ faa ŋɔ nua di gil u dɔgtɛɛzi sɛbi dau u Hɔnnanii biini faala maa labuu.

ref: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi n wa lalluu siu biini la, u ɛɛ gunnɛ di bagli lugɔ u ɛɛ u Biibaallɛ, di dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ani u Duma ge.

ref: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
text: U wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi suŋ n ni di hiiniŋ di gil n ɛɛ u huŋhunni bagli u wia ra tɛɛ nɛdee maa, bá wer sɛɛ u wia di yarduu, ú sɔŋ ge na girme.

ref: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
text: Ii gba du banla n sɛɛwɛ la biinii. Kɔraawiizii yir ia ii ɛɛ Yeesu Kristo hora.

ref: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
text: N na jaami ii banla maa n du Room di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nɛnɔŋŋaa la uŋ yittɛ ií ba wa ɛɛ u biinanaa la. Yáa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo hiini ia di tɛɛ ia bampirsɔna. Jaantɛɛi wiisuŋŋaa wia

ref: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
text: Wii la min niŋ feli ŋɔ, waabuu keŋ. N na jaami n Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ani Yeesu Kristo sɔŋ, dikuu ii maa wia. Bɔr maanii ba ra ŋɔ gunla iiŋ yarduu wia.

ref: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
text: Kɔraawiizi la minna hum ani n biini maa, di ra lizi u amaniyesuma di lii u Biibaal wia biini labuu niŋ ɛɛ n daansɛɛ hiŋ lugɔ n ɔɔ suŋŋuubuu ra tɛɛ ia saŋa maa minna jaamuu

ref: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
text: di ɔɔ ra suŋŋuu, di u sɛɛwɔ, ń jaa wer na ŋmɛnɛɛ di wer ba ii be ani bɔsɔna filaŋkeŋ.

ref: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
text: N na nyiŋŋuu ń na ia werge maa, di wer hiini ia ani Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋa bɛl, ka ií wer dɔɔ bɔkpega ii hiŋaa biini.

ref: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
text: Yaa maa daŋ hiini dɔŋa. Gunla miŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi la daŋ du ia bɔkpega, gunla ii ge n yarduu la du n ge bɔkpega.

ref: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
text: Yaabalaa, n na nyiŋŋi ii zum lugɔ saŋakpila maanii n faa ra nyiŋŋi n ba ii be, ka n faa waa wette ba. N na nyiŋŋi n wer na nɛra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi lii ii gba biini alugɔ miŋ nawɛɛ lii ii dɔŋahina banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ di du yeŋa maa biini la.

ref: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Kristo amaniyesuma la wia wanna ɛɛ hiihzi, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi fɔŋŋa wiarɛ, di wer ra lɛɛ banla maa n niŋ sɛɛ a wia. Jus hinaa ń feli ɛɛ guŋ tɛɛ, ka jaa ɛɛ tɛɛ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ.

ref: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
text: Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ yaa zum lii u amaniyesuma baglaa biini gunla un niŋ ɛɛ nɛ́ra wia deŋli u be. Yarda ɛɛ u luglii di kaa ɛɛ u tuna ge. Ba faa sɛbi guŋ wiarɛ, di ŋɔ, “Nɛr la wia n deŋlee, yardaa niŋ ɛɛ u miibɔɔ.” Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n fuuhwe werge wia

ref: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
text: Kɔraawiizi kaa gil yaa zum gunla u baaŋ n fuuhwe dikuu banla n vɛɛ u nua, ka ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la ni. Ba wia waa deŋlee. Ba ra tɔ wibii ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ,

ref: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, ba zum wibii labuu. Wia la n gillɛ nɛra zum Kɔraawiizi du denii. Kɔraawiizii lizaa chaaŋ, nɛr maa wer naa di zum u wia.

ref: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
text: Un ta durnya guŋŋ wa hel zinaa, ba wettoo na gunla un duwɛɛ. U duula waa na, ka ba wer na gunla un duwɛɛ u kuna la un tawɛɛ la be, di wer chi de zum u fɔŋŋa la n waa tuŋ la ni u Kɔraawiizi ge duula. U lizi a wia maanii chaaŋ. Awia, ba waa kaa dɔɔ nua ban niŋ ŋɔ wii maa.

ref: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, baŋ wette zum Kɔraawiizi la, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ bá tɔgzuu gunla n dɛguu. Ba biine waa huuhzɛɛ tɛu bá wer tɛu jaaŋ gba. Ba bir bugmi di ra fɛ nfɛrjagazi. Ba siwee waa pillɛɛ ka bir tɔ ra jaa.

ref: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
text: Ba ra yir bahinaa nunzunna ka ɛɛ gɛnaa.

ref: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
text: Kɔraawiizi n dɔɔ girme werge waa siwaa dɔɔwɛ la, ka ba vɛɛu ka ra tɔgzi kuna aŋhina bam mawɛɛ a ɛɛ lugɔ newea, zumbizi, kunnaazi anaazu hina ani kuntuuzaa.

ref: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
text: Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi bir har kpu baa, ba ra hiŋ ba kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa, di ra ɛɛ wikuna, di ra ɛɛ dɔŋa bɔrahɔna wichɔgaa.

ref: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
text: Ba kpa Kɔraawiizi wibii di chɛr kara wia, di ra tɔgzi kuna la un tawɛɛ la kaali u himmaa. Waabuu ɛɛ chiŋ ni hɛri taari di dɛg chɔlaa saŋa maa. Ami.

ref: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
text: Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi bir u har kpu baa, ba ra hiŋ ba kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa la. Ba haana gba vɛɛ ba ni baala chɔɔi la, Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa bá ra chɔɔ la, ka ra chɔɔ ba dɔŋa haana be.

ref: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
text: Baala ge ra ɛɛ guŋ di gil chɔɔi la n dɛkkɛ ka ra nyiŋŋi ba dɔŋa baala ani nyiŋŋichɔgaa werge maa, ba ni baa ra ɛɛ wikuna. Ba wileulaa wiarɛ ba ɔɔ na ba wichɔgaa kinturgaa.

ref: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
text: Baŋ waa sɛɛwɛ bá zum Kɔraawiizi la wiarɛ u gil ba birgi nfɛrchɔgaa hina di ra ɛɛ wia la n waa dɛkkɛ

ref: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
text: di dɔɔ wichɔgaa maa ni a dee werge maa, di ra sɛm, di dɔɔ kuna kɛkɛluu, miisɔɔh, bɔwii, nɛkpui, hɔɔzi dii, nɛdaraa ani nɛhaih werge. Ba ra munni nɛra wia

ref: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
text: di ra zɔɔzi nɛra, di hah Kɔraawiizi, di ra gbɛlli nɛra, di ra yir bahinaa nɛzenaa, di dɔɔ barabara, di ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi wichɔgfalaa, bá ra ɛɛ di ra vɛɛ ba maawaa ni ba mɛɛwaa nuuzi,

ref: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
text: di nyaa nfɛrɛ. Ba wia waa wibii dɔɔwɛ. Ba waa ba himmaa nɛra bila dɔɔwɛ, ba waa nɛra ni ra suŋ.

ref: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
text: Bannii maa, ba zum Kɔraawiizi widaulaarɛ alugɔ banla n na ɛɛ wia naa dɛg kpuirɛ, ka ba himmaa haa vɛɛ ra ɛɛa, di kaa ra chɔli banla n na ɛɛa la di ra jaa.
