ref: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
text: Hinla n na ŋɔ i dɔŋhiŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, haa nua dɔɔwɛ hin niŋ ŋɔ. I himmaanii i ra tɛɛ chɔgri la. Wichɔgaa la hiŋ kpawɛɛ chuguu la, a himmaanii i ra ɛɛ.

ref: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
text: Yaa zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ra di banla n na ɛɛ wia naa seriyaa ani wibii.

ref: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
text: Hinla n na chagzi i dɔŋhiŋ dikuu unna ɛɛ wia naa wia ka i himmaa ra ɛɛa, i daŋ wer lii Kɔraawiizi seriya dii biiniaa?

ref: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
text: Kɔraawiizi ra hiiniibuu werge, di ra tɛi sisɔna, di haa vɛɛ ra dii kanyitti werge maa, ka i ra binni a maa pɛɛ. Haa zummɛ lugɔ u ra ɛɛibuu winanaa la, í biini wer chɔgi dikuu i wichɔgaa la wiaa?

ref: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
text: Ka i bampirii du kpeg werge. Waa chɔgi dikuu wichɔgaa wia. I ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la ra dau, di u hɔpizii la wa hello un niŋ di seriyazi ani wibii la, u baaŋ daŋ fuuh i ni werge maa.

ref: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
text: U daŋ turgi bɛl maa ani gunla uŋ hummɛ.

ref: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
text: Banla n ɔɔ haa vɛɛ ra ɛɛ winanaa bá wer na girme, chɔlaa ani miibɔɔ la n waa tuŋ Kɔraawiizi be la, baabuu niŋ na u miibɔɔ la.

ref: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
text: Ka banla n na nyiŋŋi ba bɛŋ sɔŋ, ba waa Kɔraawiizi wia ra sɛɛ, ka ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la, baabuu daŋ na wia dikuu Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n kannɛ ba ni werge maa la wia.

ref: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Tɔɔrɔɔ ni biinichɔg daŋ wa huuzi nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Jus hinaa á feli huuzi, ka jaa huuzi banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ ge.

ref: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Nɛr la maa n na ɛɛ winanaa ge daŋ wa na girme, chɔlaa ani bampirsɔna. Jus hinaa niŋ feli na ka bánla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ ge na.

ref: God doesn't have any favorites!
text: Kɔraawiizi waa baŋhina ra tɔgzi kaali baŋhina.

ref: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
text: Banla n waa Moosis Gbɔg zummɛ ka ɛɛ wichɔgaa wa siu la, Moosis Gbɔg lɛi Kɔraawiizi kpa ra di ba seriya. Banla n zum u Gbɔg lawaa, aabuu ú kpa di di ba seriya.

ref: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
text: Banla n na nuu Gbɔg la wia lɛi niŋ deŋli Kɔraawiizi be. Ka banla n na hiŋaa, ba wiarɛ niŋ deŋli u be.

ref: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
text: Ba wiɛɛlaa ra bagluu lugɔ Kɔraawiizi sɛbi u Gbɔgrɛ du ba biine. Ba biine nfɛssi gba ra ɛɛ baabuu guŋ daansɛɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba himmaa nfɛssi ɔɔ tɛɛ baabuu chɔgri, ŋmɛnɛbɛl ge a kaa tɛɛ baa winanaa.

ref: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
text: Awia, gunnɛ á wa ɛɛ hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lii nɛra wolli ni baŋgia, di gil Yeesu Kristo di baa seriya. Gunnɛ n amaniyesuma la ra bagli. Jus hina ni Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg wia

ref: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
text: Ama, hinla n na yir i hiŋ Jus hinuu, i bɔra sɔɔni dikuu hiŋ zum Gbɔg la wia, i kaa kpa Kɔraawiizi ra ta bara,

ref: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
text: di zum u kipar wia, di wer zum wia la n wesse dikuu bam baglii u Gbɔg la wia,

ref: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
text: i kaa ra kpa i hiŋ zenni alugɔ i wetto ɛɛ sitɔɔri, di bagli nyuŋŋa ŋmɛnɛɛ di wer gil bɔchaaŋ ba banla n du bɔbiri la be,

ref: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
text: di ŋɔ i ɛɛ nɛbaglii, di ra bagli banla n waa wia zummɛ, di kaa ŋɔ i ɛɛ nabɔmaa di ra bagli bichalli wia, dikuu hiŋ wette dɔɔ nunzuma ni wibii, di lii Gbɔg la biini wia,

ref: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
text: hinla n na bagli nɛra wia, ɛrɛɛ haa i hiŋ a baglɛi? I ŋɔ bá gilɛɛ ra ŋmɛɛ. Hiŋwaa waa ŋmɛaa?

ref: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
text: I ŋɔ bá gilɛɛ ra sɛm. Hiŋwaa waa sɛmaa? I ra gbɛlli vugaa. Hiŋwaa waa kuna a ŋmɛɛ a diini biiniaa?

ref: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
text: Hinla n na chɔli i hiŋ lugɔ i zum Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la wia, ka bir a chɔgaa, Kɔraawiizi lɛi i ra binni pɛaa?

ref: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
text: Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini di ŋɔ, “Ii wiarɛ banla n waa Kɔraawiizi zummɛ ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ la.”

ref: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
text: Di ba teŋ i hɛŋ, i kaa ra hiŋ Gbɔg la, hɛŋ teŋaa la dɔɔ tɔnaa. Ama, di i ra chɔgi Gbɔg la, i birgi banla baŋ waa ba hɛna teŋree la bɛllɛ.

ref: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
text: Awia, di nɛr la baŋ waa u hɛŋ teŋŋe ra hiŋ Gbɔg la, ba wàá kpa guŋ ɛɛi birgi u hɛŋ teŋaa?

ref: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
text: Unla u hɛŋ n waa teŋŋe ka u ra hiŋ Gbɔg la, u daŋ tɛi chɔgri, dikuu hiŋ dɔɔ Gbɔg la di ɛɛ nɛr la baŋ teŋ i hɛŋ ka ra chɔgi a kiizi la wia.

ref: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
text: I baŋgia wikpoglaa lɛi niŋ gil i ɛɛ Jus hinuu. Bɔrahɔŋ teŋaa ge waa teŋaa himmaa ɛɛwɛ.

ref: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
text: Nɛr la n ɛɛ Jus hinuu himmaa, u biini wikpoglaa benii a lii. Nɛr la n dɔɔ bɔrahɔŋ teŋaa himmaa, u ge biinii a lii. Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii teŋaare ɛɛ teŋaa himmaa. Kii bɛl hiŋaa lɛi ɛɛ u himmaa. Newea lɛi niŋ chɔli a hiŋ. Kɔraawiizii niŋ chɔli a hiŋ.

ref: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
text: Di gunnɛ, ɛrɛɛ Jus hinawaa nuu suma kaali banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛi? Bɛɛ tɔnaa ba na ba hɛŋ teŋaa la biininei?

ref: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
text: Ba nuu sumaa werge, di kaa di tɔna yaa ni wikpila biini. Ka unnii ɛɛ wizenne a maa biini. Jus hina labuu Kɔraawiizi kpa u wiŋɔɔlaa bagli.

ref: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
text: Amɔ, Kɔraawiizi daŋ kuu baŋhina n waa yardɛɛ la wia vɛɛ u nuuzi laa?

ref: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
text: Akai! Di newee maa ɛɛ karahiŋ, ka Kɔraawiizi wia daŋ haa dɔɔ wibii. Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini, di ŋɔ, “Ba daŋ kpa wibii tɛɛ i wiŋɔzi. Di ba wa dii seriya, i hor daŋ du sum.”

ref: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
text: Di yaa wichɔgaa ɔɔ gil Kɔraawiizi wideŋlaa lii, di du wer werge, ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔi? Gil n kpa newea wiŋɔzi di kaa pɛɛzi. Di yaa wichɔgaa ɔɔ gil Kɔraawiizi wideŋlaa lii, ka Kɔraawiizi kaa tɔɔri yaa dikuu wichɔgaa la wia, wichɔgaarɛ u ra ɛɛ guŋ gɛɛ?

ref: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
text: Akai! Di Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ wichɔgaarɛ, ɛrɛɛ ú ɛɛ di wer di durnya seriyai?

ref: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
text: Di n kara wia ɔɔ gil Kɔraawiizi wibii dii ra lii nɛnnɛ u ra na sɔŋ, ɛrɛɛ ú kaa kpa n kara kannaa la ŋɔ n ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛriiwɛi?

ref: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
text: Amɔ, ya ŋɔ lugɔ ya ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa, ka winanaa wer lii a biiniaa? Baŋhina ra zɔɔzi yaabuu di ra ŋɔ lugɔ yaa ra ŋɔ gunnɛ. Ka banla n na ŋɔ guŋ, ba hor waa sum. A dɛkkɔ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ n niŋ fuuh ba ni. Nɛr maa wia waa deŋlee

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
text: Too. Ɛrɛɛ a jaa duɛi? Yaa Jus hinaa bɔmbɔ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ gɛɛ? Yaa waa baa bɔwɛɛ. Yaa faa baglɔɔrɛ lugɔ Jus hina ni banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ maanii ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra.

ref: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
text: Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, “Nɛr maa waa hoo ɛɛ nɛnanii ga tuŋ. Akai! Kpaŋkpaŋ maa waa hoo.

ref: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
text: Nɛr la n zum wia zɛɛ waa hoo. Nɛr la n na nyiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi bɔr gba waa hoo.

ref: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
text: Ba maa leuwoo ŋmɛnɛɛ, di bir pɛɛ. Bɛl maa waa hoo ra ɛɛ winanaa. Akai! Kpaŋkpaŋ maa waa hoo”

ref: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
text: “Ba nuuzi ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ŋmama la baŋ waa tɔɔgɛɛ. Ba ra ŋɔ wia ra dar nɛra.” “Ba wiŋɔzi la lugɔ duŋkpola siri.”

ref: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
text: “Nuuseei ni nyɛgzi su ba nuuzi.”

ref: These people quickly become violent.
text: “Ba hahzi manaŋ di ra la nɛkpui bɔr.

ref: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
text: Chɔgaa ni dɔgnya yaari ba ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: They don't know how to live in peace.
text: Ba waa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi ŋmɛnɛɛ zummɛ.”

ref: They don't even fear God.”
text: “Ba waa Kɔraawiizi ra ɔm.”

ref: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
text: Ii zummɔ lugɔ wii la maa Moosis Gbɔg la n na bagli, banla n na hiŋ guŋ, hiŋaa labuu a ra bagli guŋ bá gilɛɛ wer dɔɔ nua maa bá ŋɔ, dúrnya maa ge wer dɔɔ chɔgri Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
text: Gbɔg hiŋaa wàá wer gil nɛr maa wia deŋli Kɔraawiizi be. Gbɔg la biinii nɛra wer zum ba wichɔgaa. Yarda biinii wia deŋlaa ra lii

ref: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
text: Filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi pilli gunla nɛra wia n niŋ ɛɛ deŋli u benii. Gbɔg la hiŋaa bɔr lɛi á lii. A wiarɛ Moosis ni Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la faa ŋɔ la.

ref: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
text: Yeesu Kristo yarda bɔttɛ á lii. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil nɛr la maa n yardi Yeesu wia deŋli u be. Waa nɛr maa a tɔgzi kaali u dɔŋhiŋ.

ref: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
text: Nɛr maanii ɛɛ wichɔgaa di nyaa Kɔraawiizi girme.

ref: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
text: Yeesu Kristo yau yaabuu ha. Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi wer gil yaa wia deŋli u be. U ɛɛ a maanii tɛɛ yaa pɛɛpɛɛ, dikuu u nɛsunaa wia.

ref: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
text: u wia deŋloore. U daŋ gil nɛra zum a maa biini filaŋkeŋ, ka ú wer ɛɛ Wideŋlaa Hiŋ, di kaa wer gil banla n yardi Yeesu la ge wia wer deŋli u be.

ref: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
text: Awia, lee ya jaa na bɔr chɔli yaa hinaanɛi? Yaa wàá wer na bɔr. Bɛɛ n tɔ a bɔrɛi? Winanaa ɛɛi gɛɛ? Akai! Yarda labuu tɔu.

ref: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
text: Yaa zummɔ lugɔ nɛr n niŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ ú wia wer deŋli u be. Gbɔg hiŋaa wàá wer gil u wia deŋli u be.

ref: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
text: Gɛɛ Jus hina bɛnnɛ niŋ wer hiŋ Kɔraawiizɛi? Banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ wàá wer hiŋuu gɛɛ? Ba gba daŋ wer hiŋuu.

ref: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
text: Too. Yaa gillɔɔ Moosis Gbɔg la bir pɛɛ dikuu yarda wia gɛɛ? Akai. Yaa tɛɛabuu fɔŋŋa ra jaa.

ref: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
text: Ií binni yaa naabaal Abraham wia biini. Ɛrɛɛ u ge wia faa duɛi?

ref: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔ u wia deŋli u be, dikuu u winanaa la uŋ faa ra ɛɛ wia, u daŋ vii wer chɔli u hiŋ. Ka wàá wer chɔli u hiŋ Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
text: Ɛrɛɛ ba faa sɛbi u wia Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biininei? Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, “Abraham yardi Kɔraawiizii. Kɔraawiizi kuu guŋ wia gil u wia deŋli u be.”

ref: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
text: Di nɛr hummɔ, Kɔraawiizi turguu, kinnɛ u turgi. Sunzaa lɛi.

ref: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
text: Ka nɛr waa hummɛ ka dɔɔ yarda unla n niŋ gil nɛchɔgii wia deŋli u be la ni, ba daŋ ŋɔ lugɔ u yarda la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi gil u wia deŋli u be.

ref: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
text: Gunnɛ yaa naabaal Deevid gba faa bagli di ŋɔ lugɔ nɛr la maa Kɔraawiizi n waa u wiɛɛlaa binnɛɛ, ka gil u wia deŋli u be, nuu sumaa.

ref: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
text: Nɛr la maa Kɔraawiizi n wàá pɛɛzuu u wichɔgaa wia, nuu sumaa.”

ref: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
text: Suma naa, banla n na teŋri hɛna bɛnnɛ a diu gɛɛ banla n waa teŋri gba ra diubuuwɛi? Yaa n na ŋɔ dí Abraham yardi Kɔraawiizii, Kɔraawiizi kuu guŋ wia gil u wia deŋli u be naa,

ref: But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
text: ɛrɛɛ u faa du a saŋai? Ba faa teŋ u hɛnnɛ a saŋa gɛɛ, gɛɛ ba faa haa waa u hɛŋ teŋŋei? Ba faa haa waa u hɛŋ teŋŋe a saŋa.

ref: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
text: Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ u wia deŋli u be dikuu uŋ yarduu la wia la, denii u ŋɔ ú teŋ u hɛŋ, gúŋ bagli gunla uŋ gillɛ u wia deŋli u be dikuu u yarda la wia, ka ú wer ɛɛ banla maa baŋ waa ba hɛna teŋree, ka ba ra yardi Kɔraawiizi la mɛɛ, bá ge wia wer deŋli u be,

ref: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
text: di kaa ɛɛ banla ba hɛna n teŋree ge mɛɛ, banla n na yardi Kɔraawiizi gunla yaa naabaal Abraham la n faa yarduu, saŋa la u hɛŋ n faa haa waa teŋŋe la. Banla n na hiŋ guŋ jaa ba hɛŋ teŋaa ni la, ba mɛɛrɛ Abraham la.

ref: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
text: Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ Abraham ni u biizi lugɔ ba daŋ wa dɔɔ durnya, ba Gbɔg hiŋaa biini lɛi u lii. Kɔraawiizi n kuu yarda la uŋ yarduu wia di gil u wia deŋli u be la, a yarda biinii Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii la lii.

ref: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
text: Di a faa ɛɛwɔ lugɔ banla n na hiŋ Gbɔgrɛ niŋ dɔɔ durnya la, guŋwaa, yarda daŋ vii birgi kunduma, Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii la ge bir pɛɛ.

ref: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
text: Gbɔg la ra ba Kɔraawiizi baaŋ ninɛɛ. An du de nɛra ge ra chɔgaa wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi baaŋ na fuuh nɛra ni la. Di Gbɔg faa waa hoo, nɛra faa wàá wer chɔgaa.

ref: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
text: Awia, yarda benii Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii la lii, yaa wer na a maa dikuu Kɔraawiizi n na suŋ nɛra ni, di ra hiini baa la wia. Yaa maa mɛɛrɛ Abraham. Banla n na hiŋ Moosis Gbɔg di ra teŋri hɛna ani banla n waa hɛna a teŋri ka yardi Kɔraawiizi alugɔ Abraham la n faa yarduu la, ba maanii niŋ wer dɔɔ tamii Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii la biini, di na wia la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
text: Ba faa sɛbi gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini di ŋɔ, “N gillɔɔ i ɛɛ nɛdeekpila maa mɛɛ.” Kɔraawiizi la n wette gil kuna la n siuwɛ á kaa dɔɔ miibɔɔ, di kaa wer ŋɔ wia la n haa waa ɛɛwɛ wia alugɔ a teŋ ɛɛwɔɔ la, waabuu Abraham yardi.

ref: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
text: Gunla Kɔraawiizi n faa ŋɔwɛɛ la, ba daŋ faa ŋɔ lugɔ guŋ wàá wer ɛɛ. Ka Abraham n faa dɔɔ u wiŋɔzi tamii werge maa wiarɛ u wer birgi nɛdeekpila maa mɛɛ, gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛu, dí u naanna daŋ ŋmɛnɛ du kpil la.

ref: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
text: Waa Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la aanɛɛ di ŋɔ lugɔ guŋ wàá wer ɛɛ, ka bir dɔɔ yardakpeg tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ,

ref: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
text: di wer ɛɛ u tamii werge maa lugɔ wii la maa uŋ ŋɔ nua la, u daŋ ɛɛu.

ref: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
text: U bɛŋ wia lɛi ba faa sɛbi, dí Kɔraawiizi kuu guŋ wiarɛ gil u wia deŋli u be la.

ref: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
text: Yaa gba wiarɛ ba faa kuu sɛbi guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u daŋ gil yaa banla n yardi unla n lalli yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo siu biini la ge gba wia deŋli u be.

ref: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
text: Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ Yeesu siu dikuu yaa wichɔgaa wia, di kaa lalluu siu biini yáa wia wer deŋli u be.

ref: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ yaa wia deŋli u be dikuu yaa n yarduu wia naa, yaa nuu jaa dɔɔ nuukpannɛ dikuu yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo wia.

ref: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
text: U wiarɛ yaa wer dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi yarda di ba u be u suŋ yaa ni di ra hiini yaa kennaa unna hiini yaa naa. Yaa bɔra sɔɔnɔɔrɛ dikuu yaa n dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi tamii alugɔ yaa daŋ ŋmɛnɛ na girme u be wia.

ref: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
text: Yaa bɔra kaa sɔɔni yaa dikuu tɔɔrɔɔ la banna ɛɛ yaa wia, dikuubɛɛwiai, tɔɔrɔɔ labuu niŋ gil ya wer dɔɔ kanyitti.

ref: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
text: Di yaa dɔɔ tamii u ni, hiihzi wàá ka lau yaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi kpa u nɔŋŋaarɛ du yaa ni werge maa u Dumnaniinanii la un tɛɛ yaa la fɔŋŋa biini.

ref: Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful.
text: Yaa faa haa waa wikuarii maa dɔɔwɛ. Ka a saŋa n wa helle, Kristo lɛɛ nɛchɔgaa siu di siu.

ref: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
text: Di nɛr ɛɛ nɛnanii ka anɛɛ n niŋ sɛɛ lɛɛ u siu di siu tɛuwɛi? Aŋhinabe, di u ɛɛ nɛnanii, baŋhina daŋ dɔɔ bampirii lugɔ ba siu tɛu.

ref: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
text: Ka ií na gunla Kɔraawiizi n nɔŋŋi yaa werge maa. Yaa n faa haa ɛɛ wichɔgɛɛra, ka Kristo wer lɛɛ yaa siu a saŋa di siu tɛɛ yaa.

ref: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
text: Uŋ wette siu tɛɛ yaa di gil yaa wia wer deŋli Kɔraawiizi be naa, di hɔpizii la wa hello Kɔraawiizi baaŋ wa fuuh nɛra ni, Yeesu wàá ka hiini yaa werge maa, di lɛɛ yaa u baaŋfuuih wia biiniaa?

ref: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
text: Di yaa faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔma, ka u bir gil yaa nuu dɔɔ nuukpaŋ dikuu u Biibaal n siuwɛ wia, amɔ, yaa nuu n jaa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ naa, wàá hiini yaa werge maa kaali guŋŋ? U daŋ hiini yaa ya wer na lɛɛi dikuu u Biibaal miibɔɔ un dɔɔwɛ filaŋkennaa wia.

ref: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
text: U guŋ bɛŋ lɛi gba. Ka yaa bɔra sɔɔni yaabuu dikuu Kɔraawiizi n ga Yeesu Kristo ni ɛɛ la wia. Yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo gillɔɔ yaa nuu wer dɔɔ nuukpaŋ. Andama ni Kristo wia

ref: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
text: Too. Nɛkpannɛ ba wichɔgaa ni durnya. Wichɔgaa la ge ba siu ni, nɛra maa jaa ra siuzi dikuu ba maa n dɔɔ chɔgri lii nɛkpaŋ wichɔgaa la biini wia.

ref: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
text: Wichɔgaa faa du durnyaa mɔɔ ka Gbɔg la wa lii. Ka Gbɔg la n faa waa hoo la, ba faa waa chɔgri dɔɔwɛ a saŋa.

ref: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
text: Ama, siu faa di koraa lii Andama saŋa la guŋŋ wa hel Moosis ge saŋa la, di kpu banla n faa waa Andama wichɔgii la dɔŋ ɛɛwɛ gba. Andama la wiarɛ bagli unla n faa ra ba la wia.

ref: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
text: Ka nɛsunaa la Kɔraawiizi n suŋ yaa ni la, u kaali Andama wichɔgaa la werge maa. Nɛkpaŋ wichɔgaa wiarɛ nɛkpila siuzi. Nɛkpaŋ nɛsunaa wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi ge nɛsunaa bir du kaŋ werge, u kpa sunzi nɛkpila. Yeesu Kristoo a nɛkpaŋ.

ref: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
text: Nɛkpannɛ ba wichɔgaa ni. Nɛkpaŋ genii ba Kɔraawiizi sunzaa la ni. Ka ba wia waa mɛgzɛɛ. Nɛkpaŋ wichɔgaa la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi di yaa seriya tɛɛ yaa chɔgri. Ka nɛkpila wichɔgaarɛ Kɔraawiizi gil tɛɛ baa ú sunzinanii la biini, di gil ba wia deŋli u be.

ref: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
text: Di nɛkpaŋ wichɔgaa gillɔ siu wer di kora durnya dikuu a nɛkpaŋ wia, guŋwaa, banla n na hiinaa la Kɔraawiizi n suŋ ba ni, di hiini baa la ni u sunzinanii la un sunzi baa ba wia wer deŋli u be la, baawaa daŋ di miibɔɔ kora, ú dɔɔ kpegzi werge maa kaali siu hor la, dikuu nɛkpaŋ nɛɛhiŋ Yeesu Kristo la wia.

ref: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
text: Awia, gunla nɛkpaŋ wichɔgii n gillɛ nɛr maa dɔɔ chɔgri la, gunnɛ nɛkpaŋ winanii gil nɛra maa wia wer deŋli Kɔraawiizi be di gil ba dɔɔ miibɔɔ la.

ref: Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
text: Gunla nɛkpila n birgi wichɔgɛɛra, dikuu nɛkpaŋ n vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nua wia, gunnɛ nɛ́kpila ge wia wer deŋli u be, dikuu nɛkpaŋ n sɛɛ u nua wia la.

ref: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
text: A Gbɔg ballɔɔ wíchɔgaa wer gbigi. Ka wichɔgaa n gbigee la, Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa la wa kaalaabuu werge maa.

ref: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
text: Wichɔgaa lɛɛ fɔŋŋaa di di kora dikuu siu wia. Gunnɛ Kɔ́raawiizi nɛsunaa ge wer lɛɛ fɔŋŋa, dikuu gunla Kɔraawiizi n ɛɛwɛ nɛ́ra wia wer deŋli u be la wia, di di u ge kora, ya wer na miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo be.

ref: What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better?
text: Ɛrɛɛ ya jaa ŋɔ naanɛi? Ya haa ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa ka Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa la wer du kaŋ werge gɛɛ?

ref: No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning?
text: Akai. Yaa n siuwɛ wichɔgaa be naa, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ ya kaa ra ɛɛa alugɔ yaa n waa a be siuwɛnɛi?

ref: Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death?
text: Gɛɛ ii waa zummɛ lugɔ yaa banla maa baŋ sɔwɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nii, ya ra hiŋ Yeesu Kristo la, u siurɛ ba sɔ yaa, yaa siuwaa?

ref: When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
text: Awia, baŋ sɔ yaa a nii la, yaa ni Yeesu siuwɔɔ gunla, ba hug yaa. Ba ɛɛ gunnɛ, gúŋ bagli lugɔ Kɔraawiizi n lalli Kristo di bagli u fɔŋŋazeŋ la, gunnɛ u ɛɛ tɛɛ yaa ge, ya wer dɔɔ miibɔɔfalii, di ra hiŋ miibɔɔfalii la ŋmɛnɛɛ.

ref: If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him.
text: Aŋ ɛɛwɛ lugɔ yaa nuubuu kpauwɛ siu, u siu la, a daŋ kaa ɛɛ lugɔ yaa gba daŋ wer izi, u izaa la.

ref: We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin.
text: Yaa zummɔ lugɔ yaa miibɔɔbinaarɛ ba kpu Yeesu daakaŋlii la ni, guŋ gil yaa bɔrahɔna la n mani wichɔgaa la wer siu de, ya gilɛɛ kaa kpa yaa hinaa birgi wichɔgaa yoma.

ref: We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
text: Banla n siuwɛ la, nɛr maa waa kaa ra pɛɛzi baa wichɔgaa wia.

ref: As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
text: Di yaa nuubuu siuwɛ, yaa yarduubuu lugɔ yaa nuu danna nyiŋ.

ref: We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die.
text: Yaa zummɔ lugɔ Kɔraawiizi n lalli Kristo naa, wàá ka siu maa. Siu wàá ka wer dɔɔ fɔŋŋa u ni.

ref: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
text: Un siuwɛ la, kakpaŋ bɛnnɛ u siu, di wer chɔgi wichɔgaa fɔŋŋa. Uŋ izee di ra nyiŋ la ge, u du denii tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
text: Awia, ií zum lugɔ ii siuwɔɔ wichɔgaa be ɛnɛ maa, ka ra nyiŋ Kɔraawiiziwaa be, dikuu ii ni Yeesu Kristo n kpauwɛ wia.

ref: Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires
text: Awia, ií gilɛɛ gil wichɔgaa dɔɔ ii bɔrahɔna naa fɔŋŋa, ii ra sɛɛ a nua di ra hiŋ ii kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa la.

ref: or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil wichɔgaa dɔɔ ii yeŋa, ii kpaa ra ɛɛ wia la n waa deŋlee. Ii ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛra la n izi siu biini. Ií gil Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ ia, di gil u dɔɔ ii yeŋa maa fɔŋŋa, ú kpaa ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee.

ref: Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law. Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
text: Wichɔgaa wàá dɔɔ fɔŋŋa ii ni. Gbɔg la lɛi dɔɔ ia. Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa labuu dɔɔ ia. Wideŋlaa yoma wia

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not!
text: Miŋ ŋɔ kennaa lugɔ Gbɔg la lɛi dɔɔ yaa, ka Kɔraawiizi nɛsunaa labuu dɔɔ yaa naa, amɔ, ya ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa gɛɛ? Akai. Guŋ waa ŋmɛnɛɛ dɔɔwɛ.

ref: Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him.
text: Ii waa zummɛ lugɔ nɛr la maa iiŋ gillɛ u dɔɔ fɔŋŋa, ii ni ii ra hiŋ u nua, waabuu niŋ kpa ia birgi u yoma di gil ii ra hiŋ u nuaa? Di wichɔgaa nuarɛ ii hiŋ, ii daŋ humuu, siu ge ɛɛ ii huma tɔna. Di Kɔraawiizi ge nuarɛ ii hiŋ, ii daŋ hum u ge, ii wia wer deŋli u be.

ref: You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received.
text: Ka Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ jaannɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa yomaa, ka filaŋkeŋ ii bampiree tɛɛ iabuu lugɔ ií sɛɛ Kɔraawiizi baglaa la bam bagli ia, ií ra hiŋ.

ref: Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
text: Kɔraawiizi n wa lɛɛ ia wichɔgaa fɔŋŋa biini la, ii jaa kpa iihinaarɛ ra birgi winanaa ge yoma.

ref: I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
text: Minna ŋɔ yoma wia naa, newee wiarɛ n kpa ra mɛgzi, ií wer zum a zɛɛ manaŋ. Iiŋ faa kpa ii yeŋa ra ɛɛ wikuna ni wichɔgaa, di kaa ra na wichɔgaa a be la, ií jaa kpaa ra ɛɛ winanaa filaŋkeŋ, ií wer birgi nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ.

ref: When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God.
text: Saŋa la iiŋ faa ɛɛ wichɔgaa yoma la, winanaa faa waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ ii ni, ii ra ɛɛa.

ref: But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death.
text: Ii faa wettoo na winanii maa dee a biiniaa? Akai. Wia la iiŋ faa ra ɛɛ, jaa ra ɛɛ iabuu hiihzi filaŋkeŋ. A maa tunaa siu.

ref: Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, Kɔraawiizi lɛɛ iabuu lii wichɔgaa la fɔŋŋa biini, di gil ii birgi u yoma. Iiŋ wette ɛɛ nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ la, guŋ ɛɛ ii tɔnaa filaŋkeŋ. A tuna genii miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la.

ref: Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
text: Wichɔgaa kinturgaare siu. Ka Kɔraawiizi sunzaarɛ miibɔɔ la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ la, dikuu yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo wia.

ref: My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive.
text: Yaabalaa, ii ɛɛ kiizunnaa. Awia, ii daŋ zum lugɔ gbɔgrɛ dɔɔ nɛr u miibɔɔ saŋa maa.

ref: For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free
text: Di haaŋ yuuwɔ, di u jaari du de, gbɔg la ɔɔ giluu u jaari dɔɔu. Ka di u jaari hiŋ wa siuwɔ, u jaa lii u fɔŋŋa la biinii.

ref: to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
text: Di u jaari haa du de, ka u chɔ ga du baal bɛl be, ba daŋ yiruu hahsɛnsɛnni. Ka di u jaari siuwɔ, kii la waa kaa dɔɔ u fɔŋŋa. Di u laŋŋɔ ga yuu jaari bɛl, ka waa kaa ɛɛ hahsɛnsɛnni.

ref: That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God.
text: Too. Yaabalaa, Kɔraawiizi faa gillɔɔ ii gba siu Gbɔg la be, dikuu ii ni Kɔraawiizi n kpauwɛ siu la wia, ka ií wer yuu nɛfalii, unla uŋ lallɛɛ siu biini la. U ɛɛ gunnɛ wínanaa wer lii a biini tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die.
text: Saŋa la yaa bɔrahɔna n faa dɔɔ fɔŋŋa yaa ni la, Gbɔg la faa ɔɔ giluu kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa wia ra ɛɛ yaa biine, di lauri yaa yeŋa ra ɛɛ wia la siu n na lii a biine la.

ref: But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law. The Battle with Sin
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, yaa lii Gbɔg la fɔŋŋa biinii, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa siuwɔɔ, wia la n faa lauri yaa la be, di jaa wer ra hum ani bampirfalii la u Dumnanii n tɛɛ yaa la. Yaa waa kaa ra hum dikuu gbɔg n na fir yaa wia. Gbɔg ni wichɔgaa wia

ref: Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this.
text: Too. Ɛrɛɛ ya ŋɔ naanɛi? Gbɔg la waa wer gɛɛ? Akai. A wessoo. Di a Gbɔg wia lɛi, n faa waa wette zum wichɔgaa. Di Gbɔg la vii waa baglɛɛ lugɔ kɛkɛluu waa wer, n faa waa zummɛ lugɔ kɛkɛluu waa wer.

ref: It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
text: Miŋ wa zum Gbɔg la, wichɔgaa jaa na a ŋmɛnɛɛrɛ, di gil n dɔɔ kɛkɛluu werge. Di Gbɔg waa hoo, wichɔgaa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ a siuwɔɔ.

ref: Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life,
text: N faa waa Gbɔg zummɛ ka du de. Ka miŋ wa zum Gbɔg la, wichɔgaa jaa izi ra nyiŋ, di kpuŋ.

ref: and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death.
text: Gbɔg la n niŋ vii ɛɛ miibɔɔ wia tɛŋ la bir lawiŋ du lii siu biini.

ref: Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died.
text: Wichɔgaa n wa na a ŋmɛnɛɛ dikuu Gbɔg la wia, a wer dariŋ di kpaa kpuŋ.

ref: Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
text: Ama, Gbɔg la ɛɛ kunnanaarɛ. Widaulaa la bɛl maa ge ɛɛ kunnanii. A maa deŋloore, di du wer.

ref: Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is.
text: Wia la n wesse daŋ kpa siu du n ni gɛɛ? Akai. Wichɔgaarɛ niŋ ɛɛ guŋ. Aabuu gillɛ kunnanii bir duŋ siu biini, ń wer zum wichɔgaa zɛɛ. Kii la gillɔɔ n zum gunla wichɔgaa n chummɛ werge maa.

ref: We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin.
text: Yaa zummɔ lugɔ Gbɔg la ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii wiarɛ. Ka miŋwaa du newea duula. Wichɔgaa lawiŋ birgi a yom.

ref: In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate.
text: Maa n himmaa wiɛɛlaa zɛɛ zummɛ. Wia la minna nyiŋŋi ɛɛi, aa lɛi n na ɛɛ. Wia la miŋ hahwɛɛ, aabuu n na ɛɛ.

ref: Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good.
text: Miŋ waa nyiŋŋi a ɛɛi ka ra ɛɛa la, gunna bagli lugɔ n sɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Gbɔg la wessoo.

ref: So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: Miŋ lɛi ra ɛɛ a wia. Ka wichɔgaa la n du n biini labuu gillɛ n na ɛɛa.

ref: I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot.
text: N zummɔ lugɔ n manni naa, n newee mannii la, waa winanii maa dɔɔwɛ. N ɔɔ ra nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ winanaa, ka ɛɛa ra huhzi.

ref: Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong.
text: Winanaa la minna nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ, aa lɛi n na ɛɛ. Ka wichɔgaa la miŋ waa nyiŋŋi, aabuu n na ɛɛ.

ref: And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: Di n na ɛɛ wia la miŋ waa nyiŋŋi, amɔ, miŋ lɛi kaa ra ɛɛa. Ka wichɔgaa la n du n biini labuu jaa ra ɛɛa.

ref: The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right.
text: N jaa na di n mannii guŋ, n vɛɛa huhzi. Saŋa maa, di n waa nyiŋŋi n ɛɛ winanaa, wichɔgaa la ɔɔ du de.

ref: With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God.
text: Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg la wia du n biinii, n na nyiŋŋi n hiŋaa.

ref: But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do.
text: Ka n na lugɔ n bɔrahɔŋ manni kurgɔɔrɛ, di ra yoo n ni n biini nfɛrɛ la, di ɔɔ wer lawiŋ, di gil n na sɛɛ n bɔrahɔŋ wichɔgaa la.

ref: What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die?
text: Ee! Wiarɛ huuziŋ bɔnnaa. Anɛɛ n niŋ wer lɛɛŋ n bɔrahɔnnaa n na nyiŋŋi u kpuŋ naa benei?

ref: Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me. So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
text: Kɔraawiizii niŋ wer lɛɛŋ, dikuu yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo wia. U dɔɔ jaannɛ werge. Awia, n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgrɛ ani n biini maa, ka ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa ani n newee manni.

ref: If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished.
text: Awia, di yaa ni Yeesu Kristo kpauwɔ, Kɔraawiizi wàá ka di ya seriya ya chol.

ref: The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death.
text: U Dumnanii la n na tɛɛ ia miibɔɔ dikuu ii ni Yeesu Kristo n kpauwɛ la wia, u dɔɔra daŋ lɛɛ ia wichɔgaa ni siu fɔŋŋa biini.

ref: The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin.
text: Wia la Gbɔg la n faa waa wette ɛɛ dikuu newee manni n ɔɔ gil u ra bɛɛli la wia, Kɔraawiizi ɛɛabuu. U hum u himmaa Biibaallɛ dikuu nɛra wichɔgaa wia, di gil u dɔɔ newea ge bɔrahɔŋ la n ɔɔ gil ba ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa la, di wa chɔgi wichɔgaa la fɔŋŋa newea bɔrahɔŋ ni.

ref: He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
text: U ɛɛ gunnɛ, ka yáa banla n waa ɔɔ ra ɛɛ yaa wia yaa bɔrahɔŋ fɔŋŋa biini, ka ra ɛɛa Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini wer ɛɛ winanaa la maa a Gbɔg n na bagli.

ref: People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things.
text: Banla n ɔɔ gil ba bɔrahɔŋ dɔɔ baa la, ba bɔrahɔŋ wiarɛ ba kpa su siwii. Banla ge n ɔɔ gil Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii dɔɔ baa, u wiarɛ ba ge kpa su siwii.

ref: If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace.

text: dikuubɛɛwiai, gunla nɛra n ɔɔ yardi Kɔraawiizi ba bampiree biini wiarɛ u ɔɔ gil ba wia deŋli u be. Ba nuuzi n bagli ba yarda la wiarɛ u ra lɛɛ baa.

ref: The Scriptures say no one who has faith will be disappointed,
text: Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ kaa ŋɔ, “Nɛr la maa n haŋ yarduu wàá bir di hiihzi,”

ref: no matter if that person is a Jew or a Gentile. There is only one Lord, and he is generous to everyone who asks for his help.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi waa baŋhina a tɔgzi kaali baŋhina. Banla n ɛɛ Jus hina ni banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ maa ɛɛ kpannɛ u be. Ba maa Dɔɔri ɔɔ nuu banla maa n na yir u sɔnnɛ, di ra hiini ba maa werge maa.

ref: All who call out to the Lord will be saved.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛr la maa n niŋ yir Kɔraawiizi sɔŋ, ú lɛɛu, u daŋ lɛɛu.”

ref: How can people have faith in the Lord and ask him to save them, if they have never heard about him? And how can they hear, unless someone tells them?
text: Ka di ba wɔɔ yardɛɛ, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ di wer yir u sɔŋ ú lɛɛ baai? Di ba haa waa u wia nuuwɛ ge, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ di wer yarduuwɛi? Di nɛr maa waa u wia ra bagli, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ di wer nuu u wiai?

ref: And how can anyone tell them without being sent by the Lord? The Scriptures say it is a beautiful sight to see even the feet of someone coming to preach the good news.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi waa nɛra hummɛ, ɛrɛɛ á nɛra ɛɛ di wer bagli u wiai? Ií nuu gunla baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ biini. Ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Nɛra la n ɔɔ vol ra lizi amaniyesuma la balaa ɔɔ du wer ninɛɛ werge.”

ref: Yet not everyone has believed the message. For example, the prophet Isaiah asked, “Lord, has anyone believed what we said?”
text: Ka nɛra maa lɛi sɛɛwɛ tɛɛ amaniyesuma la. Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa sɛbɔɔrɛ di pɛɛzi, “N Dɔɔri, bɛl maa sɛɛ wiŋɔzi la yaa n nuuwɛ di bagli baa labuu naá?”

ref: No one can have faith without hearing the message about Christ.
text: Yarda ɔɔ lii wiŋɔzi la yaa n nuuwɛ biinii. Wiŋɔzi la ge ɛɛ Kristo wia la.

ref: But am I saying that the people of Israel did not hear? No, I am not! The Scriptures say, “The message was told everywhere on earth. It was announced all over the world.”
text: Ka ií gil n pɛɛzi ia wii bɛl. Ba waa nuuwɛ gɛɛ? Ba nuuwɔɔ. Ba faa sɛbi chiŋ kuna wiarɛ di ŋɔ, “Durnya maanii chiŋ kuna loobee ra hel. Nɛr maa waa hoo hɛri naa biini, a kuna n wɔɔ ra bagli wia.”

ref: Did the people of Israel understand or not? Moses answered this question when he told that the Lord had said, “I will make Israel jealous of people who are a nation of nobodies. I will make them angry with people who don't understand a thing.”
text: Ií gil n kaa pɛɛzi ia. Izrɛl hina waa zummɛ gɛɛ? Ba zummɔɔ. N daŋ feli bagli gunla Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Moosis n faa sɛbɛɛ, dí, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ gil ii bɔra a wii, dikuu banla n ɛɛ nɛdumazi wia, di gil ii na baaŋ dikuu nɛra n waa wia zummɛ wia.”

ref: Isaiah was fearless enough to tell that the Lord had said, “I was found by people who were not looking for me. I appeared to the ones who were not asking about me.”
text: Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya la faa lɔ bampiriire, di sɛbi, “Banla n faa waa n bɔr a nyiŋŋi, baabuu wa naŋ. Banla n faa waa n wia ra pɛɛzi, baabuu n bagli n wia tɛɛ.”

ref: And Isaiah said about the people of Israel, “All day long the Lord has reached out to people who are stubborn and refuse to obey.”
text: Ka uŋ wa ŋɔ Izrɛl hinawaa wia, u ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N yaa n noneere chɔɔzi guŋŋ bɔr wa duani, di ŋɔ bá ba n be, ka ba waa sɛɛwɛ. Ba ɛɛ dignikpega hinaa di ra vɛɛ n wiŋɔzi.”

ref: Am I saying that God has turned his back on his people? Certainly not! I am one of the people of Israel, and I myself am a descendant of Abraham from the tribe of Benjamin.
text: Amɔ, Kɔraawiizi jaa vɛɛ u nɛra haɔ? Akai. N gba ɛɛ Izrɛl hinuurɛ, di ɛɛ Abraham naana bɛl lii Bɛnjamin dee biini.

ref: God did not turn his back on his chosen people. Don't you remember reading in the Scriptures how Elijah complained to God about the people of Israel?
text: Wàá sɛɛ vɛɛ banla uŋ felee nɔŋŋi la. Ii waa liizi gunla baŋ faa sɛbi Ɛlija wia laa? U faa suŋŋi Kɔraawiizii di ra bagli Izrɛl hina wichɔgaa wia keŋ.

ref: He said, “Lord, they killed your prophets and destroyed your altars. I am the only one left, and now they want to kill me.”
text: “N Dɔɔri, i dɔgtɛɛzii ba kpuuzi la, di kaa lau i mbusu lizibɔra purgi ta. N bɛnnɛ kawɛɛ. Ba kaa ra nyiŋŋi bá kpu n ge.”

ref: This means that only a chosen few of the people of Israel found what all of them were searching for. And the rest of them were stubborn,
text: Ɛrɛɛ jaa naanɛi? Wii la Izrɛl hina n faa ra nyiŋŋi la, ba wɔɔ nawɛɛ. Ka banla Kɔraawiizi n lizɛɛ tɛɛ u hiŋ, baabuu nau. Ka banla n wɔɔ nawɛɛ, Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ ba bampiree bir du tɔg.

ref: It is the same way now. God treated the people of Israel with undeserved grace, and so a few of them are still his followers.
text: Awia, gunnɛ a du filaŋkeŋ. Izrɛl hina tamaa du de, Kɔraawiizi n suŋ ba ni di lizi baa tɛɛ u hiŋ.

ref: This happened because of God's undeserved kindness and not because of anything they have done. It could not have happened except for God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Too. Di u lizi baa dikuu un suŋ ba ni la wia, a waa kaa ɛɛ lugɔ ba hunnanaa wiarɛ u lizi baa la. Di u nɛsunaa faa lii hunnanaa biini, u vii wàá ka ɛɛ nɛsunaa.

ref: just as the Scriptures say, “God made them so stupid that their eyes are blind, and their ears are still deaf.”
text: Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ ba nfɛrɛ du tɔg werge, di kaa tɛɛ baa siwee la n waa na ani digna la ge n waa nuu, haali di wa lii zinaa.”

ref: Then David said, “Turn their meals into bait for a trap, so that they will stumble and be given what they deserve.
text: Yaa naabaal Deevid faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di ba wa chaalɔɔ, ba bɔra sɔɔni ba ra di, gil a birgi wia tɛɛ baa alugɔ sidɛɛ di lau baa bá kɛŋli, bá wichɔgaa kim wa turgi ba ni.

ref: Blindfold their eyes! Don't let them see. Bend their backs beneath a burden that will never be lifted.” Gentiles Will Be Saved
text: Gil ba siwee biri bá na bɔr huhzi. Gil ba ɔɔ haŋ bugmi, di hanna la.” Nɛra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ lɛɛi wia

ref: Do I mean that the people of Israel fell, never to get up again? Certainly not! Their failure made it possible for the Gentiles to be saved, and this will make the people of Israel jealous.
text: N daŋ kaa pɛɛzi ia wii bɛl. Baŋ kɛŋlɛɛ naa, ba cholloo bá wia tuŋ kɔrai gɛɛ? Akai. Ban cholle naa, banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ daŋ jaa wer na bɔr, Kɔ́raawiizi lɛɛ baa, á ɛɛ Jus hina bɔwii.

ref: But if the rest of the world's people were helped so much by their sin and loss, they will be helped even more by their full return.
text: Too. Durnya n wette na suma ba wichɔgaa bɔr la, banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ n wette nuu suma ba cholli bɔnnaa, di a Jus hina kaa wa na lɛɛi Kɔraawiizi be, a wàá ka ɛɛ suma werge maa?

ref: I am now speaking to you Gentiles, and as long as I am an apostle to you, I will take pride in my work.
text: N ŋɔ wia naabuu ra tɛɛ ii banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ. Kɔraawiizi gillɔɔ n ɛɛ u huŋhunni, di ra bagli banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ u wia. N na kpa huma labuu tɔgzi werge maa.

ref: I hope in this way to make some of my own people jealous enough to be saved.
text: Aŋhinabe, n daŋ wer gil n himmaa nɛra la bɔra ra wii, dikuu minna hum n huma naa wia, ka wer na baŋhina tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: When Israel rejected God, the rest of the people in the world were able to turn to him. So when God makes friends with Israel, it will be like bringing the dead back to life.
text: Durnya n wette chi ba vɛɛri bɔr la di na ba ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la, di Kɔraawiizi bittɔ wa lɛɛ baa, u guŋ wàá birgi suma werge maa di wa bɛri alugɔ siu biini izaa gba tɛɛ durnyaa?

ref: If part of a batch of dough is made holy by being offered to God, then all of the dough is holy. If the roots of a tree are holy, the rest of the tree is holy too.
text: Di ba kpa sau yeŋ tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi a ɛɛ kunnanaa, a sau maanii ɛɛ kunnanaa la. Di daa lunne ɛɛ kunnanaa, u kela gba ɛɛ kunnanaarɛ.

ref: You Gentiles are like branches of a wild olive tree made to be part of a cultivated olive tree. You have taken the place of some branches that were cut away from it. And because of this, you enjoy the blessings that come from being part of that cultivated tree.
text: Too. Jus hina ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ɔlivi daa Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ u ɛɛ kunnanii. Denii u teŋri u kela aŋhina ha ka kpa pir hor kel pɛli u ni. Ii banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ, ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ pir hor la, di wer ra di suma n lii u lunne be.

ref: But don't think you are better than the branches that were cut away. Just remember you are not supporting the roots of this tree. Its roots are supporting you.
text: Di u ɛɛ guŋ tɛi, gilɛɛ kpa i nyuu ra lɔ kela la. Hìŋ́ gillɛ lunne la du de gɛɛ aabuu gillɛ i du denei?

ref: Maybe you think those branches were cut away, so you could be put in their place.
text: I daŋ ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi teŋri u kela labuu ha, ka ú wer kpaŋ pɛli de.”

ref: That's true enough. But they were cut away because they did not have faith, and you are where you are because you do have faith. So don't be proud, but be afraid.
text: Mhmm. Jus hina n wɔɔ yardɛɛ wiarɛ u teŋ baa ha la. Hiŋwaa n yarduu wiarɛ i du de la. Awia, gilɛɛ ra kpa i hiŋ zenni. A ɔm.

ref: If God cut away those natural branches, couldn't he do the same to you?
text: Di Kɔraawiizi waa daa la kela n ɛɛ u himmaa kela la ni sunne, ka teŋraa ha, a dazi. Di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ teŋ i ge ha.

ref: Now you see both how kind and how hard God can be. He was hard on those who fell, but he was kind to you. And he will keep on being kind to you, if you keep on trusting in his kindness. Otherwise, you will be cut away too.
text: Awia, ií na gunla Kɔraawiizi hiinaa ni u baaŋ n duwɛɛ. Banla n cholle la na u baannɛ. I ge na u hiinaa. Di i haa du gunla hiŋ faa duwɛɛ u hiinii la, u daŋ haa ra hiinii. Di guŋ lɛi, u daŋ teŋ i ge gba ha.

ref: If those other branches will start having faith, they will be made a part of that tree again. God has the power to put them back.
text: Banla ge, di ba bittɔ wa yardi Kɔraawiizi, u daŋ kaa kpa baa pɛli daa la ni. Kɔraawiizi dɔɔ fɔŋŋaa ú wer gil bá kaa du u daa la ni.

ref: After all, it wasn't natural for branches to be cut from a wild olive tree and to be made part of a cultivated olive tree. So it is much more likely that God will join the natural branches back to the cultivated olive tree. The People of Israel Will Be Brought Back
text: Di u faa wetto kpa hinla n faa ɛɛ u tɛɛ bɛl kel un lawii teŋ wa pɛli daa bɛl n waa i himmaa lau ɛɛwɛ i wer du de, amɔ, a wàá ka du kpol u be lugɔ ú kpa a daa himmaa kela kaa wa pɛli a himmaa lau ni. Kɔraawiizi daŋ lɛɛ Izrɛl hina maa

ref: My friends, I don't want you Gentiles to be too proud of yourselves. So I will explain the mystery of what has happened to the people of Israel. Some of them have become stubborn, and they will stay like that until the complete number of you Gentiles has come in.
text: Yaabalaa, n na nyiŋŋi ii zum Kɔraawiizi wisuahlii naa um pillɛɛ tɛɛ yaa naa wiarɛ, ií gilɛɛ nyiŋŋi sɔŋ ra tɛɛ iihinaa dikuu ii nunzuma wia. U wolo hinnɛ keŋ. U gillɔɔ Izrɛl hina bampiree du kpeg tama mɔɔ ka bánla n waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi n niŋ lɛɛ la maga wa su.

ref: In this way all of Israel will be saved, as the Scriptures say, “From Zion someone will come to rescue us. Then Jacob's descendants will stop being evil.
text: Di u wa suwoo, Kɔraawiizi daŋ jaa bir lɛɛ Izrɛl hina la maa gunla baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ di ŋɔ, “Izrɛl hina Lɛɛri daŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa lii Ziɔn di duŋŋi wichɔgaa Jekɔb biizi la be.

ref: This is what the Lord has promised to do when he forgives their sins.”
text: N ni baa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi labuu. Saŋa la min niŋ lizi ba wichɔgaa ha ba ni labuu.”

ref: The people of Israel are treated as God's enemies, so the good news can come to you Gentiles. But they are still the chosen ones, and God loves them because of their famous ancestors.
text: Amaniyesuma naawaa biini, ba ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dɔmaa dikuu ii wia. Ka u nɛra lizaa la biini, ba ɛɛ u biinɔŋŋaarɛ dikuu ba naabaala la wia,

ref: God doesn't take back the gifts he has given or disown the people he has chosen.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, wia la maa Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ baa la ani gunla uŋ yir baa ba ba wa ɛɛ u nɛra la, wàá wer vɛɛ guŋ.

ref: At one time you Gentiles rejected God. But now Israel has rejected God, and you have been shown mercy.
text: Ii faa waa Kɔraawiizi nua ra hiŋ, ka u wa suŋ ii ni filaŋkennaa, dikuu Izrɛl hina n waa u nua ra hiŋ la wia.

ref: And because of the mercy shown to you, they will also be shown mercy.
text: Gunnɛ Izrɛl hina naa n waa u nua ra hiŋ filaŋkennaa, Kɔraawiizi daŋ wa suŋ ba ge ni ani sunaa la uŋ faa suŋ ii ge ni la.

ref: All people have disobeyed God, and that's why he treats them as prisoners. But he does this, so that he can have mercy on all of them.
text: Nɛra la n na vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuuzi la, ba wichɔgaa la vɔɔzi ba maanii dau, ka ú wer suŋ ba maa ni. Kɔraawiizi chɔlaa wia

ref: Who can measure the wealth and wisdom and knowledge of God? Who can understand his decisions or explain what he does?
text: Kɔraawiizi nunzuma ni u sichaana kannɔ. A waa maga dɔɔwɛ gba. Newee daŋ wer zum u widaulaa biini, di kaa wer bagli gunla u ŋmɛnizi n chɔɔwɛɛ?

ref: “Has anyone known the thoughts of the Lord or given him advice?
text: “Newee daŋ wer zum u nfɛrɛ biiniaa? Bɛl daŋ faa wer bagluu wiimaa?”

ref: Has anyone loaned something to the Lord that must be repaid?”
text: “Anɛɛ n du de Kɔraawiizi faa lɛɛ kuŋ u be ka u kaa wa bir kpa tɛuwɛi? A hiŋ dee waa hoo,”

ref: Everything comes from the Lord. All things were made because of him and will return to him. Praise the Lord forever! Amen.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, kummaa, kummaa lii u fɔŋŋa biini di kaa du de u fɔŋŋa wia ú wer na sɔŋ. Ií gil u sɔŋ na girme saŋaa saŋa maa. Ami.

ref: Dear friends, God is good. So I beg you to offer your bodies to him as a living sacrifice, pure and pleasing. That's the most sensible way to serve God.
text: N na suŋŋi ia, yaabalaa, ií binni gunla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ ii ni werge la, ka kpa iihinaa tɛu alugɔ mbusu iin niŋ lizi tɛu, á ɛɛ mbusu lizaa la n ɛɛ naniinanii di du wer u be, ú wer lɛɛa. Jaamaa la n wessee guŋ.

ref: Don't be like the people of this world, but let God change the way you think. Then you will know how to do everything that is good and pleasing to him.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil durnya naa wia ra fir ia, ii du a duula. Ií gil Kɔraawiizi birgi ii biine nfɛssi, ií duula ge birgi dufalaa ií ɔɔ wer zum wia la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipar wia, anla n wesse, anla n dɛkkɛ, anla n ɛɛ ananaa wa tuŋ la.

ref: I realize God has treated me with undeserved grace, and so I tell each of you not to think you are better than you really are. Use good sense and measure yourself by the amount of faith that God has given you.
text: Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be ani hiinaa la Kɔraawiizi n hiiniŋ n wer dɔɔ la. Ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ ra kpa u hiŋ zenni kaali gunla n wesse. Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ bɛl maanii yarda la un niŋ dɔɔ. Awia, ií ra pessi di zum wia la un tɛɛ ia yarda, ii wer ɛɛ la.

ref: A body is made up of many parts, and each of them has its own use.
text: Gunla yaa bɔrahɔŋ n ɛɛ kuŋkpaŋ ka dɔɔ yeŋa kpilakpila a huma kurgi la,

ref: That's how it is with us. There are many of us, but we each are part of the body of Christ, as well as part of one another.
text: gunnɛ yaa gba du kpil, ka yaa ni Kristo n kpauwɛ la, yaa maa kpau ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋkpaŋ, bɛl maa ɛɛ u dɔŋahina yeŋ bɛl.

ref: God has also given each of us different gifts to use. If we can prophesy, we should do it according to the amount of faith we have.
text: Yaa maa dɔɔ wiɛɛlaa fɔŋŋazii a kurgi gunla Kɔraawiizi n suŋ yaa ni, di hiini yaa, yaa wer ra ɛɛa la. Di u gillɔɔ i ɛɛ u dɔgtɛɛ di ŋɔ wia ra tɛi, í wer ra bagli nɛra, a ɛɛ guŋ, di ra bagli gunla maa uŋ hiinii ni yarda í wer bagli.

ref: If we can serve others, we should serve. If we can teach, we should teach.
text: Di u gillɔɔ i ɛɛ i dɔŋahina balii, a hum baa di ra hiini baa. Di i hor ɛɛ u wia baglaarɛ, a bagli.

ref: If we can encourage others, we should encourage them. If we can give, we should be generous. If we are leaders, we should do our best. If we are good to others, we should do it cheerfully. Rules for Christian Living
text: Di u gillɔɔ i wer bagli nɛra ŋmɛnizi gunla ban niŋ hiŋ, a hiini baa guŋ. Di u gillɔɔ i wer ra hiini nɛra ani kuna la baŋ waa dɔɔwɛ, a ɛɛ guŋ ani biinihuŋŋu. Di u gillɔɔ i wer ɛɛ i dɔŋahina sitɔɔri, a ɛɛ guŋ ani siaahmu. Di u gillɔɔ i wer ra na i dɔŋahina sinyɛna, a hiini baa ani bɔsɔna. Nɔŋŋaa wia

ref: Be sincere in your love for others. Hate everything that is evil and hold tight to everything that is good.
text: Ií nɔŋŋi dɔŋa biinihuŋŋu ni. Ií hah wichɔgaa ka lau winanaa kiŋkiŋ.

ref: Love each other as brothers and sisters and honor others more than you do yourself.
text: Ií nɔŋŋi dɔŋa nɛnnɛ di ra feli dɔŋa tɔgzaa.

ref: Never give up. Eagerly follow the Holy Spirit and serve the Lord.
text: Ií gilɛɛ dɔɔ bɔhuaih ka ra hiŋ ani siaahmu, di ra hum ii Dɔɔri ani bɔkpega,

ref: Let your hope make you glad. Be patient in time of trouble and never stop praying.
text: di ɔɔ gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia ani tamii la iin dɔɔwɛ la. Ií ɔɔ ra di tɔɔrɔɔ ani kanyitti, di ɔɔ lau nfɛrkpaŋ ra suŋŋi wiizi saŋa maa.

ref: Take care of God's needy people and welcome strangers into your home.
text: Ií ra hiini Kɔraawiizi biinanaa ani kuna la baŋ waa dɔɔwɛ, di sɛɛ lɛɛ hɔɔhra ra du ii biini.

ref: Ask God to bless everyone who mistreats you. Ask him to bless them and not to curse them.
text: Ií ɔɔ suŋŋi wiizi di tɛɛ banla n na tɔɔri ia, di gilɛɛ see baa nua.

ref: When others are happy, be happy with them, and when they are sad, be sad.
text: Ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia banla bɔra n sɔɔnɛɛ wia, di kaa gil ii biine chɔgi banla biine n chɔkkɛ wia.

ref: Be friendly with everyone. Don't be proud and feel that you know more than others. Make friends with ordinary people.
text: Ií gil ii maa dɔɔ nuukpaŋ dɔŋa ni, di gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi zenni, ka dɔɔ sisɔna, di ra sɛɛ hundumazi humaa. Ií gilɛɛ ra binni lugɔ ii zum wiimaanii.

ref: Don't mistreat someone who has mistreated you. But try to earn the respect of others,
text: Ií gilɛɛ waa kpa wichɔgaa ra turgi wichɔgaa kim. Ií ra ɛɛ wia la n wesse nɛr maa be.

ref: and do your best to live at peace with everyone.
text: Di ii wetto, di a lii iawaa be, ií ɛɛ ania gil ii ni nɛr maa wia ɛɛ bɔɔiih.

ref: Dear friends, don't try to get even. Let God take revenge. In the Scriptures the Lord says, “I am the one to take revenge and pay them back.”
text: N biinɔŋŋaa, ií gilɛɛ waa ŋɔ ií turgi banla n ɛɛ ia wichɔgaa la. Kɔraawiizi baaŋ na fuuuh dikuu ba wia. Waabuu niŋ turgi baa. Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Minuu dɔɔ wichɔgaa turgaa. Min niŋ turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim.”

ref: The Scriptures also say, “If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink. This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads.”
text: “Ka di lɔzi waa kpu hiŋwaa dɔm bɛl, nyiŋŋi diwee tɛu ú di. Di niinyɔgzi lawuu, ɛɛ nii tɛu ú nyɔɔ. Di i wetto ɛɛ guŋ tɛu, hiihzi daŋ lawuu.”

ref: Don't let evil defeat you, but defeat evil with good.
text: Ií gilɛɛ gil wichɔgaa ɛɛi kpegli ia. Ií kpa winanaa ɛɛi kpegli wichɔgaa.

ref: Obey the rulers who have authority over you. Only God can give authority to anyone, and he puts these rulers in their places of power.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ nɛr maa n na sɛɛ hɛri nabɔnzi dɔɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, nɛr maa wàá wer di nabɔmuu, di Kɔraawiizi wɔɔ tɛɛwɛ. Kɔraawiizii gillɛ ba ra di nabɔmuu la.

ref: People who oppose the authorities are opposing what God has done, and they will be punished.
text: Awia, nɛr la maa n niŋ vɛɛ u hɛri nabɔnzi wiŋɔzi, Kɔraawiizi nuarɛ u vɛɛ. U daŋ di u seriya, ú chol.

ref: Rulers are a threat to evil people, not to good people. There is no need to be afraid of the authorities. Just do right, and they will praise you for it.
text: Hɛri nabɔnzi wia waa hunnanaa hiŋ na ɛɛ ɔnsii. Hunchɔgaa hinnɛ hɛri nabɔnzi wia ra ɛɛ ɔnsii. Haa nyiŋŋi hɛri nabɔma wia ra ɛɛi ɔnsiiyaa? Amɔ, í ra hum hunnanaa ú chɔlii.

ref: After all, they are God's servants, and it is their duty to help you. If you do something wrong, you ought to be afraid, because these rulers have the right to punish you. They are God's servants who punish criminals to show how angry God is.
text: U ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi baliirɛ ú wer nyiŋŋi winanaa tɛi. Ka di i ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa, i danna ɔmuu. Waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ pɛɛpɛɛ. U kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi balii, ú wer tɔɔri unla maa n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa Kɔraawiizi baaŋ fuuh u ni.

ref: But you should obey the rulers because you know it is the right thing to do, and not just because of God's anger.
text: Awia, ií ra sɛɛ ba dɔɔra. Ií gilɛɛ ra sɛɛ dikuu iinna ɔm ba baaŋ bɛŋ wia, ka ra sɛɛ, ií wer dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu ií biine gilɛɛ waa tɔɔri ia.

ref: You must also pay your taxes. The authorities are God's servants, and it is their duty to take care of these matters.
text: A guŋ wiarɛ a kaa du wer lugɔ ií ra turgi lampoo. A lampoo hina gba ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi balaarɛ, ba ra hum a huma.

ref: In the Law there are many commands, such as, “Be faithful in marriage. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not want what belongs to others.” But all of these are summed up in the command that says, “Love others as much as you love yourself.”
text: Kɔraawiizi Gbɔgni labuu keŋ. Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm, gilɛɛ wàá kpu nɛr, gilɛɛ wàá ŋmɛɛ, gilɛɛ wàá dɔɔ kɛkɛluu. Gbɔgni naa ni aŋhina n kaa jaa, a maa hiŋaa du Gbɔgkpaŋ biinii. Waabuu keŋ. Nɔŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ gunla hin nɔŋŋi i hiŋ la.

ref: No one who loves others will harm them. So love is all that the Law demands. The Day When Christ Returns
text: Di i nɔŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ, hàá sɛɛ ɛɛu wichɔgaa. Awia, dɔnnɔŋŋaarɛ ɛɛ Gbɔg la maa hiŋaa.

ref: You know what sort of times we live in, and so you should live properly. It is time to wake up. You know that the day when we will be saved is nearer now than when we first put our faith in the Lord.
text: Ií ra hiŋ guŋ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii zum wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ filaŋkenne, di zum lugɔ a dɛkkɔɔ yaa n izi dɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa lɛɛi saŋa duglɔɔrɛ kaali saŋa la yaa n felee yardi Yeesu la.

ref: Night is almost over, and day will soon appear. We must stop behaving as people do in the dark and be ready to live in the light.
text: Hamuŋa a bɛruu. Hɔpizaa ge ra dugli. Awia, ií gil ya kpa bɔbiri huma ha, ka kpa Kɔraawiizi laal kuna laali yaa hinaa, di wer hum hɔpizaa huma.

ref: So behave properly, as people do in the day. Don't go to wild parties or get drunk or be vulgar or indecent. Don't quarrel or be jealous.
text: Ya gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ basabasa di ra dɛɛzi, di gilɛɛ ra ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ wia ani wikuna, di gilɛɛ ra di dɔŋa hɔɔzi di dɔɔ bɔwii.

ref: Let the Lord Jesus Christ be as near to you as the clothes you wear. Then you won't try to satisfy your selfish desires.
text: Ií gil yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo du ii ni alugɔ iiŋ kpa tagta laali, nɛ́ra wer na u manni ii ni, ka vɛɛ ii bɔrahɔŋ kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa la.

ref: Welcome all the Lord's followers, even those whose faith is weak. Don't criticize them for having beliefs that are different from yours.
text: Di Yeesu hiŋri bɛl du de, waa u hiŋaa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ ka ra nyiŋŋi u zuu ii biini, ií lɛɛu du ii biini di gilɛɛ binni lugɔ ií diu hɔɔzi.

ref: Some think it is all right to eat anything, while those whose faith is weak will eat only vegetables.
text: Ii bɛl ra binni lugɔ u daŋ wer di kummaa. Bɛl ge waa u hiŋaa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ nɛnnɛ, di ra di dɔpaŋhoori bɛŋ. Waa ol ra hee.

ref: What right do you have to criticize someone else's servants? Only their Lord can decide if they are doing right, and the Lord will make sure that they do right.
text: Anɛɛ hiŋ í wer ŋɔ nɛbɛl balii cholloowei? U himmaa dɔɔrii niŋ zum, di u cholloo gɛɛ waa cholle. Wàá gil u chol gba. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u wer chi.

ref: Some of the Lord's followers think one day is more important than another. Others think all days are the same. But each of you should make up your own mind.
text: Nɛbɛl ra tɔgzi hɔpizii bɛllɛ kaali aŋhina. Bɛl ge ra ŋɔ lugɔ a maa ɛɛ kpannɛ. A wesso ii maa n zum ii himmaa biine gunla iin niŋ ɛɛ.

ref: Any followers who count one day more important than another day do it to honor their Lord. And any followers who eat meat give thanks to God, just like the ones who don't eat meat.
text: Nɛr la n na tɔgzi hɔpizii bɛl, yaa Dɔɔrii u ra binni di ra tɔgzuu la. Unla n na di kummaa, u Dɔɔrii u ra binni di ra dia la ka ra jaamuu dikuu a wia. Unla n na kiia ge, u ge gba ra binni u Dɔɔrii di ra kiia, ka ge ra jaamuu dikuu anla unna di la wia.

ref: Whether we live or die, it must be for God, rather than for ourselves.
text: Yaa bɛl maa waa yaa bɛŋ duwɛɛ yaa miibɔɔ naa wia biini. Yaa bɛl maa ge waa yaa bɛŋ duwɛɛ yaa siu ge biini.

ref: Whether we live or die, it must be for the Lord. Alive or dead, we still belong to the Lord.
text: Di yaa du de di ra nyiŋ, yaa Dɔɔri wiarɛ yaa du de. Di yaa siuwɔ ge, yaa Dɔɔri wiarɛ yaa siu. Awia, di yaa ra nyiŋ gɛɛ yaa waa nyiŋ, ka yaa Dɔɔrii dɔɔ yaa.

ref: This is because Christ died and rose to life, so that he would be the Lord of the dead and of the living.
text: Dikuubɛɛwiai, Kristo siuwɔɔ di kaa izi siu biini, ú wer ɛɛ lalaa ni nyinee maa dɔɔri.

ref: Why do you criticize other followers of the Lord? Why do you look down on them? The day is coming when God will judge all of us.
text: Hinla n na ŋɔ lugɔ i dɔŋhiŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ, hìŋ́ niŋ ŋɔ u wia guŋ? Ɛrɛɛ i ra gbɛlli i dɔŋhiŋ gunnɛi? Yaa maanii niŋ ŋmɛnɛ wa chi Kɔraawiizi seriya diiribɔr.

ref: In the Scriptures God says, “I swear by my very life that everyone will kneel down and praise my name!”
text: Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, ‘Ií gil n ŋɔ wibii ii nuu. Miŋ du de saŋa maa wia, nɛr maa daŋ ŋmɛnɛ giŋŋi n see, di sɛɛ chɔgri.’ ”

ref: And so, each of us must give an account to God for what we do. Don't Cause Problems for Others
text: Yaa maa daŋ ŋmɛnɛ bagli yaa himmaa wia tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi.

ref: We must stop judging others. We must also make up our minds not to upset anyone's faith.
text: Awia, ií gilɛɛ kaa ra ŋɔ ii dɔŋahina wia ni wichɔgaa. Ka ií lau keŋ nfɛrɛ lugɔ bɛ́l maa gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ wiimaa n niŋ gil u dɔŋhiŋ leu, di ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

ref: The Lord Jesus has made it clear to me that God considers all foods fit to eat. But if you think some foods are unfit to eat, then for you they are not fit.
text: N Dɔɔri Yeesu gillɔɔ n zum lugɔ kummaa waa kii. Diwee dee maa waa doŋa dɔɔwɛ u hiŋ ni. Ka baŋhina be, diwee aŋhina a kiiu. A dii ra tɛɛ baa doŋa.

ref: If you are hurting others by the foods you eat, you are not guided by love. Don't let your appetite destroy someone Christ died for.
text: Ama, di i kuu i diwee wia gil i dɔŋhiŋ ɛɛ wichɔgaa, u biini chɔgi, i nɔŋŋuubuu naá? Kristo kuu a hiŋ wiarɛ siu. Awia, a waa dɛkkɛ hin niŋ bir chɔguu dikuu diwee wia.

ref: Don't let your right to eat bring shame to Christ.
text: Gilɛɛ gil nɛr maa wer kpa i winanaa ɛɛi birgi wichɔgaa, di ra gbɛllaa.

ref: God's kingdom isn't about eating and drinking. It is about pleasing God, about living in peace, and about true happiness. All this comes from the Holy Spirit.
text: Kundii ni kunnyɔɔi waa wizenaa ɛɛwɛ Kɔraawiizi Kora biini. Wideŋlaa, nuukpaŋ dɔɔi ani bɔsɔna la n lii Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini la, aabuu ɛɛ wizenaa u kora biini.

ref: If you serve Christ in this way, you will please God and be respected by people.
text: Nɛr la maa n kpa annii ra hum Kristo, u wia daŋ par Kɔraawiizi, di kaa du wer nɛra ge be.

ref: We should try to live at peace and help each other have a strong faith.
text: Awia, ií gil ya aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi ya ni yaa dɔŋahina nuukpaŋ dɔɔi, di kaa ra nyiŋŋi gunla yaa n niŋ hiini dɔŋa, yaa maa wer lau nɛnnɛ.

ref: Don't let your appetite destroy what God has done. All foods are fit to eat, but it is wrong to cause problems for others by what you eat.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kuu diwee dii wia chɔgi Kɔraawiizi huma. Kummaa dii waa kii. Ka di nɛr la maa wa di diwee aŋhina a gil u dɔŋhiŋ leu, a diwee dii waa wer tɛɛ a hiŋ.

ref: It is best not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything else that causes problems for other followers of the Lord.
text: A wesso hiŋ gil ol heei, siŋ nyɔɔi ani kuŋ la maa n niŋ gil i dɔŋhiŋ leu.

ref: What you believe about these things should be kept between you and God. You are fortunate, if your actions don't make you have doubts.
text: Wia la hinna ɛɛ, haa ra aani ni wichɔgaa wia, gil guŋ du i ni Kɔraawiizi bɛŋ be. Nɛr la biini n wɔɔ ra tɛɛ wichɔgaa dikuu wia la unna ɛɛ la wia, u nuu sumaa.

ref: But if you do have doubts about what you eat, you are going against your beliefs. And you know that is wrong, because anything you do against your beliefs is sin.
text: Ka nɛr la n na aani diwee aŋhina dii ka ra dia, u dɔɔ chɔgrii, dikuu uŋ waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ a wesso un niŋ dia, ka dia la wia. Wii la maa hiŋ waa sɛɛwɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ winaniirɛ ka ɛɛu, wichɔgiirɛ i ɛɛ.

ref: If our faith is strong, we should be patient with the Lord's followers whose faith is weak. We should try to please them instead of ourselves.
text: A dɛkkɔɔ yaa banla n dɔɔ yaa hiŋaa fɔŋŋa, n niŋ hiini banla n haa waa u fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ la, di gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋi yaa bɛŋ kipar.

ref: We should think of their good and try to help them by doing what pleases them.
text: Ií gil yaa bɛl maa ra nyiŋŋi yaa dɔŋahina kipar di ra hiini dɔŋa, ya wer lau nɛnnɛ.

ref: Even Christ did not try to please himself. But as the Scriptures say, “The people who insulted you also insulted me.”
text: Kristo gba faa waa u himmaa kipar binnɛɛ. Ba faa sɛbi u wiarɛ, di ŋɔ, “Kɔraawiizi, chagzaa la baŋ faa ra chagzii la, aabuu ba kpa ra chagziŋ.”

ref: God is the one who makes us patient and cheerful. I pray that he will help you live at peace with each other, as you follow Christ.
text: Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ kanyitti ni bɔkpega dui hiŋ la, ú gil ii wer dɔɔ nuukpaŋ dɔŋa ni gunla Yeesu Kristo n wette bagli yaa la,

ref: Then all of you together will praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. The Good News Is for Jews and Gentiles
text: ií wer ɛɛ nuukpaŋ, di ra kpa yaa ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la girme.

ref: Honor God by accepting each other, as Christ has accepted you.
text: Awia, ií ra sɛɛ dɔŋa wia di ra lɛɛ dɔŋa alugɔ Kristo n sɛɛ yaa wia la di gil Kɔraawiizi na girme.

ref: I tell you that Christ came as a servant of the Jews to show that God has kept the promises he made to their famous ancestors. Christ also came,
text: Ií gil n ŋɔ ii be. Kristo birgi baliirɛ, di hum Izrɛl hina la Kɔ́raawiizi wiŋɔzi wer ɛɛ wibii, nuúzi la uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa naabaala la wer ɛɛ,

ref: so that the Gentiles would praise God for being kind to them. It is just as the Scriptures say, “I will tell the nations about you, and I will sing praises to your name.”
text: bánla n waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ ge wer tɔgzi Kɔraawiizi dikuu u nɛsunaa wia. Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ, “N daŋ tɛi sɔŋ banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ be, di yir yira di ra dargii.”

ref: The Scriptures also say to the Gentiles, “Come and celebrate with God's people.”
text: Ba kaa sɛbi, “Ií banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia di jaa u himmaa nɛra la ni.”

ref: Again the Scriptures say, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles. All you nations, come and worship him.”
text: Ka kaa ŋɔ, “Ii banla maa n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ, ií ra chɔli Kɔraawiizi. Nɛra maa, ií ra chɔluu.”

ref: Isaiah says, “Someone from David's family will come to power. He will rule the nations, and they will put their hope in him.”
text: U dɔgtɛɛ Aizaaya faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Jɛssɛ naana bɛl daŋ izi dɔɔ banla n waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ. Ba daŋ kpau birgi ba tamii.”

ref: I pray that God, who gives hope, will bless you with complete happiness and peace because of your faith. And may the power of the Holy Spirit fill you with hope. Paul's Work as a Missionary
text: N na nyiŋŋi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ tamii hiŋ la, ú gil ii dɔɔ bampirsɔna nɛnnɛ lii yarda la iiŋ yarduu la biini, ka ií wer dɔɔ tamii werge maa u Dumnanii fɔŋŋa biini. Pɔɔl n ŋɔ wia tɛɛ nɛra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ wia

ref: My friends, I am sure that you are very good and that you have all the knowledge you need to teach each other.
text: Yaabalaa, maa ii wia ra aani. N zummɔ lugɔ ii ra ɛɛ winanaarɛ werge, di dɔɔ nunzuma nɛnnɛ, di kaa wer ra bagli dɔŋa.

ref: But I have spoken to you plainly and have tried to remind you of some things. God treated me with undeserved grace!
text: Ka n lɔ bampiriire liizi ia wia aŋhina ani fɔŋŋa la Kɔraawiizi n hiiniŋ n dɔɔ

ref: He chose me to be a servant of Christ Jesus for the Gentiles and to do the work of a priest in the service of his good news. God did this so that the Holy Spirit could make the Gentiles into a holy offering, pleasing to him.
text: di wer ɛɛ Yeesu Kristo huŋhunni banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la biini di ra lizi u amaniyesuma la alugɔ u kizee hinnɛ miŋ, ń wer na banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ tɛu. Ba daŋ lizi mbusu lizaa kunnanii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ sɛɛ lɛɛ dikuu u Dumnanii n niŋ lizi ba doŋa ba ni ha la wia.

ref: Because of Christ Jesus, I can take pride in my service for God.
text: Awia, n dɔɔ wia aŋhina min niŋ chɔli Kɔraawiizi humaa wia biini, dikuu n ni Yeesu Kristo n kpauwɛ wia.

ref: In fact, all I will talk about is how Christ let me speak and work, so that the Gentiles would obey him.
text: Màá sɛɛ ŋɔ wia maa wia, see anla miŋ wette ɛɛ dikuu Kristo n du n biini, di ɛɛa la wia ka bánla n waa Izrɛl hina ɛɛwɛ wer sɛɛ u nua. U gillɔɔ n ŋɔ u wiŋɔzi di ɛɛ u wiɛɛlaa,

ref: Indeed, I will tell how Christ worked miracles and wonders by the power of the Holy Spirit. I have preached the good news about him all the way from Jerusalem to Illyricum.
text: di bagli fɔŋŋa ra ɛɛ wizenaa ni witittaa, di kaa bagli u Dumnanii ge fɔŋŋa. Awiarɛ n wer hum amaniyesuma la huma Jɛrusalɛm di ga hel Ilirikum maa di ga tuŋ.

ref: But I have always tried to preach where people have never heard about Christ. I am like a builder who doesn't build on someone else's foundation.
text: N ɛɛ aniaa lizi amaniyesuma la bɔra la baŋ faa haa waa Kristo wia nuuwɛ, ń gilɛɛ waa hum bɔra la nɛbɛl n teŋ faari a huma de la.

ref: It is just as the Scriptures say, “All who haven't been told about him will see him, and those who haven't heard about him will understand.” Paul's Plan To Visit Rome
text: Gunla baŋ faa sɛbɛɛ la wa ɛɛ. Ba faa sɛbɔɔrɛ, “Banla baŋ faa waa baa baglɛɛ u wia daŋ wa zum u wia.”

ref: My work has always kept me from coming to see you.
text: Awiarɛ n faa ra nyiŋŋi ii be balaa saŋakpila maa, ka wia aŋhina ɔɔ tɔŋ ŋmɛnɛɛ. N faa waa wette ń ba.

ref: Now there is nothing left for me to do in this part of the world, and for years I have wanted to visit you.
text: Ka filaŋkeŋ, miŋ waa kaa dɔɔ bɔr maa ɛŋ miŋ haa waa n huma hummɛ tuŋ naa, ii nai ge n du n bampirii biŋkpila maa wia,

ref: So I plan to stop off on my way to Spain. Then after a short, but refreshing, visit with you, I hope you will quickly send me on.
text: di n wa ŋɔ ń la Speen hɛri, n na nyiŋŋi n ga ii hɛri na ia mɔɔ. Di n jaa wa du ii be a kukkiŋ tama, ií hiiniŋ n la Speen hɛri la.

ref: I am now on my way to Jerusalem to deliver the money that the Lord's followers in Macedonia and Achaia collected for God's needy people.
text: Yaabalaa la n du Masɛdɔnia ni Akaaya binnɔɔrɛ lugɔ a wesso ban niŋ kɛɛ kebee, bá tɛɛ banla n ɛɛ nyaara ba biini de.

ref: This is something they really wanted to do. But sharing their money with the Jews was also like paying back a debt, because the Jews had already shared their spiritual blessings with the Gentiles.
text: Guŋ faa wessoo ba be, dikuubɛɛwiai, a nɛra kima du ba ninɛɛ. Banla n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ n wette na Kɔraawiizi ni newea baambaaŋ wia hiinaa ba be naa, a dɛkkɔɔ Jus hina la ge n na diwee ni kuna hiinaa lii ba ge be.

ref: After I have safely delivered this money, I will visit you and then go on to Spain.
text: Di n wa hum huma naa tuŋ, di kpa ba tɔna la maa tɛɛ baa, n daŋ jaa izi de ga ii be di ra la Speen.

ref: And when I do arrive in Rome, I know it will be with the full blessings of Christ.
text: Di n wa hel ii be, n zummɔ lugɔ n daŋ kpa Kristo hiinaa werge maa di wer hiini ia.

ref: My friends, by the power of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the love that comes from the Holy Spirit, I beg you to pray sincerely with me and for me.
text: Too. N na suŋŋi ia, yaabalaa, ií binni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo ni nɔŋŋaa la u Dumnanii n nɔŋŋi ia la, ka aah siwii ra hiiniŋ di suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛŋ

ref: Pray that God will protect me from the unbelievers in Judea, and that his people in Jerusalem will be pleased with what I am doing.
text: ú lɛɛŋ banla n du Juda hɛri di vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la be, di kaa gil u huma la baŋ humiŋ ń ga hum Jɛrusalɛm la wer par Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la de.

ref: Ask God to let me come to you and have a pleasant and refreshing visit.
text: Denii ń jaa wer na n ŋmɛnɛɛ ba ii be ani bɔsɔna di wa heezi, á maa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kipar.

ref: I pray that God, who gives peace, will be with all of you. Amen.
text: Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ bampirsɔna hiŋ la, du ii be. Ami.

ref: I have good things to say about Phoebe, who is a leader in the church at Cenchreae.
text: Too. Yaa dɔŋhiŋ Fibii keŋ. U ra hum Yeesu hiŋra la n du Sɛŋkiria labuu.

ref: Welcome her in a way that is proper for someone who has faith in the Lord and is one of God's own people. Help her in any way you can. After all, she has proved to be a respected leader for many others, including me.
text: Awia, ií lɛɛu du ii be gunla an dɛkkɛ Kɔraawiizi biinanaa n niŋ ɛɛ, dikuu yaa Dɔɔri wia, di kaa hiinuu ani kunla maa uŋ waa dɔɔwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, u ra hiini nɛra kpilakpilaa, di ra hiini n ge.

ref: Give my greetings to Priscilla and Aquila. They have not only served Christ Jesus together with me,
text: Ií jaami Pirsila ni Akuila la n na hum lugɔ n dɔŋahina la Yeesu Kristo huma naa biini.

ref: but they have even risked their lives for me. I am grateful for them and so are all the Gentile churches.
text: Ba faa kpa ba miibɔɔnii chɛr siu dikuu n wia. Awia, n na jaami baa. Yeesu hiŋra la n waa Jus hina ɛɛwɛ la maa gba ra jaami baa.

ref: Greet the church that meets in their home. Greet my dear friend Epaenetus, who was the first person in Asia to have faith in Christ.
text: Ií jaami Yeesu hiŋra la n ɔɔ ra chaali ba dia la ge di jaami n nɛnɔŋŋii Ɛpinɛtus la n ɛɛ banla n sɛɛ Kristo wia Eesia hɛri lugli la.

ref: Greet Mary, who has worked so hard for you.
text: Ií jaami Mɛɛri la n hiini ia werge la,

ref: Greet my relatives Andronicus and Junia, who were in jail with me. They are highly respected by the apostles and were followers of Christ before I was.
text: di jaami n lulla Andronaikus ni Junias la baŋ faa tɔ dia di jaa n ni la. Ba dɔɔ sɔnnɛ Kɔraawiizi huŋhunna la be, di faa sɛɛ Kristo wia mɔɔ ka n ge haa wa sɛɛ.

ref: Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend whose faith is in the Lord.
text: Ií jaami Ampliatus. N nɔŋŋuubuu yaa Dɔɔri hiŋaa naa biini.

ref: Greet Urbanus, who serves Christ along with us. Greet my dear friend Stachys.
text: Ií jaami Urbanus la n ɛɛ yaa dɔŋhiŋ Kristo huma naa biini ani Stakis la miŋ nɔŋŋɛɛ la.

ref: Greet Apelles, a faithful servant of Christ. Greet Aristobulus and his family.
text: Ií jaami Apɛlis la. Kɔraawiizi ɛɛubuu na, u dirmi Kristo hiŋaa biini. Ií jaami Aristɔbulus diahina la,
