text: Kɔraawiizi la n ta kummaa, kummaa kaa du de u fɔŋŋa wia la, uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi u na biikpila bá ba wa dɔɔ u girme la, a faa dɛkkɔɔ u be lugɔ ú gil ba sitɔɔri la n niŋ lɛɛ baa la zum tɔɔrɔɔ, ka ú wer ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri nɛnnɛ ga tuŋ.

ref: Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
text: Unla n lizi nɛra doŋa ra ha ani banla un lizi ba doŋa ha la maa mɛɛ ɛɛ kpannɛ. Awia, a wɔɔ ra ɛɛ hiihzi un niŋ yir baa u niuna.

ref: He even said to God, “I will tell them your name and sing your praises when they come together to worship.”
text: U ŋɔ Kɔraawiizi be, “N daŋ bagli i wia tɛɛ n niuna di chɔlii bá chaalaa biini.”

ref: He also said, “I will trust God.” Then he said, “Here I am with the children God has given me.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ, “N daŋ yarduu,” di kaa ŋɔ, “Na n ni n biizi la Kɔraawiizi n tɛŋ la.”

ref: We are people of flesh and blood. This is why Jesus became one of us. He died to destroy the devil, who had power over death.
text: U biizi la dɔɔ chal ni bɔrahɔnaa. Awia, u ge gba birgi guŋ ka di u wa siuwɔ, ú wer chɔgi unla n dɔɔ siu fɔŋŋa, waabuu Sitaani,

ref: But he also died to rescue all of us who live each day in fear of dying.
text: di kaa wer lɛɛ banla maa n faa ɛɛ yoma ba miibɔɔ saŋa maa, dikuu baŋ faa ra ɔm siu wia la di ha.

ref: Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants.
text: Ɛnɛ maa, mɛlikazi lɛi u hiini guŋ. Abraham naannaa u hiini guŋ.

ref: And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
text: U himmaa n di tɔɔrɔɔ dikuu Sitaani n faa ra nyiŋŋi u daruu, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa wiarɛ u zum gunla un niŋ ɛɛ hiini banla Sitaani n haa ra dar la.

ref: My friends, God has chosen you to be his holy people. So think about Jesus, the one we call our apostle and high priest!
text: Awia, n niuna la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la un yittɛ ii ba u be la, ií ra binni Yeesu wia. U ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi huŋhunni ni u Kizeehina Maa Nabɔmaa yaa hiŋaa naa biini.

ref: Jesus was faithful to God, who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in serving all God's people.
text: U wia dɔɔ wibiire Kɔraawiizi la n lizuu u hum u huma la be, gunla Moosis la n faa ra hum Kɔraawiizi Diahina huma la wia n faa dɔɔ wibii u be la.

ref: But Jesus deserves more honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house.
text: Nɛr la n ma dia dɛg sɔnnɛ kaali dia la um mawɛɛ la. Gunnɛ Yeesu naa dɛg sɔŋ dɔɔi kaali Moosis la.

ref: Moses was a faithful servant and told God's people what would be said in the future.
text: Moosis faa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi baliirɛ ra hum u diahina. U wia faa dɔɔ wibii. U faa ra bagli wia la n faa haa waa ɛɛwɛ.

ref: But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope. A Rest for God's People
text: Kristowaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Biibaallɛ di ɛɛ u dia nabɔma. U gba wia dɔɔ wibiire. Di yaa haa dɔɔ bɔkpega ni tamii nɛnnɛ gunla yaa n ɔɔ ŋɔ la, yaa gba ɛɛ u diahinaa. Kɔraawiizi nɛra heezaa wia

ref: It is just as the Holy Spirit says, “If you hear God's voice today,
text: Awiarɛ Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii faa ŋɔ, “Iin nuu n wiŋɔzi zinaa naa,

ref: don't be stubborn! Don't rebel like those people who were tested in the desert. *
text: ií gilɛɛ vɛɛ di ɛɛ dignikpega hina alugɔ banla n faa zuu n ni, di ɛɛn na saŋa la baŋ faa ra vol hɛribɔduma biini la.

ref: For forty years your ancestors tested God and saw the things he did.
text: Ii naabaala ɛɛmbuu na, di na n wiɛɛlaa binni tokkoanɛɛ maa biini.

ref: “Then God got tired of them and said, ‘You people never show good sense, and you don't understand what I want you to do.’
text: A saŋa hina fuuh n baannɛ. N ŋɔ, ‘Ba bampiree ɔɔ dar baabuu ba ra ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Ba waa n ŋmɛnizi zummɛ.’

ref: God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ”
text: Baŋ fuuh n baaŋ la wia, n hɛɛhzi ŋɔ, ‘Ba wàá na heezaa la dee min niŋ faa tɛɛ baa la.’ ”

ref: My friends, watch out! Don't let evil thoughts or doubts make any of you turn from the living God.
text: Yaabalaa, ií ra dazi, ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa ɛɛ nfɛrchɔgaa hiŋ lugɔ wàá ka yardi Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa, di waa vɛɛ u ŋmɛnɛɛ hiŋaa.

ref: You must encourage one another each day. And you must keep on while there is still a time that can be called “today.” If you don't, then sin may fool some of you and make you stubborn.
text: Ií ɔɔ ra bagli dɔŋa ŋmɛnizi hɔpizibii maa, wíchɔgaa gilɛɛ waa dar ia, ii digna bir wa du kpeg Kɔraawiizi be. Uŋ faa ŋɔ zinaa la, filaŋkenne haa ɛɛ a zinaa la.

ref: We were sure about Christ when we first became his people. So let's hold tightly to our faith until the end.
text: Yaa maa ni Kristoo kpauwɔɔ. Di yaa haa yardi Kɔraawiizi gunla yaa n felee yarduu la, di lau guŋ ra la, amɔ, yaa ni Kristo kpauwɔɔ.

ref: The Scriptures say, “If you hear his voice today, don't be stubborn like those who rebelled.”
text: Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, “Iin nuu n wiŋɔzi zinaa naa, ií gilɛɛ vɛɛ di ɛɛ dignikpega hina alugɔ banla n faa zuu n ni la.”

ref: Who were those people that heard God's voice and rebelled? Weren't they the same ones that came out of Egypt with Moses?
text: Babɛlaarɛ faa nuu u wiŋɔzi ka zuu u ni lai? Banla maa Moosis n faa kpoglee lii Ijip hɛri la lɛi zuu u ni laa?

ref: And who did God say would never enter his place of rest? Weren't they the ones that disobeyed him?
text: Babɛlaa benii u ŋɔ ba wàá na heezaa la un niŋ faa tɛɛ baa lai? Banla n vɛɛ u nua la benii u ŋɔ guŋ.

ref: We see that those people did not enter the place of rest because they did not have faith.
text: Awia, yaa zummɔ lugɔ baŋ wɔɔ yardɛɛ wiarɛ ba waa wette na heezaa la.

ref: The promise to enter the place of rest is still good, and we must take care that none of you miss out.
text: Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ yaa lugɔ u daŋ tɛɛ yaa ge heezaa la, awia, ya ra dazi yaa bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa nyaa a heezaa.

ref: We have heard the message, just as they did. But they failed to believe what they heard, and the message did not do them any good.
text: Yaa gba nuu amaniyesuma labuu alugɔ ba ge n faa nuuwɛ la. Ka baabuu n nuuwɛ la, ba waa sɛɛwɛ yardi. Awiarɛ a faa waa baa hiinee la.

ref: Only people who have faith will enter the place of rest. It is just as the Scriptures say, “God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ” God said this, even though everything has been ready from the time of creation.
text: Yaa banla n yardɛɛ lawaa daŋ na u heezaa la. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N baaŋ n fuuhwe la wiarɛ n ŋɔ, ‘Ba wàá na heezaa la min niŋ faa tɛɛ baa la.’ ” Dafini, Kɔraawiizi huma tunnɔɔ lii saŋa la un ta chiŋ ni hɛri la.

ref: In fact, somewhere the Scriptures say that by the seventh day, God had finished his work, and so he rested.
text: Ba faa sɛbi hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ la wiarɛ yembɛl, di ŋɔ, “Hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛhiŋ n wa helle, di Kɔraawiizi tuŋ huma la maa unna hum. Awia, u faa heezi,”

ref: We also read that he later said, “You people will never enter my place of rest!”
text: di kaa sɛbi, “Ba wàá na heezaa la min niŋ faa tɛɛ baa la.”

ref: This means that the promise to enter is still good, because those who first heard about it disobeyed and did not enter.
text: A ɛɛwɔ lugɔ nɛra baŋhina daŋ na heezaa la. Banla n felee nuu amaniyesuma la wɔɔ nawɛɛ dikuu baŋ vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuuzi wia la.

ref: Much later God told David to make the promise again, just as I have already said, “If you hear his voice today, don't be stubborn!”
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi kaa lizi saŋa bɛllɛ di ŋɔ zinaabuu. Deevidii u gil u sɛbi wiŋɔzi la, di ŋɔ, “Iin nuu n wiŋɔzi zinaa naa, ií gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ, di ɛɛ dignikpega hina.”

ref: If Joshua had really given the people rest, there would not be any need for God to talk about another day of rest.
text: Di Josua la n faa ɛɛ ba nabɔma la faa kpogli baabuu zuu bɔr la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ tɛɛ baa heezaa la, Kɔraawiizi faa waa kaa ŋɔ hɔpizii bɛl wia.

ref: But God has promised us a Sabbath when we will rest, even though it has not yet come.
text: An du kennaa, Heezaa Hɔpizii bɛl haa du denii Kɔraawiizi nɛra n niŋ haa na.

ref: On that day God's people will rest from their work, just as God rested from his work.
text: Nɛr la maa n na Kɔraawiizi heezaa naa, u hum u humaa tuŋ alugɔ Kɔraawiizi n faa hum u huma tuŋ ka heezi la.

ref: We should do our best to enter the place of rest, so none of us will disobey and miss going there, as they did.
text: Awia, ya aah siwii ya wer na heezaa la di heezi, di gilɛɛ wa vɛɛ Kɔraawiizi nuuzi alugɔ banla n faa vɛɛwɛ di chol bɔna la.

ref: God's word is alive and powerful! It is sharper than any double-edged sword. His word can cut through our spirits and souls and through our joints and marrow, until it discovers the desires and thoughts of our hearts.
text: Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛ, di wer hum huma di ra di werge kaali tokobi la n dɔɔ nuuzi anɛɛ la maa, di wer zuu lau miibɔɔ bargi duma ni, di wer zum newee biini nfɛssi ni u jina maa.

ref: Nothing is hidden from God! He sees through everything, and we will have to tell him the truth. Jesus Is the Great High Priest
text: Kummaa waa hoo un niŋ wer suah Kɔraawiizi ni. A maa chɔɔwɔɔ kpantalaŋ unla n niŋ pɛɛzi yaa, yaa wiɛɛlaa maa wia la be. Yeesuu ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzeŋ

ref: We have a great high priest, who has gone into heaven, and he is Jesus the Son of God. This is why we must hold on to what we have said about him.
text: Awia, yaa n dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzeŋ Yeesu, Kɔraawiizi Biibaal, u ga chiŋ kaali Kɔraawiizi be la, a dɛkkɔɔ yaa n ninna hiŋuu nɛnnɛ.

ref: Jesus understands every weakness of ours, because he was tempted in every way that we are. But he did not sin!
text: Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la n wàá wer na yaa sinyɛna, di suŋ yaa gɛrga ni la lɛi Yeesu. Wia la maa n haŋ huuzi yaa, a maanii huuzuu. Wifittii ɛɛ u gbaa na, ka waa wichɔgaa ɛɛwɛ.

ref: So whenever we are in need, we should come bravely before the throne of our merciful God. There we will be treated with undeserved grace, and we will find help.
text: Awia, ya lɔ bampiree ra dugli Kɔraawiizi la n dɔɔ nɛsunaa werge la kara zɛɛ, ú wer suŋ yaa ni, ya wer na hiinaa u be. U daŋ ɔɔ suŋ yaa ni di hiini yaa, saŋa la maa wii n wa tir yaa.

ref: Every high priest is appointed to help others by offering gifts and sacrifices to God because of their sins.
text: Baŋ ɔɔ lizi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma nɛra biini, ba ɔɔ lizuubuu ú ɛɛ ba sitɔɔri, di lizi sela ni kuna ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia.

ref: A high priest has weaknesses of his own, and he feels sorry for foolish and sinful people.
text: A Kizeehina Nabɔma hiŋ daŋ wer suŋ banla n waa wia zummɛ di leu la ni, dikuubɛɛwiai, u gba waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ ú ɔɔ vɛɛ wichɔgaa ɛɛi.

ref: This is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins and for the sins of others.
text: Awia, gunla uŋ ɔɔ lizi mbusuzi tɛɛ nɛra dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia la, u daŋ ɛɛ guŋ tɛɛ u hiŋ gba, dikuu u gba n na ɛɛ wichɔgaa wia.

ref: But no one can have the honor of being a high priest simply by wanting to be one. Only God can choose a priest, and God is the one who chose Aaron.
text: Nɛr la n ɛɛ Kizeehina Nabɔma dɔɔ sɔnnɛ. Ka nɛr maa wàá wer lɛɛ a huma tɛɛ u hiŋ na sɔŋ la. Kɔraawiizii ɔɔ ra lizi baa gunla uŋ faa lizi Aarɔn la.

ref: This is how it was with Christ. He became a high priest, but not just because he wanted the honor of being one. It was God who told him, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!”
text: Gunnɛ Kristo n faa birgi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la, waa a huma nyiŋŋee tɛɛ u hiŋ na sɔŋ la. Unla n faa ŋɔ wia tɛu labuu lizuu. U faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “N Biibaallɛ hiŋ, zinaabuu n lulii,”

ref: In another place, God says, “You are a priest forever just like Melchizedek.”
text: di ka ŋɔ yembɛl, “I daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di hanna la saŋa maa gunla Mɛlkizɛdɛk n faa ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la.”

ref: God had the power to save Jesus from death. And while Jesus was on earth, he begged God with loud crying and tears to save him. He truly worshiped God, and God listened to his prayers.
text: Saŋa la Yeesu n faa du durnya la, u faa fɔrgi Kɔraawiizi la n niŋ wer lɛɛu siu be labuu, di suŋŋuu werge maa, di ra pogzi di ra wii. Kɔraawiizi nuu dikuu Yeesu n na ɔmuu la wia.

ref: Jesus is God's own Son, but still he had to suffer before he could learn what it really means to obey God.
text: Kɔraawiizi Biibaallɛ ka u gillɔɔ u di tɔɔrɔɔ, ú wer zum gunla un niŋ hiŋ u mɛɛ nua.

ref: This is because God chose him to be a high priest like Melchizedek. Warning against Turning Away
text: Kɔraawiizii ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ ɛɛ u Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la dee Mɛlkizɛdɛk la n faa ɛɛwɛ la. Yeesu hiŋaa vɛɛi karfaa wia

ref: Much more could be said about this subject. But it is hard to explain, and all of you are slow to understand.
text: Yaa dɔɔ wikpilaa yaa n niŋ faa ŋɔ wia naa wia. Ka iiŋ ɛɛ bambugee naa, a daŋ du kpol ka ya wer bagli ia a zɛɛ, ií nuu.

ref: By now you should have been teachers, but once again you need to be taught the simplest things about what God has said. You need milk instead of solid food.
text: Iiŋ helli Kɔraawiizi wia birgi kennaa, a dɛkkɔ iiŋ faa ɛɛ bagla. Ka ii haa ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ nɛr n niŋ haa bagli ia lugli karmaa Kɔraawiizi wia naa biini. Ii kaa ɛɛu lugɔ biizi la n haa waa wette ra di, ka haa ra ɔzi.

ref: People who live on milk are like babies who don't really know what is right.
text: Nɛr la maa n haa ra ɔzi Kɔraawiizi wia biini naa, u haa waa wia zummɛ. U haa ɛɛ biifulaa.

ref: Solid food is for mature people who have been trained to know right from wrong.
text: Nabɔnzii niŋ di diwee himmaa, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ɛɛ wiarɛ bini, di zum winanaa ni wichɔgaa.

ref: We must try to become mature and start thinking about more than just the basic things we were taught about Christ. We shouldn't need to keep talking about why we ought to turn from deeds that bring death and why we ought to have faith in God.
text: Awia, yaa n zum Kristo lugli wia la, ya jaa ra la see, di wer ɛɛ nabɔnzi. Ya gilɛɛ kaa faari ra ŋɔ gunla yaa n niŋ gil yaa biine chɔgi, dikuu wipɛɛri la yaa n na ɛɛ la wia ani gunla yaa n niŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi,

ref: And we shouldn't need to keep teaching about baptisms or about the laying on of hands or about people being raised from death and the future judgment.
text: gunla ban niŋ sɔ nɛra Kɔraawiizi nii, gunla ban niŋ kpa nonee sag nɛra ni, gunla lalaa n niŋ izi ani gunla Kɔraawiizi n niŋ turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim di hanna la saŋa maa la wia.

ref: Let's grow up, if God is willing.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi sɛɛwɔ, yaa daŋ jaa gil wia naa baglaa ka ra la see.

ref: But what about people who turn away after they have already seen the light and have received the gift from heaven and have shared in the Holy Spirit? What about those who turn away after they have received the good message of God and the powers of the future world? There is no way to bring them back. What they are doing is the same as nailing the Son of God to a cross and insulting him in public!
text: di ba zum annii naa maa, ka kaa bir har, ɛrɛɛ bá kaa ɛɛ bá biine kaa chɔgi, bá kaa bir ba naanɛi? Ba wàá wer bir ba Kɔraawiizi be. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ba kaa kpu Kɔraawiizi Biibaallɛ daakaŋlii la ni gunla, di gil u kaa di hiihzi nɛra baaŋ.

ref: A field is useful to farmers, if there is enough rain to make good crops grow. In fact, God will bless such a field.
text: Di hɛri yembɛl du de dooŋ n ɔɔ ra ba, u ra nyɔɔ a nii di ra lii diunanaa di ra tɛɛ banla n na paruu la, u dɔɔ wikuariirɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u ɛɛ hɛrnanii.

ref: But land that produces only thornbushes is worthless. It is likely to fall under God's curse, and in the end it will be set on fire.
text: Ama, di u ra lii sɔɔhri ni choŋgolli, waa wikuarii maa dɔɔwɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ seeu nua. Ba daŋ duu niŋ.

ref: My friends, we are talking this way. But we are sure that you are doing those really good things people do when they are being saved.
text: Ka iawaa, yaa n na ŋɔ wia kennaa, a waa lugɔ yaa ra aani iabuu, n nɛnɔŋŋaa. Yaa dɔɔ ii tamiirɛ lugɔ ii wiɛɛlaa daŋ bɔ, ií wer na lɛɛi.

ref: God is always fair. He will remember how you helped his people in the past and how you are still helping them. You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people.
text: Kɔraawiizi wia maa deŋloore. Wàá suuh gunla iiŋ humuu ani gunla iim bagli nɔŋŋaa la iin nɔŋŋuu, di hiini u biinanaa la, di haa ra hiini baa la.

ref: We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is.
text: Yaa ra nyiŋŋuu lugɔ ii bɛl maa ɔɔ haa aah siwii guŋ di ra la a tuna, ií wer na wia la ni iinna tami la.

ref: Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them. God's Promise Is Sure
text: Ií ra dazi, ii gilɛɛ waa dɔɔ bɔhuaih, ka ɔɔ ra hiŋ gunla banla n faa yardi Kɔraawiizi, nɛra ɛɛ baa wiimaa ka ba waa vɛɛwɛ, ka hiŋ di wa na wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛɛ baa lugɔ ba daŋ na la. Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlii ɛɛ wibiire

ref: No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham,
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nua bɛllɛ tɛɛ Abraham. Uŋ faa ŋɔ nua la, kummaa n waa hoo ɛɛ kunzeŋ kaaluu la wia, u hɛɛhzi u hiŋ,

ref: “I, the Lord, will bless you with many descendants!”
text: di ŋɔ, “N daŋ kissii werge maa di tɛi naanna kpila.”

ref: Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised.
text: Abraham n wette di haa vɛɛ di di kanyitti guŋŋ, u wa na gunla Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua labuu.

ref: When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves.
text: Di newea ra nyiŋŋi ba ŋɔ nua, a ba hɛɛhzi kunla n kaali baabuu. Di ba hɛɛhzɔɔ guŋ, wiŋɔzi maa waa kaa hoo. Ba nua la daŋ chi.

ref: So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi n faa ra nyiŋŋi u bagli banla n niŋ na u nuuŋɔɔlii la biini, gunla u nua un niŋ ŋɔ n niŋ waa chi bá zum lugɔ waa biraa dɔɔwɛ la, u jaa hɛɛhzi u himmaa.

ref: God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed. We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us.
text: Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua di kaa hɛɛhzi u hiŋ jaa la, a wia anɛɛ hiŋ waa biraa dɔɔwɛ, dikuu uŋ waa kara ra kanni wia. U ŋɔ a maanii ka yáa banla n chɔwɛɛ di ga du u be la wer dɔɔ bɔkpega, dikuu tamii la yaa n dɔɔwɛ u wiŋɔzi la ni wia.

ref: This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place.
text: A tamii daŋ wer gil ya chi nɛnnɛ. A tamii wiarɛ yaa wer zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la patiisazenzeŋ n faa teŋŋe la.

ref: Jesus has gone there ahead of us, and he is our high priest forever, just like Melchizedek.
text: Yeesu n birgi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma di hanna la alugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk la, u teŋ tɔ yaa seere zuu de dikuu yaa wia.

ref: Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings.
text: Mɛlkizɛdɛk la faa ɛɛ Salɛm hina koorii, di kaa ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi La N Kaali Kummaa la kizeehiŋ. Abraham faa la laallɛ ga kpu koora la ka bir ra ba di faa wa chem a Mɛlkizɛdɛk ni, a Mɛlkizɛdɛk suŋŋi wiizi tɛu, ú hiinuu.

ref: Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had. The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.”
text: Abraham ge bargi kuna la maa uŋ faa foozee laal la biini la bɔra fi, di kpa a bɔkpaŋ tɛu. Mɛlkizɛdɛk la sɔŋ zɛɛrɛ, “Wideŋlaa Koori.” Uŋ kaa ɛɛ Salɛm koori la, Salɛm ge zɛɛ ɛɛ bampirsɔna la, u sɔŋ kaa di “Bampirsɔna Koori.”

ref: We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
text: U faa waa mɛɛ ni maa dɔɔwɛ yaa zum. U faa waa nɛra dɔɔwɛ. Waa lulaa saŋa dɔɔwɛ yaa zum. Waa siu saŋa gba dɔɔwɛ, ka du de ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ di hanna la alugɔ Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la.

ref: Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies.
text: Ií na gunla uŋ faa ɛɛ nɛzeŋ werge, yaa naabaal Abraham faa bargi u kuna la maa un nawɛɛ laal biini bɔra fi, di lizi bɔkpaŋ tɛu la.

ref: The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests.
text: Levi naanna la n ɛɛ kizeehina la faa ra lɛɛ kunaa ba himmaa nɛra be. Di a nɛra bargi ba kuna bɔra fi, a Levi dee ɔɔ lɛɛ a bɔkpannɛ. Ba maanii ɛɛ Abraham naanna, ka Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ Levi deere dɔɔ bɔkpaŋ la.

ref: Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise.
text: Ka Mɛlkizɛdɛk naa, waa Levi dee biini liwɛɛ, ka lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la lii yaa naabaal Abraham, Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nuuzi tɛɛ la be, ka suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi tɛu.

ref: Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
text: Yaa maa zummɔ lugɔ nabɔmaa suŋŋɛɛ ra tɛɛ bichala.

ref: Priests are given a tenth of what people earn. But all priests die, except Melchizedek, and the Scriptures teach that he is alive.
text: Yaa Kizeehina n na lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la, ba daŋ ŋmɛnɛ siuzi. Ka unlawaa, Kɔraawiizi Hɔŋ ŋɔwɔɔrɛ lugɔ u ra nyinuu.

ref: Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth.
text: Yaa daŋ wer ŋɔ lugɔ Levi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ ú lɛɛ bɔkpaŋ la gba lizi bɔkpannɛ tɛɛ Mɛlkizɛdɛk, dikuu u naabaal mɛɛ Abraham n lizi guŋ tɛu wia.

ref: This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
text: Ba faa haa waa Levi lullɛ saŋa la Mɛlkizɛdɛk n faa chem u ni la. Yeesu ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk

ref: Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron.
text: Kɔraawiizi n tɛɛ u nɛra u Gbɔgni la, a saŋaa Levi dee faari ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la. Too. Di nɛra daŋ faa wer birgi nɛnanaa wa tuŋ, di lii mbusuzi la Levi dee n faa lizɛɛ ra tɛɛ baa la biini, amɔ, ɛrɛɛ wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi kaa ŋɔ kizeehiŋ bɛl dee n du gunla Mɛlkizɛdɛk la n faa duwɛɛ ka gil Aarɔnwaa dee la wiai?

ref: And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
text: Di ba birgi kizeehina wia, amɔ, ba daŋ birgi widaulaa la gba.

ref: The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar.
text: Unla uŋ ŋɔ u wia kennaa ge gba lii dee la n faa waa nɛr maa dɔɔwɛ un niŋ wer kpogli kizee ra hum Kɔraawiizi mbusu lizibɔr la.

ref: Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
text: Yaa Dɔɔri la, yaa zummɔ lugɔ Juda dee biinii u lii. Moosis n faa ŋɔ Juda wia la, u faa waa kizeehina wia ŋɔwɛɛ.

ref: All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest.
text: Kizeehiŋ bɛl n liwɛɛ di ɛɛ lugɔ Mɛlkizɛdɛk la, a wia jaa ra chaani nɛnnɛ di wer chi.

ref: That person wasn't appointed because of his ancestors, but because his life can never end.
text: Newea widaulaa fɔŋŋa biini lɛi u birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la. U miibɔɔ la n waa tuŋ la fɔŋŋa biinii u birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ la,

ref: The Scriptures say about him, “You are a priest forever, just like Melchizedek.”
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “I daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di hanna la saŋa maa gunla Mɛlkizɛdɛk n faa ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ la.”

ref: In this way a weak and useless command was put aside,
text: Awia, widaulibinii la n waa fɔŋŋa dɔɔwɛ, waa wikuarii dɔɔwɛ la wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi lizuu la.

ref: because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
text: Moosis widaulaa la faa waa wette gil nɛr maa birgi nɛnanii wa tuŋ. Wibinaa la n tunnɛ ka wifalaa ge lii la, a wifalaa dɔɔ tamiirɛ werge kaali wibinaa la. A daŋ gil ya wer hel Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is, “I, the Lord, promise that you will be a priest forever! And I will never change my mind!”
text: Ka baŋ wa ŋɔ Yeesu wia, ba ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Kɔraawiizi hɛɛhzɔɔrɛ, wàá ka bir ŋɔ, ‘I daŋ ɛɛ n kizeehiŋ di hanna la saŋa maa.’ ”

ref: This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God.
text: Kɔraawiizi ni nɛra nuukpaŋ dɔɔi naa bɔ ubinii labuu. Yeesu ge ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi talmaa un dauwɛ ya zum lugɔ u ɛɛ wibiire.

ref: There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died.
text: Levi dee la n ɔɔ ra birgi Kɔraawiizi kizeehina la kpillɔɔ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba wàá wer du de ra la. Ba ɔɔ ra siuzuu, baŋhina ge kaa ra di.

ref: But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever!
text: Ka Yeesu n ɔɔ du de saŋa maa la, waabuu ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehinnɛ di hanna la.

ref: He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
text: Awia, u wettoo lɛɛ banla maa n ba u be, bá wer hel Kɔraawiizi be la ha werge maa di wa tuŋ, dikuu uŋ ɔɔ du de ra suŋŋi wiizi ra tɛɛ baa wia.

ref: Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven,
text: Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la dee Yeesu n ɛɛwɛ la dɔɔ hiinaare yaa be. U ɛɛ kunnaniirɛ alugɔ Kɔraawiizi n duwɛɛ la. Waa wichɔgaa maa dɔɔwɛ. Doŋa maa waa hoo u ni. U ni wichɔgɛɛra waa kpaŋ ɛɛwɛ. Kɔraawiizi tɛubuu nabɔmuu u kaali kummaa n du chiŋ.

ref: and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself.
text: Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzi la ɔɔ ra lizi mbusuzii hɔpizibii maa. A ba feluu lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi dikuu ba himmaa wichɔgaa wia mɔɔ, ka jaa lizi ra tɛɛ nɛra la. Ka Yeesu waa guŋ dɔɔwɛ. U lizi mbusuu kakpaŋ bɛŋ. U himmaanii mbusu lizaa sel.

ref: The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
text: Banna hiŋ Moosis Hɔŋ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔnzi la, nɛra la n gɛrgɛɛ, ba waa ɔɔ wer bá vɛɛ wichɔgaa labuu ba ra lizi. Ka wiŋɔzi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ Moosis Hɔŋ harbɔɔ la, di hɛɛhzi u hiŋ la, waabuu gillɛ u Biibaal ɛɛ u Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma di hanna la.

ref: What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven.
text: Wiŋɔzi naa maa biinii keŋ. Yaa dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma la n du gunnɛ. U sogo Girme Hiŋ nabɔmbɔttɛ u bol.

ref: He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
text: U ra hum Kɔraawiizii u Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la n du u Tanti Dia la n ɛɛ u himmaa la. Yaa Dɔɔri labuu baŋuu. Newee lɛi baŋuu.

ref: If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices.
text: Di u vii du durnyaa, u vii waa Kɔraawiizi kizeehiŋ ɛɛwɛ, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba dɔɔ ba horaa ba ra lizi mbusuzi gunla Moosis Hɔŋ n baglɛɛ la.

ref: But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!”
text: Banna hum guŋ naa, ba ra chanzi gunla banna ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi be labuu. Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ Moosis benii saŋa la uŋ faa ra nyiŋŋi u baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la, “A dazi ka kuari u maa gunla miŋ baglii bizeŋ la nyuu la.”

ref: Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
text: Ka Yeesu waa huma wessoo werge kaali guŋ. Nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la uŋ ɛɛ yaa sitɔɔri, u ni Kɔraawiizi kuari la ge bɔ u binii labuu werge. Nuuzi la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ tɛɛ yaa di kuari nuukpaŋ la, a gba wessoo kaali anla.

ref: If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one.
text: Di lugli nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la faa wesso wa tuŋ, ba faa wàá nyiŋŋi bɛl ú lɛɛ u bɔr.

ref: But the Lord found fault with it and said, “I tell you the time will come, when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.
text: Ama, Kɔraawiizi faa tɛɛ u nɛraa chɔgri, di ŋɔ, “Saŋa bɛl ra bau, ń ni Izrɛl ni Juda hina ɛɛ nuukpaŋfalii.

ref: It won't be like the agreement that I made with their ancestors, when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They broke their agreement with me, and I stopped caring about them!
text: Wàá ɛɛ lugɔ unla n ni ba naabaala n ɛɛwɛ saŋa la miŋ kpogli baa lii Ijip hɛri la. Ba faa waa yaa nuukpaŋ la hiŋŋɛ, n bir har kpu baa.

ref: “But now I tell the people of Israel this is my new agreement: ‘The time will come when I, the Lord, will write my laws on their minds and hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Nuukpaŋ la n ni Izrɛl hina n niŋ kaa ɛɛ, a saŋaa keŋ. N daŋ kpa n Gbɔgni du ba biine, di sɛbaa du ba bampiree biine. N daŋ ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la ban ninna hum, bá ge ɛɛ n nɛra.

ref: Not one of them will have to teach another to know me, their Lord.’ “All of them will know me, no matter who they are.
text: A wàá ka ɛɛ lugɔ nɛr maa n niŋ bagli u niwee gɛɛ u dɔŋhiŋ, di ŋɔ, ‘A wesso hiŋ zum Kɔraawiizi,’ dikuubɛɛwiai, ba maanii niŋ zumiŋ, nɛdumazi ni nɛzenaa maa.

ref: I will treat them with kindness, even though they are wicked. I will forget their sins.”
text: N daŋ suŋ ba ni, di gil ba wia la n waa deŋlee la tɛɛ baa. Màá ka liizi ba wichɔgaa wia maa.”

ref: When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
text: Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ “nuukpaŋfalii” wia naa, lugli hor la jaa birgi u biniirɛ. Um birgi u binii naa, u fɔŋŋa ra tunuu, u wia ge ra tuŋ.

ref: The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth.
text: Lugli nuukpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi ni u nɛra n ɛɛwɛ la faa dɔɔ jaamaarɛ ban ninna jaami, di kaa dɔɔ bɔnanii hɛri naa, ban niŋ zuu ra jaami.

ref: The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
text: Ba faa baŋ Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia bɛllɛ, di kpa patiisa teŋ u biini bɔra anɛɛ, saliŋ fintina daa ni tɛɛbul bɛl ni paanuuzi aŋhina baŋ ɔɔ kpa chiŋŋi Kɔraawiizi du bɔr la n du see ba ra yir de Bɔnaniinanii la.

ref: Behind the curtain was the most holy place.
text: A Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa ge du patiisa nɛɛhiŋ la harbɔɔ.

ref: The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them.
text: Daahɛgsɔɔhsuma fuuhribɔr la baŋ kpa saliŋ kuari ni dakka la baŋ kpa saliŋ tɔ u maa, u ɛɛ ba ni Kɔraawiizi Ni U Nɛra Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la du u biini. Saliŋ vii bɛl baŋ kpa paanuu la dee n lii chiŋ la du u biini ni Aarɔn daŋkpala la n faa fur paŋhoori ani bia anɛɛ la, Kɔraawiizi n sɛbi u ni baa nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la wia a ni la, du Nuukpaŋ Dɔɔi Dakka la biini.

ref: On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy. Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things.
text: Ba sɛɛh chɛrubzi chiŋŋi u ni, a willi tɔ bɔr la baŋ faa ɔɔ ra lizi Kɔraawiizi baaŋfuuih u nɛra ni la. Yaa wàá na bɔr ŋɔ kuna naa wia nɛnnɛ filaŋkeŋ.

ref: But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties.
text: Baŋ wa ɛɛ annii maa sirya guŋ, kizeehina ɔɔ ra zuu lugli dia la hɔpizibii maa, di ra hum ba huma.

ref: However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
text: Nɛɛhiŋ lawaa, bina maa, kakpaŋ bɛnnɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma bɛŋ ɔɔ zuu de. U daŋ kpa chal zuu di mizi de, dikuu u himmaa wichɔgaa ni a nɛra wichɔgaa baŋ waa zummɛ ka ɛɛ la wia.

ref: All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship.
text: Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii ra bagli yaabuu lii wia naa biini lugɔ di u Tanti Dia la haa du de, u Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa zuui haa tɔwɔɔrɛ.

ref: This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices.
text: A wia ra bagli filaŋkeŋ wia naabuu. Ba ra lizi mbusuzii fuuh kuna ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi. Ka a wàá wer gil nɛr la n na ɛɛa la dɔɔ biinihuŋŋu wa tuŋ.

ref: These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
text: A ɛɛ bɔrahɔŋ wia bɛnnɛ, lugɔ kuna dii, kuna nyɔɔi ani niisɔi wiarɛ. Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ baabuu guŋ bá ra hiŋ mɔɔ, ka sáŋa la un niŋ wa birgi a maa la wa hel, á ɛɛ a falaa. Kristo chal wia

ref: Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world.
text: Kristo ballɔɔ di ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma, di ra hum winanaa la n liwɛɛ filaŋkeŋ la huma. U ge Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la unna hum u biini la dɔɔ girmee, di du wer kaali unla hiŋ. Newee lɛi baŋuu. Waa hɛri naa kuŋ ɛɛwɛ.

ref: Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
text: Kristo zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa labuu. Un zuuwɛ la, buuŋ ni nabii chal lɛi u kpa zuu de. U himmaa challɛ turgi yaa kim, di wer na lɛɛi la n waa tunaa dɔɔwɛ tɛɛ yaa. Kakpaŋ bɛnnɛ u zuu de. Wàá ka zuu de maa.

ref: According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf.
text: Ba ɔɔ faa kpa buuna, nabala challi ani hɔɔhrii lii bɔr la baŋ fuuh nalor labuu, di mizi banla n doŋŋe Kɔraawiizi be la ni, bá doŋa lii.

ref: But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
text: Di ba wetto ɛɛ guŋ ba doŋa lii, amɔ, Kristo chal wàá lizi yaa doŋa werge maa kaali guŋŋ? Kɔraawiizi Dumnaniirɛ faa hiinuu u kpa u hiŋ di lizi mbusu la. U faa kpekkoo nɛnnɛ. U chal la daŋ lizi yaa wipɛɛri doŋa yaa ni ha, á gilɛɛ kaa tir yaa, ka ya wer hum unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la.

ref: In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use.
text: Di nɛr sɛbi gunla ban niŋ bargi u kuna saŋa la un niŋ wa siu, ka di waa siuwɛ lɛi, ba wàá wer bɔnnaa.

ref: In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
text: Ka di u wa siuwɔ, ba daŋ jaa wer bargi u kuna. Ama, di nɛr la n sɛbi hɔŋ la haa du de, ba wàá wer kpa a hɔŋ fɔŋŋa bɔnni u kuna la.

ref: Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect.
text: Awiarɛ lugli nuukpaŋ la gba, ba faa waa wette ɛɛu tuŋ, di ba faa waa chal fukke mɔɔ.

ref: Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water.
text: Moosis n faa bagli nɛra la maa Kɔraawiizi widaulaa la maa n du u hɔŋ biini la tuŋ, u gillɔɔ ba kpu nabizi di kpa a challi, nii, pehuna la n aahwɛ ani hisɔp daa mizi hɔŋ la ni a nɛra maa ni,

ref: He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.”
text: di ŋɔ, “Chal la n kuari nuukpaŋ la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ ii ra hiŋ labuu keŋ.”

ref: Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship.
text: U kaa mizi Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la ni tassazi la maa baŋ kpawɛɛ ra hum de la ni.

ref: The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered. Christ's Great Sacrifice
text: Moosis Hɔnna ra bagluu gunla maa ban ninna ɛɛ ka wer ra lizi doŋa nɛra ni. Challɛ bá kpa ɛɛ a galga maa. Di ba waa kuŋ kpuwɛɛ u chal lii, Kɔraawiizi wàá gil ba wichɔgaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better.
text: Gunnɛ Kɔraawiizi ŋɔ bá ɔɔ ɛɛ ka wer lizi doŋa Tanti Dia la kuna la ni ha. A kuna ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ anla n du Kɔraawiizi be la, ka anla n du Kɔraawiizi be labuu ɛɛ a himmaa. Mbusu la n wesse werge kaali guŋ la, waabuu ba ɛɛ ka wer lizi a doŋa ha.

ref: This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
text: Kristo n zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii la, unla n du dia la newea n mawɛɛ u li u himmaa la n du Kɔraawiizi be la biini lɛi u zuu. Kɔraawiizi bol himmaanii u zuu du de filaŋkeŋ, ú wer kuu yaa hiinaa wia ga chi Kɔraawiizi see.

ref: Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal.
text: Un zuu de la, gunla Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma n ɔɔ kpa chal la n waa u himmaa hor ɛɛwɛ la zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa bina maa la, guŋ lɛi u zuu de ɛɛ. Waa ɔɔ kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu ra tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi digiidigii.

ref: If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
text: Di u faa ra ɛɛ guŋ, u daŋ faa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ saŋakpila maa durnya faaraa saŋa la guŋŋ wa lii zinaa. Ka u ballɔɔ durnya tuna hɔpizaa naa biini, ú wer kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, di duŋŋi wichɔgaa kakpaŋ, á tuŋ.

ref: We die only once, and then we are judged.
text: Kɔraawiizi tɛɛ neweare lugɔ bá siu kakpaŋ bɛŋ, ka ú jaa di ba seriya.

ref: So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
text: Gunnɛ Kristo n kuu nɛkpila wia di kpa u hiŋ lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi, ú wer lɛɛ nɛra wichɔgaa chi la, kakpannɛ u ɛɛ guŋ. Di u kaa wa ba, wichɔgaa wia lɛi ú ba. U daŋ ba ú wa lɛɛ banla n na binni u ŋmɛnɛɛ ani tamii la.

ref: The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year.
text: Moosis Hɔŋ wia la faa tɔ winanaa la n faa haa du harbɔɔ la seere. A faa waa a himmaa ɛɛwɛ alugɔ nɛr laalii n waa u himmaa ɛɛwɛ la. Awia, mbusuzi la banna lizi binaa bina maa la wàá wer gil banla n kpaa ba la birgi nɛnanaa.

ref: If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices.
text: Di a mbusuzi faa wetto gil ba birgi nɛnanaa guŋ, ba faa wàá gil a lizaa? Di a faa wetto lizi ba doŋa ha, ba faa wàá ka zum wichɔgaa.

ref: When Christ came into the world, he said to God, “Sacrifices and offerings are not what you want, but you have given me my body.
text: Awia, Kristo n ba durnya la, u ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Mbusu lizaa ni kuna fuuih lɛi i ra nyiŋŋi. Bɔrahɔŋ bɛl siryaa i ɛɛ tɛŋ.

ref: No, you are not pleased with animal sacrifices and offerings for sin.”
text: Baŋ fuuh sela lizi mbusuzi tɛi, dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia la, a wɛɛ pattɛ.

ref: Then Christ said, “And so, my God, I have come to do what you want, as the Scriptures say.”
text: Denii n ŋɔ, ‘Na! N ballɔɔ gunla baŋ faa sɛbi n wia i hɔŋ biini la, ń wa ɛɛ i kipar, n Dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi.’ ”

ref: The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them?
text: Uŋ faa ŋɔ gunla lugɔ mbusuzi lizaa, kuna fuuih ani anla maa banna ɛɛ dikuu ba wichɔgaa wia gunla Moosis Hɔŋ n baglɛɛ la, dí a wɔɔ pattɛ la,

ref: Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.”
text: di kaa ŋɔ, “Na, n ballɔɔ ń wa ɛɛ i kipar la,” uŋ ŋɔ kennaa naa, u lizi lugli hiŋaa labuu ha gunla, ka ú wer dau nɛɛhiŋ la hiŋaa.

ref: The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins.
text: Kizeehina la n ɔɔ chi mbusu lizibɔr hɔpizibii maa, di hum ra lizi mbusuzi la dee baŋ ɔɔ ra lizi digiidigii la, a waa wette lizi wichɔgaa maa ra ha.

ref: But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side,
text: Ama, Yeesuwaa, uŋ siuwɛ lizi mbusu dikuu nɛra wichɔgaa wia la, kakpannɛ u ɛɛ guŋ, ú chi saŋa maa ra la, ka jaa ga so Kɔraawiizi nabɔmbɔr.

ref: and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power.
text: U du denii di ra kpaŋ saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ gil u dɔma birgi u yoma la.

ref: By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
text: U mbusu lizaa kpaŋkpaŋ la wia banla maa Kɔraawiizi n lizi ba doŋa ba ni ha la, daŋ ɔɔ du wer di ra la saŋa maa.

ref: The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
text: Kɔraawiizi Dumnanii gba ra di guŋ daansɛɛrɛ ra tɛɛ yaa, di ŋɔ,

ref: “When the time comes, I will make an agreement with them. I will write my laws on their minds and hearts.
text: “Nuukpaŋfalii la n ni baa n niŋ ɛɛu keŋ, N daŋ kpa n Gbɔgni du ba biine, di sɛbaa du ba bampiree biine.”

ref: Then I will forget about their sins and no longer remember their evil deeds.”
text: U kaa ŋɔ jaa, “Màá ka liizi ba wichɔgaa wia maa.”

ref: When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices. Encouragement and Warning
text: Too. Di Kɔraawiizi gil wichɔgaa la tɛɛ baa, ba wàá ka lizi mbusuzi dikuu a wia.

ref: My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place
text: Awia, yaabalaa, yaa daŋ wer dɔɔ bampirii zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la dikuu Yeesu chal wia.

ref: by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
text: U pilli ŋmɛnifalii la n dɔɔ miibɔɔrɛ tɛɛ yaa, ya wer zuu de. U bɔrahɔŋ gba ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ patiisazenzeŋ la n faa teŋ Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la. Un siuwɛ la, bɔr la jaa pilluu tɛɛ yaa.

ref: We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house.
text: Yaa dɔɔ Kizeehina Nabɔnzenzeŋ bɛl n na binni Kɔraawiizi biizi ninɛɛ.

ref: So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water.
text: Awia, ya la ga zuu de ani biinihuŋŋu, di gilɛɛ waa aani, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi lizi yaa biine doŋaa ha yaa wichɔgaa maa lii. A wàá kaa ra tir yaa. U kaa sɔ yaa niinanii yaa lii.

ref: We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us.
text: Ya lau tamii la yaa n ŋɔ yaa dɔɔwɔ la nɛnnɛ, di gilɛɛ waa aani tama maa. Unla n ŋɔ nua la wia dɔɔ wibiire.

ref: We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things.
text: Ya ra binni dɔŋa ni, di zum gunla yaa n niŋ gil yaa maa aah siwii, dikuu dɔnnɔŋŋaa ni winanaa ɛɛi wia.

ref: Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
text: Ya gilɛɛ vɛɛ dɔŋa be chaalaa lugɔ baŋhina n na vɛɛ la. Ya chaali dɔŋa di ra bagli dɔŋa ŋmɛnizi gunla yaa n ninna hiŋ. Kɔraawiizi Hɔpizii la ra dugluu. Awia, ya aah siwii werge ra hiini dɔŋa guŋ.

ref: No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth.
text: Di Kɔraawiizi pilli yaa siwee, yaa zum wibii nɛnnɛ, ka kutti ga ɛɛ wichɔgaa, mbusu lizaa maa waa kaa hoo un niŋ wer lizi a wichɔgaa ha,

ref: They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire.
text: ka yaa danna fɔŋ, di ra guu hɔpizii la Kɔraawiizi n niŋ di yaa seriya, di du yaa chɔgri niŋ la n na lau siaahmu ni, di ra fuuh u dɔma la biini.

ref: If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death.
text: Di nɛr la maa chɔgi Moosis hɔŋ Gbɔgni la, nɛra banɛɛ gɛɛ bahoro ŋɔ u wia guŋ, ba ra kpuubuu. Ba waa ɔɔ na u sinyɛna.

ref: But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy.
text: Di gunnɛ, ɛrɛɛ bá ɛɛ nɛr la n gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi Biibaal, di binni u chal la n kuari nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la pɛɛ, di kaa gbɛlli Kɔraawiizi Duma nɛsunaa la n na hiinuu, di gil u birgi Kɔraawiizi hor lai? Di Kɔraawiizi waa turgi u ge kim, u hor wàá nyaŋŋi werge maa?

ref: We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people.
text: Yaa zum unla n ŋɔwɛɛ, “Minuu dɔɔ wichɔgaa kinturgaa. Mìń niŋ turgi nɛra ba wichɔgaa kim.” Ba kaa sɛbi yembɛl, di ŋɔ, “Yaa Dɔɔri daŋ di u nɛra seriya.”

ref: It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
text: Di i chol unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la nonee biini, ɔnsiirɛ.

ref: Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light.
text: Ií ra liizi saŋa la Kɔraawiizi n felee chaani ii siwee la. Ii faa di tɔɔrɔɔrɛ werge maa, ka faa haa vɛɛ ra hiŋ.

ref: Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others.
text: A saŋa bɛl, ba faa ra chagzi iabuu di ra tɔɔri ia nɛra baaŋ. A saŋa bɛl ge, ii faa ra hiini banla baŋ faa ra tɔɔri la.

ref: You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
text: Ii faa suŋ banla baŋ tɔwɛɛ dia la ninɛɛ. Ba foozi ii kunaa, ka ii haa gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, ii faa zummɔ lugɔ ii dɔɔ kuna la n wesse ninɛɛ kaali durnya kuna naa. A ge daŋ ɔɔ du de di ra la.

ref: Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards.
text: Awia, ii gilɛɛ gil ii yarda la iiŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi Biibaal la ta filaŋkeŋ. U dɔɔ kinturginaniirɛ werge maa.

ref: Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised.
text: A dɛkkɔ iin niŋ haa ra di kanyitti. Di ii wetto di ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizi kipar, ii daŋ na nua la maa Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ la.

ref: As the Scriptures say, “God is coming soon! It won't be very long.
text: Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, di ŋɔ, “A ka tamaa, ka unla n niŋ ba la ba. Wàá ka birgi.

ref: The people God accepts will live because of their faith. But he isn't pleased with anyone who turns back.”
text: Nɛr la wia n deŋlee, yardaa niŋ ɛɛ u miibɔɔ. Ka di u wa bir har, u wia wàá ka pariŋ.”

ref: We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
text: Ka yaawaa waa banla n niŋ bir har, Kɔraawiizi chɔgi baa la ɛɛwɛ. Yaa daŋ ɔɔ yardi di na lɛɛi.

ref: Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see.
text: Bɛɛ yardai? Yardaa hinna tami wia ni, aabuu niŋ bagli lugɔ i daŋ naa. Di i haa waa a wia nawɛɛ ka yardi, a yardaa ɔɔ gil i zum lugɔ i daŋ wa naa.

ref: It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
text: Ba Kɔraawiizi yarda hiŋ wiarɛ yaa naabaala la faa na sɔŋ.

ref: Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
text: Yaa ge Kɔraawiizi yarda gillɔɔ yaa zum lugɔ chiŋ ni hɛri maa lii Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii uŋ ŋɔwɛɛ la fɔŋŋa biinii. Awia, kuna la siwee n na na la lii kuna la siwee n waa na la biinii.

ref: Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
text: Abɛl Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ, uŋ faa lizi mbusu tɛɛ Kɔraawiizi la, u hor faa du wer kaali u kpɛɛma Keen hor la. Uŋ yarduu wiarɛ u ŋɔ u ɛɛ nɛnaniirɛ u be, di bagli lugɔ u mbusu lizaa la paruubuu. A yarda wiarɛ Abɛl siu birgi, ka haa wer ra bagli yaa wia la.

ref: Enoch had faith and did not die. He pleased God, and God took him up to heaven. This is why his body was never found.
text: Ɛnɔk Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi faa kpau kaali u be. Waa siuwɛ. Kɔraawiizi kpaubuu guŋ. Ba nyiŋŋuu huhzi. Ba faa sɛbi u wiarɛ, di ŋɔ lugɔ u wia par Kɔraawiizii.

ref: But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
text: Nɛr la n waa Kɔraawiizi yardɛɛ, u wia wàá wer paruu. Di nɛr la maa ŋɔ ú hel Kɔraawiizi be, u daŋ feli yardi lugɔ u du denii, di kaa yardi lugɔ Kɔraawiizi ra hiini banla maa n aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi u bɔttɛ.

ref: Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
text: Noowa Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u ge faa kuari muugberzeŋ la. Kɔraawiizi faa karfuubuu wia la n niŋ wa ɛɛ la. U ge n na hiŋ Kɔraawiizi la wia, u kuari muugberzeŋ la di wer lɛɛ u ni u diahina maa. Uŋ wette ɛɛ guŋ ka durnya la n kawɛɛ vɛɛ la, u tɛɛ baabuu chɔgri. Kɔraawiizi di ba seriya ba chol, ka gil Noowa waa ɛɛ nɛnanii u be, dikuu uŋ yarduu wia.

ref: Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen.
text: Abraham Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Kɔraawiizi n yiruu ŋɔ ú izi u bol la hɛri la un niŋ tɛu la, u wer izi lii. U faa waa zum bɔr la maa un niŋ la, ka izi ra la.

ref: Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise.
text: Yarda wiarɛ u wer ɛɛ hɔɔhri du hɛri la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔwɛɛ lugɔ u daŋ tɛu la. U faa ra zuu tanti diini biinee alugɔ yaa naabaala Aizik ni Jekɔb maa. U ni ba maanii Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ nua tɛɛ.

ref: Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
text: Abraham faa ra nyiŋŋi bol bɛl deere. A bol dee, Kɔraawiizi maubuu u chi nɛnnɛ. Wàá chol maa.

ref: Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son.
text: Saara Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u wer kpogli hia saŋa la uŋ faa zɛŋŋɛ tuŋ la. Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua tɛu lugɔ u daŋ lul bie la, u faa zummɔ lugɔ u wia dɔɔ wibiire.

ref: Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
text: Denii Abraham, saŋa la u fɔŋŋa maa n tunnɛ la, ka u wetto lul biizi, u naanna ge bir wa du kpil alugɔ chinchiŋwilaa gɛɛ muuzeŋ kɛrii hɛɛhriichaa n kpillɛ gunla.

ref: Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth.
text: Bannii maa faa yardi Kɔraawiizii ka siuzi. Ba faa waa wia la Kɔraawiizi n ŋɔ nua la nawɛɛ siwii ni ka siuzi. Ka ba faa naabuu alugɔ iinna nɛra bɔɔnɛɛ, di ra jaami baa gunla. Ba faa sɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ ba ɛɛ hɔɔhraa durnya naa biini.

ref: When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own.
text: Nɛra n na ŋɔ gunla, ba himmaa hɛrii ba ra nyiŋŋi la.

ref: If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time.
text: Di ba hɛri la baŋ liwɛɛ wiarɛ ba faa ŋɔ guŋ, ba daŋ faa wer bir la de.

ref: But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
text: Hɛri la n wesse werge kaaluu labuu ba faa ra nyiŋŋi. Kɔraawiizi be hɛrii ba faa ra nyiŋŋi la. Awia, banna yiruu ba dɔɔri Kɔraawiizi la, guŋ wɔɔ ra ɛɛ hiihzi. U ɛɛ bol siryaa tɛɛ baa.

ref: Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac,
text: Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔ u benii lugɔ Aizik benii ú ga na biizi ni naanna.

ref: because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
text: Ka u faa dɔɔ Kɔraawiizi tamiirɛ lugɔ di u siuwɔ gba, ka Kɔraawiizi daŋ wer lalluu. A ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ u lalluubuu siu biini la.

ref: Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons.
text: Jekɔb ge Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ unna siu, u suŋŋi wiizi ú hiini Joosɛf biizi banɛɛ la di pi u daŋkpala ni jaami Kɔraawiizi.

ref: And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
text: Joosɛf gba Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ u ge n na siu la, u wer ŋɔ lugɔ Izrɛl hina la daŋ ŋmɛnɛ lii a hɛri, di bagli baa lugɔ bá kpa u hoga ra la a saŋa.

ref: Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders.
text: Moosis maa ni u mɛɛ ge Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ baŋ lul Moosis, ba suauh baaguzi ahoro, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba faa nawɔɔrɛ lugɔ u ɛɛ biinaniirɛ. Ba faa waa koori gbɔg la ɔmmɛ.

ref: Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson.
text: Gunnɛ Moosis ge Kɔraawiizi yarda la gil uŋ wa helle, waa sɛɛwɛ ba yiruu koori biihambie la biibaal,

ref: Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
text: Gbɛllaa la un niŋ kuu Kristo wia ba gbɛlluu la, aabuu ɛɛ kunnanaa u be werge maa kaali kunnanaa la maa n faa du Ijip hɛri, dikuubɛɛwiai, u faa ra binni hɔpizii la n niŋ ba, Kɔraawiizi wa turgi nɛra maa labuu.

ref: Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger.
text: Uŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wiarɛ waa Ijip koori la baaŋ ɔmmɛ, ka izi u hɛri la. U wettoo dɔɔ bampirii, dikuubɛɛwiai, a ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ u na unla baŋ waa na labuu.

ref: His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
text: U yarda hiŋ wiarɛ u dau Gillikaali wia la, di gil ba mizi ba gbessi chal, síu mɛlika la gilɛɛ wa kpu Izrɛl hina biinabɔnzi la.

ref: Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
text: Nɛra la Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ Muuzeŋaahmu la wer bargi, hɛrhilii chɔɔ alugɔ u baŋgia, ba wer vol wa lii. Ijip hina n wa ɛɛ guŋ na, nii la di baa.

ref: God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
text: Izrɛl hina Kɔraawiizi yarda wiarɛ, baŋ volle bar Jɛriko hɔpizaa aniidaanɛɛ biini, u koŋlaa la bam mawɛɛ baruu la chogli.

ref: What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
text: Too. Ń haa vɛɛ bagli ra jaaa? Màá wer na bɔr bagli ba maa wia. Gidiɔn, Barak, Samsin, Jɛfta, Deevid, Samuɛl ani Kɔraawiizi dɔgtɛɛzi la maanii du de.

ref: Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions
text: A nɛra kuu baŋ yardi Kɔraawiizi wia di wer kpegli kossi, di wer gil nɛra ra ɛɛ wia la n deŋlee, di wer na lii Kɔraawiizi nuuŋɔɔlaa la biini, di wer tɔ bunyinzi nuuzi, a waa wette hee baa,

ref: and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
text: di wer sɔɔni ninzenaaa nuuzi, a waa wette fuuh baa, di wer lɛɛ bahinaa banla n kpa tokobizi ra nyiŋŋi ba kpu baa la be, di wer na fɔŋŋa saŋa la baŋ gɛrgɛɛ la, di wer yoo laal nɛnnɛ, di wer kpegli hɔɔhra la n ballɛ wa yoo baa la,

ref: Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life.
text: di kaa wer lalli haana baŋhina biizi siu biini. Baŋhina ge, ba dɔma tɔɔri baa di kpuuzi baa. Ba faa waa nyiŋŋi ba lɛɛ bahinaa, ka ra nyiŋŋi bá wer na miibɔɔnanii saŋa la ban niŋ izi siu biini la.

ref: Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail.
text: Ba faa lɔ baŋhina mɔmɔsia di viiri baa, di vɔɔzi baŋhina ge yɔlɔzi di tɔɔgi baa diini.

ref: Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured.
text: Ba faa lɔɔzi baŋhina bia, di ɛɛ baŋhina na, di teŋri baŋhina ge bɔra anɛɛgaa, di kaa kpa tokobi kpuuzi baŋhina. A nɛra baŋhina faa tɔɔgi peeza ni buuna hɔna ra gaagi. Ba faa waa kummaa dɔɔwɛ. Nɛra faa ra tɔɔri baa di ra ɛɛ baa wichɔgaa.

ref: The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
text: Durnya faa waa dɛg ba ni baa dui. Ba faa ra gaagi ra du hɛribɔdumazi ni giŋgimee ni bia bɔɔni biine.

ref: All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised.
text: Ba na sɔnnɛ dikuu ba Kɔraawiizi yarda la wia. Ka ba waa Kɔraawiizi nua la uŋ faa ŋɔwɛɛ la nawɛɛ,

ref: This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa zum yaa saŋa naa hina wiarɛ, di faa dau gunla n wesse, di ŋɔ ba bɛŋ wàá na a maa tuŋ, see yaa maa n niŋ kpau naa.

ref: Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us.
text: Awia, nɛkpila naa maa n chigɛ bar yaa, di ra binni yaa kennaa, a dɛkkɔɔ yaa n niŋ ɛɛ lugɔ chɔchɔɔra, di lizi kuntɔga ni wichɔgaa maa yaa ni ha, di kpa kanyitti chɔ ra la maga la Kɔraawiizi n dauwɛ tɛɛ yaa la,

ref: We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne!
text: di ɔɔ ra binni Yeesu la n ɛɛ yaa yarda maa nyuu hiŋ la. Waabuu faa kuu bɔsɔna la un niŋ wa di wia, di di tɔɔrɔɔ daakaŋlii ni la. U faa waa hiihzi wia kuuwɛ vɛɛ, ka jaa so Kɔraawiizi koorikara nabɔmbɔr la.

ref: So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
text: Ií ra liizi gunla nɛchɔgaa n faa chagzuu, ka u di baa kanyitti la, ka ii gilɛɛ gil ii bɔra wàá huah, ii wa bir ra laŋŋi harbɔɔ.

ref: None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin.
text: Iinna yoo wichɔgaa naa, ii haa waa yoowe ii challi lii.

ref: But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children, “When the Lord punishes you, don't make light of it, and when he corrects you, don't be discouraged.
text: Ii waa bɔr la baŋ yir ia biizi la wia ra liizi. Ba sɛbɔɔrɛ, “N bie, di Kɔraawiizi tɛr i digni, gilɛɛ waa binni guŋ pɛɛ. Gilɛɛ gil guŋ chɔg i biini,

ref: The Lord corrects the people he loves and disciplines those he calls his own.”
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, banla un nɔŋŋɛɛ dignaa u ra tɛrgi, bá wer zum wia, di kaa lɔɔzi bie la maa unna yir u himmaa bie.”

ref: Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children?
text: Awia, dignitɛraa naa, ií ra di guŋ kanyitti. Kɔraawiizi kpa iabuu birgi u biizi. Mɛɛ waa u bie digni ra tɛraa?

ref: God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him.
text: Di waa ii digna ra tɛrgi gunla unna tɛrgi u biizi maa digna la, amɔ, ii waa u biizi ɛɛwɛ. Ii ɛɛ sɛnsɛŋ biizii.

ref: Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is.
text: Yaa mɛɛwaa la faa tɛrgi yaa dignaa hɔpizaa tama biini gunla baŋ nawɛɛ la. Kɔraawiiziwaa ra ɛɛ gunnɛ, á wer lii tɔna tɛɛ yaa, ya ɛɛ nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ gunla u ge n duwɛɛ la.

ref: It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
text: Saŋa la unna tɛrgi yaa digna la, bɔsɔna wia lɛi. Biinichɔgrɛ. Ka di a wa ɛɛ tama, yaa daŋ na, di u gillɔ yaa birgi nɛnanaa dɔɔ bampirsɔna.

ref: Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking
text: Awia, ií du banla bɔra n huahwɛ bɔkpega, bá wer chi chigigi.

ref: and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse. Warning against Turning from God
text: “Ií ra kuari ŋmɛnizi á ra deŋli, ií wer vol a ni, nɛ́r la n na dugzi kpuŋe gilɛɛ waa lii a bɔɔni, ka á wer nyaagi.” Kɔraawiizi vɛɛi karfaazi wia

ref: Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord.
text: Ií aah siwii ra nyiŋŋi nuukpaŋ, di aah siwii, ií wer ɛɛ nɛnanaa la n waa doŋa maa dɔɔwɛ la. Nɛr la maa n waa guŋ duwɛɛ, wàá wer na yaa Dɔɔri.

ref: or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop,
text: bensunozenzeŋ ra wii, loobii bɛl ra ŋɔ wia. Nɛra la n wa nuu loobii la, ba fɔrguu ú gilɛɛ kaa ŋɔ wia ba be,

ref: because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi faa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Di kummaa, haali sel wa gbɔgzi bizeŋ la, bá kpa bia lɔɔzuu kpu ta.” Guŋ faa tir baa werge maa.

ref: The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
text: Bizeŋ la wia faa dɔɔ ɔnsiirɛ werge maa. Awiarɛ Moosis ŋɔ, “Ɔnsii lawimbuu, n bɔra ra sa.”

ref: You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate.
text: Ka iawaa, iiŋ ŋɔ ii ba Kɔraawiizi be naa, Bizeŋ Ziɔn ni Jɛrusalɛm la n du u be la benii ii ra ba. Unla n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi himmaa la bolle a Jɛrusalɛm. U mɛlikananaa kpila maa du de.

ref: Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect.
text: U biinabɔnzi la n ɛɛ u kapɛttɛ diire, ba sɔna du hɔŋ la n du u be la biini la gba chaalɔɔrɛ de. Ba ni Kɔraawiizi la n ɛɛ nɛra maa seriya diiri la benii ii ra ba ni lalaa la ŋmɛnizi n faa deŋlee, Kɔraawiizi gil ba birgi nɛnanaa la be,

ref: And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
text: ni Yeesu la n kuari yaa ni Kɔraawiizi nuukpaŋfalii dɔɔi la be ani bɔr la u chal n mizɛɛ la be. U chal la dɔɔ hiinaare yaa be werge maa. Waa ɛɛwɛ lugɔ Abɛl hor la.

ref: Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven?
text: Ií ra dazi di gilɛɛ waa vɛɛ unla n na ŋɔ wia ii be la. Di saŋa la hina la n faa vɛɛ unla n du hɛri karfi baa la waa wette lɛɛ bahinaa, yaa banla n vɛɛ unla n du chiŋ ra karfi yaa la, ɛrɛɛ ya ge wer ɛɛ lɛɛ yaa hinaanɛi?

ref: When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
text: A saŋa u loobii gbɔgzɔɔrɛ, hɛri ra zigli. Ka u ŋɔ nua bɛllɛ filaŋkeŋ di ŋɔ, “N daŋ kaa zigli hɛri kakpaŋ bɛŋ. Ama, hɛri bɛŋ lɛi ń zigli a saŋa. Chiŋ ni hɛri maanii ń zigli.”

ref: The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last.
text: Uŋ ŋɔ, “kakpaŋ bɛŋ” la, u zɛɛrɛ lugɔ di u wa ziglaa, u daŋ lizi kuna la maa un niŋ wer zigli la ha, ka anla n waa ziglaa dɔɔwɛ la wer ka.

ref: We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect.
text: Awia, Kɔraawiizi n gillɛ yaa du u kora la n waa ziglaa dɔɔwɛ biini naa, a wesso yaa n na tɛu jaaŋ saŋa maa, di ra humuu gunla n paruu, di ra tɔgzuu di ra ɔmuu,

ref: Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
text: Ií haa ra kpa dɔŋa lugɔ maa biizi di nɔŋŋi dɔŋa.

ref: Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
text: Ií gilɛɛ ra suuh hɔɔhra wia, ka ɔɔ lɛɛ baa ra dau. Baŋhina faa lɛɛ Kɔraawiizi mɛlikazii dau ka ba waa zummɛ.

ref: Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
text: Ií ra liizi banla baŋ tɔwɛɛ dia wia alugɔ ii ni baa maanii ba tɔ dia la, di gil ii bɔra ra nyiiri banla banna tɔɔri la ni dikuu ii gba n dɔɔ bɔrahɔna wia.

ref: Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
text: Ií gil nɛr maa ra tɔgzi hahdɔɔi, di gilɛɛ ra chɔɔ nɛdumazi be. Kɔraawiizi daŋ di banla n na ɛɛ wikuna, di ra sɛm la seriya, bá chol.

ref: Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us.
text: Ií gilɛɛ kpa kebee su siwii. Ií gil kunla iin dɔɔwɛ la kukki ia, dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi himmaa ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Màá ɛɛ ii wia vɛɛlai maa. Màá gil ii ta maa.”

ref: This should make you feel like saying, “The Lord helps me! Why should I be afraid of what people can do to me?”
text: Awia, yaa daŋ wer dɔɔ bɔsɔna, di ŋɔ, “N Dɔɔri ra hiinimbuu. Maa ɔm. Bɛɛ newee kaa wer ɛɛnnɛi?”

ref: Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
text: Ií ra liizi ii nabɔnzi la n bagli ia Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlaa la be. Ií ra binni gunla baŋ hiŋŋɛ ani gunla ba ni Kɔraawiizi yarda dɔɔi ge n duwɛɛ, di ge ra hiŋ guŋ.

ref: Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them.
text: Wibaglaa ni a dizi du denii ɛɛ witittaa. Ií gilɛɛ ra sɛɛa di ra leuzi. A wesso yaa n na nyiŋŋi bɔkpega lii Kɔraawiizi hiinaa biini, di gilɛɛ ra nyiŋŋaa diwee aŋhina dee dii biini. Banla n na dia gunla waa hiinaa ra na a be.

ref: But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
text: Yaa dɔɔ mbusu lizibɔr bɛllɛ banla n na hum Kɔraawiizi Tanti Dia la biini n waa dɛkkɛ ban ninna di de.

ref: After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp.
text: Sela la baŋ ɔɔ kpu lizi a challi, Kɔraawiizi Kizeehina Maa Nabɔma kpaa zuu Kɔraawiizi Bɔnaniinanii Himmaa la tɛu, dikuu wichɔgaa wia la, ba ɔɔ kpa a sela hinnɛ lii danzɛɛkɛrii ga fuuah de.

ref: Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy.
text: Awiarɛ Yeesu n faa ra siu, ú himmaa chal wer sɔ nɛra doŋa ba ni ha la, bol danzɛɛ kɛriirɛ u du di faa ra di tɔɔrɔɔ la.

ref: This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace.
text: Awia, ií gil ya ge lii la u be danzɛɛ kɛrii la, yáa maa kpau ra di hiihzi la uŋ faa diwee la,

ref: On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, yaa waa bol dɔɔwɛ durnya naa biini, yá du ra la. Yaa ra nyiŋŋi bol la n haa du har ra ba la duirɛ.

ref: But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
text: Ya gilɛɛ suuh winanaa ɛɛi wia, ka ɔɔ bɔnni yaa kuna ra tɛɛ nɛra. Guŋ gba ɛɛ mbusuzii ra par Kɔraawiizi.

ref: Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
text: Ií ra hiŋ ii nabɔnzi nuuzi, di ra sɛɛ ba dɔɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, ba ra du ii dunzi taurɛ. Kɔraawiizi daŋ wa pɛɛzi baa ii wia. Awia, ií ra sɛɛ ba dɔɔra, bá wer ra hum ba huma la ni bɔsɔna, di gilɛɛ ra humaa ni biinichɔg. Guŋ wàá hiini ia.

ref: I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon. Final Prayers and Greetings
text: N kaa ra suŋŋi iabuu werge maa, ií suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi, ú gil n wer bir ba ii be manaŋ.

ref: God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock.
text: Kɔ́raawiizi la n ɛɛ bampirsɔna hiŋ, unla n lalli yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu siu biini u ɛɛ Penɔɔnizeŋ, dikuu un siuwɛ u chal kuari nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la n wàá chɔgi maa wia la,

ref: I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
text: Kɔraawiizi hiini ia, ií wer dɔɔ bampirsɔna la iin niŋ dɔɔ, di wer ra ɛɛ u kipar. Ú hum u huma yaa maa biine, ya wer du gunla maa n paruu Yeesu Kristo fɔŋŋa biini. Waabuu niŋ dɔɔ girme saŋa maa di ra la. Ami.

ref: My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
text: N kaa ra suŋŋi iabuu, yaabalaa, ií nuu ra tɛŋ ani wia naa mim bagli ia naa biini. Maa sɛbɛɛ werge.

ref: By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
text: Ba lizi yaa dɔŋhiŋ Timotii nɛra tɔi dia la biini. Di u wa ballɔ manaŋ, n nuu maa daŋ ba wa na ia.

ref: Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people. His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
text: Ií ra jaami ii nabɔnzi maa ni Kɔraawiizi biinanaa la maa. Banla n ɛɛ Itali hina la ra jaami ia.

ref: I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
text: Kɔ́raawiizi nɛsunnaa ni u hiinaa du ii maa be.

ref: From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world. Faith and Wisdom
text: Mìŋ́ Jems n ɛɛ Kɔraawiizi ni yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo baliirɛ ra sɛbi hɔnnaa, di ra tɛɛ ii banla n ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋra di yaari du yemmaa la. N na jaami ia. Yarda ni nunzuma wia

ref: My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble.
text: Yaabalaa, di tɔɔrɔɔ kpila wa huuzi ia, ií gil ii bɔra sɔɔni ia werge.

ref: If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking.
text: Di hinla maa ra nyiŋŋi nunzuma, amɔ, í ra suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ú tɛi. Waa ɔɔ ra nyɛg banla n na suŋŋuu guŋ ni, ka u ɔɔ ra tɛɛ baabuu werge maa. Di i suŋŋuu, i daŋ na kunla hiŋ suŋŋɛɛ u be.

ref: But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm.
text: Ka di ii ra suŋŋuu, ií ra suŋŋuu ni yarda, di gilɛɛ ra aani. Nɛr la n na suŋŋi Kɔraawiizi ka ra aani lugɔ wàá tɛu la, a hiŋ ɛɛwɔɔ lugɔ muuzeŋ la peu n niŋ wer bir u nii di ra la bɔr maa labuu.

ref: Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them.
text: Di i ɛɛ Yeesu hiŋri ka ɛɛ nyaari, ka í gil i bɔra sɔɔnii. I ɛɛ nɛzenne Kɔraawiizi be.

ref: But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers
text: Di i ɛɛ daama hiŋ genii, ka í gil i ni nyaara nuukpaŋ dɔɔi la sɔɔni i bɔra, dikuubɛɛwiai, u daŋ siu lugɔ pir fiiri.

ref: scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business. Trials and Temptations
text: Gunla wiizi n ɔɔ baŋ di lɔ, koorii hil, u fiiri yɔl, u wessi chɔgi la, gunnɛ daama hiŋ ge ɔɔ ɛɛ u wia ka bir wa siu la.

ref: God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
text: Hinla maa n dɔɔ kanyitti di ra di tɔɔrɔɔ, gil i bɔra sɔɔnii. Di a tɔɔrɔɔ ɛɛi guŋŋ di wa huhzi, ka i haa vɛɛ ra hiŋ ani kanyitti, i daŋ na tɔna. Kɔraawiizi daŋ tɛi u miibɔɔ la uŋ faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ u daŋ kpa tɛɛ banla maa n nɔŋŋuu la.

ref: Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others.
text: Di kummaa wa darii lugɔ í ɛɛ wichɔgaa, gilɛɛ ŋɔ Kɔraawiizii darii. Kummaa wàá wer dar Kɔraawiizi ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa. U ge gba wàá dar nɛr maa ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa.

ref: We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us.
text: Kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa la n du bɛl maa bampirii labuu ɔɔ ra daruu, ú ɛɛ wichɔgaa. Aabuu ɔɔ ra da u zɛɛ.

ref: Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
text: Kunnyiŋŋichɔgaa a lul wichɔgaarɛ. Di wichɔgaa ge wa hello tuŋ, a ge ɔɔ lul siu.

ref: Don't be fooled, my dear friends.
text: N nɛnɔŋŋaa, ií bɛl maa gilɛɛ waa dar u hiŋ.

ref: Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing.
text: Wii la maa n wesse di ɛɛ winanii himmaa, Kɔraawiizi benii u lii, u kpa sunzi yaa. Kuna la maa n na chaani chiŋ, Kɔraawiizii ta a maa. Ka u himmaa waa ɔɔ bir kur gunla aŋ ɔɔ bir kur, di ra tɔ yaa chunchugle la.

ref: He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth. Hearing and Obeying
text: U himmaa kipar wiarɛ yaa wer nuu u wibii wiŋɔzi, di wer birgi u biizi, di ɛɛ u kunnanaa un lizɛɛ tɛɛ u hiŋ, u kuna la maa un tawɛɛ la biini. Kɔraawiizi wia nuui ni a ɛɛi wia

ref: My dear friends, you should be quick to listen and slow to speak or to get angry.
text: Ií ra liizi guŋ, yaabalaa. A dɛkkɔ nɛr maa n hahzee ra nuu nɛra be, ka sɔɔni bɔra ra ŋɔ wia, di gilɛɛ gil u baaŋ na fuuh manamanaŋ.

ref: If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done.
text: Newee baaŋfuuih waa wikuarii maa dɔɔwɛ winanaa hiŋaa la Kɔraawiizi n na nyiŋŋi la biini.

ref: But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
text: Kɔraawiizi wiŋɔɔlii la n wesse werge di ga tuŋ di lɛɛ yaa, yaa wer dɔɔ yaa hinaa la, u ɛɛ digiire. Nɛr la maa n ninna binni Kɔraawiizi digii la biini di ra pessi wiŋɔɔlaa la nɛnnɛ, waa ra suuh, ka ra hiŋ gunla maa un nawɛɛ de, Kɔraawiizi daŋ gil u nuu suma u wiɛɛlaa maa biini.

ref: If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless.
text: Di nɛr la maa ra binni lugɔ u ra hiŋ Kɔraawiizii, ka waa u himmaa nua tau ra du, u ra dar u hinnɛ. Himpɛɛrɛ u ra hiŋ la.

ref: Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
text: Wii la maa n par yaa Mɛɛ Kɔraawiizi di du wer u benii keŋ, waabuu lugɔ hinna binni lalbiizi ni luhaana la n na di dɔgnya, di ra hiini baa, di kaa ra binni i hiŋ ni, di gilɛɛ gil durnya wichɔgaa maa waa pɛli i ni.

ref: My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others.
text: Yaabalaa, di ii ra hiŋ yaa Dɔɔri Yeesu Kristo la n ɛɛ girme maa dɔɔri la, amɔ, ii gilɛɛ ra tɔgzi baŋhina di kaali baŋhina.

ref: Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes.
text: Di ii maa chaalɔɔ ra jaami Kɔraawiizi, nɛra banɛɛ wa zuu ii be, bɛl du u saliŋ nonibisiga ni u daama laala, bɛl ge laali kuŋkɔssi,

ref: You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor.
text: di ii bagli daama hiŋ la karnanii di ŋɔ ú wa so, ka ŋɔ kuŋkɔssi hiŋ la ge chi gɛɛ ú ba wa so ii naazi zɛɛ,

ref: This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
text: amɔ, ii ra tɔgzi baŋhinaa kaali baŋhina la. Ii hiŋaa wàá dɔɔ wibii di wa tuŋ. Ii birgi sitɔɔra la n ɔɔ kpa kuna wia su siwii labuu.

ref: My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him.
text: Yaabalaa, ií ra binni Kɔraawiizi ge wiɛɛlaa. Nyaara lɛi u liziaa? U lizi baabuu bá wer yarduu werge, bá yarda la ɛɛ ba daama, ka bá wer na u kora biini zuu gunla uŋ faa ŋɔ nua lugɔ banla maa n nɔŋŋuu, daŋ zuu u kora biini la.

ref: You mistreat the poor. But isn't it the rich who boss you around and drag you off to court?
text: Ka iawaa ra gbɛlli nyaara. Daama hina lɛi ɔɔ ra fir ia di ra sami ia, di kpa ia ra la seriya dii bɔra laa?

ref: Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
text: Baa lɛi ɔɔ ra gbɛlli Yeesu sɔnnanii la baŋ ɔɔ kpa ra yir ia laa?

ref: You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves.
text: Di ii ra hiŋ yaa koori widaulii la baŋ sɛbɛɛ du u hɔŋ biini lugɔ í nɔŋŋi i dɔŋhiŋ gunla hin nɔŋŋi i hiŋ la, amɔ, ii ra hiŋuu nɛnnɛ la.

ref: But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
text: Ka di ii ra tɔgzi baŋhina kaali baŋhina, ii ra ɛɛ wichɔgaarɛ. Kɔraawiizi Gbɔg lɛi ii ra chɔgiaa? U daŋ di ia seriya ii chol.

ref: If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all.
text: Di i hiŋ Gbɔgni la maa ka wa chɔg kpaŋkpaŋ, ka i chɔg a maanii. Gbɔgni la daŋ tɛi chɔgri,

ref: The same God who told us to be faithful in marriage also told us not to murder. So even if you are faithful in marriage, but murder someone, you still have broken God's Law.
text: dikuubɛɛwiai, Kɔraawiizi ŋɔwɔɔrɛ, “Gilɛɛ wàá sɛm,” di kaa ŋɔ, “Gilɛɛ wàá kpu.” Di haa sɛm, ka kpu nɛr, amɔ, hàá Gbɔgni la chɔkkɛaa?

ref: Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free.
